prs.title: fix(core): respect active YOLO mode in taint and build file checks
prs.body:
## Summary

Respect active, trusted YOLO mode (`--approval-mode=yolo` / `-y`) in shell taint/build-file risk checks and `PolicyEngine` build file protection so autonomous interactive and headless (`-y -p`) YOLO runs are no longer interrupted by confirmation prompts or hard-denied (`POLICY_VIOLATION`) when editing build configuration files or running commands referencing external context.

All indirect prompt-injection protections remain fully enforced in `default` and `auto_edit` modes, in untrusted folders (`!isTrustedFolder()`), when YOLO mode is administratively disabled (`disableYoloMode` / `secureModeEnabled` / `isYoloModeDisabled()`), when safety checkers (`checkerRunner`) deny/ask, and when higher-tier user/admin policy rules or `BeforeTool` hooks explicitly require `ask_user` or `deny`.

## Details

1. **`PolicyEngine` & `Config` (`packages/core/src/policy/types.ts`, `packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts`, `packages/core/src/config/config.ts`)**:
   - Added optional `isYoloModeDisabled?: () => boolean` to `PolicyEngineConfig` and wired it from `Config` (`isYoloModeDisabled: () => this.isYoloModeDisabled()`), initializing `this.disableYoloMode` prior to `PolicyEngine` construction.
   - Skipped the hardcoded `Build File Protection` downgrade (`ASK_USER` / `DENY` on `package.json`, `Makefile`, `BUILD.bazel`, etc.) only when `this.approvalMode === ApprovalMode.YOLO && this.isTrustedFolder() && !this.isYoloModeDisabled()`.
   - Explicit higher-tier `ASK_USER` / `DENY` policy rules and safety checkers continue to run unchanged.
2. **`ShellToolInvocation` (`packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`)**:
   - Added `isActiveYoloMode()` verifying `ApprovalMode.YOLO`, `isTrustedFolder() !== false`, and `!isYoloModeDisabled()`.
   - Updated `shouldConfirmExecute()` to skip forcing confirmation for `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` when active YOLO mode is enabled (unless `forcedDecision === 'ask_user'` from an explicit policy rule or hook).
   - Updated `isCommandSubstitutionAllowed()` so active YOLO mode delegates command substitution checks to `PolicyEngine` (`yolo.toml` sets `allowCommandSubstitution = true`) rather than unconditionally blocking on `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()`.
   - Preserved the `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` guard in `getPolicyUpdateOptions()` so tainted commands never persist permanent `"Always allow"` rules.
3. **`Scheduler` (`packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.ts`)**:
   - Skipped escalating `PolicyDecision.ALLOW` to `ASK_USER` (interactive) or `DENY` (non-interactive/headless) for `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` only when `ApprovalMode.YOLO`, `isTrustedFolder() !== false`, and `!isYoloModeDisabled()`.

| Context | Taint / Build-File Protection |
|---|---|
| `default` / `auto_edit` / `plan` modes | Enforced (`ASK_USER` / `DENY` in headless) |
| Untrusted folder (`!isTrustedFolder()`) | Enforced even if `approvalMode === YOLO` |
| Admin-disabled YOLO (`disableYoloMode` / `secureModeEnabled`) | Enforced across `PolicyEngine`, `Scheduler`, and `ShellToolInvocation` |
| Explicit higher-tier user/admin `ASK_USER` / `DENY` rules or `BeforeTool` hooks | Enforced in active YOLO mode |
| `"Always allow"` policy persistence for tainted commands | Still blocked (`getPolicyUpdateOptions()` returns `undefined`) |
| Trusted, active `--yolo` / `-y` (interactive & headless `-p`) | Allowed per `yolo.toml` without hardcoded interruption |

*(Open to gating this behind an explicit `security.*` setting if maintainers prefer opt-in over default behavior in trusted YOLO mode.)*

Fixes #30004
Related: #29682, #29680, #29687

- CLI config/settings/confirmation tests (`config.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts`, `ToolConfirmationMessage.test.tsx`): **3 test files passed, 424 tests passed**.
- A2A server tests (`@google/gemini-cli-a2a-server`): **17 test files passed, 329 tests passed**.

prs.title: fix(core): keep a tier alias's config when the tier resolves to its first model
prs.body:
## Summary

A custom alias defined on a tier (`flash-lite`, `flash`, `pro`) now keeps its `generateContentConfig`. Previously, `applyModelSelection` re-resolved the config whenever the selected model's name differed from the resolved name. For a tier the selected name is always the concrete model, so every request used that model's stock settings: temperature 1, thinking HIGH, and no output cap. The alias's own settings were silently ignored, even though no fallback had happened.

## Details

- `applyModelSelection` now re-resolves only when the selected model differs both from the resolved name and from the head of that name's policy chain (`resolvePolicyChain(config, model)[0]`). That head is the model the tier resolves to, so it is the model the alias config was written for.
- A real availability fallback, where the pick is some other model in the chain, still takes that model's config exactly as before.
- Aliases on concrete models are unaffected, because for them the chain head is the model itself.

## Documented behavior

[Advanced Model Configuration](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/blob/main/docs/cli/generation-settings.md) (`docs/cli/generation-settings.md`) describes behavior that `main` does not follow for an alias on a tier:

- **Step 1: Alias Resolution.** The docs say the requested model string is looked up in the alias map, its `extends` chain is merged, and *"this results in a base `ResolvedModelConfig`."* On `main`, that config is thrown away whenever the selected model's name differs from the resolved name. A tier alias such as `flash-lite` always resolves to a different, concrete name, so the request is re-resolved under that name and gets that model's stock settings.
- **Overrides.** The docs say an override's `match.model` *"matches the requested model name or alias."* The re-resolution uses the concrete model name, so an override that matches the alias, or the tier name, does not apply either.
- **The docs' own example.** The `precise-mode` example (`extends` a chat alias with `temperature: 0.0`) depends on this too. If the model it ends up on is resolved or promoted to another name, `temperature: 0.0` is dropped the same way.

This PR makes the runtime match the documented resolution. The alias's resolved config is kept unless an availability fallback moves the request to a different model in the chain. Only that fallback, which the docs do not describe as a config change, takes the other model's config.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30238

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/availability/
   ```
   The new test fails on `main`. It defines `my-lite` on `flash-lite` with `temperature: 0.2` and `maxOutputTokens: 256`, then checks that the selected concrete model keeps both. The existing fallback test still passes.
2. Add this to `settings.json`:
   ```json
   "modelConfigs": { "customAliases": { "my-lite": { "modelConfig": {
     "model": "flash-lite",
     "generateContentConfig": { "temperature": 0.2, "maxOutputTokens": 256 } } } } }
   ```
   Then run `gemini -m my-lite -p "Reply with the single word ok."` with a local proxy via `CODE_ASSIST_ENDPOINT` that records `generationConfig`:

   | Build | `model` | `generationConfig` |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | main `e5d88fb2c` | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` | `temperature: 1`, `thinkingLevel: HIGH`, no `maxOutputTokens` |
   | this PR | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` | `temperature: 0.2`, `maxOutputTokens: 256` |

prs.title: fix(core): quote IDE CLI path for cmd.exe in /ide install on Windows
prs.body:
## Summary

On Windows, `/ide install` fails with "Failed to install VS Code companion extension" whenever the editor CLI is in a folder whose name has a space. The "Do you want to connect VS Code to Gemini CLI?" prompt runs the same command, so it fails too. VS Code's default install folders always contain a space (`...\Microsoft VS Code\bin\code.cmd`), so IDE integration cannot be set up automatically on a standard Windows install. This PR quotes the CLI path for `cmd.exe` so the install command runs.

## Details

- **Root cause.** On Windows, the installers in `packages/core/src/ide/ide-installer.ts` run `code.cmd`, `positron.cmd` or `antigravity.cmd` with `spawnSync(commandPath, args, { shell: true })`. `shell: true` is required, because Node refuses to spawn a `.cmd` file directly (`EINVAL`, see #9995). But Node then does not quote the command. It joins the command and the arguments with spaces and runs `cmd.exe /d /s /c "<joined text>"`. `cmd.exe` cuts the path at the first space and reports `'...\Programs\Microsoft' is not recognized as an internal or external command`. The non-zero exit is caught and shown only as the generic failure message.
- **Fix.** A small `runCompanionInstall()` helper quotes the command path and arguments on Windows with the existing `quoteCmdArg()` from `utils/editor.ts`. That is the helper `openDiff` started using in #29753. On macOS and Linux nothing changes: no shell, no quoting. The three installers (VS Code and Firebase Studio, Positron, Antigravity) now call this helper instead of three identical `spawnSync` blocks.
- **No change for paths that already work.** `quoteCmdArg()` leaves paths without spaces or special characters as they are, so working installs (for example Scoop) behave exactly as before.
- **Left as is.** On Node 24, passing arguments together with `shell: true` still prints the `DEP0190` deprecation warning. That already happens today, and also in `openDiff`. Building the command line by hand to avoid it would be a separate change.
- **Tests.** The existing Windows tests expected the unquoted call, which is exactly the call that breaks in `cmd.exe`. They now expect a quoted path. New tests cover:
  - the per-user VS Code install path;
  - the default-location fallback used when `code` is not on `PATH`;
  - Positron on Windows;
  - a space-free path that must stay unquoted;
  - macOS passing a path with spaces unquoted, because it uses no shell.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30245

Earlier Windows reports of the same symptom (#12528, #15622, #17033) were closed without a root cause.

## How to Validate

1. Run the unit tests:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/ide/ide-installer.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
   ```

   All tests pass.

2. Show that the new tests catch the bug. Put back the old source, run the tests again, then restore the fix:

   ```bash
   git checkout HEAD~1 -- packages/core/src/ide/ide-installer.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/ide/ide-installer.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
   git checkout HEAD -- packages/core/src/ide/ide-installer.ts
   ```

   With the old source, 5 tests fail: two VS Code paths with spaces, the default-location fallback, Positron and Antigravity. The space-free path and macOS tests pass on both versions.

   I ran steps 1 and 2 with Node 22 (the tests mock the Windows platform): with the fix all 25 installer tests pass; with the old source the 5 new Windows tests fail. Prettier, ESLint and `npm run typecheck` also pass.

3. Manual check on Windows, with VS Code in its default folder:
   1. Run `npm run build`.
   2. In VS Code's integrated terminal, inside the repository folder, run `npm start`.
   3. Run `/ide install`.

   Before this change: "Failed to install VS Code companion extension..." (reproduced with Gemini CLI 0.68.0 on Windows 11, see #30245). After: "VS Code companion extension was installed successfully.", and IDE integration connects.

4. Optional check of how the failure happens (Windows, plain Node): run the repro script in the linked issue. It shows `spawnSync(path, args, { shell: true })` on a `.cmd` inside a folder with a space exiting with status 1 ("...is not recognized..."), and the quoted path running.

prs.title: fix(core): keep the synthetic binary ack so injected audio/video stays in its own turn
prs.body:
## Summary

With Gemini 3 models, `read_file` on audio or video fails with 400 "Requests ending with a model turn are not supported" when using Code Assist (Login with Google). The binary injection from #26352 sends the media in its own user turn behind a synthetic model ack. Because that ack is a thought-only part, thought stripping drops it. The media then coalesces into the `functionResponse` turn, which is the shape the API rejects. This PR keeps the ack as a plain-text model turn when history is sent.

## Details

- In `stripThoughts` (both copies), `scrubHistory` and `scrubContents`, a synthetic binary ack turn becomes `model[text: "Binary content received. Proceeding with analysis."]` instead of being dropped. The `!isSyntheticBinaryAckTurn` exclusions are removed because those branches can no longer be reached for the ack.
- The recorded history keeps the thought ack, so nothing changes in the UI. Sessions recorded before this change are also fixed on resume, because the conversion happens when the request is built.
- The `historyHardening` test that expected the merged `[functionResponse, inlineData]` turn now expects the three-turn shape. A new `GeminiChat` test checks the request a modern model receives. Both new assertions fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- Images and PDFs are unaffected, since they stay nested in `functionResponse.parts`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30229

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/historyHardening.test.ts src/core/geminiChat.test.ts
   ```
2. Live check on Linux with Login with Google, `-m gemini-3.8-flash`, and a small `.mp4` and `.wav` in the workspace. I recorded the request shapes with a local proxy via `CODE_ASSIST_ENDPOINT`:

   | Build | Request tail | Result |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | main `e5d88fb2c` | `user[functionResponse(read_file), inlineData(video/mp4)]` | 400 |
   | this PR | `user[functionResponse]`, `model[text]`, `user[inlineData(video/mp4)]` | 200, the model read the text in the video correctly |
   | main `e5d88fb2c` | `user[functionResponse(read_file), inlineData(audio/wav)]` | 400 |
   | this PR | `user[functionResponse]`, `model[text]`, `user[inlineData(audio/wav)]` | 200 |

prs.title: feat(acp): support session/close so clients can release a session
prs.body:
## Summary

ACP clients can now release a session with `session/close`. Today the method fails with `-32601 Method not found`, because `GeminiAgent` does not implement `unstable_closeSession`, the handler the SDK routes `session/close` to. As a result, every session holds its config, chat and MCP connections until the `--acp` process exits. This brings an explicit close in line with how the agent already releases sessions in `loadSession` and on shutdown.

## Details

- `AcpSessionManager.closeSession(sessionId)` removes the session from the map, then awaits `session.dispose()` and logs a failed disposal. This is the same order and error handling `loadSession` uses when it replaces an existing session. Because the id is forgotten first, a `session/load` of the same id that follows keeps the session it creates.
- An unknown id gets `-32602 Session not found`, like `cancel`, `prompt` and `setSessionMode`.
- `initialize` now advertises `sessionCapabilities: { close: {} }`, so clients can see the method is supported.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30231

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/acp/acpSessionManager.test.ts src/acp/acpRpcDispatcher.test.ts
   ```
   The three new assertions fail on `main` and pass here: the advertised capability, routing through the session manager, and closing a session even when its disposal throws.
2. Over stdio against `gemini --acp`, send `initialize`, `session/new`, `session/close`, and then `session/prompt` on the closed id:

   | Build | `sessionCapabilities` | `session/close` | `session/prompt` on the closed id |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | main `e5d88fb2c` | `null` | `-32601 Method not found` | answers, so the session is still alive |
   | this PR | `{"close":{}}` | `{}` | `-32602 Session not found` |
3. Two sessions in one `gemini --acp` process (this PR, `-m gemini-3-flash-preview`), closing only the first:

   | Step | Result |
   | --- | --- |
   | `session/new` × 2 | two distinct ids |
   | prompt A "remember APPLE", prompt B "remember BANANA" | both `end_turn` |
   | `session/close` A | `{}` |
   | `session/prompt` A | `-32602 Session not found` |
   | `session/prompt` B "which word?" | `end_turn`, "BANANA", so B keeps its history |
   | `session/close` A again | `-32602 Session not found` |
   | `session/close` B | `{}` |

prs.title: fix(core): avoid blocking PowerShell parsing during shell checks
prs.body:
## Summary

Avoid blocking the Node.js event loop while parsing PowerShell commands during shell policy checks, confirmation, and execution preparation on Windows.

Synchronous PowerShell startup and AST parsing can freeze the Thinking spinner and elapsed time before the Shell panel appears. This change moves those parsing operations to asynchronous process execution.

## Details

- Reuse complete parse results and in-flight promises within a single policy-check recursion or Shell invocation.
- Preserve the existing PowerShell AST parser, Bash fallback safeguards, and raw PowerShell redirection checks.
- Parse child commands independently instead of synthesizing results from parent AST nodes.
- Prepare command and stripped-wrapper forms before confirmation and execution helpers consume them.
- Await the internal taint-risk check in the scheduler.
- Introduce no process-wide cache or new parser timeout.

Standalone synchronous APIs remain supported. Existing sandbox-internal synchronous parsing and parser-process cancellation limitations are outside this change.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30249

## How to Validate

### Automated checks

From the repository root:

```powershell
npx vitest run --root packages/core src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts src/utils/untrustedContextTracker.test.ts src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts src/policy/policy-engine.powershell.test.ts src/policy/policy-updater.test.ts src/tools/shell.test.ts src/scheduler/scheduler.test.ts src/scheduler/policy.test.ts src/policy/shell-safety.test.ts src/policy/shell-substitution.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false --maxWorkers=2

npm run typecheck
npm run build
```

Results on Windows 10 Pro with Node 24.14.1:

- 769 related tests passed in an isolated checkout.
- 22 additional policy integration, AppRig, and modelSteering tests passed.
- 192 deterministic comparisons against the original policy engine produced identical policy results.
- Full ESLint, type checking, and build passed.

### Manual validation

Run npm start and ask Gemini to execute this exact command through run_shell_command:

Get-ChildItem | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 Name,Length,LastWriteTime

Verify that the spinner and elapsed time continue updating during the transition from Thinking to the Shell panel. Repeat within the same session and after restarting the CLI.

The scoped implementation was manually retested without observing the original freeze. This was not a controlled performance comparison on the originally affected machine.

### Validation limitations

The local full suite is not entirely green. Previously failing files were compared with unmodified base e5d88fb2c using separate checkouts and dependencies:

| Selected historical failures | Base passed / failed | This branch passed / failed |
|---|---:|---:|
| core | 389 / 36 | 387 / 38 |
| CLI | 86 / 18 | 86 / 18 |
| a2a-server | 3 / 1 | 3 / 1 |

Common failed assertions and primary errors match. The two additional core failures also reproduce on the base in a focused rerun. They are unchanged inode tests whose ino + 1 assumption fails when NTFS inode values exceed JavaScript's safe-integer range.

No new regression was identified in the compared tests. No security checks were relaxed or tests skipped.

Full preflight was attempted, but its YAML lint command stopped because the Windows shell could not find grep. The equivalent YAML check passed through Git Bash, and remaining static checks were completed separately. Overall preflight is not claimed passing; upstream CI and platform validation remain necessary.

prs.title: fix(acp): truncate large tool outputs for the model like the CLI does
prs.body:
## Summary

ACP now bounds large tool outputs for the model the same way the CLI does. `Session.runTool` runs tools without the scheduler, so it never reached `ToolExecutor.truncateOutputIfNeeded` and sent a large shell or MCP output whole. One `seq 1 60000` call cost 369k input tokens over ACP, compared with 60k once the CLI's rule is applied. Outputs larger than the context window failed the turn.

## Details

- `ToolExecutor.truncateOutputIfNeeded` is now public. Its `call` parameter is narrowed to what the method reads: `request`, plus an optional `tool` for the MCP check. Scheduler call sites are unchanged.
- `Session.runTool` calls it on `toolResult.llmContent` before converting the result to a function response. Both the recorded history and the response sent to the model use the bounded content. ACP therefore gets the same threshold (`getTruncateToolOutputThreshold()`), the same saved file under the project temp `tool-outputs/` folder, the same head and tail text, and context-management distillation when that is enabled.
- The `tool_call_update` sent to the client still carries the full display content. Only what the model receives changes.
- The `acpSession` test config gains the fields the shared method reads. Without them, a tool call in those tests would quietly take the error path.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30233

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/acp/
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/scheduler/
   ```
   The new `acpSession` test fails on `main`. It checks that the model gets the truncated text with the file path and not the middle of the output, and that the full output is saved to that file.
2. Over stdio with `gemini --acp -m gemini-3.8-flash`, ask the agent to run `seq 1 60000` with `run_shell_command` and reply with the last number, then approve the permission request:

prs.title: fix(acp): run parallelizable tool calls together like the CLI scheduler
prs.body:
## Summary

ACP now runs the independent tool calls of a turn together, as the CLI's `Scheduler` does. The ACP prompt loop awaited each call before starting the next, so a turn with several searches, fetches or shell commands took as long as all of them added up. In one turn with four `sleep 3` shell calls, everything finished at 12.1 s on `main` and at 3.0 s with this change.

## Details

- The loop in `Session.prompt` batches each run of consecutive calls with `isParallelizable`, the predicate the `Scheduler` uses. Edits, `update_topic`, and calls marked `wait_for_previous` still run alone and in order.
- Each batch runs with `Promise.allSettled`, so every call that was started has settled before an error is thrown, just as the scheduler waits for the calls it started. `runTool` already turns tool errors into error responses.
- Responses are appended in the model's call order, so the next request is the same as before. Only the timing changes.
- Permission requests for calls in one batch can now reach the client together, as they do in the CLI.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30235

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/acp/
   ```

   The new `acpSession` test fails on `main`. It sends two parallelizable calls and one `replace`, then checks three things: the first two start together, the edit starts only after both finish, and the responses keep call order.

prs.title: fix(acp): standardize token usage tracking and quota metadata (#24280, #27985)
prs.body:
### Description
This PR resolves two token tracking discrepancies in ACP mode:
1. **Preserve `PromptResponse.usage` on cancelled turns (#24280)**: Previously, early aborts or cancellations returned `{ stopReason: 'cancelled' }` without `usage` or `_meta`. This caused ACP clients to lose token usage metrics on cancelled prompts. Cancellation paths now return `buildPromptResponse('cancelled')` with preserved turn usage.
2. **Track cached and thought tokens in model quota metadata (#27985)**: Per-model quota breakdowns in `_meta.quota.model_usage` previously only tracked input and output tokens, omitting cached and thought tokens. We now track all four token dimensions (`input`, `output`, `cached`, `thought`) across all models and multi-turn tool loops.

### Changes
- `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.ts`:
  - Updated `modelUsageMap` type to include `cached` and `thought` tokens.
  - Added `cached_tokens` and `thought_tokens` to `_meta.quota.token_count` and `_meta.quota.model_usage`.
  - Added helper `recordTurnUsage()` to ensure tokens parsed before abort are preserved.
  - Updated abort and `AbortError` return paths to return `buildPromptResponse('cancelled')`.
- `packages/cli/src/acp/acpSession.test.ts`:
  - Added unit tests for mid-stream prompt aborts, immediate aborts, `AbortError` handling, and multi-turn multi-model token accumulation.

prs.title: fix(web-fetch): prevent SSRF via DNS hostnames and redirects (revival of #27739)
prs.body:
# fix(web-fetch): prevent SSRF via DNS hostnames and redirects (revival of #27739)

Fixes the web-fetch proxy-redirect SSRF (R5). A URL that passes the
initial private-IP check can redirect (directly, or through a configured
proxy) to a loopback / link-local / private target, and the redirect hop
was never re-validated. `fetchWithTimeout` follows redirects with undici's
default redirect handling, so a single crafted redirect reaches
`169.254.169.254`, `127.0.0.1`, or any RFC-1918 host — including through
`NO_PROXY`, where the redirect hop leaves the proxy entirely.

## Provenance — this revives closed PR #27739, it does not reopen it

#27739 was closed without merging. Its author is an external reporter,
**g0w6y <g0w6y@users.noreply.github.com>**. This PR re-applies their fix
(the two commits below) onto current main (`60f8082`), with the rebase
adaptations and extensions listed after; g0w6y is credited as co-author
on the commits. Original commits:

- `adb373cd414bfd46c1f03787fe8484979aa82ade` — "fix(web-fetch): prevent
  SSRF via DNS hostnames and redirects" (2026-06-08)
- `7695edd021969e76948f9b4c4ffa7f4ad46fb4b1` — "fix(web-fetch): harden
  redirect handling in safeFetchFollowingRedirects" (2026-06-08)

## What the cherry-picked commits add (rebased)

- `assertUrlIsPublic(url)` — throws `PrivateIpError` if the URL's literal
  host or its DNS-resolved address is private / loopback / link-local.
- `applyRedirect(...)` — rejects non-http(s) redirect targets, strips
  credential headers (`authorization`, `cookie`, `cookie2`,
  `proxy-authorization`) on cross-origin redirects, downgrades 303 (and
  non-GET/HEAD 301/302) to GET with the body removed.
- `safeFetchFollowingRedirects(url, timeout, options)` — validates the
  initial URL and **every** redirect hop with `assertUrlIsPublic` before
  the connection is made (max 5 redirects), following redirects manually
  (`redirect: 'manual'`).

## Rebase adaptations (current main differs from the June 2026 base)

- `isPrivateIp()` is now **async** (`Promise<boolean>`); the rebased
  `assertUrlIsPublic` awaits it (the original patch called it
  synchronously). `isPrivateIpAsync` still exists and is used for the
  distinct "resolves to a private address" message.
- `createSafeProxyAgent(proxyUrl)` now takes a single proxy-URL string;
  the patch's options-object form does not apply.
- `web-fetch.ts` call sites are already flat in current main (no nested
  restructure needed): both the fallback and the experimental paths now
  call `safeFetchFollowingRedirects` with the same `(url, timeout, {signal,
  headers})` shape.

## Extensions beyond #27739 (same PR, same root cause)

- **Extension registry caller migrated.** `extensionRegistryClient.ts`
  (`fetchAllExtensions`) also called `fetchWithTimeout` with only an
  initial check — it now calls `safeFetchFollowingRedirects`. This is the
  third and last `fetchWithTimeout` caller in the repo; all three are now
  covered. (`fetchWithTimeout` itself is unchanged and remains available
  for internal callers that do not fetch untrusted URLs.)
- **Proxy-dispatcher hardening.** `createSafeProxyAgent` and
  `setGlobalProxy` (the global dispatcher) now install a proxy-aware safe
  connector (`createProxyAwareSafeConnector`): direct (`no_proxy`)
  connections are validated with the safe DNS lookup, while connections
  to the explicitly configured proxy host itself use the default
  connector — blocking private proxy hosts would break legitimate
  corporate proxies, and the proxy resolves proxied targets itself.
  Proxied *targets* are validated separately by `assertUrlIsPublic`
  before the proxy is asked (see `safeFetchFollowingRedirects`). Note:
  `undici.buildConnector` in the pinned undici 7.x destructures its
  argument with no default, so the connector is created with
  `buildConnector({})`, not `buildConnector()`.
- `packages/core/src/index.ts` already does `export * from
  './utils/fetch.js'`, so the new functions are part of the public API
  with no barrel change.

## Tests

- New `packages/core/src/utils/fetch.ssrf.test.ts` (from #27739 patch 2,
  unchanged): 16 tests — `assertUrlIsPublic` (literal + resolved private
  hosts), `applyRedirect` (protocol rejection, credential stripping,
  303/302 downgrade), `safeFetchFollowingRedirects` (private target
  refused before any read).
- Updated the existing suites to the new call: `web-fetch.test.ts`
  mocks `safeFetchFollowingRedirects` (was `fetchWithTimeout`);
  `extensionRegistryClient.test.ts` mocks `safeFetchFollowingRedirects`
  and `isPrivateIp` (the latter makes the suite independent of the test
  environment's DNS resolver, matching `web-fetch.test.ts` practice).
- Results: **108/108 tests pass** — core `web-fetch.test.ts` 62,
  `fetch.spec.ts` 17, `fetch.ssrf.test.ts` 16; CLI
  `extensionRegistryClient.test.ts` 13. `tsc --noEmit` clean for both
  `packages/core` and `packages/cli`; `npm run build` in `packages/core`
  succeeds.
- Dynamic proof (local harness, 127.0.0.1 servers only, 2/2 runs each):
  pre-fix build reproduces the vulnerability — proxy asked for the
  loopback redirect target (secret returned via proxy) and the
  `NO_PROXY` redirect fetched the secret directly. Post-fix build:
  both legs and the registry-shaped leg fail with `PrivateIpError`
  before any connection to the private target (proxy sees only the
  initial hop, secret-server hits 0). The pre-existing connector-level
  guard (C3) still blocks.

## Honest limits

- The registry leg exercises `safeFetchFollowingRedirects` with the exact
  arguments `fetchAllExtensions` now passes; a live end-to-end
  `fetchAllExtensions` run against a real registry was not done here.
- Callers that keep using raw `fetchWithTimeout` directly are not
  protected; the fix covers the three call sites that fetch
  untrusted URLs.

prs.title: Fix: bind MCP tool approvals to the tool definition they approved
prs.body:
# Fix: bind MCP tool approvals to the tool definition they approved

## Summary

A `ProceedAlwaysServer` / `ProceedAlwaysTool` approval for an MCP tool was
remembered by **name only**. When the server later sent `tools/list_changed`,
the CLI re-registered the tools and the old approval silently covered
whatever the server now served under that name — a new tool, or the same
name with a different description / parameter schema. This PR binds each
approval to the **definition that was approved** (description +
parameterSchema, the exact surface the confirmation dialog shows), and
refuses to let a different MCP tool silently overwrite a registered tool
whose name collides after the 63-character truncation.

## What changed

### Approval is bound to the definition (`packages/core/src/tools/mcp-tool.ts`)

- New exported helpers:
  - `computeMcpToolDefinitionHash(description, parameterSchema)` —
    `sha256(stableStringify({ description, parameterSchema }))`.
  - `diffMcpToolDefinitions(currentTools, newTools)` — returns
    `{ added, removed, redefined }` keyed by server tool name.
- `DiscoveredMCPToolInvocation` now keeps, per grant:
  - `definitionsByServer` — the definitions currently known per server,
    recorded when a `DiscoveredMCPTool` is constructed.
  - `serverApprovalSnapshots` / `toolApprovalSnapshots` — the definition
    hash each server/tool grant was given for, recorded in `onConfirm`
    (`ProceedAlwaysServer` snapshots every currently known tool of that
    server; `ProceedAlwaysTool` / `ProceedAlwaysAndSave` snapshot the tool).
  - Each invocation computes its own `definitionHash` in the constructor.
- `getConfirmationDetails` waives confirmation only when the allowlist key
  is present **and** the snapshot hash matches the invocation's current
  hash. A missing snapshot entry, a redefined tool, or a tool added after
  the grant all prompt again (fail closed).
- `DiscoveredMCPTool` exposes a public `readonly definitionHash` and
  registers its definition on construction.

### Refresh reports definition changes (`packages/core/src/tools/mcp-client.ts`)

- `refreshTools` now diffs the new tool list against the currently
  registered tools (before `removeMcpToolsByServer`) and, when anything
  changed, emits a `warning` diagnostic:
  `MCP tools changed: <server> (added: …; removed: …; redefined: …)` —
  redefined tools are noted as "will ask for confirmation again". When
  nothing changed, the existing `info` "Tools updated for server: …"
  message is kept. The verification-retry path is unchanged.

### Truncation collisions no longer overwrite (`packages/core/src/tools/tool-registry.ts`)

- `registerTool` now refuses (logs an error, keeps the first registration)
  when two **different** `DiscoveredMCPTool`s (different
  serverName/serverToolName pair) truncate to the same registry name.
  Re-registering the *same* MCP tool still overwrites as before.

## What this does NOT fix (honest limitation)

**Persisted rules still bypass the session allowlist.** `shouldConfirmExecute`
(`tools.ts`) asks the message bus / policy first; a persisted `allow`
decision (e.g. a saved `ProceedAlwaysAndSave` rule) returns `false`
without ever calling `getConfirmationDetails`, so a persisted rule is not
bound to a definition hash by this PR. Binding persisted rules would need
the hash threaded through the policy decision path, the rule schema, and
the TOML persistence — a larger format change. Follow-up work.

`outputSchema` is deliberately **not** part of the hash: the confirmation
dialog shows exactly description + parameterSchema, so binding on those
two is exactly "what was approved".

## Tests

- `packages/core/src/tools/mcp-tool.test.ts` — grant-driven allowlist
  tests replace the old bare-key tests; new tests cover: redefined tool
  prompts after a server grant and after a tool grant; a tool added after
  a server grant prompts; an unchanged re-discovered tool after a grant
  does not prompt; `onConfirm` snapshot assertions (incl. a new
  `ProceedAlwaysAndSave` row); unit tests for
  `computeMcpToolDefinitionHash` (stability, description change, schema
  change, key-order independence) and `diffMcpToolDefinitions`.
- `packages/core/src/tools/tool-registry.test.ts` — collision refusal
  (first registration kept) and same-tool re-registration (overwrite).
- `packages/core/src/tools/mcp-client.test.ts` — the refresh test now
  expects the `warning` diagnostic when a tool was added.
- Dynamic proof (`tested-diffs/r3-1/harness/`, run with the repo's `tsx`):
  pristine 60f8082 reproduces all three bypasses 2/2 (new tool bypassed,
  redefined tool bypassed, colliding name overwritten by the malicious
  tool); patched 2/2 blocks all three (both prompt again, first
  registration wins).

## Verification

- `git apply --check` against a fresh 60f8082 tree: pass. Real `git apply`
  in a fresh worktree + full suites: **194/194 pass**
  (`mcp-tool`, `mcp-client`, `tool-registry`).
- `tsc --noEmit` (core + cli): 0 errors. `npm run build` in
  `packages/core`: exit 0.

## Re-proof

Finding re-confirmed live in current main @60f8082 on 2026-11-26
(REPROOF-2026-11-26.md). Fresh duplicate screen at that time: 0 total
matches.

prs.title: Fixes #30391: bind stored MCP OAuth tokens to the server URL they were issued for
prs.body:
Fixes #30391: bind stored MCP OAuth tokens to the server URL they were issued for

**Verdict: a stored OAuth token is now withheld instead of replayed when the MCP server URL has been repointed to a different origin. The user is asked to re-authenticate instead of the old token silently going to the new server.**

## The bug

Gemini CLI saved the OAuth access token for an MCP server under the server's name, with no check on which server URL it belonged to. If the server's configured URL was later changed to a different host — a typo, a config edit, or a malicious repoint — the next connection still sent the stored token to the new URL. A token minted for server A was replayed to server B with no re-consent.

## What this PR changes

The token is bound to the server URL recorded when it was issued (`mcpServerUrl` on the stored credentials, saved by `authenticate()`). Every path that can send the token checks the binding first:

1. `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth-utils.ts` — new `isSameOrigin` helper and `isStoredTokenBoundToServerUrl`: the recorded and expected URLs must share an origin (scheme, host, port, default ports normalized). A record with no recorded URL fails closed.
2. `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth-provider.ts` — `getValidToken` and `getValidTokenWithMetadata` both check the binding before returning or refreshing a token. On a mismatch they return `null` and tell the user to re-authenticate (`/mcp auth <server>`). The token is withheld, not deleted, and never refreshed against the new URL — refresh still goes to the stored token URL and the recorded server URL.
3. `packages/core/src/mcp/stored-token-provider.ts` — `DynamicStoredOAuthProvider.tokens()` passes the configured URL (`httpUrl || url`) into the check. This is the primary connection path: it is what the SDK auth provider calls on the first connection attempt.
4. `packages/core/src/tools/mcp-client.ts` — all three `getStoredOAuthToken` call sites (SSE fallback, retry after `www-authenticate`, retry after discovery) pass the configured URL; `createTransport` only installs the dynamic provider for a token bound to this server's URL, so on a repoint the request goes out unauthenticated, gets a 401, and the existing re-consent flow runs (including the "requires authentication" diagnostic); `showAuthRequiredMessage` threads the URL through so a repoint reports "requires authentication" instead of "rejected stored OAuth token".
5. `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth-token-storage.ts` — `saveToken` now preserves the recorded server URL when a re-save doesn't carry one (merged like the refresh token). Without this, the A2A agent provider's `persistToken()`, which shares this storage and passes only four arguments, silently unbound every record it rewrote.

## Deliberate choices

- **Origin-only binding, not origin+path.** A path change on the same origin is allowed — same-origin path changes are normally server upgrades, and the reported attack is repointing to a different host. This differs from the `isSameServerUrl` helper in Ben-Home's comment on the issue (origin + pathname); reviewers who want path-sensitive binding should say so.
- **Records with no recorded URL fail closed.** Tokens minted before the field existed, and records written by paths that didn't record a URL, need one re-consent instead of silently replaying. This is the behavior agreed in the issue thread.
- **Withheld tokens are never deleted.** The user may have repointed the URL by mistake; a later `authenticate()` for the corrected URL overwrites the record.

## Out of scope

The A2A agent provider (`agents/auth-provider/oauth2-provider.ts`) sends its cached token via `headers()` with no URL binding check of its own. It shares this token storage, so the `saveToken` merge above stops its rewrites from unbinding MCP records, but an agent-card URL repoint is a separate issue and is not fixed here.

## Testing

Local unit tests only — no live replay testing was done in this PR (see below).

- `packages/core/src/mcp/oauth-provider.test.ts` (69 tests), `oauth-utils.test.ts` (77), `oauth-token-storage.test.ts` (32), `stored-token-provider.test.ts` (3), `tools/mcp-client.test.ts` (85) — all passing.
- New tests cover: token withheld for a different origin (both `getValidToken` and `getValidTokenWithMetadata`), no refresh attempted on mismatch, same-origin path change allowed, explicit default port treated as the same origin, missing stored URL withheld (fail closed), no-check when no expected URL is known, `saveToken` preserving/overwriting the recorded URL, and `createTransport` not installing the dynamic provider on a repoint or on a record with no URL (with the "requires authentication" diagnostic).
- `tsc --build` (via `npm run build` in `packages/core`) and `eslint` on all changed files pass with no errors or warnings.

## Still owed (not verified in this PR)

A live A-vs-B check: mint a token for server A, repoint the config to server B, and confirm no `Authorization` header reaches B and the CLI asks for re-authentication — plus the trailing-slash A-vs-A control (should connect silently) and the http→https control (must mismatch). The unit tests cover the same logic with mocks, but the end-to-end replay check needs real servers and was not run here.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop trusted-workspace settings from redirecting telemetry export
prs.body:
# fix(cli): stop trusted-workspace settings from redirecting telemetry export

## Summary

A trusted workspace's `.gemini/settings.json` wins over user settings for
every key, including `telemetry.otlpEndpoint` / `outfile`. A cloned repo
(trusted with one click) could therefore set `telemetry: {enabled: true,
otlpEndpoint: <attacker collector>, traces: true}` and receive full user
prompts, tool-call args and errors, API error strings, and full LLM
input/output span messages — `logPrompts` defaults to true, so the
attacker need not set it. No warning is emitted for a remote telemetry
destination. (No stored credentials are in telemetry payloads; this is
user/tool-content exfiltration, not token leakage.)

This change scopes telemetry destination keys to user/system settings
only, so a workspace can no longer choose where telemetry goes.

## What changed

`packages/cli/src/config/settings.ts` — `mergeSettings` now passes the
trusted workspace object through `stripWorkspaceTelemetryDestinations`
before merging. The following keys are removed from the workspace's
`telemetry` object (a copy is made; the caller's object is never mutated):

- `enabled`, `target`, `otlpEndpoint`, `otlpProtocol`, `otlpHeaders`,
  `outfile`, `useCollector`, `useCliAuth`

Deliberately **not** stripped: `logPrompts` and `traces`. Without a
destination they export nowhere, so they may stay workspace-settable.

Untrusted workspaces are unaffected (their settings are already dropped
entirely). User, system, env, and argv telemetry config keeps working
unchanged — the strip applies to the workspace object only, and only to
the destination keys.

## What this does NOT do

- No warning is emitted when a workspace tries to set these keys (the
  pack's option 2). The keys are silently ignored at merge time. A
  loud per-session warning for a remote endpoint supplied by workspace
  settings would be a complementary follow-up.
- `outfile` paths from user settings are not restricted here; only the
  workspace's ability to choose one is removed.

## Tests

- `packages/cli/src/config/settings.test.ts`:
  - New `describe('mergeSettings telemetry workspace scope')`: all 8
    destination keys stripped from a trusted workspace (logPrompts /
    traces kept); user telemetry untouched; the caller's workspace
    object not mutated; a workspace cannot override user telemetry.
  - New loadSettings-level test in the workspace-trust describe: a
    trusted workspace's full telemetry block is ignored except
    logPrompts / traces.
  - Two pre-existing tests updated to the new intended behavior (they
    asserted workspace telemetry wins): "should load telemetry setting
    from workspace settings" → workspace `enabled` is now ignored;
    "should prioritize workspace telemetry setting over user setting" →
    the user value now stands.
- Dynamic proof (`tested-diffs/t1/harness/`, run with the repo's `tsx`):
  the REAL `mergeSettings` feeds the REAL `resolveTelemetrySettings` +
  REAL OpenTelemetry SDK init + REAL loggers against a loopback
  collector. Pristine 60f8082: workspace leg exports 7/7 markers 2/2.
  Patched: workspace leg exports 0/7 markers 2/2 (merged telemetry
  keeps only `traces` / `logPrompts`). User leg (regression): 7/7
  markers on both trees, 2/2 each. Fake stored credentials never arrive
  in any run.

## Verification

- `git apply --check` against a fresh 60f8082 tree: pass. Real
  `git apply` in a fresh worktree + full settings suite: **154/154 pass**.
- `tsc --noEmit` (cli + core): 0 errors.

## Re-proof

Finding re-confirmed live in current main @60f8082 on 2026-11-26
(REPROOF-2026-11-26.md). Fresh duplicate screen at that time: 5 total
matches, no match (#29641 OTLP headers feature; #29099 fail-closed
workspace trust for mcpServers only; #6818; #5952; #9009).

prs.title: fix(core): exclude evicted binary payloads from exempt retrieval byte budget
prs.body:
## TLDR

Fixes #30446.

`collapseOlderFunctionResponses` now sizes older retrieval turns using their retained byte size (after evicted sibling `inlineData` and nested `functionResponse.parts` are excluded) instead of `calculateHistoryByteSize([turn])`, preventing a single older image `read_file` from exhausting the 64 KB `MAX_EXEMPT_RETRIEVAL_HISTORY_BYTES` budget and collapsing earlier text reads.

## Dive Deeper

- **Root cause:** `collapseOlderFunctionResponses` always evicts binary payloads from older turns (replacing sibling `part.inlineData` with `OMITTED_BINARY_MESSAGE` and stripping nested `part.functionResponse.parts`), even for preserved exempt retrieval turns. However, the budget loop measured each candidate turn with `calculateHistoryByteSize([turn])`, which counts those evicted binary bytes. One >64 KB screenshot `read_file` exhausted the entire exempt retrieval budget and caused older text `read_file` / `grep` outputs to collapse to 2 KB previews.
- **Fix:** Added a private `calculateRetainedTurnByteSize(turn)` helper in `packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.ts` used only in the exempt-budget loop. It counts `OMITTED_BINARY_MESSAGE_BYTES` for sibling `inlineData` parts and omits nested `functionResponse.parts`, while leaving `calculateHistoryByteSize` untouched so memory-pressure thresholds continue measuring full binary size.
- **Tests:** Added a parameterized regression test in `packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.test.ts` covering both `nested` (`functionResponse.parts[].inlineData`) and `sibling` (`part.inlineData`) layouts. Both cases fail on `main` and pass with this fix.

## Reviewer Test Plan

```bash
npx vitest run packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.test.ts packages/core/src/agents/memory-leak-regression.test.ts --coverage.enabled=false
```

- `packages/core/src/context/chatCompressionService.test.ts`: 38/38 passed
- `packages/core/src/agents/memory-leak-regression.test.ts`: 18/18 passed
- `prettier --check` & `eslint --max-warnings 0` on modified files: passed

prs.title: fix(core): enforce origin consistency and display endpoint origin in MCP OAuth flow
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->
Enforces RFC 8414 Section 3.3 issuer matching and endpoint origin consistency across MCP OAuth metadata discovery and authentication, displays the target authorization origin (and token origin when configured across distinct domains) in the OAuth consent prompt, and sequences Dynamic Client Registration after user consent is granted to prevent unintended token routing and premature registration requests.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->

- **RFC 8414 Section 3.3 Issuer Verification (`oauth-utils.ts`)**:
  - Updated `OAuthUtils.discoverAuthorizationServerMetadata()` to verify that `metadata.issuer` is non-empty and matches the queried authorization server URL via `areIssuersEqual()`, continuing across non-OAuth responses while rejecting mismatched metadata documents.
  - Normalized trailing slashes on path-scoped issuer URLs without regex backtracking and separated path-scoped well-known discovery from MCP base-URL fallback in `OAuthUtils.discoverOAuthConfig()` so servers hosted at subpaths (such as `/mcp`) continue to support root authorization server metadata when Protected Resource Metadata is absent.
- **Endpoint Origin Consistency & URL Validation (`oauth-utils.ts`, `oauth-provider.ts`, `oauth-flow.ts`, `mcp-client.ts`)**:
  - Updated `OAuthUtils.metadataToOAuthConfig()` and `OAuthUtils.discoverAuthorizationServerMetadata()` to validate that
    dynamically discovered `authorization_endpoint`, `token_endpoint`, and optional `registration_endpoint` URLs share the canonical `issuer` origin, and rejected embedded URL userinfo components in `validateOAuthEndpointUrl()`.
  - Updated `MCPOAuthProvider.authenticate()`, `MCPOAuthProvider.registerClient()`,     `MCPOAuthProvider.discoverAuthServerMetadataForRegistration()`, `exchangeCodeForToken()`, `refreshAccessToken()`, and automatic OAuth discovery in `mcp-client.ts` to preserve and verify configured `issuer` values and enforce `expectedOrigin` across dynamically discovered and partially merged configurations, while continuing to support explicit manual multi-domain configurations (such as Google OAuth) where `authorizationUrl`, `tokenUrl`, and `clientId` are explicitly specified upfront and `authorizationUrl` matches any configured `issuer`.
- **Consent Origin Display & Post-Consent Registration Sequencing (`oauth-provider.ts`)**:
  - Updated the `getConsentForOauth()` prompt in `MCPOAuthProvider.authenticate()` to include the `authorization_endpoint` origin (and `token_endpoint` origin when explicitly configured on a distinct origin).
  - Reordered `MCPOAuthProvider.authenticate()` so `getConsentForOauth()` resolves before starting the local callback server or executing Dynamic Client Registration (`registerClient()`).
- **Test Coverage (`oauth-utils.test.ts`, `oauth-provider.test.ts`)**:
  - Added unit and integration tests covering RFC 8414 Section 3.3 `issuer` matching, non-OAuth 200 candidate continuation, subpath (`/mcp`) to root authorization server metadata fallback, endpoint origin consistency across discovery, partial configuration merges, and `discoverAuthServerMetadataForRegistration()`, explicit manual multi-domain     configurations (including `issuer` vs. `authorizationUrl` origin consistency), consent prompt origin formatting, and post-consent registration execution order.

## Related Issues

only related to an issue or is a partial fix, simply reference the issue number
without a keyword (Related to #123). -->


prs.title: fix(cli): cover all extension content in install and update consent
prs.body:
## Summary

Extension install and update consent now describes everything that an extension adds, not only its manifest fields, and updates compare that description between the installed folder and the new one. An update asks for confirmation again when its hooks, context files (and the files they import), skills, sub-agents, custom commands, policy files, MCP server entries, or the files that hook and MCP server commands reference through `${extensionPath}` change. It doesn't ask when they stay the same, including for extensions with skills. On updates, the prompt also lists what changed, and the interactive extension consent dialog now selects "No" first.

## Details

- **Content signatures (`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/contentSignature.ts`)**: Walks a file or folder inside the extension and hashes each regular file with SHA-256 (raw bytes, `/` paths, and UTF-16 code unit order, so the result doesn't depend on the platform, the locale, or where the folder is). Links that stay inside the extension folder are followed. Links that leave it, broken links, link loops, and special files get a marker and are never read. Display helpers escape control, zero-width, and bidirectional characters, and wrap each value in a Markdown code span.
- **Content summary (`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/extensionContentSummary.ts`)**: Builds the same summary for the installed folder and the new one from the raw files, without resolving variables and regardless of settings such as `hooksConfig.enabled`:
  - Hooks: each hook in `hooks/hooks.json` with its event, matcher, name, full command, and environment variables (sensitive values masked with the same rules as MCP servers), plus every file under `hooks/` and the paths referenced through `${extensionPath}`. A `hooks.json` that isn't valid is listed without failing.
  - Context files: the declared files or the default `GEMINI.md`, plus the files they import with `@`, resolved with `processImports` and limited to the extension folder. `processImports` is now exported from `@google/gemini-cli-core`.
  - Skills: `Source:` paths relative to the extension folder, and a signature over `skills/`.
  - Sub-agents, custom commands, and policy files, matching what their loaders read: `agents/*.md` (except names that start with `_`), `commands/**/*.toml` (hidden folders included), and `policies/*.toml`. Sub-agent MCP servers are listed with their values as written, including `Trust` when it's set.
  - MCP servers: read from the raw `gemini-extension.json`, resolving only `${/}` and `${pathSeparator}`, so the `Config signature` no longer depends on the folder path or the workspace. Each server that references files gets `Files used` and `Files signature` lines.
- **Consent text (`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/consent.ts`)**: Renders one section per kind of content, one entry per item, and one signature line per section. On updates, a "Changes since the installed version" block right above the question names the new, changed, and removed items; it isn't part of the compared text. Without a summary, the text is the same as before, so existing snapshots don't change, and `skillsConsentString` (used by `gemini skills install` and `gemini skills link`) doesn't change either.
- **Staged copy for local installs (`packages/cli/src/config/extension-manager.ts`)**: After the manifest is validated, a local source is copied to a temporary folder. The summary, the consent text, and the installed files all come from that copy, so the installed files are the ones that the prompt describes. The existing cleanup removes the copy. Linked extensions don't change.
- **Declined updates (`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/extensionConsentErrors.ts`, `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/update.ts`)**: Declining throws `ExtensionConsentDeclinedError` with the existing `Installation cancelled for "<name>".` message. `updateExtension` keeps the `ERROR` state, so auto-update doesn't ask again in the same session, but it no longer logs a rollback or copies files back, and it rethrows the error as is. `updateAllUpdatableExtensions` waits for every update with `Promise.allSettled` and logs each failure with the extension name. Non-interactive prompts run one at a time, so each one reads its own answer.
- **Dialog default (`packages/cli/src/ui/components/ConsentPrompt.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/ui/components/DialogManager.tsx`)**: `ConsentPrompt` accepts an optional `defaultToNo` prop. `DialogManager` passes it only for extension consent requests, so pressing Enter declines them. Other consent dialogs keep "Yes" first.
- **Inline code spans (`packages/cli/src/ui/utils/markdownParsingUtils.ts`)**: Inline code now matches on the length of its backtick fence and removes one space of padding from each side, as Markdown does. Values that contain backticks, `*`, `_`, or `$` render as written in the consent dialog.
- **Docs (`docs/extensions/reference.md`)**: Describes when updates ask for consent again, that declining keeps the installed version, and that `--consent` skips the prompt and its details.
- **Commits**: Each commit builds and passes its own tests, so the PR can be reviewed commit by commit.

Planned follow-ups, not part of this PR: a dedicated "declined" status in `/extensions list`, the `extensions update --all` summary when every update fails and exit codes for `extensions update`, restoring the previous files when an approved update fails partway, and `trust` handling for sub-agent MCP servers.

## Related Issues

N/A

## How to Validate

1. Run the new and updated tests:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extensions/contentSignature.test.ts src/config/extensions/extensionContentSummary.test.ts src/config/extensions/extensionUpdateConsent.test.ts src/config/extensions/consent.test.ts src/config/extensions/update.test.ts src/ui/components/ConsentPrompt.test.tsx src/ui/components/DialogManager.test.tsx src/ui/hooks/useExtensionUpdates.test.tsx src/ui/utils/markdownParsingUtils.test.ts
   ```

2. Run the extension suites and the core import processor tests:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extension src/commands/extensions
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/memoryImportProcessor
   ```

3. Optional manual check: create an extension with `gemini extensions new <path> hooks` and install it with `gemini extensions install <path>`. Expected results:
   - The prompt lists `SessionStart: node ${extensionPath}/scripts/on-start.js`, `Files used by hooks: scripts/on-start.js`, and a `Hooks signature` line.
   - An update that only changes the `version` doesn't ask for consent.
   - An update that changes the extension's content asks again and lists the changes under "Changes since the installed version". If you decline, the installed version stays as it is.
   - In the interactive CLI, the extension consent dialog starts on "No".

Edge cases covered by the tests: links that stay inside or leave the extension folder, broken links and link loops, binary and malformed files, a `hooks.json` that isn't valid, imports outside the extension folder, files skipped by the loaders (for example `agents/_notes.md`), a source folder that changes while the prompt is open, concurrent non-interactive prompts, and `update --all` with one declined and one successful update. Tests that need symbolic links are skipped on Windows, following the existing pattern.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any): The interactive extension consent dialog now starts on "No", so pressing Enter declines. Extension consent text now lists hook commands, context and imported files, skills, sub-agents, custom commands, policy files, and signatures, and updates ask again when any of them change. `gemini extensions update --all` finishes every update and logs each failure instead of stopping at the first one.
- [x] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
  - [x] Linux
    - [x] npm run

prs.title: fix(core): cap grep_search output size and tell the model to narrow broad searches
prs.body:
## Summary

A broad `grep_search` can still send the model far more text than it can use. The match cap limits how many lines come back, not how big they are: with the default 100 matches over long log or minified lines, the tool builds about 150K characters today. The executor's generic 64KB cap then cuts that mid-line and tells the model to read the full output from a file, which is the opposite of what you want after a search that's too broad. This PR bounds grep output by size inside the tool and tells the model to narrow the search instead.

## Details

- `formatGrepResults` stops adding lines once the output would pass `MAX_GREP_OUTPUT_CHARS` (40,000 characters). It always cuts on a whole line and closes the file block, so the result stays well formed.
- When it cuts, it adds a short notice saying how many matches (or files, for `names_only`) were shown out of how many, and suggests a more specific pattern, `include_pattern`, `dir_path`, or `names_only`.
- If context lines are what doesn't fit, it drops them first and keeps the matches. That matters for the 1 to 3 match auto-context case on files with long lines, where 50 context lines can push the match itself out.
- 40,000 is the default `tools.truncateToolOutputThreshold` and the distillation threshold (10,000 tokens x 4), and it's under `MAX_STORED_TOOL_OUTPUT_BYTES`, so for normal text the generic truncation no longer fires on grep.
- Results under the budget are byte-for-byte the same as before, and the existing grep and ripgrep tests pass unchanged. The `(limited)` summary also shows when output was cut for size.

This complements #29822, which caps `total_max_matches` and rewords the overflow message. They don't overlap: 5000 matches of 120-character lines is still about 640K characters, and this is what bounds that.

## Related Issues

Related to #17448

The core of that report (one search sending ~41M tokens) can't happen on main anymore. The default match cap (#17146), per-line truncation (#21147) and the 64KB tool output cap (#29451) bound it, and the pre-send check has blocked oversized requests since #10459. This PR covers the "agent should refine its search" part; the UI wording is in #29822, which should be the one that closes the issue.

## How to Validate

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/tools/grep-utils.test.ts src/tools/grep.test.ts src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts`
2. On main, the new tests fail. The two end-to-end ones report 151,330 and 152,905 characters for a default search over long lines.
3. Manual: in a folder with a few files of long lines that share a word, ask the agent to search for it. The result ends with "Output truncated: showing N of 100 matches..." and stays under 40,000 characters.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any): none, output under the budget is unchanged
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods (unit tests ran on macOS; no manual CLI run yet)

prs.title: fix(core): inspect shell wrapper variants for command substitution and policy checks
prs.body:
## Summary

Hardens shell wrapper inspection in `detectCommandSubstitution`, `stripShellWrapper`, and `PolicyEngine` so command substitutions and denied commands inside wrapped shell invocations are consistently detected and enforced across prefix utilities, shell flags, trailing tokens/operators/redirections, and Windows shell wrapper variants.

## Details

- **Structured wrapper payload extraction (`packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts`)**:
  - Added `extractWrappedShellCommands()` using tree-sitter-bash AST decomposition (including `redirected_statement` mid-command redirections) with a linear-time fallback segmenter when the WASM parser is unavailable or on Windows/PowerShell.
  - Added a POSIX/ANSI-C (`$'...'`) wrapper tokenizer with redirection stripping and declarative prefix-utility peeling (`env` including `-S`/`--split-string`, `nice`, `timeout`, `nohup`, `setsid`, `sudo`, `stdbuf`, `ionice`, `chrt`, `taskset`, `time`, `command`, `exec`, `builtin`, `watch`, `xargs`, etc.).
  - Extracts inner payloads from POSIX shells (`sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, `dash`, `ksh`, `ash`, `mksh`, `csh`, `tcsh`) with arbitrary flags before or after `-c`, `eval`, `cmd`/`cmd.exe` (`/c`, `/k`, `/r` and pre-switches), and `powershell`/`pwsh` (`-c`/`-co`..`-command`, `-e`/`-ec`/`-enc`..`-encodedcommand` UTF-16LE base64, and parameter prefixes).
- **Recursive substitution detection & safer wrapper stripping (`packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts`)**:
  - Updated `detectCommandSubstitution()` to recursively inspect all extracted wrapper payloads up to `MAX_SHELL_WRAPPER_DEPTH = 5` and `MAX_WRAPPER_DETECTION_STATES = 64` (failing closed when exceeded).
  - Hardened `stripSingleShellWrapper()`, `unwrapCmdCommandArg()`, and `unwrapPowerShellCommandArg()` so single/double-quoted wrapper arguments with trailing operators, arguments, comments, redirections, post-`-c` flags, ANSI-C quoting, or hidden substitutions are preserved rather than partially stripped, while maintaining existing sandbox-manager stripping behavior for benign argv-joined commands and PowerShell `\"` unescaping.
- **Recursive policy enforcement (`packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts`)**:
  - Updated `PolicyEngine.checkShellCommand()` to recursively validate extracted wrapper payloads (per subcommand and on the full command for wrappers split across AST redirections) with bounded recursion depth (`wrapperDepth`), preserving `DENY` enforcement and `ALLOW -> ASK_USER` downgrades without upgrading unapproved outer wrappers or regressing known-safe wrapped commands such as `bash -lc "ls -la"`.
- **Tests (`packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/policy/shell-substitution.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/tools/shell.test.ts`)**:
  - Added regression tests covering prefix utilities, shell flags, ANSI-C quoting, trailing arguments/operators/redirections, Windows PowerShell/`cmd.exe` switches (including `-enc`), recursion caps, benign wrapped command preservation, policy enforcement (interactive & non-interactive), and `ShellToolInvocation.execute()` defense-in-depth blocking.

## Related Issues

N/A

1. Run unit, policy, and sandbox test suites:
   ```bash
   cd packages/core
   npx vitest run \
     src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts \

     src/policy/shell-substitution.test.ts \
     src/policy/shell-safety.test.ts \
     src/policy/shell-safety-regression.test.ts \
     src/policy/shell-argument-expansion.test.ts \
     src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts \
     src/policy/policy-updater.test.ts \
     src/services/sandboxManager.integration.test.ts
   ```
2. Run full `@google/gemini-cli-core` test suite, typecheck, and lint:
   ```bash
   npm run typecheck
   cd packages/core && npx vitest run
   ```
3. Verify wrapper handling in bundled CLI with a prefix-allow policy for wrapper commands:
   - Wrapped commands containing command substitution (e.g., `env sh -c 'echo $(id)'`, `sh -e -c 'echo $(id)'`, `sh -c 'echo $(id)' ''`) prompt (`ASK_USER`) in interactive mode and are denied (`policy_violation`) in non-interactive `--approval-mode default`.

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve Markdown code fence boundaries
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix three terminal rendering problems around fenced code blocks. A fence can open with a tag such as `c++` or an info string with attributes. A fence line followed by a tag stays visible inside a code block, and a table renders before a code block that follows it. A heading, list item or horizontal rule that follows a table without a blank line is rendered as that block instead of plain text, as the automated review pointed out.

## Details

Opening and closing fences use separate rules. The opener uses the first word of its info string for highlighting. A closing fence needs the same marker, at least as many characters as the opener, and only spaces or tabs after it. The first non-table line now closes the table before block detection, so code fences, headings, list items, and horizontal rules use their normal renderers. The blank line that ends a table is still consumed without adding a spacer.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30465.

## How to Validate

```sh
npm run test --ignore-scripts --workspace @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/utils/MarkdownDisplay.test.tsx --coverage.enabled=false
```

All 50 renderer tests passed on Linux x86-64. Tested opening fences include `c++`, `cpp`, `c#`, `objective-c`, `{r}`, `javascript title="a.js"`, and `javascript {title="demo.js"}`. Both code lines rendered under each tag, including the deliberately unregistered `gemini-test-unregistered-language` tag. Prettier and ESLint passed on the changed files.

The full CLI run was made with the first commit of this PR and passed 7,884 tests and skipped four. It preceded the additional info-string tests above and the table change in the second commit. Ten tests in `src/gemini.test.tsx` failed on workspace trust, with the same ten failures on the unmodified base. The devtools suite could not load on that run and passed all 17 tests after its workspace was built.
