issues.title: Opt-in package namespace (pi.namespace) for skills and prompt templates

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

An opt-in `pi.namespace` field in a package's `package.json`. Every name-keyed resource the package loads through package resolution — skills and prompt templates — resolves through one unified surface: both load under the composed name `<namespace>:<name>`, with `/myorg:<name>` resolving the package's template first and its skill when no template owns the name. `/skill:myorg:foo` remains available as the explicit form for skills when disambiguation is needed. The prefix composes at load time; resource content — SKILL.md frontmatter, template filenames — stays untouched.

### Why?

Package resources are named by independent authors with no coordination, and pi loads them into flat name-keyed maps right next to user and project resources. As the package ecosystem grows, same-name collisions are a when-not-if outcome. Today's precedence (first-found-wins, user/project first) means the package loses its invocation name behind a collision warning — the precedence is right, but the package has no way to vacate the bare name while staying callable without mutating the resource.

The current escapes mutate the resource itself: prefixing the SKILL.md name, or colon template filenames. Both fork the artifact from its source of truth — the escape does not survive syncing from upstream, so the bare name stays claimed on one side or the other.

A provider-declared prefix is the standard content-neutral answer to independently-chosen identifiers colliding — npm scopes, DNS, every package manager — and it needs core support because the collision maps and exposed-name composition live in the core loaders — the skills collision map inside `loadSkills`, the template dedupe in resource-loader; extensions receive already-loaded resources and cannot rename them.

### How? (optional)

Implemented on a fork ([maskshell/pi](https://github.com/maskshell/pi), branch `package-namespace`, single commit): manifest field → PathMetadata → validated path→namespace associations in resource-loader → rename-at-load before collision dedupe → unified `/myorg:<name>` invocation (template first, then exact skill match) with `/skill:myorg:foo` as the explicit form; user/project resources always keep the bare name. 31 new tests (the four touched suites pass 315); `npm run check` clean. Happy to open the PR once approved.

---

### Status: maintained as a release-tracked fork patch (2026-10)

This proposal is now shipped and maintained outside upstream: [maskshell/pi](https://github.com/maskshell/pi) carries it as a release-managed patch on the [`namespace-patch` branch](https://github.com/maskshell/pi/tree/namespace-patch/patch) — every upstream release is re-based mechanically, repaired when needed, re-verified (full check chain + touched suites), and published as the npm alias [`pi-namespace-patch`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/pi-namespace-patch) via trusted publishing with signed provenance. Same pi, one feature ahead; pin exact `X.Y.Z-namespace.N` versions.

It is exercised in production by the [solidforge](https://github.com/maskshell/solidforge-pi) toolchain (`/solidforge:*` skills). Release-tracking notes continue in the comments below, one per tracked upstream release.

issues.title: Pi Durable support for client-side tool execution and tool approval
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Submitting this as a contribution proposal because there's no feature option and this isn't a bug. I initially submitted a [discussion](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/discussions/10632) but not sure if that's the right area.

Some tools require human approval before they run, or require client-side information before they run. Here's an example for each scenario.

Destructive tool that requires human approval:
1. The model calls a tool
2. The run stops before the tool executes. The pending call is persisted, and nothing is held in memory
3. The user approves, denies it, maybe hours or days later 
4. The run continues from that same tool call and the tool executes (or a denial result is written), and the agent loop continues.

For requiring client-side information for a tool result (a good example of this is WebMCP, or a `askUserQuestion` style tool):
1. The model calls a tool
2. The run stops before the tool executes (because it has no execute function in its definition). The pending call is persisted, and nothing is held in memory
3. The client receives the tool call, executes what's necessary, and sends back the tool output result
4. The run continues from that same tool call: the agent loop receives the tool result, and the agent loop continues.

It seems like something like this doesn't exist for Pi durable. There's some similar examples but they seem to wait in memory or return a terminated tool result.

Questions:
- Is there an existing solution I missed?
- Is support for something like this planned or in consideration?

If you only plan on supporting one of these, I would kindly ask for it to be the second: client-side tool execution (it doesn't have to be client side, but basically "paused" or "deferred" tool execution). I think this pattern can support the human-approval feature if need-be, it just might be a bit awkward in its implementation depending on the design.

Related:
- https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5901 but that was for pi, not pi durable
- This could also tie-in with support of the MCP spec with tools that return with an [input required] request(https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#input-required-tool-results), 
- Examples of how this is designed elsewhere:
  - Vercel's AI sdk has approval states for tool execution: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/agents/tool-approvals. And for client-side tool output, if you don't define an `execute` for a tool, when that tool is called it stops the agent run, and the client can start the run again by providing the tool result (see `getLocation` tool here https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/chatbot-tool-usage)
  - Cloudflare think similarly has a [tool approval](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/harnesses/think/tools/#tool-approval), as well as [client side tools](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/harnesses/think/client-tools/) 

### Why?

The UX for many agent interfaces need humans to approve certain actions. There's also many situations where a tool's execution is done on the client.

### How? (optional)

issues.title: Anthropic /login fails on Claude Team/Enterprise seats: "Unknown scope"
issues.body:
# Anthropic `/login` fails on Claude Team/Enterprise seats: "Unknown scope"

## Summary

`/login` → Anthropic (Claude Pro/Max) fails for accounts on a Claude **Team**
seat. The authorization request is rejected before any consent screen:

```
Invalid OAuth request
Unknown scope: user:i…
```

The rejected scope is `user:inference` — the only `user:i*` scope pi requests.
That scope is **not** the real problem: requesting it from a different
authorization endpoint, alongside a narrower scope set, succeeds and returns a
working subscription token.

## Affected versions

Reproduced on **1.5.0**. The relevant constants in
`dist/bundle/chunks/anthropic.js` are byte-identical in **1.5.2**, so latest is
affected too:

```js
AUTHORIZE_URL = "https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize"
TOKEN_URL     = "https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token"
SCOPES        = "org:create_api_key user:profile user:inference " +
                "user:sessions:claude_code user:mcp_servers user:file_upload"
```

## Diagnosis

The request is rejected as a whole, not scope-by-scope. Against
`claude.ai/oauth/authorize`, the three claude.ai-oriented scopes —
`user:sessions:claude_code`, `user:mcp_servers`, `user:file_upload` — appear not
to be grantable to a Team seat, and the endpoint reports the failure against an
earlier scope in the list.

Running the **same PKCE flow with the same `client_id`** against the console
endpoint with only the three classic scopes is accepted:

```
authorize    https://console.anthropic.com/oauth/authorize
token        https://console.anthropic.com/v1/oauth/token
redirect_uri https://console.anthropic.com/oauth/code/callback
scope        org:create_api_key user:profile user:inference
```

The token response grants:

```
scope: user:inference user:profile
```

Note that `org:create_api_key` is **silently dropped** (a Team seat cannot mint
org API keys) rather than failing the request — so the authorization server is
willing to narrow a scope set it partially supports, but not this one.

The resulting credential works end to end in pi: stored as
`{"type":"oauth", access, refresh, expires}` in `auth.json`,
`pi auth check --provider anthropic` reports `ready`, and inference succeeds.

**The two token backends interoperate.** A refresh token issued by
`console.anthropic.com` refreshes successfully against pi's configured
`platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token` (verified by forcing `expires: 0` and
letting pi refresh). So this is an authorize-side scope problem only; the token
and refresh paths need no change.

## Reproduction

1. Use an account whose only Claude access is a **Team** seat.
2. `pi` → `/login` → Anthropic (Claude Pro/Max) → either login method.
3. The browser shows `Invalid OAuth request / Unknown scope: user:i…`, no consent screen.
4. Repeat the same PKCE flow against `console.anthropic.com/oauth/authorize`
   with `scope=org:create_api_key user:profile user:inference` → consent screen
   appears, code exchanges, token works.

## Suggested fix

Fall back to the narrower scope set when the full request is rejected, or offer
the console endpoint as a second login method. Minimal version: on an
`Unknown scope` / invalid-request response from `claude.ai/oauth/authorize`,
retry with `org:create_api_key user:profile user:inference` against
`console.anthropic.com/oauth/authorize` (+ its matching
`redirect_uri`/`TOKEN_URL`).

The extra three scopes gate claude.ai-side features (Claude Code sessions, MCP
servers, file upload). A seat that cannot grant them can still do inference, so
failing the whole login costs those users the provider entirely.

## Possible second issue (unconfirmed)

`console.anthropic.com` sits behind Cloudflare and returned
**HTTP 403, error 1010 "browser_signature_banned"** to a Python `urllib` client
using its default `User-Agent`; adding an ordinary `User-Agent` fixed it. If pi
adopts the console endpoint, its HTTP client may need an explicit `User-Agent`
on that host. Go's default client was not blocked.

### Expected behavior

Represent the project exclusion once if that is compatible with inherited-resource matching. If both entries are required, document why the plain path accompanies the exclusion.

issues.title: npm 12: no way to declare allowScripts for git-installed packages (follow-up to #6600)
issues.body:
## Context

Follow-up to #6600 (npm 11.16 warns / npm 12 errors on blocked install scripts). That issue covered **npm sources**, where the practical workaround is manually editing `~/.pi/agent/npm/package.json` to add an `allowScripts` field. **Git sources** have the same problem but no comfortable escape hatch.

## What happens

Pi clones git packages into `~/.pi/agent/git/<host>/<owner>/<repo>` and installs their dependencies in that clone (a `node_modules/` and `package-lock.json` appear there). With npm 12, any dependency with install scripts — e.g. `@ffmpeg-installer/ffmpeg` (postinstall `chmod u+x ffmpeg`), `mupdf`, `protobufjs` — is blocked unless the *clone's* `package.json` carries an `allowScripts` field:

```
npm warn install-scripts 3 packages had install scripts blocked because they are not covered by allowScripts:
npm warn install-scripts   @ffmpeg-installer/darwin-arm64@4.1.5 (postinstall: chmod u+x ffmpeg)
```

## The problem

Pi reconciles git clones (fetch + reset to the remote ref), so a local edit of the clone's `package.json` is wiped on the next reconcile. The only durable place for the approvals is the **upstream repo's own `package.json`**. That is awkward for consumers of third-party git packages (you must fork/patch the source repo to allow a script you trust) and is an undocumented requirement on package authors.

## Ask

Surface `allowScripts` in settings, per package entry, applied by Pi when it installs dependencies for git (and npm) sources — e.g. merged into the managed `package.json` before/after the install, or passed through npm config. Something like:

```json
{
  "packages": [
    {
      "source": "git:github.com/example/pkg",
      "allowScripts": ["@ffmpeg-installer/darwin-arm64", "protobufjs"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Alternatively, if the repo-level `allowScripts` field in the source package is the intended mechanism for git packages, that should be documented (packages.md currently only mentions that bun runs install scripts "only for packages it trusts").

## Environment

- Pi (Pi-Bolt, compiled Bun build), macOS darwin-arm64
- npm 12.0.2
- Affected example: a git package depending on `@ffmpeg-installer/ffmpeg`, `@s8fy/pptx-converter`, `mupdf`

prs.title: feat(tui,coding-agent): report session resume command via OSC 7577
prs.body:
Implements the program side of the [Program Resume Protocol (OSC 7577)](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-resume): terminals that set `OSC7577_TOKEN` can bring pi back after they restart.

## Problem

A terminal restart (update, crash, reboot) ends pi. The user has to find and run the resume command themselves. OSC 7577 lets the program tell the terminal the command, authenticated with a SHA-256 `mac` over the report and a per-pane token, so text that only passes through the terminal (`cat`, logs, `ssh`) cannot register commands.

## Changes

- **pi-tui** `program-resume.ts`: `formatProgramResume()`, `formatProgramResumeClear()`, `takeProgramResumeToken()`. Commands the spec cannot carry (control characters, relative program or cwd, over the 64-argument / 2048-byte limits) return `undefined`; the caller sends `clear` instead so an older command is not resumed in its place. Tests use the spec's example reports and `mac` values.
- **coding-agent** `ProgramResumeReporter` (sibling of `ProgramStatusReporter`): reports the command pi already prints on exit, `pi [--session-dir D] --session <id>`, with the session cwd. `formatResumeCommand` now builds on a shared `getResumeArgs()`.

| Moment | Action |
|---|---|
| Startup, `/resume`, `/fork` | report |
| First message of a new session written | report |
| `/new` without messages | clear (no file to resume) |
| `fg` after Ctrl+Z | report again (a program may have replaced it while suspended) |
| Ctrl+D, Ctrl+C twice, `/quit` | clear |
| SIGHUP / SIGTERM | keep (the terminal needs it then) |

- **main()** takes the token out of `process.env` first, in every mode, so `!` shells, `$EDITOR`, extension processes and tool commands cannot replace pi's command or register their own.

## Testing

- `npm run check`
- `packages/tui/test/program-resume.test.ts`, `packages/coding-agent/test/program-resume-reporter.test.ts`, `format-resume-command.test.ts`
- Manual in tmux with `PI_TUI_WRITE_LOG`: mac verified with `sha256sum`, `!env | grep OSC7577` finds nothing, `fg` re-reports, Ctrl+D and `/new` clear, killing the tmux session sends no clear.

## Known limitations

- The command uses the bare name `pi` (the spec's preference, survives updates); a source checkout resumes the installed `pi`.
- `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` set for one run only is not carried; the spec forbids sending environment variables and pi has no flag for it.

prs.title: feat(durable)!: delete conversations for good
prs.body:
Refs #11026. This was also escalated to us directly, outside the issue.

Adds `Harness.deleteConversations(ids, context)`: it aborts a conversation's work, background work included, then removes the conversation for good, together with the conversations its tasks own (subagents).

## What it does

1. Tries the deleting commit first. That commit refuses, before anything is aborted or deleted:
   - the root conversation, because `root()` would recreate it with the reserved ID 1;
   - a conversation whose owner task, outside the deleted set, is still live;
   - a conversation with a fork outside the deleted set, because the fork's history reads the parent's entries. Pass the forks in the same call.
2. If a task in the set is still live, the commit rejects with `ConversationBusy`. The method then runs `abort({ background: true })` on each given conversation and tries again, up to 3 attempts.
3. The deleting commit:
   - settles queued and placed submissions `unanswered` with reason `deleted`, so `wait()` and `notify` resolve;
   - retires every current document, so watches and the document cache follow through the existing retirement path;
   - appends one new `StorageWrite`, `{ type: "conversation.delete", id }`, per conversation, after the other writes.
4. When the commit is published, the Session drops the conversation from its record cache, the newest-entry index and the kept context, and ends conversation views with `ended`.

There is no separate tombstone. Once the conversation record is gone, every write path already fails with "Conversation X does not exist". Unknown IDs are skipped, so calling it again after a crash or after restoring a backup is harmless. IDs stay claimed and are never reused.

## Backends

| Backend | Result |
|---|---|
| Memory, IndexedDB | Records removed |
| SQLite, Durable Object SQLite | Rows removed with a few `DELETE`s on existing indexes, no schema change. The host still has to run `secure_delete`/`VACUUM` and a WAL `TRUNCATE` checkpoint for a forensic erase. |
| JSONL | **Not covered.** Only a marker: reads no longer find the conversation, but `main.jsonl` and the sidecars keep its records. Erasing them needs a rewrite of `main.jsonl`, which the backend does not have (spec §13 lists JSONL compaction as a non-goal). |
| Chord store (`StoreStorage`) | **Not covered.** The write is refused, which fails the Session. Chord has no write that removes a rewindable document's revisions, and the outbox keeps every commit's writes until trimmed. |

Both gaps need a design decision, so let's discuss them separately before extending this.

## Also

- `StorageWrite` and `TableCommitChange` gain the new write (breaking for custom Storage implementations and for replicas that consume `observeCommits()`). The conformance suite has a case for it; the `StoreStorage` suite skips that case.
- Spec: invariant 5, §2.2, §10, §11.x (new §11.4), §12 footguns. Also README and CHANGELOG.
- Tests: the conformance case (memory, SQLite, JSONL, IndexedDB, and Durable Object SQLite in workerd) and `test/harness-delete-conversations.test.ts` (memory and SQLite).

prs.title: fix(ai): replay GitHub Copilot reasoning_opaque in openai-completions
prs.body:
Fixes #12418.

Problem: on `openai-completions`, Copilot streams `reasoning_text` deltas followed by a single `reasoning_opaque` delta (observed live with `claude-opus-5.5` on `/chat/completions`). Pi kept the text but dropped the opaque value, so later requests replayed `reasoning_text` without it.

Fix, following the existing `reasoning_details` handling:

- While streaming, keep the latest `reasoning_opaque` in memory and, when the thinking block ends, store it with the reasoning field in `thinkingSignature`: `{"field":"reasoning_text","reasoning_opaque":"..."}`.
- On replay, send `reasoning_opaque` next to the reasoning text in its original field. When it arrived without text, send it alone, without `reasoning_text`.
- With interleaved reasoning, the text is concatenated and the latest opaque value is replayed (as the Copilot VS Code client does).
- Thinking from another model is already dropped by `transformMessages`, so the opaque value is never sent to a different model.

Tests: `packages/ai/test/openai-completions-reasoning-opaque.test.ts` (text + opaque, interleaved, opaque without text, other model). Verified live with a two-turn tool call against Copilot `/chat/completions` (`claude-opus-5.5`): the replay carried `reasoning_text` and `reasoning_opaque` and the request succeeded. Gemini was not available on the test account, so the reported missing-`finish_reason` failure was not reproduced directly.

prs.title: fix(ai): stop sending earlier reasoning to Bedrock Kimi K3 models
prs.body:
## Problem

The AWS model cards for [Kimi K3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-moonshot-ai-kimi-k3.html) and [Kimi K3.1](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-moonshot-ai-kimi-k3-1-highspeed.html) list a known Converse limitation: requests fail with `InternalServerException` when reasoning content from earlier turns is included. AWS says to remove reasoning blocks from prior turns.

Pi sends them back. `transformMessages()` keeps thinking from the same model, and `convertMessages()` sends it as `reasoningContent.reasoningText` for non-Claude models. A normal tool loop hits this on the second request:

1. user -> assistant `[thinking, toolCall]`
2. request 2 sends `user, assistant[reasoningContent, toolUse], user[toolResult]` -> `InternalServerException` per AWS

## Fix

- New Bedrock compat flag `compat.supportsReasoningReplay` (default `true`). When `false`, `convertMessages()` skips thinking blocks of earlier assistant messages, including redacted ones.
- The catalog sets it to `false` for the `moonshotai.kimi-k3` family (K3 and K3.1, all six profiles; `npm run diff:model-catalog -- amazon-bedrock`). A flag in the catalog rather than a model-name check in the request code follows `compat.supportsStrictMode`, and lets `models.json` set it for application inference profiles whose ID and name do not say Kimi.
- `docs/models-configuration.md` regenerated from the schema.

Released clients ignore the unknown flag and keep today's behavior, so the catalog minimum version does not change.

Trade-off: Kimi loses its earlier reasoning between turns on Bedrock Converse. AWS documents no other way to make multi-turn Converse requests work for these models.

Not verified against a live Bedrock account; the change follows the AWS documentation. Tests in `test/bedrock-convert-messages.test.ts` check that reasoning is still sent back by default and dropped for the catalog's Kimi K3 and K3.1 models.

prs.title: feat(ai): keep the prompt cache across effort and tool changes on GitHub Copilot
prs.body:
Closes #12316

## Problem

On GitHub Copilot, pi resent or rebuilt the request in ways that drop the prompt cache, although Copilot supports the cache-preserving forms that direct Anthropic and OpenAI models already use:

- Claude: changing the thinking level or the tool set rewrote top-level `output_config` / `tools`. A catalog comment said Copilot rejects `tool_addition`/`tool_removal` blocks; that is no longer true.
- GPT-6: changing the thinking level changed `reasoning.effort`, which drops the whole cache on Copilot.
- Claude models had no `promptCache` lifetimes, so cache warming never ran for them.

`supportsStrictTools` from the issue already shipped in v1.6.0 (#12332).

## Change

`packages/ai/catalog/providers/github-copilot.ts`, following the direct `anthropic`, `openai`, and `openai-codex` providers:

- Claude: `supportsMidConvoEffort` where `supportsClaudeMidConvoEffort` matches (Opus 5/5.5, Sonnet/Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.1/5.2), `supportsMidConvoToolChanges` where mid-conversation system messages are already enabled, and `promptCache: { short: 300, long: 3600 }` on every Claude model.
- GPT-6 family (`OPENAI_MID_CONVO_EFFORT_MODEL_IDS`): `supportsMidConvoEffort` (`configuration_update` items).

With `promptCache`, the default `idle` cache warming now applies to Copilot Claude models. Copilot bills per token since June 2026, so the warming cost estimate applies.

## Verification

Live against the Copilot account, through pi-ai with a ~20K-token stable prefix:

| Check | Models | Without | With |
|---|---|---|---|
| Effort high -> low (Claude, per-message `output_config`) | opus-5.5, sonnet-5.5, haiku-5.5 | accepted | accepted, cache read |
| Remove `alpha`, add `beta` mid-conversation | opus-5.5, sonnet-5.5, haiku-5.5 | cache read 0 | cache read 19,853, model calls `beta` |
| Effort high -> low (`configuration_update`) | gpt-6-sol, -luna, -astra, 6.1-sol, 6.1-terra, 6.2-astra, 6.2-sol | cache read 0 | cache read ~24K |
| `configuration_update` effect, gpt-6-luna, same math prompt | | | low: ~950 output tokens, xhigh: ~17K |
| Default cache lifetime | opus-5.5, sonnet-5.5, sonnet-5, haiku-4.5 | | hit after 270 s, miss after 330 s |
| `ttl: "1h"` lifetime | opus-5.5 | | hit after 420 s |
| Warming replay (same request, 1 output token) | opus-5.5 | | cache read, 1 output token |

Claude Fable and Opus 4.8 are not available to the test account and follow the same shared family rules.

`test/providers.test.ts` covers the new flags and the changed tool-change expectation. `npm run check` passes; `./test.sh` failures are limited to clipboard, harness memory, and subagent tests in packages this change does not touch.



## Follow-up commit

- Renamed `supportsClaudeMidConvoSystemMessages` to `supportsClaudeMidConvoChanges`: it gates both mid-conversation system messages and tool changes (anthropic, github-copilot, opencode callers).
- Enabled `supportsMidConvoSystemMessages` for `gpt-5.3-codex`, `mai-code-1.1-flash`, `mai-code-2`, and `mai-code-2-flash` on Copilot. Live: an instruction sent as a mid-conversation developer message was followed in 11 of 12 runs (mai-code-2 missed once) with the prompt cache kept; folded into the leading prompt it was ignored by the flash models and gpt-5.3-codex, and gpt-5.3-codex lost the cache.

Also checked and left off on Copilot: message threads (rejected with 400 "thread: Extra inputs are not permitted"), `supportsExplicitPromptCacheMode` (`ttl: "30m"` rejected, which would break long retention), and mid-conversation system messages on Grok 4.6/4.7 (accepted but ignored).

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): honor DO_NOT_TRACK for install telemetry and attribution
prs.body:
Draft for discussion. Context: a public telemetry audit of 25 agent harnesses (https://x.com/ZryMiller/status/2125497546772812061) rated pi C. It found no third-party SDKs or IDs, but pi does not honor `DO_NOT_TRACK`.

## Problem

`DO_NOT_TRACK=1` (https://consoledonottrack.com) is a cross-tool opt-out. Today pi ignores it. A user with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` in their shell profile still sends:

- the `pi.dev/api/report-install?version=...` ping after an install or update
- provider attribution headers (`HTTP-Referer: https://pi.dev`, `X-OpenRouter-Title: pi`, ...)

## Change

`isInstallTelemetryEnabled()` now resolves in this order:

1. `PI_TELEMETRY` set: use it. It names pi explicitly, so it wins.
2. `DO_NOT_TRACK` is `1`/`true`/`yes`: off.
3. Otherwise the `enableInstallTelemetry` setting (default `true`).

Both call sites (install ping, `getClientIdentity` attribution) go through this function, so both honor it.

## Not in this PR (open questions)

- Should `DO_NOT_TRACK` beat `PI_TELEMETRY=1`? Currently no.
- Should `DO_NOT_TRACK` also skip the `pi.dev/api/latest-version` check (same as `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK`)? That request carries the pi version in `User-Agent`, but it is an update check, not telemetry. The convention does not cover update checks.
- Should `DO_NOT_TRACK` also force `enableAnalytics` off? Nothing reads that setting yet beyond first-run setup.
- `/settings` still shows "Install telemetry: true" when an env var overrides it. Could show it as locked/overridden.
- `DO_NOT_TRACK` should not imply `PI_OFFLINE`: that would also stop model catalog and package update checks, which are not tracking.

prs.body:
Fixes #12462.

## Problem

Bedrock's Kimi K3.1 profiles (`global.`, `us.`, `in.moonshotai.kimi-k3.1`) had no `thinkingLevelMap`, so pi offered the generic `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high` and clamped `--thinking max` to `high`. `buildAdditionalModelRequestFields()` in the Converse API only handled Claude, GPT and gpt-oss, so no effort reached Kimi at all. With no `reasoning_effort` the model reasons at `max`, whatever level is selected, including `off`. GLM 5.3 (`global.`, `us.zai.glm-5.3`) has the same bug.

models.dev already lists the right effort values for these models, matching the AWS model cards ([Kimi K3.1](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-moonshot-ai-kimi-k3-1-highspeed.html), [GLM 5.3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-zai-glm-5-3.html)). The shared catalog rule (`applyModelsDevEffort`) skips `bedrock-converse-stream` because the Converse request field differs by family:

| Family | Converse field |
|---|---|
| Claude | `thinking` + `output_config.effort` |
| GPT-5.x / GPT-6 | `reasoning.effort` |
| gpt-oss, Kimi K3, GLM 5.3 | flat `reasoning_effort` |
| Nova 2 | `reasoningConfig` |
| Grok, Gemma | none documented for Converse |

## Fix

- `src/api/bedrock-converse-stream.ts`: Bedrock models outside the Claude and GPT families send `additionalModelRequestFields.reasoning_effort` whenever their `thinkingLevelMap` maps the selected level to a string, including `off`. The request code has no model-name check for this. AWS notes that Converse forwards `reasoning_effort` without validating it, so nothing is sent without a mapped value.
- `catalog/providers/amazon-bedrock.ts`: the families whose AWS model cards document flat `reasoning_effort` on Converse (`moonshotai.kimi-k3`, `zai.glm-5.3`) take their `thinkingLevelMap` from models.dev via `getEffortThinkingLevelMap()`, as the zai, mistral and kimi-coding providers do. Nova, Grok and Gemma are left out: they use another field or none on Converse.

Catalog result (`npm run diff:model-catalog -- amazon-bedrock`): the three Kimi K3.1 profiles offer `off` (`none`), `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. The two GLM 5.3 profiles offer `low` through `max`; `off` is hidden because GLM 5.3 rejects `none`. Kimi K3 (non-.1) has no effort list in models.dev yet and is unchanged.

Released clients that get the new catalog but have the old request code show the new levels but still send nothing. They behave as before: the model reasons at `max`.

Tests: `test/bedrock-thinking-payload.test.ts` covers the offered levels, each effort value for Kimi K3.1 and GLM 5.3, `off` -> `none` for Kimi, no field for GLM `off`, and no field without a map.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): shut down gracefully on Ctrl+Break on Windows
prs.body:
## Problem

On Windows, interactive pi listens for SIGTERM and SIGHUP but not SIGBREAK. Without a listener, a console Ctrl+Break ends the process at once: no `exit` handler, no crash log, no Windows crash record. The terminal stays in the alternate screen with mouse reporting and keyboard modes on, and the shell prompt fills with mouse reports. This matches the 1.6.0 report in #12133 (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12133#issuecomment-7153937569). That report has no direct evidence of Ctrl+Break, but the process died without running any cleanup, which #12336 cannot cover.

Raw mode does not block Ctrl+Break the way it blocks Ctrl+C. Besides the key itself, any child process in the same console can send it, for example bash tool commands or subagent workers. A process that calls `GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_BREAK_EVENT, pid)` on a `pid` that is not a process group leader sends the event to every process in the console. A tool that stops its own child this way, as Python's `os.kill(pid, CTRL_BREAK_EVENT)` does, also kills pi.

Trace (raw-mode Node in its own console, a child in the same console sends the event):

| Child sends | Result |
|---|---|
| `CTRL_C_EVENT` to group 0 | survives |
| `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` to group 0 | exit `0xC000013A`, exit handler does not run |
| `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` to a pid that is not a group leader | same |
| same, with a `SIGBREAK` listener | survives, exit handler runs |

## Fix

On Windows, add `SIGBREAK` to the signals that start the graceful signal shutdown (same path as SIGTERM: extension cleanup, terminal restore, stdout flush, exit 0).

## Tests

- `test/suite/regressions/12133-sigbreak-shutdown.test.ts`: on Windows, SIGBREAK starts a signal shutdown; the listener is removed on unregister; no listener is added on other platforms.
- End to end: real pi in its own console; a child process sends Ctrl+Break into that console. Released 1.6.x exits with `0xC000013A`, this branch exits with `0x0` through the normal shutdown path.

Still not covered: forced kills and V8 running out of memory run no JavaScript, so no in-process handler can restore the terminal.

fixes #12133

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): report models.json errors in every mode
prs.body:
Closes #12522.

**Problem.** `modelRuntime.getError()` is read by interactive mode and by `listModels`, but not by the runtime diagnostics that print, JSON and RPC modes write to stderr. With a typo in `models.json` (`"contextWindow": "32000"`), the whole file is ignored and:

- `pi -p --model local/qwen-local hi` prints only `Model "local/qwen-local" not found`;
- `pi -p hi` prints `No API key found for the selected model.`;
- `--mode json` and `--mode rpc` print neither the error nor the file.

**Fix.** `createRuntime` in `main.ts` adds the error to the runtime diagnostics as a warning, next to `collectSettingsDiagnostics`. That is how invalid settings files are reported, and the same channel #11973 (model scope warnings) and #12234 (model fallback) moved to. Every mode now reports it once: interactive through `showRuntimeDiagnostics`, the others through `writeDiagnosticsToStderr`, and session replacements do not repeat it (`takeUnreportedDiagnostics`).

It is a warning, not an error: pi keeps running without the file's models, as with an invalid settings file, and an error diagnostic makes startup exit with code 1. `--list-models` already printed it as a warning.

Two separate copies are removed so the message is not shown twice: the startup `showError` in interactive mode and the print in `listModels`, which `main.ts` calls right after writing the startup diagnostics. The message keeps the interactive wording, `models.json error: ...`. The `/reload` and `/model` selector reports are unchanged.

**Validation** on main `9553d58343`:

- New `test/models-json-error-diagnostic.test.ts`, modeled on `model-fallback-diagnostic.test.ts`: runs the CLI with an invalid `models.json` and checks the warning is written to stderr exactly once in print mode, RPC mode and `--list-models`. All three fail without the fix.
- Manual, empty agent dir, no extensions:
  - before: `-p`, `--mode json` and `--mode rpc` show only "Model not found" / "No API key found"; after: each also shows `Warning: models.json error: Invalid models.json schema: - providers.local.models.0.contextWindow: must be number`.
  - interactive startup in tmux shows the warning once.
- `npm run check` passes. In `./test.sh` the only failures are unrelated to this change: the find tool tests (fd is not installed here and the test config prevents downloading it) and the pi-env tests (they need cargo, which is not installed here).

prs.title: fix(coding-agent,tui): name the configured keys in key hints
prs.body:
Follow-up to #12518. That PR fixed the `!` command hint, which named `tui.select.cancel` although the command is cancelled through `app.interrupt`. This PR fixes the remaining hints that name the wrong keybinding or hardcode a key.

**Hints that name the wrong keybinding.** These are correct with default bindings only because both bindings default to the same key. After a remap they name a key that does nothing.

- Extension editor (`ctx.ui.editor`): the hint named `tui.select.confirm` to submit, but the inner `Editor` submits on `tui.input.submit`.
- Session rename in `/resume`: same problem. The `Input` submits on `tui.input.submit`.
- `/hotkeys` said `app.interrupt` cancels autocomplete. Autocomplete is cancelled by `tui.select.cancel`; `CustomEditor` passes the key through to the editor when autocomplete is open. Example: with `app.interrupt` remapped to `ctrl+g`, pressing `ctrl+g` with autocomplete open does nothing. The row now says the key aborts streaming or a running bash command, and a separate row names `tui.select.cancel` for autocomplete.

**Hardcoded keys** that now read the binding:

- Settings submenu: "Enter to select · Esc to go back".
- `SettingsList` (pi-tui): "Enter/Space to change · Esc to cancel". Space stays literal because the handler checks `" "` directly.
- `/config` selector: `esc` to close (the handler matches `tui.select.cancel`, so the hint also left out `ctrl+c`).
- Session selector empty state: "Tab to view all".
- Fullscreen copy on select setting: "copy selections with Ctrl+X" (`app.message.copy`).

With default bindings the visible change is formatting: hints now show key ids like the rest of pi (`enter to select · escape/ctrl+c to go back`) instead of "Enter" and "Esc".

Not changed: the static descriptions "Ctrl+P cycling" (`/scoped-models`) and "Ctrl+G external editor" (settings schema) are built before keybindings load.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): name the interrupt key in the ! command cancel hint
prs.body:
Closes #12517.

**Problem.** While a `!` command runs, its hint reads `tui.select.cancel`, whose defaults are escape and ctrl+c:

```
⠇ Running... (escape/ctrl+c to cancel)
```

The command is cancelled through `app.interrupt` (escape by default): `onEscape` calls `abortBash()`. Ctrl+C goes to `app.clear`, which clears the editor, and a second press within 500 ms quits pi. So following the hint quits pi instead of stopping the command. The warning shown for a second `!` command while one runs also hardcodes "Press Esc to cancel it first", which goes stale when `app.interrupt` is remapped.

**Fix.** Both now use `keyText("app.interrupt")`, like the retry, compaction and branch-summary hints in `status-indicator.ts` and the "Working..." hint in `interactive-mode.ts`. No key handling changes.

I checked the other `tui.select.cancel` hints (session delete and rename, thinking selector, trust, first-time setup, tree labels): each one belongs to a handler that does match `tui.select.cancel`, so this was the only mismatch.

**Validation** on main `c11a73bfba`:

- New tests in `test/bash-execution-width.test.ts`, the component's test file: the running hint names `escape` with default bindings and `ctrl+g` with `app.interrupt` remapped. Both fail without the fix.
- In tmux, with an empty agent dir, no extensions and no model, running `!sleep 30` and then `!echo second`:
  - before: `Running... (escape/ctrl+c to cancel)`; Ctrl+C does not stop the command and a second Ctrl+C quits pi.
  - after: `Running... (escape to cancel)` and `Press escape to cancel it first.`; with `{"app.interrupt": "ctrl+g"}`, both say `ctrl+g`.
- `npm run check` passes. In `./test.sh` the only failures are unrelated to this change:
  - The find tool tests fail because fd is not installed here and the test config prevents downloading it.
  - The pi-env tests need cargo, which is not installed here.
  - chord's `http` close test failed once under load and passes on its own.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): confirm the highlighted /llama search result after the selection moved
prs.body:
In `/llama` → "Download model…", pressing Enter always used the typed query if it looked like `owner/repository[:quant]`, even when the user had arrowed to a different result. For example, typing `bartowski/Orn`, highlighting `bartowski/Ornith-1.5-9B-GGUF`, and pressing Enter started a download of `bartowski/Orn`. That repository does not exist, and Hugging Face answered with `Invalid username or password.`

The Hugging Face search component already tracks whether the user moved the selection since the query last changed (`selectionTouched`). Enter now uses the typed `owner/repository` only when the selection has not moved, and otherwise confirms the highlighted row. These cases behave as before:
- Typing an exact repository (or `repo:quant`) and pressing Enter without browsing.
- Editing the query after browsing, which resets the flag.

No other selector lets typed text override the highlighted row, and this component has no copy in other packages.

Testing:
- Added two cases to `test/llama-ui.test.ts`, using the existing search harness with fake timers:
  - Browsing to a result and pressing Enter confirms that result. This fails without the fix (`Received: "bartowski/Orn"`).

### New Features

- **Decision models in codemode**: GitHub Copilot's `gpt-6-luna-decisions` and Radius decision models can be called from codemode `models.classify()`, and results include the provider's `responseId`. - **One setting per transcript notice**: cache misses, cache warming, compaction costs, and reasoning drops each have their own setting under Notices in `/settings`. See [Model and thinking](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.6.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/settings.md#model-and-thinking).
- **Dialog status kind for extensions**: `ctx.ui.select()`, `ctx.ui.confirm()`, and `ctx.ui.input()` accept `blockedKind`, so terminals with program status can show a dialog as a permission request, question, or login. See [Program Status Kind](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.6.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md#program-status-kind).

### Breaking Changes

- Replaced the `showCacheMissNotices` setting with one setting per transcript notice: `notices.cacheMisses`, `notices.cacheWarming`, `notices.compactionCosts`, and `notices.reasoningDrops`, configured under Notices in `/settings`. An existing `showCacheMissNotices` value is migrated to all four. `SettingsManager.getShowCacheMissNotices()` and `setShowCacheMissNotices()` are removed; use `getNotices()` and `setNotice()` instead

### Added

- Added `compat.supportsStrictMode` for `google-generative-ai` and `google-vertex` models in `models.json`, so Gemini 3+ models served under IDs without the version can use strict tools ([#12321](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12321))
- Added a `blockedKind` option to `ctx.ui.select()`, `ctx.ui.confirm()` and `ctx.ui.input()` that sets the kind of blocked program status (OSC 7501) the dialog reports, for example `"permission"` for a select that approves an action. See [Dialogs](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.6.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md#program-status-kind)
- Added `full_output_error` to the bash tool's structured output and `fullOutputError` to its details, `BashResult` and `BashExecutionMessage`, giving the reason when truncated output could not be saved to a temp file. User bash output that was truncated without a saved file now says so in the model context and the TUI ([#10585](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10585))
- Added the `gpt-6-luna-decisions` decision model for GitHub Copilot, callable from codemode `models.classify()` with text and images ([#12395](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12395))
- Added decision models on the Radius provider, callable from codemode `models.classify()`
- Added `responseId` to codemode `models.classify()` results. OpenRouter's System One fills it with its generation ID, and its billed cost replaces the catalog estimate. See [codemode](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.6.1/packages/coding-agent/docs/codemode.md)

### Changed

- Changed the default Mistral model from `devstral-medium-latest` to `mistral-medium-latest`, because Mistral retired Devstral and the model catalog no longer lists it
- Changed `after_provider_response` to also fire for HTTP error responses (4xx/5xx) and for each retried attempt on OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google models, as it already did for OpenAI Codex, Mistral, Radius, and Amazon Bedrock, so extensions can read the status and `retry-after` of rate-limited requests ([#12376](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12376))
- Changed first-time setup to show the colored pi logo and only ask about analytics; the theme defaults to the system theme, which follows the terminal's colors

### Fixed

- Fixed selecting the `xhigh` thinking level for Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Neon on the `google` and `google-vertex` providers failing with `Unsupported Google thinking level mapping ... xhigh -> xhigh` ([#12184](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12184))
- Fixed sessions with very many entries after the last compaction (about 120k or more) failing to load with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` when building the context ([#12154](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12154))
- Fixed `ctx.ui.pasteToEditor()` and `ctx.ui.setEditorText()` not repainting the editor when called outside terminal input handling, such as after an `await` in a command handler ([#12295](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12295))
- Fixed the bash tool returning `(no output)` when the output ended with a line over 50KB followed by an empty line; it now shows the end of that line ([#12350](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12350))
- Fixed `/tree` navigation adding the branch's prompts to Up-arrow history again on every navigation; prompts already in history now move to the most recent position instead of repeating ([#12279](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12279))
- Fixed closing the console window or terminal tab on Windows skipping `session_shutdown` and leaving commands started by the bash tool running, for example `sleep 300` from `bash -c "sleep 300"`. pi now handles SIGHUP on Windows like on POSIX and waits for `taskkill` to finish before it exits. Quitting with Ctrl+D or `/quit` while a `!` command runs, or ending RPC mode while a `bash` command runs, no longer leaves that command running on Windows either
- Fixed the `AuthStorage` coalesced-reload test failing intermittently on systems with coarse file timestamps ([#12190](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12190))
- Fixed the `thinkingLevelMap` reference in the models.json schema and docs suggesting pi does not support the `xhigh` and `max` thinking levels; it now says they are opt-in and only offered when mapped, and the model guide explains how to map thinking levels ([#12281](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12281))
- Fixed Mermaid diagrams wider than the terminal falling back to their source without explanation; a note now says how many columns the diagram needs ([#12324](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12324))
- Fixed copies on Wayland silently failing when `wl-copy` guessed a non-text MIME type from the copied text, for example `application/x-ruby` for text starting with `def`, which clipboard managers such as Klipper discard; pi now copies as `text/plain` ([#12446](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12446) by [@ttempaa](https://github.com/ttempaa))
- Fixed pi crashing when the bash tool or a `!` command could not write its full-output temp file, for example when `/tmp` was full, over a per-user quota or not writable; both now keep the truncated output and say why the full output could not be saved. Opening the external editor and `/share` now report such failures instead of crashing ([#10585](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10585))
- Fixed `/login` showing a provider as configured when its stored `auth.json` key is a `!command` that fails, while requests failed with `No API key found`. `/login` now shows `stored key did not resolve`, `getProviderAuthStatus()` returns `{ configured: false, source: "stored" }`, and entering the same `!command` again in `/login` runs it again instead of reusing the cached failure ([#12164](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12164))
- Fixed `pi update` run from WSL through the Windows installation of pi rebuilding that installation with Linux npm; it now stops and says that running the Windows installation from WSL is unsupported ([#12172](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12172))
- Fixed right-click paste inserting the clipboard twice in Tabby on Windows, which pastes on right-click itself ([#12406](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12406))
- Fixed dialogs shown before interactive mode starts, such as the project trust prompt, the missing session folder prompt and first-time setup, reporting no `blocked` program status (OSC 7501). Blocked messages of multi-line dialog titles are now the first line only, for example `Trust project folder?` instead of the folder path and explanation. The project trust prompt and first-time setup report `kind=permission` ([#12439](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12439))
- Fixed GitHub Copilot listing decision models the account cannot use, such as `microsoft-decision-1` on accounts whose plan does not include it, where every call failed with HTTP 400. After `/login` or the next token refresh, only the decision models in the account's Copilot model catalog are listed ([#12395](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12395))
- Fixed the bash tool on Windows not finding Git for Windows installed outside Program Files and running commands through the WSL launcher `System32\bash.exe` instead. pi now asks the `git.exe` on `PATH` for its installation (`git var GIT_SHELL_PATH`, Git 2.47+) and uses its Git Bash before other `bash.exe` on `PATH` ([#12408](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12408))
- Fixed RPC mode, session loading, and llama.cpp model events rescanning an incomplete line on every chunk, which made large lines, such as messages with images, take time quadratic in their size. llama.cpp model events also accept lone CR line endings and CRLF split across chunks ([#12224](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12224))
- Fixed `!` command output coming back collapsed after compaction, `/reload`, `/resume` or `/tree` while ctrl+o was set to expanded ([#12426](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12426), [#12427](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/pull/12427) by [@acmerfight](https://github.com/acmerfight))
- Fixed more temporary provider failures not being retried automatically: Cloudflare HTTP 525, gateway "provider is temporarily unavailable" and partial-response errors, Anthropic `api_error` events during streaming, OpenRouter empty responses and stops without output, streams ending with `finish_reason: "error"`, and "request rate increased too quickly" throttling ([#12206](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12206), [#12227](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12227), [#12240](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12240), [#12407](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12407))

- Fixed HTTP 400 with thinking `off` on Claude Sonnet 5.5 through GitHub Copilot, and on Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 through Cloudflare AI Gateway and Vercel AI Gateway; selecting `off` on those models now uses the lowest supported level ([#12429](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12429))
- Fixed Gemini 3+ models whose IDs carry a prefix, such as `vendor-gemini-4-argon`, being treated as older Gemini models: they now get strict tools, tool-call IDs, and images inside function responses ([#12321](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12321))
- Fixed Google prompt blocks being reported and retried as incomplete streams; the error now includes the block reason and safety ratings ([#12330](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12330))
- Fixed `openai-codex` starting GPT-6 requests at `medium` regardless of the selected thinking level ([#12361](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12361))
- Fixed GPT-6.2 dropping earlier reasoning as `prefix_mismatch` after the OpenAI Codex WebSocket connection expired ([#12367](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12367))
- Fixed Amazon Bedrock requests hanging behind `HTTPS_PROXY` with AWS SSO profiles ([#12353](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12353))
- Fixed HTTP 400 after tool calls without text on Cloudflare Workers AI's GPT-OSS 120B and 20B, Granite 4.0 H Micro, and Llama 3.3 70B Instruct FP8 Fast ([#12194](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12194))

- Fixed extension providers with `fetchModels` making model lookups quadratic in catalog size, which blocked pi for about a second with ~10k models ([#12311](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/12311))

issues.title: Web Shell: pass native reasoning selection when creating a standalone session
issues.body:
### Problem

Embedded Web Shell hosts may accept model configuration only when creating a standalone session. With `@qwen-code/web-shell@0.27.1`, the native model menu selection is available at first-prompt preparation, but the standalone `createSession` call forwards model and approval mode without the selected reasoning effort. Web Shell tries to set `reasoning_effort` after creation, which fails for hosts that only accept initial configuration.

I also checked [the standalone first-prompt preparation on main](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/packages/web-shell/client/utils/sessionPreparation.ts). It still omits the reasoning selection at creation and applies it through a post-create setter in both the attached and detached paths.

### Reproduction

1. Embed Web Shell with lazy standalone session creation and advertise model reasoning options in the standalone session options response.
2. In the native model menu, select **Thinking off** (`none`) or a non-default effort before creating a session.
3. Send the first prompt. The standalone create request omits the effort, and the post-create setter fails on a host that rejects updates to initial configuration.

### Requested behavior

Expose an optional, typed reasoning selection through the standalone creation contract, or provide a supported pre-create hook that receives the native menu selection. When creation confirms that it applied the selected value, skip the post-create setter for that session. Preserve that setter path for daemons that only support post-create configuration.

Please cover explicit `none`, a non-default effort, no explicit selection, and both attached and detached first-prompt paths. In a local browser test against a mock host, forwarding `none` and `low` at creation let the first prompt proceed without a separate reasoning update.

### Related

#9595 addressed showing reasoning controls before lazy creation. This request covers forwarding the value selected in those controls. #17570 covers navigation while preparing an already attached session.

issues.title: After automatic compaction, the next request's size estimate counts the pending tool result twice and adds a 20K pad, so the turn is stopped or sent with `max_tokens: 1`

labels.name: priority/P1
labels.description: High priority issue

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/core
labels.description: Core engine and logic

labels.name: scope/token-management
labels.description: Token handling and limits

labels.name: roadmap/context-performance
labels.description: Roadmap: Context and performance

issues.body:
## What happened?

Automatic compaction can run while a tool result is still pending, either through the hard-tier rescue or through auto compaction in the middle of a tool loop. In that case the compression succeeds, but the size estimate for the next request counts that tool result twice. Every compaction also adds a 20,000-token pad to the estimate. The compacted prompt fits the window, yet the turn fails in one of two ways, depending on which check reads the estimate:

1. The hard-tier guard stops the turn with "Context is too large to send safely after automatic compression. … compression status: COMPRESSED. Start a new session or reduce the resumed history before continuing."
2. The request is sent with `max_tokens: 1`. The model returns nothing, and the turn fails with "Model stream ended after a tool result without visible progress."

On a small window, the pad alone causes the second failure after any compaction, whether or not a tool result is pending.

### Observed

| Run | Window | After compaction | Estimate the check used | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mock provider, released 0.24.6. Hard-tier auto compaction after two file reads. | 64,000 | `COMPRESSED`, `newTokenCount` 25,225 (already includes the pending result) | 45,241 against a hard limit of 41,000 | Turn stopped: "Context is too large … Start a new session" |
| OpenRouter `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`. Hard-tier auto compaction after a 476K-character `read_file`. Run on the #14953 branch, where this compression can succeed. | 262,144 | `COMPRESSED`. The next request was about 126K tokens (chars/4). | At least the window: the clamp only returns 1 once the estimate reaches it | 5 requests with `max_tokens: 1`, 0 bytes each. Turn failed with "Model stream ended after a tool result without visible progress." |
| Mock provider, `/compress`, #14953 branch, no files restored | 16,000 | `COMPRESSED`, count 4,805 | 24,903 (4,805 + the follow-up message + 20,000) | Next request sent with `max_tokens: 1`. The mock counted that prompt at 7,812 tokens, so about 8K tokens were free. The mock's one-word reply fit in one token; a real reply would be cut off. |

## What did you expect to happen?

After a successful compaction, the next request should be sized from the compacted history, with the pending tool result counted once. A prompt that fits the window should then go out with a usable output budget, and the turn should continue.

## Root cause

All links point to main at `87735a9`.

1. **The pending message ends up inside `newTokenCount`.** For auto compaction and the hard-tier rescue, `tryCompress` passes `precomputedEffectiveTokens` as `originalTokenCount`. Its own comment says that count "always folds in locally estimated parts (pending user message, previous output)" ([llm-chat.ts#L2925-L2948](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts#L2925-L2948)). `ChatCompressionService.compress` documents the same option as the count that "reflects only the prior turn's API usage" ([chatCompressionService.ts#L316-L318](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/services/chatCompressionService.ts#L316-L318)). It derives `newTokenCount` from that count:
   - with provider usage: `original − (compressionInput − 1000 − pending) + output` ([#L1348-L1357](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/services/chatCompressionService.ts#L1348-L1357));
   - on the reduced or usage-missing path: `(original − estimate(history)) + estimate(newHistory)`, where `history` does not contain the pending message ([#L1373-L1394](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/services/chatCompressionService.ts#L1373-L1394)).

   Either way, the pending tool result stays inside `newTokenCount`.
2. **It is added a second time.** After compaction the chat stores `setLastPromptTokenCount(newTokenCount, true)` ([llm-chat.ts#L3025](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts#L3025)). Both consumers then add `userContent` on top of it:
   - the hard-tier guard ([#L3547-L3555](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts#L3547-L3555));
   - the output clamp ([#L3740-L3753](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts#L3740-L3753)). The clamp also multiplies the new content by `CONSERVATIVE_NEW_CONTENT_SAFETY_FACTOR` = 1.5 ([tokenEstimation.ts#L99-L120](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/services/tokenEstimation.ts#L99-L120)).
3. **Every compaction adds a 20,000-token pad.** The service always reports `newTokenCountIsEstimated: true` ([chatCompressionService.ts#L1464](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/services/chatCompressionService.ts#L1464)). Because of that flag, the clamp adds `ESTIMATE_CLAMP_OVERHEAD_PAD` ([llm-chat.ts#L856](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/core/llm-chat.ts#L856)).
   - The pad covers what an estimate can miss, such as the fixed instructions and tool definitions sent with every request. Some margin is warranted: in the 16K run the estimate before the pad was 4,903, while the mock counted 7,812.
   - But the pad is a fixed 20,000, whatever the window. Its comment says it "costs nothing on large windows". On a 16K window, though, it is larger than the window itself, and `clampOutputTokensToWindow` ([tokenLimits.ts#L83](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/core/tokenLimits.ts#L83)) returns 1.

The pad's comment also says that once provider usage arrives, it corrects an over-count. That did not happen in the real run: the retries within the turn reused the same budget, so the turn failed before any later request could pick up the provider's count.

## Possible direction

- Give `newTokenCount` one meaning on every path: the compacted history plus the non-visible remainder, without the pending message, because both consumers add `userContent` themselves. The service already computes `pendingToolResultTokenCount` ([chatCompressionService.ts#L679](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/87735a9a4fda96d688bc252e97146292197053e5/packages/core/src/services/chatCompressionService.ts#L679)). Subtracting it whenever `originalTokenCount` came from the precomputed count would be enough.
- Size the pad to the window, for example as a fraction of it, so that it cannot take up a small window by itself.

## Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

- Code references: main `87735a9`.
- Reproduced on the released 0.24.6 (mock run), and on the #14953 branch at `6cadd29` (mock runs and the real-provider run). The guard and clamp code on that branch is the same as on main.
- macOS 15.6.1, Node v24.15.0.

</details>

## Login information

OpenAI-compatible. Two setups:
- a local mock provider that counts tokens as chars/4 and rejects any request where `prompt + max_tokens` exceeds the window;
- OpenRouter (`qwen/qwen3.8-27b`, pinned to 262,144-token endpoints) for the real run.

## Anything else we need to know?

- Found while testing #14953 (#9455), where it is listed as out of scope. #14953 makes the compression request itself fit. That is why the second and third rows only appear on that branch: on main, those sessions already fail at the compression request.
- Related but with a different cause: #14331, where a tool result really is too large for the room left in the window. Here the compacted prompt fits, and the estimate over-counts it.
- I have the request dumps and debug logs for every row and can attach them.
- I can send a fix for this.

issues.title: Russian CLI count forms and remaining ru copy after #17719

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/ui
labels.description: User interface and display

issues.body:
Follow-up from #17719 / #17710. #17719 fills the missing Russian Settings/CLI strings and the account-menu layout; it keeps the existing two-key English singular/plural split in the CLI i18n layer, so these items stay open after that PR lands.

## Remaining

1. **CLI 2–4 count forms.** `t()` is a flat key lookup. Callers pick the singular key at `count === 1` and the plural key otherwise, so one plural value has to serve 2–4, 5–20, and 21+. Current ru many-forms are ungrammatical at 2–4 (`2 дней`, `2 расширений`, `2 MCP-серверов` instead of `2 дня` / `2 расширения` / `2 MCP-сервера`). #17710 expected «3 расширения». A proper `Intl.PluralRules` (or count-agnostic rewrites) belongs here, not in the coverage PR.
2. **`toolDisplayName.TodoList` and `toolDisplayName.TaskList`** both render «Список задач», so a turn that runs both collapses to «Список задач × 2». Other locales keep them distinct (zh: 任务清单 vs 任务列表).
3. **`/extensions list` always uses the plural keys** (`{{count}} MCP servers`, skills, commands), so a count of 1 reads «1 MCP-серверов». The unbranched caller predates #17719; the new singular values are unreachable from that site.
4. **Settings descriptions translated from the stale zh table**, so a few ru entries omit facts the English schema now serves (`ultracode` on `disableWorkflowKeywordTrigger`, models.dev on `privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled`, and the other keys named on #17719 R1-6).

Optional coverage that can ride along: block-scope the more-menu `text-align: start` CSS assertion; pin `.moreLocalFiles::after`; pin `hooks.compactSummary` one/few/many.

## Not in this issue

Account-menu wrapping and Settings/CLI key coverage — those are #17719.
