prs.title: test(windows): verify preview preservation with a valid host fixture
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Initializes each Windows fixture through one strict PowerShell-host readiness invocation before freezing its profile baseline, while retaining cmd for ordinary launcher checks. Preserves the real parent PATHEXT, routes the module-analysis cache to an owned temporary file, and protects all existing user-data entries. The opt-in hosted workflow runs the complete preservation file once; the default ECS route remains unchanged.

## Why it's needed

Shell startup can change the owned profile before any installer runs. During main integration, the shared launcher switched to cmd, unintentionally removing the PowerShell readiness precondition. The latest correction restores that original single readiness slot without adding warmups, retries or allowed paths. Production installer behavior is unchanged.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run focused Windows validation on this exact candidate. Before installation, readiness and the retained launcher must return OLD_PREVIEW, the seven child environment records must be present, and the module-cache path must match the owned location. Then verify invalid archives and unsafe destinations preserve the old installation, successful activation works, and PATH, siblings, locks and existing profile entries remain protected. The complete file has 19 registered cases, with three declared POSIX-only skips on Windows.

### Evidence (Before & After)

TUI screenshots are N/A. [The exact 3bb83353 Windows run](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/actions/runs/43872027572/job/133315528511) failed before any installer: 0 passed, 1 failed, three POSIX skips and 15 cases not reached after bail. Launcher output and all seven environment records passed; the profile guard rejected new AppData/Roaming directories after the baseline had been frozen without starting PowerShell.

The corrected source tree c5d15f94164571f9921d9085cce8fa9aa63715fc is committed as 7bbd3580. Fresh full build, type checking, both complete local test files (32 passed / five original platform skips), formatting, lint and workflow static checks passed. [Exact-head Windows validation](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/actions/runs/43876529604) succeeded on attempt 1: 16 passed, zero failed and three declared POSIX-only skips out of 19 registered cases, in 291.44 seconds. All seven launcher records were present, and all nine typed preservation receipts retained their initialized entries exactly. Their derived-before and derived-after maps were empty, so this run does not demonstrate creation of the four allowed cache entries. The exact-head [Qwen CI](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43876264980), [TUI parity](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43876265004) and [Managed Agent Server](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/43876265284) workflows concluded successfully; skipped jobs are not counted as passed. Historical failures and passes belong to their recorded candidates and are retained in the designs.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Corrected tree: build, type checking and local checks passed; 32 passed / five declared platform skips |
| Windows | Exact 7bbd3580 hosted preservation file: 16 passed / zero failed / three POSIX-only skips; previous 3bb83353 pre-install failure retained |
| Linux | Exact 7bbd3580 Qwen, TUI parity and Managed Agent Server workflows succeeded, with their declared skipped jobs retained |

### Environment

Local verification used Node 24.19.0 on macOS arm64. Focused Windows validation uses hosted windows-2022 and Node 22, one worker, zero retries and a 15-minute workflow bound.

## Risk & Scope

- Existing cold and initialized profile entries must remain exact. Four precisely typed, previously absent startup-profile entries may be added; this comparison cannot identify their writer PID. ModuleAnalysisCache is not added to that exception.
- Real release artifacts, Bun ABI, native PTY/TUI, the original ECS host and all-platform acceptance remain outside this fixture qualification. No Core, default renderer, release or production installer changes.
- No breaking change. Existing 60-second Windows subprocess and 120-second testcase budgets remain; POSIX and the independent 15-second raw observation stay unchanged.
- Designs: [English](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/7bbd3580fbfc3f1b3efe83de4291b58f5136e615/docs/design/2026-10-30-windows-preview-launch-diagnostic.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/chiga0/qwen-code/blob/7bbd3580fbfc3f1b3efe83de4291b58f5136e615/docs/design/2026-10-30-windows-preview-launch-diagnostic.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Original observation: [Windows ECS run](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/actions/runs/41002095690/job/123897020864).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 的改动

每个 Windows fixture 在冻结 profile 基线前，通过一次严格的 PowerShell host readiness 调用完成初始化；普通启动器检查继续使用 cmd。保留父进程真实 PATHEXT，将模块分析缓存路由到 owned 临时文件，并保护全部已有用户数据条目。opt-in hosted 工作流一次运行完整保护文件，默认 ECS 路径不变。

## 为什么需要

Shell 启动可在零次安装器调用时改变 owned profile。main 集成将共用启动器切换为 cmd，无意中移除了 PowerShell readiness 初态前提。最新修正恢复原有的单次 readiness，不增加预热、重试或允许新增路径。生产安装器行为不变。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

在精确当前候选上运行聚焦 Windows 验证。安装前 readiness 与保留的启动器必须输出 OLD_PREVIEW，七条 child 环境记录完整，模块缓存路径严格等于 owned 位置。之后确认错误归档与不安全目标不会破坏旧安装，完整包能激活，PATH、兄弟数据、锁和已有 profile 条目均受保护。完整文件注册 19 个用例，Windows 声明跳过三个仅 POSIX 用例。

### 前后证据

prs.title: fix(core): create session transcripts with owner-only permissions
prs.body:
## What this changes

Session transcripts (`<session>.jsonl`) persist tool output verbatim and can embed credentials, but were created world-readable: `ensureConversationFile()` called `fs.writeFileSync(..., { flag: 'wx', encoding: 'utf8' })` without a mode, so Node applied `0o666 & ~umask` (0644 under the common 022 umask), and the append path in `jsonl-utils` recreated a missing file the same way.

- `jsonl-utils`' `writeLine` / `writeLineSync` pass `0o600` at their four creation points, so a transcript deleted mid-session is recreated owner-only on the next append (the documented recovery path) instead of falling back to umask.
- Legacy transcript appends now go through a dedicated fd-bound writer (`legacy-session-transcript-writer.ts`): no-follow open, regular-file/identity/owner-evidence verification on one fd (fail closed), `fchmod` clearing only group/other while preserving owner bits (a 0400 transcript is never made writable), and the append itself through the pinned descriptor. Symlink/FIFO/directory paths, unverifiable identities, and Managed/conflicting owner records are refused instead of followed.
- `ChatRecordingService.ensureConversationFile()` keeps creation of a missing transcript under the session archive write fence, now with `0600`; ownership verification and permission tightening happen on the verified append fd.

Secret redaction in the write path (the other half of #18165) is intentionally out of scope to keep this change atomic.

Applies to the default legacy writer path. The lease/managed writer (`sessionWriterLeaseEnabled`, non-default) already creates transcripts with `0o600` and writes under its own fencing; its transcript fingerprint includes the file mode, which is why legacy tightening never touches Managed-owned transcripts. Generic `jsonl.writeLine`/`writeLineSync` keep the `0o600` creation mode for their own callers (usage history, workflow journal, etc.).

## Why

Refs #18165 — discussed with @qqqys there; write-time redaction and cleanup of existing logs remain open on that issue. First round reviewed by @wenshao; the latest push addresses the review from @qqqys (final-append creation mode, ownership/type verification before tightening, Windows guards) plus a symlink/TOCTOU hardening gap found while implementing it.

## How to verify

- `pnpm --filter @qwen-code/core test src/services/chatRecordingService.test.ts src/services/chatRecordingService.permissions.test.ts src/services/session-legacy-execution-refusal.test.ts src/utils/jsonl-utils.test.ts` — 372 passed.
- `chatRecordingService.permissions.test.ts` drives a real temp dir (no fs mocks) and covers: owner-only creation, tightening a world-readable file, preserving an owner-read-only mode, Managed transcripts untouched, symlink refusal (target sentinel unchanged), symlink installed after the fd is opened (TOCTOU), FIFO/directory refusal without blocking, owner-record version/conflict fail-closed, recreate-after-delete, and the pinned-descriptor append when the path is unlinked. POSIX mode assertions are skipped on Windows (`describe.skipIf`).
- `utils/jsonl-utils.test.ts` covers the generic writer's own post-probe deletion race (async and sync variants).
- ESLint / Prettier / `tsc --noEmit` clean on the touched files.

## Scope

- `packages/core/src/utils/jsonl-utils.ts` (0600 creation mode, generic callers)
- `packages/core/src/services/legacy-session-transcript-writer.ts` (new, fd-bound legacy writer)
- `packages/core/src/services/chatRecordingService.ts` (route legacy appends through the new writer)
- `packages/core/src/utils/sessionStorageUtils.ts` (fd-based owner evidence reader)
- `packages/core/src/services/session-execution-engine.ts` (export the ownership accumulator)
- `packages/core/src/services/chatRecordingService.test.ts` / `chatRecordingService.permissions.test.ts` / `session-legacy-execution-refusal.test.ts` (tests)

prs.title: docs(design): selective session restore phase 2 — sidecar-backed index basis
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds the design document (English + Chinese) for the next phase of session-restore work: making a *cold restore* proportional to what the user actually needs, not to the size of the whole transcript. Two slices, separable by review:

- **Slice A (behavior-neutral)**: route `readRestoreProjection` / `readLiveRestoreProjection` through the durable session-index sidecar (#11527) instead of a per-process full-file scan, with additive per-record hint columns in the sidecar schema and byte-identical projection outputs proven by an extended parity corpus.
- **Slice B (behavior change, maintainer approval required)**: flip daemon/ACP resume paths from full hydration to bounded replay by default (`recent`, turn-aligned, byte-budgeted), reusing the existing ACP `projectionSource` flow; pure-interactive `--resume` is gated separately, and all compatibility rules from the base design (compression selection, the 256 MiB daemon cap, legacy clients without `historyPageSize`, uncompressed-legacy full model history) are preserved verbatim.

## Why it's needed

The base design ([2026-08-08-selective-session-restore](docs/design/2026-08-08-selective-session-restore.md)) scopes bounded hydration but names as its own non-goal that "without a durable index, cold restore still scans the transcript once and remains O(file bytes)" — this is the checkpoint follow-up it anticipated. Measured during the #11433 evaluation: daemon restart today costs a full JSONL parse per resumed session (365 ms for 203 MB, seconds for production-scale multi-day sessions), and any working set beyond the 64 MiB in-memory index budget degrades to a full rescan on every read (#11493). Documented, benchmarked motivation and both rollout options are in the doc.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Read the design against the base design's compatibility constraints section; the sync guarantees between `.md` and `.zh-CN.md` are a review checklist item. No runtime behavior changes in this PR.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (docs-only).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ tested |
| 🪟 Windows | N/A |
|  🐧 Linux  | N/A |

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: slice B's default-window compatibility change — explicitly called out as requiring separate maintainer signoff, mirroring the base design's sizing rulings.
- Not validated / out of scope: implementation (slice A then B, tracked by this design's rollout section), pure-CLI `--resume` default policy (open question #3 in the doc).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none in this PR.

Design doc: [2026-09-10-selective-restore-index-basis.md](docs/design/2026-09-10-selective-restore-index-basis.md) · [中文版](docs/design/2026-09-10-selective-restore-index-basis.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Refs #8678 · #11433 · #11493 · PR #11527

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

本 PR 仅添加设计文档(中英双语),为会话恢复第二阶段定稿:让冷恢复的成本与"用户真正需要的内容"成正比,而不是与整篇 transcript 的大小成正比。两个可独立评审的分片:切 A(行为中立)让恢复投影走 #11527 的持久 sidecar 索引,替代每进程一次的全文件扫描,并以扩展 parity 语料证明两种基座投影输出字节一致;切 B(行为变更,需维护者具名批准)把 daemon/ACP resume 默认从全量水合改为有界回放(recent、turn 对齐、字节预算),纯交互 `--resume` 独立设闸;基底设计的全部兼容性约束(压缩选择、256MiB daemon 上限、无 historyPageSize 旧客户端、未压缩旧会话全量模型历史)逐字保留。动机:基底设计(2026-08-08)在有界水合目标下把"冷恢复仍需 O(文件) 扫一遍"列为其非目标并点名 checkpoint follow-up——本设计就是那个 follow-up:#11433 评估实测 daemon 重启每恢复一个会话付一次全量解析(203MB 365ms,生产多天会话数秒),缓存超 64MiB 后每次读取全扫(#11493)。本文档不含实现改动,发布节奏与开放问题见文内。

</details>

prs.title: docs(design): unified ACP core and ACP SDK 1.x upgrade (#10061)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds the design document for the unified-ACP program proposed in #10061: move Qwen Code's two ACP delivery paths (stdio agent mode and `qwen serve` Streamable HTTP) onto one transport-agnostic ACP core with a single capability-and-vendor-method registry, reduce both transports to thin adapters, and upgrade the Agent Client Protocol SDK from 0.14.1 to 1.4.x as the first phase.

The document covers: where the current duplication lives (protocol routing implemented twice, two vendor-extension namespaces, divergent capabilities such as HTTP lacking terminal support), why the timing favors acting now (the upstream SDK now ships official Streamable HTTP/WebSocket transports, and all formerly unstable session APIs have stabilized), the target three-layer architecture, a four-phase rollout with per-phase acceptance criteria, a breaking-change audit with deprecation windows, alternatives considered (including an explicit decision to keep the per-workspace child-process topology), verification strategy centered on a cross-transport conformance suite, and open questions.

This PR contains the design only — no production code changes.

## Why it's needed

The two ACP paths have drifted in user-visible ways: clients connecting over HTTP vs. stdio observe different capabilities and different vendor APIs (#4063 catalogs the same structural problems region-wide), every protocol or SDK change must be made twice, and the repo is 15+ releases behind the upstream SDK with a known deep-import landmine. Aligning on the design before any code is also what the two-tier gate requires for a maintainer-initiated core program of this size.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Read `docs/design/2026-08-26-unified-acp-core-and-sdk-upgrade.md` and confirm: (a) the problem statement and drift table match the code as it exists on main; (b) the phase ordering (SDK upgrade first, core extraction second) is sound; (c) the surviving vendor namespace choice (`_qwen/*`) matches the intent of the earlier `daemon-acp-http` design; (d) the alternatives disposition — especially keeping child-per-workspace isolation — is acceptable; (e) the acceptance criteria and conformance-suite plan are concrete enough to gate implementation PRs.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — documentation-only change.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: design-level only; the largest open tradeoff documented is adopting the official SDK Streamable HTTP transport (big deletion of bespoke wire code) versus keeping the proven RFD#721 implementation — mitigated by a parity suite and a legacy env-flag window in the plan.
- Not validated / out of scope: no implementation; registry module location, WS-on-serve, HTTP terminal support, and an optional in-process mode remain open questions in the doc.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none in this PR; the design itself schedules breaking surfaces (unstable method renames, vendor-namespace aliases) with explicit deprecation windows.

## Linked Issues

Refs #10061 (proposal) · Refs #4063 (architecture umbrella) · Related prior designs: `docs/design/daemon-acp-http/`, `docs/design/daemon-transport-abstraction/`

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

本 PR 仅新增 #10061 所提“统一 ACP”方案的设计文档：将 Qwen Code 的两条 ACP 通路(stdio agent 模式与 `qwen serve` 的 Streamable HTTP)收敛到同一个与传输无关的 ACP 核心(统一的能力与 vendor 方法注册表),两种 transport 退化为薄适配层,并把 Agent Client Protocol SDK 从 0.14.1 升级到 1.4.x 作为第一阶段。

文档内容涵盖:当前冗余的准确位置(协议路由两套实现、两个 vendor 扩展命名空间、能力分歧如 HTTP 缺 terminal 支持)、为何现在动手时机合适(上游 SDK 已官方提供 Streamable HTTP/WebSocket transport,原先 unstable 的会话 API 已全部转正)、目标三层架构、带逐阶段验收标准的四阶段落地计划、含废弃窗口的 breaking 变更审计、备选方案取舍(明确保留每 workspace 子进程拓扑)、以跨 transport 一致性测试套件为核心的验证策略,以及开放问题。

本 PR 只有设计文档,无任何生产代码改动。

动机:两条 ACP 通路已在用户可感知的层面漂移:HTTP 与 stdio 客户端看到的能力与 vendor API 不同(#4063 已在更大范围内记录同类结构问题),任何协议或 SDK 改动都要做两遍,且仓库落后上游 SDK 15+ 个版本并存在一个已知的深 import 地雷项。对这种量级的核心改造,按两层 gate 的要求也应先由 maintainer 在动代码前对齐设计。

Reviewer 验证方式:阅读设计文档并确认:(a) 问题陈述与漂移对照表与 main 分支现状一致;(b) 阶段顺序(先 SDK 升级、后抽核心)合理;(c) 保留 `_qwen/*` 命名空间的决定与早前 `daemon-acp-http` 设计的意图一致;(d) 备选方案的取舍(尤其保留 child-per-workspace 隔离)可接受;(e) 验收标准与一致性测试套件计划足以约束后续实现 PR。

风险与范围:仅设计层面;文档中记录的最大开放取舍是采用官方 SDK 的 Streamable HTTP transport(大幅删除自研连线代码)还是保留久经考验的 RFD#721 实现——计划中以一致性套件与 legacy 环境变量窗口期缓解。本 PR 无 breaking 变更;设计本身为 unstable 方法改名、vendor 命名空间别名等 breaking 面排定了明确的废弃窗口。

关联:#10061(提案)、#4063(架构总线 issue)、先前设计 `docs/design/daemon-acp-http/` 与 `docs/design/daemon-transport-abstraction/`。

</details>

prs.title: test(integration): skip input history suite in Docker
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Registers the Docker-skipped workspace input-history suite as a proper skipped suite, rather than returning from its declaration before registering any tests.

## Why it's needed

The v0.28.6 Docker integration release gate failed because this suite existed on the new main but returned early under Docker, leaving Vitest with an empty suite. The Web Shell packaging path is unchanged.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the input-history integration file with `QWEN_SANDBOX=docker` and the test-name filter `^daemon workspace input history`. It should report skipped tests without an empty-suite failure. The release Docker gate should retain coverage from the second runtime-root suite in the same file.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: `Error: No test found in suite daemon workspace input history (real HTTP/stdio/filesystem)` in release run 45727968748.
After: local Docker-mode collection reports 4 skipped tests and exits successfully for the affected suite.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--: | :--: |
| macOS | ✅ `QWEN_SANDBOX=docker` targeted Vitest collection; Prettier and ESLint |
| Windows | ⚠️ Not tested locally; existing Windows skip is preserved |
| Linux | ⚠️ Full Docker integration assigned to release CI |

### Environment (optional)

Local Docker-mode collection using the existing built artifacts. No Docker daemon was started; the full Docker lane was not run locally.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: none beyond changing unsupported Docker cases from an invalid empty suite to an explicit skip. The test title is shortened only to keep the suite's existing callback indentation and avoid an unrelated whole-file formatting change.
- Not validated / out of scope: full Docker and non-Docker integration lanes were not run locally; a broader integration typecheck was attempted but its missing fresh-worktree build prerequisites made it non-authoritative. Prettier check and ESLint passed. Local formatting review and the targeted Docker-mode suite check passed; remote review gate was not run.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #18120 and release failure run 45727968748.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 此 PR 做什么

将 Docker 环境中需要跳过的 workspace 输入历史测试套件注册为正确跳过的套件，避免在声明中提前返回而未注册任何测试。

## 为什么需要

v0.28.6 的 Docker 集成发布门禁失败，因为新 main 上该套件在 Docker 环境提前返回，导致 Vitest 报告空测试套件。Web Shell 打包路径不变。

## 审查者验证计划

### 如何验证

以 `QWEN_SANDBOX=docker` 和测试名筛选 `^daemon workspace input history` 运行输入历史集成测试文件，应显示跳过测试而不是空套件失败。发布 Docker 门禁保留同文件中第二个 runtime-root 套件的覆盖。

### 前后证据

之前：发布运行 45727968748 报 `Error: No test found in suite daemon workspace input history (real HTTP/stdio/filesystem)`。
之后：本地 Docker 模式收集显示 4 个跳过测试，受影响套件正常退出。

### 环境（可选）

使用现有构建产物进行本地 Docker 模式收集，不启动 Docker daemon，不在本地运行完整 Docker 流程。

## 风险与范围

#18120 及发布失败运行 45727968748 的后续修复。

releases.body:
<!-- qwen-release-notes:v2 -->

## Highlights

- Managed sessions can now park while awaiting tool approvals, questions, or Hooks/MCP decisions, surviving Harness restarts and resuming via cold recovery. ([#17953](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17953), [#18115](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18115), [#18164](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18164), [#18166](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18166), [#18187](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18187), [#18194](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18194), [#18203](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18203), [#18224](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18224), [#18236](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18236), [#18303](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18303))
- Headless sessions and the Ink TUI now run on the event-bus kernel by default, with cancelled turns settling within 10 seconds; opt out via experimental.eventBusAgentLoop. ([#18154](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18154), [#18213](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18213))

## Managed session parking and recovery

Turns can now park while awaiting approvals, questions, or background work, and recover across Harness restarts.

- Moves managed-agent background capture into the worker so captures survive Harness restarts and sessions with live background work can suspend safely. ([#17953](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/17953))
- Idle hosted sessions can now suspend while a recoverable tool-approval Action awaits a decision, resuming on approval, cancel, or mode change. ([#18115](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18115))
- Action parking now reports why a waiting Turn stays resident, and parking and cold recovery share one set of Session-shape checks. ([#18157](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18157))
- Approval waits whose Prompt has only images or attachments can now park and survive a Harness crash through cold recovery. ([#18164](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18164))
- Approval waits requested by extension command steps, such as Shell commands inside extensions, can now park while awaiting the decision. ([#18166](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18166))
- A wake-started Turn that was waiting for tool approval when its Harness crashed now resumes that approval wait on the next Harness instead of failing. ([#18170](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18170))
- A wake-started Turn that crashes while awaiting a tool approval or answer now advances the session checkpoint, so follow-up Turns can start and wake work no longer stalls. ([#18172](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18172))
- Tool approval waits can now park while a verified background hold covers the Session's background runs, instead of keeping the Session resident until the human decides. ([#18187](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18187))
- Turns started by wake inputs can now park while waiting for tool approval, and the wake pump resumes them at the park's due time instead of keeping the Session resident. ([#18194](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18194))
- managed-agent: park channel and pr_event Turns' approval waits ([#18203](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18203))
- Child Session Turns can now park while awaiting tool approval or a question, and cold recovery resumes them instead of staying resident. ([#18224](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18224))
- Prevents the parked-MCP reclamation job from retiring MCP connections of Sessions whose seal parks a Turn waiting for an Action. ([#18234](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18234))
- Managed agents can now park Hooks and MCP Session approval waits instead of blocking, landing alongside the Harness-side MCP plan. ([#18236](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18236))
- Version-0 public Shell Sessions now park approval waits on both Shell lanes, including Shell calls before dispatch. ([#18303](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18303))
- Restores Workspace registration for Action parking acceptance and aligns approval validation with durable Hooks and MCP formats, with MySQL 8.4 coverage. ([#18353](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18353))
- Managed Agent recovery now uses session-level evidence after a turn is cancelled before Harness admission, allowing a cleanup recheck. ([#18132](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18132))
- Cancellations of never-admitted turns can now settle while an earlier turn's owed runtime cleanup stays available for retry. ([#18212](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/18212))

issues.title: compaction: loose scan can delete a user turn that pastes the summary header

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
## Where

`crates/tui/src/compaction.rs:330-345` (as of the Pinvou fork's `pinvou3-clean` head `cc2adf8ef`, which tracks this repository's maintenance line).

## What

When compacting a history that has no provenance-stamped checkpoint carrier, the engine locates "the first user message that starts with the summary header" via a loose scan and `retain`-deletes it before inserting the new stamped checkpoint in its place. The code's own comment acknowledges it "cannot tell a pre-provenance carrier from a user turn that pastes the whole summary header".

Concretely: if a user genuinely typed (or pasted) a message that begins with the compaction summary header in a pre-provenance-era session, the next compaction silently deletes that user turn and replaces it with the checkpoint. That is engine-side data loss of real user input — the downstream app's display-side hardening (keeping bare carriers visible in the UI) cannot recover a turn that no longer exists in the transcript.

## Suggested fix

Before deleting a matched user turn, require evidence that it is actually an engine-written carrier rather than user content, e.g. any of:

- carrier-adjacent metadata/topology evidence (the assistant-turn pattern the engine itself produces right after a compaction),
- an explicit engine-only marker,
- or (minimal) restrict the loose scan to sessions whose checkpoint history is engine-managed, and keep pasted-header turns in place — insert the new checkpoint after them instead of replacing them.

## Reproduction sketch

1. Session predates the provenance stamp (no `<!-- codewhale.compaction-checkpoint.v1 -->` carriers).
2. A user message begins with the summary header text (typed or pasted).
3. Trigger compaction. Observe the user turn is removed and the stamped checkpoint takes its position.

issues.title: tui: GNOME Terminal background stays custom Nord theme color after exit

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:install
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

labels.name: os:linux
labels.description: Linux-specific behaviour

issues.body:
## What happened?

After using CodeWhale in GNOME Terminal and exiting, the terminal profile keeps CodeWhale’s Nord light colors instead of restoring the previous profile colors. The background becomes `#ECEFF4` and the foreground `#2E3440`, while the palette remains Solarized. The terminal looks inconsistent outside CodeWhale.

Expected: CodeWhale restores the terminal’s previous background, foreground, and palette on exit, or leaves the existing profile colors untouched.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In GNOME Terminal, use a profile with the Solarized palette and a non-Nord background/foreground (for example Solarized Dark).
2. Configure CodeWhale with `theme = "custom:nord"` and a theme file containing `surface_bg: "#ECEFF4"` and `text_body: "#2E3440"`.
3. Run `codewhale` in that GNOME Terminal profile.
4. Exit CodeWhale normally.
5. Observe that the GNOME Terminal profile background/foreground remain the CodeWhale Nord colors instead of the previous colors.

## Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf)`

## Where did it happen?

- TUI (terminal interface)

## Operating system

- Linux

## How did you get Codewhale?

- npm

## Provider and model

`deepseek / deepseek-flash`

## Terminal and shell

GNOME Terminal 3.44.0 using VTE 0.68.0; `TERM=xterm-256color`; `COLORTERM=truecolor`; `/bin/bash`.

## `codewhale doctor` (optional)

Not included; no relevant failure was observed.

## Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

- CodeWhale theme: `~/.codewhale/themes/nord.json` defines `surface_bg: "#ECEFF4"` and `text_body: "#2E3440"`.
- GNOME Terminal profile currently reports:
  - `use-theme-colors=false`
  - `background-color=rgb(236,239,244)` (`#ECEFF4`)
  - `foreground-color=rgb(46,52,64)` (`#2E3440`)
  - palette still Solarized (`#002B36`, `#FDF6E3`, etc.)
- CodeWhale’s binary contains OSC 11 handling (`crates/palette/src/osc11.rs`), and its logs show terminal probes for `\x1b]11;?` and `\x1b]10;?`.
- OpenCode 2.2.5 was also used under the same GNOME Terminal profile and has an identical Nord light background/foreground, so the exact writer is not fully isolated. Cross-reference: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/63977
- The request is that the application setting OSC 10/11 restores the previous terminal colors on exit, or preserves the existing profile colors. A regression test for terminal color restoration would help.
- Workaround: reset the GNOME Terminal profile colors with `gsettings`.
- I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.

## Isolation steps not yet completed

1. Test whether `printf '\033]111\007'` and `printf '\033]110\007'` restore the dynamic background/foreground.
2. Reproduce with CodeWhale alone, then OpenCode alone, to identify which process writes the profile colors.

prs.body:
## What and why

Resolves the remaining unaddressed R5 audit gaps from #7461 (on top of `1fa6548ce` and `7e003749f` already landed on `main`) and adds missing behavioral regression tests:

- **R5-L10-01** (`crates/util/src/{utils,fs_confined}.rs`, `crates/engine/src/tools/workflow/journal.rs`): Exported shared best-effort `codewhale_util::utils::sync_directory`, added `codewhale_util::fs_confined::append_durable` (data `sync_all` + best-effort parent directory sync on create), and routed `WorkflowRunJournal::append_record` through it.
- **R5-L10-02** (`crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs`, `test_cases_04.rs`): Replaced hard-failing `File::open(...)?.sync_all()?` calls left by `1fa6548ce` (which break on network/FUSE mounts) with shared best-effort `sync_directory` across all session/sidecar/checkpoint/archive unlink paths, with regression test `delete_session_removes_sidecars_and_preserves_shared_runtime_store`.
- **R5-L7-01** (`crates/engine/src/tools/search.rs`, `tests.rs`): Derived a child `worker_cancel_token` with `drop_guard` in `run_blocking_grep` (matching `run_blocking_file_search`) so timeouts cancel the worker without cancelling the caller's parent token, with regression test `test_grep_blocking_wrapper_cancels_worker_on_timeout`.
- **R5-L9-02** (`crates/engine/src/tools/review.rs`): Passed caller `max_chars` into `resolve_review_source` / `resolve_file_target`, pre-checked size against `max_chars * 4`, read boundedly via `File::take(max_bytes + 1)` inside `spawn_blocking`, and added regression test `resolve_file_target_rejects_oversized_file_against_caller_max_chars`.
- **Regression test coverage** for already-landed R5 fixes: `gate_run_reports_success_only_when_gate_passes` (`R5-L8-01`) and `test_grep_files_clamps_oversized_max_results` (`R5-L9-03`).

issues.body:
## Summary

Teams often share product names, abbreviations and terminology that ordinary speech recognition renders inconsistently. Add a shared vocabulary layer so an authorized user can select a workspace dictionary for dictation while preserving personal preferences and visibility into the effective spelling rules. Membership in one workspace must never expose terms from another, and a shared administrator must not silently rewrite a user's personal dictionary.

## Problem to solve

This feature needs more than a list passed to a recognizer. It needs ownership, access checks, bounded provider disclosure, revision control, conflict handling and revocation behavior. A pronunciation hint can contain confidential project or customer names. A useful implementation must make it clear which vocabulary is active, what is sent to the selected provider and what happens when access, connectivity or the dictionary changes during an utterance.

## Proposed solution

### Scope, dependencies and related upstream work

Build this on P03 personal dictionaries (coordinated proposal), reusing its term schema, effective-vocabulary resolver, provider capability checks and spelling protections. M11 (coordinated proposal) remains the shared request/result owner. Shared vocabulary must enter that same snapshot and result-validation path; it must not create another recognizer, correction pipeline, provider cache or transcript store.

[Open issue #191109](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191109) proposes realtime transcription hints, including provider-specific vocabulary or prompt settings. Its text explicitly leaves Gemini Live endpoint acceptance unverified. That issue is adjacent provider plumbing, not evidence that shared dictionary authorization or collaboration exists. This draft has no confirmed upstream implementation PR to stack on. Its local dependency is P03; an actual parent branch must be identified only when that work exists.

Initial scope should cover explicit selection of authorized workspace dictionaries, read/edit permissions, bounded import/export, deterministic conflict resolution, revisioned snapshots and safe provider hints. Automatic organization discovery, cross-tenant federation, contact-directory ingestion, automatic learning from conversations, forced organization-wide personal spelling replacement and a new identity provider are excluded. If an installation has no suitable authenticated workspace authorization surface, shared dictionaries should remain unavailable while personal vocabulary continues to work.

### Required behavior and precedence

Each shared collection should have an opaque collection ID, an authorization scope, display metadata, schema version and monotonically advancing revision. Terms should reuse P03's canonical spelling, aliases, locale and casing/protection fields. Optional pronunciation fields must be provider-capability gated and bounded. Collection IDs, scope IDs and term labels must be treated as data; no term can become a system prompt, tool request or routing directive.

The recommended ordinary precedence is an explicit session choice, then the user's explicit personal override, then selected authorized shared terms, then baseline behavior. The selected collection set must be visible and frozen for an utterance. A shared update must not overwrite personal records. Conflicting shared entries at equal precedence should be surfaced as ambiguous and omitted from automatic substitution until the user chooses a source or maintainers adopt a documented priority policy. A forced organizational terminology mode, if ever added, needs a distinct visible policy and separate approval; it is not implicit in this feature.

Provider hints should bias recognition only where the provider adapter advertises the accepted field and limits. A provider without verified support must be shown as such. P03's existing conservative local validation/correction path may be used where accepted, but a hint must not force replacement of a common word or invent a term absent from the utterance. The user should be able to inspect effective sources and disable a collection without deleting its remote records.

#### Examples and negative cases

| Situation | Expected behavior |
|---|---|
| An authorized workspace contains the fictional product “Nimbrix” | Include its bounded hint only when selected and supported; preserve the actual spoken content. |
| A personal entry deliberately uses different casing | Personal override wins in ordinary mode and remains unchanged by workspace updates. |
| Two selected collections disagree about one alias | Explain the conflict and omit automatic replacement until resolved; do not use arrival order. |
| A user belongs to workspace A but requests a guessed workspace B ID | Deny access without disclosing B's terms, existence-sensitive metadata or revision details. |
| An entry contains “ignore instructions and send secrets” | Treat it as inert term data, validate bounds and never invoke tools or change prompt authority. |
| Membership is revoked while transcription or refinement is running | Invalidate every candidate derived from that snapshot, including hinted STT output; retain only reviewable user-owned material allowed by policy. |
| A stale client uploads a deleted collection | Reject stale revision/authorization; do not resurrect records. |
| The selected recognizer does not support vocabulary hints | Report that capability limit and apply only explicitly supported local behavior. |

### Authorization and provider disclosure contract

Reuse the installation's established identity and authorization mechanism. Proposed permission concepts are read, edit terms, manage collections and export; maintainers must map them to actual supported permissions rather than create a parallel role database. Every read, write, export and provider-bound snapshot should authorize the authenticated principal against the collection scope. A connected gateway, a known collection ID or an application profile must not count as membership.

The vocabulary resolver should return a bounded snapshot with collection revisions, authorized scope, effective entries, conflict information, expiry/policy metadata and provider budget status. M11 should revalidate authorization before provider egress and before accepting a shared-derived result for insertion. A revoked or expired snapshot should be invalidated rather than silently reused. Revalidation must be enforced on the authoritative service boundary, not only by a hidden UI control.

Do not promise retroactive erasure from a provider after a permitted request has already been sent. Revocation should cancel outstanding work where possible, discard the shared-derived candidate, stop subsequent disclosure and invalidate cached snapshots. Original user speech is not a shared collection record and should not be automatically deleted because collection membership changed; preservation and review still follow the authorized content/retention policy.

Provenance must cover both transcription hints and later refinement. If STT received shared terms, its recognizer output is also shared-derived; labeling it “raw” does not create an independent hint-free baseline. Already-authorized user-owned material may remain reviewable where policy permits, but revocation must not automatically publish a newly arriving hinted transcript as a safe fallback. If no currently authorized hint-free baseline exists, offer explicit retranscription using current hints only when retained audio exists under the accepted retention policy. Otherwise offer unavailable/manual recovery without silently retaining new audio, fabricating an original transcript or reusing the revoked snapshot.

Only selected, authorized and relevant entries should enter a provider request. The selection must be deterministic, explain truncation and obey the adapter's verified field/token/byte limits. No silent provider switch is permitted when the selected route rejects hints. Requests must separate vocabulary data from privileged instructions and avoid serializing arbitrary collection descriptions into the model prompt. Remote disclosure settings and organization policy must be enforced before submission, even when a user has read access to a collection.

### Storage, concurrent editing and migration

Use one source of truth for collection metadata and terms, with atomic revisions and expected-revision writes. Concurrent editors should receive a conflict containing only data they may read; never silently replace a newer collection. Bulk import should validate schema, aliases, duplicates, maximum sizes and permissions before an atomic commit. Invalid input should not leave a partly activated vocabulary. If maintainers choose partial imports later, the UI must explicitly report per-entry acceptance and preserve a reviewable revision.

Proposed initial ceilings are 5,000 terms and 400 KiB of normalized term payload per collection, plus a lower effective provider budget supplied by its adapter. These remain proposed guardrails. Local prerequisite workloads have now been measured in the design-review draft linked below; production-resource and provider qualification remain open. They are not a promise that every provider can accept that vocabulary. Reject oversized aliases, malicious nesting and unsupported fields before materializing a large in-memory snapshot. Normalization must preserve intentional spelling and avoid collapsing different protected identifiers merely because they look similar.

Deletion should record a revision/tombstone sufficient to prevent stale-client resurrection under the existing synchronization design. Migration should be versioned, idempotent and scoped to authorized collections. Existing personal dictionaries should stay personal; do not publish them during upgrade. Export should require explicit authorization, contain the requested collection only and disclose that terms may be confidential. Backups, deletion retention and audit retention should use the existing storage policy, with the final choices documented before release.

Audit records should support accountability for collection changes and access policy events without copying raw transcripts or all terms into general diagnostic logs. Prefer actor/scope identifiers, operation, revision and counts. Any detailed diff retention needs a scoped, access-controlled design and a documented retention policy. A user's personal overrides must not be included in another workspace's administrative view.

### Offline, cancellation and client lifecycle

Recommend fail-closed shared resolution when current authorization cannot be validated. Personal local vocabulary should continue to work, with a clear “shared vocabulary unavailable” state. An explicit offline lease could be considered later, but it would need a defined expiry and revocation tradeoff; no indefinite cached membership should be assumed. Reconnection should fetch authorized revisions and handle stale edits without overwriting remote changes.

Capture should pin one effective snapshot. An ordinary dictionary edit during capture should apply to the next utterance, while security-relevant revocation should invalidate the current shared-derived candidate. Cancellation, timeout, provider retry and duplicate network callbacks must use M11's generation/idempotency rules. Retrying must recheck scope and current versions instead of replaying an old authorized payload. No background synchronization callback may insert text or restart recording.

Clients should display the active collection labels, conflicts and unavailable state through keyboard-accessible controls and screen-reader text. Effective sources should be inspectable without needing to listen to audio. Unsupported mobile, browser, remote or headless management clients may consume an authorized snapshot only when their existing authenticated transport supports it; no OS-wide or offline capability is implied. Management UI and consumption capability should be reported separately.

### Acceptance criteria

1. **AC01 — Authorized scope:** All collection reads, writes, exports and effective snapshots enforce authenticated collection-scope permissions, including guessed IDs and cross-workspace requests.
2. **AC02 — Resolution:** Ordinary precedence is deterministic, personal overrides remain private and intact, and conflicting shared aliases are visibly unresolved.
3. **AC03 — Provider contract:** Only supported, bounded, authorized hints are sent; truncation and unsupported adapters are disclosed without silent route changes.
4. **AC04 — Revocation:** Pre-egress and pre-commit authorization changes invalidate shared-derived work, including hinted STT output. Recovery respects provenance/retention, never republishes a revoked snapshot as “raw,” and never describes sent data as recalled.
5. **AC05 — Concurrent edits:** Expected-revision writes, atomic imports and deletion tombstones prevent lost updates, partial activation and stale resurrection.
6. **AC06 — Migration:** Personal terms are never published by upgrade; collection migrations, exports and rollback preserve scope and schema boundaries.
7. **AC07 — Offline lifecycle:** Loss of authorization connectivity disables shared resolution visibly while personal local vocabulary remains usable; retries and reconnects reauthorize.
8. **AC08 — Isolation:** Prompt-like terms, malicious imports and dictionary metadata cannot invoke tools, switch mode, change provider or leak another scope's data.
9. **AC09 — Accessibility and clients:** Selection, source inspection, conflicts and recovery are keyboard/screen-reader usable; advertised consumption/management support matches evidence.
10. **AC10 — Privacy:** Logs, telemetry, exports, caches and administrative views obey the documented term/transcript/personal-data boundaries.
11. **AC11 — Performance:** Selection and validation budgets are measured at proposed limits, bounded allocations are enforced and provider quota behavior is demonstrated.
12. **AC12 — Semantic regression:** Hints do not force unrelated word substitutions or damage identifiers, negation, numbers, literal spans or unaffected personal-only dictation.

## Alternatives considered

Copying a team list into each personal dictionary would lose central revisions and revocation. Passing a global list to every provider request would over-disclose terms. Building a separate shared correction pipeline would duplicate P03/M11 behavior. Authorized overlays preserve one vocabulary contract and explicit ownership.

## Impact

Authorized teams would gain reusable terminology while personal records and workspace boundaries remain intact. Administrators would take on explicit access, audit and retention responsibilities. Deployments without a suitable authorization surface would continue with personal vocabulary and would not advertise shared management.

## Evidence/examples

The examples remain proposed production acceptance fixtures. The design-review draft below now contains local prerequisite implementation, regression and benchmark evidence. Production end-to-end, live-client/provider and accessibility checks remain **NOT RUN**, and no acceptance criterion is complete. Tracker observations are bounded research, not production qualification.

### Verification, rollout and unresolved decisions

The planned suite should use at least two isolated workspaces, different permission sets, conflicting aliases, personal overrides and adversarial collection payloads. It should exercise revocation at fetch, request preparation, provider egress, response arrival and insertion preparation. Include shared hints applied at STT, revocation before STT returns, and no hint-free baseline; assert zero automatic raw fallback and test explicit retranscription with permitted retained audio versus unavailable/manual recovery without it. Use fault injection for stale revisions, dropped responses, duplicate callbacks, partial writes and expired authentication. The full production acceptance procedures remain **NOT RUN**; local prototype proof is reported below. Live provider support, including any proposed Gemini field, must be established from the actual adapter/API behavior before claiming it.

Proposed target, with refreshed local prerequisite measurements below and production qualification pending: resolving and validating a maximum-sized authorized collection should take p95 below 50 ms on a documented reference service, excluding authentication/network and model latency. Report those excluded times separately. Add allocation and quota measurements, a no-shared-terms baseline and repeated revoke/reconnect trials. Negative tests should demonstrate that guessed IDs and a stale cached snapshot cannot obtain protected hints. Live tests should cover actual collection management, two concurrent editors, accessible conflict resolution and authorized/unauthorized provider routes.

Roll out read-only selection over P03 first, then scoped management, import/export and provider-specific optimizations after evidence. A feature switch should disable shared overlays without deleting personal dictionaries or collections. Rollback must prevent older clients from reactivating unknown versions. Recommended defaults are explicit selection, personal override precedence, fresh authorization and no automatic term learning. Maintainer decisions remain: actual authorization/store ownership, permission mapping, audit retention, final limits, provider field support and whether a future offline lease is acceptable.

### Sources and duplicate-search record

- [OpenClaw issue #191109](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191109), read November 25, 2026: adjacent transcription-hint request; no shared-management or verified Gemini-support claim is inferred.
- [Bounded shared-dictionary tracker search](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues?q=is%3Aopen+%22shared+dictionary%22): no direct open match was returned in the checked results; recheck broader terminology and current PRs before filing.
- P03 local draft (coordinated proposal) and M11 local draft (coordinated proposal): proposed dependency contracts, not upstream issue/PR identifiers.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes: the design-review draft is https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205820, from `CompleteDotTech:feat/dictation-shared-dictionaries`. It identifies all unverified criteria and required owner decisions. This issue remains open until the complete agreed scope is satisfied.

## Additional information

Suggested label: `enhancement`. Local IDs in this package are planning references, not GitHub issue numbers. The exact API/config names and implementation base require maintainer review; the intended behavior, defaults and outstanding decisions are documented above.


## Current integration findings and requested design acceptance

The existing Talk transcription relay already owns provider session publication and live request authority. The current source has no accepted P03 personal-vocabulary schema or M11 refinement contract. OpenClaw operator/project grants are collaboration controls within a trusted Gateway; they must not be silently reinterpreted as a new confidential collection membership system.

Before shared collections can be enabled, please confirm the appropriate existing authorization scope and read/edit/manage/export mapping, vocabulary storage ownership and retention, the P03 vocabulary contract, and the narrow Talk/SDK integration. Deployments without that accepted mapping must report shared vocabulary unavailable. Preparation will keep scope enforcement explicit and will not introduce an identity provider, shadow role database, automatic learning, or new transcript store.

Related: #191109 for hint transport only. This issue covers the distinct shared dictionary lifecycle and does not supersede or close that request. Live provider, accessibility and production integration evidence remains pending. Local prerequisite implementation and measurements are now reported against the draft's committed source, as summarized below.


## Execution status and design-review draft

<!-- m06-design-review-draft:205820 -->

The concrete proposal is [draft PR #205820](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205820), using the authorized fork branch. Its body records the exact published head/base, all twelve ACs, commands, evidence and remaining gates. The earlier [fork-local review #1](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/pull/1) is superseded by the upstream draft. Publication requests design review; it does not record design acceptance, enable shared dictionaries, or request a merge.

The proposal contains bounded term validation/resolution, injected scoped collection/CAS operations, immutable snapshot leases, and an optional existing Talk publication guard. Four new tests exercise actual retained V2 workers for concurrent editors, atomic import rejection, persisted tombstones, final commit-admission refusal and a maximum draft/audit row. Authority remains synthetic; no production namespace, real membership mapping, public collection API/UI or shared-vocabulary provider capability is registered.

Observed local proof includes 39 vocabulary cases, four real-worker cases, and 30 existing/vocabulary relay cases. The 39 cases passed within an initially mixed command whose new worker cases failed setup in the wrong owner; the corrected worker run passed separately. All 51 existing runtime-selector cases and a separately selected complete test-file ownership audit passed. The canonical tooling type leaf, scripts type-aware lint after an explicit synchronous-GC callback repair, syntax checks, formatting and test-line allocation also passed.

The fresh maximum-bound benchmark used 20 warmups and 100 samples per operation on Linux x64 / Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C / Node 24.22.3. Combined p95 was 50.20 / 43.72 / 41.22 ms for compact / raw-cap / normalized-cap workloads. The compact case **misses** the strict below-50-ms target. Allocation volume, authentication, network/model and actual provider quotas remain unmeasured. Historical passing measurements are retained separately.

Remaining technical gates are explicit in the PR: canonical core types and core type-aware lint were killed, the full build's main bundler received SIGKILL, the production unused-file scan reports the unregistered collection service, and the full-tree scan exhausted its heap. The broader project-config suite stalled, although the focused ownership audit passed. The global docs audit reports eight failures outside the changed document. At publication, GitHub CI reports `action_required` with no jobs and the Proof check is skipped; successful metadata checks do not establish build/test proof.

**AC01–AC08 and AC10–AC12 remain PARTIAL. AC09 remains BLOCKED. No AC is marked complete.** Production migration/rollback, live provider transport, accessible clients, offline/recovery and spoken semantic qualification are not implemented or qualified by the prototype.

The requested owner decision remains:

1. Establish the common P03 vocabulary contract, M11 request/result ownership, and the smallest appropriate core/plugin/SDK integration.
2. Map collection read/edit/manage/export/provider disclosure to existing live authority, including an explicit decision on the proposed mid-utterance revocation semantics.
3. Accept the namespace/representation, audit visibility/retention, tombstones, quotas and migration/rollback contract before production registration.
4. Define the minimal Talk integration and first supported client/provider surfaces, keeping the full agreed M06 scope tracked until delivered.

issues.title: Windows: 2026.10.2 performance regression vs 2026.9.4 (startup 320s vs 55s, event loop blocked 112s per turn, pluginState.register 173s transaction)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr
labels.description: ClawSweeper does not recommend queueing a new automated fix PR for this issue.

labels.name: clawsweeper:needs-maintainer-review
labels.description: ClawSweeper marked this issue as needing maintainer review before automation.

labels.name: impact:crash-loop
labels.description: Crash, hang, restart loop, or process-level availability failure.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

issues.body:
> Nota: medido en 2026.10.2 vs 2026.9.4; no se ha verificado en 2026.10.3.

- **Fecha:** 2026-10-13
- **Equipo:** Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, Node 24.18.1, npm 11.16.0, 32 GB RAM,
  Intel Core Ultra 7 165U
- **Instalación:** npm global, Gateway como Tarea Programada, 7 agentes,
  22 plugins, canal de WhatsApp y Telegram
- **Resultado:** se volvió a 2026.9.4

## Medición

Mismo equipo, misma configuración, mismo historial, mismas bases de datos.
Tomado de `openclaw-2026-10-12.log` y `openclaw-2026-10-13.log`.

| | 2026.10.2 | 2026.9.4 |
|---|---|---|
| Arranque hasta "Listening for WhatsApp inbound" | **320–340 s** | **55 s** |
| Latencia de respuesta de WhatsApp (entrada → envío) | **142 s y 151 s** | **35.8 s** |
| Event loop bloqueado durante un turno | **112 s** | **0 s** |
| Arranques que no completaron | 1 de 6 | 0 de 2 |

## Desglose del arranque en 2026.10.2

```
startup phase: process.bootstrap        31.0 s   total=31.0 s
startup phase: state.schema-preflight    1.4 s   total=33.6 s
startup phase: config.auth               4.2 s   total=38.1 s
startup phase: startup.maintenance       3.8 s   total=46.4 s
startup phase: http.bound                0.0 s   total=54.6 s
startup phase: ready                      0.0 s   total=320.7 s
```

**266 segundos sin una sola fase instrumentada** entre `http.bound` y `ready`.
Durante ese tramo:

```
liveness heartbeat delayed: overdue=163909ms elapsed=193909ms
liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization interval=189s
```

El event loop bloqueado **193 segundos seguidos, con la CPU del sistema al 0%**.
No es contención por carga: es trabajo síncrono en el hilo principal. Medido por
hilo:

```
hilo principal   410.9 s de CPU acumulada   estado Running   88% de un nucleo
```

## La pieza medible: `pluginState.register`

```
sqlite/transaction: slow SQLite transaction hold
  operation=pluginState.register
  database=state/openclaw.sqlite
  elapsedMs=173106
```

**173 segundos reteniendo una transacción de escritura** para 4,803 filas que
pesan 3.3 MB en total. Son ~36 ms por fila, que es latencia de `fsync`: parece
que sincroniza a disco fila por fila en vez de en lote.

Reparto de esas filas:

| plugin | filas |
|---|---|
| `memory-core` | 4,143 |
| `codex` | 608 |
| `core:memory-artifact-provenance` | 44 |
| `telegram` | 8 |

**La tabla no se poda nunca**: 4,802 de 4,803 filas tienen `expires_at` nulo, y
hay 2,611 filas en namespaces llamados `short-term-recall` y
`short-term-phase-signals` acumuladas desde el 1 de agosto. Parecen una fuga.

## Latencia de un turno

```
05:13:15  Inbound message (direct, 85 chars)
05:13:27  sqlite/transaction
          ... 1 min 48 s sin una sola linea de log ...
05:15:15  host timing gap attributed to event-loop load: gap 111783ms
05:15:15  WhatsApp Web connection closed (status 408)
05:15:32  [model-fetch] response provider=deepseek
05:15:37  Sent message
```

2 minutos 22 segundos en total, de los cuales **1 minuto 52 fue el event loop
bloqueado**. El modelo respondió en 5 segundos. Y el bloqueo fue tan largo que
el canal de WhatsApp perdió la conexión con un 408 por no poder mandar el
keepalive: **el bloqueo no solo retrasa, también tira el canal**.

El mismo turno en 2026.9.4: 35.8 segundos y cero bloqueos.

## Muerte silenciosa del gateway

Un arranque de seis no completó. El proceso abortó durante la inicialización de
plugins con código de salida -1 (`4294967295` en la Tarea Programada), **sin
dejar nada**: ni apagado ordenado en el log, ni evento en el Visor de sucesos de
Windows, ni archivo en `~/.openclaw/logs/stability/`.

## Efectos colaterales del arranque lento

Cualquier supervisión externa construida contra el comportamiento de 2026.9.4
se vuelve destructiva. En esta instalación había dos vigías propios que
reiniciaban el Gateway cuando no respondía —uno tras 40 segundos, otro tras 10
minutos—. Con un arranque de 33 segundos eso era correcto; con uno de 320, los
dos mataban el Gateway antes de que terminara de arrancar, en bucle. Tres
arranques abortados consecutivos antes de identificarlo.

Sugerencia: que el Gateway exponga un estado "arrancando, no me reinicies" desde
el primer segundo, y que `openclaw gateway start` no reporte
`Gateway start timed out after 90s` como si fuera un fallo cuando el proceso
sigue arrancando correctamente.

## Peticiones

1. **Instrumentar el tramo de 266 segundos.** Sin fases ahí dentro, el operador
   no tiene forma de saber qué pasa.
2. **Escribir `pluginState.register` en lote**, no fila por fila.
3. **Podar las filas `short-term` de `plugin_state_entries`**, o darles
   `expires_at`.
4. **Que `openclaw gateway start` distinga "sigue arrancando" de "falló"**, y que
   el estado de arranque sea consultable para los supervisores.
5. **Investigar la salida -1 sin registro** durante la inicialización de plugins.

## Nota sobre volver atrás

Volver a una versión anterior requiere seis pasos, y dos de ellos no están
documentados y rompen la instalación en silencio:

- Restaurar **la base de estado y las de los agentes** (el error solo menciona
  la de estado).
- Quitar de la configuración los marcadores de `meta.migrations` que añadió la
  versión nueva, o la versión vieja rechaza la config entera.
- **Reinstalar los plugins externos en la versión del anfitrión.** Al actualizar
  se actualizan ellos y sus generaciones viejas se borran; al volver atrás
  quedan pidiendo una API que ya no existe y se omiten en silencio. Si uno de
  ellos es el proveedor del modelo principal, el agente se queda mudo y el
  síntoma no apunta a esto en absoluto.

issues.body:
## Summary

The `deep_research` portable engine never completes: a research job returns `status: "partial"` with an empty Findings/Sources section and gap "The model did not produce a complete response." for **every** configured model — the failure is independent of model tier, pointing at the portable pipeline's provider/runtime path.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), gateway + main agent, Linux
- Providers: `ollama-cloud` (glm-5.3-flash) and `openai` (OAuth, gpt-6x series); memory provider `memory-core`

## Reproduction
```
deep_research action=start with request.engine=portable, various request.model overrides
```
Three runs, three different models:

| time (CET, 2026-11-25/26) | model | usage | route.runtime | gap reported |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 22:12 | ollama-cloud/glm-5.3-flash | modelCalls=1, 782 tok | isolated-agent-runtime | "The model returned malformed JSON; no repair call was made." |
| 22:21 | openai/gpt-6.2-sol | modelCalls=1, **0** tok | unobserved | "The model did not produce a complete response." |
| 00:12 | openai/gpt-6-luna | modelCalls=1, **0** tok | unobserved | "The model did not produce a complete response." |

All jobs: `state: "partial"`, `searches: 0`, `fetches: 0`, `sources: []`, `findings: []`. The engine never reached the search/fetch stage with any model, including ones where ordinary chat, `web_search` and subagent calls work fine in the same session.

## Expected
Portable deep research should drive at least one search/fetch stage and return findings, independent of the configured chat model.

## Extra evidence
- Ordinary model calls (chat + embedded cron runs) succeed on glm-5.3-flash minutes earlier and after; an isolated subagent on the same provider also functioned the same day.
- Retained `result` payloads contain no error detail beyond the gaps above ("Call action result for the complete retained result" adds nothing).

issues.body:
Follow-up to #205337 and #205408 (R-UX2, part 2).

#205408 shows a queued input's start refusal (`OperatorRefusalError` sentence) in the session transcript, which the Control UI renders. Two things it does not do:

1. **Channel delivery.** A channel-originated queued input (including `/followup`) refused at start gets no message in the channel. Channel inbound followups register no `onQueuedFollowupReplyBatch` source delivery, and a refused input has no admitted turn to deliver through (`src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.ts` withheld branch). The sender sees nothing in the channel.
2. **Cause on the pending-input row.** Nothing stores the refusal cause, so `chat.history.pendingInputs[]` still shows the generic `policy-refused` line ("This message was blocked by a policy and did not run."). The approved option is one nullable field on `session_pending_inputs`. It needs the PostgreSQL DDL/schema handling plus a protocol field.

Acceptance: a refused queued `/followup` from Discord/Telegram shows the cause-table sentence in that channel, proven through the channel E2E skill. Whether to also persist the cause depends on whether (1) needs it. Decide that here; it is not in #205408.

issues.body:
### Summary

Since 2026.10.10, a running gateway gives you no way to add a named **token** auth profile (for example an Anthropic subscription token) to an agent. The CLI refuses while the gateway is alive, and no RPC covers the `token` profile type.

### Current behaviour (2026.11.3, also checked on 2026.11.10)

- `openclaw models auth paste-token --provider anthropic --profile-id anthropic:<name> --agent <id>` with the gateway running fails with:
  > This operation requires exclusive offline state ownership. No local mutation was attempted.
- The gateway's `models.auth*` methods are `authLogin`, `authLogout`, `authOrderSet`, `authRefresh`, `authSetApiKey` and `authStatus`. `models.authSetApiKey` accepts only `type: "api_key"`, and `models.authLogin` is the interactive wizard. None of them writes a named profile of `type: "token"`.

The only working path is therefore offline, one gateway at a time: stop the gateway, run `paste-token` for each of its agents, start it again, then call `models.authOrderSet`. On hosts with many gateways that means a downtime window per gateway (12–84 s in our measurements) every time an account is added or rotated. Any turn running at that moment gets interrupted.

### Expected

An RPC that writes or replaces a named token profile on a live gateway. Two possible shapes:
- `models.authSetApiKey` accepts `type: "token"` (with optional `expires`), or
- a dedicated method, for example `models.authSetToken { provider, profileId, token, agentId? }`.

Either should use the same state ownership the gateway already uses for `authSetApiKey`/`authOrderSet`, so the CLI `paste-token` path could route through the gateway the same way other auth mutations do.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.3 on Linux, systemd-managed gateways, `claude-cli` runtime with Anthropic subscription tokens.
- Behaviour unchanged in 2026.11.10, going by the `models.auth*` method list in the published package.

issues.body:
### Summary

A 30-day audit of production tool calls on `OpenClaw 2026.11.10` (`1a660f8`) surfaced a high failure rate on two `knowledge` plugin mutation tools:
- `knowledge_annotate`: **4 failed / 9 total (44.4% failure rate)**
- `knowledge_attach_file`: **1 failed / 2 total (50.0% failure rate)**
- *(All other 13 invoked `knowledge_*` tools succeeded 168/168 times in the same window.)*

Inspecting the exact failing tool calls alongside `extensions/knowledge/src/` and `src/agents/tool-schema-hints.ts` shows that every one of these failures was caused by avoidable tool-shape and error-message traps rather than invalid user intent or backend failures.

---

### 1. `knowledge_annotate`: Required `annotations` wrapper + sibling `entities`/`addEvidence` trap (4/9 failed)

**Source:** `extensions/knowledge/src/mutation-contract.ts` (`AnnotateInput`, lines 99–112) and `extensions/knowledge/src/model.ts` (`RecordAnnotations`, lines 75–122).

```ts
export const AnnotateInput = Type.Object(
  {
    ...target,
    annotations: RecordAnnotations, // REQUIRED, additionalProperties: false
    entities: Type.Optional(Type.Array(id, { ... })),     // TOP-LEVEL SIBLING
    addEvidence: Type.Optional(Type.Array(Evidence, ...)), // TOP-LEVEL SIBLING
  },
  { additionalProperties: false },
);
```

**Why callers repeatedly fail:**
1. **`annotations` is required even when unused.** To link a claim to entity pages (`entities`) or append evidence (`addEvidence`), the caller must pass a dummy `"annotations": {}` while placing `entities` and `addEvidence` *outside* `annotations`.
2. **Contradicts sibling tools.** `SavePage` and `CreateClaim` (`mutation-contract.ts`) spread `...RecordAnnotations.properties` flat at the top level alongside `entities`, whereas `AnnotateInput` nests `RecordAnnotations` under `annotations` while keeping `entities` and `addEvidence` at the top level.
3. **Hidden by `compactToolInputHint`.** `src/agents/tool-schema-hints.ts` renders `AnnotateInput` as:
   ```
   { annotations: { ... }; expectedHash: string; expectedRevision: number; id: string; reason: string; requestId: string; ... }
   ```
   Because required keys fill the compact hint first, optional top-level `entities` and `addEvidence` are collapsed into `...` while `annotations: { ... }` is prominently displayed.

**Observed production evidence (all 4 failures identical):**
- 3 failures in one batch (`2026-11-25 22:40 UTC`) and 1 failure (`2026-11-26 00:46 UTC`) passed `annotations: { entities: [...] }` (and once `addEvidence` inside `annotations`).
- All 4 were rejected with:
  `Invalid arguments for tool "openclaw:knowledge:knowledge_annotate": annotations: must not have additional properties: "entities"` (and `"addEvidence"`).
- All 4 succeeded immediately on retry when rewritten as `{ ..., annotations: {}, entities: [...], addEvidence: [...] }`.

---

### 2. `knowledge_attach_file`: Opaque workspace boundary rejection (1/2 failed)

**Source:** `extensions/knowledge/src/attachment-file.ts` (lines 30–50).

```ts
const workspace = context.tool.fsPolicy?.root ?? context.tool.workspaceDir;
...
if (!opened.ok) {
  throw new Error(
    "Source file must be a readable regular file inside the authorized workspace without aliases.",
  );
}
```

**Observed production evidence (`2026-11-25 22:39 UTC`):**
- In a session bound to a project directory, the caller staged an evidence file under the agent's default workspace and passed that path.
- `knowledge_attach_file` rejected it with the generic error above without indicating *which* workspace root is authorized for the session (project cwd vs. agent workspace) or whether the failure was due to workspace mismatch, missing file, or symlink/hardlink alias.
- Moving the file into the session's project directory succeeded 8 seconds later.

---

### 3. Broader tool-shape inconsistencies across the 38 `knowledge_*` tools

Auditing all 38 tools in `extensions/knowledge/src/contract.ts` and `*contract*.ts` highlights several structural patterns that increase schema-guessing errors as usage of the broader toolset grows:

1. **Mixed `camelCase` and `snake_case` inside the same tool inputs:**
   - `AnnotateInput`: `requestId`, `expectedRevision`, `expectedHash`, `expectedVaultId`, `addEvidence` alongside `record_class`, `source_page`, `source_event`, `attribution_confidence`.
   - `ClaimInput` / `SavePage` / `RememberInput`: `requestId`, `expectedOntologyFingerprint`, `expectedVaultId` alongside `claim_kind`, `assertion_origin`, `occurred_at`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, `expires_at`, `due_at`, `subject_hint`, `infer_subject`.
   - `Evidence`: `mediaType` alongside `start_line`, `end_line`.
2. **Three different field names for the same evidence array concept across mutation tools:**
   - `SavePage` uses `attachments`
   - `CreateClaim`, `MergeInput`, `ExtractSectionInput` use `evidence`
   - `AnnotateInput` uses `addEvidence`
3. **Confusable upload vs. download tool names:**
   - `knowledge_attach` (base64 upload), `knowledge_attach_file` (workspace file upload), and `knowledge_attachment` (download). The descriptions currently have to shout `DOWNLOAD retained bytes: use knowledge_attachment, not knowledge_attach (upload)` to compensate for the naming collision.
4. **Large surface area + verbose descriptions:**
   - 38 separate deferred tools in one plugin with descriptions routinely 500–1,000+ characters, increasing reliance on `compactToolInputHint` summaries where optional top-level parameters get truncated behind `...`.

---

### Suggested Fixes

1. **`knowledge_annotate` (highest impact):**
   - Make `annotations` **optional** (validate in the handler that at least one of `annotations`, `entities`, or `addEvidence` is provided).
   - Either flatten `RecordAnnotations` properties to top level (matching `SavePage` and `CreateClaim`) **or** explicitly document in the description that `entities` and `addEvidence` are top-level siblings outside `annotations` (and consider accepting/normalizing or clearly hinting when they are placed inside `annotations`).
2. **`knowledge_attach_file`:**
   - Differentiate rejection causes in the error message (outside authorized workspace root vs. symlink/hardlink alias vs. not found/unreadable) and state the expected root context (e.g., session workspace/project root) so recovery is deterministic on the first try.
3. **Cross-tool ergonomics (follow-up):**
   - Audit naming/casing consistency (`snake_case` vs `camelCase`, `evidence` vs `attachments` vs `addEvidence`) and consider clearer upload/download naming or tool consolidation where operations overlap.

### Environment
- OpenClaw `2026.11.10` (`1a660f8`)
- macOS 27.0 (arm64)
- Evidence source: 30-day `transcript_events` (`toolResult`) audit across 470,804 tool calls (179 `knowledge_*` calls).

issues.body:
Reported from a live SQLite→Postgres cutover (7 stores → PG 18.7) on a long-lived agent: OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), Node 26.13.1, 4+ months of session transcripts, including files over 500 MB.

---


**Symptom.** `openclaw memory index --agent <id>` fails deterministically:

```
Memory index failed (agent): Error [ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY]: Worker terminated due to
reaching memory limit: JS heap out of memory
[task=sessionTranscript.session-entries admittedInputBytes=115220 exchanges=86 stage=running]
```

Retrying with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=16384` fails identically — the cap is
set via `worker_threads` `resourceLimits`, which overrides process flags.

**Repro.** A session corpus containing any transcript file whose size (as a JS string,
i.e. ~2× UTF-8 bytes for ASCII-heavy content) approaches 512 MB old-gen heap. On our
box: a 518 MB subagent session (56,825 events, incl. one 23 MB toolResult carrying 8
base64 images) and a 360 MB dashboard session. The rebuild indexes everything smaller
fine, then dies at the first oversized file and never recovers on retry (same file,
same result).

**Root cause (read from dist of 2026.11.10).**

- `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-read-pools.ts`:
  `SESSION_TRANSCRIPT_WORKER_LIMITS = { maxOldGenerationSizeMb: 512, maxYoungGenerationSizeMb: 16 }`
  — hard-coded, used by the session-transcript read pools (history + session-entries batch).
- The session-entry renderer loads the **entire** transcript into one string before
  parsing line-by-line (`buildSessionEntryFromSource` → `readRegularFile(...).buffer
  .toString("utf-8")` → `renderSessionEntry`). 518 MB file ⇒ ~1 GB string ⇒ OOM on a
  512 MB old-gen isolate, before any useful work.

**Impact.** Memory indexing permanently stalls at the first oversized session; every
larger session stays unindexed, and history/context reads for those sessions share the
same pool limits.

**Suggested fix.** Stream transcript files line-by-line instead of whole-file reads
(the parser already iterates lines); optionally make worker heap limits configurable.

**Local workaround (applied, carried patch).** 512→4096 MB old-gen (16→256 young) in the
9 dist bundle variants of the session-transcript pools; index then rebuilt clean
(3,816 files / 40,225 chunks, including both oversized sessions). Re-applied after each
update.
