issues.body:
## Summary

Add a configurable cleanup policy that can remove non-semantic hesitations and accidental repetitions from dictation while preserving meaningful words, deliberate repetition, dialect, quotes and corrections. The output should read naturally without requiring the user to speak as if reading a script. The critical requirement is that cleanup remain faithful: “I, I disagree” can become “I disagree,” while “I really, really disagree” must retain its emphasis.

## Problem to solve

This is a proposal for the user's dictated text, not filtering an assistant's prose or removing narration from agent responses. Some speech fillers are meaningful in context. A token list that always deletes “like,” “well,” “so,” or “you know” would damage ordinary sentences. A stutter or accent is not an error to erase automatically. The default must favor preserving intent over maximizing a cleanup percentage.

## Proposed solution

### Scope and dependencies

M11 (coordinated design; not a filed issue or implemented dependency) owns the refinement request and final candidate; this feature supplies one policy and one set of semantic guardrails within it. M03 (coordinated design; not a filed issue or implemented dependency) resolves actual revisions. M02 must not delete a correction marker before M03 can interpret it. M01 (coordinated design; not a filed issue or implemented dependency) may repair punctuation left by an accepted removal, and M05 (coordinated design; not a filed issue or implemented dependency) may choose the cleanup setting. None may independently re-run a model.

The first delivery covers English hesitation patterns plus explicitly declared locale extensions. Translation, grammar rewriting, shortening long sentences, content moderation, automatic censorship, speaker identification and medical interpretation of speech are excluded. No inference about disability, confidence, credibility or emotional state is stored or reported.

### Policy and expected behavior

Provide **Off** and **Conservative** modes initially. An aggressive mode should be a later separately evaluated feature because its error tradeoff is materially different. Existing users retain current behavior. In Conservative mode:

1. Remove an isolated hesitation such as “um” or “uh” only where the available transcript/acoustic metadata and sentence context support a non-semantic reading. When acoustic timing is absent, the system must not fabricate it; require stronger text context or retain the token.
2. Collapse a repeated function word or aborted exact restart only when the second segment clearly continues the same construction. Preserve purposeful repetition, rhetorical devices, quoted speech, lyrics, word lists and code identifiers.
3. Preserve lexical occurrences: “I like this,” “the well is dry,” “so that it works,” “say the word um,” and a project named `UM` are not disfluencies. Honor literal mode and protected ranges before cleanup.
4. Keep every negation, contrast, uncertainty qualifier, numeric value, unit, date, name and instruction polarity. “Maybe,” “approximately,” “not,” and “I think” must not disappear simply to make the statement sound stronger.
5. Do not automatically remove a word merely because its recognizer confidence is low. Low confidence may reflect a proper name, non-native pronunciation, background noise or dialect. Preserve or mark uncertainty through the shared review mechanism.
6. If an edit could change the speaker's stance, keep the original. The user may manually request a separate rewrite after reviewing the draft; that does not justify broad cleanup in this mode.

#### Authored examples

| Input | Conservative requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `um please call me tomorrow` | May produce `Please call me tomorrow.` after punctuation. |
| `I I need the invoice` with an unambiguous restart | May collapse the repeated `I`; keep the rest. |
| `this is very very important` | Preserve both occurrences unless the user explicitly selects a separate stronger editing mode. |
| `I like the blue one` | Preserve `like`. |
| `Well the well is dry` | Preserve the lexical second `well`; retain the first when its discourse meaning is uncertain. |
| `we should not not without approval` | Do not collapse the repeated negation into affirmative meaning; return unchanged or review-required. |
| `fifteen no fifty` | Leave correction resolution to M03; do not treat `no` as filler. |
| `quote um I do not know end quote` in literal quotation mode | Preserve the quoted hesitation. |
| `the variable is um_count` | Preserve the identifier exactly. |

These outcomes define invariant tests rather than a claim that any current provider achieves them.

### Shared transform contract

The request should carry raw transcript/revision, cleanup policy, protected spans, available locale/timing metadata and an immutable effective profile. A proposed removal record identifies the source range, category (`hesitation` or `exact_restart`), evidence available and reason. Category names are proposed contract vocabulary, not shipped API.

M11 must keep the immutable raw transcript separate from the candidate. Removal edits must reference the original token/range identity so subsequent punctuation does not shift what was removed. Candidate validation should check protected-span preservation, lexical coverage and unchanged critical tokens. Do not rely on one model checking its own answer as the sole correctness control.

Semantic edits should be decided jointly with M03 where necessary, then validated as one coherent plan. There is no requirement for a separate “filler model” before a “correction model.” If source alignment or ordering is ambiguous, return the raw segment. Partial transcripts may be revised in the preview; only finalized, validated text can become an insertion candidate.

An accepted removal applies to this draft only. It must not train a user-specific speech profile or auto-add a global rule such as “always remove well.” Personal style learning would require a separately authorized preference workflow. Explicit saved settings can select Off or Conservative, but should never encode sensitive inferences about the user's speech.

### Lifecycle, recovery and concurrency

The capture/session revision and output revision remain under M11. A user edit during refinement invalidates stale edits to that range. A second utterance can append through the existing ordered queue, but an earlier late cleanup cannot rewrite a newer draft. Escape, mode change, target change and session disposal cancel pending cleanup through the same abort signal.

Refinement failure must retain the raw recognized text. When the user opts to insert raw text, the old refinement request is retired; it must not overwrite that committed text later. Retry is explicit and reuses captured text or retained audio only under the retention policy already selected by the capture owner. M02 adds no audio file or retry buffer of its own.

Undo should restore the complete insertion transaction when that adapter supports reliable undo. A review view may display removed ranges transiently, but a “restore removals” control acts only on the current unsent draft unless M10 can safely replace an owned committed range. No global find-and-replace is allowed.

### Configuration, privacy and accessibility

Recommended configuration is a versioned cleanup enum in the common dictation profile, with an explicit per-session override. Existing installations keep cleanup disabled. A setting change is effective on the next session; an intentional reprocess operation snapshots the new setting and creates a new preparation revision.

Do not log removed text, raw speech, uncertainty scores tied to identity or identifiable before/after examples by default. Diagnostics may count validation categories and elapsed time, subject to existing telemetry policy, without serializing user content. Cloud refinement is governed by M11/P04 route consent; this feature never opts a local-only session into a remote model.

The control label should explain that conservative cleanup may retain ambiguous words. Review must be available by keyboard and screen reader. Do not interrupt dictation with a question for every “um”; use a single final review state for genuinely ambiguous destructive edits. Display disabled/unsupported states with readable labels and preserve normal focus.

Proposed, unmeasured stage budget: policy resolution plus deterministic deletion validation should add no more than 25 ms p95 for 2,000 characters on agreed reference hardware. Model work shares M11's total deadline. Memory usage must scale with the bounded input and edit list, not accumulate across sessions; include a repeated-session retention check in qualification.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **M02-AC01:** Off preserves current output and Conservative is opt-in; no hidden aggressive rewriting is enabled.
- [ ] **M02-AC02:** Golden cases remove clearly non-semantic hesitations/restarts while lexical uses, emphasis and quotations remain.
- [ ] **M02-AC03:** Negation, uncertainty, numbers, units and protected strings never disappear in the adversarial invariant corpus.
- [ ] **M02-AC04:** M03 correction markers and source ranges remain available until the joint semantic plan is validated.
- [ ] **M02-AC05:** Missing timing, unsupported locales and low-confidence tokens produce preservation or review, not invented metadata.
- [ ] **M02-AC06:** Streaming revisions, retries and late callbacks cannot duplicate insertion or rewrite a newer draft.
- [ ] **M02-AC07:** Raw text remains recoverable after timeout, rejection or cancellation; choosing raw retires the candidate.
- [ ] **M02-AC08:** Review and policy controls are usable with keyboard/screen reader and do not shame or classify the user's speech.
- [ ] **M02-AC09:** Same-state settings upgrade/disable is safe, no new transcript/audio storage appears, and route restrictions remain effective.
- [ ] **M02-AC10:** Report stage overhead, memory bounds and removal precision separately from deletion volume.

### Platform and offline boundary

The transform contract is independent of OS insertion. A desktop, web or mobile client may expose it only through its qualified M11 request/review path; external-field insertion still depends on M10. A headless caller receives a text/result value, not desktop control. Initial support must name actual tested clients and locales rather than imply universal availability.

Deterministic operations may continue offline when recognized text is already available. Model-assisted behavior follows the selected route and locality policy. If the required route is unavailable, retain available recognized text and disclose the missing refinement; do not silently use a cloud service. This does not promise offline speech recognition or recover words a recognizer never returned.

## Alternatives considered

A global filler-word blacklist would remove meaningful words such as “like” and “well.” Deleting every repeated token would damage emphasis and quoted text. Always preserving recognizer output remains an explicit supported choice, but does not address conservative cleanup. A second model request dedicated to cleanup would duplicate M11 ownership and latency.

## Impact

Users who want cleaned prose would avoid editing obvious hesitations while retaining uncertainty, dialect and emphasis. Literal and cleanup-off paths would remain available. Evaluation must prioritize false deletions and protected meaning rather than maximizing the amount of removed speech.

## Evidence/examples

The examples define the requested acceptance fixtures. Current observed implementation and qualification results are recorded in the implementation status section below. Tracker observations are bounded research, not proof that a capability is absent.

### Verification and quality measurement

Use a balanced, consented corpus with a high proportion of negative controls. Include dialectal and non-native English examples, code-switched utterances, quoted dialog, rhetorical repetition, word lists, hesitation-like names, short commands and sentences where deleting one negation changes the action. Annotators should label “safe remove,” “must retain,” and “ambiguous retain” rather than treating every token as removable or essential.

Report precision of removed spans and critical-token preservation. The proposed launch threshold is zero critical semantic changes in the mandatory adversarial suite, plus a maintainer-approved removal-precision threshold after corpus selection. Zero fixture failures does not prove a zero real-world error rate. Do not optimize for the largest percentage of deleted words.

Add shared-pipeline tests with correction, punctuation, profile and snippet features enabled together. Reproduce failure on the pre-feature route only for the requested missing cleanup behavior; do not label the base “broken” when it correctly preserves ambiguous speech. Run real microphone/provider samples and clearly separate recognition errors from cleanup errors. A provider can omit fillers before OpenClaw receives text; Off cannot restore words it never received.

### Sources and audit note

- [Open issues containing filler words](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues?q=is%3Aopen+%22filler+words%22) and [open PR search](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+%22filler+words%22), checked November 25, 2026. The bounded issue search surfaced [#151191](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/151191), a spoken-confirmation language problem, not a dictation disfluency-removal implementation. It must not be cited as coverage of this feature.
- [Unicode text segmentation](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/) is the boundary reference for non-destructive range handling. Semantic retention rules above are this proposal's requirements.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself. A focused implementation is being prepared on a dedicated contributor-fork branch. The PR will remain draft until its required evidence and upstream design decisions are satisfied.

## Additional information

### Rollout and decisions

Implement pure policy/validation first, then the shared model instruction and preview affordance, then opt-in qualification. Rollback disables cleanup with no history rewrite. Keep the raw candidate available until the chosen insertion completes or is discarded under the owner's retention policy.

Maintainers need to choose the first locale set, annotated corpus ownership and launch precision threshold. Recommended resolved choices are conservative-only initial behavior, protected correction/negation tokens, no speech-trait learning and unchanged behavior for existing users.

### Current implementation placement and requested design review

Inspected current main at `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c`. The intended first client is the Control UI's existing composer dictation owner and ordered transcript queue; no desktop insertion claim is made. The existing Control UI plugin composer API can propose/set drafts but has no dictation transform/capture metadata contract. Extending the existing app owner avoids replacing its capture and publication lifecycle.

The initial path is deterministic and local after recognition, with zero additional refinement-provider requests. Proposed private edit records use version 1, original UTF-16 half-open ranges, and opt-in English only. Proposed saved preference is versioned Off/Conservative in the existing browser settings owner; no new transcript/audio history, remote route, public RPC, or plugin SDK export is proposed. These choices are offered for maintainer review, not represented as accepted upstream design.

Related: #108246 closed the local transcription recipe; its final maintainer comment explicitly leaves built-in glossary/cleanup as a separate product request. #200235 supplies the existing ordered pending transcript owner. Neither #151191 nor spoken agent-confirmation work is covered or closed by this feature.

The implementation will retain an acceptance ledger and truthful NOT RUN entries for physical microphone/provider and screen-reader evidence when unavailable. Please review the app-owner placement, first English policy, saved preference shape, and removal-precision release gate. This issue remains open until all accepted criteria are satisfied.


## Implementation status — November 25, 2026

The private Control UI prototype is published as **draft PR [#205789](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205789)** from the user's verified fork. It is **not accepted or merge-ready**. This issue remains open and its acceptance criteria above remain unchanged.

- Immediate physical base: `openclaw/openclaw` commit `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c`.
- Local task branch: `feat/dictation-conservative-cleanup`.
- Tested/reviewed local head: `b632d7829aa401eacb23b3c863ad09183cf880f8`. Published head: [`aae4919e4744a791d7edf4e3ad94aa841af0a877`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/aae4919e4744a791d7edf4e3ad94aa841af0a877), in three focused commits. Both have the identical complete source tree `96ef3028a13186996dab4e19eba55d480857a652`; recovery/publication changed commit metadata only.
- Fork branch: [`CompleteDotTech:feat/dictation-conservative-cleanup`](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/tree/feat/dictation-conservative-cleanup). Draft PR #205789 is open with maintainer edits enabled and no source merge conflicts at the observed head. No product CI pass is claimed.
- The preparation contract is a minimal private proposal. No accepted common M11 contract or maintainer design endorsement is claimed.

The prototype keeps Off as default, admits explicit English Conservative, independently validates bounded original-source removal ranges, preserves correction and critical-word evidence, and stages one transient raw/candidate review through the existing dictation and unsent-draft owners. It adds no cleanup-provider request, transcript history, audio buffer, public RPC, or plugin SDK export. Restoration is limited to the unchanged owned unsent draft. Conservative permits one pending review; Off retains the existing ordered multiple-recording behavior.

### Current acceptance evidence

| Criteria | Observed coverage at the local head | Remaining qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC01–AC03 | Focused settings/owner/invariant tests pass; balanced corpus has 36/36 expected candidates, 13/13 accepted spans correct under the authored oracle, zero false-deletion cases. | Actual browser flow and broader corpus/precision acceptance remain open. |
| AC04 | Correction markers and original-source maps are retained and validated. | Joint enabled correction/punctuation/snippet/profile plans through an accepted common owner are not qualified; these handlers are absent from the prototype. |
| AC05 | Missing/invalid timing, low confidence, unsupported locale, mixed script, provisional source, and sequencing boundaries pass local tests. | Real provider/source provenance evidence is not run. |
| AC06–AC07 | Finality, generation retirement, retry, edit-and-undo, raw-before-late-result, authorization changes, bounded recovery, direct publication, and unchanged-draft restoration pass focused tests. | No broader concurrent Conservative preparation claim. Oversized or revoked source is not retained for automatic recovery; uncertain attempted writes are exposed without replay. |
| AC08 | Neutral labels and native review controls are implemented. | Browser suite failed in missing-Chromium setup: six scenarios skipped, zero assertions/screenshots. Pinned browser installation returned HTTP 403. Real screen reader is NOT RUN. |
| AC09 | Same-state settings upgrade/disable, invalid values, Gateway scope, capture authorization and routing boundaries pass local tests. No new cleanup content storage or provider route. | Preference scope/common provenance design is pending acceptance; browser upgrade/disable qualification remains blocked. |
| AC10 | Named 2,000-character processor workload: cold p95 7.785 ms (N=5); warm p95 1.566 ms, p99 3.100 ms, max 27.764 ms (N=5,000). Forced-GC 10,000-session loop: final heap −5,208 B, RSS +8,519,680 B. Removal volume 37/939 corpus characters, reported separately from precision. | This excludes settings-storage normalization, DOM/capture-owner retention, recognition and total provider latency. Physical microphone/provider timing is NOT RUN. |

### Checks and review

The final focused run passed **180 tests in six files**. Changed UI lint, repaired benchmark/Knip-entry lint, i18n verification, code/docs format, test-line budget, line-cap budget, and whitespace checks passed. UI lint retained one warning on an unchanged Sidechat line.

Required broad checks remain incomplete: UI typecheck attempts exited 137 before diagnostics; production UI build exited 137 after module transforms; the production Knip child was SIGKILLed and the wrapper stopped without an unused-file verdict. These are not passes. Seven fork workflows now require maintainer approval. The CI run has zero jobs, the required `openclaw/ci-gate` status is expected, and Proof is skipped/on request. PR context-and-evidence passed; administrative checks do not establish product build/test qualification.

Independent review found and resolved an uncertain-publication replay race, authorization sampled too late, and an oversized-source cancellation recovery bug. Affected boundary tests passed after repair. No local ClawSweeper tool run is claimed.

The [automated issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205635#issuecomment-7178237401) requests preparation ownership, preference scope and removal-precision decisions before acceptance. Parallel drafts now include [M01 #205788](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205788), [M03 #205794](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205794), [M04 #205791](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205791), and [M05 #205792](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205792). None is an accepted implementation parent; common owner/policy consolidation and enabled-together proof remain open. M05's proposed `users.prefs` scope differs from this private browser/Gateway preference and remains an explicit design decision. No human acceptance of these proposals was established.

The implementation should remain draft pending required checks, actual accessibility/visual and microphone/provider evidence, integration qualification, and maintainer design/corpus decisions. No adjacent issue is closed by this prototype.


### Published evidence and current unblock

[Download the qualification evidence ZIP](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35447695/openclaw-m02-publication-evidence.zip) (99,267 bytes; SHA-256 `18bc7ab129720bf728a4a45d9f1faccd19339195e21bcf540d6dfe8daefce429`). It retains raw passing/failed/incomplete logs, exact commands, all original ACs, corpus and latency/memory results, source/review binding, and publication metadata. It contains no real microphone sample or browser screenshots.

Upstream maintainer approval of [CI run 45766368456](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45766368456) and the other pending fork workflows is needed before product CI can execute. The full local typecheck/build/unused-file and actual client/device proof gaps remain as documented. This issue stays open; publication does not satisfy those gates or supply maintainer design acceptance.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (release), CLI install, macOS 27.2.1, Apple Silicon, **16 GB RAM**
- LM Studio 0.4.28+2, llama.cpp runtime 2.73.0
- Embedding model: `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` Q8_0 GGUF (639 MB), model-reported `max_context_length = 32768`
- `memory.search`: `provider: lmstudio`, `model: text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b`
- No `models.providers.lmstudio.models` entries existed at first (default config)

## Symptom

Memory indexing fails on every attempt:

```
Memory index failed (lily): lmstudio embeddings failed
(model: text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b:2, batch size: 52) (400): Model is unloaded.
```

LM Studio server log shows a ~20 GB allocation for a 639 MB model:

```
[WARNING] Batch size (2048) is < context length (8192). Resetting batch size to context length
ggml_metal_buffer_init: error: failed to allocate buffer, size = 10371.12 MiB
ggml_gallocr_reserve_n_impl: failed to allocate MTL0 buffer of size 22194684928
llama_init_from_model: failed to initialize the context: failed to allocate compute pp buffers
```

## Apparent cause

1. `resolveEmbeddingPreloadContextLength` returns `undefined` when the configured model has no matching `models.providers.lmstudio.models` entry.
2. The provider then requests a 64000-token context, clamped to the model's advertised `32768`.
3. LM Studio loads embedding models with `batch = context length`, so a 32768 context asks for ~20.7 GB of buffers — impossible on a 16 GB host.

So a missing catalog entry silently turns into the largest context the model advertises.

## Workaround that works

1. Load with CPU and a small context:
```bash
lms load text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b --gpu off --context-length 1024
```
2. Add an explicit catalog entry so OpenClaw stops requesting the maximum:
```json5
{ models: { providers: { lmstudio: { models: [
  { id: "text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b",
    name: "Qwen3 Embedding 0.6B",
    contextTokens: 1024,
    contextWindow: 32768,
    input: ["text"] }
] } } } }
```

With that, the requested context becomes `min(1024, 32768) = 1024`, the existing instance is reused, and indexing completes (`Memory index updated: 106 files indexed`).

## Suggestions

- Lower the embedding fallback context (e.g. 8192) instead of relying on the model maximum, or skip preload entirely when no catalog entry matches.
- When the load fails, include the requested context length in the error (today the message is only "Model is unloaded", which points nowhere).
- Document that embedding models on memory-constrained hosts need an explicit `contextTokens` entry — the current docs only say "lower the model's `contextTokens`" after the failure has already happened.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug. Observed once, with no known last-good revision.

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

I started **Learn from Memory** with `MEMORY.md` and daily notes selected. The scribe found 122 files totaling 4,112,467 bytes, read `MEMORY.md`, then stopped without reading a daily note or saving anything. The Scribes tab offered **Start again**, but there was no saved position to resume from.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an agent with writable private Knowledge, a `MEMORY.md`, and a substantial set of `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` notes. The observed archive contained 121 daily notes. This is the size of the observed case, not a known threshold.
2. Open **Knowledge → Scribes → Learn from Memory**, select both sources and start the import with the generated prompt.
3. Open the scribe conversation and compare the notes actually read and the Knowledge writes with the result on the Scribes tab. The model's decision to stop may vary between runs.

### Expected behavior

Starting an import once should let it work through the selected files even if that takes multiple turns. If it has to stop, it should report what was reviewed and be able to continue from the first unfinished file without changing the source notes or duplicating saved items.

### Actual behavior and logs

Knowledge reported `ready` with writes enabled. The scribe listed the notes and summed their sizes from file metadata, then successfully read `MEMORY.md`. It made no duplicate lookup or Knowledge write before reporting that the archive was more than it could review in one turn. The provider returned `response.completed` with `stopReason: "stop"`. No tool rejected a read or write, and the provider did not report a context overflow. The conversation ended normally while the Scribes tab showed **Failing**. Memory was unchanged.

### Environment

OpenClaw Git checkout `b22df8b94835e90191a36cf8496ad2cdffee7223` on macOS arm64, using `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` through ClawRouter. The relevant scribe code and skill were unchanged on upstream `main` at `1a660f87c7f0e187cb87cbe52a9e86f646a135f9`. That comparison was against source, not a second live import.

### Implementation evidence and test case

The [generated prompt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b22df8b94835e90191a36cf8496ad2cdffee7223/extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-catalog.ts#L508-L537) requires the work to happen “in this turn.” The [start handler](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b22df8b94835e90191a36cf8496ad2cdffee7223/extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-actions.ts#L46-L65) sends one chat message. The [Memory instructions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b22df8b94835e90191a36cf8496ad2cdffee7223/extensions/knowledge/skills/knowledge-ingest/references/learning.md#L39-L75) check for duplicate facts but do not checkpoint reviewed files, unlike the conversation scribe directly above them. The [restart test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b22df8b94835e90191a36cf8496ad2cdffee7223/extensions/knowledge/src/scribes-view.test.ts#L819-L847) expects a new attempt in the existing conversation.

The existing scribe state and view suites passed (56 tests). A useful regression case would use a synthetic archive larger than one batch, interrupt after the first verified batch, then check that the import resumes without duplication and reports **Done** only when every selected file has been accounted for.

issues.body:
## Summary

Let a person review explicit spoken corrections inside the current unsent dictation capture. For example, “Meet on Tuesday, sorry, Wednesday” should offer “Meet on Wednesday” when the source target is unique. Amounts, negation, conditions, quoted words and ambiguous names must remain recoverable.

This is a feature/design proposal with a published draft implementation: [#205794](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205794), from `CompleteDotTech:feat/dictation-spoken-self-correction`. It is not a claim of maintainer approval, recognition accuracy, or complete platform qualification.

## Proposed behavior

Corrections start **Off**, including existing installations. **Explicit corrections (English)** is an opt-in browser preference. **Literal** applies to one recording and preserves correction words as recognized text.

The first grammar is deliberately bounded:

- Adjacent weekday or numeric replacement using “no”, “sorry”, or “actually”.
- A final “change John to James” request only when the current capture contains exactly one preceding John.
- “scratch that last sentence” only when this capture owns a complete, bounded last sentence.
- “restart this sentence” only for the capture's current unfinished sentence and bounded replacement clause.

Every changed candidate requires review in the initial implementation. Show the original, proposed text, and affected before/after spans; provide **Keep original**, **Accept correction**, and **Cancel**, without a timer. Acceptance inserts into the unsent draft and never sends the message automatically. Missing timing is disclosed rather than invented.

| Recognized text or context | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Meet on Tuesday sorry Wednesday | Offer Meet on Wednesday. |
| The total is fifteen no fifty dollars | Offer fifty dollars; retain currency and transient edit evidence. |
| Do not send it Tuesday sorry Wednesday | Retain Do not send; change only the day. |
| Tell John that John should call change John to James | Retain/review; do not guess which John. |
| He said quote no Wednesday end quote | Preserve the quote. |
| Tuesday, no Wednesday, actually Thursday | One stable-source correction ending in Thursday. |
| Scratch that last sentence with no owned sentence | Preserve existing field content and report no target. |
| Actually open the browser and buy it | Dictated text only, with zero tool dispatch. |

Unsupported or uncertain grammar preserves recognized words. Provider-normalized text is used as returned; earlier words and correction events must never be fabricated.

## Ownership and integration

The scope is the current unsent capture, not past messages, external documents, another utterance, or undoing agent actions. Source inspected at `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c` already has `ComposerDictationOwner`, `ComposerDictationSession`, and the single `ComposerDictationCommits` insertion queue. The proposal extends these owners.

A private transient plan binds the actual capture token and source revision to UTF-16 ranges, grapheme boundaries, source span identifiers, trigger ranges, replacements, categories, protected spans and grammar version. Recognizer IDs and sequence metadata are retained only when supplied; callback arrival time is not acoustic timing. Wrong ownership, duplicate/reordered metadata, cross-speaker evidence, overlap and stale revisions fail closed.

Use one semantic plan before any later surface punctuation. No filler pass may erase correction markers first. No additional model, recognizer, insertion queue, context collector, provider routing, transcript log or tool authority is introduced. Dictation retains the existing transcription-only / brain-none route. No accepted general refinement, filler-removal or punctuation implementation was identified in the bounded source audit; the private foundation is not a claim that those separate capabilities are complete.

Draft edits (including equal-text edits), a new capture, target/session/account/client changes, mode changes and cancellation must prevent stale writes. Disconnect failures should retain recognized text for local recovery within the same authorized context. Revoked or changed context must not carry text into another destination. Choosing original consumes the pending candidate.

## Preferences, privacy and resource bounds

Proposed persistence: the existing browser-local, Gateway-scoped settings owner, with a versioned English opt-in. Missing, malformed, disabled and unsupported future settings fall back to Off. Literal and before/after text are transient. Disabling correction preserves existing drafts; rollback does not attempt historical external edits.

Proposed bounds are 10,000 UTF-16 code units, 32 final edits, eight revisions per chain, and 256 protected/metadata spans. Measure validator p95 against the proposed 50 ms target on named hardware; do not infer semantic correctness from speed. The transform is local and does not promise offline recognition.

## Acceptance and qualification

- [ ] **M03-AC01:** Off, Explicit and transient Literal are documented and preserve existing defaults.
- [ ] **M03-AC02:** Unique replacement/retraction/restart fixtures produce intended content with a valid source plan.
- [ ] **M03-AC03:** Ambiguous references, quotes, literal strings and ordinary negations are preserved or reviewed.
- [ ] **M03-AC04:** Chains and overlaps are bounded, deterministic, and applied at most once.
- [ ] **M03-AC05:** Semantic ordering preserves correction evidence and protected tokens without extra rewrite calls; actual optional M01/M02 integration is distinguished from its absence.
- [ ] **M03-AC06:** Edits, target/session/mode changes and cancellation prevent stale patches and unauthorized writes.
- [ ] **M03-AC07:** Failures retain recognized text where context remains authorized; original/raw retires corrected candidates.
- [ ] **M03-AC08:** Dictated commands cannot invoke tools or change dictation into agent mode.
- [ ] **M03-AC09:** Keyboard and screen-reader review supports long text and magnification without a timeout.
- [ ] **M03-AC10:** Upgrade, disable, privacy, routing and resource evidence is recorded on named builds.

Qualification must include the actual composer/session/insertion path, stale-result fault schedules, malformed edit-map and Unicode properties, and honest provider-request assertions. Real microphone/provider proof must demonstrate one correction and one ambiguous example; injected transcripts do not establish acoustic accuracy. Manual screen-reader proof and named client/platform support remain separate gates.

## Current evidence and requested design review

Draft [#205794](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205794) publishes two commits and 33 changed files. Its head is `95b1575c9368f1ded179ee914e9dfb2a3f2eb781`, based on `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c`. The final source tree, `8a86b349fbad0d58911124c9eb7e4869c6b9d9b4`, exactly matches the tested local head `afaf479c6e10b661aa67c3cbe5efc33db970c6c0`.

**197/197 canonical tests passed across five files**, covering the engine, existing capture owner, correction lifecycle/insertion, composer actions and preferences. A separate native text/property harness passed **2,259 assertions**; its complete 10,000-character/32-correction preparation measured **15.958 ms p95** on the recorded Linux/Xeon host. Scoped UI lint, formatting, CSS lint, controller guard, catalog verification and docs MDX checks passed. Independent agent source-review findings were fixed; that review is not maintainer acceptance or a ClawSweeper implementation review.

Qualification remains incomplete: the combined M01/M02/M11 pipeline is absent; final production build and full typechecks terminated with exit 137; catalog-script lint was blocked in declaration generation; unused-file scans exhausted their bounded heap. Sixteen browser cases are authored but **zero executed**, with **zero screenshots** after Chromium provisioning returned HTTP 403. Real microphone/provider, manual keyboard/zoom/screen-reader, live privacy-route and end-to-end latency checks are **NOT RUN**. The PR records all ten acceptance criteria with these boundaries and remains draft.

The [ClawSweeper proposal review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205645#issuecomment-7178569403) recommends evaluating a bounded English opt-in built-in prototype. Built-in versus plugin ownership, grammar and the saved preference still need maintainer decisions in coordination with filler removal. Its proposal review did not exercise this implementation or provide design acceptance.

Please review the first locale/grammar, explicit opt-in UX, private capture ownership boundary and settings placement. No public RPC/SDK contract or general external-field editing is proposed.

Bounded live searches for dictation self-correction and spoken correction titles did not identify a direct matching open implementation. Related #108246 was closed for an existing dictation issue and explicitly left built-in cleanup as a separate product request; it is not evidence that this feature is implemented. #198845 concerns failed-dictation recovery and is not an implementation parent.

## Do you plan to open a PR?

Published as **draft [#205794](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205794)** from the contributor's own fork. Missing qualification and maintainer design acceptance remain explicit. No merge is requested.

issues.body:
### Summary
After updating from OpenClaw 2026.9.4 to 2026.10.5 on Linux ARM64, the Gateway baseline memory increased dramatically from ~300 MB to 1.89 GB RSS at boot (before any chat turns). Exchanging messages over Telegram then causes memory warnings, slow SQLite transaction holds (>1.5s), and crash/abort with `idempotency key conflicts with the admitted message`.

Rolling back to 2026.9.4 drops tasks from 77 down to 12 and restores baseline memory to normal levels (~300–800 MB).

### Environment
- **OpenClaw version:** 2026.10.5 (regression observed vs 2026.9.4)
- **OS:** Linux ARM64 (Ubuntu)
- **Node runtime:** v24.22.1
- **Channels enabled:** Telegram

### Diagnostic Data & Telemetry (Captured from 2026.10.5 live run)

1. **Memory Warning at Boot / Idle:**
```
[diagnostics/memory] memory pressure: level=warning reason=rss_threshold rss=1.89 GiB heap=437.2 MiB threshold=1.72 GiB limit=2.15 GiB used=1.89 GiB rssBytes=2030075904
workerHeapTotalBytes=862588928 workerHeapUsedBytes=688175024 workerCount=15
workerHeaps=[
  {"script":"prepared-model-catalog.worker.js","threadId":13,"heapUsed":154496160,"heapTotal":201625600},
  {"script":"session-transcript.worker.js","threadId":11,"heapUsed":68981800,"heapTotal":76898304},
  {"script":"sqlite-store.worker.js","threadId":7,"heapUsed":54203688,"heapTotal":62312448},
  {"script":"disk-budget.worker.js","threadId":27,"heapUsed":50074696,"heapTotal":97349632}
]
```

2. **Slow SQLite Holds on Message Ingress:**
```
[sqlite/transaction] slow SQLite transaction hold async=false database=/root/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite operation="session context snapshot read" elapsedMs=1628
database page-cache residency: database=state scope=file-sample resident=3.5% readBytes=34050863 diskBytes=34127872
```

3. **Telegram Run Failure:**
```
[telegram] embedded run agent end: isError=true error=⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply. rawError=Transcript idempotency key "channel-user:v1:7500290e0bd8e774bbfc2c487c7a6c108e94076d1307a483670a589cd80e8ada" conflicts with the admitted message.
```

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Start OpenClaw 2026.10.5 gateway on Linux ARM64 under systemd.
2. Check memory immediately after startup: Gateway uses 1.89 GB RSS across 15 worker threads.
3. Send a message in a conversation channel (Telegram).
4. Gateway exceeds typical memory caps (e.g. 2 GB), hits slow SQLite transactions, and fails to deliver the reply.

### Expected Behavior
Gateway idle memory should remain bounded (as in 2026.9.4, where baseline RSS is ~300 MB and tasks are 11–12).

issues.body:
**Local draft ID:** M05 · **Target repository:** [openclaw/openclaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) · **Prepared:** November 25, 2026

**Status: published draft; acceptance pending.** [PR #205792](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205792) is open as a draft from [CompleteDotTech/openclaw](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/tree/feat/dictation-application-writing-profiles), at `e5ec6f06f9fd2ba2ae13b00ccb6eb29510edbe3d`. Its complete source tree is identical to reviewed local commit `6d87b615292ff1302f63d9a9bb746cbca92276e6`; the parent remains `04b854b239cd8ab8a14beae4914ed9c54d791e62`. Full M05 is incomplete. The draft integrates manual/global composer metadata; accepted M11/P02 contracts, contextual adapters, storage/permission acceptance and live qualification remain required.

Companion: PR description draft (companion design specification). Shared contracts: architecture (companion design specification), stacking plan (companion design specification), validation plan (companion design specification).

## Summary

Add explicit application-scoped writing profiles to intelligent dictation. A user should be able to prefer concise chat messages, structured email prose or literal technical text without changing settings before every utterance. The selected profile should be visible, predictable and stable for that utterance. It must not change the user's facts, commitments, uncertainty or intended recipient.

## Problem to solve

An application name alone cannot establish the intended writing behavior. A browser can host an email composer, a code editor and a search box; a desktop application can contain both ordinary text fields and sensitive fields. Profile selection therefore needs a small, authorized context contract, an explicit fallback and a separate destination-format contract. It must not require screenshots, clipboard reads, browsing history or automatic analysis of previous messages.

## Proposed solution

### Scope and dependencies

This feature depends on M11 (companion design specification) for the single refinement pipeline and P02 (companion design specification) for bounded, consented destination context. It will resolve policy before M11 prepares a request. It may configure punctuation, cleanup and structure capabilities supplied by M01 (companion design specification), M02 (companion design specification), M03 (companion design specification) and M04 (companion design specification), but it must not implement those transforms again.

P03 (companion design specification) remains the spelling owner. M10 (companion design specification) remains the insertion owner. P06 (companion design specification) remains the mode owner. A style profile must not grant agent tools, select an unapproved provider, authorize capture, bypass a sensitive-field block or force insertion into a changed target. Automatic learning from a user's writing, recipient inference, translation, persona impersonation and unrestricted user-supplied system prompts are excluded from the initial scope.

### Required behavior

The initial profiles should express bounded choices: literal versus prose handling; supported locale; capitalization and punctuation preference; conservative filler removal; explicit self-correction; paragraph/list preference; and a small approved register preset. A register preset may adjust phrasing only where the accepted product scope explicitly permits rewriting, and any such rewrite must preserve modality, uncertainty, negation, names, numbers and commitments. The recommended first release should keep register presets advisory or preview-only until a semantic-preservation corpus passes. Users must be able to use all deterministic policy choices without enabling prose rewriting.

Selectors should use P02's validated application identity and, when separately authorized, an exact web origin. A proposed native selector should contain the platform identity type and stable application identifier, not merely a display name. A proposed origin selector should match scheme, host and port; it should omit path, query, fragment, document title and page contents. Origin availability must be treated as a client capability. Do not guess an origin from the window title or claim a native bridge can inspect every browser tab.

Resolve selection in this order: explicit session override; enabled application-plus-exact-origin rule; enabled application rule; global default. A saved priority may disambiguate multiple user rules within one specificity level, but duplicate equal-priority selectors must be rejected or surfaced as a configuration conflict. Never resolve ties by array order, filesystem enumeration, network arrival or model preference. A missing or untrusted identity should select the global default with an understandable reason.

The resolved profile must be frozen with the utterance's context revision. Changing focus, editing a profile, switching workspaces or receiving a context update after capture begins must not silently change in-flight output. Users may explicitly reprocess an unsent draft using a newly selected profile; that action must allocate a new refinement revision and invalidate the old candidate. Changing the destination after preparation must pass the M10 target guard, even if the new destination would select an identical profile.

#### Behavioral examples

| Situation | Expected behavior |
|---|---|
| The user selects a chat profile and dictates “maybe we can ship Friday” | Preserve “maybe,” “can” and “Friday”; do not turn the sentence into a promise. |
| An email profile is selected for an authorized exact origin | Apply accepted policy choices; do not invent a greeting, subject, recipient, sign-off or attachment. |
| The same browser opens another origin | Use that origin's explicit rule or the application/global fallback; never carry an origin-specific rule across sites. |
| Two applications share a display name | Match their validated identities, not the shared label; unresolved identity uses fallback. |
| A terminal or code field selects literal handling | Preserve command text and syntax; no shell execution or agent dispatch occurs. |
| The user switches focus during refinement | Keep the original profile snapshot and require target revalidation before any write. |
| A profile requests an unavailable transform | Show the unavailable capability and use the documented safe fallback; do not silently claim it ran. |
| A secure field is detected | Follow P02/P01 capture policy and block the profile from weakening it. |

### Proposed contracts and lifecycle

Use one versioned profile record containing an opaque ID, display label, enabled state, bounded selectors, explicit priority, supported policy references and a revision. Use one resolved-profile snapshot containing the chosen ID/revision, resolution reason, allowed policy values, context capability/revision and supported-transform status. These names and shapes are proposals, not existing repository interfaces. M11 should consume the snapshot as typed policy; it should not concatenate profile labels, origins or arbitrary configuration strings into privileged model instructions.

The resolver should be deterministic and side-effect free. It should accept only the already authorized P02 context subset, not independently query OS APIs. It should resolve once per capture boundary, with a separate explicit preview operation for settings. Profile editing should use expected-revision checks so simultaneous settings windows cannot overwrite each other silently. A stale edit should retain the user's unsaved values and show a conflict with the current revision.

Registration and capability validation should happen before a profile can be enabled. If a referenced transform is unavailable, distinguish “saved but unavailable” from “active.” When a session-wide privacy or provider policy is more restrictive than a profile, the restrictive policy wins and the UI should explain the effective policy. A profile must not create another provider request, model cache, transcript history or context collector. The only content rewrite remains the M11 request and validated result.

### Configuration, migration and data

Recommend opt-in application rules with a global profile that preserves the user's existing behavior. Offer sample profiles as disabled templates; importing settings or upgrading should not activate new content rewriting. A profile export should contain settings and selectors only, with clear disclosure that application IDs and origins may reveal workflow information. It should exclude transcripts, provider credentials, dictionary contents, page content and private URLs. Import should validate schema/version, bounds, enums, duplicate selectors and referenced capabilities before committing an atomic revision.

Proposed initial limits are 100 profiles, 20 selectors per profile and short human-readable names; these are product guardrails to validate, not measured capacity. Schema migration should be idempotent and preserve unknown future records in a disabled/quarantined state rather than silently applying guessed semantics. Deleting a selected profile should use the global fallback for future utterances; existing prepared results keep their snapshot until canceled or explicitly reprocessed. Rollback must preserve saved profiles without activating them in an older implementation that cannot interpret their version.

### Privacy, accessibility and platform support

Keep application selectors and resolution local unless an approved remote refinement route actually needs a bounded style enum. The provider does not need a complete application inventory, raw window title or exact origin to apply “literal” or “prose” policy. Diagnostics should record opaque IDs and resolution classes when enabled, not full browsing context or dictated text. Untrusted document content and profile display labels must be treated as data; neither can alter tool authorization, provider routing or prompt roles.

The session UI should announce the active profile through a concise accessible label, allow keyboard selection and restore focus predictably. Changes should not be conveyed only by color. A screen reader user should be able to inspect why a profile was selected, disable it and recover the original draft without navigating a transient popup. Do not force a review timeout on a user who needs longer to compare text.

Support should follow actual P02 capability reports. A desktop client with an authorized app identity may offer application rules. Exact-origin rules require an observed supported integration. Mobile, browser-only, remote and headless clients should offer manual/global profiles where they lack reliable external context. Settings must not advertise “all apps” based on one platform's implementation. Loss of context permission should select the global fallback and cancel or revalidate affected prepared candidates under the shared lifecycle rules.

### Failure and performance requirements

The resolver should operate without network access. Proposed, unmeasured target: p95 resolution below 5 ms for the proposed maximum profile set on a documented reference desktop. Shared M11 budgets cover refinement; profile selection must not add another inference round trip. Measure cold load, import validation, simultaneous profile changes and long-lived settings sessions before choosing production limits.

Offline sessions should continue with locally available valid profiles and available local transforms. An unavailable remote transform must retain recognizer output or offer an explicit retry under M11 policy; profile selection must not silently change the provider. Cancellation should prevent late results from writing. A lost client connection should preserve only the shared recovery state; it must not create an independent background profile job. Session privacy changes must invalidate any candidate using context that is no longer authorized.

### Acceptance criteria

1. **AC01 — Selection:** Exact selectors and explicit precedence produce one deterministic profile; conflicting equal-priority rules are surfaced.
2. **AC02 — Identity:** Display-name spoofing, origin mismatches and unavailable context cannot activate a scoped profile.
3. **AC03 — Stability:** Profile/context revisions are frozen for the utterance; explicit reprocessing invalidates older results and target changes remain guarded.
4. **AC04 — Semantic integrity:** All enabled style choices preserve facts, names, numbers, negation, uncertainty, protected syntax and the user's level of commitment.
5. **AC05 — Capabilities:** Unsupported policy options are visibly unavailable and never reported as applied; client claims match qualification evidence.
6. **AC06 — Permissions:** Profiles cannot enable capture in blocked fields, expand context scope, switch agent mode or override provider/privacy restrictions.
7. **AC07 — Settings:** Atomic import, revision conflicts, deletion, migration and rollback preserve valid user preferences without new automatic opt-ins.
8. **AC08 — Accessibility:** Keyboard and screen-reader users can select, inspect and disable profiles and review/recover the original draft.
9. **AC09 — Failure:** Offline routes, revoked permissions, cancellation, reconnects and stale callbacks cannot produce an unauthorized or duplicate write.
10. **AC10 — Observability:** The proposed latency target is measured with methodology; diagnostics do not disclose text, browsing context or credentials.

## Alternatives considered

Manual selection alone is a useful first milestone but leaves repetitive switching. Matching window titles or display names would be ambiguous and expose more context. Learning from prior messages would expand retention and consent scope. A bounded deterministic resolver over authorized application/origin identity is the preferred design.

## Impact

Users would gain predictable per-destination preferences with a visible override. Existing settings would stay unchanged until opt-in. Clients with limited context could still offer manual/global profiles, and identity-sensitive behavior would be advertised only after actual client qualification.

## Evidence/examples

The examples define the full acceptance scope. The implementation checkpoint below records executed resolver, adapter, lifecycle, UI and benchmark evidence separately from the live-client and remaining gates that are **NOT RUN**. Tracker observations are bounded research, not proof that a capability is absent.

### Verification and rollout

Build a table-driven resolver suite covering each precedence level, exact origin matching, Unicode/display-name collisions, missing capabilities, equal-priority conflicts, deleted profiles and simultaneous edits. Add negative tests for path/query leakage, a fake application display name, prompt-like profile labels, disallowed transforms and permissive settings competing with stricter session policy. Test profile A and profile B against the same content to distinguish allowed formatting differences from semantic changes. The checkpoint below identifies which parts of this plan have executed; missing live and durable-version proof is still required.

Live qualification should include an actually supported native text field and browser integration, profile changes while recording, focus switches while refining, secure-field handling, manual/global fallback and a keyboard/screen-reader pass. Record exact OS/client versions and permission state. Provider-based style quality should be evaluated separately from deterministic selector accuracy; do not treat a good selector unit test as proof that rewritten prose is safe.

Roll out manual/global profile selection first, then opt-in native selectors, then independently qualified origin selectors. Keep automatic register rewriting gated behind its own semantic evaluation. Rollback should disable resolution and leave saved configuration available for export and future migration. Recommended defaults are explicit rules, exact origins, local resolution and no learned style. Maintainer decisions still needed: the accepted register-rewrite scope, stable identity guarantees for each client, origin integration support and final schema ownership within existing settings.

### Sources and duplicate-search record

- [Bounded open issue/PR search for writing styles](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues?q=is%3Aopen+%22writing+styles%22): checked November 25, 2026; no direct match was identified in the returned results. This wording is a research limit, not an exhaustive absence claim.
- [OpenClaw repository](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw): the future implementation must follow the then-current contribution and configuration conventions. This draft deliberately proposes contracts rather than asserting present source symbols.
- P02 context specification (companion design specification) and M11 pipeline specification (companion design specification): local draft dependencies, not GitHub issue numbers.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, preparing a contribution from the authenticated contributor's fork. Public schema/permission ownership and native adapter qualification remain review gates.

## Additional information

Suggested label: `enhancement`. Local IDs in this package are planning references, not GitHub issue numbers. The exact API/config names and implementation base require maintainer review; the intended behavior, defaults and outstanding decisions are documented above.


## Current source audit and concrete design questions

Source inspected at `04b854b239cd8ab8a14beae4914ed9c54d791e62`. Bounded current tracker searches did not identify a direct profile implementation. The implementation will reuse `ComposerDictationOwner` / `ComposerDictationCommits`, the existing speech route, and the SQLite-backed `users.prefs` owner. Current user-preference bounds are 4 KiB per value and 32 writes per transaction; the proposed full profile limits require a bounded storage design review. Existing native browser-tab inventory is not an authorized target identity source and will not be consumed. No accepted M11/P02 contract or qualified external-origin adapter was identified.

Requested design review: ownership of the private refinement/profile policy boundary; a bounded catalog within the existing user-preference owner; opt-in focused application identity and exact-origin adapter guarantees; and the first native/browser combination to qualify. No prose register rewrite, permission expansion, or universal app support is claimed. A concrete draft will distinguish tested resolver/persistence/lifecycle behavior from live platform checks that remain NOT RUN. Related context-hint transport: #191109; this issue does not duplicate or close that transport request.


## Implementation checkpoint — November 25, 2026

**Reviewable blocked draft; this issue remains open and incomplete.**

- Local branch: `feat/dictation-application-writing-profiles`.
- Local commit: `6d87b615292ff1302f63d9a9bb746cbca92276e6`; base: `04b854b239cd8ab8a14beae4914ed9c54d791e62`.
- Publication: [draft PR #205792](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205792), published head `e5ec6f06f9fd2ba2ae13b00ccb6eb29510edbe3d`. The reviewed/tested local commit below has the identical source tree `270e24e76df3d82b6c3bf3a21fc32301f78ca47b`; only publication commit metadata differs.
- Implemented: bounded versioned catalog; deterministic override → authorized app+exact-origin → app → global resolution; strict origin/identity validation and tie refusal; immutable capture snapshots; restrictive capability policy; existing preference-owner CAS with disabled atomic imports/future-schema quarantine; Talk settings and manual/global main-composer inspection/original-text preview; stale Send guards through existing composer owners.
- Unsupported: external application/origin inputs in this browser client; actual native adapters; optional transformations. The recognizer transcript is preserved and register is advisory. No added profile/destination context or extra model call is introduced. Existing provider language/prompt configuration means recognizer output is not universally context-independent.

### Executed evidence

| Check | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Domain resolver/schema | 56 tests passed |
| Preference adapter | 7 tests passed, including deeply nested future-schema export |
| Existing dictation owner/direct composer | 59 tests passed |
| Focused settings, main/rail/New Session Send intent and upload preflight | 29 tests passed across 7 files; 68 intentional filter skips |
| Total focused tests | **151 passed** |
| Source review | All 51 changed paths independently reviewed, including cross-review of author exclusions; hashes match the committed tree |
| Domain strict TypeScript/typed lint; new CSS lint | Passed for those stated scopes |
| Normal commit hooks and exact committed test-line ratchet | Passed without bypass; +1,627 net test lines, 400 allowance, 1,227 explicit allocation |
| Exact-head benchmark | 100 profiles × 20 selectors, 10,000 samples/warm scenario: p95 exact 0.129488 ms, full miss 0.194632 ms, override 0.005455 ms, interleaved revisions 0.122582 ms; all below proposed 5 ms |
| Cold/import observations | Module load 50.588780 ms / first call 4.888080 ms single observations; fresh validation/import p95 18.874344/22.815444 ms across 200 samples each |
| Upstream compatibility | Complete 408-path audit against `b8992c005468f7ad6b04b372c101a2d42fab8531`; read-only merge-tree is conflict-free. No combined-head CI is implied. |

The benchmark uses a 283,977-byte full-cardinality catalog and no model/provider. Its local fetch guard counted zero calls after import. Import measurements exclude adapter UUID rotation/RPC/SQLite/rendering; interleaved revisions do not simulate concurrent writers; aggregate memory and cold single observations are not browser/native qualification.

### Blocked criteria and gates

- **AC01:** pure deterministic contract passes; automatic production consumers still depend on accepted contracts.
- **AC02–AC06:** accepted M11/P02 contracts, actual native/external-origin adapters, physical target/permission qualification, and P02-derived-candidate revocation after context-influenced dispatch remain missing. No prose rewrite quality is claimed.
- **AC07:** adapter fixtures pass, but three real SQLite/worker tests did not collect because the compiled-subprocess prerequisite exited 137. Real prior-version upgrade/downgrade/rollback and proposed 1 MiB preference/retention acceptance remain pending.
- **AC08:** DOM controls/focus fixtures pass; actual browser keyboard, screen reader, large-text/reflow and before/after media are **NOT RUN**. The source mock started, but the available browser could not reach it; the local browser binary was unavailable.
- **AC09:** synthetic stale-callback/cancellation/reconnect/no-replay coverage passes; actual native/provider/permission races remain **NOT RUN**.
- **AC10:** pure resolver bounds and redacted diagnostics are covered; long-lived real-client memory/concurrent durable writes/native/provider performance remain **NOT RUN**.
- Full UI types and the later production build exited 137 on the shared host. An earlier build completed with five bundle-budget violations; loading/CSS were changed afterward, but final budgets are **unverified**. Full typed UI/storage lint and exact-head CI do not have passing results.
- `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` is incomplete and must be rerun on the exact candidate on a qualified host; ordinary PR CI does not automatically provide this proof.

The complete local package preserves the commit, patch, source files, exact-head AC ledger, review manifests, commands, and passing/failed logs. Defaults and imports are disabled. Rollback requires disabling the catalog and exporting settings; older Gateways may reject catalogs above their generic 4 KiB write limit. This checkpoint does not request merging or closing the issue and does not represent maintainer acceptance.

The fork branch and draft PR are published. The upstream CI workflow currently reports `action_required`; full CI is not a pass. The draft remains blocked on the stated product/contracts, worker/build/type/budget/unused-file gates, and native/browser/provider/accessibility/migration proof. issues.body:
# Gateway: runaway RSS outside V8 heap causes host OOM and shutdown timeout

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.9.5`
- Node.js `26.4.0`
- Linux x64
- Gateway as a systemd user service
- Host memory visible to the service: ~15 GiB

## Incident

On 2026-09-20, the Gateway reached `9.32 GiB` RSS with only `962 MiB` V8 heap used. The Linux OOM killer terminated processes in `openclaw-gateway.service` repeatedly between 18:48 and 19:04; the Gateway was eventually killed and restarted.

The issue is reproducible after a fresh restart: RSS grows to roughly `2–4 GiB` within minutes, while V8 heap remains around `620–700 MiB`.

## Evidence

- Stability sample: RSS `2.12 GiB`, heap used `638 MiB`.
- Shortly after: RSS `3.50 GiB`, heap used `620 MiB`.
- Heap profile capture: heap used fell from `722 MiB` to `673 MiB`, while RSS rose from `2.48 GiB` to `2.73 GiB` during the 5-second sample.
- V8 external memory was only ~30 MiB and ArrayBuffers ~6 MiB.
- A persisted stability bundle before shutdown recorded RSS `4.75 GiB` with heap used `1.41 GiB`.
- The heap profile did not identify a large JavaScript allocation owner. SQLite-related sample allocations were small.
- Startup also logged `MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventEmitter memory leak detected. 11 exit listeners added to [process].`

This points to native allocation/retention, allocator fragmentation, or a loaded integration outside normal V8 heap accounting.

## Operational impact

The Gateway service previously used `TimeoutStopSec=330`. During controlled restart it exceeded the graceful shutdown window, producing `gateway.stop_shutdown_timeout` and extending downtime.

## Temporary mitigations applied

- 4 GiB swap added to avoid host-wide OOM.
- systemd service guard: `MemoryHigh=5G`, `MemoryMax=6G`.
- `TimeoutStopSec=60s`.
- Runtime options: `--max-old-space-size=4096 --trace-warnings` and `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`.

These protect the host and improve recovery but do not resolve the RSS growth.

## Request

Please advise on collecting attribution for non-V8 RSS and on known regressions in `2026.9.5` involving Gateway native memory growth, spawn-broker/service-child supervision, MCP/plugin loading, or shutdown listener accumulation.

A payload-free diagnostics archive was generated locally with `openclaw gateway diagnostics export` and can be shared through an appropriate private channel if needed.

issues.body:
## Problem

On mobile Safari, scrolling up through a long chat can replace the visible history with a much older page, or move the paragraph being read by about 200 CSS pixels while a finger is still down.

## Reproduction

1. Open a long Control UI conversation whose history-page boundary separates a tool call from its result.
2. Swipe toward earlier messages until the older page loads and joins the result to its call.
3. Begin another downward finger drag as the older page lands. A row above the viewport can change its measured height during that touch.

Expected: the same paragraph stays under the reader's finger; a released flick continues coasting.

Actual: regrouping removes the former first rendered key, so prepend detection loses the reader. Separately, a pending prepend suppresses relative reader correction even though absolute prepend correction is paused during native touch.

## Supplied reproduction evidence

Dan supplied a seven-file patch and recordings from Safari in an iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.4, Xcode 26.4.1, with production Control UI builds and real isolated gateways using 1,432 synthetic history entries. Source base: `cdadcea9047c83025b9c462abf25811d0f3c8add`.

His verification records whole-page jumps on the unmodified base. The paired video compares **regrouping fix only** with **both fixes**, not unmodified main: the same row shrinks from 240 to 36 CSS pixels, producing 204 CSS pixels of backward paragraph movement with regrouping alone and zero with reader correction. Six full-patch trials had no reverse in-range movement over 1 CSS pixel. A separate release recording shows continued momentum after finger lift.

I confirmed both MP4s decode completely, inspected their frames, checked source ownership/history, and confirmed all seven affected files are unchanged between that base and the current task base `e4517b0ef2f4e`. I have not rerun the simulator or automated tests.

Related but different: #202344 concerns a cached-refresh pending-frame correction; closed #149619 concerns a transient estimate-height shift. I found no existing report for this tool-regrouping/native-touch combination.

No message loss is established. Model/provider routing is not involved.

issues.title: [Bug]: 2026.11.2 gateway main heap retains every prepared-model-runtime generation (~1 per 6 min) until OOM

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:bug
labels.description: Preliminary submission classification; full source review pending.

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:needs-repro
labels.description: Preliminary submission classification; full source review pending.

issues.body:
## Summary

On 2026.11.2, the gateway's **main** JS heap grows steadily until V8 aborts with "JavaScript heap out of memory". With `--max-old-space-size` raised, this takes about 90 hours. Heap snapshots show that every model-catalog refresh (about one every 6 minutes) leaves a full prepared-model-runtime "generation" reachable. Each generation holds its own `pluginMetadataSnapshot` with per-file `sourceAdmissions` for every plugin file. Old generations are never released.

This looks like the main-thread side of #160548 ("prepared-model-catalog worker leaks ~1 GiB per 5 min"). That issue has a similar cadence, but it was closed as stale on 2026-11-24 without a fix. #160522 / #166581, fixed in 2026.11.7, caps the worker isolate's heap and does not cover this main-heap growth.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (npm), Node v24.22.1, Linux aarch64. The gateway is run with `--heapsnapshot-signal=SIGWINCH`.
- Plugins installed through the npm project store include `openclaw-codex` and `openclaw-llama-cpp-provider`.
- Three OOM crashes in 14 days. Raising the heap limit only lengthened the interval.

## Evidence (two V8 heap snapshots of the gateway main thread)

Snapshot 1 was taken on a fresh process. Snapshot 2 was taken after 39 h uptime (RSS 3.4 GiB).

| | snap1 | snap2 (39 h) |
|---|---|---|
| heap nodes | 8.4M | 22.9M |
| heap self size | 0.79 GiB | 1.88 GiB |
| strings | 346 MiB | 1,074 MiB |
| `isGenerationCurrent` closures | 71 | 465 |
| `loadCatalog` / `refreshExpiredModelCatalog` / `readCurrentUsage` closures | 71-79 | 465-475 |
| `workerInput` contexts | 71 | 465 |
| `closeModelRuntime` closures | 1 | 1 |

That is about 394 retained generations in about 41 h, roughly one every 6 minutes.

**What the generations hold:**
- About 937K strings are file paths under `<openclaw home>/npm/projects/openclaw-codex-<hash>__openclaw-generation__.../`.
- About 858K are paths under `.../openclaw-llama-cpp-provider-<hash>__openclaw-generation__.../`.
- Those two directories contain only about 3.4K and 0.9K files, so each path is held hundreds of times.
- About 109K strings are `tmp/plugin-captures/...` paths, one of them held 30,083 times.

**Retainer chain** (shortest path to the GC root, sampled 200 strings per prefix, the same shape for every sample):

```
string <-source- Object <-<relative file path>- Object <-members- Object <-<dir>- Object
  <-nativeNamespaces- Object <-<plugin dir>- Object <-sourceAdmissions- Object <-element- Array (plugins)
  <-index | registryIndex <-pluginMetadataSnapshot <-context.workerInput <-loadCatalog closure <-worker
  <-WeakMap (catalogCaptures / authByFullCatalog / runtimeAuth / ownersBySnapshot / admittedCatalogs)
  <-closeModelRuntime context <-Set closeCallbacks <-ProcessModelRuntimeLifetimes
  <-global[Symbol(openclaw.preparedModelRuntimeLif...)]
```

**Counts behind the chain:**
- 936,806 codex path strings sit in 902,704 distinct `{source}` objects. These converge into 931 `plugins` arrays and 471 distinct `pluginMetadataSnapshot` objects, each with an `index` and a `registryIndex` copy.
- The WeakMaps are not the root cause. Their keys (the published snapshots) stay alive because each snapshot reaches the previous one through `snapshot.isCurrent` -> closure context -> `previous` (enclosing context) -> Map -> previous snapshot.
- The resulting chain is up to 5,853 hops long, so no generation ever becomes unreachable.

## Where in the code (2026.11.2 dist)

`dist/prepared-model-runtime-*.mjs`, `publishPreparedModelRuntimeOwnerBatch`:
- Every publish does `owner.generation += 1`.
- It builds per-candidate closures (`isGenerationCurrent`, `isCurrent`, `isEligible`, `markRegistered`) that capture `owner`, `params` and the batch's `results` Map.
- `isGenerationCurrent` is handed to `createFullModelCatalogAccess` as `isCurrent`, so each published snapshot keeps its whole publish batch alive.

We have not pinned down exactly which reference links one batch to the previous one. The heap shows that link exists, but we did not trace it in source.

In 2026.11.10 the same construct is still present (`isGenerationCurrent` passed as `isCurrent` into `createFullModelCatalogAccess`), and its changelog has no entry for a catalog or generation leak. We have not run 2026.11.10, so it may differ at runtime.

## Expected

When a new model-runtime generation is published, the previous generation (its snapshot, catalog worker input and plugin metadata index) becomes unreachable and is collected.

## Repro notes

The gateway is left running with two npm-installed provider plugins (Codex and llama.cpp). Two `SIGWINCH` heap snapshots about 24 to 40 h apart show the `isGenerationCurrent` closure count rising by about 10 per hour. Grouping string nodes by path prefix shows the plugin file index duplicated once per generation.

We can share the analysis scripts (V8 snapshot summarizer and retainer walker) on request. The snapshot files themselves contain host-local data and are not attachable.

issues.body:
### Summary
On PostgreSQL agent stores, `openclaw memory index --agent <id>` fails for an agent with a large session history:

```
Memory index failed (<agent>): Error [ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY]: Worker terminated due to reaching memory limit: JS heap out of memory [task=sessionTranscript.session-entries admittedInputBytes=115220 exchanges=58 stage=running]
```

The session-transcript workers are created with a hardcoded `resourceLimits.maxOldGenerationSizeMb: 512` (e.g. `T={maxOldGenerationSizeMb:512,maxYoungGenerationSizeMb:32}` in the transcript worker-resources module; the same literal appears in ~15 transcript/session worker modules in `dist`). There is no config or env override.

### Environment
OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (`e13cf15`), Node 26, Linux x64; agent store on PostgreSQL 18.7 after a native `database port`. The same agent indexes fine on SQLite. The largest session is a long-running DM (tens of thousands of entries, several months).

### Steps to reproduce
1. Agent with one very large session transcript; port the agent family to PostgreSQL.
2. Gateway stopped; `openclaw memory index --agent <id>` (the port's own post-port rebuild fails first for a separate reason, see linked issue).
3. Worker dies with `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` after ~28 s.

### Evidence
In a disposable clone, raising the transcript worker caps to 8 GB in `dist` gets past the OOM (the reindex then runs for minutes and stops on a separate NUL-byte issue, filed separately). So the cap, not a leak, is the limit for this data size.

### Suggested fix
Make the transcript worker heap configurable (e.g. `memory.workers.maxOldGenerationSizeMb` or an env var), or size it from the batch/input instead of a fixed 512 MB. A clearer error naming the session would also help.

issues.body:
### What happened

On OpenClaw 2026.11.10, the “Learn from conversations” scribe was set to read active and archived conversations from any time. A November 25 run reported that history was still truncated when requested one message at a time and stopped without advancing any checkpoints. The checkpoint note contained only its heading. The scheduler marked the agent turn completed, but the scribe reported failure.

### What remains after #205335

The run preceded the merge of #205335, which fixed the false truncation signal from stripping usage metadata (#205271). The individual tool response was unavailable, so we can't tell whether this run hit that bug or a genuinely clipped text block. This is not a report that the metadata fix failed.

A genuine over-limit text block still cannot be recovered by asking for fewer messages. The [scribe instructions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1a660f87c7f0e187cb87cbe52a9e86f646a135f9/extensions/knowledge/skills/knowledge-ingest/references/learning.md#L45-L58) explain when to advance each checkpoint but not how to continue past one incomplete conversation.

### Expected behavior and suggested verification

Give the scribe two eligible conversations. Have the first return genuinely clipped text even with `limit: 1`, and give the second a complete, short exchange containing a decision worth remembering. The scribe should leave the first checkpoint untouched, process and checkpoint the second, and report that one conversation was skipped because its history was incomplete. A later run should be able to retry the first without relearning the second.

This two-conversation case is a proposed regression test, not a reproduction on post-merge main.
