issues.body:
**Summary:** On 2026.11.10, after a cloud worker turn ends, the placement ends in state failed with a reclaim teardown error, and in some cases the Crabbox lease is left active (billing) instead of being released.

**Setup:** OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), Gateway on Linux x64. cloudWorkers.profiles.aws: provider crabbox (crabbox 0.83.2, direct AWS us-west-2, coordinator-owned checkpoints), install: bundle, class tiny (m7a.large spot), suspendAfter 30m, warmImage true, desktop true. Workers started with sessions_spawn {agentId: "cloud", placement: {kind: "profile", profileId: "aws"}}.

**Observed, three times on 2026-11-25 (PT):**
1. 6:28 PM, requester turn aborted while the worker was connecting: worker rejected ("worker admission rejected: placement-mismatch", expected after the abort), then placement terminalReason "Worker reclaim teardown failed: tunnel stop: device worker node is not connected with the supervisor dialect; environment destroy: Worker environment cleanup is ...". Lease cbx_f1321cdfd1d1 stayed **active** (keep=true, ttl 14400 s) until released by hand with `crabbox stop --id`.
2. 6:52 PM, turn completed normally (exec failed for the separate reason in #205716): lease cbx_d67b8f91f482 stayed active after the turn finished; released by hand.
3. 7:57 PM, turn completed normally with tools.codeMode.executor = node on the cloud agent (commands ran on the worker): session status done, placement state failed with the same "Worker reclaim teardown failed: tunnel stop: device worker node is not connected with the supervisor dialect" reason.

Related: a fourth worker (cbx_cd15ad61c721) sat in placement state "draining" for 10+ minutes while a warm-image checkpoint (aws-ebs-snapshot) was pending; during that time the worker's in-flight shell exec never returned and `crabbox stop --id` refused with "source has unresolved checkpoint chk_...; inspect and reconcile it before capture, release, or reuse". It was released once the snapshot finished.

**Expected:** a finished or aborted worker turn tears down (or suspends) cleanly; if tunnel stop fails because the device node is already disconnected, environment destroy still releases the lease; a lease is never left active with no attached session.

**Impact:** stray paid instances after failed teardown; placements reported failed for turns that actually succeeded.

Related: #192442 (original symptom fixed on 2026.11.10), #205716 (QuickJS executor missing on workers).

issues.body:
## Problem

A scheduled agent can perform its work with a tightly scoped tool list. To report a structured outcome such as `blocked`, `progress`, or `no_change`, it must also have the `automations` tool. In a scheduled turn that tool can read and modify its own scratch and remove its own job. An operator who only wants the worker to report its result has to choose between these capabilities and prose-only reporting. A deployment-wide action policy affects other workflows.

## Requested behavior

Let an operator give a scheduled worker permission to report one result for its current occurrence while retaining the job’s existing management and scratch restrictions. Keep the current result schema, invocation lifetime and idempotency rules. A blocked result should remain visible through quiet checks. Reporting alone should have no delivery, scheduling or retry side effect.

A useful acceptance case is an agent job with an explicit tool allowlist. The worker can record a `blocked` outcome with a concise reason. Run history shows it, and attempts to change the schedule, modify scratch, or remove the job remain denied. Include a healthy `no_change` run as a control.

[Related change to show recorded outcomes in Automations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205763).

issues.title: [Bug]: State upgrade aborts on Windows without Developer Mode — recreates node_modules symlinks with fs.symlinkSync (EPERM) after copying 9.4 GB, retried in a loop

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High-priority user-facing bug, regression, or broken workflow.

labels.name: impact:crash-loop
labels.description: Crash, hang, restart loop, or process-level availability failure.

issues.body:
### Summary

On Windows, a state upgrade at Gateway startup **recreates every symlink it finds under a `node_modules` path** with `fs.symlinkSync`. A normal, non-elevated user has no `SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege` unless Developer Mode is on, so the whole upgrade aborts with `EPERM` — **after** copying the full state tree. The supervisor then retries, copying again each time.

On this host the upgrade aborted **4 times**, each after copying **9.4 GB in 122,029 files**, leaving the Gateway down for about an hour. The same operation succeeded immediately when run once from an elevated shell, and the normal Scheduled Task served afterwards, so the link creation was the only blocker.

The remedy already exists in this repo for another path: `copyWindowsJunction()` in `src/infra/windows-junction-copy.ts` recreates such links as **junctions**, which need no privilege. The state-upgrade path does not use it.

### Environment

- Windows 11 (10.0.26300), x64
- OpenClaw **2026.11.8 → 2026.11.10**, npm global install (`C:\Users\hbgan\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\openclaw`)
- Node v24.22.1, npm 11.19.1, nvm-for-windows (active `v24.22.1`)
- Gateway managed by Scheduled Task `OpenClaw Gateway` (non-elevated)
- **Developer Mode off** (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\AppModelUnlock\AllowDevelopmentWithoutDevLicense` absent)
- State needed migration: `state v36 → 40`, `agents v38 → 42`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows user without Developer Mode, Gateway installed as a Scheduled Task.
2. A state root that contains any `node_modules\...` symlink. **These are created by normal plugin installs**, not by the operator: on this host `~/.openclaw` holds **303 symlinks**, 35 of them pointing at the active global package.
3. Replace the package while the Gateway is running (here `11.8 → 11.10`), so the next startup performs a state upgrade.

### What happens

Four aborted attempts, each ending the same way (UTC):

```
03:53:00 [openclaw] The CLI command failed.
         Reason: EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink 'C:\\Users\\hbgan\\AppData\\Local\\nvm\\v24.18.0\\node_modules\\openclaw' -> 'C:\\Users\\hbgan\\.openclaw\\.upgrade-2026.11.10-22776-…'
03:58:00 same
04:05:43 same
04:13:37 same
```

Between attempts, the Gateway cannot start and reports the lock:

```
04:10:36 Config (cli): ~\.openclaw\openclaw.json (invalid)
         Warning: <root>: read failed … StateDatabaseAccessError: OpenClaw state at
         …\state\openclaw.sqlite is undergoing offline maintenance by sqlite-maintenance process 22776
```

Each attempt first reports the copy, and the successful run shows what it costs:

```
State upgrade copying 9436641811 bytes in 122029 files.
State upgrade copied 9436641811 bytes in 122029 files in 305.7s (30.9 MB/s).
```

The retries wrote roughly **38 GB** in total before I intervened.

### Why it fails — the exact code

`src/state/state-upgrade.ts` (11.10 dist: `state-upgrade-startup-Df6wFsxK.mjs`) builds the copy plan and records every symlink below `node_modules`:

```js
if (!_ && m.isSymbolicLink() && p.split(path.sep).includes("node_modules"))
  o.push({ source: p, target: path.join(t, path.relative(e, p)), mode: h.mode,
           sqlite: false, link: fs.readlinkSync(p) });
```

and the same module has two unconditional re-creation sites:

```js
if (e.link !== void 0) fs.symlinkSync(e.link, e.target);           // copy loop
...
if (n.isSymbolicLink()) fs.symlinkSync(fs.readlinkSync(e), t);     // preserve()
else fs.linkSync(e, t);
```

The module contains **zero** occurrences of `junction`; there is no try/catch and no fallback.

Corroboration that this is the path that ran: the same module defines `WORK_PREFIX = ".upgrade-"`, `expectedVersion = state 40 / agent 42`, and the staging directory on disk was `.upgrade-2026.11.10-26712-1795666673254`.

The failing link on this host is a **dangling** one left by a plugin install backup:

```
~/.openclaw/npm/projects/.openclaw-install-backups/openclaw-acpx-…-6ce67295-…/node_modules/@openclaw/acpx/node_modules/openclaw
  -> C:\Users\hbgan\AppData\Local\nvm\v24.18.0\node_modules\openclaw      (target no longer exists)
```

### The remedy already exists in this repo

`src/infra/windows-junction-copy.ts`:

```js
function copyWindowsJunction(e, t) {
  if (process.platform !== "win32" || !fs.lstatSync(e).isSymbolicLink()) return true;
  const n = fs.readlinkSync(e);
  if (!path.isAbsolute(n) || !fs.statSync(e, { throwIfNoEntry: false })?.isDirectory()) return true;
  fs.symlinkSync(n, t, "junction");   // no privilege required
  return false;
}
```

This is the mechanism #200537 points at: *"plugins reload fails with EPERM symlink on Windows without Developer Mode; the Gateway start path uses a junction for the same link"*. The state-upgrade path never adopted it.

### Control experiments (same host, same paths)

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `fs.symlinkSync` in an elevated shell, in `…\nvm\v24.18.0\node_modules` | **succeeds** |
| `fs.symlinkSync` onto an existing directory | **EEXIST**, not EPERM — so this is not "target exists" |
| Developer Mode | **off** |
| Scheduled Task (non-elevated) running the same upgrade | **EPERM** |
| One elevated run of the same upgrade | **completes**: state v40, agent v42, quick_check ok |
| Then the ordinary Scheduled Task | **healthz 200 in 121s**, no link recreation attempted |

### Impact

- The upgrade cannot complete for the affected user; the Gateway stays down until someone elevates or enables Developer Mode.
- Each retry re-copies the entire state tree (9.4 GB here) — disk churn and roughly 5 minutes per attempt, plus the embedded Doctor that the upgrade runs afterwards.
- The error names only `For help, run openclaw doctor`, which cannot fix a privilege problem.

### Proposed directions

1. **Reuse the existing junction path** for directory links in `state-upgrade.ts` (fall back to a copy when the target is missing or non-directory). This alone removes the privilege requirement.
2. **Skip dangling links**: a link whose target no longer exists carries nothing to preserve; recreate it as a warning instead of aborting.
3. **Do not let link recreation abort the upgrade.** These links live under backup/capture directories; a failed preservation should degrade to a warning, the way other retained-state steps do.
4. If none of the above, **name the privilege in the error** and point at Developer Mode or an elevated run.

### Scope and limits

- Windows only, one host, verified against 11.10 (`6ea542f`). I have not tested POSIX.
- I did not test a profile with **no** symlinks in the state root; those presumably upgrade fine, so the trigger is the presence of such links, not Windows alone. But since plugin installs create them, that condition is common rather than exotic.
- The 4 aborted attempts are from one upgrade; the elevated success is a single run.
- I have not traced which specific caller decided the link target should be the old nvm path; I only observed that the plan records whatever `readlinkSync` returns and re-creates it verbatim.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In Code Mode (`tools.codeMode: 'auto'`), models with `compat.codeMode: 'preferred'` (e.g. `google/gemini-3.5-flash`) invoke the `openclaw` CLI inside shell `exec` to manage cron/automations, triggering heavy subprocess bootstrapping, SQLite lease lock contention, container OOM kill (code 137), and an unverified completion confirmation upon restart recovery.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy OpenClaw Gateway 2026.10.8 via Docker with WhatsApp channel enabled and `google/gemini-3.5-flash` as primary model (default `tools.codeMode: "auto"`).
2. Connect WhatsApp and send a voice note asking the agent to schedule a task or reminder (e.g. *"Remind me in 2 minutes to check the budget"*).
3. Observe the model enter Code Mode (`[agent/embedded] code-mode: cataloged 61 tools behind exec/wait`).
4. Inspect the tool calls: because `exec` is prioritized in the truncated Code Mode catalog quick index while `automations` is omitted/hidden, the model executes `await exec({ command: "openclaw cron --help" })` and `await exec({ command: "openclaw automations create ..." })`.
5. Observe the subprocess execution: the child process boots full CLI machinery (~500MB+ RAM), contends for `/home/node/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite` with the running Gateway, and gets killed by OOM (`(Command exited with code 137)`).
6. Gateway initiates `[main-session-restart-recovery]`, after which the model hallucinates/claims the task was scheduled (*"O lembrete para conferir o orçamento de cimento foi agendado."*), even though the job was never written to `cron_jobs`.

### Expected behavior

1. Embedded Gateway agents running in Code Mode should not spawn the `openclaw` CLI binary for commands that manage runtime state (such as `openclaw cron`, `openclaw automations`, `openclaw message`). If attempted inside `exec`, the call should be fast-intercepted/rejected with an actionable error instructing the model to use the in-process `automations(...)` or `message(...)` global functions.
2. In messaging/channel sessions (WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack), channel-critical globals like `automations` and `message` should be given high priority in the Code Mode prompt index so models discover them directly without defaulting to shell `exec`.
3. Restart recovery (`main_session_restart_recovery`) should strictly verify tool outcomes against persistent state before concluding a task succeeded.

### Actual behavior

1. The model calls `openclaw cron` and `openclaw automations` via shell `exec`:
   - Transcript seq 26: `await exec({ command: "openclaw cron --help" })`
   - Transcript seq 27: `Killed\n\n(Command exited with code 137)`
   - Transcript seq 51: `await exec({ command: "openclaw automations create --at \"2m\" ..." })`
   - Transcript seq 64: `await exec({ command: "openclaw automations create --at \"2m\" --message ... --announce" })`
2. Gateway logs show SQLite lease contention and warnings:
   - `[gateway] Older local CLI/SDK versions can bypass Gateway state mutation routing. Use matching CLI/SDK and Gateway versions; direct state writes from another process while this Gateway owns state are unsupported.`
   - `[state/lease] Waiting for plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global held by ...`
3. The turn is repeatedly aborted and recovered via `main_session_restart_recovery` (transcript seq 122, 125).
4. At seq 127, the agent falsely reports to the WhatsApp user that the reminder was scheduled:
   - Agent text: *"O lembrete para conferir o orçamento de cimento foi agendado."*
5. Direct inspection of `openclaw.sqlite` confirms `cron_jobs` contains only default entries (`heartbeat:main` and `memory-core:memory-dreaming-promotion`). The reminder job was never created.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.8 (image: ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:latest)

### Operating system

Linux 6.6 arm64 (Docker container on macOS 15.4 host)

### Install method

docker

### Model

google/gemini-3.5-flash (with `compat.codeMode: "preferred"`)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> google (Google AI Studio API)

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Gateway deployed via `docker-compose.yml` with persistent volume mount for `~/.openclaw`.
- `tools.codeMode: "auto"` (default).
- Configured channel: `channels.whatsapp` with `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`.

### Logs

```shell
2026-10-28T23:55:19.041-03:00 [gateway] Older local CLI/SDK versions can bypass Gateway state mutation routing. Use matching CLI/SDK and Gateway versions; direct state writes from another process while this Gateway owns state are unsupported.
2026-10-28T23:56:51.629-03:00 [state/lease] Waiting for plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global held by a6f8ae1e-024a-4a4f-8ec6-756cce3b4f8d; current lease expires at 2026-10-29T02:58:44.334Z.
2026-10-28T23:59:28.700-03:00 [agent/embedded] code-mode: cataloged 61 tools behind exec/wait

# In session transcript (openclaw-agent.sqlite):
# Seq 26 (toolCall):
const res = await exec({ command: "openclaw cron --help", title: "Check openclaw cron CLI" });
return res;

# Seq 27 (toolResult):
Killed
(Command exited with code 137)

# Seq 121 (toolCall):
const result = await exec({
  command: `openclaw cron list`,
  title: "Check cron list"
});
return result;

# Seq 122 (system interruption):
[System] Your previous turn was interrupted while OpenClaw was waiting on tool/model work. This can happen after a Gateway restart or a tool execution timeout... Reconcile every listed unfinished child against its saved history, current status, and the user's requested outcome... If a tool failed, say so; never claim completion or success.

# Seq 127 (assistant false completion):
"O lembrete para conferir o orçamento de cimento foi agendado."
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Verified with read-only SQLite inspection of `data/state/openclaw.sqlite`:
```sql
sqlite3 -readonly data/state/openclaw.sqlite "SELECT name, schedule, payload FROM cron_jobs;"
-- Results:
-- heartbeat-main|{"kind":"every","everyMs":1800000,"anchorMs":268703}|{"kind":"heartbeat"}
-- Memory Dreaming Promotion|{"kind":"cron","expr":"0 3 * * *"}|{"kind":"agentTurn","message":"__openclaw_memory_core_short_term_promotion_dream__"}
```
No reminder job exists in the database.

### Impact and severity

- **Affected**: Any OpenClaw deployment using Code Mode (enabled by default on models with `compat.codeMode: 'preferred'` such as `gemini-3.5-flash`, `gemini-4-argon`, etc.) in messaging channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, Slack).
- **Severity**: High (causes container OOM crashes, SQLite lock contention, and silent task drop with false positive completion confirmation to the end user).
- **Frequency**: 100% reproducible when a user asks to schedule an automation via natural language in Code Mode without explicit system prompt workarounds.

### Additional information

Root causes in codebase:
1. `src/agents/code-mode.ts`: `formatCodeModeCatalogIndex` gives priority 0 to `isCoreCodingSurfaceToolName(entry.name)` (which puts shell `exec` at the top of the prompt index), while `automations` is given priority 1 or 2 and gets truncated when catalog exceeds `MAX_CODE_MODE_CATALOG_INDEX_CHARS` (8,000 chars across 61 tools).
2. Shell `exec` tool lacks an environment check or command blocker for `openclaw` CLI commands that mutate state or boot the CLI inside the Gateway container.
3. Mitigation applied locally: Adding strict CLI avoidance instructions to `AGENTS.md` (`Never call 'openclaw' via exec; call in-process globals`).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After `openclaw plugins reload` of a plugin that only registers a `before_tool_call` hook (a tool-policy guard, manifest `reload.turnHandover: true`), agent runs that were already admitted keep dispatching the hook to the disposed instance. Every later tool call of those runs is blocked (`Tool call blocked because before_tool_call hook failed` / `PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin <id> was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.`) until each run ends. Retrying inside the run does not help; a new turn works at once.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

**Where the stale instance is reached** (code at `dd896426271`, current main; none of these paths changed since v2026.11.10 except two unrelated lines in `mcp-http.ts` and the policy file):

1. A CLI-backend run's tool calls come in over the MCP loopback and run in the grant's captured request scope: `src/gateway/mcp-http.ts:488-502` → `runInMcpGrantRequestScope` (`src/gateway/mcp-http.grant-generation.ts:15-27`).
2. The hook runner picks the registry from that scope: the generation registry wins while it is not retired (`src/plugins/hook-runner-global-state.ts:123-133`). So the run keeps calling the old generation's `before_tool_call` registration.
3. The disposed instance refuses (`src/plugins/plugin-instance.ts:307-321`). It offers `replacement` only while the reservation is pending. Once the reload has applied, the reservation is released (`src/plugins/plugin-replacement-operation.ts:52-56`), so the error carries no `replacement`.
4. `isPluginReloadingError` needs `replacement` (`src/plugins/plugin-replacement-retry.ts:5-7`), so `HookDispatchSelection` does not reselect (`src/plugins/hook-dispatch-replacement.ts:52-55`). `runBeforeToolCallHook` fails closed (`src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.policy.ts:48`, `:344`).
5. #202446's re-admission outside the retired generation (`mcp-http.grant-generation.ts:34-59`) only triggers when tool *construction* throws. A hook-only plugin never makes construction fail, so the grant stays on the old generation for the rest of the run.

**Not isolated:** why the old generation registry stays un-retired after `Plugin replacement applied` in the failing cases, when in most runs the same handover rebinds fine. The candidate is the "whole-run hold yields its work count but keeps its custody" branch (`src/agents/plugin-turn-handover.ts:37-39`, `:71-74`). Both live and in the test, the failures followed a run being admitted around the reload request: live, a `cli live session start` landed between `replacement queued` and `applied`; in the test, a run waiting in the CLI lane behind another.

**Not a duplicate of:** #201903 / PR #203202 (cron Code Mode trigger evaluations, which hold no reference; that report assumes agent runs are safe). #156883 (stale plugin *tool handles* until restart; a 2026-10-03 comment there shows this hook symptom on 2026.9.6). #154891 (failed/rolled-back reload). #144291. PR #202446 (construction-time failures only).

**Test rig** (no model, no keys): two local plugins, loaded via `plugins.load.paths`.

- `hook-probe` (`openclaw.plugin.json`: `{"id":"hook-probe","activation":{"onStartup":true},"reload":{"turnHandover":true},"configSchema":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false}}`):

  ```js
  const fs = require("node:fs");
  const LOG = process.env.PROBE_DIR + "/out/hook.jsonl";
  module.exports = { id: "hook-probe", register(api) {
    const load = require("node:crypto").randomUUID().slice(0, 8);
    api.on("before_tool_call", (event) => {
      fs.appendFileSync(LOG, JSON.stringify({ at: new Date().toISOString(), load, tool: event.toolName }) + "\n");
    });
  } };
  ```

- `probe-cli`: a scripted CLI backend (`registerCliBackend({ id: "probe-cli", bundleMcp: true, bundleMcpMode: "claude-config-file", nativeToolMode: "none", config: { command: node, args: [client.mjs], output: "json", input: "arg", sessionMode: "always", sessionArgs: ["--session-id", "{sessionId}"], sessionIdFields: ["session_id"] } })`) plus a `probe_tick` tool. Its `client.mjs` reads `--mcp-config`, calls `initialize`, then `tools/call probe_tick` 10 times 1.5 s apart, and prints `{"result":"<ok>/10 tool calls ok","session_id":…}`.
- Config: `agents.defaults.model.primary probe-cli/local`, `tools.alsoAllow ["probe_tick"]`.
- Driver: run A `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:race-a --message "run the probe"` in the background; 4 s later `openclaw plugins reload hook-probe --json` in the background, and at the same moment run B (`race-b`). The CLI lane runs A then B. Count ok calls per run and `before_tool_call hook failed` lines.

**Test results**

| Build | Tries | Run A / run B | `hook failed` lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026.11.10 | 1 of ~25 | 4/10 / 0/10 | 16, from 1 s to 24 s after `Plugin replacement applied`; all hook calls after the reload went nowhere (only the 4 old-load calls were logged) |
| 2026.11.10 | other ~24 | 10/10 / 10/10 | 0; hook calls moved to the new load |
| main `dd896426271` | 8 | 10/10 / **0/10** every time | 0, but run B's calls of the CLI backend plugin's own tool fail with `Plugin "probe-cli" tool runtime is no longer active.`; with a core tool (`session_status`) run B is 10/10 (2/2); with no reload, both runs are 10/10 |

So the hook failure is a narrow race in the test (I could not make it deterministic), while on main a run that waits across a reload loses its plugin tools every time. The main result may be a separate cause; I can file it on its own if that helps.

**Fix direction (not attempted):** a refusal from an instance whose replacement has already applied could be retryable for hook dispatch (reselect against the current registry), or `resolveHookRegistry` could skip a captured generation whose instance for that plugin was replaced. The risk is the deliberate rule in `refuseFreshCall` never to offer a replacement to work the drain is joining.

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

1. Load a plugin that only registers `before_tool_call` (manifest `reload.turnHandover: true`) and run agents on a CLI backend (`bundleMcp: true`, so OpenClaw tools are called over the MCP loopback).
2. While one run is making tool calls and another is being admitted, run `openclaw plugins reload <hook-plugin> --json`.
3. Watch the gateway log after `Plugin replacement applied`. The live trigger (below) and a scripted rig are in the details block above.

### Expected behavior

After `Plugin replacement applied`, a running turn's next tool call goes to the new instance's hook: the gateway logs `Running turns on <id> continue on the new version at their next step`, and in most of our test runs that is what happens.

### Actual behavior

The runs' later tool calls are all blocked until each run ends: `before_tool_call hook failed: tool=exec … error=PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin tool-guard was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.` The agent sees `Tool call blocked because before_tool_call hook failed` and, retrying, fails again; one stopped its task. New turns started afterwards work.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10 (8a8ea66); code path unchanged on main dd896426271

### Operating system

Linux x86_64, Node 26

### Install method

npm global

### Model

claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 (live); scripted CLI backend, no model (test)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> claude-cli (Claude Code CLI; OpenClaw tools over the MCP loopback)

### Logs

Live gateway, 2026-11-25 (UTC), plugin `tool-guard` (hook only), 5 retained work items (running agents):

```
23:58:58.868 [reload] plugin metadata changed with identical config; applying plugin lifecycle
23:59:04.274 [event-loop] main-thread stall: elapsedMs=5334 task="secrets.prepare"
23:59:04.790 [gateway] Plugin replacement queued behind 5 retained work item(s) for plugin tool-guard. Running turns on tool-guard continue on the new version at their next step. …
23:59:04.791 [agents/plugin-turn-handover] plugin tool-guard reload requested; whole-run hold yields to the reload   (x5)
23:59:04.834 [agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 activeSessions=4
23:59:04.917 [gateway] Waiting for admitted plugin cleanup before replacing it.
23:59:05.245 [gateway] Plugin replacement applied: tool-guard
23:59:09.121 [agents/tools] before_tool_call hook failed: tool=process … error=PluginInstanceUnavailableError: Plugin tool-guard was reloaded or disabled; use its current tools.
…           13 such lines in total (exec, process, read, tool_search), last at 23:59:59.542
23:59:28.700 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=23875   (the run admitted at 23:59:04.8 ends)
```

### Impact and severity

Every agent that is mid-turn when a hook plugin reloads can lose all tools for the rest of that turn (about 50 s here), with no recovery inside the turn. Hook plugins are typically policy guards, so failing closed is right; what's wrong is that the dispatch stays on the disposed instance.

### Additional information

Workaround: end the affected turn; the next turn uses the new instance. Avoid reloading hook plugins while runs are starting.

issues.body:
## Problem

A collected group batch can run with the last sender's owner rights when one of its messages has no sender admission evidence.

`resolveCollectedRun` in `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain.ts` (lines 152-158 at `7a570c41bc27`) returns the source run unchanged when any item's participant comparison is not `"same"`:

```ts
if (
  participantComparison === "same" ||
  !items.every((item) => compareChannelAdmissionParticipants([item.channelAdmissionEvidence]) === "same")
) {
  return source;
}
```

The second clause is meant to detect "every item is verifiable". When one item is unverifiable it returns the **source** (the last item's run, including `senderIsOwner` and its private owner grant) instead of the stripped mixed-sender run below it.

## Impact

In a group chat with collect-mode queueing, a non-owner message without sender evidence collected together with an owner message can run with owner tools. Single-sender batches are unaffected.

## Expected

Unverifiable or mixed participants share no sender authority: the collected run drops the sender identity, `senderIsOwner` and the owner grant, as the mixed branch already does.

## Repro sketch

Owner and non-owner send in one group while a turn is running (collect mode). Make one queued item lack `channelAdmissionEvidence`. The drained collected run has `senderIsOwner: true`.

issues.body:
## Problem

Queued channel messages are refused after a Gateway restart and get no reply.

Native channel producers do not save a recovery source when they stage queued input (`reply-source-admission.ts`, `dispatch-from-config.lifecycle.ts`, `get-reply-run-execute.ts`). On restart replay, `src/gateway/queued-chat-inputs.ts` finds no recovery source and ends the row as `restart-unrecoverable` (lines 83 and 198 at `7a570c41bc27`). The bytes are cancelled, no reply is generated, and the sender sees nothing in the channel.

## Impact

A Telegram, Discord or Slack message queued behind a running turn is silently lost when the Gateway restarts (update, crash, config restart) before it starts. Control UI `chat.send` input is not affected because it saves a Gateway recovery source.

## Expected

Queued channel input either survives the restart and runs through normal start admission, or the sender gets a visible message in the channel that names the next step (send again).

## Repro sketch

1. In a channel chat, start a long turn and send a second message so it is queued.
2. Restart the Gateway before the first turn finishes.
3. The second message is never answered; the session row ends as `restart-unrecoverable`.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After upgrading to 2026.11.10, one long-running, image-heavy Slack channel session (~835k tokens) can no longer be compacted by either path. Manual `openclaw sessions compact` is refused by the session-history worker's 256 MiB pending-bytes cap, and automatic (trigger=budget) compaction times out after a fixed 60 s on every turn, so every turn of that agent stalls ~1 min and the session keeps growing. The same session compacted fine on 2026.10.x. Regression appears to come from the compaction facts view added in #201304.

My ops agent, Arkeologist, found the root cause and built the workaround below; filing so there's something to link to.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run 2026.11.10 with a long-lived channel session that has grown large since its last compaction (ours: ~38k transcript events / ~415 MB since last compaction, ~323 MB of that base64 images in tool results, ~835k tokens).
2. Run `openclaw sessions compact "<session key>" --agent <agent> --timeout 900000`.
3. Separately, let the session exceed its compaction budget and send a normal message so trigger=budget compaction runs.
4. Watch `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway | grep compaction-diag`.

### Expected behavior

- Large sessions can still be compacted, as on 2026.10.x.
- The manual path doesn't send the preflight facts back across the thread boundary (keep them worker-side or drop `source`), or sizes that request by what's actually transferred rather than JSON.stringify().length * 2.
- Compaction-preparation worker tasks use a timeout derived from agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds, not a fixed 60 s.
- Possibly: since the summarizer drops image data anyway, skip decoding image payloads during preparation.

### Actual behavior

Manual: fails after ~33 s with
  worker task capacity reached [task=sessionTranscript.task pool pending bytes: pendingBytes=0 maxPendingBytes=268435456 inputBytes=445943294]

Budget: every attempt ends "[compaction-diag] end ... trigger=budget outcome=failed reason=timeout durationMs≈60000" ("preflight compaction failed: worker task timed out"). Repeats on every turn.

Root cause (from the shipped dist):
1. prepareGatewaySessionCompaction runs a "preflight" in the session-history worker (27 s, succeeds) and gets back "source": per-entry compaction facts for the whole active window.
2. prepareEmbeddedCompactionSession sends that object straight back to the same worker as {kind:"plan", source}.
3. readPreparedCompaction sizes the request as JSON.stringify(e).length * 2 ≈ 446 MB, over the pool default maxPendingBytes (268,435,456). createSessionTranscriptHistoryPool doesn't set its own, and an oversize request is refused outright, not queued.
4. That estimate is ~4x too high. Running the shipped fact builder over the same rows offline: the facts contain no image bytes; real cost is ~133 MB heap / ~111 MB via v8.serialize (contextReplay ~47%, contextSummaries ~31%, summary ~10%). Building the estimate also creates a ~223M-char string on the Gateway main thread (~5 s stall under gateway:rpc:sessions.compact); a session ~2.4x larger would hit V8's max string length there.
5. On the budget path there's no prepared "source", so "plan" re-reads and decodes the whole window in one worker task. readPreparedCompaction passes no timeoutMs, so the 60 s default applies regardless of compaction.timeoutSeconds. The SQLite read alone logged elapsedMs=20783.

Workaround we're running (two one-line edits in dist/session-transcript-worker-resources-*.mjs, then a gateway restart):
- createSessionTranscriptHistoryPool: pass maxPendingBytes: 1073741824 to createOwnedWorkerTaskPool (this pool only; global default untouched).
- readPreparedCompaction: pass {timeoutMs: 3e5} to runRequest.
With that, manual compaction of the same session succeeded: 883,499 → 19,298 tokens in 165 s, no memory pressure on a 7.7 GB host.

I'll follow up with a PR for the sizing and timeout pieces.

Related: #201304, #195361, #180514, #191784, #197374, #196505

issues.body:
# Bug report: auto-compaction ignores the explicit reasoning-off UI setting; guard_blocked failure loop on thinking-enabled backends

**OpenClaw version:** 2026.11.7 (e31bbf0) — first hit; behavior differs from v2026.11.3 (see "Regression history")
**OS / runtime:** Linux x64 (Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0-44-generic), Node v24.22.3
**Surface:** webchat dashboard sessions, auto-compaction
**Provider:** custom OpenAI-compatible provider (model `Qwen3.8-Flash-Event`), 128K context

## Summary

When the reasoning/thinking selector in the UI is set to **off** (the default), normal agent turns honor it, but **compaction (session summarization) requests do not**. The compaction path applies the `thinkingLevelMap` mapping only if the model definition declares `reasoning: true`. For any model that does not declare this flag, no thinking-off signal is sent at all, and the server's default applies.

On backends that **default to thinking enabled server-side** (common for Qwen-style models behind OpenAI-compatible proxies), the hidden reasoning output consumes the whole completion budget. The summary comes back truncated, and since v2026.11.6+ compaction rejects truncated summaries, every auto-compaction attempt fails with `guard_blocked`. The session is then permanently stuck once it reaches the compaction threshold — it can neither compact nor continue.

This is a product-level sync defect, not a model misconfiguration: the user explicitly chose "off" in the UI, and that choice must reach the request on **all** completion paths. Asking every user to add `reasoning: true` + `thinkingLevelMap` to each of their (potentially many, arbitrary) models to work around the defect is not acceptable as the primary resolution.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a provider/model that:
   - is **not** declared with `reasoning: true` in `models.providers.<id>.models[n]`, and
   - defaults to thinking **enabled** server-side (and, in my case, ignores `max_tokens`, so thinking is not bounded by the output budget).
2. Leave the UI reasoning level at its default **off**.
3. Use the session normally until it approaches the compaction threshold (128K context here).
4. Wait for auto-compaction, or trigger `/compact`.

### Observed

- Gateway log (sanitized, 2026-11-24): **22/22 compaction attempts** failed:
  `outcome=failed reason=guard_blocked`
- The session cannot recover: every retry fails identically while the UI still shows reasoning = off.
- Normal (non-compaction) turns with the same model and the same UI setting succeed — the difference in behavior between the two paths is what isolates the defect to compaction.

## Root cause (from the shipped dist bundle)

- **Agent-turn path** (`dist/attempt-*.mjs`) explicitly passes `openclawThinkingExplicit` (the user's explicit UI choice) down to the transport, so "off" is emitted as a real signal even for proxy-like endpoints.
- **Compaction path** (`dist/compaction-*.mjs` → `resolveAgentReasoningOption`, reached from the summarization completion via `resolveAgentCoreCompleteFn` / `runSummarizationCompletionFromSource`) only applies `thinkingLevelMap` (e.g. `{"off":"none"}`) **when the model declares `reasoning: true`**. If the flag is absent, no thinking parameter is attached at all.
- Verified by grep over the installed bundle: `openclawThinkingExplicit` appears in the agent-turn/transport modules but **does not appear anywhere in the compaction modules** — the explicit-user-choice marker is simply dropped on this path.

Net effect: compaction silently falls back to the server default (thinking on), the summary is truncated by the token budget, and the truncated-summary guard turns a recoverable quality problem into a hard, repeating failure.

## Regression history

- **v2026.11.3:** same missing sync, but truncated summaries were accepted, so compaction "worked" (with degraded summaries) and the defect was invisible.
- **v2026.11.6+ (incl. 2026.11.7):** the strict rejection of truncated summaries is a good change, but it exposes the sync defect as a permanent compaction failure loop. The guard is not the problem; the un-sent reasoning-off signal is.

## Expected behavior

The UI reasoning selector is an explicit user intent and must be honored on **every** completion path, including compaction/summarization, regardless of whether the model definition declares `reasoning: true`. If the user selected "off", OpenClaw should emit the corresponding provider signal (or, at minimum, a documented per-provider off-control) whenever it makes a compaction request.

## Suggested fix

1. Thread the same explicit reasoning option (`openclawThinkingExplicit`, or an equivalent "user explicitly chose X" marker) from agent-turn options into the compaction completion path, and apply the thinking control based on that explicit choice — not only on the model's declared capability flag.
2. For models without a declared reasoning control: either (a) still send the provider-standard off signal where one exists (e.g. `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false` / `thinking: disabled` shapes already used elsewhere), or (b) log a clear one-time warning like "model <id> has no declared reasoning control; UI setting may not apply to compaction", so the failure mode is visible instead of mysterious.
3. When compaction fails repeatedly with `guard_blocked`, surface an actionable message in the session UI (today it is only visible in gateway logs).

## Workaround applied (confirms the diagnosis, but is not the fix)

Added to `openclaw.json` for the affected models:

```json
"reasoning": true,
"thinkingLevelMap": { "off": "none" }
```

After this, one previously stuck session compacted successfully (`131648 -> 15312 tokens`). This proves the "off" signal reaches the backend when the mapping is enabled. However, it requires every user to hand-edit each model definition to compensate for a system rule — which is exactly what should not be necessary. (One session continued to fail after the change; whether that was an in-flight guard/state issue or a remaining path gap was not fully isolated.)

## Impact

- Any user on a thinking-enabled-by-default model without `reasoning: true` declared can be locked out of auto-compaction entirely once their session grows past the threshold.
- The failure is silent in chat and opaque in the UI (log-only `guard_blocked`), with no hint that the UI reasoning setting was never sent.

### Summary
A configured core tool provider (`web_search` pinned to `provider: "codex"`) failed 100% of calls across all sessions for **34 days** (October 22 → November 25, 2026) with zero operator visibility — no Gateway log error, no Control UI or `openclaw status`/`doctor` warning, and no distinction in `audit_events` between a dead provider and ordinary transient tool retries.

### Problem
When a configured tool or provider breaks permanently (for example, an expired or removed OAuth credential after migrating providers, a revoked API key, or a vestigial config pin like `tools.web.search.provider: "codex"`), OpenClaw currently provides no passive signal to the operator that the capability is dead:

1. **Silent per-turn workarounds hide systemic failure.** Each failed `web_search` call returns a `provider_error` JSON payload directly to the model (`Search failed (HTTP 401)`). Capable models routinely work around the failure on the spot (falling back to `web_fetch` on known URLs, browser automation, or local knowledge) and complete the user's request without mentioning the failure — or mentioning it only as a passing footnote.
2. **Gateway file logs record nothing.** Across 37+ MB/day of Gateway logs (`openclaw-*.log`) on Nov 24–25, there were **0 entries** mentioning `web_search`, `provider_error`, or the Codex `HTTP 401` failure — even while dozens of `web_search` calls failed during those exact hours.
3. **Configuration UI only checks presence, not health.** **Settings → Search** reports a provider as "Configured" based on config/credential presence rather than live or recent execution outcomes (as documented in `docs/tools/web.md`: *"Configured means credential or setup information is present. It does not prove that the provider accepts the credential or is reachable."*).
4. **Audit records flatten the cause and roll over quickly.** `openclaw audit --kind tool_action --status failed` records every failure with the same generic `errorCode: "tool_failed"` (without the HTTP status, provider name, or `provider_error` category). In addition, `audit_events` caps at ~100k rolling rows (~28–36 hours on an active multi-session Gateway), so without external snapshots the historical transition from healthy → broken is lost.
5. **No way to distinguish a dead tool from noisy-but-healthy tools.** In the same ~28-hour live audit window where `web_search` had a **100% failure rate** (19 failed, 0 succeeded), `browser` had **450** `tool_failed` events (mostly routine stale-ref / missing-element retries during normal automation). Raw failure counts alone cannot surface a permanently broken capability without drowning in routine retry noise.

### Context & Forensic Timeline (Real Production Instance)
**Environment:**
- Local macOS Gateway (arm64), currently running **OpenClaw `2026.11.10` (`b22df8b94835`)** (the 34-day outage spanned multiple upgrades from October through `2026.11.10`).
- Relevant config in `openclaw.json` (unchanged since before Nov 17):
  ```json
  {
    "tools": {
      "web": {
        "search": {
          "enabled": true,
          "provider": "codex",
          "openaiCodex": {
            "enabled": true,
            "mode": "cached"
          }
        },
        "fetch": {
          "enabled": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
  ```
- Background: The operator had previously used Codex OAuth and later migrated primary inference to another router/provider, leaving `tools.web.search.provider: "codex"` behind as a vestigial pin (with `plugins.entries.openai.enabled: false` and `plugins.entries.codex.enabled: true`).

**Observed timeline reconstructed from `openclaw audit` + 15 retained SQLite backup snapshots (`audit_events`):**

| Window (UTC) | `web_search` Succeeded | `web_search` Failed | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| **2026-09-14 → 2026-10-22 23:34** | **602** | **4** | Healthy baseline (~99.3% success rate across 39 days) |
| **2026-10-22 23:34:03 UTC** | — | — | **Last recorded `web_search` success** (5:34 PM MDT) |
| **2026-10-22 23:46 → 2026-10-26 01:03** | *(no snapshot)* | *(no snapshot)* | ~3-day gap due to ~100k-row rolling `audit_events` cap |
| **2026-10-26 → 2026-10-29 06:30** | **0** | **34** | 100% failure rate (`Oct 26`: 7, `Oct 27`: 13, `Oct 28`: 12, `Oct 29`: 2) |
| **2026-10-29 06:30 → 2026-11-24 14:15** | *(no snapshot)* | *(no snapshot)* | ~26-day gap due to rolling `audit_events` cap |
| **2026-11-24 14:15 → 2026-11-26 02:51** | **0** | **71** | 100% failure rate (`Nov 24`: 53, `Nov 25`: 6, `Nov 26`: 12 through 02:23 UTC) |

- **Total observed after last success:** **105 failed, 0 succeeded** across 11+ distinct dashboard and subagent sessions in the captured windows alone (with 29 days of unobserved gaps in between, implying hundreds of silent failures over 34 days).
- **How it was finally discovered:** Only by accident on **2026-11-25 at 8:22 PM MST**, when an assistant happened to include a parenthetical footnote (`web_search returned HTTP 401 from the Codex search provider, so I pulled the docs directly via web_fetch`) in a research reply.
- **Live tool-failure landscape (~28-hour audit window on 2026-11-24 → 2026-11-26):**
  - `browser`: 450 `tool_failed` (normal UI/ref churn)
  - `dispatch_action`: 305 `tool_failed`
  - `sessions_search`: 42 `tool_failed`
  - `skill_workshop`: 40 `tool_failed`
  - `tool_search`: 35 `tool_failed`
  - `automations`: 35 `tool_failed`
  - `web_search`: 19 `tool_failed` (**0 succeeded — completely dead**)

### Impact
- **Affected:** Operators running long-lived OpenClaw Gateways across provider/auth migrations or expiring credentials (search providers, MCP servers, external API tools).
- **Severity:** High (silent degradation of a core agent capability across every session and subagent).
- **Frequency:** Persistent — once a configured provider credential breaks, 100% of calls fail indefinitely until the operator happens to notice a side comment.
- **Consequence:** Over a full month of degraded research, wasted tool-call turns/latency on guaranteed `401` failures, and assistants silently falling back to slower or less complete workarounds without the operator ever knowing the tool was broken.

### Scope Note (Problem-Focused)
This issue intentionally does **not** prescribe a specific UI, notification channel, or implementation mechanism. The core problem to solve is **operator observability for persistently failing tools/providers**: when a configured capability stops working across sessions (e.g., sustained auth/provider errors or 0% success over consecutive calls), operators currently have no practical way to notice or diagnose it from the Gateway without manually mining `audit_events` backups.

### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

OpenClaw 2026.10.10's gateway was killed by the Linux host OOM killer at 2026-11-04 20:24:39 UTC with approximately 5.49 GiB anonymous RSS, after slow large-session operations; this is a production incident report, not a confirmed memory leak or deterministic reproduction.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The gateway continues serving the existing Telegram workload, as it did immediately before the incident: successful outbound deliveries were logged at 20:22:42 and 20:22:56 UTC. No controlled comparison or known-good version for this workload has been established.

### Actual behavior

- Before the kill, the gateway logged slow session actor, transcript-export, and context-snapshot operations. One actor operation reported 18,374 transcript events and 18,373 active events.
- At 20:24:39 UTC the kernel explicitly recorded `global_oom` / `CONSTRAINT_NONE` and killed `openclaw-gateway` (kernel process name truncated to `openclaw-gatewa`).
- At 20:24:40.950 UTC the image entrypoint recorded gateway exit status 137.
- A subsequent loopback request to `http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz` returned HTTP 503 with `{"ok":false,"status":"unavailable"}`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10 (7dc3350)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 25.04, Linux 6.14.0-37-generic x86_64; container Node.js v24.22.2.

### Install method

Docker via Coolify 4.5.3, using the third-party `coollabsio/openclaw:latest` image. The installed OpenClaw version was checked directly with `openclaw --version`; no upgrade was performed during investigation.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

Telegram -> OpenClaw gateway -> Codex app-server is present in the preceding turn logs. The exact effective model/provider request at the instant of the kill was not established.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Relevant workload configuration and storage measurements:

- `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent = 4`
- `agents.defaults.subagents.maxConcurrent = 8`
- Main agent SQLite database approximately 1.1 GiB on disk.

These are configured limits, not measured simultaneous active-run counts. No provider authentication failure has been established as the cause of the process death.

### Logs

Sanitized extracts from the host kernel journal and container stdout; timestamps are UTC. Hostname, PIDs, container/cgroup identifiers, database paths, session/chat identifiers, and message content are omitted.

```text
2026-11-04T20:22:55.331Z [sqlite/transaction]

actorResident=false actorTranscriptEvents=18374 actorActiveEvents=18373
actorReadMs=5745 elapsedMs=5801

2026-11-04T20:23:27.412Z [sqlite/transaction]
operation="session transcript export batch"
elapsedMs=12725 phases={"beginMs":2,"sqlMs":12724,"hostAdmissionWaitMs":0,"databaseAdmissionWaitMs":0,"commitMs":1}
isMainThread=false

2026-11-04T20:23:41.102Z [sqlite/transaction]
operation="session context snapshot read"
elapsedMs=9683 phases={"beginMs":1,"sqlMs":9681,"hostAdmissionWaitMs":0,"databaseAdmissionWaitMs":0,"commitMs":2}
isMainThread=false

2026-11-04T20:24:39+00:00 kernel:
oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE,...,global_oom,
task_memcg=<openclaw-container>,task=openclaw-gatewa,pid=<redacted>,uid=0

2026-11-04T20:24:39+00:00 kernel:
Out of memory: Killed process <redacted> (openclaw-gatewa)
total-vm:6133916kB, anon-rss:5757808kB, file-rss:296kB,

2026-11-04T20:24:40.949Z /app/scripts/entrypoint.sh: line 648:
<gateway-pid> Killed openclaw gateway run
2026-11-04T20:24:40.950Z [entrypoint]
gateway exited with status 137; /healthz will return 503
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Read-only measurements from the same still-running container/host:

| Measurement | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Host `MemTotal` | 7,936,608 KiB (~7.57 GiB) |
| Host swap | None; `/proc/swaps` has only the header |
| Container `memory.max` | `max` |
| Docker `HostConfig.Memory` | `0` (no explicit container RAM cap) |
| Container `memory.peak` | 6,428,008,448 bytes (~5.99 GiB; entire cgroup, not gateway RSS alone) |
| Container `memory.events` | `low 0; high 0; max 0; oom 0; oom_kill 3; oom_group_kill 0` |
| Docker restart policy / count | `unless-stopped` / `0` |
| Container status | Running, unhealthy |

The cgroup counters cover the container lifetime, not three confirmed gateway crashes. The kernel record, rather than exit code 137 alone, establishes a **host/global OOM kill**, not a container memory-cap hit.

The inspected 20:00-20:25 UTC stdout window contained no matching `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` or `FATAL ERROR` entries. This does not exclude earlier worker failures or establish how memory was divided among V8 heaps, native allocations, or worker threads. No heap profile or time series was captured before death.

### Impact and severity

One confirmed gateway process death on one production installation, blocking gateway availability and its Telegram workflow. Frequency beyond this incident is unknown; no permanent data loss is established.

Deployment-specific recovery context: the third-party image intentionally keeps PID 1/nginx alive after gateway death, leaving HTTP 503 and an unhealthy container instead of exiting. Consequently Docker's restart policy did not trigger. This is documented in the [image entrypoint](https://github.com/coollabsio/openclaw/blob/main/scripts/entrypoint.sh), and is separate from attribution of OpenClaw's memory use.

### Additional information

**Investigation candidates, not confirmed allocation owners:**

- The version-matched [v2026.10.10 actor hydration code](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/config/sessions/session-actor-hydration.worker.ts) aggregates session identities, active-event rows, and navigation rows without a row limit before decoding them into JS collections. [Merged PR #172970](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172970) introduces bounded resident actor hydration. This source comparison does not prove that actor hydration allocated the ~5.5 GiB observed here, or that the merged change resolves this incident; no newer-package comparison was run.
- Related [#191273](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191273) and [#191847](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191847) concern SQLite worker heap OOM. This incident killed the entire gateway via the host kernel; a shared allocator/cause has not been demonstrated.
- [#154812](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154812) concerns high gateway RSS outside V8 heap on an older version. This installation has no corresponding heap/RSS breakdown, so it cannot yet be classified as the same cause.

Could maintainers advise which supported, payload-free diagnostics should capture gateway/worker/native memory attribution and distinguish large-history/concurrency pressure from retained allocations? Confirmation of which published release includes the bounded actor hydration change would also help target a version comparison.

No restart, configuration change, transcript rewrite, compaction, or database repair was performed during this investigation. No private transcripts, database files, credentials, raw configuration, or full logs are attached.

issues.title: [Bug]: Memory reindex exceeds worker input limit because session.current sends full replacement including embeddings

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Normal backlog priority with limited blast radius.

labels.name: impact:session-state
labels.description: Session, memory, transcript, context, or agent state can drift or corrupt.

issues.body:
### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.10.10, memory indexing fails with `WorkerTaskError: worker task capacity reached` even when the Gateway is stopped and no other worker tasks are pending.

The `session.current` check in `assertMemorySessionNotForgotten` sends the entire session source replacement, including chunks and embeddings, to the read worker. The reader only uses `agentId` and `sessionId`. On the affected installation this unnecessary payload exceeds the 256 MiB worker input limit.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (`7dc3350`)
- Linux under WSL2, Gateway managed by systemd user service
- Bundled Node 24.19.0
- SQLite agent database
- Memory provider: Gemini, `gemini-embedding-001`, 3072 dimensions
- Sources: memory and sessions

### Observed reproduction

1. Existing memory index had 118/121 files indexed and required rebuilding because of `chunking_version` identity mismatch; vector search was paused.
2. Stop the Gateway through systemd and wait for exclusive offline ownership.
3. Run `openclaw memory index --agent main`.
4. Indexing fails with `Memory index failed (main): worker task capacity reached`.
5. Restrict the `session.current` input to the two identifiers and rerun the same command: indexing completes successfully.

This was reproduced on an existing installation, not a minimal clean fixture. No private conversation content or database is attached.

### Diagnostic evidence

Temporary instrumentation of the worker admission error (subsequently removed) captured:

```json
{
  "inputBytes": 270109442,
  "pendingTasks": 0,
  "pendingBytes": 0,
  "kind": "index-read",
  "compute": {
    "limit": 9,
    "active": 0,
    "waitingPools": 0,
    "pendingTasks": 0,
    "pendingBytes": 0
  }
}
```

The input exceeds `268435456` bytes. This is an oversized single request, rather than concurrent queue saturation.

Relevant stack, with installation prefixes omitted:

```text
WorkerTaskPoolCore.enqueue (dist/src-BIG1flG6.mjs:1013)
WorkerTaskPoolCore.run (dist/src-BIG1flG6.mjs:958)
WorkerTaskPool.run (dist/worker-task-pool-b3d99sVy.mjs:125)
runRetrieval (dist/manager-cpu-worker-runtime-DyhbW6NE.mjs:27)
runMemoryIndexRead (dist/manager-cpu-worker-runtime-DyhbW6NE.mjs:97)
MemoryIndexDatabase.read (dist/extensions/memory-core/manager-runtime.js:704)
assertMemorySessionNotForgotten (dist/extensions/memory-core/manager-runtime.js:2981)
dist/extensions/memory-core/manager-runtime.js:3355
```

Gateway logs before the offline reproduction also showed:

```text
[memory] sync failed (watch): WorkerTaskError: worker task capacity reached
[memory] session update failed: WorkerTaskError: worker task capacity reached
```

### Cause and minimal fix verified locally

The installed implementation passed the complete replacement:

```js
const predicate = await database.read({
  type: "session.current",
  input: session
}, assertCurrent);
```

The `session.current` reader in `dist/manager-index-read-DrB3q5E0.mjs` only calls:

```js
hasMemorySessionTombstone(db, command.input.agentId, command.input.sessionId)
```

Changing the request to the following preserves the tombstone check while avoiding transmission and JSON size estimation of unrelated embeddings:

```diff
 type: "session.current",
-input: session
+input: { agentId: session.agentId, sessionId: session.sessionId }
```

This local patch was applied with a backup; no worker limits were raised and no memories or conversations were deleted.

### Validation

- Syntax check passed.
- The same `openclaw memory index --agent main` completed: `121 files indexed`.
- Subsequent status: 121/121 files, 3885 chunks, `Dirty: no`; the chunking identity mismatch / vector-search-paused warning disappeared.
- Gateway restarted and connectivity check passed.

Suggested regression coverage: verify that the session-current worker command contains only agent/session identity even when its source replacement contains large embeddings.

### Related report

#190528 concerns stale-error persistence after a forget/index collision in the same publication area. This report is specifically about oversized `session.current` worker input, with no forgotten session required.

A Gateway shutdown/restart hang was also observed during troubleshooting, but we have not established that it shares this cause.

issues.title: [Bug]: Gateway pins a CPU core forever: prepared model catalog refresh loop (OpenAI live catalog TTL 60s < per-agent refresh time)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: regression
labels.description: Behavior that previously worked and now fails

labels.name: P2

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary


**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (eb377ac), Node 24.19.0, Linux x64, gateway via systemd user service
**Setup:** 7 agents (main, review-controller, cursor, cursor-minimum, codex-reviewer, heartbeat-monitor, openclaw), all using `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` through the Codex harness. Enabled plugins include `acpx`, `codex`, `whatsapp`, `openai`, `ollama`, `claude-mem`, `gitlab-review-bot`.

## Symptom
- The `prepared-model-catalog.worker.js` worker thread sits at ~100% CPU from gateway start and never goes idle.
- 4 V8 GC threads run at 40–100% each. Gateway RSS grows from about 2 GB to more than 9 GB over a few hours (systemd reported a 15.7G memory peak). The host becomes sluggish.
- `~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/<id>/captures/openclaw-model-catalog-*/` creates and deletes an `openclaw-plugin-build-*` directory every 4–10 s, alternating between the `acpx` capture (618 MB, which bundles `@openai/codex` and `@anthropic-ai/*`) and the `codex` capture (372 MB). The directory reached 7.9 GB.
- Restarting and running `openclaw doctor --fix` do not help. The loop resumes right after `gateway ready`.

## Evidence
CPU profile of the worker (10 s): 26% `Hash.update`, 25% `recordContent` (`plugin-generation-artifact-*.mjs:808`), 15% GC, about 10% lstat/read/realpath.

Hot stack, about 93% of worker samples:
```
runCatalogRequest            prepared-model-catalog.worker.js:109
load                         prepared-model-runtime.plugin-generation-*.mjs:1614
acquireAgentRuntimePluginRegistry  runtime-plugins-*.mjs:219
acquirePluginRegistryForInspection loader-runtime-load-*.mjs:6665
withPluginCache              plugin-cache-*.mjs:262
loadOpenClawPluginsCore      loader-runtime-load-*.mjs:5178
loadCandidate                loader-runtime-load-*.mjs:5389   -> copy()+hash of plugin package
```

Logpoint on `runCatalogRequest` (75 s window):
```
20:22:53 agent=review-controller providers=["openai"]
20:23:08 agent=main              providers=["openai"]
20:23:21 agent=cursor            providers=["openai"]
20:23:34 agent=cursor-minimum    providers=["openai"]
20:23:47 agent=codex-reviewer    providers=["openai"]
... then repeats
```

## Root cause
1. `OPENAI_MODELS_CACHE_TTL_MS` and `OPENAI_CODEX_MODELS_CACHE_TTL_MS` are `6e4` (`extensions/openai` provider). Through `recordLiveCatalogExpiry`, this becomes the `expiresAt` of the `openai` provider in every agent's prepared catalog inventory.
2. `refreshExpiredCatalog()` (`prepared-model-runtime-*.mjs:250`) runs on catalog reads such as `models.list` or `models.authStatus`. It queues `acquireCatalog({ providerIds: ["openai"], refresh: true })` for each agent owner.
3. Each worker request rebuilds the plugin registry from scratch. That means copying and hashing every runtime plugin package, including the 600 MB+ `acpx`. It takes about 13 s per agent, and requests are serialized in the single worker.
4. 7 agents × ~13 s ≈ 90 s, which is more than the 60 s TTL. The first agent's catalog has expired again before the last agent finishes, so the worker never idles.

## Suggested fixes
- Reuse or cache the captured plugin generation across catalog refreshes when plugin sources are unchanged, instead of re-capturing and re-hashing on every request.
- Refresh provider catalogs once per credential group instead of once per agent. Agents sharing credentials should share the result.
- Make the live catalog TTL configurable. At minimum, don't start a new refresh round until the previous one has finished (no TTL shorter than refresh time).
- Put the `plugin-captures` directory under a size bound and clean it up.

## Local workaround
Set both constants to `36e5` (1 h) in `dist/openai-provider-BTlZbwVX.mjs` and `dist/extensions/openai/.setup/openai-provider-BG-q98qt.mjs`.


### Steps to reproduce
1. Install OpenClaw 2026.9.6 and run the gateway as a service (`openclaw gateway --port 18789` under systemd).
2. Authenticate the `openai` provider (Codex / ChatGPT OAuth or API key), so its models come from the live catalog.
3. Enable at least one heavy runtime plugin, for example `acpx` (its captured package is about 618 MB because it bundles `@openai/codex` and `@anthropic-ai/*`), plus `codex`.
4. Configure several agents (we have 7) that all use an `openai/*` model, for example `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`.
5. Start the gateway and open the Control UI dashboard (`http://127.0.0.1:18789/`). The UI polls `models.list` / `models.authStatus`, which triggers `refreshExpiredCatalog()`.
6. Wait about 2 minutes after `gateway ready`.

**Observe:**
- `top -H -p <gateway pid>`: one `WorkerThread` stays at about 100% CPU indefinitely, and the V8 GC threads are busy.
- `ls -l --time-style=+%T ~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures/*/captures/openclaw-model-catalog-*/` run every 10 s: new `openclaw-plugin-build-*` directories keep appearing and disappearing (acpx / codex captures), and the total size grows by several GB.
- Gateway RSS keeps growing over hours.

**Rough threshold:** the loop becomes permanent when `number_of_agents × per-agent refresh time` exceeds 60 s. Here that was 7 × ~13 s ≈ 90 s. Fewer agents or lighter plugins may only show periodic spikes.

**To confirm:** raise `OPENAI_MODELS_CACHE_TTL_MS` / `OPENAI_CODEX_MODELS_CACHE_TTL_MS` to `36e5` in `dist/openai-provider-*.mjs` and `dist/extensions/openai/.setup/openai-provider-*.mjs`, then restart. The worker should go idle after the initial round.

### Expected behavior

- After the initial prepared model catalog build, `prepared-model-catalog.worker.js` goes idle. CPU usage drops to near 0% until the next scheduled refresh.
- When a live provider catalog (for example `openai`) expires, the refresh runs once and finishes well within the TTL. It must not overlap or chain into a new round before the previous one has finished.
- Agents that share the same provider credentials share one catalog refresh, instead of one full refresh per agent.
- A refresh for a single provider does not re-capture and re-hash every runtime plugin package (such as `acpx` or `codex`) when their sources are unchanged. The captured plugin generation is reused.
- `~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures` stays bounded in size, and stale capture directories are cleaned up.
- Gateway memory (RSS) stays stable over time, not growing from about 2 GB to more than 9 GB within a few hours.

### Actual behavior

- The catalog worker runs at about 100% CPU continuously from startup, and never goes idle.
- It refreshes `providers=["openai"]` once per agent, back to back, about 13 s each. By the time the last agent finishes, the first agent's catalog has expired again, so the rounds never end.
- Every request re-captures and re-hashes the `acpx` (618 MB) and `codex` (372 MB) plugin packages. The capture directory reaches 7.9 GB.
- Gateway RSS grows to more than 9 GB, and heavy GC slows the whole host.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS x86_64

### Install method

npm global

### Model

codex-sol-medium

### Provider / routing chain

codex

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

**Suggested severity: High.** No data loss or security impact. But the gateway degrades continuously on a normal multi-agent setup, and neither a restart nor `openclaw doctor --fix` helps.

**Impact observed:**
- **Constant CPU burn.** One core is pinned at about 100% (worker) plus about 2 more cores of GC. Gateway process CPU was about 230–320% sustained. systemd reported 8h 34m of CPU time for a process that had run for only about 2.5 h.
- **Memory growth.** RSS climbs from about 2 GB after start to more than 9 GB within a few hours (systemd memory peak 15.7 GB). The 64 GB host was also swapping heavily (7 of 8 GB swap used).
- **Disk churn.** About 100 MB/s of copy+hash into `~/.openclaw/tmp/plugin-captures`, which reached 7.9 GB.
- **Degraded responsiveness.** `slow SQLite session write` with queue waits up to 5 s. RPCs such as `tools.effective`, `projects.list` and `sessions.github.options` take 7–9 s. Agent runs feel slow to users.
- **Host-wide slowdown.** Other applications on the machine (IDE, browser) became sluggish, with load average around 11.

**Who is affected:** likely anyone with several agents on a live-catalog provider (`openai`) plus large runtime plugins such as `acpx`/`codex`. Severity scales with `agents × plugin size`. Single-agent setups may only see periodic spikes.

**Workaround:** none via config. The only mitigations are patching the TTL constants in `dist`, which is lost on update, reducing the number of agents, or disabling heavy plugins.

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.body:
## Summary

On 2026.10.9 (gateway in Kubernetes), stdio MCP server child processes accumulate over time: the gateway keeps spawning fresh instances of the same configured stdio server while the previous instances stay alive indefinitely. Each orphan holds its full RSS, contributing to container memory pressure until the kernel OOM-kills the pod.

## Evidence

Agent with Google's `analytics-mcp` configured as a stdio MCP server (python, launched via uv). Within ~1h45m of a fresh container start, six instances were alive simultaneously:

```
USER   PID %CPU %MEM    VSZ    RSS START COMMAND
node 14606  0.0  0.4 320864 141936 21:55 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
node 10778  0.0  0.4 320860 137164 21:44 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
node 17477  0.0  0.4 320860 141832 22:08 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
node 30894  0.9  0.4 320860 141924 23:00 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
node 31201  2.1  0.4 320860 142004 23:02 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
node 31419  5.8  0.4 320860 141924 23:02 .../bin/python .../bin/analytics-mcp
```

(Container started 21:18; only the newest instance appears to serve traffic. The rest never exit and are never killed.)

That is ~850MB of leaked RSS in under 2 hours, growing roughly linearly with session/cron activity (~1GB/day on this agent). The pod was OOM-killed at its 18Gi limit the same evening (the leak was a contributor alongside page-cache pressure from a large agent DB).

## Expected

When a session/run that spawned a stdio MCP server ends — or when a replacement instance is launched — the old child process (and its descendants, for npm/uv wrapper chains) should be killed and reaped.

## Notes

- Looks like the same class of bug reported against other MCP hosts (host kills only the wrapper, not the process tree; stdio servers do not exit on stdin close).
- 2026.10.10's notes mention child-process *metrics* ("identify more launch owners") but no reaping fix.
- Workaround we are deploying: a periodic reaper that kills all but the newest instance of each stdio server binary.

Happy to provide more diagnostics (gateway logs around spawn times, MCP config shape) if useful.

issues.body:
## Summary

The OpenClaw gateway process suffers from a severe memory leak. RSS grows from ~350 MB at startup to 15.5 GB over 2-3 days of normal use, eventually causing the process to be killed by the OS OOM killer. This triggers repeated `launchd-handoff` restart cycles.

## Environment

- **OpenClaw version**: 2026.6.1 (2e08f0f)
- **Node.js**: v22.22.0
- **OS**: macOS 20.6.0 (Big Sur), x64
- **System RAM**: 8 GB
- **Plugins loaded**: claw-mem (v6.15.0), claw-ctx (v5.2.0) — custom local plugins

## Evidence

### Before Restart (memory leak peak)

```
PID 19893  RSS: 15,513 MB  CPU: 89.7%  (openclaw-gateway)
PID 40226  RSS:    201 MB  CPU:  0.0%  (openclaw-tui, running 2+ days)
```

### After Restart (immediately)

```
PID 19926  RSS:    350 MB  CPU:  0.3%  (openclaw-gateway)
PID 40226  RSS:    197 MB  CPU:  0.0%  (openclaw-tui)
```

The gateway dropped from 15.5 GB to 350 MB after a single restart, confirming a **memory leak in the long-running process**, not a configuration or disk-space issue.

### Restart/Crash Frequency

From `~/.openclaw/logs/gateway-restart.log`, `launchd-handoff` restarts (process died → launchd auto-restarted):

| Date | Count | Pattern |
|------|:-----:|---------|
| 2026-06-04 | 6 | Including one I/O error (`Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error`) |
| 2026-06-05 | 9 | 8 crashes within a 2-hour window |
| 2026-06-09 | 7 | Before manual restart, 7 crashes between 00:41 and 03:33 UTC |

### Crashes Produce No Error Logs

The gateway error log (`gateway.err.log`) has no entries since May 21. The process dies silently — consistent with OOM kill or Node.js heap exhaustion with no chance to write diagnostics.

## Analysis

1. **Memory growth is monotonic**: RSS increases steadily over days, never decreases.
2. **No automatic recovery**: The process dies silently, leaving only `launchd` to restart it.
3. **Plugin state accumulation suspected**: With `claw-mem` (in-memory index, search cache) and `claw-ctx` (token caches, session state, drift alerts) loaded, the gateway never purges accumulated state between sessions.
4. **No heap limit configured**: The gateway Node.js process has no `--max-old-space-size` flag. On an 8 GB machine, this means it can consume all available RAM before being killed.
5. **Physical RAM saturation**: 15.5 GB RSS on an 8 GB machine causes heavy swapping, degrading the entire system before the OOM kill.

## Impact

- **Critical**: Gateway becomes unresponsive or crashes multiple times per day
- Intermediate crashes interrupt ongoing conversations and tool operations
- Repeated restart cycles generate noise in stability logs
- Degrades confidence in OpenClaw as a reliable long-running agent platform

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Root cause**: Investigate and fix memory leaks in the gateway process, particularly around plugin lifecycle (plugin state not released between sessions) and internal caches (unbounded growth).
2. **Self-protection**: Add a `--max-old-space-size` default (e.g., 4096 MB) to the gateway Node.js process to trigger a clean GC/OOM error before the OS OOM killer.
3. **Health monitoring**: Implement an RSS-based self-restart (e.g., if RSS > 4 GB, gracefully restart). This is a pragmatic safeguard even after the leak is fixed.
4. **Periodic restart**: Consider an optional `--auto-restart-interval` flag (e.g., daily at 3 AM) for production deployments.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start `openclaw gateway` with memory/caching plugins loaded
2. Use the gateway normally over 2-3 days (send messages, perform tool calls)
3. Monitor RSS with `ps -o pid,rss,comm`
4. Observe RSS grow from ~350 MB to 10+ GB
5. Eventually the process is killed by the OS

## Additional Context

A prior separate issue (May 21) caused a startup crash loop: the `claw-mem` plugin manifest was not found at the configured path. This was fixed by rebuilding the plugin. The two issues are independent but compound: the startup crash prevents recovery after the OOM kill.

---

*Submitted via gh CLI by Jarvis (Peter Cheng's assistant)*

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Three separate places decide whether a plugin is enabled by hand, instead of asking the existing enablement owner. Each one disagrees with what actually loads, so users get misleading diagnostics and a gate that silently lets a restricted config through.

1. `openclaw doctor` skips the Codex CLI asset reminder when `plugins.allow: []` is present, even though an empty allowlist restricts nothing.
2. The `/tools` inventory notice blames `plugins.allow` for a missing browser tool no matter why the browser plugin is off, and says nothing at all when the plugin is denylisted.
3. The OpenShell agent-workspace binding does not match padded or differently cased plugin ids in `deny`, so a restricted policy is accepted.

### Steps to reproduce

Case 1 - doctor scan skipped:

1. Put a personal Codex skill at `~/.codex/skills/tweet-helper/SKILL.md` and another at `~/.agents/skills/agent-helper/SKILL.md`.
2. Configure `{"plugins":{"allow":[],"entries":{"codex":{"enabled":true}}}}` in the state dir.
3. Run `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` and look at the `Doctor info` section.

Case 2 - /tools notice names the wrong reason:

1. Start a Gateway with `plugins.entries.browser.enabled: false` (and no `plugins.allow`).
2. Create a session and call `tools.effective` for it.

### Expected behavior

- Doctor reports the personal Codex assets, because `allow: []` adds no restriction and the Codex entry is enabled.
- The `/tools` notice names the actual reason the browser plugin is off (`disabled in config`), and still appears when the plugin is denylisted.
- The OpenShell binding rejects a denylisted plugin regardless of whitespace or case in the configured id.

### Actual behavior

Case 1: the `Doctor info` section is missing entirely - no "Personal Codex CLI assets found" line. Dropping the `allow` key from the same config makes the line appear and report 2 skills.

Case 2: the notice reads

> Browser is configured, but plugins.allow does not include browser. Add "browser" to plugins.allow or remove the restrictive plugin allowlist.

even though the real cause is `plugins.entries.browser.enabled: false`, so following the advice changes nothing. With `plugins.deny: ["browser"]` there is no notice at all.

Case 3: `deny: [" File-Transfer "]` is a legitimate config id, but the binding gate resolves instead of rejecting.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10 (source build 5cb1764fc2), observed November 26, 2026

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu 26.04)

### Install method

Git checkout

### Model

Not applicable: local CLI diagnostics and Gateway RPC.

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable.

### Impact and severity

Misleading maintenance advice during routine diagnostics, and a silently skipped asset reminder. No crash or data loss. Following the `/tools` advice makes operators widen plugin policy for a plugin they already enabled.

### Additional information

Observed with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `HOME` per case, on a built `origin/main` checkout. The empty allowlist semantics were established in #191708.
