issues.body:
This issue collects the design of the new update path: what has landed, what is in progress, and who owns which part. It is meant as the shared reference for everyone working on updates, so we stop colliding on the same files with different designs.

## Goal

A user opens Settings in the Control UI and clicks Update. Within minutes the Gateway serves the new build, or it keeps serving the old build and the UI says why. No terminal, no manual step, no false "succeeded", no stuck Gateway.

## Why the old path keeps breaking

Root-cause analysis of about 2,700 upgrade failure reports (2026-11-15/17):

1. **In-place replacement of the running install was the largest cause** (about 600 field failures). The old updater stops the Gateway, swaps the package and runs checks while nothing serves.
2. **The installed old updater drives every upgrade.** Every fix needs one copy in the updater and another on the candidate side for older updaters. `docs/install/updating.md` carries dozens of "the installed updater must contain this fix" notes for this reason.
3. **It is slow.** Average update about 23 minutes with about 5.7 minutes of downtime. Pre-switch checks run while the Gateway is down took about 42% of update time.

The code swap itself almost never failed. The work around it did.

## The design

| Part | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Prepared releases** | Each update installs into its own `releases/<id>/` folder while the old Gateway keeps serving. Built on the release folders and link switch from #198835 (@fuller-stack-dev) and the proposal in #197949. |
| **Resident launcher** | The service always starts the launcher, never a release path. The launcher picks the active release. |
| **Trial with switch-back** | The new release starts once as a trial. If it fails to start twice, the launcher switches back to the previous release and restores its `.pre-<generation>` state files. |
| **The new release finishes its own update** | The old updater only prepares and checks. Activation, verification, plugins and the final result run in the new release's code, so a fix ships with the release that carries it. |
| **State copy-and-swap at first start** | The new Gateway migrates a private copy of the state, validates it and switches to it (#198389). The old state stays untouched for rollback. PostgreSQL uses the same model through a private namespace copy (#204502). |
| **Doctor is advisory** | It runs after the Gateway is listening. It never gates or rolls back an update. |

Measured on Linux and macOS after the switch: a normal update takes 2–3 minutes with 7–17 s of outage.

## What landed

- Git installs on prepared releases: #199706, #200578, #203194.
- npm, pnpm and Bun installs on prepared releases, with the old Gateway serving during preparation: #203497.
- Fixes from real-host testing: #203735 (containers and the official image), #203769 (no systemd user bus), #203504 (consent survives the restart; wrong-install refusal), #203990 (faster switch-back after a stalled start), #203994 (Doctor findings after success), #204054 (plain rollback message), #204094 (Windows state databases), #204127 (plugins update after the new Gateway is ready), #204215, #204515 (`npm i -g` then `gateway restart` applies the new version), #204502 (PostgreSQL copy-and-swap).
- Interim-snapshot recovery for Git checkouts on 2026-11-17–19 `main`: #201463, #201538, #204275, #204322, #204676.

## In progress: one owner per bug class

Instead of one fix per report, the remaining work is grouped into four classes. Each class gets one owner change.

| Class | Problem | The one change | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Proof** | The release path merged before it had a real `T → T+1` run with a schema change on every platform | One CI lane: build `T` and `T+1` from the same source with a fixture-only schema step, and prove trial and rollback | #204685 |
| **B. One writer for the update result** | Several places write an update's final status: the old Gateway in process, a guess from process ID and uptime in `announceReady`, and the early-release recovery from #204322 | Before activation, `prepareUpdate` records refusals and preparation failures. After activation, one function at Gateway ready derives the final result from the lock and the trial. Every other writer is removed. Restart and health waits end on a committed trial, report "connected without operator scope" as its own outcome, and always have a deadline (#204704). | #204700 |
| **C. One state inventory, refuse before the stop** | Some databases fall outside the copy (#204394, #204227). Very large stores can exceed the trial budget. PostgreSQL stores that are too large migrate in place. | `discoverDatabases` becomes the single inventory. Everything the new release migrates is in the copy set, or the update refuses before the old Gateway stops, with the reason. The in-place PostgreSQL branch is removed. Normal startup outside an update still migrates as before. | #204752 |
| **D. Only the launcher is named after conversion** | Other installers and routes can bypass the launcher or take over the release slot: #204516, #203807, #204266 | After conversion, `gateway install` writes the launcher. Local routes that would fall through to the old in-place code refuse with a reason and a next step. Every service that runs the package is restarted through its owner or named in the result. | queued after B |

Before the next stable freezes the launcher and trial format, we also:
- pin that frozen contract with one test: trial fields, launcher IPC messages, exit 78, and the `.pre-<generation>` scan;
- keep the second start attempt (real launchd restarts during the trial needed it);
- refuse before the stop when the estimated state upgrade will not fit the trial budget, on SQLite and PostgreSQL.

## Test matrix before stable

Linux, macOS and Windows × npm and Git:
- `T → T+1` Control UI click with a schema bump;
- crash after migration;
- hang before listening;
- kill during prepare;
- reboot during the trial;
- first update from 2026.11.7.

Windows 11 runs from 2026.11.7 are required: #200756 reproduces on Windows 11 but not on Windows Server.

## What the old updater still has to do

The first update from any already-installed version is driven by that version's updater. Neither the new code nor a fix on `main` can change that. Until the oldest supported upgrade base contains the new path:

- **Fixes to the old updater belong on the release branches** that users will update from, for that first update. Examples: the pnpm fixes in #203401 and #204716.
- **On `main`, the old in-place code is frozen.** Change it only to land a fix that is ported to a release branch.
- **The old updater is deleted** once the oldest supported upgrade base includes #203497.

## Ownership

- **New update path on `main`:** `src/update/`, the launcher, `src/state/state-upgrade*` and run settlement. Changes go through the class owners above.
- **First updates from shipped versions:** release-branch fixes for the installed updaters (@fuller-stack-dev).
- **Design changes** to anything in the table above get raised here first.

## Open design questions

- **#201716 proposes in-place state migration at start** to avoid the copy's disk cost: about 70 GiB to copy with about 100 GiB free. The space problem is real. In-place migration loses rollback after a crash, though: of 98 schema steps in our history, 68 cannot be read by the previous release. Proposal: class C refuses before the stop when the copy will not fit. #201716 becomes a class C test case.
- **Windows:** outage on #204704's run was 82 s, against 7–17 s on Linux and macOS. Not yet explained.

## Open issues tracked here

#203764, #203807, #203628, #204394, #204516, #204227, #204704, #200756, #204266

issues.body:
After updating oc-prod 2026.11.8 → 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), a recurring cron job on session agent:main:status-board (openai/gpt-6-luna via the codex harness) fails at runtime-start. This happened 27 times in 7 h; there were 0 occurrences in the previous 7 days on 2026.11.8.
Log sequence (17:07 PT example): 'Codex app-server required forced shutdown; process cleanup confirmed' → 'codex app-server preparation timings … stage=runtime-start outcome=error totalMs=24376' → 'Codex agent harness failed; not falling back to embedded OpenClaw backend … error="Codex uncommitted thread cleanup failed | Native history allowance cannot fit its omission notice"' (errorName CodexAppServerUnsafeSubscriptionError, modelFallbackCandidate=true) → 'model fallback decision: candidate_failed … reason=unknown next=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5', and the run succeeds on the fallback.

**Root cause analysis (added 2026-11-25 18:30 PT, from the 2026.11.10 dist; supersedes the "Expected" line above):**
- Throw site: `bindBoundedSeed` → `select()` in core `dist/host-capability-*.mjs`. When a fresh native thread is seeded and some history must be omitted (x>0), it reserves `BOUNDED_CONTEXT_NOTICE` (~45 tokens): `s -= estimateTokens(notice); l = min(maxActiveTranscriptBytes - bytes(notice) - 1, s*4); if (l < 2) throw "Native history allowance cannot fit its omission notice"`. `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` is 15mb here, so the byte cap is not the limiter; the token allowance `s` is ≤ ~45.
- The allowance is `c = min(historyTokenBudget, contextTokenBudget)` minus active continuation / plugin-runtime-refresh messages. `historyTokenBudget` comes from Codex `reserveCodexHistoryBudget` (extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-history-items.ts): `max(1, contextTokens - reserve - inputTokens - ceil(contextTokens*16/PAYLOAD_BYTES)*(ceil(FRAME_BYTES/4)+32) - estimateRenderedLlmBoundaryTokenPressure(systemPrompt + instructions + JSON(toolSpecs) + prompt))`. With contextTokens 272000 (gpt-6-luna) the per-item frame reservation alone is ~30k tokens. Because of the `max(1, …)` clamp, any case where the prompt/tool pressure (or the trailing runtime-refresh exchange) consumes the budget yields an allowance of 1 token; with any history to omit, the turn then hard-fails instead of seeding an empty history with the notice, or omitting the notice.
- The seed failure happens after `thread/start`, inside `rejectUncommittedThread`; `discardUnattestedCodexPluginThread` then also fails, so it is rethrown as `CodexAppServerUnsafeSubscriptionError("Codex uncommitted thread cleanup failed", {cause})` (thread-lifecycle-run ~L1804) and the client is abandoned. The thread is never bound, so the next run seeds a fresh thread again and fails the same way: a self-sustaining loop (10 consecutive runs, 13:07–17:37 PT, every run preceded by "Codex app-server required forced shutdown"). It cleared only when the Gateway process restarted (18:09 PT); after that the same job, session and model succeeded 3 times in a row.
- A sibling job on the same session (gpt-6.1-sol, same 3 tools, same 272k window) succeeded throughout, so session size alone does not explain it (session context 43k/272k).
**Expected:** (1) when the history allowance cannot fit the notice, seed no history (notice only, or no notice) instead of failing the turn; (2) a failed discard of an uncommitted thread should not turn a recoverable seed error into an unsafe-subscription error that poisons every later run until restart; (3) classify the error for model fallback (currently reason=unknown, which sent each run to a paid Anthropic fallback at ~250–290k tokens/run).
**Env:** OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), @openclaw/codex from the same generation, Linux x64, Node v26.13.1, agents.defaults.compaction {mode: safeguard, maxActiveTranscriptBytes: "15mb", midTurnPrecheck: on}.

**Local mitigation:** the job's fallback chain was changed so a failure no longer lands on the expensive fallback; the loop itself only cleared with a Gateway restart.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a Linux systemd-user Gateway deployment with local embeddings enabled, the kernel recorded 223 OOM kills of `llama-server` processes in `openclaw-gateway.service` within one calendar day, plus three OOM kills of processes named `openclaw`.

This is an incident report with kernel evidence, not a confirmed memory-leak diagnosis or a deterministic reproduction. Please advise whether it belongs to an existing issue and which supported, payload-free diagnostic would identify the memory owner and bound recovery attempts.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Actual behavior

Read-only examination of the retained kernel journal for 2026-10-03 00:00 through 2026-10-04 00:00, timezone UTC+08:00, found:

| Kernel OOM victim process name | Recorded kills |
| --- | ---: |
| `llama-server` | 223 |
| `openclaw` | 3 |
| `MainThread` | 7 |

All 223 `llama-server` victim PIDs were paired with an `oom-kill` record naming `openclaw-gateway.service` as their cgroup. These were `global_oom` / `CONSTRAINT_NONE` records, not proof of a service-specific memory cap being exceeded. The generic process name `MainThread` alone does not identify the executable; those seven events are not attributed to the Gateway main process here.

Distinct PIDs recur through the day. This demonstrates repeated kills of this process family, but does not establish whether each restart was automatic recovery, demand-driven loading, or another lifecycle path.

Three `openclaw` OOM kills occurred at 18:28:43, 19:03:49, and 19:05:59 UTC+08:00. The process name alone does not distinguish CLI invocations from the Gateway.

### OpenClaw version

Installed package inspected at report time (2026-10-04 UTC+08:00): `2026.9.8`. The exact build running at each earlier OOM event was not independently established; this installed version is not asserted to be the version of every historical victim.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux `6.8.0-142-generic`, x86_64; Node.js `v24.19.0` at report time.

Report-time `/proc/meminfo`: `MemTotal: 8128448 kB`, `SwapTotal: 4092924 kB` (approximately 7.75 GiB RAM and 3.90 GiB swap). Historical RAM size or changes earlier in the incident window were not independently established.

### Install method

Installed Node package; Gateway launched as a systemd user service. Package installation provenance: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Model

Report-time local embedding model configuration: `embeddinggemma-300m-qat-Q8_0.gguf`. The model used by each killed child is not individually verified. No conversational-model dependency is established.

### Provider / routing chain

Report-time memory search provider: `local`, enabled. Kernel victim membership establishes Gateway-service child involvement; exact per-event request routing is NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Report-time service contains `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=3969`. This is a context observation, not proof that the worker-limit interaction in #157575 caused these incidents. Non-minimal deployment with additional integrations; no plugin-isolation A/B or clean-install comparison was performed for this report.

### Logs

Minimal redacted kernel extracts; timestamps preserved, hostnames/account details omitted:

```text
2026-10-03T00:01:16+08:00 global_oom CONSTRAINT_NONE victim-cgroup=openclaw-gateway.service task=llama-server pid=138998
2026-10-03T00:01:16+08:00 Out of memory: Killed process 138998 (llama-server) anon-rss:632308kB
2026-10-03T18:26:32+08:00 Out of memory: Killed process 380069 (llama-server) anon-rss:1113332kB
2026-10-03T18:28:43+08:00 Out of memory: Killed process 380902 (openclaw) anon-rss:345556kB
2026-10-03T18:39:27+08:00 Out of memory: Killed process 385053 (llama-server) anon-rss:1157876kB
2026-10-03T20:34:15+08:00 Out of memory: Killed process 405313 (llama-server) anon-rss:985076kB
```

Later retained Gateway memory-diagnostic sample (2026-10-03 23:50:38 UTC+08:00):

```text
level=critical reason=rss_threshold
rssBytes=3573121024 heapUsedBytes=1795562496
externalBytes=536553075 arrayBuffersBytes=214917684
workerHeapUsedBytes=597964432 workerCount=12 workerHeapSampledCount=11
workerMemoryCoverage=partial workerMemoryScope=direct
```

This is a later warning sample, not a measurement at the time of an OOM kill. ArrayBuffers must not be added to external memory as an independent total, and partial worker coverage does not account for every allocation.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

At report time the currently running service's systemd accounting showed:

```text
MemoryPeak=7424712704
MemorySwapPeak=4089634816
```

These are service-cgroup peaks, not Gateway-process RSS; they include children and cgroup-accounted memory. The peaks need not have occurred simultaneously. They are not the total memory of the whole host.

No raw configuration, database, session contents, heap dump, or full log archive is attached. No stress reproduction, restart, configuration change, or forced OOM was performed while preparing this report.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed Linux deployment. Repeated process termination is confirmed by the kernel (223 embedding-service-family victims and 3 `openclaw` victims in the retained day). Resource pressure can disrupt availability, but individual missed messages, data loss, or failure of every semantic request have not been established. Normal semantic recall was able to succeed during report preparation; the deployment is not asserted to be continuously unavailable.

### Additional information

Related reports reviewed before filing:

- #159356: managed embedding-child failures and OOM-correlated recall failures; different deployment and historical readiness concerns. Related symptoms, not proven identical cause.
- #125792: oversized context allocation for a different embedding model; this report does not establish the same context-allocation mechanism.
- #125344 (closed): accumulating local embedding workers / app-server processes; this report does not establish unbounded concurrent live children.
- #154812: RSS growth outside V8 heap; no native-leak attribution has been established here.
- #157575: managed Gateway heap policy overrides per-worker old-space limits; presence of a heap option alone does not prove that mechanism explains these kills.

No known-good/first-bad version, isolated regression, or deterministic trigger is established. The question for triage is how to attribute aggregate memory pressure and prevent repeated local-service kills/recovery attempts from compounding it, without exposing private memory or deliberately exhausting production RAM.

issues.body:
## Summary

The managed `memory-core` Dreaming automation can encounter repeated narrative-generation failures, finish with pending narratives, and still record the cron run as fully successful with zero errors. Pending narrative work is not retried after Gateway admission recovers; the next scheduled attempt remains the following day.

This makes a degraded Dreaming run invisible to normal automation health checks and failure notifications.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (`1391f7c`)
- Linux x64
- Node.js 24.20.0
- Built-in `memory-core`
- Managed `Memory Dreaming Promotion` automation
- Light, REM, and deep phases enabled

## Observed behavior

During one managed run, Gateway admission was draining. Narrative generation repeatedly failed and used fallback output:

```text
[plugins] memory-core: narrative generation failed for light phase: Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted
[plugins] memory-core: narrative generation used fallback for light phase because the narrative run failed (...)
[plugins] memory-core: narrative generation failed for rem phase: Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted
[plugins] memory-core: narrative generation failed for deep phase: Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted
```

One later attempt also failed while inspecting Codex processes:

```text
[plugins] memory-core: narrative generation failed for light phase: Cannot inspect Codex processes. Process inspection exceeded its deadline. Retry when the host is responsive.
```

The promotion owner then repeatedly logged:

```text
[plugins] memory-core: dreaming promotion complete (workspaces=26, candidates=4, applied=0, failed=0, degraded=0, narrativesPending=5).
```

Despite `narrativesPending=5` and the explicit narrative failures, the managed automation state was:

```json
{
  "lastRunStatus": "ok",
  "lastStatus": "ok",
  "consecutiveErrors": 0,
  "lastFailureNotificationDeliveryStatus": "not-requested",
  "lastDurationMs": 224675
}
```

The next run remained scheduled for the normal daily interval. No bounded retry was scheduled after Gateway admission recovered.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Enable the managed `memory-core` Dreaming automation with narrative phases enabled.
2. Start a Dreaming run while the Gateway is draining and rejecting new task admission.
3. Allow narrative generation to fail and fallback handling to run.
4. Observe the final `dreaming promotion complete` record and the managed automation state.

## Expected behavior

At least one of the following should happen:

1. The run records a degraded or failed status when narrative generation fails or `narrativesPending > 0`, so automation health/failure notification surfaces the condition; and/or
2. Pending narratives receive a bounded retry after Gateway admission returns, with durable retry state and no duplicate diary writes.

The completion metrics, automation status, and notification state should agree.

## Actual behavior

- Narrative generation fails repeatedly.
- Fallback diary entries may be written.
- Five narratives remain pending.
- Completion reports `failed=0, degraded=0`.
- The automation records `ok`, zero consecutive errors, and requests no failure notification.
- No retry occurs before the next daily schedule.

## Impact

Operators see a healthy managed automation even though Dreaming work is incomplete. A transient Gateway drain can silently defer narrative work for at least one schedule interval, and ordinary health checks do not expose the degraded result.

## Duplicate check

Searched open issues for `narrativesPending`, Dreaming fallback/status, Gateway draining, restart recovery, and managed Dreaming failures. Related Dreaming timeout, event-loop, and crash-recovery reports exist, but none found covered the specific invariant that a run with explicit narrative failures and pending work is persisted as `ok` with no retry or failure notification.

## Privacy

Paths, hostnames, agent names, session identifiers, credentials, prompts, and memory contents have been removed. The counts and sanitized log messages above are sufficient to describe the observed state transition.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect state; no crash)

### Summary

An agent whose heartbeat scratch contains **only the shipped boilerplate** is not recognised as empty, so it runs a heartbeat model turn every interval. Sibling agents with comment-only scratch correctly skip with `empty-heartbeat-file`. Net effect: one agent out of five burned heartbeat turns — and, during a provider outage, churned in the retry/stall loop for hours — purely because its scratch file carried a docs template with a markdown link instead of an HTML comment.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Several agents inherit `agents.defaults.heartbeat = { "every": "4h", "target": "none", "lightContext": true }`, each with its own heartbeat job.
2. Give four of them comment-only scratch, and one the stock template, i.e. `#`-prefixed lines, a fenced code block, and a trailing list item:

```markdown
# Keep this file empty (or with only comments) to skip heartbeat API calls.

# Add tasks below when you want the agent to check something periodically.
```

## Related

- [Heartbeat config](/gateway/config-agents)
```

3. Inspect: `openclaw cron list --all --json`.

### Expected behavior

With no real tasks present, every tick should be `skipped` with `heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file` — as it is for the four comment-only agents.

### Actual behavior

Only the agent whose scratch contains the trailing markdown list item runs heartbeat turns; the others skip:

```
heartbeat-architect | status=error    | (ran; later aborted by stuck-session recovery)
heartbeat-librarian | status=error    | (ran)
heartbeat-main      | status=error    | (ran)
heartbeat-pm        | status=skipped  | error="heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file"
heartbeat-scanner   | status=skipped  | error="heartbeat skipped: empty-heartbeat-file"
```

The two that skip carry a leading HTML comment plus the same `#` lines and **no** trailing list item; the one that runs has the trailing `- [Heartbeat config](/gateway/config-agents)` list item. So a boilerplate markdown link is being counted as heartbeat content.

### Suggested fix

Treat a scratch file as empty when it contains no task content — strip HTML comments, fenced code blocks, `#`-prefixed lines and bare markdown links before the emptiness test.

### Workaround

Replace the scratch with a comment-only body:

```bash
openclaw cron scratch <jobId> --set "<!-- no periodic checks -->"
```

Do **not** use `--unset`: with no scratch at all, the heartbeat still runs a model turn.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)
- macOS 27.0 (arm64), Node v24.18.1

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After upgrading from 2026.10.8 to 2026.10.10-beta.5, long-lived-session operations repeatedly fail with SQLite worker heap OOM; beta.5 performs unbounded session-actor hydration although main already has the bounded-tail repair #172970.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed production sequence, not an independently executed synthetic reproduction:

1. Upgrade an existing Linux Gateway with a roughly 4.1 GB agent database and long-lived sessions from 2026.10.8 (`dc2523e`) to 2026.10.10-beta.5 (`7e15622`). The upgrade ran a startup migration.
2. Continue ordinary scheduled session events, transcript appends, and Workboard reads.
3. Observe six grouped worker-OOM incidents on November 2, 2026 (UTC table below). The previous day's log on 10.8 has no matching heap-OOM lines. This is an observation window, not a controlled A/B test.
4. Inspect the version-matched hydration query: all transcript identities, active-event rows, and navigation rows enter JSON aggregate strings and are decoded into retained JS collections before a metadata-only actor read returns.

**Proposed synthetic discriminator (not run here):** in disposable state only, seed a linear synthetic transcript at increasing sizes (e.g. 10k, 100k, 200k+ events), with compact synthetic messages and synthetic tool frames. Acquire a cold session actor and call its `read`, then append one event. Run beta.5 versus main's bounded actor implementation in fresh worker processes using the existing 512 MiB carrier limit. Instrument collection counts and worker heap, not only wall time; test a second co-tenant read concurrently. Verify exact durable identities/ancestry after old-id retries and rewrites. #172970 already supplies window-crossing/historical-lookup regressions and synthetic scale results. No particular event count is claimed to reproduce OOM deterministically on this host.

### Expected behavior

Routine session admission/appends should not hydrate history-sized actor state or kill unrelated requests sharing the worker. Main's merged #172970 uses a 512-row resident transcript tail, fetching 513 rows per collection to determine completeness and using durable indexed readers for older facts.

### Actual behavior

| UTC, Nov 2 | Agent reservation overlapping slot failure | Execution ms | Observed failed clients |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 12:42:46 | `session.actor.read`, `agentDatabases`; outcome `error` | 16993 | Scheduled session event |
| 14:03:13 | `session.actor.read`, `agentDatabases`; outcome `error` | 23456 | Scheduled event, script awaiting Workboard list |
| 14:27:14 | `session.actor.appendTranscriptEvent`, `agentDatabases`; outcome **`ok`** | 25079 | Three Workboard lists, script awaiting list |
| 14:34:21 | `session.actor.appendTranscriptEvent`, `agentDatabases`; outcome **`ok`** | 22357 | Three Workboard lists, script awaiting list |
| 14:48:46 | `session.actor.appendTranscriptEvent`, `agentDatabases`; outcome **`ok`** | 28384 | Script awaiting Workboard list |
| 16:03:35 | `session.actor.read`, `agentDatabases`; outcome `error` | 12133 | Scheduled event, script awaiting Workboard list |

There are 29 matching error lines across these six timestamps, not 29 independent worker deaths. Read-reservation queue waits are zero. At 16:03:35, other agent requests report ~10.7 s and ~6.8 s queue waits behind the actor read, then fail after only 2-3 ms of execution.

The append reservations are explicitly logged `ok`: they establish concurrent expensive activity, **not** proof that those appends were the failing operation or that a write was rolled back. They must not be blindly replayed.

Workboard is a shared-slot casualty/candidate, not the proven allocator: its list API hydrates board-scoped card history, but successful readback of all six boards totals 300 cards, 2,458 comments, and about 3.69 MB formatted JSON. The script's failing line is the native Workboard list call, not model inference or compute allocation.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.10-beta.5 (`7e15622`), previously 2026.10.8 (`dc2523e`)

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Linux x64; Node 24.22.1; 16 GB RAM

### Install method

npm global, Gateway service

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

Gateway scheduled session event / native Workboard read -> shared SQLite worker. The failure is local persistence, not an established provider error.

### Additional provider/model setup details

No provider-specific cause established. Native session metadata reports `contextTokens=1048576` with `totalTokensFresh=false`; that is capacity, **not measured usage**. A separate log reports 1,139 context messages and an estimated 349,518 input tokens, not the total stored-event count. A bounded native `chat.history` request (`limit=1`, 1-character content projections) subsequently reported `totalMessages=66853` and `pendingInputs.total=67`; bodies were discarded rather than stored. This is the API pagination count, not a direct count of all stored transcript events. Full stored-event and allocation sizes were not measured because production databases were neither opened directly nor copied.

### Logs

Sanitized operation facts (no transcript or account data):

```text
workerOperations=[session.actor.read,agentDatabases]
outcome=error elapsedMs=23456 queueWaitMs=0 writerExecutionMs=23456
SqliteWorkerError: SQLite worker stopped before its result was received:
Worker terminated due to reaching memory limit: JS heap out of memory

workboard.cards.list: three requests fail together after 24965/13965/2951 ms
Worker terminated due to reaching memory limit: JS heap out of memory
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Version-matched code:

- [beta.5 hydration aggregation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10-beta.5/src/config/sessions/session-actor-hydration.worker.ts#L216-L274): full identity/active/navigation projections, ordered ascending with **no limit**. [Decoding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10-beta.5/src/config/sessions/session-actor-hydration.worker.ts#L335-L354) constructs Maps and parsed navigation while the raw aggregate strings still exist.
- [Actor read/cold hydration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10-beta.5/src/config/sessions/session-actor.worker.ts#L379-L437): cache miss calls hydration before returning even a metadata actor snapshot; mutation commands use the same state owner.
- [Residency](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10-beta.5/src/config/sessions/session-actor-residency.worker.ts#L23-L61): 8 MiB normal budget exempts one oversized working set; measuring competing states serializes them. This is not a hard cap on one session's navigation.
- Carrier `maxOldGenerationSizeMb:512` / `maxYoungGenerationSizeMb:32` are [unchanged in 10.8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.8/src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.ts#L308-L313) versus [beta.5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10-beta.5/src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.ts#L150-L156). Raising global `NODE_OPTIONS` alone does not replace these explicit worker limits.
- `session-actor-hydration.worker.ts` does not exist in v2026.10.8; on the beta ancestry, it arrives via snapshot commit [5a94eab2146](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5a94eab2146e558b3ebcd41cb174fc5adc469c2a), before beta.5.
- [Merged repair #172970](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/172970), commit `dd9cdee4d3b350807631c6825058a011069071fe`, is present in current main (`47697052914a6390772d249618a7bc4bcb1246cc`) as [513-row hydration queries](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/47697052914a6390772d249618a7bc4bcb1246cc/src/config/sessions/session-actor-hydration.worker.ts#L247-L308) and a [512-row retention bound](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/47697052914a6390772d249618a7bc4bcb1246cc/src/config/sessions/session-actor-transcript-window.worker.ts#L7-L40), absent from the installed beta.5 bundle and tag. No duplicate fix PR proposed.

### Impact and severity

Intermittent local automation failures, including scheduled session inputs not being processed and unrelated Workboard requests failing together. Six grouped incidents in approximately 3h21m after the upgrade. The main Gateway process stays up; the SQLite worker dies. No permanent data loss has been established.

### Additional information

**Cause confidence:** operation-level evidence strongly implicates the new, unbounded actor cold-hydration/residency path, especially the three failing actor reads. It does not identify the exact allocating function or prove that every co-tenant failure originated in that same actor. No heap profile, forced production replay, or synthetic OOM run was taken. The three successful append reservations remain attribution gaps.

`session context snapshot read` is a separate large-history path: it already scanned full navigation on 10.8. In three prewindows, snapshot transactions finished **before** the failing reservations (8.957/13.823/8.702 s durations), so a slow snapshot label alone does not identify the OOM source. #185111 covers the remaining full-context-read problem. #185610 covers post-OOM lease recovery, not the original allocating operation.

Please evaluate release inclusion of the already-merged bounded actor repair, preserving its historical-id/anchor fallback semantics and tests; adding LIMIT alone is not sufficient. A fresh-package, synthetic worker-heap comparison is the remaining acceptance test. No live restart, configuration edit, compaction, reset, database copy, or database write was performed during diagnosis.

Prepared with AI assistance. No private session contents, names, phone numbers, message text, configuration, or state artifacts are attached.

issues.body:
Version: OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55), Windows 11, single agent "main", agent schema user_version 25. Same keys and wording in the v2026.11.4 docs.

## Summary
The agent database table session_transcript_archives holds a compressed canonical copy of every reset/deleted transcript. After the derived *.jsonl.deleted.<ts>.zst / *.reset.* file is published, the row stays in SQLite forever. resetArchiveRetention ages the FILES, not the rows, and the disk budget only touches archives when the store is over maxDiskBytes. There is no documented command to drop rows that are already published and older than a cutoff, and doctor --session-sqlite compact only rewrites the file (VACUUM). On our install this table is now a third of the database and grows about 1.2 GB per week.

## What we measured (read-only, on a VACUUM INTO copy of the live DB, 2026-11-25 04:39)
- DB file 13.2 GB (live 13.45 GB). session_transcript_archives: 6,973 rows / 4,529 MiB (dbstat), all with reason "deleted", all with published_at set.
- Rows older than 30 days: 1,969 rows / 1,543 MiB, every one already published to a .deleted file in the sessions directory (the sessions dir holds 7,019 matching .deleted/.reset files).
- Growth: about 1.2-1.3 GB per week since 2026-11-09 (week of 11-09: 1,970 rows / 1,272 MiB; 11-16: 2,392 / 1,223 MiB; 11-23 first 3 days: 582 / 353 MiB). Driven by many short-lived subagent/cron sessions being deleted.
- resetArchiveRetention "30d" on a dev gateway against that copy for 80 minutes, plus "openclaw sessions cleanup --enforce" on the stopped copy: 0 rows removed (6,973 -> 6,975). Caveat: the copy also logged "Held agent main database (deletion journal unavailable); skipped session retention" every minute because only the DB file was copied, so we will re-measure on production after enabling the key.
- maxDiskBytes "30gb": not over budget (12.2 GB counted on the copy), so nothing evicted, as expected. Lowering the budget to force eviction would also walk historical sessions after the archives, and each evicted session becomes a new archive row, so it is not a fix.
- doctor --session-sqlite compact: docs say it checkpoints and VACUUMs; "it does not select additional history for deletion".

## Docs that describe the behaviour
- reference/session-management-compaction/maintenance.md: "Converting reclaimed history to a transcript archive replaces those rows with a compressed canonical blob in SQLite's session_transcript_archives table and a derived JSONL file in the sessions directory. The compressed payload therefore still occupies database space; the file is not its only copy." and "Retained reset history is bounded by the disk budget, not by resetArchiveRetention, which only ages archive artifacts."
- gateway/config-agents/sessions.md: resetArchiveRetention = "age-based retention for reset/deleted transcript archives".

## Ask
One of:
1. Make resetArchiveRetention (or a new key, e.g. session.maintenance.archiveRowRetention) also delete session_transcript_archives rows older than the cutoff once the file copy is published and verified (or move the payload out like cold storage does, keeping only the file reference), or
2. Add a supported offline command, e.g. openclaw doctor --session-sqlite prune-archives --older-than 30d [--dry-run], that drops published, verified archive rows and reports bytes reclaimed, or
3. Document that the table is meant to be permanent and how operators should bound it.
We do not want to delete rows by hand-written SQL.

## Environment detail
auto_vacuum INCREMENTAL, journal WAL, page_size 4096; config session.maintenance { mode: "enforce", pruneAfter: "30d", archiveDashboardAfter: "7d", maxEntries: 2000 }, coldStorage planned { enabled: true, afterDays: 14 }.

Filing attempt 2026-11-25 18:01 PT: NOT posted. gitdp token (workspace .github-token) got 403 Resource not accessible by personal access token on create-issue for openclaw/openclaw. No duplicate found. gh CLI is logged in as ava-perry (different account), not used.

issues.body:
Related fix: #137895

## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

When an OpenAI Realtime Voice Call agent speaks a farewell and invokes `openclaw_end_call`, OpenClaw can request carrier hangup before the carrier has finished playing the buffered farewell audio.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Voice Call plugin with OpenAI Realtime and a Twilio media stream.
2. Place a call and have the agent speak a known multi-word farewell immediately before invoking `openclaw_end_call`.
3. Say goodbye so the agent produces the farewell and requests the model-driven hangup.
4. Observe the call disconnect while the farewell is still playing.

The same boundary is reproducible in the realtime handler by queuing farewell audio and then processing the end-call tool request before the carrier returns a playback-mark acknowledgment.

## Expected behavior

OpenClaw should wait until the carrier confirms that all accepted farewell audio has played before requesting hangup. If playback is interrupted or cannot be confirmed within a bounded wait, it should keep the call connected.

## Actual behavior

The realtime end-call handler requests carrier hangup immediately after the model invokes `openclaw_end_call`, even though generated audio can still be buffered in the outgoing media stream. In the observed Twilio call, the caller heard the beginning of the farewell and then an immediate disconnect.

## OpenClaw version

Current `main`; the direct-hangup behavior is also present in v2026.9.4.

## Operating system

Linux (Docker-hosted); exact host distribution is not relevant to the carrier playback boundary.

## Install method

Docker-hosted OpenClaw with the bundled Voice Call plugin.

## Model

OpenAI `gpt-realtime-2.1`

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Voice Call plugin → OpenAI Realtime → Twilio media stream

## Additional provider/model setup details

The failure occurs when the model emits farewell audio and then invokes the built-in end-call tool in the same response. Carrier identifiers, phone numbers, endpoints, and credentials are omitted.

## Logs

The observed ordering was:

```text
farewell audio started
farewell audio generation completed
openclaw_end_call invoked approximately 2 ms later
carrier hangup requested while playback remained buffered
```

The current-main regression reaches `manager.endCall()` before emitting or acknowledging any terminal playback mark.

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Live Twilio reproduction: the caller heard only the beginning of the farewell before disconnect.
- Source-level regression on current `main`: the end-call path closes immediately without waiting for carrier playback confirmation.
- Proposed fix and validation: #137895

## Impact and severity

- Affected: callers using model-driven hangup in Realtime Voice Call sessions.
- Severity: moderate; the call completes, but the agent's final spoken response is truncated.
- Frequency: reproducible when buffered farewell audio remains at the time `openclaw_end_call` runs.
- Consequence: callers hear an abrupt, incomplete goodbye and may miss final information.

## Additional information

The Voice Call transport already supports named carrier playback marks. The missing behavior is an end-call drain that waits for the exact terminal mark, cancels hangup after interruption or unconfirmed playback, and does not let later model output cross the terminal boundary.

issues.body:
**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.11.6, macOS.

## Summary

Once a curated memory file (`MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, or a tracked `memory/**/*.md`) is recorded with `originClass: "untrusted"`, it is excluded from automatic context injection, and nothing in the docs or CLI lets an operator restore it after reviewing the content. Even an owner re-saving the file through the agent's own file tools keeps it untrusted. Please add a documented operator command to re-trust a file, plus a docs note on the stickiness.

## Current behavior (from dist and docs, 2026.11.6)

- Trust is stored per file as a row in the state database, table `plugin_state_entries`, owner `core:memory-artifact-provenance`, namespace `workspace-files`, holding `originClass` (`agent` or `untrusted`) and the file's content hash after the last tool write.
- A tool write (write, edit, apply_patch) records `agent` only if the turn class is agent (sender is owner and no network-sourced tool result, including any MCP tool, has tainted the turn) AND the stored row is absent, or `agent` with a hash equal to the file's content before the write. Everything else records `untrusted` (`dist/memory-artifact-provenance-*.mjs:66-95`; turn class at `dist/agent-tools.async-*.mjs:716-728`; line numbers for 2026.11.6).
- Consequences: a single tainted turn, a non-owner write, or a shell/script/git/sync edit that makes the stored hash stale flips the file to untrusted; every later write stays untrusted because the stored row is no longer `agent`.
- Reads never compare hashes: an `untrusted` row keeps the file excluded whatever the content now is, and an `agent` row stays eligible after an out-of-band edit (`dist/memory-path-provenance-*.mjs:44-56`; line numbers for 2026.11.6).
- Verified: an owner session re-saving an untrusted file via the file tools left the row untrusted.
- The only exit in code is `clearMemoryArtifactProvenance` (`dist/memory-artifact-provenance-*.mjs:113-127`; line numbers for 2026.11.6), reached only when a file tool deletes a file whose row hash equals the current content; a later agent-class tool add then records `agent`. It is undocumented, depends on the model passing a delete-plus-add patch verbatim, needs two passes if the hash is stale, and relies on an agent turn to restore trust in content the operator has already reviewed.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/memory-architecture.md` and `docs/concepts/memory-provenance.md` describe classification and note that shell and external edits are not tracked. `docs/cli/memory.md` covers `memory forget` and `session-backfill`; the CLI only lists provenance records. A search of the docs for re-trust, reset or restore-trust wording finds nothing.

## Why this matters

- Curated core files are meant to be injected every session. When one goes untrusted, the agent silently loses that context (it stays reachable only via explicit memory tools), and the operator has no supported fix.
- The documented-by-omission workaround is to edit the state database directly while the gateway is stopped, which is fragile across schema changes and easy to get wrong.
- The flip is easy to trigger by accident (any MCP tool call in the same turn as a memory edit), so operators will hit this repeatedly.

## Request

1. Add `openclaw memory trust <path>` (optionally `--workspace <dir>`, `--yes`) that: shows the file's current record (class, stored hash, whether the hash matches the file), requires an explicit operator confirmation, then records the current content hash as `agent` or `owner` with an audit note (who, when, via CLI). Refuse or warn if the stored hash does not match the file, unless forced.
2. Add `openclaw memory provenance list [--untrusted]` (or extend the existing listing) so operators can see which files are excluded and why (non-owner write, network taint, stale hash).
3. Docs: add a short section to the memory provenance page covering (a) the sticky rule, (b) that an owner re-save does not clear it, (c) which tools taint a turn (including MCP tools), (d) the new command.
4. Optional: surface a warning at injection time ("MEMORY.md excluded: untrusted") in `openclaw status` or the context report so the loss is visible without querying state.

## Workaround today

Stop the gateway, back up the state database, delete exactly the one provenance row inside a transaction, and restart; or have an agent turn run a verbatim delete-plus-add patch of the file. Both are undocumented.

issues.body:
Gateway-methods exhausted the Linux qualification host's memory under the source-owned Bun pin. The complete owner remains on Node; the failed Bun run was not replayed for admission.

### Reproduction scope

- Source: [`cb01febf9fa4fbda271d10b3adff3b384c6ece76`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cb01febf9fa4fbda271d10b3adff3b384c6ece76).
- Published fork: [`openclaw-v1.4.3-20261005-667c4ab22c-webkit-f1e1ca1156`](https://github.com/openclaw/bun/releases/tag/openclaw-v1.4.3-20261005-667c4ab22c-webkit-f1e1ca1156) (`1.4.3-canary.1+667c4ab22`). Linux x64 executable SHA256: `76ede220307e41e36c6f4981abf203536de469d2a6628a7ce503616fd477c467`.
- Linux x64, eight logical CPUs, 33,084,002,304 bytes observed RAM (about 30.8 GiB), no swap; four non-isolated fork workers.
- Complete `test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts`, 447 files, no file filters. Fresh private state and runtime caches, canonical current-head `qaRuntime` preparation, `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`.
- Existing test/hook deadlines stayed at 120,000/180,000 ms; the outer bound stayed at 2,562 seconds. No skips, worker limits or deadlines were changed to obtain a passing result.

The consumer command was:

```sh
CI=true OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4 \
  NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts --maxWorkers=4
```

The exact fork binary was staged on PATH. The full qualification also retained resource, JSON and sealed per-file reporters.

### Observed failure

The Bun arm began at 2026-10-07 15:38:53 UTC. At 15:57:38 UTC, the kernel recorded global OOM and killed a Bun worker with `anon-rss:12299036kB` (about 11.7 GiB) and `total-vm:28994680kB`. The workload cgroup peak was 32,033,415,168 bytes; its OOM-kill count was one and CPU throttling counters were zero. The time-specific kernel record associates the OOM with this run; the cgroup counters alone are cumulative.

The final collection contains 415 completed files, 5,628 passing assertions and 16 existing skips, with no observed assertion failure. Thirty-two files have no completed receipt. There is no complete Bun Vitest report or completed candidate cell, so these partial passes do not qualify the owner.

The workspace-owner renewal subsequently failed closed. The command transport exited 7 and the interrupted execution pipeline recorded 141. Source/runtime identities and process closure were checked directly afterward, and both the original archive and a separate final post-join archive were retained.

### Node comparison

The first, previously unexecuted Node 24.21.0 control completed on the same frozen source, host, CPU/worker/memory profile and unchanged deadlines: **447 files, 5,700 passes, 16 existing skips, exit 0, 1,028.066 seconds**. Its wrapper and process cleanup also completed successfully, with no OOM recorded in the control window.

Independent verification confirms exact unredacted case identity/status parity for the 415 files observed in both engines. The other 32 Bun files remain unobserved. The preserved failed Bun artifacts were checked unchanged after the Node control. This is a single control and an observed candidate-side resource failure; it does not establish the memory-growth root cause or qualify the owner.

### Investigation boundary

The root cause of the memory growth is unclassified. A prior source, `fbac0bec89805765cba15e2bc146be9f6c88217a`, completed two full passing Bun/Node pairs on the same runtime/profile. The newer source changes native SQLite worker admission, session-reader lifetimes, and async placement/worktree ownership. These are investigation leads, not a proven cause or an engine-versus-fixture conclusion.

This was the complete unfiltered owner. The result does not establish that every smaller CI include stripe would exhaust memory. Whole-owner admission remains blocked; narrowing the proof, adding skips, or widening memory/timeouts is not the proposed resolution.

Please identify the owning retained-memory/lifetime boundary, produce a bounded reproducer and fix, then perform fresh admission qualification on the then-current shared pin. The failed candidate and first Node control must remain recorded rather than being replayed to green.

issues.body:
# Bug type
Crash or process termination under memory pressure (recurrence on a version that includes the #136275 fix)

## Summary
On OpenClaw 2026.9.2 — which includes the #136275 fix (PR #136276, shipped v2026.9.1) — the Gateway process still exhibits the classic RSS-growth/OOM-restart cycle originally described in #74182 (closed May 2026) and #136275 (closed as fixed in 2026.9.1). Since neither closed issue's fix appears to be holding, this looks like a fresh regression rather than a recurrence of either root cause.

## Environment
- **OpenClaw:** 2026.9.2 (3928bad)
- **OS:** macOS 26.6.2 (arm64, Apple Silicon M4)
- **Node:** node@24 (/opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin/node)
- Gateway launched via launchd (`ai.openclaw.gateway`), `KeepAlive=true`, not inside a cgroup (macOS, not Linux) — so the #136275 cgroup-specific OOM-priority mechanism is not directly applicable here, but the underlying RSS-growth pattern matches #74182's description closely.
- A second, independent process (Hermes Agent's own gateway, `ai.hermes.gateway`) runs alongside OpenClaw on the same machine and has recorded 3 unclean SIGKILL/OOM deaths in the same 48-hour window that OpenClaw's RSS climbed and cycled — suggesting host-level memory pressure from OpenClaw is likely collateral-damaging sibling processes, not just itself.

## Evidence — RSS growth pattern (2026-09-06, all times CDT)
```
09:52:29  rss=1.17 GiB  rssGrowth=686.9 MiB  (window 30s)
10:22:29  rss=1.38 GiB  rssGrowth=655.0 MiB
10:52:29  rss=1.46 GiB  rssGrowth=770.1 MiB
11:22:29  rss=1.43 GiB  rssGrowth=695.5 MiB
11:52:30  rss=1.47 GiB  rssGrowth=770.8 MiB
12:22:30  rss=1.47 GiB  rssGrowth=774.5 MiB
12:52:30  rss=1.60 GiB  rssGrowth=895.9 MiB
13:22:26  rss=1.37 GiB  rssGrowth=890.8 MiB
13:53:28  rss=1.36 GiB  rssGrowth=881.6 MiB
14:23:30  rss=1.28 GiB  rssGrowth=679.7 MiB
14:53:48  rss=1.34 GiB  rssGrowth=566.6 MiB
```
Every entry crosses the internal 512 MiB threshold (110–175% of threshold) inside a single 30-second sampling window, i.e. RSS is growing by 500-900 MiB in 30 seconds repeatedly, all day, not a one-time event after hours of uptime as in #74182's original 2h14m report.

## Restart cycle correlation
Internal notes captured by the running agent during the same window:
```
"Gateway restart cycle: bounces roughly every 20-25 minutes on memory pressure,
 got as tight as two restarts 20 seconds apart, then settled."
"Restart cycle unchanged (11 today, ~25-30 min rhythm), no new auth events."
```
11 restarts logged in a single day, all correlated with the memory-pressure warnings above, not with auth/model-catalog events.

## Sibling-process collateral damage
A separate, unrelated always-on Python process (Hermes Agent gateway, not part of OpenClaw) sharing the same Mac recorded 3 unclean terminations in the same 48h window, each logged as "no exit path ran — SIGKILL / OOM / VM death":
```
2026-09-04T00:39 -> killed, gap until 2026-09-05T08:02 (~7h down)
2026-09-05T13:02 -> killed, gap until 2026-09-05T14:28 (~1.5h down)
2026-09-05T19:28 -> killed, gap until 2026-09-06T08:02 (~12.5h down)
```
No independent memory-pressure signal was found for that process itself; the timing strongly suggests host-level memory exhaustion driven by OpenClaw's RSS growth is taking down sibling processes via the OS-level OOM killer, not just OpenClaw's own gateway.

## Reproduction
1. Run OpenClaw Gateway 2026.9.2 on macOS (non-cgroup environment) with normal daily usage (Telegram + Discord channels connected, periodic cron/agent activity).
2. Observe `[diagnostics/memory] memory pressure: level=warning reason=rss_growth` log lines recurring every ~20-30 minutes, each showing RSS crossing 110-175% of the 512 MiB threshold within a 30s window.
3. Observe the Gateway self-restarting on this cadence throughout the day.
4. Optionally: run another always-on process on the same host and watch for correlated unclean terminations during OpenClaw's high-RSS periods.

## Expected behavior
RSS should stabilize after warm-up, not repeatedly balloon by 500-900 MiB in 30-second windows throughout a full day of otherwise-normal usage. Memory-pressure mitigation (if any exists client-side) should prevent the restart cadence from degrading into an ~every-25-minute cycle, and should not create measurable host-level memory pressure capable of affecting sibling processes.

## Notes
- This is filed as a fresh regression, not a duplicate: #74182 was closed by PR #75008 (May 2026, on the 2026.4.x line) and is specifically about *embedded LLM run* object retention after timeout/abort over hours of uptime. #136275 was closed by PR #136276 (2026.9.1) and is specifically about the Linux cgroup OOM-priority wrapper for managed local provider services. Neither describes a recurring ~every-25-minute cycle from cold/warm start on macOS (no cgroup) with no local provider service involved.
- Happy to run `openclaw gateway diagnostics export` and attach if a maintainer wants a heap snapshot — did not want to post a full diagnostics dump into a public issue without review first.

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

**Beta release blocker:** No

> Edited 2026-11-24 after two audits. This overlaps #153426 (existing recovery gap) and #203532 (`openclaw memory trust`). It stays open for the beta `fix-now` aspect until a maintainer consolidates it. A sufficient trigger observed on this host (a Control UI / `webchat` `gateway-owner` exec-completion wake) is filed separately as #204767. Timeline, version, and counts below are corrected.

**Summary**
2026.11.10-beta.x (since `v2026.11.10-beta.1`, #189727; absent in 2026.11.7) adds `core/doctor/memory-provenance`. It reports `Agent "main": MEMORY.md is excluded from automatic context: its memory provenance is untrusted. Last recorded tracked write: 2026-11-21T19:32:20.280Z, session agent:main:main. The record names only the latest tracked write, not necessarily the write that quarantined the file.` with category `fix-now`. No in-place fix exists: `openclaw memory`, `doctor --fix` and `docs/concepts/memory-provenance.md` offer no owner-approved re-trust. Once an untrusted record is persisted, there is no supported in-place way to clear it (only a tracked delete via `clearAfterDelete` / `clearMemoryArtifactProvenance` removes an existing matching entry; write rollback only deletes a failed first write).

**Steps to reproduce**
See #204767 for a concrete trigger. Then run `openclaw doctor --lint --all`, review the file, and try to restore it to automatic context.

**Expected behavior**
An owner-only re-trust of a reviewed file at its current hash, as #203532 requests, which this `fix-now` finding can point to. It should also re-classify the derived memory index entries for that file. The record should keep why it became untrusted.

**Actual behavior**
- The `fix-now` finding has no actionable fix.
- **Timeline (corrected):** in a `2026-11-20T12:06Z` state DB backup, `main` had no provenance record for `MEMORY.md`. On `2026-11-21`, `MEMORY.md` was edited via tracked `mcp__openclaw__edit` at `02:46:45Z` (owner turn), at `02:53:10Z` (during the exec-completion wake described in #204767, which is a code-guaranteed trigger for `untrusted`), and again at `19:32:20Z` (owner turn, sticky follow-up). Because the provenance store keeps only the latest write with no history or reason, the first transition to `untrusted` and any user-visible effect across interactive turns cannot be established from the DB alone. `MEMORY.md` was definitely recorded `untrusted` by `2026-11-21T19:32:20Z`, stayed excluded silently on 2026.11.6 and 2026.11.7 (the provenance gate predates beta; cf. #158912), and `beta.3` surfaced it on `2026-11-24`.
- **Counts (corrected):** at the time of the audit, 81 of 121 provenance records on this install are `untrusted`. 76 of those are daily `memory/*.md` notes last written in the second agent's Telegram group sessions (outside normal bootstrap; the provenance table does not store why each record became untrusted — 11 of the 76 had a preceding user event with `senderIsOwner=true`, and 9 other Telegram group daily notes remain `agent`). The only excluded curated root is the main agent's `MEMORY.md`, and all 45 of its derived index chunks (`memory_index_chunk_provenance`) are `untrusted` too. The first version's "quarantine is the common state" overstated this.

**OpenClaw version:** 2026.11.10-beta.3 (3d2d379); `core/doctor/memory-provenance` present since `2026.11.10-beta.1`; silent exclusion on 2026.11.6 and 2026.11.7

**Operating system:** macOS 27.2.1 (arm64), Node 26.13.0

**Install method:** npm global, launchd Gateway

**Model:** anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (current config and 19:32Z write; morning 02:53Z sequence in #204767 ran on anthropic/claude-fable-5-2)

**Provider / routing chain:** openclaw -> claude-cli runtime -> Anthropic

**Additional provider/model setup details**
Memory plugin: bundled `memory-core`.

**Logs**
```shell
2026-11-24T15:26:24.613Z WARN {"subsystem":"agent/cli-backend"} excluding MEMORY.md from automatic memory context: memory provenance is untrusted; run `openclaw doctor` for the last recorded write (sessionKey=agent:main:cron:<id>:run:<id>)
```
(Note: this log line fired during a cron session — where root `MEMORY.md` is also filtered separately by session bootstrap rules in `src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts` — because provenance eligibility is checked before that filter; `openclaw doctor --lint --all` independently confirmed the untrusted quarantine on `main`'s `MEMORY.md`.)

**Screenshots, recordings, and evidence**
- Provenance record (read-only, `plugin_state_entries`, `core:memory-artifact-provenance`/`workspace-files`): `MEMORY.md | untrusted | 2026-11-21T19:32:20.280Z | agent:main:main`. The current file bytes match the `fileHash` from that last tracked write.
- `recordMemoryArtifactWriteProvenance` (`src/memory/memory-artifact-provenance.ts`): a write is recorded `agent` only for an owner/agent write when there is no valid prior record, or the prior record is `agent` and `fileHash === sha256(contentBefore)`. Otherwise it records `untrusted`, and that sticks across later tracked owner edits.

**Impact and severity**
Blocks workflow: once a curated `MEMORY.md` is quarantined, automatic context excludes it and `core/doctor/memory-provenance` reports `fix-now` with no supported in-place recovery path.

**Additional information**
Related: #153426 (existing recovery gap), #203532 (re-trust command), #165452, #180796, #158912, #189727, #204767.

issues.body:
## Summary

On stable **OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)**, background usage/cost refresh repeatedly terminates with `ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY` in `sessionTranscript.usage-cost`. The Gateway and chat remain operational during the observed failures, but usage refresh fails and token/cost totals may remain stale or incomplete.

This is a scoped follow-up to closed #156898, not a claim that its original allocation bug has returned. The earlier bounded hot-SQLite reader fix (#156937) is already present in this installation. Our [previous follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156898#issuecomment-6781784923) remains unanswered at filing time. A bounded search found no matching open report for this task on 2026.11.3.

## Environment

- macOS arm64; Node 24.22.1 (recorded during the prior investigation).
- Gateway stable 2026.11.3, freshly confirmed on 2026-11-12.
- SQLite-backed retained conversation history.
- Mac companion also updated to 2026.11.3; this did not restart the Gateway.
- No local Core/plugin patch or worker heap-limit change applied for this investigation.

## Current evidence

Fresh log events on **2026-11-12, UTC+01:00**:

| Time | Task envelope bytes | Exchanges | Stage |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 01:33:03.531 | 5480 | 11 | running |
| 01:37:17.831 | 5744 | 10 | running |
| 01:37:34.160 | 5480 | 11 | running |

All three report the same error class:

```text
[usage-cost-cache]
Error [ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY]: Worker terminated due to reaching memory limit: JS heap out of memory
[task=sessionTranscript.usage-cost admittedInputBytes=5480 exchanges=11 stage=running]
```

These are log observations, not a claim of deduplicated crash counts. `admittedInputBytes` measures the task envelope, not the transcript/archive bytes subsequently read or the worker heap allocation.

The same failure class was observed before the upgrade and again after Gateway 2026.11.3 became ready on 2026-11-10 at 23:43:48 UTC+01:00. The first observed post-start error was 23:44:16; another was recorded at 23:59:51. **We do not claim that this release introduced the error.**

## Reproduction status

Observed repeatedly during ordinary operation of this existing history-bearing installation:

1. Run stable 2026.11.3 with the existing SQLite-backed histories.
2. Allow the normal background usage refresh to run.
3. Observe the usage-cost worker heap error while the Gateway/chat continue operating.

We do not yet have a minimal portable fixture, exact failed session/archive identity, or allocation stack. This is a repeatable field observation on this installation, not a deterministic fresh-install reproduction. No production history replay was forced for this report.

## Existing fix and remaining source-level lead

Read-only inspection on 2026-11-10 of the installed bundle and tag `v2026.11.3` found:

- Explicit worker limits remain **512 MiB old generation / 32 MiB young generation**.
- The hot-SQLite reader already processes bounded pages (up to 1,024 rows and approximately 8 MiB per pass). The earlier bounded-reader behavior is not simply missing.
- Usage/navigation projections are still collected for branch analysis; bounded payload pages do not prove bounded total metadata retention.
- The inspected cold-archive path uses `readVerifiedSessionColdArchive` followed by `decodeSessionColdRecords`. This is a possible allocation lead, **not a proven cause**.

Related archive-streaming work #192743 is relevant background, but we have not demonstrated that it resolves this specific failing task. Other SQLite/session-actor OOM reports should not be assumed to have the same allocator.

## Expected behavior / diagnostic request

- Complete supported usage refresh under the existing worker budget, or expose a bounded, actionable failure without repeatedly exhausting the worker.
- Preserve correct stale/incomplete status; do not silently mark failed rollups fresh.
- Please identify any known follow-up fix, or advise on supported **non-content** diagnostics that identify the failing session/archive and scan/allocation phase.
- A regression test should exercise the actual usage worker with representative large retained/cold history, verify rollup correctness, and retain the current heap limit.

No data loss or whole-Gateway crash is established by these observations. Raising the heap limit alone is not a demonstrated repair.

## Privacy and changes

No private conversation contents, account identifiers, raw databases, credentials, or full session IDs are attached. No cache deletion, database reset, runtime patch, or heap tuning was performed for this investigation. Prepared with AI assistance and published with the operator's explicit approval.

### Bug type
Regression / cloud workers

### Summary
On 2026.10.10, a Crabbox (AWS) cloud worker allocates, completes setup, enrolls and goes live, but every OpenClaw turn on it fails immediately:

```
Cloud worker process failed before completing the turn: node worker failed with exit code 1: Runtime config is not prepared. Await captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader()() first.

1. Lease allocated, setup finished (~3 min), node paired and connected from the worker's public IP through the public origin, runtime bundle installed, session went live on the worker.
2. The first turn fails with the error above. Every model fallback (GPT-6.1-sol, Grok 4.7, GPT-6-astra) fails identically, so it is not provider-specific.
3. The failure also caused OpenClaw to start a replacement lease automatically.

### Expected
The `openclaw worker` process prepares runtime config (awaits the async reader) before the turn starts, as the Gateway does.

Looks like the same class as #170715 (runtime config read before it is published), but on the worker entry path. Possibly related to #182647 (worker-preparation failures before inference). Tailnet-delivery background: #192175.

issues.body:
## Recurrence check (update 2026-10-15)

Re: the review's next step ("trace fresh-session provider exhaustion at the execution owner"). That trace runs in source on `main`; from a release install I can only report whether the failure still reaches us, and it does not. Gateway journal 2026-09-28 → 2026-10-15 13:40 UTC (859,987 lines, `openclaw@2026.9.6`–`2026.9.8`): **0** `trajectory-flush error=FOREIGN KEY` lines and **0** `agent cleanup failed` lines, against **316** lines matching `status=429` in the same window. The one `FOREIGN KEY` hit in the window is our own grep command echoed by the exec log (2026-09-28 11:59 UTC), excluded. Control: the same grep over 2026-09-01..09-08 returns 5. So 17 days with the trigger (429 on a fresh run) present and the failure absent. I am not claiming a fix and I have no commit to point at; if a maintainer can name the change between 2026.8.1 and 2026.9.6 that commits session identity before the first provider call, this issue can close against it. Until then there is nothing further a reporter on a release build can supply.

## Recurrence check (2026-10-12)

No new evidence of the original failure. Gateway journal from 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-12 18:00 UTC (185,560 lines, `openclaw@2026.9.8`): **0** `FOREIGN KEY` lines and **0** `agent cleanup failed` lines, with 84 lines matching HTTP 429 in the same window. Control: the same grep over 2026-09-01..09-08 returns 5 `FOREIGN KEY` lines. Together with the 2026-10-08 update below, that is 14 days with no FK failure on 2026.9.6–2026.9.8. I cannot separate cleanup failure, terminal-event suppression and audit-persistence loss from this install while the failure does not occur; I am not claiming a fix.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash): the run registry keeps a leaked `agent.run.started`; the gateway process does not exit.

### Beta release blocker

No — not a plugin-compatibility blocker for the current beta window.

## Summary

A run whose session was never committed dies during teardown, and the run registry keeps its
`agent.run.started` open forever because no `agent.run.finished` is ever recorded.

Session identity is created **lazily**: `ensureSessionEntrySync`
(`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-initial-entry.ts`, doc comment *"Lazy session
identity creation, including the original admission's first writer claim"*) is reached from
`SessionManager` persistence (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-persistence.ts:205-215`), i.e.
on the **first transcript persistence of the turn**. A run that fails before that point — ours
died on a provider `429` on its first assistant call, then exhausted auth-profile rotation — has
no `session_nodes` row and no `session_windows` row.

Teardown then assumes both exist, and fails twice for the same reason:

1. **Trajectory flush.** `trajectory_runtime_events` is keyed to the session window:

   ```sql
   -- src/state/openclaw-agent-schema.sql:436-444
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS trajectory_runtime_events (
     session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
     ...
     FOREIGN KEY (session_id) REFERENCES "session_windows"(session_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
   ) STRICT;
   ```

   With no window row the insert fails, and the cleanup wrapper logs and swallows it:
   `agent cleanup failed: ... step=openclaw-trajectory-flush error=FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`.

2. **Transcript persistence.** `appendTranscriptEventSync`
   (`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts:321-353`) reads the entry row,
   `resolveTranscriptAppendRefusal` finds none, and because the scope carries a writer fence the
   refusal is escalated to a throw:

   ```ts
   // session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts:334-351
   const fresh = readSessionEntryRow(database, resolved.sessionKey);
   const refusal = resolveTranscriptAppendRefusal(fresh?.entry, resolved, fencedScope);
   ...
   if (fencedScope.expectedWriterRunId !== undefined && !result.ok) {
     throw new SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError(result.error);
   }
   ```

   ```ts
   // session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write-guard.ts:29-36
   const identity = {
     agentIdHash: redactIdentifier(resolved.agentId),
     expectedSessionIdHash: redactIdentifier(resolved.sessionId),
     sessionKeyHash: redactIdentifier(resolved.sessionKey),
   };
   if (!entry) {
     return { ...identity, code: "session-entry-missing" };
   }
   ```

   That is byte-for-byte the payload we observe in production, so the failing path on `main` is
   the one we are running.

The throw escapes to the command-queue lane (`src/process/command-queue.ts:413`,
`lane task error: ...`) and the message is recorded `outcome=error`. **What never happens is the
terminal run event.** `agent.run.finished` is projected exclusively from a lifecycle event with
`phase: "end" | "error"` (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts:139-168`), every emitter of it is
guarded by `state.lifecycleEnded` (`src/agents/command/lifecycle.ts:123-200`), and there is no
reconciliation anywhere else: the lane's error boundary only logs. The `agent.run.started` row
stays as the newest event for that session forever.

**Second, smaller defect on the same line:** `agent cleanup failed ... error=FOREIGN KEY
constraint failed` names neither the table nor the session, so the operator-visible message
cannot be attributed without reading the schema. SQLite's bare FK message is the whole diagnosis
we get.

I could not pin **which** of the three terminal emitters was reached before the throw replaced the
run's outcome — the ordering in the logs (cleanup failure at `.100`, lane error at `.104`) is
consistent with `post-run.ts:640-645` (`catch { emitPostTurnError; throw }` / `finally { await
deferredLifecycle.complete() }`) but I did not prove it. The **absence of the terminal audit row
is not an inference**; it is queried below.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a turn on a session key with no committed session yet (a fresh cron/isolated run is the
   natural case — the session row does not exist until the first transcript write).
2. Make the run fail before its first transcript persistence. Ours: provider returns HTTP 429 on
   the first assistant call, auth-profile rotation runs, all candidates fail.
3. Watch teardown: `openclaw-trajectory-flush` fails the FK, transcript persistence throws
   `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError` with `code=session-entry-missing`.
4. `openclaw audit --run <runId> --kind agent_run --json` — only `agent.run.started`.

## Expected behavior

Every `agent.run.started` gets a terminal counterpart. A run that dies on the session-persistence
path is still a run that ended, and the registry is the documented way to ask whether a session is
busy — a leaked `started` is indistinguishable from a live turn.

Secondarily: teardown of a run that never committed a session should be a no-op, not two failures.
Nothing is being flushed for a session that does not exist.

## Actual behavior

Two runs, 2026-09-06, gateway journal (verbatim, `America/Sao_Paulo`):

```
19:52:46.916 [discord] embedded run agent end: runId=443ca53f-2767-4245-b187-18e06dae00ec isError=true
             model=claude-opus-5 provider=anthropic error=⚠️ API rate limit reached.
             rawError=HTTP 429: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"rate_limit_error", ...}}
19:52:46.953 [agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: runId=443ca53f-... stage=assistant
             decision=rotate_profile reason=rate_limit from=anthropic/claude-opus-5
19:55:36.100 [agent/embedded] agent cleanup failed: runId=443ca53f-... sessionId=443ca53f-...
             step=openclaw-trajectory-flush error=FOREIGN KEY constraint failed
19:55:36.104 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested durationMs=170082
             error="session writer claim changed before transcript persistence |
             {"agentIdHash":"sha256:befa156f0283","expectedSessionIdHash":"sha256:b86d508bc19f",
              "sessionKeyHash":"sha256:cdffe4490bef","code":"session-entry-missing"}"
19:55:36.107 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=cron sessionId=443ca53f-...
             sessionKey=agent:arthur:heartbeat outcome=error duration=170111ms error="session writer
             claim changed before transcript persistence | {... "code":"session-entry-missing"}"
```

The second run (`0aeb6ffc-3768-498f-8997-e5b832bc7bbc`, 20:27:18 → 20:34:37, `durationMs=440619`)
is identical line for line.

State that proves the leak — the run registry itself, not the log:

```console
$ openclaw audit --run 443ca53f-2767-4245-b187-18e06dae00ec --kind agent_run --limit 100 --json \
  | jq -r '.events[]? | "\(.occurredAt/1000|todate) \(.action) \(.status) \(.sessionKey)"'
2026-09-06T22:52:46Z agent.run.started started agent:arthur:heartbeat

$ openclaw audit --run 0aeb6ffc-3768-498f-8997-e5b832bc7bbc --kind agent_run --limit 100 --json | ...
2026-09-06T23:27:17Z agent.run.started started agent:arthur:heartbeat
```

No terminal row, ever — queried 24h later. For contrast, the healthy runs on the same session key
in the same hour pair correctly:

```
2026-09-06T22:39:16Z agent.run.started  started  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:44:53Z agent.run.finished blocked  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:45:25Z agent.run.started  started  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:45:35Z agent.run.finished blocked  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:46:36Z agent.run.started  started  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:47:45Z agent.run.finished blocked  run=6e06c409
2026-09-06T22:52:46Z agent.run.started  started  run=443ca53f   <-- never finishes
2026-09-06T23:27:17Z agent.run.started  started  run=0aeb6ffc   <-- never finishes
```

There was no concurrent run on that session key between 22:52:46Z and 23:27:17Z, so the session
was not rebound by a sibling turn — the row was simply never created.

## Environment

- openclaw **2026.8.1 (ea80657)**, global npm install (`~/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw`)
- Failing code re-verified against `main` @ `0015b20995` — `resolveTranscriptAppendRefusal`,
  `appendTranscriptEventSync`, the `trajectory_runtime_events` FK and the audit projection are
  unchanged, and the error payload our production emits is produced verbatim by current `main`.
- Node v22.23.2, Debian in a Proxmox LXC, Linux 6.17.2-1-pve x64
- Model `anthropic/claude-opus-5`, embedded runtime

## Provider / routing chain

Cron job (`channel=cron`, lane `cron-nested`) → embedded agent runner → anthropic provider with
several auth profiles. First assistant call HTTP 429 → `decision=rotate_profile reason=rate_limit`
→ profile cooldown → candidates exhausted → teardown on the path above. The 429 is only the
trigger; any failure before the first transcript commit reaches the same teardown.

## Additional setup details

Multi-agent fleet (7 agents, one gateway), local plugins (a context-engine plugin and MCP servers),
Discord + WhatsApp channels, cron-driven heartbeat sessions. We carry local `dist` patches for
other, unrelated defects — none touches sessions, transcripts, trajectory or audit, and the
`session-entry-missing` payload above is produced by stock `main` code.

## Impact and severity

- **Frequency:** 3 occurrences in 7 days on this gateway (2026-08-31 → 2026-09-07), all with both
  signatures, against 1,623 `agent.run.started` events in the same window.
- **Cost:** any consumer of the run registry reads a leaked `started` as a live turn. Ours is a
  pre-restart guard: both corpses blocked every gateway restart until an age backstop expired, one
  of them while an operator restart was pending — the operator waited on a session that had been
  dead for minutes. Time-to-notice was a day: nothing surfaces a leaked run, the session simply
  looks busy.
- The turn's own outcome is also lost: no transcript, no trajectory, and the only trace is a
  `[diagnostic]` line.

Happy to test a patch against this gateway; the failure reproduces on its own roughly twice a week
under provider rate limiting.
