issues.body:
## Status update — November 16, 2026

Proposal only. We are no longer pursuing implementation or preparing a PR for this request. Earlier implementation plans and promises in this issue or its comments are superseded by this update. The proposal and previously reported evidence remain available for maintainer consideration; this is not a claim that the feature has shipped or that outstanding validation is complete.

## Summary
Improve Android reply notifications with session-aware foreground behavior, agent/session labels, internal Dreaming exclusions, and same-user cross-device suppression.

## Problem to solve
Using Control UI on a laptop currently produces duplicate phone notifications for replies the user is already reading. Globally disabling notifications also hides completions from other sessions and replies that arrive after the user leaves the laptop.

Basic Android conversation notifications already exist upstream. Foreground suppression is currently app-wide, so a reply from another session is silenced while the app is open. Generic labels also obscure the originating agent and session.

## Proposed solution

- Suppress only the chat actually visible on the phone, not every session when the app is foregrounded.
- Show configured agent name and session title; preserve routing and private lockscreen content.
- Exclude canonical internal Dreaming narration, not ordinary scheduled or background-session replies.
Reuse session-viewer declarations with a short server-owned lease. Control UI renews the declaration only while visible, focused, and recently interacted with; the Gateway attaches a recipient-specific silent-notification hint to final chat events for the same authenticated profile and exact session. Android honors the hint only when publishing the notification; chat events and history synchronization are not withheld.

Notifications remain enabled for other sessions and resume when the viewer leaves or its lease expires. Missing identity or uncertain presence defaults to notifying. No new configuration or persistent store is needed.

## Alternatives considered
- Disable phone notifications globally: loses useful background-session alerts.
- Suppress based on prompt origin: misses users leaving while a long reply runs.
- Withhold final chat events: risks broken terminal state and history synchronization.

## Impact
Users who alternate between Control UI and Android receive fewer redundant alerts without losing unrelated completions. This is a recurring usability issue, not an outage.

## Evidence/examples
A local implementation based on v2026.9.3 was exercised with a laptop and Android: active laptop chat was silent on the phone; closing the laptop page restored phone notifications; reopening suppressed them again. These are user-observed live results. The local build also passed user-observed phone-active/closed and other-session notification checks. No Android notification QoL PR is being prepared; the local observations are retained as historical evidence only.

## Implementation intent
No, proposing the idea only. We are not undertaking implementation or committing to a PR.

issues.body:
## Summary

Sixteen production call sites across eleven files throw or return the **byte-identical** string
`Session "<key>" changed while starting work. Retry.` No discriminator — no reason code, no call-site
tag, no cause field — reaches the log or the thrown error. When this fires in production, **which of
the sixteen branches ran is not knowable from the output.**

This is the diagnosability half of the family that #118873 / #117096 / #116694 / #121269 covered
behaviourally. Those are all closed and the stuck-session behaviour is fixed. The string is not.

## Verified against `main`

`587c7524e58`. `rg 'changed while starting work' src --type ts`, excluding tests and comments:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ts` | 573 |
| `src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts` | 333 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-admission.ts` | 259 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` | 166 |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/agent-session-prepare.ts` | 185 |
| `src/sessions/session-diff-baseline.ts` | 41 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/session-entry-persistence.ts` | 98 |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.ts` | 241, 284, 292 |
| `src/agents/agent-command-recovery-owner.ts` | 110, 132 |
| `src/agents/agent-command.ts` | 213, 220 |
| `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-session-state.ts` | 73 |
| `src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` | 57 (the shared helper) |

Three of these are in one function's three branches (`reply-turn-admission.ts:241/284/292`), so even
narrowing to a single file does not narrow to a single cause.

## Why it costs an operator a diagnosis

Production, `2026.8.1-beta.2`, one Discord channel session: **27 rejected runs across 4 inbound user
messages** between `09:58:05` and `10:24:09` (-03:00), each aborting in 4–8 ms with exactly this
string. Worst case, 9 attempts over 6 min 11 s before one user message ran. Every cluster started
within ~90 s of a gateway restart.

```text
[diagnostic] message processed: channel=discord outcome=error duration=4ms
  error="Error: Session \"agent:<redacted>\" changed while starting work. Retry."
```

The three plausible causes on that path — an `expectedSessionId` mismatch, a recovery-owner claim
returning `invalidated`, and the abort check — call for three different operator responses. The log
distinguishes none of them, so triage is guesswork or a source read per occurrence. Filing this
separately because a fix here is useful whether or not any specific admission bug is open: the next
one in this family will produce the same undiagnosable line.

## The seam already exists

`src/config/sessions/lifecycle.ts` already owns the discriminating helper:

- `resolveSessionWorkStartError()` already distinguishes *deleted* / *changed* / *still initializing*
  / *archived*, and
- `SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED_ERROR_CODE = "SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED"` (line 24) is already
  the shared code.

Roughly fourteen sites route through that helper. The sixteen above bypass it with a hardcoded
template literal, which is what makes them indistinguishable.

## Suggested shape

Not a behaviour change and not a message rewording — the retryable contract and the operator-facing
sentence can stay exactly as they are.

1. Give the helper a `reason` discriminator alongside the message (e.g.
   `session-id-mismatch` | `recovery-owner-invalidated` | `aborted` | `entry-deleted` |
   `initializing` | `archived`).
2. Route the sixteen hardcoded literals through the helper so the reason travels with the error.
3. Log the reason on the rejection path.

Happy to send the PR if the shape is agreeable — I would rather have the reason names settled by a
maintainer first than guess at the taxonomy.

## Version

`2026.8.1-beta.2` for the production data; source claims verified against `main` at `587c7524e58`.

> **Form note (edited 2026-10-08):** this is a feature request that was filed in bug shape. The sections below add what `feature_request.yml` asks for (alternatives, implementation intent) without changing the evidence above.

## Environment (form fields)

- Production data: `2026.8.1-beta.2`, npm global install, Linux (Debian in a Proxmox LXC).
- Model / provider routing chain of the 27 rejected runs: **unknown** — not recorded with the 2026-08 occurrences. The string is emitted before any model call, so the defect is model-independent.
- Steps to reproduce / actual: this is a diagnosability gap, verified by source inspection (table above) and confirmed by ClawSweeper on current `main`; no runtime repro on current `main` was run.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Status quo — read the source per occurrence.** What we do today; it costs a source read per incident and still cannot separate the three branches inside `reply-turn-admission.ts`.
2. **Reword the sixteen messages.** Rejected: it changes an operator-facing sentence and the retryable contract, and the next caller that copies the template literal is undiagnosable again.
3. **A stable public `reason` field on the shared error.** Possible, but it creates a compatibility obligation. ClawSweeper's recommendation — bounded **diagnostic-only** labels in operational logs, retry codes and public messages unchanged — is the shape we prefer.

## Implementation intent

We will open the PR once a maintainer settles the open question (diagnostic-only labels vs public field, and the label names). Not before: we would rather not pick the taxonomy unilaterally.

issues.body:
**Version:** `2026.8.1-beta.1` (ff8a3fe)
**Runtime:** `claude-cli` backend, `anthropic/claude-opus-5`
**Surfaces affected:** Control UI (webchat) and the Android app. Telegram is **not** affected.

## Summary

With the `claude-cli` backend, every assistant turn is persisted twice through two independent writers, and clients that render the transcript show both. The user sees the full turn, then immediately a second copy of the same turn as one plain block.

The two copies are not byte-identical, so the Control UI's "consecutive duplicate text-only messages collapse into one bubble with a count badge" rule (documented in `web/control-ui.md`) never fires.

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** one assistant turn appears once.

**Actual:** the turn appears twice:

1. **Live/canonical view** — each assistant text block as its own bubble, interleaved with tool-call cards, imported from the Claude Code transcript (`importedFrom: "claude-cli"`, `api: "anthropic-messages"`, `stopReason: "end_turn"`).
2. **Aggregate record** — a single message whose `content` holds **one text block** with every intermediate narration line *and* the final answer concatenated (`api: "cli"`, `stopReason: "stop"`, `idempotencyKey: "cli-assistant:<runId>"`), written ~650 ms later.

The more intermediate text a turn emits, the larger the visible duplicate.

## Evidence

Session store: `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`, table `transcript_events`.

```sql
select seq, event_json, created_at
from transcript_events
where session_id like '<session>%'
order by seq;
```

A turn that emitted two narration lines plus a final answer produced this aggregate:

```
seq 44  api=cli  len=1835  text blocks in content: 1
"Son 18 (16 "New chat", una sin etiqueta y la del móvil). Voy con la del móvil primero…
 \n\nLa herramienta está limitada a mi propio árbol de sesiones. Voy por la CLI.
 \n\nHecho. Las 18 archivadas, verificado contra la base de datos. …"
```

That single record reproduces, verbatim and in order, the three separate bubbles the client had already rendered for the same turn.

Across the whole store: **84 duplicated turns out of 307 assistant messages carrying text.** The pattern is constant — a `cli` record paired with a twin whose `api` differs (`anthropic-messages`, `openclaw-transcript` or `openai-responses`) and whose byte length is identical.

## Where it comes from

`persistCliAssistantTranscript()` in `dist/cli-runner-*.js` writes the aggregate via `appendExactAssistantMessageToSessionTranscript` with `idempotencyKey: cli-assistant:${runParams.runId}`.

It is gated by `runParams.persistAssistantTranscript`, computed in `dist/agent-runner.runtime-*.js` as:

```js
persistAssistantTranscript:
  turn.followupRun.currentInboundEventKind !== "room_event" &&
  turn.followupRun.run.suppressTranscriptOnlyAssistantPersistence !== true
```

and `suppressTranscriptOnlyAssistantPersistence` is only set for room events (`get-reply-*.js`: `suppressTranscriptOnlyAssistantPersistence: isRoomEvent`). So for ordinary DM turns the aggregate is always written, in addition to the per-block import from the CLI transcript. There is no user-facing setting to disable it.

## Possibly related condition

`openclaw doctor` reports on the same install:

```
- Main session transcript missing (~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/sessions/<sessionId>.jsonl).
```

That directory holds **138 `*.trajectory-path.json` pointers and zero `.jsonl` transcripts**. With no native transcript to reconcile against, the two writers never converge.

## Why Telegram is unaffected

Channel delivery sends the final text once — the gateway log shows a single `outbound send ok` per message. Telegram renders what was delivered, not the transcript, so the aggregate is never shown there.

## Related

PR #98117 (`fix(ios): avoid transient duplicate final replies`) addresses a neighbouring symptom in the shared chat view model, where a live `chat.final` row is adopted by the canonical `session.message` instead of being appended twice. This report is one layer lower: two rows are genuinely persisted, so adopting at render time would hide the duplicate rather than prevent it.

issues.body:
## Environment
- openclaw 2026.11.7 (regression first observed after 2026.11.6 → 2026.11.7 auto-upgrade; the same code is still present in 2026.11.10 and main as of 2026-11-26)
- Platform: Telegram private chat with the gateway's main agent (direct conversation)

## Symptom
Outbound messages to the user's Telegram direct chat are silently skipped — the delivery resolver binds them to a wrong/ended conversation instead of the live direct chat.

First observed 2026-11-23 23:35+ (18 messages skipped silently). Recurrence confirmed 2026-11-25: after demoting 38 stale rows to `related`, five new subagent windows created ~23:37-23:38 the same day immediately re-created fresh `role=primary` rows for the same conversation, and the very next outbound (00:02:46) was skipped again.

## Root cause
Write side: `prepareSessionConversationForWrite` (session-accessor.sqlite-conversation) assigns

```
role = (sessionScope === "shared-main" && kind === "direct") ? "participant" : "primary"
```

to **every** non-shared-main session — including ephemeral subagent windows that inherit the parent conversation identity.

Read side: `currentBindingOnly` does not exclude ended windows (no `ended_at IS NULL` / status filter for `done`/`timeout`/`failed`).

Combined: every subagent spawned under a direct conversation adds another "current destination" binding → `resolveCurrentConversationByDelivery` ambiguity → outbound silently skipped (no error surfaced, the skip is not logged).

## Suggested fix (either)
1. `currentBindingOnly` should exclude ended windows (`s.ended_at IS NULL` / `s.status = 'running'`), or
2. subagent/transient sessions should not be assigned `role=primary` for the parent conversation (e.g. `related`), or
3. session maintenance should advance `current_session_id` off finished windows.

## Local mitigation (until fixed upstream)
A reaper sentinel demotes stray current bindings every 60s (role → `related`, reversible, snapshot-logged). This only narrows the window, it does not remove the race.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
In `enforce` mode, `session.maintenance.maxEntries` and `maxDiskBytes` are silently exceeded without bound because thread/channel/topic session entries are treated as protected and skipped by all three reclaim paths (age prune, entry cap, and disk-budget last-resort eviction).

### Steps to reproduce
1. Configure `session.maintenance` with `mode: "enforce"`, `maxEntries: 500`, `maxDiskBytes: "400mb"`.
2. Operate a busy Slack/Telegram deployment so thread/channel session entries exceed 500 and the sessions directory exceeds 400mb.
3. Observe the store keeps growing past both limits: `pruneStaleEntries`, `capEntryCount`, and `enforceSessionDiskBudget` all call `shouldPreserveMaintenanceEntry`, which returns `true` for thread/channel entries, so they are never removed and the configured limits are never met.

### Expected behavior
In `enforce` mode the store is bounded by the configured `maxEntries` and `maxDiskBytes`. Hard resource ceilings apply even to conversation sessions.

### Actual behavior
The store grows unbounded. Observed: 562 entries and ~420MB with `maxEntries` effectively 500. Because only unprotected entries are removable, the reclaim evicts the wrong sessions (see #112637, `agent:main:main` eviction) instead of bounding the store.

### OpenClaw version
2026.7.1

### Operating system
Linux (Docker container, linux/arm64) on macOS host

### Install method
Docker (docker compose)

### Model
openai/gpt-5.6-terra

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> openai

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence
- `src/config/sessions/store-maintenance.ts`: `pruneStaleEntries` and `capEntryCount` skip entries where `shouldPreserveMaintenanceEntry` is true.
- `src/config/sessions/disk-budget.ts` (`enforceSessionDiskBudget` last-resort loop): `if (shouldPreserveMaintenanceEntry({ key, entry, preserveKeys })) continue;` — protected thread/channel entries are skipped even under disk pressure.
- `isProtectedSessionMaintenanceEntry` unconditionally protects `:thread:`, telegram topics, and group/channel keys.
- Observed store: 546 Slack thread entries across allowlisted channels; directory ~420MB.

### Impact and severity
- Affected: any active Slack/Telegram deployment in `enforce` mode.
- Severity: Medium-High — unbounded entry and disk growth; a configured hard limit that is silently exceeded; directly forces the wrong-session eviction in #112637.
- Frequency: Continuous on active deployments.
- Consequence: Disk exhaustion risk and eviction of unprotected sessions instead of honoring the operator's configured budget.

### Additional information
Proposed fix (PR to follow): keep thread/channel sessions protected from age-based `pruneAfter` (preserve idle-but-under-budget conversations), but make them evictable oldest-first under genuine `maxEntries`/`maxDiskBytes` pressure; always protect `agent:<id>:main` (#112637). If maintainers prefer to preserve today's unbounded default, the same behavior can be gated behind a `session.maintenance` opt-in flag.

issues.body:
# Codex harness: thread stays "claimed by active work" after turn completes, wedging the session until gateway restart

## Summary

With the Codex agent harness, a session's Codex thread is not released after a turn finishes normally. Every following message to that session fails with:

```
Codex thread <threadId> is claimed by active work; stop it first.
```

The harness does not fall back (`Codex agent harness failed; not falling back to embedded OpenClaw backend`), so the agent stops replying entirely. Restarting the gateway clears it, but the next completed turn on the new thread wedges it again.

## Environment

- OpenClaw CLI: 2026.10.9 (8b18b55), Homebrew `openclaw-cli`
- `@openclaw/codex` plugin: 2026.10.9
- `@openai/codex`: 0.160.0 (darwin-x64 app-server)
- Node: v26.13.0
- macOS 15.8.2 (x86_64), gateway under launchd (`ai.openclaw.gateway`, port 18789)
- Channel: Discord DM, agent on Codex harness (`openai/gpt-5.6-sol`, fallback `gpt-5.6-luna`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run an agent on the Codex harness, bound to a Discord DM.
2. Send a message, and let the turn run tools and finish normally.
3. Send another message to the same session.

**Expected:** the second message runs a new turn on the thread.
**Actual:** it fails immediately with `is claimed by active work`. Every later message fails the same way, and each model fallback candidate fails too, until the gateway restarts.

## Evidence

The latest stuck thread is `01a19f8e-60b7-7fb1-b2ec-4689de6cc154`. Its rollout file shows the last turn ending cleanly:

```
2026-11-03T04:02:17.208Z  event_msg  task_complete  turn_id=01a19f90-5a8d-7000-8871-ed9011a6f36f
```

Three minutes later, the next inbound message was rejected:

```
2026-11-03T04:05:09.836Z  ERROR  Codex thread 01a19f8e-... is claimed by active work; stop it first.
```

Around turn completion, the log also has:

```
WARN agent/embedded  codex settled-turn finalization context is unavailable  reason=context_unavailable
INFO agent/embedded  codex app-server turn released after terminal dynamic tool result  tool=sessions_yield
```

The pattern repeats across gateway restarts (all times UTC, 2026-11-02 to 11-03):

| Thread | First error | Last error | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01a198bb-6040-70c1-8f60-2f24f2b70f2a | 13:30 | 01:59 | 35 |
| 01a19d4f-9fa8-7792-bc33-5b234394551a | 17:36 | 00:44 | 90 |
| 01a19f19-7e19-7430-9b32-49bc9ec81120 | 02:20 | 03:39 | 37 |
| 01a19f8e-60b7-7fb1-b2ec-4689de6cc154 | 04:05 | 05:06 | 29 |

The same error also appeared on 2026-11-01 for thread `01a198a5-3bd1-7250-af32-9f7e6d73e46d` (14 failures). Gateway restarts at 02:02, 03:44 and 03:53 UTC each cleared the wedge only until the next completed turn.

The claim doesn't appear in `state/openclaw.sqlite` (`state_leases` holds only `gateway-owner`) or in the agent's `openclaw-agent.sqlite`. It seems to live only in gateway memory, which would explain why a restart clears it. The error string comes from `@openclaw/codex/dist/.setup/thread-lifecycle-run-*.mjs` and `session-retirement-*.mjs`.

## Possibly related symptoms on the same gateway

- About 70 Codex app-server or code-mode-host processes (about 3.3 GB RSS) built up as children of the gateway within ~75 minutes of a restart. The gateway itself ran at ~150% CPU and 3 GB RSS, and CLI commands (`openclaw status`, `openclaw codex --help`) hung. After a restart, this dropped to one Codex process.
- A `memory-core` short-term workspace lock was held by a pid that no longer exists (`Timed out waiting for memory workspace lock ... held by 53114:...`).
- `memory session startup catch-up failed: Error: Agent database Worker owner is closed`.

## Related issues

- #188422: a sibling native child holds the parent, giving "claimed by active work". The shape is similar (the turn also ended through `sessions_yield`), but the stuck thread here made no native `spawn_agent` calls during its turns.
- #190932: the first dashboard reply hits the claimed-work guard on 2026.10.9. Here the first turn succeeds and every later turn fails.
- #172837, #182549, #181046: earlier claim, pin and fallback bugs.

## Suggested direction

The thread claim should be released whenever a turn reaches `task_complete`, including when settled-turn finalization hits `context_unavailable` or the turn ends through a terminal dynamic tool such as `sessions_yield`. A stale claim whose turn has already completed should also expire or be reclaimable, so the session doesn't stay dead until a restart.

issues.body:
## Status of the A/B evidence (update 2026-10-12)

The review of 2026-10-08 notes that the lost final replies were never correlated with a final-delivery exception or registry transition. I cannot add that correlation from production: every WhatsApp account on this install now runs with `streaming.block.enabled: true` (checked in `openclaw.json` on 2026-10-12), because `false` loses real users' replies. No lost reply has been observed with that setting. The A/B evidence below stands as recorded; reproducing again requires flipping a live account back to `false`, which I will do only on a test account if a maintainer asks for a specific log or trace to capture.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash). Whether it is a regression is unknown: the bot flags a suspected regression, but we have no confirmed working run of this account with `block.enabled: false` before 2026.9.8.

### Beta release blocker

No — not a plugin-compatibility blocker for the current beta window.

## Summary

On 2026.9.8, a WhatsApp direct-message account with `channels.whatsapp.accounts.<id>.streaming.block.enabled: false` never delivers the agent's final reply. The model completes (`stopReason: stop`), the reply is held in pending-final custody, and no `[whatsapp] Sending message` is ever logged for it. On the user's next inbound message, main-session restart recovery settles that custody as an uncertain delivery and sends the generic notice "I couldn't confirm whether my previous reply reached this chat…" instead of the reply. The reply content is never re-sent.

Flipping only `streaming.block.enabled` to `true` (hot reload, no gateway restart) restores delivery immediately; flipping it back to `false` breaks it again. A/B done 3 times on the same account and session within 25 minutes.

I did not isolate the exact function in the shipped bundle. The custody path that ends in the notice is `deliverOnce` in `dist/reply-dispatcher-*.mjs` → `settlePendingFinalDelivery({ kind: "pending-final", ... })`; with block streaming off, the final apparently never reaches `options.deliver` for the WhatsApp adapter, so custody stays `queued`/`prepared` until recovery picks it up. Related but distinct: #154416 (spurious notice while a queued reply is mid-send), #149325 (Telegram pending-final swapped for the notice), #81078 (closed; block streaming *on* suppressing finals).

## Steps to reproduce

1. OpenClaw 2026.9.8, WhatsApp channel, multi-account. One account with:
   ```json
   "streaming": { "chunkMode": "length", "block": { "enabled": false } }
   ```
2. Send a DM to that account's number. Agent replies (any model; reproduced with `gpt-5.6-terra` and `claude-haiku-4-5`).
3. Observe: ✅ reaction is sent, no reply arrives.
4. Send a second DM.

## Expected behavior

The final reply is delivered to the DM after step 2, exactly as with `block.enabled: true` and as on 2026.9.6 and earlier with the same config.

## Actual behavior

- After step 2: no outbound message for the reply.
- After step 4: the restart-recovery notice is sent in place of the previous reply; then the new reply is again held.
- Transcript of the session: each assistant turn with `stopReason: stop` is followed by a `delivery-mirror` entry with idempotencyKey `main-session-restart-recovery:pending-final:*`.

Gateway log (America/Sao_Paulo, -03:00), `block.enabled: false`. Each `Sending message` right after an inbound is the recovery notice for the previous turn, never the reply:

```
2026-10-07T06:29:20.242-03:00 [whatsapp] Inbound message +55119XXXXXXXX -> +5511954211992 (direct, 82 chars)
2026-10-07T06:29:20.260-03:00 [whatsapp] Sending message -> sha256:28c3e0f7e09d
2026-10-07T06:29:20.587-03:00 [whatsapp] Sent message 3EB06F041B1C499E2FA931 -> sha256:28c3e0f7e09d (328ms)
2026-10-07T06:32:28.144-03:00 [whatsapp] Inbound message +55119XXXXXXXX -> +5511954211992 (direct, 82 chars)
2026-10-07T06:32:28.170-03:00 [whatsapp] Sending message -> sha256:28c3e0f7e09d
2026-10-07T06:32:28.878-03:00 [whatsapp] Sent message 3EB0044088067334950600 -> sha256:28c3e0f7e09d (709ms)
```

Flip to `true`:

```
2026-10-07T06:32:48.811-03:00 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (channels.whatsapp.accounts.arnold.streaming.block.enabled)
2026-10-07T06:33:00.778-03:00 [reload] config hot reload applied (channels.whatsapp.accounts.arnold.streaming.block.enabled)
2026-10-07T06:35:23.415-03:00 [whatsapp] Inbound message +55119XXXXXXXX -> +5511954211992 (direct, 78 chars)
```

The 06:35 reply was delivered (confirmed on the recipient's device). Note: replies sent via the block-reply path do not log `[whatsapp] Sent message`, so the log alone cannot confirm block-path delivery.

Flip back to `false` at 06:36:37 → the 06:49 DM again got no reply. Flip to `true` at 06:50:43 → one residual recovery notice for the 06:49 turn, then 06:56 and 06:57 DMs answered normally.

Window affected in production: 2026-10-05 10:38 → 2026-10-07 06:56, 6 user turns lost on one account. Last good delivery with the same config: 2026-10-03 13:27 on 2026.9.6.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (npm global, `npm ls -g openclaw` → `openclaw@2026.9.8`), upgraded from 2026.9.6 on 2026-10-04 09:53
- Linux 7.0.14 (Proxmox LXC), Node v24.21.0, systemd user service
- WhatsApp channel, 4 accounts on one gateway; only the affected account had `block.enabled: false`

## Provider / routing chain

WhatsApp inbound DM → agent `arnold` main session (`agent:<id>:whatsapp:direct:<peer>`) → embedded run (OpenAI `gpt-5.6-terra`; also reproduced with Anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5`) → reply dispatcher → WhatsApp outbound.

## Additional setup details

Local plugins loaded via `plugins.load.paths`: `nexus-context` (context engine), `backlog-v2`, `promise-wake`, `discord-voice-call`. None touches outbound reply delivery. One local dist patch (`dispatchTrustedPluginGatewayMethod`, #164545) unrelated to the reply path.

## Impact and severity

Silent message loss on an entire account: every DM final reply dropped, replaced by a generic notice one turn later. Time-to-notice was ~44 h because the account still sends ✅ reactions and the recovery notice, so it looks alive. Workaround: `streaming.block.enabled: true`.

## Model

OpenAI `gpt-5.6-terra`; also reproduced with Anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5` (same routing chain above). The defect sits in reply delivery, after the model returns.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In a long-running webchat session on a local lmstudio model, the context-usage surface (UI bar + `/status`) reports a prompt size that (a) is more than double what the provider actually receives and (b) keeps growing every turn even when turns add only a few KB. The bar visibly bounces up/down between turns instead of climbing smoothly. Under this inflated estimate the session enters `route=compact\_only` pressure mode prematurely.

## Environment verification (denominator is correct)

* LM Studio `/api/v0/models`: `qwen3.8-flash-next | state: loaded | loaded\_ctx: 262144 | max\_ctx: 262144`
* OpenClaw config: same model `contextWindow: 262144`

So this is not a context-window misconfiguration; the **numerator** (estimate) is the problem.

## Evidence (same session, same day, gateway log + LM Studio server log)

OpenClaw's own estimate (`agent/embedded` `\[context-pressure-diagnostic]`):

```
10:41:42  admitted provider attempt ... route=compact\_only estimatedPromptTokens=181228 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=12288
11:15:43  admitted provider attempt ... route=compact\_only estimatedPromptTokens=208189 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=12288
```

`/status` at \~11:08 for the same session:

```
🧮 Tokens: 92k in / 82 out
🗄️ Cache: 50% hit · 91k cached, 0 new
📚 Context: 182k/262k (70%)
```

LM Studio llama.cpp `print\_timing` for the same window — per-request newly-evaluated prompt tokens:

```
11:18:28  prompt eval time = 2133 ms /   585 tokens
11:19:16  prompt eval time = 8834 ms /  2670 tokens
11:20:40  prompt eval time = 4732 ms /  1531 tokens
11:20:53  prompt eval time = 2094 ms /   610 tokens
11:21:12  prompt eval time = 3531 ms /  1050 tokens
11:22:07  prompt eval time = 1438 ms /   421 tokens
```

Provider-reported usage for the last full request: **\~92k input** (≈91k cache-hit). The tiny per-turn prefill deltas (400–2,700 tokens at \~300 t/s = 0.5–3 s) show a stable KV base of roughly 92k. If the real prompt were 208k with a broken prefix cache, each turn would re-prefill tens of thousands of tokens (30+ s), which it does not.

### The numbers don't reconcile

1. **Estimate vs reality:** OpenClaw estimates 181k→208k while the provider reports \~92k actual prompt tokens, flat across turns. Divergence >2x and still climbing (+27k in \~35 minutes of light chat).
2. **Internally inconsistent cache line:** `Cache: 50% hit · 91k cached, 0 new` cannot be simultaneously true with either a 92k or a 182k prompt (91k/92k ≈ 99%, not 50%; and "0 new" contradicts the observed per-turn prefill).
3. **Between-turn bounce:** the UI context bar / per-message usage footer moves up *and down* across consecutive turns instead of monotonically increasing — consistent with the estimate being recomputed against a shifting hydration window (see related issues below).

## Impact

* Context bar is misleading (shows \~70–80% when actual usage is \~35%).
* Session enters context-pressure handling (`route=compact\_only`) and will **compact prematurely**, summarizing away real context that still fits comfortably.
* With local models the cost impact is zero, but on a metered provider this estimate would also mislead budgeting/compaction decisions.

## Related (likely same family)

* \#159799 — byte-capped history hydration slides the transcript window by one event per turn, busting local prefix caches
* \#202001 — prompt cache invalidated by system-prompt section churn between requests in one session

Happy to provide additional log excerpts (timestamps above) if useful.



### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a local lmstudio provider with `contextWindow` matching the loaded model (verified via `/api/v0/models`).
2. Run a tool-heavy webchat session (several large `exec` outputs) on that model for \~30–60 minutes.
3. Watch `\[context-pressure-diagnostic] estimatedPromptTokens` in the gateway log vs LM Studio's reported usage / `print\_timing` lines per turn.
4. Observe estimate climbing well past provider-reported prompt size; UI bar bounces between turns.


### Expected behavior

The context estimate should track what is actually sent to the provider (provider-reported prompt tokens when available), and cache-hit accounting should be internally consistent (`cached + new ≈ input`).


### Actual behavior

OpenClaw's estimate diverges from actual sent size by >2x and keeps inflating every turn

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (06afb10)

### Operating system

 Arch/CachyOS, Linux 7.3.5-2-cachyos x64

### Install method

gateway as systemd user service

### Model

Qwen 3.8 Flash Next - Q4_K_KL Unsloth

### Provider / routing chain

LM Studio

### Additional provider/model setup details

`lmstudio` (local llama.cpp backend), `contextWindow: 262144`, `maxTokens: 8192`

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

* Context bar is misleading (shows \~70–80% when actual usage is \~35%).
* Session enters context-pressure handling (`route=compact\_only`) and will **compact prematurely**, summarizing away real context that still fits comfortably.
* With local models the cost impact is zero, but on a metered provider this estimate would also mislead budgeting/compaction decisions.


### Additional information

_No response_

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a helper (subagent) waits for its background command with `sessions_yield`, the command's exit wakes it with the `[OpenClaw exec completion]` prompt, which ends with "If no user-facing update is needed, reply NO_REPLY only." The helper's run doesn't accept that reply, though: on Claude CLI it fails as "CLI backend returned an empty response", the turn shows "The AI service returned an empty reply", and model fallback reruns the turn on the next model. In our case that next model wrote a second full report, which reached the parent and the user as a duplicate.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Code at `69b81b5a063` (origin/main, 2026-11-25); 2026.11.10 has the same code on these paths.

- A helper session only gets an exec wake after `sessions_yield` awaited the command (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.ts:60`, `:143`, `:389`), so the helper still owes its result when the wake runs.
- That's why its reply policy is result-required: `src/agents/reply-completion.ts:108` returns `result-required` for a subagent session key before the exec-completion check at `:112` that makes ordinary exec wakes optional. The order is deliberate (#184005: "so subagent results stay required"; kept in #202423) and pinned by `src/auto-reply/reply/source-reply-expectation.test.ts:59` ("subagent exec wake" → `result-required`).
- The system prompt already respects that: `get-reply-run-context.ts:279` drops the silent-reply guidance for result-required turns. The wake prompt doesn't: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-run-params.ts:156-162` always ends with "reply NO_REPLY only".
- So a model that follows the wake prompt is rejected: Claude CLI at `src/agents/cli-runner.ts:454` (empty response, then model fallback), the embedded runner at `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.ts:170` (a "visible-answer continuation" retry).

Not a duplicate of #186413 (sessions_send into WebChat), #184718 (queued group followup), #169614 (cron repair) or #172209 (Slack thread policy): those are turns where silence should have been allowed. Here the policy is right and the prompt contradicts it. #177766 (private parent completion) was closed as not planned.

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh profile, Claude CLI model (seen with `claude-opus-5-5` in production and `claude-haiku-5-5` on a test profile).
2. In a session with a subagent key, e.g. `openclaw agent --session-key agent:main:subagent:wake-repro --message "…"`, ask the agent to start `sleep 6; echo build-ok` with exec `background: true`, reply `started`, then call `sessions_yield`, and say there is nothing new to report when it finishes.
3. Wait for the command to exit.

### Expected behavior

The wake turn ends with a short visible result (for example "build-ok, nothing new"), with no error and no model fallback.

### Actual behavior

The wake turn answers exactly `NO_REPLY` (8 bytes), then:

```
[agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 durationMs=4165 outBytes=8
[agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 … error=CLI backend returned an empty response.
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed … reason=empty_response next=none
```

and the session shows "⚠️ The AI service returned an empty reply. Please try again." With a fallback model configured, that model reruns the turn instead; in production it wrote a second copy of the helper's already-delivered report, which the parent passed on to the user.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10; origin/main `69b81b5a063` has the same code paths.

### Operating system

Linux x86_64 (distribution left out; not needed for the bug)

### Install method

npm global, systemd user service

### Model

claude-cli `claude-opus-5-5` (production), `claude-haiku-5-5` (repro); fallback `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`

### Provider / routing chain

claude-cli runtime, then model fallback to an OpenAI model

### Additional information

Fix PR: #205712.

## Summary

On 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8, Linux, system-scope Gateway), every `claude-cli` backend run costs roughly two full copies of the configured stdio MCP servers, and each Gateway-owned stdio child carries about 145 MB of supervisor wrapper overhead that no setting can turn off:

1. **Duplicate set per CLI run.** `prepareCliBundleMcp…` (dist `prompt-context-*.mjs`) calls `acquireSessionMcpRuntime(...)` under `nativeMcpPolicy` to work out native tool policy. That spawns every configured stdio server inside the Gateway (spawn-broker → `service-child-relay.js` → `service-child-group-anchor.js` → server). Then the generated `/tmp/openclaw-cli-mcp-*/mcp.json` makes `claude --strict-mcp-config` spawn the **same servers again** as its own direct children. One live CLI session = 2 × N server processes.
2. **Wrapper pair per stdio child.** Each Gateway-spawned stdio server sits under one relay and one group anchor. Both are full Node processes; the anchor loads a 1.6 MB bundle. Measured: anchor ≈ 78 MB RSS, relay ≈ 66 MB RSS, **≈ 144 MB per stdio child**, regardless of how small the server is (the wrapper is 3–10× the size of a Go MCP server such as github-mcp-server at ~21 MB). I found no config key or env var to choose a lighter supervisor for MCP children (`OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE` only covers database ownership).

Related: #155563 (retention of relay/anchor groups after a turn). This issue is about the steady-state cost of **live** sessions, which is separate from retention.

## Measurement (live production Gateway, 8 CPUs, MemoryHigh 24 GiB)

Before (2026-10-04 01:33 UTC): 10 live claude-cli sessions, 9 stdio servers configured.
- Gateway cgroup: anon 16.7 GB, `memory.events high` 18,441 (rising), memory.current at MemoryHigh.
- 92 `service-child-relay.js` (6.03 GB RSS) + 92 `service-child-group-anchor.js` (7.17 GB RSS) = **13.2 GB of wrapper processes**.
- Plus 9 direct stdio children under each `claude` process (~0.47 GB per session).
- To stay within memory, `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent` and `tools.swarm.maxConcurrent` had to stay at 2.

Workaround applied: the 9 servers run once each as loopback streamable-HTTP endpoints (stdio→HTTP proxy, ~780 MB total, outside the Gateway cgroup), and `mcp.servers.<name>` was changed to `{url, transport: "streamable-http"}` (hot reload, no restart).
- After (01:47 UTC): relays 65 → 1, anchors → 1, Gateway anon 16.7 → 8.4 GB, `memory.events high` flat; new CLI sessions' `mcp.json` holds only `type: http` entries and `claude` spawns no MCP children.

## Expected

- A CLI-backend run should not spawn a Gateway-side stdio set just to compute tool policy. Reuse the live session runtime, cache the tool list per server-config hash, or list tools once per config revision instead of per session.
- The relay + anchor supervisor for MCP stdio children should be much lighter (a single small process, or a mode without the full bundle), or configurable for hosts that already run under systemd/launchd process-group supervision.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8), Node 26.10.0, Ubuntu (kernel 6.8), Gateway as a systemd system unit
- Runtime: `claude-cli` backend (Claude Code), 9 stdio MCP servers (node, python and Go servers)

issues.body:
### Summary

On 2026.11.5 the Gateway process keeps file descriptors open on read-only SQLite snapshot copies after their staging directories under `~/.cache/openclaw/` have been unlinked. The disk space is never released while the Gateway runs. `du` and `~/.cache/openclaw` look small; only `df` vs `du` (or `/proc/<pid>/fd`) shows the loss, so the existing snapshot reclaimer has nothing to reclaim.

This is the "held open after unlink" variant reported in a comment on #170496 (cosu, 2026.11.1). That issue is about copy *rate* and is marked stale/needs-info, so I am filing the descriptor leak separately with fresh numbers on 2026.11.5.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (e13cf15), npm global install
- Node v24.22.1, Linux 6.8.0 x64 (Ubuntu, AWS EC2)
- Two Gateways on one host as systemd **user** units: default profile (port 18789, 7 agents, `state/openclaw.sqlite` = 192,233,472 bytes) and a second profile (port 18810, `state/openclaw.sqlite` = 11,063,296 bytes)
- `~/.cache` and the state dirs are on a 100 GB ext4 volume

### Observed

Default-profile Gateway, single PID, uptime 35 h:

- **244** deleted files held open, **23.45 GB** total. The volume reached **98 %** used (2.3 GB free); `du` of the whole volume reported 74 GB vs 96 GB used in `df`.
- Every leaked descriptor points to `~/.cache/openclaw/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-XXXXXX/database.sqlite (deleted)` (192,233,472 bytes each, a full copy of `state/openclaw.sqlite`) or to the matching `.../owner.sqlite (deleted)`.
- No other process held them. `~/.cache/openclaw` itself was 640 MB.
- `openclaw daemon restart --safe` (preflight: 0 active work) released all 23.45 GB immediately.

After the restart:

- Within the first ~4 minutes (startup / post-ready maintenance) the new PID was already holding 2 × `database.sqlite (deleted)` + 2 × `owner.sqlite (deleted)` = 366 MB, and that stayed flat for the next 30+ minutes.
- Running `openclaw status`, `cron list`, `sessions list`, `channels status`, `plugins list` and `health` against it (from a clean environment) did **not** add any held descriptors. So the leaking reader seems to be inside the Gateway (startup plus some recurring in-process path), not the CLI RPC path from #157712.

The second-profile Gateway on the same install shows the same pattern at a smaller scale: 84 held deleted files (41 × `database.sqlite`, 42 × `owner.sqlite`, plus one nested `openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-XXXX/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-XXXX/database.sqlite`), 437 MB after 36 h of uptime.

Average leak rate on the busy Gateway: about 7 copies per hour, or 0.67 GB/h at this DB size.

### How to check

```bash
PID=$(pgrep -f 'dist/index.js gateway' | head -1)
find /proc/$PID/fd -lname '*readonly-v2*(deleted)' -printf '%l\n' \
  | sed -E 's/-v2-[A-Za-z0-9]+/-v2-XXXX/g' | sort | uniq -c
df -h ~ ; du -sh ~
```

### Expected

When a snapshot's staging directory is removed, every SQLite connection (the database and its `owner.sqlite` token) opened on it inside the Gateway, including worker threads, is closed first, or removal waits for those readers to close. Unlinked snapshots should not outlive their readers. The reclaimer could also count space pinned by unlinked-but-open snapshots in its health output, so this shows up somewhere other than `df`.

### What I could not determine

I could not attribute the held descriptors to a specific worker or thread: they are process-wide, and the journal shows no snapshot-specific events. The leaked descriptor numbers were spread from about 45 to about 498 over the 35 h, which fits a recurring in-process path and not only startup. I am logging the held count every 20 minutes and can add a timeline if it helps narrow the trigger.

### Local mitigation

A user timer measures the bytes held by deleted files per Gateway PID and runs `openclaw daemon restart --safe` when the leak reaches 6 GB, or when free space falls below 10 GB with at least 1 GB leaked.

Related: #170496 (copy rate; same held-open variant in a comment), #157712 (CLI reads leaving snapshot directories behind), #188593 (reclaimer never reclaims anything), #193013.

issues.body:
### What happens

On a Gateway host installed with npm (Linux, user-systemd service), every update leaves a full database snapshot directory next to the package, and nothing removes it afterwards:

```
~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/.openclaw.package-backup-<pid>-<ts>.databases   (about 7 GB each here)
```

On our host four of these had accumulated by 2026-11-23 (updates on 11-17, 11-19 and two runs on 11-23), 28 GB in total. Together with the per-agent `*.pre-startup-migration-*.bak` copies (about 7.6 GB per update here), each update keeps roughly 15 GB, and a 309 GB root disk went from 78% to 89% in one day.

### Why this looks like a gap

- `update.cleanup` (dry run and real run) lists only the `pre-startup-migration` `.bak` copies. The `.openclaw.package-backup-*.databases` directories never appear in its artifacts, as candidate or protected.
- `openclaw update status --json` contains no reference to the two older directories (11-17 and 11-19), so they look unowned, but there is no supported command that says they are safe to remove or removes them.
- The update notice says: "Verified successful activation removes these snapshots only if automatic restoration remains available; otherwise retain them with the update's recovery artifacts." On this host they were retained after every update, including updates that verified healthy, and they are never retired later.

### Expected

One of:
- `update.cleanup` / `openclaw update` cleanup covers `.openclaw.package-backup-*.databases` with the same candidate/protected reporting it gives the `.bak` copies, or
- a retention rule (for example keep the newest N) applied after a later update verifies, or
- `openclaw update status` lists these directories with their size and whether anything still depends on them.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (e31bbf0), npm install, Ubuntu 24.04, Node 26
- Shared SQLite state about 7.1 GiB at snapshot time
- Related: #170335 (opposite problem, snapshots removed too early), #204226 (update run left as failed on this host)

### Workaround used

Removed the two oldest directories by hand after confirming `update status --json` did not reference them; kept the newest two.

## Summary

On 2026.11.7 (e31bbf0), `openclaw update repair --yes` fails every time at `finalize:targetConfigConvergence`. Doctor reports that the state database is "undergoing offline maintenance by sqlite-maintenance process <pid>", the Gateway is left stopped, and the run stays recorded as failed with reason `service-authority-revoked-recovery-pending`. The Gateway itself runs fine on 2026.11.7 once started manually.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (e31bbf0), npm package install (`~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw`)
- Linux x64 (kernel 6.8), systemd user service, Node 26.13.1
- SQLite state at `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`

## What happened (2026-11-23, times in PT)

- Automatic 2026.11.7 update campaigns at 08:25 and 10:05 were rolled back (`post-core-update-failed`).
- A chat `/update` at 10:56 installed 2026.11.7, but the run was recorded as failed (`post-update-failed`; package-backup-retention: "Installation recovery is unverified").
- `openclaw update repair --yes` was then run twice from a `systemd-run` unit outside the Gateway:
  - Run 1: started 11:34:31, failed (rc=1), unit ended 11:49:47.
  - Run 2: started 12:02:08, failed (rc=1), unit ended 12:17:10.
- Both runs failed at the same point with:

  ```
  Warning: Doctor could not complete Gateway restoration: UPDATE_NATIVE_AUTHORITY: OpenClaw state at ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite is undergoing offline maintenance by sqlite-maintenance process <pid> (ownerKind=process)
  ```

  then `finalize:targetConfigConvergence` failed, followed by "Could not read update recovery history: … offline maintenance …", and the Gateway was left stopped.
- During run 2 no other `openclaw update` or `doctor` process was running and our external watchers were paused. The maintenance owner therefore appears to be the repair's own Doctor (self-contention). We have not confirmed which process the reported pid belonged to.
- The Gateway was started manually after each run (ready 11:52 and 12:18) and works normally on 2026.11.7.

For update progress, run `openclaw update status --json`. | service-authority-revoked",

`~/.openclaw/logs/support/openclaw-update-failure-6c8ef230_74a3_4dfb_b958_2cd71d49f9ff.json` (run 2, written 12:15) is byte-for-byte identical except for the maintenance process pid (1084597 instead of 1057181).

## Expected

`openclaw update repair` completes on an installation where the target version is already installed and the Gateway is healthy, or at least does not fail on a maintenance lock held by its own Doctor, and does not leave the Gateway stopped.

## Questions

1. Is the failed run record harmless while the Gateway is healthy on 2026.11.7?
2. Will it block the next automatic update?
3. What is the supported way to clear it?

## Related

- #164986: 2026.9.8 `update repair` fails at `finalize:plugins` after Doctor offline maintenance (macOS). Same family; this report is a different phase (`finalize:targetConfigConvergence`) on a Linux systemd user service.
- #163950: failed post-update verification leaves a permanent warning on a healthy Gateway (closed as fixed; its closing comment asks for a new linked issue if it recurs on a release containing the fix).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Summary

Since 2026.10.10, delegating work to native Codex helpers fails roughly once for every helper launched.

The parent agent starts helpers and ends its turn (`sessions_yield`). When a helper finishes, OpenClaw opens a separate wake-up turn on the parent's Codex thread. Two things go wrong with that turn:
- it runs on authority borrowed from the turn that already ended;
- the parent's original Codex turn is often still live on the same thread.

The wake-up turn then fails ("agent harness host capability is no longer active"). The helper's result is lost, any active `/goal` is paused, and the user's next messages are rejected ("Codex session became active in another runner", "still has background work after waiting for cleanup").

This is the underlying problem behind a family of errors that have been reported separately. They are all symptoms of one lifecycle bug: OpenClaw ties authority and thread ownership to a single turn, while native Codex helpers and background work routinely outlive that turn.

### Impact and severity

**Severity: blocks the core workflow on every delegated task, and locks the user out of their own assistant.**

Delegating work to parallel helpers is the main reason to give an assistant a substantial job. On 10.10 and later, that is exactly the moment it breaks:

- **Work silently stops.** Helpers finish their work, but the results never reach the assistant. Nothing tells the user that progress has halted; the conversation just goes quiet.
- **Goals are paused out from under the user.** A failed wake-up pauses the active `/goal` with "Paused after an error." On native Codex sessions the operator cannot resume it ("requires the built-in OpenClaw runtime"), so the user has to notice the stall and re-establish the goal by hand.
- **The user is locked out.** Messages sent afterward are rejected with errors telling the user to "stop its running work and retry", meaning stop the very work they asked for. The user gets no reply at all; the rejected messages are simply dropped.
- **It recurs constantly.** In my installation this happened ~100 times a day on a single long-running task. The assistant becomes something to babysit rather than something that gets work done: every few minutes, check whether it is stuck, abort it, resend the message, re-set the goal.
- **The cost is spent and thrown away.** Helpers run to completion and consume usage, and then their results are discarded.

The experience is that the assistant falls over the moment it is asked to do anything ambitious, and that the user has to spend their time diagnosing and recovering it instead of getting the outcome they asked for. It is deeply frustrating, and it undermines trust in delegating anything substantial at all.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On 2026.10.10 or later (observed through 2026.11.2), use the native Codex runtime (`agentRuntime.id = codex`) for an OpenAI model.
2. In a channel session (Discord in my case), give the agent a long task that it delegates. The agent calls `spawn_agent` for one or more helpers, then `sessions_yield` while they run.
3. Let a helper finish after the parent's turn has ended.
4. Observe the following:
   - the completion "announce" turn fails;
   - any active goal pauses;
   - a user message sent shortly afterward is rejected with no reply.

### Expected behavior

- A helper's completion is delivered to the parent reliably: once the parent's Codex thread is idle, as a turn with its own valid authority.
- If delivery fails, it is retried. It does not lose the result or pause the goal.
- The user's messages are always accepted and answered (queued if necessary). They are never rejected with an instruction to stop running work.

### Actual behavior

A representative sequence from 2026-11-09 (times are America/Los_Angeles; one session; IDs shortened):

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 07:03:59, 07:04:05 | The parent calls `spawn_agent` twice. |
| 07:05:49 | The parent calls `sessions_yield`, ending its turn while both helpers run. |
| ~07:07:09 | A helper finishes. OpenClaw starts `announce:codex-native:<parentThread>:<childThread>:succeeded` on the parent thread. |
| 07:08:18 | `codex app-server notification ignored for inactive turn`, with `matchesActiveThread: true` and `matchesActiveTurn: false`. Codex is still emitting `item/started` and `item/completed` for the parent's original turn, while OpenClaw has already made the announce turn the active turn. Two turns are live on one thread. |
| 07:09:38 | `agent cleanup failed … step=codex-trajectory-flush error=agent harness host capability is no longer active`, then `lane task error … durationMs=148848 error="agent harness host capability is no longer active"`, then `Subagent completion direct announce failed`. The session goal changes to `paused`, with `lastStatusNote: "Paused after an error. Resume to continue. agent harness host capability is no longer active"`. |
| 07:14:09, 07:14:42 | Two user messages are rejected with `CodexAdoptedThreadActiveError: Codex session became active in another runner; wait for it to finish before continuing`. The log records `visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads … cause=error`, and the user receives nothing. |

Error counts in the gateway log:

| Error | 2026-11-08 | 2026-11-09 (until ~07:30) |
|---|---|---|
| `agent harness host capability is no longer active` | 56 | 131 |
| `Codex did not confirm unloading its previous configuration` | 28 | 76 |
| `still has background work after waiting for cleanup` | 20 | 27 |
| `Codex session became active in another runner` | 0 | 6 |
| `Session … placement authority changed` | 0 | 3 |

### Regression boundary: 2026.10.9 → 2026.10.10

I counted these errors per day in the agent's transcript events, alongside `spawn_agent`/`sessions_spawn` calls. The transcripts capture only a subset of the gateway-log errors, but the pattern is unambiguous:

| Period | Version | Helper launches/day | Errors/day |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 8–21 | ≤ 10.9 | ~4 | ~0.5 |
| Oct 22–Nov 2 (proactive delegation enabled) | 10.9 | ~63 | ~2 |
| Nov 3–9 | 10.10 → 11.1 → 11.2 | ~97 | ~106 |

- Heavy delegation on 10.9 (~760 helper launches over 12 days) was essentially error-free.
- The first `host capability` / `background work` / `another runner` error in the entire history appears at 2026-11-03 11:16, a few hours after updating to 10.10 that morning. It has continued on every release since.
- Whatever changed between 10.9 and 10.10 in harness authority binding, announce delivery, or Codex thread retention is the most likely origin.

### Code-level observations (2026.11.2 dist)

- `bindHarnessHostSourceAuthority` (`src/agents/harness/host-source-authority.ts`) throws "agent harness host capability is no longer active" in any of these cases:
  - `attempt.admittedRunContext.operationalRunInstance` differs from the instance captured at bind time;
  - the captured admitted-run assertion fails;
  - the gateway is not current.

  The announce turn for a helper launched by an earlier turn appears to carry that earlier turn's delegated authority. It fails as soon as it touches a host capability, which in the trace above was the trajectory flush during cleanup.
- The announce turn is started while the parent's original Codex turn is still producing items on the same thread (see 07:08:18). That makes the follow-on errors expected:
  - "did not confirm unloading previous configuration",
  - "still has background work",
  - "became active in another runner".
- The `codex-trajectory-flush` cleanup failure has the same signature as #171197, which was closed as fixed in October. It is recurring on 2026.11.2.

### Suggested direction

The fix needs to be in the lifecycle model, not in individual guards:

- **The session, not the turn, should own outstanding helper work and background commands.**
- **Completions should be queued per session and delivered once the parent Codex thread is idle.** Simultaneous completions should be coalesced into one wake-up, instead of one competing announce turn per helper.
- **Wake-up turns should be admitted with fresh authority of their own,** rather than inheriting authority from the turn that spawned the helpers.
- **A failed delivery should be retried.** It should never discard the helper's result or pause the user's goal.
- **User messages should always be queued and answered,** never rejected with "stop its running work and retry".

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.2 (b556fdf); `@openclaw/codex` 2026.11.2. The regression first appeared on 2026.10.10.

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (Apple Silicon)

### Install method

npm global (Homebrew Node 26.13.0)

### Model

openai/gpt-6.1-sol

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw → native Codex runtime (`agentRuntime.id = codex`, codex-cli 0.164.0) → OpenAI

### Beta release blocker

No

### Additional information

Related reports that I believe are symptoms of this same underlying issue:
- #194403: helper-completion continuations lose authority and block conversations.
- #196061 and #196062: a silent turn with a retained command is falsely marked failed. That is one entry point into the stuck state, not the root cause.
- #171197: the `codex-trajectory-flush` "host capability is no longer active" failure, closed as fixed but recurring.
- #147759 and #167280: delayed or stalled prompts after native Codex handoff and stop.

Diagnostic signal: when the parent keeps its turn open and collects helper results with `wait_agent` instead of calling `sessions_yield`, the completion arrives inside the live turn and this path is not exercised. That is consistent with the announce/wake-up turn being the failure point.

issues.body:
## 现象

飞书插件（`@openclaw/feishu`）把 **p2p 私聊**按 `chat_id`（`oc_` 前缀）发送时，outbound 会话路由一律判定为 `group`，导致同一个私聊同时存在两条会话 key：

- `agent:<id>:feishu:group:oc_xxx`   ← outbound 新建（错误）
- `agent:<id>:feishu:direct:ou_xxx`  ← inbound 真实私聊

后果：入站消息与出站消息落到不同 session，触发 `Conversation binding changed while preparing the reply` / `SessionWorkStartChangedError`，表现为**私聊消息静默不回复**。

## 根因

插件层有两处**各自独立**的 peerKind 判定，判据都是「target 长得像 chat_id 就是群」：

1. `messaging.inferTargetChatType`:
   ```js
   inferTargetChatType: ({ to }) => resolveReceiveIdType(to) === "chat_id" ? "group" : "direct",
   ```
2. `resolveFeishuOutboundSessionRoute()` 内:
   ```js
   let isGroup = receiveIdType === "chat_id";
   ```

两者都**不查询飞书 `chat_mode`**。而飞书 API `GET /im/v1/chats/{chat_id}` 返回的 `chat_mode` 才是 p2p / group 的权威判据（p2p 私聊同样有 `oc_` 开头的 chat_id）。

OpenClaw 核心 `inferPeerKind` 已经优先调用插件钩子 `plugin.messaging.inferTargetChatType`，所以问题完全在插件层，核心无需改动。

## 建议修复（插件层，单一 helper，两处共用）

1. 新增 helper：target 是 `chat_id` 形态时，调 `GET /im/v1/chats/{chat_id}` 读 `chat_mode`
   - `chat_mode === "p2p"` ⇒ `direct`，并把 peerId 换成该 chat 的 p2p 对方 `open_id`（否则 session key 会用 `oc_` 当 peerId）
   - 其余（`group` / `topic_group` 等）⇒ `group`
2. 加 TTL 缓存（建议 10 分钟，**正负结果都缓存**），避免每条消息打一次 API
3. API 失败 / 拿不到 ⇒ **回落到旧行为（group）**，并计数上报
   （宁可把 p2p 误判成 group，也不能把真群误判成 direct —— 后者会把群消息投进私聊）
4. `inferTargetChatType` 是**同步**钩子、核心不会 await 它；`resolveFeishuOutboundSessionRoute` 是 **async**。
   ⇒ 探测放在 async 路径，同步路径读同一份 TTL 缓存（缓存未命中时退回 group）。
5. 判定逻辑**只写一份**，两处都调它，不要各自复制。

## 影响面

所有按 `chat_id` 向 p2p 私聊目标主动发送的场景（消息工具 / 定时任务 / Agent 互发）都会命中。属于社区插件 `npm` 包，升级即覆盖本地补丁，故建议在上游修掉。

## 环境

- `@openclaw/feishu@2026.9.8`
- OpenClaw `2026.9.8 (fc23bc8)`

（本 issue 已做脱敏：不含 chat_id、app_id、凭据等任何实例标识。）

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (update blocker)

### Beta release blocker

No (stable 2026.11.10)

### Summary

A stable 2026.10.8 npm-global install cannot be upgraded to 2026.11.10 with the documented manual path (stop Gateway → `npm i -g openclaw@2026.11.10` → `openclaw doctor --fix`) when the config is multi-agent with explicit ownership and still carries legacy keys that Doctor is supposed to migrate.

The config has:
- `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "main"`, and 9 agents in `agents.entries`;
- legacy keys `agents.defaults.heartbeat`, `agents.entries.main.heartbeat`, `agents.entries.<second-agent>.heartbeat`, `skills.workshop` (`autonomous.mode: "off"`) and `plugins.entries.<memory-plugin>.hooks.allowPromptInjection`;
- 2 enabled heartbeat monitors (every 1h).

Doctor starts with `Config unavailable; using environment and default agent directory settings. (Invalid config … Unrecognized key …)` listing those 5 keys. It then runs on that fallback, which ignores the real config, so `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` is never visible. When the heartbeat retirement / legacy config migration tries to write the config, it throws `AgentSelectionRequiredError`:

```
Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner. Select an agent explicitly; CLI callers can pass --agent <id>, channels can add a binding, and ambient services can set their agentId target.
```

This surfaces as `config-lock-refused`. Doctor has no `--agent` option. The legacy config is never published, so 11.10 rejects the config and the Gateway cannot start, although the databases have already been migrated.

### Steps to reproduce

Reproduced on an isolated full copy of the state. `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` pointed at the copy, the live Gateway was not involved, and 2026.11.10 was installed in its own prefix.

1. Start from a 2026.10.8 state and config shaped as above (state DB `user_version` 20, agent DBs 25).
2. Run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`. It exits 1 with:
   - `[state-migrations] Plugin "codex" data/settings upgrade is unfinished: The configured plugin package is missing or has not converged. … Run "openclaw update repair", then "openclaw doctor --fix"`
   - and `Plugin codex Doctor source must be prepared before loading`, which looks like the #203442 family.

   The state DB is migrated (20 → 40), but the agent DBs stay at 25 and the config is unchanged.
3. Run `openclaw update repair --yes --no-restart`. The agent DBs migrate (25 → 42). Then:
   ```
   Doctor: heartbeat retirement
   Doctor: maintenance finish
   Doctor could not complete maintenance. Check the reported service state and resolve the failure.
   Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner. …
   [update finalize] {"step":"finalize:doctor","status":"failed","detail":"Updated pre-plugin Doctor failed:","failureFacts":[{"check":"config-write","code":"config-lock-refused","message":"Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner. …"}],"exitCode":1,"reason":"config-lock-refused"}
   ```
   Afterwards `update repair` keeps polling for a Gateway listener (`lsof -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN`) until it is stopped.
4. `openclaw config validate` still reports the same 5 unrecognized keys.

### Expected behavior

When Doctor or `update repair` migrates legacy keys, they resolve the owner from the raw config they are migrating, here `agents.ownership: "explicit"` with `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId`. Alternatively, they finish the documented legacy migrations (heartbeat retirement, `allowPromptInjection` → `allowPromptModification`, `skills.workshop` → `plugins.entries.skill-workshop.config`) before any agent-scoped write. Either way, the documented manual upgrade completes.

### Actual behavior

The config write is refused with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` / `config-lock-refused`. The config keeps the legacy keys and 11.10 rejects it. The only way back is restoring a pre-upgrade backup.

### Additional context

- In `config-doctor/agent-scope-config-*.js`, owner resolution reads `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` when `agents.ownership === "explicit"`. Doctor is on the env/default-agent-directory fallback because the config does not validate, so that branch never sees the real config.
- Earlier in the same rehearsal, the pre-repair capture ("Preserve original state") failed on a legacy 0-byte `memory/main.sqlite` placeholder: `State schema inspection failed … after 120.346 second; last progress: pre-migration database backup for …/memory/main.sqlite`. Moving the empty file aside let the capture complete (~2.8 GB).
- Related: #200224 (heartbeat retirement on upgrade), #193594 (CLI ignores the configured `systemAgent`), #203442 (`Doctor source must be prepared before loading`).

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.8 (`dc2523e`) → 2026.11.10 (`6ea542f`)

### Operating system

Ubuntu, Linux x64, Node v26.13.1

### Install method

npm global, systemd user service (Tailscale Serve mode, so `openclaw update` is not usable here: #205405)

issues.body:
Bug type: Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

Beta release blocker: No

### Summary

When a plugin approval is requested from inside the Gateway process (single-phase), a prompt that was delivered and then expired comes back to the agent as `Plugin approval unavailable (no approval route)`. The plugin's `requireApproval.timeoutReason` never reaches the agent. The agent then tells the user the conversation can't approve things, when the prompt was posted there and nobody clicked in time.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a plugin's `before_tool_call` return `requireApproval` with `timeoutMs: 75_000` and a `timeoutReason`.
2. Trigger the tool from a Discord channel turn, with the agent on the bundled Codex harness inside the Gateway.
3. Let the Discord approval card post, and don't answer it.

### Expected behavior

After 75 seconds the tool call is blocked with the plugin's `timeoutReason`, as the two-phase path already does at `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.approval.ts` around line 442.

### Actual behavior

The tool call fails after 75 seconds with `Plugin approval unavailable (no approval route)`.

Why, as far as I can read it on `main` and v2026.11.10:

- `hasInProcessGatewayToolCaller()` is true, so the request goes out with `twoPhase: false` and `expectFinal: true`.
- In `src/gateway/server-methods/approval-shared.ts`, `handlePendingApprovalRequest` answers a single-phase request from the decision handoff with `{ id, decision, createdAtMs, expiresAtMs }`. An expired prompt and a `manager.expire(id, "no-approval-route")` both resolve that handoff with `decision: null`, and the response doesn't say which one happened.
- In `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.approval.ts` (the `hasImmediateDecision` branch, around line 404), any `decision === null` is reported as "no approval route", and `approval.timeoutReason` is never read there.
- `agent-tools.before-tool-call.approval-policy.test.ts` mocks `{ id: "server-id", decision: null }` and expects that no-route text, so the test pins the current behavior.

A possible fix: include the resolved `deliveryRoute`, or the record's expiry reason, in the single-phase final response, and treat `null` with a real route as a timeout that uses `timeoutReason` the same way the two-phase path does.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10 (same code on `main` as of 2026-11-25)

### Operating system

Linux (official Docker image)

### Install method

Docker

### Model

openai/gpt-6.2-sol

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> bundled Codex harness -> OpenAI (ChatGPT plan sign-in)

### Logs

The tool progress line in the channel read `automations remove · 1m 15s · Plugin approval unavailable (no approval route)`, while the approval card had posted in the same thread with `Expires in: 75s`. The thread then got a "Plugin approval expired" message for that ID.

### Impact and severity

The agent gets a false reason and repeats it to users. In our case it told the people who could approve that their thread had "no route for scheduler approval" and sent them to another channel, when they'd only missed the prompt. The plugin can't correct this itself, since no hook can change a blocked call's reason after the approval resolves, and `onResolution` gets `cancelled` on this path rather than `timeout`.

### Additional information

Related, on the same expiry: Discord then also posted "Plugin approval denied" for the prompt nobody answered, which looks like #158944, closed as not planned, with the fix in open PR #159524.

issues.title: claude-cli: prompt cache fully rewritten whenever the turn's surface changes (webchat / telegram heartbeat / event)

issues.body:
Related: #182891, #155878, #143017

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.10.8 (npm global), Windows 11 (10.0.26300), Node v24.22.1
- Agents on the `claude-cli` backend with Claude subscription auth (Opus 5 1M, Fable 5); 5 agents; largest agent DB is 966 MB
- Operator chats via Control UI (webchat). Heartbeats are delivered to Telegram (`agents.entries.<id>.heartbeat.accountId` set, no `target`)
- Cache figures are `cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens` from the Claude CLI session transcript (`~/.claude/projects/<workspace>/<session>.jsonl`)

### Summary

On the `claude-cli` backend, the live Claude CLI process is fingerprinted on the full system prompt and tool set. Both differ by inbound surface. When an operator talks in webchat between Telegram-delivered heartbeats, almost every surface switch respawns the process with a different appended system prompt and tool block. Each switch rewrites the whole conversation cache, 400–830k tokens on a 1M-context session.

### Evidence (before)

One agent, 2026-10-28 00:45–10:44. There were 8 full rewrites: 1 after a restart, 1 after more than 1 h idle, and **6 at a surface/trigger switch**:

```
01:08:33 read=      0 write= 728729   first turn after restart
01:11:24 read=      0 write= 737826   event after user
01:13:54 read=  35478 write= 710319   user after event
01:55:55 read=      0 write= 748303   heartbeat after user
04:56:49 read=      0 write= 781960   event after heartbeat
07:10:50 read=      0 write= 793405   >1h idle (expected)
10:00:25 read=      0 write= 813803   user after heartbeat
10:39:57 read=      0 write= 834159   user after heartbeat
```

Matching gateway lines:

```
[agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5[1m] promptChars=4171 trigger=heartbeat useResume=true session=present resumeSession=… reuse=reusable-drift:system-prompt,prompt-tools historyPrompt=none
[agent/cli-backend] cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5[1m] promptChars=746 trigger=user useResume=true session=present resumeSession=… reuse=reusable-drift:system-prompt historyPrompt=none
```

### What actually differs (captured argv, appended system prompt and MCP `tools/list`, webchat turn vs heartbeat turn)

1. **Tool set:** the webchat run has 44 tools. The Telegram heartbeat has 41 (`screen`, `suggest_task`, `dismiss_task` missing). The event run has 40 (`portal` also missing).
   - `screen` is gated by `requiredClientCaps: [UI_COMMANDS]`, then `filterToolsByClientCaps` (`src/agents/openclaw-tools.client-caps.ts`, `src/agents/tools/screen-tool.ts`)
   - `suggest_task`/`dismiss_task` exist only when `taskSuggestionDeliveryMode === "gateway"` (`src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts`)
   - Even with the same tool names, `screen`'s description and schema change with `UI_AGENT_GITHUB_SETTINGS` (`githubIdentitySettingsAvailable`, `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts`)
   - `portal` returns `[]` when `senderIsOwner === false` (`src/agents/tools/portal-tool.ts`)
   - `sessions` switches to an assignment-only schema when `senderIsOwner === false` (`controlOnly`, `src/agents/tools/sessions-tool.ts`)
   - `skill_workshop` switches to the library variant when `run.libraryAuthoring` is present (`src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool-factory.ts`). That is true on event runs and not on webchat runs.
2. **System prompt.** Everything after `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY` (`src/agents/system-prompt.ts`) is surface-specific, and it is all sent to the CLI:
   - Tool list lines (in the stable prefix, but filtered by the tool set above)
   - `## Authorized Senders` (heartbeat only)
   - `## Control UI Embed`, `## Control UI Side Chat`, `## Collapsible Details` (webchat only)
   - `## Conversation Context` channel JSON (`"channel": "webchat"` vs `"telegram"`) plus `### Delivery Format` (Telegram rich markup rules)
   - `Runtime:` line (`active_node_identity=requester` vs `unknown`)
3. These feed the live-session fingerprint (`systemPromptHash`, `promptToolNamesHash`, `extraSystemPromptHash` and argv including `--allowedTools`, in `src/agents/cli-runner/live-session-fingerprint.ts`). A changed fingerprint means a new process, initialized with `appendSystemPrompt: context.systemPrompt` (`extensions/anthropic` `cli.runtime`). Because tools come first in the API cache prefix, then system, then messages, every mismatch invalidates the entire conversation.

Two consecutive webchat turns produced byte-identical prompts, so the variance is purely per surface.

### Local patch (works)

Scoped to `backendResolved.id === "claude-cli"`, in `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`:

1. **Surface-invariant tool set:** force `clientCaps ∪ {"ui-commands", "ui-agent-github-settings"}` and default `taskSuggestionDeliveryMode` to `"gateway"` before tool projection.
2. **Cache-stable system prompt:** send only the part before `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY` as the CLI system prompt. Move the tail (date, channel/delivery format, Control UI sections, Runtime line) into an `<openclaw_turn_context>` block appended to the user turn, but only when its hash changes (or every 6 h). This reuses the existing turn-context path (`context: [turnRuntimeFacts?.relocatable, …]`); `runtimeFactsInTurn` already does this for the Runtime line alone.
3. **`portal`:** keep it listed for non-owner turns and throw from `execute` instead (`portal-tool.ts`), so the owner-only rule still holds.

### Evidence (after)

```
14:10:52 read= 407252 write=  16014   heartbeat, first turn after a gateway restart
14:13:52 read= 426197 write=   3700   webchat user turn right after the telegram heartbeat
16:01:45 read= 520079 write=   3071   (second agent) user after heartbeat
16:58:55 read= 560879 write=   5649   (second agent) user after heartbeat
```

`cli turn context: … system=0f6db5e19dae trigger=heartbeat tools=44` and `… system=0f6db5e19dae trigger=user tools=44`: identical hashes across surfaces. A side effect is that the cache now also survives gateway restarts (13:37: the first turn after a restart read 381,350).

### Still open

Event (non-owner) turns still differ in the `sessions` schema and the `skill_workshop` variant. We did not patch these, because doing it safely means moving the `senderIsOwner` checks into `execute`. Cost: one full rewrite per event turn when no event turn happened in the past hour.

### Suggested upstream direction

- Treat listing-time capability and owner gating as call-time checks for CLI backends: list a stable superset and refuse in `execute`. Alternatively, make the live session fingerprint per surface and keep a warm process per surface.
- Never put post-boundary content into `--append-system-prompt` / `initialize.appendSystemPrompt`; deliver it per turn, with change detection.
