issues.body:
## What happens

I reproduced this on main at `6ef3c6096a48e8a1abc776559940b28d137725cd`, using its production Control UI, an isolated local Gateway, and Chromium on Linux. Returning HTTP 503 for only `assets/markdown-streaming-runtime-*.js` leaves the authenticated connection healthy, but Send clears the composer and marks the local message **Not sent / Retry**. No `chat.send` frame reaches the Gateway and its transcript remains empty.

## Reproduction

1. Build main and start an isolated Gateway with the Control UI enabled.
2. In a fresh browser document, make only the streaming-Markdown formatter asset return HTTP 503.
3. Type a message in an existing chat and click Send.

Expected: delivery should proceed using the required transport, with the existing standard Markdown renderer until the optional formatter is available.

Actual: the optional import rejects the combined preparation promise in `chat-send-delivery.ts`, preventing delivery.

## Checks

- I reproduced the outage in three fresh local runs, each with zero send frames and zero persisted user messages. The normal-resource control sent and stored its message once and received a formatted local-model reply.
- A focused local fix removes the formatter from the delivery dependency. With formatter 503, a held formatter request, and normal resources, each final-code trial sent, acknowledged, and stored one message and rendered the reply's bold text and code.
- History traces the dependency to #183198 (`a36d0483f8375`), whose stated intent was to preserve Chat behavior while deferring evaluation. I found no stated requirement to block delivery on formatter failure.

Reported by Dan Riccio, who supplied the original reproduction and proposed patch. I independently reproduced it before filing this issue.

Not checked: Safari/Firefox, hosted model providers, or broad latency benchmarks.

## Clean comparison

Before: main, formatter HTTP 503.

![Before: message marked Not sent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33a9da54-9360-48d7-8277-f885e7feabc1)

After: same formatter HTTP 503, local fix.

![After: delivered message and formatted reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9cad12df-96f5-4c3f-9ae4-3c8fc333bbf2)

## Annotated comparison

![Before: formatter failure blocks delivery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/875bbde4-8e89-46b4-a270-c656a77acb83)

![After: delivery and formatting succeed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3327d028-b64b-4cfe-a847-71b363c3799c)

Actual production UI at 1280 × 900 with an isolated real Gateway and synthetic conversation content. Only the formatter asset is fault-injected. The after reply is generated by local Qwen3 4B Instruct.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
The shared Markdown renderer builds an image's alt text from the raw label source, so Markdown inside the alt (`**bold**`, `_italic_`, escapes, entities, nested images) reaches channels as literal characters: `![**Bold** chart of _sales_](…)` shows `**Bold** chart of _sales_`, and a README-style badge `[![**build**](badge.svg)](https://ci.example)` shows a link reading `**build**`.

### Steps to reproduce
1. On `main`, render a reply with a Markdown image through the Telegram formatter:
   ```ts
   import { markdownToTelegramHtml } from "./extensions/telegram/src/format.ts";
   console.log(markdownToTelegramHtml("![**Bold** chart of _sales_](https://example.com/c.png)"));
   console.log(markdownToTelegramHtml("![a & b \\* c](u)"));
   ```
2. Or send a reply containing such an image through the plain Telegram reply path (`deliverReplies`).

On Telegram the durable final-reply path lifts valid `https` images into photos, so the alt text is only rendered for images that are not lifted (relative, `http://`, `data:` or blocked-host URLs, reference-style images) and for text sent through the plain reply path (fallback delivery, native command replies) or message edits. Channels that render image alt text from the shared IR show it for every image.

### Expected behavior
Alt text is plain text, as CommonMark recommends for image descriptions ("only the plain string content of the image description be used"): `Bold chart of sales`, a link reading `build`, `a & b * c`. Literal HTML and code spans in the alt stay as written.

### Actual behavior
```
**Bold** chart of _sales_
a &amp; b \* c
```
Nested images keep their source: `![outer ![inner *i*](i.png) end](o.png)` shows `outer ![inner *i*](i.png) end`.

### OpenClaw version
main @ ce7788f5a (package.json 2026.11.2), first reproduced at 4b077d31b; run from source

### Operating system
macOS (Apple Silicon); the renderer is platform-independent

### Install method
Source checkout (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`)

### Model
Not model-specific

### Provider / routing chain
Not applicable (outbound Markdown rendering)

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
`packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`, `case "image"`, passes `token.content` to `appendImageAlternative`. For markdown-it image tokens `content` is the raw label source; markdown-it's own renderer derives alt from the parsed children (`renderInlineAsText`).

### Impact and severity
- Affected: replies whose images are rendered as alt text and whose alt contains Markdown, escapes or entities (README badges, generated charts).
- Severity: cosmetic; the alt reads with stray `**`, `_`, backslashes or `&`.
- Frequency: always, for that input.

issues.body:
**Summary**

With agents.entries.marv.heartbeat.isolatedSession: true, two failures recur in scheduled heartbeat runs on OpenClaw 2026.11.4:

1. Every heartbeat logs:

```
[plugins] [hooks] agent_end handler from active-memory failed: Plugin invocation scope is closed
```

The active-memory plugin is configured for agent jeeves only (plugins.entries.active-memory.config.agents: ["jeeves"]), yet its agent_end hook runs and fails on marv heartbeat sessions.

2. Intermittently the model calls heartbeat_respond and the runtime rejects it:

```
[tools] heartbeat_respond failed: heartbeat_respond is only accepted during a heartbeat run
```

The turn then ends incomplete and the heartbeat wake fails:

```
[agent/embedded] incomplete turn detected: ... provider=deepseek/deepseek-flash stopReason=stop hasLastAssistant=yes hasCurrentAttemptAssistant=yes payloads=1 tools=1 replaySafe=no compactions=0 ... surfacing error to user
[heartbeat] session event wake failed; no wake retry scheduled source=interval intent=scheduled agentId=marv wakeReason=interval error=agent-runner-failure
```

**Environment**

- OpenClaw 2026.11.4
- macOS 27.0.1 (arm64), Node 26.12.1
- Session: agent:marv:main:heartbeat
- Heartbeat config: { "every": "2h", "isolatedSession": true }
- active-memory: stock plugin, enabled; config { "agents": ["jeeves"], "allowedChatTypes": ["direct"], "persistTranscripts": false }

**Observed**

- Error 1 at each 2-hour heartbeat (examples: 2026-11-20 06:29, 08:29, 10:29, 12:29, 16:29, 18:29; 2026-11-24 06:29, 10:29, 14:29).
- Error 2 on 2026-11-18 10:38, 2026-11-19 12:29, 2026-11-24 16:29. The last one aborted the heartbeat with agent-runner-failure; consecutiveErrors: 1.

**Expected**

- The agent_end hook should either be skipped for heartbeat/isolated sessions or execute before the plugin invocation scope closes.
- heartbeat_respond should be accepted during a scheduled heartbeat run, including isolated heartbeat sessions.

**Impact**

Log noise every heartbeat, and occasionally a lost heartbeat wake. No data loss or incorrect actions observed.

**Related**

#203452 (same heartbeat_respond rejected → wake failed signature), #197940 (agent_end scope closed after dispatch_action).

issues.body:
A containerized Gateway that is hard-killed (SIGKILL, OOM kill) does not come back when Docker restarts the container: the restarted Gateway waits about 95 s and exits 1 at `cli.bootstrap.gateway-lock`:

```
cannot verify Gateway ownership … holder 1 at <host>/pid-ns 4026533702 … Run this command inside the Gateway container or with a shared PID namespace; if the holder has stopped, run `openclaw gateway recover-lock` …
```

**Observed** (2026-11-23, isolated Docker container, self-installed npm package, Gateway as PID 1, state on a volume; receipts in the maintainer's `update-rewrite/beta-gate/dead-owner-at-start/`): SIGKILL PID 1, then `docker start` (same as a restart policy). The new container has a new PID namespace; the lock records holder PID 1 in the old namespace, which this process cannot classify as dead, so startup refuses (`src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.ts` `GatewayLockNamespaceError`, `classifyGatewayLockProcessNamespace`). The same code is in v2026.11.7.

**Impact:** with `restart: unless-stopped`, an OOM-killed or force-killed Gateway container stays down until someone runs `openclaw gateway recover-lock` by hand. The refusal protects against two containers sharing one state volume, but a restarted container of the same deployment hits it too.

**Related:** #196846, #202040 (other PID-namespace refusals in containers). Found while proving the update fix in #203925, which cannot prove its container case because the Gateway never starts.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In the Control UI Customize sidebar, the `Installed` section truncates the list at 8 entries and applies sidebar-only exclusion filters that hide installed plugins (including active external plugins past position 8 and bundled plugins listed in `Plugins → Settings → Installed`), and its shared scroll container does not recompute scroll-fade classes when a deferred `plugins.list` response grows the list past the viewport height.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run Control UI from `main` (`2e3e081c2e4`) in a short desktop viewport (for example `1280×480`).
2. Return a `plugins.list` inventory with more than 8 installed external plugins (for example 9 external plugins where an active plugin such as Lossless Claw sorts 9th by `installedAt`), bundled installed plugins (some without `sidebar: true` or disabled), and at least one uninstalled catalog-only plugin (`installed: false`).
3. Open a plugin detail route under the Customize sidebar (for example `/plugins/acme/shopify`) and inspect the `Installed` list in the sidebar.
4. Compare the entries shown in Customize → `Installed` against `Plugins → Settings → Installed`.
5. Repeat with a delayed `plugins.list` response (for example `250–500 ms`) in a viewport where the loaded Customize list overflows `.sidebar-shell__body` (`scrollHeight > clientHeight`), and inspect the scroll-fade modifier class on `.sidebar-shell__body` before scrolling.

### Expected behavior

- Customize → `Installed` lists the complete set of installed plugins returned by `plugins.list`, matching the inclusion rule of `Plugins → Settings → Installed` (`plugin.installed === true`) and excluding catalog-only entries (`installed: false`).
- Consistent with `docs/plugins/manifest/surfaces.md` ("Plugins installed from outside OpenClaw always appear") and the `Installed` heading, active installed plugins beyond the 8th entry are never silently dropped.
- Existing sort order (external plugins newest `installedAt` first, then bundled plugins, then alphabetical by `name`), selected-row highlight (`aria-current="page"`), icon retention across updates, and keyboard navigation (`Tab` / `Shift+Tab` + `Enter`) remain intact.
- When the list exceeds viewport height, it scrolls vertically inside the existing `.sidebar-shell__body` container (the same scroll pattern as the Sessions list, with the `Customize` panel header and left navigation rail remaining pinned and accessible), updates its `.sidebar-shell__body--scroll-*` fade state immediately when deferred `plugins.list` content lands, and adds no unnecessary vertical scroll for short lists.

### Actual behavior

Verified on `main` (`2e3e081c2e4`) via bundled Playwright Chromium E2E against `ui/src/pages/plugins/plugins-customize-sidebar.e2e.test.ts`:

1. **Silent truncation at 8 entries:** With 13 installed plugins (9 external + 4 bundled) and 1 catalog-only entry (`installed: false`), Customize → `Installed` renders only 8 rows and omits the 9th active external plugin (`Lossless Claw`) as well as the remaining entries.
2. **Inclusion mismatch with `Plugins → Settings → Installed`:** With 10 installed plugins (4 external + 6 bundled) and 1 catalog-only entry, Customize → `Installed` renders only 6 rows, omitting installed bundled plugins without `sidebar: true` (`Anthropic`, `ClawRouter`, `OpenClaw Memory`) and disabled bundled plugins (`Diffs`) that appear under `Plugins → Settings → Installed`.
3. **Stale scroll-fade state on deferred load:** In a `1280×340` viewport with a `500 ms` delayed `plugins.list` response, `.sidebar-shell__body` starts at `scrollHeight: 288, clientHeight: 288` (`sidebar-shell__body--scroll-none`) and after `plugins.list` resolves grows to `scrollHeight: 420, clientHeight: 288` (`overflow: 132`) while keeping `sidebar-shell__body--scroll-none` until a manual scroll or viewport resize occurs.

### OpenClaw version

main (2e3e081c2e4)

### Operating system

macOS (arm64)

### Install method

Source checkout (Control UI bundled E2E / Playwright Chromium)

### Model

N/A (Control UI sidebar presentation)

### Provider / routing chain

N/A (Control UI Gateway RPC: plugins.list)

### Logs

```text
FAIL ui-e2e-bundled ui/src/pages/plugins/plugins-customize-sidebar.e2e.test.ts:228 > lists every installed plugin in order, excludes catalog-only items, and keeps selection across Customize pages
AssertionError: expected [ Array(6) ] to deeply equal [ Array(10) ]

- Expected
+ Received

  [
    "Shopify AI Toolkit",
    "Linear",
    "Lobster Theme",
    "Zulu",
-   "Anthropic",
-   "ClawRouter",
-   "Diffs",
    "Knowledge",
-   "OpenClaw Memory",
    "Workboard",
  ]

FAIL ui-e2e-bundled ui/src/pages/plugins/plugins-customize-sidebar.e2e.test.ts:268 > scrolls long installed lists in a short window, keeps header and rail accessible, and reaches 9th and last plugins by scroll and keyboard
AssertionError: expected [ Array(8) ] to deeply equal [ 'Shopify AI Toolkit', …(12) ]

- Expected
+ Received

@@ -5,11 +5,6 @@
    "Figma",
    "Notion",
    "Stripe",
    "Vercel",
    "Lobster Theme",
-   "Lossless Claw",
-   "Anthropic",
-   "Diffs",
-   "Knowledge",
-   "Workboard",
  ]

# Delayed plugins.list probe (viewport 1280x340, methodDelays: { "plugins.list": 500 }):
WHILE_PENDING: {"cls":"sidebar-shell__body sidebar-shell__body--scroll-none","sh":288,"ch":288}
AFTER_RESOLVE: {"cls":"sidebar-shell__body sidebar-shell__body--scroll-none","sh":420,"ch":288,"overflow":132}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- Observed on `main` `2e3e081c2e4` in Chromium (`1280×480`) with synthetic `plugins.list` fixture (9 external installed plugins + 4 bundled installed plugins + 1 catalog-only `installed: false` plugin): sidebar stops at row 8 (`Lobster Theme`) with `scrollHeight: 428, clientHeight: 428` and no scroll affordance; row 9 (`Lossless Claw`) and bundled rows are absent.
- Source inspection confirms the exact boundaries:
  - `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-customize.tsx`: `MAX_SIDEBAR_PLUGINS = 8`, `.slice(0, MAX_SIDEBAR_PLUGINS)`, and sidebar-only filter `Boolean(plugin.catalogId) && (plugin.origin !== "bundled" || (plugin.enabled && plugin.sidebar === true))`.
  - `ui/src/pages/plugins/settings-inventory.tsx`: `InstalledInventory` filters only on `plugin.installed` (plus optional user search).
  - `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-owner.tsx` & `ui/src/components/scroll-state-observer.ts`: `.sidebar-shell__body` already provides the shared vertical scrollport, pinned panel header (`SidebarCustomizeHeader`), and rail, but `observeScrollState` only attaches `ResizeObserver` to `.sidebar-shell__body` itself rather than content growth inside lazy/deferred views.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Any Control UI user with more than 8 installed plugins, or anyone expecting Customize → `Installed` to reflect all installed plugins shown in `Plugins → Settings → Installed`.
- Severity: Medium (UX / discoverability defect).
- Frequency: Always once installed count exceeds 8 or includes non-opted-in/disabled bundled plugins.
- Consequence: Active installed plugins silently disappear from the sidebar `Installed` list without any overflow indicator, and delayed inventory loads omit the scroll fade affordance until the user manually scrolls or resizes.

### Additional information

**Related PRs / history:**
- #201220 (`b9cffaedf01`) introduced the Customize sidebar plugin list with `MAX_SIDEBAR_PLUGINS = 8` and the bundled `enabled && sidebar === true` filter as a curated shortcut list; `docs/plugins/manifest/surfaces.md` simultaneously stated that external plugins always appear.
- #201792 (`ea749009e96`) moved inventory loading to `createDeferred` so route transitions stay responsive while `plugins.list` refreshes.
- #203214 (`344366a60c1`) stabilized plugin icon retention across inventory updates.
- #109694 (`9d3389008d1`) established `.sidebar-shell__body` as the single shared sidebar scroller with pinned panel header and fade masks.

**Proposed fix scope & compatibility note:**
1. Remove `MAX_SIDEBAR_PLUGINS = 8` and sidebar-only bundled/`catalogId` exclusions in `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-customize.tsx` so inclusion matches `Plugins → Settings → Installed` (`plugin.installed === true`, never catalog-only `installed: false`), preserving current ordering, active highlight, icon caching, and falling back to `pathForPluginSettings` if `catalogId` is omitted.
2. Reuse `.sidebar-shell__body` directly (no nested scroller, no new CSS or DOM wrappers); lift `SidebarScrollContext` to wrap the `<Switch>` inside `.sidebar-shell__body` in `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-owner.tsx` and expose an `observeContent()` `ResizeObserver` ref in `ui/src/components/sidebar-context-controller.ts` so deferred `plugins.list` growth/shrink immediately updates `.sidebar-shell__body--scroll-*` fades.
3. Preserve `catalog.sidebar` in manifest/protocol schemas for compatibility and update its description in `docs/plugins/manifest/surfaces.md`.
4. Add E2E regressions for >8 installed plugins in a short viewport (verifying 9th and last entries, scroll, keyboard `Tab`+`Enter`, pinned header/rail, delayed fade update, and short-list no-scroll) plus a unit test for `createSidebarScroll.observeContent()`.

*(Note: removing the bundled opt-in filter is an intentional shift from #201220's curated shortcut subset to a complete installed inventory matching the `Installed` label and Settings inventory; `plugins.list` backend feature-visibility filtering such as `idFeatureVisible` remains unchanged and shared by both views.)*

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (update never completes; Gateway stays down)

### Summary

On a Linux npm-global install, `openclaw update` to **2026.11.10 (6ea542f)** stopped the Gateway and then sat in the final step. The `update-migrated-finalize.worker` process ran for 81 minutes at about 100% of one CPU core without finishing or reporting an error. A stack sample showed it re-loading the full config for a policy check, again and again. The operator stopped the worker by hand; the Gateway then came up on 2026.11.10, and the update record is left as `failed` / `update-recovery-pending`.

### Environment

- Update from 2026.11.8 to 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), per the update run record (before.version / target.version)
- Ubuntu, Linux 6.8.0-147-generic x64, Node v26.13.1
- npm global install (`~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw`), Gateway as a systemd user service
- Multi-agent host (about a dozen agents, several created from templates), large config

### Timeline (2026-11-25, Pacific time)

| Time | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 10:01 | Update run requested; staging, candidate admission (all checks ok), candidate doctor (exit 0) follow |
| 10:17 | validating step ends; Gateway goes down for the update |
| 10:54 | `update-migrated-finalize.worker` starts |
| 10:54 to 12:15 | Worker runs at ~100% CPU, no completion, no error |
| 12:15 | Operator stops the worker by hand; run record updated to failed / update-recovery-pending |
| 12:18 | Gateway ready on 2026.11.10 |

Gateway downtime: about 2 hours. Worker runtime before it was stopped: 81 minutes.

### Stack sample

Sampled while the worker was spinning. Frames as reported by the operator who took the sample (innermost last):

```
assertRollbackOwned / checkAuthority
  -> readCurrentConfigForPolicyCheck
    -> loadConfig
```

Repeated samples showed the same path: the full config being loaded again for the policy check each time, under the rollback-ownership / authority assertion. It looks like the authority check re-reads and re-parses the whole config on every call instead of once per run, and the finalize step calls it in a loop (or retries it) without a bound.

### Expected

The finalize step completes, or fails within a bounded time with an error, and the Gateway is restarted either way. The config is read once for the policy check, not once per assertion.

### Actual

- The worker never finished and never timed out. Nothing stopped it for 81 minutes until an operator did.
- The Gateway stayed down for the whole time.
- After the worker was stopped, the Gateway started normally on 2026.11.10.
- `openclaw update status` records the run as `failed` with `update-recovery-pending`.
- The 11.10 state migration had already rewritten 8 template-created agents before the hang, so the host was left migrated but with a failed update record.

### Related, but not the same

- #198218: maintenance livelock with the Gateway stopped, but there the update-run admission reader re-hashes the state DB. Here the hot path is config loading under `assertRollbackOwned` / `checkAuthority` in the migrated finalize worker.
- #181662 and #164800: long Gateway-down windows during update activation / after Doctor, without this stack.
- #205167: `update-recovery-pending` on pnpm with a lost plugin lifecycle lease; different cause, and this host uses npm.

### Requests

1. Cache the config for the policy check within one finalize run (or otherwise bound the re-reads).
2. Give the migrated finalize worker a wall-clock limit, after which it fails the step and lets the Gateway restart.
3. Say whether `openclaw update repair` is safe to run on a host in this state (worker killed mid-finalize, migration already applied, Gateway healthy on the new version).

I can provide more detail from the host (update run record, logs around 10:17 to 12:18) on request.

### Summary

Upgrading from `2026.11.3 (847611d)` to `2026.11.10 (6ea542f)` hits a **100% circular deadlock** when `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` has malformed FTS5 inverted indexes (`main.memory_index_chunks_fts`, `main.session_transcript_fts`):

1. `openclaw update repair` and `openclaw doctor --fix` both fail at `Doctor: database migrations` during pre-migration SQLite snapshotting because `quick_check` flags the malformed FTS5 inverted indexes — **before** reaching Doctor's FTS5 repair (`classifySqliteFtsIntegrityFindings`), and their error message tells the user to run `openclaw doctor --fix`.
2. Running the dedicated FTS/session recovery command `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover` fails immediately because `state/openclaw.sqlite` has a pending client-credentials schema migration and refuses to run until `openclaw doctor --fix` completes it.

Neither command can run first. (Related to closed #180904 and open #200922 / #205182.)

### Environment

- OS: Linux x64 (Ubuntu)
- Node: v26.12.1 (bundled SQLite 3.54.0)
- Install: npm-global
- Source version: `2026.11.3 (847611d)` → Target version: `2026.11.10 (6ea542f)`
- Gateway & Node services: **stopped** (0 processes holding any `*.sqlite*` file open)
- Database sizes: `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` ~10.45 GiB (schema v27), `state/openclaw.sqlite` ~295 MiB

### Exact Sequence & Observed Errors

All commands were executed offline with Gateway and Node stopped:

1. **`openclaw update repair --yes --json --timeout 3600 --no-restart`** (rc=1 after 427.5 s in `database-migrations`):
   ```
   Doctor: schema admission
   Doctor: state database repair
   Doctor: database migrations (423s elapsed)
   Doctor: maintenance finish
   Doctor could not complete maintenance. Check the reported service state and resolve the failure.
   SQLite database cannot be snapshotted safely: ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.
   SQLite quick_check failed for ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite:
     malformed inverted index for FTS5 table main.memory_index_chunks_fts;
     malformed inverted index for FTS5 table main.session_transcript_fts.
   Stop the Gateway, run "openclaw doctor --fix" to inspect and repair this database, and restart.
   ```

2. **`openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions`** (rc=1 after 670 s `Preserve original state` + 60 s `database preflight` + 441 s `database migrations`):
   - Failed with the **exact same** `SQLite database cannot be snapshotted safely` / `malformed inverted index for FTS5 table` error, pointing back at `openclaw doctor --fix` without ever reaching `classifySqliteFtsIntegrityFindings()` FTS5 repair.

3. **`openclaw doctor --session-sqlite inspect --session-sqlite-agent main --session-sqlite-store ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json --json`** (rc=0):
   - Succeeded with `issues: []`, `sqliteEntries: 1958` (note: required `--session-sqlite-store` because retired `heartbeat` keys caused `cli_error` without it; noted in #200224).

4. **`openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover --session-sqlite-agent main --session-sqlite-store ~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json --non-interactive`** (rc=1 immediately, with `TMPDIR`/`XDG_CACHE_HOME` on a volume with sufficient space):
   ```
   [state/db] state database schema migration pending; verifying integrity first
   Client credentials require backed-up migration custody; stop the app and run openclaw doctor --fix.
   ```

At this point, the only supported recovery on `2026.11.10` was a full package downgrade to `2026.11.3` and cold-state restore.

### Expected Behavior

One (or both) of the following should break the circular dependency:

1. In `openclaw doctor --fix` / `openclaw update repair`: when `quick_check` returns **only** FTS5 inverted-index findings recognized by `classifySqliteFtsIntegrityFindings()`, do not abort the pre-migration snapshot with `SQLite database cannot be snapshotted safely`; either rebuild the derived FTS5 indexes before snapshotting/migrating, or allow the snapshot to proceed and rebuild FTS5 after migration.
2. In `openclaw doctor --session-sqlite recover`: repairing an offline agent SQLite database's FTS5 indexes should not be blocked by a pending `state/openclaw.sqlite` client-credentials migration.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

Yes

### Summary

Upgrading from 2026.9.6 to 2026.11.10 leaves the gateway unable to start. The
startup state upgrade copies the whole state directory, then the migration
chain stops at agent-schema reporting "schema 23 after the chain, expected
42", and the CLI exits 1 with "no such module: vec0". The sqlite-vec
extension itself loads fine on the same Node runtime and the same dylib when
tested directly, which points at the database being opened without extension
loading enabled on the upgrade path rather than at a missing or broken
extension.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a working 2026.9.6 install on macOS arm64, npm global, started by
   launchd, with existing agent databases at schema 23.
2. npm i -g openclaw@2026.11.10
3. Start the gateway (launchd, or `openclaw gateway` in the foreground).

Observed on both paths. Under launchd with KeepAlive the failure repeats:
17 runs, each one copying the state directory again.

### Expected behavior

The state upgrade completes, the agent schema reaches 42, and the gateway
starts. If the migration needs the sqlite-vec extension, the databases it
migrates should be opened with extension loading enabled.

### Actual behavior

Foreground run, 2026.11.10, install scripts allowed:

  [state/upgrade] State upgrade copying 16,884,907,953 bytes in 72,112 files
  State upgrade chain failed at agent-schema:
    <agent db> is at schema 23 after the chain, expected 42
  The CLI command failed. Reason: no such module: vec0
  exit code 1 after 237.7 s

Under launchd (KeepAlive true, ThrottleInterval 10) the same failure repeated
17 times; the repeated state copies consumed roughly 10 GB of disk and the
gateway log reached 1.05 GB before I unloaded the job. The staging
directories removed themselves on each failure.

What I ruled out:

- The extension is present and not quarantined.
  node_modules/sqlite-vec-darwin-arm64/.../vec0.dylib exists; xattr shows no
  com.apple.quarantine.
- The extension loads on this runtime. Loading it directly with node:sqlite
  succeeds on both Node versions on this host:
    node v24.21.0 (the version launchd uses): vec_version = v0.1.9
    node v26.8.2:                             vec_version = v0.1.9
- npm install scripts are not the cause. The first attempt ran under a local
  allowScripts policy that had blocked openclaw's
  postinstall-bundled-plugins.mjs. I retried with
  --allow-scripts=@google/genai,koffi,protobufjs,openclaw; openclaw's
  postinstall then ran (only esbuild@0.28.2 remained blocked) and the failure
  was byte-for-byte the same.
- Config validation is not the cause. The gateway's config guard passed in
  160 ms on this config.

Where I think this is, from reading dist (version 2026.11.10):

- The chain runs from dist/state-upgrade-startup-Df6wFsxK.mjs. That module
  imports OPENCLAW_AGENT_SCHEMA_SQL from dist/openclaw-agent-schema-*.mjs,
  OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION / OPENCLAW_AGENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, and
  dist/sqlite-database-admission-BVeAafOy.mjs, which is the module that
  defines the extension-capability gate:
    function supportsNodeSqliteExtensionLoading() {
      requireNodeSqlite(); return extensionLoadingSupported }
- `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ... USING vec0(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  embedding FLOAT[...])` appears in three modules, one of them under state/:
    dist/state/openclaw-state-read-openclaw-agent-write-admission-Cp6Uaj7U.mjs
    dist/sqlite-memory-search-fragments-B7DKjnT5.mjs
    dist/config/sessions/transcript-sqlite-search-schema-BjgT_xlF.mjs
  It does not appear in openclaw-agent-schema-*.mjs itself, so I cannot say
  which step of the chain issues the statement.
- allowExtension is passed inconsistently at the database open sites:
    dist/local-repository-ChfeZU3d.mjs:9          allowExtension: true
    dist/openclaw-agent-db-DrRnlTfH.mjs:9         allowExtension: <variable>
    dist/infra/database-engine/sqlite-vector.child.js:3
      allowExtension: supportsNodeSqliteExtensionLoading()

  If the upgrade path reaches openclaw-agent-db with allowExtension false, or
  if supportsNodeSqliteExtensionLoading() returns false in that context, a
  `USING vec0` statement in the 23 -> 42 chain fails with exactly this error
  while a direct load of the same extension succeeds.

I could not confirm which of those two it is from the bundled output, nor
which migration step issues the vec0 statement.

Secondary observation: the reported copy size is inconsistent between
attempts for the same state directory. The first attempt reported
~4.3 GB in 72,006 files; the retry reported 16,884,907,953 bytes in
72,112 files. du on the state directory gives ~4.05 GiB. Same file count,
roughly four times the bytes.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10 (fails to start). Working version on the same host: 2026.9.6

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (arm64)

### Install method

npm global (npm i -g openclaw), started by launchd with --max-old-space-size=8192. Node v24.21.0 (homebrew node@24). Also reproduced by running `openclaw gateway` in the foreground with the launchd job unloaded.

### Model

Not model-specific; the gateway exits before serving any request. Providers configured: openai, google, anthropic.

### Provider / routing chain

Not model-specific; the gateway exits before serving any request. Providers configured: openai, google, anthropic.

### Additional provider/model setup details

9 agents are configured, each with its own agent directory and workspace
directory, so there are 9 agent databases for the chain to migrate. The state
directory is about 4 GiB excluding caches.

No API keys, tokens or passwords are included here.

### Logs

```shell
Foreground run, 2026.11.10, install scripts allowed. Paths shortened,
agent names replaced with agent-1..agent-9.

  [state/upgrade] State upgrade copying 16,884,907,953 bytes in 72,112 files
  [state/upgrade] chain failed at agent-schema
  Error: ~/.openclaw/agents/agent-3/db.sqlite is at schema 23 after the
         chain, expected 42
  The CLI command failed. Reason: no such module: vec0
  (exit 1 after 237.7 s)

Direct extension load on the same host, same dylib:

  $ node -e "<open node:sqlite, enableLoadExtension(true), loadExtension(vec0),
             select vec_version()>"
  node v24.21.0  OK  vec_version = v0.1.9
  node v26.8.2   OK  vec_version = v0.1.9

Under launchd before I unloaded the job:

  runs = 17, last exit code = 1
  gateway.log reached 1.05 GB
  ~10 GB of disk consumed by repeated state copies

Full logs can be shared; they contain agent identifiers and local paths and
no credential values.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshots. Evidence is the foreground run output above, the launchd job
state, and the grep results from the installed 2026.11.10 dist quoted in
"Actual behavior". The 2026.11.10 dist is no longer installed on this host
(rolled back to 2026.9.6 to restore service), so I cannot run further
queries against it without upgrading again, which I am willing to do if that
would help.

### Impact and severity

Affected: macOS arm64, npm global install, 9 agents, agent databases at
  schema 23
Severity: High (the version cannot be installed at all; the gateway does not
  start)
Frequency: Always, on both launchd and foreground runs, with and without
  install scripts allowed
Consequence: the host stays on 2026.9.6. Under KeepAlive the retry loop
  consumes disk at roughly 4 GB per attempt and produced a 1 GB log in
  about 20 minutes.

### Additional information

I filed the catalog rebuild loop I am seeing on 2026.9.6 as a separate issue,
#205661, per the one-issue-per-submission rule. I attempted this upgrade partly
because 2026.11.10's notes mention keeping cached models available while
catalogs refresh in the background, which looked relevant to that issue.

If it is useful I can:
- reinstall 2026.11.10 and run any queries you want against the dist or the
  failing chain
- run the upgrade with the agent databases copied aside first
- test a patched build

I have not tried --allow-scripts=esbuild; esbuild@0.28.2 is the one
postinstall still blocked by the local policy. I do not think it is related,
since openclaw's own postinstall ran on the second attempt and changed
nothing, but I can test it.

issues.body:
**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10), Node 24.22.3, Linux x64, npm global install, systemd user service.

**Expected behavior**
With an explicit `plugins.allow` allowlist that does not contain `browser`, setting only a hardening key under `browser.*` (for example `browser.extensionRelay.allowLegacyAuth: false`, the value the lint check for legacy relay auth recommends) should not enable the bundled browser plugin. `doctor --fix --non-interactive` should leave an operator-authored allowlist unchanged, or at most report the mismatch.

**Observed behavior**
`OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` reports under "Doctor changes": `browser configured, enabled automatically.` and writes:
- `plugins.entries.browser = { "enabled": true }`
- `"browser"` appended to `plugins.allow`

After the next Gateway start the browser plugin is loaded (one more plugin in the "http server listening (N plugins: …)" line). Before the doctor run `openclaw plugins list` showed it as disabled.

**Minimal reproduction (synthetic config)**
1. Config with an explicit allowlist without the browser plugin, e.g. `plugins: { allow: ["whatsapp", "anthropic"], entries: { whatsapp: { enabled: true }, anthropic: { enabled: true } } }`.
2. Add only: `browser: { extensionRelay: { allowLegacyAuth: false } }`.
3. Stop the Gateway and run `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`.
4. Diff the config: `plugins.entries.browser.enabled: true` and `browser` in `plugins.allow` were added.

**Regression comparison with 2026.11.5**
Not established. On 2026.11.5 the same installation had no `browser` section when doctor last ran, so the auto-enable path was not exercised there. The config section was added between the two doctor runs.

**Sanitized messages**
`browser configured, enabled automatically.`

**Functional impact**
A security-hardening setting silently turns a previously disallowed bundled plugin on and edits an operator-maintained allowlist during a routine upgrade. In this case agent access stayed blocked only because `tools.deny` already listed the browser tool. Operators who rely on `plugins.allow` as the boundary get a wider plugin surface without asking for it.

**Suggestion**
Do not treat keys that only restrict a feature (such as `extensionRelay.allowLegacyAuth: false`) as "configured" for auto-enable, and never widen an explicit `plugins.allow` in non-interactive doctor runs; report it as a finding instead.

issues.body:
When the relay process of a running stream automation dies, the Gateway notices within seconds but marks the job `streamRestartExhausted` at once instead of restarting it with backoff. Re-enabling it does not help until the Gateway restarts, and every restart keeps it off. Nothing tells the user, so an unattended stream just stops.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A dead stream relay (`service-child-group-anchor`) is handled as a failed stop: the job goes terminal with `streamError: "stream source failed to stop: service child cleanup identity lost: anchor channel closed without a matching closing receipt"`, although no stop was requested and the source's process tree is already gone.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `cron.triggers.enabled: true`. Add a stream job whose source prints a line every 2 s: `openclaw automations add --name probe --stream-command '["/tmp/feeder.sh"]' --stream-mode match --stream-match '^\{' --system-event probe` (`feeder.sh`: `while :; do echo '{}'; sleep 2; done`).
2. **(a) mid-run:** `kill -9` the source's parent `service-child-group-anchor.js` process. Wait 20 s, check `openclaw cron list --json`. Then `openclaw automations disable <id>` and `enable <id>`, check again.
3. **(b) at shutdown:** re-enable after a Gateway restart, `kill -9` the anchor again and stop the Gateway right away. Start it and check the job.

### Expected behavior

The source has gone away while running, so it restarts with the built-in error backoff, as [schedules.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dce3c298384/docs/automation/cron-jobs/schedules.md?plain=1#L188) describes for fast failures, or at least re-enabling the job clears the cap ("manually re-enable the job to clear the restart cap"). If it must stay off, a failure alert says so.

### Actual behavior

| Step | 2026.11.6 | main dce3c29 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (a) +20 s after the relay dies | `streamStatus: error`, `streamRestartExhausted: true`, source gone | same |
| (a) disable + enable | still exhausted (`cron-stream: post-commit lifecycle routing failed`) | same |
| (a) after a Gateway restart | still exhausted; `enable` now works | same |
| (b) after a Gateway restart | stopped with `[shutdown] … identity lost`, still exhausted | same (shutdown "completed with warnings: cron") |
| control: relay frozen with SIGSTOP, then stop/start | stream restarts | — |

No failure alert or run notice reached the owner in any case.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (98d2780) and main dce3c29 (`src/gateway/cron-stream-*` and `src/process/supervisor/` unchanged up to 39c3099). First seen on 2026.11.5.

### Operating system

Linux x64, Node 26.13.1

### Install method

npm global; Gateway as a systemd user service (KillMode=mixed)

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not model-related)

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (not provider-related)

### Additional provider/model setup details

none

### Logs

```
cron-stream: supervised wait failed  err="service child cleanup identity lost: anchor channel closed without a matching closing receipt"
cron: job run returned error status   error="stream source failed to stop: service child cleanup identity lost: …"
cron-stream: owner operation failed   operation="process-exited"
cron-stream: post-commit lifecycle routing failed   (on the later enable)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Disposable test gateways (stubbed models, no channels), repro script in the details below. Production occurrence: a progress-message stream stayed off for ~3.5 h after a Gateway stop logged `service child cleanup did not complete before its hard deadline` and `identity lost: write EPIPE`, through three later restarts.

### Impact and severity

Medium: unattended stream automations stop silently and need a person to notice, restart the Gateway and re-enable them.

### Additional information

Question for a maintainer, since the fail-closed behavior looks deliberate (98742bc, #112387): should a relay death whose descendants are gone use the normal restart budget, and should `enable` recover a stuck owner without a Gateway restart? Related: #172918 (same terminal state from matcher timeouts, closed by the stale bot while awaiting this decision), #196765 (stdin-EOF EPIPE no longer loses identity; doesn't cover this path), #144336, #162194.

<details><summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

**Code path** (main dce3c29):

- `processExited` treats any `waitForExtinction`/`releaseHostScope` error as terminal and calls `stopOperation("restart-exhausted", …, "stream source extinction is unconfirmed")`, bypassing the `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES` backoff: [`cron-stream-job-owner.ts:257`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dce3c298384/src/gateway/cron-stream-job-owner.ts#L257).
- The failed stop persists `streamRestartExhausted: true` and leaves the owner in `stopping`: [`cron-stream-job-owner.ts:614-622`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dce3c298384/src/gateway/cron-stream-job-owner.ts#L614-L622). A later `enable` resets the durable state (`resetJobFailureState`), but routing it to the same owner reruns the stop, which fails again on the lost identity and re-persists the flag.
- A fresh Gateway reads the persisted flag and never spawns: [`cron-stream-job-owner.ts:189`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dce3c298384/src/gateway/cron-stream-job-owner.ts#L189). Only `enable` on the new process clears it, and that spawns without any extinction proof, so after a restart the flag only waits for a human.
- `server-cron.stream-lifecycle.test.ts` pins "clears its error only after confirmed cleanup" within one process; nothing covers a relay that dies on its own.

**Repro script** (run against a disposable gateway; finds the source via the unit's cgroup):

```sh
F=<pid of feeder.sh>; A=$(ps -o ppid= -p $F)   # service-child-group-anchor.js
kill -9 $A; sleep 20; openclaw cron list --json   # (a)
openclaw automations disable $ID; openclaw automations enable $ID; sleep 8; openclaw cron list --json
kill -9 $A; <stop Gateway>; <start Gateway>; openclaw cron list --json   # (b)
```

In every run the source process was already gone after the relay died (no orphan), so restarting would not have duplicated it here. A frozen (SIGSTOPped) relay does not fail the stop: the forced SIGKILL settles it.

Machine-specific details (paths, host name, job names) are left out; none matter to the bug.

</details>

issues.body:
# Knowledge plugin: Control UI panel is not registered (v2026.11.10) and tools only appear after a later restart

## Summary

On OpenClaw **2026.11.10 (6ea542f)** on Windows, selecting the bundled `knowledge` plugin as the memory provider activates the plugin and registers its 38 tools, but:

1. The first activation (slot switch, hot reload) exposes **zero** `knowledge_*` tools to sessions until `plugins.allow` is updated **and** the Gateway is restarted.
2. The Control UI Knowledge panel is never registered: `/plugin?plugin=knowledge&p.agent=main` renders “Plugin panel unavailable / The plugin behind this tab is not enabled on the connected Gateway, or does not provide a panel.”, even after a restart with `knowledge` present in `plugins.allow`.

This makes the documented **Settings → Stores & sharing → Conversation access** grant unreachable, which is required to let scheduled/unattended sessions read the owner-private store.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), Windows 10.0.26200, node v26.12.1
- Memory provider: `plugins.slots.memory = "knowledge"`
- `plugins.allow` includes `knowledge` (added after the first attempt)
- Config entry: `plugins.entries.knowledge = { enabled: true, config: { operatorRead: true, writesEnabled: true } }`

## Observed

```
openclaw plugins inspect knowledge --runtime
  CLI status: loaded
  Gateway status: active
  Tools: knowledge_* (38)
  httpRoutes: 0

openclaw plugins list --json  (knowledge entry)
  { "enabled": true, "status": "loaded", "httpRoutes": 0 }
  (no UI / panel field)
```

- Immediately after switching the slot and letting the plugin hot-reload, new sessions had **0** `knowledge_*` tools while `plugins inspect … --runtime` reported `activated=true`.
  - Adding `knowledge` to `plugins.allow` and restarting made the 38 tools available.
- Control UI still shows “Plugin panel unavailable” on the correct Gateway origin, in the same authenticated tab, after that restart.
- Because the panel is missing, `Conversation access` cannot be granted.
- Without that grant, a scheduled agent turn in a bound session reports:
  `{"scope":"conversation:<id>","records":0}` from `knowledge_status`, while an interactive owner turn on the same Gateway reports 244+ records. `knowledge_relink` there scans 0 claims.

## Expected

- Selecting the memory slot should expose the plugin’s tools to new sessions without requiring an allow-list edit, or the hot-reload path should refresh the session tool catalog.
- The bundled Knowledge plugin should register its Control UI panel so **Settings → Stores & sharing → Conversation access** is reachable.
- Scheduled turns routed to an owner conversation should use the owner-private partition (or the docs should state the required grant explicitly for cron/automation sessions).

## Notes

- Docs (`docs/plugins/knowledge.md`) state that a bundled memory plugin selected by `plugins.slots.memory` is enabled even when `plugins.allow` does not list it. In practice the allow-list gate blocked tool injection in this build.
- Docs also state slot changes “reload the plugin runtime without a Gateway restart”, but the session tool catalog did not pick up the new tools until a restart.
- Happy to run further diagnostics if useful; the store itself is healthy (SQLite integrity ok, 500+ records, git-backed vault).

issues.body:
## Who is affected

You installed OpenClaw with pnpm, you reached 2026.11.10 (or 2026.11.10-beta.3) by running `openclaw update`, and you then run `openclaw update` again to a release with the same database schema.

- **Today:** pnpm installs that went from 2026.11.10-beta.3 to the final 2026.11.10 with `openclaw update`.
- **From the next release on:** every pnpm install that got 2026.11.10 through `openclaw update`, on its first update to 2026.11.11.

Not affected:
- npm installs.
- A pnpm install where 2026.11.10 was put there with `pnpm add -g openclaw` and has not been updated since. That one updates cleanly, once.
- The update to 2026.11.10 itself from 2026.11.9. It exited 0 in three runs.

Measured on Linux with the Gateway as a systemd user service, pnpm 12.23.0, and the published 2026.11.9, 2026.11.10-beta.3 and 2026.11.10 packages. It behaves the same on macOS (27.2, arm64, the Gateway as a launchd LaunchAgent, pnpm 12.23.0), from the failure through the repair. The 2026.11.11 targets were local builds of the `release/2026.11.11` branch, because that release is not published yet.

## How to tell

- `openclaw update` ends with an error (exit code 1):

  ```
  ⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: update-recovery-pending.
  First failure: plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global was lost; retry the operation | OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST | Cannot find module …
  Run `openclaw update repair` to finish this recovery.
  ```
- The new version is installed anyway. `openclaw --version` prints it and the Gateway is running it. The Gateway was down for 67 to 79 seconds on Linux and about 103 seconds on macOS during the update.
- `openclaw update status` says "needs attention" and keeps saying so. In our run it did not change in 17 minutes.
- Running `openclaw update` again is refused: "has unfinished recovery; reconcile it before starting another update". We saw this on a 2026.11.11 build, within two seconds.

Nothing is lost. What is wrong is the record of the update, and it blocks the next one.

## How to fix it

Run this once, as the same user that runs OpenClaw. You do not need to stop the Gateway first:

```
openclaw update repair
```

It took 59 to 71 seconds in our runs on Linux and macOS and restarts the Gateway once (46 to 54 seconds down). Afterwards `openclaw update` works again.

Things to know:
- **Waiting does not help.** The status text says the Gateway will reconcile the update. It did not in our runs.
- **You can ignore the other suggestions** in `openclaw update status` and in the refused update (`openclaw gateway stop --force`, `openclaw update cleanup --dry-run`, `openclaw triage`). We did not need them, and we did not test them.
- **The status stays noisy.** After the repair, `openclaw update status` still lists the failed update as "unresolved after a failed update" and suggests inspecting a `manifest.json`. Later updates worked regardless. The failed update's capture stays on disk, about twice the size of your databases. `openclaw update cleanup --dry-run` lists it as protected, so there is nothing to clean up by hand.

## Cause

The update is run by the version you already have installed. When that version was itself installed by an update, pnpm keeps it in a folder that the next update moves away while the updater is still running. Two background workers of the updater then cannot find their own files, the update loses a lock it needs to finish its bookkeeping, and it reports failure after the new version is already running.

## Fix status

#205078 fixes the updater for the 2026.11.11 line. It was merged into `release/2026.11.11` on November 26 as `3d1e4fff043`, before any 2026.11.11 beta or tag. No published release contains it yet. The same fix is already on `main` (#203458) and on the `release/2026.11.15` branch.

The fix cannot reach the update that fails: that one is run by the 2026.11.10 you already have. What we measured:

- **With the fix in 2026.11.11:** the update to it fails once as described. After `openclaw update repair`, the next update exits 0.
- **Without the fix in 2026.11.11:** the update fails again on every release that has the same database schema, each time needing the repair.
- **A release that changes the database schema** is not affected. From the published 2026.11.10, an update to a build of the `release/2026.11.15` branch exited 0.

Not tested: Windows, Bun installs, 2026.11.10-beta.1 and beta.2 as the installed version, and updates started from the Gateway (Control UI or automatic) instead of the command line.

The earlier pnpm problem on 2026.11.7 to 2026.11.9 is #204836. The wider update work is tracked in #204775.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a successful dev-channel Git upgrade, Doctor reported that it could not migrate inference accounts for automations because the `cursor-cli` plugin source was not prepared. This is the Cursor automation case, distinct from the DeepSeek activation rollback in #203442.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed once; not independently reproduced:

1. Start with a Git installation on OpenClaw 2026.11.5 with existing automation state that reaches the `cursor-cli` provider during Doctor's inference-account migration.
2. Perform the managed dev-channel update to the 2026.11.10 tree at `2cb81bbb`.
3. Inspect the completed updater report for automation migration warnings.

The minimum automation and plugin configuration needed to reproduce has not been isolated.

### Expected behavior

Doctor prepares the provider source before inspecting the saved automation account, so it can evaluate migration eligibility. If account ownership cannot be verified, it should still leave the binding unchanged and report that reason.

### Actual behavior

The upgrade completed; the Gateway booted and passed HTTP/core readiness. The updater receipt contained eight occurrences of the Cursor source-preparation warning. The warning indicates that those migration attempts were skipped; subsequent automation execution was not tested.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.5 (`e474acd`) → 2026.11.10 (`2cb81bbb`)

### Operating system

Debian 13 x86_64, systemd user service

### Install method

Managed dev-channel Git upgrade; Node.js 26.13.0

### Model

Not isolated; observed in Doctor migration, not a model call.

### Provider / routing chain

Doctor automation inference-account migration → `cursor-cli` provider source preparation. No inference call was exercised.

### Logs

Sanitized excerpt from the updater's completion receipt:

```text
Automation <redacted>: inference account was not migrated: Plugin cursor-cli Doctor source must be prepared before loading
```

### Impact and severity

Doctor skipped automation account migration checks while the update itself succeeded. No Gateway failure or post-upgrade job failure was established.

### Additional information

The activated Git commit contains the merge of #204122, which addressed the same error class for official npm provider plugins. The updater receipt doesn't establish which Doctor build or phase emitted these warnings, so this is not proof that #204122 regressed or that its scope includes Cursor. It would be useful to identify which Doctor pass emitted this warning and whether it needs to prepare the Cursor source before checking these bindings.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Regression / update blocker

### Summary
`openclaw update --yes --json` from 2026.11.9 → 2026.11.10 (macOS arm64, npm global install, SQLite state ~1.3 GiB, 5 agent databases at schema 38) fails in `validating` → `candidate-doctor`:

```
Failed: candidate-doctor — Exit code: 1
Failing check plugin-doctor-post-session-state (blocked-by-session-repair-failure):
  Post-session plugin repair was blocked because prerequisite session repair failed:
  Error: cannot read legacy session store [redacted-path]
Failing check update (doctor-failed)
Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue.
```

The updater rolls back cleanly: the gateway keeps running on 2026.11.9 and never stops.

The throw is `onUnreadable` in `migrateLegacyMainSessionKeysInternal` (`legacy-main-session-migration-*.mjs`). In `doctor-fix` mode any store that `readClaimsFromStores` can't read aborts the whole Doctor, and the diagnostics redact the only identifying detail (the store path and the underlying error), so the operator can't tell which store it was.

### Relevant candidate-doctor stderr just before the failure (sanitized)
```
[state/agent-db] agent database integrity gate for <agent-A>: reason=no-proof, mode=deferred, outcome=pending
[state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: verification-missing; agent=<agent-A>
Session recovery warning: ... Retired terminal unmatched legacy restart custody (original state backed up).   (x2)
Session SQLite: Canonicalized entry state for 2 durable session row(s).
```
`<agent-A>` is the default (sole configured) agent, the only agent DB without a `.seal` sidecar, and the one with live WAL. Also present: a stray pre-migration state root nested inside that agent's dir (`agents/<agent-A>/agent/state/openclaw.sqlite`, user_version 17, plus `agents/<agent-A>/agent/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`) from an old run. Either could be the "unreadable" store. The 2026.11.9 `doctor --lint --all` reports no session-store findings.

### Expected
- Either skip or preserve unreadable or held stores (as `selectSessionStoreMaintenanceTargets` already does for held stores, cf. #172259), or report the failing store path and error class unredacted in the update report so it can be fixed.
- `doctor --lint` on the installed version should be able to surface the same finding before an update attempt.

### Related
#172259 (closed; same family: the legacy-main scan opens DBs that the earlier repair skipped).

### Environment
2026.11.9 (0032b1d) → 2026.11.10, macOS 27.0.1 arm64, node 26.12.1, npm global install, stable channel.

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

**Beta release blocker:** No

> Edited 2026-11-24 after deeper audits. Corrected: where the root-level files came from (not the Workshop), where the error escapes (before the `try`, not through the `catch`), body sizes, `remove_file` behavior on `SKILL.md`, and the full impact (undo/restore). The mechanism itself is unchanged.

**Summary**
The Skill Workshop daily maintenance fails for an agent with `workshop maintenance failed: Support file paths must be under one of: assets, examples, references, scripts, templates.` The skill diet selects a learned skill whose `SKILL.md` body is over 12,000 bytes. `dietWorkshopSkill` calls `readSupportMarkdown(…, files)` **before** its `try` block. That reads every non-`SKILL.md` Markdown file returned by `listSkillFiles`, including root-level files such as `<skill>/notes-a.md`. `readSkillFile` → `normalizeSkillFilePath` → `normalizeWorkspaceSkillSupportPath` rejects them with `SkillAuthoringError(invalid_path)`. The error never reaches the diet's skip handler, which also only skips `SkillDietRejected` and `WorkshopWriteError`, and the whole maintenance run fails. `listSkillFiles` lists files that `readSkillFile` refuses.

**Steps to reproduce**
Minimal case, with no history needed:
1. One learned skill in `~/.openclaw/agents/<agent>/agent/workshop-skills/<skill>/` with standard frontmatter, a body of at least 12,001 bytes, all file mtimes older than a day, and one root-level `notes.md`.
2. skill-workshop enabled with autonomous mode `auto` (the default here) and `skill_workshop` allowed for the agent.
3. Let the agent finish a turn. Maintenance is scheduled after a turn, at most once per 24 hours per agent per process.

**Expected behavior**
Skip that skill with a log line naming the skill and the file, and finish maintenance.

**Actual behavior**
Real instance on agent `chat`: two eligible skills, with `SKILL.md` of 12.9 KB and 19.5 KB (bodies 12.7 KB and 19.1 KB) and 4 and 3 root-level `.md` files. Both rotation choices hit the invalid support path, so the diet phase aborts whenever it selects either affected oversized skill (observed on 2026-11-22, 2026-11-23, and 2026-11-24):
```
2026-11-24T15:29:10.921Z INFO {"subsystem":"agent/cli-backend"} cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=146853 ...
2026-11-24T15:29:10.955Z WARN {"plugin":"skill-workshop"} workshop maintenance failed: Support file paths must be under one of: assets, examples, references, scripts, templates.
```
The same warning (then from `skills/workshop`) appears at 2026-11-22T22:36:24.520Z (2026.11.6) and 2026-11-23T23:25:50.725Z (2026.11.7). No diet model call is made before the failure on the failing path.

**Also affected (verified in code and on disk):**
- Every archived version of the three skills with root-level files contains them (9/9, 3/3, 1/1). `readRestorableVersion` rejects any non-`SKILL.md` file that fails `normalizeSkillFilePath`, so restore/undo of all 13 versions fails.
- `view`, `patch` and `remove_file` fail when the target is a root-level file, so the Workshop cannot move or remove these files. `view` and `patch` still work on `SKILL.md` and allowed support paths; `remove_file` accepts allowed support files only (`SKILL.md` is rejected by design in `removeWorkshopSkillFile`).

**Where the files came from (correction).** The root-level files were created on 2026-10-17…19, before any Workshop history of these skills: the earliest archive snapshot, from 2026-10-27, already contains them. The Workshop writer has rejected such paths since at least 2026.10.3, so they were most likely written outside the Workshop (agent file tools or a manual edit). Exact origin unknown.

**OpenClaw version:** 2026.11.10-beta.3 (3d2d379); same failure on 2026.11.6 and 2026.11.7 since the diet was introduced (#186861)

**Operating system:** macOS 27.2.1 (arm64), Node 26.13.0

**Install method:** npm global, launchd Gateway

**Model:** anthropic/claude-opus-5-5

**Provider / routing chain:** openclaw -> claude-cli runtime -> Anthropic

**Additional provider/model setup details**
N/A

**Logs**
See above.

**Screenshots, recordings, and evidence**
`extensions/skill-workshop/src/skill-diet.ts` at v2026.11.10-beta.3: `readSupportMarkdown` runs before the `try` (around lines 453 vs 470), and `catch` (around 511) handles only `SkillDietRejected` and `WorkshopWriteError`. `selectSkillForDiet`: `candidates[floor(now / DAY_MS) % candidates.length]`. The same code is on main.

**Impact and severity**
Low. No data loss, but the diet aborts whenever it selects either affected oversized skill, the warning names neither the skill nor the file, and the Workshop cannot repair, undo or restore these skills.

**Additional information**
Related: #186861 (diet), #192471 (moved to plugin), #150367 (support-path rules elsewhere). Since moving files would require relinking (including cross-skill links like `../<other-skill>/notes.md`), a safe skip that names the file is the lower-risk fix.

issues.body:
### Summary

`openclaw plugins doctor` reports five first-party plugins using OpenClaw APIs whose declared
retirement date has already passed, and the notice is still written as if the date were in the
future: *"Uses OpenClaw APIs that retire on Sep 30, 2026. It keeps working until then; check for a
plugin update."*

```
Compatibility:
- groq     Uses OpenClaw APIs that retire on Sep 30, 2026. It keeps working until then; check for a plugin update. [info]
- moonshot Uses OpenClaw APIs that retire on Sep 30, 2026. ... [info]
- qwen     Uses OpenClaw APIs that retire on Sep 30, 2026. ... [info]
- tavily   Uses OpenClaw APIs that retire on Oct 1, 2026. ... [info]
- whatsapp Uses OpenClaw APIs that retire on Oct 1, 2026. ... [info]
```

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.5 (7e15622), Linux (WSL2, arm64), Node 24.22.2
- Affected: the plugin compatibility registry, and the five shipped plugin packages
  (`@openclaw/{groq,moonshot,qwen}-provider`, `@openclaw/tavily-plugin`, `@openclaw/whatsapp`),
  all installed at 2026.10.10-beta.5

### Reproduction

1. `openclaw plugins doctor` (or `openclaw status --all`, which shows the same blocks).

### Expected behaviour

Past the removal date, either the surface is removed (and the plugin fails to load, loudly), or the
notice says it is overdue and names who must act. A plugin update should not be suggested when the
newest published build is the one carrying the call.

### Actual behaviour

Two registry records are `status: "removal-pending"` with `removeAfter` dates now in the past:

- `media-understanding` subpath — `removeAfter: "2026-09-30"` — replacement
  `api.registerMediaUnderstandingProvider(...)` plus `openclaw/plugin-sdk/plugin-entry`, with the
  note "retain the public subpath through the 2026-09-30 window while official plugin consumers
  migrate". groq, moonshot and qwen are media-understanding providers and still import the subpath.
- `media-legacy-projection` — `removeAfter: "2026-10-01"` — replacement is ordered
  `MsgContext.media` / `InboundMediaFacts[]`; tavily and whatsapp still read the legacy projection.

`buildPluginSdkDeprecationNotices()` has no branch for "the date has passed" — it always renders
"retire on `<date>`. It keeps working until then."

### Why this is not fixable locally

`npm view @openclaw/groq-provider dist-tags` returns `beta: 2026.10.10-beta.5` — the exact installed
version — and `latest: 2026.10.9`, an older channel. The same holds for the other four (all
inspected, all beta.5), and `openclaw plugins update --all` reports them up to date.

### Impact

No functional loss today: the facades are still present and every one of the five plugins loads.
The cost is a permanent, unfixable-looking warning in the compatibility section of `status`/`doctor`,
which teaches operators to ignore that section, and a migration that has silently slipped its own
documented deadline.

### Suggested fix

Any of: migrate the five packages' imports to the replacement surfaces; move the `removeAfter`
dates; or make the notice state that the surface is overdue and stop suggesting a plugin update when
the newest published build is the one carrying the call.

issues.title: Bug: gateway install replaces the resident launcher with a release-slot entry after conversion

labels.name: P2

issues.body:
## Problem

After an npm installation is converted to resident releases, `openclaw gateway install --force` can rewrite the native service to the serving slot's `dist/index.js` instead of `openclaw-launcher.mjs`. A service reinstall then silently drops the resident launcher and its rollback/ready-IPC owner.

## Observed Linux reproduction

AWS Crabbox run: https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_884b2280eacd6e200b8e337d2be67c35

1. Install published `2026.11.10`; install/start an isolated systemd user Gateway.
2. Use public `openclaw update --tag <head-package.tgz> --yes --json` to update to source `7f07553a09ec2443dbdddfdcde4c0000ec812115` (build `2026.11.10-07484900409e-2026-11-25T22-05-40.010Z`). Verified serving/ready.
3. Prepare a successor through `openclaw update --tag <successor.tgz> --no-restart --yes --json`. This creates the actual v2 pending trial, the release slot and format-4 launcher.
4. Reinstall with public `openclaw --profile manifest-proof-51143 gateway install --force --runtime node --port 25471`, then `gateway start`.

Actual `systemctl --user show ... -p ExecStart` (receipt `proof/022-failure-unit.stdout`):

```text
ExecStart={ path=/work/crabbox/cbx_ec78c3fc00cd/.crabbox-local-actions/crabbox-local-actions-cbx-ec78c3fc00cd-22077618f890512c/tmp/openclaw-node-v24.22.1-linux-x64/bin/node ; argv[]=/work/crabbox/cbx_ec78c3fc00cd/.crabbox-local-actions/crabbox-local-actions-cbx-ec78c3fc00cd-22077618f890512c/tmp/openclaw-node-v24.22.1-linux-x64/bin/node --max-old-space-size=8192 /home/crabbox/.openclaw-manifest-proof-51143/git-install/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port 25471 ; ignore_errors=no ; start_time=[Wed 2026-11-25 23:09:39 UTC] ; stop_time=[n/a] ; pid=63998 ; code=(null) ; status=0/0 }
```

Expected entry: `/home/crabbox/.openclaw-manifest-proof-51143/git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs`, never the slot's `dist/index.js` on a converted install.

The candidate migrated to schema43 and served HTTP, but the trial remained `phase: trial`, `attempts: 2`, with no ready-IPC commitment. No trial/slot/service result was fabricated. All paths and the token in this lane belong to a disposable isolated test profile; the native unit was stopped/uninstalled after capture.

## Scope

This is the service-entry/one-installer ownership class, not the manifest interpreter. Found while qualifying #205578; the existing public `gateway install --wrapper <actual-launcher>` is authorized only to pin that reader proof, not to hide this default-route bug. Fix the ordinary service selector and preserve explicit retained CLI recovery precedence. Main assigned UpdateOwner as the next item after #205578.

issues.body:
### Summary

On a Linux host running only the managed OpenClaw node service, a manual npm update installed the target version and exited 0. The final output said the Gateway restart was skipped, but the running node service retained its original PID and start time. A separate node restart was needed to load the new package.

### Environment

- Omarchy 4.5.0, Linux x86_64, system Node 26.12.0.
- Global npm package under a mise prefix, OpenClaw 2026.9.6 → 2026.11.10-beta.2 (bbcf2a4).
- Enabled systemd user service `openclaw-node.service` pointing into the same package via `dist/index.js node run`. It was connected to a separate Gateway. There was no local Gateway unit.

### Observed sequence

1. Record the node service's `MainPID` and active state, then run `openclaw update --channel beta --tag 2026.11.10-beta.2 --yes`.
2. The update exited 0 after 8m 51s. The CLI reported the beta version and updater status reported `finished / succeeded`. The output included `Gateway restart skipped: no Gateway service or listener is running.`
3. The node unit remained active with the same PID. After `systemctl --user restart openclaw-node.service`, it had a new PID and its journal confirmed reconnection to the Gateway.

### Expected behavior

When a running managed node uses the package being replaced, the update summary should explicitly identify that the node was left running and give the operator the correct restart command. If automatic node activation is intended for this path, it should honor the node's idle or drain rules.

The restarted node also logged that its legacy unit bypasses the launcher. That unit migration is covered by #175831 / #175860, which document `openclaw doctor --fix` for existing units. I did not run that repair, so this field report covers the manual update's service activation and reporting behavior.

issues.body:
### Summary

After a Control UI tab boots from its cached offline shell and reconnects to a Gateway with the Terminal enabled, opening the Terminal side panel can display `failed to load Ghostty WASM | Failed to fetch WASM: 404`. A manual reload after recovery is a workaround.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Load the Control UI so the service worker installs and caches its offline shell.
2. Navigate to the UI during a transient 503 or network failure so the worker serves the offline shell.
3. Restore the Gateway and let the UI refresh its config with `terminalEnabled: true`.
4. Open the Terminal side panel.

### Expected behavior

Reload into the live Gateway document before enabling Terminal, or keep Terminal disabled while unsaved work prevents a reload.

### Actual behavior and evidence

The offline shell deliberately uses a CSP without `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` but does not declare `data-openclaw-terminal-enabled="false"`. The config refresh reads a missing marker as unknown and skips its reload check, enabling Terminal on the existing document. Ghostty's embedded WASM cannot compile under this CSP, and its fallback asset fetches surface a 404.

A local Vitest regression reproduced the state transition using the service worker's actual 503 navigation fallback and the Control UI config refresh. Marking only the cached shell as terminal-disabled fixes the transition without changing CSP.

### Environment

Source build on Linux x64, based on `09c738a859b`. No model or provider involved.

issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary After `openclaw tui` is closed and reopened on a session, an assistant reply longer than 8,000 characters is shown cut off with `...(truncated)...`, although the full reply is stored and was shown in full before the TUI was closed. ### Steps to reproduce 1. `openclaw tui --session tidepool-test` 2. Send: `Write a plain essay of about 2,000 words on tide pools. No headings, no lists. End with the single line: THE END.` 3. When the reply has finished, scroll to its end. It ends with the `THE END` line. 4. `/exit`, then `openclaw tui --session tidepool-test` again. Scroll to the end of the same reply. ### Expected behavior The reopened TUI shows the same complete reply it showed in step 3. The Control UI does this for the same stored reply since #122207 (issue #95318). ### Actual behavior In step 4 the reply stops a little past character 8,000 and its last line is `...(truncated)...`. Nothing in the TUI indicates that more text exists. ### OpenClaw version 2026.11.5-beta.4 (2c173a3) ### Operating system Windows 11 x64 and Debian 13 aarch64 ### Install method npm global ### Model kimi-k2.6:cloud (Windows run) ### Provider / routing chain openclaw -> ollama -> kimi-k2.6:cloud (Windows run) ### Additional provider/model setup details _No response_ ### Logs ```shell The Gateway's two views of the same reply, from `openclaw gateway call chat.history` and `openclaw gateway call chat.message.get`: | | Windows 11 | Debian 13 aarch64 | | --- | --- | --- | | `chat.message.get` | 11,532 characters, ends `THE END` | 17,223 characters, ends `THE END.` | | `chat.history` row | 8,018 characters, ends `\n...(truncated)...` | 8,018 characters, same ending | | `chat.history` row `__openclaw` | `truncated: true`, `reason: "display-cap"` | the same | | Stop reason | `stop` | `stop` | 8,018 is the 8,000-character cap plus the 18-character marker. On Windows, the history text without the marker is exactly the first 8,000 characters of the stored text (3,532 characters hidden). On Debian the reply was written with `openclaw agent` and then opened with `openclaw tui --session tidepool-test`. ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence Reopened TUI (Windows), end of the reply. The text stops mid-sentence at "forest ecology", followed by `...(truncated)...`; the stored reply continues for another 3,532 characters to `THE END`. ### Impact and severity - Affected: `openclaw tui` users (Gateway mode) reading back a reply over 8,000 characters after reopening a session. - Severity: annoying; the stored reply is intact, but the TUI shows an incomplete one. - Frequency: every reopen observed (2 machines). - Consequence: the reply looks as if the model stopped early or the conversation lost text. ### Additional information Source on `main` at 054fd9788bc (unchanged from v2026.11.5-beta.4): - `src/tui/gateway-chat-requests.ts:136-140` sends `chat.history` with `sessionKey`, `agentId` and `limit` only, so the Gateway applies its default 8,000-character cap (`DEFAULT_CHAT_HISTORY_TEXT_MAX_CHARS`). - No file under `src/tui/` reads the `truncated` flag or calls `chat.message.get`. - `src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:458` calls `resolveEffectiveChatHistoryMaxChars()` with no argument, so `openclaw tui --local` should apply the same cap. Not tested. The docs describe two ways for a client to get the full text: per-request `maxChars` on `chat.history` (`docs/web/webchat.md`), or `chat.message.get` for one truncated entry (`docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-session-control.md`), which is what the Control UI does. I can prepare a PR; which route would you prefer for the TUI? Related: #95318 and #122207 (Control UI, fixed), #126229 (truncation flag), #122043 (Android).
