issues.body:
**Version:** v2026.11.10 (6ea542f), macOS 27.2.1 arm64, self-hosted Gateway
**Vision model:** `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-qat`, declared in `models.providers.ultra-local.models[]` with `input: ["text","image"]`, served by a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint

## Summary

In `prepareEmbeddedAttemptTransport`, the provider streaming handoff calls `materializeProviderContext` with neither `maxBytes` nor `maxDimensionPx`, so both fall back to the hardcoded defaults in `src/agents/image-sanitization.ts`:

```js
const DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION_PX = 1200;
const DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES = 5242880;
```

On this host `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx` was `2400` on disk from at least 03:35 until a hot reload at 21:18:33, yet the twelve traced `Image resized to fit limits` entries before that reload all logged `maxDimensionPx=1200`. After the reload set it to `4096`, the next traced entry still logged `1200`.

Two distinct source images — JPEGs at 854×1280 and 1000×1280, both well under 5 MB — were re-encoded into a larger payload.

Scope note: the other prompt-image callers do read `maxDimensionPx` from config (`prompt-image-preparation`, `context:assistant`, and the agent-harness and worker variants). Only the provider handoff omits both values, and only the CLI path omits `maxDimensionPx` while still passing `maxBytes`.

## Evidence from the log

Snapshot taken 2026-11-26 00:35 (+01:00). The 2026-11-25 log holds 20 `Image resized to fit limits` entries, but the same source repeats across turns, so the useful unit is the distinct source image. Deduplicating on `(sourceBytes, sourceWidth, sourceHeight, sourceMimeType)` leaves **9 distinct sources: 7 from Gateway traffic, 2 I generated myself offline**. The two synthetic ones are identified by their byte counts matching my repro inputs exactly; the log carries no source field, so that attribution is an inference.

Times are local (Europe/Berlin, +01:00); the log's `_meta.date` is UTC, so subtract one hour when grepping.

| source (w×h) | mime | src → out | delta | occurrences | traced | px / bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2470×1570 | png | 626210 → 145685 | -76.7% | 2 | 2 | 1200 / 5242880 |
| 1176×1740 | png | 868415 → 191905 | -77.9% | 3 | 3 | 1200 / 5242880 |
| 1162×1704 | png | 659289 → 195506 | -70.3% | 3 | 3 | 1200 / 5242880 |
| 1158×1202 | png | 493584 → 213093 | -56.8% | 2 | 2 | 1200 / 5242880 |
| 1054×1812 | png | 638027 → 174068 | -72.7% | 1 | 1 | 1200 / 5242880 |
| **1000×1280** | **jpeg** | **130790 → 198497** | **+51.8%** | **2** | **1** | 1200 / 5242880 |
| **854×1280** | **jpeg** | **226680 → 353095** | **+55.8%** | **2** | **1** | 1200 / 5242880 |

Excluded: the two synthetic 1400×1200 inputs (JPEG 37,278 → 47,601; PNG 7,178 → 47,953).

Of the 7 distinct production sources, 5 PNGs shrank and both JPEGs grew. Both growing sources appear twice; only one occurrence of each carries a `traceId`, and the untraced duplicates (22:01:51) are not used as evidence anywhere in this report. The image log entries carry no `pid` field (143 of the file's 184,765 lines have one, all in other subsystems), so I cannot attribute those duplicates to a process.

**Config timeline.** Backups on disk: `imageMaxDimensionPx` was `2400` at 03:35, at 11:48, and again in the pre-reload backup taken 21:18:30. It became `4096` at 21:18:33. So the twelve traced entries from 04:55:55 through 21:07:55 all ran while the configured value was 2400, and all logged 1200 — a 2470×1570 PNG should have been resized to 2400, not 1200. The entry at 21:33:05 then confirms the same behaviour at 4096. `tools.media.image` did not exist in config until 21:31:41.

Every one of the 20 entries logs `triggerOverDimensions: true` and `triggerOverBytes: false`.

## Attributing the traced entries to the provider path

`MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` is `6291456` in `constants-cCp4CBUF.mjs`. Every caller that passes it explicitly would log `maxBytes=6291456`; none of the 20 does. All log `5242880`. The prompt-image callers that do pass a byte limit — `prompt-image-preparation-BZ7h591w.mjs`, `context-media-runtime-CWPtH-4Q.mjs`, `agent-harness-runtime-D8E6Ejys.mjs` (`detectAndLoadAgentHarnessPromptImages`), `worker-turn-execution-Ck8wYKze.mjs`, `attempt-system-prompt-prepare-D_-oXLup.mjs`, and `helpers-Bg9O7o3B.mjs` (`loadCliPromptImages`) — all pass `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` (6291456). Only the provider handoff passes neither. I did not exhaustively enumerate every `5242880` literal in the bundle, so this narrows rather than proves the origin.

A second signal: the label is `prompt:images` on every entry. That string is a literal inside `detectAndLoadPromptImages` in `images-DArgDQKo.mjs`, not a caller-supplied value, so all these entries passed through that one function (`sanitizeImageBlocks([e.image], \`prompt:images\`, x)`).

## Root cause

`dist/images-DArgDQKo.mjs` → `detectAndLoadPromptImages(e)` forwards whatever it was given, so omitted keys stay omitted:

```js
const x = { maxBytes: e.maxBytes, maxDimensionPx: e.maxDimensionPx, verifyDecodability: true };
sanitizeImageBlocks([e.image], `prompt:images`, x);
```

`dist/tool-images-D8vogS6M.mjs` → `sanitizeContentBlocksImages` (exported as `n`; `sanitizeImageBlocks` is `r`) substitutes the defaults:

```js
const r = resolveIntegerOption(n.maxDimensionPx, DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION_PX, {min:1});
const i = resolveIntegerOption(n.maxBytes,        DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES,        {min:1});
```

The provider streaming handoff reaches this with neither key set. In `dist/attempt-D0eWH9Mj.mjs`, `prepareEmbeddedAttemptTransport`, the transform lambda is **passed to** `wrapStreamFnWithMessageTransform` (imported from `attempt-transcript-helpers-BEGc_WgE.mjs`):

```js
const T = wrapStreamFnWithMessageTransform(S, e => e, async ({context: n, ...r}) => {
  // r is { signal }; context was destructured out
  let i;
  const a = await materializeProviderContext({
    ...r,                    // no maxBytes, no maxDimensionPx
    context: n,
    imageSessionKey: promptImageSessionKey(t),
    workspaceDir: e.workspaceDir,
    agentWorkspaceDir: t.workspaceDir,
    workspaceOnly: e.workspaceOnly,
    localRoots: ...,
    onCurrentTurnImageFailure: e.onCurrentTurnImageFailure,
    sandbox: ...,
  });
  assertRunCurrent?.();
  return a;
});
```

`materializeProviderContext` forwards its argument into `materializePromptMediaMessages`, which calls `detectAndLoadPromptImages` with a spread copy — still missing both limits. `t.config` appears in this function's scope and in the sibling calls (`resolveImageSanitizationLimits` is what `prompt-image-preparation` uses), so threading the value should not need new plumbing — though I have not written or tested a patch.

## Second defect: the resize loop can return a larger payload

Inflation is only possible on the byte-untouched path. When `triggerOverBytes` is true the source exceeds `maxBytes`, so any accepted candidate is smaller than the source by construction. Both production inflations, and everything reported here, have `triggerOverBytes: false` — the resize was triggered by dimensions alone.

`imageWithinLimits` is the gate: metadata readable, under `maxBytes`, both sides within `maxDimensionPx`, under the 25 MP input cap.

```js
function imageWithinLimits(e,t,n,r,i){
  return t!==null && t.width>0 && t.height>0 && e.byteLength<=r
      && t.width<=n && t.height<=n && t.width*t.height<=i
}
```

When it fails, the side grid is built from `maxDimensionPx` (call it `r`) and the actual longest side `_ = min(r, longestSide)`:

```js
buildImageResizeSideGrid(e,t){return [t,1800,1600,1400,1200,1e3,800].map(t=>Math.min(e,t)).filter(...).toSorted((e,t)=>t-e)}
```

so the first candidate side is `min(maxDimensionPx, longestSide)` — equal to `maxDimensionPx` only when the image exceeds it. The loop then returns the first candidate under `maxBytes`:

```js
for (const e of v)                                                   // v = side grid, descending
  for (const t of c.IMAGE_REDUCE_QUALITY_STEPS) {                    // [85,75,65,55,45,35]
    const a = await c.resizeToJpeg({buffer:o, maxSide:e, quality:t, withoutEnlargement:true, maxInputPixels:l});
    if (S === void 0 || a.byteLength < S) S = a.byteLength;
    if (a.byteLength <= i) { /* log + return this candidate */ }
  }
```

`resizeToJpeg` re-encodes to JPEG regardless of input format. `o` is the source buffer and is never compared against `a.byteLength`. The grid starts at the largest permitted side and the quality ladder starts at 85, so when the first candidate already fits under `maxBytes` it is returned, and it can exceed the source length.

In production that happened to 2 of 7 sources — both JPEG — and none of the 5 PNGs. I have not measured enough inputs to say whether the JPEG/PNG split reflects format or just these particular files, so I treat format-independence as an inference from the two synthetic cases below rather than an established property:

| input (offline repro) | source | `{verifyDecodability:true}` | `{maxDimensionPx:4096, maxBytes:20971520, verifyDecodability:true}` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `solid-1400x1200-q85.jpg` | 37,278 | 47,601 (+27.7%) | 37,278 (byte-identical) |
| `solid-1400x1200.png` | 7,178 | 47,953 (+568.1%) | 7,178 (byte-identical) |

## Reproduction

**Offline.** Generate the two inputs with PIL:

```python
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
import io
shapes = [((200,60,60),(50,50,300,200)), ((60,160,90),(400,80,700,350)),
          ((70,90,200),(150,400,550,700)), ((220,200,60),(700,150,1100,500))]
def make(fmt, quality=None):
    im = Image.new('RGB', (1400,1200), (240,240,240))
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    for color, box in shapes:
        d.rectangle(box, fill=color)
    b = io.BytesIO()
    im.save(b, fmt, **({'quality': quality} if quality else {'optimize': True}))
    return b.getvalue()
open('solid-1400x1200-q85.jpg','wb').write(make('JPEG', 85))   # 37,278 bytes
open('solid-1400x1200.png','wb').write(make('PNG'))            # 7,178 bytes
```

Then call the sanitizer the way the provider handoff does. The import path below is specific to build 6ea542f (bundle filenames carry a content hash) and to this machine's Homebrew prefix; I executed only the dist version:

```js
import fs from "node:fs";
import { r as sanitizeImageBlocks } from "<openclaw>/dist/tool-images-D8vogS6M.mjs";

const src = fs.readFileSync("solid-1400x1200-q85.jpg");
const res = await sanitizeImageBlocks(
  [{type:"image", data: src.toString("base64"), mimeType:"image/jpeg"}],
  "prompt:images",
  { verifyDecodability: true }
);
const out = Buffer.from(res.images[0].data, "base64");
console.log(src.length, "->", out.length, res.images[0].mimeType);
```

Produces `Image resized to fit limits: 1400x1200px 36.4KB -> 46.5KB (+27.7%)` with `maxDimensionPx: 1200, maxBytes: 5242880`. Passing `{maxDimensionPx: 4096, maxBytes: 20971520, verifyDecodability: true}` returns the source byte-identical. Against `src/`, the equivalent entry point is `sanitizeImageBlocks` from `src/agents/tool-images.ts`; I have not run that variant.

**Through the Gateway** — not reproduced live, so this is the expected result rather than an observation. With `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx: 4096` applied and `openclaw config get agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx` returning `4096`, send a JPEG taller than 1200 px on any channel, then grep the log for `Image resized`. The entry is expected to report `maxDimensionPx: 1200` and `maxBytes: 5242880`.

## Expected behavior

1. The provider handoff should pass `resolveImageSanitizationLimits(t.config).maxDimensionPx` into `materializeProviderContext`, matching what `prompt-image-preparation` and `context:assistant` already do. The CLI path should do the same.
2. The resize loop should avoid returning a payload larger than its source where the constraints allow it. The source cannot always be kept — a 1400 px-wide source under a 1200 px limit must be re-encoded — so the realistic rule is to prefer, among candidates that satisfy `maxDimensionPx` and `maxBytes`, the one with the smallest byte length rather than the first that fits. I have not tested this against the two production cases.
3. Separately, `tools.media.image.maxBytes` does not reach these prompt-image callers: the handoff omits it and the others hardcode the 6 MB constant instead. Whether it *should* is unclear to me — `resolveMaxBytes` in `resolve-C57Befyo.mjs` reads `tools.media.<capability>.maxBytes` for media-understanding entries, but with a native-input model like this one, auto-detected image entries are skipped and images go to the model directly without passing that function. Raising it as an open question, not a defect claim.

## Impact

On this path, `imageMaxDimensionPx` had no effect at either 2400 or 4096. Of the 7 distinct production sources, 5 shrank as intended and 2 were re-encoded larger than their source.

## Related

- **#67031** — "media: hardcoded image size limits (bytes/input-pixels) are not user-configurable across sanitize layers". The reporter describes it in their own words as a companion request to the sandbox-only #40880 / #40950, and #41987 addresses the same `imageMaxDimensionPx` key at the `browser:screenshot` call site; none of the three is merged. #67031 was opened 2026-04-15, auto-marked stale 2026-06-03, and closed 2026-06-10 by the reporter (`closed_by: gucasbrg`) with `stateReason: COMPLETED` and no closing PR or commit. The gap described here survives in 2026.11.10, so I am filing separately and linking — if maintainers prefer, this can be folded into a reopened #67031.
- #25844 — `imageMaxDimensionPx` not applied to `optimizeImageToJpeg`; closed as not planned (auto-marked stale). Different function and module.
- #72193 — image size limits too restrictive for modern phone cameras; `stateReason: not_planned`, closing comment records it as a duplicate of #67031.
- #75742 — "Failed to optimize image" above the 1200 px default; `stateReason: not_planned`, closed as a duplicate of #73424 and #74243.
- #2954 — `tools.media.image.maxBytes` defined but not applied to inbound; closed as completed by a triage sweep rather than by a fix.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

### Summary

Updating 2026.11.6 → 2026.11.10 fails at the candidate-doctor step. The candidate Doctor's session repair throws "Agent database resources are closing", and the update aborts with doctor-failed. Happens every retry.

### Steps to reproduce

1. openclaw gateway stop
2. openclaw update --yes
3. Fails at validating → candidate-doctor (~42s) every time.

### Expected behavior

The update should complete, as on 2026.11.6 where "openclaw update repair" session-transcripts completes in 2.4s.

### Actual behavior

Failing check plugin-doctor-post-session-state (blocked-by-session-repair-failure):
Post-session plugin repair was blocked because prerequisite session repair failed:
Error: Agent database resources are closing: [redacted-path]

Doctor stopped because a state migration refused to continue.
Resolve the reported migration failure before retrying. Later repairs were not run.
Failing check update (doctor-failed)

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (updating to 2026.11.10)

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (arm64)

### Install method

npm, /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw, channel stable

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Additional provider/model setup details

Multi-agent: 5 agents (main, architect, dacai, homework-tutor, xiaoyan). Node.js: 24.22.1

### Logs

```shell
Failing check plugin-doctor-post-session-state (blocked-by-session-repair-failure):
Post-session plugin repair was blocked because prerequisite session repair failed:
Error: Agent database resources are closing: [redacted-path]

```

_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected users/systems: user updating 2026.11.6 → 2026.11.10 on macOS 27.2.1 (arm64) with 5 agents.
Severity: blocks workflow — update cannot complete.
Frequency: always, every retry.
Consequence: update aborts with doctor-failed at candidate-doctor (~42s).

### Additional information

Ruled out (not data / not processes):
- Gateway fully stopped before update → identical failure (the "still running" PIDs in the log are only the update process itself).
- openclaw doctor --session-sqlite inspect --session-sqlite-all-agents → 0 issues, 193 entries, 0 legacy.
- No renamed agents: all session_nodes.session_key match their agent id.

- openclaw doctor --fix on 2026.11.6 completes; its session-transcripts section runs ~2.4s, no error.

- 2026.11.6 "openclaw update repair" → session-transcripts completes in 2.4s.
- 2026.11.10 candidate-doctor → the same session repair throws "Agent database resources are closing".

### Bug type

Regression in Codex native isolated completions; remaining subscription-route branch of #196617.

### Summary

On a ChatGPT subscription route, internal utility sampling defaults make Codex native isolated completions require an owned inference relay. Relay preparation returns no route, so the request fails before `thread/start` with:

```text
Prepared Codex request requires an owned inference relay; no direct fallback was attempted.
```

Two consecutive failures disable session-observer assessments for the run. Activity recaps also defer, and generated conversation labels fail. Ordinary chat on another provider remains usable.

### Observed sequence

Evidence is from production Gateway logs, not an isolated repro.

- OpenClaw `2026.11.10-beta.1` (`995f905`), Codex plugin `2026.11.10-beta.1`, Linux x64, Node `26.12.1`, Control UI/WebChat.
- `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command` explicitly selects a Codex `0.171.0` binary over stdio; plugin startup reports `0.169.0` as its validated version. The failure occurs before native `thread/start`. I have not repeated it with the managed app-server.
- Utility configuration was Auto with `openai/gpt-6-luna` as its only fallback. Configured-model status shows OAuth profiles for OpenAI and no API-key or token profiles.
- `2026-11-22 14:56–15:43 UTC`: six Activity/observer failures with the exact relay error.
- `2026-11-23 01:57:56 UTC`: observer assessments disabled after two failures in a Telegram run.
- `2026-11-23 16:03:11 UTC`: Activity recap deferred with the same error.
- `2026-11-23 16:04:21 UTC`: observer assessments disabled after two failures in a dashboard run; the user received the system warning.
- `2026-11-23 16:05:08 UTC`: the automatic Anthropic candidate first failed with HTTP 429. The configured Luna fallback then failed with the relay error, and another dashboard run disabled assessments at `16:05:31 UTC`.

There are eleven exact relay-error records across the two daily logs. Session keys, run IDs, auth-profile IDs, credentials, and prompt contents are omitted here.

Sanitized excerpt:

```text
[gateway/session-observer] session observer disabled after consecutive failures
  consecutiveFailures=2
  error="Prepared Codex request requires an owned inference relay; no direct fallback was attempted."

[gateway/activity-summary] Activity recap deferred
  error="Prepared Codex request requires an owned inference relay; no direct fallback was attempted."

[model-fallback/decision] candidate_failed
  candidateModel=claude-haiku-5-5
  reason=rate_limit
  fallbackStepToModel=gpt-6-luna
```

The Anthropic 429 is a separate candidate failure, not the cause of the Codex relay error seen on the preceding day and runs.

### Why

The observer supplies internal utility defaults, including `answerTokenBudget: 300` and `streamParams: { temperature: 0.2 }`:

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.10-beta.2/src/gateway/session-observer-completion.ts#L145-L155

Codex treats either stream parameter as `hasStreamParams`, then sets `requireInferenceRoute` even when the selected auth route is a subscription rather than an API key:

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.10-beta.2/extensions/codex/src/app-server/isolated-completion.ts#L73-L103

The bounded turn throws when route preparation returns no owned inference route:

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.10-beta.2/extensions/codex/src/app-server/bounded-turn.ts#L290-L311

Correction after recheck: in this installation, the missing route is explained by the explicit app-server command. `shared-client.ts` registers relay ownership only when the stdio command source is `resolved-managed`. An explicitly configured command is labelled `config`, so the client is never registered, and `prepareCodexInferenceRoute` returns `undefined` because no owner exists. Ordinary Codex turns on the same configuration continue to work. Production logs begin on November 22; the first relay error appears after that day's command override, but earlier logs are unavailable, so I cannot prove that the managed binary succeeds here.

The closed, unmerged #196640 explicitly identified and addressed this subscription-default branch: internal utility sampling should be advisory instead of unnecessarily requiring an inference relay. The merged #196641 fixed API-key temperature compatibility at the shared model-capability boundary, but did not land that subscription-route handling.

### Release status

- Observed in production on `2026.11.10-beta.1` with an explicitly configured app-server command.
- The same failing lines are present in `2026.11.10-beta.2`, the current beta on npm.
- Current `main` at `3ff1109b0a666e1163fea47abc5d24afb80cda1e` retains the same `hasStreamParams` and `requireInferenceRoute` logic; the beta.1 and main copies of `isolated-completion.ts` were identical when checked.
- Latest stable `2026.11.7` uses the older isolated-completion shape without this `requireInferenceRoute` branch. That is not a fix for users on the beta/native host-authorized path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On the affected beta, set `plugins.entries.codex.config.appServer.command` to a local Codex binary over stdio, then select `openai/gpt-6-luna` as the utility model through the native Codex runtime and a ChatGPT subscription auth route.
2. Enable session observation and send a Control UI turn that produces observer notes. An Activity recap or generated conversation label exercises the same isolated-completion boundary.
3. Watch the Gateway log for the relay error. After two observer failures, the UI reports that assessments stopped for the run.

Control evidence from the same production Gateway: ordinary chat on a separate provider completes, and the automatic Anthropic utility candidate reaches its provider and returns HTTP 429 rather than the local relay error. No successful Codex subscription utility control is claimed.

### Expected

Internal observer/recap defaults should not force an owned relay on a route that cannot provide one, including an explicitly configured app-server command. If the relay is intentionally required, the failure should name the unsupported command source instead of reporting a generic missing relay. The selected native model should complete without forwarding unsupported sampling requirements, while explicit caller limits retain their strict contract. A model-specific failure should then be eligible for the configured utility fallback instead of repeatedly disabling assessments.

### Suggested direction

Recover the subscription/advisory-default portion of #196640 rather than requiring users to move to API-key auth. Keep API-key endpoint ownership and explicit-limit validation intact, and add a regression that drives an actual observer or recap completion through a ChatGPT subscription route with internal sampling defaults. Verify that no inference relay is required and that the utility result is returned.

### Related

- #177227 introduced host-authorized native isolated completions and the owned-relay requirement.
- #196617 reported the Luna utility regression and was closed by the narrower API-key temperature fix.
- #196640 contained the broader subscription-route repair but closed unmerged.
- #196641 merged the API-key temperature filtering only.
- #196344 proposes advisory observer sampling for ChatGPT token sharing.
- #189508 is a different Codex observer failure caused by model-discovery timeouts.

AI-assisted: investigated and drafted with Claude Opus through OpenClaw from production logs and released source. No isolated Gateway or managed-app-server reproduction was performed.

issues.body:
I want my team’s agent to post follow-ups on GitHub using the same Gateway-held bot account it uses to open PRs. I checked `main` at `8b17822bec4`. `create_issue` already files in the conversation’s registered repository, and `request_review` posts the fixed `@clawsweeper re-review` comment. `publish` already updates an eligible PR from its publishing conversation. The missing action is posting an ordinary issue or PR comment. [Issue creation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203369) · [Current publication behavior](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b17822bec4f36582bf5e15743087b32fd3460b1/docs/gateway/config-tools/github-identity.md#L187)

I’d add `create_comment` with an issue or PR number and a Markdown body. I’d have the Gateway derive the repository from the conversation’s registered project, require operator approval of the exact target and text, and recheck current access and the selected publisher before posting. The Gateway should return the comment URL and record who approved it, which account posted it, the target, and the outcome without logging the body or credential. If GitHub’s response is lost, report the result as unconfirmed so the operator can check the thread before retrying.

I’d reuse the existing bot credential and keep it outside agent execution. For source updates, I’d continue using `publish` from the original conversation so the Gateway retains its existing checks on the recorded PR and head branch.

issues.body:
**Bug type:** Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Summary
`knowledge_grep` returns 0 hits for a Chinese or Japanese word that sits inside a longer CJK sentence, and for Latin tokens glued to CJK text (e.g. `NAS` in `按NAS方式`), even though the record is indexed. The keyword corpus is created in `extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.ts` with `tokenize='unicode61 remove_diacritics 2'`. unicode61 does not segment CJK, so every unbroken run of Han/kana characters becomes a single token. `docs/plugins/knowledge/retrieval.md` already notes that "unsegmented CJK substrings may not match". In practice this makes `knowledge_grep` unusable for Chinese and Japanese vaults. (`recall-keyword.ts` tokenizes the same way for automatic-recall triggers; that is a separate follow-up and out of scope here.) The same class of bug was fixed for `sessions_search` (#140736, #186583) and is being worked on for memory-core (#170997, #193815). Knowledge still has it.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Select Knowledge as the memory provider (`plugins.slots.memory: "knowledge"`).
2. Save a page whose body is `客户希望地理位置在新加坡，出网流量单价按100G计价。共享存储先按NAS方式配置10TB。`
3. `knowledge_grep({query: "新加坡"})` → 0 hits. The same happens with `出网流量`, `补贴` and `NAS`.
4. `knowledge_grep({query: "苏林"})` matches only when the name is surrounded by spaces or punctuation in the stored text.

## Expected behavior
A CJK word that appears in a record is found: exact substring semantics for the CJK part in `all`/`phrase` modes, with BM25 ranking, as already happens for space-delimited languages.

## Actual behavior
0 hits unless the stored text happens to put spaces or punctuation around the word.

## Evidence (real meeting notes, 348 passages, 60 LLM-generated queries + 300 random substrings)
| Index | keyword `any` hit@5 | question `any` hit@1 | exact-substring recall | false hits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| current unicode61 | 0.18 | 0.00 | 0.066 | 0 |
| trigram | 0.70 | 0.00 | 0.368 | 0 |
| CJK unigram | 0.90 | 0.53 | 1.000 | 2 |
| **CJK bigram** | **0.92** | 0.55 | **1.000** | **0** |
| Intl.Segmenter words | 0.90 | 0.63 | 0.698 | 2 |

Ranking differences between the CJK-aware options are within noise. Dictionary segmentation (Intl.Segmenter/ICU) loses about 30% of exact substrings because the same word segments differently in different contexts. Trigram cannot match two-character words. node:sqlite cannot register custom FTS5 tokenizers (see #193815).

## Proposed fix (happy to send the PR)
- Before inserting into the keyword corpus, expand each Han/Hiragana/Katakana run into overlapping character bigrams, and also keep each run's last character as a unigram, so every character starts some token and single-character queries keep 100% recall. Hangul and other scripts are unchanged.
- Apply the same expansion to queries. In `all`/`phrase` modes a CJK term becomes a phrase of adjacent bigrams, which gives exact-substring semantics. In `any` mode it becomes an OR of bigrams.
- Keep stored text, hashes and line citations verbatim. Map highlight offsets back to the original text so snippets stay exact.
- Bump the keyword table version (`keyword_fts_v1_*` → `v2_*`) so existing stores rebuild automatically through the existing untracked-table path.
- Zero new dependencies, CPU-only string work. Expanding CJK text for the index runs at about 17 MB/s in Node (27 KB of Chinese in ~1.6 ms); a filtered search over 200 selected Chinese records costs ~160 ms, and the index grows about 2.3× for CJK text only. Non-CJK text is unchanged.
- Because the highlight budget applies to the indexed text, CJK bodies lose exact snippet location at a smaller original size unless the budget is measured on the original text; the PR measures that budget on stored bytes instead, which keeps the same token-count bound as Latin text.
- Changes the keyword index schema, so I'd like a maintainer ack on the approach before the PR lands.

## OpenClaw version
2026.11.9 (0032b1d)

## Operating system
Ubuntu 22.04 (Linux 6.8, x64), Node 24.22.1

## Install method
npm global

## Impact and severity
Affected: every Chinese/Japanese Knowledge user. Severity: high for those users, because keyword recall is the main entry point besides exact lookup. Frequency: deterministic. Consequence: agents conclude "no relevant record" for facts that are stored.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
On `main` (`107c145f25d0`), a cron job with `sessionTarget: "session:<key>"` ends its turn after its first `message`-tool send to its delivery target when `final` is omitted, while an isolated job with the same delivery target continues.

### Steps to reproduce
1. QA Lab from a source checkout: `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --channel-driver crabline --channel telegram`, default `replyToMode`.
2. Open a Telegram DM, then add two cron jobs with `delivery: { mode: "announce", channel: "telegram", to: <that DM> }`: one with `sessionTarget: "isolated"`, one with `sessionTarget: "session:<that DM's session key>"`.
3. Force-run each job. The scripted model sends two messages to the DM with the `message` tool, `final` omitted, then replies `NO_REPLY`.

### Expected behavior
Both jobs send both messages. The delivery docs state, without naming a session target, that "A send to the delivery target does not end the job's turn unless it sets `final: true`, so steps after the send, such as updating a state file, still run." (`docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`). If this rule is meant for isolated jobs only, the docs should say so.

### Actual behavior
| job | message-tool sends | Telegram received | run status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sessionTarget: "isolated"` | 2 | 2 | `ok` |
| `sessionTarget: "session:<dm key>"` | 1 (no model call after the first send) | 1 | `ok` |

### OpenClaw version
`main` at `107c145f25d0` (source checkout)

### Operating system
macOS 15.5 (arm64), Node 26.5.0

### Install method
Source checkout (pnpm)

### Model
QA Lab mock-openai (scripted turns)

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> QA Lab mock-openai

### Logs
Bot API calls recorded by Crabline (job sends only):

    isolated:  sendMessage "QA-SESSION-MULTI-SEND-1", sendMessage "QA-SESSION-MULTI-SEND-2"
    session:   sendMessage "QA-SESSION-MULTI-SEND-1"

### Impact and severity
A conversation-targeted job that posts a result and then continues (posts more results or updates its state) stops after the first send, and the run still records `ok`. Deterministic with the scripted model: 2/2 runs.

### Additional information
Only the isolated-run executor sets `messageToolFinalByDefault` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts`); it serves `isolated` and `current` jobs. A `session:<key>` job runs as a session event through the reply pipeline, so it keeps the chat default. #176141 landed while `session:<key>` jobs still ran on the detached executor; #178764 moved them to the session controller on 2026-10-21 without carrying `messageToolFinalByDefault`. The existing `qa/scenarios/scheduling/cron-send-then-continue.yaml` only covers `sessionTarget: isolated`. Related: #193481 (the chat default). Not the same as #204148/#204149 (a send batched with other tool calls in one step): here each step makes only the send. If the cron rule is meant to cover these jobs, giving scheduled session-event turns the cron plan's `finalByDefault: false` would leave chat turns unchanged; I can open that PR.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On an explicit multi-agent gateway, `openclaw message send --media` fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner. Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId.` even though the account binding resolves correctly and the text part of the same command would send fine. The failure occurs only when `--media` is supplied; text-only sends with identical flags succeed. No CLI flag exists to pass an agentId/agent-scoped session key through to the gateway's outbound media-staging resolver, and no config-level owner satisfies that code path.

This looks like the same class of bug as #186392 (iOS share attachment path resolves the agent from a raw/non-agent-scoped session key instead of the canonical one), but on the `message send` CLI → gateway outbound media path. I searched for an existing report of this exact surface and could not find one.

### Steps to reproduce

- OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10), npm global install, Linux arm64 (Raspberry Pi OS).
- Explicit multi-agent fleet: `agents.ownership: "explicit"` with 7 agents (`portfolio-guardian`, `sql`, `lead-scout`, `gmail-cleanup`, `ai-news`, `health-monitor`, plus a `default` Telegram account), each bound to its own Telegram bot account via `bindings[].match.accountId`.
- `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` set to `portfolio-guardian`.

1. Text-only send — succeeds:
   ```
   openclaw message send --channel telegram --account portfolio-guardian --target 6938637819 --message "test"
   ```
2. Same command plus a local media file that lives inside the bound agent's own workspace:
   ```
   openclaw message send --channel telegram --account portfolio-guardian --target 6938637819 --message "test chart" --media ~/.openclaw/workspace-portfolio-guardian/staging/test_chart.png
   ```
   → fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError` (verbatim below).

### Expected behavior

With a valid `--account` whose binding unambiguously resolves to a single configured agent (the verbose log shows this resolution succeeding before the failure), outbound media staging should use that same resolved agentId, as it presumably does for text-only sends.

### Actual behavior

```
[routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=telegram accountId=portfolio-guardian peer=direct:6938637819 guildId=none teamId=none bindings=1
[routing] binding: agentId=portfolio-guardian accountPattern=portfolio-guardian peer=none guildId=none teamId=none roles=0
[routing] match: matchedBy=binding.account agentId=portfolio-guardian
[routing] resolveAgentRoute: ... (second pass, also matches)
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner. Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId."
  }
}
```

Stack points at the gateway request path (`client-*.mjs` `GatewayClientRequestError`), i.e. the error is thrown gateway-side during media staging, not by CLI argument parsing. `--dry-run` with the same flags succeeds and echoes the correct `mediaUrls`, so the failure happens in the real send's session-agent resolution step.

### What I ruled out (no config workaround found)

- File location: fails identically for paths under `/mnt/...` (SMB mount), `/tmp`, and inside the bound agent's own workspace dir — not a media-root allowlist issue.
- `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId = portfolio-guardian`: already set; fixes CLI-owner resolution for other commands but does not affect this path (same finding as #186392: "systemAgent.agentId is not used on this path").
- `agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId = portfolio-guardian`: added, tested, still fails.
- Removing `agents.ownership: "explicit"`: rejected by config validation ("multi-agent rosters require agents.ownership=\"explicit\"..."), consistent with the note in #128637 that removing the flag is not a viable workaround.
- No `--agent` flag on `message send`, and no session-key flag either (`message send --help` has no session option), so there is no way to supply any of the three accepted owners (agentId / agent-scoped session key / fallbackAgentId) from this CLI surface.

Reading `resolveSessionAgentIdsStrict`/`resolveSelectedSessionAgentId` in `agent-scope-config`, the resolver accepts exactly those three owner sources; the outbound media path appears to pass none of them, falling through to `resolveDefaultAgentId`, which throws under explicit ownership with >1 agent.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.6 (06afb10)

### Operating system

Linux 6.18.60+rpt-rpi-2712 (arm64), Raspberry Pi OS

### Install method

npm global (~/.npm-global prefix)

### Model

Not model-specific; fails before any model call (CLI → gateway media staging).

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw CLI → gateway WebSocket → telegram channel plugin (bot API)

### Additional provider/model setup details

No response

### Logs

```
AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but session agent resolution has no explicit owner. Pass an agentId, an agent-scoped session key, or a prepared fallbackAgentId.
GatewayClientRequestError
    at Object.createRequestError (file:///.../dist/client-cecYKgQa.mjs:1037:31)
    at GatewayPendingRequests.handleResponse (file:///.../dist/client-cecYKgQa.mjs:469:43)
    at GatewayProtocolClient.handleMessage (file:///.../dist/client-cecYKgQa.mjs:875:17)
```

### Impact and severity

Blocks our nightly portfolio report automation: charts are generated and the text report delivers, but chart attachments cannot be delivered from any cron/script context on a multi-agent gateway. 100% reproducible for `message send --media`; single-agent installs are unaffected (consistent with this being introduced by the explicit-ownership refactor in #114388).

### Additional information

Likely-related prior reports, all same error family:
- #186392 — iOS share attachment path resolves agent from raw session key (closest root-cause match)
- #145217 — sessions.compact ignores explicit agentId on global-keyed sessions
- #128637 — umbrella multi-agent `AgentSelectionRequiredError` report; confirms removing ownership flag is not a workaround
- #159334 / #159080 — channel default routing has no explicit owner

Suggested fix direction: thread the already-resolved binding agentId (visible in the verbose routing log) into the outbound media-staging session resolution, or accept an explicit `--agent` on `message send` and pass it through to the gateway request.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The prepared-model-catalog worker rebuilds continuously and never serves a
cache hit: over a 1h49m instrumented window on 2026.9.6 with 9 configured
agents it ran 2,944 rebuilds with 0 cache hits, while gateway RSS grew
~250 MB/min to 8.6 GB in ~25 minutes at 300-450% CPU.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure two or more agents that share the same model providers
   (observed with 9 agents and 3 providers: openai, google, anthropic).
2. Start the gateway normally (npm global install, launched by launchd).
3. Observe the catalog worker: it starts a new task roughly every 2 seconds
   with cacheHit false on every task, and worker utilisation stays near 77%.
4. Observe gateway RSS growing ~250 MB/min with no user activity.

Observed by instrumenting the catalog path and collecting 42,592 events over
1h49m. The fingerprint fields that differ from the last cached generation are
agentId (2,936/2,944), agentDir (2,936), workspaceDir (2,936) and authStore
(2,280), i.e. requests from different agents evict each other from a
single-entry cache.

### Expected behavior

The implementation's own cache implies far fewer rebuilds than observed. The
worker reuses a previous generation when
`previous?.fingerprint === value.generationFingerprint`
(dist/agents/prepared-model-catalog.worker.js:365), the catalog pool is
maxWorkers=1 (dist/prepared-model-catalog-worker-*.mjs:24,82), and the
provider TTL is 60 s. With 3 providers that implies on the order of a few
refreshes per minute, not ~27, and a non-zero cache hit rate once warm.

I have no known-good earlier version to cite: the normal logs predating this
observation are no longer on disk, so I cannot state a last-known-good
version. For that specific question: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Actual behavior

Over 1h49m with 9 configured agents and no user activity:

- 2,944 catalog worker tasks started; cacheHit was false on all 2,944.
- Requests were uniform across agents: 328 x7, 326, 322.
- 2,134 of 2,206 catalog acquisitions (96.7%) originated from the expiry
  path, scheduled via queueMicrotask from readFullModelCatalog
  (dist/prepared-model-runtime-*.mjs:250-259; expiry test at
  dist/prepared-model-runtime.full-catalog-*.mjs:133-134).
- 2,652 of 3,100 publications (85.5%) reported modelFactsChanged: false,
  yet each publication still drove an all-agents catalog read via the
  chat-metadata listener (dist/chat-metadata-runtime-*.mjs:56-69), returning
  to the expiry path. The loop is self-sustaining and bounded only by worker
  throughput.
- Provider expiry after a refresh was median 51.6 s, max 59.9 s, consistent
  with a 60,000 ms TTL. Expiry was detected a median of 10.7 s after it had
  already passed.
- Worker utilisation 77.1%; median task duration 1,628 ms, of which only the
  51 ms median generation build is attributed. The remaining ~1,577 ms is not
  attributed by my instrumentation (it covers provider fetch, auth,
  normalisation and teardown).
- Gateway RSS grew ~250 MB/min, reaching 8.6 GB in ~25 minutes at 300-450%
  CPU. Worker heap went 2.1 GiB to 3.2 GiB in 5 minutes.
- The gateway does not exit on its own; it has to be restarted externally
  every 15-20 minutes to stay usable.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6

### Operating system

macOS 27.2.1 (arm64)

### Install method

npm global (npm i -g openclaw), started by launchd with --max-old-space-size=8192

### Model

Not model-specific; the defect is in provider catalog discovery. Providers in use: openai, google, anthropic.

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> openai | google | anthropic (direct; no model router or proxy)

### Additional provider/model setup details

9 agents are configured, each with its own agent directory and workspace
directory. All of them resolve the same three providers. models.providers is
currently empty, so provider resolution happens through implicit discovery
(models.mode is not set to "replace").

The three providers each hardcode a 60,000 ms catalog TTL independently:
- openai: dist/openai-provider-*.mjs:29-30 (both API and Codex OAuth paths)
- google: dist/provider-catalog-runtime-*.mjs:9,59
- anthropic: dist/register.runtime-*.mjs:529-544, which calls the compat
  builder and uses the default at
  dist/provider-catalog-live-runtime-*.mjs:841
  (`ttlMs: params.modelDiscovery?.ttlMs ?? 6e4`)

expiresAt is computed as completion time + ttlMs
(dist/provider-catalog-shared-*.mjs:21,44-47), and multiple expiries are
reduced with Math.min (dist/provider-catalog-expiry-*.mjs:26). It is not
derived from Cache-Control or expires_in.

modelDiscovery.ttlMs exists in that code path, but I could not find any
config schema key that feeds it. I read the Zod config definitions and the
three providers' plugin configSchema and found no key that sets this TTL;
adding a ttl to free-form params is not read by the consumers.
models.catalogRefresh (enabled/url) is a separate ~6-hourly hosted-catalog
mechanism and does not affect this loop.

No API keys, tokens or passwords are included here.

### Logs

```shell
Aggregated from 42,592 instrumented events, 1h49m, agent names replaced with
agent-1..agent-9.

worker-task-start                 2944
  cacheHit: true                     0
  changed vs last cached generation:
    agentId 2936  agentDir 2936  workspaceDir 2936  authStore 2280
  per agent: 328 328 328 328 328 328 328 326 322

catalog-acquire                   2206
  (refresh=true,  changedOnly=false)  2134   <- expiry path, queueMicrotask
  (refresh=false, changedOnly=true)     72   <- startup commit

expired-refresh                   2134
publication                       3100
  modelFactsChanged=false, refreshStatusChanged=true   2652
  modelFactsChanged=true,  refreshStatusChanged=true    360

durations (ms)          n      median    mean     max
  worker-task        2940      1628.0  1735.9  3690.3
  generation-build   2944        51.3    53.1  1607.0
  host-request       2947      2118.4  2154.3  4458.7
worker utilisation 77.1%, median inter-task gap 439 ms

provider expiry (s)
  at detection (overshoot)   n=2515   median -10.7   min -48.5
  remaining after refresh    n=3381   median  51.6   max  59.9

representative events (redacted)

{"event":"worker-task-start","task":1,"agentId":"agent-1","kind":"catalog",
 "providerIds":["openai"],"cacheHit":false,"changedFields":["initial"],
 "heapUsed":113671616}
{"event":"generation-build-end","task":1,"agentId":"agent-1",
 "durationMs":1568.6,"matches":true,"heapUsed":125428848}
{"event":"worker-task-end","task":1,"agentId":"agent-1",
 "durationMs":3601.5,"heapUsed":202984992}
{"event":"expired-refresh","agentId":"agent-1",
 "providerIds":["openai","google","anthropic"],
 "expiryDeltas":[{"provider":"openai","deltaMs":-34058}]}
{"event":"catalog-provider-complete","agentId":"agent-1",
 "providerIds":["openai"],
 "expiryDeltas":[{"provider":"openai","deltaMs":59944}],
 "outcomes":[{"provider":"openai","status":"ready"}]}

Note on "matches": this field compares the requested fingerprint with the
worker's recomputation, so it is a self-consistency check and not evidence
that the catalog content was unchanged. The content-level signal is
modelFactsChanged above.

[openclaw] gateway memory warnings from the normal log, catalog heapUsed:
  12:20:06  2,168,219,272
  12:25     3,299,832,576
  12:30     4,268,584,320
  12:32     4,637,691,792
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

No screenshots. The evidence is the instrumented JSONL above (42,592 events,
15.5 MB, SHA256 7d8c6c03...47d3548) plus the aggregation script. Both can be
shared if useful; the log contains agent and provider identifiers, file-level
fingerprint hashes, durations and heap figures, and no credential values.

### Impact and severity

Affected: a single-host install with 9 configured agents on 2026.9.6
Severity: High (the gateway must be restarted every 15-20 minutes to stay
  usable; 1.5-4 CPU cores are consumed continuously)
Frequency: Always, with no user activity; observed across 7 worker
  generations in one 1h49m window
Consequence: scheduled jobs are interrupted by the restarts (one cron task
  was killed 358 s into its run by an external memory watchdog), and if the
  unattributed portion of each task is dominated by HTTP then this is also
  ~27 redundant model-list requests per minute against three provider APIs

### Additional information

Regression status: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. The normal logs predating this
observation are no longer on disk, so I cannot give a last-known-good or
first-known-bad version.

Not verified on the latest release. I attempted to upgrade to 2026.11.10
(the release notes mention keeping cached models available while catalogs
refresh in the background), but the gateway could not start: the state
upgrade copies ~4.3 GB / 72,006 files and then fails with
"State upgrade chain failed at agent-schema: ... is at schema 23 after the
chain, expected 42", ending in "The CLI command failed. Reason: no such
module: vec0" and exit code 1, in a loop. vec0.dylib is present under
node_modules/sqlite-vec-darwin-arm64/ with no macOS quarantine attribute.
Separately, npm reported that install scripts were not run under the local
allowScripts policy, including openclaw's postinstall-bundled-plugins.mjs,
which may be related. A second blocker appeared behind it: the config
validator rejected agents.defaults.heartbeat as an unrecognized key. I
rolled back to 2026.9.6. I can retry with install scripts allowed if that
would help.

Only configuration-level avoidance I could find: defining every model
explicitly and setting models.mode: "replace", which skips implicit provider
discovery (dist/models-config-*.mjs:301-305). That trades away automatic
new-model discovery, so it is a workaround rather than a fix.

Possible directions, from the code paths above rather than from testing:
- skip the all-agents catalog read when modelFactsChanged is false
- give the generation cache more than one entry, or keep the
  agent-independent part across a miss (the plugin-discovery cache at
  dist/agents/prepared-model-catalog.worker.js:219-221 is keyed on sorted
  plugin IDs and does not depend on the agent)
- expose modelDiscovery.ttlMs in the config schema, noting that the same
  expiry also gates propagation of entitlements, context limits, max output,
  modality/tool/reasoning support and pricing, so a single longer TTL would
  delay those
- de-duplicate concurrent provider fetches across agents

Related but filed separately to keep this to one issue: the catalog worker
sets resourceLimits to 512 MiB, but the parent's --max-old-space-size=8192
wins. Reproduced in an isolated Node test on the same runtime: 8,384 MiB
total heap limit with the parent flag, 704 MiB without; execArgv: [] did not
change it.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When an exec command runs past its `timeoutSeconds` and its processes then take more than about 5 seconds to finish shutting down, the tool result no longer says the command timed out. It shows only `service child cleanup did not complete before its hard deadline` (twice, in the foreground result), so the agent and the person reading it can't tell that the command was simply too slow for its timeout.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Code at `1bc412fb747` (origin/main, 2026-11-25); 2026.11.10 behaves the same.

- `src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay-host.ts:201` (`expireCleanup`): when the stopped command's tree is not confirmed gone within the cleanup deadline, it rejects the pending root result with the cleanup-expiry error, so `ManagedRun.wait()` rejects instead of returning the `overall-timeout` exit the supervisor already chose (`supervisor.ts:276`, `forcedReason`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts:707-720`: exec turns that rejection into a generic runtime error (`buildExecRuntimeErrorOutcome`), so `buildExecExitOutcome` never writes "Command timed out after N seconds". Finalization (`:466-482`) then appends the same cleanup error a second time.

The supervisor rejecting here looks deliberate (an unconfirmed result must not turn into success), so the fix belongs where exec reads the result: it already learns the stop reason through the spawn's `onCancel`.

Not shown: what kept the real `openclaw doctor` tree alive for longer than the deadline (the host was under heavy disk load); the repro uses a process outside the tree that holds the command's output open, which leads to the same cleanup expiry.

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

1. Linux, Gateway running as a service.
2. Start a helper outside the Gateway that receives a file descriptor over a Unix socket and holds it for 20 s (`holder.py` below).
3. Have an agent call exec with `timeoutSeconds: 4` and the command `python3 send-stdout.py <socket>; echo started; sleep 60`, where `send-stdout.py` passes its stdout and stderr to the helper. (Seen with a stub model that makes exactly this tool call, on a fresh 2026.11.10 profile.)
4. Read the exec result the model receives.

Minimal helper scripts:

```python
# holder.py <socket> <seconds>: receive descriptors and hold them open
import os, socket, sys, time
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); s.bind(sys.argv[1]); s.listen(1)
c, _ = s.accept(); socket.recv_fds(c, 16, 4); time.sleep(float(sys.argv[2]))
```

```python
# send-stdout.py <socket>: hand this process's stdout and stderr to the holder
import socket, sys
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); s.connect(sys.argv[1]); socket.send_fds(s, [b"x"], [1, 2])
```

### Expected behavior

The result says why the command stopped, then that cleanup failed:

```
started

Command timed out after 4 seconds.
...
service child cleanup did not complete before its hard deadline; pending: {...}
```

### Actual behavior

```
started

Error: service child cleanup did not complete before its hard deadline; pending: {"closingReceipt":true,"controlClose":true,"relayExit":true,"lineageEof":true,"extinctionUnconfirmed":true,"stdoutEnd":true,"stderrEnd":true}

service child cleanup did not complete before its hard deadline; pending: {...} | service child cleanup owner: {...,"treeOwnership":"linux-subreaper",...}
```

The same command without the helper reports `Command timed out after 4 seconds.` as expected.

First seen with `openclaw doctor --json` run through exec with `timeoutSeconds: 420`: doctor needed about 11 minutes, and the result showed only the cleanup error.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10; origin/main `1bc412fb747` has the same code paths.

### Operating system

Linux x86_64 (distribution left out; not needed for the bug)

### Install method

npm global, systemd user service

### Model

Any (the model plays no part)

### Provider / routing chain

Not involved: exec tool on the Gateway host

### Additional information

Fix PR: #205646.

issues.body:
### Summary
Updating a managed Git installation of OpenClaw to 2026.11.6 left two Git-installed plugins linked to the previous OpenClaw release. Both had been active before the update and were absent from the serving Gateway’s active plugin list on its next two startups. A fresh CLI inspection still showed the provider plugin as loaded, so it was easy to mistake a missing runtime plugin for a sign-in problem.

### Steps to reproduce
1. In a disposable profile using managed Git releases, install a Git plugin pinned to a commit that declares `openclaw` as a peer dependency. A fixture with a simple tool is enough; no external account is needed.
2. Confirm the tool works through the running Gateway and record the target of `<plugin checkout>/node_modules/openclaw`.
3. Update the host into a different release directory without changing the plugin pin. After restart, compare the link target with the serving release and call the same tool through the Gateway.

### Expected behavior
The pinned plugin remains usable after the host update. Its OpenClaw peer resolves to the serving release without requiring a plugin upgrade or manual filesystem edit.

### Actual behavior and evidence
On one macOS arm64 host (Node 26.12.1), two managed Git plugin checkouts still pointed at release A after the Gateway switched to release B. The migration reported `status: pending` for the plugins and the Gateway continued in degraded mode. Sanitized startup evidence:

```text
Plugin declares peerDependency "openclaw" but peer link audit failed:
<managed-git-plugin>/repo/node_modules/openclaw points to <release-A>/openclaw
instead of <release-B>/openclaw. Run `openclaw update repair`.
```

`readlink` confirmed the stale target. No repair was run as part of this diagnosis, so this is not a claim that the repair command itself failed.

### Where to investigate and how to verify a fix
In the [affected core build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f1a6dbd25380d95ee8f9b950b81ae80649e09801/src/plugins/plugin-peer-link.ts#L443-L487), `reconcileRegisteredHostLinks` skips `source: "git"` and expects a package directly under the extensions directory. Managed Git checkouts use a different layout. Please cover that layout in both update and repair while retaining the existing path-ownership checks; arbitrary developer checkouts should not be rewritten.

A regression test should keep the plugin commit fixed, switch the host root from A to B, and verify the peer target **and** a successful Gateway tool call. A second case should start from the already-stale link and verify the supported repair restores it. This differs from #180903 (npm host moved after a Node version change) and #201589 (two spellings of the same Windows directory): here the two release directories really are different.

Related: #204189 (host-link repair PR), #205569 / #205573 (explicit reload recovery after in-place repair), #205567 (quarantined bystander veto on unrelated lifecycle toggles).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On a multi-agent Gateway, one agent's "Learn from conversations" scribe read another agent's private conversations and saved claims from them into its own Knowledge store.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Gateway with two agents (A and B), each with its own isolated Knowledge store. Leave `tools.sessions.visibility` unset, so the default `all` applies.
2. Talk to agent A in a few Control UI conversations and mention some preferences or decisions.
3. On agent B's Knowledge > Scribes page, start "Learn from conversations" and let a run finish.
4. Open agent B's Knowledge > Recent.

### Expected behavior

B's scribe learns only from B's own conversations. The scribe is set up per agent, it saves into that agent's store, and the Knowledge page shows that store as "Not shared". This is the same scoping that #196224 added to the scribe setup step for automations.

### Actual behavior

B's store had 4 new claims quoted from my conversations with agent A, attributed to A's session keys. B's "Knowledge scribe checkpoint · Learn from conversations" note listed 7 of A's `agent:<A>:dashboard:*` sessions as learned. The run reported "36 sessions" in its list step, which is every agent's sessions, not just B's.

It goes the other way too. Agent A's checkpoint note lists sessions from both other agents on the Gateway (14 and 2 of them).

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.10 (6ea542f)

### Operating system

Linux 6.18 (WSL2)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> claude-cli -> anthropic

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
# Step 2 of "Learn from conversations" in
# extensions/knowledge/skills/knowledge-ingest/references/learning.md
# (same text on main today):
2. **List.** `sessions_list` with `archived: false` for active only or
   `"all"` to include archived, `excludeSubagents: true`, following
   `nextOffset`. ...
3. **Learn.** Read each with `sessions_history`, ...
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

There is no agent filter in the list step, so the scribe gets whatever `sessions_list` returns. With the default visibility, that is every agent's sessions on the Gateway (docs: concepts/session-tool.md, "Visibility").

### Impact and severity

Affected: Gateways with more than one agent that use "Learn from conversations" with the default session visibility.
Severity: Privacy. Content from one agent's conversations ends up in another agent's store, which the UI labels as not shared.
Frequency: Every run. The checkpoint holds the other agents' sessions, so later runs keep learning from them.
Consequence: Per-agent private memory isn't actually private. Cleanup means withdrawing the claims by hand, and withdrawn claims still stay in the vault's git history.

### Additional information

Workaround: set `tools.sessions.visibility: "agent"`. If agents still need to message each other, also set `agents.entries.<id>.tools.agentToAgent.send`. After that change, B can no longer list A's sessions.

A possible fix: pass the scribe's own `agentId` in the list step, or skip sessions whose key isn't `agent:<own id>:...`.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`{ "action": "capabilities" }` always returns `portable.runtime: "direct-provider"`. The portable adapter sends every request without `requiredAuthMode` through `execution: { mode: "isolated-agent-runtime" }`, and the Gateway log records those completions under `isolated-agent-runtime`. The capabilities answer is a constant, not a description of the route the next job will take.

### Where it happens

Unchanged on `main` at `40146bcf19e8bca13f61e7ae2db653629e8f9855`.

- [`extensions/deep-research/src/tool.ts#L46-L50`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/40146bcf19e8bca13f61e7ae2db653629e8f9855/extensions/deep-research/src/tool.ts#L46-L50):

  ```ts
  portable: { runtime: "direct-provider", nativeFunctionCallingRequired: false },
  ```

- [`extensions/deep-research/src/portable-tool.ts#L97-L99`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/40146bcf19e8bca13f61e7ae2db653629e8f9855/extensions/deep-research/src/portable-tool.ts#L97-L99):

  ```ts
  ...(request.requiredAuthMode
    ? { requiredAuthMode: request.requiredAuthMode }
    : { execution: { mode: "isolated-agent-runtime" as const } }),
  ```

`docs/tools/deep-research.md` says `capabilities` "reports the portable route", and `docs/plugins/sdk-runtime/models.md` documents that isolated agent-runtime completions reject direct-provider controls, so the two modes are not interchangeable.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Call `deep_research` with `{ "action": "capabilities" }`. Result: `portable.runtime: "direct-provider"`.
2. Start a portable job without `requiredAuthMode`. The Gateway log records its `runtime.llm` completion under `isolated-agent-runtime`, and the job's `route.runtime` is copied from that completion's `execution.mode`. (A commenter on #205501 reports `route.runtime: "isolated-agent-runtime"` in a job result.)

### Expected behavior

`capabilities` reports the route a default request takes (`isolated-agent-runtime`), or both routes and which conditions select each.

### Actual behavior

`capabilities` reports `direct-provider` regardless of the route.

### OpenClaw version

OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f). Also unchanged on `main` at `40146bc`.

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1 (arm64)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

Any; observed with `openai/gpt-6-astra`.

### Provider / routing chain

`deep_research` tool, `engine: portable` → `api.runtime.llm.complete` with `execution.mode: "isolated-agent-runtime"` → `openai` provider.

### Impact and severity

Low. An agent or operator that checks `capabilities` before choosing a model or auth setup reasons from the wrong route. While diagnosing a failed job, it also points at direct-provider transport, which the job never used.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add Nodecode, the OpenAI-compatible API that serves Cyber v1, as an official external provider plugin with API-key onboarding and live model listing.

### Problem to solve

People who want Cyber v1 (an abliterated DeepSeek V4.1 Flash for security work) in OpenClaw today add https://api.nodecode.ai/v1 by hand as a custom OpenAI-compatible provider. They get no onboarding, no context, output or price metadata, no reasoning-effort mapping, and no per-session `prompt_cache_key`, which Nodecode uses to keep a session on the machine that holds its cache.

### Proposed solution

An `@openclaw/nodecode-provider` plugin shaped like the Abliteration plugin (#182248):
- `openclaw onboard --auth-choice nodecode-api-key` or `NODECODE_API_KEY`
- base URL `https://api.nodecode.ai/v1`, default model `nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1` (alias `Cyber v1`)
- live listing of the account's `/v1/models` (`refreshable`), as the live-listing contract expects of hosted providers
- every OpenClaw thinking level sent unchanged as `reasoning_effort` (`off` sends `none`)
- a provider docs page and icon

### Alternatives considered

A hand-written `models.providers.nodecode` entry works, but every user has to copy the metadata and there is no onboarding. A community plugin on ClawHub would stay outside the official provider list and catalog.

### Impact

Affects OpenClaw users who run security-research and pentest agents on an abliterated model. Low risk: a new optional provider, no change for anyone who does not install it.

### Evidence/examples

A PR is ready: unit tests, the live-listing contract, and a live text request plus tool-call round trip against api.nodecode.ai pass. A real `openclaw agent exec` turn on Cyber v1 wrote a file and ran a command.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, it is ready.

### Additional information

Disclosure: I run Foresight Labs, which operates Nodecode. We can provide a key for the scheduled live checks.

1. Lightpanda successfully reads pages for the agent, but the panel says it could not load the browser because this engine has no screenshot support.
2. The address bar can retain the previous page after agent navigation. Component reproduction: focus the address, navigate the agent to a second page, then leave the address field.
3. After switching Chromium tabs, the panel can retain a 16:9 frame with a black lower area. Component reproduction: select a static tab with a different viewport size; the resize succeeds but the existing stream does not send another frame, and the panel never reacquires one.

## Expected

A screenshot-free browser should explain its preview limitation without a false load failure. The address should catch up after editing focus leaves. A successful managed-viewport resize should refresh the stream even when the page does not repaint on its own. Shared/attached browser windows must retain their current sizing policy.

## Verification

Three regression tests fail against main `2407c717932356ac345258ebc2da67889f80623c`. Full before/after runtime and screenshot verification is deferred until the fixing PR is open; the component tests do not prove the black-pixel symptom has disappeared in a real Chromium run.

issues.body:
## Environment
- **OS**: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26200) x64
- **Node**: v26.7.0
- **OpenClaw**: 2026.9.2 (commit 9098b23)
- **Install method**: GitHub source checkout (pnpm install && pnpm build)

## Problem
Gateway starts, loads all plugins, logs:
```
[gateway] http server listening (18 plugins: ...; 46.8s)
[gateway] ready
[heartbeat] started
[cron] started
```

But **never actually binds to the configured port** (tested 4242, 4243, 18789). Both `ws://127.0.0.1:PORT` and `http://127.0.0.1:PORT/` return `ECONNREFUSED`.

## Reproduction
```bash
# Minimal config
echo '{"gateway":{"port":4242,"mode":"local"}}' > ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json

# Run gateway
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 4242 --auth token --allow-unconfigured --verbose
```

Process exits silently after `cron: started` (no error, no crash report).

## Tested variants (all fail)
| Variant | Result |
|---------|--------|
| `--auth none --allow-unconfigured` | Same |
| `--auth token` (with token in config) | Same |
| `gateway install` + `gateway start` (Scheduled Task) | Same |
| WSL2 with Windows node binary | Same |
| Different ports (4242, 4243, 18789) | Same |

## What works
- Plugin loading (17-18 plugins load successfully)
- Configuration parsing
- Token generation
- Database initialization (SQLite)
- Logs show "http server listening" and "gateway ready"

## What doesn't
- **Actual TCP port binding** - netstat shows nothing on the port
- WebSocket/HTTP connections - all ECONNREFUSED
- Process stays alive after startup (exits silently)

## Logs
Full startup logs available showing the sequence:
1. Plugin loading (18 plugins)
2. "starting HTTP server..."
3. "http server listening (18 plugins...)"
4. "gateway ready"
5. "heartbeat started"
6. "cron started"
7. **Process exits** (no further logs)

## Hypothesis
The log message "http server listening" is emitted **before** the actual `server.listen()` call, and then:
- The `listen()` fails silently on Windows (IPv6 vs IPv4, permissions, firewall)
- OR the event loop has no pending work and process exits
- OR there's a race condition in the startup sequence

## Additional notes
- No Windows Firewall prompts appear
- Running as Administrator doesn't help
- Same binary works on Linux (per CI), suggesting Windows-specific code path issue
- Telegram plugin also fails with "Cannot find module ... telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.js" (separate build issue)

**This blocks all Windows users from running OpenClaw gateway.**

issues.body:
## Problem

Typing `/approve <id> allow-once` in WebChat resolves the approval, but recording the confirmation can fail the original waiting turn with `SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite`. The approval command and confirmation also enter the next model context.

## Reproduction and evidence

On current main `ac9a0c6ab463c6f698203877ade316793c299601`, a focused regression uses the real WebChat `chat.send` handler, shared fast-approval dispatch, SQLite transcript writers, and SessionManager. Only the external approval-resolution RPC is stubbed. It prepares the original turn's manager, sends the approval, waits for WebChat's final confirmation, and then reads the next model context and appends the original assistant's continuation.

Both assertions fail on unmodified production source:

- The next context contains the typed approval and confirmation, including WebChat's separately recorded rows.
- The original assistant append rejects with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for cloud-session`.

A supplied live WebSocket comparison independently reports the command marker absent before approval and present afterward on main `2407c717932356ac345258ebc2da67889f80623c`, while the original run fails with the same conflict. The supplied comparison also reports the failure on #194034 head `9a127a4edc681600339ba441ccdd6459aa567e48`: its shared copy is context-free, but WebChat's own copy is not. That live run was performed on another machine, not as part of this regression run.

## Expected behavior and cause

The approval and confirmation should remain visible in history, without becoming model input or invalidating the turn they release. Fast approval dispatch does not carry the existing `commandReply` / `contextFreeCommand` classification through both the delivered reply and its shared transcript mirror. WebChat's independent finalizer therefore persists an ordinary context-bearing pair.

## Related work and intent

- #194034 / #194029 concern Signal approval ingress and include a partial shared-recorder fix, not WebChat's second writer.
- #201271 fixes shared command recording during a turn and explicitly excludes WebChat's independent recorder. #201592 concerns ordinary inbound messages, not this approval path.
- Commit `2987571782893d3c9568852861ab579739a07fea` introduced the fast approval path to release active turns before ordinary admission. #169026 added shared command transcript capture. #152512 established visible, context-free `/status` recording without weakening transcript conflict checks. Aborting an approved turn is not their intended outcome.

No VM or new live gateway run was performed. A live runtime check of the fix is planned on another machine after the PR is opened.

issues.body:
## What happens

A terminal session row for the current run clears the Control UI's active-run state, but the page does not fetch the saved reply. The transcript can remain at the user prompt until another event or refresh recovers it.

A user reported a roughly five-second gap on the first reply in one of three new Safari chats. That exact Safari timing is not yet reproduced. The missing-recovery path is reproduced independently through the real pane and session-state owners on main `d290bbe6be8e2`.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Begin with a user prompt and an active local run.
2. Make the saved history contain the assistant reply.
3. Publish an idle session row with `lastRunId` matching the local run, without a `chat.final` message.
4. Observe that `chatRunId` becomes null, but no `chat.history` request is issued and the assistant reply remains absent.

Both shared session publication and direct `sessions.changed` delivery reproduce this result. A focused regression in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-recovery.test.ts` fails in both cases on unchanged main: expected one history request, received zero.

## Cause and intent

`reconcileChatRunAfterSessionStatePublication` correctly retires the exact completed run. Its page callers omit transcript recovery; the later reconciliation sees no active run and returns without reading history. The terminal-row recovery introduced in #126180 intentionally unlocks queued follow-ups. Recovering the missing saved answer preserves that behavior rather than undoing it.

## Scope of proof

This is UI owner-boundary proof, not a live Gateway or Safari reproduction. Live before/after verification remains needed.

issues.body:
## Summary

When `agents.defaults.decisionModel` selects a provider route whose model id is **not declared in that provider's decision catalog**, `decision_evaluate` rejects every call pre-dispatch with `unavailable / unsupported-input` in ~2 ms, and the returned guidance omits the capability sentence that would reveal the real cause.

The rejection looks identical to an over-large or malformed batch, so the actual problem (capabilities were never resolved for the selected id) is invisible from the tool result.

## Environment

- OpenClaw `2026.11.10` (6ea542f), official container image.
- Plugin: `@openclaw/typesafe` `2026.11.10` (installed from npm into the plugin stage).
- Provider: `models.providers.typesafe.baseUrl = http://<in-cluster System One server>/v1`, `models: []`, no hosted credential (local Kev-style server).
- Config: `agents.defaults.decisionModel: "typesafe/decision"` — the in-cluster server's model name is `decision`, but the plugin catalog declares only `jev-latest`, `jev-preview`, `jev-1.13.0`, `kev-latest`.

## Actual

```json
{"status":"unavailable","reason":"unsupported-input",
 "guidance":"Shorten the state or rubric, reduce question counts, and check the selected model's declared limits. Host bounds are 256 questions for legacy input or 400 with contractVersion 2, 1 MiB of JSON, 20000 JSON nodes, and depth 32. No evidence was truncated or sent on a host-bound rejection."}
```

Note what is **missing** compared with the guidance shown in #182920 (declared row): there is no `The selected provider supports … questions. Supported input modalities: …` sentence. Capability resolution for `typesafe/decision` produced nothing, and nothing in the result says so.

## Expected

Either:

1. capability resolution falls back to the provider manifest's declared decision models (boolean/choice/score, `text` input) and the call dispatches, or
2. the call fails with a diagnostic that names the problem — e.g. `"decisionModel 'typesafe/decision' is not declared by provider 'typesafe' (declared: jev-latest, jev-preview, jev-1.13.0, kev-latest)"` — or the config is rejected at load/write time.

A generic `unsupported-input` plus input-size guidance is misleading: the payload was 44 characters with one boolean question.

## Reproduction

Config (read-only in-cluster, applied via GitOps):

```yaml
agents: { defaults: { decisionModel: "typesafe/decision" } }
models: { providers: { typesafe: { baseUrl: "http://decision.local:8080/v1", request: { allowPrivateNetwork: true }, models: [] } } }
```

Then from any agent turn:

```json
decision_evaluate({
  "state": {"type": "text", "text": "A used RTX 3090 is listed at 1500 CAD in Calgary."},
  "questions": {"deal": {"type": "boolean", "instructions": "Is this below street price?",
                          "criteria": {"true": "below street", "false": "at or above street"}}}
})
```

## Demonstrated impact

- Reproduced identically from three callers (`main`, `saffron`, `sage`), including an agent with thinking disabled — so it is not caller/model config.
- Reproduced with `choice`-only questions and with `state` as both tagged (`{type:"text"}`) and legacy string form — so it is not question shape or `contractVersion`.
- The provider plugin's own `evaluate` entry is never entered: an `appendFileSync` instrumentation line placed at the top of `createPreparedDecisionProvider(...).evaluate` never fires, while the tool still returns `unsupported-input`. That places the rejection upstream of the provider, consistent with capability resolution failing for an undeclared id.
- The same decision server answers correctly when called directly (`POST /v1/systemone` with `{"state","questions","model":"decision"}` returns `choice: skip`, score ≈ 2/5 for the case above), so the endpoint and model are healthy.
- Effect: the decision-model role is silently dead for every consumer (explicit tool and decision-assisted flows) with no operator-visible reason.

## Remediation advice

- In the decision request preflight, when the selected model id has no catalog entry, distinguish *undeclared model* from *unsupported input*: return a dedicated reason/guidance (or a config validation error) naming the id and the provider's declared ids.
- Optionally allow provider-declared capabilities to apply to custom endpoints (`models: []` + `baseUrl`), which is the documented local-Server route for `kev-latest`.

---
Drafted from live gateway logs by an automated agent running on the affected instance; every command above was executed on that instance. Happy to supply full `[decisions]` log lines or a trimmed config on request.
