issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Since 2026.11.7, the agent tool `sessions_search` without `sessionKey` (the `recall` path of `sessions.search`) fails with `Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request` whenever any session on the gateway writes a transcript event while the search is reading. Parallel `sessions_search` calls in one agent turn fail together because each call's own tool-call transcript write invalidates the others. The same searches with `sessionKey` don't fail.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a gateway with several agents and some ongoing activity, such as cron turns or other conversations. One agent has a large history (~6 GB `openclaw-agent.sqlite`, hundreds of sessions).
2. In one turn, ask that agent to look up several distinctive terms in its past conversations, so the model issues parallel tool calls: `sessions_search({query: "<term>", limit: 10})` × 6, with no `sessionKey`.
3. All 6 calls return the tool error `Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request` within ~3 s.
4. A single retry issued 4 s later fails the same way, in ~0.3 s.
5. The same queries with `sessionKey` set to a specific conversation succeed.

### Expected behavior

A recall search returns results, or at least succeeds on retry, while unrelated sessions keep writing. Transcript writes from other sessions, or from the same turn's other tool calls, shouldn't count as a change of search scope. That should only happen when visibility, sharing or the lifecycle of the matched sessions changes.

### Actual behavior

`searchRecallSessionTranscripts` (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-search-recall.ts`) captures `projection.sharingRevision` in `prepareTargets()` and compares it again inside `withReadySessionRows` after the awaited per-target `searchSessionTranscripts` reads. The revision object is reset by `invalidate()`, which runs on any transcript refresh (`createSessionRowProjectionTranscriptUpdates.refresh`), on `mark()` of most runtime changes and on row removal. On a busy gateway, both of the two attempts see a different revision, and the handler throws `Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request`.

The guard came with b66dc6fa3a ("fix: hide revoked conversations from session recall", 2026-11-21). On current `main` it's unchanged apart from the shared list preparation, so it still throws. The 2026.11.8 to 2026.11.10 tags don't contain this code.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.7 (previous: 2026.11.5 had no failures)

### Operating system

Ubuntu Linux (x86_64)

### Install method

npm global (managed runtime generation), gateway as a systemd user service

### Model

gpt-6.2-sol

### Provider / routing chain

openai via codex app-server (native Codex harness)

### Additional provider/model setup details

The agent tool profile includes `sessions_search` and `sessions_history`, with the default session visibility.

### Logs

Production numbers from one agent, read from `transcript_events` (toolCall/toolResult pairs for `sessions_search`):

| Period | Version | Searches | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 days before the upgrade | 2026.11.5 | ~590 | 0 |
| First 30 min after the upgrade | 2026.11.7 | — | first failure |
| Next ~44 h | 2026.11.7 | 317 | 37 (all without `sessionKey`) |

- With `sessionKey`: 179 of 179 succeeded.
- Without `sessionKey`, run in parallel with other calls: 25 of 71 failed. Run alone: 12 of 67 failed.
- In two bursts, every call failed together: 11 of 11 and 10 of 10 parallel calls.
- Failures cluster when many scheduled turns run on the gateway at the same time.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

A controlled rehearsal turn on the same agent, with read-only lookups of 6 terms:

| Run | `sessions_search` calls | Failed | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model left free to run calls in parallel | 253 | 6 of 6 parallel, then 1 retry | ~2 min |
| Calls run one at a time (via agent instructions) | 16 | 1, recovered on 1 retry | 47 s |
| Calls run one at a time, second run | 13 | 0 | — |

In the first run, the agent recovered by sweeping `sessionKey`-scoped searches over every conversation, which accounts for the 253 calls.

### Impact and severity

Medium. Agents that recall prior conversations (scheduled reviews, "what did we agree") lose that context or burn many tool calls. The error says "retry the request", so models retry in bursts and make it worse. We mitigated it in the agent instructions (run searches one at a time, retry once, then fall back to `sessionKey` searches or `sessions_history`) and will remove that once a fixed release ships.

### Additional information

Related but different path: #160237 (open). It makes the `scope` / Control UI search tolerate ordinary row refreshes, but doesn't touch `sessions-search-recall.ts`, which the agent tool uses when no `sessionKey` is given.

A possible direction: compare a revision limited to the matched hits' rows, their lifecycle and their sharing facts, rather than the gateway-wide sharing revision. Alternatively, let transcript refreshes that don't change visibility leave the sharing revision as it is.

issues.body:
## Summary

With `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"` on an `anthropic/*` model and two Anthropic token profiles in `auth.order.anthropic`, a **long-lived session stays pinned to the profile it first selected even after that profile hits its weekly limit**. Every later turn in that session starts Claude Code on the exhausted profile, fails immediately (`You've hit your weekly limit · resets Sep 27, 6pm (UTC)`), records the cooldown again (`reused=true`), and goes straight to the next **model** fallback — although a second, healthy Anthropic profile is configured and new sessions select it fine.

## Version

OpenClaw 2026.9.5 (upstream main `359a8a35`), Claude Code CLI 2.1.x, Linux x64. `auth.order.anthropic = [anthropic:claude2, anthropic:claude]`, both setup-token profiles, different subscriptions.

## Observed (2026-09-25, one gateway)

```text
[agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=1515 runId=d27cd6fb-… error=You've hit your weekly limit · resets Sep 27, 6pm (UTC)
[agent/embedded] auth profile failure state updated: runId=d27cd6fb-… profile=sha256:7fb648e05b37 provider=anthropic reason=rate_limit window=cooldown reused=true
[model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 reason=rate_limit next=openai/gpt-6-sol
```

- Hourly persistent session (`agent:<id>:board-warden`) did this on every run 06:35–13:24Z; another long-lived agent main session 3× in one hour. Dozens of runs, all on the same exhausted profile fingerprint.
- In the same period, freshly created sessions of the same agent and model ran on Opus through the other profile with 0 fallbacks.

## Expected

On a limit failure of the pinned profile, the CLI backend should re-select the next eligible profile from `auth.order` (the cooldown is already recorded) and retry the same model before model fallback — as the Codex harness does for ordered `openai` profiles (usage-limit reset recorded, next profile tried inside the same run). Context carry-over across the auth boundary is already handled with the history prelude (`history refused across auth boundary` path).

## Related ask (policy, not bug)

Operators with several subscriptions of one vendor often prefer **waiting for the recorded reset** over switching model families for non-urgent work. A per-agent option like `onAllProfilesLimited: "fallback" | "wait-until-reset"` (reset time is in the error text for Claude and recorded natively for Codex) would let orchestrators hold non-urgent work instead of silently changing model.

Not the same as #151155 (mid-turn auth refresh) or #144047 (cron followups not forwarding the profile).

### Summary
Enabling the bundled Knowledge plugin on 2026.11.10 repeatedly failed in `prepare` with `plugin load failed: gemini: configured plugin payload verification failed (missing-openclaw-peer-link)`. Knowledge has no Gemini dependency. This narrows a gap in #157907: an unchanged quarantine is tolerated for a bystander, but pending install bookkeeping can turn the bystander into a replacement target.

### Environment and observed sequence
macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1, managed Git host build `b22df8b94835e90191a36cf8496ad2cdffee7223`, Git-installed Gemini 0.5.4. Times below are local, Nov 25.
- 11:44: startup verification correctly found Gemini's `node_modules/openclaw` pointed to the previous release. The Gateway continued with the plugin quarantined. At 11:45:36 the same checkout's link was updated; read-back resolves to the serving release. A subsequent reload failed in prepare.
- 15:15:45: the reload log listed `plugins.entries.knowledge.enabled`, `plugins.slots.memory`, and `plugins.installs.gemini.{resolvedAt,installedAt,acceptedSurfaceAt}` in the same candidate. Other plugins also had install timestamps in the diff. No Gemini version, source, integrity, or entry-config change appeared in that diff.
- Five `plugins.setEnabled` RPCs between 15:15:46 and 15:16:45 returned `UNAVAILABLE` naming Gemini. `Gateway generation 2: replacement not applied`. Knowledge was enabled in persisted config, not applied to the serving generation. No live retry or restart was performed to generate this report.

### Code path on upstream main
Inspected `e18a8298867e849533e64f9721fa050df9372f1d`; the relevant selector and strict-load gate match the incident build.
1. [Config reload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e18a8298867e849533e64f9721fa050df9372f1d/src/gateway/config-reload.ts#L426-L448) combines config and managed install-record diffs. [The planner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e18a8298867e849533e64f9721fa050df9372f1d/src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts#L491-L544) classifies `installedAt`/`resolvedAt` as no-ops but retains the original `changedPaths`. `acceptedSurfaceAt` is not in that two-key exemption.
2. [Hot reload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e18a8298867e849533e64f9721fa050df9372f1d/src/gateway/server-reload-hot.ts#L475-L490) forwards the full list. [Replacement selection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e18a8298867e849533e64f9721fa050df9372f1d/src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-recovery.ts#L113-L135) adds an owner for **any** `plugins.installs.<id>.*` path.
3. [Candidate loading](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e18a8298867e849533e64f9721fa050df9372f1d/src/plugins/loader-runtime-candidate.ts#L140-L160) uses the existing verification failure for the same plugin root. [Strict replacement](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e18a8298867e849533e64f9721fa050df9372f1d/src/plugins/loader-shared.ts#L380-L406) rejects a selected ID even if the previous source, phase and error match. This is not a fresh failed peer-link audit at click time.

### Minimal A/B reproduction
Ran the production `resolvePluginReloadReplacementIds` and `maybeThrowOnPluginLoadError` together on the incident checkout with synthetic registries: previous and next both have an identical Gemini error (distinct record objects), and the explicit target is Knowledge. No account or real plugin install is needed.

| Changed paths beyond `plugins.entries.knowledge.enabled` | Selected IDs | Strict gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | knowledge | passes |
| `plugins.installs.gemini.installedAt` alone | knowledge, gemini | throws the Gemini error |
| all three Gemini timestamps from the incident | knowledge, gemini | throws the same error |

This reproduces the selection and rejection, not the entire UI flow on current main. The production RPC failures above are from 2026.11.10.

### Expected / regression coverage
An unrelated toggle accompanied only by no-op install bookkeeping should apply and leave the quarantined plugin unavailable. Keep atomic rejection for actual plugin changes, explicit replacement of the failing owner, and newly introduced failures. Distinguish a changed capability approval from merely refreshing its timestamp; don't blanket-ignore install records. Please cover the combined lifecycle + pending install diff through `plugins.setEnabled`, checking both the active Knowledge state and continued quarantine of the other plugin.

Related: #204156 tracks the original managed-Git stale link, not the cross-plugin veto after correction. #157907 protects an unchanged bystander but not one selected by incidental metadata. #192027 reported similar pending timestamps after a Windows junction failure; this case requires no Windows junction or fresh filesystem error.

Also related: #204189 (managed-Git host-link repair PR) and #205569 / #205573 (explicit reload recovery after in-place repair).

issues.body:
# [Feature]: Expand explicitly spoken snippet names into reusable text during dictation

**Package ID:** M07 · **Classification:** missing capability in the earlier comparison.  
**Repository:** `openclaw/openclaw` · **Draft date:** 2026-11-25.  
**Status:** feature proposal for scoped implementation on the contributor's fork; upstream design acceptance is requested. Verification results will be recorded on the implementation PR. Local IDs refer to documents in this package, not GitHub issue numbers.

## Summary

Add user-authored text snippets that a person can insert by saying an explicit trigger during a dictation capture. The first release should support exact named expansion of static saved text, preview, cancellation and predictable literal escaping. Dynamic variables are a possible later extension, not a prerequisite or acceptance requirement for the missing snippet capability. An expansion remains ordinary editable text in the destination draft. It must never send a message, run a command, call an agent tool, fetch a secret or recursively activate another snippet.

The motivating workflow is repetitive writing: a support signature, appointment instructions, an address, or a standard paragraph. Speaking an entire paragraph repeatedly is cumbersome; a user should be able to say “insert snippet support signature” and get the paragraph they previously approved, with its spelling and line breaks preserved. The same words occurring in a quotation must remain text.

## Problem to solve

A bounded current search of open issues and PRs for `dictation snippet` returned no matching item. This is a search result, not proof that no equivalent proposal exists. Recheck before filing. Existing general agent skills and tool execution are different from deterministic expansion into an unsent document. The transcript recovery work in [PR #198845](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198845) is adjacent and should remain the audio recovery owner; it is not a snippet implementation. The dictation/Talk separation in [PR #204505](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204505) is another related surface, not a required code parent.

M11 owns refinement request/result processing. M07 contributes bounded expansion intents and protected output spans. P03 owns vocabulary hints; adding a spelling to that dictionary must never implicitly create a snippet. M10 alone owns destination insertion. P06 owns whether the capture is dictation or an agent request.

## Proposed solution

### User journeys and exact semantics

| Spoken input / state | Required result |
|---|---|
| “Insert snippet support signature” with one enabled exact match | Expand the stored body into the editable preview, preserving configured newlines. |
| “I told her to say insert snippet support signature” | Keep prose; a quoted or embedded mention is not an invocation. |
| “Literal insert snippet support signature” | Insert the words without expansion; strip only an explicitly recognized literal escape. |
| Two enabled snippets normalize to the same trigger | Refuse automatic expansion and offer a bounded chooser; never choose by most recent use. |
| A saved body contains `{{tracking_number}}` or `<name>` | Insert those placeholder characters literally; do not guess, browse, interpolate, or mine history. |
| “Insert snippet signature” while in literal code mode | Keep literal words unless the person explicitly invokes snippet mode. |
| A snippet body contains “insert snippet other” | Insert that body literally; do not recurse. |
| The person cancels while reviewing a candidate | Discard that expansion intent; preserve unrelated draft text. |

Use a deliberate trigger boundary in the first release: a standalone finalized phrase or an explicit UI-selected command segment. Do not start with fuzzy phrase activation in arbitrary speech. Trigger recognition may normalize whitespace and locale-aware case but must not collapse distinct Unicode words, accents or punctuation-bearing identifiers into one key without showing the collision to the author. A confidence score alone is not sufficient authorization to expand.

A capture may contain several expansion intents mixed with prose. Assign stable sequence positions before refinement so later ASR revisions cannot duplicate expansion. If the recognizer revises the trigger before finalization, replace the pending intent rather than append a second body. The complete utterance must be reviewable before first use of a newly imported snippet.

### Scope and exclusions

Include creation, editing, deletion, enabling, search, trigger validation, preview, import/export of a documented versioned format, and account-scoped persistence. Include native and web dictation consumers that implement M11, plus a generic plain-text output path for clients without rich snippet UI. Sharing is optional future work through an explicit shared-content owner; do not make M06's vocabulary synchronization carry snippet bodies.

Exclude executable templates, JavaScript expressions, shell interpolation, arbitrary network calls, file reads, clipboard reads, password-manager access, agent tool calls, automatic sends, implicit organization-wide sharing and nested expansion. Exclude syntactic editor tab stops in arbitrary applications; a plain-text target cannot promise editor-native snippet navigation. M08 may consume the resulting protected literal text but cannot reinterpret it as executable code.

### Proposed data and configuration

The following schema is a proposal for review, not an existing OpenClaw API:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "id": "user-generated-stable-id",
  "revision": 3,
  "name": "Support signature",
  "locale": "en-US",
  "triggers": ["support signature"],
  "body": "Thank you,\nAlex\nCompleteTech support",
  "enabled": true,
  "sensitivity": "normal"
}
```

Store the immutable identifier separately from the editable name. Edits use optimistic revision checks. Proposed limits are 500 enabled snippets per account, 16 KiB UTF-8 per static body, and 64 KiB total expanded snippet text per capture; validate them both when saving and when expanding. These are resource-control proposals, not measured capacity claims. Surface which limit was exceeded and leave the previous valid version intact.

Version one treats every body as static text. Angle-bracket names, braces, dates, numbers, dollar signs, and shell-like syntax have no substitution meaning. Preserve them exactly, including leading zeroes. Importing a format that declares executable or required dynamic-template features must fail visibly rather than silently converting it into a different grammar.

A separately reviewed future version could add typed text/choice/date/number variables. That extension would need explicit value entry, preview for unknown or sensitive values, declared date locale/time zone, bounded output, no external lookups, and a migration story. It is deliberately excluded from this issue's first-release criteria and PR scope. Wispr Flow's current desktop snippet documentation also describes static text and says dynamic variables are unsupported; this focused proposal follows that capability boundary.[1]

Recommended defaults: feature disabled until enabled; expansion requires an explicit named trigger; no automatic clipboard/context variables; sensitive snippets always require preview; exports include authored static definitions only, with a clear sensitivity warning. Record only content-free counters by default. A `sensitivity` flag changes presentation/retention policy, not permission to access other data.

### Architecture and lifecycle

1. Snapshot the authorized snippet catalog revision and mode at capture start, using existing account ownership and persistence services.
2. Resolve a finalized trigger to an exact snippet identifier and revision. Recheck that it is still enabled and authorized before materializing the body.
3. Load the approved static body without template evaluation. Validate its encoding, size, and catalog revision in the existing draft/preview owner.
4. Produce an expansion candidate with source segment, body revision, exact body text and protected literal ranges.
5. Let M11 compose the candidate with surrounding dictated prose. The model may not alter protected snippet bytes or interpret placeholders.
6. On acceptance, let M10 apply the one final result to the captured destination, or leave the preview available for manual copy if that destination changed.

Use the capture's existing cancellation signal and generation. Do not create a background executor, independent transcript store or second insertion queue. A snippet edit during capture must invalidate a pending expansion or present the old/new versions; recommended behavior is to keep the captured version in preview while requiring an explicit refresh before acceptance if it was deleted or disabled. Permission removal always invalidates it immediately. Once text is inserted, later snippet edits do not rewrite the user's document.

### Privacy, accessibility and failure behavior

Snippet bodies can contain confidential text. Keep them out of default diagnostic logs, analytics labels, exception bodies and crash attachments. Local-only dictation must not upload the full snippet catalog; deterministic expansion can occur locally. If cloud refinement is authorized, send only the chosen body when its text is actually needed, respecting the same disclosure as the utterance. Imported bodies are untrusted text even if they resemble instructions.

Provide keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels for the chooser and preview controls. Announce “snippet ready for review” once, not every transcript delta. Long snippets should use a bounded scrollable preview with a plain-text alternative; do not move focus out of the destination without a clear way to return.

An offline catalog miss is a miss, not permission to fetch a different account's data. A network error during catalog refresh must leave a clearly identified last authorized local snapshot, if policy permits; revocation cannot be ignored just because a stale snapshot exists. If insertion fails or is ambiguous, retain the expanded preview according to the capture retention setting and do not expand or insert again automatically.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **M07-AC01:** Exact explicit triggers expand once in utterance order; prose mentions and literal escapes remain literal.
- [ ] **M07-AC02:** Trigger collisions, disabled items and unknown names produce a useful chooser/error without guessed expansion.
- [ ] **M07-AC03:** Static bodies preserve placeholder-looking text, dates, numbers and leading zeroes literally; no variable interpolation or external lookup occurs.
- [ ] **M07-AC04:** Snippet text, line breaks, leading zeroes and protected literals survive all enabled M11 transforms byte-for-byte where the target encoding permits.
- [ ] **M07-AC05:** Catalog revisions, account switches, permission removal and capture cancellation fence stale expansion results.
- [ ] **M07-AC06:** A body containing another trigger, shell syntax, URLs or instructions remains inert text.
- [ ] **M07-AC07:** Unsupported targets receive plain text or an explicit copy fallback; the feature never sends/executes.
- [ ] **M07-AC08:** Import/export round-trips supported schema data; malformed, oversized or unknown required versions are rejected without partial writes.
- [ ] **M07-AC09:** Keyboard and screen-reader flows cover chooser, preview, cancel and restoration of focus.
- [ ] **M07-AC10:** Default logs contain no body or trigger content; content inspection requires a separately enabled local diagnostic mode.
- [ ] **M07-AC11:** With the feature off, prior dictation output and audio lifecycle remain unchanged.

## Evidence/examples

All implementation tests below are **NOT RUN**; no passing runtime or performance evidence is supplied.

| Layer | Concrete proof required | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| Parser | Exact trigger, embedded quotation, accent collision, punctuation, literal escape, recursive body, partial ASR revision | AC01–02, AC06 |
| Static-body fidelity | Literal braces/angle brackets, fixed dates, numeric leading zero, expansion cap, rejected dynamic-schema import | AC03–04, AC08 |
| Ownership | Edit/delete during capture, account switch, revocation while awaiting review, cancellation during refinement | AC05 |
| Integration | Mixed prose plus two snippets through M11, changed target through M10, offline local expansion | AC01, AC04, AC07 |
| Accessibility | Real keyboard and screen-reader chooser/preview journey on supported desktop and mobile clients | AC09 |
| Privacy/regression | Capture logs during success/failure; disabled feature comparison; import rollback | AC08, AC10–11 |

Proposed performance target: exact local trigger lookup and deterministic expansion should add no more than 25 ms p95 for 500 enabled snippets and a 4 KiB selected body on a declared reference device, excluding user input and storage cold start. Report actual device, runtime, samples and cold/warm results before adopting that target. The complete dictation budget belongs to M11.

## Alternatives considered

Repeating the full paragraph avoids a catalog but defeats the repetitive-writing use case. An agent prompt can generate a response but cannot guarantee the saved wording. Editor-native snippets are useful inside one editor, yet their executable or variable grammar should not be implied in a generic dictation target. Fuzzy activation and dynamic variables can be separate future proposals after static exact expansion is reliable.

## Impact

Implement the catalog/validator and pure expansion contract first, then connect the preview and M11, then enable one qualified client. Later client adapters must pass the same conformance cases. Rollback disables the feature while preserving stored snippets in a version-readable format; never delete authored text. A failed migration must restore the last valid catalog and provide an export path.

Maintainers should decide trigger localization, initial limits, whether imported snippets always require a first-use preview, and which existing store owns account-scoped content. The recommended initial answer is conservative exact triggers, no sharing, no variables or executable templates, and preserved literal bodies. Do not attach a `Closes` reference to P03 or any adjacent upstream issue: this feature has its own acceptance scope.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself in an isolated contributor branch. Proposed initial scope is the existing browser dictation draft; native adapters remain unqualified until independently tested. The existing SQLite-backed personal preference owner can store a reserved, bounded `dictation.snippets` catalog under current personal-profile admission. This proposal asks maintainers to confirm that ownership and core-vs-plugin placement before upstream acceptance.

## Additional information

### Sources and relationships

- [1] [Wispr Flow: create and use snippets](https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/5784437944-create-and-use-snippets) — current desktop static-text capability; dynamic variables are explicitly unsupported. The proposed exact invocation rules are an initial OpenClaw design, not a claim of identical matching behavior.

- [OpenClaw PR #198845: explicit dictation recording retry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198845) — adjacent recovery work, not implemented snippet support.
- [OpenClaw PR #204505: separate dictation and Talk controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204505) — adjacent mode-selection work.
- [VS Code snippet documentation](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editing/userdefinedsnippets) — established editor template concepts; compatibility with its entire grammar is not proposed.
- Package contracts: M11 refinement, M10 insertion, P03 vocabulary, P06 modes; M08 literal code handling.


### Current source inspection

At upstream main snapshot `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c`, Control UI uses Solid 2 and composer dictation already requests transcription with `brain: "none"`. This feature will extend that draft path. Related PRs #204505 and #198845 remain adjacent, unmerged work and are not assumed parents. Bounded current searches found no equivalent snippet implementation. The plugin SDK does not currently expose the composer final-result/protected-span boundary required here; the proposed core addition stays within the existing transcription and draft owners, without adding an agent tool.

issues.body:
### Summary

Show Gateway operators how often OpenClaw repairs tool-call arguments before accepting them. Start with terminal JSON string repair on the Anthropic Messages transport.

### Problem to solve

OpenClaw can accept a tool call after repairing a raw newline or an invalid escape inside a JSON string. From the operator’s perspective, that call looks like one whose arguments were valid on arrival. After changing a model, provider, or Gateway version, operators lack a repair rate they can compare across equivalent workloads. [Terminal argument parser](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0b9114291429df561ed41340cdc035f51e0f163b/packages/ai/src/transports/transport-stream-shared.ts#L194)

### Proposed solution

Expose two counters through the existing authenticated Prometheus endpoint. [Prometheus exporter](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/prometheus)

- **Accepted tool calls.** After the transport accepts the complete set of calls in a response, count each call once. Set `outcome` to `unchanged` if its arguments parsed directly or `repaired` if terminal string repair made them parseable.
- **Responses rejected for malformed tool arguments.** Increment once when terminal argument validation rejects the response. That response contributes zero accepted calls, including otherwise valid siblings.

Use the same observation window for `repaired / (unchanged + repaired)`. Report the rejected-response count alongside that rate. Limit exported fields to the counter value and fixed transport and outcome labels. This keeps arguments, argument hashes, tool names, model IDs, endpoint URLs, and error text out of the metrics.

### Alternatives considered

Counting streaming warnings would overstate successful repairs. OpenClaw has a documented case where an early chunk looked repairable and a later chunk invalidated it. [Repair invalidation fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/43824)

### Impact

Operators using Anthropic Messages and Prometheus could detect a change in repair frequency after an update without collecting argument content. Production frequency is currently unknown. The initial scope covers aggregate transport behavior.

### Evidence and acceptance criteria

The existing loopback fixture provides two concrete expectations. [Test cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0b9114291429df561ed41340cdc035f51e0f163b/packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts#L1883)

| Provider response | Unchanged calls | Repaired calls | Rejected responses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| One valid call and one call with a repairable raw newline | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| One valid call and one call with truncated JSON | 0 | 0 | 1 |

Splitting the same argument bytes across different stream deltas must produce identical totals. Consuming both the event stream and its final result must count the response once. A Prometheus scrape should expose only the specified labels and counts.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance.

A managed Git plugin declaring an OpenClaw host peer was quarantined during startup after a host update. Maintenance repaired its host peer symlink in place, but the ensuing `plugins.reload` failed during prepare with the original `missing-openclaw-peer-link` diagnostic. The plugin remained unloaded; the plugin update step reported failure.

Source verification on main `072481c1683c56a692ce602cfeadfa1b963cd29f`: startup preflight records the finding in process-local state. `loader-runtime-candidate.ts` returns the stored diagnostic for an enabled candidate at the same root before attempting to load it. Its clear-after-load path applies only to a different root. The repair changes the payload, not the path.

Expected: explicitly reloading the repaired target re-verifies its owned payload and allows activation without restarting the Gateway. A still-invalid target must remain unavailable; unrelated quarantined plugins must not be released.

Related: #204156 / #204189 address host-link repair after update; #205567 addresses an unrelated plugin vetoing a lifecycle operation. This report concerns recovery of the explicitly targeted plugin *after* its files have been repaired. Incident reported on macOS arm64, 2026.11.8 → 2026.11.10; current-main verification so far is source-level.

issues.body:
**Status: feature proposal filed for maintainer review.** This issue covers M01, a local planning ID rather than a GitHub issue number. Bounded live tracker searches did not identify an equivalent implementation; that is not proof of absence. A private opt-in implementation is being prepared from the source revision recorded below. Its placement, preference contract, initial client and locale remain proposals pending maintainer acceptance.

Companion: `PR description draft` (companion specification). Shared contracts: `architecture` (companion specification), `stacking plan` (companion specification), `validation plan` (companion specification).

## Summary

Add an optional punctuation and capitalization transform to the shared intelligent-dictation pipeline. A user should be able to speak ordinary prose and receive readable text while retaining exactly the intended facts, numbers, negation, names and literal strings. The transform must also handle already punctuated provider output without doubling punctuation or changing existing intentional formatting.

## Problem to solve

This proposal is about producing the user's text. It does not change how the conversational agent answers, and a spoken word such as “period” must not become an application action. It must be possible to select verbatim output, inspect the prepared text and undo the resulting insertion through the insertion owner. The problem is especially visible in mixed technical prose, where a sentence-ending period and the dots in a version, hostname or decimal must be treated differently.

## Proposed solution

### Scope and relationship to adjacent work

The shared `M11 refinement pipeline` (companion specification) owns provider calls, deadlines, cancellation, result validation and publication. This issue adds a punctuation policy and validation rules inside that owner. `M04` (companion specification) owns paragraph/list structure; `M08` (companion specification) owns code and identifier syntax; `P03` (companion specification) supplies explicit spelling and casing. `M10` (companion specification) owns the final text write.

No second speech recognizer, parallel rewrite request, hidden transcript database, clipboard manager or application automation is introduced. Translation, summarization, grammatical paraphrasing, sentiment changes, automatic spelling correction and alteration of text predating this dictation session are excluded. A UI may expose these capabilities together later, but their semantic boundaries and tests must remain separate.

### Required behavior

1. Provide **Verbatim**, **Automatic**, and **Explicit punctuation** policies. Verbatim leaves recognizer-provided punctuation and casing alone; it is not a promise to recover the exact acoustic transcript. Automatic improves only punctuation/casing. Explicit punctuation interprets supported spoken punctuation phrases in an expressly enabled grammar.
2. Apply a resolved locale and document it in the result metadata. An explicit per-session locale wins over an enabled application profile, then the user's saved preference. A provider language hint may help recognition but must not silently select a different formatting locale after capture starts.
3. Preserve lexical tokens except narrowly specified casing changes and recognized punctuation commands. Do not turn “fifteen” into “15,” change units, expand abbreviations, guess people, or insert an unstated date. Preserve sentence fragments when a title, search box, code field or selected profile calls for fragments.
4. Detect protected ranges before punctuation changes: literal mode, code spans, URLs, email addresses, paths, version strings, decimal numbers, account/reference IDs and explicitly cased dictionary entries. Do not split a protected range or append punctuation inside it.
5. When punctuation is ambiguous, return the least invasive valid candidate or retain recognizer output. Model confidence, if provided, is advisory; structural validation is mandatory. Never choose a fluent but semantically changed sentence merely because it scores higher.
6. Avoid punctuation drift on repeated processing. With the same input and effective policy, a validated result must not accumulate periods, quotes or spaces. Do not promise byte-identical model sampling; require structural idempotence and stable rendering of an accepted candidate.

#### Acceptance examples

Examples are authored fixtures, not measured model results. Exact capitalization expectations apply to the stated English profile only.

| Input and context | Required outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `please call tomorrow can you confirm` in ordinary prose | Sentence punctuation may produce `Please call tomorrow. Can you confirm?`; no added time or recipient. |
| `I do not authorize the transfer` | `I do not authorize the transfer.`; negation is preserved exactly. |
| `version 1.2.3 costs 3.50` with those strings protected | Punctuation may be added around the sentence; neither dotted value changes. |
| `The word period belongs here` in Automatic | Retain the lexical word `period`; do not treat every occurrence as a command. |
| `hello comma world period` in Explicit punctuation | `Hello, world.` if this grammar is enabled and unambiguous. |
| Already punctuated `Hello, world!` | Preserve one exclamation mark; no second terminal mark. |
| `iPhone API OpenClaw` with protected dictionary casing | Preserve those spellings and casing; do not title-case every word. |
| Dictating into the middle of an existing sentence | Use bounded surrounding context only when authorized; do not capitalize the first token unconditionally. |

Unsupported language-specific rules must be declared unavailable or fall back to preserving provider output. Passing English fixtures does not establish support for Arabic, Japanese or code-switched speech. Locale packs require separate golden examples reviewed by a speaker of that language.

### Processing contract and lifecycle

M11 should pass the immutable raw transcript, its revision, resolved policy, optional locale, protected ranges, authorized left/right text context and a target-class hint. The proposed transform result contains the candidate text, source-range edit map, effective locale, policy version, validation outcome and bounded reason codes. Proposed names are conceptual; implementation must reuse the accepted M11 types and repository conventions.

An edit map should distinguish inserted punctuation, deleted redundant punctuation and casing changes. Every edit must map to grapheme-safe boundaries and the correct transcript revision. Unicode's segmentation specification provides the reference for grapheme/word boundaries; language-aware punctuation still needs separate policy [source S2]. A source-map failure must reject the candidate rather than allow a best-effort write.

Streaming previews may change within the overlay, but punctuation revisions must not repeatedly overwrite an external application's field. A finalization barrier selects one validated final candidate. User edits, a cancelled capture, a target revision change, a new mode or a replaced session revoke the old candidate's eligibility to commit. Provider callbacks arriving later are discarded by the shared owner.

When right-side context is unavailable, do not remove or replace punctuation already in the target. M10 can handle explicitly supported spacing joins as a separate validated insertion transaction. This feature must never infer authority to rewrite neighboring text from a screenshot or application name.

### Settings, data and migration

Recommended initial default: preserve current behavior for existing installations; expose Automatic as an opt-in intelligent-dictation setting, with Verbatim immediately accessible per session. Explicit punctuation is separately enabled. Profiles may choose fragment behavior or terminal punctuation, but must not create their own transform implementation.

Store only policy preferences by default. Raw transcripts, audio, before/after text and protected terms do not become telemetry or persistent history through this feature. The configuration must have a version, reject unknown enum values clearly and retain unknown future fields only if the repository's config owner already supports that behavior. Do not invent an unsafe catch-all compatibility path.

Changing policy while recording applies to the next session unless the user explicitly requests reprocessing of the current unsent draft. Reprocessing increments the preparation revision and invalidates the prior candidate; it cannot reinsert already committed text. Removing the feature setting restores previous behavior without deleting unrelated voice configuration.

### Failure, accessibility and performance requirements

The user must always retain the recognized text if refinement fails. The overlay should say whether text is raw or refined and offer an explicit insertion choice when refinement timed out; it must not display a successful refined state before validation. An undo action must address the insertion transaction, not send synthetic application-wide undo keys without a known target.

Keyboard and screen-reader users must be able to choose policy, review the result and recover after error without losing the original field. Live-region announcements should report meaningful state changes rather than every punctuation delta. Literal mode and unsupported locale states require text labels, not color alone.

Proposed, unmeasured budget: the deterministic punctuation validator should add no more than 25 ms at p95 for a 2,000-character final transcript on the chosen reference desktop. Record longer-input scaling and the reference hardware before treating this as a gate. Any model-assisted change shares M11's single total deadline and request budget; it must not add a second serial model round-trip simply to capitalize text. No performance result is claimed here.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **M01-AC01:** All three policies have distinct documented behavior; disabling the feature preserves the existing path.
- [ ] **M01-AC02:** Protected strings, numeric values, negation and dictionary casing survive positive and adversarial fixtures without semantic changes.
- [ ] **M01-AC03:** Already punctuated output remains structurally idempotent and contains no duplicated terminal punctuation.
- [ ] **M01-AC04:** Unsupported locales and absent context preserve raw output or surface an explicit limitation; they never silently apply English rules.
- [ ] **M01-AC05:** Every accepted edit has a valid source map; combining marks, emoji sequences and non-Latin text are never split.
- [ ] **M01-AC06:** Cancellation, user editing, target replacement and a newer transcript revision prevent late insertion.
- [ ] **M01-AC07:** Failures retain recoverable text, and the UI distinguishes raw from refined candidates.
- [ ] **M01-AC08:** Policy controls and result review work with keyboard and screen reader; user focus remains predictable.
- [ ] **M01-AC09:** Measured stage overhead and total latency are recorded against a named baseline without hiding provider latency.
- [ ] **M01-AC10:** Privacy, configuration migration and rollback tests show no new default transcript retention or cloud routing.

### Platform and offline boundary

The transform contract is independent of OS insertion. A desktop, web or mobile client may expose it only through its qualified M11 request/review path; external-field insertion still depends on M10. A headless caller receives a text/result value, not desktop control. Initial support must name actual tested clients and locales rather than imply universal availability.

Deterministic operations may continue offline when recognized text is already available. Model-assisted behavior follows the selected route and locality policy. If the required route is unavailable, retain available recognized text and disclose the missing refinement; do not silently use a cloud service. This does not promise offline speech recognition or recover words a recognizer never returned.

## Alternatives considered

Keeping recognizer punctuation only remains the Verbatim option, but does not provide consistent user-controlled punctuation across routes. Asking a general model to rewrite freely would broaden semantic risk beyond this feature. Separate client-specific punctuation engines would duplicate policy and produce inconsistent behavior; the shared M11 transform is preferred.

## Impact

Users would gain readable prose and an explicit literal escape without losing technical strings or meaning. The initial change would be opt-in, with no automatic provider change. The release burden is a locale/protected-span regression corpus and actual qualification of the clients that expose the shared policy.

## Evidence/examples

The examples are proposed acceptance fixtures. Implementation, regression, performance and live-client checks are **NOT RUN**. Tracker observations are bounded research, not proof that a capability is absent.

### Verification plan

Build a consented, synthetic golden corpus with separately labeled punctuation, casing and protected-range expectations. Include ambiguous comma placement, abbreviations, quote nesting, names, repeated punctuation, sentence fragments, decimals, negative numbers and speech containing literal instructions. Compare lexical invariants independently of prettiness. A model evaluator may propose disagreements, but human-reviewed expected invariants are the acceptance oracle.

Run the same corpus through raw, already punctuated and partial-to-final provider shapes. Introduce out-of-order responses and cancel at every await. Exercise a real target adapter with focus changed during finalization, proving no external write occurs. Test an actual microphone and the selected provider separately from deterministic fixtures; retain sanitized before/after evidence and report each provider/locale combination actually exercised. Screen-reader and physical-device evidence cannot be replaced by DOM snapshots.

### Sources and duplicate-search record

- **S1:** [OpenClaw issues: dictation punctuation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues?q=is%3Aopen+dictation+punctuation) and [PR search](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+dictation+punctuation), checked November 25, 2026. No direct match in the bounded query; repeat before filing.
- **S2:** [Unicode Standard Annex #29: Text Segmentation](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/), read November 25, 2026. Used only as the boundary reference; it does not prescribe this product's punctuation semantics.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself. A local task branch is being prepared from upstream b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c. No implementation PR has been published yet.

## Additional information

### Delivery sequence and open decisions

Land the M11 contract first. Add pure policy resolution and validators; integrate the transform in its existing refinement call; expose settings and preview labels; finally qualify one desktop adapter and one locale. Further locales should be additive and versioned. Rollback disables the transform while retaining raw text and the unchanged transcription path.

Recommended choices are conservative lexical preservation, explicit command grammar and an opt-in launch. Maintainers still need to select the supported first locales, reference hardware, configuration owner and whether punctuation-only refinement may use a model when a local deterministic path is unavailable. These decisions affect acceptance scope, not permission to bypass the shared authority or privacy model.

Suggested label: `enhancement`. Local IDs in this package are planning references, not GitHub issue numbers. The exact API/config names and implementation base require maintainer review; the intended behavior, defaults and outstanding decisions are documented above.


## Current source inspection and proposed first implementation

Inspected upstream `main` at `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c` on November 25, 2026. Live issue/PR searches across all states for dictation punctuation, dictation capitalization, intelligent dictation, and low-latency refinement did not identify an equivalent direct implementation. This is a bounded search, not proof of absence.

The existing Control UI owners `ComposerDictationSession`, `ComposerDictationCommits`, and `ComposerDictationOwner` already own capture, final drain, ordering, and insertion. The proposed implementation extends those owners with a private, revisioned preparation/result boundary and uses the existing insertion path. It will not create another speech client, provider queue, store, or agent turn. The existing default remains unchanged. A deterministic local `en-US` punctuation pack is the initial proposed scope, with explicit unsupported-locale fallback; no additional model round trip is proposed. All claimed client/locale qualification remains pending actual evidence.

The plugin SDK was considered: merged composer task work in #201898 and #202243 supports draft proposals and insertion, but it does not currently expose the microphone finalization/revision/protected-span boundary needed to satisfy this feature automatically without rewriting unrelated pre-existing draft text. A narrow private prototype is being prepared for review; no new public SDK or RPC contract is assumed accepted. Related open work #204107, #198845, #196063, and #204505 touches capture/recovery/controls and will not be copied or represented as this feature.

**Design decisions requested:** confirm initial Control UI composer / `en-US` scope, the refinement owner and plugin extension strategy, and the authoritative preference location before accepting new public configuration or SDK contracts. External application insertion remains owned by the separate M10 work; a browser-composer test is not native insertion proof. Real microphone/provider, screen-reader, native target, performance, and complete migration evidence will be recorded as PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, or NOT RUN at the actual tested head. The issue will remain open if any required criterion is unresolved.

## Summary

On 2026.9.6, `MEMORY.md` is not injected into the bootstrap context. `/context list` shows only AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, and USER.md as injected workspace files. The docs at /concepts/memory still describe MEMORY.md as "Loaded at the start of a session" with truncation over the bootstrap budget.

## Repro

- Two independent hosts, both on 2026.9.6, both reproduce.
- `MEMORY.md` exists in the workspace (~100 lines, well under the 20K per-file / 60K total bootstrap budgets).
- `plugins.entries.memory-core.enabled = true`; no `contextInjection` override set.
- `/context list` "Injected workspace files": AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, USER.md — MEMORY.md absent.

## Question

Intentional lazy-load change (per the direction in #67419, which proposed replacing MEMORY.md bootstrap injection with on-demand `memory_get`) or regression? Notably, #154923's description also enumerates the bootstrap set as SOUL/AGENTS/IDENTITY/USER without MEMORY.md.

Either way the docs at /concepts/memory need updating — they still promise session-start injection with truncation, and the truncation guidance ("raise the bootstrap limits") is now misleading.

## Expected (per docs)

MEMORY.md content present in the system prompt at session start, truncated if over budget.

## Actual

MEMORY.md absent from injected workspace files; recall only via memory_search/memory_get.

issues.body:
### Summary
If a card's `automation.workspace` points to a directory that does not exist, every run of the card dies at start with `FsSafeError: root dir not found`. The card ends up blocked, but the reason is not recorded on the card or the attempt, and nothing checks the path when the card is created.

### Version
OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f).

### Steps to reproduce
1. Create a card with `automation.workspace = { kind: "dir", path: "/existing/project/not-yet-created-folder" }`.
2. Dispatch it.
3. The gateway logs `lane task error: lane=workboard:<board>:<card> … error="root dir not found" errorName=FsSafeError taskKind=turn`, and the CLI backend logs `cli terminal failure … error=root dir not found`.
4. The attempt has no `error` text. The card is retried and then blocked, and its notifications do not mention the missing directory.

### Expected
One of:
- `workboard_create` / `specify` rejects a workspace path that does not exist, with a clear message to the creator;
- dispatch reports it as a start failure with the reason ("workspace directory does not exist: <path>") instead of starting a run;
- or the directory is created when it lies under an allowed workspace root.

Whichever is chosen, the error text should be stored on the attempt and in the card's failure notification, so automations and humans see the cause.

issues.body:
### Summary
After a failed run, the card keeps its claim until the claim TTL (30 min) expires. A card in that state that is moved back to `ready` is **silently skipped** by `workboard dispatch`: nothing starts, and no `startFailures` entry is returned.

### Version
OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f).

### Steps to reproduce
1. Start a card whose run fails right at start (for example, see the missing-workspace case in the related issue).
2. The card is blocked, but `metadata.claim` is still set with `expiresAt` about 30 minutes ahead.
3. `openclaw workboard move <id> --status ready`.
4. `openclaw workboard dispatch --board <board> --max-starts 1 --json` returns `"started": [], "startFailures": []`. The card does not start until the claim expires.

### Cause (reading the source)
In `selectStartableCards()` a card with an active claim gets the rejection "Card is already claimed by …", but in `scheduled` mode the rejection is only `continue`d. It is returned only in `exact` mode, so the caller never learns why the card was skipped.

### Expected
- The claim of a run that ended (failed or blocked) is released, or at least cleared when the card is moved back to `ready`/`todo`.
- In scheduled mode, a skipped `ready` card appears in `startFailures` with its reason.

### Workaround
`workboard.cards.reclaim` with `status: "ready"` clears the claim.

issues.body:
### Summary
A Workboard card in status `todo` **without parents** is never promoted to `ready`, so `workboard dispatch` never starts it. Cards with parents are promoted as soon as their parents are `done`, so the same card starts or does not start depending only on whether it has a parent.

### Version
OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), also seen on 2026.11.2.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Create a card on a board with an assignee, no parents, status `todo`.
2. Run `openclaw workboard dispatch --board <board> --max-starts 1 --json`.
3. Result: `"promoted": [], "started": []`. The card stays `todo` indefinitely.
4. `openclaw workboard move <id> --status ready`, then dispatch again: the card starts.

### Cause (reading the source)
`dependencyTargetStatus()` returns `card.status` when `parents.length === 0` (except for `scheduled`), so a parentless `todo` card never becomes `ready`. `selectStartableCards()` in scheduled mode only takes `ready` cards, so the card is silently skipped.

### Expected
Either a parentless `todo` card is treated like a card whose parents are all done (promoted to `ready`), or dispatch reports why it is not started, so an automation can tell the user.

### Impact
Automations that create a single follow-up card (for example a maintenance card) as `todo` see it never run, and nothing reports it.

issues.body:
## Summary

I reproduced an empty agent switcher when opening an unknown Control UI URL directly. The intended “Page not found” screen from #202399 appears, but the sidebar menu only offers “Create new agent”, even though two agents are configured.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the real Control UI build with a Gateway exposing two agents, Main and Research.
2. Navigate directly to `/c` in a fresh browser context, without visiting chat first.
3. Open the sidebar agent menu.

## Expected behavior

The 404 page and requested address stay in place, while the sidebar continues to offer the existing agents. #202399 intentionally preserves invalid links instead of silently opening an unrelated chat; it does not call for disabling sidebar navigation.

## Actual behavior and evidence

I tested main `8b3aa88a18ba5aa3378ea9cb79dbf6ae2e34498c` using the production Vite build in headless Chromium on Linux, with the repository's mock Gateway supplying two agents. On `/c?proof=missing#anchor`, the 404 page remains visible, the agent rows are empty, and `agents.list` has zero requests. I captured a screenshot of that state. A browser regression against the unchanged implementation fails because neither Main nor Research appears.

This is a real app build with synthetic Gateway data, not a recreated UI. A live Gateway was not tested.

## Cause

An unmatched URL has no route ID. Both `ShellGatewayOwner.synchronizeGateway()` and `ensureAgentsList()` in `ui/src/app/app-shell-gateway.ts` gate agent loading on a route ID, even though the sidebar is still rendered. The menu reads the unpopulated agent list.

Related: #202399. The requested fix should retain its 404 behavior.

## Environment

OpenClaw 2026.11.10 source build at the main commit above; Debian 12 container; Chromium 156. No model/provider calls are needed.

I reproduced this on main (`d8fc8b7`) with a local gateway and the real scheduler.

1. I created a scheduled job using `openai/MODEL@openai:retired`, then removed that account.
2. The job failed and suggested `openclaw models auth list`. While the gateway was running, that command exited 1 with “This command is offline-only”. `openclaw gateway call models.authStatus` worked.
3. I edited the broken job:
   ```sh
   openclaw automations edit JOB --model openai/gpt-4.1
   ```
   The command exited 0, but the next scheduled run still failed on the deleted account.
4. I created a fresh job with the same plain model. It ran successfully using the gateway’s existing static OpenAI key. Auth status showed `static`, with no saved profiles.
5. I also checked rebinding to `openai/gpt-4.1@openai:manual`. That worked immediately and on the next scheduled run.

I expect an explicit plain-model edit to let me recover a dead binding onto the configured static-key route, without recreating the job. I am not asking for automatic account switching when a credential disappears, or for ordinary model edits to discard valid bindings.

The recovery error should also point to a command that works while the gateway runs.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In Control UI chat, expanding a long fenced JSON block in the last message moves the activated block out of view instead of preserving the operator's visual position.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Control UI chat with a transcript whose last assistant message contains an 86-line fenced JSON block.
2. Leave the block collapsed as `79 hidden lines`.
3. Position the transcript 180 px from the end, with the disclosure visible near the bottom of the viewport.
4. Activate the disclosure with a mouse click or keyboard Enter.
5. Observe the activated block move above the viewport.

### Expected behavior

Opening the disclosure preserves its viewport position while reading. If the transcript is actually pinned to the end, it remains pinned to the new end.

### Actual behavior

Remote Chromium reproduction on commit 554dfbe0a2ce measured the disclosure at `top=547.8px`, `distanceFromEnd=180px` before activation and `top=-1016.2px`, `distanceFromEnd=6px` afterward. Keyboard activation produced the same result. From the true end, the transcript followed the new end but still moved the activated disclosure from `top=367.8px` to `top=-1016.2px`.

### OpenClaw version

main at 554dfbe0a2ce685dceaeb2a52a1647dfaf9493e6

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 remote Chromium

### Install method

Source checkout, mocked Control UI Gateway E2E

### Model

Not applicable; deterministic history fixture

### Provider / routing chain

Mock Gateway history response; no provider request

### Additional provider/model setup details

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

```shell
[code-block-anchor] mouse-180 {"before":{"distanceFromEnd":180,"scrollTop":1104,"top":547.796875},"after":{"distanceFromEnd":6,"scrollTop":2668,"top":-1016.203125}}
[code-block-anchor] keyboard-180 {"before":{"distanceFromEnd":180,"scrollTop":1104,"top":547.796875},"after":{"distanceFromEnd":6,"scrollTop":2668,"top":-1016.203125}}
[code-block-anchor] mouse-0 {"before":{"distanceFromEnd":0,"scrollTop":1284,"top":367.796875},"after":{"distanceFromEnd":6,"scrollTop":2668,"top":-1016.203125}}
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Crabbox AWS run `run_44f96fc0dc13`, lease `cbx_f272f056f229`, failed the new boundary assertions in all three scenarios on the current pre-fix source.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Control UI operators reading long assistant code blocks in the last chat message.
Severity: Annoying and disruptive; it loses reading context but does not lose data.
Frequency: 3/3 deterministic remote scenarios, covering mouse, keyboard, reading near the end, and true end-pinning.
Consequence: The operator must find the disclosure and reading position again after opening it.

### Additional information

The transcript uses TanStack Virtual with end anchoring. Its current row-size correction can classify the interaction from stale virtual geometry, then apply the full row-growth delta. CSS scroll anchoring is not a sufficient contract here because transformed virtual rows are a suppression trigger and browser support is not universal.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect state without a crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The Control UI forgets the selected sidebar owner/person filter after a page reload, including reloads associated with Gateway/server restarts.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Control UI with at least two session owners available.
2. Open **Filter & sort** and select one owner.
3. Restart the Gateway and wait for the browser to reconnect.
4. Reload the page.
5. Open **Filter & sort** again.

### Expected behavior

### Steps to reproduce

2. Place a unique tag into `MEMORY.md`.
3. Start a new, non-shared conversation.
4. Ask the agent to reproduce the tag without retrieving it through tools.
5. The agent is unable to reproduce the tag.

### Expected behavior

`MEMORY.md` content is automatically injected regardless of the selected harness, subject to [configuration overrides](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/config-agents/workspace-and-bootstrap).

`MEMORY.md` content is not automatically injected. The `memory_search` and `memory_get` tools remain available, as they are in the embedded harness.

Container

_No response_


_No response_

### Impact and severity

Affected: Codex App Server users, particularly OpenAI subscription users.

Severity: The agent is functional, but output quality is degraded.

Frequency: Always when memory tools are available.

Consequence: Memory becomes largely ineffective in practice. In my experience, agents rarely query memory on their own.

### Additional information

Regarding documentation: general OpenClaw documentation ([Memory](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/memory), [Memory architecture](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/memory-architecture)) states that `MEMORY.md` is automatically injected into eligible sessions. [Documentation specific to Codex App Server](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/codex-harness-reference/workspace-bootstrap-files) states that it is an exception. This option (or an equivalent option controlling injection rather than creation) should be used instead of hardcoding an exception for Codex App Server.

issues.body:
### What happened

On OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), `sessions_history` can return `contentTruncated: true` and `droppedMessages: false` for a short final assistant message whose visible text is intact. The installed implementation's `sanitizeHistoryMessage` sets the same truncation boolean when deleting top-level `details`, `usage`, or `cost` as it does when shortening a text field. Fetching one message at a time therefore does not clear this flag.

### Minimal reproduction

1. In a test conversation with a provider that records usage, ask for a short plain-text reply such as “Reply with hello”.
2. From an authorized agent, read the reply with `sessions_history` (`includeTools: false`, `limit: 1`, anchored by message ID if needed).
3. For an assistant record with top-level `usage`, the tool can report `contentTruncated: true` even though “hello” is fully present, without the truncation marker. A unit fixture can use `{ role: "assistant", content: [{ type: "text", text: "hello" }], usage: { output: 1 } }` to avoid provider dependencies.

### Expected behavior

Keep stripping metadata, but distinguish that from shortened visible text in the result (for example, separate `metadataOmitted` and `visibleTextTruncated` fields, preserving the old aggregate flag if compatibility requires it). Add separate tests for a short message with usage metadata and a genuinely over-limit text block.

This matters for consumers like conversation scribes that need to decide whether they can safely checkpoint a history read. Small pages help with the separate response-size cap in #22920 but do not resolve this ambiguity.

issues.body:
### Summary

On stable **2026.10.7**, background `exec` completion wakes still fail the way #168637 describes. #177063 fixed this on `main` on 2026-10-19, but the change isn't in `v2026.10.7` or `v2026.10.10-beta.3`. The installed `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-cache-publication-state` still gates settings on any pending sharing publication: `readGenerationSettings: () => active && !pending(true) ? … : void 0`.

Two gaps also remain on `main` after #177063:

1. **A failed wake is never retried.** `session-event-handoff` only readmits a session event after a config-publication change (`MAX_CONFIG_READMISSION_ATTEMPTS = 2`). `SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE` says "retry after session storage is ready", but the handoff calls `ownership.cancel()`. The exec notifier then only logs `completion delivery failed`, so the completion notice is lost and the user sees a failed turn.
2. **Model fallback runs a candidate that can't succeed.** `prepareAgentRunAdmission` latches `sourceFailure`, so the fallback candidate fails in about 30 ms with "source execution authority is no longer active". The log reads like a model failure (`candidate_failed … next=opencode/…`) instead of a lifecycle or authority failure.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (npm global), Linux VPS, Gateway running as a systemd user service. Primary model `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` on the `claude-cli` runtime, fallback `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash`. Sessions come from the Control UI dashboard and Slack threads. `exec` runs with `notifyOnExit`.

### Observed (2026-10-26 UTC)

5 of about 20 event-triggered wakes failed in one day. Each one started a turn that died about 0.2 s into preparation, and the completion notice was dropped.

| Wake failed | Session | Previous turn in same session ended | Session-row write during preparation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15:57:24.9 | dashboard | 4.5 min earlier | none logged (likely run-start bookkeeping) |
| 18:46:26.5 | dashboard | 1.4 s earlier | Control UI `sessions.patch` at 18:46:26.045 |
| 19:05:15.5 | Slack thread | 40 s earlier | Control UI `sessions.patch` at 19:05:15.177 |
| 19:47:31.3 | dashboard | 1.4 s earlier | Control UI `sessions.patch` at 19:47:30.759 |
| 21:35:19.5 | dashboard | 1.2 s earlier | none logged (turn-end bookkeeping; that turn followed a `prompt-tools` CLI session reset after config revision 40) |

Three of the five fired right after another turn in the same session settled. All five match #168637: a session-row publication lands inside the wake's preparation window.

```text
19:47:29.930 [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=1705663
19:47:30.759 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ sessions.patch 87ms bytes=18779
19:47:31.300 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:dashboard:<id> durationMs=228 error="admitted run authority is no longer active | Session delivery generation is unavailable; retry after session storage is ready. | SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE"
19:47:31.322 [model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 reason=unknown next=opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash detail=admitted run authority is no longer active
19:47:31.454 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested durationMs=24 error="source execution authority is no longer active | Session delivery generation is unavailable; retry after session storage is ready. | SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE" taskKind=turn
19:47:31.469 Embedded agent failed before reply: source execution authority is no longer active | …
19:47:31.480 [session-events] session event execution failed source=exec agentId=main sessionKey=agent:main:dashboard:<id> error="Session event execution failed"
19:47:31.481 [exec] completion delivery failed (Session event execution failed); inspect the process result.
```

### Repro conditions

- `claude-cli` runtime, background `exec` with `notifyOnExit`.
- The completion arrives while another turn in the same session is running or just settling, or while the Control UI has that session open and sends `sessions.patch`.
- The settled-foreground fixture in #168637 reproduces it on code without #177063.

### Ask

1. Backport #177063 to the stable 2026.10.x line.
2. Treat `SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE` as retryable in `session-event-handoff`: readmit with a bound once `prepareRead()` settles, as is already done for config changes. Or fall back to a passive system event so the next turn still sees the completion. Revoked or permission-restricted cases should keep failing closed.
3. Skip model fallback for latched admission or authority failures.

issues.body:
### Summary

For agents on the `claude-cli` runtime, an "allow always" decision on a native Claude Code tool (ToolSearch, Read, Skill, `mcp__*`) only lasts for the current CLI live session. A new CLI live session starts on every turn, so the grant is gone on the next turn and the same tool asks again. For runs with nobody to answer (cron jobs, scheduled briefings, subagents), every native tool call stalls on an approval prompt.

#69512 was closed with "please open a fresh issue if approval prompts alone don't meet your needs on a current release". This is that case.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an agent whose model resolves to `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"` (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`), exec `security: "allowlist"`, `ask: "on-miss"`.
2. Turn 1: the model calls `ToolSearch` (or an MCP tool). Answer the approval with "allow always".
3. Turn 2 in the same OpenClaw session: the model calls the same tool.
4. Run the same agent from cron.

### Expected behavior

- "Allow always" persists for the OpenClaw session (agent + session key + session id), not for a CLI live session that is recreated per turn.
- A way to let unattended runs use non-mutating native tools without a human, while `Bash` and file-editing tools (`Write`, `Edit`, `MultiEdit`, `NotebookEdit`) stay gated by the exec policy.

### Actual behavior

- Turn 2 asks again. In our logs: `[agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli …` on every turn; before a local workaround we counted 54 approval prompts over 54 claude-cli turns in one day, the same MCP tool asked 24 times, answered "always" every time.
- Cron runs stall on the prompt.

In 2026.11.10 the handler (`createPluginToolPermissionHandler`) stores grants in `getCliLiveSessionApprovalGrants(context) ?? grants`, and the allow condition is `plan === "allow" || policy.ask !== "always" && grants.has(toolName)`.

### Workaround we run

A local dist patch: grants kept per agent+sessionKey+sessionId for the gateway process lifetime, and native tools other than Bash/Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit allowed without a prompt when `ask !== "always"`. `security=deny`, `ask=always` and `before_tool_call` hooks keep working. We re-anchor it on every release, which is why we'd prefer a supported setting.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), stable channel, npm global install
- Linux (Ubuntu 24.04), systemd user service
- Model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 via `agentRuntime.id: claude-cli`

issues.body:
### Summary

When Google Search grounding returns no pages, the Gemini `web_search` provider still returns the model's text as `content` with `citations: []`. The agent can't tell this apart from a grounded answer: the schema has no field for it and models do not notice an empty array. The text is then repeated as "found on the web".

Over 30 days we saw this on 2 of 126 `web_search` results (~1.6%). One produced a hardware cost estimate based on list prices the search model made up, presented as search results.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `tools.web.search.provider: "gemini"`.
2. Ask the agent something grounding finds no pages for (niche or very recent query).
3. The tool result has `citations: []`; the agent answers as if the content came from search.

### Expected behavior

A zero-source answer is explicitly marked, for example a `grounded: false` / `sourceCount: 0` field in the payload, or a short notice prefixed to `content` when `citations` is empty, so the agent treats it as unverified model knowledge.

### Actual behavior

`executeGeminiSearch` in `extensions/google/src/gemini-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` returns `{ content, citations }` unchanged when `groundingChunks` is empty (current main and 2026.11.10).

### Workaround we run

A local dist patch prefixes `content` with a one-line `[NO SOURCES: … unverified …]` notice when `citations.length === 0`.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), npm global install, Linux
- Provider: gemini (`generativelanguage.googleapis.com`), model gemini-4-hydrogen
