issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On 2026.10.8, the first compaction in an agent database triggers the first memory index publication. That publication creates the memory FTS tables. The gateway's main connection then observes a schema change, and the schema-mutation listener of every live session delivery generation lease sets invalidated = true. Nothing clears that flag, so:

1. An exec-completion (event-woken) run that performs the first compaction fails right after the summary is committed, with admitted run authority is no longer active | Session delivery generation is unavailable; retry after session storage is ready. | SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE.
2. Exec-completion notices queued behind a compacting run are dropped with completion delivery failed (SessionDeliveryGenerationUnavailableError ...) and never retried. If nothing else wakes the session, it stops silently while its status still reads done.

Only the first compaction is affected. Later compactions in the same database do not change the schema and work normally.

#196724 says the invalidating producer behind these refusals is unknown. This report identifies one producer. It is the same class as #189020 (first-use DDL revoking prepared state), with a different owner.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start from a fresh agent database with memory-core enabled. Do not run any memory command, so the database has no memory_index_*_fts* tables yet.
2. In the main session, start a background exec with exit notification, and keep the run busy until the notice is queued.
3. Push the context over the window so that the first compaction happens while the notice is queued. Alternatively, let the notice wake a run that overflows and compacts.
4. Watch the gateway log.

Lowering the model's contextWindow makes step 3 quick.

These steps summarise my experiments on long-running sessions.

### Expected behavior

- A schema change that only adds tables unrelated to session rows should not permanently revoke delivery leases. The lease could re-read its entry and continue when the session id and lifecycle revision are unchanged.
- Failing that, the memory FTS tables could be created when the agent database is bootstrapped, so that no DDL runs at first compaction.
- A wake refused with SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE should be retried, as its message says (the open half of #185085).

### Actual behavior

Event-woken run performing the first compaction: the compaction summary is written, then the run fails 0.7 to 1.9 s after the compaction entry is committed. compactionCount stays 0. The session id and lifecycle revision are unchanged. Every notice queued behind it is dropped.

User-triggered run performing the first compaction: the run survives, but notices queued behind it are dropped and never retried.

After a failure, sending one more user message resumes the session normally.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.8

### Operating system

Linux (x86_64 container)

### Install method

npm global, Node 24.22.2

### Model

an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions model with a 256K context window. The failure does not depend on the model.

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> custom openai-completions provider -> self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway -> model

### Additional provider/model setup details

Gateway (openclaw gateway run) plus a TUI client on the main session.
SQLite agent database, memory-core enabled, no embedding provider configured (FTS only), dreaming disabled.
agents.defaults.compaction.midTurnPrecheck.enabled = false.
Long coding tasks that start background exec commands and are woken by their completion notices.

### Logs

```shell
[context-overflow-diag] ... source=assistantError trigger=overflow ...
context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction
[compaction-diag] end ... trigger=overflow attempt=1 maxAttempts=3 outcome=failed reason=unknown detail=admitted_run_authority_is_no_longer_active_Session_delivery_generation_is_unavailable_... durationMs=208668
lane task error: lane=cron-nested ... error="admitted run authority is no longer active | Session delivery generation is unavailable; retry after session storage is ready. | SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE"
Embedded agent failed before reply: admitted run authority is no longer active | ...
completion delivery failed (SessionDeliveryGenerationUnavailableError: ...); inspect the process result.   (repeated for every queued notice)
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

_No response_

### Additional information

Run openclaw memory index --agent main once before starting the gateway. On a fresh state directory this takes 7 to 9 s and creates the same tables.

issues.body:
### Summary

Add a supported, targeted way to list and retire one stranded requester settle wake (a `subagent_runs` row whose `requesterSettleWake` keeps retrying without ever settling), without editing the state database by hand. This is the operator recovery part of #154252 ("a supported operator command for this would be valuable on its own"). It is separate from bounding the retry (the closed #158518) and from the owner-changed diagnostic in #164529, and is still needed after both, because rows that are already stranded stay stranded.

### Problem to solve

A completed subagent run can keep a durable `requesterSettleWake` that never settles. The reported state shape (#154252, observed on 2026.9.4, same code in 2026.9.5):

```
subagent_runs.payload_json
  execution.status            terminal
  endedReason                 subagent-killed (killReconciliation set)
  expectsCompletionMessage    true
  delivery.status             pending
  requesterSettleWake.status  dispatching
  requesterSettleWake.attemptCount  3   (= REQUESTER_SETTLE_WAKE_MAX_ATTEMPTS)
  matching task_runs row      purged by cleanupAfter
```

A second report on #154252 (2026.9.6) shows `requesterSettleWake = {status: "dispatching", attemptCount: 1, batchRunIds: [<own run>], requesterYieldBatch: true, rearmGeneration: 1}`, `delivery.status = "pending"`, `cleanupHandled = true`, and `requester settle wake failed ... subagent completion owner changed before settlement: <runId>` about once per minute per run, surviving a Gateway restart.

On #154252 the only recovery that worked was deleting the `subagent_runs` rows directly; the reporter found no supported RPC or CLI for it. No producer of these states is established on current main (#159612, the owner-changed variant, is closed), but the rows are durable and survive upgrades, so a database that already holds one needs a recovery path regardless.

What current main (`c5b1c315d05`) offers:

- `cancelRequesterSettleWake` (`src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-lifecycle-wake.ts:148`) can retire a terminal wake: it sets `suppressCompletionDelivery` and clears `requesterSettleWake`. It returns without retiring the wake of a `sessions_yield` member (`:154`).
- It is reached only through session-wide stops that pass `suppressTaskDelivery: true`: `/reset` (`stopSessionResetSubagents`, `src/auto-reply/reply/session-reset-cleanup.ts:108`, calls `killSessionSubagentRuns`, `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control-kill.ts:543`) and abort (`src/auto-reply/reply/abort-operation.ts:247` and `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-descendants.ts:183`, both call `killAllControlledSubagentRuns`). These act on the requester session's whole child selection, so retiring one stranded row also stops the other running children, and `/reset` also starts a fresh conversation.
- The per-run kill path `killSubagentRunAdmin` is reached from the `subagents` tool `cancel` action (`src/agents/tools/subagents-tool.ts:398`), `src/gateway/session-kill-http.ts:116` and `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-abort-runtime.ts:144`. None of them passes `suppressTaskDelivery`, so none enters the wake cancellation branch (`src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-control-kill-runtime.ts:133`).
- `doctor` state integrity (`src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.ts`) reports wedged subagent recovery sessions but has no check for a retained `requesterSettleWake`.

So an operator cannot list stranded wakes, and cannot retire one without stopping or resetting the whole requester session (which still does not retire the wake of a `sessions_yield` member) or editing SQLite.

### Proposed solution

A Doctor check with an explicit, per-run fix:

1. Detect (default, read-only): list `subagent_runs` rows whose `requesterSettleWake` is present on a terminal run, with run id, requester session key, wake status, `attemptCount`, `nextAttemptAt`, age, `batchRunIds`, `rearmGeneration`, delivery status, and whether a captured result exists. Rank by stored `attemptCount` and age, since the per-episode failure count is in memory only.
2. Retire one row, named by run id, through the running Gateway using the same ownership-checked mutation `cancelRequesterSettleWake` already uses, never as a direct SQLite write from the Doctor process. Keep the `rearmGeneration` and `batchRunIds` checks, so a stale listing fails closed with the existing "changed during cancellation; retry" rejection. Leave every other child of the requester untouched.
3. Make the outcome explicit: the captured outcome and result stay on the row, but `suppressCompletionDelivery` means the requester never receives this child's result. Print that, and require explicit confirmation (or `--yes`) before retiring.
4. Handle `sessions_yield` cohort members explicitly: retire the whole cohort together or refuse with a reason, rather than skipping silently.

### Alternatives considered

- Bounding the dispatching retry by count: #158518 tried this in the admission path and was closed because it discards completions behind a pending requester turn or an unspent ambiguous replay. A bound also does nothing for rows that are already stranded.
- `/stop` or `/reset` of the requester session: stops the other running children (and `/reset` also resets the conversation) to retire one row, and does not retire the wake of a `sessions_yield` member.
- An automatic clear of retained wakes, the direction of #166267: that covers markers kept after a successful delivery, not rows that can never settle because their stored state is rejected.
- Deleting `subagent_runs` rows by hand: unsupported, bypasses the ownership checks and the in-memory registry of a running Gateway, and loses the captured result.

### Impact

- Affected: requester sessions holding a subagent completion whose settle wake cannot settle (#154252 and the 2026.9.6 report on it).
- Severity: blocks workflow; the wake keeps retrying and logging until someone edits the database.
- Frequency: edge case, but persistent once entered; it survives restarts and upgrades.
- Consequence: manual SQLite edits on a live state database, or a session-wide stop or reset that interrupts unrelated work.

### Evidence/examples

- #154252: state shape, logs, and "Only recovery found: Deleting the orphaned `subagent_runs` rows directly".
- The triage review on #154252 includes in its best solution: "provide an in-product Doctor or Fix recovery path for already stranded batches".
- Source references above are at `c5b1c315d05`.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Related: #154252, #164529, #159612, #166267, #155163 (retirement of failed deliveries after the task record is pruned, a different state).

issues.body:
**Summary**

The bundled `deep_research` portable engine replaces the real error of two failure paths with generic strings, and drops the original error object entirely. A provider timeout, an auth failure, a tool-policy refusal and a model refusal all surface as the same two sentences, so the job reports `status: partial` with no usable cause.

**What the operator sees**

```
## Unresolved
- Search unavailable: <query>
- The model did not produce a complete response.
```

**Where it happens**

In the portable engine (bundled `stock:deep-research`, shipped as `dist/portable-tool-*.mjs`):

search path:

```js
try{const e=await t.search(r,i);current();n.push(...e.map(e=>e.url))}catch{current();c.push(`Search unavailable: ${r}`)}
```

model path:

```js
try{n=await t.complete(e,i)}catch{current();throw new ModelUnavailable(`The model did not produce a complete response.`)}
```

Both `catch` blocks take **no error parameter**, so the thrown error is unreachable. The *fetch* path in the same module already does it correctly:

```js
catch(e){current();c.push(`Source unavailable: ${r} (${e instanceof Error?e.name:`error`})`)}
```

So the module has the pattern — the search and model paths simply don't use it.

**Reproduction**

OpenClaw OpenClaw OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f), `deep_research` with `engine: portable`, model `minimax/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`, request budget `{searches: 2, fetches: 2, modelCalls: 3}`, one question, no `sources`:

- result: `status: partial`, `findings: []`, and one of the two generic gap strings above.

Across 9 runs on one gateway the search path failed in 2 runs and the model path in 4 runs.

**Underlying cause of the model failures** (from the gateway log, subsystem `provider-transport-fetch`):

```
[model-fetch] error provider=minimax api=anthropic-messages model=MiniMax-M3 elapsedMs=59997 name=LlmIdleTimeoutError
```

The same gateway logged 42 such errors in one day (38 in cron-triggered runs at elapsed ~60 s, 4 in interactive sessions at ~120 s) — see the separate report on the idle timeout not being configurable.

**Impact**

Automation cannot alert on the real cause. `status: partial` with "no source-backed findings" looks like a research-quality problem rather than an infrastructure problem, and the retry logic cannot distinguish "retry may help" from "the tool is not available".

**Requested fix**

Preserve the original error in the gap entry (at least the error name, ideally `code: message`), the way the fetch path does, and expose the raw error in the job result (e.g. a `diagnostics` array). With that, the timeout above would read:

```
- The model did not produce a complete response. (LlmIdleTimeoutError: no response from model)
```

Related but different: #205440 (research duration ceiling) is the *budget*; this is the model-call timeout.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid the Windows boot probe stall at startup
prs.body:
Related: #171831 (one reproduced startup stall; not the minute-scale report).

## What Problem This Solves

On some Windows hosts, the Gateway stops responding for about five seconds as it marks its listener ready. A Windows boot-time lookup can hit its timeout; today the Gateway waits synchronously for it while holding the SQLite writer.

## User Impact

The Gateway can keep processing its event loop while Windows answers the boot-time query. A timeout still leaves boot provenance unavailable. No config, schema, permissions or persisted provenance format changes. This does not claim to resolve the longer startup or per-turn delay in #171831.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the optional Windows boot provenance asynchronously alongside owner-heartbeat startup, before listener publication. Keep the same OS query, deadline and strict validation as the synchronous handoff reader; retain the existing checks and guarded SQLite write when publishing the listener receipt.

## Proof

- [Windows baseline and causal trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/171831#issuecomment-7185158463): on Windows ARM64 build 26340, both fresh stable runs and both packaged main runs saw one 5.01–5.03 s main-thread `state.startup-checkpoint.write`. An independent instrumented main run attributed 5.014 s to `powershell.exe` timing out in the boot-identity call stack, with SQLite BEGIN/COMMIT each rounding to 0 ms. The issue reporter uses x64 build 26200.
- Focused tests passed: `pnpm test src/state/openclaw-agent-db-lease-provenance.test.ts src/infra/gateway-owner-lease.test.ts src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-identity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The new cases cover pending/success/timeout behavior, no repeated synchronous fallback, and byte-for-byte provenance compatibility. Author self-review and `git diff --check` passed.
- Exact-head Linux production build passed after a frozen dependency install.
- Exact-head packaged Windows replay: pending. Acceptance: zero synchronous CIM boot waits in the listener checkpoint, all fixture plugins loaded, and both real loopback Gateway turns complete on each fresh start.

## What Problem This Solves

The dashboard gallery E2E test can try to resolve a deferred session-list response before its request reaches the mock Gateway. [Scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45769333980/job/139738500061) failed in the light-mode empty-gallery case with `No deferred mock Gateway response for sessions.list`.

## User Impact

Makes the existing gallery checks wait for their fixture request before releasing its response. No product or visual change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loading skeleton can appear before the list request is sent. Use the existing `waitForRequest` helper with the same `hasBoard: true` scope as the deferral. Apply it to the first load, reload, and equivalent phone geometry setup; retain every loading, loaded, empty-state, and layout assertion. No new helper, sleep, retry, or production change.

## Evidence

- Base failure at `22be06d7d2fd4025f94b6e8c20405e9f3b268a2c`: the linked main job identifies the empty deferred queue at the reload's response release.

prs.title: fix(pr): retain equivalent reviewed workflows for baseline proof
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Initial baseline-proof preparation rejects a retained reviewed workflow whenever main advances, even when the complete workflow, dependency and policy inputs remain equivalent. This change admits that case without relaxing later publication or merge gates.

## User Impact

Maintainers can reuse an equivalent reviewed workflow for initial baseline proof while preserving authenticated ancestry, source identity, signed evidence and custody. This is maintainer tooling; it does not change the runtime product. No measured speedup or resolution of the macOS test deadlines is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Authenticate current main and compare complete workflow inventories, file types/modes, dependency/install inputs and runtime policy. Carry provenance through native context and signed baseline bindings. Reuse same-commit facts only within each check; preserve fresh admission boundaries.
- Validate custody and preparation inputs before retiring active evidence. Preserve pending-proof acceptance retirement and qualified-baseline rejection. Keep the selected workflow's dependency revision independent of bootstrap, including creator reentry and unbound commands.
- Integrate frozen main `107c145f25d0edee99b830f7ef38486641d769de`, preserving verified-bootstrap completion and expansion order alongside workflow proof verification. Keep main's bounded invocation-local captured-byte hash reuse and exact-byte collision check, while retaining fresh authority reads. Retain main's native Git captured-byte stdin hashing, `--no-filters`, conditional object writes and no-spill ownership. The proposed descriptor batching was removed. Replay, signatures and FD7/8/9 custody retain their existing owners.
- Keep the private fixture adapter's fresh ordered ref reads and remove both the standalone adapter-only suite and lifecycle query-count instrumentation. The final cleanup removes 73 test lines while preserving all 27 native calls, publication/replay outcomes, signed OIDs, receipt bytes and transport-authority refusals.
- Exercise historical six-field signed-proof records through current native consumers, with the optional field absent before signing. Preserve binding/signature identity, retained bytes and tamper refusals. This qualifies a historical format through current code, not an old released binary. Correct operation-scoped archive assertions, custody injection and the creator-reentry FD9 oracle without weakening assertions or deadlines.

- Add a deterministic initial `prepare-baseline-refresh --for-proof` regression where the first locked qualification fetch advances main from M1 to its equal-tree child M2. Keep the reviewed workflow W, requested baseline M1, signed source+M1 parents, captured/admitted M2 and exact archived review/publication receipt bytes. The same focused proof retains strict dependency-drift refusal and unqualified-audit fallback. This does not qualify a real dependency change merely because workflow identity is preserved.

The authored difference from frozen main is **20 files**: production **+739/-328 (net +411)**, tests **+1279/-237**, docs **+28/-5**, inventory **+17**, and a three-line allocation record. Production growth owns workflow equivalence, sealed provenance, validation before retirement and consolidated dependency/materialization accounting. The native staged test-line ratchet passed: **1023 eligible net lines = 400 allowance + 623 allocation**, with no extra credit. The separate `.mjs` fixture explains the difference from test numstat. Allocation does not waive proof or review.

## Evidence

Current signed merge commit: `2e776d862cffe526f12c85eb46839b715f297d2d`; tree `fc13c6d96f1128db577e6ea2da82cb5235ca4f9e`; parents `bee3ec8f3b32db2d99f309bdcffe4687b28d4919` and frozen main `107c145f25d0edee99b830f7ef38486641d769de`. The conflict resolution combines the shared hash probe's captured-input/call-sequence behavior with lifetime-FD checks, fault injection and native Git forwarding. It changes no production behavior beyond the preserved upstream integration.

Focused integration proof at this exact tree passed **29/29 cases and all three static checks** on **Linux x64, Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0 and Vitest 5.0.5**, using normal Blacksmith Testbox. Coverage: captured hashes **13/13**, snapshot hashes **8/8**, actual-write refresh **4/4**, and initial workflow admission **4/4**; 72 other cases in the latter two files were intentionally unselected. Targeted format, tooling test types and lint passed. All case deadlines and assertions were unchanged. The receiver verified source `bee3ec8f`, full raw tree `fc13c6d9`, transport base `181656c5` and fresh selected-source dependencies; the later signed commit has that exact tree. The transport base and synthetic carrier are not the integration target. All children settled, source was preserved and the exact lease was released. [Testbox workflow 45573394084](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45573394084) may show cancelled after normal cleanup; proof is the successful native exit and collected results. Result archive SHA-256: `1e647e0203275d5184de0192324eaf932d0aab362e55ca64f644338556c76634`. This Testbox result is focused Node-only proof; current hosted qualification is reported below.

Historical `bee3ec8f` focused proof passed **4/4 admission cases plus format/types/lint**, including locked-fetch advancement, static-main advancement, real dependency-drift refusal and unqualified-audit fallback. Result JSON SHA-256: `705d0b4448a6cf18c7081315a64b8eeb5d1cd597959ace5c72a079c057dc7a67`; [Testbox workflow 45571126572](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45571126572). Its [CI 45572097815](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45572097815) failed preflight before target tests: the fetched PR merge ref still named `fdd9ab4a` as its head parent while the requested checkout was `bee3ec8f`. The exact-head guard correctly refused that mismatch. The new integration preserves that guard; new dispatch waits for a matching server merge-ref parent.

Historical parent evidence follows and is not attributed to the new commit. At `fdd9ab4aee15fbbfe307be55940311784edfc4a4` (tree `853ccaef3f39e4c4c57b6d7f97ac207186352a7f`, parent `6dd41479d11142b3f213fd4cc1c4e26c7cf56c12`), the signed one-line backport matches merged [PR #202401](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202401): remove only `export` from the internal Gateway token issuer. Its body, public preparation/completion, tests and dependency inputs are unchanged. Independent scoped review accepted the exact patch; normal hooks and signature verification passed.

[Dual-runtime CI 44924189700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44924189700) completed **SUCCESS on 2026-11-21 at 16:59:36 UTC: 41 successful jobs, zero failed, 31 skipped**. Checkout and workflow control were exactly `fdd9ab4aee15fbbfe307be55940311784edfc4a4`. Comparison base `a81218e17a0bed096972ea4b47de9eba62fb72fd` and synthetic merge ref `4cfe58c7117ff31bc39923906973f89bace832db` are CI comparison inputs, not new source integration. prs.title: feat(dictation): propose shared dictionaries for design review
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205633.

Teams need an explicitly selected shared vocabulary without publishing personal dictionary entries or treating a known collection ID as authorization. The existing transcription-provider prompt setting does not supply collection membership, revision ownership, or per-utterance source provenance.

**Design-review draft: M06 is incomplete and the issue must remain open.** This PR presents the prerequisite proposal and its observed evidence for the required owner/design decision. It does not enable a production shared-dictionary capability or claim acceptance of its proposed permission, persistence, retention, or public contracts.

## User Impact

There is no enabled shared-dictionary user flow. The proposal provides reviewable validation/resolution, scoped collection operations, immutable snapshot leases, and an optional guard at the existing Talk publication boundary. Existing personal records are not migrated or written. No new audio retention, automatic replay, recognizer, or provider route is introduced.

Every client and provider remains unqualified for this shared-vocabulary feature. Collection selection/management, visible source/conflict inspection, accessible recovery, live provider disclosure, and full P03/M11 integration are still required. The proposed mid-utterance revocation semantics need an explicit owner decision against the existing admitted-request policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collection operations use the existing action-bound V2 worker-store interface, with injected host authority and expected-revision CAS. Real retained-worker tests now cover two editors, atomic malformed-import rejection, tombstones after orderly close/reopen, final commit-admission refusal, and an exact 400-KiB/5,000-term draft with the full audit ring. Those grants are synthetic; no production collection namespace, membership mapping, public RPC/UI, or provider capability is registered.

The proposed representation, retained tombstones, 32-event private audit ring, scope/visibility rules, and rollback/retention contract require the recorded design acceptance in #205633 before production wiring. Unknown versions are preserved and rejected. The current unregistered proposal migrates no existing data. An eventual rollout/rollback must be implemented and qualified by the accepted store owner. M11 remains the intended sole request/result coordinator.

The commits separate term/budget foundations, collection operations, snapshot/relay boundaries, and qualification evidence. No reviewed physical P03/M11 parent was identified. The internal term/resolution contract is a proposed minimal P03 prerequisite, not a completed personal-dictionary feature. Optional management placement should be decided through the existing plugin/SDK boundary. #191109 is adjacent provider-hint transport, not a stack parent or closing target.

Source and merge base: `04b854b239cd8ab8a14beae4914ed9c54d791e62`. Target: `openclaw/openclaw:main`, observed at `954928a0bf1c1dc72ab43152f62a7c15577815a7`. Head: `CompleteDotTech:feat/dictation-shared-dictionaries` at `70bac82c4c24bded28615002d52701940ee3494a`, tree `eb08efeb6faff3e688b0bca3a09e9b9e9e78aa03`. The original four commits were published through the authenticated GitHub connection with each complete tree verified equal to the saved local commits; only metadata changed. The final qualification commit adds the real-worker proof, exact existing test-lane registrations, explicit synchronous benchmark GC, and updated evidence. The earlier fork-local review is https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/pull/1; this upstream draft owns continuing design review.

## Evidence

Full owner/procedure/AC mapping and benchmark methodology are in [the committed experiment record](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/blob/70bac82c4c24bded28615002d52701940ee3494a/docs/experiments/shared-dictation-vocabulary.md). A validation receipt binds source hashes, commands, raw logs, original-to-published commit mapping, and historical results to the published head. Evidence below is self-reported local execution and independent automated source review, not maintainer acceptance or CI success.

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Complete physical dependency install | PASS: frozen lockfile, pinned pnpm 12.15.0, 215 workspaces; supply-chain check passed for 1,764 entries. |
| Standard vocabulary behavior | 39 passing cases across three files. Their initial combined unit-src command also ran the new worker suite in an incompatible thread owner and failed setup; the corrected worker run is separate below. |
| Real retained-worker integration | PASS: 4 cases in the standard isolated-process infra lane, with compiled production runtime declarations and synthetic grants. |
| Existing and vocabulary Talk relay | PASS: 30 cases across two files in the existing aggregate Gateway configuration; 18 existing regressions and 12 vocabulary cases. Provider callbacks remain synthetic. |
| Runtime selection / file ownership | PASS: 51 existing selection tests and the separately selected complete file-ownership audit. The latter selected one case and filtered out 40. The broader project-config suite stalled after two passing cases and was stopped by its unchanged 120-second no-output watchdog (exit 143); it is not a full-suite pass. |
| Targeted static proof | PASS: canonical tooling test type leaf, type-aware scripts lint after the GC repair, syntax-only lint on all 14 changed TS/MTS/MJS files, formatting on 15 supported changed files, and test-line budget (+1,435 net, 400 allowance, 1,035 allocated for distinct boundaries/real worker proof). |
| Core static proof | BLOCKED: canonical core types exited 137; native type-aware core lint received SIGKILL. Other full core/test/script type graphs are not claimed complete. |
| Documentation | Changed-document MDX sanity passed. Global link/anchor audit found eight failures outside this document in unchanged source/target files; the global audit is not a pass. ClawHub fragments remain unverified without their external mirror. |
| Full build | BLOCKED: default preflight could not observe its memory limit. A supported explicit 1,536-MiB attempt completed protocol/scripts/assets/AI/packages, then main tsdown received SIGKILL; overall exit 1. |
| Required unused-file gate | FAIL: production scan reports `vocabulary-collections.ts` because the proposal has no production registration. Full-tree scan exhausted its 1,536-MiB JavaScript heap (SIGABRT). No fake entrypoint or ignore was added. |
| Fresh maximum-bound benchmark | EXECUTED, target partial: 20 warmups + 100 samples per operation/workload, all 5,000 terms. Combined p95: **50.20 / 43.72 / 41.22 ms** for compact / raw-cap / normalized-cap cases. The compact case misses the strict below-50-ms target. Linux x64, Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C, Node 24.22.3. Occupancy counters are not cumulative allocations; auth/network/model/provider quotas remain unmeasured. Historical passing and initial failing runs are retained separately. |
| Required CI | NOT RUN to completion. At `70bac82c4c24bded28615002d52701940ee3494a`, [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45773743254) reports `action_required` with zero jobs, and [Proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/runs/139752289972) is skipped. The PR context/evidence check passed; metadata/dispatch success is not build/test proof. Upstream workflow action is required before those checks can execute. |
| Production qualification | NOT RUN: accepted host ACL/disclosure, production namespace, migration/rollback, accessible clients, real hint payload/quotas, spoken corpus, and M11/M10 recovery integration remain absent. |

The original worker failure was diagnosed as missing host-broker ownership in a thread. The existing database-worker registry routes the new test to a fork process. Full fixture-worker preparation also hit exit 137; independent inspection qualified these exact worker/relay tests for the existing production-runtime preset because their test helpers execute in Vitest and their child entries are production code. Broad/mixed selections retain the full graph. No compiler integrity, admission, IPC, lifetime guard, assertion, or timeout was weakened.

Independent agent review repaired and rechecked mutable selection across authorization awaits, provider-error leakage, sparse aliases, stage/provider admission, and the persisted-winner assertion in the two-editor test. A final review of the new worker/routing delta and explicit synchronous-major-GC callback found no remaining actionable code finding in that scope. This is automated source review, not a local ClawSweeper/autoreview tool result or human owner approval.

Current official OpenAI documentation confirms the existing adapter's optional transcription prompt field, but no live M06 hint request was made and exact current token/byte/term budgets remain unverified. The archived 2025 Cookbook's numeric prompt limit is historical only. The 5,000-term/400-KiB collection ceiling is not an advertised provider payload allowance; the committed record links the primary documentation and model-lifecycle constraint.

| AC | Status | Remaining production proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01 — Authorized scope | PARTIAL | Accepted real membership/disclosure, scoped store opener and RPC guessed-ID/export matrix |
| 02 — Resolution | PARTIAL | Accepted P03/private personal lifecycle and visible effective-source/conflict controls |
| 03 — Provider contract | PARTIAL | Verified current endpoint fields, exact real budgets, authorized transmission and visible capabilities |
| 04 — Revocation | PARTIAL | Production STT/refinement/insertion races, accepted mid-utterance policy and explicit recovery |
| 05 — Concurrent edits | PARTIAL | Production namespace/authority and actual management conflict recovery; real worker CAS/reopen is now observed |
| 06 — Migration | PARTIAL | Accepted and exercised saved-state migration, rollback and retention |
| 07 — Offline lifecycle | PARTIAL | Actual client offline/reconnect reauthorization and personal-only recovery |
| 08 — Isolation | PARTIAL | Live adapter, tool/mode/route and cross-scope transport inspection |
| 09 — Accessibility/clients | BLOCKED | Selection, management, source/conflict and recovery UI with keyboard/screen-reader proof |
| 10 — Privacy | PARTIAL | Production telemetry/cache/admin/audit/export review and accepted retention |
| 11 — Performance | PARTIAL | Repeatable latency target, cumulative allocation/resource proof and actual provider quotas |
| 12 — Semantic regression | PARTIAL | Spoken common-word/identifier/negation/number/literal corpus and unaffected personal-only dictation |

Requested design decision: establish the vocabulary owner and common P03/M11 contract, map collection selection/management/export/provider disclosure onto existing live authority, and accept the namespace/representation/retention and minimal Talk integration. Keep this PR draft and the umbrella issue open until the agreed scope and required proof are delivered. No merge is requested.

prs.title: fix: make progress cards callable from the first model request
prs.body:
Related: #126189

## What Problem This Solves

An agent on the default OpenClaw runner can be allowed to update its progress card without receiving the tool’s arguments in its first model request. With the default structured Tool Search, it has to discover the tool before using it directly. Codex already exposes the card up front.

## User Impact

When allowed, the agent can update the card directly on its first turn. No configuration or migration is needed. This adds one admitted schema to the request; it does not change when the agent should create cards, subagent denial, or the `tools.updatePlan` kill switch.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing tool presentation list keeps selected tools directly visible without removing their catalog entry or granting permission. Reusing it preserves discovery and leaves the existing Codex root-function contract alone. No tool definition, model instruction or other tool’s placement changes.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on `main` at `677fd700f47f3a3bcf7c1868d0fcca0aed3cad97` using an isolated Gateway, embedded OpenClaw runner, Code Mode off and `tools.toolSearch` unset. The first Responses API request contained only `dispatch_action`, `tool_describe` and `tool_search`; there was no `progress_card` function schema.
- On the fix, the same first-request capture contained those controls plus `progress_card`, with the full markdown and plan schema (50-step cap, required step/status, all three statuses, closed objects). The unrelated admitted `session_status` remained deferred.
- Forwarded the fixed request to real `gpt-5.4-mini`: its only tool call was a direct `progress_card`. The tool result confirmed the write; an independent `progressCard.get` returned revision 1 with the requested markdown and both steps completed. No live Gateway changes.
- Regression failed on base and passed on the fix. Four focused suites passed (103 tests), including prefix stability, registration and the card executor. Changed suite wall time: 36.84 s including cold transform; CI timing not yet available. Runtime build, agents-root typecheck, targeted lint, format and diff checks passed.
- Independent read-only agent review of the three-file diff against the base found one documentation scope issue, corrected to say default OpenClaw runner. No outstanding findings. Bound autoreview was unavailable.

Contributor: @hannesrudolph

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f2e828f4-4c7f-4e70-b448-78bf616f21af)

## Worked on by

- @hannesrudolph

prs.title: improve: share identical Control UI assets across clients
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two clients can request the same Control UI script with different accepted compression formats. Even when both receive the exact same representation, the Gateway indexes the prepared body by the clients' full preference lists.

## User Impact

The proposed change would avoid duplicated Gateway file reads and retained buffers when clients select identical bytes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing HTTP suite already covers clients selecting different representations. This draft adds the complementary case where the selected file is the same, for both a Brotli sidecar and a file served without compression.

## Evidence

The draft currently contains the regression tests. They check real HTTP status, encoding, Vary, and response bytes, then count worker body reads and distinct buffers sent for four alternating requests. Runtime validation and implementation are pending.

prs.title: fix: withhold meeting records when a transcript lacks usable evidence
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A finished voice capture with no usable speech can still say it is waiting for a transcript. A recorder summary can also sound conclusive when the complete transcript contains only greetings or disconnected fragments. Publishing that material gives people meeting records and action items the recording does not support.

## User Impact

A completed empty capture reports that it captured no usable speech. Meeting ingestion keeps the source available and withholds publication when the transcript supports no meeting fact. A brief, intelligible exchange can still establish a decision or commitment in any language. If an operator reviews a previously published suspect meeting, the scribe flags the affected records for review and preserves them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture completion is known when OpenClaw builds the transcript overview. The scribe can judge evidence after reading the complete source and before writing a meeting or attributing work. An interrupted read remains pending. A complete source with insufficient evidence stays checkpointed until the source changes.

## Evidence

Added regression coverage for open and closed captures, prompt-only input and a short Japanese utterance. Skill reference synchronization, the Knowledge size budget, formatting and diff checks passed. In one read-only model run across five synthetic fixtures, the scribe withheld a fabricated approval, deferred incomplete pagination, retained a two-line multilingual decision and commitment, flagged a previously published suspect record, and recognized an explicitly absent transcript. This exercise used synthetic data and made no Knowledge writes.

prs.title: fix: skip unused GitHub profile work at Gateway startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway with no managed GitHub profiles still enumerates agent configuration and asks the shared secret store for GitHub recovery records on every ordinary startup. It also imports the GitHub identity runtime and OAuth schema to discover that both profile directories are missing.

## User Impact

Starting an unconfigured Gateway skips this work. Installations with managed profiles still protect configured and pending OAuth generations before deleting retired profiles. Directory errors and unsafe paths still produce cleanup warnings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The filesystem cleanup owns the decision to retire a profile. It now opens each root in the existing order, imports the profile path helpers directly, and reads the recovery snapshot once when a safe root exists. The captured filesystem identity stays attached to each operation if a directory changes during the recovery read.

## Evidence

- On Linux x64 with Node 24.22.1, the original cleanup requested the OAuth list once and read the empty agent roster five times. The new cleanup performed zero of either operation. All 15 focused tests passed, including both scope types, unavailable records, symlink warnings, and root replacement. [Focused Testbox workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45771994867)
- In separate fresh Node processes against a temporary state directory, the source cleanup loaded 2,365 file modules on the baseline and 228 on the change. Peak process RSS was 499.3 MiB and 121.5 MiB, respectively. This single pair includes the TypeScript loader and measures the cleanup in isolation. Whole-Gateway RSS and release behavior require separate measurements.
- Local autoreview covered the complete signed range `f7c8162d8304..3c7e5fb8ee11` at P0–P2 and found no actionable issue. The native pre-commit checks passed.
- The normal Linux ARM64 compiler target built the production change against the same baseline. The packaged runtime image SHA-256 was `823c37cc53a2c5283442c6c282f9734d568f19f11f72dbe8cadf95123e2cb5ac`. its cleanup module contains the deferred recovery reader. An independent source review checked the filesystem identity guards and existing-only shared-store contract, with no actionable finding.

prs.title: fix: let Doctor repair a Git checkout install after its first update (2026.12.1)
prs.body:
> **Retargeted to `release/2026.12.1`.** That branch continues the former `release/2026.11.15` branch: `ae07e2709f3`, the commit this port was built and tested on, is its ancestor, and none of the five files this port touches has changed on the branch since. The port merges into the current `release/2026.12.1` head without conflict. Where the text below says `release/2026.11.15`, it means that tested commit. The cells were not rerun on the newer head. Port of #204676 (merged to `main` as `04d96995063`) to `release/2026.11.15`. ## What Problem This Solves On a Git checkout install, `openclaw doctor --fix` fails after the first update with "the service belongs to a different OpenClaw installation", although the Gateway service is the installation's own. `openclaw update repair` stops at the same refusal, and `openclaw gateway status --deep` reports that the service runs an older version than the CLI. `release/2026.11.15` carries Git release mode (#199706) but not this fix, so every Git install that set up its service before updating to a 2026.11.15 build loses the repair path the update messages point to. ## User Impact User impact: on a Git checkout install running a 2026.11.15 release, `openclaw doctor --fix` and `openclaw update repair` run their maintenance, and `gateway status` stops reporting a false version drift. A service that really belongs to another installation is still refused. No configuration, state or service definition changes. ## Why This Change Was Made The branch still has the defect. Service ownership on `release/2026.11.15` (`ae07e2709f3`) follows only a unit that names the release launcher: - `src/daemon/service-layout.ts:171`: `return resolveGitReleaseEntrypointForLauncher(entrypoint) ?? entrypoint;` - `src/update/run.ts:476-486` (`markForwarding`) writes the checkout's forwarding marker (`.git/openclaw-launcher`) on the first Git release update, so the checkout's `dist/index.js` starts the release, while ownership still reads the checkout as the service's package root. This is one `git cherry-pick -x 04d96995063` commit. It makes service layout follow the same forwarding marker the checkout's entry follows, and keeps such a definition unchanged like a unit that names the launcher. The reasoning and design are in #204676. **Conflict.** The pick conflicts in one expression, `refreshDefinition` in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-plan.ts`, because this branch already has #204835 (a Git install switching back to the npm package rebinds its owned definition). The resolution keeps both intents and is the form `main` has: the package override stays first, and the forwarded-checkout exclusion applies only on the Git side. ```ts refreshDefinition: (state.definitionMutationCapability?.kind ?? "writable") === "writable" && (params.updateInstallKind === "package" || (!command.programArguments.some((arg) => path.basename(arg) === GIT_RELEASE_LAUNCHER) && !isForwardedServiceEntrypoint(command))), ``` After the pick, `update-command-service-plan.ts`, `service-layout.ts` and `docs/cli/update/how-updates-run.md` are byte-identical to `origin/main`. The hunks in `git-release-paths.ts` and `git-release.test.ts` are identical to the original commit's; those two files differ from `main` only by later `main` commits this port does not carry. Nothing else from `main` rides along (5 files, +176/−10). The commit keeps the original author and the `(cherry picked from commit …)` line. Update behavior: the fix runs in the release that Doctor and `update repair` execute, so an install gets it with its next ordinary `openclaw update` to a release that contains it. The installed updater's code is not involved. ## Evidence Cells: Linux Docker, real systemd user Gateway from `openclaw gateway install`, a Git checkout installed and built at T0 = `release/2026.11.15` head `ae07e2709f3` (2026.11.15-beta.1), a 512 MiB agent database under 1 MiB/s Gateway-gated writes. Every update is `openclaw update --yes --json` (trigger `api`, three `update.run … actor=gateway-client` journal lines per cell). T and T+1 are unpublished version bumps (2026.11.15-p1115r.1/.2 in red, 2026.11.15-p1115g.1/.2 in green) of the code under test. Each cell ran once. | Step (same cell) | RED: unmodified `ae07e2709f3` (cell R1) | GREEN: this commit `acd794e06f8` (cell G1) | | --- | --- | --- | | Update T0 → T | exit 0, 419 s, outage 12.1 s | exit 0, 370 s, outage 11.8 s | | `gateway status --deep` | false drift: "CLI 2026.11.15-p1115r.1 … differs from the Gateway service's 2026.11.15-beta.1 at ~/openclaw" | no drift reported | | `doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes` | **exit 1** in 2.1 s: "the service belongs to a different OpenClaw installation"; nothing repaired | **exit 0** in 56 s: "Gateway restarted and verified after Doctor maintenance" (outage 39 s) | | Update T → T+1 | exit 0, 389 s, outage 7.1 s | exit 0, 359 s, outage 7.3 s | | No-op update | exit 0 (skipped), 7.0 s | exit 0 (skipped), 7.2 s | | Doctor again | **exit 1**, same refusal | **exit 0**, 54 s | | `gateway restart` | exit 0 | exit 0 | | `update repair` | **exit 1**, same refusal, hands off to `openclaw triage` | **exit 0**, "Update finalization completed with warnings" (the warning is the cell's plaintext token) | | Service definition after Doctor | `ExecStart=… /home/appuser/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway` | unchanged: `ExecStart=… /home/appuser/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway` | In both cells the checkout's `.git/openclaw-launcher` names `~/.openclaw/git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs`, `git-install/openclaw` links to the release Doctor runs from, and after the last step the Gateway served T+1 (`/readyz` 200). RED, unmodified `release/2026.11.15` (`ae07e2709f3`), cell R1: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37b1e01e-25d5-4c49-8a25-ff13b2280110 GREEN, this commit (`acd794e06f8`), cell G1: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5cc069f2-f224-44a9-81e2-b2ae2122cef8 The recordings replay each cell's own step outputs; they are not live captures. Negative control (cell N1, same T0 → T on this commit): a copy of the checkout without the forwarding marker installs the service (`node ~/other-openclaw/openclaw.mjs gateway install --force`, older-binary guard waived for that one command), and its Gateway serves (2026.11.15-beta.1, `MainPID=11803`, `/readyz` 200). Doctor still refuses it: exit 1 in 2.1 s with the unchanged "belongs to a different OpenClaw installation" message, and the same Gateway keeps running. `openclaw gateway install --force` from the release CLI then writes `ExecStart=… ~/.openclaw/git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs gateway`, and Doctor passes (exit 0, 62 s). G1 also ran these two steps at its end, but there the copy's Gateway exited (`status=78/CONFIG`) before Doctor ran, so Doctor took the stopped-service path; that run is not used as evidence. Adjacent guard and published driver (cell P1): npm `openclaw` 2026.11.10, the current `latest`, with its systemd user service, updated by its own shipped updater to a pack of this commit served as the registry's `latest` under the unpublished version 2026.11.31: exit 0 in 175 s, outage 72 s, serving 2026.11.31 (`acd794e`). Then `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes` with the Gateway running: exit 0 in 49 s, "Gateway restarted and verified after Doctor maintenance" (PID 4558 → 7871, outage 32 s), unit unchanged (`ExecStart=… ~/um/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway`). An npm tree has no `.git`, so the new rule does not apply there.
Decisive raw lines ```text # RED (R1), after T0 -> T --- marker /home/appuser/.openclaw/git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs --- slot /home/appuser/.openclaw/git-install/releases/7b3e8d2b-6914-4c1e-972f-440d3e220324/openclaw --- unit ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/node --max-old-space-size=8017 /home/appuser/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port 39531 Doctor: maintenance begin Doctor: maintenance release Doctor could not enter maintenance. Error: Gateway service management skipped: the service belongs to a different OpenClaw installation and was left untouched. Run openclaw gateway status --deep to find the Gateway installation. [...] exit=1 ms=2065 # GREEN (G1), after T0 -> T --- unit ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/node --max-old-space-size=8017 /home/appuser/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port 36395 Stopped the managed Gateway for Doctor repair. Restarted systemd service: openclaw-gateway.service Gateway restarted and verified after Doctor maintenance. exit=0 ms=55719 MainPID=13553 ```
Raw step output of all four cells (R1, G1, N1, P1): [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205804#issuecomment-7185138572). The full cell directories are not attached: GitHub's attachment upload accepts media only and rejected the zip.
Checks on acd794e06f8 - Regression tests, red/green: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/git-release.test.ts`. With this commit's test file on the unmodified branch (`ae07e2709f3`), 4 of 44 fail: the three forwarding cases (`expected { kind: 'foreign' }`) and the other-state-directory case (`expected '1.0.0' to be '3.0.0'`), the same failures #204676 recorded on `main`. On this commit, 44 of 44 pass. The test file is carried unchanged; I audited all of it and removed nothing. - Each run one at a time under Node, all pass: `src/daemon/service-layout.test.ts` (15), `src/cli/daemon-cli/status.gather.test.ts` (61), `src/cli/run-main-service-installation.test.ts` (8), `src/commands/doctor-maintenance.{installation,service-identity,service-inspection}.test.ts` (33 + 1 skipped, 4, 2), `src/infra/restart-intent.test.ts` (13), `src/update/convert-service.test.ts` (4), `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-service-{maintenance,install-root,plan}.test.ts` (40, 4, 41), and #204835's tests, which cover the other side of the conflict: `update-command-target.git-to-package.test.ts` (3) and `update-command-original-service.test.ts` (50). Also `update-command-checkout-link-switch.test.ts` (9), `src/commands/doctor-gateway-services.authority.test.ts` (21), `src/infra/update-runner-git-release.test.ts` (39), `test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts` (1). - `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`: 23 of 23 pass with a default `pnpm install`. Under the hoisted install I first used, 8 cases fail with `ENOENT … packages/markdown-core/node_modules/mdast-util-from-markdown`; that is the install layout, not this change. - `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-rollback.test.ts`: 49 passed, 1 failed (`excludes a competing config writer …`, setgid mode `0o2770` on macOS). It fails the same way on the unmodified `ae07e2709f3`. - `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test`: pass. `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` on the touched files: clean. `git diff --check`: clean. - Session identity ratchet (`scripts/check-session-identity-ratchet.mts --base origin/release/2026.11.15 --no-merge-base`): OK. - `autoreview` (Codex, branch mode against `origin/release/2026.11.15`): scoped-clean, no findings. It checked that the resolution keeps #204835's package override and that forwarding to another installation does not grant ownership.
## Reproduce 1. Install a Git checkout of `release/2026.11.15` (`pnpm install`, `pnpm build:runtime`, `pnpm add --global openclaw@link:`), set `update.channel` to `dev`, and run `openclaw gateway install` so the systemd user unit starts `/dist/index.js`. 2. Point the checkout's upstream `main` at a version bump of the same tree and run `openclaw update --yes`. 3. Run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes`. Unmodified branch: exit 1, "the service belongs to a different OpenClaw installation". With this commit: exit 0, Gateway restarted and verified. ## Not proven - macOS LaunchAgent and Windows Scheduled Task services were not run; only Linux systemd user services. Windows forwarding through a junction is not exercised. - A Linux container without a user bus was not run. - A published 2026.11.15 driver does not exist yet, so every cell here starts from local builds of this branch. - `update-command-rollback.test.ts` fails one macOS-only case locally (also on the base); CI runs it on Linux. - PR CI runs `src/infra/git-release.test.ts` under Bun, where the file skips itself (a skip that predates #204676). On Linux, checking a Gateway with a named profile, an explicit unit, or a separate state directory can open every system service file when the ordinary unit names are absent. Most of those files cannot identify the selected Gateway. The extra I/O happens each time the CLI checks service ownership.

A dependency-free fixture exercised the changed scan and selection functions with 255 unrelated marked service files and a matching template symlink. prs.title: fix(automations): surface blocked work and incompatible reasoning settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An automation can finish its agent turn and record that its work is blocked. Run history currently labels that occurrence “Completed” in green, even when the worker supplied a specific blocker. An unsupported reasoning setting can also stop a scheduled conversation before the model starts, leaving a generic admission error in its receipt.

## User Impact

Run history shows each occurrence’s recorded outcome. An enabled automation keeps its blocker and summary visible across quiet checks, and clears the notice when the worker reports progress or completion. Execution failures still take precedence. The editor identifies reasoning levels the selected model no longer offers, and prevents saving newly incompatible combinations when the catalog supplies authoritative choices.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler already records authored outcomes and retains the last meaningful result. The Control UI now reads those facts in history, job details and the sidebar. A retained blocker links to no unrelated occurrence. At session admission the owner receives the same specific validation reason as the interactive caller. Existing schedule, retry and notification behavior is preserved. Jobs that report only prose still need to use the existing `record_result` action for structured status.

The reporting-only permission request is tracked in [issue #205770](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205770).

## Evidence

- On the base, a successful execution with a recorded blocker produced no attention indicator. The same projection on this branch recognizes blocked and needs-attention results, clears them on progress or completion, and gives execution errors precedence.
- The [first CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45759648265) built the distribution and exposed a second failure. On an already-open job, an execution error could leave the previous “Needs attention” message visible. The follow-up commit refreshes the existing alert and keeps expanded diagnostics open when the cause changes.

prs.title: fix: keep saved attachments after quick caption-edit reloads
prs.body:
Closes #205793

## What Problem This Solves

Editing only the caption of an already saved unsent attachment and immediately reloading can keep the caption while silently losing the file. The issue contains the supplied main reproduction: five immediate reloads lost the attachment, while both five-second controls retained it.

## User Impact

Previously saved attachments can be recovered alongside a newer caption after an interrupted browser draft write. Explicit attachment removal still wins. No settings or migration steps are required, and this does not recover files already discarded by an older build.

## Why This Change Was Made

I retain the attachment set's existing write identity across caption-only edits, in the existing synchronous metadata and durable draft. Recovery can then recognize unchanged files without replacing newer text, goal, mention, or reply metadata. Changing the attachment set changes its identity, so removal cannot resurrect an old file.

The optional metadata keeps older saved drafts readable. No new store, schema version, timer, or persistence owner is introduced. The change is production +106/-19 and test +103/-0 against main. The simplification pass kept one regression at the real browser-storage boundary, including the removal control.

## Evidence

- The new regression fails against the unchanged production base: recovered filenames are `[]` instead of `["saved.txt"]`. With the fix it preserves both the newer caption and exact file bytes, then confirms an interrupted removal does not restore that file.
- The regression uses real Chromium, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, and the production persistence owners. It aborts the draft transaction to deterministically exercise the interrupted-write state; it is not a full Gateway reload test.
- Focused checks: 6 Chromium tests and 64 unit tests passed. UI TypeScript, changed-file lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. The changed browser suite took 1.42 seconds wall time (1.055 seconds in tests); CI timings are pending.
- Published head `8ffdfbed8bb6a974dab88c3f435846cebaf7789b` has the identical source tree as tested local commit `2115bb19f3c1a8e613af7703bf786036bace9bc0`. Publication rewrote commit attribution, not the tested code.
- Local autoreview could not start because the Codex installation failed its read-only sandbox preflight. No independent review result is claimed.
- Full real-Gateway end-to-end recheck of the fix is pending and will be run separately by the requester. This PR stays draft for that proof and review. CI results are not claimed here.

Reported by Dan Riccio.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-attachment-lost-on-quick-reload-s67febd17)

prs.title: fix: stop the directory-watch helper when its last watch fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can leave a directory-watch helper running after its last watch fails. For example, asking the helper to watch a missing directory removes the registration, but the helper keeps waiting for input while the parent process stays up.

## User Impact

The unused process exits automatically. Other directory watches keep receiving events, including when the error handler immediately starts watching a parent directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The parent process owns the set of live watches and the helper’s input pipe. After delivering the error, it checks whether that same helper still owns any watches before ending its input. This preserves synchronous recovery and covers a registration write that throws.

## Evidence

The regression uses a real helper and a missing directory. It checks for the child’s exit while the parent is live, plus a replacement admitted from the error handler. The existing suite covers an already-active sibling and helper rollover. The pinned formatter and `git diff --check` passed. The runtime comparison and independent review are pending.

prs.title: test: trim workflow and runtime performance coverage
prs.body:
Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198737

## What Problem This Solves

The test-maintenance campaign is reducing selected profiling workloads, implementation counters and workflow presentation inventories. These ten existing test/support files carry selected low-value oracles whose maintenance cost the maintainer chose to retire; the patch does not claim every removed assertion is duplicated.

## User Impact

No production behavior change. Developers maintain 1,130 fewer tracked lines. The deliberate tradeoff is less cosmetic probability/phrase coverage, allocation and callback scheduling budgets, stress/read-byte probes, and selected CI count/layout/placement/permutation checks. The functional guards retained for each touched file are named below; no equivalent performance-measurement claim is made.

## Why This Change Was Made

Trim existing suites and keep their functional owner tests rather than adding replacement harnesses. Auth, trust, provenance, data-preservation, stale/race, actual selected-manifest execution and native output-fidelity guards remain. No files are added or deleted. Production code, metadata files, workflow definitions and dependencies are unchanged.

| Category | Paths | Added | Deleted | Net removed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Test/support | 10 | 9 | 1,139 | **1,130** |
| Runtime production / metadata / new tracked files | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The accepted preformat proposal was 1,122 net. One redundant blank-line deletion and two normal-formatter array-wrapping collapses add seven net deletions without changing test values; the one-line orphan-import repair adds one more.

## Evidence

**READY / CURRENT CI GREEN; native landing gates remain authoritative.** Signed source `b98ea82d6a873d70d34416a12aa24cb84d52f9cf`, parent `f212d7696fc1f73eeb61c4d6817415647562ae6b`, frozen base `973e0ba78f7b970dafdd9166c6598a572a5d0d46`, tree `99de80e73810c47959a732d07e8f1571f20bde09`.

- Complete: exact ten-file pre/post projections; 48 pinned source contexts; 46 explicit complete retained-guard block hashes and two cross-file compositions; nine native Node **parse-only** probes; diff/path/import/privacy checks; normal signed commit hooks, admitted oxfmt 0.74 and native i18n freshness.
- **Parent f212 source-review chain complete:** the original native review had 15 attempts, 13 complete and 2 incomplete, with 0 reported findings; its aggregate remains historically **INCOMPLETE (exit 2)**. One targeted workflow-context completion is now **1/1 COMPLETE, 0 findings, source verification PASS**. Independent coverage of the original 13 complete allocations plus that completion covers all ten changed units and all 48 required owner contexts. This is the accepted **13-plus-1 source chain**, not a claim that the original 15 attempts were clean or that any runtime proof ran. prs.title: fix(cli): observe ambient cancellation on stdin byte reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a CLI command reads its payload from stdin (`--script -`, `--value-file -`, `--message-file -`, piped auth/credential input, etc.) and the operator presses Ctrl-C while stdin is held open, the bounded read never observes the cancellation: cleanup stalls until the runtime's force-kill grace expires (~2 s) and the process dies with SIGKILL (`137`) instead of exiting promptly and gracefully (`130`/`143`).

- Problem: `readByteStreamWithLimit` (`packages/media-core/src/read-byte-stream-with-limit.ts`) only had `maxBytes`/`onOverflow` and no way to observe ambient cancellation, so a held-open stdin read never settles after an interrupt; the CLI read sites also had no abort guard before turning the bytes into a mutation.
- Solution: add an optional `signal` to `readByteStreamWithLimit` that destroys the held-open upstream stream and rejects with `AbortError` on abort; pass `getAsyncWorkSignal()` at the eight CLI/extension stdin read sites and `signal?.throwIfAborted()` before the mutation.
- For a WHATWG `ReadableStream` (e.g. `response.body`) the abort is delivered through an owned reader (`getReader()` + `reader.cancel()`); async iteration locks such a stream, so `cancel()` on a locked stream rejects and is swallowed, leaving the held-open read never settled. Native streams still tear down via `.destroy()`.
- What changed:
  - `packages/media-core/src/read-byte-stream-with-limit.ts` — `signal` option with per-chunk `throwIfAborted()`; abort listener tears down the held-open upstream and surfaces the error as `AbortError`; Web streams read through an owned reader (`isWebReadableStream` + `readWebReadableStreamWithLimit`).
  - Six CLI sites: `src/cli/cron-cli/trigger-options.ts`, `src/cli/secrets-store-input.ts`, `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.shared.ts`, `src/commands/agent-message-input.ts`, `src/commands/agent-exec-input.ts`, `src/commands/models/auth-manual-input.ts`.
  - Two extension sites: `extensions/matrix/src/cli-shared.ts` (recovery-key stdin), `extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.ts` (`--actions-file -`).
  - `config/test-lines-allocations/187522-cli-stdin-abort.txt` — `98` lines of test-budget record: the 82 lines these reader cases add plus the 16-line overage the ratchet base already carried. It is an exact grant (net growth + inherited debt), so it creates no headroom; the cases are the cancellation proof this PR ships, so the growth is recorded instead of paid for by deleting unrelated coverage.
- What did NOT change: byte limits, overflow errors, the shared read contract's return shape, the update-executor/update-capability stdin that are private updater-protocol holders, and `main`'s generalized `readBoundedCliTextInput(inputFile, { maxBytes, label })` shape (the merge keeps it; the new `agents render-blobster` caller inherits the cancellation fix through the same owner at no extra cost).

## Why This Change Was Made

The same ambient signal (`getAsyncWorkSignal`) already cancels async work across the CLI; the stdin byte read was one of the few hot paths that never consulted it. Patching every caller individually with `addAbortSignal` would leave the shared `readByteStreamWithLimit` contract signal-unaware and force each site to reinvent held-open-stream teardown, so the fix lives in the shared reader plus a per-site throw-if-aborted guard before the mutation.

- Best fix: a shared `signal` option that both tears down the held-open upstream and rejects with `AbortError`, so every stdin site gets identical cancellation semantics and the `throwIfAborted()` immediately after the read guarantees a cancellation that lands after EOF is still not turned into a mutation.
- Alternative(s) rejected: per-site `addAbortSignal(signal, process.stdin)` only, because it leaves the shared reader unaware of cancellation and duplicates teardown at eight sites.
- Risk: the abort listener is registered only when `signal` is non-undefined; when no signal is present behavior is unchanged. `config-cli-input.ts` (the same family) is fixed separately by #187336 and is out of scope here.

## User Impact

Pressing Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or SIGTERM while a CLI command waits on stdin now stops the read and exits promptly and gracefully (`130`/`143`, ~0.1 s after the signal) instead of stalling ~2 s in cleanup and being force-killed (`137`); a late payload typed after the interrupt is never read, and the post-EOF `throwIfAborted()` guard keeps an accepted cancellation from being turned into a cron/secret/message/browser mutation.

## Merge and Conflict Resolution

Merged `origin/main` `8fea10c4543` (2026-11-26) into the branch (merge commit, no force-push, review history preserved). One file conflicted; the resolution is additive to what `main` already does:

- `src/commands/agent-message-input.ts` — `main` generalized the helper into `readBoundedCliTextInput(inputFile, { maxBytes, label })` and added the `agents render-blobster` caller. The resolution keeps that parameterized shape and adds this PR's wiring inside the stdin branch: `const signal = getAsyncWorkSignal()`, `signal` passed to `readByteStreamWithLimit`, and the existing `signal?.throwIfAborted()` after the read. The file-path branch is untouched. Because the fix lives in the shared reader, `main`'s new `agents render-blobster -` stdin path is covered automatically (verified below).

The other ten changed files auto-merged. Re-verified on the merged head: `packages/media-core/src/read-byte-stream-with-limit.test.ts` 7/7; the six affected owner suites (`agent-message-input`, `agent-exec-input`, `cron-cli/trigger-options`, `secrets-store-input`, browser `browser-cli-actions-input/shared`, `exec-approvals-cli.utf8`) all green; `check-test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main`: `Test lines OK. Net test lines: +82; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 98`; oxlint 0 warnings/0 errors and oxfmt clean on all ten changed source files.

## Evidence

**Real built CLI + real signals, frozen `main` `8fea10c4543` vs this merged head `3c5e1680186` (2026-11-26).** Both arms built with `build-all.mts cliStartup`; `--version` self-reports `OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (8fea10c)` and `OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (3c5e168)`. Same command, stdin held open by a FIFO write-holder, signals sent with `kill` to the launcher pid, isolated state dir per arm:

| scenario (`cron add myjob --script - --cron '0 0 * * *'`) | Before: `main` `8fea10c` | After: this head `3c5e168` |
|----------|----------------|----------------------|
| SIGINT while waiting | **SIGKILL/137** ~2.0 s after signal (cleanup never completes) | **130** ~0.14 s after signal |
| SIGTERM while waiting | **SIGKILL/137** ~2.0 s after signal | **143** ~0.16 s after signal |
| SIGINT, late payload written +0.3 s | **SIGKILL/137** ~2.0 s, no stopping error, late payload not rejected by the read | **130** ~0.08 s, read aborted before the late payload arrives |
| normal script + EOF (control) | reads script, reaches `gateway cron.add` | identical: reads script, reaches `gateway cron.add` |
| `agents render-blobster -` SIGINT while waiting (new `main` caller) | **SIGKILL/137** ~2.0 s, no stopping error | read aborted, `CLI stopping (SIGINT)` emitted, nothing rendered |
| `agents render-blobster -` with `{}` + EOF (control) | reads stdin, reaches design validation | identical validation error (read path unchanged) |

Commands (run identically on both arms; FIFO write-holder keeps stdin open, `kill -INT`/`kill -TERM` target the launcher pid):

```
node openclaw.mjs cron add myjob --script - --cron '0 0 * * *'
node openclaw.mjs agents render-blobster - --out blobster.svg --json
node dist/entry.js cron add myjob --script - --cron '0 0 * * *'
```

Raw observations:

```
VERSION base: OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (8fea10c)
CELL base sigint-wait:  exit=SIGKILL(137) afterSignal=2047ms  OUT: Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
CELL base sigterm-wait: exit=SIGKILL(137) afterSignal=2053ms  OUT: Command interrupted by SIGTERM. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
CELL base direct-entry-SIGINT (node dist/entry.js): exit=SIGKILL(137) afterSignal=2032ms
CELL base blobster-sigint: exit=SIGKILL(137) afterSignal=2040ms  OUT: Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.

VERSION head: OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (3c5e168)
CELL head sigint-wait:  exit=130 afterSignal=138ms  OUT: Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
CELL head sigterm-wait: exit=143 afterSignal=161ms  OUT: Command interrupted by SIGTERM. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
CELL head sigint-late-input-fast: exit=130 afterSignal=81ms (payload written +300ms, after the exit)
CELL head direct-entry-SIGINT (node dist/entry.js): exit=130 afterSignal=79ms
CELL head blobster-sigint: read aborted, OUT: CLI stopping (SIGINT) (JSON cli_error), no SVG written
```

Both arms' normal-EOF control cells read the payload and reach the same downstream step (`gateway cron.add` credential error in the isolated state; identical Blobster design-validation error for `{}`), confirming ordinary input behavior is unchanged.

Note on current-`main` symptom shape: the entry runtime force-kills a stalled cleanup after its ~1 s grace, so the pre-fix observable today is a ~2 s stall ending in SIGKILL/`137` rather than an indefinite hang; the underlying never-settling read is pinned directly by the base-RED unit cases below (they hang to the 120 s test timeout on `main`).

**Unit tests, bidirectional.** `packages/media-core/src/read-byte-stream-with-limit.test.ts` (original 5 cases + Web-reader read, stalled-read abort, Web overflow-cancel):

```
this head: Test Files 1 passed (1)  Tests 7 passed (7)
main base: Test Files 1 failed (1)  Tests 3 failed | 4 passed (7)
  × rejects immediately with AbortError when the signal is already aborted
  × destroys the stream and rejects with AbortError when the signal aborts mid-read (120025ms timeout — read never settles)
  × cancels the owned reader and rejects with AbortError when a WHATWG ReadableStream stalls (120083ms timeout — read never settles)
```

**Owner suites on the merged head**: `src/commands/agent-message-input.test.ts`, `src/commands/agent-exec-input.test.ts`, `src/cli/cron-cli/trigger-options.test.ts`, `src/cli/secrets-store-input.test.ts`, `extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/shared.test.ts`, `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.utf8.test.ts` — 6 files, all green (3 Vitest shards, exit 0).

**Budget and hygiene**: `check-test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main` → `Test lines OK. Net test lines: +82; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 98`. oxlint: `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors` on the ten changed source files; oxfmt: `All matched files use the correct format`.

**Open PR collision check (2026-11-26)**: searched open PRs for `stdin abort` / `stdin cancellation` / `readByteStreamWithLimit` and swept the 200 most recent open PRs' changed files against this PR's eleven paths — no open PR touches any of them (the only keyword hit besides this PR, #172128, changes sqlite-worker files exclusively). `main`'s `readByteStreamWithLimit` still has no `signal` option at `8fea10c4543`, so no shared fix has superseded this repair.
