prs.title: fix(cli): share process failure listeners across invocations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Running multiple full CLI commands in one Node process adds uncaught-exception and unhandled-rejection listeners on each call. An earlier command's arguments can stay referenced after it finishes. The legacy executable can register the same error policy twice on a single run.

## User Impact

OpenClaw handles each process error event once. During a command, the exception renderer uses that invocation's arguments. A callback that fails after command cleanup uses the host process's arguments.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both executable entry points share process-lifetime listeners. An async context carries the active invocation's arguments through dispatch and cleanup, then clears them. The installer checks for the shared listener by identity. Each invocation supplies its own reporter so the module that owns the command also receives its exit outcome. After cleanup, the most recently installed reporter handles process errors. A separate follow-up covers Commander’s process-wide JSON setting. When two parses overlap, its latest setting can govern both commands.

## Evidence

- Added focused cases for two successive commands, a nested JSON/text command, and an async callback that runs after command completion.
- Verified on Node 26.7.0 that duplicate listeners fire twice and deferred callbacks retain their originating async context.
- At `9d760e4`, the fatal-detection tests passed. Three exit tests then failed while looking for a fresh registration on every invocation. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45751782914)
- At `1f1c726`, the tests invoke the installed OpenClaw listener for fatal, transient, and legacy-entry errors. Targeted formatting and TypeScript syntax checks passed for all changed files. CI found a lint error in a newly added test spy. [CI run for `1f1c726`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45754373526)
- At `1745682`, the test also checks that each failure emits a console diagnostic. The pinned linter reproduced the original naming error and passed on the revised file, including the unused-variable check. The pinned formatter and TypeScript syntax checks passed. Both lint jobs passed. Node passed the dispatch and cleanup suites. One Node exit assertion failed when a second module instance finalized the command. Bun passed all three suites. [Node and Bun results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45756515082/job/139696832910)
- At `4072cf6`, the same Node fixture loads the listener and exit barrier twice. On `1745682`, the initial module received exit code 1 and the active module received no exit outcome. The repair delivers the exception and rejection to the active module. Native process events also exercised nested JSON/text scopes, a detached callback and an asynchronous shutdown finalizer. The five focused files passed all 90 tests on Node and all 90 on Bun. Both runtimes passed the formerly failing machine-output exit case, the repeated and nested dispatch cases, and 17 additional cleanup tests. [CLI and cleanup tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45758533970/job/139703292884) · [Legacy entrypoint tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45758533970/job/139703293005) · [Fatal-detection tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45758533970/job/139703292984)
- Both affected core lint jobs passed on `4072cf6`. The full workflow failed. Its type and extension-boundary checks reported a listener parameter mismatch. [Type diagnostics](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45758533970/job/139703293265) [Core lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45758533970/job/139703293420) · [Release lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45758533970/job/139703292617) · [Full workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45758533970)
- At `6d142aa`, the listener declares the native event tuples for both exceptions and rejections. The fixtures pass the exception origin or rejected promise supplied by Node. Both pinned type checkers reproduced all three type errors on `4072cf6` and passed on the revised listener and tests using the repository’s Node and Vitest declarations. The Node module-reload fixture, formatting, and native lint checks also passed. prs.title: improve: keep only the newest Doctor pre-repair copy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Every `openclaw doctor --fix` saves a full copy of the state it may repair before it starts (the pre-repair capture). Doctor kept the newest three of these copies from the last 30 days, and each one is the size of the whole state store. Measured on real installs, that is 13.3 GB kept for a 4 GiB store and 33 GB for a 10 GiB store, which is disk most users never get back unless they run cleanup by hand.

## User Impact

- Doctor now keeps only its newest pre-repair capture. Each successful `doctor --fix` capture removes the older Doctor captures, so the space held drops from about three store-sized copies to one.
- Manual recovery from an earlier Doctor repair can start only from that newest copy. Take a verified backup when you need a longer history.
- `openclaw update cleanup` and its `--dry-run` preview use the same rule: older Doctor captures show as `candidate` / `superseded-doctor-capture`, the newest as `protected` / `retained-doctor-capture`.

What does not change: what a capture contains and when it is taken; update captures and migration originals; a Doctor capture still referenced by a pending update recovery; the capture the current run (or a container's activation marker) is using; incomplete, interrupted or linked captures. Unreadable recovery records still stop all retirement.

**Update behavior.** The installed updater runs first and does not retire Doctor captures, so updating changes nothing on disk by itself. After updating to a release with this change, the first `doctor --fix` that takes or reuses a capture removes the older Doctor captures and frees that space; each removal is named in the debug log (`openclaw --log-level debug doctor --fix`). Nothing else is removed. No config, schema, stored field or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repository owner approved cutting the count from three to one on 2026-11-26. The count has one owner, `collectStandaloneDoctorCaptures`, which both Doctor's automatic retirement and `openclaw update cleanup` read, so this is a one-place change. The newest capture was already kept at any age, so with a count of one the 30-day limit can no longer change which capture stays; its unused clock option is removed rather than left as dead code.

## Evidence

Tested commit: `dc2abb9bdb3` (patch-identical to `b560447fa4b`, the commit the packs were built from, rebased onto current main with no overlapping paths).

Focused tests, failing on the base before the change and passing after it:

- `src/infra/doctor-capture-retention.test.ts`: five captures leave only the newest; an install holding three (the old limit) ends with one; the newest is kept even when older than 30 days; a capture referenced by a pending update recovery and the caller's own capture stay; incomplete, interrupted, linked and update captures stay; unreadable recovery records still stop retirement.
- `src/commands/doctor-capture-repeat.test.ts`: real, unmocked `doctorCommand` repairs. Healthy runs reuse one capture; after a real config change the next repair leaves exactly one capture, the new one.
- `src/infra/doctor-capture-reuse.test.ts`: a fresh capture after a source change, an unusable original or `--full-integrity-check` replaces the earlier copy instead of adding to it; reuse verification still leaves the original's bytes untouched.
- `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-capture-cleanup.test.ts`: `openclaw update cleanup --dry-run` marks the four older Doctor captures `superseded-doctor-capture` and the newest `retained-doctor-capture`; `--yes` removes exactly those four.

Real-flow Docker cell: in progress; this section will be updated with the result, recording and raw logs.

prs.title: feat(context): show prompt budget card for /context on every channel
prs.body:
## Problem

The Control UI shows a prompt-budget popover (how the context window splits across messages, workspace files, tool schemas, skills and system instructions, plus cache hit rate and cost). Chat channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, ...) had no equivalent: bare `/context` only printed the help text, and the category math lived inside the Control UI.

## Solution

- Bare `/context` now renders a text version of the popover on every channel: a header (used / limit / %), a 20-cell emoji bar, the five categories, and `Latest run:` / `Session total:` cache hit rate and cost. The limit is the one the popover uses: the last run's validated prompt budget (`resolveProjectedSessionContextBudgetStatus`), else the context window. `/context help` keeps the mode list; `list`, `detail`, `map` and `json` are unchanged.
- One owner for the category math: `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-context-breakdown-model.ts` moved to `src/shared/context-budget-categories.ts` (`buildContextBudgetCategories`). The Control UI and `/context` both use it.
- One owner for the cache hit rate: `src/shared/prompt-cache-hit-rate.ts` (moved out of `ui/src/lib/sessions/usage.ts`). The popover, the usage page and `/context` use it.
- The session total reuses the `/usage cost` reader (`loadCurrentSessionCostSummary` in `commands-session-cost.runtime.ts`). Same semantics as the Control UI: a partly priced or unfinished total shows `≥ $X`, usage with no price shows `unpriced`, never `$0`.
- `Latest run:` cache rate sums every measured model call since the last user message (shared `latestRunCacheHitRate`, used by both the Control UI popover and `/context`). Calls without cache telemetry are left out, not counted as misses.
- Each non-empty category keeps at least one bar cell so a small share stays visible; the remaining cells go by largest remainder, so the bar is always 20 cells.
- Dollar figures follow the existing chat surfaces (`/status`, `/usage cost`), which show estimates for every auth mode.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/context.md`, `docs/tools/slash-commands.md`.

## Impact

- Users on any channel see where their context window goes with one command.
- Behavior change: bare `/context` no longer prints help; use `/context help`.
- No schema, protocol, config or dependency change.

## Evidence

- Unit: `commands-context-report.test.ts` (card layout, limit from the validated prompt budget and the window fallback, latest-run rate read from a stored transcript, stale usage -> `unknown` messages, latest-run rate across several calls incl. a call without cache telemetry, 20-cell bar with minimum cells, session total incl. `≥` / `unpriced` / unmeasured-cache cases), plus the moved UI tests (`chat-context-breakdown`, `session-context-report`, `view-overview`, `chat-composer-context` browser).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, type-aware oxlint on changed files clean.
- Head E2E (708c674d) on the real product: isolated Gateway from source, real `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` turns with tool calls on the embedded runtime, `/context` and `/usage cost` sent through `chat.send`:

```

🟦🟧🟩🟨🟪⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜

🟦 Messages & other · ~5.4k
🟧 Workspace files · ~56
🟩 Tool schemas · ~3k
🟨 Skills catalog · ~1k
🟪 System instructions · ~7.8k

Latest run: 97.05% cache · $0.0036
Session total: 73.84% cache · $0.02

More: /context list · /context detail · /context map · /context json
```

  `sessions.list` for the same session: `contextTokens` 400,000, `contextBudgetStatus.promptBudgetBeforeReserve` 380,000 (the card's limit, as in the popover). The latest run made two model calls (input 841 / cacheRead 16,256 and input 168 / cacheRead 17,024): 33,280 / 34,289 = 97.05%; cost 0.00217 + 0.00143 = $0.0036. `/usage cost` in the same session: `Session $0.02`.
- E2E on the first head (same setup):

```

🟦🟧🟩🟨🟪⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜
```

prs.title: fix(update): count a leftover Startup entry for the updated Gateway as that Gateway
prs.body:
## Problem

Refs #205650. A Windows `openclaw update` from 2026.11.7 to 2026.11.10 failed at `runtime-artifact-publication` and rolled back. The report redacted the failing check, code and message.

The refusal is `Cannot replace <root>: another managed Gateway (Startup entry …) is still using this installation` in `assertManagedGatewayArtifactPublication`. When a profile has its Scheduled Task and also a leftover Startup entry for the same `gateway.cmd`, both entries resolve to the one live Gateway process. The 2026.11.7 in-place updater read the Task's own Gateway, seen through the Startup entry, as a second live Gateway and refused before stopping anything. All three `runtime-artifact-publication` refusals had no public check or code, so the report redacted them.

## Solution

- `update-command-service-revalidation.ts`: in the in-place updater's `before-stop` check, a Startup-entry binding whose live PID and profile match the selected Gateway's recorded `servicePid` counts as the selected Gateway. A different live Gateway that uses the same installation still refuses. PID reuse since inspection is an accepted edge case, noted in a comment.
- The three existing `runtime-artifact-publication` refusals now carry the public check `runtime-artifact-publication` and their own codes: `git-runtime-gateway-running`, `installation-shared-by-gateway` and `runtime-artifact-gateway-unverified`. Each code has a fixed, path-free description in `UPDATE_PREFLIGHT_DETAILS`. Local error messages keep their paths and owner names.

## Scope (read this first)

On the current base, `openclaw update` for a package install goes through the prepared-release updater (`tryRunReleaseUpdateCommand`). That updater builds a private release under `<state dir>/git-install/releases/…` and never replaces the shared npm root. It does not reach the `before-stop` check that this PR changes. `--tag main` on a package install is refused with `unsupported-package-target` before the in-place updater runs. The Windows runs below show the same outcome **with and without** this PR's change. The #205650 scenario succeeds on the merge-base too. So for package installs on current versions, the Startup-entry match does not change any reachable outcome. The refusal ran inside 2026.11.7's own updater, so the fix cannot help 2026.11.7 users either. They need to remove the leftover Startup entry, or run `openclaw gateway stop` before updating. The public codes still apply to the Git and runtime-artifact publication paths, which are still reachable.

## Error surfaces

Diff against merge-base `0fa34123b322`. This PR adds no throw, refusal, exit, rollback trigger or validation.

| Changed path | Can fire for a healthy user? | Rollback/outage risk | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Startup-entry PID+profile match in `selectedConsumer` (`before-stop`) | Removes a refusal. It never adds one. | None added. It lets the in-place updater continue only when the "other" consumer is the selected Gateway's own PID, which the Task stop ends. | Kept. Unreachable for package installs on current versions (see Scope). |
| `installation-shared-by-gateway` code on the existing shared-installation refusal | Same condition as before: another live Gateway uses the root being replaced. | Unchanged. It is pre-mutation, and nothing is stopped. | Kept. This only relabels the report fact. |
| `git-runtime-gateway-running` code on the existing Git-runtime refusal | Same condition as before. | Unchanged. It is pre-mutation. | Kept. This only relabels the report fact. |
| `runtime-artifact-gateway-unverified` code on the existing publication refusal | Same condition as before. | Unchanged. It is pre-mutation. | Kept. This only relabels the report fact. |
| `runtime-artifact-publication` added to public native checks, and three new `UPDATE_PREFLIGHT_DETAILS` keys | No. They affect report projection only. | None. The JSON `reason` stays `runtime-artifact-publication`. Reports show a fixed description instead of a redacted message, and they no longer append a generic `update-failed` fact for these refusals. | Kept. |

## Evidence (exact head `3fe157c0787604af3533288f95ef931912eea4c3`)

Disposable AWS Windows x64 Crabbox lease `cbx_b914eef8fbca` (m7i.4xlarge), Node 24.19.0, isolated profiles. The tarballs were built on the Mac from the exact head (`GIT_COMMIT` set; `dist/build-info.json` reports commit `3fe157c0787604af…`). One is the 2026.11.10 serving build. The other is the same source as 2026.11.12, used as the update target. The merge-base build is `0fa34123b322`. Tarball SHA-256 values were checked on the lease. The lease has been released.

1. **#205650 scenario, exact head:** npm-global install in its own prefix, `onboard --install-daemon` (Scheduled Task `OpenClaw Gateway (r205739d)`, PID 2892), plus a Startup entry launching the same `gateway.cmd`. `openclaw --profile r205739d update --tag <2026.11.12 tgz> --yes --json` exited 0 in 571 s with `status: succeeded`. Steps: `staging`, `prepare:pack`, `prepare:install`, `validating`, `candidate-release-check`, `service-definition`, `activating`. Verification: `booted`, `versionMatch`, `coreReady`, running build `2026.11.12-3fe157c07876-…`. Afterwards the Gateway ran from `~/.openclaw-r205739d/git-install/openclaw` as PID 7020, `health --json` returned `ok: true, coreReady: true`, and the shared npm root stayed at 2026.11.10.
2. **Same scenario, merge-base (without this PR):** same steps in another prefix (profile `r205739f`). The update exited 0 in 562 s and moved the Gateway to 2026.11.12 on its private release. `health` returned `ok: true`. **This means the PR's Startup-entry change is not what makes the scenario succeed.**
3. **Separate live Gateway on the same install, exact head:** profiles `r205739a` and `r205739b` were both Task-managed from the same npm root. I updated `r205739a`. The update succeeded (554 s) by building a private release for `a`. Gateway `b` kept serving: same PID 3452, `health ok: true`, and the shared root unchanged at 2026.11.10. No refusal fired, because the release updater replaces nothing that `b` uses. That is a correct non-refusal and causes no outage.
4. **In-place route:** `openclaw update --tag main` on a package install exited 1 with `unsupported-package-target`, and both Gateways kept their PIDs. I found no user-reachable way to reach the changed `before-stop` check for a package install.

**Not proven end to end:** the `installation-shared-by-gateway` refusal with its new public code and fixed message on a live Windows install, and the public report text for all three codes. No reachable package-update path on current versions triggers them on Windows. They are reachable on Git/dev-checkout runtime-artifact publication, which this run did not exercise. These remain unit-tested only (`update-command-service-maintenance-identity.test.ts`, `update-managed-service-preflight-report.test.ts`).

The earlier Windows run in this PR reproduced the refusal on published 2026.11.7. Its "with the fix" update started from a 2026.11.10 npm install, which `tryRunReleaseUpdateCommand` routes to the same prepared-release updater as runs 1–2, so it does not demonstrate the fix.

CI: exact-head checks green (60 pass, 58 skipped, 0 failing).

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix: let large sessions compact again after 2026.11.10
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-readers.ts:366-372` (on main) charged compaction-preparation requests as `JSON.stringify(input).length * 2` and passed no request options, so a manual plan carrying Gateway preflight facts was refused by the history pool's 256 MiB pending-bytes cap (`packages/worker-runtime/src/worker-task-capacity.ts:2`), and every preparation read fell back to the 60 s default in `session-transcript-worker-runtime.ts:183`.

Fixes #205752

Thanks @jredbeard for the report, the root-cause trace and this fix.

## What Problem This Solves

Since 2026.11.10 (#201304), long-running sessions with a lot of history (the report: a Slack channel session at ~835k tokens, ~415 MB since the last compaction, ~1,460 images) can't be compacted. Manual `openclaw sessions compact` fails with `worker task capacity reached [... pool pending bytes ... inputBytes=445943294]`, and budget compaction can fail with `worker task timed out` after 60 s on every turn on slower hosts.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **Manual path, refused for size.** The Gateway preflight returns per-entry compaction facts for the whole active window and the plan request sends them back to the history worker (so planning does not extract the window twice). The reader charged that request as UTF-16 JSON: about 4.7x the structured clone that actually crosses the thread boundary, and it built a string as large as the window on the Gateway thread. `readPreparedCompaction` now charges the request by its `v8.serialize` byte length, the serializer the worker transport uses. The facts still travel and are still charged; the 256 MiB cap is unchanged and still refuses genuinely oversized requests.
2. **Preparation deadline.** Preflight, plan, render and finalize reads used the 60 s default worker read deadline regardless of `agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSeconds`. The Gateway runner and the embedded compaction owner now pass the existing `resolveCompactionTimeoutMs(config)` (default 180 s) to those reads, the way `readTrajectoryRetention` already takes a caller-owned `timeoutMs`. Caller abort signals still apply.

No config, schema or stored-data changes.

## Evidence

Built Gateway, merge base vs this head, seeded session the size of the report (37,801 events, 413.7 MB transcript, 1,500 distinct base64 PNG tool results): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205783#issuecomment-7185040847

- Manual: main refused twice (`worker task capacity reached ... inputBytes=828669298`, 7 s); this head compacted twice in 15 s (21,870,587 -> 20,708 tokens).
- Preflight facts measured 174 MB as a structured clone vs 828 MB charged before. A plan with twice those facts (349 MB) is still refused with the same capacity error on this head; on main the JSON estimate throws `RangeError: Invalid string length` first.
- Budget path: at the report's size preparation took ~8 s on this host on both main and this head, so the 60 s timeout did not reproduce here. The timeout change is covered by the integration regression in `compact.summary-fallback.test.ts` (red on main, green here).
- Small session: unchanged on both (10,926 -> 1,140 tokens).
- Regressions: `session-transcript-worker-readers.test.ts` (plan facts charged at least their clone and under the old estimate) and `compact.summary-fallback.test.ts` (`timeoutSeconds: 600` reaches every preparation read), both red on main.

Production +18/-2, tests +103 against the merge base.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the old charge and the 60 s deadline; nothing is written or migrated. Blast radius: compaction-preparation reads only (Gateway manual compaction and embedded compaction).

prs.title: fix(cron): keep scheduled session turns going after a configured send
prs.body:
Closes #205660

## What Problem This Solves

A cron job with `sessionTarget: "session:<key>"` ends its turn on the first `message`-tool send to its configured delivery target when `final` is omitted. The same job with `sessionTarget: "isolated"` keeps going and sends every message.

The cron source-delivery plan already says a send to a configured target is delivery, not a conversation answer: it sets `messageTool.finalByDefault: false` so post-send work still runs (`src/cron/isolated-agent/source-delivery-plan.ts`). Isolated runs forward that value (`run-prompt-executor.ts`), but scheduled session turns execute through the auto-reply embedded runner, and `buildEmbeddedRunExecutionParams` never forwarded it. The attempt therefore ran with the chat default (absent = an omitted `final` ends the turn), so the run recorded success after the first send.

## User Impact

Scheduled conversation jobs silently drop every message after the first one and record the run as `ok`, so users only see part of the intended output and have no failure signal. Jobs that update a state file after sending also skip that step.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing owner-defined value instead of inventing a new default: when the scheduled turn carries a cron `sourceDelivery` plan, pass `messageTool.finalByDefault` into the embedded run params. The message tool and prompt guidance already consume `messageToolFinalByDefault`, and `false` already means "omitted `final` keeps the turn going" everywhere else.

Ordinary chat turns have no cron `sourceDelivery` plan, so they keep the current default — a send answers the inbound message. Explicit `final: true/false` keeps working in both cases.

## Evidence

- Regression in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts`: a scheduled run with `sourceDelivery.messageTool.finalByDefault: false` must produce `messageToolFinalByDefault: false` in the embedded run params.
  - Base (`9ad935f281e0`, fix removed): `FAIL … carries the cron finality default into scheduled session turns` — 1 failed / 11 passed.
  - Head (`a25e44dcbaa9`): 12/12 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts` — 12 passed.
- Line-cap ratchet OK; test-lines +25/400; oxfmt and oxlint clean on both files.

Live A/B through the repo QA lane (isolated real Gateway child, `mock-openai` provider, `qa-channel`; cron `sessionTarget: session:agent:qa:main`, delivery `dm:qa-cron-send-continue-session`; script = message send with `final` omitted, then a `write`; Windows 11 host):

| Run | Build | Model tool calls after the send | qa-channel deliveries | Suite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | fix removed | `[message]` — no model call after the send | `QA-CRON-SEND-CONTINUE-SENT` | FAIL: turn ended after the send |
| after | `a25e44dcbaa9` | `[message, write, final]` | `QA-CRON-SEND-CONTINUE-SENT` | PASS |

Instrumented at the terminal owner (`final` derives from `messageToolFinalByDefault`): before `final=true` (turn ends after the send), after `final=false` (turn continues to the write).

![Live A/B](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/205660/proof.png)

## What was not tested

- Real Telegram/Discord delivery: the live leg used the QA lane's `qa-channel` transport; no external bot token was used.
- Scheduled turns on a CLI agent harness (`claude-cli`) build their params through a different path and were not changed or tested here.
- The QA scenario was a temporary local lane (not committed) and its Windows staging needed a local file-symlink→copy workaround in the tooling harness; neither touches the shipped fix.

prs.title: fix(update): the update after a failed 2026.11.10 pnpm update settles it instead of asking for repair
prs.body:
Related: #205167 (what users see and how to recover today), #205078 (stops the failure for updates driven by 2026.11.11), #204775

**Reviewer note:** this reverses a refusal that an existing test asserted. The next update no longer refuses, on that ground alone, a dead update whose driver released its own lease. One test is removed and its other assertions move into new cases; a related refusal test is unchanged. See [Tests: contract changes](#tests-contract-changes-the-reviewer-should-see).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a pnpm install that reached 2026.11.10 through `openclaw update`, the update after the one that ends with `update-recovery-pending` is refused and the user has to run `openclaw update repair`.

The installed 2026.11.10 runs the update to 2026.11.11, so nothing in 2026.11.11 can stop that update from failing once, although the new version is installed and serving (#205167). 2026.11.11 runs the next `openclaw update`. Today that update is refused within two seconds ("has unfinished recovery … The update lease store no longer holds that update's lease"). After the repair, the failed run is closed as failed/abandoned and its capture (about the size of the databases, 560 MB here) stays protected from cleanup.

## User Impact

With this commit in 2026.11.11, a pnpm user on 2026.11.10 still sees the update to 2026.11.11 end with `update-recovery-pending` once. Their next plain `openclaw update` then settles that run itself, provided the managed Gateway is running, ready and serving exactly the version and build that update installed. It records the run as succeeded and carries on with the update. They need no `openclaw update repair`, `openclaw update status` no longer says "needs attention", and the failed run's capture is released.

Affected: pnpm global installs that got 2026.11.10 (or 2026.11.10-beta.3) through `openclaw update`, on their first same-schema update. npm installs and installs where 2026.11.10 came from a plain `pnpm add -g` are not affected.

Update behavior: the change runs in the updater, so it acts only once 2026.11.11 or later is installed. It adds no migration, stored field or option, and when it cannot show the conditions below it refuses exactly as today and names `openclaw update repair`.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Contract

On a pnpm install where the update from 2026.11.10 to 2026.11.11 ended with `update-recovery-pending` and the candidate is installed and serving, the next `openclaw update`, run by 2026.11.11 or later, with no manual step:

1. exits 0 and installs the target;
2. removes the recovery pair (`update.recovery.<run>`, `update.pluginCohort.<run>`);
3. keeps the failed update's plugin and configuration changes and records that run as `succeeded` with the existing step `warning:reconcile:driver-lost-after-verification`;
4. leaves `openclaw update status` without "needs attention";
5. releases that run's capture: it no longer counts as an unresolved failed update, so retention cleanup can remove it (T2: the update's own cleanup removed it).

It still refuses, names `openclaw update repair`, and leaves the pair unchanged when the managed Gateway is stopped, not ready or serving another version or build; when the update lease store cannot be shown to be the file that existed before that run began (removed, replaced, or a host that reports no creation time); when the installed core is not exactly the recorded target; when the settlement would roll back; and when the run was not a killed command-line update (for example one the Gateway started).

### Root cause

Measured in the red cell below and confirmed in its databases:

- The 2026.11.10 driver reserves the recovery pair, activates, restarts and verifies the candidate, then loses the plugin lifecycle lease at the commit step (`Cannot find module`, the defect #205078 fixed for later drivers). The cohort stays `disposition: "pending"` with no settled publications, and the run stays `running` in phase `verifying` with the candidate's version and build recorded serving.
- The driver then returns through its executor's normal unwind, which deletes its row from the update lease store. The store's file is unchanged otherwise: in the cell it was created at 03:50:59, before the run (03:54:52), and its last change is the release at 03:57:52, 0.1 s before the command exited.
- The next update's `inspectInterruptedUpdateRecovery` accepts two proofs that the dead driver's processes are gone: the store still holding that driver's lease, or a reboot since. Neither applies, so it refuses with `The update lease store no longer holds that update's lease`.
- `openclaw update repair` then settles the pair, and history reconciliation closes the run as failed/abandoned. `recordedServingCandidate` rejects it for one reason only: the run's verification has no `booted: true`. Every other condition (phase, reason, repair, failed steps, version) passes.

### Why relaxing the tested refusal is sound

An executor's row in the update lease store is deleted only while that store records none of the executor's children as unsettled: `releaseAll` and `canRelease` check `hasUnsettledChildren`, and a later claim that reclaims a dead executor's row checks the same before replacing it. So in the store that held the lease, a missing row shows the driver's processes and children gone, which is the same fact the existing lease-held route relies on. The refusal existed because a missing row can also mean the store itself is new, for example after a temporary-directory cleanup; such a store recorded nothing about that driver.

The new route accepts the missing row only when all of these hold, checked at inspection and again under the installation claim:

- the store file's creation time is known (not zero and not equal to its change time, which older Linux reports in its place) and earlier than the run's creation;
- every driver the run recorded is dead by pid and start identity, and no driver went unrecorded or was a managed handoff;
- the run recorded the reservation's target version and build serving, and that exact version and build is the installed core;
- the cohort is not rolling back, and settlement admission sees a commit, no original core, the candidate core, and no package recovery authority;
- a fresh probe (the existing `observeInterruptedUpdateGateway`) finds the managed Gateway running, ready and serving that version and build.

Anything else keeps today's refusal and names repair. After settlement the probe's verification is recorded on the run, so the existing reconciliation rule closes it as succeeded with `warning:reconcile:driver-lost-after-verification`; if that write fails, the run closes as abandoned, as it does after repair today.

### Change

- `src/cli/update-cli/update-released-lease-proof.ts` (new): the store-age check, the forward-only preconditions, the probe, the admission rule and the verification write.
- `src/cli/update-cli/update-plugin-cohort-settlement.ts`: a third route beside "lease held" and "rebooted"; settlement admission now also reports whether the candidate core is installed and whether package recovery authority remains.
- `src/infra/update-run-interruption-health.ts`: the probe can check a given installation root instead of the running process's.
- `docs/install/update-troubleshooting.md`: what pnpm users on 2026.11.10 see, what 2026.11.11 settles, and when to run repair.

No schema, config option, protocol, dependency, retention-count or stored-field change.

### Tests: contract changes the reviewer should see

- **`update-command-killed-run-replaced.process.test.ts`, "is settled by repair after its driver released its lease, and the next update proceeds" is removed.** It asserted that the next update refuses after the driver released its lease, which this commit reverses. Its other assertions are kept in the new cases: the refusal when the update cannot be settled forward (no recorded build, store replaced, rollback, Gateway-started, original version installed again), and repair settling it and the next update proceeding ("is left to repair … when the Gateway …").
- **`update-command-killed-run-refusals.process.test.ts`, "another command already retired the dead updater's lease", is unchanged and still refuses**: that update never installed its candidate, so the forward-only route does not apply.

## Evidence

Tested commit: `dd2e8809500` on `release/2026.11.11` at `19d8a5ce791`. The PR head `30000c15416` is the same patch rebased onto `9ade94a23e0` with one test-only edit (typed table rows in the new tests, an import order and a stronger message assertion; production files are byte-identical to `dd2e8809500`). The only commit between the two bases, `9ade94a23e0`, changes `src/agents/model-catalog.ts` and nothing on the update, lease, Gateway probe or packaging path, so the cells were not rerun on it.

Each cell: Linux Docker (kernel 7.2, arm64), a real systemd user Gateway, pnpm 12.23.0 global install, a 512 MiB agent database under light writes (256 KiB/s), a 250 ms `/readyz` probe, plain `openclaw update --yes` with each pack served as the npm registry inside the container. Published 2026.11.9 is installed from npm; published 2026.11.10 is the registry tarball (integrity matches npm). "2026.11.11" is a local pack of the commit under test and "2026.11.12" the same tree with only a version bump; neither version is on npm. Cells ran one at a time, once each.

| Cell | Commit | Step | Exit | Wall | Gateway outage | Afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RED u2 | base `19d8a5ce791` | published 2026.11.10 → 2026.11.11 (driven by 2026.11.10) | **1** `update-recovery-pending` | 183 s | 117 s | CLI and Gateway on 2026.11.11; run `running`/`verifying`; pair present; lease row gone |
| **RED u3** | base `19d8a5ce791` | 2026.11.11 → 2026.11.12 | **1**, refused | 2 s | none | "The update lease store no longer holds that update's lease … By hand: Run openclaw update repair"; pair unchanged; status "needs attention"; capture 560,095,308 bytes protected (`unfinished-update-run`) |
| T2 u2 | fix `dd2e8809500` | published 2026.11.10 → 2026.11.11 (driven by 2026.11.10) | **1** `update-recovery-pending` | 122 s | 76 s | as RED u2 (the fix cannot reach this update) |
| **T2 u3** | fix `dd2e8809500` | 2026.11.11 → 2026.11.12 | **0** | 190 s | 83 s | "Settled interrupted update …"; pair rows gone; old run `succeeded` with `warning:reconcile:driver-lost-after-verification`; status "up to date"; the old run's capture was removed by this update's own retention cleanup (cleanup dry-run: 0 protected) |
| **T3 u3** | fix `dd2e8809500` | Gateway stopped by the operator (`systemctl --user stop`) after the failing update, then 2026.11.11 → 2026.11.12 | **1**, refused | 16 s | Gateway left stopped as the operator left it | "Its updater released its lease after verifying OpenClaw 2026.11.11, but the managed Gateway is not serving OpenClaw 2026.11.11 (build …) now (unverified during settlement) … By hand: Run openclaw update repair"; pair rows byte-identical before and after; run still `running`; status "needs attention" |
| **T4 u3** | fix `dd2e8809500` | update lease store file deleted after the failing update, then 2026.11.11 → 2026.11.12 | **1**, refused | 2 s | none | "The update lease store no longer holds that update's lease … By hand: Run openclaw update repair"; pair rows byte-identical; no new store created |
| T5 u3 | fix `dd2e8809500` | 2026.11.10 driver SIGKILLed the moment its run entered `verifying` (before it recorded the candidate serving), then 2026.11.11 → 2026.11.12 | 1, refused | 3 s | none | Not the lease-held path: the existing pnpm rule refuses first ("this installation cannot show it replaced that one: its update did not record OpenClaw 2026.11.11 serving"). The dead driver's two lease rows are still in the store. This route is untouched by the commit. A rerun that kills the driver after it records the candidate serving is queued (T5b). |
| T5b, T7, T8 | fix `dd2e8809500` | | | | | running one at a time; added here when each finishes |

The first hop (published 2026.11.9 → published 2026.11.10) exited 0 in every cell (138 to 191 s, 71 to 103 s of outage).

Settlement cost in T2 u3: about 5 s from the command start to the new run's creation, including CLI start-up, the probe and the settlement; it happens before the update stops the Gateway, so it adds no outage.

Red, unmodified `release/2026.11.11` at `19d8a5ce791`:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a40bbcf-0c19-454a-af60-78c9542403b8

Green, T2 with this fix (`dd2e8809500`), same chain and fixture:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72f5e861-20cc-492f-8bdd-207d28b5e6a3

Recordings of the refusal cells T3, T4 and T5 are in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205760#issuecomment-7185023258).

The recordings replay the recorded cell logs and facts; they are not live captures. Raw excerpts of every cell (exit records, decisive output lines, recovery pair rows, update run rows, lease store identity) are in PR comments, because the attachment service accepts only images and video: [RED and T2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205760#issuecomment-7183060902), [T3, T4 and T5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205760#issuecomment-7185023258).

### Unit tests

- `update-command-killed-run-replaced.process.test.ts`: new cases drive a real updater child that returns through its executor's unwind (so it releases its lease) after reserving the pair, then the next `openclaw update` from its command entry. The success case and the three "Gateway not serving" cases fail on `19d8a5ce791` (4 failed, 22 passed with the new tests on base production code) and pass with this commit.
- Mutation checks: dropping the `birthtimeMs > 0` guard fails "the host reports no creation time"; dropping the `< run.createdAtMs` comparison fails "a new update lease store replaced the one that held its lease".
- Commands on `77d04fd13fc` (same tree as the PR head's patch): `tsgo` core and core-test shards, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files, `git diff --check`, the session-identity and line-cap ratchets, and 9 test files (the 5 killed-run suites, `update-run-interruption-health`, `update-plugin-cohort-settlement`, `update-restart-module-outcome`): 122 tests passed.
- Test files audited in full: the replaced suite, `update-command-killed-run.process.test-support.ts` and `update-run-kill.process.test-support.ts`. The support files gain a `released` ending for the updater child, an optional candidate build ID (recorded with the run's target, as the updater does), an optional build ID for the replacing package directory, and a `servingGateway` probe stand-in restored after each test. Nothing else in them was dead or redundant.

## What was not measured

- macOS and Windows. On macOS the lease store lives in the per-user temporary directory and APFS reports creation times; that was not run. Windows was not run.
- T6 (original core still installed) in a cell: the installed core runs the next update, so with 2026.11.10 installed again the unfixed 2026.11.10 driver runs, not this code. Covered by the unit test "the version it replaced is installed again".
- A host without file creation times: covered by a unit test only.
- Bun installs and 2026.11.10-beta.1/beta.2 as the installed version.

## Left as is

- The failed 2026.11.10 run's database snapshot (`.openclaw.package-backup-<pid>-<time>.databases`, 547 MB here) stays next to the pnpm home after the settled update, as it does after `openclaw update repair` today; `openclaw update cleanup --dry-run` does not list it. That is the 2026.11.10 driver's retention and is not changed here.

## Cherry-pick for the release line

- One commit, 7 files (+501/−61): `30000c15416` on `release/2026.11.11` at `9ade94a23e0`. It applies with no conflicts on that head; `release/2026.11.11` at `19d8a5ce791` was the tested base.
- The update files it touches are the same at `v2026.11.10`.

prs.title: test(android): wait for the archive browser fixture to finish connecting
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Android archived-session test counts list requests after the screen mounts. Its setup waited for the first active session while the view model was still publishing the connection and session owner. In a controlled replay, that late update triggered a second archive request before the screen displayed the first result. The test then held the second response for a later assertion and timed out.

## User Impact

Android developers can now check that the archive browser reads once per change under delayed startup. The fixture change affects the test suite only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before mounting the screen, the fixture now waits for the view model to match the runtime’s connection, catalog revision, browser revision, and effective session owner (the selected agent or its default). The existing assertions still check pagination, rejection, superseded responses, an empty result, and a query change. The change touches one test file.

## Evidence

On SDK 34 with Robolectric, delaying the initial connection, catalog revision, or browser revision reproduced the timeout on the parent. A partial fix still timed out when both owner projections arrived late. The final fixture passed all seven schedules, including ordinary startup and each owner arriving separately. Every run completed the original six archive reads.

The local replay used a scoped runtime adapter and the real chat controller. The prior hosted timeout recorded no request trace, so its exact trigger remains unknown.

The hosted Android Play job ran `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` on `c74ecce8a3d343a54b809f5a665282acb24c58b2`. Its JUnit XML records `archivedQueryRetainsOnlyItsOwnAcceptedPageAndReadsOncePerChange` passing in 0.142 seconds. The class ran one test with zero failures, errors, or skips. [Play job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45769823249/job/139740012999) · [JUnit report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45769823249/artifacts/15094062261)

prs.title: fix(gateway): identify interrupted work when a chat resumes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A restarted chat could see an interrupted outer tool call without knowing which execution produced the nested scheduler results. An older reminder with the same name could lead it to confirm the wrong request. Leandro F. Chaves (@fonchaves) reported this in [issue #187354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187354). His [contributor PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187392) handles scheduler discovery and the extra CLI process.

## User Impact

When recovery can identify the interrupted run, the assistant receives its ID and can verify a scheduled job by its returned ID, report a recorded error, or say that an interrupted action has an unknown outcome. It can continue independent work in the same request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session marker now carries the originating run through the existing restart event provenance. A unique live root supplies its own ID. A pending continuation can retain it within the same supervisor scope. A backend that observed execution start can supply it at shutdown even if the snapshot missed it. Starting a replacement attempt clears that observation. A client request interrupted before backend execution keeps its empty marker. When a different run takes writer ownership, the session store clears its predecessor’s retained marker in the same write. This also covers a failed startup cleanup followed by a fresh browser input. Capture reuses the pass over live runs and adds no startup transcript scans or scheduler reads. The persisted field is optional and uses the existing event shape.

## Evidence

- [3e97bba47d3b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3e97bba47d3bfae254efba39705fd72e8177efc3) merges [0780dd62406b](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0780dd62406b81d8c597dd6ddbfa86ea20bcd454) into the [previously reviewed head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/de456c5489c85fa20a63b78e0ff354e14c7a6956). A workspace preparation failure retains its own error even after an observed backend start and competing restart and provider metadata. A genuine restart still attributes only the current executing attempt. The session writer still clears a predecessor’s marker on independent admission and preserves it while recovery is pending. **99/99 focused tests passed across six files** on AWS. Scoped formatting and lint passed. Twelve unaffected PR files are byte-identical to the prior head, and main’s provider-summary change in the lifecycle projection merged cleanly. [AWS test run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_bb473591ecb4119fb6057f307360cafc) · [Previous green CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45763179806) · [Current CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45769401132)

- On baseline, **0/5** restart events supplied the originating run. On [98ccbc7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/98ccbc72e7095d6c7172cea8f8a71f5baac0d573), all **5/5** supplied the correct ID. A scripted model used real session history and the native scheduler to verify the saved job, report both typed errors, and leave both interrupted shell commands unretried. An older successful job of the same name was present in the invalid session. All five independent shell tasks completed. [Baseline](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_20d20803d4e8fce1a19a22ecea6443b6) · [Gateway and shell proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_b4a9d4fcd73c4122d5d965ecb00ac936)
- **93/93 tests passed** across eight restart, admission, terminal, and upgrade suites. The runtime build, scoped lint, formatting, and session-identity ratchet passed. The unchanged browser test verifies that a pre-runtime client request cannot supply the backend ID. The captured-start test failed before the terminal writer fix and passed after it. [Failing test](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0fd6441455ae862799c71d9181aca944) · [Exact-tree validation](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_9242e09d74067ac8d6bfa533a165dfaf) · [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45760457871)

It retained the session ID, user label, and original user message, produced one recovery reply, and supplied no invented run ID. prs.title: fix(feishu): route p2p chat ids to the sender session
prs.body:
Closes #205708

## What Problem This Solves 📌

Replying to a Feishu one-to-one chat started a different conversation than the one the message came from, so the assistant "forgot" the thread it was answering. The reply now lands in the same conversation.

- Problem: Feishu chat ids (`oc_...`) are used by both group chats and one-to-one chats, but outbound routing assumed every `oc_` target was a group. A reply to a DM's chat id produced a group-scoped session key (`...:feishu:group:oc_...`) while the inbound message had been recorded under the sender (`...:feishu:direct:ou_...`), so the two never joined up.
- Solution: Resolve the chat kind before choosing the session peer. When the chat reports `chat_mode = p2p`, route to its `p2p_chatter_id` as a direct peer — the same identity inbound DM routing uses — while keeping `chat:<chat_id>` as the delivery address.
- What changed: `extensions/feishu/src/session-route.ts` (peer resolution), `extensions/feishu/src/chat.ts` (expose `p2p_chatter_id`), plus route regression tests and one updated delivery baseline.
- What did NOT change: Group routing, receive-id handling for `ou_`/legacy `user:` targets, and the delivery address for any existing target. Unknown chat kinds and failed lookups fall back to today's group behaviour.

## Why This Change Was Made

The receive-id type alone is not enough information — for Feishu, `chat_id` only says "this is a chat address", not "this is a group". The chat directory already knows the kind (`chat_mode`, `resolveFeishuChatType`), so routing now consults it instead of guessing.

- Best fix: Yes. It reuses the same chat metadata and the same direct-peer identity that inbound routing already derives, so both directions converge on one session key.
- Alternative: Matching on `oc_` prefix or on `chat_type` presence was rejected — neither distinguishes p2p from group reliably.
- Risk / non-goals: The p2p lookup is one extra API call per `oc_` target route. When the lookup fails, the previous (group) behaviour is preserved rather than erroring, so no existing send breaks.

## User Impact

Feishu DM replies now continue the originating conversation, so context, routing, and per-session state stay intact. Behaviour for groups is unchanged, and operators need to do nothing.

## Evidence 📌

Routing matrix for an `oc_` target, asserted in `extensions/feishu/src/session-route.test.ts`:

| Chat kind | Peer | Deliver to | Session key |
|---|---|---|---|
| p2p (`p2p_chatter_id` present) | `ou_sender` (direct) | `chat:oc_...` | `...:feishu:direct:ou_sender` — matches inbound |
| group | `oc_...` (group) | `chat:oc_...` | unchanged |
| p2p without counterpart | `oc_...` (group) | `chat:oc_...` | unchanged (fallback, no regression) |
| lookup throws | `oc_...` (group) | `chat:oc_...` | unchanged (fallback, no regression) |

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/feishu/src/session-route.test.ts \
                extensions/feishu/src/outbound.send-authority.test.ts \
                extensions/feishu/src/channel.test.ts \
                extensions/feishu/src/bot-group-name.test.ts
 ✓ extensions/feishu/src/session-route.test.ts (5 tests)
   ✓ routes a p2p chat id to the sender-scoped direct peer while keeping the chat address
   ✓ keeps genuine groups group-scoped
   ✓ falls back to group routing when p2p chats cannot name the counterpart
   ✓ falls back to group routing when chat metadata cannot be resolved
   ✓ does not claim an exact group route when inbound sessions include sender or topic
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
```

`tsc --noEmit` on the touched files reports no errors; `oxlint` reports 0 warnings, 0 errors.

What was not tested: no live Feishu tenant was exercised — the p2p path is covered through the mocked chat directory, and the wire-level behaviour of `GET /open-apis/im/v1/chats/:chat_id` is unchanged.

prs.title: feat: review spoken self-corrections before adding dictation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #205645

Dictation can leave both an original phrase and its spoken correction in the unsent draft: for example, “Meet on Tuesday sorry Wednesday.” This change prepares a reviewable correction tied to the recording that supplied those words, while retaining the recognized original and protecting existing composer text.

**This is a draft for design acceptance and client qualification.** It does not claim completion of all M03 criteria. The first integration is the current unsent **Control UI conversation composer**, with **en-US** selected and **Off** as the existing-installation default. The private ownership and edit-plan foundation is minimal support for this integration; it is **not an accepted public M11 contract**.

## User Impact

Users can opt into **Explicit corrections (English)** and review supported replacements, sentence retractions and restarts after recording stops. **Literal for this recording** preserves correction phrases for one capture. Every proposed change requires review; **Keep original**, **Accept correction** and **Cancel** do not send a message. Missing or ambiguous evidence retains the recognized words rather than choosing a destructive interpretation.

Corrections affect only this recording's unsent text. They cannot replace a selection that predates recording, edit sent messages, undo actions, invoke agent tools, or switch into Talk. Editing the draft, changing its identity or permissions, or cancelling invalidates the old result. Preferences are scoped to this browser and Gateway; original/candidate text and Literal are not persisted as preferences.

**Rollback:** choose Off. Existing draft text remains intact, future dictation returns to the established raw-transcript behavior, and an eligible pending review can still keep its original. Disabling does not revive a retired candidate or attempt to reverse historical edits.

This PR does not add M01/M02 cleanup/punctuation integration, an M10 external insertion path, or correction support in native clients, headless callers, or New Session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The implementation reuses the existing capture, finalization, FIFO delivery and composer insertion owners. A deterministic local grammar prepares a private versioned plan with source/trigger ranges, protected spans, correction category and capture/revision identity. Validation rejects stale, malformed, overlapping, duplicated or protected edits and enforces bounded input, plan and chain sizes. The grammar preserves ordinary negation, quotation, code strings, identifiers and unsupported numeric forms.

Before inserting a result, the owner binds it to the live pane, physical session, compose permission, capture identity, component edit revision and authoritative draft-publication revision. That publication revision advances even when an external draft replacement has equal text. A review choice is retired before insertion, and pending review holds Send. Same-context connection failure keeps recognized text available for recovery; context revocation clears its transient private review.

The planner adds no model/provider request, broader context collection, tool authority, transcript logging or public Gateway/SDK refinement contract. M01/M02 and an accepted shared M11 pipeline remain separate dependencies. Their combined behavior cannot be qualified by this standalone implementation.

Independent agents reviewed the grammar/validator, ownership boundaries and UI wiring. Findings led to fixes for protected triggers, numeric trailing fragments, external draft mutation fences, disconnect recovery and Off-mode Send behavior. **ClawSweeper has not completed a source review of this implementation.**

ClawSweeper did [review the issue proposal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205645#issuecomment-7178569403) on November 26 at 00:14 UTC, against upstream `26898ee0732b9ef426d175503a07ea6c76be3324`. It recommends evaluating a bounded English-only, opt-in built-in prototype using the existing owners, while leaving built-in versus plugin ownership, grammar and the saved browser preference for maintainers to decide in coordination with filler removal. The issue carries `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr`, `clawsweeper:needs-maintainer-review` and `clawsweeper:needs-product-decision`. This advisory proposal review did not exercise the private implementation, microphone or accessibility; it is not design acceptance or a source-review pass. No human maintainer acceptance appears in the issue thread. Those decisions and the unrun client checks below remain pending.

## Evidence

**Source identity**

- Base: `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c`.
- Initial implementation commit: `4f5ae244f472f764f6616accd0145aa52a4d48ca`.
- Final local head: `afaf479c6e10b661aa67c3cbe5efc33db970c6c0`; source tree `8a86b349fbad0d58911124c9eb7e4869c6b9d9b4`.
- Published branch: [CompleteDotTech/openclaw:feat/dictation-spoken-self-correction](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/tree/feat/dictation-spoken-self-correction).
- Published commits: [d1ed1d9044ed3e7ccc615a9e4302995ee4f28996](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/d1ed1d9044ed3e7ccc615a9e4302995ee4f28996), then final head [95b1575c9368f1ded179ee914e9dfb2a3f2eb781](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/commit/95b1575c9368f1ded179ee914e9dfb2a3f2eb781).
- API publication recreated the commit identities. The initial tree is exactly `1ce605922c14cc41126660ac4752784c8aba9bed`, and the final tree is exactly `8a86b349fbad0d58911124c9eb7e4869c6b9d9b4`, matching the corresponding local trees. The fetched final remote source has an empty diff against local `afaf479c6e10b661aa67c3cbe5efc33db970c6c0`; the base-to-remote comparison contains two commits and 33 changed files.
- Final source hashes and exact local commands/results are retained in `FINAL_SOURCE_MANIFEST.json`, `final-checks.json`, and the evidence package. No public upload of the retained evidence package or screenshot evidence is claimed. The local identities above remain the tested-source record; publication did not rerun the checks.
- Published as **draft [#205794](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205794)**, targeting `openclaw/openclaw:main`, with maintainer edits enabled. GitHub reports no merge conflict against base `8fea10c4543eb3c7e586a277b0a1d274a7d974dd`; merge remains blocked while this is a draft.

**Completed automated checks on the final source**

Canonical repository runner: **197/197 tests passed across five files**, with Node **v24.22.3** and Vitest **5.0.5**. Breakdown: engine **68**, new owner/integration **38**, existing dictation **47**, composer actions **38**, settings **6**. Duration: **15.44 s** in Vitest / **19.60 s** through the wrapper. This run follows the final ownership/UI helper extractions and the controls/review loading split. Evidence: `final-controls-split-tests.log`.

The separate native Node text/property harness passed **2,259 assertions**. These are separate from the canonical test count and do not represent browser or acoustic tests. `correction-engine-results.json` records source hashes, workload timings and memory; `correction-engine-evidence.mjs` is the retained procedure.

| Local workload, 50 warmups and 500 measured samples | p95 |
| --- | ---: |
| Validate 32 disjoint edits / 10,000 ASCII characters | 2.487 ms |
| Reject 32 pathological overlapping edits / 10,000 characters | 3.352 ms |
| Validate 32 edits with a long protected quotation / 10,000 characters | 6.909 ms |
| Prepare complete candidate / 32 corrections / 10,000 characters | 15.958 ms |

Measured host: Linux x64, kernel `6.18.57`, Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C, nine reported logical CPUs. Maximum harness RSS: **194,768 KiB**; the JSON retains per-workload and post-GC memory snapshots. The pure harness made **zero provider calls**; correction preparation adds **zero additional model/provider/tool requests**. Existing speech-provider routing remains in place. These measurements satisfy the proposed 50 ms validation p95 on this host; they do not establish agreed target-device performance, provider latency, a product memory budget, or total Stop-to-preview latency.

**Acceptance-criterion status**

| Criterion | Current evidence and status |
| --- | --- |
| **AC01 — Modes, documentation and defaults** | **Verified locally.** Off/default, one-capture Literal, opt-in/disable, malformed policy fallback and Gateway isolation pass engine/owner/settings tests. `docs/web/webchat.md` documents behavior. Actual browser upgrade and control interaction remain unrun. |
| **AC02 — Unique replacement/retraction/restart** | **Verified with synthetic text.** Engine cases cover day/amount/named replacements, preserved negation/units, empty retraction and restart; owner cases verify reviewed insertion. Actual microphone/provider recognition and resulting live review remain unrun. |
| **AC03 — Ambiguity, quotation, literals and negation** | **Verified with synthetic text/metadata.** Repeated names, competing targets, no-target commands, quotes, backticks, identifiers, ordinary negation and unsupported numeric forms are preserved or reviewed. Injected timing/speaker/order fixtures do not establish real acoustic behavior. |
| **AC04 — Bounds, chains, overlap and at-most-once** | **Verified for the private plan/owner.** Range/source/protection/grapheme checks, duplicate/overlap rejection, 80 generated Unicode samples, 56 generated chain cases and retired-choice/capture tests pass. Bounds are 10,000 UTF-16 units, 32 edits, a maximum chain depth of eight and 256 protected/recognizer spans. External insertion is not exercised. |
| **AC05 — Combined M02/M01 pipeline** | **Incomplete.** M03 retains correction markers until its single local semantic pass and adds no rewrite request. There is no live M01/M02 integration or accepted shared M11 contract; combined protected-token preservation and request/commit counts have not been demonstrated. |
| **AC06 — Stale edits and target/session/mode cancellation** | **Verified at the local production boundary.** Owner/adapter tests cover changed/equal/A→B→A drafts, real ChatState publication, physical session and account/client changes, permission revocation, Talk, cancellation, selected existing text and late callbacks. Native/external application insertion is outside this implementation and unrun. |
| **AC07 — Failure recovery and original-choice retirement** | **Partial.** Unsupported/oversized/ambiguous input, disconnect during capture/finalization, draft invalidation and original/disable retirement are covered. Eager raw-text fallback is implemented, but its browser failure case, live provider faults and complete timeout/import-fault schedules are unrun. “Every failure” is not established. |
| **AC08 — Text-only commands and P06 boundary** | **Verified at the mocked Gateway/composer boundary.** “Actually open the browser and buy it” remains draft text; only existing session create/close requests occur and Talk remains inactive. Pending review holds keyboard/pointer Send without changing Off behavior. A live P06/provider trace is unrun. |
| **AC09 — Keyboard, screen reader and long/magnified review** | **Implemented, unverified in a browser.** Native controls, labelled text regions, changed-span details, count-only live announcement and bounded scrolling are present. Sixteen browser cases are authored; **zero executed, zero screenshots captured or inspected**. Manual keyboard, screen reader and actual browser zoom checks are unrun. |
| **AC10 — Upgrade/disable, privacy/routes and bounded resources** | **Partial.** Node storage tests cover migration/defaults, isolation, disable and transient-field stripping. Code inspection and the recorded local benchmark establish the narrow transform boundary and host measurements. Actual browser migration, live privacy/routing traces, agreed client hardware and end-to-end latency remain unrun. |

**Repository and client qualification**

Final scoped UI lint, formatting, CSS stylelint and the controller guard passed. i18n verification, the single-file docs MDX check and final test-line allocation also passed. Catalog-script lint was blocked before lint execution by plugin-SDK boundary declaration preparation (exit 13, unsettled top-level await). UI and UI-test typecheck attempts exited **137**; no typecheck pass is claimed.

The production UI build at `4f5ae244f` succeeded, but its report-only asset budget reported five overages: document gzip +8 B, largest CSS gzip +344 B, chat boot +1 JS request and +1 CSS request, and chat boot JS gzip +2,144 B. The final commit separates the small native policy controls from the full lazy review, removing the source-level eager loading edge without changing controls or recovery. Its build transformed 5,714 modules, then exited **137** while rendering chunks. Two exact-base builds also exited 137. **Final build and asset-budget qualification remain blocked; final byte savings and inheritance of earlier overages are unproven.** No limit was raised or suppressed.

Chromium was unavailable and canonical provisioning returned **HTTP 403**. Therefore the 16 authored browser cases ran **zero assertions**, and planned screenshot paths are not visual evidence. Real microphone/provider sessions, acoustic accuracy, manual accessibility, native external insertion and total Stop-to-preview latency are **NOT RUN**. The enlarged-root-text browser fixture, even when executed, is not a substitute for actual browser zoom or screen-reader checks. Keep this PR draft while required qualification/design acceptance is pending.

**Test-line allocation and author limit**

Literal-LF accounting against the named base, including all changed and untracked test files, gives **+1,449 lines**. The 400-line allowance leaves **1,049 lines**, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/dictation-spoken-self-correction.txt`. The additional coverage spans grammar/protected-range properties, production ownership and race schedules, recovery/Send regressions, preference migration, and prepared accessibility/layout cases; reusing existing dictation and settings helpers avoids duplicating their owners. Detailed counts and file hashes are retained in `test-line-delta.json`. Recalculate if final changes alter tests.

The pre-publication audit found no existing M03 PR. A post-publication author audit observed **5 open upstream PRs for CompleteDotTech**, including this draft, within the **20-PR limit**. Companion drafts include punctuation #205788, conservative cleanup #205789, formatting #205791 and writing profiles #205792. Their existence does not establish accepted M01/M02/M11 integration in this source tree.

The final independent source re-review found no actionable issue in the controls/review split; it did not execute browser or hardware checks. Post-publication [PR context and evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45767260580/job/139731040021), [Socket PR alerts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/runs/139731146682) and [Socket project report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/runs/139731070310) checks passed.
