prs.title: feat: review dictated paragraphs and lists before applying them
prs.body:
Related: #205634

## What Problem This Solves

People dictating paragraphs or shopping lists into the Control UI currently receive a text transcript and must manually recreate its structure. Treating every occurrence of “bullet” or “new paragraph” as a command would also corrupt ordinary discussion, quotes, and code. This contribution adds an explicit, reviewable formatting path while retaining the current recognized-text behavior by default.

## User Impact

Users can opt into **Interpret explicit structure (English)** in the existing microphone controls. After Stop, they can compare semantic, plain, and original-text previews, confirm ambiguous paragraph commands, and apply an eligible result or copy it for recovery. Formatting never continues into Send. The draft remains editable in Explicit mode; editing it invalidates the captured insertion target instead of allowing an older result to overwrite it.

The initial grammar supports paragraphs, line breaks, ordered and unordered lists, and nesting up to the proposed depth of three. Explicit item numbers, order, quantities, negation, names, protected strings, and literal marker discussion stay source-backed. Headings, tables, inferred Suggest structure, attachments, spreadsheet operations, and document automation are outside this initial scope.

| Representation | Supported boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Plain text | An unchanged direct-dictation field whose actual capabilities support safe multiline text and an existing undoable adapter; otherwise review/copy. |
| Markdown (`commonmark-0.31.2-lists`) | The built-in Markdown composer with an empty draft or the entire captured draft selected. Partial insertion is refused because surrounding Markdown could reinterpret the result. |
| Rich preparation (`safe-blocks-v1`) | Allowlisted paragraph/list HTML and semantic preview only. **No native/external rich insertion adapter is qualified by this PR.** |
| Unknown, stale, or revoked capability | Readable review/copy recovery; no guessed target and no automatic fallback write. |

**This PR must remain a draft.** Full UI types, production build, browser/device/accessibility proof, native rich insertion/Undo, final-head CI, and maintainer acceptance remain open as detailed below. The requested full feature path is implemented, but its mandatory external qualifications are not complete.

Rollback is the existing mode control: choose **Preserve recognized text**. Absence, malformed policies, unsupported versions, and Preserve normalize to the previous behavior. The version-1 Explicit opt-in is stored in the existing Gateway-scoped browser preference record; it is not synchronized through server `ui.prefs`. Disabling it preserves drafts, speech-provider selection, unrelated preferences, and message history.

## Why This Change Was Made

One bounded semantic document drives plain text, Markdown, and allowlisted HTML. Its validator checks source coverage and order, consumed-marker reasons, source/grapheme ranges, protected content, cycles, node kinds, and resource bounds before any representation is used. Markdown is checked with independent `markdown-it` parsing; rich output is checked with `parse5`. No generated HTML or remote resource is trusted, and spoken URLs are never fetched by formatting.

Live triage did not establish an accepted physical M11 parent to stack on. This PR therefore implements the minimal private lifecycle prerequisite in the **existing** dictation owner/session: immutable capture policy and source revision, generation and deadline eligibility, current target/selection/capability, cancellation, and truthful delivery receipts. It does not claim the wider M11 proposal is complete. Optional M01/M02/M03/M05/M08 integrations are not implemented as new renderer-local rewrites. The formatter adds no speech/model request, durable transcript store, clipboard manager, automation owner, or public RPC.

Related parallel proposals now published are [M01 punctuation #205788](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205788) and [M02 cleanup #205789](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205789). Both remain drafts; neither establishes an accepted M11 parent. Their shared owner/policy boundaries require consolidation and enabled-together proof before joint acceptance. This contribution does not claim that integration.

Preparation and insertion are separate. Main, Side chat, and New Session reuse their existing draft owners and editor history boundary. An attempted indivisible edit produces `not-committed`, `committed`, or `outcome-unknown`; uncertainty cannot trigger a plain-text retry. Rich preview success does not qualify an external rich editor. A proposed 2,500 ms Explicit finalization deadline cannot turn partial recognition into a complete formatted result.

The implementation is cohesive across recognition finalization, validation, preview, settings, and reviewed placement. A renderer-only slice would leave the required lifecycle and user recovery behavior unimplemented. The stateless helper extraction keeps lifecycle authority with the existing owner. Test growth is +2,269 LF lines against the base, supported by the explicit 1,869-line allocation request above the 400-line default. Separate suites cover independent parser/source invariants, owner races, settings retention, real owner/adapter/component boundaries, submission guards, and the canonical browser fixture; the test file cap remains unchanged.

## Evidence

### Revision and acceptance

- Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205634 (M04 is a planning identifier).
- Base branch: `openclaw/openclaw:main`; checkout base: `04b854b239cd8ab8a14beae4914ed9c54d791e62`.
- Contribution branch: `CompleteDotTech:feat/dictation-semantic-formatting`.
- Original reviewed local commit: `0ac21ce48c7ece9fa6730953d568c9329cac7e8d`; final pushed head: `75070f7628a8651907294c60ce33037e08be1c85`. The connected GitHub API created the publication commit with the exact same tree (`e8150681855fb9bb915e30439169fdf79b4aa1d9`); every changed source hash matches the reviewed/tested local commit.
- Companion manifest and evidence package: [m04-dictation-implementation.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35448007/m04-dictation-implementation.zip) ([publication comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205791#issuecomment-7184441110)). Archive SHA-256: `47d926ae9da08ef637f18f6b11358c8beaf578c43f2807bc6717a497431e68e7`. Includes the exact published-head bundle/patch, 52-file source manifest, AC ledger, 28 check/blocked-attempt logs, original benchmark and GitHub publication/CI receipt.
- Full AC ledger: `docs/reference/dictation-formatting-evidence.md`; user guide: `docs/web/control-ui-dictation-formatting.md`.
- Maintainer acceptance of the private contract, local preference, grammar/formats, provisional bounds, and test allocation remains pending. The [automated issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205634#issuecomment-7178200686) recommends a bounded private prototype and shared preparation/preference decisions; it is not human maintainer acceptance. No public schema or dependency approval is asserted.

| Criterion | Implemented and observed | Required remaining qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC01: defaults and policy | Preserve/default/invalid-version behavior; Explicit opt-in; prior-record and rollback tests pass. | Production upgrade/downgrade journey. |
| AC02: meaning and item invariants | 33 semantic cases include exact numbering, nesting, negation, names, RTL, protected bytes, delimiters, and independent parser comparisons. | Actual microphone recognition fidelity. |
| AC03: literal markers and intent | Ordinary discussion, quoted/code content, exact reviewed marker confirmation, and replacement invalidation pass. | Real voice/keyboard review journey. |
| AC04: bounded representation | Malformed ranges, missing/duplicate/reordered content, cycles, node/version/count/depth violations, and bounded mutations pass. | Maintainer acceptance and broader corpus qualification of limits. |
| AC05: safe deterministic forms | Shared validated source; independent Markdown and HTML parsing; hostile text stays inert. | Real-browser zero-resource-load observation. |
| AC06: capability choice | Actual owner/adapter/component tests cover editable/history capability, readonly/disabled, selection, focus, edit-then-restore, and unknown targets. | Browser plain/Markdown and qualified native rich insertion/Undo. |
| AC07: lifecycle and receipts | 47 existing-owner and 34 review-lifecycle cases pass, including stop reentrancy, timeout, cancellation, source/scope/policy invalidation, incomplete recovery, and uncertain effects. | Final-head browser/CI integration proof. |
| AC08: inert delivery | Four editor-history transaction cases and main/Side chat/New Session submission regressions pass. | Native Undo and complete browser no-Send journey. |
| AC09: accessible review | Eight preview-component and seven actual owner/adapter/Solid view cases pass, including focused Finish removal and eligible focus return. | Real keyboard, screen reader, 400% browser zoom, large text/high contrast, and before/after visuals. |
| AC10: migration/privacy/resources | Local policy normalization/rollback and draft retention pass; validation/render warm p95 meets the proposed budget. | Real speech-route/egress evidence, production downgrade, and resource-limit acceptance. |

### Executed checks

**295 distinct focused cases pass across 13 suites.** The final combined batch passed 294/295 (16.44 s Vitest; 20.05 s wrapper). Its one failure used the former read-only state as a proxy for recording completion. Only that trigger changed from `!locksComposer` to `!active`; assertions were unchanged, and all 34 review-lifecycle cases passed on rerun (3.07 s / 5.71 s). The final editor API guard was independently reviewed and its four history cases passed again (2.05 s / 4.65 s). This is combined evidence, not a claim of one clean 295-case run.

The actual owner/session/direct-adapter/Solid-view regression reproduced two failures before the fixes; the final seven-case integration suite passed. Only external media/Gateway/editor-engine seams are synthetic in that suite.

Passing static checks: four production formatter modules through the supported `tsgo` wrapper; scoped type-aware lint (45 UI/i18n files, with five unchanged baseline Solid warnings); final controller ratchets; English catalog baseline and verification; review CSS; changed-file formatting; three changed MDX documents. The standalone benchmark's exact audit entry is included. Direct configuration syntax lint and both maximum-line/test-line ratchets pass. Canonical root configuration type-aware lint was blocked in SDK boundary declaration preparation (exit 13), before lint ran. The production unused-file audit passes with zero entries; its full-tree companion exhausted the configured 1 GiB JavaScript heap and remains blocked. All results are recorded in the companion manifest.

The full documentation-anchor audit reports eight failures. An actual base-snapshot run reproduced the identical eight; there are **zero new broken links** across 20,259 checked links. The optional ClawHub mirror was unavailable. This is not a claim that the aggregate documentation gate is green.

### Measured performance

Linux 6.18.57, Node 24.22.3, Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C, nine logical CPUs, 10,451,423,232 bytes RAM. Each workload has 10,000 characters/100 blocks, ten warmups, and 100 warm samples; nested input has 99 items/depth three.

| Workload | Validation + rendering p50 / p95 / max (ms) | Full preparation p95 (ms) | First call (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Paragraphs | 11.588 / 21.880 / 30.903 | 59.576 | 69.272 |
| Escaped paragraphs | 9.823 / 14.926 / 38.760 | 36.211 | 15.240 |
| Nested lists | 18.170 / 34.074 / 95.481 | 70.478 | 35.917 |

All three validation/rendering p95 values meet the proposed 50 ms budget. Full preparation includes planning and does not meet 50 ms for every workload. Only the first workload's first call was process-first; these are not repeated cold-start distributions. The harness did not record p99. Maximum observed between-iteration RSS was 199,987,200 bytes and heap use 72,333,120 bytes; these are not continuous peaks. The benchmark makes zero provider calls; STT, microphone-to-preview, and user-review latency remain **NOT RUN**.

The original benchmark artifact retains measured source hashes. A later identifier-only rename in `formatting.ts` satisfies the shadowing lint rule; the other measured modules and harness are unchanged. The final manifest preserves both the measured and committed hashes.

### Review and remaining gates

Independent reviews covered source-token coverage, protected whitespace, literal marker discussion, sanitizer/parser independence, selection and Markdown context, incomplete-result reprocessing, stop reentrancy, target authority, focused-control removal, no-Send guards, and unknown-effect fallback. Actionable findings were fixed and affected tests rerun. Final production review, separate settings review, and the final history-guard review found no outstanding actionable findings. This review does not replace native/browser qualification.

- **Full UI types and changed integration graph: BLOCKED**, checker processes exited 137 under the available memory limit.
- **Production build: BLOCKED**, including a bounded-memory retry; 5,711 modules transformed before exit 137 at chunk rendering.
- **Browser E2E: BLOCKED**, pinned Chromium revision 1248 unavailable. Its supported installer received HTTP 403 from `cdn.playwright.dev`. One setup-failed suite / ten skipped scenarios; no browser assertions or screenshots executed. A separate baseline screenshot dependency installation exhausted disk and was removed without deleting the base Git metadata.
- **Real microphone/STT, native rich editor/Undo, screen reader, browser-chrome 400% zoom, current-build visual evidence, production downgrade, and speech-route egress: NOT RUN.** The fixture's narrow/RTL/enlarged-text/forced-colors/200%-equivalent CSS checks do not certify these.
- **CI: BLOCKED awaiting upstream maintainer approval.** All ten pull-request workflow runs are `action_required`; GitHub displays “10 workflows awaiting approval” and “This workflow requires approval from a maintainer.” The main CI run has no jobs, and `openclaw/ci-gate` is expected. This is no passing build/test execution evidence. Draft CI policy does not waive the build. Required exact-head CI and the above evidence must pass before readiness; maintainer-only dispatch or approval is not invoked without maintainer authority.
- **Publication:** `CompleteDotTech/openclaw` is verified as the author’s writable fork. Only `feat/dictation-semantic-formatting` was published. The current contribution limit is 20 open PRs including drafts; the immediate pre-publication check found two (both drafts), leaving this contribution within the limit. Maintainer edits are enabled.

Recovery: restore the patch/bundle against the recorded base, provision enough build/typecheck resources and the pinned Chromium browser, run the canonical `dictation-formatting.e2e.test.ts` against the production bundle, then execute the named-device procedures in the AC ledger. Supply a genuinely qualified M10 rich adapter and record actual insertion/Undo before claiming that boundary. Preserve the original-text and review/copy paths while qualifications remain open. This PR references the issue and must not close it or be merged while those gates remain unresolved.

prs.title: feat: review conservative English dictation cleanup before sending
prs.body:
Related: #205635

**Draft — implementation is published for review; required build, client, integration, and design qualification is incomplete.**

- Fork branch: [CompleteDotTech/openclaw:feat/dictation-conservative-cleanup](https://github.com/CompleteDotTech/openclaw/tree/feat/dictation-conservative-cleanup)
- Immediate implementation base: `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c`; target: `openclaw/openclaw:main`.
- Published head: `aae4919e4744a791d7edf4e3ad94aa841af0a877`.
- Tested/reviewed local head: `b632d7829aa401eacb23b3c863ad09183cf880f8`.
- Both heads have the identical source tree `96ef3028a13186996dab4e19eba55d480857a652`. The workspace restarted during GitHub authentication; the verified saved package was recovered and published through the authenticated connector in the same three focused commits. Commit metadata changed; source did not. Remote comparison confirms exactly 31 changed files and three commits above the named base.

This work was implemented with Codex and peer-agent review. It does not claim human maintainer design acceptance. Allow edits by maintainers is enabled; no workflow files or new secrets are part of this change.

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI dictation places the recognizer's text into the draft. Users who want to remove a clear hesitation or exact restart must edit it themselves. An optional cleanup policy needs to preserve meaningful repetition, qualifiers, negation, names, numbers, and the recognized original wherever recovery remains authorized.

## User Impact

- Cleanup starts Off. An explicit **Conservative — English** choice enables a narrow set of English suggestions for future recordings.
- Final review shows the original recognized text, the candidate, and removed source text. Choosing either version adds it to the unsent draft. Cleanup itself never sends the message.
- After accepting a candidate, **Restore original** is available only while the exact owned draft is unchanged. Manual edits revoke replacement. Eligible original text remains available for manual copying.
- Explicit retry prepares retained recognized text against the current draft and selected policy. Cancelled, stale, unauthorized, and uncertain attempted writes cannot silently replay into the draft.
- Resolve, cancel, or dismiss an unaccepted Conservative review before the next capture. One pending preparation is retained. Off keeps the existing ordered queue for multiple stopped recordings. Concurrent pending Conservative reviews are not supported.
- Conservative review drops source text above the shared 32 KiB UTF-8 bound and shows an unavailable state. Dismiss it and record a shorter utterance. Raw recovery from that oversized review is not promised.
- Cleanup adds no model-provider request, audio buffer, transcript log, or learned speech profile. Existing recognition can still use its configured network provider.

The implementation covers browser Control UI Chat, New Session, and the session sidebar. It does not add cleanup to native applications or external text fields. The small initial English pattern set limits coverage. It proposes deletion only, with no punctuation, grammar, translation, or style rewrite. The original is the text the recognizer returned and cannot restore words that recognition already omitted.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing composer dictation owner already owns capture, ordered finalization, connection and draft scope, and publication. This change adds one private local preparation/review stage there, carrying source identity and revision, an explicit policy, original-source deletion ranges, and a source map. Validation reconstructs the candidate from retained source slices and rejects unsafe plans.

The Control UI plugin SDK can propose composer text but does not register a dictation transform or supply the capture owner's revision and recognition metadata. The existing owner avoids a second capture or publication path. There is no new Gateway RPC, public SDK registration, or per-feature model call. Settings use the existing browser-local, Gateway-scoped owner, and Off removes the new override. Missing recognition metadata stays missing. Low confidence can veto a deletion, never authorize it.

This remains a bounded private proposal, not an accepted common M11 lifecycle. The [automated M02 comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205635#issuecomment-7178237401) requests common ownership and precision decisions before acceptance. It is not human maintainer endorsement. Parallel drafts are now published for [M01 punctuation #205788](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205788), [M03 corrections #205794](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205794), [M04 structure #205791](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205791), and [M05 profiles #205792](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205792). They are separate proposals with overlapping private owner boundaries, not accepted physical parents. Their existence does not qualify combined plans; a common owner/plan and enabled-together proof still need consolidation before joint acceptance. The [M05 issue #205638](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205638) proposes `users.prefs`, which differs from this browser/Gateway setting. Common preference scope, concurrency, and migration remain design decisions.

## Evidence

[Download the retained qualification evidence](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35447695/openclaw-m02-publication-evidence.zip) — 99,267 bytes, SHA-256 `18bc7ab129720bf728a4a45d9f1faccd19339195e21bcf540d6dfe8daefce429`. This contains raw passing/failed/incomplete check logs, the AC ledger, benchmark JSON, review records, command manifests, and publication/source binding. It contains no real-user audio or transcript and no claimed screenshot proof.

### Final source and local checks

Published commit: `aae4919e4744a791d7edf4e3ad94aa841af0a877`, with the identical source tree as tested local commit `b632d7829aa401eacb23b3c863ad09183cf880f8`. The validation source tree was `a99371fd69383f8529596cf10a7b72b197f9fba6`. Only the benchmark script changed afterward to repair its JSON decoder lint finding. That repaired script passed separate typed lint and a complete benchmark run. Product UI, tests, configuration, and docs are unchanged from the validated tree. `FINAL_HEAD_BINDING.json` records this source comparison, final file hashes, clean working tree, and final benchmark-format and committed-diff checks. The separate `final-binding.json` records repaired-lint file hashes and final benchmark parity. `REVIEW.md` separates peer review scope from author self-review.

| Check | Observed result | Evidence and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Focused regression tests | **180 passed across 6 files**, wrapper duration 29.73 s | Processor, refinement, settings, capture owner, source revision/finality, and direct adapters. `focused-verified.log` and full command in `final-validation.manifest.json`. |
| Changed product UI lint | **Exit 0** | One pre-existing `visibleDraft` Solid reactivity warning remains. `lint-ui-verified.log`. |
| Repaired benchmark/Knip config lint | **Exit 0**, empty log | Checked files match committed blobs. `lint-scripts-repair.log` and `FINAL_HEAD_BINDING.json`. |
| I18n verification | **Passed** | `i18n-verified.log`. |
| Test-line budget and line caps | **Both passed** | `test-line-budget.log`, `line-caps.log`. |
| Changed TS/CSS/JSON and docs formatting, diff check | **Passed** | `format-verified.log`, `docs-format-verified.log`, `diff-check.log`. |
| UI typechecks | **Incomplete**: default, bounded, supported alternate-backend, and capacity retry exited 137 before diagnostics | No typecheck pass. All `types-ui*` logs retained. |
| Production UI build | **Incomplete**: 5,707 modules transformed, then exit 137 | No completed build. `ui-build.log`. |
| Unused-file scan | **Incomplete** | Resource-heavy wrapper interrupted, production Knip child SIGKILL recorded, no usable scan verdict. `deadcode.log`. |
| Browser E2E | **Blocked before assertions**: one failed suite, six skipped scenarios | Required Chromium absent. Standard install returned HTTP 403. No screenshot or keyboard result. |
| Upstream CI | **Awaiting maintainer approval; no product CI pass** | Seven fork workflows report `action_required`; [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45766368456) has zero jobs. The PR page explicitly says approval from a maintainer is required. `openclaw/ci-gate` is expected; Proof is skipped/on request. PR context-and-evidence passed; administrative success is not build/test qualification. |

Earlier actual assertion/lint failures and resource-killed attempts remain in the evidence directory. They are not relabeled as passes. The final successful checks above supersede only the scope they exercised.

### Deterministic stage measurement

The final command ran on the committed script, engine, and corpus, with all three SHA-256 hashes unchanged during execution and matching committed blobs. It exited 0 in 22.99 s. The workload was exactly 2,000 ASCII characters, SHA-256 `c40b2264aa0a877f766117a38dfe0966bdd39d710514fce12ae7c0cfa51a4cba`. The stage times actual policy admission of a prepared policy, proposal, validation, and source mapping. It excludes UI settings lookup, module import, browser rendering, microphone acquisition, and recognition. Off is a current-revision control, not a pre-feature baseline.

| Policy and state | Samples | p50 | p95 | p99 | Maximum |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Off, cold first call | 5 | 0.150 ms | 0.160 ms | 0.160 ms | 0.160 ms |
| Conservative, cold first call | 5 | 5.494 ms | 7.785 ms | 7.785 ms | 7.785 ms |
| Off, warm | 5,000 | 0.000089 ms | 0.000187 ms | 0.000286 ms | 0.232 ms |
| Conservative, warm | 5,000 | 0.211 ms | 1.566 ms | 3.100 ms | 27.764 ms |

The proposed 25 ms p95 target passed on Node v24.22.3 / Linux 6.18.57 / Xeon Platinum 8573C, with 9 logical CPUs visible. One-minute host load was 1.80 before and 4.45 after. The warm maximum was 27.764 ms, so this is a percentile result, not a maximum-latency guarantee or an agreed reference-hardware launch gate. Cold samples are five fresh processes per policy, interleaved Off/Conservative. Warm samples follow 1,000 warmup calls per policy.

The separate process actually used `--expose-gc`, warmed up for 1,000 calls, and processed 10,000 synthetic sessions with post-GC samples after each 1,000. Final retained heap changed by -5,208 bytes, with RSS increasing 8,519,680 bytes. The declared +2 MiB retained-heap guard passed. This measures released pure-function results, not browser or audio retention.

The 36-case authored corpus is balanced 12/12/12 across safe remove, must retain, and ambiguous retain. All 36 complete expected candidates matched. All 13 accepted removal spans matched the authored oracle, with zero false-deletion cases. Both retention classes stayed unchanged, and critical-content controls preserved their complete expected remainder. Deletion volume was 37 of 939 source characters and is reported separately from precision. These are synthetic expectations, not independent semantic annotation or a real-world error-rate estimate.

Reproduce:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-dictation-cleanup.mts
```

Full current proof: `benchmark-final.json`, `benchmark-final.manifest.json`, and `BENCHMARK_REPORT.md`. The first run and its different host conditions remain preserved separately. No speedup is attributed to comparing those two runs.

### Browser and remaining qualification

The maintained six-scenario browser file covers default policy/persistence, light/dark desktop and narrow review, keyboard actions, cleaned acceptance/restoration, and New Session manual-edit suppression. None executed: Chromium setup failed, and the ordinary pinned Chrome download returned HTTP 403 “Site Unavailable”. The visible system launcher also lacked its backing binary. No skip flag, alternate download route, or fabricated image was used. Exact commands are in `UI_E2E_REPORT.md` and `ui-e2e.manifest.json`, with raw failure logs retained.

Physical microphone/transcription-provider behavior, provider latency, a named real screen reader, exact-base comparison screenshots, and enabled-together correction/punctuation/snippet/profile handlers are **not qualified**. Recognized-source provenance and common-profile decisions remain open. There are no inline PR screenshots to claim as evidence.

This PR stays draft and uses **Related** until the original acceptance criteria and design decisions are resolved. `AC_LEDGER.md` retains all ten original criterion sentences and distinguishes measured, partial, blocked, and unmeasured coverage. The issue should not be closed solely by the deterministic unit corpus or stage benchmark.


### Acceptance coverage

| Criteria | Demonstrated coverage | Open requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC01–AC03 | Defaults/settings and owner tests; narrow removal, critical protection, malformed plans, source mapping, and 36-case corpus pass | Actual browser qualification and broader accepted corpus/precision gate |
| AC04 | Correction evidence and immutable source ranges retained | Actual joint enabled correction/punctuation/snippet/profile handlers through a common accepted owner |
| AC05 | Absent/invalid metadata, low confidence, unsupported locale, provisional/final source cases pass | Live provider/source provenance proof |
| AC06–AC07 | Raw choice, late callbacks, edits/Undo, retries, cancel, auth changes, explicit refusal/uncertain attempted write, and owned restoration pass | Broader concurrent Conservative lifecycle, actual browser recovery; oversized/revoked source deliberately has no automatic raw recovery |
| AC08 | Neutral labels and native review controls implemented | Real keyboard/browser screenshots and named screen reader |
| AC09 | Same-state settings upgrade/disable and local privacy/route/authorization boundaries pass | Common preference/provenance acceptance and actual browser upgrade flow |
| AC10 | Processor latency, released-result retention, authored precision and removal volume measured separately | Full recognition/provider latency, browser-owner retention, agreed hardware and annotated corpus |

### Review and simplification

Independent review found and resolved three concrete faults: a thrown original-text write could leave a late-final route alive; authorization was sampled at Stop instead of capture admission; cancelling an oversized source could enable its empty placeholder as original. Their boundary regressions pass in the final 180-test run. Reviewer authorship is separated from self-review in the retained review record. No local ClawSweeper execution is claimed.

The author completed the required `pr-simplify` full-diff pass before committing. The smallest coherent first stage is the private, opt-in English review through the existing capture, ordered-commit, and owned-draft paths. This avoids a disconnected engine with no recoverable user flow. No separate model route, public contract, native/external insertion, or speculative sibling engine is included. The pass required no additional architectural change; it does not claim removal of nonexistent machinery. Production changes are 17 files, +1,494/−86; focused tests/corpus +1,133/−23; prepared E2E +313; docs +186/−8; benchmark/config +382. Total: 31 files, +3,508/−117.

### Capacity, rollback, and proof availability

The local runner could not complete UI typecheck/build or the unused-file scan despite bounded serialized recovery attempts. A qualified remote build runner is not available to this contributor session. This uses the repository's explicit draft/build-capacity route; draft status does not waive build success. No required CI gate is bypassed or reported green. Knip unused-file proof remains a separate required check beyond ordinary PR CI.

Set cleanup to Off to retire pending suggestions and return future recordings to the recognizer-output path; Off removes the persisted override without rewriting drafts or history. Restore remains limited to the unchanged owned unsent draft. Recognition route selection is unchanged.

Raw logs, exact command/environment manifests, corpus and benchmark JSON, the AC ledger, source binding, and review records are available in the evidence ZIP linked above. Browser assertions and screenshots do not exist yet and are not substituted with a mock image.

prs.title: feat: review dictation with optional punctuation
prs.body:
# feat: review dictation with optional punctuation

**Draft implementation — M01 acceptance remains incomplete.** The source is
published on the author’s fork with passing focused proof and open qualification
gates. This PR requests review of the bounded private proposal; it does not claim
maintainer acceptance of its preparation or preference boundary.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205630

- Base repository/branch: `openclaw/openclaw:main`
- Chosen base SHA: `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c`
- Head branch: `feat/dictation-automatic-punctuation`
- Pushed head SHA: `35050a50ddaeb76a071627305df9eff7810c7196`
- Originally tested local commit: `38902b0cc0a1f692dd08442b3eec38629c28e669`
- Verified identical complete source tree: `61018a84ddda2bcd0a4e9c4c86a58a28b2505b2d`
- Head repository: `CompleteDotTech/openclaw`
- Required upstream CI: **NOT RUN**; draft dispatch requires an authorized upstream maintainer.

The GitHub-authenticated publication created a new commit identity from the same
parent and exact source tree. The original 225-case run and benchmark therefore
remain byte-identical source evidence. A fresh run on the published commit will
be recorded separately if completed; prior results are not relabeled as new runs.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI dictation path at the chosen base inserts recognizer output without
an optional punctuation review. People dictating technical prose need an explicit
choice about casing and marks while preserving negation, numeric values, names,
and literal strings. They also need to inspect the original and prepared text
before inserting it, recover when recognition or refinement is incomplete, and
undo a known insertion.

## User Impact

Existing installations remain **Off**. Settings → Talk → Dictation punctuation
opts this browser into review before insertion. The modes are:

- **Verbatim:** preserve recognizer-provided text, punctuation, and casing. It
  cannot recover words or punctuation already changed by the recognizer.
- **Automatic:** for explicitly selected `en-US`, capitalize an eligible
  unprotected opening at the beginning of a field and add a missing final period
  when authorized right context is empty. It does not infer internal sentence
  boundaries or questions. Fragment mode suppresses automatic casing/endings.
- **Explicit:** additionally requires the separate spoken-command setting. The
  grammar uses `insert comma`, `insert colon`, `insert semicolon`, and supported
  final commands such as `insert period`. The only bare shorthand is
  `hello comma <one plain word> period`. Other bare punctuation words remain
  literal; quoted/code spans stay protected.

Review distinguishes the original from the validated candidate and explains
fallbacks in text. Use original and Reprocess original retire the previous
preparation revision without another provider request. Insert into draft performs
one local transaction and never sends the message. Sending during an opted-in
capture stops for review. A known unchanged insertion can be undone once through
the existing composer history boundary. An attempted or unknown result cannot be
automatically pasted again.

Editing, target replacement, cancellation, a new capture, or revoked provenance
removes old insertion authority. Eligible text already recognized before target
retirement remains recoverable; later provider events cannot replace it.
Hint-influenced original text is redacted when its source is revoked. Incomplete
provider output is visibly incomplete and cannot be inserted as a final result.

The declared initial scope is the Control UI's main composer and direct dictation
adapter. Only synthetic `en-US` fixtures are qualified so far. Unsupported or
absent locale/context, non-Latin text, and explicitly flagged mixed language keep
the original. Arbitrary Latin-script code switching, other language packs, native
app dictation, external application insertion, and system-wide Undo are not
qualified or supplied here.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing dictation owner still owns capture, provider admission, finalization,
and its commit queue. A private helper holds one preparation/review/receipt state;
the local engine returns bounded source-mapped edits. Validation replays half-open
UTF-16 edits at ICU grapheme boundaries, checks capture/revision/schema identity,
protects literal and technical ranges, and independently checks lexical coverage.
It rejects unauthorized punctuation even if the same words survive. There is no
second provider client, model call, punctuation queue, transcript store, or cloud
fallback.

The smallest needed M11 foundation is included in this change because bounded
source/tracker inspection did not establish an accepted upstream M11 implementation
or parent branch. No M11 dependency issue/PR was bulk-published, so there is no
remote dependency URL or ref to invent. The live design discussion is the linked
issue. Optional dictionary/literal producers can supply explicit protected spans;
their absence does not disable the local protection layer. Local insertion and
Undo reuse the existing composer transaction owner, including its existing task
caller. No public plugin SDK or Gateway schema was added.

The [ClawSweeper issue review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205630#issuecomment-7178173319)
asks maintainers to resolve preparation and preference ownership together with
[companion formatting proposal #205634](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205634).
That review examined the proposal and upstream source, not this implementation.
It recommends reviewing a bounded deterministic opt-in en-US private prototype;
it does not supply maintainer acceptance. This PR keeps the existing capture owner
and one private preparation/review helper. Formatting remains a distinct proposed
transform; no competing provider client or preparation queue is introduced here.
The remaining decision is whether that private boundary and preference owner are
accepted for both transforms or a public plugin contract must precede them.

Core/plugin placement, the browser preference, the initial locale/client, and the
reference desktop still need upstream acceptance. The private implementation is a
concrete proposal for that review. It does not claim approval to introduce a new
public schema or retention policy.

Only a strict, versioned browser preference is saved. Invalid/future preferences
disable refinement and show a warning; unvalidated fields are not copied back on
settings writes. The setting is excluded from Gateway preference synchronization.
No transcript, audio, context, or protected term is added to telemetry or storage.
Inserted text keeps the existing draft/message storage behavior. Recognition still
uses the configured provider; local punctuation does not promise offline STT.

Rollback is content-preserving: select Off or remove the preference, cancel/dismiss
any current review if desired, and subsequent captures use the existing path.
An utterance's resolved policy stays frozen unless its unsent original is explicitly
reprocessed. Existing voice settings and committed draft text are retained.

prs.title: refactor(admission): command owner comes from admission (OA2 PR 7)
prs.body:
## Problem

OA2 PR 7 (one admission owner, same person same answer).

`/status`-class commands got their owner bit from `resolveCommandAuthorization` itself: it matched the sender against `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, read `operator.admin` from the socket scopes, and OR-ed in the command-owner capability bound at ingress. That match was the last owner decision outside the admission module (`OWNER_PRODUCER_FILES`), and it is the only owner source for asserted-identity channels (iMessage, SMS, IRC, Tlon, Slack relay, A2A, Feishu) and pre-turn senders (native commands).

## Fix

- `operator-admission.ts`: new `readCommandSenderAdmission(ctx, owners, senderIds)`. It returns the owner principal's grant when the internal turn's grant (or a bare connection's scopes) is owner, when ingress admitted a command owner for this context, or when one of the sender's identifiers is a configured owner. `command-auth.ts` reads `.grant.owner` from it and no longer decides: the identity match, the scope fallback and the capability read are deleted there.
- The `ownerAllowFrom` match and the command-owner preparation (`resolveOwnerAllowFromList`, `resolveConfiguredCommandOwners`, `isConfiguredCommandOwner`, `prepareCommandOwnerAuthority`, `captureCommandOwnerIdentity`) move unchanged from `command-auth.ts` to a new `src/auto-reply/command-owner-facts.ts`. This breaks the `command-auth` ↔ `operator-admission` import cycle; `operator-admission.ts` is at its `max-lines` limit, and putting them in `command-owner-authority.ts` closes a madge cycle through `channel-operator-authority`. Importers point at the new file; no re-exports.
- Deleted while moving: the two thin wrappers `resolveCommandOwnerAuthority` / `resolveUpdateRequesterIdentityAuthority` (the update requester passes its resolver to `captureCommandOwnerIdentity`), the unread `operatorProfile` field on `PreparedCommandOwnerAuthority`, a redundant dynamic import in `session-event-target.ts`, and four `TURN_FLAGS` names with no reader left (`senderIsOwnerByScope`, `recordedOperatorAuthority`, `isHumanTurn`, `canPrepareSkillAuthoring`).
- Lint: `OWNER_PRODUCER_FILES` 13 → 12 (`command-auth.ts` leaves). `TURN_FLAG_FILES` stays at 18: `command-auth.ts` leaves, `command-owner-facts.ts` (where the owner list match now lives) joins.

## Decisions (recorded, not asked)

- Asserted-identity owners keep owner-only commands but get no operator scopes (DESIGN §10): the returned grant is used only for the owner bit. `commands: "all"` (passing `commands.allowFrom`) still comes only from the internal turn grant, so no listed channel owner gains `commands.allowFrom` bypass in this PR.
- Command owner is answered by `readCommandSenderAdmission` in the admission module, not by `decideOperatorAdmission`. Asserted-identity owners and pre-turn senders have no operator principal; `decideOperatorAdmission` needs prepared facts (async) and refuses empty scopes, and `resolveCommandAuthorization` is a synchronous public SDK API. Routing them through it would need a new command-only facts kind or grant field. Its inputs are all admission outputs: the admitted turn grant, the owner capability bound at ingress, and the same configured-owner match `decideChannelOwnerPrincipal` uses.
- A Control UI sender whose id is listed in `commands.ownerAllowFrom` is still a command owner (6i decision; `client-permission-parity` unchanged).

## User impact

None intended. Every principal gets the same owner answer as before on every channel; only the producer moved.

## Evidence

- Production (`src` + `scripts`, non-test): +270 / −273.
- Matrix cells (`command-auth.owner-default.test.ts`, "command owner comes from admission"): asserted iMessage owner (ingress-admitted and pre-turn), asserted non-owner, verified Discord owner, pre-turn Telegram native sender, Control UI listed id, Control UI owner grant; plus "/status from an asserted iMessage owner still says owner" through `buildCommandContext`.
- Pre-push: `ocx test` over the touched tests plus every test importing a changed source (`OPENCLAW_NODE_TEST_PLAN_CONTINUE_ON_FAILURE=1`): 133 files green on the final head (first head: 145 files; 22 shards hit a source-changed-mid-run error from my own edit, rerun green). `madge` + runtime import-cycle checks clean. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test`, oxlint, oxfmt, `check-import-cycles` clean.
- E2E (one-admission run.sh Q/R/S) on the exact head: see comment.

prs.title: fix: keep your place while scrolling older chat on mobile Safari
prs.body:
Closes #205745

## What Problem This Solves

On mobile Safari, scrolling into older chat history can jump to another page or move the paragraph under your finger. Even after regrouping and touch-time measurement are corrected, reaching the loaded-history top can replace the visible answer with older tool rows when scrolling settles.

## User Impact

The reader keeps their place through regrouping, measurements, and settlement at the top boundary. Reaching the top still requests older history. No settings or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing prepend anchor uses source-message identity when regrouping removes the former rendered key, and the reader anchor compensates while touch pauses absolute restoration.

Settlement now also folds the held layout correction into the native offset at zero, rather than dropping it and moving the paragraph. The zero exception came from [#204220](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204220); [#204600](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204600) subsequently moved older-history triggering into the pane's history-edge owner. Loading no longer depends on discarding the visual correction.

The `pr-simplify` pass kept the follow-up to two existing files: net -2 production lines and one new case in the existing browser test. Whole PR versus its main merge base: production +48/-19; tests +69/-20. No new scrolling owner or unrelated cleanup.

## Evidence

### Parent/head regression proof

Linux, Node 26.12.1, repository test wrappers, real Chromium layout for browser cases. I retained the same regression cases and restored production code to the stated negative-control revision.

| Case | Negative control | Fixed head `2d55b2e73e51` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tool regrouping while touch holds a prepend | Parent `e4517b0ef2f4e`: fails, older content is rendered during touch (`true` instead of `false`) | Pass |
| `touch-after-prepend` measurement | Parent `e4517b0ef2f4e`: fails, retained top is 160 instead of 240px | Pass |
| New `touch-at-start` settle case | Previous PR head `9a4e402`: fails after release, retained top moves 320→360px | Pass: 320→320px; held correction becomes scrollTop 40px |

The original two cases also pass on `9a4e402`; the added settle case is what fails there. Parent run: 2 failures, 2.85s. Previous-head run: 1 failure / 2 passes, 6.80s. No assertion was weakened.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands and source selection</summary>

```sh
reader=src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-reader-anchor.browser.test.ts
touch=src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-touch-prepend.test.tsx
history=src/pages/chat/chat-pane-history.test.ts

# Parent production code, current regression cases
node scripts/ui.js test "$reader" "$touch" -t 'while touch-after-prepend|regrouped=true' --maxWorkers=1

# Previous PR production code, including the new settle case
node scripts/ui.js test "$reader" "$touch" -t 'while touch-at-start|while touch-after-prepend|regrouped=true' --maxWorkers=1

# Final committed head
node scripts/ui.js test "$reader" "$touch" "$history" --maxWorkers=1
```

For the parent control I restored the PR's five production files to `e4517b0ef2f4e`, leaving the test cases in place. The new settle control ran before changing production code from `9a4e402`. Temporary source replacements were restored; neither control was committed.

</details>

### Preserved behavior and checks

- All 72 focused reader, touch-prepend, and history-owner tests pass on published head `2d55b2e73e51` (5.93s), including Home-triggered older-history loading.
- The production Control UI builds. Chromium history-reading flows pass at 390px and 1280px.
- A one-off 390px Chromium run of the same history fixture with native Home instead of wheel also passes: older history loads and subsequent reading remains stable. The test driver was restored afterward.
- Scoped formatting and lint, UI production types, and the UI-chat test typecheck pass.

Linux WebKit times out waiting for the initial Answer 190 before any scroll. One bounded comparison reproduces the identical timeout on unchanged `9a4e402`; I left that unrelated failure visible and did not alter the test.

### Supplied Safari before/after

This earlier comparison is **regrouping only** versus **regrouping plus reader correction**, based on `cdadcea9`, not proof of the new settle change. Real production UI and isolated gateways, synthetic history, iPhone 17 Pro simulator / iOS 26.4 / Xcode 26.4.1.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc8291b9-94e3-4d1d-b803-0cb3daada526

Released-flick proof from that earlier build:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e6950ed-6578-481c-827d-67f20e393f51

Dan's later matched main-`ecd534c` / PR-`9a4e402` simulator runs reproduced the top-boundary loss on both builds and isolated the delayed settle jump on the PR. I decoded all three supplied comparison recordings.

**Still draft:** the new-head iPhone simulator rerun and independent review of this follow-up are pending. I have not marked the PR ready.


Patch and simulator proof supplied by Dan.

Co-authored-by: daniel-lxs <57051444+daniel-lxs@users.noreply.github.com>

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-mobile-chat-scroll-jump-s81845e9b)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Before this change, persistent OpenClaw agents were externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation custody store** in the per-agent database persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts, and hands each delegate off to the subagent run registry before spawn (RFC `docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md` §5.4). The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **Durable custody**: delegates and their replay state live in the continuation custody store, with one transactional authority for replacement and a pre-spawn handoff to `subagent_runs` (upstream has removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime, #159179) - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → custody record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from the custody store (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Historical proof head (2026-11-05):** `a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb` (tree `53363f7964f31a47109cf0575aa23f31eefa0338`). The receipts below are preserved for that exact head, not claims about the current PR head. The current head and its separate evidence are identified in `## Evidence`. ### Receipts bound to this exact head Each is a separate receipt in the preserved exact-head packet, [`PROOFS/a22bd9c05c…/`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb) (docs `main` at `9ba5518b`). | gate | ruling | scope | |---|---|---| | Recipient-authority row (`R-CD-RECIPIENT-AUTHORITY`) | PASS-candidate ([docs#620 comment 6651745479](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/pull/620#issuecomment-6651745479)) | the gate-3 fire only; the row stays `partial` until a corpus fold review | | Mode-B and the locally run cut shards | PASS-candidate ([karmaterminal/openclaw#1271 comment 6653747059](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/issues/1271#issuecomment-6653747059)) | the candidate-owned regression gate; it doesn't claim Mode-B was green | | Fold source review of the `2907e656 → a22bd9c05c` delta | PASS-candidate ([#1271 comment 6655365352](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/issues/1271#issuecomment-6655365352)) | source review only | **Mode-B** [`41927761314`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/41927761314) ran on product `a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb` with workflow `a768f04231bd0a6f94cc7b845aecaec28a4a4c9e`, from 2026-11-04 22:43Z to 2026-11-05 04:47Z. It finished terminally **non-green**: 91 jobs (53 succeeded, 27 failed, 3 cancelled, 8 skipped) and 218,033 tests passed / 220 failed. - Its receipts are valid, routed equals planned, and every hosted job ran on the project's own runner pool. - **Its 64 distinct failing tests are exactly the previous accepted head's set** (the same sorted-set sha256 `185b6dea…`), and none is new. - The four shards the workflow cuts at 90 minutes were run locally at this exact SHA, serially with one worker: - two were clean; - two carry only baseline or test-order failures, each classified in the receipt with counterfactual runs. **Packet status: preserved, NOT acceptance-complete, NOT terminal.** Of 37 required rows, **0 pass, 1 partial (the recipient-authority row above), and 36 missing**. No live row has fired at this SHA, because no deployment runs it yet: the deployed fleet is on a separate, older line. Running live rows here needs a deployment whose runtime has this SHA as an ancestor. That is a migrating cut (an agent-schema step), gated on its own timed restore rehearsal. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` does not point at this packet, and nothing here is a terminal rollup claim. ### Earlier evidence: provenance, not exact-target proof The live behavior observed on earlier heads, and the earlier corpora, are ancestry and materiality evidence for this head. They aren't exact-target execution, and no row is carried over from them as a pass: - Mode-B [`35364768803`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw-bootstrap/actions/runs/35364768803) at `3821eaef72`, 2026-09-18; - corpora [`7cb9d71f…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/7cb9d71f622250bedbf565e327bd7d7b9d90b567) and [`139e3657…`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/tree/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393). The behaviors those corpora observed are the ones this feature exists for: - stale ambient backlog suppression; - typed and bracket `continue_work` wakes with granted provenance and Tempo model-call spans; - cost-cap rejection; - max-chain, scheduler, durable recovery and delegate surfaces. They are re-fired against this head's runtime once one is deployed. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. - [Exact-head packet for `a22bd9c05c`: README, status and limits](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/9ba5518bdb079da3c3c75961fd8cd26be040eb1e/PROOFS/a22bd9c05c4a7a9c86e72a132cb7939e399104cb/README.md) -
