prs.title: feat(apple): add Talk status chimes
prs.body: Related: #204311 ## What Problem This Solves In Talk on iPhone or Mac, people may have to look at the screen to know when a call is listening, ready for another reply, or ended. ## Why This Change Was Made Key points: - Three cues mark the moments a hands-free user cannot see: Talk first becomes ready (**Listening**), a call ends cleanly (**Call end**), and native speech recognition resumes after a completed reply (**Ready for reply**). - **Decision needed (ClawSweeper), quoted:** "Should the three Apple Talk chimes default on independently of an existing macOS Phase sounds opt-out?" **Author’s design (pending Apple Talk owner approval):** the three cues default on (voice use means not watching the screen), and an explicit Phase-sounds opt-out carries over to the chimes. When the `talk.chimes.*` keys are unset, a user who explicitly turned macOS **Phase sounds** off reads all three chimes off; a user who never set **Phase sounds** reads them on. A stored chime setting always wins, and reading never writes. The chimes replace Submarine and Bottle, Pop is removed because speech announces itself, and Tink stays under **Phase sounds**. - Owner decision, macOS phase sounds consolidated: the **Listening** and **Ready for reply** chimes replace the built-in Submarine (listening) and Bottle (listening after speaking) sounds. Pop (speaking) is removed because speech announces itself. Tink (thinking) stays under the existing **Phase sounds** setting (`talkPhaseSoundsEnabled`), which now covers only the thinking sound. The setting key and label are unchanged. No overlap workaround is needed. - Unchanged: realtime stays always-listening and plays no reply cue. Switching routes does not overwrite the saved preference. The microphone is gated around cue playback where it could feed the cue back into Talk. - Decision rules: the end cue plays on a clean user stop, including while thinking or speaking (push-to-talk is excluded). The reply cue follows the active route and plays only after the assistant's speech played to its end, including the incremental speech path, where a failed or interrupted segment now blocks the cue. Starting push-to-talk cancels the end cue's delayed audio-session cleanup so it cannot deactivate the new capture. The iOS realtime-to-native fallback now plays the "Ready for reply" chime. - Upgrade safety: the three new keys read as on when unset, except that an explicit macOS Phase-sounds opt-out is inherited as off; reading never writes. The rule lives in one shared function (`TalkChimePlayer.isEnabled`). iOS has no Phase-sounds setting, so it reads on when unset. ## User Impact Three independent, device-local **Status chimes** default on when unset (a macOS user who explicitly turned **Phase sounds** off keeps all three off): **Listening**, **Call end**, and **Ready for reply**. Each can be turned off separately. On macOS, Submarine, Bottle and Pop no longer play; Tink still plays under **Phase sounds**. ## Evidence ### Real iPhone: split STT/TTS turns with the follow-up (reply) chime (26 Nov 2026) > Review: *native turn-based reply playback*. The same physical iPhone and device build (OC 102513), with Talk in **STT/TTS** mode, did three consecutive spoken turns: "nine squared", "10 squared" and "11 squared". The screen recording was made on the phone with audio. Video: [ios-device-split-turn.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/pr-evidence-apple-chimes-204362/apple-chimes-204362/ios-device-split-turn.mp4) (48 s). | Recorded sound | Time | Normalised cross-correlation | |---|---|---| | follow-up chime after the spoken reply "100" | 28.9 s | `chime_follow.caf` **0.91** (wake 0.64, bye 0.59) | | spoken replies "100" and "121" | 25.6 s, 41.9 s | none (TTS speech, not a cue) | | end chime after the call ends | 44.6 s | `chime_bye.caf` **0.77** (follow 0.63, wake 0.52) | The next question, "What's 11 squared", was spoken after the follow-up chime and was recognized correctly (). ### Follow-up cue waits for live capture (542873c917d) During an earlier device turn, the tester's speech straight after the follow-up chime was not recognized. That miss was not reproduced. The code had a real ordering gap, though, and this commit closes it: ### iOS: wait for the microphone before playing listening cues On iPhone build OC 102513 in STT/TTS mode, speech immediately after the reply cue was missed once and heard in a second recording. The first miss was not reproduced on hardware. The native path played the cue after scheduling recognition, without confirming microphone buffers reached a running task. Its input gate also stayed closed for 200 ms past the nominal end of playback. The chime player did not change the audio session category. The wake and reply cues now wait for a running recognition task and a nonempty microphone buffer appended to its request. The input gate opens on playback completion, without the fixed post-cue delay on this path. Failed replies still do not trigger a follow cue, and end-cue cleanup is unchanged. Evidence: on baseline 8acd5b4de2f with the test fixture installed, the delayed-capture regression observed wake and follow with no readiness events and failed its ordering assertion (pmac talk-capture-red-r2). The fix passed the regression and all 56 focused iOS simulator tests plus 8 Kit tests (pmac talk-capture-green-r1). SwiftFormat 0.63.1 passed on all three changed files. No patched iPhone retest or independent local automated review was performed. Local commit: 542873c917d3cda32cf4b880e8172a4eb30a795d. ### Real iPhone: one Live Talk turn with audible chimes (26 Nov 2026) > Review: *audible native cue playback* and *real-device evidence*. This is a physical iPhone running a device build of this PR's code (OC 102513: main `b48d578d023` plus this PR at `8acd5b4de2f`). It shows one **Live (Realtime)** Talk turn against a real Gateway. The screen recording was made on the phone, with audio. Video: [ios-device-talk-turn.mp4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/pr-evidence-apple-chimes-204362/apple-chimes-204362/ios-device-talk-turn.mp4) (24 s). | Listening started | Reply received | |---|---| | | | Audio track of the recording: | Recorded sound | Time | Normalised cross-correlation with the bundled asset | |---|---|---| | when Listening (Realtime) appears | 2.6 s | `chime_wake.caf` **0.97** (follow 0.66, bye 0.26) | | after the call ends | 23.4 s, cut off when the recording stops | `chime_bye.caf` **0.71** (follow 0.61, wake 0.48) | There is no ready-for-reply chime in this recording, and none is expected. `TalkChimeLifecycle.resumedListening(isRealtime:)` plays the reply cue only for STT/TTS turns, never for Live. The model's spoken reply is also absent from the recording, because iOS screen recording didn't capture the Realtime voice stream. Only the app's own cue playback appears. Limits: this covers a Live turn only. A split STT/TTS turn, which is where the reply chime plays, wasn't recorded here. Proof job on head `8acd5b4de2f` (iOS 27.2 simulator and macOS test run), all steps passed: macOS app build, 8 OpenClawKit tests in 3 suites, macOS `TalkModeControllerPublishingTests` and `AppStateRemoteConfigTests`, and 80 iOS simulator tests. **Audio.** Waveform of the shipped chime assets laid out on the call timeline decided by the real `TalkChimeLifecycle` (markers: Listening 0.5 s, Ready for reply 4.0 s, Call end 7.5 s). Generated by `TalkChimeAudioProofTests`, which decodes `chime_wake.caf`, `chime_follow.caf` and `chime_bye.caf` and checks they carry audible samples (peaks 0.60, 0.34, 0.38): Audio file: [talk-chimes-call.wav](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35390557/talk-chimes-call.wav) (48 kHz mono, 9.4 s, the three chimes at those markers). Cue events, with asset SHA-256 hashes: ``` wake Listening 0.5 s 0.45 s peak 0.600 chime_wake.caf 808e0d89bd71... follow Ready for reply 4.0 s 0.45 s peak 0.339 chime_follow.caf 5b6f24fa22d9... bye Call end 7.5 s 0.92 s peak 0.380 chime_bye.caf dc0e69bf94cb... ``` **Cue lifecycle in the iOS app logic** (simulator test with the player stubbed; the microphone recovers after the reply): ``` TALK_CUE_TRACE cue wake | listening=true | cue follow | listening=true (microphone recovered after reply) | cue bye ``` **Settings** (the Control UI device section `talk-device-controls.tsx` rendered in headless Chromium with a mocked macOS native-device-settings snapshot; Status chimes shown with all three on): **Upgrade** (settings stored before the chimes existed; no `talk.chimes.*` keys). All passed: ``` ✔ settings stored by the previous stable release carry an explicit Phase sounds opt-out to the chimes (Phase sounds off -> start, end, reply all off; nothing written) ✔ settings stored by the previous stable release with Phase sounds unset keep the chimes on ✔ an explicit legacy opt-out carries over only to cue keys that were never stored (a stored cue choice wins; reading never writes) ✔ defaults saved before chimes existed read all three cues on ✔ an explicit stored choice survives and a mixed snapshot reads per key ``` iOS tests also cover: the fallback-route and end-chime behavior, push-to-talk taking over during the end cue keeping its audio session, and a single-line reply whose whole-reply playback fails not requesting the reply cue. Lint: the repo's pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 in lint mode reports 0 files needing formatting on the touched Swift sources. Build lint phases were bypassed in the proof job. **Proof limits, stated plainly.** - The WAV and waveform are the shipped chime assets placed on the lifecycle timeline, not a tap of the app's live output: the player uses `AVAudioPlayer`, which cannot be tapped without changing production playback. - The cue trace uses a stubbed player: it shows cue order and microphone recovery, not audible output. - The upgrade tests seed the old settings shape rather than loading a real install. A real-device "upgrade" isn't reproducible here: the shipped v2026.11.10 app is App Store–signed, and a development build can't be installed over it, so iOS refuses the install or wipes the app's data. The closest available run, a development build of the stable tag followed by the PR build installed over it, only re-exercises the same `UserDefaults` read that these tests already cover. The change is read-only on upgrade: the three new keys default on when unset, and an explicit Phase-sounds opt-out is inherited as off. Nothing is migrated or rewritten, so there's no stored-data transformation that a device run could break. - The settings screenshots are the Control UI component with a mocked snapshot, not the shipped native iOS or macOS settings screens. - The earlier hands-on iPhone check (main004 build 4, earphones) predates this head. AI-assisted. Reviews: Codex found macOS native fallback still reported the reply cue as unavailable (fixed). A separate cross-family review of the shared lifecycle, player, defaults and capture gate reported no blocking findings. Second review: Marvin (claude-opus-5-5), no blocking findings.

prs.body:
Refs https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198737

## What Problem This Solves

The test-maintenance campaign is reducing optional profiling workloads, implementation counters, repeated wiring and presentation inventories. This packet removes a selected maintenance surface while keeping named functional guards; it deliberately retires the listed noncritical coverage rather than claiming every removed assertion is duplicated.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. Developers maintain 3,984 fewer tracked lines. The tradeoff includes less optional stress/performance and large-input parity coverage, selected placement forwarding/progression checks, and native cosmetic/default-positive payload permutations. Those losses are explicit below; retained tests do not claim identical performance measurements.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prefer existing functional keeper suites and a few small guard folds over replacement harnesses. Preserve auth/privacy, stale-result, session placement, retirement and data-preservation checks. The added folds retain created-session INITIAL assistant-final visibility and a literal-derived Codex fingerprint digest; Android's new bare-CR math and stronger CRLF UTF-8-limit fixtures remain.

| Category | Paths | Added | Deleted | Net removed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Tests/support | 44 | 31 | 4,000 | 3,969 |
| Owned test routing/mock/timing metadata | 5 | 0 | 15 | 15 |
| Total | 49 | 31 | 4,015 | **3,984** |
| Runtime production / new tracked files | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The five metadata paths are `scripts/lib/ci-policy-test-watch.mts`, `scripts/lib/ci-proof-test-inventory.mts`, `test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server-paths.mjs`, `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt`, and `config/ci-test-timings.json`. They remove only references belonging to the retired suites. Six normal-formatter blank-line deletions account for the difference from the 3,978-line preformat proposal.

## Evidence

**Draft / validation incomplete.** Source head `b70aafe40aec7bcbf6cad6303f5a69e54fd9f905`, frozen parent `973e0ba78f7b970dafdd9166c6598a572a5d0d46`, tree `1afbe9204fdb0f86f50a2785b79c05d79bbdfc4a`. Patch SHA-256: `28572c40cb4678c75529c517ed00acdae27bf77591a714e276d56a61646bb972`.

- Complete: signed commit and normal hooks; admitted native oxfmt 0.74; native i18n freshness; exact 49-file pre/post bindings and 59 keeper bindings; `git diff --check`; deleted-path reference closure; timing JSON parse and three metadata syntax probes; added-line privacy check.
- **UNRUN:** application execution, Vitest/scoped runtime, test types, oxlint, Android and broad/required CI. Existing app dependencies are unqualified; no install or provider fallback was used.
- **Source review BLOCKED / no verdict.** Native full-context preflight exited 1 before any model ran: `refusing sensitive --source-context: src/secrets/runtime-degraded-state.ts`. The mandatory keeper `src/secrets/runtime-state.test.ts` also needs an installed reviewed pin absent from native policy. This review attempt is stopped; the PR remains **OPEN / DRAFT / on hold**. Resumption requires supported policy-owner admission for the required source and keeper contexts. This is an admission blocker, not a coverage objection or a passed review; no helper/policy change or bypass is proposed.
- No current-head CI or review proof is borrowed from the preceding campaign PR. No ClawSweeper re-review has been requested by this agent.
- Dependency/source inspection only: Codex `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/dynamic_tools.rs:1–173`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs:106–139,1054–1180,1254–1265`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:210–318,1210–1217`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs:1891–1978,2153–2255`, and `codex-rs/state/src/runtime/threads.rs:399–448,1180–1250`. These establish protocol/list/read boundaries, not performance equivalence or execution proof.
- AI-assisted, maintainer-requested cleanup. This public 49-row table is the durable keeper/value manifest. The ignored local replay manifest is maintainer-only bookkeeping, not a publicly available artifact or a substitute for this table.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): scope conversation learning to its agent
prs.body:
## Problem

The Knowledge conversation-learning scribe could read transcripts outside the agent that runs it when ordinary session visibility is broad. Ref: #205581.

## Fix

For Run once and ongoing conversation learning, cap session listing and history reads at the owning agent, without widening stricter visibility. The scribe uses these bounded tools rather than transcript search. Checkpoints remain progress cursors: an old entry is not permission to read a session that is absent from this run’s list.

The cap is switched on only for:
- a scheduled run whose job `declarationKey` is exactly `knowledge:scribe:conversations`, or
- a turn whose run ID starts with `knowledge:scribe:conversations:<this run's own session key>:` (the Scribes page start request).

A caller-chosen run ID can only narrow tools. Every other run keeps today's session-tool behavior.

No schema or data migration is needed. Existing checkpoints, claims, and evidence are left unchanged. The docs explain how a vault owner can review historical claims and citations.

## Error surfaces

Full diff against merge-base `3fa253a2dc68`. This PR adds no throws, exits, rollback triggers, or turn/update failures, and does not touch update, Doctor, migration, config validation, or startup paths. The only new failures are tool results returned to the model inside an agent-only scribe run.

| New or changed failure path | Can it fire for a healthy user? | Rollback/outage risk | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invocation_agent_scope_restricted` (`forbidden`, "This run can read only its own agent's sessions.") from `sessions_history` on another agent's key, via the shared session-access check | Only inside an agent-only scribe run that asks for another agent's session. Never for the run's own agent: the check runs only when target agent ≠ requester agent. Never outside scribe runs: the flag is unset. | None. It is a tool result, the turn continues. | **Kept.** It prevents a scribe from copying another agent's private conversations into this agent's vault (#205581). |
| `sessions_list` in a scribe run: `agentId` clamped to the run's agent, other agents' rows filtered, `visibility.restricted: true` | Same scope as above. It filters results and is not an error. | None | **Kept.** Same reason. |
| `sessions_history` with a bare session ID in a scribe run resolves only inside the run's agent, so other agents' IDs return the existing "Session not found" | Same scope. Own session IDs still resolve (proven below). | None | **Kept.** Without it, a session ID would bypass the key check. |
| `sessions_search` in a scribe run returns `forbidden` ("Use sessions_list and sessions_history for this agent-scoped run.") | Only if a scribe run calls search. The learning skill never does. Ordinary runs are unchanged (proven below). | None | **Kept.** Transcript recall can return cross-agent descendants. Agent-scoping the recall index would be a much larger change. |
| ~~Early `sessions_history` refusal ("…only its own agent's session history.")~~ | It could refuse a run's own `current` session when `agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId` pins a different agent | — | **Removed** in `9a23272`. The shared access check above already covers it. |
| `sessions_list` visibility checker switched to the core decision checker | No: only `.allowed` is read, and requester derivation matches main | None | **Kept, behavior-neutral.** `9a23272` dropped an explicit `requesterAgentId` that could have changed ordinary list results. |

Accepted edge: a fixed shared session store (`agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId`) attributes legacy, non-agent-qualified rows to that store's agent. In a scribe run for a different agent, those rows count as cross-agent and are skipped. The run fails closed and visibly, and nothing outside scribe runs changes.

## Evidence

End-to-end on exact head `9a23272911d93ee98cfa5534c76f8b1f37c5b44c`, before = merge-base `3fa253a2dc68`. Each side ran a real in-process Gateway with its own HOME, state, config, and loopback port, inside the repository's isolated Vitest adapter. That ran in private rootless Podman (`network=none`) with task-owned storage and runtime dirs, not the default store or the live Gateway. Config had agents `main`, `alpha`, and `beta` and the default `tools.sessions.visibility`. Sessions were seeded with `chat.send`. A deterministic loopback model issued the tool calls.

| Check, beta's runs | before `3fa253a2` | after `9a23272` |
|---|---|---|
| Run once (Scribes start ID + generated prompt): `sessions_list` / with `agentId: alpha` | **3 alpha** listed | 4 beta only / clamped to 4 beta |
| Run once: alpha history by key / by session ID / via old checkpoint key | **ALPHA content read** | `forbidden` / not found / `forbidden` |
| Run once: `sessions_search` | **alpha content** | `forbidden` |
| Run once: own beta1, beta2 (checkpoint), beta1 by session ID, `current` | readable | readable |
| Scheduled (`declarationKey: knowledge:scribe:conversations`, `cron.run` force): list / list `agentId: alpha` / alpha key / checkpoint alpha key / own beta1 / `current` | **alpha listed and read** | beta only / beta only / `forbidden` / `forbidden` / readable / readable |
| **Control, ordinary beta conversation** (random run ID): list `agentId: alpha`, alpha history by key and by ID, `sessions_search`, `current` | 3 alpha, read, read, ok, ok | **same:** 3 alpha, read, read, ok, ok, not restricted |
| **Control, ordinary automation** (no declaration key, same agent, `cron.run` force): list `agentId: alpha`, alpha history | 2 alpha, read | **same:** 2 alpha, read, outcome `ok` |

Result: after, 2/2 passed (exit 0, 311 s wall including the in-container build; tests 38.6 s). Before failed on the scribe rows (alpha listed and read). A second before run used `expect.soft` on the two scribe tables, the only spec difference, so the control rows could run on main. They passed and match the after rows. Image `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.64.1-noble` = `sha256:a0d7b2b49ffa…`; Node v26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Vitest 5.0.5. The scratch spec (sha256 `7d4409a6aa77…`) was staged only and not committed.

```bash
umask 022; HOME=$root/home XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$root/runtime npm_execpath=<pnpm 12.15.0 native> \
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --isolated-image sha256:a0d7b2b4… run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner \
  src/gateway/knowledge-scribe-scope.proof.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Gaps:
- The model is scripted, so this does not show whether a real model follows the updated `learning.md` text. The refusal is enforced at the tool either way.
- The "old checkpoint" was supplied as note text in the prompt, not a Knowledge vault page.
- The Scribes page's start request was reproduced with the same idempotency key and prompt builder. This was not a Control UI click-through.
- Not proven end to end: the fixed shared session-store edge case above.
- The affected behavior is present in `release/2026.11.11` by source inspection. No release changes were made.

Review requested from @jalehman and @openclaw/openclaw-secops. Keep CODEOWNERS and security review gates in place.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(macos): offer app downloads when local state needs a newer build
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #205258 and #205231. An older macOS app can quit before its updater starts if its bundled CLI needs credential maintenance and refuses the local state schema already advanced by a newer Gateway. The current modal sends the user back to Doctor even when no invocation of the older CLI can make that state readable.

## What Changed

When the bundled CLI's credential maintenance has **already failed**, the startup owner checks whether its diagnostic is the CLI's newer-schema refusal. If it is, the app shows an **OpenClaw app update required** alert with **Open Downloads** and **Quit** instead of the Doctor advice. The link works without starting the Gateway or Sparkle and does not select a different release channel. Every other credential failure keeps the existing message. Startup and Mac-node status now share one diagnostic parser. This adds no schema, migration, state-store, or update-policy changes.

## Error surfaces

Full diff against merge-base `b8992c005468`. This PR adds **no** new throw, refusal, exit, rollback trigger, or tightened validation. The paths it touches:

| Changed path | Can it fire for a healthy user? | Rollback/outage risk | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ClientCredentialStartup.prepare`: `throw NewerStateSchemaError` | No. It sits inside the existing `guard result.success, !result.timedOut, exitCode == 0 else` failure branch, which already threw `OpenClawNativeStateError`. It only changes *which* error is thrown. It requires a failure that did not time out and whose first diagnostic contains `uses newer schema version N; this build supports M` with integer `N > M`. Only the CLI's schema refusal produces that text. Every other failure, and any timeout, still throws the old error unchanged. | None. Startup fails exactly when it already failed. No new termination, no state write, no update or rollback involvement. | Kept: this is the fix. |
| `showCredentialStartupFailure`: title, message and buttons chosen by error type; Open Downloads opens the GitHub releases URL | Only reached after credential startup has already failed, as before. | None. It still calls the existing `requestTermination()`. Quit and Open Downloads both exit and leave state untouched (proved below). The `URL(string:)` guard wraps a constant literal and falls back to the old single-button alert. | Kept. |
| `MacNodeChannelStatusStore`: private `workerSchemaMismatch` replaced by `NewerStateSchemaError(diagnostic:)` | Same as before. The parsing logic is identical: same marker, separator and integer parse, and the same `required > supported` check. It only labels an already-failed status. | None. Display only. | Kept: removes a duplicate parser. |

There was nothing to simplify, so there is no new commit. The head is still `dcd507c0ebf8`.

## Verification (end to end, exact head `dcd507c0ebf8710a191d2022b325b5e5b4f1f8d9`)

**Build and harness.** On the Mac Studio (macOS 26.5.1, Swift 6.3.3), we fetched `pull/205670/head`, asserted it equals `dcd507c0ebf8…` with a clean tree, and ran `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --product OpenClaw` (100 s, binary sha256 `566af172…ccd28`). The binary was bundled with the published **2026.11.9** app runtime (schema 36, zip sha256 `d2bd4965…cbb` checked), ad-hoc signed, and given its own bundle id per scenario, with the Sparkle feed blanked. It was launched via `open -n` in a fresh disposable Tart **macOS 26.6.2** guest with its own `OPENCLAW_PROFILE`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and config. Before launch, we ran the packaged 2026.11.9 `doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive` against the synthetic schema-40 fixture (`state/openclaw.sqlite`, `user_version = 40`). It exited 1 with `uses newer schema version 40; this build supports 36`. Alerts use `sharingType = .none`, so frames were captured from the VNC framebuffer. Buttons were clicked through System Events.

| Scenario (head build) | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Schema-40 state → **Quit** | The alert read "OpenClaw app update required … schema 36 … schema 40" with Open Downloads and Quit. The app logged `Credential startup failed: This app supports schema 36, but your local data requires schema 40…`. After Quit, the app process was gone and Safari was not launched. Every state file was byte-identical (sha256 manifest before vs after), and `user_version` was still 40. |
| Schema-40 state → **Open Downloads** | Same alert. After the click, the app exited and Safari opened. AppleScript read back `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases`. State was byte-identical, still schema 40. |
| **Normal schema, existing install** (`state/openclaw.sqlite` at `user_version = 36`, written by the packaged 2026.11.9 `doctor --fix`, exit 0) | No alert. Zero `credential startup failed`, `update required` or `need recovery` log lines. The app was still running at 35 s, and the onboarding window, mac-node, control channel and presence all started. Each logged "Gateway not configured", as expected for an unconfigured profile. Schema stayed at 36. |
| **Normal schema, fresh state** (empty state dir) | Credential maintenance created `client/credentials.sqlite` and `control/services.sqlite`. No alert. The app was still running at 30 s and 60 s with onboarding shown. A relaunch on that same state also started normally. |

**Trigger reproduction (published packages, not head code).** 2026.11.9 created schema 36, and the 2026.11.10 Gateway advanced it to 40. With a returning legacy credential forcing maintenance, the 2026.11.9 `doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive` refused schema 40 (exit 1) and changed nothing. The 2026.11.10 command succeeded on the same fixture. This ran under Linux/Node.

### Clean comparison

| Before (`b8992c005468`) | After (`dcd507c0ebf8`) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: alert says client credentials need recovery and points to doctor --fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0b60389-02b8-4453-a1e9-eaef5c384a0d) | ![After: alert says OpenClaw app update required, schema 36 vs 40, with Open Downloads and Quit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d2d8d30-32dc-4c3f-adc5-76587efc04c2) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before annotated: Doctor recovery message highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d71b0bd-6a58-4775-90ae-5452e54c3192) | ![After annotated: schema mismatch message and Open Downloads highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9cc26bfc-4e17-4899-adf3-35e15ae06d42) |

### Both choices on the exact head

| Choosing Quit | After Quit |
| --- | --- |
| ![Head alert with the Quit button highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b60af0d3-cb1f-4a9f-be94-5b443408a1a4) | ![After Quit: desktop with no OpenClaw app or browser open; state byte-identical, schema still 40](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5d683c7-6f12-4422-959a-e7ec50f2e18b) |

After choosing **Open Downloads**:

![After Open Downloads: Safari shows the openclaw/openclaw GitHub releases page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5470f289-dfab-4574-a773-0a7c1d0d2197)

![After annotated: Safari address and releases tab highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4bfc28bd-dab2-496c-8a94-7214e9d159de)

### Normal-schema launch on the exact head (no regression)

| Existing schema-36 state | Annotated |
| --- | --- |
| ![Head app on schema-36 state: onboarding window, no alert](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c53d1531-5020-434d-8517-495b5e9aa2e0) | ![Annotated: credential startup passed, app kept running](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12754439-6594-43de-8fe8-118146a1ff49) |

Scenario: the head app with the 2026.11.9 bundled runtime (schema 36), run against synthetic state fixtures in a disposable macOS VM. The user's installed app and real state were not used. The "before" frames come from the merge-base build in an earlier run of the same harness, which isolated HOME; a harness-only "Keychain Not Found" prompt was dismissed there. The head frames above come from the 2026-11-26 re-run, which used the guest's own HOME.

## Release Impact

Three-way cherry-pick simulation is conflict-free on `release/2026.11.11` at `3d1e4fff043f`. This changes future app recovery only. Installed 2026.11.9 apps still need a separately published, compatible signed DMG/ZIP. The PR does not change the independent macOS release policy or publish assets.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(test): focus meeting title before checking its ring
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The hourly main CI meeting-navigation test fails before reaching its capture-settings and new-tab assertions. It expects the meeting heading to receive focus on a direct URL load, although the page requests focus only after an existing selection changes.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203332

## User Impact

Restores valid setup for the existing browser regression test. No production behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicitly focus the heading before checking focus and text-width geometry. Keep the geometry, capture-settings round trip, search-query restoration, and native new-tab assertions unchanged.

The simplification pass retains one setup line: production delta 0; test delta +1/-0. No new helper, timeout, retry, or assertion removal.

## Evidence

- Main CI reproduction: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45761646412/job/139713338664 failed this case at the initial active-element assertion (1 failed, 374 passed). The meeting test and focus owner are unchanged between that run's base and this branch's base.
- Source and history inspection: the focus owner deliberately leaves initial deep-link focus unrequested; the earlier focus-ring change added this assertion without changing that contract.
- Pinned oxfmt 0.74.0, commit hook including the line-cap growth check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local ClawSweeper 0.3.3 reviewed `f76b87badadd0c4d244d6529fb4da41894eb8b83` → `3ba0119364ac9979ce8202317bf3bc6af61aaf8a`: complete, zero reported findings, no priority filter. Browser execution remained unverified in that source review.

prs.title: test: pin the frozen candidate-launcher contract
prs.body:
Related: #204915, #205578, #204868

## What Problem This Solves

Existing launcher tests construct the trial, restore manifest and candidate IPC messages themselves. A candidate producer can drift while those consumer tests remain green, despite an installed launcher keeping its frozen interface.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. This adds one owner test file for compatibility with today's format4 launcher, v2 trial, v1 per-release restore manifest and compiled20-minute default. The current2-attempt and exit78 behavior remain unchanged and covered by their existing lifecycle tests. No production/stored/header/schema change or new production test seam.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three small cases cover the missing boundaries without replaying the lifecycle suite:

- Real `createTrialPending` bytes, minimal/full optional input, independent stored-key/v2 ABI guard, and literal `1_200_000` default.
- Real candidate manifest publisher output independently checked against the deployed literal v1 root/pair ABI (entry order is not pinned; positive preimages must be absolute), then consumed by the frozen manifest reader on actual files. The literal check prevents coordinated writer/reader drift from moving the oracle; existing writer tests retain their SQLite inventory coverage.
- One isolated child imports the real `announceReady`/stop listener and exchanges frames with a pinned format4 peer. A collector is installed at spawn, return must precede stop, stdin provides the serving keepalive without sleeps/polling, and child home/state/config paths are all private.

The IPC case does not distinguish ACK processing from the supported on-disk fallback. Actual stage-mark producer coverage at `config-preflight-snapshot.ts:468` is separately recorded: exercising its full admission/recovery graph is outside this bounded harness; existing launcher stage-consumer tests remain unchanged. This PR does not claim that fourth producer frame is exercised.

Production delta: **0**. One228-line owner file, below the400net test-line allowance; no allocation/waiver.

## Evidence

- Base: `b1d355fcc9fcf91a4514c2612ce7b33211c710b6`.
- **Mutation RED:** [AWS run_14f78c186994742f3077d3a597297ada](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_14f78c186994742f3077d3a597297ada),2artifact cases passed and the IPC assertion failed with expected `openclaw.ready` / actual `openclaw.contract-mutant`. This was one temporary producer discriminant edit, restored exactly before GREEN and not included in this PR.

No production changes or mutation repeat.

prs.title: fix(update): check delegated owners against Doctor-migrated config
prs.body:
### Problem
Refs #205485. A delegated configured-owner check can reject an installed candidate's config on the retired `skills.workshop` key before Doctor has a chance to migrate it. The issue was closed without a linked closing commit; the failing path is present on main and `release/2026.11.11`.

### Fix and impact
For delegated configured-owner checks, use the existing Doctor migration planner to project valid config when the offline policy read encounters a repairable legacy shape. The policy reader never writes or observes the projection as disk config; Doctor still owns persistence. An owner replaced in the current config is still denied (proven end to end below). Normal valid config loads and profile continuation are unchanged. No new schema or migration.

### Upgrading from 2026.11.10
The fix runs in the newly installed version. The installed 2026.11.10 updater checks the owner first and may refuse a chat `/update` before it installs anything (`INVALID_CONFIG` on `skills.workshop`). When that happens the Gateway keeps serving the current version. Workaround: run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then retry the update.

### Verification
All proof below is end to end on exact head `590bd2e1ca7f`: private rootless Podman, systemd user unit, `--network none`, offline npm. The installed package's `build-info.json` records commit `590bd2e1ca7f74409b5a43a8668a9743b210272f`, and its build source tree matches `git archive` of that commit. This commit applies conflict-free by itself to `release/2026.11.11`. Combined with the typed-owner fix (#205666), both regressions insert at the same place in the shared test file; keep both when resolving.

**Legacy hop, owner kept.** Telegram owner `telegram:1001`, retired root `skills.workshop.autonomous` present. The base was published 2026.11.8, because 2026.11.10 refuses this config before installing (see above). Chat-requester `update.run` → candidate (relabeled 2026.11.11, build ID unchanged):

| Stage | Time |
|---|---|
| requested → validating | 26 s |
| validating → activating (old Gateway still serving) | 79 s |
| activating → candidate `/readyz` (Gateway down) | 4 min 34 s |
| verifying → `succeeded` | 7 s |
| total, request → succeeded | 6 min 29 s |

The candidate served build `2026.11.10-590bd2e1ca7f-2026-11-26T01-58-41.388Z` on a new boot and passed `/healthz`, `/readyz` and authenticated `health`. Doctor removed `skills.workshop` and kept `mode: auto` and `channelNotices: true` under the Skill Workshop plugin. Afterward the installed owner check accepted sender 1001 and denied 1002. Most of the downtime was post-install Doctor (config flow about 90 s, contributions about 50 s). Doctor was mostly idle while it waited for the fixture-missing `codex` plugin (npm 404, then `clawhub.ai` DNS `EAI_AGAIN` with no network). A warm standalone Doctor afterward took 14 s.

**Revoked owner, retired key still present.** This was the same legacy hop. A watcher waited until the installed candidate spawned its delegated Doctor (`update-migrated-finalize.worker.js --doctor`). Then it changed `commands.ownerAllowFrom` from `telegram:1001` to `telegram:1002` and left `skills.workshop` in place, so the owner check had to read through the Doctor projection. The candidate Doctor refused config promotion with `requester-revoked` ("Doctor config promotion refused for top-level keys: meta, plugins, skills"). The published driver also recorded `requester-revoked` at activation, and the run ended `failed / requester-revoked`. The projection did not resurrect the old owner. The reader wrote nothing: the file still held `telegram:1002` and the retired key afterward. Timing: revocation 05:56:00, refusal 05:56:07.

Pre-existing behavior, not changed by this PR: after the refusal, the published driver did not restart the Gateway ("managed update recovery not attempted"), so the service stayed inactive. A control run that revoked at package swap was denied by the published driver itself during activation and ended the same way. This PR does not touch restart or recovery code. This will be reported separately.

### Error surfaces
I audited the full diff against merge-base `abd58266467d`. The PR adds no new refusal or rollback trigger. It removes one: `INVALID_CONFIG` on a repairable legacy key during the delegated owner check.

| Changed path | Can fire for a healthy user? | Rollback/outage risk | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| `io.load` `projectInvalidConfig` hook in the existing invalid-config branch | No. It runs only when config is already invalid, a branch that always threw `INVALID_CONFIG`, and only for the offline reader (`!deps.observe`) that supplies the hook. If it returns `undefined`, the same throw happens. If the planner throws, that error replaces an existing failure | Reduces it: a repairable legacy key no longer fails the delegated check | Kept (the fix) |
| `planLegacyConfigForUpdateChannel` projection | No. It returns a validated config or `undefined`, and `undefined` keeps the old path | None | Kept |
| Eager `import("../commands/doctor/legacy-config-repair.js")` in the delegated configured-owner check | Only with a corrupt package. `update-command-admit`, which the same worker loads next, already imports this module statically. It also sits in the existing try block, whose failure becomes the run's recorded authority error | None added | Kept |
| `isRecord(snapshot.parsed)` guard | No. It returns `undefined`, which keeps the old path | None | Kept |
| `io.factory` / `io.runtime` type and option plumbing | No | None | Kept |

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: improve: avoid an extra worker during transcript archival
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cold transcript maintenance qualifies its database readers on the session-store lane, then starts a foreground-history worker just to enumerate the same targets. A cold process can pay for a second transcript worker before archival begins.

## User Impact

Reuse the already-qualified store lane for cold target inventory. This is intended to avoid an unnecessary worker startup when history is cold. A process whose history reader is already active may see no memory reduction. The completed serial owner-workload comparison reduced cold-history median end RSS by 117.563 MiB (7.028%) and removed one transcript-worker startup in every cold pair. This is not Gateway RSS or concurrent-load proof. This PR remains on performance HOLD.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the existing session-store lane to the cold-inventory read owner, matching ordinary store inventory. Registry checks, qualification before FIFO admission, replacement detection, final validation, and reader cleanup stay in place. No pool merge, new cache, configuration, dependency, or schema change. Store-lane contention remains an unresolved merge gate. Foreground-history latency during active cold inventory must be qualified before lifting HOLD; the prewarmed control does not test concurrent load.

Existing inventory tests cover replacement and rejection for status and maintenance on this route. They are safety coverage, not a claimed failing baseline for the startup count. The committed archive-worker workload now reports worker starts and separates cold-history from a real prewarmed-history reader.

## Evidence

Source review and final committed-range local review found no actionable findings. Linux Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun each passed the corrected nine-case inventory suite; the unchanged four sibling files contribute 44 previously passed cases per runtime, qualified by a complete physical-source comparison. Scoped format, lint, types, and the full candidate-tree build passed. The required isolated Gateway cold-storage flow subsequently PASSED: automatic archival, hot reload, missing-payload/backup refusals, restart/recovery, and archive/restore byte checks; all three task-owned Gateway process groups were absent afterward. Earlier budget/preflight attempts did not execute this proof. Exact-head required CI/native acceptance remains incomplete.

The build succeeded with five advisory UI budget violations: largest CSS gzip 57.2 > 56.9 KiB; total CSS gzip 331.1 > 329.4 KiB; total CSS raw 1707.5 > 1699.4 KiB; chat boot JS requests 21 > 20; chat boot JS gzip 1302.6 > 1301.4 KiB. Their attribution is unproven; this PR does not claim those budgets passed.

### Acceptance rule declared before measurement

- Workload: committed `scripts/perf/archive-worker-churn-measure.ts`, 64 finished sessions across two stores, 40 sweeps per fresh process, no built-entry override. Its real archive/restore byte oracle must pass in every process. This is a representative small-device fixture, not proof for the benchmark default of 10,000 sessions or large installations.
- Two separately reported modes: cold-empty-history and `--warm-history` (two real reads through one retained reader, with a foreground-worker assertion). Prewarming is not concurrent user load.
- Five serial counterbalanced baseline/candidate pairs per mode: 20 fresh processes, independent n=5 per arm per mode. Identical committed workload, Node 24.22.1, dependencies, full source graph and fixture; only the reviewed cold-target owner differs between arms. The baseline is a counterfactual using the frozen pre-change cold-target module on the same candidate graph, not a separate historical build.
- Counts first: every cold pair must remove exactly one history worker startup, with no added worker in another lane. The prewarmed mode must add no worker startup. Report all-worker and per-lane counts, not just archive workers.
- Report iteration 0 separately. For iterations 1–39, summarize each child's median and p95 before comparing arms; 195 sweeps are not 195 independent samples. Include spread, paired deltas, process CPU, main-thread CPU, event-loop p99/max over each whole 40-sweep child, and host load.
- Report process-wide RSS before/end and the 25 ms sampled peak separately from worker counts. Never add isolate heaps or call this Gateway RSS. Both arms use the same source loader and owner-overlay mechanism; this is an owner workload, not a pristine no-preload process. No RSS saving is assumed.
- Acceptance cells are fixed before the run: for each mode and each declared latency, CPU, RSS, or event-loop metric, compare the baseline and candidate arm median and p95 across the five independent child summaries. Use the usual midpoint median and nearest-rank p95 (`ceil(0.95 × n)`, so the maximum for n=5); adverse percentage is `100 × (candidate / baseline − 1)`. Cold iteration 0, each child’s warm median, and each child’s warm p95 stay separate. Report every matched-pair delta and range as well; do not select a different estimator after seeing results. A zero baseline gets an absolute delta, not an invented percentage, and any increase remains a regression under the rule below.
- Win requires the count reduction and no regression in the declared latency/CPU/memory/tail metrics. Disclose every adverse cell; a >=20% adverse cell stops acceptance. Any worse metric needs explicit owner acceptance recorded here, not an appeal to noise. Otherwise remove the change if no measurable gain.

The rule above was published before measurement in body SHA-256 `49c5ceb46724af1bf87e465aac43363a48b76cb4972309570f3c0771abc19cb3`. The historical instrumented diagnostic motivated this experiment and does not qualify this candidate or waive another PR's HOLD.


## Completed measurement — acceptance HOLD

All 20 fresh serial children completed with exit 0, no signal/error, 40 observations each (800 total), matching archive/restore byte oracles, and zero active/pending lane tasks. Full source and installed-dependency seals matched before/after. Execution is valid; acceptance is still HOLD: **14 of 56 aggregate cells worsened; none reached 20%**. No adverse cell has been waived. There are also 46 adverse matched-pair deltas, including 16 at least 20%; correlated metrics/checkpoints are not separate independent experiments.

Cold-history first-operation median wall time fell 22,098.191 → 14,531.898 ms (−34.239%). Median end RSS fell 1,672.773 → 1,555.211 MiB; sampled peak fell 1,672.648 → 1,555.086 MiB. All five paired cold end-RSS deltas improved (−70.719 to −148.395 MiB). Prewarmed-history median end/peak RSS fell 1,727.367 → 1,709.641 MiB (−1.026%), but first-operation median wall/process CPU/main-thread CPU increased 3.551% / 5.390% / 11.774%. Their causes remain unproven; instrumented diagnosis is separate from acceptance.

The 40 measured sweeps have no eligible archive work; each process then exercises one eligible archive and verifies restored event bytes. These numbers describe the committed owner workload, not 40 real archival jobs, total OS threads, a pristine no-loader process, or Gateway memory. The 25 ms RSS sampler stops before the separate endpoint read: three sampled peaks are 128 KiB below end RSS. The two measurements remain separate.

### Work counts

All five pairs in each mode had the same counts below. Counts are starts in the measurement window; cumulative lane counts include the prewarming worker.

| Worker type | Cold A | Cold B | Prewarmed A | Prewarmed B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

### Remaining contention gate

The exact-head hosted review requires resolving simultaneous cold inventory versus ordinary store reads before merge. A source-backed bounded risk remains: with two SQLite history workers busy, cold inventory occupying one store worker can overlap another status request’s pre-FIFO qualification and create a second store worker (four retained workers versus three in the baseline scenario). Existing pool caps and retirement remain; this is not evidence of an unbounded leak. Serial/prewarmed measurements do not resolve that overlap or prove load savings. prs.title: fix(update)[2026.11.11]: recover timed-out and orphaned finalizers to a verified Gateway
prs.body:
## Problem

On the 2026.11.11 in-place updater (the legacy migrated-finalizer path, which is not on `main`; `main` updates go through `src/update/`), two faults left the managed Gateway **stopped** until someone ran `openclaw update repair` (#205547):

1. **Finalizer timeout.** When the migrated finalizer worker hit its deadline, the updater reported `update-activation-timeout` with `serviceRestartSafe: false` and left recovery "to the owning updater". The managed helper is that owner. It logged `recovery not attempted: updater explicitly rejected activation` and left the Gateway down.
2. **Lost waiting updater or worker.** The waiting updater binds the run's child lease to the candidate worker. When the updater was SIGKILLed while that worker or its process group was still alive, the helper could not rebind its claim. It logged `managed update command lease binding was lost`, never reached interrupted recovery, and exited 1, with the run stuck at `running/activating`.

## Fix

This reuses the helper's existing verified interrupted recovery (`recoverInterruptedUpdater` → `recoverInterruptedManagedUpdate`, the same post-core repair and verification that `update repair` runs). No new state or store.

- **Timeout → interrupted recovery.** A result with `status: "error"`, `reason: "update-activation-timeout"` and no `dataAtRisk` now enters the same recovery as a killed updater.
- **Lease handoff.** If the helper cannot rebind after the updater exits, it waits, within the existing recovery budget, for the candidate worker's child lease to settle. Then it rebinds and continues into interrupted recovery.
- **No implicit finalizer deadline.** As on the base (and #205675's `b9adfb0`), only an explicit `--timeout` / `timeoutMs` bounds the finalizer worker. An earlier head of this PR restored a default deadline. `e978dfa8e13e` drops it again: it added a failure path a healthy but slow update could hit (#153085 removed it for that reason), and ClawSweeper found that its expiry is reported as `update-recovery-pending`, which this recovery does not take.
- Recovery still either finishes the published candidate or keeps the previous installation, starts the Gateway, and requires an authenticated health RPC with the expected version and build. A recovery receipt alone is not proof. Data-risk and ownership refusals are unchanged.

This branch also carries #205675's legacy-path commits (requester policy checked once in the adopted finalizer; RPC-verified interrupted recovery).

## Error surfaces (full diff vs `release/2026.11.11`)

| Changed failure path | Fires for a healthy user? | Can cause or extend a rollback or outage? | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interrupted recovery now also requires `healthRpcVerified` (authenticated health RPC plus version/build); before, HTTP readiness was enough. Unverified → run recorded `failed` (`Recovered runtime could not restore Gateway readiness and identity`). From #205675. | Only if the started Gateway never answers an authenticated health RPC within the recovery budget. | It does not stop or roll back the Gateway the helper already started. It changes only the recorded verdict. It can lengthen the helper's wait, up to `recoveryTimeoutMs`, before that verdict. | **Kept.** This is the acceptance bar for #205547: a receipt or HTTP readiness is not proof the Gateway serves. |
| `update-activation-timeout` result → `recoverInterruptedUpdater()`, replacing "recovery not attempted". | Only after a finalizer timeout. | Recovery finishes forward, or keeps the previous installation if publication had not happened. Before, the Gateway was left stopped. If recovery itself fails, the outcome is the same as before (stopped, with `update repair` guidance). | **Kept.** This is the fix. |
| Lease rebind failure: the old immediate `throw "lease binding was lost"` becomes a bounded wait for the worker's child lease, then the same throw if it is still unsettled. | Only after the waiting updater exited while its worker still held the lease. | The Gateway is already stopped in this state. The wait delays only the same final failure, by up to `recoveryTimeoutMs`, and otherwise leads to recovery. | **Kept.** This is the fix. |
| `checkRequesterOnce` in the adopted finalizer (#205675) removes a per-mutation requester re-check. | No new failure. A failure path is removed. | It reduces failures; requester policy is still checked at admission. | **Kept.** Fail-open direction. |

No other throw, refusal, exit or rollback trigger is added. Everything else in the diff is docs, test fixtures and the `healthRpcVerified` probe field.

## End-to-end proof on exact head `e978dfa8e13e`

Setup: private rootless Podman (one task-owned store per cell, `--http-proxy=false`), systemd as PID 1, a systemd user unit, synthetic state, and an authenticated `update.run` RPC against a loopback registry.
- Installed baseline: `2026.11.11` package built from exactly `e978dfa8e13e`.
- Candidate: the same bytes relabeled `2026.11.12` (`2026.11.12-e978dfa8e13e-next-fixture`). Only the version, build ID and dist inventory changed.

A cell passes only with authenticated `health` RPC `ok` **and** a `gateway status --require-rpc` build ID equal to the expected package, with no manual repair.

| Cell (head `e978dfa8e13e`) | Injection | Result | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) normal | none | Candidate serving `2026.11.12-e978dfa8e13e-next-fixture`. Health RPC `ok`. Run `succeeded`. | `update.run` 05:56:37 → verified 06:00:07 (3m30s) |
| (c1) waiting updater SIGKILL | updater SIGKILLed 20 s after the `--doctor` worker appeared; worker left running | Helper logged `managed update command child lease settled after the updater exited`, then repair, recovery, and `gateway service recovery succeeded (readiness and runtime identity verified)`. Candidate verified serving, health RPC `ok`, run `succeeded` / `managed-service-handoff-recovered`. No manual repair. | SIGKILL 06:00:10 → verified 06:01:49 (1m39s) |
| (c2) updater and worker SIGKILL | `--doctor` worker and updater SIGKILLed together | Candidate verified serving, health RPC `ok`, run `succeeded` / `managed-service-handoff-recovered`. No manual repair. | SIGKILL 05:53:38 → verified 05:55:40 (2m02s) |
| **Red control** for (c1) on the unfixed build (`release/2026.11.11` + #205675 only) | same as (c1) | `handoff failed: managed update command lease binding was lost`, `terminal writer lost its current claim`, helper exited 1. Gateway `down` in every sample until the cell was stopped. | SIGKILL 06:03:55; still down at 06:06:56 |

Both recovered runs also logged `Update notice changed or belongs to another handoff; it was not replaced` / `restoration result could not be durably recorded`. The run ledger still reached `succeeded` and the Gateway was verified. This is a notice-recording warning only.

**(b) Hung finalizer: not met.** On this line the finalizer's only worker process is `update-migrated-finalize.worker.js --doctor`. Hanging it hits the Doctor data-at-risk stop described below, not `update-activation-timeout`. The timeout routing in this PR is therefore not reached by a real hang in these cells. It is backed only by the supporting unit test.

## Not proven end to end (supporting tests only)

- The `update-activation-timeout` → recovery branch (forward and before publication). No real installed hang produced that result on this line (see (b)). Supporting unit test only.
- `checkRequesterOnce` reducing the stall reported in #205547.

Supporting unit tests (red on the base, green on this head) are in `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-interrupted.test.ts` (`candidateWorker`, `finalizerTimeout` fixtures). They are not counted as proof.

## Open maintainer decision: a hung Doctor phase stays stopped

A service cell on `98eef07638c7` (helper and timeout handling identical to this head when an explicit `timeoutMs` is given) SIGSTOPped the finalizer's **Doctor** worker (`update-migrated-finalize.worker.js --doctor`) with an operator `timeoutMs: 420000`.

- At the deadline the updater did not return `update-activation-timeout`. It refused with `Doctor processes remain unsettled, data-at-risk. PIDs/process groups: …; custody receipt unavailable. Keep the Gateway stopped`.
- The helper logged `recovery not attempted: no verified recovery result` and the Gateway was left stopped.
- After the helper exited, the stopped Doctor process was gone as well (its process group ended with the helper's transient unit). The stop outlived the risk it was guarding.

This PR does **not** change that outcome. It is an existing data-risk refusal: `recoverInterruptedManagedUpdate` refuses a run with a recorded data-at-risk mark, and only `update repair` verifies and clears marks. Bringing the Gateway back automatically would mean the helper terminates the unsettled Doctor and runs the mark-verifying repair without a human. That changes data-safety policy, so it needs a maintainer decision. Until then, a hang inside the Doctor phase still needs `openclaw update repair`.

Without an operator timeout, a hung finalizer stays unbounded, with the Gateway stopped, exactly as on the base.

## Accepted edge case

A candidate worker that **hangs** after its waiting updater was killed has no deadline owner left. The helper waits up to the recovery budget (30 min, or the operator timeout), then falls back to today's `update repair` guidance. This needs two faults at once.

Refs #205547, #205675. Head: `e978dfa8e13e`. Release-line-only fix: `main` does not run this updater for owned installs.

prs.title: fix: honor Agent and node exec settings in Dedicated workers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Dedicated Agent's exec tool could use different timeouts and executable search paths than its owner configured. When a model invoked Git, the supervised worker also lost the Git configuration selected by the node.

## User Impact

Dedicated workers honor the Agent's configured timing and can find tools in directories that the node permits. The node can provide an image-owned Git configuration and public tool inputs to local commands. Explicit per-turn GitHub identity retains precedence.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway sends the resolved exec settings through the tool surface defined in #205571. The node admits requested directories and supplies the local tool inputs. Source credentials remain with their existing owners, and the exec approval path stays in effect.

## Evidence

At `2895edef`, 20 local worker-supervisor tests passed. Hosted CI passed all five core typecheck shards and the baseline check. The full local Gateway exec suite could not complete because the local environment lacks the pinned native fs-safe companion.

Hosted CI at `2895edef` passed the required gate after the Android retry. The earlier Android timeout also occurred on scheduled `main`. All five Gateway worker exec approval tests passed in the first hosted attempt, including the new case for the Agent timeout and the executable directory admitted by the node. [Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45758786322/job/139717822754) · [Worker exec tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45758786322/job/139704242385) · [Scheduled main Android job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45749158542/job/139672856639)

Earlier compiled worker tests exercised model-invoked exec and system Git using the node-selected configuration, with the model credential and private launch configuration kept outside the tool process. OCE qualified and merged the Runner pinned to `9a838501`. Qualification of the newer upstream-main Runner follows this stack. [OCE qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/7346)

prs.title: fix(update): settle a 2026.11.10 update that released its lease after verifying its candidate
prs.body:
Related: #205167, #205078

## Problem

On a pnpm global install that reached 2026.11.10 through `openclaw update`, the 2026.11.10 updater loses its plugin lifecycle lease while it updates to 2026.11.11. The new version is installed and its Gateway is verified serving. The updater then unwinds the normal way: it releases its executor lease and exits 1 with `update-recovery-pending`. Its run stays `running`/`verifying` and its plugin cohort stays reserved.

The next `openclaw update` then refuses:

> The update lease store no longer holds that update's lease, so this update cannot show that its processes are gone. … By hand: Run openclaw update repair

So every install in this state needs a manual `openclaw update repair`. The candidate cannot stop the first failure, because 2026.11.10 drives that hop. #205078 stops the failure from coming back on later hops, but this refusal stays.

## Fix

`inspectInterruptedUpdateRecovery` already lets the next update settle a dead update's plugin cohort. Before this change it accepted two proofs that the dead updater's processes were gone:

- the lease store still holds the dead driver's lease;
- the driver ran in an earlier boot.

An executor releases its lease only after its command scope has joined every child and confirmed cleanup (`update-command-executor.ts`, the same in v2026.11.10). A later claim also succeeds only once those processes are gone. So when the store still exists but the lease is missing, the processes have ended.

In that case the next update now settles the recovery if both of these hold:

- the run recorded its candidate verified serving: service running, version match, same version and build;
- that version and build is still the installed core.

It then settles the recovery the way it already does for the other two proofs, which is the way `openclaw update repair` does. That includes a dead update that had begun rolling back: the update finishes the installed version as repair would.

Every other case keeps the existing refusal, including a missing store and a different installed build.

**Accepted edge case:** a store deleted and recreated in the same boot while a killed driver's children are still running looks the same as a released lease. This is named in the code comment.

### What changed since the first review

`57cb5d2` removes two refusals that the earlier commits added on this path:

- the "settling it would roll back the version it verified" refusal (for a rollback outcome or a begun rollback);
- the claim-time "installed version changed while this update was starting" recheck.

Neither prevented damage. A released lease is the same processes-gone proof as the other two. For those proofs the update already finishes a begun rollback by doing what repair does. The refusal only sent the user to `openclaw update repair`, which does exactly the same work. The Podman `rollback` cell below runs this path end to end.

## Error surfaces

Diff against merge-base `54dc563`: one production file, `src/cli/update-cli/update-plugin-cohort-settlement.ts`, plus docs and tests. Every added or changed failure path:

| Path | Can it fire for a healthy user? | Rollback or outage risk | Kept / removed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Existing refusal "update lease store no longer holds that update's lease" | No. It needs a pending plugin recovery from a dead update. | None. It refuses before changing anything. | **Narrowed, not added.** It no longer fires when the store exists, the lease is gone, and the verified candidate is installed. All other cases are unchanged. |
| New file reads in `isVerifiedCandidateInstalled` (`package.json`, `dist/build-info.json`) | No. They run only in the state above. | None. Both readers return `null` on failure, and the check then fails open to the existing refusal. | Kept. Nothing new throws. |
| Existing settlement steps, now reachable from a released lease: "could not be settled", other pending recovery, and repair-equivalent finishing (Doctor, plugin convergence, Gateway restoration) | No. They run only in the stuck state above, which was a hard refusal before. | They do what `openclaw update repair` does, and repair was the only way out before. On a begun rollback, Doctor stops the Gateway once, for 51 s in the `rollback` cell. A finishing failure stops the update and names repair, as on the existing paths. | Kept. This is the fix. |
| Refusal "settling it would roll back the version it verified" (added in 959dc01 / dbc426c) | No. | It caused no damage, but it kept the user stuck and needing repair. | **Removed** in 57cb5d2. It did not prevent damage (see above). |
| Claim-time refusal "The installed version changed while this update was starting" (added in 959dc01) | Only with two concurrent updaters. | None. | **Removed** in 57cb5d2. Settlement already decides from the installed core under the claim, and `pendingRecovery()` already catches another command settling it first. |

No new throws, exits, rollback triggers or tightened validations remain. No refusal is added.

## Evidence (exact head `57cb5d26ea97`)

**Setup.** Private rootless Podman with task-owned storage (`--storage-driver vfs`, `--http-proxy=false`) and systemd user services. The image is Node 26.12.1 bookworm with systemd (`718f08f98802`), and pnpm is 12.15.0. Two plugins are retained: a local-archive native plugin and an npm-registry managed native plugin. Each cell ran in one container boot.

**Packs.**

- `openclaw-2026.11.12-head.tgz` (sha256 `7b850e7b…`, `buildId 2026.11.12-57cb5d26ea97-…`) is packed from the exact head. The only change is `package.json` version 2026.11.12, so an update has something to install.
- `openclaw-2026.11.11-rel-head.tgz` (sha256 `dcf5d02a…`) is `release/2026.11.11` (`19d8a5c`) with `update-plugin-cohort-settlement.ts` replaced by the exact-head blob `41cc01e5`. The base blob `d34e4e7d` is identical on the merge-base and on `release/2026.11.11`.

**Why the release-based pack is needed.** The 2026.11.10 updater dies (#205167) only when it installs a release-line 2026.11.11. When it installs a main-based pack it finishes cleanly; see the `chain` cell. To reach the stuck state, the dead update therefore installs the release tree carrying this PR's exact settlement file. That code then drives the next update, onto the exact-head pack.

| Cell | 11.10 → 11.11 (driven by 11.10) | Follow-on update (driven by this PR's settlement code) | End state |
|---|---|---|---|
| `released` | exit 1 `update-recovery-pending` in 110 s. CLI 2026.11.11 (19d8a5c), Gateway verified serving. Run `running/verifying`, cohort reserved. | **exit 0** in 142 s: `Settled interrupted update …: its plugin and configuration changes were kept, because its Gateway was verified on the version it installed, which this installation replaced`. Then 11.11 → 11.12. | CLI `OpenClaw 2026.11.12 (57cb5d2)`. systemd `active/running`. Authenticated `health` RPC `ok: true` with 0 plugin errors, `/readyz` ready, both proof plugins loaded. Dead run `failed/abandoned`, no `update.recovery.*` or `update.pluginCohort.*` rows. `doctor --fix` exit 0. A further update exits 0 (`skipped/already-current`). |
| `rollback` (state-injected: the dead cohort's `disposition` set to `rollback` after the dead hop, as if its rollback had begun) | the same, exit 1 in 110 s | **exit 0** in 212 s: `Settled interrupted update …: That update had begun rolling its plugin changes back on the version it installed … settled as openclaw update repair settles them`, then `Finished interrupted update … as openclaw update repair does (Doctor, plugin convergence and Gateway restoration); recorded as update run 7809a888…`. Then 11.11 → 11.12. | The same as `released`: 2026.11.12 (57cb5d2) serving, health `ok`, `/readyz` ready, plugins loaded, no recovery rows, Doctor exit 0, `already-current` exit 0. Gateway downtime in that hop: 51 s for finishing Doctor plus 18 s for activation, against 56 s + 19 s in `released`. |
| `chain` (healthy path) | 11.10 → 2026.11.11 exact-head pack: **exit 0** in 177 s (no lease loss) | exact-head 11.11 → exact-head 11.12: exit 0 in 91 s | Serving 2026.11.12 (57cb5d2), health `ok`, `/readyz` ready. Doctor exit 0 and `already-current` exit 0. |

Earlier evidence on the original head, recorded before this change: the unmodified `release/2026.11.11` follow-on refused in 3 s with the lease-store message, and the install stayed on 2026.11.11 with the run `running` and the cohort reserved.

## Tests

- `update-command-killed-run-replaced.process.test.ts` covers the settled released lease, the begun-rollback case (now settled), and the refusal once the verified candidate is no longer installed. The touched suites (replaced, refusals, cohort settlement) pass locally.
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` are clean on the touched files.
- Exact-head CI is green.

## Not covered

- The capture directory of the failed 2026.11.10 run (`~/.openclaw.update-captures/<run>`) is still listed by `openclaw update status` as an "ambiguous" recovery set, with next action `openclaw update cleanup --dry-run`. It does not block updates.
- The `rollback` cell injects the rollback disposition. A 2026.11.10 run that really began a rollback and then released its lease was not reproduced.
- Windows, macOS, npm, Bun and Gateway-started updates were not run. The backport is left to the release owner, and the production file applies cleanly to `release/2026.11.11`.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa
