prs.title: fix: keep reminder scheduling visible in crowded Code Mode sessions
prs.body:
Related to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187354.

## What Problem This Solves

A crowded Code Mode catalog can expose shell execution while omitting the native scheduling signature. An agent can then start a second OpenClaw CLI merely to schedule a reminder. Leandro F. Chaves identified the catalog issue and proposed promoting scheduler tools in this PR.

## User Impact

The compact index pins the admitted core scheduler alongside the core file and shell tools. The existing character budget, capability grants, independent profiles, and shell execution are preserved. Plugin or client tools that share the scheduler name retain ordinary catalog ranking.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tool ownership and admission are already established when Code Mode builds its index. Using those facts preserves independent-profile CLI use and gives same-named plugins their ordinary ranking.

## Evidence

A scripted agent chose the visible scheduler when present, otherwise shell exec. Both runs used the same 154-tool catalog, Linux x86-64 host, reminder name, scheduled time and payload. The Gateway, CLI, scheduling tool, and state store were real.

| Case | Matching jobs saved | Matching job ID returned to agent | CLI starts | CLI peak RSS |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main baseline | 1 | yes | 1 | 210,480 KiB |
| This change | 1 | yes | 0 | no child |
| Explicit shell to independent `--profile dev` Gateway | 1 in that profile, 0 in the primary | yes | 1 | 210,668 KiB |

RSS covers the CLI child that successfully executed `automations create`. The same scripted tool-selection rule ran against each catalog. Provider-specific selection rates and arm64 container memory remain open.

The packaged build passed. The final regression failed against the frozen baseline on native-scheduler priority. All 9 tests in the changed suite passed on the published tree, including learned ranking, ordinary plugin ranking and the absent-scheduler control. Local autoreview of `4986dd0c31cac5d92c7692651bd7ae688536965b` through P2 returned no actionable findings. The production diff is +5/−3 lines; the remaining changes are regression tests.

## Remaining scope

Restart recovery can still report that a rejected or unacknowledged reminder was saved. This change addresses tool discovery and child-process cost. The paired restart results and the outstanding arm64 container OOM are tracked on the [issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187354#issuecomment-7182070508).

prs.title: fix(memory): ground dated daily notes when the query names their date
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory search ranks dated daily notes (`memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`) from the date in their path. When the query already names an explicit date, that signal is ignored: the matching daily note ages out by temporal decay and loses its result window to newer, less relevant notes.

Reproduction used a private workspace query that names an explicit date; the dated note for that date did not appear in the top results while current notes did.

## Change

- `parseQueryDates()` extracts explicit dates from query text: ISO (`2026-11-16`, `2026/11/16`) and written forms (`November 16 2026`, `November 16, 2026`).
- A dated daily-note entry whose embedded date matches a query date gets a 1.25x multiplicative boost, composed with temporal decay.
- `queryText` is threaded through `mergeHybridResults` and every `applyTemporalDecayToHybridResults` call site.
- Queries with no explicit date behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/memory-core/src/memory/temporal-decay.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

prs.title: fix(mcp): compile tool output validators on first call, not at catalog load (#199327)
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/agents/mcp-tool-metadata.ts:76-79` (on `main`) compiles an output-schema validator for every included tool inside `normalizeMcpToolCatalog`, on every `tools/list`, and keeps it for the catalog's lifetime. Each session MCP runtime normalizes its own catalog, so a ~200-tool server costs ~200 compiled TypeBox validators per session, almost all for tools that session never calls.

Fixes #199327. Thanks @Subseaking for the report and heap snapshots, @lonexreb for the fix, and @brandon-julio-t for the real-model Gateway check and session-start measurements in #205723 (same two commits, rebased).

## What Problem This Solves

With per-session MCP runtimes and a long `mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs`, every new session that uses a large MCP catalog compiles and retains a validator for every tool. The reporter saw Gateway heap grow from 0.73 GB to 1.05 GB in an hour and TypeBox validators from 1,461 to 5,111, with ~25 session runtimes each holding ~202 compiled validators for the same ~200-tool HTTP server.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `normalizeMcpToolCatalog` now records each included tool's output schema; `validatorForCall` compiles it on that tool's first call and reuses it for the rest of the catalog's life. Each catalog still owns its validator provider: no shared or global cache, no change to refresh or TTL.
- Schemas that contain an `$id` still compile at catalog load, in catalog order, because compiling registers that resource for other tools' `$ref`s (lonexreb's second commit).
- Native HTTP calls go through the SDK's `client.callTool`, which never consults the catalog validator. The native bridge now acquires the validator before that call, so an uncompilable output schema still fails before any request reaches the server. Without this line the PR head let such a call through (shown below).
- The two new tests are folded into one regression covering both boundaries (unused schemas stay uncompiled; a shared `$id` still compiles at load and a `$ref` to it resolves on first call). Against `main`: production +47/-26, tests +26/-0 (contributor revision: tests +37).

## User Impact

- Less retained memory per MCP session runtime and less catalog work per new session (numbers below).
- Output validation is unchanged: same validator, same accept/reject results, same error text, on first and later calls; tools without an output schema, `isError` results and missing structured content behave as before.
- One behavior differs, only for a server that advertises an output schema that cannot compile. Before: the whole server failed to start (`bundle-mcp: failed to start server "X": Invalid MCP draft-2020-12 JSON Schema: ...`) and none of its tools were available. Now: the server starts, its healthy tools work, and calling the broken tool fails with the same `Invalid MCP ... JSON Schema: ...` message, before any `tools/call` is sent. This matches the MCP SDK's own per-tool handling of uncompilable output schemas (SEP-2106).

## Evidence

Built Gateway (`pnpm build`) for `main` `40f3903e6e2b` and this head, each in a secretless `node:24.22.1` container. Local streamable-HTTP MCP server with 205 tools (200 `bulk_*` with draft 2020-12 schemas using nested objects, `$defs`/`$ref`, enums, formats and patterns, plus `good`, `bad`, `plain`, `missing`, `iserr`); the server never validates its own output. Scripted local OpenAI-compatible model, `mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs: 86400000`, `tools.toolSearch: false`. Each of 20 fresh sessions ran one turn calling `bulk_<k>` and `good`. Forced-GC `heapUsed` read in the Gateway main isolate, TypeBox `Validator` objects counted from a heap snapshot. Serial interleaved runs, base/cand alternating.

Acceptance rule: win = lower forced-GC heap growth and fewer retained TypeBox validators after 20 sessions, with session start and first-turn time not worse beyond run spread; any cell more than 20% worse is a stop.

Settled set: 60 s after Gateway ready, 3 runs per side (ABAB):

| 20 sessions, 2 tool calls each | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| heapUsed growth after forced GC (median, range) | 208.1 MB (206.9–209.4) | 131.6 MB (130.4–133.8) |
| per session | 10.4 MB | 6.6 MB |
| TypeBox `Validator` objects in heap snapshot | 4,145 | 105 |
| first session: chat.send to first model request (median) | 2,558 ms | 2,503 ms |
| sessions 2–20: chat.send to first model request (median / p95, n=57) | 297 / 459 ms | 283 / 370 ms |
| first turn to final (median / p95, n=60) | 384 / 577 ms | 367 / 585 ms |
| Gateway `mcp-materialize` stage on the first session (median of all runs) | 153 ms (n=7) | 102 ms (n=8) |

Unsettled set: first session sent as soon as the Gateway was ready, 5 runs per side (ABAB): heap growth 212.7 vs 138.9 MB, validators 4,145 vs 105, sessions 2–20 start median/p95 363/2,480 vs 335/952 ms. The first session here overlaps Gateway warm-up and swings widely (`main` 2,348–11,349 ms, this PR 3,190–10,405 ms, medians 2,776 vs 3,687 ms); the difference sits in the Gateway's `preparation`/`replyInitialization` startup stages, not the MCP stage (lower on this PR in every run), and disappears in the settled set.

`main` count: 26 Gateway-internal validators + ~203 per session runtime. This PR: 26 + one per called tool per runtime + a small per-turn constant that also appears on `main`.

Controls (same on both builds unless noted; observed tool results handed back to the model):

| case | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `good` (valid output), first and second call in one session | `structuredContent: {"ok":true}` | same |
| `bad` (`{"ok":"not-a-boolean"}`), first and second call | `Structured content does not match the tool's output schema: /ok must be boolean` | same |
| `missing` (schema, no structured content) | `Tool missing has an output schema but did not return structured content` | same |
| `iserr` (isError result) | passed through: `P199346-ISERR tool reported a problem` | same |
| `plain` (no outputSchema) | `plain text result P199346-PLAIN` | same |
| same tools over stdio | good passes, bad rejected with the same text, plain unchanged | same |
| repeated calls in one runtime (`good`,`bad` again): Validator delta | +2 | +2 (same per-turn constant; no recompilation) |
| server `broken` with one uncompilable outputSchema | server fails to start: `failed to start server "broken": Invalid MCP draft-2020-12 JSON Schema: <schema>.properties.a.$ref: unresolved ref`; 0 `tools/call` | `fine` works; `broken` call fails with `Invalid MCP draft-2020-12 JSON Schema: <schema>.properties.a.$ref: unresolved ref`; server saw only `tools/call fine` |

Native HTTP bridge (`createSessionMcpRuntime` + `acquireNativeMcpServer` + `view.callTool` against an HTTP server with tools `fine` and `broken`):

```
main 40f3903e6e2b:      catalog fails (same Invalid MCP ... unresolved ref), server tools/call: 0
f992f15609 on main:    fine -> {"ok":true}; broken -> complete {"a":1}; server tools/call: fine, broken
this head:              fine -> {"ok":true}; broken -> rejected Invalid MCP draft-2020-12 JSON Schema: <schema>.properties.a.$ref: unresolved ref; server tools/call: fine
```

Tests: `mcp-tool-metadata.test.ts` regression fails on `main` (`expected "getValidator" to be called 1 times, but got 3 times`) and passes here; touched-area MCP tests pass.

Proof comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199346#issuecomment-7183498000

## Merge danger

Two-way door: no stored state, config, schema or protocol change; a revert restores eager compilation. Blast radius: MCP tool catalogs and calls in the bundle runtime, node host and native bridge; the only visible difference is the per-tool timing of the uncompilable-schema error described above.

prs.title: feat: add opt-in Antigravity sessions with safe restart resume
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

People who use the Antigravity CLI cannot select it as a bundled OpenClaw runtime. If a Gateway restart interrupts a native command after it takes effect but before its result is recorded, automatically retrying the old turn can repeat that effect.

## User Impact

Eligible users on Linux amd64 can explicitly opt in to the native Antigravity account runtime in a Full access session. Antigravity model choices come from the installed CLI, without a separate OpenClaw provider entry. After an interruption, **Resume** keeps the same Antigravity conversation and releases already accepted messages in order, without retrying the interrupted turn or sending a new prompt. Check what changed before resuming.

Off by default; updating does not select or enable Antigravity. The CLI owns account sign-in. Guarded or sandbox-required sessions are refused rather than silently running outside their restrictions. Gateway-mediated tools and protected Gemini are not part of this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

A bundled plugin uses the installed CLI and its native conversation binding. Its harness publishes the native model catalog before first-turn resolution. The session store records an in-flight native turn before dispatch and retires that receipt in the same write as successful logical completion, not when the native process merely returns. If that final write did not commit, the Gateway can hold the interrupted turn and its input queue until an authorized operator acknowledges it. Released messages still use their original senders’ authority. Other runtimes are not opted into this recovery policy.

Contributor: @joshavant

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b0dc2b4a-b40b-482e-b75e-53d2716ea194)

## Evidence

- **Chat boot budget fix (`bb469e3`):** the recovery notice renderer now uses the existing lazy notice boundary and loads only when a hold is present. On the exact prior hosted CI merge tree (`d36f2f1`, base `9137b6e`) with just this patch applied, `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` passed: cold chat JavaScript dropped from 1,336,290 B to 1,336,154 B gzip, below the unchanged 1,336,272 B cap, with no increase in startup requests. Focused lint and the Chromium test for one-click Resume without a new prompt passed. The notice markup, copy, and CSS did not change.
- **Fresh opt-in first turn (`e37fd1a`):** the installed Gateway was tested against a deterministic Antigravity CLI fixture, with no `models.providers` entry. Before the catalog fix (`f3d966b`), the cold first turn returned `Unknown model`, `models.list` had no native row, and no native turn process launched. The package from the exact `e37fd1a` source tree returned the fixture reply on the first turn, published the discovered native model, and launched exactly one native turn process. Package integrity, all 22 focused extension tests, extension typecheck, and lint passed. This runs the packaged Gateway, not a live Antigravity account.
- **Durable completion fix (`a370a21`):** 69 focused Gateway and SQLite lifecycle, restart, and custody tests passed, along with core typecheck and focused lint. The new regression exercises both sides of the durable terminal write: the unfinished turn holds input across two starts with no automatic continuation; the committed successful turn retires its own receipt and no longer holds the queue. Existing FIFO sender-admission tests also passed. These are automated boundary tests, not a stock Antigravity crash trace between native success and the terminal commit.
- **Upgrade on `f3d966b`:** published OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (`6ea542f`) used its npm updater to install a tarball built from the exact source tree of `f3d966b`. The upgraded Gateway loaded the same saved session ID and label, preserved the existing plugin setting, and did not enable or select Antigravity. The package passed tarball integrity validation. The isolated test used `--no-restart` and then booted the upgraded Gateway; it does not cover managed-service restart or rollback. The subsequent receipt and catalog fixes add no migration or dependency changes.
- **Earlier upgrade:** the published OpenClaw 2026.11.9 npm updater installed the R43 qualification build (base `f98a602`). The upgraded Gateway preserved the original session ID, a saved plugin setting, and the stable channel. SQLite state and agent schemas advanced, and Antigravity stayed off.
- **Earlier live crash and Resume:** with stock Antigravity CLI 1.5.17, R43 was killed after the command committed one effect but before the result was recorded. Two Gateway boots held both original messages. One real Control UI click released them FIFO on the same native conversation with zero new chat sends and one total effect. This is one tested crash window, not an exactly-once guarantee.
- **Prior branch checks (`f3d966b`):** the ready CI workflow and its gate passed. The repair adds the required bundled artwork, regenerates plugin inventory and references, and fixes test routing, typecheck, and lint errors. The Chromium test verified one-click Resume without a new prompt. Hosted CI is tracked separately on the exact PR head.
- The test allocation covers the 311 lines above the default budget for distinct native process lifecycle, durable queued-input authority, restart, and browser behavior. No production migration was added by this branch. The generated config inventory grows by 24 standard plugin registration paths; the plugin has no custom settings.

### Control UI comparison

[Clean and annotated before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205731#issuecomment-7182026099) show the same synthetic chat on main (`9ad935f`) and the R43 candidate UI (base `f98a602`). Before: no recovery action. After: the composer explains the hold and offers Resume.

## Worked on by

- @joshavant

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): tell a channel sender why their queued input was refused
prs.body:
## Problem

A queued input from a channel (Discord, Telegram, ...), including `/followup`, that admission refused before its turn started gave the sender nothing in that channel. Since #205408 the cause sentence (for example "I did not run your saved work. …") is written to the session transcript, so Control UI shows it, but the channel stayed silent. Channel inbound follow-ups register no source delivery (`queuedFollowupReplyDisposition`), and a refused input has no admitted turn, so neither existing send path ran.

## Fix

`src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.ts`, withheld branch:

- The refusal (`OperatorRefusalError` before admission) is found once in `catch` and kept. This replaces the `withheldNotice` helper, which searched the error graph a second time.
- When the input has no source delivery owner and its origin is a routable channel, the runner sends the refusal sentence once to the origin through `routeReply`. This is the same outbound owner that queued follow-up replies use, with the same origin fields from the queued row: channel, to, account, thread. It uses `mirror: false` because the transcript notice is already recorded.
- It honors the session send policy (`resolveSendPolicy`, including a `/send off` session override) and does not send for passive room events. Both checks match how normal follow-up replies are gated.
- A Gateway chat source (`queuedFollowupReplyDisposition: deliver`) keeps its existing path, so a Control UI message gets no second copy.

No new column, no schema or protocol change, and no new delivery manager. #205417 also asked whether the pending-input row should store the cause. It does not need to: the sentence reaches the channel from memory at the moment of refusal.

Production `src`: +76/−28 (**net positive**). The cause was missing code: no send path existed for an unadmitted input. The only removable code was the `withheldNotice` duplication, which is gone. The rest is the routing call, the send-policy (read from the live config and session entry, like admission) and room-event gates that normal replies already apply, and a log line when the send fails.

## User impact

Say a Discord or Telegram sender queues a message, and before it starts the sender loses access (for example, they are removed from `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, or their role is lowered). The same channel now shows the sentence that explains why it did not run. Before, the sender saw nothing.

## Evidence

- `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts` "tells a channel sender why their queued input was refused before it started": an admission refusal on a Telegram-originated queued input. With send policy `allow`, it is routed once to the origin with the cause sentence (fails on base `e4517b0ef2f4`, passes on head). With `deny`, nothing is sent. The transcript notice is the same sentence in both cases.
- Importers of `followup-runner.ts`, plus `chat-send-direct-followup.test.ts` (the #205408 transcript test): 15 files, run locally.
- E2E: see comments.

prs.title: fix(plugins): read plugin policy through the canonical enable owner
prs.body:
Closes #205672

## What Problem This Solves

Running `openclaw doctor` with `plugins.allow: []` and an enabled Codex entry silently drops the personal Codex asset reminder, the `/tools` inventory notice tells operators to add `browser` to `plugins.allow` even when the browser plugin was disabled somewhere else entirely, and the OpenShell workspace binding ignores a padded denylist entry and enables File Transfer against the operator's policy.

- Problem: three call sites decided plugin enablement by hand instead of asking the existing policy owner, so they disagreed with what actually loads. The doctor scan treated any `allow` array as authoritative and never consulted `entries`, so an empty allowlist (which restricts nothing, as established in #191708) turned the scan off. The `/tools` notice blamed `plugins.allow` for every missing browser and produced no notice at all when the plugin was denylisted. The OpenShell workspace binding compared raw ids in `allow`/`deny`/`entries`, so `" File-Transfer "` never matched the denylist and the binding enabled File Transfer anyway.
- Solution: each site now normalizes with `normalizePluginsConfig` and asks `resolveEffectiveEnableState` for the decision, which returns both `enabled` and the reason (`plugins disabled` / `blocked by denylist` / `disabled in config` / `not in allowlist`). The notice now names that reason and only suggests editing `plugins.allow` when the allowlist is actually the cause.
- What changed: `extensions/openshell/src/worker-workspace.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/shared/codex-native-assets.ts` and `src/agents/tools-effective-inventory.ts` replace their hand-rolled checks with the shared owner; the new scenarios are folded into three existing test cases (net test line delta -1).
- What did NOT change: the decision order, empty-allowlist semantics and every other rule still live in `resolveEffectiveEnableState`; no new option, schema, or config surface was added, and the two notices keep their existing ids and severities.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Best fix: route all three call sites through the single existing owner (`normalizePluginsConfig` + `resolveEffectiveEnableState`) rather than teaching each site the policy rules again. The owner already encodes the order deny -> entry -> allowlist and the empty-allowlist rule, and the repo already uses it this way from `extensions/browser/src/plugin-enabled.ts` and `extensions/codex/index.ts`, so this removes duplicated policy instead of adding a fourth variant.
- Alternative(s): patching each site locally (add an `allow.length > 0` guard, add a deny check, normalize the ids inline) was rejected because it leaves three copies of the same policy that can drift again; writing a new shared helper for these three callers was rejected because the owner already exists.
- Risk: the doctor scan and the OpenShell gate now consult the bundled default (`enabledByDefault`) as well as the config, so a Codex config block or an explicit allowlist entry counts as opt-in even with an empty allowlist. That matches what the Codex plugin itself gates on, and the widest supported case (no `plugins` section at all) still skips the scan, as before. The notice's accessory sentence changed for non-allowlist causes, so any doc that quoted the old sentence needs a look.

## User Impact

Operators who keep an empty `plugins.allow` now still see the personal Codex asset reminder, and when the browser tool is missing the reason reported matches the reason the plugin is actually off. Following that advice no longer means widening plugin policy for a plugin that was disabled on purpose. An operator who denylisted File Transfer (even with padded whitespace in the id) no longer gets it silently re-enabled by an OpenShell workspace binding.

## Evidence

Every cell below states its full `plugins` input. Doctor cells share one `HOME` fixture containing two personal skills (`.codex/skills/tweet-helper/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/agent-helper/SKILL.md`); the count is `grep -c 'Personal Codex CLI assets found'` on `doctor --non-interactive` output. Every `tools.effective` cell also has `browser: { enabled: true }` in the config; the notice column quotes the `browser-plugin-not-allowed` message.

| Case | Full `plugins` input | Before (base `1342a4e`) | After (head `eb5e466`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| doctor, empty allow + enabled entry | `{"allow":[],"entries":{"codex":{"enabled":true}}}` | 0 asset lines | 1 line, `2 skills` |
| doctor, enabled entry, no allow key (control) | `{"entries":{"codex":{"enabled":true}}}` | 1 line, `2 skills` | 1 line, `2 skills` |
| doctor, padded allow id (control) | `{"allow":[" CODEX "]}` | 1 line, `2 skills` | 1 line, `2 skills` |
| doctor, padded deny id (control) | `{"allow":[],"deny":[" Codex "]}` | 0 | 0 |
| doctor, allowlist without codex (control) | `{"allow":["slack"]}` | 0 | 0 |
| doctor, no plugins section (control) | (key absent) | 0 | 0 |
| tools.effective, entry disabled | `{"allow":[],"entries":{"browser":{"enabled":false}}}` | `plugins.allow does not include browser` | `disabled in config` |
| tools.effective, plugins globally disabled | `{"enabled":false,"allow":[]}` | `plugins.allow does not include browser` | `plugins disabled` |
| tools.effective, denylisted | `{"deny":["browser"]}` | no notice at all | `blocked by denylist` |
| tools.effective, browser enabled (control) | `{"entries":{"browser":{"enabled":true}}}` | no notice | no notice |
| tools.effective, empty allow only (control) | `{"allow":[]}` | no notice | no notice |
| tools.effective, other allow + entry on (control) | `{"allow":["slack"],"entries":{"browser":{"enabled":true}}}` | no notice | no notice |

| Case | Before (base `1342a4e`) | After (head `eb5e466`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| openshell worker configure, `plugins.deny: [" File-Transfer "]` + agent workspace binding | exit 0; config rewritten with File Transfer enabled and the workspace binding applied | exit 1; refusal message; config file byte-identical |
| upgrade, latest stable -> head, same state dir, `{"allow":[],"entries":{"codex":{"enabled":true}}}` | stable doctor: 0 asset lines | head `doctor --fix` then `doctor`: 1 line, `2 skills`; `plugins` subtree preserved |

Both arms were built with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup` and driven by the shipped launcher, each case in an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `HOME`. The base arm is frozen at `1342a4e`, an ancestor of this PR's base `dd89642`; the three touched production files are byte-identical between those two commits (`git diff` empty), so the base arm exercises exactly the base behavior of every changed line.

### Doctor scan, real `openclaw doctor`

Both arms report their own commit, so the cells cannot be confused:

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (1342a4e)     # base arm
OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (eb5e466)     # this head

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated> HOME=<isolated> node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive
# base, plugins: {"allow":[],"entries":{"codex":{"enabled":true}}}
(no "Doctor info" section at all - grep -c 'Personal Codex CLI assets found' => 0)

# this head, same config
┌  Doctor info ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  - Personal Codex CLI assets found (2 skills, 0 plugins, 0 config        │
│    files, 0 hook files) in <home>/.codex and <home>/.agents/skills;      │
│    native Codex-mode agents use isolated per-agent homes and will not    │
│    load them.                                                            │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Counts across the six doctor configs are the first six rows of the table above: base `0 1 1 0 0 0`, head `1 1 1 0 0 0`; only the empty-allow-plus-entry cell changed.

### `/tools` inventory, real Gateway + real RPC

A real Gateway (`node openclaw.mjs gateway --port <port> --auth token ...`) served the cells, the session came from `sessions.create`, and each cell is a full `gateway call`. Five cells ran as config hot-reloads on one Gateway per arm; the `plugins disabled` cell ran as a cold Gateway start on both arms (its base notice only fires when `allow` is an array, which is why its input includes `allow: []`).

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs gateway call tools.effective --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:dashboard:..."}' --json

# base, plugins: {"allow":[],"entries":{"browser":{"enabled":false}}}
{"id":"browser-plugin-not-allowed","severity":"warning","message":"Browser is configured, but plugins.allow does not include browser. Add \"browser\" to plugins.allow or remove the restrictive plugin allowlist."}

# this head, same config
{"id":"browser-plugin-not-allowed","severity":"warning","message":"Browser is configured, but the browser plugin is disabled by plugin policy (disabled in config). Remove the plugin disable that applies to browser."}

# base, plugins: {"enabled":false,"allow":[]}  (cold start)
{"id":"browser-plugin-not-allowed","severity":"warning","message":"Browser is configured, but plugins.allow does not include browser. Add \"browser\" to plugins.allow or remove the restrictive plugin allowlist."}

# this head, same config (cold start)

```

### OpenShell binding, real shipped `openshell worker configure`

Config: `plugins.deny: [" File-Transfer "]` plus an agent workspace binding (`agentId: main`, `remoteRoot: /sandbox/agent-main`) and the worker profile/model settings the command requires. The OpenShell sandbox peer is a synthetic executable that answers only the node-identity and workspace-check sandbox calls; every OpenClaw step — config snapshot, plugin policy decision, binding composition, config mutation — runs from the shipped bundle. No real OpenShell device is available locally.

```console
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated> HOME=<isolated> node openclaw.mjs openshell worker configure demo-sandbox --worker-profile w1 --apply

# base (1342a4e): exit 0

# binding and cloudWorkers profile applied despite the deny entry.

# this head (eb5e466): exit 1
Agent workspace binding requires File Transfer; preserve the existing plugin restriction and enable it explicitly before retrying.
# config file UNCHANGED (cmp against the pre-run copy: identical).
```

One state dir, config `plugins: {"allow":[],"entries":{"codex":{"enabled":true}}}`, the same two-skill `HOME` fixture throughout:

```console
$ openclaw --version                      # npm openclaw@2026.11.10
OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f)
$ openclaw doctor --non-interactive       # stable: grep count => 0

$ node openclaw.mjs doctor --fix          # this head, migration entry, exit 0
$ node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive
# grep count => 1 ("2 skills"); plugins subtree parsed-equal to the input
# ({"allow":[],"entries":{"codex":{"enabled":true}}}); both SKILL.md assets
# intact; no files removed.
```

### Built bundle form

The bundles the two arms actually executed:

```text
base  dist/codex-native-assets-*.mjs
  isCodexPluginConfigured(e){const t=e.plugins;if(t?.enabled===false)return false;const n=t?.allow;
  if(Array.isArray(n))return n.some(e=>normalizeOptionalLowercaseString(e)===`codex`); ... }

  id:`codex`,origin:`bundled`,config:t,rootConfig:e,enabledByDefault:t.entries.codex!==void 0||t.allow.includes(`codex`)}).enabled}
```

### Focused tests

The new scenarios are folded into the existing cases, so the test line delta is -1 (`+19 / -20`):


The OpenShell binding has no real sandbox device here; the shipped run above uses a synthetic sandbox peer (disclosed in that section), backed by the red-on-base `worker-cli` test. Local verification ran the targeted vitest lanes and the shipped builds; the repository-wide typecheck runs in CI.

prs.title: fix: plugin reload points to a registry refresh when a load path overrides the installed plugin
prs.body:
Related: #205033

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a plugin is selected from `plugins.load.paths` and an installed package with the same ID exists, a plugin reload or other package maintenance fails with "has no authoritative package-owner metadata" and tells you to refresh the plugin registry and run Doctor. Neither step helps: the explicit load path keeps overriding the installed package, so the refusal repeats.

## User Impact

User impact: the refusal now says where the selected plugin is, that it comes from `plugins.load.paths`, which installed package it overrides, and the step that works: remove the `plugins.load.paths` entry that selects it, then retry. The refusal itself and load-path precedence are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ownership resolver already detects a config-selected plugin that shadows an install record for the same ID (the update path reports it as operator-managed). Package maintenance and reload still returned the generic missing-owner error, which points at the registry and Doctor. The resolver now returns a specific message for that case; every other ownership error is unchanged.

Not included, so this PR is linked as related rather than closing the issue: the issue also asks for the installed package version in the message and for an owner-reviewed, automatic config reconciliation. The message shows the plugin root rather than the exact configured entry, because a standalone-file entry selects its parent folder as the root.

## Evidence

- New test in `src/plugins/manifest-registry-installed.ownership.test.ts` runs the ownership check that plugin reload uses for a plugin selected from `plugins.load.paths` that shadows a same-ID install. On the base commit it returns the generic "has no authoritative package-owner metadata ... Refresh the plugin registry and run openclaw plugins doctor" message from the issue. With the fix it says where the plugin is, that it comes from `plugins.load.paths`, and which installed package it overrides. It is still a refusal.
- `pnpm test src/plugins/manifest-registry-installed.ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 3/3 pass. The file takes about 24 seconds wall time locally with a warm transform cache (about 4.5 minutes cold); CI seconds to follow.
- The consumer tests that pin the existing ownership messages, `src/plugins/update-cohort.test.ts` and `src/plugins/management-service.uninstall-ownership.test.ts`, pass 23/23. Global-origin and ambiguous plugins keep their current messages.
- oxlint and the format check pass on the two changed files.
- Live reload on an isolated Gateway built from this branch (fdf55a13d, Node 26.10.0, own state dir and port). Fixture: a plugin `shadow-demo` 1.2.1 installed with `openclaw plugins install <path>`, and a 1.2.0 copy of the same ID selected through `plugins.load.paths`. Paths are throwaway `/tmp` folders.

```text
$ openclaw plugins list | grep shadow
│ Shadow Demo │ shadow-demo │ openclaw │ enabled │ /tmp/oc-proof-205467/dev/shadow-demo/index.js │ 1.2.0 │ record-missing │

$ openclaw plugins reload shadow-demo
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: Plugin "shadow-demo" at /tmp/oc-proof-205467/dev/shadow-demo comes from plugins.load.paths and overrides its installed package "shadow-demo". Refreshing the plugin registry keeps that override. To maintain the installed package, remove the plugins.load.paths entry that selects this plugin, then retry.

$ openclaw config unset plugins.load.paths
Removed plugins.load.paths. Change will apply without restarting the gateway.

$ openclaw plugins reload shadow-demo
shadow-demo: Selected entry: /tmp/oc-proof-205467/state/extensions/shadow-demo/index.js. Rebuild compiled output after source edits.
Reloaded plugin "shadow-demo" (generation 4).

$ openclaw plugins list | grep shadow
│ Shadow Demo │ shadow-demo │ openclaw │ enabled │ global:shadow-demo/index.js │ 1.2.1 │ origin-path │
```

  The table rows are trimmed to one line each. The same reload on a base build was not run live; the base message comes from the unit test above and the issue report.
- Not run: targeted typecheck (`tsgo` is not installed in this checkout) and local autoreview (not available here). Broad checks are left to PR CI.

prs.title: fix: find Chinese and Japanese words inside sentences in Knowledge search
prs.body:
Closes #205667

## What Problem This Solves

When Knowledge is the memory provider, `knowledge_grep` and the Knowledge page's search cannot find a Chinese or Japanese word that sits inside a sentence. Chinese and Japanese text has no spaces, so the whole sentence is indexed as a single word. Searching for `新加坡` returns nothing for a page that says `客户希望地理位置在新加坡`. Latin words written next to CJK text, like `NAS` in `按NAS方式`, are not found either. Agents then tell the user that nothing relevant is stored, even though the record exists.

## User Impact

- People who keep notes in Chinese or Japanese can find a word wherever it appears in a record. No spaces are needed, and the user does not have to do anything.
- In `all` and `phrase` modes, the CJK part of a query matches as an exact substring. This includes single characters. The same characters in a different order do not match: `坡新` does not find `新加坡`.
- Stored Markdown, hashes, citations and snippets stay byte-for-byte unchanged. Snippets show the original text, not the index form.
- Existing stores upgrade on their own. The keyword index is a rebuildable projection. Its tables move from `v1` to `v2`. The first search in each scope builds the `v2` tables and drops that scope's `v1` tables. No migration step or user action is needed.
- Cost applies only to CJK text. The CJK part of the index grows about 2.3×, and building the index for CJK text is about 5.6× slower than before the fix. Non-CJK text is indexed exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`node:sqlite` cannot register a custom FTS5 tokenizer (see #193815). The fix therefore keeps FTS5 `unicode61` and changes the text it indexes. Before a record is indexed, each Han, Hiragana or Katakana run is expanded into overlapping character bigrams, plus the run's last character as a unigram. Queries are expanded the same way:

- In `all` and `phrase` modes, a CJK term becomes a phrase of adjacent bigrams. This is exact-substring matching.
- In `any` mode, it becomes an OR of its bigrams.
- A single character uses an internal prefix. Every character starts some token, so single-character recall is complete. Users still cannot use prefix search: a `*` they type is treated as punctuation.

Highlight offsets are mapped from the index text back to the stored text, so snippets stay exact. The issue's evaluation on 348 real meeting passages compared unicode61, trigram, CJK unigram, CJK bigram and `Intl.Segmenter`. Bigram had complete exact-substring recall and zero false hits. Dictionary segmentation lost about 30% of exact substrings, and trigram cannot match two-character words. The change adds no dependencies.

### Differences from the issue's proposal

- **The last character of each CJK run is kept as a unigram.** The first proposal kept a unigram only for runs of one character. Keeping it for every run means every character starts some token, so single-character queries always find their match. It also lets a term that ends in CJK followed by Latin, such as `先按NAS`, require that the run ends there. The cost is one extra token per run.
- **Index-only folding.** Inside CJK runs, the index text is NFC-composed and combining marks are removed. This covers three cases:
  - **Decomposed kana:** unicode61 splits a token at U+3099/U+309A. Without folding, NFD `が` was indexed as `か`. A search for `か` then matched it by mistake, and NFC and NFD `が` did not find each other.
  - **Ideographic variation selectors:** `葛\u{E0100}城` matches `葛城`.
  - **CJK compatibility ideographs:** U+F900 `豈` matches the unified U+8C48, as the existing rule says canonically equivalent spellings must.

  Folding applies only to the index text. Stored bytes and snippets do not change.
- **The highlight bound counts stored bytes.** The 64 KiB bound that decides between a located snippet and an opening excerpt used to count the indexed text. CJK index text is about 2.3× longer than the stored text, so located snippets would have stopped at about 28 KB of Chinese. The FTS tables now have a `body_bytes UNINDEXED` column, and the bound compares the stored body's UTF-8 size.

  This does not loosen the cost bound. For any text, the number of tokens is at most (stored bytes + 1) / 2, the same as the worst Latin case (`a a a …`). The 64 KiB CJK worst case measured about 500 ms of highlight work, against about 1,150 ms for the existing Latin worst case.

### Not in this PR

- `extensions/knowledge/src/recall-keyword.ts`, which matches automatic-recall triggers, tokenizes the same way and has the same CJK problem. It is a separate code path with its own contract. I will send it as a follow-up.

### Known limitations

These are accepted edge cases, so the code does not handle them:

- **Spaces and punctuation at a CJK/Latin boundary count as word breaks**, as they do for Latin text today. `坡NAS` also matches stored `坡 NAS` and `坡，NAS`. "Exact substring" applies to the CJK part of a term.
- **In `phrase` mode, a space between two CJK words is a word break.** `新加坡 补贴` does not match stored `新加坡补贴`, but `all` mode does. Matching both forms would need an OR over every boundary combination, which grows exponentially. The docs describe this behavior.
- **`v1` cleanup is lazy and per scope.** After the upgrade, a scope's `v1` tables stay until that scope is first searched or verified. The isolated Gateway run below shows this.

## Evidence

### End-to-end reproduction on an isolated Gateway (real agent and model)

**Setup**

- Two source builds from this checkout: base `a143512578c` and this PR's commit `0f389e08044`. The current head differs from `0f389e08044` only by an oxfmt line wrap in `retrieval.test.ts`.
- Each build ran with `pnpm openclaw gateway run --port 19891 --bind loopback` under a clean `env -i`, using a temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`/`OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1` and `plugins.slots.memory: "knowledge"`.
- The model was `amazon-bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5`, using an assumed AWS IAM role.
- No service was installed, and no existing Gateway or state was touched.

**Flow**

1. On base, a Control-UI-style `chat.send` turn asked the agent to call `knowledge_save_page`. The page had title `客户资源需求记录`, type `note` and body `客户希望地理位置在新加坡，出网流量单价按100G计价。共享存储先按NAS方式配置10TB。`. The receipt was `81d6d6b4-…`, revision 1.
2. In the same session, the agent called `knowledge_grep` once per query.
3. I stopped the base Gateway and started the fix build on the **same state directory**. This is the upgrade path existing users take. The same grep turn then ran in the same session.
4. The counts and snippets below are copied from the verbatim tool results in `chat.history`, not from the model's summary.

| Query (default `all` mode) | Base `a143512578c` | This PR `0f389e08044` | Snippet on this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `新加坡` | 0 | **1** | `客户希望地理位置在新加坡，出网流量单价按100G计价。共享存储先按NAS方式配置10TB。` |
| `出网流量` | 0 | **1** | same as above |
| `NAS` | 0 | **1** | same as above |
| `坡新` (reversed, must not match) | 0 | 0 | — |
| `客户资源需求记录` (whole title, control) | 1 | 1 | `客户资源需求记录` |

- On base, only the control query that equals an entire unbroken CJK run matched. This shows that the record was indexed and that the misses come from segmentation.
- After the upgrade, the searched scope had `keyword_{fts,rows,history_fts,history_rows}_v2_*` tables and no `v1` tables. Two other scopes that were never searched on the fix build still had their `v1` tables. This is the documented lazy cleanup.
- Gateway logs had no knowledge errors on the fix build.
- The `knowledge_grep` result returned to agents only has a compact snippet, so this run does not show where the highlight landed. Exact highlight offsets are covered by the focused test below.

### Focused tests (on the final commit `0d4a79c8d9b`)

```
pnpm test extensions/knowledge/src/retrieval.test.ts extensions/knowledge/src/lifecycle.test.ts extensions/knowledge/src/record-capacity.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  52 passed (52)
   Duration  191.62s (tests 83%, transform 11%, import 5%)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 198.66s

pnpm tsgo:extensions
EXIT=0
```

The same command on `0f389e08044` also passed (52/52, 283.50 s, of which 40% was transform on a cold compile cache).

**Why this run takes more than 30 seconds**

- Each test in these files builds a real vault, with a SQLite state database, the storage worker thread and local Git checkpoints. Nothing is mocked.
- Summed test time was about 159 s: `lifecycle.test.ts` about 85 s over 23 tests, `retrieval.test.ts` about 41 s over 24 tests, and `record-capacity.test.ts` about 34 s over 5 tests. The single `near-limit records …` capacity test took 30.9 s.
- The rest of the wall time was Vitest transforming and importing the plugin and core import graph with one worker. That share was 11% with a warm cache and 40% with a cold one.
- The two tests this PR adds take about 2.1 s (`CJK words match inside sentences as exact substrings with exact snippets`) and 1.6 s (`a v1 keyword projection is dropped and rebuilt as v2 on the next search`). Both are in `retrieval.test.ts`, which was already over 30 s before this change.
- `record-capacity.test.ts` is included because it consumes the highlight bound. It checks that bodies over 64 KiB and NUL-containing bodies still fall back to an opening excerpt.
- CI timings are not available yet.

The new CJK test covers:

- Chinese, Japanese and mixed Latin/CJK terms inside sentences, plus single characters in `all` and `any` modes.
- Queries that must not match: reversed order, a simplified-only form, and decomposed kana.
- `phrase` mode in order and reversed.
- Aliases and titles.
- Folding of NFD kana, IVS and compatibility ideographs.
- Exact snippet offsets more than 100 characters into the body.
- A filtered query, which uses the temporary corpus.
- A superseded-history match, with `via`.
- A Chinese body of about 46 KB whose snippet is still located.

The long-body case failed on the intermediate commit that still bounded highlights by the indexed text. I did not separately rerun the new unit tests against base. The base side is shown by the end-to-end table above.

### Other checks

Run on the current head:

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: pass.
- oxlint on the three touched `.ts` files (including `max-lines`): pass. `retrieval.ts` is about 657 of 700 non-blank, non-comment lines.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` on the three `.ts` files and `retrieval.md`: pass. This check found one unformatted test line, which the final commit fixes.
- `pnpm check:assertion-safety`: pass (checked on `0f389e08044`).
- `git diff --check`: pass.

Run on the pre-squash branch, with `docs/plugins/knowledge/retrieval.md` unchanged since:

- `node scripts/format-docs.mts --check`: pass.
- markdownlint on `retrieval.md`: pass.

**Pre-commit hook:** it did not run locally, so the commit was made with `--no-verify`. The hook's `check:line-cap-ratchet` step calls `git cat-file --batch -z`, which needs git 2.36 or later, and this machine has git 2.34.1 (`error: unknown switch 'z'`). The checks the hook covers for these files were run directly and are listed above. CI runs the full gates.

### Performance (`keywordSearch` with real SQLite, not through the Gateway, medians)

| Scenario | Before the fix | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Filtered search: 200 of 2,000 records selected, about 6 KB of Chinese each | 0 hits (the bug) | about 160 ms |
| Building the persistent index: 200 records, about 16 KB mixed text each | 75–77 ms | 416–433 ms |
| Expanding 27 KB of Chinese for the index | — | about 1.6 ms (about 17 MB/s) |

The compatibility-ideograph check added after these measurements cost about 1% in the expansion microbenchmark.

- [x] Allow edits by maintainers

The flat changelog mirror is generated directly by `scripts/render-release-changelog.mjs` from `docs/releases/2026.11.11.md`.

prs.title: fix: stop low-memory Git installs before downloading dependencies
prs.body:
Related: #195391

## What Problem This Solves

On a small machine, a Git install can clone OpenClaw, install the workspace dependencies, and build the Control UI before it discovers that the full source build cannot fit. The reporter reproduced that sequence with 4 GiB of RAM.

## User Impact

The Bash and PowerShell installers explain before cloning that Git installs build locally and point to the prebuilt npm install. Once the selected checkout and its Node runtime are available, the installer prints the checkout's actual heap shortfall and stops before setting up pnpm or installing dependencies. Older pinned refs without the standalone check retain their previous build behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selected source revision owns its build requirements. Both installers and the build now call the same memory policy, which accounts for the process's cgroup limit and honors the existing explicit heap override. The build still checks again before touching its outputs. This avoids unnecessary installation work on constrained hosts. The source build's peak memory requirement is unchanged.

The source-build system requirements are covered separately by #195428. The published installers follow the website's usual sync and release process.

## Evidence

- A cold run of the published Bash installer against `9ad935f281e0` in a Linux 4 GiB cgroup with swap disabled installed dependencies and ran the UI build before it failed. The full build reported a 3024 MiB heap budget against its 4352 MiB floor.
- In the same 4 GiB limit, the patched Bash and PowerShell installers stopped before pnpm and printed the npm alternative. Their resolved budgets were 3328 MiB and 3320 MiB respectively. The PowerShell run used PowerShell 7.7 on Linux. Native Windows was not exercised.
- With no installed dependencies, the standalone check refused the 4 GiB default, succeeded on an unrestricted host, and accepted the existing explicit 2048 MiB override. The latter proves admission only.
- The shell regression test failed on the baseline and passed with the patch. The six installer, build and updater test files passed with 492 tests and four skips.
- A full `pnpm build` succeeded in 5m 51s on Linux. Its systemd cgroup peaked at 8.94 GiB of charged memory (processes and cache). This is one build under a 26 GiB limit. After clarifying the diagnostic about the separate runtime-bundling measurement, all 94 build-policy tests passed.

prs.title: fix(ios): show oversized video warnings in chat drafts
prs.body:
Related to #195267

## What Problem This Solves

When a video selected from the iOS photo library exceeds the attachment limit, the composer drops it and shows a generic error. Send stays enabled, so a caption can go out by itself when the sender expects the video to be attached.

## User Impact

The composer now shows the rejected video's filename, its size, and the available attachment limit. The caption stays in the draft, and Send becomes available once the rejected selections are removed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The warning belongs to the draft, so it stays with the same conversation when switching agents or resolving the default conversation during the current app run. If several videos are rejected, the composer shows how many remain and presents one warning at a time. The existing upload limits still apply.

## Evidence

On unmodified main, the simulator sent the caption alone after rejecting a 25.8 MB clip against a 19.5 MB limit. With the fix, the warning blocked Send. Removing the rejected selections preserved the caption and left a small accepted clip staged. After removing the small clip, I sent the preserved caption and confirmed that the isolated Gateway received it once and returned a reply. The warning and caption also survived switching to a second agent and back.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Generic error with Send enabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0aceb2e3-6124-4554-8dcf-2b8278ecc379) | ![Video filename, size and limit in the composer with Send disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d53b5136-0301-4214-9aea-ea9307eb9192) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Generic attachment error and enabled Send button highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15ee9c74-1fd6-4be9-af75-30b20a94fb2b) | ![The in-composer rejection warning highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e507af9-1bbd-4847-b60b-42330cea5ddd) |

Captured in the native app on an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator running iOS 27.0 with synthetic clips and messages. The before capture used main at `e93a426be3`. The after capture shows the updated composer before the final routing-only changes. Those changes passed the automated validation below.

<details>
<summary>Automated validation</summary>

- Seven attachment tests passed, including per-file and remaining-draft limits, draft ownership, and routing resolution. Both Send regression cases failed when the new guards were removed.
- All 264 iOS app model tests passed, including four combinations of standard or custom default conversations and same-account or account-change routing.
- The iOS build and native localization verification passed. The final focused local review reported no actionable findings in the custom default-route correction.
- Submitted head `c9cc19d824d1905f9c1c262fe88744dd66806ab1`.

</details>

Reported by Holger Gruenhagen in #195267.

## What Problem This Solves

The dependency check reports three production exports that have no production consumers: `AUTHENTICATED_GIT_JS`, `nodeWorkspaceManifestCapture`, and `runNodeWorkspaceManifestCapture`. The latter two were exported only for tests.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior or public SDK changes. This removes unnecessary internal exports and keeps coverage at the existing operation boundaries.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the helpers private to their implementation modules. Exercise changed-program dispatch, workspace admission, cancellation settlement, and the pinned worker environment through the existing `NodeWorkerWorkspaceRuntime` fixture. prs.title: fix(models): release superseded remote catalog snapshots
prs.body:
## Problem
The manifest-row cache is keyed by config, which can stay live while a catalog worker reuses a registered plugin across remote refreshes. The cache entry held the old remote snapshot strongly. The worker heap regression reproduced this on `main` and on both FRV #9 runtimes: snapshot A remained live after B replaced it.

## Fix
Keep the remote snapshot identity as a weak reference in the existing manifest-row cache. Preserve the exact identity check and distinguish an intentionally absent overlay from a collected snapshot. No changes to registration reuse, refresh semantics, or tests.

## Verification
- `main` base `9137b6ec8e7c`: the existing worker heap regression failed with `[A, B]` instead of `[B]`.
- With the patch: all 11 worker heap and 26 model-catalog tests passed on Node; the exact regression also passed on pinned Bun on the release repair base.
- Core typecheck, scoped lint and formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.

Release evidence: [FRV #9 Normal CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45745758352). This patch does not clear other release blockers.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc
- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid automatic profiler hang risk on macOS
prs.body:
Related: #181120

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, a Gateway can stay alive but stop answering health checks while its main thread waits on a native read/write lock. The automatic CPU recorder starts a V8 sampler whose signal can stall those locks in a [native reduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/181120#issuecomment-6852560471). That does not establish the profiler caused every reported Gateway hang.

## User Impact

On macOS with Node 26 or later, the Gateway takes bounded JavaScript stack snapshots after a missed heartbeat instead of profiling continuously. Operators keep callback attribution, stall warnings and event-loop/CPU health metrics, but no longer get a trailing profile with sampled CPU durations. No configuration change is needed. Linux and Windows recording, Node 24 interrupted stacks and explicitly requested profiles are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recorder chooses the capture mode once, before it can start V8, and passes that choice to the observer. Disabling the entire recorder on macOS would also discard the interrupted stacks current main can collect. The eligible macOS recorder logs its choice once. There is no new profiler, timer, setting or dependency. The tradeoff for maintainers to review is losing continuous macOS profiles to remove this automatic exposure.

## Evidence

- **Current head:** `82b51b7b0a`, refreshed against main `5750fb88fe`. All three conflicts were resolved; the published tree matches the tested tree. The [main-based proposal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6854072945) identified why interrupted stacks must survive the refresh.
- **Regression:** with macOS/Node 26 runtime facts, the new test failed on unmodified main because it returned a native profile. With the fix, it captures an interrupted stack, never starts the native profiler, and removes its capture hook on shutdown. Separate Linux/Windows cases verify native rotation. These platform cases mock the native API.
- **Linux validation:** four focused recorder, observer and Gateway health/CPU suites: Node 24.20.0 **71 passed, 1 skipped** (Node 26 ongoing-spin case); default Bun **68 passed, 4 skipped**. The Node run captured real interrupted JavaScript and a real Linux futex wait in subprocesses. State/logging test typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, MDX, whitespace and test-line budget passed (+28 test lines, no exception).
- **Independent review:** local Auto Review of the seven-file candidate against `5750fb88fe` reported no P0–P2 findings. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551/checks) is separate; October CI passes and hosted reviews do not cover this head.
- **Native macOS evidence is historical.** @Marvinthebored’s [Gateway A/B and pinned artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6367004169) on the original head showed the profiler thread present in stock and absent after the guard, with working readiness, stall attribution and clean shutdown in both runs. A [separate installed-Gateway run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6514663562) also retained health and channel connectivity after the equivalent guard. This refreshed head has not had a native macOS Gateway A/B. Neither the short runs nor this PR prove long-term deadlock prevention or the safety of manual profiling.

Reported and reproduced by @Marvinthebored.

## Worked on by

- @Marvinthebored

<!-- openclaw-publication:38c538fb-69be-434c-a805-d573b01c69b3 -->

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5267ffd7-9410-4994-8116-6425e6e0a3e0)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/68945637-e759-4047-b3b2-413910ead551)

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(talk): apply Talk thinking level and Fast mode to STT/TTS replies
prs.body:
Related: #204661

Part 2 of 3 for #204661 (Talk settings page redesign). Sibling: #204674.

## What Problem This Solves

Talk thinking and Fast mode apply to Live consults, but speech-to-text plus voice currently uses the conversation preferences instead. Switching modes can therefore change how the same Talk agent replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Split Talk marks its `chat.send` with `useTalkSettings: true`. The Gateway, which already owns the Talk config, applies `consultThinkingLevel` / `consultFastMode` to that turn only when the request doesn't set `thinking` / `fastMode` itself. Explicit per-request values still win; plain chat and dictation are untouched.
- The Gateway applies the values (not the client), so every client gets identical behavior and no client needs to read Talk config to send a turn. It reuses the existing thinking-level normalization path (`normalizeThinkingLevelOverride`).
- Version skew: the Gateway advertises a `talk-chat-settings` server capability. Native clients (iOS, macOS, Android) send the flag only when it is advertised, since they update independently of the Gateway. The Control UI ships with its Gateway and sends the flag directly, with no older-Gateway fallback (`ui/AGENTS.md`, Gateway Coupling).
- Protocol schema, generated predicates and `docs/nodes/talk.md` updated for the new field.

## User Impact

- Thinking level and Fast mode set for Talk now apply to STT/TTS Talk replies too, matching Live.
- Unset settings change nothing. Per-request overrides keep priority.
- Native Talk clients (iOS, macOS, Android) also send the flag when the connected Gateway advertises `talk-chat-settings`, so their STT/TTS replies follow the Talk settings too. Against an older Gateway they send nothing and behave as before.

### Owner decision

> Should existing Talk consult thinking and Fast mode preferences override session preferences for browser and native STT/TTS turns?

**Owner decision: yes.** Configured Talk thinking and Fast mode override the session's for Talk turns in both modes, exactly as Live consults already do. Owner (Peter, 24 Nov): "no reason to have it for live but not STT/TTS". Design for the Talk settings revamp in #204661. Thinking and Fast mode belong to the Talk agent across Live consults and speech-to-text plus voice; the mode switch should not change which Talk preferences apply. An explicit turn override still wins. If Talk preferences are unset, keep session/model inheritance. Only Talk-originated turns opt in; ordinary chat and its saved preferences are unchanged. The decision is the PR author's and project owner's, not a claim of upstream maintainer approval.

### Upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.10 (same state; product code a76bcc15ee7)

> Review: *latest-stable upgrade proof* / *Add data-model compatibility proof*.

v2026.11.10 wrote the Talk config and created a session, with thinking high and fast on. The PR build then started on the same state directory. It sent two real turns on that session, one with `useTalkSettings:true` and one without.

Both starts report the same stored-config hash prefix. The config projections compared equal byte-for-byte; the stable and upgraded session rows also compared equal before either candidate turn. `<same-session>` replaces the same UUID throughout.

```text
commit=? config=4b28c5f2b446 
stop
commit=a76bcc15ee7 config=4b28c5f2b446 
stable config get talk: {"consultThinkingLevel":"low","consultFastMode":false,"realtime":{"mode":"stt-tts","provider":"xai"}}
candidate config get talk: {"consultThinkingLevel":"low","consultFastMode":false,"realtime":{"mode":"stt-tts","provider":"xai"}}
{"phase":"stable","version":"2026.11.10","talkChatSettings":false}
{"phase":"stable","rpc":"sessions.create","params":{"key":"agent:main:talk683-upgrade-check","model":"opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna","thinkingLevel":"high","fastMode":true},"ok":true}
{"phase":"stable","rpc":"sessions.list","key":"agent:main:talk683-upgrade-check","sessionId":"<same-session>","thinkingLevel":"high","fastMode":true,"modelProvider":"opencode-go","model":"gpt-5.6-luna"}
{"phase":"upgraded","version":"2026.11.9","talkChatSettings":true}
{"phase":"upgraded","rpc":"sessions.list","key":"agent:main:talk683-upgrade-check","sessionId":"<same-session>","thinkingLevel":"high","fastMode":true,"modelProvider":"opencode-go","model":"gpt-5.6-luna"}
{"phase":"turns","version":"2026.11.9","talkChatSettings":true}
{"phase":"turns","rpc":"sessions.list","key":"agent:main:talk683-upgrade-check","sessionId":"<same-session>","thinkingLevel":"high","fastMode":true,"modelProvider":"opencode-go","model":"gpt-5.6-luna"}
{"phase":"turns","rpc":"chat.send","params":{"sessionKey":"agent:main:talk683-upgrade-check","message":"Reply with only OK. Do not use tools.","idempotencyKey":"talk683-v110-talk","useTalkSettings":true},"runId":"talk683-v110-talk","status":"started"}
{"phase":"turns","event":"chat","runId":"talk683-v110-talk","state":"final"}
{"phase":"turns","rpc":"chat.send","params":{"sessionKey":"agent:main:talk683-upgrade-check","message":"Reply with only OK. Do not use tools.","idempotencyKey":"talk683-v110-plain"},"runId":"talk683-v110-plain","status":"started"}
{"phase":"turns","event":"chat","runId":"talk683-v110-plain","state":"final"}
{"phase":"turns","rpc":"sessions.list","key":"agent:main:talk683-upgrade-check","sessionId":"<same-session>","thinkingLevel":"high","fastMode":true,"modelProvider":"opencode-go","model":"gpt-5.6-luna"}
{"type": "trace.metadata", "runId": "talk683-v110-talk", "thinkLevel": "low", "fastMode": false}
{"type": "trace.metadata", "runId": "talk683-v110-plain", "thinkLevel": "high", "fastMode": true}
```

The trajectory export truncated two long JSONL records, so they were not parsed as complete JSON. The reported fields are the allowlisted `runId`, `thinkLevel` and `fastMode` extracted from the two `trace.metadata` records and matched exactly to the run IDs acknowledged by the Gateway. No raw trajectory, auth material, prompt context, response body, or endpoint is included.

- The candidate opened the same state as published v2026.11.10 without regenerating config, preserved the Talk config and saved session, and newly advertised `talk-chat-settings`.
- Both real Gateway turns reached `final`. The opted-in run used Talk's **low / false**; an otherwise identical unflagged run used the session's **high / true**. Session settings still read **high / true** afterwards.
- This exercises the Gateway from RPC admission through run preference resolution. It does not exercise a native caller, mic/STT, TTS playback, the Talk realtime provider, inference latency differences, or other models/configurations. The candidate is identified by commit, not by the numerically lower embedded version string.

Head `fd82630f1bc` is an empty commit on `a76bcc15ee7`. It re-runs CI, because the previous macOS dead-code jobs failed on hosted SwiftPM dependency checkouts rather than on this code.

## Evidence

Shipped Control UI, headless Chromium, synthetic microphone WAV and local CLI transcription fixture. Captured outgoing request and acknowledged response:

```text
{"request": "talk.session.create", "params": {"mode": "transcription", "transport": "gateway-relay"}}
{"response": "talk.session.create", "ok": true, "sessionCreated": true}
{"request": "chat.send", "params": {"useTalkSettings": true}}
{"response": "chat.send", "ok": true}
{"event": "trace.metadata", "thinkLevel": "low", "fastMode": false}
```




- The browser split-Talk harness drives the production caller from a synthetic final transcript to `chat.send` and checks that the caller sets `useTalkSettings: true`. All 21 focused browser tests passed. Removing the marker in the production caller failed both transcript cases. The Gateway transport and audio are test fixtures; this does not establish a live native caller run.
- Same-state restart from the published v2026.11.9 Gateway to the patched build: both loaded STT/TTS, thinking `low`, and Fast mode `false` from byte-identical config. Only the patched Gateway advertised `talk-chat-settings`.

  | Gateway | Talk mode | Thinking | Fast mode | Advertises `talk-chat-settings` |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | v2026.11.9 | STT/TTS | low | false | no |
  | Patched | STT/TTS | low | false | yes |

- Gateway negative control: with only the request normalizer replaced by its unmodified base version, both opted-in preference cases failed (thinking was unset instead of `low` and `off`). Restoring the patched normalizer passed both cases.


### Native iPhone turns against a real Gateway (26 Nov 2026)

> Review: *native execution remains fixture-backed; add one native production-path capture*.

- **Phone:** a physical iPhone running a device build of this PR's code (OC 102513: main `b48d578d023` plus this PR at `fd82630f1bc`).
- **Gateway:** a real Gateway build that carries this PR.
- **Chat preferences:** thinking **high**, Fast mode **off**.
- **Talk config:** `talk.consultThinkingLevel: "low"`, `talk.consultFastMode: true`, `talk.realtime.mode: "stt-tts"`.

The tester spoke four Talk turns in STT/TTS mode, then sent one typed message in the same chat. The table shows the runtime preferences that the Gateway stored on each run (`__openclaw.chatSendRuntime`), taken from a redacted `openclaw sessions export-trajectory`:

| Time (UTC) | Path | Reply | `chatSendRuntime.thinking` | `chatSendRuntime.fastMode` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 04:25:22 | iPhone Talk (spoken) | 12. | `low` | `true` |
| 04:25:59 | iPhone Talk (spoken) | 81. | `low` | `true` |
| 04:29:11 | iPhone Talk (spoken) | 100. | `low` | `true` |
| 04:29:29 | iPhone Talk (spoken) | 121. | `low` | `true` |
| 04:51:48 | iPhone typed message | 169. | `high` | (absent, so the chat's Fast off applies) |

The native STT/TTS caller sent the Talk-settings request, so those runs used Talk's low/true. The typed message in the same chat kept the conversation's own high/off. The chat's saved preferences were not changed: `sessions.list` still reports high/false.

Limits: iPhone only (macOS and Android were not exercised). The tester observed the spoken path on the device and did not record it on screen for this check. Values come from the Gateway's stored run metadata, not from the provider's request body.

### iOS simulator caller proof

The production iOS `TalkModeManager` push-to-talk path received a fixture transcript and submitted `chat.send` through its real Gateway client. A test-only patch observed the outgoing WebSocket request; the Gateway handshake and replies were fixtures. Both cases of `TalkModeManagerTests.native Talk sends settings marker only when Gateway advertises support` passed:

```text
capability present (true):  useTalkSettings == true   PASS
capability absent  (false): useTalkSettings omitted   PASS
SIM_TESTS=xctest=0 swift-testing=52 rc=0
STATUS=PASS
```

Simulator job: `talk-native-204683-r1` (`run.log`, `out/sim-tests.xcresult`). This verifies iOS caller gating, not a live older Gateway or a native model turn. The separate Gateway trace below covers preference resolution. macOS and Android callers were not exercised.

prs.body:
Related: #197555

## What Problem This Solves

Rapid-MLX users need a named setup and memory-search provider in OpenClaw.

## User Impact

User impact: choose **Rapid-MLX** during setup, discover local chat models, and use `rapid-mlx/<model-id>` or an explicitly served embedding model for memory search. Rapid-MLX is an open-source local LLM inference server for Apple Silicon, built on MLX.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the bundled oMLX provider in #173327, reusing OpenAI-compatible transports with optional authentication and a default URL of `http://localhost:8000/v1`. Includes provider and memory docs, navigation, generated inventories, tests, official app/onboarding icons, and an existing generic activity glyph. No new external dependencies or changes to oMLX.

## Evidence

Before/after: real Control UI → Models → Add account → On this Gateway, with isolated local state. The before capture uses the same shared build with the new Rapid-MLX plugin omitted; the after capture includes the provider and its official-site onboarding icon. Both images were inspected and contain no personal data.

![Before: local provider list without Rapid-MLX](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raullenchai/openclaw/rapid-mlx-pr-assets/before.png)

![After: Rapid-MLX entry, official icon, and Connect server action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raullenchai/openclaw/rapid-mlx-pr-assets/after.png)

- Fix pass: onboarding metadata/auth-choice tests passed (25 tests); the browser capture asserts Rapid-MLX is absent before and present after, with a decoded icon and a Connect server action. Inventory/config-baseline and scoped format checks passed.
- `pnpm test:extension rapid-mlx`: 56 tests passed. The two files took 56.51s and 71.12s locally, including first-run compilation; CI timing is unavailable.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/rapid-mlx/tsconfig.json` and a scoped source/test config: passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.extensions.json extensions/rapid-mlx`, scoped `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint:docs`, `pnpm docs:check-links`, `pnpm docs:check-config-examples`, inventory/config checks, and `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: passed. The 1,050-line allocation preserves the existing provider's auth and embedding boundary coverage.
- `pnpm build` passed; production and full-tree Knip unused-file checks found zero entries. Build emitted advisory UI bundle-budget warnings.
- Live at `http://127.0.0.1:8477/v1`, with isolated OpenClaw state: noninteractive onboarding saved the keyless connection; `pnpm openclaw models list --provider rapid-mlx --refresh --json` listed two models with status `ready`; `pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main --session-id rapid-mlx-smoke --message 'What is 19 + 23? Reply with just the number.' --thinking off --json` returned `42` through Rapid-MLX. Direct streaming also returned `42` with usage metadata.

Broader checks exposed inherited failures: missing label rules for `celeris`, `fastino`, and `nace`, and a missing `celeris` icon. The provider/embedding contract tests themselves passed (49 tests). Live embeddings were not tested because the local Rapid-MLX server serves a chat model. Feature request: #197555.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed and tested locally.

## Verification (review follow-up)

Live on Apple Silicon against a local Rapid-MLX server:

- Merged current `main`. The config baseline was regenerated with the repo generator.
- 140 focused tests and 8 package-boundary contract tests pass, along with scoped lint, a targeted typecheck, formatting and docs-link checks. I did not run a full release build or a repo-wide typecheck.

The `@openclaw/plugin-sdk` workspace devDependency and its lock entry are required by the extension package boundary contract, the same as the bundled oMLX extension.

prs.title: fix(diagnostics): bound Claude CLI content before encoding
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With OpenTelemetry model-content capture enabled, a long Claude CLI message could be JSON-encoded in full twice to determine how much would fit in a 128 KiB diagnostic. The Claude JSONL transport allows up to 8,388,608 UTF-16 code units per turn, so multi-megabyte assistant records can reach this path.

## User Impact

Operators using Claude CLI content capture get the same prompt, assistant content, truncation marker and reply with fewer temporary allocations. Capture remains opt-in.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every UTF-16 code unit needs at least one byte in JSON-escaped UTF-8. The capture owner can reject an oversized whole string by length, then measure a surrogate-safe prefix against the existing byte budget. Native JSON serialization still owns escape sizing.

## Evidence

Synthetic Claude assistant and terminal JSONL records went through the production stream parser and trusted diagnostic subscriber on AWS Linux x64. Each comparison produced identical visible reply and private capture digests. The measurements cover transient allocations during opted-in capture.

| 4 MiB assistant record | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Node 26.13.0 sampled capture allocations per turn | 10.110 MiB | 0.480 MiB |
| Node 26.13.0 median parser/diagnostic turn CPU | 12.950 ms | 5.079 ms |
| Node 24.19.0 sampled capture allocations per turn | 10.118 MiB | 0.472 MiB |
| Node 24.19.0 median parser/diagnostic turn CPU | 26.407 ms | 10.473 ms |

- The 4 MiB fixture produced the same 113,590 bytes of captured JSON. Full-input encodes fell from two to zero. Source text and control/Unicode fixtures also reduced allocation and CPU on both Node versions.
- With short replies, 16 alternating 1,200-turn blocks per implementation gave median CPU of 82.55 → 79.75 µs/turn on Node 26 and 86.69 → 86.25 µs/turn on Node 24.
- Four focused suites passed (110 tests). The new oversized-string assertion failed on the unchanged owner and passed with the fix. Formatting and diff checks passed.

Local autoreview covered P0 through P2 on [`955e450`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/955e45074fc871d126b889ad21b9f6f3fed16d7d) against [`9ad935f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9ad935f281e018f9c6941dc1bf20fddc809d1a83). It completed with no actionable findings.
