prs.title: fix: keep the full search query when testing a provider
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Settings → Search, pasting a valid query with supplementary Unicode characters could silently discard its final words. An administrator could then see “Search succeeded” for a different query. In a Japanese railway-guide search, the discarded text was `只見線`, the name of the railway line.

## User Impact

A query of up to 500 Unicode code points can be submitted in full. If a paste exceeds that limit, the field keeps the entire draft and explains how to shorten it. Editing the draft back to the limit enables the test again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Search field and its submit actions counted UTF-16 units. The existing Gateway request schema counts Unicode code points. The change applies that bound in Settings and reports excess input before sending. It preserves the named provider test introduced by @steipete and the IME confirmation behavior fixed by @etzelm. [Original Search settings feature](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154135) · [IME confirmation fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177545)

## Evidence

| Chromium action | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paste a multilingual query ending in `The line was 只見線`, then click Test (499 code points, 504 UTF-16 units) | Field and submitted query ended in `The line was`. Status read “Search succeeded”. | Field, request and provider adapter retained the full ending. |
| Paste 499 ASCII characters followed by `𠮷`, then press Enter | The final character was dropped. | All 500 code points were submitted. |
| Paste 501 ASCII characters and use click or Enter | Each action sent the clipped 500. | The draft retained all 501, the length warning appeared and both actions sent zero requests. Removing the last character and pressing Enter sent the corrected 500 once. |

The browser ran the compiled Settings page against the registered Gateway handler with an inert search provider. A composing Enter sent zero requests, and the next deliberate Enter sent the committed `東京` once. Live provider results and native platform IMEs were outside this test.

The new mounted regression failed on the parent when the field lost text. All 37 Search browser tests passed on the patch in Chromium. Scoped Oxlint, formatting and keyless Control UI i18n verification passed.

### Hosted verification

The protected Chromium job passed all 37 Search page cases, including the 500-code-point boundary and composing Enter. The mounted tests inspect the request after an operator paste, correction, or submit. Two separate jobs in the full dispatch failed. The dependency check reported 12 distinct path/symbol pairs across eight parent-identical files. The other failure was the chat position rail’s focused-run retargeting assertion. The Search suite passed in that shard. [Protected Chromium](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45734256784/job/139624177856) · [Dependency report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45734194678/job/139623986691) · [UI shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45734194678/job/139623986803)

### Shipped Control UI verification

Chromium exercised the compiled Settings → Search page on main `9137b6ec8e7c` and PR head `ed8bb3127e15` with the same synthetic Gateway and search provider. The valid paste contained 499 Unicode code points. Main dropped the final station name, 只見線. The PR sent the complete query once. A separate 501-character paste was clipped and sent on main. The PR kept all 501 characters visible, displayed the limit and sent zero requests after Enter.

#### Clean comparisons

![Valid paste before and after, showing the station name at the end of the PR query](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64d97a2b-c1e2-4941-b2b9-d901f9c016f0)

![Over-limit paste before and after, showing the complete draft and disabled submit action on the PR](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2a01e20-1177-44e0-acd6-2944746d0c01)

#### Annotated comparisons

![The query ending on main and the complete Japanese line name on the PR are highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fa47170-ba30-430d-b8bb-e444bbfa9666)

![Main submitted a shortened draft and the PR displayed the 500-character warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7125c7dc-c81a-476a-b35b-e08b3a141a1f)

prs.title: test(auto-reply): pin queued channel restart and collected sender authority (#203464, #203463)
prs.body:
## Problem

Two issues reported possible admission gaps from static reads of `main`:

- #203464: a queued channel message could be silently lost after a Gateway restart, because native channel staging saves no operator recovery source and startup replay cancels such a row as `restart-unrecoverable`.
- #203463: a collected group batch could run with the last sender's owner rights when one message has no channel admission evidence (`resolveCollectedRun` in `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/drain.ts` returns the source run for unknown evidence).

Neither has a regression test for the reported scenario.

## Change

Test-only. Production code is unchanged (+0/−0).

1. `dispatch-from-config.pending-restart.test.ts`: a Discord message is staged by a native-shaped recorder (channel `observation` sender, channel source turn key, no operator source). The test runs Gateway shutdown preservation, then the real startup replay `continueSessionQueuedInputs`. The replay ends the row as `restart-unrecoverable` (as the issue says). Then the durable ingress redelivers the same message under a fresh run id: the recorder reclaims the cancelled row (`reclaimCancelledSourceTurn`, `isRetryableSessionPendingInputEndCause`), `dispatchReplyFromConfig` runs it through normal reply admission, and the transcript holds the message exactly once.
2. `queue.collect-sender-authority.test.ts` (new file; `queue.collect.test.ts` is at its line cap): in one group (collect mode, identity audit on), a guest message without admission evidence is queued, then an owner message with evidence. The guest text never runs in the owner's batch and never runs with `senderIsOwner: true`.

## Why no fix

- #203464: Discord, Telegram and the other durable-ingress channels keep the message in ingress custody until turn adoption (`docs/concepts/queue.md`, "Channel messages retained by durable ingress remain retryable…"; `ingress-monitor.test.ts` "defers a claimed event across restart drain…"). The Gateway replay refusal is not the end of the message: the redelivery reclaims the row (since #193602 and #200533, both before the issue). No OA2 PR changed this; the issue's chain stopped at the Gateway replay and missed the ingress redelivery.
- #203463: the collect storage key (`resolveFollowupAuthorizationKey`, `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/delivery-context.ts`) includes the requester principal, `senderId`, `senderE164` and `senderIsOwner` (since #122863 / #152460). An owner and a non-owner never share a collected claim, so the "return source" branch only sees items with the same sender and owner bit. Making that branch strip authority would remove owner tools from a single owner's batch when identity audit is off (no evidence is minted then), which is a UX regression with no security gain.

## Evidence

- Both tests pass on `main` `e4517b0ef2f4`.
- Red when the guarding code is removed (local mutation, reverted):
  - `resolveFollowupAuthorizationKey` returning a constant → #203463 test fails: `expected '[Queued messages while agent was busy…' not to contain 'owner message'`.
  - `isRetryableSessionPendingInputEndCause` without `restart-unrecoverable` → #203464 test fails: `Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input` (the redelivered message would be refused).
- One-admission E2E on the exact head `aa63024ad82d`: Q, R, S pass (`verdict.json` + `results.jsonl`: https://gist.github.com/obviyus/9dfe6c3b490daebc5442b456a46e10d1).

Closes #203463
Closes #203464

prs.title: fix(imessage): group activation mode now controls replies
prs.body:
Related: #50490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes iMessage groups continuing to use static `requireMention` after an owner runs `/activation mention` or `/activation always`. The command could report success and persist the new mode while iMessage ingress ignored it.

## User Impact

iMessage group owners can change reply behavior with `/activation mention` and `/activation always` without editing channel config, matching Telegram and WhatsApp.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage ingress gate resolved `requireMention` only from channel config. It now reads `groupActivation` from the exact routed session and uses a valid persisted mode as the per-group override.

If the session read fails or contains no valid activation mode, iMessage preserves the existing configured `requireMention` policy. This change does not introduce a new fail-closed fallback contract. Explicit bot-thread mention policy and authorized control-command admission remain unchanged.

## Evidence (exact head)

- Exact signed head: `21df6ff29c9610a1e34337fabbc1f26bcbafc9ff`
- Frozen base: `466a4b6f5073b5fe83b6a0b479a6dfc8392c82e4`
- Clean merge tree: `065c19a15148006d3d01b2e6fc1f68a53be0b592`
- Focused proof: `pnpm test extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.activation.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session.activation.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **24/24 passing** across three shards.
- Behavior regression: the exact six-case iMessage test is **6/6 green** on this head and **2/6 red** on the frozen base. The base failures are the missing persisted `mention` and `always` overrides; both session-read-failure fallback cases pass on base and head.
- Static proof: `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, touched-file `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Latest-stable compatibility: `v2026.11.3` (`847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`) already stores `groupActivation` and `groupActivationNeedsSystemIntro`; this branch changes no session schema or migration.
- Canonical pre-PR receipt ran on this exact head for 404 seconds. Every branch-relevant gate passed, including SQLite worker/dialect ratchets, extension typechecks/lint, plugin boundaries, database-first guards, and import cycles. Its only failure was the repository-wide dead-export scan; the exact same three untouched exports fail on the frozen base.
- The iMessage regression test exercises the production ingress decision through the injected session runtime and mock Gateway admission. It does **not** claim live Apple Messages transport proof.
- Live Messages proof remains externally blocked because the isolated macOS pilot is not signed into Messages. No production Gateway, Messages account, or channel state was changed for this repair.

Hosted CI and maintainer review on this exact head remain authoritative.

prs.title: fix(exec): keep owner memory trusted after background commands finish
prs.body:
﻿Fixes #204767

## What Problem This Solves
When a Gateway owner’s background command finishes and wakes their WebChat session, the wake can lose the owner decision. A tracked edit to `MEMORY.md` then becomes untrusted and drops out of automatic context.

## User Impact
An untainted completion in the same owner session keeps ordinary agent provenance. Guest, tainted, and cross-session cases still produce untrusted provenance. Existing quarantined files are not reclassified.

## Why This Change Was Made
Capture operator-owner continuation only when the caller, the process, and the wake target share the same agent session. Build the exec event context through the existing owner-binding path without authorizing the completion text as a command.

## Evidence
- On Linux, the regression launches a real background Node process, checks that its output reaches a normally admitted completion, passes the runtime owner bit to the real tracked write tool, and reads the saved `MEMORY.md` provenance. On pre-fix `a298c5a19cb6` the owner and tainted-owner cases failed because runtime ownership was false; the clean owner write was untrusted. With the fix, the clean owner is owner/`agent`; tainted owner is owner/`untrusted`; guest and cross-session are non-owner/`untrusted`.
- `pnpm test src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.owner-continuation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 4 passed. The requester, storage-failure, background-followup, and session-event handoff suites also passed while validating the same production change. Focused lint, format, and agent-tool typecheck passed.
- Model inference was stubbed at its boundary. A live model-driven Control UI run was not performed.

## Real behavior proof

[Real-model Gateway proof and redacted logs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204785#issuecomment-7182969039). Three disposable Gateway runs used Qwen3-1.7B via loopback llama.cpp with no provider API key. The model generated the native tool calls and arguments for background `exec` and the tracked `MEMORY.md` write on the automatic wake. The adapter required the one relevant offered tool on action steps; it did not supply or rewrite arguments or replies. The network-tainted wake called `web_fetch` first and got an HTTP 200 result marked untrusted.

| Build and case | Hash-matched `MEMORY.md` provenance | Badge in actual outgoing system prompt after `/new` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base `c734b2de`, clean | `untrusted` | No |
| Head `f286bd3a`, clean | `agent` | Yes |
| Head `f286bd3a`, network-tainted | `untrusted` | No |

In all three runs, the persisted wake transcript remained `internal_system` with `senderIsOwner=false` (not human authorship). prs.title: fix: return a receipt when steering a busy Claude CLI turn
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent used `sessions_send` with a zero-second wait to steer a busy Claude CLI turn, the sender could time out after 30 seconds even though the child received the message. Retrying based on that error could send the same guidance twice.

## User Impact

The sender now gets `status: "submitted"` and `consumption: "unconfirmed"` after the transport write succeeds. That confirms the write, **not** that the CLI queued or consumed the message. The sender can check the pending input by `runId` and find the original forwarded message by `messageId` once the receiver records it, without sending it again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The receiving turn reserves the input in its existing pending-input store before writing to the CLI. A successful write releases sender ordering; native start or completion still controls when the input enters the transcript. An explicit refusal before start cancels the pending input; losing the connection leaves consumption unknown. Neither case starts a fallback turn. No new storage schema, polling service, configuration, or migration is needed. Positive waits and ordinary user messages keep their existing paths.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the isolated zero-wait steering regression returned `error` after about 32 seconds instead of a submission receipt.
- On the fix, a real `sessions_send` call drove the Claude CLI plugin against an isolated protocol subprocess. The tool returned before native start. With start held for a further 31 seconds, `chat.history` reported the original run as pending and `chat.message.get` found no transcript entry yet. After release, the same message ID returned the original text and forwarding provenance.
- Separate cases exercised explicit refusal and subprocess exit after the write. The former recorded cancellation, the latter interruption; neither dispatched another agent turn. All three integration cases passed.
- 102 existing tests across five files passed, including positive waits, sender identity checks, user steering, and the Claude CLI transport. Focused type, lint and formatting checks passed. The independent diff review had no actionable P0–P2 findings. The proof used an isolated CLI protocol fixture, not a hosted model or production Gateway. Startup replay eligibility was inspected, not exercised across a Gateway restart.

prs.title: fix: keep Doctor from restarting the Gateway in the middle of a package update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` refuses to repair while an update is in progress, but it only checked for one when the Gateway service was running. A package update stops the Gateway first, then replaces the installed files. A `doctor --fix` started from another shell during that window saw a stopped service, skipped the check, repaired state, and could start the Gateway again on a half-replaced install.

The sequence:

1. `openclaw update` stops the Gateway service while holding the service operation lock, then releases the lock.
2. It replaces the installed package tree, runs its own Doctor pass, and restarts the Gateway. None of this holds the service lock.
3. A stopped service inspects as offline (systemd: inactive; launchd: not loaded). Doctor built its update-ledger admission only when the service was not offline, so it never read the running update record.
4. Doctor repaired state and restored the owned service it found stopped, starting the Gateway while the update still owned it.

## User Impact

- While an update is running, `openclaw doctor --fix` from another shell now refuses with the update's run ID, driver PID and host, and leaves state and the stopped Gateway alone. The update finishes and restarts the Gateway itself.
- Recovery still works. If the recorded update driver is dead or the run was abandoned, Doctor repairs a stopped Gateway as before. A run owned by another host or a renamed machine is refused with the existing guidance to use `openclaw update repair`, the same refusal a running Gateway already got.
- The updater's own Doctor child still continues under its run: it inherits the run ID and passes the existing ancestry check.

No config, schema, stored field or update-driver change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor already owns this decision through `resolveDoctorUpdateAdmission`, which uses the same driver-admission rules as `openclaw update repair` (continuation, recovery after driver death or abandonment, refusal of a live foreign driver). The `offline !== true` condition was carried over from the older parent-activation refusal, where an offline service meant there was nothing to stop. For admission, an offline service says nothing about whether an update owns it. The fix removes that condition, so Doctor reads the ledger for every installed service. Services that inspect as absent keep their current behavior.

## Evidence

Evidence for this draft is still being collected. See the sections below.

### Process-level tests (`src/commands/doctor-maintenance.stopped-systemd.test.ts`)

These tests run `runDoctorHealthFlow` with a real legacy v1 state database, a real update-ledger row and a stopped systemd user service:

- `leaves state and the stopped Gateway alone while an update run is active`: the recorded driver is the live test process. On the base production code (`973e0ba78f7`) it fails: Doctor migrated the database (`Saved pre-migration SQLite backup: ...`) and returned no refusal. With the fix it passes: Doctor refuses with the run ID, `user_version` stays 1, and the service is never started, restarted or installed.
- `repairs state beside the stopped Gateway when the recorded update driver is dead` (new, guards against overreach): the row records this PID with a different start identity, which proves the driver exited. Doctor completes and migrates the database. This passes on base and on the fix. It confirms the fix still lets a dead driver's row through.

### Checks on the merged head

- Focused Doctor maintenance files (stopped-systemd, admission-activation, admission-warm, finish-revalidation, service-inspection, serving-owner, installation, settlement, service-identity): 9 files, 141 passed, 1 skipped. The skip is an existing skip in `installation.test.ts`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxfmt, oxlint, `git diff --check`: pass.
- Session identity ratchet: OK.
- Not run, out of scope: the update-restart vm fixture and eager-import closure tests. No module or import under `src/cli/update-cli` or `src/infra/package-update-*` changed.

### Not measured

macOS launchd and Windows Scheduled Task were not exercised. The changed condition does not depend on the platform; each platform only decides what counts as offline.

prs.title: fix: keep cancelled requests out of agent history previews
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If you stop a queued request, an agent that later reads the session history can still see the original request as a user message, along with its attachments. The agent can mistake that cancelled request for work you still want done.

## User Impact

The agent can see which pending input was cancelled, when it was accepted, and why it ended if the cause is known. It can no longer recover its text, file paths, or attachment references from that entry. You can still inspect visible cancelled messages in the Control UI. Queued and interrupted previews are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway serves human chat history as well as agent tools. Only the agent's `sessions_history` projection clears the cancelled message, before previewing content or media. The row and its pagination cursor stay in place. Nothing changes how Stop works, how long inputs are kept, or when queued work runs.

## Evidence

- Called the real `sessions_history` tool with a synthetic Gateway response and an anchored, paginated read. On `9ad935f281e0` it returned the cancelled instruction, a file path, and a media reference as a user message. With the fix the same row has `message: null` and `endCause: "user-stop"`. The anchor, cursor, queued media, and interrupted text are preserved without truncation.
- The human-facing `chat.history` RPC test still returned the original visible cancelled text before dismissal. All 51 focused tests passed (history tool, anchor and byte budgets, Gateway handler, and prompt-prefix stability). Targeted typecheck, lint, and formatting passed.
- Local autoreview covered the complete `9ad935f281e0` → `4bc4e2355f0c` patch at P0–P2 and found no actionable issues. The proof checks what the tool returns, not a live model's next action; no live model or browser E2E was run.

prs.title: fix(feishu): honor explicit filename override for media uploads
prs.body:
Fixes #205246

## Problem

Sending a local file through the `message` tool with an explicit `filename` override could deliver the attachment under the basename of the `media` path instead of the requested name:

```json
{ "action": "send", "media": "/tmp/repro/report_en.pdf", "filename": "季度报告.pdf", "forceDocument": true }
```

Expected: the recipient sees `季度报告.pdf`. Reported actual behaviour: the recipient sees `report_en.pdf`, and server-side evidence in #205246 (reading `file_name` back via `GET /open-apis/im/v1/messages`) showed the override never reached `im.file.create` on the paths below. A control send whose file is actually named in Chinese, with no `filename`, was delivered correctly — so this is specific to the override, not to non-ASCII names.

## What has changed since the report

Current `main` has since landed the direct-path plumbing: `FeishuOutboundSendMedia` now lives in `extensions/feishu/src/outbound-types.ts` with a `filename` field, `channel.ts` puts `filename: normalizeOptionalString(ctx.params.filename)` into the outbound context, and `sendMedia` forwards `fileName: ctx.filename` to `sendMediaFeishu`. That covers a top-level `filename` on the direct send path only. This PR is rebased on current `main` and closes the remaining gaps, aligning with that new `filename` contract instead of duplicating it.

## Remaining gaps this PR closes

1. **Attachment-carried names were still dropped.** Core places the message tool's `filename` into `payload.attachments[].name`, but the Feishu outbound paths only forwarded media URL strings (`resolvePayloadMediaUrls` returns plain strings), discarding `attachments[].name`. This affected `sendMedia`, the `sendPayload` card path, the fallback payload path, and the TTS-supplement path.
2. **The reply-dispatcher path dropped it too.** Media sent as an agent reply never resolved a name from `payload.attachments`.
3. **The `fileName` alias and attachment `name`/`filename` on the direct action were not read.** `channel.ts` only read the top-level `filename` param; an attachment's own name never reached `sendMedia`, and the presentation-fallback payload carried no named attachment.

`sendMediaFeishu` in `extensions/feishu/src/media.ts` already accepts `fileName` and uploads it as `file_name` to `client.im.file.create` (`fileName ?? media.fileName ?? "file"`); the fix is plumbing inside the Feishu plugin, with no core changes.

## Changes

- **Attachment names are resolved through the SDK's owner.** All Feishu payload paths now pair media with attachment names via `collectReplyMediaEntries` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound` — the same pairing the SDK itself uses — instead of resolving names from flattened URL lists. The earlier revision of this PR carried a plugin-local resolver (`media-attachment-name.ts`); it has been removed entirely, along with its `media.ts` re-export, because positional/reference pairing is the SDK helper's job.
- `extensions/feishu/src/outbound.ts`: the `sendPayload` card path, the fallback payload path (`sendFeishuFallbackPayload`), and the TTS-supplement path resolve each media entry's name through `collectReplyMediaEntries` and pass it to `sendMediaFeishu`; `sendMedia` keeps the explicit context `filename` first, then the paired attachment name.
- `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts`: the agent-reply media path pairs entries through `collectReplyMediaEntries` **before** any flattening to URL strings, so positional names (attachments that carry only a `name`, no path) survive to the upload.
- `extensions/feishu/src/channel.ts`: the direct `send` / `thread-reply` action reads `filename` / `fileName` (or the first attachment's `name` / `filename`) and passes it to `sendMedia` as `filename`, and into the presentation-fallback payload as `attachments: [{ path, name }]`.
- Tests: regression coverage in `outbound.test.ts` and `reply-dispatcher.test.ts` for the review's two counterexamples — a referenced name that belongs only to the second file, and positional names with no path references — across the card, fallback, and reply paths. Low-value uploader cases flagged in review were removed.

## Real behavior proof (live Feishu tenant)

Verified against a real Feishu tenant with a dedicated self-built app, a Gateway built from this branch, and two test PDFs (`a.pdf`, `b.pdf`). Every delivered file was read back from Feishu's servers with `GET /open-apis/im/v1/messages/{message_id}`; the `file_name` values below are the server-side records.

| Case | Expected `file_name` | Server-recorded `file_name` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline (a.pdf, no override) | `a.pdf` | `a.pdf` (`om_x100b7f4f0e9f28a4cfbd0aafa9547ff`) | PASS |
| Referenced name (b.pdf + `attachments: [{path: b.pdf, name: "B-report.pdf"}]`) | `B-report.pdf` | `B-report.pdf` (`om_x100b7f4f0fd7bca8df78c0124450259`) | PASS |
| Positional name, first file (a.pdf + `attachments: [{name: "A-report.pdf"}, {name: "B-report.pdf"}]`) | `A-report.pdf` | `A-report.pdf` (`om_x100b7f4f09c050a0df837813bfb9ccd`) | PASS |

Scope of the live proof, stated plainly:

- Feishu's direct-send surfaces are single-media by design (the send action rejects more than one distinct media source, and the Gateway `send` RPC schema has no `attachments`), so multi-media payloads can only be produced by channel-session reply delivery. The live sends above therefore went through the shipped agent `message` tool, one call per file, with each scenario's `attachments` array passed verbatim.
- Through that entry, the mismatch counterexample (media `a.pdf`, attachment pointing at `b.pdf`) is rejected before sending by the single-media validation — the misassignment cannot be produced there.
- The second positional send through the single-media action took the first named attachment (`A-report.pdf` for `b.pdf`): the send action resolves the upload name as the first named attachment in the call and a per-file call carries no position. That is the direct send-action path, not the payload pairing changed here; in `sendPayload` / fallback / reply delivery the whole payload is paired by `collectReplyMediaEntries` before flattening, which the new unit regressions assert (see Tests).
- A live reply-turn trace could not be captured in the sandbox used for this proof: the host's egress could not sustain Feishu's inbound long-connection (WSS), so no genuine inbound reply turn was available. The pairing paths are covered by the unit regressions below, including red/green verification.

## Tests

- Feishu extension suite: **315 tests passed** (7 files), including the new pairing regressions. Red/green verified: reverting the production changes makes exactly the 5 new regression tests fail with the review's counterexamples; restoring them returns the suite to green.
- Typecheck (`tsgo` for extensions and tests) — clean. `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` — clean. (oxlint could not run in the sandbox; CI will cover it.)

## Notes / out of scope

- This PR supersedes #205407, which was opened against an older `main` and conflicted after upstream's partial fix landed; it was closed in favour of this rebased version.
- Known remaining gap, deliberately **not** in this PR to keep it Feishu-scoped: the Gateway RPC send path (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) builds outbound payloads without `attachments` / `filename`, so a Gateway-relayed send can still lose the override. Happy to open a follow-up issue/PR for that core path if maintainers prefer.
- `forceDocument` is intentionally untouched: it is not read anywhere in the Feishu plugin, and a `.pdf` already routes to `msgType: "file"` via `detectFileType`.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw starts a short-lived SQLite reader to fetch an agent’s stored profile rows. The reader loads Gateway ownership code just to start, even though it only calls those helpers when preparing a metadata snapshot.

## User Impact

Ordinary profile reads can start without importing these metadata helpers from the worker entry point. Metadata snapshots still check the source file and its owner before preparation and again before delivery. The change requires no configuration or database migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The metadata operation already owns the decision between a live backup and a private copy. Loading its two helpers there keeps that decision and its validation order together. Production changes are two lines added and two removed.

## Evidence

- Reviewed the worker, the profile-row caller, both metadata helpers and the existing ownership and identity checks against base `427900b2`. The new test observes evaluation of the real owner module and includes a positive control.
- Draft head `3d4f8c7fdd19bcb58b380a5f1afdb04e45a86379` is signed. The source diff passes whitespace checks. Independent source inspection found no actionable issue.
- All 29 focused cases passed on both Node and Bun (58 executions): one import regression, seven worker-session cases and 21 worker cases. [Exact-head Linux tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45754319589/job/139689853047).
- Compared the official packages for `427900b2` and `3d4f8c7` in the same production-only npm 12 installation setup on macOS ARM64 with Node 26.7. Their package manifests match. Both workers returned the two expected synthetic profile rows over IPC and closed cleanly. The signed-head tarball has SHA-256 `1c0b761b25522165c64ab8ff956b30ae1db9cd86e84922348699797b8cd08c8b`. [Candidate package build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45754810101).
- The profile read loaded **54 → 44 files**. Their combined on-disk sizes fell from **1,618,264 to 1,369,655 bytes** (248,609 fewer). The candidate skipped the Gateway lock-payload parser and the Zod schema chunk. Metadata snapshots loaded both, succeeded on both builds, and left the source database bytes intact. On that path the counts were 41 → 48 files and 1,387,087 → 1,392,026 bytes.
- The shared Knip check reported unused exports. The npm 12 installed-tree acceptance check counted 47,828 entries against its 47,500 budget. A matched parent installed-tree count is unavailable, so attribution of that overage remains open. [Dependency check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45754319589/job/139689852680) · [Install acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45754810101/job/139696150497).
- Local ClawSweeper stopped before model execution with `incomplete_source` during a bounded Git blob-size read. All three blobs were subsequently readable. The formal run produced no verdict.
- The device trace identified the helper process without recording its requested operation. This change has no measured device latency or memory result.

prs.title: fix(ui): name the connected account, apply the sign-in's recommended model, show full model names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three gaps in the Control UI provider sign-in:

1. **Confirmation wording.** After a provider sign-in, the dialog said `{provider} is ready` and did not name the account. A plugin that returns an account email in its auth profile (for example `user@example.com`) had that email shown on the Providers row, but not in the confirmation.
2. **Recommended model ignored.** A provider auth method can return a recommended model (`ProviderAuthResult.defaultModel`). `openclaw onboard` applies it when the agent has no model. The Control UI sign-in (`models.authLogin`) runs credential-only, so the recommendation never reached the Gateway's model selection. That selection picked the hosted catalog's recommended model or else the first available row. With a synthetic plugin that recommends `Acme 4 Hydrogen`, the agent got `Acme 3.5 Flash`.
3. **Picker names cut short.** Chat model-picker rows stripped any leading word that matched the title-cased provider id. Example: the model `Acme 4 Hydrogen` showed as `4 Hydrogen` under the group `Acme Pro plan`, although the heading did not show `Acme`.

## What Changed

- **Confirmation:** `modelSetup.providerConnected` is now `{provider} connected`. Under the heading, the dialog shows the email of the account this sign-in added or renewed. The sign-in owner (`login-sign-in.ts`) compares the auth status from the start of the sign-in (saved profiles and their expiry) with the status after it, which is the comparison it already used for lost sessions. Auth status already projects `email` to admin clients.
- **Recommended model, one owner:** `runModelsAuthLoginFlow` now returns the provider's own `defaultModel` for credential-only sign-ins too. It still applies nothing: config writes, runtime-plugin repair and the CLI log line still read the credential-only result. The existing `models.authLogin` model-selection step (`resolveFirstModel` → saved-sign-in activation) prefers that model, then the catalog's recommended model, then the first available one. The rule for when it selects is unchanged and matches `openclaw onboard` (`preserveExistingDefaultModel`): only for an agent without a model. A primary that the operator set is never replaced. The Control UI asks for selection only when the agent has no model.
- **Picker names:** `formatModelLabel(label, groupLabel)` strips a prefix (or a trailing `(Provider)`) only when it equals the visible group heading. Favorites rows and the chat model-change divider have no provider heading, so they show the full name. The Models page default selector and the agent overview already use the generic `ModelPicker` with full catalog names, so they need no change. `formatRawProviderLabel` is no longer exported.
- Docs: `concepts/model-providers/quick-rules` covers the Control UI rule.

## Defaults recorded

- **Existing model kept.** An agent that already has a model keeps it after a Control UI sign-in. This is the same rule as `openclaw onboard` and `openclaw configure`, and as `models auth login` without `--set-default` (docs: quick-rules "Adding provider auth does not change your primary model").
- **Plugin recommendation first.** The sign-in's own recommendation ranks above the hosted catalog's recommendation, because the sign-in knows the account's plan.
- **Email only for this sign-in.** The email appears only when auth status shows a new or renewed account for this provider. A re-sign-in that returns the same profile with no expiry shows no email (a rare, visible case; the heading is still correct).
- **Locales:** only the English source changed. With no translation provider configured, `ui:i18n:sync --write` refuses new fallbacks and says to commit only the English source and let `control-ui-locale-refresh` translate after merge. The CI parity step `ui:i18n:check` is `continue-on-error`.

## Evidence

**Red on base, green on this branch** (merge base `427900b2d539`, tier vitest-source):

| Test | Base | Branch |
|---|---|---|
| `models-auth-login.test.ts` › a credential-only sign-in selects the model its provider recommends for an agent without one | fail | pass |
| `auth.test.ts` › reports the provider's recommended model from a credential-only login without applying it | fail | pass |
| `model-providers-page.login-select-model.test.ts` › names the account a sign-in connected under its heading | fail | pass |
| `chat-model-picker.test.tsx` › drops a provider name from a row only when the group heading shows it | fail | pass |

**Consumers:** 49 test files that import a changed source (model-providers page, chat picker, favorites, preferences, models auth, `models.authLogin`, chat `/login`, plugin-sdk login flow), all passing.

**Control UI E2E** (tier dist-nodts). Two scratch Gateways (base `427900b2d539`, and this branch), each with a fresh state, no agent model, and a synthetic `acme` provider plugin loaded through `plugins.load.paths`. The plugin's browser sign-in returns an OAuth profile for `user@example.com` and recommends `acme/acme-4-hydrogen`; its catalog lists `Acme 3.5 Flash` before `Acme 4 Hydrogen`. Models → search `acme` → Connect.

| | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Heading | `Acme Pro plan is ready` | `Acme Pro plan connected` |
| Account | (none) | `user@example.com` |
| Agent model after sign-in | `acme/acme-3-5-flash@acme:user@example.com` | `acme/acme-4-hydrogen@acme:user@example.com` |
| Picker rows | `3.5 Flash`, `4 Hydrogen` | `Acme 4 Hydrogen`, `Acme 3.5 Flash` |

Captures from head `d08d75fd1123` (base: merge base `427900b2d539`). Cropped to the dialog and the picker; no operator identity. The same run on the final head `f0016520875e` gave the same heading, account line, selected model and picker rows.

| Connected, light | ![Before: Acme Pro plan is ready, no account](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/632a59a1-9c28-4ed4-8033-4865e5ea041f) | ![After: Acme Pro plan connected, user@example.com, Acme 4 Hydrogen ready](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3867673-9a19-440d-8199-e7e3a4d73780) |
| Connected, dark | ![Before: Acme Pro plan is ready, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/279e2230-94a3-48f9-83cf-dd173336bcd6) | ![After: Acme Pro plan connected, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7368342a-aaae-4674-add5-5ce11574653f) |
| Picker, light | ![Before: rows 3.5 Flash and 4 Hydrogen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73457a5d-c4f2-4e24-83f6-27fa931877e2) | ![After: rows Acme 4 Hydrogen and Acme 3.5 Flash](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9969130e-5252-4b25-98df-48d43e2fbcb7) |

**Review:** local ClawSweeper round 1 found that a sign-in reopened after a page reload never named the account (`restore()` did not record the starting auth status). Fixed in `d08d75fd1123`: the reopened page records the status it reads when it reopens the sign-in. `model-provider-login-recovery.e2e.test.ts` now asserts the email after a reload. Round 2: patch correct, no findings. CI then failed `ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control-view.test.tsx`: a row's search name re-read the row presentation and lowercased labels on unrelated updates. Fixed in `f0016520875e` (the name depends only on the label and group heading again); review of that head: patch correct, no findings.

## Not in this PR

- `chat-model-picker-panel.tsx` is over the 700-line cap on `main` (709); this PR reduces it to 704.

prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

The Environment row uses the host control wrappers and explicit plugin icon/diff styling. The following synthetic browser captures show the repaired layout.

prs.title: feat: add opt-in Agent Profiles for small local models
prs.body:
Part of #204354. Related: openclaw/rfcs#18 (Agent Profiles RFC)

## What Problem This Solves

A local model with a small context window gets the same system prompt as a hosted model. On a 32K window that prompt fills about 40% of the window before the user says anything. Lean mode (`experimental.localModelLean`) trims only some of it and cannot be set per model size. Agent Profiles (RFC 18) give each agent a named profile that sets the workspace budget, context serialization and tool surface.

This is slice 1 of 3 of the Agent Profiles work, split from one 90-commit branch so each part can be reviewed on its own. Base of the stack. Slices 2 and 3 are stacked on this branch.

Dependencies: none. This PR does not depend on slice 2 or slice 3.

## This slice

Original reviewed range: `1601f86def0..f6a84ab8cb4` (24 signed commits: 5 by Onur Solmaz and 19 by Mitchell Etzel). Current head `179a52a0d7d5` adds a five-file documentation correction without rewriting those commits.

This slice adds the profile object and everything that applies it. It does not select a profile by model size.

- Agent Profiles: the `agentprofiles` dev dependency, the OpenClaw profile extension, the built-ins `openclaw/base` and `openclaw/small`, the resolver, and `agents.defaults.agentProfileId` with the per-agent override.
- The workspace budget: `openclaw/small` caps the content OpenClaw prepares from `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md` and `USER.md` at 11,500 characters together. Project-local instructions that Codex loads natively follow Codex's own settings and are outside these caps. The Codex attempt test checks OpenClaw's intermediate projection, not the native instructions delivered to the model. Compaction uses the shared `resolveBootstrapContextForRun` owner.
- The tool surface: `openclaw/small` filters seven heavy tools out by default before building the Tool Search catalog. Explicitly preserved tools still follow normal tool policy. The compact filter does not remove `automations` or `exec`.
- Diagnostics: `/context` and the system prompt report show the selected profile and budget; `openclaw agent exec --agent-profile` picks one for a run.
- Lean retirement: `openclaw doctor --fix` turns `experimental.localModelLean: true` into `agentProfileId: "openclaw/small"` and an explicit `false` into `agentProfileId: "openclaw/base"`, at the same scope (defaults and agent), as the Agent Profiles RFC specifies. An absent flag is left alone. `openclaw/base` keeps the full tool surface, so it preserves the behavior of `false`. `--local-model-lean` stays as an alias for `--agent-profile openclaw/small`.

## User Impact

- With no `agentProfileId` set, every agent uses `openclaw/base`: the prompt and tool list are the same as on `main`.
- An operator picks `openclaw/small` by hand, per agent or in defaults.
- An operator who set `experimental.localModelLean: true` keeps the small profile after `openclaw doctor --fix`. `openclaw/small` also applies the 11,500-character workspace budget.
- `auto` and size classes are not in this slice (slice 2). Compact context serialization is not in this slice (slice 3); here `openclaw/small` keeps the default serialization.

## Why This Change Was Made

The workspace budget, the tool surface and the Doctor migration all read one resolved profile, so they land together: split apart, a profile would select nothing. Selection by model size (slice 2) and compact serialization (slice 3) build on this resolver.

Config and API surface: this slice adds `agents.defaults.agentProfileId` and the per-agent `agentProfileId`, the `openclaw agent exec --agent-profile` flag, and the `agentProfileApplied` harness option (`localModelLeanApplied` stays as a deprecated alias). A persisted selector is needed because the profile has to survive restarts and be set per agent; Doctor retires `experimental.localModelLean` into it, so there is one setting, not two.

## Evidence

### Documentation follow-up on `179a52a0d7d5`

Clarifies the native Codex boundary and that the profile removes optional tools before Tool Search builds its catalog. Verified the exact five-file diff, links, whitespace, and local Auto Review at P2 or higher. No runtime code changed; the model and upgrade captures below are from the original head.

### Update on `ee3f53e01f45`: merged main and aligned with the RFC

- Merged main `9ad935f281e0` into the branch with one plain merge commit, `955f864be60e` (no rebase, no force). Conflicts were in the tool-surface bridge, the embedded attempt tool preparation and bundle tools, the session runtime test support (both sides added the file; the two helper sets now live in one file), `agent-scope.test.ts`, and the generated config baseline, which was regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`. The profile filter still runs before the Tool Search catalog is built, and it composes with on-demand tool loading.
- Doctor now rewrites a legacy `experimental.localModelLean: false` to `agentProfileId: "openclaw/base"` at that scope instead of removing it (openclaw/rfcs#18). It is idempotent, keeps an explicit profile, and the rewritten config passes validation. Before the change the five new cases failed against the old code (`5 failed | 10 passed`); after it the file passes (`16 passed`).
- The built-in profile index rejects a duplicate profile id instead of letting the later entry win. With the check removed, the new test fails.
- `agentprofiles` moved from `dependencies` to `devDependencies`. Runtime files import only types, which are erased at build, and the validator runs only in tests. The Plugin SDK entry that re-exports `ResolvedAgentProfile` has no `types` export and its declaration file is excluded from the package, so no published declaration references the package. The plugin-sdk declaration build output contains no `agentprofiles` reference.
- Removed three added test cases that check model routing and not profiles (`agent-runner-memory.tools.test.ts`, `session-companion-ask.test.ts`, `assistant.configured.test.ts`); the files match main.
- Fixed `attempt-system-prompt.worker-placement.test.ts`, which arrived on main after this branch started and did not pass a resolved profile.

### Runtime output

Shipped entry points at this slice, on original build `f6a84ab8cb4` (`pnpm build`, before the docs-only follow-up), against a real Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on llama.cpp (`qwen3-8b-q8_0`), one request at a time. A capture proxy sits between OpenClaw and the model server and records every request body and every server `usage` block. Every response reports model id `qwen3-8b-q8_0`. Throwaway `OPENCLAW_HOME`, no Gateway, from a clean environment. Hostnames, IPs, ports, paths and session ids are redacted.

#### (a) Over-budget workspace truncation

`agents.defaults.agentProfileId = "openclaw/small"`, an `AGENTS.md` of 12,000 characters and an `IDENTITY.md` of 3,000 characters, one shipped CLI turn: `openclaw agent --local --agent main --session-key <key> --message "Reply with one word: pong (<nonce>)" --json --timeout 300`.

```text

turn exit: 0   request: req-1.json (the captured turn that carries the nonce trunc-mwu0b0vs)
workspace files on disk:        AGENTS.md 12000 chars, IDENTITY.md 3000 chars
in the system prompt:           AGENTS.md section 4626 chars, IDENTITY.md section 1035 chars
truncation markers in the prompt: ["[...truncated, read AGENTS.md for full content...]", "[...truncated, read IDENTITY.md for full content...]"]
server call: status=200 model=qwen3-8b-q8_0 messages=3 tools=13 tool_schema_chars=15392 system_chars=27146 usage.prompt_tokens=10357 completion_tokens=2 finish=stop reply="pong"
```

The profile bounds the four injected files to 11,500 characters together (per-file caps 7,500 for `AGENTS.md` and 1,024 for `IDENTITY.md`), and the prompt tells the model to read the file for the rest. Without a profile the default limits (20,000 per file, 60,000 total) inject the same files whole.

The same captured request offers 13 tools: `apply_patch`, `dispatch_action`, `edit`, `exec`, `ls`, `openclaw`, `process`, `read`, `session_project`, `sessions_yield`, `tool_describe`, `tool_search` and `write`. The filtered tools are unavailable in this capture. `tool_search` and `tool_describe` operate only on tools that remain in the catalog.

#### (b) Doctor upgrade from the latest stable release, explicit Lean choices kept as profiles

The latest stable release (`OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (e31bbf0)`, installed read-only in a scratch directory) wrote its own state in a throwaway home: its own onboarding, a config with explicit Lean choices (`agents.defaults.experimental.localModelLean: true`, an agent entry `optout` with `localModelLean: false`, `agents.ownership: "explicit"` as that release requires for two agents), unrelated settings (`ui.seamColor`, `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`, the model route), and one agent turn that stored a code word. #### (c) Existing stored data still loads and works after the upgrade

The session the stable release stored (agent `main`, key `agent:main:upgrade-proof`) is read by this branch after Doctor, and a new turn in that same session answers from the stored history.


### Gates and local review

Gates, run one at a time on the Studio. The tsgo, format, config docs, build, oxlint, eager import and touched-test rows ran on `09f2909e9ee`; the only change since is the text of the test-line allocation record (`config/test-lines-allocations/*.txt`), re-measured at the head. The ratchets, madge and `check:changed` ran on `f6a84ab8cb4` in a git clone on the Studio (they need `.git`, which the crabbox sync does not carry).

`pnpm check:changed` on this head exits 1. Every failing lane reports only items outside this change: the Plugin SDK surface budget (public entrypoints 164 against 163) fails the same way on base `1601f86def0`; the dead export scan lists `scripts/lib/docker-e2e-watchdog.mjs: parseTimeoutMs`, a file this stack does not touch; the lint lane reports only `max-lines` errors, in files this stack does not touch (CI prints them as warnings). ### Hosted review and CI follow-up

Findings of the hosted review of `d1587b2b80b` and of the first CI run, each fixed in this slice as its own signed commit:

- `e02aef016b4` inlines the single-use worker profile forwarding call into `worker-turn-prompt.ts` and deletes `worker-turn-agent-profile.ts` (hosted review P3; the earlier decision to keep it is withdrawn).
- `d9ce2699571` removes two low-value tests: the small-profile preservation case in `agent-harness-private-options.test.ts` that repeated the preceding case, and the field-copy test in `system-prompt-report.test.ts`.
- `5e290475574` bounds compaction through the shared bootstrap owner: `prepared-compaction-runtime.ts` passes the model to `resolveBootstrapContextForRun`, the parallel `compaction-workspace-context.ts` adapter and its tests are gone (including the base-profile case that repeated the no-profile scenario), and one consumer test shows an over-budget `AGENTS.md` bounded in compaction. Red before the change, green after.
- `dc5e7c84411` keeps the `message` tool in the three profile preservation fixtures of `agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.agent-profile.test.ts`. The hosted run failed all three with `expected [ 'presence', 'gateway', ... ] to include 'message'`; the same failure reproduces here before the change and passes after it. This was a fixture defect, not a flake.
- `41afefa34f3` oxlint: removed the unused `hashCliSessionText` import and the spread inside `map` in `workspace-context.ts` (oxc no-map-spread).
- `da17569700e` added `legacy-config-migrations.agent-profiles.ts` and `agent-profile-ids.ts` to `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`. This fixes `eager-import-closure.test.ts` and the three `pr-worktree-provision.test.ts` native cases that could not find `agent-profile-ids.js`.
- `5e38527fa4d` listed the new codex `attempt-workspace-context.agent-profile.test.ts` in the codex attempt-light vitest config (`test/vitest-projects-config.test.ts` reported it as owned by no project).
- `config/test-lines-allocations/202517-agent-profiles-core.txt`: record of 1581. Main #205403 removed an old `localModelLean` agent-scope test that this change rewrote, so the replacement test now counts in full.

The gates found three type errors that the unit tests do not show (vitest does not typecheck): an implicit `any` in the compaction test support file, a `string | undefined` argument in the inspected-prompt route of slice 2, and an incomplete model row in the worker prompt test fixture of slice 2. Each is fixed in the commit that introduced it.

Why the test lines are needed: each profile effect has its own regression test on each runtime that consumes it, because each runtime builds its prompt and tools through its own seam: embedded runner, CLI runner, Codex app-server attempt, ACP harness, agentsapi prompt, isolated completion, worker turn, compaction and the coding-tool surface. The resolver, workspace-context budgets and the doctor migration have their own suites. The three tests named by the hosted review were deleted; the remaining ones differ by behavior (budget caps, never widen an operator budget, size selection off, native-owned thread).

Not from this change (reproduced on base and main):

- `bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts` (hook token) and `host-credential-execution.test.ts` (2 tests) fail the same way on base `1601f86def0` and on main.
- `thread-lifecycle.native-config.test.ts` fails on base and on main `712ae033851`; it passes on `91dee122ee6`. This PR is not rebased onto that main, so the failure shows here.
- `android-ktlint` and `android-test-wear` could not resolve `com.pinterest.ktlint:ktlint-cli:1.8.0` from Maven; this stack changes no file under `apps/`. A re-run is the fix.

| Worker profile forwarding wrapper | Inline it (withdraws the earlier keep) | hosted review P3: one production caller, no distinct behavior | revert `e02aef016b4` |

| Compaction budgeting | Use `resolveBootstrapContextForRun`, delete the adapter | red/green consumer test; hosted P2 on the duplicate path | revert `5e290475574` |
| Message-tool fixtures | Give the fixtures a real `message` tool, keep the assertions | red reproduces the hosted failure, green after | revert `dc5e7c84411` |
| Test-line overage | Allocation record 1581 with the reasons above | ratchet message: net +1971, credit 1569 before | delete tests and lower the record |
| Upgrade proof | Latest stable release 2026.11.7 with its own `agents.entries` schema | the stable release validated the config and ran the turn | n/a, evidence only |
| Local ClawSweeper P3: four call sites decide the workspace budget | Not changed here | same P3 class as an earlier round; the model gate in `resolveBootstrapContextForRun` is deliberate (a caller that names no model gets operator limits), and merging the four paths touches CLI, harness and embedded preparation in one change | follow-up refactor, own tests |
| Merge main into the branch | Plain merge commits, config baseline regenerated | merge conflicts resolved in six files; config docs check, 124 scoped tests and `tsgo:core:test` pass on `ee3f53e01f45` | revert the merge commits |
| `localModelLean: false` migration | Write `openclaw/base` at that scope, at defaults and on agents | RFC 18 migration rule; `openclaw/base` keeps the full tool surface; red 5 failed, green 16 passed; the rewrite validates | revert the migration commit |
| Duplicate built-in profile ids | Reject in the profile index | new test fails without the check | revert the duplicate-id commit |
| `agentprofiles` dependency kind | Move to `devDependencies` | type-only imports at runtime; no published declaration references it; dependency ownership and pin checks pass | revert the dependency commit |
| Three model routing tests | Remove | they test model routing, not profiles; main is trimming such tests | restore the three files from this branch's earlier head |

### Credit

Onur Solmaz and Mitchell Etzel authored the original signed commits. Mitchell Etzel is credited on the docs follow-up.

### Needs a maintainer

- Sign-off on the new `agentprofiles` 0.1.0 dev dependency (MIT, exact pin, published by the RFC author). It is not a runtime dependency: production code imports only its types, and the validator runs in tests. This is part of slice 1.
- The security-review and dependency-review approvals on the current head.
- vincentkoc's go-ahead.

prs.title: test(gateway): restore publication wake authority coverage
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The native child-completion publication test fails before exercising participant authority. Its fixture has no selected GitHub writer, so `github_publish` exposes the readiness-only schema and rejects the test's `{ draft: true }` call.

## User Impact

Restores regression coverage for default-mode participant authority across a native child completion wake. Production behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Declare a synthetic, unprovisioned writer through the existing Gateway fixture options. Keep the participation ceiling and unchanged permission-mode checks, and require the real publication handler's missing-workspace refusal. The fixture has no publication workspace and reaches that refusal before credential preparation or external publication.

## Evidence

- Existing failure: [main CI, compact-large-38](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45749158542/job/139672858902), at `427900b2d53987797eae1dd47f8a77ee16588b40`.
- Formatting, staged line-cap check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local ClawSweeper 0.3.3 completed on base `1140fc54a32dc3715e8f95f62f541ae634e97c18` through head `3a3d26a34b81d41c82e29414e4578cc52802bdf0`: zero reported findings, no summary priority filter.
- [Exact-head qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45755768227) executed the repaired Gateway test under Bun: 1/1 passed, including the native child-completion wake and missing-workspace assertion. [Test job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45755768227/job/139694402896).
- Selected lint, test type checks, source contracts, runtime architecture, and guard jobs passed.
- [Dependency checking failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45755768227/job/139694403044) on inherited unused exports: `AUTHENTICATED_GIT_JS`, `nodeWorkspaceManifestCapture`, `runNodeWorkspaceManifestCapture`, and four planner-test exports. Their producer/consumer files are unchanged between the main failure revision, this PR's base, and this head; this patch changes no imports or exports. The planner work remains with [#204549](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204549). No claim of a matching earlier CI signature for the three production exports.
- [Normal PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45756375049) passed: 18 jobs succeeded, 31 skipped. It tested merge commit `959fbc39b8fd105f8bd3538f23bceaf8a7f32868` (base `1140fc54`, head `3a3d26a3`); its tree matches the reviewed head. Dependency checking was not selected in this run, so the earlier unused-export failures remain open.
- Local execution remains unavailable in the code-only author checkout; exact-head CI supplies the runtime proof.
- Simplification: one existing fixture option and one stronger boundary assertion; no helper or production changes. Test delta: +3/-1 lines.
