prs.title: feat(ui): redesign the Talk settings page
prs.body:
Related: #204661 (this is part 3 of the redesign proposed there) **Stacked on #204355 (Talk status chimes), currently at `456f638dc8e`.** The first eight commits are that PR's (including its one-line chat-boot budget record); the only commit that belongs here is `feat(ui): redesign the Talk settings page`. This PR adds no chat-boot bytes of its own. Optional siblings, both feature-detected: #204674 (Talk's own speech-to-text provider key and the Gateway-reported live route) and #204683 (Talk thinking level and Fast mode on speech-to-text replies). This PR works without either. AI-assisted (Claude and OpenAI coding agents under @Marvinthebored's direction); reviewed by a read-only codex pass, whose findings are fixed in the commit. ## What Problem This Solves The Talk settings page does not say which mode is in use or which service handles each stage. It is titled "Realtime voice" even when Talk runs speech to text + voice. The realtime settings are split between a curated card and raw `talk.realtime.*` rows in a generic editor further down. The mode itself is only a row in that editor. Provider choices show no readiness. The same Provider/Model/Speaker voice rows carry explanatory sentences that the controls already make obvious. ## User Impact User impact: Talk settings now start with the conversation mode and a readiness line for the stage(s) in use, then the cards for that mode. The other mode's settings stay one click away. Every provider list comes from the Gateway's `talk.catalog`, with readiness shown on each option. Nothing a user could edit before becomes unreachable: whatever has no curated control stays in an Advanced editor. ## Why This Change Was Made Each choice below is deliberate, with the code that forces it. Owner decisions are marked **Owner decision**. **Page rules** - No explanatory prose; subtitles only where they add information the control does not show. **Owner decision.** The page header is only the docs link (the old header read "Realtime voice: provider, model, and speaker voice" in every mode). - No hard-coded provider lists or orders: every list and readiness value comes from `talk.catalog`. **Owner decision.** - The page never shows an auth route the Gateway would not use. **Owner decision.** Unset values show "Default", not an invented value. **Order:** Conversation mode, Talk agent, chimes and wake words, the active mode's cards, the other mode's cards (collapsed), Advanced. Universal settings first, then the mode in use. **Owner decision.** **Mode** - The mode picker offers only Live and Speech to text + voice. **Removed: the Transcription option.** It set a config value that neither the [browser launcher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/53c88cfb0d7036aa878e60b009c89dc7c2cf663c/ui/src/pages/chat/chat-realtime.ts#L281) nor the [iOS route picker](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/53c88cfb0d7036aa878e60b009c89dc7c2cf663c/apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkModeGatewayConfig.swift#L126) uses to launch a transcription session. The [mic requests transcription per session](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/53c88cfb0d7036aa878e60b009c89dc7c2cf663c/ui/src/pages/chat/composer-dictation-session.ts#L232), so dictation is unaffected. Existing browser configs with that value display Live without a write; the config schema is unchanged. This is a deliberate product choice. - The other mode's cards are collapsed and carry no "Not in use" label. The Mac app always runs its native speech-to-text/voice loop, and iOS and Android use it for routes they cannot run live (`docs/nodes/talk.md:12-16`), so `talk.provider`, `interruptOnSpeech` and `silenceTimeoutMs` can be in use while the Gateway mode is Live. **Owner decision.** - The mode card has one readiness row per stage in use (Live: "Hearing and voice"; speech to text + voice: "Speech to text" and "Voice"), so the old Status row is gone from the Live card. With no Talk speech provider chosen, the Voice row says "General text-to-speech" (browser Talk speaks through `tts.speak`, `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-realtime.ts:285`) rather than "Not configured"; its readiness is not in the Talk catalog, so it shows a neutral status. Readiness uses the group's `ready` for the active provider (it is applied after runtime provider selection, so configured does not mean ready); when a Gateway omits it, as the speech group does today, the page falls back to `configured` and says "Configured", not "Ready". **Talk agent card** (both modes) - `talk.agentId` is the agent for Talk sessions created without an agent-scoped session key (native apps, Watch); it applies in both modes (`docs/nodes/talk.md:204`). It is a picker over the configured agents; unset shows " (default)". - Thinking level and Fast mode (`talk.consultThinkingLevel`, `talk.consultFastMode`) today apply only to realtime consults (`src/gateway/talk/client-agent-consult.ts:235`, `src/gateway/talk/handlers/client.ts:442`). **Owner decision:** speech to text + voice must honor them too, which is #204683. **Until that lands, those two rows appear only in Live.** In Live they apply only when Brain is agent consult and are disabled otherwise. **Chimes** (setting owned by #204355): Listening, Call end, Ready for reply, all on by default. Ready for reply appears only in Speech to text + voice: Live is full duplex and always listening, so there is no "your turn" moment. **Live voice card** - The provider menu lists providers only, from the catalog, with readiness. It never lists auth routes: no config key selects the route. It follows from the model and key presence (`extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider-factory.ts:86-104`, `extensions/openai/realtime-voice-session-policy.ts:484-520`) and differs per agent and per surface, so a "ChatGPT sign-in" entry would have to silently rewrite `talk.realtime.model`. - Under Provider the page shows the route the Gateway will use, read-only, for example "API key · gpt-live-1". It reads the catalog's `authRoute` field from #204674. **Without #204674 no line is shown rather than a guessed one.** - Live tuning (transport, turn detection, reasoning effort, instructions, brain, consult routing) is collapsed; same keys as today, regrouped. The existing provider/model change handlers that reset transport and consult routing are kept. - There is no "auto order" line. **Owner decision:** do not hard-code it or copy docs. **Speech to text card** - Provider writes `talk.transcription.provider` (#204674). **Owner decision:** Talk stops writing Voice Call's `plugins.entries.voice-call.config.streaming.provider`. Today the Gateway picks Talk speech to text by fixed precedence (`src/gateway/talk/session-config.ts:195-240`), so a pick on the page would be silently ignored whenever Voice Call has streaming config. **The picker only appears when the Gateway's config schema declares that key; otherwise the existing read-only row stays.** - Speech locale (native apps) is `talk.speechLocale` (`docs/nodes/talk.md:207`), moved here from Advanced. The old "Language" row (`tools.media.audio.language`) is not on this card: it also changes channel voice notes and native apps ignore it. - Voice notes is `tools.media.audio.preferredModel`, its own picker as today, no "Same as Talk" coupling. **Owner decision.** Composer dictation uses Talk transcription (`ui/src/pages/chat/composer-dictation-session.ts:232`), so it follows the provider above, not this row. Voice notes stays visible in Live mode too: voice notes work in both modes. **Voice card** (speech to text + voice) - Provider writes `talk.provider`. Default clears the explicit selection without naming a destination; the Gateway can still use the sole configured Talk provider. If the catalog is unavailable, the configured choices or a text field keep the provider editable. Local engines appear by name; selecting the custom command reveals its program and arguments. - Choices the Gateway would reject (a `talk.provider` outside a non-empty `talk.providers` map, or unset next to several entries) are shown but disabled. - Silence before sending (`talk.silenceTimeoutMs`) shows "Default": the default differs per client. Interrupt on speech is `talk.interruptOnSpeech`. **Editing that the curated controls cannot do (answers the #115409 full-schema-fallback item).** #115409 kept the shared schema editor so that Talk stays configurable when provider metadata offers no choices. That contract is preserved, not dropped: a saved provider the catalog does not list, a provider with no voice inventory, or a model the provider does not enumerate each get an editable text row in the same row style (Provider, Model, Speaker voice); the Model picker has an "Other model..." custom entry; `talk.realtime.speakerVoiceId` (the legacy alias the curated rows do not write) stays in Advanced; and everything else with no curated control stays in Advanced too. **Advanced:** the schema editor narrowed to keys with no curated control (provider-owned settings maps), so nothing is duplicated and nothing is lost. Per-provider API key fields remain only where they exist today. Making Talk provider setup work like inference provider setup is a separate follow-up. **Kept from today's page (not regressed):** the native device section (microphone, languages, mic test); catalog loading, unavailable and failed states; a configured provider from a disabled plugin stays visible; the voice notes custom model entry, "Not ready" status and Open Models button. **Maintainer decision: Should this PR adopt the mode-focused Talk layout and include the stacked default-on chimes and startup-budget increase?** Our proposal is to lead with the current mode and service readiness here. The default-on behavior and measured budget for chimes belong to #204355 and should be approved there; this PR does not change that budget. ## Evidence **Talk reply settings compatibility (#204683).** Chromium connected to an isolated Gateway with the split Talk settings patch and observed `talk-chat-settings` in its hello. At 1440 and 1600 px, the old UI showed only the Talk agent picker; the corrected UI added two enabled rows, Talk reply thinking level and Talk reply fast mode. No CSS or shared layout changed. This verifies rendering, not an end-to-end voice reply or native app behavior. All 124 focused Talk settings and dictation tests passed. New tests cover STT/TTS with and without the capability and Live with its existing brain-based disabling. The capability-present test failed before the fix. Scoped lint reported no errors and one existing catalog-subscription warning. The UI build produced the tested bundle and reported CSS and chat boot budget violations; budget compliance was not established. ### Same-state Control UI upgrade from v2026.11.10 > **Add real behavior proof** — “Provide a same-state upgrade from v2026.11.10 through the shipped UI showing Talk configuration and unrelated preferences intact, with chime opt-outs surviving save and reload.” **Pass, scoped to the Control UI.** In a fresh Chromium context on one origin, the shipped v2026.11.10 UI saved Dark mode and 125% text size. I then restarted the same v2026.11.10 scratch Gateway with only `gateway.controlUi.root` changed to serve the built Control UI from `baeeff68626`. No config import, browser storage injection, or `talk.catalog` stub was used. v2026.11.10 has no chime controls or stored chime opt-outs to migrate. On first load all three were on. I turned **Listening** off, let a Talk configuration edit autosave, and reloaded: Listening remained off; Call end and Ready for reply remained on. The same browser settings record retained Dark mode and 125% text size. > **Add data-model compatibility proof** — “Show that existing data still loads and works with this change.” **Pass for the exercised settings.** The stored Talk object was identical before and after the UI swap. The new page showed the saved Speech to text + voice mode, live model `gpt-realtime-2.1`, and speaker voice `marin`. The stored provider, interrupt setting, consult Fast mode and thinking level were unchanged. I edited **Silence before sending**; after autosave and reload the input read 1800 ms, and a deep comparison against the original Talk object found exactly one changed value. Redacted diff: ```diff - "silenceTimeoutMs": 1500 + "silenceTimeoutMs": 1800 ``` This is a UI-only transition against stable Gateway state, not a full binary upgrade. The PR checkout embeds version 2026.11.8, so its Gateway binary refuses state last written by 2026.11.10. No provider call, audio playback, or failed-provider failover was tested here. [Review context](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205068#issuecomment-7152206345): the layout, inherited default-on chimes, and the parent PR's chat-startup budget remain upstream maintainer decisions. As noted in [the provider UI follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205068#issuecomment-7161820699), selected/default provider, Gateway-reported route, and readiness do not establish failover; ordered failover remains separate (#186263). **Chromium draft retention (head `baeeff68626`).** With `talk.catalog` returning a fixture `UNAVAILABLE`, the fallback Provider field remained editable. I entered `openai` without blurring the field, injected a `config.changed` notification, and observed a second successful `config.get` from the real test Gateway. The catalog retry still failed. After editing another unsaved field, the same Provider input still contained `openai`; the Gateway provider remained unset and the browser sent zero config writes. This verifies an unsaved draft survives a settings reread, not a persisted save or upgrade. - **Chromium draft-refresh proof (`baeeff68626`):** On an isolated Gateway, the browser test injected an unavailable response for `talk.catalog` only. The fallback showed the saved speech provider. A separate field autosave returned a successful `config.set` and a fresh `config.get`; the unsaved speech-provider draft remained in the input. No production state was used. This draft-retention test is separate from the same-state upgrade proof above. All shots are dark mode. Before is unmodified `main` (build `3f96030c6d7`) on a proof Gateway with the same config; after is this branch. Provider shows Ready because the proof Gateways use placeholder keys, not a real account. "Full design" shots ran on a Gateway with #204674; the PR-alone shots at the end show what this PR does against a Gateway without it. **1. Header and mode** (before: no mode control, header says "Realtime voice") **2. Chimes and wake words** (main has no chimes section) **3. Live voice** (the route line needs #204674) **4. Live provider menu: readiness on each option, from the catalog** **5. Speech to text in Live mode: Voice notes stays** **6. Speech to text + voice mode** (before: still titled "Realtime voice") **7. Speech to text** (provider picker needs #204674) **8. Generic editor (before) and Advanced (after)**
After only: Talk agent, Voice card, Voice provider menu, collapsed Live voice
Review follow-up states (new in the latest head) Editable Model and Speaker voice rows for a provider the catalog cannot list: Transcription mode (always selectable; speech-to-text cards only): General text-to-speech in the Voice readiness row (no Talk provider chosen):
This PR alone, on a Gateway without #204674 (feature detection) Speech to text keeps the read-only row, and no route line is shown:
**Tests for the two-option picker.** 121 scoped Talk settings and composer dictation tests passed. The regression test failed on the previous implementation because it selected Transcription. It now verifies that a saved legacy value shows Live without a config write, that only two options exist, and that choosing Speech to text + voice writes `stt-tts`. Earlier screenshots and Gateway proof were captured before this picker change. **Known, not caused by this PR** - `ui/src/pages/config/memory-page.browser.test.ts` "keeps the header and every tab panel on one column" fails the same way on the unmodified base (expected 12 <= 1). - `ui:i18n:check` reports catalog fallback baseline drift on the unmodified base too. This PR edits only the English locale files (it removes `subtitles.talk` and the keys it made dead); the generated locale files are left to the locale refresh workflow. - Control UI build budget: the chat-boot growth over `main` is the stacked #204355 code (module attribution: `chimes-gesture.ts` +175 B, `chat-realtime.ts` +85 B, `settings.ts` +65 B, `talk/input.ts` +42 B gzip), and none of it is in this PR. #204355 now carries one commit that raises `chatBootJsGzipBytes` by its measured cost, so this stack adds no startup bytes beyond that recorded line (maintainer approval of that line is pending there). This PR removes the dead `.talk-provider-options` rule and adds no CSS. - The Talk settings tests cover readiness, provider editing, and preserving uncommitted text when another setting refreshes. The draft regression reproduced the lost text before the fix; 66 focused tests pass. The 98-line test allocation covers the measured growth above the shared 400-line allowance, including the stacked chime tests.

prs.title: improve: show restored and extended guest access in the Inbox
prs.body:
Related: #182352, #182528

## What Problem This Solves

When a visitor is invited back after access ends, OpenClaw starts another Welcome chat. Extending a current invitation changes the expiry without telling the visitor in the app.

## User Impact

User impact: returning visitors see “Welcome back” in their private **Inbox → System**, and a visitor whose current access is extended sees the new expiry there. Neither action opens, creates, or restores a chat. First-time visitors still get a Welcome chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

Visitor Access decides which notice applies from the signed-in guest’s admitted invitation. The Inbox displays that notice without browser push permissions. Visitor Access keeps a bounded record of which verified profiles have already received a Welcome chat so it can recognize them after a grant ends. Active welcomes are recognized when guests next sign in; already-ended grants from older builds are not backfilled. Existing chats and access permissions are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Visitor Access and Gateway welcome tests passed (six files). These cover one first-time conversation, no new chat on re-invite, and the committed expiry after an extension.
- All seven guest Control UI browser tests passed. The new test exercises Inbox → System for both notices without navigating away or creating a session. Browser data is synthetic; no live identity provider or production Gateway was changed.
- Targeted UI and extension type checks, lint, formatting, and Auto Review passed.

### Review follow-up

- Fixed the Outbox test's typed Inbox fixture and kept the Welcome callback bound to its store. The UI test typecheck and targeted type-aware lint passed.
- Added a Chromium regression against an isolated real Gateway and the real Visitor Access plugin. The only external fixture is the Cloudflare policy transport. It checks first-time Welcome creation, the original chat staying archived on re-invite, and the new expiry appearing in **Inbox → System** while the guest stays connected.
- Ran the same flow after upgrading an isolated source installation from latest stable `v2026.11.10` (`6ea542fd9`). The stable Gateway wrote the original grant, transcript, and archive. Doctor migrated a copy in its final state directory (shared schema 40 → 41; agent schema 42 → 43). The revised Gateway loaded the same archived chat and transcript, and Chromium verified restored and extended notices without creating another chat.

- The same regression failed on the original base `3091ba81d`: two Welcome chats (one active and one archived) instead of one archived chat. It passed with the PR applied. The separate Dashboard Gallery case that failed in the original CI run passed on the base replay; no gallery code was changed.

### Stable upgrade: real Gateway and Control UI

Chromium connected to an isolated Gateway using a copy of state created on `v2026.11.10`, after Doctor migrated the copy in place. The Visitor Access plugin, Gateway, browser UI, and database were real; only the external Cloudflare policy API was simulated. All profiles and invitation text shown are synthetic.

1. **After upgrade:** the original Welcome transcript and archived state are intact.

   ![Archived Welcome chat with its original invitation note and the archive banner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ef6bd25-a962-47a7-8f11-3c6783ccb93d)

2. **After re-inviting:** the guest sees the new note and expiry in System, without reopening or creating a chat.

   ![System Inbox showing Welcome back, the expiry, and the inviter note](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c96e068-06ed-4bd8-9ccd-ea9f27ff3daf)

3. **After extending access while still signed in:** System shows the new expiry.

   ![System Inbox showing Guest access extended and the new expiry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efdec370-0561-4606-918f-e2c3b0ad08e0)

The revised regression fits within the CI test-line limit (399/400; no allocation). Type-aware lint, the fresh real-Gateway regression, and the stable upgrade browser run passed. The two Dashboard Gallery and Meetings cases that failed in the prior CI run passed in focused local replays; neither feature was changed.


Captured in the real Control UI with a synthetic guest and a mocked Gateway, in dark mode at 1280 × 800 and cropped to the Inbox. Before: base `3091ba81d`. After: the new notice row; the final extraction of the row and loader was rechecked in Chromium.

### Clean comparison

![Before: no access extension notice in the System Inbox](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c000e3a3-3330-4764-bdda-72a21584f939)

![After: guest access extension and the full expiry in the System Inbox](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aaa66df9-d8b3-4a91-ac17-993c2ae14217)

### Annotated comparison

![Before: no access notice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/266a8c6b-6865-43b3-a0a8-f3a78894b03f)

![After: the updated expiry is visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84d22182-d721-43df-b30f-eb05c6b6d7bb)

## Contributor

Requested by @jjjhenriksen.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dfca6b2e-ac17-43fb-8e35-5803421d765b)

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.title: fix(signal): unblock approvals while the requesting turn is waiting
prs.body:
Closes #194029

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Signal approval responses wait behind the turn they need to release. Once dispatched, UUID approvers can be rejected after command normalization, and a typed approval confirmation can cancel the waiting turn with a transcript conflict.

## User Impact

An authorized owner can approve a waiting command from Signal using `/approve` or a supported reaction. Ordinary messages and session-mutating commands retain their conversation ordering. Existing access, exact-target approval checks, and durable audit records remain enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Route the existing narrow set of Signal controls and canonical approval-reaction candidates through a conversation-scoped control lane. Previously stored controls can move only from their exact original conversation lane to that conversation's control lane.
- Supply text-command facts for core active-run admission.
- Preserve UUIDs through Signal command/allowlist normalization instead of stripping their letters into phone-number-like values.
- Keep fast `/approve` exchanges visible in history but outside model context, using the existing context-free recorder contract. Their confirmations must not invalidate the transcript snapshot of the turn waiting for approval; the decision still reaches the model through the tool result.

The lifecycle type lives in the existing leaf types module, removing the review's import cycle. The existing routing helper moves unchanged into the context sibling to respect the oversized handler's growth guard. No schema, dependency, public SDK surface, or configuration option is added.

Related reviews: #175345 does not change Signal ingress; #191787 concerns native-approval capability metadata; merged #153829 supplies the Telegram control-lane precedent. The final recorder fix follows the existing context-free status mechanism from #192585.

## Live Signal group reaction approval proof

On 2026-11-26 I built and ran `b2cc508a51e8c102f06efb76578addeae49fda1a` in an isolated Gateway with the bundled Signal plugin, a real model, and two registered accounts in a private Signal group. Exec approvals were gated, with `session` forwarding and one explicitly listed Signal approver. A scoped relay forwarded the selected native Signal envelopes unchanged.

The group requested a harmless `printf` command piped to `tee` in the test workspace. I checked the Gateway's approval record and the output file before reacting. I then applied 👍 to the native approval prompt in Signal Desktop.

```text
Group request       -> native approval prompt delivered to the same group
Before reaction     -> approval pending; decision unset; output file absent
Signal Desktop 👍   -> native dataMessage.reaction; prompt author and timestamp matched
Envelope shape      -> dataMessage.groupInfo present; reaction.groupInfo absent
Gateway decision    -> allowed / allow-once; resolver = channel
Command completion  -> output file contains signal-group-approval-ok-194034
Same-group reply    -> signal-group-approval-ok-194034 observed in Signal Desktop
```

The command result reached the group 2.9 seconds after the thumbs-up reached the relay. The thumbs-up was the approval action forwarded to the candidate.

## Conflict refresh — 2026-11-22

Merged upstream `5e371a0b7799801eb738b993ae3b9687f78dd636` into the existing branch. Updated head: `9a127a4edc681600339ba441ccdd6459aa567e48`.

The sole conflict was in the slash-command guide. The resolution documents both the context-free fast `/approve` exchange and upstream's deferred recording of other command exchanges during an active turn. The TypeScript patch introduced by this PR is identical to the previous revision.

- **152 focused tests passed across 10 files** on the merged tree. Coverage includes Signal approval scheduling, replay, UUID handling, mentions, view-once attachment handling, and command history during an active turn, including late `/stop` delivery.
- Scoped review found no issue in the manual resolution or the overlapping automatic merges. Targeted lint, formatting, diff checks, the test-line budget, pre-commit, and the import-cycle check passed.
- The earlier live Signal/model, upgrade, and authorization tests below remain evidence for their recorded revision. GitHub CI on the refreshed head is tracked separately in the PR checks.

## Conflict refresh — 2026-11-17

Merged upstream `edbc5bcea9b605a826cc722d298c784c6a8fef78` into the existing branch, preserving its four original commits. Updated head: `8ce7760f3ebe8ea065b5f00099fbc6c0448fafab`.

The only textual conflict was in Signal's inbound context helper: this branch relocates the existing routing helper, while upstream #200058 renders native mentions in quoted messages. The resolution retains both. Automatically merged changes preserve upstream response-prefix handling and restart tests alongside the approval fixes. The introduced PR diff remains 15 files, +269/-70.

- **176 focused cases pass in 10 files** on the resolved tree: 81 Signal cases (including upstream quoted-mention and group-mention tests), and 95 shared command/transcript cases. Signal wrapper wall time: 120.55 seconds; shared wrapper wall time: 98.78 seconds, including compilation.
- Production core and Signal package type checks, focused regression-test types, targeted lint, formatting, diff checks, pre-commit guard, and import-cycle check pass (0 runtime value cycles). The current test-line budget passes: +138 test lines, 400 allowance, 138 existing allocation credit; no baseline or allocation changes.
- Fresh independent read-only review of the public conflict-resolution bundle found no actionable merge regression. The initial agy review timed out without a result; the completed fallback review covered the manual resolution and overlapping automatic merges.
- The first sandboxed test attempt was stopped after process-identity/loopback restrictions caused fixture failures. The completed run used the required local process and loopback permissions. One type-check attempt overlapped lint's artifact ownership; it was rerun successfully after lint completed.
- Live Signal/model, stable-upgrade, and final-effect authorization receipts below remain evidence for the explicitly pinned earlier head `d24bc8ab8ccbd869accc368c9b6a595016e65055`; those external/live checks were not repeated for this conflict refresh. New-head GitHub CI is separate from the earlier passing runs. [CI run 43902495410](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43902495410) currently reports `action_required` with zero jobs; no new-head CI pass is claimed. GitHub reports the updated PR mergeable; maintainer review and the workflow action remain pending.

## Evidence from the earlier tested head

- Base used for local proof: `8b023da72a1a595450b3071782ec1d4940bd459f`. Previously live-tested candidate: `d24bc8ab8ccbd869accc368c9b6a595016e65055`.
- Red before repair: DM/group queue controls do not dispatch; command context is `normal` rather than `text-slash`; three UUID formats fail approval authorization after command formatting; the fast-approval recording boundary omits `contextFreeCommand`. Corresponding regressions pass after repair.
- **206 relevant cases pass across 11 test files**: 113 Signal cases and 93 shared command/transcript cases. The final consolidated fixture was also verified by rerunning its 74-case lifecycle suite. Signal validation took 63.80 seconds; shared validation took 103.85 seconds, including compilation. Existing authorization, wrong-target, ordinary FIFO, replay, and routing controls remain covered.
- Official production-core and extension type checks, focused changed-test type checks, type-aware lint, formatting, diff and pre-commit checks pass. Temporary test configurations extend the repository configuration; no compiler settings were committed.
- Final clean Linux CLI-startup build passed in **2m 10.7s**. This is the startup profile, not a full release/package/declaration build. Local architecture check reports **0 cycles**.
- Independent reviews of the cycle repair, UUID repair, and final recorder diff returned scoped-clean. The test fixture stays in its existing suite and shrinks by consolidating repeated values.

### Live Signal and model proof

Verified the exact clean candidate with a real agent, configured OpenAI model, and the registered Signal account through Signal Desktop. Approval mode remained gated; only allow-once decisions were used.

```text
candidate: d24bc8ab8ccbd869accc368c9b6a595016e65055
whoami request: pending
/status during the wait: replied; displayed d24bc8a
/approve <redacted> allow-once: allowed via channel policy
whoami final reply: stdout openclaw
separate printf signal-final-ok request: pending
thumbs-up on its native prompt: allowed via channel policy
final reply: signal-final-ok
ingress after both cases: completed=20, pending=0, claimed=0, failed=0
```

These checks exposed and reproduced both the UUID normalization refusal and the typed-confirmation transcript conflict before their repairs. The final run completed without those failures. Only sanitized decision metadata and receipts are included here; no private transcript, account identifier, credential, or screenshot is published.

### Actual stable upgrade

The installed stable core and official Signal plugin, both 2026.11.1, accepted real Signal events into a separate state directory. The stable journal contained an ordinary completion, a claimed typed approval, and a pending reaction in the original direct-conversation lane. After stopping stable, applying the supported offline Doctor migration to the test copy, and starting the candidate, all three records were completed, with the pending reaction reconciled to the control lane; no pending or failed ingress remained.

Account, account UUID, owner allowlist, agent/session filters, default model, and exec/elevated/filesystem policies were checked against the verified native backup and retained. The fixture uses a separate workspace and disables scheduled jobs. Native reaction tests explicitly use forwarding mode `session` with the existing private-session filter; `targets` alone does not start Signal's native approval handler. This demonstrates real packaged-state transport replay, not continuation of an already terminated process's exec call.

### Final-effect authorization proof

The follow-up security review requested rejection at the actual decision owner, beyond the identity helper. On the same exact built head, a separate credential-free Gateway loaded the real Signal plugin and approval capability. Its real exec tool requested a harmless file-marker command; no approval or execution callback was mocked.

For each public resolver used by Signal—legacy `exec.approval.resolve` for typed commands and canonical `approval.resolve` for reactions—both checks passed:

| Resolver | Refused actor | Approval after refusal | Decision waiter released | Command ran before current approval | Same command ran after current approval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exec.approval.resolve` | Unlisted UUID | pending; no decision | no | no | yes |
| `exec.approval.resolve` | Queued, then revoked UUID | pending; no decision | no | no | yes |
| `approval.resolve` | Unlisted UUID | pending; no decision | no | no | yes |
| `approval.resolve` | Queued, then revoked UUID | pending; no decision | no | no | yes |

The unlisted UUID differs from the listed UUID only in letters, retaining the same numeric projection. In each revocation case, the old actor's control was first persisted with the real SQLite channel-ingress queue, and its pending row was checked. The Gateway's runtime configuration publisher then replaced the Signal approver policy while the original exec request remained alive. Only after publication was the unchanged queued control claimed and submitted to the real resolver. It was refused with `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND`; `approval.get` still showed pending without a decision, the real decision waiter remained blocked, and the command's marker did not exist. A current listed actor then approved that exact request; the waiter returned allow-once and the real command created its marker. This positive control was repeated for all four cases.

This is an owner-boundary integration proof with synthetic identities and a test-controlled dispatch barrier, not another live Signal-network/model run. It deliberately submits to the final resolver rather than relying on earlier channel rejection. Runtime policy publication isolates the custody guard from file-reload scheduling; no authorization checks or process guards were bypassed. Separately, an attempted public `config.patch` policy reload was observed deferring Signal reload until active Gateway requests finish, so that timed-out attempt is **not** counted as revocation proof. The earlier exact-head live Signal/model proof remains the transport/user-flow evidence. The final isolated Gateway closed cleanly. No production source change was needed for this additional proof.

### Check boundaries

The local test-line guard against the historical base remains **25 lines over due to inherited debt**: base 6,533,876/6,533,851; candidate 6,534,014/6,533,989. The patch adds 138 counted regression lines and exactly 138 allocation credit. The shared baseline and unrelated tests were not changed.

The SQLite and HTTP fixtures were run on a qualified host with process-owner and loopback access. The exact candidate's [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42223925652/job/127915523030) and [architecture guard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42223925652/job/127913150828) pass.

The candidate was used for bounded tests, and the normal stable service was restored. No permanent deployment or merge has been performed. Maintainer/security review remains required.

prs.title: improve(usage): reduce memory use when refreshing long conversations
prs.body:
Related: #197430

Builds on #201064.

## What Problem This Solves

A full usage refresh built the complete conversation tree twice. Forked histories with inherited events built it three times. Ordinary histories also built a map relating each message to its user turn and then discarded it because their billing uses file order.

## User Impact

Token and cost accounting no longer allocates duplicate navigation trees for large conversations. Branch billing, per-reply latency, and the checkpoint used by the next refresh keep their existing semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

The billing selector now uses the same tree to resolve inherited history and return its visible leaf to each checkpoint writer. It builds the user-turn ancestry map only when a leaf control makes that map necessary. Append-only scans still advance the existing leaf directly. Both the SQLite refresh worker and the in-memory transcript scanner consume the leaf the selector already computed.

## Evidence

A full scan should build one tree and an eligible append should build none. A counting wrapper called the actual tree builder from the production usage scanners. On a single isolated Node 24.22.1 runner, the matched baseline and candidate produced the same output hashes (excluding scan time) on five repetitions per case.

| Production scan | Trees before | Trees after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| SQLite worker, flat history | 2 | 1 |
| SQLite worker, inherited history | 3 | 1 |
| SQLite worker, append only | 0 | 0 |
| In-memory transcript, flat history | 2 | 1 |
| In-memory transcript, inherited history | 3 | 1 |

The first five-sample comparison used `69b81b5a`. On its small fixture, median post-call heap growth for flat and inherited worker scans declined from 2,857 to 2,488 KiB and from 2,468 to 1,880 KiB. These figures measure net heap growth across one call. Whole-Gateway peak RSS and the original installation’s field retest remain open on #197430.

The initial five-sample flat in-memory scan had a slower p95 (4.832 to 6.921 ms). Its p95 was the single slowest observation. A second comparison used the integrated parent `625045f4` and signed candidate `7bbfef4e`, the same 721 rows and runner, 12 warmups per build, then 64 observations per build in alternating AB/BA order. The complete output digest matched. Median time went from 1.584 to 1.475 ms and p95 went from 2.052 to 1.875 ms.

Local ClawSweeper reviewed all three changed files on `625045f4..7bbfef4e` and found no actionable issues. Its offline comparison of 502 synthetic transcripts preserved billed rows, order, reply timing, cursor and leaf. Targeted formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Production lines +34/−39. On the signed head, the five full output hashes matched the baseline and the tree counts stayed at 1/1/0/1/1. All 26 SQLite worker tests, both memory scanner tests and the selected real Gateway `sessions.usage` rewound-session test passed in the native Testbox command (exit 0). Stopping its lease marked the [hosting workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45739770172) cancelled. The separate [PR CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45741561033) completed successfully.

prs.title: fix: let a Workboard card start again after its worker run fails
prs.body:
Related: #205625 (fixes the retained claim; the issue's second expectation, reporting skipped cards in `startFailures`, is not changed here)

## What Problem This Solves

When a Workboard worker run fails after it was accepted (for example the model keeps returning errors, or the run times out or is killed), the card moves to `blocked` but stays claimed by the dead worker for 30 minutes. If you move the card back to `ready` and dispatch, nothing starts and the result lists no failure. Other `ready` cards of the same owner wait as well, because the leftover claim still fills the owner's one active slot.

## User Impact

A card whose worker failed can be moved to `ready` and dispatched again right away, and the owner's next card is no longer held back for the rest of the claim. No config or schema change.

Not changed:

- A run that ends successfully and lands in `review` keeps its claim until it expires. Worker selection documents that a card waiting for review counts while its claim has not expired, so I left it.
- A card that was manually moved out of `running` (for example to `backlog`) while its worker was still running keeps the claim when that worker later fails. Lifecycle sync does not change the status of such a card, and this change only acts where the card is moved to `blocked`.
- Scheduled dispatch still skips claimed cards without a `startFailures` entry (the second expectation in the issue). ClawSweeper's review on the issue notes that this would change the selection contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

`WorkboardStore.syncLifecycle` (`extensions/workboard/src/store.ts`) writes the `blocked` status with a fresh lifecycle source. `updateCard` skips `settleManualStatusTransition` for those writes, which is where a plain status move to `blocked` drops the claim. Attempts and `failureCount` are already settled on this path by `syncExecutionAttemptMetadata`; of what `finishRun` does for a blocked run, only the claim release was missing. `workboardCardConsumesOwnerSlot` and the dispatcher's `cardHasActiveClaim` then keep honoring the claim until `expiresAt`.

The fix releases the claim in the same lifecycle write that moves the card to `blocked`. It is tied to the status write, not to every terminal observation, so a claim taken later on an already settled card is not touched by the once-a-minute sweep.

## Evidence

Source Gateway from this checkout, isolated dev profile, default agent on a local OpenAI-compatible stub that answers every request with HTTP 500, so the worker run is accepted and then fails. Same steps on `main` (4d2d537) and on this fix applied to that commit. The branch was rebased onto cdadcea afterwards; no Workboard file changed in between, and the tests and checks below ran on the rebased commit:

```
openclaw workboard create "Retry after a failed worker" --status ready --json
openclaw workboard dispatch --max-starts 1 --admin --json
# wait until the run has failed
openclaw workboard show <id> --json
openclaw workboard move <id> --status ready --json
openclaw workboard dispatch --max-starts 1 --admin --json
```

Output condensed to status, claim, and dispatch result.

`main`:

```
show      {"status": "blocked", "execution": "blocked", "attempts": ["blocked"], "failureCount": 1, "claim": {"ownerId": "workboard-dispatcher", "expiresInMin": 29}}
move      {"status": "ready", ..., "claim": {"ownerId": "workboard-dispatcher", "expiresInMin": 29}}
dispatch  {"started": [], "startFailures": []}
```

With the fix:

```
show      {"status": "blocked", "execution": "blocked", "attempts": ["blocked"], "failureCount": 1, "claim": null}
move      {"status": "ready", ..., "claim": null}
dispatch  {"started": [{"cardId": "0cf38620", "runId": "workboard:0cf38620-…:1795661798594"}], "startFailures": []}
```

Store-level script with the real dispatcher and SQLite store, before and after:

- `subagent_ended` with `error`, `timeout`, `killed`: before, the claim stays for 30 minutes and neither the same card (after a move to `ready`) nor the owner's next `ready` card starts; after, both start.
- Recovery sweep that reads a `failed` session: stuck before and starts after, like the hook path.
- `subagent_ended` with `ok`, and a card parked in `backlog` while its worker fails: claim kept before and after (see "Not changed").
- A card that failed, was then claimed by another owner while `blocked`, and is swept again with the failed session reporting a newer timestamp: the new claim is still there after the sweep.

Tests and checks:

- `pnpm test extensions/workboard/src/lifecycle-sync.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 40 passed. The new test `dispatches a card again after its failed worker ended` fails on `main` with `expected [] to deeply equal [ ObjectContaining{…} ]` and takes about 0.7 s.
- The ten Workboard test files that use the lifecycle write path (`lifecycle-sync*.test.ts`, `store-lifecycle`, `store.attempts`, `store`, `store-verification`, `tools`, `dispatcher-compensation`, `index.lifecycle`): 174 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint on the two touched TypeScript files, and `pnpm format:check` on the three touched files: clean.
- Tests ran with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` on Node 26.10.0; the pinned Bun fork was not used.

Not done: the full suite, `pnpm check:changed` as a whole (I ran its format, lint, typecheck and line/assertion ratchet steps one by one; `check:test-timeout-race-ratchet` did not finish in my shallow clone), the Control UI dispatch action, the PostgreSQL store, and local autoreview or ClawSweeper.

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

Tracking: cbire880/the-roost#2473, OP#1548

prs.title: feat: send compact chat context to models on the small profile
prs.body:
Closes #204354. Related: openclaw/rfcs#18 (Agent Profiles RFC)

## What Problem This Solves

A local model with a small context window gets the same system prompt as a hosted model. On a 32K window that prompt fills about 40% of the window before the user says anything. Lean mode (`experimental.localModelLean`) trims only some of it and cannot be set per model size. Agent Profiles (RFC 18) give each agent a named profile that sets the workspace budget, context serialization and tool surface.

This is slice 3 of 3 of the Agent Profiles work, split from one 90-commit branch so each part can be reviewed on its own. Stacked on slice 2. Retarget to `main` after slices 1 and 2 merge.

Dependencies: depends on #202517 (slice 1: `contextSerialization` and `toolProfile`) and on #204132 (slice 2: `auto` selection).

## This slice

Original signed slice: `adc667c7b8c..a6e30e0ad36` (18 commits: 1 by Onur Solmaz and 17 by Mitchell Etzel). Current head `a0fafb43ed31` appends the compact history fix and carries forward the fixes from #202517 and #204132 without rewriting signed commits. To inspect this slice against the updated auto tree, use `git diff 705e733030e7 a0fafb43ed31`.

This slice lets `openclaw/small` send a compact inbound context. It needs slices 1 and 2.

- Compact context serialization: one marked `Context facts:` block replaces the verbose inbound metadata, with bounded strings like the default path.
- Worker turns use the serialization the profile selects: `prepareWorkerTurnPrompt` resolves it from the selected profile and passes it to the prompt context, as the embedded prompt phase does.
- The Telegram current-message carrier stays outside the marked block, so stripping the block never removes user text.
- A session transcript row is removed from compact history only when a native row of the same window or history has the same timestamp and trimmed raw body. Distinct bodies that display identically are kept. A delivered cron close-out, a message-tool source reply, or an assistant row that happens to share its body with another speaker's message is kept.
- The compact Reply target falls back to the nearest `ReplyChain` entry that has a body, so channels that quote only through `ReplyChain` (Nextcloud Talk) keep the quoted sender and body on `openclaw/small`.
- The benchmark script `scripts/benchmark-context-serialization.ts` and the prompt build entry point tests.

## User Impact

- Only a turn on a profile that selects compact serialization (`openclaw/small`) is affected, on embedded, CLI and worker routes. `openclaw/base` and no profile keep the default context byte for byte.
- On the captured Qwen3-8B turn, the inbound block shrinks, and the history, a transcript-only row and a `ReplyChain` quote stay as quoted data.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compact context is the part of the small profile that shrinks per-turn inbound metadata. It belongs to the profile, so worker, embedded and CLI routes read the same selection instead of a separate switch.

Config and API surface: no new user-facing config option. `contextSerialization` is a field of the profile spec, not a key operators set (`agent-profile-config.test.ts` and the schema do not expose it standalone).

## Evidence

### Transcript preservation follow-up on `a0fafb43ed31`

Compact history now compares trimmed raw bodies before display sanitization. A focused regression reproduced the dropped row before the fix and passed after it. The final local integrated stack passed 76 focused tests. The worker and Qwen captures below are historical and were not rerun on the new head: the short worker quote grew from 220 to 227 characters, while the richer Qwen fixture shrank from 915 to 515. These show selection and quote preservation, not universal token savings or hosted-worker parity.

### Running-worker verification on original head `a6e30e0ad366`

A real Gateway and local paired worker completed two turns per profile against a deterministic loopback HTTP model endpoint. With identical prior text, acknowledgment and reply, the second request preserved the quote on both paths. `openclaw/base` sent the verbose reply-target label (220 decoded characters). `openclaw/small` sent `Context facts:` and `Reply target:` (227). The recorded profile and serialization mode matched the request bytes. This proves selection and quote preservation through worker execution, **not token savings**: the compact representation was seven characters longer for this short quote. It does not measure cloud workers or model quality.

### Runtime output

Compact serialization with history at this slice, on build `745a2db4a37` (`pnpm build`; the tree of this head differs from the build only in `agent-profile-config.test.ts` and the allocation records), against a real Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on llama.cpp, one request at a time, through a capture proxy that records every request body and server `usage` block. Throwaway `OPENCLAW_HOME`, no Gateway. The turn goes through `getReplyFromConfig` (`get-reply-run-context`), the entry every channel plugin reaches, with a Telegram-style group message that carries five history entries: four native rows, one transcript-only session row (`#session:close-out-1`, an assistant close-out), and a `ReplyChain` entry that quotes message 1002 (which is also in the window, so the quote is checked on the compact `Reply target`, not as a quote that only the chain carries). Hostnames, IPs, ports, paths and session ids are redacted.

The same home, model route and message are run twice. The only difference is `agents.defaults.agentProfileId`: unset (control, `openclaw/base`) and `"openclaw/small"`.

```text
control (no profile)    nonce req-none-dynamic-mwu0mxna   proxy call #4
  agentProfile = {"id": "openclaw/base", "selectionSource": "fallback"}
  contextSerialization = {"mode": "default", "source": "fallback", "defaultChars": 915, "serializedChars": 915, "removedSessionMessages": 0, "deduplicatedMessages": 0, "providerInputTokens": 7785}
  server call: status=200 model=qwen3-8b-q8_0 messages=3 tools=14 tool_schema_chars=18197 system_chars=30757 usage.prompt_tokens=12585 completion_tokens=2 finish=stop reply="pong"

openclaw/small          nonce req-explicit-dynamic-mwu0ojhr   proxy call #4
  agentProfile = {"id": "openclaw/small", "selectionSource": "defaults-explicit"}
  contextSerialization = {"mode": "compact", "source": "agent-profile", "defaultChars": 915, "serializedChars": 515, "removedSessionMessages": 0, "deduplicatedMessages": 0, "providerInputTokens": 6687}
  server call: status=200 model=qwen3-8b-q8_0 messages=3 tools=13 tool_schema_chars=15403 system_chars=29959 usage.prompt_tokens=11421 completion_tokens=2 finish=stop reply="pong"
```

The inbound context as sent to the model, from the captured request bodies (first `Conversation data` fragment of the runtime-context user message, JSON string decoded):

Control, `mode: default`, 915 characters:

````text
Conversation info: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
```json
{"message_id":"1005","conversation_label":"Deploy room","sender":{"id":"2001","name":"Alice"},"timestamp":"Sun 2026-11-22 08:05:00 PST","group_subject":"Deploy room","is_group_chat":true,"was_mentioned":true,"history_count":5}
```

Reply chain of current user message (nearest first): ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
```json
[{"message_id":"1002","sender":"Carol","body":"Nice. Who is on call for the deploy window?","is_quote":true}]
```

Chat history since last reply: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
#1001 2026-11-22 08:00:00 PST Bob: Morning all. The build is green again.
#1002 2026-11-22 08:01:00 PST Carol: Nice. Who is on call for the deploy window?
#1003 2026-11-22 08:02:00 PST Bob: Alice is. She will post the plan here.
#1004 2026-11-22 08:03:00 PST Dave: Please keep the plan under ten lines.
#session:close-out-1 2026-11-22 08:04:30 PST assistant: Close-out: the deploy window starts at 10:00.
````

`openclaw/small`, `mode: compact`, 515 characters:

````text
Context facts: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
Context: {"message_id":"1005","sender":{"name":"Alice","id":"2001"},"was_mentioned":true}
Reply target: {"sender":"Carol","body":"Nice. Who is on call for the deploy window?","is_quote":true}
History:
#1001 Bob: Morning all. The build is green again.
#1002 Carol: Nice. Who is on call for the deploy window?
#1003 Bob: Alice is. She will post the plan here.
#1004 Dave: Please keep the plan under ten lines.
#session:close-out-1 assistant: Close-out: the deploy window starts at 10:00.
````

- The compact block is 400 characters shorter (915 to 515); the server counted 12585 prompt tokens for the control and 11421 for `openclaw/small`. The control offered 14 tools (18197 schema characters); `openclaw/small` offered 13 (15403). In this capture `message` was filtered out before Tool Search and was unavailable, not deferred. The profile also bounds workspace files, so the token difference does not measure the inbound block alone.
- The transcript-only row `#session:close-out-1` is kept in the compact history: `removedSessionMessages` is 0 and `deduplicatedMessages` is 0.
- The `ReplyChain` quote (Carol, message 1002) is kept in compact mode as `Reply target`.
- Second call of each run, the shipped CLI (`openclaw agent --local`), has no inbound history: control `usage.prompt_tokens` 11672, `openclaw/small` 10659.

Cleanup: the capture proxy was stopped after each run, the scratch homes were removed, nothing is left listening on the capture port. The model server was started for these runs and stopped after them.

### Gates and local review

Gates, run one at a time on the Studio, all on `a6e30e0ad36`. The ratchets, madge and `check:changed` ran in a git clone on the Studio (they need `.git`, which the crabbox sync does not carry).

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:core:test` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:extensions` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:scripts` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm format:check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm config:docs:check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm build` (includes the declaration build) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec oxlint` on the files the slice adds or changes | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` | exit 0 |
| `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` and `test/vitest-projects-config.test.ts` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` | exit 0 |
| 14 test files the slice adds or changes (`pnpm test <files>`) | exit 0: 182 passed |
| `pnpm check:changed` (see the note below the table) | exit 1 |

`pnpm check:changed` on this head exits 1. Every failing lane reports only items outside this change: the Plugin SDK surface budget (public entrypoints 164 against 163) fails the same way on base `1601f86def0`; the dead export scan lists `scripts/lib/docker-e2e-watchdog.mjs: parseTimeoutMs`, a file this stack does not touch; the lint lane reports only `max-lines` errors, in files this stack does not touch (CI prints them as warnings). Typecheck, the npm package-lock guard and every ratchet pass in that run. Log: `final-s3-changed.log`.

Local ClawSweeper (native, on a clean checkout, `pnpm install`, committed-range mode, this body passed with `--body-file`), one row per round:

| round | head | P0 to P2 | P3 | tiers overall / proof / patch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r1 | `7eb5a1f7ba8` | P1 transcript-only session rows dropped from compact history | 1 P3 | C / D / C |
| r2 | `8ab09a0ee96` | 3 P2: producer instruction fragments demoted to data in two fallback paths; InboundHistory session rows still dropped | 2 P3 | C / D / C |
| r3 | `790a79f5be7` | 2 P2: `ReplyChain` reply context missing in the compact projection; session rows matched on body text alone | none listed | D / D / C |
| r4, with the earlier body as input | `41360955935` | none | 1 P3 (skip the compact Reply target when the Telegram carrier already quotes it) | C / C / B |
| r5, body-file input (earlier body) | `745a2db4a37` | none | 1 P3 (compact serialization on the private plugin CLI transport; kept, see Decisions) | C / C / B |
| r6, body-file input (an earlier draft of this body) | `a6e30e0ad36` | none | none; 2 low-value test notes (kept, see Decisions); proof tier C because the capture is in-process, not Gateway or worker hosted | C / C / B |

### Hosted review and CI follow-up

Findings of the hosted review of `941587be29c` and of the first CI run. The wrapper inventory, the Codex test project and the message-tool fixtures are fixed in slice 1 (#202517), and the worker test fixture in slice 2 (#204132); both are in this branch. Fixed in this slice, each as its own signed commit:

- `a6e30e0ad36` passes the selected context serialization to the worker prompt (hosted review P2). A worker-hosted turn on `openclaw/small` with both projections used to send the verbose one. The worker prompt test sends a verbose and a compact inbound projection for `openclaw/small` and `openclaw/base` and checks which one the worker receives. Red: without the call argument the small case fails; green: 4 passed.
- The hosted low-value finding about resolver-wrapper cases in the worker test is covered by the same test, which now exercises the worker prompt composition (the profile budget and the serialization) instead of the resolver.
- From the first CI round, unchanged and in this slice's history: `b1bde35608d` re-adds the `hashCliSessionText` import in the CLI profile drift test, `ed36237ee2a` imports `CurrentInboundPromptContext` from its owner (madge), `99ea6365dbf` drops redundant `String(...)` conversions, `6e2d0a5dc2f` drops unused runtime context exports, and `50ef67198e2` moves the compact builder to `inbound-meta.compact.ts` (line-cap ratchet).
- `config/test-lines-allocations/204133-agent-profiles-compact.txt`: current allocation is 943 net test/helper lines above #204132 (stacked total 3,799 against the original main base).

Why the test lines are needed: compact serialization rewrites what the model sees for inbound metadata, history, reply chains and the resumable prompt carrier, and its tests pin each lossy edge: bounded tails and strings, the duplicate rules for transcript-backed rows, the ReplyChain fallback, the carrier on normal, runtime-only and v4 turns, the mark that display stripping removes, and the worker route. Several came from review findings. Each duplicate-rule case uses different roles or bodies, so none restates another.

Not from this change (reproduced on base and main):

- `bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts` (hook token) and `host-credential-execution.test.ts` (2 tests) fail the same way on base `1601f86def0` and on main.
- `thread-lifecycle.native-config.test.ts` fails on base and on main `712ae033851`; it passes on `91dee122ee6`. This PR is not rebased onto that main, so the failure shows here.
- `android-ktlint` and `android-test-wear` could not resolve `com.pinterest.ktlint:ktlint-cli:1.8.0` from Maven; this stack changes no file under `apps/`. A re-run is the fix.

### Decisions

| decision | choice | evidence | how to reverse |
|---|---|---|---|
| Worker serialization | Resolve it from the selected profile and pass it to `prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptContext` | red/green worker prompt test; hosted P2 | revert `a6e30e0ad36` |
| Local ClawSweeper low-value notes: `builtins.test.ts` assertion, `context-serialization/resolve.test.ts` | Kept | `resolve.test.ts` is the original unit test of the resolver (Onur Solmaz); the `builtins.test.ts` assertion pins the documented serialization of `openclaw/small`; the hosted review did not flag either | delete them and lower the record |
| Worker test shape | One test that sends both projections for both profiles | the old cases repeated resolver selection and missed the omission | restore the earlier worker cases |
| Test-line overage | Allocation record 943 after adding the collision regression | stacked test-line ratchet passed | — |
| `agent-tools` preservation tests | Treated as a fixture defect (fixed in #202517), not a flake | the failure reproduces on the slice-1 fixtures and passes with the real `message` tool | revert `dc5e7c84411` in #202517 |
| Local ClawSweeper P3: compact serialization on the private plugin CLI transport | Not changed here | the private transport projects producer fragments on purpose so quoted data cannot become host instructions; compact fragments would need the same escape guarantees and a test on that transport. Only a plugin-executed CLI backend with a group message that has history is affected | follow-up commit in `prompt-context.ts` with a test on that transport |
| Gateway or worker-hosted capture | Exact-head Gateway and local paired worker with deterministic HTTP model endpoint, separately from the in-process Qwen capture | verified on-wire serialization and preserved quote | cloud-worker behavior and model quality not measured |
| Proof design | Same home and message, only `agentProfileId` differs; a transcript-only row and a `ReplyChain` quote in the input | the captured blocks above | n/a, evidence only |

### Credit

Onur Solmaz and Mitchell Etzel authored the original signed commits. Mitchell Etzel is credited on the follow-up.

### Needs a maintainer

- Sign-off on the new `agentprofiles` 0.1.0 dependency (MIT, exact pin, published by the RFC author). Production code imports only its types. This is part of slice 1.
- The security-review and dependency-review approvals on the current head.
- vincentkoc's go-ahead.

prs.title: fix(update): preserve actionable run history and disclose truncation
prs.body:
Fixes #204768

## What Problem This Solves

Late cleanup could push a saved update run over its 16 KiB history budget. The ledger silently removed warnings, so the saved update report and `openclaw update status` could hide recovery instructions for a failed service-definition refresh.

## Fix

- Keep the existing 16 KiB and 128-step bounds. Evict ordinary diagnostic rows and compact optional detail before evicting warnings or failures. Preserve the named lifecycle and owed-finalize receipts used for recovery. Large config-write refusal key inventories can shrink without removing failure advice.
- Count every removed row across repeated writes and surface the count in the saved report and CLI. The marker is an ordinary step, so no SQLite migration or step-wire change is needed. Warning totals count the visible warnings; the omission notice tells the reader when history is incomplete.
- Keep @EnesKartal's named service-refresh warning protection and extend it to the general overflow policy. Target: the 2026.11.10 patch, via `main`.

## Evidence

### Published-driver upgrade (exact PR head)

The actual published npm `v2026.11.10` package (`6ea542fd97e2`, SHA-512 verified against the compatibility inventory) seeded a succeeded two-step SQLite run and drove `openclaw update --tag /proof/artifacts/upgrade-target.tgz --yes --json --no-restart --timeout 120` in a disposable Podman container with `--network none`, an offline npm cache, and synthetic config/state. The target came from a full build of `f1f2c0177d3ee76df9e56985d3e7eae07bd9a8c4` that passed package tarball integrity; `2026.11.11` was set as a test-only target version using the fixture version helper, not fetched as a release. The published updater returned `status: ok`, `2026.11.10 → 2026.11.11`; package install, swap, Doctor, DB migration writes, driver handoff, and cleanup exited 0. No Gateway was restarted.

The installed build reported that exact commit. Four config fields (`gateway.mode`, `gateway.bind`, `update.checkOnStart`, `agents.defaults.workspace`) remained equal, and the saved run ID, trigger, status, before/after fields and **238-byte `steps_json`** were unchanged. Repeating the overflow sequence below via the installed recorder persisted **16,050 bytes / 22 rows**, with one omitted row. The installed CLI printed the omission notice, `SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN`, the failed service-refresh step, and the owed follow-up.

### Base-red regression and recorder replay

The committed regression `keeps actionable rows through late cleanup and counts unavoidable warning overflow` failed on base `cdadcea9047c` as expected (the Browser Relay warning and omission marker were missing) and passed on head.

Separately, I used the real run recorder, reopened its SQLite database, and ran the built CLI in a separate process. Both revisions were built with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`, then exercised via `node openclaw.mjs update status --timeout 65`. Each replay used disposable config and state, loopback-only registry/Gateway settings, and disabled Git network transports.

Reproduction: record the service-refresh warning, a failed step, and `finalize:owed:service-definition`; add 14 UTF-8 Doctor warnings and one disposable diagnostic; finish the run and append three cleanup rows. Both versions start at **15,242 bytes / 19 rows** before cleanup.

| Revision | Persisted after cleanup | `openclaw update status` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base `cdadcea9047c` | 15,775 bytes / 18 rows; service-refresh warning missing; no marker | `15 warnings need attention`; no `SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN` line |
| Head `f1f2c0177d3e` | 16,076 bytes / 22 rows including one marker; warning, failure, and owed step retained | `18 warnings need attention`; `Update history truncated: 1 row omitted.`; `Warning: Failed to refresh the Gateway service definition: SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN; inspect Environment.PATH.` |

Compatibility: the same 538-byte, four-row database produced by the pre-change recorder reopened on head with all four rows unchanged, no marker, and `3 warnings need attention`.

The exact-head packaged replay also printed the owed refresh and the failed step:

```text
Update history truncated: 1 row omitted.
Warning: Failed to refresh the Gateway service definition: SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN; inspect Environment.PATH.
Warning: Gateway service definition refresh is owed: Review the service installation before retrying. Settled when `openclaw update` next refreshes the service definition; `openclaw update repair` rechecks it.
Failed: service-refresh — The installed service definition was not changed.
```

Focused tests: 73 passed across compaction, ledger, and CLI status (142.78 s wrapper wall time). The follow-up conformance checks passed 24 tests across the trusted-wrapper import closure and SQLite interruption store (226.38 s wrapper wall time). Together they cover both bounds, late cleanup, warning overflow, owed/failure retention, oversized Doctor refusal inventories, the pre-timing SQLite fixture, and marker accounting on a step-only write. Targeted formatting and lint passed.
