prs.title: feat: pick an Agent Profile automatically from a model's size
prs.body:
Part of #204354. Related: openclaw/rfcs#18 (Agent Profiles RFC)

## What Problem This Solves

A local model with a small context window gets the same system prompt as a hosted model. On a 32K window that prompt fills about 40% of the window before the user says anything. Lean mode (`experimental.localModelLean`) trims only some of it and cannot be set per model size. Agent Profiles (RFC 18) give each agent a named profile that sets the workspace budget, context serialization and tool surface.

This is slice 2 of 3 of the Agent Profiles work, split from one 90-commit branch so each part can be reviewed on its own. Stacked on slice 1. Retarget to `main` after slice 1 merges.

Dependencies: depends on #202517 (slice 1: the resolver and `agentProfileId`).

## This slice

Original signed slice: `f6a84ab8cb4..adc667c7b8c` (14 commits: 1 by Onur Solmaz and 13 by Mitchell Etzel). Current head `705e733030e7` appends the diagnostics fix, test cleanup, and matching docs from #202517 without rewriting the signed commits. To inspect this slice against the updated core tree, use `git diff 179a52a0d7d5 705e733030e7`.

This slice adds selection by total parameter count behind `agentProfileId: "auto"`. It needs slice 1.

- Size classes (tiny, small, medium, large) from total parameters, as the RFC defines them. Mixture-of-experts models count total parameters. A model name is never read.
- Sources of the count: provider discovery for Ollama and LM Studio, `models[].modelSizeClass` in config, the model catalog, and llama-server's `/v1/models` `meta.n_params`.
- Size metadata is passed through the workspace, harness, worker, Codex and catalog routes so `auto` selects the same profile everywhere, including the `/context` and prompt export route, which reads the size from the prepared catalog entry of the inspected model.
- `--agent-profile auto` on `openclaw agent exec`.

## User Impact

- Nothing changes until an operator sets `agentProfileId: "auto"`.
- With `auto`, a model that reports 20B or fewer total parameters selects `openclaw/small`. Larger models use `openclaw/base`.
- A model that reports no count stays on `openclaw/base` until the operator sets `modelSizeClass`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Operators of small local models should not have to name a profile per agent. `auto` reads the total parameter count the provider or the config reports, never a model name, and an unknown size keeps `openclaw/base`.

Config and API surface: this slice adds the value `auto` for `agentProfileId`, `models[].modelSizeClass` (and `parameterCount` from llama-server discovery) so a size can be set where a provider reports none, and `--agent-profile auto`. The class cannot be derived without a place to state it for providers that report no count.

## Evidence

### Diagnostics follow-up on `705e733030e7`

`/context list` and `/context detail` now show the Agent Profile and selection source saved by the last run. Older reports without that data stay unchanged. Both new cases failed before the fix on `adc667c7b8c`; all 22 context-report tests passed after it. The final local integrated stack passed 76 focused tests. These are local results, not fresh hosted CI; the llama.cpp capture below describes the original implementation.

### Runtime output

`auto` selection at this slice, on build `011149c8faf` (`pnpm build`; the tree of this head differs from the build only in `agent-profile-config.test.ts` and the allocation records), against a real Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on llama.cpp, one request at a time, through a capture proxy that records every request body and server `usage` block. Throwaway `OPENCLAW_HOME`, no Gateway, no `modelSizeClass` and no `parameterCount` in user config: the size comes only from llama-server discovery. Hostnames, IPs, ports, paths and session ids are redacted.

Discovery on the same server, run through `discoverLlamaServer` at the build:

```text
{"kind":"success","models":[{"id":"qwen3-8b-q8_0","parameterCount":8190735360,"contextWindow":32768}]}
```

Config: `agents.defaults.agentProfileId = "auto"`, one `models.providers.llama-cpp` entry with only a `baseUrl` and `api` (no model row), agent model `llama-cpp/qwen3-8b-q8_0`. Workspace files: the default templates plus a 7,200-character `AGENTS.md` and a 1,453-character `IDENTITY.md`.

```text
selection (system prompt report of the stored turn):
  agentProfile = {"id": "openclaw/small", "selectionSource": "model-size"}
  workspaceContext = {"totalMaxChars": 11500, "rawChars": 11255, "injectedChars": 10825, "truncatedChars": 430}
  files: agents 7200->7200 (cap 7500), soul 1526->1526 (cap 2000), identity 1453->1023 (cap 1024, truncated), user 1076->1076 (cap 2000)

path A: inbound turn through getReplyFromConfig (the entry every channel plugin reaches), nonce req-auto-dynamic-mwu0h7i0, proxy call #4
  server call: status=200 model=qwen3-8b-q8_0 messages=3 tools=13 tool_schema_chars=15403 system_chars=29935 usage.prompt_tokens=11509 completion_tokens=2 finish=stop reply="pong"

path B: shipped CLI, openclaw agent --local --json, same home, config and proxy, proxy call #8
  agentProfile = {"id": "openclaw/small", "selectionSource": "model-size"}
  server call: status=200 model=qwen3-8b-q8_0 messages=3 tools=13 tool_schema_chars=15392 system_chars=29724 usage.prompt_tokens=10649 completion_tokens=2 finish=stop reply="pong"
```

`auto` resolves `openclaw/small` with `selectionSource: model-size` on both paths, from the 8,190,735,360 total parameters llama-server reported (class `small`: over 1B, up to 20B). The workspace budget of the profile is applied: `IDENTITY.md` is cut to its 1,024-character cap and the report counts the 430 truncated characters. The Gateway lifecycle owner is replaced by one `GatewayScheduler` bound to the session MCP runtime for path A; nothing else is stubbed.

Cleanup: the capture proxy was stopped after the run, the scratch home was removed, nothing is left listening on the capture port. The model server was started for these runs and stopped after them.

### Gates and local review

Gates, run one at a time on the Studio, all on `adc667c7b8c`. The ratchets, madge and `check:changed` ran in a git clone on the Studio (they need `.git`, which the crabbox sync does not carry).

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:core:test` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:extensions` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:scripts` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm format:check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm config:docs:check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm build` (includes the declaration build) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec oxlint` on the files the slice adds or changes | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` | exit 0 |
| `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` and `test/vitest-projects-config.test.ts` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` | exit 0 |
| 23 test files the slice adds or changes (`pnpm test <files>`) | exit 0: 284 passed, 1 skipped |
| `pnpm check:changed` (see the note below the table) | exit 1 |

`pnpm check:changed` on this head exits 1. Every failing lane reports only items outside this change: the Plugin SDK surface budget (public entrypoints 164 against 163) fails the same way on base `1601f86def0`; the dead export scan lists `scripts/lib/docker-e2e-watchdog.mjs: parseTimeoutMs`, a file this stack does not touch; the lint lane reports only `max-lines` errors, in files this stack does not touch (CI prints them as warnings). Typecheck, the npm package-lock guard and every ratchet pass in that run. Log: `final-s2-changed.log`.

Local ClawSweeper (native, on a clean checkout, `pnpm install`, committed-range mode, this body passed with `--body-file`), one row per round:

| round | head | P0 to P2 | P3 | tiers overall / proof / patch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r1 | `27c94260833` | none | 1 P3 | C / D / B |
| r2 | `ce7372c5981` | none | none | F / F / B |
| r3, with the earlier body as input | `070a441d92c` | none | 1 P3 (size metadata for the `/context` and export prompt bundle) | C / B / B |
| r4, body-file input (earlier body; the first attempt failed with a runner error and was run again) | `011149c8faf` | none | none; 1 low-value test (fixed in this head) | C / B / B |
| r5, body-file input (an earlier draft of this body) | `adc667c7b8c` | none | none; 1 low-value test note (kept, see Decisions) | C / B / B |

### Hosted review and CI follow-up

Findings of the hosted review of `d00e03f758f` and of the first CI run. The wrapper inventory, the Codex test project, the compaction owner and the shared low-value tests are fixed in slice 1 (#202517), which this branch contains. Fixed in this slice, each as its own signed commit:

- `d0131592b84` moves `MODEL_SIZE_CLASSES` and `ModelSizeClass` to `model-config-vocabulary.ts` next to `MODEL_APIS`, re-exported from `types.models.ts`. This breaks the cycle `zod-schema.core.ts -> types.models.ts -> zod-schema.core.ts` that the architecture check reported. `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 1 cycle before, 0 after.
- `09df1e4938e` selects the profile of the inspected prompt (`/context`, prompt export) from the prepared catalog entry of the inspected model, so a model that `auto` selects as small is also shown as small there (hosted review P3). The build found a `string | undefined` argument in this commit; it is fixed in the same commit.
- `56539a05136` covers size-class selection in direct compaction through the compaction consumer.
- `443fec83d7c` covers the worker prompt profile through the worker turn and replaces the size-like-name negative control, which passed even if `auto` inferred a size from a name. The model row of its fixture is complete so the test typechecks.
- `fe72a034194` validates the model size class at the config schema boundary instead of casting `huge` to `never` in a unit test, and keeps the positive check of `openclaw/base`, `openclaw/small` and `auto` in `agent-profile-config.test.ts` instead of the low-value "no standalone `contextSerialization` key" case that local ClawSweeper flagged.
- `581d38740b8` folds the two small-size-class Tool Search cases into one table.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/204132-agent-profiles-auto.txt`: current allocation is 885 net test/helper lines above #202517 (stacked total 2,856 against the original main base).

Why the test lines are needed: size selection reaches the profile through independent routes, and each has one regression test: embedded attempt (primary, fallback, catalog row), CLI runner capabilities, the prompt a worker turn receives, direct compaction, prompt inspection, workspace routes and catalog projections, and llama-server discovery of the total parameter count. The class resolver has one table test for its precedence rules and the models schema rejects an unknown class. No test restates another.

Not from this change (reproduced on base and main):

- `bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts` (hook token) and `host-credential-execution.test.ts` (2 tests) fail the same way on base `1601f86def0` and on main.
- `thread-lifecycle.native-config.test.ts` fails on base and on main `712ae033851`; it passes on `91dee122ee6`. This PR is not rebased onto that main, so the failure shows here.
- `android-ktlint` and `android-test-wear` could not resolve `com.pinterest.ktlint:ktlint-cli:1.8.0` from Maven; this stack changes no file under `apps/`. A re-run is the fix.

### Decisions

| decision | choice | evidence | how to reverse |
|---|---|---|---|
| Size vocabulary location | A schema-independent leaf, re-exported from `types.models.ts` | madge red 1 cycle, green 0; no caller changes | revert `d0131592b84` |
| Prompt inspection size source | The prepared catalog entry of the inspected model | hosted P3; test red before, green after | revert `09df1e4938e` |
| Invalid size class and config surface test | Reject it in the schema, not in a cast unit test; restore the positive accept check, drop the absent-key case | hosted low-value finding and the local ClawSweeper low-value finding; schema test red/green | revert `fe72a034194` |
| Tool Search size cases | One table | two cases exercised the same decision | revert `581d38740b8` |
| Worker test | Test through the worker turn, no name-based control | the old control passed under a wrong implementation | revert `443fec83d7c` |
| Test-line overage | Allocation record 885 after the follow-up | stacked test-line ratchet passed | — |
| Local ClawSweeper low-value note: `attempt-tool-prepare.agent-profile.test.ts` | Kept primary/fallback; removed the catalog-entry case in the follow-up | That case supplied a size class directly and did not exercise catalog projection | — |
| Proof source of the size | Discovery only (no size in user config) | proof run, `selectionSource: model-size` | n/a, evidence only |

### Credit

Onur Solmaz and Mitchell Etzel authored the original signed commits. Mitchell Etzel is credited on the follow-up.

### Needs a maintainer

- Sign-off on the new `agentprofiles` 0.1.0 dependency (MIT, exact pin, published by the RFC author). Production code imports only its types. This is part of slice 1.
- The security-review and dependency-review approvals on the current head.
- vincentkoc's go-ahead.

prs.title: feat(providers): add XingChen-AGI provider plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds the **XingChen-AGI** provider plugin for OpenClaw, exposing the **Xing4.1-Preview** model (China Telecom AI Technology Co., Ltd.) through its OpenAI-compatible API.

- Provider id: `xingchen-agi`
- Package: `@openclaw/xingchen-agi-provider`
- Auth env var: `XINGCHEN_API_KEY`
- API: `openai-completions`
- Base URL: `https://api-maas.teleai.com.cn/v1`
- Default model: `xing4.1-preview`
- Also published as a community plugin on ClawHub: `@xingchen-agi/xingchen-agi-provider@1.0.0`, source-linked to `XingChen-AGI/openclaw-xingchen-agi-provider` (community channel).

## What Problem This Solves

An OpenClaw user who wants to use Xing4.1-Preview currently has to hand-configure an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and model metadata. This PR adds a ready-made provider plugin plus documentation, so the model becomes selectable as `xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview` once the plugin is installed and `XINGCHEN_API_KEY` is provided.

## What's included

- `extensions/xingchen-agi/` - provider plugin (`index.ts`, `openclaw.plugin.json`, `package.json`)
- `docs/providers/xingchen-agi.md` - provider docs page
- `docs/providers/index.md` - registered in the provider directory

## Manifest

Uses the current provider schema (`setup.providers[].envVars`, declarative `modelCatalog` with `discovery: static`) and the `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-entry` SDK entry point.

## Model

| Model ref | Input | Context | Max output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview` | text | 1,024,000 | 128,000 |

- Reasoning: supported (deep-thinking mode; no `reasoning_effort` tiers exposed)
- Pricing (USD / 1M tokens): list price input $0.225 / cached input $0.01125 / output $0.90; limited-time offer at 20% of list through 2026-12-20 — input $0.045 / cached input $0.00225 / output $0.18. The catalog fields carry the offer price currently in effect (see https://xingchen-agi.github.io/pricing/).

## Verification

- Endpoint reachable over HTTPS from outside mainland China (tested: TCP 443 / TLS / HTTP 200, median latency ~120 ms)
- Auth is standard `Authorization: Bearer` (unauthenticated request returns a business 401, not a signature error)

## Evidence

Validation was run end-to-end on OpenClaw `2026.11.3` (`847611d`), Windows, Node `v24.18.0`, with the plugin from this PR installed. All output is redacted (the API key is masked as `sk-****`). Two layers are covered: local one-shot inference through the plugin, and a full Gateway agent turn using a saved credential profile with the standard plugin set loaded.

### Real behavior proof

Verified end-to-end against OpenClaw `2026.11.3` (`847611d`) on Windows, Node `v24.18.0`. The plugin from this PR was installed in link mode, the model catalog resolved, credentials resolved from `XINGCHEN_API_KEY`, and real one-shot model turns returned responses.

**1. Plugin installed and enabled**

```
$ openclaw plugins install --link ./extensions/xingchen-agi --accept-capabilities
Saved for the next Gateway start

$ openclaw plugins list
@openclaw/xingchen-agi-provider | xingchen-agi | openclaw | enabled | ...\extensions\xingchen-agi\index.ts | 2026.11.3
```

**2. Model present in the catalog**

```
$ openclaw models list --provider xingchen-agi --all --plain
xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview
```

**3. Credentials resolve for the provider**

```
$ openclaw models status --json
  "provider": "xingchen-agi",
  "effective": { "kind": "env", "detail": "sk-****" },
  "env": { "value": "sk-****", "source": "env: XINGCHEN_API_KEY" }
```

**4. Real inference through the plugin**

```
$ openclaw infer model run --model xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview --local --json \
    --prompt "Reply with exactly this string and nothing else: XINGCHEN-OK-2026"
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "model.run",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "xingchen-agi",
  "model": "xing4.1-preview",
  "outputs": [ { "text": "XINGCHEN-OK-2026", "mediaUrl": null } ]
}
```

```
$ openclaw infer model run --model xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview --local --json \
    --prompt "A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 8 run away. How many sheep are left? Answer with just the number."
{
  "ok": true,
  "provider": "xingchen-agi",
  "model": "xing4.1-preview",
  "outputs": [ { "text": "8", "mediaUrl": null } ]
}
```

### Gateway agent turn (saved credentials, standard plugin set)

Beyond the local runs above, a full **Gateway** agent turn was exercised with the API key **saved as an auth profile** (not an environment variable) and the standard plugin set loaded.

**1. Credential saved as a profile**

```
$ openclaw models auth paste-api-key --provider xingchen-agi
Auth profile: xingchen-agi:manual (xingchen-agi/api_key)

$ openclaw models auth list
Agent: main
Profiles:
- xingchen-agi:manual [xingchen-agi/api_key]

$ openclaw models status --json
  "provider": "xingchen-agi",
  "effective": { "kind": "profiles", "detail": "~\\.openclaw\\state\\openclaw.sqlite" },
  "profiles": { "count": 1, "apiKey": 1, "labels": [ "xingchen-agi:manual=sk-****" ] }
```

(No `XINGCHEN_API_KEY` environment variable was set during this run.)

**2. Gateway running**

```
$ openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured
[gateway] ready

$ openclaw gateway health
Gateway Health
OK (8ms)
```

**3. Agent turn through the Gateway**

```
$ openclaw agent --model xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview --json \
    --message "Reply with exactly this string and nothing else: XINGCHEN-GATEWAY-OK"
{
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": "completed",
  "result": {
    "payloads": [ { "text": "XINGCHEN-GATEWAY-OK", "mediaUrl": null } ],
    "meta": {
      "agentMeta": {
        "provider": "xingchen-agi",
        "model": "xing4.1-preview",
        "agentHarnessId": "openclaw",
        "credentialSource": { "kind": "profile" }
      }
    },
    "executionTrace": {
      "winnerProvider": "xingchen-agi",
      "winnerModel": "xing4.1-preview",
      "attempts": [ { "provider": "xingchen-agi", "model": "xing4.1-preview", "result": "success", "stage": "assistant" } ],
      "fallbackUsed": false
    },
    "requestShaping": { "authMode": "auth-profile" }
  }
}
```

Gateway log confirming the turn was served over the gateway transport:

```
[ws] -> res agent 1342ms runId=909023f7-bb83-48cc-96ef-6b0968d56cf9
[agents/agent-command] [agent] run 909023f7-bb83-48cc-96ef-6b0968d56cf9 ended with stopReason=stop
```

The run executed with the normal plugin set loaded (42 of 70 built-in plugins enabled, 23 skills and the standard tool surface present), not an isolated single-plugin environment.

prs.title: fix: skip unused model rows during credential refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A credential refresh sends a copy of every prepared model row to the catalog worker. For an installation with many configured models, that copy adds work to every refresh even though the worker returns the credentials before reading those rows.

## User Impact

Credential refreshes transfer less data between threads. Catalog requests still receive the full configured inventory, including when they immediately follow a refresh on the same worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The parent already knows which operation it is sending. It can send empty catalog facts for an auth refresh while preserving the original prepared rows for catalog requests. Credential inputs, worker registration, and the catalog request format stay intact.

## Evidence

Measured complete task payloads with `node:v8.serialize` around the real parent `loadAuth` and `loadCatalog` entry points, using synthetic model definitions and a transport that acknowledges worker registration. The table shows serialized bytes on a new worker and a worker with an acknowledged registration.

| Configured models | Auth, new worker | Auth, reused worker | Catalog, new / reused |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 1,397 → 1,059 | 1,255 → 917 | 1,402 / 1,260 in both versions |
| 1,000 | 362,042 → 24,038 | 361,899 → 23,895 | 362,047 / 361,904 in both versions |

The 1,000-model fixture saved 338,004 serialized bytes per refresh. Process RSS was outside this measurement.

The integration regression uses the real worker in the order auth → catalog → auth. It checks credential values, catalog discovery, and the configured model IDs in each actual transfer. Independent source review covered this interleaving and worker registration reuse. Local autoreview (P0–P2) reported no findings on `427900b2..3704e3a2`. Pinned formatting passed. The [real worker regression passed on Node and Bun](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45750472290/job/139677336784) and all five core test-type jobs passed. This internal payload change leaves package boundaries and exports intact. The CI planner skipped the full artifact build.

Two other jobs failed in that run. The dependency check reported the same 15 unused exports as the [frozen parent](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45749158542/job/139672857486). A [Bun snapshot-retention test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45750472290/job/139677336812) retained generations A and B. The [unmodified parent](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45749158542/job/139672859054) and the [ready PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45751366584/job/139680196019) reproduced the same expected `[B]`, received `[A,B]` result. That test constructs a catalog request directly and calls the pool itself. The retention issue is tracked separately in [#205737](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205737).

prs.title: fix(codex): plugin tool denies disable unrelated native apps
prs.body:
Related: https://community.openclaw.ai/t/denying-intent-disables-the-native-codex-github-plugin/423

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native Codex hosted apps disappearing when an agent denies OpenClaw-owned memory plugin tools such as Memory Core `intent`.

## User Impact

Users can deny the audited Memory Core, LanceDB, and Memory Wiki tools without losing unrelated native apps such as GitHub. The named tools remain denied on newly admitted turns. Unknown or unaudited tools, restrictive allowlists, wildcards, and mixed unsafe policies still isolate the native surface. No configuration migration is needed. This change does not promise retroactive revocation of an already-admitted turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared harness policy now recognizes explicitly audited plugin tool identities from the existing configuration- and workspace-scoped manifest metadata, rather than requiring every safe deny to be a core tool. One owner resolves the known audited set for both restriction classification and native-enforcement projection. Manifest ownership alone never grants an exemption or tool execution.

The Codex audit covers the adjacent OpenClaw memory-store and wiki tool families, not just `intent`. An unrelated synthetic plugin regression proves that the mechanism is generic; undeclared and unaudited controls remain restricted. These stores and vaults are separate from Codex native memory and goals. No new state store, cache, permission setting, or plugin manifest field is introduced.

## Evidence

- Current head `594b08d48c89` integrates `bf3729e4` and resolves the conflict without changing main’s model-less policy behavior. **115 focused tests passed**, including the production Codex dynamic-tool bridge: an authenticated owner’s `intent` list succeeds before tightening, and a fresh admitted turn rejects the previously registered callback after the deny. The fixture uses production host capabilities, not a hosted connector. Local independent autoreview did not launch under the checkout/scratch isolation requirements. See [exact-head checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197030/checks).

### Loopback behavior proof (head `da692a1eef7f`, base `cdadcea9047c`)

[Full proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197030#issuecomment-7182040719). The setup was a disposable loopback Gateway with the real codex app-server binary from node_modules (`@openai/codex` 0.172.0), plus a loopback scripted OpenAI-compatible model. A test-only stdio tee recorded the real `thread/start` params and sent read-only `mcpServerStatus/list` and `mcpServer/tool/call` probes on the same thread. The stand-in for the hosted GitHub app was a native Codex MCP server named `github`, a loopback stub. Restricted turns gate it exactly like hosted apps.

- **Base, `deny: ["intent"]`:** `thread/start` sends `features.apps: false` and `mcp_servers.github.enabled: false`. The `github` server is `disabled`, and `github.get_repo` fails with `unknown MCP server 'github'`.
- **Head, `deny: ["intent"]`:** no restriction is sent. `github` is connected and `get_repo` returns data. `intent` is absent from `dynamicTools`; with no deny, the positive control includes it.
- **Head controls:** `deny: ["intent*"]` and `deny: ["proof_unknown_tool"]` still restrict, just like base.
- **Exact-head checks:** all required checks passed, and focused tests passed (17 policy + 77 Codex dynamic-tool bridge).
- **Already-admitted turns:** a callback admitted before a deny reload is outside this PR. The per-turn tool map is identical on base and head. The next admitted turn rejects it (bridge test), and the docs state next-turn semantics.

### Prior-head evidence

- The exact and normalized `intent` policy regressions fail on base because native apps are restricted. The PR reports 145 passing focused policy, environment, harness-selection and prompt-prefix tests, with 31 of those cases rerun after the final helper rename. Scoped type, lint, formatting and diff checks passed; the aggregate test-line ratchet retained seven inherited overage lines. Independent local static review reported no actionable findings.
- Native source was inspected at Codex `rust-v0.164.0` (`6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9`), including the dynamic-tool handler and the native memory and goals tool definitions.
- [Real macOS base/head proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197030#issuecomment-6803150138): with only `intent` denied, the base lost the unrelated native GitHub app and the candidate returned real public GitHub metadata. An allowed native intent persisted successfully as a positive control. The mixed `intent` + `exec` deny still restricted native apps. The `tools.invoke` denial left the relevant rows unchanged, but that path is separate from the native callback bridge.
- [Later retained-turn result on the same head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197030#issuecomment-6806960012): a callback from a turn already under way before config reload persisted a write after reload; GitHub remained usable. That rules out a claim of immediate revocation for an in-flight turn. It did not exercise a new turn admitted after reload. The earlier safe-successor result and old-thread ownership refusal do not fill this gap.
- **Not covered:** a credentialed hosted-connector replay of a newly admitted turn after a deny. The loopback proof above covers turn-start admission on a real Gateway and app-server. The bridge test covers next-turn rejection. Immediate revocation of an already-admitted turn is out of scope.

Contributor credit: Jacqueline Henriksen requested the repair; Saul_Burgos supplied the original community report.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: improve(auth): avoid copying shell key lists during provider discovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw scans providers for credentials, each provider lookup copied the list of keys imported from the login shell into an array and a set. Even providers with no matching environment variable paid for both copies.

## User Impact

Provider discovery checks shell provenance only for a selected environment key. Credential priority, shell and environment labels, and the ordered list reported by `models status` stay the same. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shell environment owner already knows which keys it imported. Callers that need one membership check can ask it directly. Callers that display or export the full list continue to receive an independent snapshot.

## Evidence

- Measured the production scan and auth lookup function bodies over 108 prepared lookup keys from bundled manifests, aliases and core candidates, plus a synthetic setup provider included in that total. An all-environment-miss scan went from 108 array copies and 108 sets to zero of each, with zero provenance checks. With two matching keys, the new scan performed two checks, preserving the credential map, source labels and setup fallback. A mixed-origin pair of AWS variables retained its combined shell label.
- CI passed the [shell-env lifecycle tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45750840855/job/139678569730), [models status tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45750840855/job/139678569712), and [all six auth-planning, alias and fallback tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45749859032/job/139675545678). The latter link is from the first head. The correction touched only a status-test mock and retired its old ratchet exception. The [corrected-head mock-export ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45750840855/job/139678569261) passed.
- The first draft dispatch encountered a Gateway teardown error after the compaction hot-reload integration test. The same Bun test ran successfully in 41.129 seconds on the corrected head. The draft also reported exactly the same 15 unused-export file/symbol pairs as its base. [Original teardown failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45749859032/job/139675545550) · [corrected-head pass](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45750840855/job/139678569698) · [draft dependency job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45749859032/job/139675546253) · [base dependency job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45749158542/job/139672857486)
- Independent semantic review passed. Autoreview covered the full `427900b2d539..38aad90e6666` range through P2 and reported no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper lacked its TypeScript dependency, so the hosted fallback applies.
- These measurements count temporary data structures. Gateway RSS and OOM behavior were outside the measurement.

prs.title: fix(onboard): wait for a Gateway this run started under --skip-health
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw onboard --install-daemon --skip-health` installs and starts the Gateway service, then skips the startup wait and judges the fresh service from one 1.5 s probe. On a host where the Gateway binds slower than that, setup reports the Gateway it just installed as unreachable: the Control UI link is hidden, the outro is the "Gateway not detected" recovery summary that suggests restarting the service, and the TUI opens in `{ local: true }` mode. `--skip-health` should skip the health RPC, not the readiness of a service this run started.

Closes #201394.

## User Impact

A first-time `--install-daemon --skip-health` setup waits for the service it started, then shows the dashboard link and ends with the normal completion outro instead of a false recovery prompt, and the TUI connects to the Gateway instead of running local. `--skip-health` still skips the health RPC, and runs that awaited nothing (no service started this run, e.g. `--skip-daemon`) keep the single-probe fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The readiness block in `finalizeSetupWizard` is guarded by `!opts.skipHealth || sessionGateway`, so `--skip-health` with a fresh service install never reaches `waitForGatewayReachable`; the later single `probeGatewayReachable` then decides the verdict with `timeoutMs = max(1500, ...)`.

The decision is now planned from the service outcome in a sibling module (`setup.finalize-gateway-readiness.ts`, keeping `setup.finalize.ts` under its line cap): a Gateway this run started (`status === "ready"` and not reused) is awaited with `resolveGatewayStartupTiming()` even under `--skip-health`, and only a run that awaited nothing keeps the single-probe fallback. The health RPC itself stays gated on `!opts.skipHealth`. This matches the non-interactive path, which already waits with the startup timing whenever it installed the daemon.

`OnboardOptions.skipHealth` is optional, so the helper takes `boolean | undefined` and normalizes it (`skipHealth === true`); the earlier revision compared the optional value directly and failed strict type checking for every onboarding caller that omits the flag.

## Evidence

### Shipped `openclaw onboard` CLI, before / after / control

The real CLI was spawned through a Windows ConPTY (`node-pty`), so `process.stdin.isTTY` is true and the classic wizard runs its prompts; defaults were accepted with Enter. Per leg: wiped state dir, no service installed, port 28793 free, isolated `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=proofcli201394`. Only `src/wizard/setup.finalize.ts` and the new readiness helper differ between the legs.

```
node openclaw.mjs onboard --classic --flow quickstart --install-daemon --skip-health
  --skip-ui --skip-channels --skip-skills --skip-search --skip-bootstrap --accept-risk
  --auth-choice skip --gateway-auth token --gateway-port 28793 --agent-name main
```

| Leg | Service | Output | Elapsed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before (`setup.finalize.ts` from main) | login item installed at +27.9 s | `Gateway not detected yet. The managed Scheduled Task did not become reachable after setup.` at +39.0 s | 40 s |
| After (this branch) | installed at +25.1 s | `Gateway: reachable` at +38.9 s, then `Onboarding complete. Use the dashboard link above to control OpenClaw.` at +47.7 s | 49 s |
| Control (this branch, `--skip-daemon`) | nothing started | `Gateway not detected yet. Start now: openclaw --profile proofcli201394 gateway run` at +19.9 s | 21 s |

The before run's Gateway log records `{"message":"gateway ready"}` at 23:28:06.697 local, while that onboarding process had already exited at 23:27:58.975: the service was ready 7.7 s after setup declared it unreachable, which is the false negative this PR removes. The after run waits (`Gateway: reachable` at +38.9 s) and ends in the normal outro; the control still fails closed without spending the startup budget.

![Shipped onboarding CLI before/after/control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/201394/proof-cli-onboard.png)

### In-process rig (same finalizer, scripted prompter)

Earlier evidence, still valid: the finalizer invoked directly with a real per-user Windows service install (`OPENCLAW_PROFILE=proof201394`, port 28793), only the wizard source differing between legs.

| Run | Wizard source | Service action | Outro | Elapsed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before | `upstream/main` | real install (per-user Startup login item) | `Gateway not detected yet. The managed Scheduled Task did not become reachable after setup.` | 16 s |
| After | this branch | same install | `Onboarding complete. Use the dashboard link above to control OpenClaw.` | 50 s |
| Control | this branch | `--skip-daemon` (nothing started) | `Gateway not detected yet. Start now: openclaw --profile proof201394 gateway run` | 69 s |

After the before leg's "not detected" summary, `127.0.0.1:28793` was already LISTENING, the same false negative seen through the shipped CLI above.

![Live before/after onboarding readiness on the isolated Windows profile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/201394/live-onboard.png)

![Verbatim rig log excerpts for the three legs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/201394/live-logs.png)

### Tests and gates

- `src/wizard/setup.finalize-gateway-readiness.test.ts` (new in this revision): the plan is covered directly instead of through the wizard run — `skipHealth` `false` and omitted both await, `--skip-health` with a reused service probes once, `--skip-health` with a service installed this run still awaits with the startup budget, and the session gateway awaits. 5/5 pass.
- Merged `upstream/main` at `0fa34123b322`. Upstream #205574 deleted the `readiness budget after service <action>` permutation from `src/wizard/setup.finalize.test.ts` as low-value coverage, so this branch now leaves that file byte-identical to `main` and the fix is covered by the dedicated unit test above.
- The two remaining failures in `src/wizard/setup.finalize.test.ts` (`passes physical catalog routes…`, `skips the doomed hatch seed message…`) fail identically when that file runs against `upstream/main`'s own `setup.finalize.ts` on this Windows checkout.
- `src/wizard/setup.test.ts` has one pre-existing failure on this checkout (`re-prompts for auth when applyAuthChoice requests retry selection`), reproduced with the upstream `setup.finalize.ts`; the other 28 pass.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` exits 0 on this merged revision (it flagged the optional `skipHealth` argument before the fix).
- `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the three changed files.

## What was not tested

- Prompt answers are the wizard defaults accepted with Enter through a real ConPTY, not hand-typed; nothing else about the shipped CLI run is simulated. The pty capture mis-decodes box-drawing glyphs (cosmetic only; the ASCII lines quoted above are verbatim).
- Provider/model auth is skipped (`--auth-choice skip`), so onboarding makes no real model request.
- Only the Windows per-user Startup login item was exercised; no macOS launchd or Linux systemd run.
- The `sessionGateway` (container user-systemd) path keeps its existing wait; only the service-outcome decision moved out of `setup.finalize.ts`.

prs.title: fix: preserve Unicode when shortening Android attachment names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Android, picking a photo with a long filename could leave a broken character immediately before `.jpg` in the chat preview and the outgoing attachment name. A provider name containing 127 ASCII letters followed by 📷 reproduced the issue.

## User Impact

A character that fits at the end of a shortened filename stays intact. If it would cross the limit, the name ends immediately before that character. The photo keeps its usual JPEG extension and image content.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attachment reader shortened the provider name at 128 UTF-16 units, which could separate the two units of a supplementary character. It now uses the Android app’s existing surrogate-safe shortening helper at the same point in filename sanitization.

## Evidence

- The new provider-backed test failed on the parent. The 127-letter prefix left an unmatched high surrogate. With the fix, that prefix is followed directly by `.jpg`, and a 126-letter prefix keeps the entire 📷. All 17 tests in `ChatImageCodecTest` passed in the focused Robolectric run.
- A synthetic photo provider exercised 22 picker journeys through Compose and a locally captured `chat.send` envelope. The expected filenames, pixel markers, dimensions and order matched for all 26 images, including four two-image selections. All 17 repeated parent controls produced identical JPEG bytes.
- These local checks used Robolectric API 34 with native graphics and an inert send sink. Physical-device picking, real photos, live delivery and the full Gradle Android suite were outside the local proof.

prs.title: fix: keep side chat emoji selections whole near the text limit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Near the 400-unit limit in Side chat, choosing the face exhaling emoji from the suggestions for `:f` could replace the shortcode with 😮 or with 😮 followed by an invisible joiner. Ask received that partial emoji.

## User Impact

When the whole selected emoji fits, the composer inserts it in one edit. When it is too long, the shortcode, surrounding text and caret stay in place. Undo still reverses the preceding typing. The primary composer continues to accept the full emoji without a length limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser can truncate an editing command at the textarea’s UTF-16 limit and still report success. The picker now checks the size of the complete catalog value against the space available after replacing the token, before changing the selection or issuing the editing command.

## Evidence

- In Chromium, selected `:face_exhaling:` by clicking and pressing Enter in a mounted Side chat. With two, three or four UTF-16 units available, the original composer inserted a partial emoji. The fix preserved the literal `:f`, selection and suffix, and emitted no input event. Undo and Redo matched the same edit history with no option selected.
- A five-unit exact fit inserted the full 😮‍💨. A shorter emoji, a roomy Side chat question and an unlimited main-chat draft also accepted the complete option. Native clipboard paste retained its ordinary browser behavior.
- One new regression failed on the parent and its exact-fit control passed. All 122 tests passed across the emoji composer, Side chat rail and New Session composer suites. Scoped formatting and type-aware lint passed.
- The browser used a synthetic Gateway and captured the Side chat Ask callback locally. Message delivery and persisted answers were outside this proof.

prs.title: fix: honor opt-in heartbeat busy guard for agent lanes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an operator opts a heartbeat agent into `heartbeat.skipWhenBusy`, queued or active work for that same agent in a canonical `session:` or `nested:` lane should make the wake skip; the previous behavior did not apply that guard to these sibling lanes.

## User Impact

With the opt-in enabled, heartbeats now honor the busy guard for same-agent work across those lanes. `false` or an unset option preserves baseline behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change restores the opt-in guard by reading existing command-lane totals. Doctor migration preserves the option while handling unrelated retired configuration. The implementation adds no queue reservation or atomic queue lock.

## Evidence

- Focused source tests: 587 tests across six shards passed.
- Independent runtime, config, Doctor, and active-queue checks: 48/48 passed.

prs.title: fix: let Knowledge scribes read Slack on a schedule when set up from a remote Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Learn from Slack set up from a remote Control UI never read Slack. The Scribes page asked the agent, in a chat turn, to create the scribe's automation. A remote Control UI turn records the automation as account-owned with an unknown creator origin, and scheduled Slack reads require a matching origin, so every run failed with "Scheduled slack:channel-list requires matching recorded creator origin." Re-saving the tool cap from the same kind of turn could not fix it. Runs still reported `ok`, so the failure only showed in the scribe's status line.

## User Impact

- An administrator sets up, repairs, reschedules and updates ongoing scribes from the Scribes page, and their scheduled runs can read channel plugins such as Slack. Granola and consolidation runs keep working as before.
- A scribe still on an automation that an earlier version created through a chat turn shows **Upgrade available**. Its detail explains why and offers **Upgrade automation…**. Upgrading replaces it with an administrator-owned automation in the same conversation and keeps its schedule, run message, on/off state and saved options. Runs then use the upgrading administrator's model account, and **Recent runs** starts over. The page never upgrades an automation on its own (Josh's decision).
- Ongoing scribes now need a Gateway administrator (`operator.admin`). Writers without it can still run scribes once; the page says scheduling needs an administrator. Members who could set up scribes through the chat turn before can no longer do so (Josh's decision).

## Why This Change Was Made

Operator-created automations "use the current operator read policy" (docs/automation/cron-jobs/payloads.md), so the page writes the automation itself with `cron.add` / `cron.update` instead of asking a turn to. That puts one writer on the scribe automation and deletes the turn-based re-declaration machinery: the repair and update prompts, the attempt and idempotency bookkeeping, the "Updating…" wait and Try again, and the first-run forcing that watched for the setup answer. A once run is still a chat turn, since it never reads on a schedule.

An account-owned automation can't be widened in place, and a same-key operator `cron.add` converges onto it with its old authority. So an upgrade removes it first and then adds the replacement. The page can't read or carry over the model account recorded on the old automation (`inferenceBinding` is private to cron), and a rejected add leaves no automation. For both reasons, upgrading is an explicit administrator action behind a confirmation, never something the page does on load.

The updates the page still makes on its own touch only administrator-owned automations, in place. They reduce duplicates, move a legacy `session:<key>` target to `current`, and replace an unedited earlier run message. They never touch an automation that was changed to another payload kind, such as a script. On Repair, an automation recorded for another conversation is replaced rather than patched, because an edit can't move its recorded parent conversation.

## Evidence

- Live, on openclaw-fsn1 before the change: an operator `cron.add` automation in the Slack scribe's conversation recorded `scheduledToolPolicy: trusted`. Its forced run had private Knowledge access with writes enabled, and `channel-list` returned 101 Slack channels. The turn-created Slack scribe was refused on both manual runs.
- Live, with an earlier revision of this branch on that Gateway: the three turn-created scribe automations (Slack, Granola, consolidation) were replaced with `trusted` ones. Schedule, sessionTarget, sessionKey, delivery, failure alert, name and run message matched the pre-migration backup. A forced Granola run finished `ok`. A forced Learn from Slack run listed Slack channels, read #all-openclaw-foundation with the user token and wrote claims. The upgrade now runs that same replacement on an explicit click instead of on page load.
- Data compatibility: that replacement loaded the stored scribe jobs written by the released turn-based setup and carried their saved settings over unchanged.
- Tests: the scribe view and state tests pass (55). They cover four cases:
  - turn-created automations are never written on load;
  - Upgrade replaces one and keeps its options and pause;
  - a script-payload automation is never updated;
  - a failed update is tried once per revision.
- Earlier on this branch, the full Knowledge suite passed (74 files, 569 tests). `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean on this head.
- Reviews: a separate review found three issues, all fixed with tests. A declarative `cron.add` answers `{ created, job }`, so the first run was never requested. Repair moved an automation to a new conversation without moving its recorded parent. And the removal-first migration could lose a user-edited automation. ClawSweeper's findings on customized payload kinds and the recorded inference account are resolved by never replacing an automation automatically.
- Not checked: a non-admin Control UI session against a live Gateway (covered by unit tests only).

prs.title: fix: stop telling helpers to stay silent when their command finishes and their result is still owed
prs.body:
Closes #205705

## What Problem This Solves

When a helper (subagent) waits for its background command with `sessions_yield`, the command's exit wakes it with a prompt that ends "If no user-facing update is needed, reply NO_REPLY only." A helper's turn must end with a visible result, so following that advice fails: on Claude CLI the turn ends with "The AI service returned an empty reply", and a configured fallback model reruns the turn and can send the parent (and the user) a second copy of a report they already have.

## User Impact

A helper woken by its own finished command is asked for a short visible result instead of `NO_REPLY` ("if nothing changed since your last report, say so in one short line"), so the turn ends normally, without an empty-reply error or a fallback. Exec wakes in every other session (main chats, groups, cron) get the same prompt as before, `NO_REPLY` offer included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reply policy stays as it is: a helper gets an exec wake only after it yielded on that command, so its result is still owed, and `resolveCommandReplyExpectation` marks subagent exec wakes `result-required` on purpose (#184005). The system prompt already drops the silent-reply guidance for such turns; only the exec-wake prompt still offered `NO_REPLY`. It now reads the turn's reply expectation, already resolved by then. Making these wakes optional instead would let a yielded helper's result vanish.

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** one repro script run unchanged on fresh test profiles of released 2026.11.10 and of this PR, Claude CLI `claude-haiku-5-5`. The helper starts `sleep 6; echo build-ok` in the background, replies `started`, calls `sessions_yield` and is told it has nothing new to report.

| Wake turn | Released 2026.11.10 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wake prompt sent to Claude CLI | ends "If no user-facing update is needed, reply NO_REPLY only." | ends "This turn must end with a visible result: if nothing changed since your last report, say so in one short line." |
| Model reply | `NO_REPLY` (8 bytes) | "The background command finished with exit code 0 and printed `build-ok`. Nothing else is outstanding." |
| Gateway log | `CLI backend returned an empty response.`, `model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed … reason=empty_response` | no error, no fallback decision |
| Session shows | "⚠️ The AI service returned an empty reply. Please try again." | the one-line result above |

Tested on `98b15a2e9c2` (based on `69b81b5a063`).

- Tests: one new case in `agent-runner-execution-session-events.test.ts`, for the embedded and the CLI runner: a subagent exec wake gets the result-required wording and no `NO_REPLY`. It fails on main and passes here; the other 20 cases pass, and the queue-overflow case still asserts the `NO_REPLY` offer outside a helper. `run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`: 74 s (26 s in tests). Lint and `tsgo` pass; CI has not run yet.
- Review: upstream autoreview, `69b81b5a063..98b15a2e9c2`: no P0-P2 findings, clean.
- **Request proof** (embedded runner, a recording stub as the model): on this PR the helper's wake prompt as the model received it byte-equals the transcript's copy, minus the send-time timestamp prefix. A main-session exec wake (all 3 requests) is byte-identical to a build of the base `69b81b5a063`, with install paths and exec ids masked; on the helper path the wake guidance is the only difference.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Code at `69b81b5a063`:

- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-notify.ts:389`: a subagent session gets an exec wake only when `resumesYieldedRun` is set, i.e. `sessions_yield` awaited the command (`:143`); hidden helpers without a yield get none (`:60`).
- `src/agents/reply-completion.ts:108` returns `result-required` for a subagent session key before the exec rule at `:112` returns `optional`. The `lane`/`privateCompletion` rule at `:97` doesn't apply: exec wakes don't run on the subagent lane.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-run-params.ts:156-162` built the wake guidance with a fixed `reply NO_REPLY only`; `get-reply-run-context.ts:279` already sets silent-reply prompt mode `none` for result-required turns.
- Rejection: `src/agents/cli-runner.ts:454` (empty response, then fallback) and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.ts:170` (visible-answer continuation).

The expectation comes from `resolveFollowupReplyExpectation`, which returns `followupRun.run.terminalReplyExpectation` once the runner has set it (`agent-runner-run.ts:133`) and computes the same value otherwise, so the prompt and the runner's check can't disagree.

First seen in production on 2026.11.10: a Claude Opus helper had already delivered its result, its awaited command then finished, it answered `NO_REPLY`, and the fallback model rerunning the turn sent the report a second time.

</details>

prs.title: fix(workboard): preserve pasted board names and column text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pasting a Sessions board column label could silently change “bed 12” to “bed 1”. A leading space counted against the browser’s raw text limit, so the final digit disappeared before Save trimmed the space. The same problem affected column descriptions and board names.

## User Impact

Board names, column labels and descriptions now keep the full pasted text when it fits after trimming. The existing limits are 120, 60 and 400 UTF-16 units respectively. If the text is genuinely too long, Save leaves the editor open so the user can correct it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removing the three raw input limits lets the existing save and validation paths evaluate the whole draft. This keeps the modal’s existing save order, including the protection for newer column edits during a name-only save. Earlier work by steipete covered concurrent renames, and roboclaw-bot kept Save reachable after a board error. [Concurrent rename](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167348) · [Save after a board error](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199380)

## Evidence

- Used native Chromium paste on a synthetic board, with an offline transport into registered Workboard Gateway methods and a real SQLite worker. After reopening both the worker and browser, the column header, hovered tooltip and board title retained “bed 12”, “bed 34” and “bed 56”. The parent showed “bed 1”, “bed 3” and “bed 5”.
- One column update matched the direct registered transition. A stale reader received the changed columns, and a reader with the current revision received an unchanged response. A name-only save preserved a peer’s newer column label.
- Pasted values one unit over each trimmed limit stayed editable and left SQLite unchanged. Correcting them allowed Save to finish.
- The new mounted modal regression failed on the parent and passed with the fix. The concurrent rename, fallback-only edit and inline validation controls also passed. Formatting passed. Scoped lint reported the same existing reactivity warning on both revisions.

Hosted project checks are pending.

prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:start -->
## Adoption decision and fresh distribution evidence — 2026-11-02

The Slack-owner decision remains whether to expose the compatibility-preserving `requireExplicitBotMention` opt-in. The current submission section below owns the latest head and CI status; maintainer edits remain enabled. Owner acceptance is still outstanding.

The historical [advisory review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177555#issuecomment-6274222081) reports no actionable findings and sufficient recorded isolated-Gateway output, and recommends accepting the opt-in. It does not record Slack-owner acceptance. Its two outstanding checklist entries both concern that same public-contract decision. The review is scoped to `39d01116dd2d5e01fa7f8ab50dbb1e44613a0e9a`; the earlier12-input comparison was bound to8fa0cc0d85711ab2ee19e488ec9e325309a476c2. That earlier integration retained11 byte-identical inputs; access-control documentation only adds accepted official Slack read-bound guidance. The strict opt-in authored delta and committed Gateway scenario are retained. The older proof retains its original head; that earlier head's CI supported its integration. No fresh live Slack run or current employee acceptance is claimed.

Recorded official distribution evidence confirms that the need remains after the implicit-thread silence repair: unmodified Core/Slack **2026.10.10-beta.5**, build `7e15622f37bd0ced194a3b0fccacb4ad6bc78d85`, still admits untagged bot messages through both `bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot` in the isolated distributed-function/compiled-gate fixture. The same 20-case matrix passes 17, with these two strict-admission requirements and the separate optional-completion policy remaining. Package integrity and the scope are recorded in the [release follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621). This is not a new live Slack incident or a claim that existing documented defaults were silently changed.

**Decision requested from the Slack owner:** accept or reject this optional public setting at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Omitted/false keeps existing implicit bot handoffs. With `allowBots: "mentions"` and the opt-in enabled, untagged bot activation is rejected while explicit bot requests, implicit human follow-ups, DMs, authorized commands, and existing sender restrictions retain their controls. This is the compatibility-preserving alternative to #160752's default change; no new default change is requested here.

This PR decides **admission**, not whether an already admitted explicit bot notification may finish empty. That latter product-policy question remains separate in #186514. A scoped acceptance/rejection of this opt-in is the missing adoption decision; existing code/proof work is not being represented as owner approval. No new review command or redundant behavior replay was added for this mechanical integration.
<!-- forone-stable-adoption-evidence-20261103:start -->
### 2026-11-03: the same admission requirement remains in stable2026.10.10

Official npm/latest Core/Slack **2026.10.10**, distributed Core build`7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be`, was checked with the unchanged20-case synthetic matrix: **17PASS / 3FAIL**. The two untagged-bot admission cases (`bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot`) still admit the bot under existing mentions-only behavior. The two implicit-thread optional/silent conditions from merged #164877 nowPASS in stable; the third remaining failure concerns #186514's separate explicit-bot completion policy.

The [stable distribution follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621) fixes the verified immutable Core/Slack hashes and execution scope. This is actual distributed Core-function / verbatim compiled Slack-gate evidence, with unchanged cases/assertions and shipped package bytes. The existing native Gateway proof retains its original binding. This paragraph updates distribution evidence only; the current PR head and compatible opt-in proposal remain unchanged. Slack-owner acceptance or rejection remains unrecorded.
<!-- forone-stable-adoption-evidence-20261103:end -->
<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:end -->

## Evidence

## Earlier accepted evidence (previous head)

Candidate: 41974794c4ab5eb235d153d7926de7dedba834f6. Current-head hosted CI completed **SUCCESS** with no nonpassing jobs: [run 39427790673](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39427790673).

prs.title: fix: let macOS updates refresh the Gateway service when PATH lists Node later
prs.body:
Closes #204735

## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, `openclaw update` can refuse to refresh the Gateway LaunchAgent with `SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN: Environment.PATH … The installer would discard or change an operator setting`. It happens when the installed `PATH` lists the Node directory after another directory, for example `~/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:…` with Node at `/opt/homebrew/bin/node`. The planner rebuilds the macOS `PATH` with the Node directory first, and the preservation audit then rejects that reorder, so every update leaves the refresh owed.

## User Impact

On macOS, package updates refresh the Gateway service again instead of refusing on a `PATH` the installer itself would only reorder.

## Why This Change Was Made

The planner and the audit disagree only on order. On macOS the planner still keeps just the regenerated entries, as before. Entries that the installed `PATH` also lists now keep the installed order among themselves, in the slots they already take. A Node directory that moved is new, so it still leads, which the audit already allows. Linux and Windows are unchanged.

## Evidence

- On `e8aa261c7aa8`, the unchanged-Node case in `src/commands/daemon-install-path.test.ts` uses the real service environment generator, install planner, and preservation audit. It models a retained CLI entrypoint in `/Users/test/.local/bin` and an unchanged `/opt/homebrew/bin/node`. It asserts the exact installed `PATH` survives and the audit returns no findings. The moved-runtime case still tests the distinct leading-runtime exception with a fixed generated environment.
- The preservation-audit implementation and its existing definition-facts tests are byte-identical to main. Those fixtures still cover refusal to drop or reorder operator directories, reject an unrelated leading directory, reject a replacement missing the selected Node directory, and reject an opaque launcher. No plist, env-file, config, or data format or reader changed; this is a change to the proposed PATH order only.
- The strengthened test passed targeted lint and command-test typecheck on the Linux base with the test applied, and formatting and `git diff --check` passed on the updated candidate. The independent Linux execution did not reach assertions: the repository test runner timed out preparing compiled subprocess fixtures. The pinned author output below is from the earlier two-case test, not an execution of the strengthened case. Exact-head CI: [run 45736141881](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45736141881).
- See **Native macOS proof** below for the before/after service refresh and live RPC check.

<details>
<summary>Author's before/after output for the original planner-to-audit fixtures</summary>

The author ran these on Windows in a throwaway test copy with `path.delimiter` set to `:`. The author also reported the same 41 passes before and after in `daemon-install-helpers.test.ts`, `doctor-gateway-daemon-flow.test.ts` and `install.definition-repair.test.ts`. Windows `pnpm check:changed` passed typecheck, lint, format, import cycles and other guards; the SQLite worker ratchet hit `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME` on a raw `C:` path, and the dead-export scan was skipped after a timeout. Neither SQLite nor exports changed.

```text
=== main (1bec22471)
 ✓ drops existing paths for macOS LaunchAgents
 × keeps macOS PATH precedence through install-plan audit: an unchanged runtime whose directory is not first
 × keeps macOS PATH precedence through install-plan audit: a moved runtime directory that still leads
"Gateway service Environment.PATH: The installer would discard or change an operator setting. Current: \"/Users/test/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:/usr/bin:/bin\"; installer: \"/opt/homebrew/bin:/Users/test/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:/usr/bin:/bin\"."
"Gateway service Environment.PATH: The installer would discard or change an operator setting. Current: \"/opt/node-a/bin:/Users/test/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin\"; installer: \"/opt/node-b/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/Users/test/.local/bin:/usr/bin\"."
      Tests  2 failed | 1 passed

=== this PR (5df1ad75b)
 ✓ drops existing paths for macOS LaunchAgents
 ✓ keeps macOS PATH precedence through install-plan audit: an unchanged runtime whose directory is not first
 ✓ keeps macOS PATH precedence through install-plan audit: a moved runtime directory that still leads
      Tests  3 passed
```

</details>

## Native macOS proof

Tested on macOS 26.6.2 (arm64) with Node 24.22.0 at `/opt/homebrew/bin/node`, a disposable named Gateway profile and npm prefix, and a proof-owned `.local/bin/openclaw` shim. Used the real launchd service refresh command in update mode (`gateway install --force --port … --json`) after swapping the package in place; this was not a full registry-driven `openclaw update` run.

- **Official 2026.11.10 (`6ea542f`):** refresh exited 1 with `SERVICE_DEFINITION_UNKNOWN` / `Environment.PATH` because it would move the Node directory ahead of the shim directory. The existing proof LaunchAgent PID, plist and environment sidecar were unchanged.
- **Exact head `e8aa261c7aa8`:** the same refresh exited 0 and restarted the proof LaunchAgent. The complete effective `PATH` was identical before and after, with the proof shim directory still ahead of `/opt/homebrew/bin`. These builds store `PATH` in the LaunchAgent's private environment sidecar, not inline in the plist. `gateway status --json` reported loaded, running and RPC healthy; the proof config remained byte-identical.
- Removed the proof jobs, plists, profiles, npm prefixes/caches and tarball staging. Both pre-existing Gateway PIDs and start times were unchanged.

prs.title: fix: preserve the full query when searching session transcripts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pasting a long query into Search chats on the Sessions page could drop its last character and show an unrelated transcript. In a two-chat example, the intended query ended in `pear`. The field clipped it to `pea`, which also matched a chat about peas.

## User Impact

The search field keeps the full draft. If the trimmed query exceeds the limit, the field shows its current length and limit, clears earlier matches, and lets the user edit and submit again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser applied its input limit before the search could trim surrounding whitespace. The form and request owner now check the trimmed query against the transcript search limit of 4,096 UTF-16 units. The request receives the complete trimmed text and the field retains what the user entered.

## Evidence

- On the parent, Chromium submitted `pea`. The registered search returned both Cedar and Birch from synthetic SQLite transcripts, and clicking Birch opened that chat. The complete `pear` query returned Cedar alone.
- With the fix, a 4,097-unit draft containing a leading space and an astral character submitted all 4,096 trimmed units. Both the initial search and a fresh browser and reader reopening the database returned Cedar alone.
- A genuinely oversized query of 4,096 Unicode scalars and 4,097 UTF-16 units stayed editable, issued zero search requests and showed zero stale matches. An ASCII overflow and a blank query also issued zero requests. Correcting the draft to `peas` opened Birch.
- The focused Chromium Vitest regression failed on the parent and passed on the reviewed tree. Scoped lint and formatting passed on all three files.

The registered replay used the compiled Sessions page, controlled transport, the real search handler and worker, and two synthetic transcripts. Live Gateway accounts and other browser engines were outside this proof.

prs.title: fix(workboard): let bulk label edits continue after a selected card is archived
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If two people are working on the same board, one can archive a card while the other has a bulk label edit open. When the archived card had 12 labels, the dialog disabled **Apply changes** even after it showed just the remaining card. The editor had to reopen the dialog to add the label.

## User Impact

The editor can apply the label in the open dialog. A selected card that would exceed 12 labels still blocks the edit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bulk Add now checks the opening labels of just the cards that remain selected. The update uses the revision seen when the dialog opened, so a concurrent edit to a surviving card still goes through the existing conflict check. This builds on the label picker and bulk limit contributed by @roboclaw-bot and @vyctorbrzezowski in [the earlier Workboard change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199295).

## Evidence

- In two Chromium tabs, one editor opened Add and the other archived the full card. Before the fix, Apply stayed disabled. With the fix, the surviving card received exactly one update, and its labels survived a cold SQLite reopen. The archived card and unselected sibling received no label writes.
- Eight additional selection cases passed. A remaining full card blocked Add with zero writes. An ordinary one-card selection produced one write.
- The new regression failed on the original disabled button. Both focused Vitest files passed all 31 tests on the fix, including a refresh from revision 10 to 11 where Apply still submitted revision 10 and the opening labels.

The Chromium replay used synthetic cards, a local mock Gateway transport, and the registered Workboard handlers with a scratch SQLite store. Hosted CI is pending.

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

prs.title: fix: keep matched text visible in session search previews
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Sessions search could find the right message and show a preview that omitted the only matching word. A search for `Marigold`, for example, found it at offset 660 in a SQLite excerpt, beyond the 500-unit display budget. When a CJK substring matched inside a word, the preview could also begin with half of an emoji.

## User Impact

The result shows the matching text when it fits, including the original spelling of prefix and diacritic matches. The surrounding context stays within the existing preview budget, and the start and end of the preview are valid UTF-16 boundaries.

## Why This Change Was Made

SQLite knows where the match occurred. For long full-text excerpts, the search worker compares the ordinary excerpt with a marked projection from the same native query. It takes the display text from the ordinary excerpt, so punctuation and marker characters in the message survive. A substring search uses the position returned by the database. Short messages keep their existing excerpt and need only one full-text snippet evaluation.

## Evidence

- Replayed both failing seeds and their minimized cases through SQLite, the asynchronous search worker, and the mounted Sessions page. The word at offset 660 appeared in the preview, and the CJK result retained its match without a dangling surrogate.
- All 78 worker and mounted-result cases passed. These covered exact, prefix, diacritic and quoted-phrase matching, authored markers, 420- and 500-unit matches, ties, empty results, and mixed-case CJK text.
- Compared 441 additional SQLite excerpts against independent native highlights. Previously visible matches kept the original bounded text. All four Ephyra replay points passed.
- The pinned TypeScript compiler reproduced both projection alias errors on the previous head. The corrected projection, inferred result row, and SQLite adapter passed the focused compile. The native dialect inventory returned to the frozen count of two design sites. Formatting and scoped lint passed.
- Hosted production types, all five core test-type jobs, and the baseline ratchets passed on `5c169c98563d`. Architecture flagged the SQLite table identifier's missing local explanation. The final commit documents the existing store-binding check at that identifier. The repository's Kysely guard reproduced the failure on the parent and passed on the corrected sparse checkout. SQLite admission also returned the expected plain and marked snippets and rejected a foreign index, an unknown field, and a closed connection.
- Replayed the embedded Gateway fixture in its original order under Node. Searches for `quasar` and `会` returned only the visible message on frozen source and on the correction. The previous hosted Bun run timed out waiting for the host's visibility response. The log does not identify the inner wait.
- On `08738d2e`, all 25 transcript-search tests passed, including the late exact, prefix and diacritic matches, the long token, and the CJK/emoji boundary. The dist build, production types, all five test-type stripes, Kysely rule and dialect ratchet passed. [Transcript-search suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45633320207/job/139273501779) · [Build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45633320207/job/139273499121)
- The hosted embedded Gateway job timed out on both `quasar` and `会`. On one two-CPU Linux runner with pinned Bun and the same ordered 18 cases, the frozen parent reproduced both worker host-callback timeouts (60.727 s and 60.673 s). The PR head preserved all 16 parent passes. On that head `quasar` passed in 319 ms and `会` reached the same timeout at 60.524 s. The cause of the wait inside the callback remains unresolved. [Hosted failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45633320207/job/139273501448) · [Paired runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45652251202)
- The dependency check reported the same 14 path/symbol entries as the frozen baseline. The aggregate diagnostic remains red. The mounted Sessions-page proof used jsdom and the real search worker. A live Gateway, a browser session and PostgreSQL remain outside this proof. [Dependency report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45633320207/job/139273501671)
