prs.title: fix: keep user approvals settled after compaction
prs.body:
Fixes #205387

## What Problem This Solves

After a long conversation is compacted, the compaction summarizer can treat missing older tool outputs as unresolved uncertainty and inject fabricated verification/stop gates into `## Open TODOs` for work the user already explicitly approved. In the motivating incident (#205387), an unattended scheduled turn woke up after compaction, treated a compactor-authored `"stop and report any material contradiction found before publishing"` TODO as a pre-send gate, and held all five user-approved `v2026.11.10` launch announcements instead of publishing them.

## User Impact

The summary records settled user decisions, explicit approvals, and observed outcomes under `## Decisions`, updating superseded facts when corrected. `## Open TODOs` is limited to unfinished user-requested work or unresolved execution failures. On replay, `<summary>` is framed as compressed history from earlier turns rather than new instructions that outrank explicit user approvals. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made (Provenance & Research Context)

### How the removed lines got there (`git blame` on `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.ts`)

The 8 replaced lines in `buildCompactionStructureInstructions` were not a single deliberate design — they accumulated across four commits over seven months:

1. **Lines 136 & 139 (`df0f2e349f`, #25555, 2026-03-04):** Introduced the 5 fixed section headings (`## Decisions`, `## Open TODOs`, `## Constraints/Rules`, `## Pending user asks`, `## Exact identifiers`) for consistent downstream parsing.
2. **Line 140 (`4b5341ce43`, #130620, 2026-08-27):** Added after feeding the latest user ask back to the summarizer caused completed asks to leak into `## Pending user asks`.
3. **Line 141 (`cbbaa0d3ad`, #161293, 2026-10-02):** Explicitly merged as a partial prompt mitigation for a synthetic **Nemotron 3.5 Super** eval (#162023) where a failed `verify()` check kept being placed back under pending work.
4. **Lines 142–145 (`0cf5e291a0`, #167757, 2026-10-09):** Added one week later for the same synthetic eval (Maya / Oct 8 → Oct 15 / `verify()`). The actual bug in #167757 was a **code routing bug** in `compaction-safeguard.ts` (recent-turn preservation stripped all main-summary inputs so the summarizer was skipped via fallback). That routing fix stays completely intact here; however, #167757 also added four dense epistemic-policing paragraphs (`"Distinguish requested, attempted, completed, and failed actions without inferring overall success from a completed check"`, `"If evidence does not resolve a conflict, record the uncertainty"`).

### Why subtractive simplification instead of an additive rule (and why #205412 was closed)

Earlier candidate PR #205412 tried to fix #205387 by bolting two more `"Do not invent..."` rules onto the same bloated block. We closed #205412 in favor of a holistic, subtractive simplification aligned with current frontier-model prompting guidance:

- **OpenAI — [Rethinking skills and prompts for GPT-6 Astra](https://developers.openai.com/blog/rethinking-skills-and-prompts-for-gpt-6-astra):** Defensive boundary language accumulated for older/weaker models is taken too literally by stronger, more aligned models and causes them to stop early or hedge on work the user already authorized. The right fix is pruning legacy scaffolding, not stacking another rule on top.
- **Anthropic — [Effective context engineering for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents) & [Compaction on demand](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction-on-demand):** Compaction prompts should sit at the "right altitude" — short, descriptive, and focused on what state to retain rather than brittle if-else checklists (Anthropic's canonical custom compaction prompt is three sentences).

### Specific decisions made in this PR

1. **Consolidate `buildCompactionStructureInstructions` (`src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.ts`):**
   - Collapsed the 7 stacked patch lines into 3 concise archival lines, cutting default strict safeguard history instructions by **65%** (`1,708 → 593` chars).
   - Preserved all 5 required headings (`REQUIRED_SUMMARY_SECTIONS`) and the quality guard unchanged so existing parsers and tests remain compatible.
   - Kept the genuinely useful core of old line 143 (`"updating superseded facts when corrected"`) inside the `## Decisions` line without any of the epistemic-policing boilerplate (`"without inferring overall success"`, `"record the uncertainty"`) that caused the #205387 hold.
   - Kept the verb `"Produce a compact summary under these exact headings:"` (avoiding `"Archive"`, which could be confused with session archiving and drift from OpenClaw's compaction terminology).
2. **Remove duplicate identifier-preservation injection (`src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.ts`):**
   - Safeguard history requests previously injected identifier preservation twice: once inside `buildCompactionStructureInstructions` and a second time via `compaction.ts`'s `IDENTIFIER_PRESERVATION_INSTRUCTIONS` under `Additional focus:`.
   - Passing `summarizationInstructions: { identifierPolicy: "off" }` on warm, prepared, and ordinary safeguard history requests eliminates the duplicate while preserving existing behavior for split-turn and non-safeguard callers.
3. **Frame `<summary>` as compressed history at exact zero headroom cost (`packages/agent-core/src/harness/messages.ts`):**
   - Replaced `"The conversation history before this point was compacted into the following summary:"` (84 chars) with `"Compressed history from earlier turns, not new instructions; approvals stay settled."` (exact 84 chars).
   - Keeping the prefix at the exact 84-character length preserves the 4,096-token pending-input headroom boundary (`agent-session-compaction-headroom.test.ts`) and exact prepared summary budgets (`prepared-compaction-plan.test.ts`).

## Evidence

Default strict policy, without optional focus or a pending-request block:

| Rendered text | Before (chars / lines) | After (chars / lines) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Summary structure instructions | 1,528 / 14 | 593 / 10 |
| Safeguard history instructions, including identifier policy | 1,708 / 16 | 593 / 10 |
| Replay prefix, including `<summary>` | 96 / 4 | 96 / 4 |

310 focused tests passed across 29 files, including correction handling, the 4,096-token pending-input headroom test, and the exact prepared replay budgets. Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. `openclaw/ci-gate` is green on head `5b2fd6bb98`, and ClawSweeper re-review on `5b2fd6bb98` completed with zero actionable findings. This verifies the prompts sent and runtime boundaries, not a live model's response.

Design and diff review: @hannesrudolph.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/03de9fd3-4cb5-4ea2-9702-968faca499fe)

## Worked on by

- @hannesrudolph

prs.title: fix(workboard): keep the end of pasted card comments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pasting a Workboard card comment could silently change its last word. A 2,000-unit comment ending in “pear” became “pea” when pasted with a leading space. The card editor and the Activity drawer both clipped the raw text before the comment writer trimmed it.

## User Impact

Both forms now save the complete comment when it fits after trimming. If it exceeds the existing 2,000 UTF-16 unit limit, the writer rejects it and the text stays in the editor for correction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two textareas now pass the full draft to the existing comment writer. That keeps validation, comment identity and storage semantics in one place. Earlier work by gokay-ai preserved oversized historical comments when performing unrelated card actions. [Prior Workboard fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/154958)

## Evidence

- Used native Chromium paste in both forms on a synthetic card, with an offline transport to registered Workboard Gateway methods and a real SQLite worker. The parent saved “pea” twice. After the fix, a fresh worker and browser showed both full comments ending in “pear” and “peas”. Each successful save inserted one comment and one “Comment added” event on the intended card.
- Pasted 2,001-unit comments after trimming. Both forms retained the full raw draft after rejection, and SQLite stayed unchanged. A corrected submission then inserted exactly one comment.
- Short comments, near-limit and ASCII text, trailing whitespace, and CRLF input passed on both surfaces. Sibling cards, labels, and the separate card description were preserved.
- Both new mounted regression cases failed on the parent. All five selected Vitest cases passed with the fix. Formatting passed, and scoped lint reported the same four pre-existing reactivity warnings on both revisions.

Hosted project checks are pending.

prs.title: fix: preserve side chat text when dictating at the limit
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Dictating over a selected word in a full Side chat question could delete letters at the end of the question. Dictating an emoji near the limit could leave half of its UTF-16 surrogate pair in the submitted text.

## User Impact

Dictation now preserves the text on both sides of the selection. The preview shows what fits, and Ask receives the same question as it would after typing or pasting the replacement. Main chat and New Session still accept longer transcripts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The textarea already supplies the 400 UTF-16-unit limit. The dictation insertion code now subtracts the space occupied by the unselected text, then fits the spoken text and its separators into the remaining space without cutting a surrogate pair. The caret lands after the text that actually fits.

## Evidence

- In Chromium, dictating an emoji at offset 398 previously left a lone high surrogate. The corrected field and draft matched native typing and paste at 399 units, with the caret at 399. Ask received the same trimmed text by all three routes.
- In a 400-unit question, dictating over `basil` previously shortened the untouched ending `peas?` to `pe`. All three input routes now preserve `peas?` and place the caret at 56. Seven adjacent scenarios covered exact fits, overflow, whitespace, punctuation, and unchanged input.
- Three regressions failed on the parent. All 160 tests across five focused suites passed on the fix, including late finals and provisional previews. Separate main-chat Send and New Session late-final controls each accepted a 450-unit transcript.
- Formatting passed. Scoped type-aware lint exited successfully with one existing reactivity warning on `visibleDraft`. The browser used synthetic speech events and an intercepted Ask callback. Live microphone capture, transcription services, and persisted answers were outside this proof.

prs.title: fix(android): all-day calendar events land one day early with a positive UTC offset
prs.body:
Closes #193280

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an Android all-day calendar event is created one day early when `startISO` has a positive UTC offset, such as `2026-07-05T00:00:00+10:00`.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent that adds an all-day event in a local time zone east of UTC now gets the date it asked for. Events with `Z` times and timed events do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Android stores all-day events as UTC midnights. The old code converted the input to a UTC instant first and then cut it to the UTC day, so the date written by the caller could move back one day. The new code reads the date from the offset time and then builds the UTC midnight. The parser now uses `OffsetDateTime`, which also accepts offsets on older Android versions where `Instant.parse` accepts only `Z`.

Related: #100032 and #100483 added the UTC-midnight encoding that this change keeps.

## Evidence

- New test `handleCalendarAdd_keepsAllDayDateWrittenWithPositiveOffset` in `CalendarHandlerTest`. On base it fails with start `2026-07-04T00:00:00Z`. With the fix it passes.
- The existing all-day and timed tests still pass, and so does the whole `ai.openclaw.app.node.*` package.

- `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.CalendarHandlerTest :app:ktlintCheck` passes on this branch (upstream main `ff8fe0731`, Windows). The new test fails on main.
- Real app run. I built the play debug app from main and from this branch, and ran it on an Android 36 emulator with a Gateway built from the same main commit (no proxy). From the Gateway CLI I sent this to the paired app:
  `openclaw nodes invoke --node <id> --command calendar.add --params '{"title":"OffsetHoliday","startISO":"2026-07-05T00:00:00+10:00","endISO":"2026-07-06T00:00:00+10:00","isAllDay":true}'`
  Then I read the stored event back from the emulator calendar with `content query`.

| App build | Event the app reports | Stored in the calendar (UTC midnight) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | `startISO 2026-07-04T00:00:00Z` | `dtstart=1783123200000` = 2026-07-04, allDay=1 |
| this PR | `startISO 2026-07-05T00:00:00Z` | `dtstart=1783209600000` = 2026-07-05, allDay=1 |

The date I asked for is July 5. Main stores July 4. This PR stores July 5.

Setup notes: the emulator has no calendar account, so I added one local writable calendar. `calendar.add` is not allowed by default, so I added `gateway.nodes.commands.allow: ["calendar.add"]` to my test Gateway and approved the new command list for the node. Both are test setup only.

Terminal output for both builds and the run scripts are in [this folder](https://github.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/tree/proof-android-2026-11-04/calendar-all-day-offset/): `result-main.txt`, `result-branch.txt`.

prs.title: refactor(subagents): retire finished child rows by one rule instead of two handed-off flags
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a sub-agent finishes, its result must reach the agent that started it exactly once, or that agent must see why it did not. That holds across restarts too. The registry tracks this with two outboxes on one row: completion `delivery` and the `requesterSettleWake`.

Cleanup's "retire this row later" intent was kept in two places that handed off to each other: `requesterSettleWake.retireAfterSettle` and the row's `retireAfterRequesterTurn`. The wake handed off to the row when it completed while the requester turn was still open, and the row handed back to the wake when the requester yielded. A missed handoff in either direction drops the intent or leaves a row behind. Separately, five call sites repeated their own mix of the three delivery-suppression facts.

This is the most-fixed area of the registry: 403 of 788 commits in the last six months were fixes, and most of them were about delivery, wake or restart. Each fix added a guard or a handoff and rarely removed one.

## User Impact

There is no intended visible change for completed runs. One behavior changes: cleanup's retire intent is no longer lost when the wake goes away without completing. Before, the intent rode on the wake, so any path that cleared the wake directly dropped it, and the row stayed until the retention sweep. Those paths are a yield-paused child's wake clearing, a pause notice consumed without a cohort, a yielded batch whose final was already delivered, and restart custody retiring the obligation. Now the row keeps the intent and retires at its next settle check, which is what cleanup asked for. A regression test covers the yield-paused case.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One retirement fact plus one rule.** `retireAfterSettle` now lives only on the row, and `isSubagentRetirementSettled` checks it in one place: the row is marked, no settle wake remains, and no open requester turn awaits its result. Wake completion and requester yield both call that rule. Both handoffs are deleted, along with the branch in `transitionRequesterSettleWakeState` that preserved the flag and the `RequesterSettleWakeBatchState = Omit<…>` alias that hid it from batch transitions.
- **Named suppression rules.** `subagent-delivery-state` owns `isSubagentDeliveryClosed` (an accepted closure, which a kill rollback cannot undo) and `isSubagentDeliveryWithheld` (closed, or a pending kill asked to withhold delivery). Five sites that matched those definitions exactly now call them. Three other sites have their own definition of "still owed", for example the batch-level rule in `requester-cron-authority`. Changing them would change behavior, so they are left as they are. `suppressAnnounceReason` stays because it records a reason other code reads, not a suppression flag.
- **Legacy rows.** `normalizeSubagentRunState`, which already normalized the old row flag on load, now also folds `requesterSettleWake.retireAfterSettle` and `retireAfterRequesterTurn` from rows written by released builds into the new fact. This needs no Doctor migration. Remove the fold once no supported build can write those shapes.

Size against the merge base: production code +84 −73 across 13 files (tests +75 −32 across 9 files). The change adds one rule and two predicates, and removes two flags, both handoffs and one type alias. The point is fewer places that decide retirement, not fewer lines. The larger follow-up merges the settle wake into the delivery obligation, which removes the second outbox and its separate retry policy. It is left out of this PR so this cutover stays reviewable.

Open overlap: the stale draft #140956 builds on the old two-flag shape and will conflict. #199455 sets `requesterSettleWake.retireAfterSettle` in one test line and needs a one-line rebase change.

## Evidence

- New tests in `subagent-delivery-state.test.ts`:
  - legacy rows fold from both old locations
  - an open requester turn keeps the retire intent
  - a yield-paused child keeps its intent until its next settle
- Updated the existing lifecycle, requester-yield, terminal-effects, wake-receipt, wake-settlement and completion-admission tests to the single fact.
- Local gates on `4ecd1640b0525` (the proof test was added in `68f5284694cca`) (base `0b99555d5f7dd`):
  - `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:test:src` clean
  - `oxfmt --check` clean
  - oxlint clean on the changed files

prs.title: fix: keep complete meeting searches when pasting or reopening filters
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A pasted Meetings search could lose its final character when an emoji used two UTF-16 units. Reopening the complete saved URL showed the full query but searched a shorter prefix, so another meeting could appear.

## User Impact

Meetings keeps the entire query through 256 Unicode code points. Longer text stays editable with a visible error and no results. Correcting it runs the complete search with the other filters intact. Opening Meetings without a query still lists all meetings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway counts code points. The input and saved-route reader now follow that limit. While the route loader is pending, Meetings retains its last resolved filter so switching searches cannot issue an unintended unfiltered request.

## Evidence

- Chromium clipboard paste and fresh-browser reopen used the registered `transcripts.list` handler and an isolated SQLite store. The bilingual 256-code-point query returned only `notebook-cedar` both ways. Before the fix, both paths also returned `notebook-birch`.
- Eight valid cases covered ASCII, combining marks, astral characters, literal surrounding spaces, and 256 code points occupying 512 UTF-16 units. Three 257-code-point cases sent zero list requests and showed zero rows on paste and reopen. Each correction sent one filtered request. Opening `/meetings` without a query returned both seeded IDs in one request.
- The UI-pages typecheck reproduced TS2352 in the route test fixture. Type-aware lint reproduced `no-base-to-string` on the form’s query field. After reusing the Meetings test provider and reading the field as text, both checks passed with zero diagnostics. All 41 Meetings unit tests and three Chromium view tests passed. Formatting and the English catalog check passed. Scoped lint exited successfully with one existing warning on the capture-settings callback.
- Nine native `FormData` controls covered missing, file, and empty values, literal spaces, combining characters, and 256- and 257-code-point ASCII and emoji inputs.
- The browser used a synthetic Gateway transport and synthetic records. Live deployment, non-Chromium browsers, and hosted CI were outside this local proof.

prs.title: improve: reduce sidebar work for large automation inventories
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Opening chat with 201 visible automations made the sidebar sort and wrap all 201 jobs twice to decide whether the Automations clock should show a failure. The shared compact inventory had already fetched both pages.

## Change

The sidebar reads the complete scoped inventory once and retains each visible job ID in either the healthy or failed set. Runtime events can update that membership without sorting, scanning, or manufacturing access to a job. Automation tables keep their existing filters, sorting, and pagination. A malformed membership row leaves the prior failure visible until a valid refresh succeeds. A superseded page yields to the current inventory before validation.

## Evidence

- With 201 jobs and the same two ordinary Gateway requests, the base read display names 402 times and the repaired sidebar read them zero times. The [before/after Testbox proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45740582591) also covered sidebar events and the shared inventory.
- On the frozen base a malformed current page preserved the indicator but the retry reused bad cached data. On the interim revision an incomplete row hid a known failure, an obsolete malformed response rejected a current co-subscriber, and a successful queued reload could still ignore a later live failure. The final commit passed all four error/recovery cases, all three focused test files, and the production UI build. The [final Testbox command](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45743345941) exited zero. The standalone build reported advisory CSS size and chat request-count warnings. The [official Control UI performance comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45743851139/job/139655588270) passed.
- Both one-shot Testbox commands exited zero and the leases stopped. GitHub records the two linked lease workflows as cancelled after teardown. The [separate pull-request CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45743851139) checks the actual merge checkout.
- The [mounted browser suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45743851139/job/139655588628) passed all three cases on the final integration checkout. It exercised first- and last-page failures, clearing the final failure, and an empty Inbox with the failure dot still lit.
- Review follow-ups reproduced on both the base and the final head. An invalid status or malformed auto-disable object can misclassify a job. A transport rejection on an invalidated request still rejects its direct subscribers. Defining payload validation and transport-error behavior for every inventory consumer is separate from the sidebar change. The sidebar itself now recovers through its queued read.

This measures browser work. The shared Gateway pagination and canonical inventory cache are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): preserve the causal failure when a continuation loses operator authority
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #198360. When a same-session cron continuation loses operator authority before admission, `followup-runner.ts` discarded the failure entirely: it set `completion = { kind: "aborted" }`, logged a constant message, and never propagated the causal error to the internal session-event execution. The result was that a denied continuation recorded a generic "Session event was abandoned before execution" receipt with no actionable reason — even though the original error (e.g. "original operator role changed") was available and the sibling internal-event branch already preserves it via `onFailed`.

## Solution

In the authority-loss branch of `executeFollowup` (src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.ts), preserve the causal failure through the existing session-event outcome:

- Call `queued.run.internalEventExecution?.onFailed?.(error)` so the cause flows into the session-event handoff's failure (the same channel the adjacent internal-event branch uses).
- Set `completion = { kind: "failed", error: formatErrorMessage(error) }` so the receipt carries the safe, actionable reason instead of a generic abandonment.
- Keep `disposition = { kind: "consumed" }` — the terminal denial and settlement-once semantics are unchanged; revoked input is never replayed or retried.
- Preserve a **distinct secondary authority refusal** too: when the post-failure authority recheck throws its own reason that differs from the original failure, both are reported — `"<original>; authority check: <authority reason>"` — with the original failure kept as the `cause`, so the receipt distinguishes which condition failed instead of hiding it (per the issue's expected behavior).

No conversation content or credentials are exposed: only the already-logged error messages are propagated.

## Evidence

- **RED → GREEN regression**: new tests in `followup-runner.test.ts` — `records the causal failure on an internal event when revoked input is denied` and `preserves a distinct secondary authority refusal alongside the original failure`. On the pre-fix code both fail (2 failed / 28 passed); with the fix all pass.
- Full file suite: `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts` — **30/30 passed** (including the new cases).
- Format: `run-format.mts --check` clean on both changed files.

Closes #198360

prs.title: fix: show the first message when session naming fails
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When automatic naming fails, a session can end up with a random nickname or show its checkout instead of the conversation. If the first message is already available, it can also briefly replace the loading state before the generated name arrives.

## User Impact

During initial naming the header keeps its loading bar and the sidebar reserves the title line. A generated name appears directly; if naming fails, a short excerpt of the first message appears instead. Later attempts keep the excerpt visible until a generated title is available. Naming does not change activity order. A textless session keeps its checkout or “New session”; neither the excerpt nor an eventual rename changes its branch.

## Why This Change Was Made

For dashboard sessions, the naming owner records that a fallback is available, not the message or a made-up name. The roster reads the excerpt from the transcript for failed sessions; the existing branch-naming path still uses a real title or its own two-word fallback. The header menu first appears next to the settled title rather than moving from a provisional position. Existing explicit and saved names are unchanged. Native iOS and Android session keys retain their saved two-word fallback because the shipped apps do not display derived titles.

## Evidence

Same open conversation, 1280 px Chromium, cropped to the title and adjacent sidebar rows. Synthetic Gateway responses hold the title request until each state can be observed.

**Before — excerpt and menu visible during naming:**

![Excerpt appears before the generated title](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cf31eb4-2cb5-45d4-8875-33433895122a)

**After — naming in progress:**

![Header loading bar, hidden menu, sidebar title space reserved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22a0a6b6-d031-42e3-9e57-4bdc2a49e841)

**Annotated comparison — the sidebar row and header during initial naming:**

![Before: premature excerpt and menu outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6577c74b-e9ca-4957-a7e5-3ad41fd758c2)

![After: reserved title space outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1024dad7-e3d5-40f8-99ee-c6a532216014)

**After — naming failed:**

![Excerpt and menu appear; the neighboring row stays in place](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4df82b50-cb67-4b40-a97c-450a03249ba6)

The browser regression exercises initial success and failure, followed by recovery, and measures unchanged sidebar row and link bounds. The desktop menu waits for the settled title. A later genuine rename keeps the menu beside its text.

Chromium against the built Control UI and an isolated real Gateway (`d5c987d2a96c`), with a controlled title provider: sampled every animation frame from Start session through navigation. No frame showed “New session” or the message excerpt while initial naming was held. After the provider failed, both the header and sidebar showed the first message; they kept it during retry and then displayed “Release checklist”. This exercised the real transport and session store, not a failure at an external model service.

The native transport regression failed with no saved name before the compatibility fix and passes for both iOS and Android session keys. Local autoreview covered `1da4ec2b1537..885f79747e34` at P0/P1 and reported no actionable findings at those priorities.

prs.title: fix(update): finish the Gateway restart a shipped pnpm updater refused
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A pnpm install updated by published 2026.11.5 to a release with the same database schema (2026.11.5 → 2026.11.6) keeps a working `openclaw` command. Since #201735 the Gateway stays down: `openclaw update` exits 1 with `service-revalidation-failed`, and the restart and the recovery restart are refused with `managed-service-ownership (service-ownership-changed)`. In a real cell the Gateway stayed down for 402 s, until the user ran another command.

Root cause, in the installed updater, which this change cannot patch:
- After the package swap, 2026.11.5 checks the service's loaded command against the new root (`update-command-service-revalidation.ts:333-398` at v2026.11.5).
- Its fallback compares against the pnpm global entry, which pnpm has just repointed into a new versioned store directory. The unit still names the 2026.11.5 store entry, so the service looks foreign.
- `main` fixed this check (#201735), but only a fixed updater runs it. 2026.11.5 hands the remaining steps to the new package only when the schema migrated (`update-command-migrated.ts:141-146` at v2026.11.5).
- So schema-migrating hops already work (2026.11.4 → 2026.11.6, 2026.11.5 → 2026.11.10, both shown in real cells), and same-schema hops do not.

## User Impact

On a same-schema pnpm hop driven by 2026.11.5, the Gateway now comes back on the new version without another command. The new package's Doctor, which that updater does run after the swap, prints one line saying OpenClaw will try to restart the Gateway after the updater exits. After the updater exits, a background process refreshes the service definition and starts the Gateway through the ordinary `openclaw gateway install --force` and `openclaw gateway start` owners. The installed updater still prints its own failure and exits 1, because it decides that before this code can act.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is compatibility code for shipped updaters that cannot be patched. It applies to 2026.11.5 and earlier, and to 2026.11.6 and 2026.11.10 builds without the #201735 fix. The module comment names those versions, and the module is removed once no supported upgrade path starts from such an updater.

Two other routes were rejected:
- **Forcing the handoff by reporting a schema migration that did not happen.** That would publish false `dataAtRisk`/no-rollback records and turn off the updater's own recovery.
- **Editing the unit from the Doctor during the update so the shipped check passes.** On systemd the shipped check reads the manager's loaded `ExecStart` over D-Bus (`systemd-service-files.ts:204-222` at v2026.11.5), so passing it would need `daemon-reload`. The updater also spawns its Doctor with service repair and activation disabled.

How it works:
- **Gate.** The Doctor step "Gateway restart handoff" in `src/flows/doctor-health-startup.ts` acts only when all of these hold:
  - an update is in progress, and the parent's no-repair and no-activation flags are set;
  - exactly one running update run, whose recorded driver is alive and is this Doctor's parent;
  - the running package is the active pnpm global entry's store directory;
  - the service names this same pnpm home's store entry for an earlier version, is owned by this installation, and has a writable definition.
- **Spawn.** The finisher is spawned detached and confirms that it took the single-instance lock before the Doctor prints its line.
- **Wait and re-check.** It waits up to 60 minutes for the run to finish and the updater to exit. It acts only on `service-revalidation-failed`, and re-checks every gate under the Gateway service operation lock. It yields if a newer update started, if the service is running, or if the Gateway answers.
- **Fixed drivers.** The driver's version cannot tell a fixed build from an unfixed one, so the gate does not use it. Under a fixed driver the finisher only waits for the run to end with another outcome and exits.
- **Recording.** On success it records the verification on the run (existing fields) and a warning row. If it gives up, the warning names the reason and the verified recovery: `openclaw gateway install --force`, then `openclaw gateway restart`, or `openclaw triage`. A real cell showed that `openclaw gateway restart` alone exits 78 in this state.

**Where the finisher runs.** On Linux it is launched through `systemd-run --user --scope --collect --unit=openclaw-update-restart-<runId>.scope`, using the managed-service handoff launcher's existing `systemd-run` resolution (`update-managed-service-handoff-launcher.ts`). Without its own scope it would share the updater's cgroup and die with it. For a Gateway-started update, that cgroup is the transient `openclaw-update-<id>.service` (`KillMode=control-group`, v2026.11.5 `update-managed-service-handoff-launcher.ts:49-76`), which stops when its helper exits. The scope has no `PartOf=` on the Gateway, so the finisher's own `gateway install --force` cannot stop it. If `systemd-run` is missing, it falls back to a plain detached spawn. On macOS it is a detached process.

**Single instance.** A per-run file lock. The existing owners were checked and none fits:
- the update executor fence and the managed-handoff lease are exclusive per installation, so holding either through the wait would block the `openclaw update` the finisher must yield to, and the lease has no row kind for this;
- the Gateway service operation lock serializes every Gateway command, so it is taken only around the final re-check;
- `sqlite-live-owner` authorizes only the Gateway's own database reads.

**What readers show after a successful finish.** The stored run keeps `status: failed`, `reason: service-revalidation-failed`, plus the verification and the warning row; no new field or status value was added. `isRefusedRestartFinishedLater` (`src/infra/update-run-restart-finished.ts`) recognizes that combination. With it:
- `openclaw update status` leads with "✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.11.6 (from 2026.11.5); 1 warning needs attention.";
- it states that the recorded outcome is unchanged, and drops the failure lines and the triage advice;
- the Control UI update card shows no failure banner, and the chat `/update` summary reads as updated;
- `update status --json` prints the stored record unchanged;
- a run that gave up still reads as failed.

**Gateway-started updates.** The shipped 2026.11.5 Gateway refuses `update.run` for a pnpm global-virtual-store install before changing anything (`update.ts:427-432`, install surface `package-root`). So that path never reaches the finisher. That refusal also exists on `main` and is handled in a separate PR.

The docs correct the earlier claim that 2026.11.4 and 2026.11.5 always hand the later steps to the new package: they do so only when the schema migrates.

## Evidence

Draft. Unit tests: `update-shipped-restart-finisher.test.ts`, 14 tests, using a real update run ledger and a real pnpm store layout on disk. Each gate was removed in turn, and every case that guards it failed. Real Docker cells on the 2026.11.6 line (#201739 plus this commit) are running and will be added here:
- green: 2026.11.5 → this build;
- the user running a plain `openclaw update` 5 s after the failure;
- npm control;
- fixed-driver control;
- forced post-swap failure;
- 2026.11.4 start;
- the CLI-started and Gateway-started hops on real systemd.

The red cell is published 2026.11.5 → #201739 head `848912c`: exit 1, the Gateway down for 402 s, and back only after a second update.

**Start layout covered.** Every cell starts from a registry install made by `pnpm add -g`, which puts the package in `store/v11/links/@/openclaw/<version>/…`. That is also where a user who recovered by hand with `pnpm add -g` ends up, so a later update from such an install starts from the layout the cells already use. The target layout is the project-store layout the updater itself produces (`global/v11/<group>/node_modules/.pnpm/openclaw@<version>…`), which a real public-registry cell confirmed.

## Steps left to a person

None on the covered hop. If the finisher gives up, its warning names the verified recovery and `openclaw triage`.

## Not proven yet

- **Target layout from a registry: now covered.** A real cell ran published 2026.11.5 → a plain `openclaw update` → published 2026.11.6 from the public registry only. The updater installs a registry target in the project-store layout (`global/v11/<group>/node_modules/.pnpm/openclaw@<version>…`), the same layout class the earlier tarball-target cells used. See https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201739#issuecomment-7018135106.
- **Still unproven:** a fixed target installed from a registry. It cannot be exercised before a fixed version is published; the fixed builds were proven as tarball targets.
- **Still unproven:** pnpm 11, which ignores the `virtualStoreType=project` setting the updater passes, so its target layout may differ. A pnpm 11 cell is being prepared.
- Real systemd and launchd, the Gateway-initiated update path, and `KillUserProcesses=yes` at logout. In the last case the next `openclaw update` or the verified recovery heals the install.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the Control UI session details, the "People" section is rendered as an HR department in eight locales: zh-CN `人力资源`, zh-TW `人力資源`, ja-JP `人事`, ko `인사`, fr `Ressources humaines`, tr `İnsan Kaynakları`, id `Sumber daya manusia`, fa `منابع انسانی`. The English source is just `People` — the participants of a conversation — and the sibling key `chat.sessionHeader.peopleParticipants` already reads `参与者` in zh-CN. Fixes #204347.

prs.title: fix: keep chat sending when the streaming formatter is unavailable
prs.body:
Closes #205702

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI messages can get stuck as “Not sent / Retry” when the optional streaming-Markdown formatter asset fails to load. The message never reaches the Gateway, even though its connection and required transport are healthy.

## User Impact

Messages send without waiting for the optional formatter. Replies use the existing standard Markdown rendering while it loads or is unavailable. Ordinary streaming, required transport failures, queue ownership, and cancellation checks are preserved. No settings, dependencies, or migrations change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The formatter is presentation, not a delivery prerequisite. I kept its prewarm best-effort and let the existing renderer handle load failure. The change stays within two production files and the existing preparation tests: no new loader wrapper or outbox recovery changes. Production delta: +8/-11; tests: +50/-10.

The dependency came from #183198, which intended to preserve Chat behavior while deferring evaluation.

## Evidence

I built main at `6ef3c6096a48e8a1abc776559940b28d137725cd` and exercised its production UI in Chromium against an isolated real local Gateway. Only the formatter asset was fault-injected; all chat traffic and persistence were real. The final patched run used local Qwen3 4B Instruct with llama.cpp b12732. The before outage performs no inference; its successful normal control used Qwen3 0.6B.

| Scenario | Main | This change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Formatter HTTP 503 | Not sent; 0 sends, 0 stored messages | 1 send, 1 acknowledgment, 1 stored message; formatted reply |
| Formatter request held through the reply | Not measured in the real UI | Sends and renders bold/code before release |
| Normal assets | 1 send and stored message; formatted reply | Same |

- Two new regressions fail on main for the intended reasons (pending formatter stalls; rejected formatter fails delivery), and pass with this change.
- 56 focused preparation and Markdown tests pass, including required transport failure, durable/memory ownership, cancellation, pending-runtime rendering, sanitizer and DOM retention coverage.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, production UI build, and diff checks pass. Main and candidate both report the same existing CSS-size and 21-vs-20 chat-request budget warnings; this change reduces normalized chat JS by 40 gzip bytes without changing startup or CSS sizes.
- Local autoreview could not launch because the installed Codex executable failed its read-only sandbox preflight. I did not weaken review isolation. [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205703#issuecomment-7180876869) completed on `fca762900d2d18ca1b520854dc5a655983a3273e` with no actionable findings.
- The first proof setup reused a session label, then the 0.6B model did not reliably follow the inline-code prompt. I corrected the fixture label and used the instruction-following 4B model without weakening formatting assertions.

- [CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45742336021) on the exact published head `fca762900d2d18ca1b520854dc5a655983a3273e`. I also reran the 56 focused tests, UI typecheck, and targeted lint on that head. Skipped CI lanes are not claimed as proof.
- I stopped the local gateways, model servers, and browsers; removed test state, downloaded models, installed dependencies, generated builds, caches, and scratch. The PR checkout and delivered screenshots remain.
- This is a same-repository PR. GitHub's fork-only maintainer-edit toggle is not applicable.

Not verified: Firefox/Safari, hosted providers, or broad latency/load benchmarks.

### Clean comparison

Before

![Before: message marked Not sent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33a9da54-9360-48d7-8277-f885e7feabc1)

After

![After: delivered message and formatted reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9cad12df-96f5-4c3f-9ae4-3c8fc333bbf2)

### Annotated comparison

![Before: formatter failure blocks delivery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/875bbde4-8e89-46b4-a270-c656a77acb83)

![After: delivery and formatting succeed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3327d028-b64b-4cfe-a847-71b363c3799c)

Both captures are the actual production UI at 1280 × 900 with synthetic conversation content, under the same formatter-503 fault.

Thanks to Dan Riccio for the report and proposed patch.

## Work sessions

prs.title: fix(markdown): an image whose alt text uses **bold** shows the asterisks
prs.body: Closes #196194 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: when a Markdown image in a reply is rendered as text instead of being sent as an attachment, any Markdown inside its alt text arrives as literal characters. - A README-style badge `[![**build**](https://ci.example/badge.svg)](https://ci.example)` arrives as a link reading `**build**`. - `![**Bold** chart of _sales_](https://example.com/c.png)` arrives as `**Bold** chart of _sales_`. - `&` in alt text arrives as the literal `&`, and `\*` keeps its backslash. On Telegram the durable final-reply path lifts valid `https` images into photos, so this shows up for images that are not lifted: relative, `http://`, `data:` or blocked-host URLs, reference-style images, and text delivered through the plain reply path (`deliverReplies`, used by fallback delivery and native command replies) or message edits. Channels that render image alt text from the shared IR show it for every image. ## User Impact User impact: image alt text in replies reads as plain text (`Bold chart of sales`, a `build` badge link) instead of leaking Markdown delimiters, escapes or double-escaped entities. Literal HTML and code spans in alt text are unchanged. The renderer is shared (`packages/markdown-core`), so other channels that render image alt text from the IR get the same result. ## Why This Change Was Made The shared Markdown renderer built the alternative text from the image token's `content`, which is the raw label source. It now builds it from the label's child tokens, as CommonMark specifies for image descriptions ("only the plain string content of the image description be used"): emphasis, strike and link markup are dropped, escapes and entities are decoded, nested images contribute their own alt, and code spans and inline HTML stay literal text (the existing "authored HTML provenance" behavior). The assistant-transcript role-header path that supplies its own projected alt text is untouched. ## Evidence `markdownToTelegramHtml` on `main` vs this branch: | Reply Markdown | `main` | this branch | | --- | --- | --- | | `![**Bold** chart of _sales_](https://example.com/c.png)` | `**Bold** chart of _sales_` | `Bold chart of sales` | | `[![**badge**](b.svg)](https://x.y)` | `**badge**` | `badge` | | `![outer ![inner *i*](i.png) end](o.png)` | `outer ![inner *i*](i.png) end` | `outer inner i end` | | ``![a x & \* `c`](u)`` | ``a x & \* `c` `` | `a x & * c` | - Regression coverage is a row in the existing `preserves authored HTML provenance` table in `packages/markdown-core/src/ir.test.ts` (emphasis, strong, strike, code span, escaped `\*`, and the literal-HTML case). It fails on the base commit and passes with the fix. Net test-line growth is zero. - `pnpm test packages/markdown-core` and the Telegram, Google Chat, Teams, Matrix, WhatsApp, Zalo User, Tlon and `src/media` suites that mention Markdown images pass. - `pnpm check:changed` passes except `changelog attributions`, which fails on untouched `CHANGELOG/*.md` files on `main`. - Based on `ce7788f5a`; tests were run on `81ab38df6` and none of the touched files changed in between. ### Live Telegram proof The same reply sent to a real Telegram chat through the plain reply path (`deliverReplies`, which does not lift Markdown images), first from `main` (`81ab38df6`), then from this branch. Each message starts with a `PROOF main` / `PROOF fix` header; the four lines are a bold/italic alt, a README-style badge inside a link, a nested image, and escapes plus an entity. | | rendered alt text | | --- | --- | | `main` | `**Bold** chart of _sales_`, badge link `**build**`, `outer ![inner *i*](i.png) end`, `a & b \* c` | | this branch | `Bold chart of sales`, badge link `build`, `outer inner i end`, `a & b * c` | ![Telegram: main (top message) vs this branch (second message)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chr0mium24/openclaw/pr-proof-telegram-20261110/telegram-proof-image-alt-and-commands.png)

prs.title: fix(update): read SQLite lock bytes as zeros through fs-safe
prs.body:
> **Draft, blocked on an fs-safe release.** This needs `@openclaw/fs-safe` with `zeroRanges` (openclaw/fs-safe#1111). After that PR is released, this branch will add the `package.json` and lockfile bump to the new version. Until then, typecheck in CI fails against 0.28.2. The branch is rebased on `main` after #205668 merged.

## Problem

#205668 fixed the post-migration hash, the step that fails in the Windows `EBUSY` reports in #197083. On Windows, SQLite's lock bytes at 1 GiB are mandatory locks. Another path still reads them: when the database has retained WAL frames, `prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocation` makes a private copy with `copyRootFileSync` and verifies it with `sameFileContentsSync`. Both read every byte. Under another connection's `EXCLUSIVE` lock, that copy fails on any database larger than 1 GiB. #205668 also added a hand-written hash loop to OpenClaw.

## Solution

Use the new fs-safe `zeroRanges` option: byte ranges treated as zeros without being read.

- `SQLITE_LOCK_BYTE_RANGES` (`sqlite-snapshot-file.ts`) is the single definition of SQLite's 512 lock bytes.
- The main-database generation hash calls `hashFileDescriptorSync(fd, { zeroRanges })`. The hash loop from #205668 is removed. Digests are unchanged, because SQLite leaves those bytes zero.
- The main-database private copy (`copySourceFile`) and its verification (`sourceMatchesCopy`) pass the same ranges. WAL and journal copies pass none and still read every byte, since a WAL can hold frames at that offset.
- `hashFileDescriptorSync` now takes an options object (`maxBytes`, `zeroRanges`); its three `maxBytes` callers are updated.

## Evidence

Real Windows proof on Windows 11 ARM64 (Node 24.22.3) with a 1.15 GB WAL database:
- **Setup:** a second process held the migration owner's native exclusion (`PRAGMA schema_version`, then `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE; BEGIN EXCLUSIVE; ROLLBACK`). In one case it kept committed WAL frames, which forces the private copy.
- **Build:** the real `readUpdateDatabaseGeneration`, bundled from #205668 and from this branch. This branch used a locally built fs-safe#1111 together with the published 0.28.2 binaries and win32-arm64 native binding.

| Owner state | #205668 | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| unlocked | ok | ok |
| exclusive, drained | ok | ok; digest matches the unlocked empty-reader alternate |
| exclusive, retained WAL frames (copy path) | `guarded synchronous file copy failed` | **ok**; same content digest as unlocked |

Local checks:
- New test `sqlite-readonly-location.lock-bytes.test.ts`: a read of the lock bytes throws `EBUSY`, and a sidecar copy fails. The main-database copy succeeds and writes zeros there. Test time is about 0.7 s.
- Consumer tests pass: `update-database-generations`, `sqlite-readonly-location` (base and copy), `update-doctor-migration-wal-rebuild`, `sqlite-snapshot`, `file-descriptor`, `plugin-runtime-artifact-identity`. That is 184 passed and 2 skipped.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, format check and `git diff --check` pass against the patched fs-safe.

Not covered: the async `copySqliteFile` (`root.copyIn`) path. It isn't used under the migration owner's exclusion, and fs-safe#1111 doesn't add `zeroRanges` there.

Refs #197083

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: feat: confine native node worker filesystem access
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OCE OpenClaw node workers cannot safely use writable OpenShell PVC ancestors unless model-controlled processes are also prevented from replacing them.

## User Impact

Adds opt-in `nodeHost.workerRuns.isolation: "filesystem"` for Linux workers, alongside the scoped writable-ancestor exception. The worker and its descendants can write their admitted workspace, model HOME and scratch directory, but cannot replace those roots through their parents. Unsupported kernels/helpers reject launch; existing defaults remain unchanged.

The PR now pins the published packages `@openclaw/proc-safe@0.6.0` (includes [#39](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/39)) and `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.28.2`. Operators must stop existing workers and exclude all other unconfined untrusted writers, including same-UID processes, for the entire workspace lifetime. A dedicated Pod or PVC alone is insufficient.

Josh’s [#198073](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198073) is included. The node now rejects writable roots that overlap trusted runtime or shared storage before launching a worker. An explicitly assigned workspace remains usable.

At [`1a639e0`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1a639e0e6d3b2f6fd25849071efb37a4a4841af7), the default supervisor loads the filesystem launcher only when filesystem isolation is selected. With the PR’s locked proc-safe 0.4.2 and fs-safe 0.27.1, 27 Linux worker supervisor and workspace retention tests passed, including launching a downloaded worker through the standalone executable. With a locally packed proc-safe launcher and fs-safe 0.28.0, all three Linux filesystem supervisor tests passed. The latter run used local packages and does not qualify a published install.

At [`2d3e3d4`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2d3e3d4e3bfc28f649dad6840dee113c07aa98c2), the Git cancellation test expects the existing `-c core.fsmonitor=false ls-files` invocation. The manifest suite reproduced the CI failure on the parent and passed all six cases on Linux after this test-only change ([CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43506279639)).

## Why This Change Was Made

Pre-exec Landlock confinement covers model-launched subprocesses while keeping existing Git transfer/publication APIs and process ownership. Descriptor-relative fs-safe I/O could harden its own operations, but subprocess and lifecycle integration would still need additional work. This approach requires Linux Landlock ABI 3+; inherited descriptors and other sandbox boundaries remain the caller's responsibility.

The real repository path also needs named-device dispatch to preserve its profile and use existing device eligibility. Trusted Git inventory disables repository fsmonitor/lazy fetch; anonymous credential checks retain explicit hostname selection without ambient `GH_HOST`. No new recovery manager or state is introduced. Host-side Git transfer and publication helpers now preserve that same boundary instead of trusting worker-controlled Git configuration or object-directory indirection.

## Evidence

### Current security repair and main reconciliation

The current head is [`279998e6`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/279998e634a108925b0446bfa58516a075c46da5), following the security repair at `89017efa`, reconciled with `main@1b06bd7b` without rewriting the original feature history. The security repair was prepared with @joshavant.

- Workspace Git operations now retain the admitted filesystem boundary. History export uses a trusted standalone Git view, and publication no longer borrows a mutable worker object store. Unsafe history is rejected; independently safe file changes remain available with a visible explanation.

prs.title: fix: stop unrelated plugin timestamp updates from blocking plugin enablement
prs.body:
Closes #205567

## What Problem This Solves

Enabling or toggling one plugin via `plugins.setEnabled` can fail if another quarantined or broken plugin has pending install timestamp updates (`installedAt`, `resolvedAt`, or `acceptedSurfaceAt`) sitting in the live config diff. Because the hot-reload handoff passed unfiltered `plan.changedPaths` to `reloadPlugins`, `resolvePluginReloadReplacementIds` treated those timestamp bookkeeping updates as active edits to the unrelated plugin, forcing `maybeThrowOnPluginLoadError` to reload it and reject the enable operation.

## User Impact

- Operators running `plugins.setEnabled` on a healthy plugin are no longer blocked by stale install timestamp refreshes on an unrelated quarantined plugin.
- Genuine capability consent changes (`acceptedSurface`, `acceptedSurfaceHash`, `acceptedSurfaceIntegrity`) still mark `acceptedSurfaceAt` as an actionable change and trigger a plugin reload when needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **`src/gateway/server-reload-hot.ts`**: Pass `plan.reloadPluginPaths` (or `plan.changedPaths` minus `plan.noopPaths` when `reloadPluginPaths` is absent on synthetic test plans) into `params.reloadPlugins` instead of raw `plan.changedPaths`, so no-op bookkeeping paths never expand `resolvePluginReloadReplacementIds` while `plan.changedPaths` stays intact for logging and status callers.
2. **`src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts`**:
   - Treat `plugins.installs.<id>.acceptedSurfaceAt` as a timestamp no-op alongside `installedAt` and `resolvedAt` when capability approval (`acceptedSurface`, `acceptedSurfaceHash`, `acceptedSurfaceIntegrity`) is unchanged, and push it to `forceChangedPaths` whenever approval changes.
   - Default `plan.reloadPluginPaths` to `[]` whenever `pluginLifecycle` sets `plan.reloadPlugins = true` so a reload whose only config diff paths were timestamp no-ops does not fall back to raw `plan.changedPaths`.
3. **`src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-install-timestamps.test.ts`**: Added Red → Green unit and hot-reload integration coverage for `acceptedSurfaceAt` (unchanged vs. changed capability approval) and `applyHotReload` / `resolvePluginReloadReplacementIds` isolation.

## Evidence

- Reproduced Red state before implementation edits (`pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-install-timestamps.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` failed 4/4 assertions: `acceptedSurfaceAt` returned `hot` instead of `none`, `forceChangedPaths` omitted `acceptedSurfaceAt`, and both hot-reload modes forwarded bystander timestamp paths).
- Verified Green state after final edits:
  - `pnpm tsgo:core` (passed)
  - `pnpm tsgo:test:src` (all 22 shards passed)
  - `pnpm exec oxlint src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts src/gateway/server-reload-hot.ts src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-install-timestamps.test.ts` (`Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`)
  - `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/gateway/config-reload-plan.ts src/gateway/server-reload-hot.ts src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-install-timestamps.test.ts` (`All matched files use the correct format`)
  - `pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-install-timestamps.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload-plan.test.ts src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-quarantine.test.ts src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/server-plugin-reload-lifecycle.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (**7 passed (7) files, 309 passed (309) tests**)

prs.title: fix: show every installed plugin in the Customize sidebar
prs.body:
Fixes #205392

## What Problem This Solves

Customize → Installed could omit the plugin you were using: the sidebar showed at most eight eligible shortcuts and hid some installed bundles. When a delayed inventory made the panel overflow, its scroll fade could still indicate there was nothing to scroll.

## User Impact

Every installed plugin returned by the Gateway is reachable by pointer or keyboard, including disabled bundles and local plugins without a catalog entry. Catalog-only items stay out. External plugins still appear first, newest first, followed by bundled plugins. No migration or enablement change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

This intentionally changes Customize from curated shortcuts to the same inclusion rule as Settings → Plugins → Installed. The manifest’s optional `catalog.sidebar` hint and protocol projections remain intact. Customize observes its content height and asks the existing Sessions scrollport to remeasure; there is no new scroller, wrapper, CSS rule, or controller effect.

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway, published head `2c187bd83`:** Chromium 156 at 1280×480 loaded the bundled Control UI from a disposable loopback Gateway; the served entry asset matched the build byte-for-byte. All **186 installed plugins** in the unmodified `plugins.list` response appeared with the expected labels, links, and ordering. Clicking row 9 (`alibaba`) and using Tab + Enter on row 186 (`Zoom meetings`) each opened the matching detail heading with exactly one selected plugin row. The fade changed at the top, middle, and bottom (6,102 px of scroll); the Customize header and rail remained pinned and actionable. All 186 entries were bundled; the synthetic cases below separately cover third-party and catalog-only entries.
- Bundled Playwright Chromium, synthetic Gateway: on `73dc1946b`, 8 of 13 installed entries appeared and the open ninth plugin was absent. An independent delayed-load probe overflowed but retained `scroll-none` without interaction. On the fix, all 13 appear and delayed content changes the fade to `scroll-top` before any scrolling. At the end of the list the 428 px scrollport held 624 px of content, with the header and rail pinned and clickable.
- Four Chromium tests cover selection, both route types, Tab / Shift+Tab / Enter, short lists, and icon retention after `plugins.changed`. Seven scroll/controller tests and one isolated lazy-sidebar test passed. UI TypeScript, targeted oxlint, Solid controller baselines, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Local Auto Review of the complete working-tree candidate against `73dc1946b`: no P0 findings. No native client was exercised.

Matched 1280×480 Chromium captures, scrolled to the last available installed row with Lossless Claw open. Before: `73dc1946b`. After: `2c187bd83`. Both use the same synthetic inventory (13 installed, one catalog-only).

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: Lossless Claw is open but the list stops at Lobster Theme.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa4315ea-ad8f-41b4-ae9a-024fb8409f82)

**After**

![After: Lossless Claw is selected at row nine and Workboard is visible at the end.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6c9c70a-f03c-4aa0-a8ee-12a9fdf92c98)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![The eighth and final visible entry is highlighted.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5767f0d0-dd39-44c9-998d-a69fdc33fc4a)

**After**

![The ninth and thirteenth entries are highlighted below the fixed Customize header.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fa740e9-a422-4caa-8e50-c0232db6f8d5)

Reported and initial patch contributed by @TheAngryPit.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7eaab6d9-0ae8-4d1d-b72d-a50b7ad49ace)

prs.title: fix: recover a completed Codex reply after a brief disconnect
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

After a Codex WebSocket disconnect, chat can report a failure even though the native parent saved its answer. A worker result can also wake the parent twice, or disappear when the same worker finishes another task. If the parent is idle, the Gateway can declare shutdown safe before it has delivered the result.

## User impact

The Codex plugin recovers completed replies after brief connection loss. It leaves a paused goal paused, respects Stop, and never resubmits work or executes tools from history. If an acknowledged follow-up on the same worker is still running, the plugin watches for its result. Failed or ambiguous work can still require explicit recovery.

## How it works

- On abnormal socket closure, recheck the current session, binding, runtime and turn. Read the latest parent turn at most twice within ten seconds. A proven foreground wait can acknowledge an already completed first child without a second wake.
- When reusing a worker, distinguish the previous assignment from the accepted successor. Release an unused input reference once that exact task succeeds. Keep the separate reference for result delivery.
- When the parent has already detached, keep the accepted worker receipt through cleanup and attempt a bounded history read on the original endpoint. Require the latest completed successor of that child, current delivery authority and an unconsumed receipt. Use the existing per-turn delivery claim. Other workers keep their receipts.
- If the latest turn is the exact accepted successor and is in progress, observe it on the read-only connection. An idle or unloaded notification for that worker triggers a fresh read. A system error clears the running status without triggering an immediate read. After five quiet minutes, check the thread’s status without loading its turns. Each read has a ten-second deadline. A live parent that takes back the same active assignment takes precedence.

Use verified TLS or a trusted isolated endpoint. A bearer token alone cannot authenticate the server. The changes stay inside the Codex plugin.

## Evidence

I ran a real Gateway and Codex CLI with synthetic inference. One goal used the same worker twice. I dropped the socket during the first wait, paused the parent after the second submission, and dropped the socket again after the worker finished but before the Gateway received the notification.

- At `96b29225`, after 60.536 s the parent had no result and the Gateway reported ready to stop. A separate read found the exact completed turn and answer.
- At `42682e51`, shutdown stayed blocked while the worker ran, after it finished, and during a deliberately held history read. One announcement arrived 1.393 s after the second disconnect. Explicit Resume read the original goal and completed it. After returning to the original Gateway, the same session and threads retained both answers.

The packaged comparisons used CLI 0.164.0 and the production changes on OpenClaw `82b682c6` alongside #193024. Earlier trials on CLI 0.164.0 and 0.169.0 exercised the original foreground recovery. The remote configuration change in #201621 was omitted from this trial.

Earlier tests covered changed certificates, wrong turns, Stop, concurrent registration, queued siblings and stale authority. Removing the cleanup fixes left an extra receipt for the completed task and produced an unhandled abort.

### Disconnect before the worker finishes

I paused the parent, disconnected while the worker was still running and held the response for over eleven seconds. At `42682e51`, the Gateway reported ready to stop and the parent missed the result.

At `3e0756c7`, the worker was the only shutdown blocker after 11.406 s. The Gateway still refused to stop during the result read. The parent received one announcement 2.313 s after the worker replied and stayed paused until Resume. With an active goal, the next automatic turn waited on the same worker. It finished without another input or announcement. An intermediate build without the handoff attempted a redundant announcement. In both cases the worker ran exactly two tasks.

Lint, formatting and the commit hook passed. The updated `native-subagent-submission-store.test.ts` suite passed 39/39 in 230.89 s with one worker, including compilation. Six additional cases took 10.459 s total. They cover both orders of a status change during the read, an inconclusive reread, authority revoked while waiting, an unrelated parent releasing its guards and re-registration on a live connection.

### Stored worker records across an upgrade and return

Three separate Vitest processes using local dependencies ran the old, proposed and old binding-store code against the same SQLite database. The PR merge base (`81d69df5`) wrote two synthetic V1 child receipts and an assignment with a recorded result. Candidate `3e0756c7` reopened the database and recovered both receipts and the assignment exactly. It rejected an incorrect submission ID without modifying the row, then consumed only the matching receipt and assignment. On return, the original code reopened the same parent binding with only the sibling receipt remaining. No schema migration was needed.

The probe reused the fixture in `native-subagent-submission-store.test.ts`. Each process passed one assertion-based test and reported its final state.

```jsonl
{"phase":"seed","assignments":1,"submissions":2,"binding":true}
{"phase":"candidate","assignments":0,"submissions":1,"binding":true}
{"phase":"return","assignments":0,"submissions":1,"binding":true}
```

### Worker visibility during recovery

At `3e0756c7`, `sessions.describe` with `includeNativeSubagents` lost the running worker after a disconnect, even as the plugin watched for its result. The session now shows the worker from that same watcher while its pending assignment, session and delivery authority remain valid. A live parent takes priority. This adds no Codex RPC or permission.

With the plugin changes from `afd551cc`, the same worker was visible 11.421 s after the disconnect. Shutdown still reported busy. The parent received one result and the running row disappeared. One explicit Resume completed the paused goal. Switching back preserved both results.

The binding-store suite now registers the recovery scenarios in a separate file. Three cases failed on the prior implementation. All 43 cases passed with the fix, including status changes during a read, an unrelated turn and five simulated minutes without a notification. The final suite took 244.58 s on one worker including compilation, with zero skips. The split keeps the same cases and order.

## Limits

Detached observation requires a saved, acknowledged follow-up under the same authority. A lost recovery connection, changed binding, read timeout or inconclusive history can still leave the result pending. These trials used local maintenance restarts. They do not establish zero downtime or recovery across a cluster outage.

The worker view relies on status changes from the recovery connection between reads. An empty worker list can mean observation was lost. If observation fails, a ready-to-stop status alone cannot prove that the worker finished. Reconcile the original task before shutdown or resubmission. If the goal is paused and you intend to resume it, the following command worked in the same conversation on the original Gateway.

```text
/goal resume Read the current goal. Wait for the existing worker and verify its result. Do not resend the task or spawn a replacement.
```

Resume starts a parent turn. Check for activity, unresolved effects and the reason for the pause first. In the unmodified Gateway trial, the scripted parent used `wait_agent` on the existing worker. The native server stayed up.

The available registry lacked the locked `@openclaw/fs-safe` version. Local typechecking with the existing dependencies reported the same 48 diagnostics before and after the change. Exact-lockfile CI and maintainer review remain outstanding. Independent source reviews were completed. The standalone review helper could not start on this host.

prs.title: fix: keep startup integrity test snapshots alive
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The startup integrity test retains its SQLite reader only inside a one-shot message callback. Garbage collection can close that reader while the child process remains alive, releasing the snapshot and making the checkpoint assertions fail.

## User Impact

CI keeps testing the intended scheduled-checkpoint and owned-scan cancellation behavior with a live pinned snapshot. Production behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing probe callback now queries the same database before replying. This retains the connection for the child’s lifetime and verifies that it is still usable. Checkpoint, cancellation, unrelated-database, and recovery assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

- Linux, pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`, 8 CPUs: controlled GC collected the original reader and failed the existing blocked-checkpoint assertion. The candidate retained the reader and passed the full scenario under the same GC control.
- The candidate also passed the uninstrumented owning test. Formatting and lint passed (0 warnings, 0 errors).
- The original CI run did not record collection timing; the controlled comparison establishes the fixture lifetime defect. [Original failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45721282246/job/139580633540).

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204943

prs.title: fix(doctor): keep migration recovery available with stale FTS indexes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #205506: Doctor could not complete a pending credential migration when the agent database had malformed canonical FTS indexes. Dedicated recovery also required that migration to finish.

## Changes and User Impact

This keeps @sunlit-deng’s preserving approach and original commit. Doctor can retain canonical FTS-only findings in the pre-migration backup, then use the existing preserving index repair before reader admission. A QUICK finding triggers FULL classification before it can be tolerated. Mixed or unknown damage is still refused. A tolerated finding never creates a clean integrity receipt, and a prior clean FULL receipt is reused across the version and media phases. No database schema or version bump.

## Evidence

- **Original contributor proof (`e48a9cd2`):** Identical isolated v28 state/v27 agent copies under `doctor --fix --full-integrity-check`. Stable `2026.11.10` exited 1 on both malformed canonical indexes; the contributor build exited 0 after saving the backup, rebuilding both indexes, and moving credentials. State v42, credentials v1, and agent v44 passed integrity. Device identity and token rows, all 8 transcript events, 6 active events, and 5 FTS rows matched; all 9 config keys remained present.
- **Additional shipped-CLI proof on the recovery implementation:** Disposable rootless Podman, Node 26.12.1. Real `doctor --fix` recovered v27 and v38 (2026.11.9-era) agents; v38 used `--full-integrity-check`. Packaged `update repair` completed from v38. Canonical damage was confirmed before each run. Final agent v45/shared v42 passed integrity, both FTS searches found the preserved data, and v27 credential custody passed. Mixed table/FTS damage and unknown FTS both exited nonzero with verified-backup guidance, leaving original versions and transcript intact.
- **Focused tests on the adopted repair:** 75 migration, integrity-worker, and FTS tests, core typecheck, changed-file lint/format, and 23 wrapper extraction tests passed. The original backup regression was red on base; the follow-up clean FULL regression measured 2 live scans before the receipt-reuse fix and 1 afterward. These local results precede the contributor-branch integration; GitHub CI qualifies the integrated head. The offline CLI runs did not exercise a live Gateway or service restart.
- **Release applicability:** `release/2026.11.11` at `3d1e4fff043f852e2969c6cf2969d4d00b5071c1` retains the defective full-image check without the canonical FTS exception. The complete patch applied cleanly in an isolated three-way check. No release-branch CLI run or branch change was performed.

prs.title: test(gateway): expect a revoked person's Goal retry to be hidden as not found
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/gateway/chat-goal-created-authority.e2e.test.ts` fails on `main` in the revoked-role scenario of "finishes started Goal returns after role loss, refuses the next start, and honors Stop":

```
Expected: "missing scope: operator.write"
Received: "Session "agent:main:dashboard:<id>" was not found."
```

It turns `checks-node-changed` red on every PR whose changed-test selection includes it. For example, #205482 changes only `src/agents/subagents` and fails this check.

## User Impact

None. Test-only change. The product already refuses the revoked person's retry, starts no work and sends no reply. Only the error text the test expected is different.

## Why This Change Was Made

#204899 made `chat.send` from a personal profile that holds `operator.sessions.read` a session-participation request (`requiresSessionParticipation` in `method-scopes.ts`, deferred in `method-authorization.ts`). The participation check refuses a session the person can no longer join with `hiddenSessionNotFound`, so it does not reveal that the session exists. Before #204899 the same request stopped at the scope gate with `missing scope: operator.write`. The test still expected that older refusal.

The test now expects the hidden not-found refusal for the exact session key. The checks after it are unchanged and pass: the Gateway drains, the parent makes no new provider call (`parentCalls` stays 5), and the child call count is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/gateway/chat-goal-created-authority.e2e.test.ts`: fails before this change with the error above and passes after it (1/1).
- `oxfmt --check` clean.
- A direct push to `main` was refused by the repository ruleset ("Changes must be made through a pull request"), so this repair is a PR.
