prs.title: feat(msteams): send private and shared channel files to the channel's own SharePoint site
prs.body:
Closes #185926

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bots cannot send files in Microsoft Teams private or shared channels unless an operator configures a single central `sharePointSiteId`, which exposes every private channel's files to that site's members and still shows "request access" to channel members.

## User Impact

User impact: in private and shared channels, file sends now land on that channel's own SharePoint site, where exactly the channel's members already have access, and the file card opens without extra permissions. No organization-wide sharing link is created for those files. Standard channels, group chats and explicit `sharePointSiteId` keep their current behavior. No new Graph permissions and no config changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on #189339. Teams keeps a private/shared channel's site membership in sync with the channel, so the channel's own site is the only upload target that preserves the channel audience. For a non-standard `membershipType`, the resolver reads `GET /teams/{groupId}/channels/{channelId}/filesFolder`, then `GET /drives/{driveId}?$select=sharePointIds` (drive resources spell it `sharePointIds`; driveItems use `sharepointIds`), and builds the site ID `{hostname},{siteId},{webId}`. Results are cached per account, tenant, bot, team and channel, like the team-site cache.

`resolveMSTeamsSharePointSiteId` now returns `{ siteId, memberScoped }`. Member-scoped uploads skip `createLink`: the organization link that channel sends create would let anyone in the tenant holding its URL read a private-channel file, and channel membership already grants access through the file card's `webDavUrl`. An incomplete drive response fails closed before upload.

## Evidence

- **Focused tests:** `vitest` msteams config, 92 files / 943 tests pass. New cases run the real send paths (proactive and reply) against stubbed Graph `fetch`: private and shared channels upload to the channel site, never call `/groups/.../sites/root` or `createLink`, and cache the channel site (one `filesFolder` call across two sends); member-scoped uploads create no link; incomplete `sharePointIds` fails closed.
- **Static:** `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: typecheck (extensions and extension tests), lint, plugin boundaries and the other guards pass. The dead-export scan fails only on `src/gateway/control-ui-session-pr-prepared-read.ts` (`retireControlUiSessionPrState`), unrelated to this change.

### Real behavior proof (production)

Multi-team production deployment, private channel, `sharePointSiteId` absent.

**Before** (#189339's behavior; private channels rejected). Gateway file log, redacted:

```
14:00:01Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 3 rows of test data"
          conversation: 19:<private-channel-id>@thread.tacv2;messageid=<id>
14:00:01Z [msteams] dispatching to agent
14:02:57Z [tools] tool_call failed: msteams file send failed: Automatic SharePoint site discovery
          supports standard channels only. Set channels.msteams.sharePointSiteId to upload to a specific site.
14:03:02Z [msteams] dispatch complete — counts: { tool: 0, block: 0, final: 1 }
```

The user received a text-only reply. No file reached the channel.

**After** (this change, backported onto the deployed release). Same private channel, first file send after a gateway restart (empty cache):

```
11:24:17Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 4 rows of test data"
11:24:17Z [msteams] dispatching to agent — sessionKey: agent:main:msteams:channel:19:<private-channel-id>…
11:24:36Z [msteams:send] sent native file card — fileName: <report> 1.csv
```

Graph check after the send (bot application credentials):

- `<folder>/<report> 1.csv` (created 11:24:35Z) sits on the private channel's own site (`/sites/<team>-<private-channel>`).
- Item permissions are only the channel site's Owners / Members / Visitors groups. No `organization` link.
- The parent team site has no entry for this send.
- The requester opened the file card from the channel.

During rollout, the first build read `sharepointIds` from the drive and failed closed ("incomplete SharePoint IDs") without uploading anything; Graph returns `sharePointIds` on drive resources. A later build still created the organization link; Graph showed it on the item, which is why member-scoped uploads now skip `createLink`.

### Access check (member, non-member, removal)

Same private channel. Each person opened the file's direct document URL in a browser, signed in with their own work account. Times are UTC.

| Step | Who | File | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Channel member | `<report-1>.csv`, sent by the bot | Opens (09:14) |
| 2 | Owner of the parent team, not a channel member. Also tried with their admin account | `<report-1>.csv` | Access denied (09:16) |
| 3 | The step 1 member, removed from the channel about 6 minutes earlier | `<report-1>.csv` | "You need access" (09:24) |
| 4 | Bot sends a new file in the same channel. No gateway restart, so the channel site comes from the cache | `<report-2>.csv` | Lands on the channel site (09:23). Inherits the library permissions; no sharing link |
| 5 | The removed member | `<report-2>.csv` | "You need access" (09:26) |
| 6 | A channel owner | `<report-2>.csv` | Opens (09:25) |

The removed user left the channel site's Members group without any bot action (checked 09:18). Access follows Teams channel membership.

Before step 1, an organization link on `<report-1>.csv` was deleted. A manual "Copy link" in the Teams client had created it, not the bot. After that, both files grant access only to the channel site's Owners, Members and Visitors groups (checked through SharePoint REST as a channel owner).

prs.title: fix(agents): honor imageMaxDimensionPx in provider and CLI image handoff
prs.body:
Refs: #205642

## What Problem This Solves

The provider streaming handoff in `prepareEmbeddedAttemptTransport` calls `materializeProviderContext` with neither `maxBytes` nor `maxDimensionPx`, so every replayed image falls back to the hardcoded `DEFAULT_IMAGE_MAX_DIMENSION_PX = 1200` in `src/agents/image-sanitization.ts`. `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx` therefore has no effect on that path: the report traced twelve `Image resized to fit limits` entries logging `maxDimensionPx=1200` while the config on disk read `2400`, and one more at `1200` after the value became `4096`.

The CLI prompt-image loader has the same gap in the other direction: `loadCliPromptImages` passes `maxBytes: MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` but never `maxDimensionPx`.

Every other prompt-image caller already reads the setting — `prompt-image-preparation`, `attempt-setup`'s context transform, `context:assistant`, and the agent-harness and worker variants all pass `resolveImageSanitizationLimits(cfg).maxDimensionPx`.

## User Impact

A configured `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx` now reaches provider replay and CLI prompt images. Users who raise it to keep screenshot or OCR detail get the value they configured instead of a silent 1200px downscale; users who lower it to cut vision tokens get the smaller payload on these two paths too.

Nothing changes for anyone who leaves the setting unset: `resolveImageSanitizationLimits` returns `{}` and the sanitizer keeps its existing default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The setting already existed and was already documented as applying "before provider calls" (`docs/gateway/config-agents/workspace-and-bootstrap.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`); only these two call sites dropped it. Threading the existing value is the narrow repair, and it reuses the owner that already resolves the limit rather than adding a second policy.

- `images.ts`: `materializeProviderContext` no longer omits `maxDimensionPx` from its parameter type. `maxBytes` stays omitted — whether `tools.media.image.maxBytes` should reach these callers is an open question in the report, not part of this fix.
- `provider-context-materializer.ts` (new): the handoff lambda moves out of `attempt-stream-settle.ts` into a named factory that passes `resolveImageSanitizationLimits(attempt.config).maxDimensionPx`. The move keeps `attempt-stream-settle.ts` inside its line cap (664 counted lines, under the 680 on the base) and puts the wiring next to the rest of the handoff.
- `cli-runner/helpers.ts`, `cli-runner/execute.ts`, `cli-runner.ts`: `loadCliPromptImages` accepts and forwards `maxDimensionPx`; both CLI callers pass the resolved config value.
- `message-transform-stream-wrapper.ts`: exports the `ProviderContextMaterializer` type the new factory returns.

The resize loop's separate "a candidate can be larger than its source" behavior is untouched; the report raises it as a second, independent defect.

## Evidence

Regression tests are red on the base behavior and green with the fix. Both assert the dimensions of the image block the provider actually receives, read back from the PNG header — not an intermediate argument.

`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/provider-context-materializer.test.ts` drives the production factory and inspects the resulting provider context:

```
base (limit line removed) — configured 40px ignored, source kept:
× resizes provider replay to the configured agents.defaults limit
  → expected { width: 80, height: 40 } to deeply equal { width: 40, height: 20 }

with the fix:
✓ keeps a source under the configured dimension limit byte-for-byte
✓ resizes provider replay to the configured agents.defaults limit
```

`src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts` drives `prepareCliPromptImagePayload` and reads the written CLI image:

```
base (passthrough removed):
× resizes CLI prompt images to the configured dimension limit
  → expected { width: 80, height: 40 } to deeply equal { width: 40, height: 20 }

with the fix:
✓ resizes CLI prompt images to the configured dimension limit
```

Consumers of the changed signatures still pass — 63 tests across `provider-context-materializer`, `images`, `message-transform-stream-wrapper`, `cli-runner.helpers`, and `attempt-prompt-execution-prepare`. `oxfmt --check` passes on every changed file.

Known gaps, stated rather than papered over: this machine cannot run `tsgo` (the binary needs a newer glibc) or `oxlint` (it aborts in its allocator), and its Node 24.13.1 embeds a SQLite build the runtime rejects, so `attempt-stream-settle.test.ts` cannot execute here. Those four SQLite failures reproduce identically on the untouched base (4 failed / 4 passed either way), and CI will cover type and lint. The end-to-end Gateway replay from the report was not re-run locally for the same reason.

## Merge Danger

Low. The default is unchanged when the setting is unset, and the newly threaded value only ever replaces the built-in 1200px constant with the operator's configured one. Non-provider image callers keep their current behavior, and `maxBytes` handling is deliberately unchanged.

The one intentional behavior change: images on provider replay and CLI prompt input can now be larger than 1200px when the config asks for it. That is the documented contract for these paths and the point of the fix; the marker text is measured after sanitization, so chunk limits are unaffected.

Related: #199621. Regression coverage for the selected-agent contract merged in #201207.

## What Problem This Solves

Changing sidebar owner filters used to change which agents' conversations appeared. #201207 fixed that behavior, but this PR's original real-Gateway diagnostic still expected the old cross-agent results and would fail when integrated with current main.

## User Impact

**Test-only: no shipped behavior or permission changes.** This PR now protects the already-merged rule that the selected agent scopes My sessions and All owners. It does not choose a new membership policy, claim a new product fix, or reproduce the reporter's installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The regression uses the existing isolated Gateway/browser fixture to select My sessions → All owners → My sessions while keeping the chat URL and selected agent unchanged. Every sidebar request must retain agentId=main. My sessions shows Main mine; All owners shows Main mine + Main other; the Research mine conversation stays excluded throughout.

The cross-agent session remains seeded and included in the three-key locator, so the test catches leakage rather than ignoring that row. The narrow locator also preserves coexistence with the preceding request-rate test. No new production helper, test server, schema, configuration option, or real provider call is introduced.

The product decision is no longer open: #201207 landed as [5d106ddc20f8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5d106ddc20f8fc5176f4048fb24ee9c2ddd93790). Related #198985 covers a different navigation-triggered transition.

The repair removes the obsolete conditional agent expectation and cross-agent personal membership expectation; it adds no machinery. The existing rate/ownership-refresh scenario and the real owner-filter round trip protect distinct boundaries. The three-key shared-fixture repair and unchanged-chat checks remain.

prs.title: fix: keep browser disabled when only hardening relay authentication
prs.body:
Closes #202959

## What Problem This Solves

Running `doctor --fix --non-interactive` after setting only `browser.extensionRelay.allowLegacyAuth=false` enables the browser plugin and adds it to an explicit plugin allowlist. A setting intended to restrict relay authentication should not itself request browser activation.

## User Impact

That exact hardening-only browser block no longer enables or allowlists browser. Explicit browser configuration, plugin entries, and browser tool references retain their existing activation behavior; disable and deny controls still apply.

If you relied on that sole flag to activate browser control, also set `browser.enabled=true`. Existing enabled/allowlisted browser entries are not removed. This does not change noninteractive allowlist repair generally or classify other hardening-only combinations.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser-owned setup probe now distinguishes the reported hardening-only shape from activation intent, while continuing its plugin-entry and tool-reference checks. Shared activation/materialization policy is unchanged. Both browser recovery guides document the narrow exception to the existing root-browser configuration rule.

## Evidence

The reported behavior was reproduced through the real Doctor CLI on Linux/Node 24.20.0, then rerun on this fix with isolated HOME, state, config, workspace, logs, named profiles, and loopback ports. No serving Gateway or real user state was changed.

| Real Doctor input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sole `allowLegacyAuth:false` | Browser enabled and allowlisted | Browser remains absent |
| No browser block | Inactive | Inactive |
| Hardening plus `defaultProfile` | Enabled | Enabled |
| `browser.enabled:false` | Inactive | Inactive |
| Browser plugin explicitly disabled | Inactive | Inactive |
| Browser in `plugins.deny` | Inactive | Inactive |

Actual Gateway processes confirmed browser loaded before the fix and absent afterward; the configured-browser positive control still loaded it. All reached ready, shut down cleanly, and released their ports.

Latest-stable source-upgrade proof used signed tag `v2026.11.6` at `06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638`, with its normal frozen-lockfile installation. Candidate Doctor preserves newly added hardening without enabling browser and retains browser entries written by stable Doctor. The separate documented Skill Workshop migration was explicitly accounted for; repeated candidate Doctor preserved the entire plugin policy exactly. The npm package was age-gated, so this is exact-source Doctor upgrade proof, not packaged-updater certification.

The regression failed on the original probe and passes with the fix. Browser tests: 10 passed; shared auto-enable and Doctor consumers: 75 passed. Full build, browser production and extension-test typechecks, targeted lint/format, docs inventory, and whitespace checks passed. The build emitted nonfatal UI bundle-budget warnings; no UI code changed.

**Review limitation:** native Auto Review captured the complete local candidate against `0c475b963b585012a180030bdabbfb0016027505`, but its 600-second attempt and authorized 1,200-second retry timed out without a validated report. No clean-review verdict or patch rating is claimed. Publication follows the repository's explicit timeout-without-report continuation rule; normal maintainer judgment and enforced GitHub checks remain required. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44918557130) passed for `a15d4d19eead04b159203db4214fe38fb4c0423b`: 21 jobs passed and 31 were skipped by scope. The exact-head `openclaw/ci-gate`, security-sensitive review, and dependency-review statuses are successful. The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203137#issuecomment-7065101244) requested inspectable runtime and compatibility evidence; the captured output below addresses that request without changing the source head.

prs.title: fix: recover Linux stream automations after command-anchor crashes
prs.body:
Closes #202900

## What Problem This Solves

A Linux stream automation can stop permanently when its command anchor crashes: it immediately exhausts its restart budget, and disabling and re-enabling it cannot recover the retained cleanup failure. Simply clearing that failure is unsafe: a detached child can remain alive after both the source and anchor disappear.

## User Impact

Stream automations recover through their existing backoff after the command anchor dies, including across shutdown and restart. Old descendants are stopped and reaped before replacement. No configuration or data migration is required.

Strict Linux child scopes retain one additional native relay process. Losing that final custodian remains fail-closed: neither retry nor manual enable overrides unconfirmed extinction. macOS/Windows, owned workers, and intentional root-exit handoffs keep their existing paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing relay now retains kernel subreaper custody outside the command anchor for strict, non-handoff Linux child scopes. After anchor loss, it adopts and reaps detached descendants and supplies an independent extinction certificate. The host joins that certificate, output/lineage closure, and relay exit before releasing cleanup. Cron continues using its existing restart owner and backoff; no exhaustion bypass is added.

Certificate observation stays with the retirement owner. Existing startup/private-input settlement moves into preparation to preserve the enforced module-size limit without changing its admission or cleanup behavior.

## Evidence

**Verified result (2026-11-21 16:51 UTC):** The [completed exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203149#issuecomment-7065332600) rates patch quality **4/6 platinum**, proof **5/6 diamond**, with no actionable findings and ready for maintainer review. The [exact-head CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44926099508) is successful on `0c080a7fc16a7f0c341eb400df78e93a0d635b99`; the full observed check inventory has no failed or active checks. This PR is open and non-draft; it has not been merged or deployed.

### Forced-cancellation review repair

The [second hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/44923917782), on `f2430a8c0f37f957dbda9dff0a03895fc014e2db`, accepted both prior fixes and rated the real terminal proof 5/6, but found a P2 cancellation-result regression. That finding is repaired in `0c080a7fc16a7f0c341eb400df78e93a0d635b99`: after independent extinction is certified, an explicitly requested cancellation uses the existing requested-signal result instead of becoming an unexpected-anchor-loss error. Unexpected anchor loss still rejects its missing command result; loss of final custody still rejects cleanup.

The new native regression runs a real child that ignores SIGTERM, then closes its strict scope within a 500ms cleanup budget. On the reviewed head cleanup succeeds but `run.wait()` rejects; on the repaired head it returns `reason: manual-cancel`, `exitSignal: SIGKILL`, and the child is absent. The unexpected-loss regression now explicitly requires the error rather than swallowing it. **88 native/supervisor cases pass** (40.9s wrapper), including the failed-custody and deadline controls. Core/services-test types, touched-file lint/format, session-identity and line-cap guards pass; the runtime build and real Gateway matrix were rerun on this repaired tree. The final exact-head review and CI now pass, as recorded above.

### Review and CI repairs

The [initial review of 3789e953445a](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/44921819901) identified two P2 defects, both reproduced locally and repaired in `f2430a8c0f37f957dbda9dff0a03895fc014e2db`:

- Prepared and overlay matrix runtimes now bind **both** compiled native owners through the existing sealed-runtime manifest. This restores the intent of [d782bc046eba / #181621](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d782bc046ebaa39fcea10fc98798c04d74f899a3): source-loader compiler children cannot share exclusive kernel child-wait ownership. The loader prohibition is unchanged; the companion fixture supplies the same complete native closure.
- Custody receipts now enter through the host's existing generation-validated dispatcher. The retirement owner no longer adds a second filtering listener. The session-identity guard passes without a baseline change or renamed comparison.

Repair proof: the previously failing matrix file now passes all 4 cases; the selected matrix/resolver/native-host group passes 74 tests (45.2s wrapper), sealed-build consumers pass 70 tests, and the real cloud-worker mid-turn-loss composition passes (85.8s wrapper). That last local fixture initially lacked Debian `ps`; genuine signed-repository procps 4.0.2 and its library were staged only in task scratch, then the same test passed through the real native utility. No application guard or test assertion was relaxed. Core, scripts, tooling-test and E2E-test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, line-cap, session-identity and runtime-process-lifecycle checks pass. The runtime build and full disposable Gateway matrix were rerun after repair. Initial CI run [44920799768](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44920799768) remains failed evidence for the first head; the final head has its own successful CI receipt above; the original failed run is not backdated green.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal receipts from the repaired real Gateway run</summary>

The following is the terminal receipt projection from the same public CLI/Gateway reproduction, completed 2026-11-21 16:28 UTC on the repaired tree. Addresses, paths, process/job identifiers and credentials are omitted; statuses and observed cleanup results are retained. The published file blobs were compared with that tested tree. The before-state and source regression are described above; this is not an in-process mocked Gateway.

```json
{"case":"midrun-recovered","at":"2026-11-21T16:27:57.933Z","streamStatus":"running","failures":1,"restartExhausted":false,"oldExtinct":true}
{"case":"same-gateway-disable-enable","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:02.756Z","streamStatus":"running","failures":0,"restartExhausted":false}
{"case":"gateway-stop","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:03.168Z","exitCode":0}
{"case":"shutdown-reopen-recovered","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:10.774Z","streamStatus":"running","failures":1,"restartExhausted":false}
{"case":"detached-descendant-reclaimed","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:47.538Z","streamStatus":"running","failures":1,"restartExhausted":false,"oldExtinct":true,"noOverlap":true}
{"case":"custodian-loss-fail-closed","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:52.256Z","streamStatus":"error","failures":1,"restartExhausted":true,"noReplacement":true}
{"case":"gateway-stop","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:52.644Z","exitCode":0}
{"case":"cleanup","at":"2026-11-21T16:28:52.648Z","allRecordedProcessesAbsent":true,"portRebound":true}
```

The source emitted `{}` periodically with a deliberately nonmatching predicate, so these cases made no model turn. Faults targeted only fixture processes after checking their birth identity and ancestry. The real custodian-loss control remained in error and could not admit a replacement.

</details>

The real disposable Gateway reproduced the original failure before the change. The repaired source passed the same production CLI/Gateway flows:

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Command anchor killed mid-run | Error/exhausted with zero restart attempts | Old processes extinct, restart after normal 30-second backoff |
| Disable/enable in the same Gateway | Remained exhausted | Running again, restart counter reset |
| Anchor killed immediately before shutdown; same state reopened | Persisted cleanup error/exhaustion | Clean stop and running source after reopen |
| Detached descendant outlives root and anchor | Descendant remained alive | Adopted and reaped before replacement; no overlap |
| Final custodian killed | No equivalent additional custodian on base | Cleanup remains unconfirmed; manual enable does not start a replacement |

The final proof used a nonmatching stream predicate: no channel or model execution was needed. Every recorded fixture process disappeared, both Gateway stops exited 0, and the fixture port rebound successfully. This is Linux source proof with the normal pinned OpenClaw Bun runtime and a Node 24.20 feeder, not packaged-release or Node-26 parity.

- Native regression fails on base `0c475b963b585012a180030bdabbfb0016027505` with the missing closing receipt, and passes on the candidate. The existing deadline test now stalls the final custodian rather than the recoverable inner anchor; it still requires a failed cleanup result.
- Initial published-head focused run: **122 passed, 1 platform-specific skip**, across 12 files, 64.8 seconds wrapper wall. The changed native file also ran independently; baseline wrapper 38.6 seconds, initial candidate 37.2 seconds. Per-file CI seconds were not collected.
- `pnpm build:runtime`, core and selected services-test typechecks, touched-file typed lint/format, line-cap/assertion-safety guards, import-cycle check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Review history:** Auto Review was attempted on the full local candidate against the pinned base, P0–P2, with relevant unchanged owner context. The same managed route timed out after 1,200 seconds without a report. That attempt supplies no clean-review verdict. All three findings across the two subsequent hosted review cycles were repaired. The final exact-head review is linked above and reports no actionable findings, patch quality 4/6 and proof confidence 5/6.
- No failure-alert destination was configured in the reported reproduction. The existing alert path is unchanged; configured external terminal-source notification delivery is not claimed as live-tested.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands and scope</summary>

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay-host*.test.ts src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay.native-owner.test.ts src/process/supervisor/supervisor.cleanup-history.real.test.ts src/process/supervisor/supervisor.test.ts src/process/supervisor/supervisor.root-exit.real.test.ts src/gateway/cron-stream-watchers.extinction.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron.stream-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

`node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay-host.test.ts","src/process/supervisor/supervisor.cleanup-history.real.test.ts"]'`

The repair changes 14 existing files. No production cleanup path was replaced with a PID census or a fabricated receipt. Necessary growth is the independent native custody join and its regression coverage; the input-startup movement is behavior-preserving. Broader platform/CI proof remains with normal PR CI.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): align offline shell terminal capability with CSP
prs.body:
Fixes #205656.

## What Problem This Solves

After the Control UI recovers from its cached offline shell, reconnecting to a Gateway with Terminal enabled can expose Terminal in a document whose CSP cannot compile WebAssembly. Ghostty then fails and its fallback asset requests can display a misleading 404.

## User Impact

Terminal stays disabled in the offline document until an existing config refresh can request a reload into a document with the appropriate CSP. Unsaved-work reload guards remain respected. Releasing a guard alone does **not** trigger a reload: a subsequent config refresh requests it once permitted. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The offline-shell producer now declares `data-openclaw-terminal-enabled="false"`, matching its strict CSP. This reuses the existing document-policy reconciliation and reload guard; it neither widens CSP nor adds another reload mechanism.

The regression uses the shared service-worker harness to install synthetic build assets, receive actual worker-generated HTML after a 503 navigation, and apply its attributes before importing config. It extends the existing reload-owner test instead of duplicating it, retaining the guarded transition and proving that an explicit later refresh requests exactly one reload. Existing navigation cases retain CSP/import-map and root/subpath coverage.

## Evidence

Verified against base `c7824fb4d2b0f11fd3e6e9740f30489dba150b76`:

- **Red before repair:** the changed suites failed in four expected cases: three missing-marker navigation assertions, and Terminal incorrectly becoming enabled while the reload guard blocked.
- **Green after repair:** `pnpm test ui/src/app/service-worker-cache.test.ts ui/src/app/document-reload-owners.test.ts ui/src/app/config.test.ts ui/src/app/vite-config-cache.node.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **4 files, 71 tests passed**, runner shard wall time 2.62s. This independently observed count replaces the previously reported 72; the existing reload-owner case was expanded, not duplicated.
- Changed suites also ran separately with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: service-worker cache, 52 tests, runner wall time 1.35s (Vitest 414ms); document reload owners, 1 test, runner wall time 1.58s (Vitest 713ms). Per-suite CI seconds were not extracted; the complete CI workflow finished successfully.
- `pnpm format:check ui/public/sw.js ui/src/app/service-worker-cache.test.ts ui/src/app/document-reload-owners.test.ts` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/public/sw.js ui/src/app/service-worker-cache.test.ts ui/src/app/document-reload-owners.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, and `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pnpm ui:build` — passed, including finalized compressed-sidecar verification. The emitted worker contains the Terminal-disabled marker and its offline CSP excludes `wasm-unsafe-eval`. The build's report-only performance step reported largest CSS gzip 58,659 B versus 58,315 B and chat boot JS 21 requests versus 20; this is not a passing performance-budget check.
- `pr-simplify` author pass: retained the existing producer, reload owner, and shared harness; no new production mechanism. Delta against base: production +2/-1 lines; tests +41/-9 lines. Test growth covers the actual offline HTML-to-config boundary rather than a hand-supplied capability marker.
- Bound Auto Review of the complete three-file local snapshot against the base above (verified tree-identical to published head `61c779b076f614b21a31cfaed50ea80f60546cc9`): `scoped-clean`, no findings at its default **P0-only** priority. This is not an all-priority review or a hosted ClawSweeper rating.

**Verification gaps:** These are VM/jsdom boundary tests with synthetic network responses, not real-browser, Gateway, Ghostty-rendering, or PTY proof. No live reproduction of the fallback 404, local full Gateway build, or production-browser/Gateway/PTY acceptance proof is claimed. A local browser preflight found no runnable Chromium at the pinned, cached, or system fallback locations. Draft CI was skipped; after the requester authorized landing and the Control UI build passed, this PR was marked ready for review.

- [CI run 45737693561](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45737693561) completed successfully for head `61c779b076f614b21a31cfaed50ea80f60546cc9`. prs.title: fix(whatsapp): identify voice-note captions as text in delivery receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the WhatsApp listener sent a voice note with a caption, WhatsApp accepted two messages. The combined delivery receipt labeled both as media, so a consumer reading the receipt could not identify the caption as text.

## User Impact

The receipt now identifies the audio message as media and the caption as text, in send order. It keeps both provider message IDs and counts the pair as one outbound activity.

## Why This Change Was Made

The send API already records the kind and provider key of each accepted message. The combined receipt now carries those physical parts forward and numbers them in delivery order.

## Evidence

Replayed a 251-frame Ogg voice note with a caption through the listener and send API against an in-memory transport. The original returned two media entries. The fix returned media at index 0 and text at index 1, with the same primary ID, destination, participant and sender metadata.

Eight send scenarios covered the caption, voice-only and whitespace-only inputs, plain text, separate calls, video, poll and the higher-level voice/text split. Formatting, focused lint and the line-cap check passed. Hosted Vitest passed 32 send-api cases, including the two child receipt kinds and partial caption acceptance. prs.title: fix: keep container dashboard origins current after public origin changes
prs.body:
Related: #157170

## What Problem This Solves

A container's published host port can differ from the Gateway listener. Treating listener origins as saved defaults strands the dashboard after a custom mapping or a public-origin change.

## User Impact

Docker and Podman users can open and pair the dashboard after selecting a custom published port, without saving stale listener origins. Explicit origin lists remain authoritative. Existing lists that no longer match the chosen port receive actionable guidance rather than being rewritten; selected older images may need an upgrade to preserve an authored empty list.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Carry the existing Docker/Podman mapping as an internal, launch-only fact. Explicit `--published-port` wins; valid host-qualified/dynamic Compose mappings remain supported. No saved config field or user-facing environment control is added. Config-env and dotenv owners exclude the internal transport from persisted inputs.
- Use the canonical origin resolver across Gateway HTTP/WS, pairing, image CORS, and plugin dispatch. Mapped loopback grants require direct ordinary ingress, not trusted-proxy auth, reverse proxies, managed Serve/Funnel, or relayed ingress. Plugin defaults weakly bind to the exact serving request (without retaining its headers/socket) and must satisfy its policy as well as caller-supplied policy; omitted caller config keeps former behavior.
- Preserve direct image entrypoint and Doctor activation, with early port validation and explicit-flag precedence. Omitted policy inherits the current public origin and mapped loopback pair; usable authored lists and `[]` remain authoritative on current images. Blank-only legacy lists retain their existing runtime-only recovery.
- Keep older images' omitted-field/no-public-origin custom-port seed without inferring list provenance. Probes invoke Node directly (including Node-only custom images), remain isolated/state/credential-free, clean up, and pin the selected immutable image for invocation. The existing Podman launch timeout also bounds probe preparation. Fresh legacy Podman setup works without Python; existing JSON5 uses the canonical CLI reader and scoped writer.
- Align the security audit with canonical launch defaults, effective auth mode, and authored `[]`; preserve missing/blank/trusted-proxy diagnostics without recommending dangerous Host-header fallback. Malformed inherited launch input yields a warning rather than aborting the audit or logging its raw value. When an explicit startup override is unknown to the audit, an otherwise-derived missing-origin conclusion is marked uncertain; independent authentication findings remain intact.
- Preserve current main's admit-once request authority and retired Fleet paths. Remove duplicate provider fixtures, test-only SDK exports, wrapper negotiation, and unrelated policy-revocation tests. The change stays one vertical container-origin repair rather than adding an origin-policy manager.

### Saved-policy and older-image tradeoff

Setup never appends to or overwrites authored lists. A saved loopback list that no longer matches the selected port gets an actionable warning before Podman replacement: edit that list explicitly, or remove the field to inherit current-image defaults. Warning-only replacement is intentional; this does not introduce a new launch permission gate.

**An older selected image may rewrite authored `[]` during its own Doctor activation, using internal-listener origins.** The shared probe warns before replacement and the guides explain that the image must be upgraded if `[]` must remain authoritative. Setup neither rewrites `[]` nor bypasses Doctor to conceal this older-image limitation.

## Evidence

Validation base: `ba6d94ec17712094f485b85d6923f246b459844b`. Retained production-validation head: `6d677b7345b70cea66303a935f9bd26d5e53fa84`; subsequent changes are test-only CI repairs, recorded below.

- Review defects reproduced red before repairs: entrypoint Doctor activation, browser pairing, ambient-Serve protected image bytes, Doctor/onboarding persistence, inherited-port validation before reset, launcher metadata from saved config/dotenv, SDK partial/omitted configuration, legacy JSON5/fresh Python-free setup, and missing outer HTTP policy plumbing.
- The runtime/policy repair replay passed **83 tests / 7 files / 3 shards in 89.88s**, including actual Docker/Podman shell entrypoints, the native Gateway, real non-loopback plugin HTTP dispatch/client, and persisted dotenv loader admission.
- The latest deployment/audit replay passed **129 tests / 7 files / 2 shards in 83.36s**. Actual launch boundaries reproduced the Node-only image refusal and lost configured-timeout delivery; the audit owner reproduced false critical findings for launch defaults and intentional `[]`. Docker/Podman, actual native image entrypoint, and security-audit siblings all pass. Timeout fixtures prove budget delivery, not a real container stall.
- The final request-binding/audit-recovery replay passed **67 tests / 7 files / 2 shards in 87.85s**, including real prior-request versus current-request HTTP effects, live Gateway HTTP/WS/settlement siblings, and retained independent audit findings after malformed metadata.
- The first published CI found a core/SDK exported-name collision. The internal Gateway resolver now has its own distinct spelling; the public SDK export and behavior are unchanged. The actual collision guard reproduced red and now passes; **40 affected origin/pairing/real HTTP tests** pass in 47.90s, with core/Gateway-test types and focused type-aware lint green.
- The next exact-head CI exposed two writer fixtures replacing the complete container module and hiding the canonical published-port parser. Both now pass through real exports while retaining their simulated non-container host; the mock-debt baseline shrinks by two. The actual update writer reproduced three failures red; **17 owner/sibling cases across 3 files passed in 72.91s** after repair. Dedicated update and Doctor test type graphs, type-aware lint, formatting, diff and mock-export ratchet passed. Local ClawSweeper review of `023e0a08..6d677b73` found no correctness/security findings; no production policy changed.

prs.title: fix: show provider usage for model API key SecretRefs
prs.body:
Closes #150173

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw status --usage` and Gateway `usage.status` can omit a provider when its configured model API key is a SecretRef. A failed credential lookup could also interrupt the entire CLI status report.

## User Impact

Operators can see usage with their existing SecretRefs. If one lookup fails, status keeps reporting available usage and includes a diagnostic without the resolver’s raw error. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

CLI status resolves only the configured provider API keys within its existing time budget, keeping the original config available for fallback. Uncertain subprocess cleanup still stops the command. Managed Gateway usage continues to check the captured credential owner at request time.

Thanks to @alex-strattab for the report, @Samay10 for the original investigation in #150192, and @meska for the Z.AI store report.

## Evidence

- On Node 24.22.1, all **74 tests across six files** passed (70.37 seconds across three repository test shards). The new regression failed before the fallback change and passes now; it also verifies that uncertain cleanup still fails the command. Online JSON coverage verifies that scan and usage diagnostics both reach the output.
- Core and command/infra test typechecks, scoped lint and formatting, test-line/timeout/mock guards, the unified runtime build, and the CLI bootstrap import guard passed. The test allocation is exactly 275 net lines for the credential, deadline, cleanup, and output regressions; it uses the upstream budget restored by #196432.
- Independent source review verified the follow-up. Earlier built loopback evidence for [CLI and Gateway usage and the deadline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187360#issuecomment-6489445493) and [managed credential checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187360#issuecomment-6490298252) remains scoped to the revisions recorded there. Callers that already hold independently resolved plaintext config remain outside the managed snapshot’s revocation guarantee.
- Hosted CI and maintainer review for this head are separate from the local checks.

### Built CLI fallback proof

Node 24.22.1, repository `cliStartup` build, head `ee435a893be7652c4f41c04e86b3f5ebd8423ab5`. The CLI command was `openclaw status --usage --agent main --json` with an isolated config and synthetic credentials.

The missing-env case leaves a configured environment SecretRef unset. A separate loopback Gateway protocol fixture returns a malformed `secrets.resolve` reply to exercise the preparation-error fallback in online JSON (`collection.source=gateway`, `gateway.reachable=true`). The real CLI emits the generic diagnostic and retains healthy OpenRouter usage from two native loopback HTTP requests. The raw resolver error and fixture credentials are absent from CLI output.

```text
malformed-response exit=0 secrets.resolve=1 diagnostics=1 credits=200 key=200 balance=21 USD key_budget=20% credentials_or_fault_marker=false
missing-secret exit=0 secrets.resolve=1 diagnostics=2 credits=200 key=200 balance=21 USD key_budget=20% credentials_or_fault_marker=false
healthy-control exit=0 secrets.resolve=0 diagnostics=0 credits=200 key=200 balance=21 USD key_budget=20% credentials_or_fault_marker=false
```

These three product CLI cases passed locally. A subsequent Node 24.22.1 rerun compiled and verified the full test fixture graph and passed all 72 cases across five files in three repository Vitest shards. The same 72 cases and the required checks passed in hosted CI for this head.

AI-assisted implementation and verification.

### November 24 upstream refresh

- Synced upstream main at `7cbf1585ed7` to resolve the merge conflict. The refresh preserves status usage diagnostics and fallback for ordinary lookup failures. Ctrl+C now reaches the credential Gateway request and owned subprocesses, then stops the status operation before usage collection.
- On Node 24.22.1, commit `00773a43612` passed 100 tests across six files and four repository Vitest shards. Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, the staged test-line budget, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The two new cancellation regressions both failed with signal forwarding removed and passed after it was restored. Independent Codex source review identified the missing Gateway signal and rechecked the transport path after the correction.

### November 26 upstream refresh

- Synced upstream main at `03b61bcb974`. Upstream moved the credential request into `command-secret-gateway-request.ts`. The same explicit abort signal now travels through that request module, and cancellation still skips local fallback.
- On Node 24.22.1, `8866c0514a3` passed 117 tests across seven files, including the Gateway abort suite and upstream offline credential resolution cases. Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, the test-line budget, and `git diff --check` passed.

prs.title: fix: repair orphaned Workboard card rows with Doctor
prs.body:
Related: #205245

## What Problem This Solves

Workboard card-child rows that reference a missing card can block an update at the candidate state snapshot. The snapshot correctly refuses those broken foreign keys, but affected operators don't have a supported repair.

## User Impact

With the Gateway stopped and Workboard enabled on a build containing this repair, run `openclaw doctor --fix`, then retry the update. Doctor preserves a private WAL-aware SQLite backup, deletes only supported orphan rows in one transaction, and refuses unrelated foreign-key violations. A clean rerun changes nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Workboard owns the repair in its existing Doctor contract. The updater and its integrity gate are unchanged; the recovery instructions live in the docs. The existing Doctor SQLite backup helper is exposed through the existing repair SDK subpath because the generic capture rejects FK-invalid databases. The backup retains the removed rows, so no separate export is needed. The writer that created the orphans remains unknown.

## Evidence

**Stable v2026.11.10 → branch-built Doctor, synthetic state.** Stable created the Workboard database and healthy card. After inserting one synthetic orphan, both CLIs ran `doctor --fix` against that same isolated state. Redacted log and SQLite verification excerpts:

```text
v2026.11.10 doctor --fix: Doctor complete; foreign_key_check still reports 1 Workboard label orphan.
Branch doctor --fix: Repaired orphaned Workboard card rows; backup: <private-state>/plugins/workboard/openclaw-workboard-card-orphans-recovery-<id>/database.sqlite
foreign_key_check: []; integrity_check: ok
Preserved: card="Keep stable card", label="keep-label", Workboard enabled, Gateway mode and configured port unchanged.
Backup contains the original orphan: card_id="orphan-fixture", label="remove-label".
Clean doctor --fix rerun: Doctor complete; no Workboard repair reported; recovery backups: 1 (no second backup).
```

**Regression red on main, green on PR head.** Ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/doctor-contract-api.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on both. On main, transplanted only the test diff; production sources were unchanged.

```text

FAIL  repairs card orphans only when no unrelated FK violations exist
Error: expected Workboard orphan repair to be defined
Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11) — exit 1

PR head c77e357c3110
✓ repairs card orphans only when no unrelated FK violations exist
Tests  11 passed (11) — exit 0
```

The 10 Doctor declaration/import-closure tests, targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, SDK export synchronization/check, docs links, and diff whitespace checks also passed. The smoke was a manual CLI handoff, not an end-to-end run of the native updater. The full runtime build timed out at startup metadata after emitting the CLI exercised here; the full SDK API diff timed out during rendering. Neither is claimed as a pass.

prs.title: fix(test): unblock restart-auth plugin and worker publication qualification
prs.body:
## Problem

Two test-fixture defects surfaced in `2026.12.1-beta.1` Full Release Validation. Hosted validation is still needed to confirm whether they explain the observed failures.

1. **Docker `update-restart-auth` (FRV R7, job 139515690632):** `Error: whatsapp plugin version changed: 2026.12.1-beta.1`. A resident Gateway can finish the core update before its watcher records the `plugins` step. The survivor could read the old install before maintenance finished. The core-only receipt does not establish whether maintenance was delayed or failed.
2. **Normal CI `checks-node-compact-large-16` (FRV R7, job 139500906507):** the direct worker context-engine case hit the prepared model runtime publication timeout. The test replaced the fixture's entire `plugins` object to select its context engine, inadvertently discarding its narrow allowlist and disabled memory slot.

## Fix

- Wait up to 720 s for the resident recovery run's `plugins` step, matched by `runId`, before checking the plugin. Report a failed step with its detail and time out separately on unfinished maintenance. Keep the existing version, integrity, no-fallback and serving checks.
- Merge the context-engine slot into the worker fixture's existing plugin config. Keep the publication deadline unchanged.

## Evidence

- Restart-auth fixture: 5/5 passed before shortening the fixture deadline from 3 s to 2 s. The regression failed on the original harness; the fixture covers late, failed, missing and wrong-run maintenance.
- Worker fixture: 3/3 passed before and after. A local sequential comparison under changing host load measured 97.6 s before and 29.1 s after for the direct case. This is not a controlled benchmark or hosted proof.
- Targeted lint, formatting, shell syntax and diff checks passed. Hosted Docker and the affected CI shard still need verification.

Release backport target: `release/2026.12.1`.

prs.title: fix: let long chats fork without losing searchable history
prs.body:
Related: #174730 ([incident evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/174730#issuecomment-7136416297))

## What Problem This Solves

Forking a long chat could fail before creating the child because the Gateway compared the selected history with the child model's input capacity. That prevented branching even though the full transcript need not be sent to the model. The incident showed the rejection; the later roster reading did not establish which estimator input produced it.

## User Impact

User impact: an explicit chat fork on the built-in OpenClaw API runner keeps the selected, searchable history and can continue from the recent decision. The child writes to its own transcript. This does not raise a model cap, shorten the parent, or change automatic/subagent or native-runtime fork admission. Active parents still require a completed fork point; reset boundaries and access checks stay in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

Copying a branch and fitting a model request are different operations. The runner now selects inherited turns against the space left after instructions, tools, current input and output reserve. Child-owned turns stay under normal compaction. Reply preflight no longer mistakes unmeasured copied history for a child request. Simply removing the creation check was insufficient: in the control run the first request summarized the old ledger and missed the recent decision.

## Evidence

- **Before:** at `f57a179eb81fc48c3d3f64bf2489c1fec3537bf1`, the real `sessions.create` WebSocket call returned `INVALID_REQUEST (45912/32768 tokens)`. No child and no model call. The old ledger alone was 104,868 tokens under `o200k_base`, not an inflated usage counter.
- **After:** clean build of PR head `d3aad208067b5e4eb158666a554d4a6e0e15bac8`, same saved synthetic parent. Child-scoped `sessions.search` found the old receipt in the child's own transcript. The neutral question did not repeat the answer. The first **and only** outbound request contained the recent decision, instructions and four tools, but none of the 2,800 old ledger rows. The built-in runner sent it to a real local Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct model via llama.cpp: **6,987 measured input + 2,048 reserved output = 9,035 / 32,768 tokens**. The generated and delivered answer was “The QA canary code we chose is CobaltTrellis49.” All seven parent events and the active leaf were unchanged. This is not a Gemini or live-parent retest.
- On that head, the committed [first-request E2E](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d3aad208067b5e4eb158666a554d4a6e0e15bac8/test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/session-fork-first-request.e2e.test.ts) and focused Gateway, automatic/subagent, active-run, reset and reply-preflight suites passed. The E2E uses a deterministic wire reader; the separate measurement above is actual model inference. The QA build passed. Local autoreview could not start its read-only reviewer sandbox; no local clean-review claim. Hosted review and CI are separate.

Reported, investigated and scoped by @hannesrudolph.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7078c128-58fd-4971-9162-a776152c87ac)

## Problem

Fixes #205506. When a state migration is pending, Doctor can refuse the rollback image because agent FTS5 indexes are stale, while recovery cannot begin until migration finishes. This builds on @sunlit-deng’s preservation approach in #205557 and addresses the review finding about false full-integrity receipts.

## Changes

- Allow preserving migration images (including heartbeat reuse) to retain findings only for canonical, rebuildable agent FTS indexes. A QUICK candidate with these findings gets a FULL classification so ordinary index damage cannot hide behind them.
- Reuse the existing clean full-verification receipt across migration and media preparation. Tolerated FTS findings produce no clean receipt and still reach the existing preserving index repair before reader admission.
- Include the existing FTS schema module in the trusted PR wrapper’s source inventory. No database schema/version bump or new recovery mechanism.

## Evidence

- The released 2026.11.10 CLI reproduced the snapshot refusal; the base regression failed on canonical FTS-only damage, while mixed damage was refused. With full policy propagated through both Doctor phases, the prior candidate repeated the live full scan (2); the corrected patch passes the test at 1. All 75 targeted migration, worker, and FTS tests passed, plus core typecheck, targeted lint, and format.
- The first CI run found the missing wrapper dependency. After adding it to the inventory, the full `eager-import-closure.test.ts` suite passed locally (23/23), including both failing checks.
- In disposable rootless Podman with Node 26.12.1, the recovery candidate’s real `doctor --fix` migrated agent v27 (2026.11.3) and agent v38 (2026.11.9); the v38 run used `--full-integrity-check`. Packaged `update repair` completed from v38. Damaged indexes were confirmed before execution. Agent v45/shared v42 passed SQLite integrity, both FTS searches found the original content, and the v27 synthetic identity and token moved to the credential vault.
- Mixed table/FTS damage and unknown FTS both exited nonzero with verified-backup guidance, retaining the original schema versions and transcript. That offline CLI proof predates the wrapper-inventory and clean-receipt follow-ups; it did not exercise Gateway serving or service restart.
- The defective snapshot path is still present on `release/2026.11.11` at `3d1e4fff043f852e2969c6cf2969d4d00b5071c1`: the full image checks integrity without the canonical FTS exception. prs.title: fix: reduce memory during SQLite usage refresh
prs.body:
Related: #197430

## What Problem This Solves

The background usage refresh can run out of memory on long SQLite chat histories, leaving token and cost totals stale. The paged reader limits decoded payloads, but the worker retains the navigation projection and every parsed billing entry while building the exact-timestamp rollup.

## User Impact

Lower peak heap during SQLite usage refresh without widening time buckets, dropping entries, or changing the cache format. No configuration change or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve billing, latency ancestry and the checkpoint first. Release the navigation projection, then drain the owned billing list in the same order into the existing pricing batches. The latency lookup uses weak keys so it does not keep processed entries alive. Exact buckets still scale with the number of distinct timestamps; this reduces overlapping memory, not the size of the final rollup.

## Evidence

- On current main (6ec27bd739c), the production SQLite scan with an in-memory SQLite fixture of 270,391 billed rows at unique millisecond timestamps reached **473 MiB** maximum sampled post-GC JS heap. The candidate reached **297 MiB** (37% lower), with identical exact-timestamp bucket output (SHA-256 d86644baa3562655253cf070d3254feee0fa59bdeb7cbb3e7108c429bad5cb53). This measures the scan and aggregation, not a production worker restart or an end-to-end cache publication.
- 60 targeted tests passed across refresh, snapshots, scan, codec and SQLite cache, including append, inherited history, rewinds, and branch-local latency. Targeted type-aware lint, format and diff checks passed.
- Reviewed the final diff locally against the billing and checkpoint contracts; the standalone autoreview helper was not installed.


### End-to-end Gateway proof

Tested the unchanged PR head `91e8b402593a1fbd9ef07a32963d481ca7a3f67d` (macOS arm64, Node 24.22.3). Seeded a fresh, isolated agent SQLite store through the existing transcript batch writer with 270,391 synthetic billed messages, each at a distinct millisecond. Started the real loopback Gateway with its usage sidecar enabled, without a heap override or mocks for the worker, SQLite, or cache. Polled `sessions.usage` from an empty cache until fresh, asserted exact expected totals, and checked the persisted SQLite cache after clean shutdown.

Redacted terminal evidence (selected fields; the worker measurement uses sampling, not forced GC):

```text
SQLite input: 270391 rows, 270391 unique generated timestamps
sessions.usage: cacheStatus=fresh input=540782 output=270391 totalTokens=811173 totalCost=33798.875
usage-cost refresh worker: old-generation limit=512 MiB, sampled peak JS heap=440 MiB (3526 samples)
Persisted cache: session-cost-usage-rollup-v3=1, session-cost-usage-projection-v2=1, session-cost-usage-quarters-v1=1
Gateway shutdown: completed cleanly; harness exit=0
```

The worker was sampled externally with Node's `Worker.getHeapStatistics()` while the Gateway owned the real refresh. This is a candidate-only end-to-end pass; the separate post-GC benchmark above is the before/after comparison. No production logs, personal chat data, or credentials were used.

prs.title: feat(doctor): repair externally managed runtime state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Deployment controllers need Doctor's runtime-state repairs without handing it ownership of deployment config or Gateway service lifecycle.

## User Impact

Deployment operators can stop their Gateway, repair supported runtime state, inspect a structured result, and restart through their own supervisor without Doctor rewriting their config or replacing their service. Config or credential problems still require deployment-owner action; incomplete repair is not reported as success.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openclaw doctor --fix --externally-managed --non-interactive --json` uses the canonical Doctor flow, maintenance custody, migration receipts, and existing state/session repair owners. It leaves deployment config bytes unchanged and does not stop, start, uninstall, or replace the deployment's Gateway service. The deployment must stop its Gateway before invoking repair.

The structured report distinguishes committed repairs, intentionally skipped config/service work, blocking warnings/refusals, and recoverable advisory warnings. Early exits and incomplete repair are not convergence. Cancellation still propagates through normal custody cleanup. Migration evidence is recorded after commits, including when a later step fails; aggregate summaries do not count the same committed repair twice.

This ports the proposal onto current main rather than restoring its retired parallel health entry point or duplicate auth-refresh helper. Existing deletion recovery, schema rehearsal, plugin-source custody, and write-authority behavior remain with their current owners. The feature's output/ownership posture crosses these owners as one complete change; splitting it into only some repairs would silently omit work or evidence.

## Evidence

- Current canonical-flow/evidence suite: 23 cases passed, including actual cancellation and incomplete/refused repair.
- Retained-state integration: 8 cases exercise real SQLite released-schema backup/repair and startup admission, unchanged config, raw session-row repair, committed evidence after later failure, and memory-repair warnings. A duplicate workspace-receipt regression failed before the projection correction.
- Real legacy-service scan with the actual Doctor prompter reproduced an uninstall attempt under this posture; the fix passes the full 33-case prompter/service suite.
- Changed command/session consumers: 59 cases across six files passed. These totals overlap the flow suite; they are not an aggregate test count.
- Qualified Doctor, flow/other, and config-CLI test type graphs, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, exact-base assertion/mock/test-line guards, documentation MDX/links, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full `pnpm build` passes, including UI, all SDK subpaths, declarations, and graph guards.
- Isolated shipped-CLI proof uses synthetic config/state and real SQLite migration, not the running Gateway. Config bytes remain unchanged. Remaining plugin/config warnings correctly keep the report non-converged.

Fresh local review identified six related faults: later repairs could consume an unpersisted config candidate, redacted stored Gateway credentials could still rotate, advisory migration warnings became blockers, heartbeat/dashboard results were dropped, and ordinary config-repair option shapes changed. These are repaired at the existing flow/evidence owners, without adding another repair orchestrator. The real credential-store regression failed before the guard; all 10 owning credential cases now pass. Canonical migration/advisory completion and heartbeat evidence regressions pass; real dashboard/session and external read-only flow integration passes.

The 280-line test allocation covers the excess beyond the normal 400-line budget for distinct actual SQLite, cancellation, legacy-service ownership, output, retained-schema, unchanged-credential, persisted-config, recoverable-advisory and previously dropped heartbeat/dashboard evidence boundaries, rather than duplicating implementation-only tests. Final review additionally reproduced a long-path advisory promoted after display shortening, a post-session receipt duplicated through unclassified callbacks, and ordinary token-generation hints under external custody. Classification now precedes display normalization; the receipt owns its repair evidence; recovery copy points to the deployment credential owner. Subsequent caller review restored the shared warning/change callbacks used by Gateway startup and updater failure capture; only Doctor filters duplicate receipt evidence. Raw contribution warnings are classified at their producer, never reclassified from the shortened display buffer. Optional trusted-proxy passwords retain the replace-or-remove choice through the deployment source, without touching healthy proxy authentication. Startup recovery-capture warnings share that same evidence sink before display normalization, and summary projection does not duplicate a refusal already owned by its migration receipt. The combined startup/refusal regression failed before this correction. Gateway auth flow moved intact into the existing auth-health owner instead of adding another repair helper or growing the over-budget registry. All three regressions pass with unchanged normal-credential controls.

The existing heartbeat ordering/evidence case was moved intact into the coherent evidence suite to avoid growth of its already-over-budget sibling; the 16-line excess records that shared setup, not a line-cap exception.

Final capture-warning correction keeps the capture owner's returned best-effort warnings advisory while required-evidence exceptions remain blocking. The new real-maintenance regression failed before the correction and passes alongside the 22-case refusal suite (28 cases total). Shared startup diagnostics remain unchanged. Local ClawSweeper reviewed `10f2fdf98dcc` → `079e481ba7da` and identified text-mode advisory visibility; the command now renders advisories without changing the success exit. The command regression covers JSON and text modes.

The committed capture correction also passed the full build, qualified flow test graph, scoped lint/format, and isolated real CLI first/repeat migration proof: config bytes unchanged, one workspace receipt on the first pass and none on repeat, SQLite setup preserved. Outstanding config/auth/plugin work still exits nonzero. The initial pre-commit launcher probe refused stale runtime-artifact publication under synthetic service inspection; the supported committed rebuild resolved it without changing the live Gateway or bypassing the guard.

## Limits

Current container-image replacement, full latest-stable binary upgrade/rollback, and a deployment supervisor's stop/start cycle have not been exercised here. Historical prior-head Package Acceptance is not current-head proof. Exact-head PR CI and fresh local committed-range review are recorded below after publication; pending or inherited failures are not passing checks.
