prs.title: fix: let Git updates build when pnpm uses a global virtual store
prs.body:
Related: #204775

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update` on a Git (source checkout) install stops at `staging: prepare:build` with "The new version could not be built. The current version is still running." whenever the host's user-level pnpm config sets `virtualStoreType: global` (pnpm 12). The Gateway keeps serving the old build, and every later update fails the same way. A plain `pnpm install && pnpm build` in a checkout on such a host fails too.

Root cause: `pnpm-workspace.yaml` pins `nodeLinker: isolated` but not the virtual store type, so pnpm takes `global` from the user config and links `node_modules/typescript` (and every other dependency) into the shared store under the user's home. The build's declaration-input guard (`scripts/lib/local-check-runtime.mts`, used by `scripts/lib/tsdown-declaration-boundary.mts`) requires compiler inputs to sit physically inside the checkout and rejects it: `Declaration input escapes checkout: … shared installs and external symlinks are unsupported`. The older Git runner wrote `virtualStoreType: project` into the candidate's workspace file (`src/infra/update-runner-git-commands.ts`). The release-based path `src/update/prepare-git.ts` runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm build` in a worktree of the target commit with the Gateway's environment and no store setting, so the user config wins.

## User Impact

- Git installs on hosts with a global pnpm virtual store can update again once the target contains this change. No action, migration or config change is needed.
- Developers who set `virtualStoreType: global` in their user pnpm config get a project-local `node_modules/.pnpm` in OpenClaw checkouts instead of links into the global store. The first install after this change relinks into the checkout, and pnpm may ask to remove and reinstall `node_modules`. That uses more disk per checkout, but it is the only layout the build accepts.
- No lockfile, dependency, schema, config-key or protocol change. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` accepts the existing lockfile; the setting is not recorded in it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installed updater cannot be patched, but it installs and builds inside the target tree, so the target's own `pnpm-workspace.yaml` reaches it. One line there, `virtualStoreType: project` next to `nodeLinker: isolated`, fixes the update path and plain source builds together. Relaxing the declaration guard was not an option, because the guard protects build correctness.

Update behavior: this reaches already-installed updaters, because they install and build the target commit inside its own tree. The first update toward a commit that contains this line succeeds; an update toward an older target still fails safely, as before (Gateway keeps serving, nothing activated). No migration and no Doctor change.

Scope notes:
- `src/update/prepare-git.ts` still does not apply `resolvePnpmCandidateEnv` (`src/infra/update-package-manager.ts`). That belongs to the update stream's owner and is tracked on #204775. It matters for one case this PR does not cover: pnpm 12.15 gives the environment variable `pnpm_config_virtual_store_type=global` precedence over the workspace file (measured below), so a Gateway that exports that variable still builds with the global store.
- The old runner's own write of `virtualStoreType: project` is kept. It is now redundant for targets that contain this line but still covers dev and preflight candidates whose target predates it, and it also sets `virtualStoreDir`.

Audit:
- Readers of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: CI setup and crabbox hydration set only `store-dir`/`virtual-store-dir`; `dependency-fingerprint.mjs` hashes the file (one cache miss); `check-dependency-pins.mts` reads only overrides and package extensions; `scripts/worktree-setup.mjs` only checks the file exists. None asserts the store type.
- `test/scripts/baileys-materialization.test.ts` writes `virtualStoreType: global` into its own fixture workspace and env after reading the repo file, so it is unaffected (passes on the head).
- Docs: `CONTRIBUTING.md` (source dependency layout) and `docs/install/updating/update-methods.md` (candidate builds) now state that the workspace pins the project store.

## Evidence

Tested commits: base `ddc83401337` (red), PR head `ac2ec1ef7a7` for the direct green and update cell G2. The branch was then rebased onto `4f873f44066` (head `4dd5ed51ab5`). That movement changes only a Swift test and drops one `export` keyword in `src/state/state-upgrade-tree.ts`; neither touches installs, the workspace file or the declaration guard, so the proofs were not rerun.

### 1. Direct build, macOS, user pnpm config `virtualStoreType: global`, no environment overrides

Fresh worktree each time, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`, pnpm 12.15.0 from the `packageManager` pin.

- RED, base `ddc83401337`: `pnpm config get virtualStoreType` = `global`; `node_modules/typescript` -> `../../../../../Library/pnpm/store/v11/links/@/typescript/…`; install exit 0, build exit 1 in `tsdown-ai`: `ERROR  Error: Declaration input escapes checkout: ~/Library/pnpm/store/v11/links/@/typescript/7.1.0-dev.20261028.1/…/node_modules/typescript/package.json … shared installs and external symlinks are unsupported.`
- GREEN, head `ac2ec1ef7a7`: `pnpm config get virtualStoreType` = `project`; `node_modules/typescript` -> `.pnpm/typescript@7.1.0-dev.20261028.1/node_modules/typescript`; install exit 0, build exit 0 (`total 3m 21.8s`).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfc0473e-44c3-4bb3-a222-8f8473ff8c4e

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4f3ebef-364f-460d-b52d-e4cdefbdef5e

### 2. Update cell, Linux Docker (real systemd user Gateway), installed updater from base x candidate

Each cell: Git install cloned from a local upstream at `ddc83401337`, built with `pnpm build:runtime`, managed Gateway via `openclaw gateway install`, a Gateway-gated SQLite writer probing during the run. Then `~/.config/pnpm/config.yaml` gets `virtualStoreType: global` (written after the install was built, since the base itself cannot build under it), upstream `main` moves to the target, and `openclaw update --yes --json` runs.

- RED (R1), target = base + empty commit `688aa5d60c8`: `status=failed reason=build-failed`; `nextAction: The new version could not be built. The current version is still running.`; steps `prepare:install=completed, prepare:build=failed` (`tsdown-ai failed after 6.15s`, stack frames under `~/.local/share/pnpm/store/v11/links/…`); process exit 1 after 40 s. Serving build before and after: `2026.11.8-ddc834013375-…`, `readyz` true, systemd `NRestarts=0`; writer 217 probes, 0 failed, no outage.
- GREEN (G2), target = PR head `ac2ec1ef7a7`: `status=succeeded`, steps through `prepare:build=completed, validating, activating, restarting`; process exit 0 after 350 s. Serving build after: `2026.11.8-ac2ec1ef7a78-…`, `readyz` true, release link moved to the new release, whose `pnpm-workspace.yaml` has `virtualStoreType: project` and whose `node_modules/typescript` -> `.pnpm/typescript@…`. The writer saw one 12.3 s outage, during the planned restart onto the new build (`NRestarts=1`).
- Same container after G2, base tree `ddc83401337`, same user config: install exit 0, typescript linked into `pnpm-home/store/v11/links/…`, build exit 1 with `ERROR  Error: Declaration input escapes checkout: /home/appuser/um/pnpm-home/store/v11/links/@/typescript/…`. This confirms the R1 build failure is the same guard on Linux. (The R1 ledger keeps only the tail of the build output.)
- An earlier green cell G1 toward the first push `847eb181a24` (same workspace change, no test/docs) also succeeded.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67a8b286-abf4-4169-b254-4f974e8481fa

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db1856cf-f41b-494b-8f8e-d32be49b4982

The cell recordings replay the decisive raw lines from each cell's own step outputs; the direct recordings are live with idle time compressed. Full raw logs are not attached; the decisive lines are above.

### Published stable driver x candidate (installed updater from `v2026.11.9`)

Tested: installed `v2026.11.9` (`0032b1d7ffd`); targets current `main` `4a180835802` (S-main) and PR head `4dd5ed51ab5` (S-head). Same Linux Docker harness with a real systemd user Gateway, one fresh container per cell. The source mirror has history back to 2026-10-25, so the release branch (forked from main at `9559c51dd05`) connects to both targets.

Install, as the `v2026.11.9` install docs describe for a server checkout: Git checkout detached at the tag, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build:runtime`, `pnpm add --global "openclaw@link:$PWD"`, `openclaw gateway install --force`, config `update.channel: dev`. State: a Gateway-gated writer filling the agent database to 331 MiB and probing `/readyz` every 250 ms. A separate table holds 1,000 marker rows with a known SHA-256. `ui.seamColor` is set to `#5a17d0` with the installed CLI (`openclaw config set ui.seamColor '"#5a17d0"'`). Then `~/.config/pnpm/config.yaml` gets `virtualStoreType: global`, upstream `main` moves to the target, and the installed CLI runs `openclaw update --yes --json --channel dev`.

| | S-main (to `4a180835802`) | S-head (to `4dd5ed51ab5`) |
|---|---|---|
| `openclaw update` result | `status=ok`, run `succeeded`, exit 0 | `status=ok`, run `succeeded`, exit 0 |
| Wall time | 458 s | 475 s |
| Candidate install / build (preflight worktree) | exit 0 in 7 s / exit 0 in 110 s | exit 0 in 7 s / exit 0 in 114 s |
| Gateway outage (`/readyz` every 250 ms) | one outage, 181.1 s (updater reports 182 s) | one outage, 191.1 s (updater reports 192 s) |
| Serving build before | `2026.11.9-0032b1d7ffd0-…` | `2026.11.9-0032b1d7ffd0-…` |
| Serving build after | `2026.11.9-4a180835802d-…`, `readyz` true | `2026.11.8-4dd5ed51ab55-…`, `readyz` true |
| `ui.seamColor` after | `#5a17d0` | `#5a17d0` |
| Marker rows after | 1000, same SHA-256 `69cb2f125f43dd66…`, `quick_check=ok` | 1000, same SHA-256, `quick_check=ok` |
| Agent DB after | 331 MiB, schema 38 -> 44 | 331 MiB, schema 38 -> 44 |
| `node_modules/typescript` in the installed tree | `.pnpm/typescript@7.1.0-dev.20261028.1/…`, resolves inside the tree | same |
| Final `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | no `virtualStoreType` key (main has none), file matches `HEAD` | one `virtualStoreType: project` (line 43), file matches `HEAD` |
| Checkout after | `main` at target, `git status --porcelain` empty | `main` at target, `git status --porcelain` empty |

Decisive raw lines (S-head; S-main matches except where the table differs):

```text
$ openclaw update --yes --json --channel dev   # the installed v2026.11.9 CLI
   status=ok run.status=succeeded before=0032b1d7ffd after=4dd5ed51ab5
   preflight-deps-install exit=0 7s, preflight-build exit=0 114s, preflight-runtime-stage exit=0 43s
   verification: runningBuildId=2026.11.8-4dd5ed51ab55-2026-11-25T02-42-28.208Z readyz=True versionMatch=True
-- after the update
   43:virtualStoreType: project
   virtualStoreType-key-count=1
   pnpm-workspace.yaml matches HEAD
   link: .pnpm/typescript@7.1.0-dev.20261028.1/node_modules/typescript
   typescript resolves inside tree: yes
   {"seamColor":"#5a17d0","updateChannel":"dev","port":34819,"authMode":"token"}
   virtualStoreType: global        # user pnpm config, unchanged
```

What this shows: the stable driver already builds under a global user store, because its own candidate preparation writes `virtualStoreType: project` into the preflight worktree. This PR neither breaks nor changes that. With the PR's line already in the target file, that write replaced the existing key: the final file has one key, matches `HEAD`, and no workspace backup is left behind. The cell is a no-regression control, not a red/green pair. The stable driver had no failure to fix here.

Observations that are the same in both directions, so they do not come from this PR:
- The long outage belongs to the stable driver's in-place activation. It stops the Gateway before checkout, and its own step list puts a 105 s Git object import (`git-import-admitted-target`, 4.98 GB pack) inside that window. The cell's upstream borrows objects from a shallow mirror, so the import is probably larger here than on an ordinary clone. Not measured on one.
- On restart, the driver's service reconciliation rewrote the unit's `ExecStart` from `<checkout>/dist/index.js` to the pnpm global link path of the same package (it served the target build).
- The PR head reports version `2026.11.8` because its base predates main's version bump; the dev channel accepted it.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ee7a611-2ddd-4063-867d-bf25ce6fc312

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0fa87589-ec40-4aaf-9ddf-70fb3243d023

### 3. Regression test

`test/scripts/pnpm-install-isolation.test.ts` already runs real pnpm 12 offline in a private HOME. It now copies `virtualStoreType` from the repo's workspace file, writes `virtualStoreType: global` into the fixture's private user pnpm config, and asserts each installed package file resolves inside its checkout (the guard's requirement), in addition to the existing cross-checkout isolation checks.
- Red on base `ddc83401337` (workspace without the line): `AssertionError: expected '../store/v11/links/@/isolation-fixtur…' not to match /^\.\./u`.
- Green on head: passes.
- Precedence measured with this fixture on pnpm 12.15: the workspace setting beats user config, but the environment variable `pnpm_config_virtual_store_type=global` beats the workspace setting. The test covers user config only.

### Checks (head `ac2ec1ef7a7`, rebased content identical)

- `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm check:docs`: pass.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/pnpm-install-isolation.test.ts test/scripts/baileys-materialization.test.ts`: 2 passed.
- `pnpm changed:lanes --json`: `all` (root config surface). `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: typecheck all, format, dependency pin, package-lock, config docs and the other guards pass. Two failures, both in files this PR does not touch: full `lint` (`eslint(max-lines)` in about 25 untouched files) and the dead-export scan (`src/state/state-upgrade-tree.ts: skipEntry`, fixed on main by #204988, now in the base).

### Not proven

- macOS update cells, from either driver (the macOS evidence is the direct build only); Windows not run; other package managers not run.
- Stable driver from a branch checkout (the stable-driver cells start detached at the tag), and stable-driver outage on a full, non-shallow clone.
- A Gateway environment that exports `pnpm_config_virtual_store_type=global` (see scope notes).

### Review

One independent reviewer read the diff and the raw evidence. Its findings, all addressed: extend the existing pnpm isolation test instead of adding none (done); the update-methods doc wording (done); the env-variable precedence gap (measured and documented above). `$autoreview` does not run on this machine.

prs.title: fix: remove color fringes from Linux desktop chat text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In OpenClaw Desktop on Linux, chat and other reading surfaces can pick up RGB subpixel smoothing from WebKitGTK. With RGB smoothing enabled in GNOME, the colored edges make prose look less crisp than the surrounding controls.

## User Impact

The Linux desktop client uses grayscale smoothing for reading text, including chat replies, drafts, and Markdown panels. This applies automatically. Grayscale smoothing can make the edges of light typefaces look different on displays set up for LCD subpixels.

## Why This Change Was Made

Set a shared CSS override for the existing Linux desktop host marker. The other platform paths retain the existing automatic smoothing for reading text, including the stem darkening used on macOS.

## Evidence

Used the actual OpenClaw 2026.11.10 desktop client and a real isolated Gateway on Ubuntu with GNOME Wayland, 125% text scale, and system RGB smoothing. Applied the same CSS change to a copy of the shipped Control UI assets. Both runs opened the same synthetic conversation. WebKit reported `auto` before and `antialiased` after. A crop of the same line went from 4,007 colored edge pixels to zero. The session heading matched pixel for pixel.

![Three-times enlargement of real Ubuntu desktop captures showing colored character edges before the fix and grayscale edges after it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44b814fe-2d78-4fce-a452-5355c93dc649)

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Original Linux desktop chat with RGB subpixel smoothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e40722e4-8c0c-4f8d-b7f5-d6a575a41d99) | ![The same chat after the Linux desktop CSS change](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e537faf2-05e7-46b3-8f56-dcc64067dcef) |

Extended the existing side-chat typography test for Linux and macOS smoothing values in the main chat, side chat, and side-chat composer. The CSS and test source parsed with Bun, and the focused CSS values were confirmed in Chromium on Ubuntu. The full Vitest suite is pending.

prs.title: feat: use Nodecode's Cyber v1 as a model provider
prs.body:
Closes #205653

## What Problem This Solves

People who run security-research agents on Cyber v1, Nodecode's abliterated DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, have to add api.nodecode.ai as a custom OpenAI-compatible provider by hand: no onboarding, no context, output or price metadata, no reasoning-effort mapping, and no per-session cache key.

## User Impact

Users can install `@openclaw/nodecode-provider`, run `openclaw onboard --auth-choice nodecode-api-key` (or set `NODECODE_API_KEY`) and get `nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1` as the default model, with its 1,048,576-token context, 131,072-token output limit and prices. The model list is read live from the account's `/v1/models`; Nodecode's non-chat models in that list (Decide v1, Image v1) stay out of the default model picker. The Control UI shows the Nodecode mark next to the provider and the model. Signing in again, or adding Nodecode beside another provider, keeps the primary model, aliases and hand-written `models.providers.nodecode` settings the user already has. Nothing changes for anyone who does not install the plugin.

## Why This Change Was Made

It follows the Abliteration plugin (#182248), the closest existing provider: an official external package, a manifest catalog, and the OpenAI-compatible replay and tool-schema hooks. Unlike Abliteration it lists models live (`discovery: refreshable`), with `unknownModelChatEvidence: "unlikely"` because Nodecode's model list carries no capability fields. The API accepts all seven `reasoning_effort` values, so every OpenClaw level passes through unchanged and `off` sends `none`. `prompt_cache_key` is on because Nodecode routes a key's requests to the same machine. Onboarding sets `preserveExistingPrimary`, as Cerebras does: without it, signing in replaced a primary model the user had already chosen (caught by the new upgrade test, fixed in the second commit).

Disclosure: I run Foresight Labs, which operates Nodecode. The icon is our own mark, used with permission (see `ui/public/provider-icons/ATTRIBUTION.md`). We are glad to maintain this plugin, either as an official package here or published by Nodecode on ClawHub if maintainers prefer.

## Evidence

### Gateway run from a fresh `OPENCLAW_HOME` (this branch, f4b6932d6)

- `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health --mode local --auth-choice nodecode-api-key --nodecode-api-key "$NODECODE_API_KEY" --gateway-port 18805 --gateway-bind loopback --gateway-auth token` set `nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1` as the primary model with the alias `Cyber v1`.
- With `openclaw gateway run --port 18805 --bind loopback` running (`openclaw gateway status`: connectivity check ok), `openclaw models list --provider nodecode --refresh` listed the account's models live: `nodecode-cyber-v1` (1049k, `default,configured,alias:Cyber v1`), `nodecode-decide-v1`, `nodecode-image-v1`, and one staff-only model.
- A Gateway-backed turn, `openclaw agent --agent main --session-id gateway-proof --message "Create ports.txt with the lines 22/tcp ssh and 8080/tcp http-alt, run wc -l ports.txt, and reply with its output only."`, created the file and answered `2 ports.txt`.

### Upgrade from latest stable (OpenClaw 2026.11.10, 6ea542f), then signing in with the plugin

On stable: Nodecode added by hand as a custom provider (`openclaw onboard --auth-choice custom-api-key --custom-provider-id nodecode ...`, key stored in `models.providers.nodecode.apiKey`, then `openclaw config set models.providers.nodecode.timeoutSeconds 300`), DeepSeek signed in and made the primary model (`openclaw models set deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`), and Nodecode added as a fallback with an alias (`openclaw models fallbacks add nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1`, `openclaw models aliases add cyber nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1`). A Gateway turn on stable created `notes.txt` in session `signin-proof`. Then the same `OPENCLAW_HOME` on this branch:

- The branch Gateway started on the stable state and was stopped again: non-interactive sign-in needs the state directory to itself, and with a Gateway still running OpenClaw refuses the state migration. That refusal is where the previous transcript stopped.
- The config stayed byte-identical to stable's.
- `openclaw onboard --non-interactive ... --auth-choice nodecode-api-key` ran to its end. Because a Nodecode key already existed, OpenClaw saved the new key as a separate, inactive profile and changed nothing else: "Replacement credential saved but inactive. Your connection is unchanged." It exits 1 there, which is how core non-interactive onboarding reports a staged replacement for any provider (`src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/auth-choice.plugin-providers.ts`).
- Before and after the sign-in, the primary model (`deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`), the fallback (`nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1`), the aliases, the hand-written provider entry (128k context, `timeoutSeconds: 300`) and the stored key (same SHA-256 prefix) are identical.
- `openclaw models auth list --agent main` lists the new inactive profile `nodecode:setup-...` next to `deepseek:default`.
- Through the restarted branch Gateway, the stable session resumed on the DeepSeek primary (`notes.txt: axolotl`), and a turn with `--model cyber` ran a tool on Nodecode (`8 notes.txt`).

### Provider mark in the Control UI

The chat model picker with the same hand-configured `nodecode` provider on both sides (from `openclaw onboard --auth-choice custom-api-key`), each on its own Gateway with a real key, light theme, 1280x800 at 2x. Before: main dcba477b0. After: this branch f4b6932d6. No fixtures or DOM edits.

- `pnpm test:extension nodecode`: 4 passed. The new test signs in over a config with another primary model, a fallback, an alias and a hand-written provider entry, and checks all four are kept; without `preserveExistingPrimary` it fails (`Expected: "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5"`, `Received: "nodecode/nodecode-cyber-v1"`).

- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, format, config docs baseline and the other lanes pass. Three lanes fail only on files this PR does not touch: changelog attributions (`CHANGELOG/2026.11.10.md:8130`), the dead export scan (`scripts/publish-model-catalog.mts`) and lint max-lines (crabbox, agents, gateway, wizard and ui files). `oxlint` on the changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.

prs.title: fix(plugins): readmit native captures with a dangling host link
prs.body:
Refs #205198.

A pnpm package swap can remove the versioned OpenClaw directory referenced by a retained native plugin capture. Resolving its dangling SDK symlink raises `ENOENT` before the existing host-mismatch path can create a replacement namespace.

Treat only `ENOENT` on an existing symbolic link as a host mismatch. Reuse the existing namespace replacement path, leaving the prior receipt, link and captured bytes untouched for rollback. Other resolution errors and reference-owned namespace checks stay strict.

### Validation

- **Red/green and rollback:** The owning admission regression failed with `ENOENT` on baseline `40757d73039f`. With the patch, activation created a successor namespace without retargeting the original link. In a separate forced-verification failure at the production swap/admission boundary, package rollback restored the original link target; the prior receipt, symlink inode and captured native bytes were unchanged.
- **Focused checks:** 21 native-admission and recovery tests passed; scoped types, lint, format and diff checks passed.
- **Shipped CLI plus real service:** Disposable rootless Podman, Linux x64, pnpm 12.15.0, real systemd user service; no live state. Started with the published stable `2026.11.10` pnpm-global install, two enabled synthetic native plugins and an existing managed native capture linked into the baseline's versioned `.pnpm` directory. Both local package targets were built from main `3fa253a2dc68` plus the three changed files, each byte-identical to this PR head; the two targets differ only in version/inventory metadata.

| Shipped CLI command | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `openclaw update` from `2026.11.10` to local `2026.11.11-first-hop.1` | pnpm mode, exit 0. Both updating Doctor steps exited 0. The old link dangled and a separate successor resolved; both plugins stayed loaded. New CLI, active systemd service and `/readyz` HTTP 200 with no failing checks. |
| Immediately run `openclaw update` again to local `2026.11.11-first-hop.2` | Current main's prepared-package updater, exit 0; the new CLI and Gateway both reported the second version. Both plugins remained loaded; systemd was active and `/readyz` returned 200. `update status` reported `succeeded`/`finished`, no active or stale run, and no repair or owed steps. Only the pre-existing standalone Doctor inspection capture remained; no update recovery set. |

The follow-on exercised current main's prepared package route, not the older in-place retained-worker route from #205167. Forced rollback was tested separately at the swap/admission boundary, not on the published-package run. This was not an Ubuntu arm64 or release-branch qualification.

prs.title: fix: keep daily skill maintenance running when a learned skill has Markdown files outside its support folders
prs.body:
Closes #204737

## What Problem This Solves

In auto mode, the daily Skill Workshop maintenance pass shrinks one oversized learned skill (the skill diet). If that skill has a Markdown file outside `assets/`, `examples/`, `references/`, `scripts/` or `templates/`, for example a `notes.md` next to `SKILL.md`, the whole pass fails with `workshop maintenance failed: Support file paths must be under one of: assets, examples, references, scripts, templates.` The warning names neither the skill nor the file, and it comes back every time the rotation picks such a skill.

## User Impact

User impact: maintenance finishes, and the affected skill is skipped like any other skill that cannot be dieted, with an info line that names the skill and the file:

```
skill diet skipped: skill=deploy notes.md: Support file paths must be under one of: assets, examples, references, scripts, templates.
```

The skill and its files are left untouched, no model call is made for it, and other oversized skills still get their turn in the rotation.

Not covered here: restoring or undoing versions that contain such files, and `view`/`patch`/`remove_file` on them, still refuse those paths as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The diet reads every listed Markdown support file before its skip handler starts, and the file listing includes files that the read refuses. The read now happens inside the skip boundary, and a refused path becomes a normal diet rejection that carries the file name. Moving the files into `references/` was not chosen because it would need relinking, including links from other skills; silently ignoring them would weaken the diet's link checks. The path rules themselves are unchanged. The Skill diet docs name this case among skills that are left unchanged.

## Evidence

**Live Gateway, scheduled maintenance after a real agent turn.** An isolated Gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway`, own state directory, loopback, channels skipped) on Linux, with Skill Workshop in its default `auto` mode. The agent `main` has one learned skill `deploy`: a 15.2 KB `SKILL.md` that links a root-level `notes.md`, both two days old. One turn was sent with `pnpm openclaw agent --agent main --message "Say done."`; the turn completed and the plugin's maintenance ran right after it. Lines from the Gateway's log file, `skill-workshop` plugin:

Before, `main` at `6400a15695d`:

```
2026-11-24T21:05:28.475Z WARN skill-workshop: workshop maintenance failed: Support file paths must be under one of: assets, examples, references, scripts, templates.
```

After, this PR at `622252eb2e1`:

```
2026-11-24T21:07:52.959Z INFO skill-workshop: skill diet skipped: skill=deploy notes.md: Support file paths must be under one of: assets, examples, references, scripts, templates.
```

In both runs the model endpoint received exactly one request, the agent turn itself, so no diet model request was made. After the run on this PR, the skill directory still holds only `SKILL.md` and `notes.md`, with the same SHA-256 as before the run.

The model in these runs is a local OpenAI-compatible stub that answers every request with fixed text (configured as a custom `openai-completions` provider), not a hosted model. The failing path and the skip both happen before any diet model call.

**Tests and checks**

- New regression test through `runWorkshopSkillDiet`, for `notes.md` at the skill root and `docs/guide.md` in an unsupported folder: no model call, the log line above, `SKILL.md` and the file list unchanged, no change record.
- On the base (`6400a15695d`) the `notes.md` case fails with `SkillAuthoringError: Support file paths must be under one of: assets, examples, references, scripts, templates.`, raised from the support read in `dietWorkshopSkill`. With the fix, all 21 tests in `skill-diet.test.ts` pass.
- `pnpm test:extension skill-workshop`: 16 files, 132 tests passed (includes `library.test.ts` and `review-service.test.ts`).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files, and both extension import-boundary lints passed.

Gaps: the live runs used a stub model, not a hosted provider. No local autoreview or ClawSweeper run.

prs.title: fix(update): hash SQLite lock bytes as zeros so Windows exclusion cannot fail verification
prs.body:
## Problem

Windows updates whose agent or state database is larger than 1 GiB fail post-install Doctor with:

```text
SQLite migration publication could not be verified: SQLite read-only worker EBUSY: resource busy or locked, read (code=EBUSY)
```

This is the recurring Windows variant in #197083 (2026.11.6 → 11.7 → 11.8 → 11.9 → 11.10). The reporter's main agent database is about 5 GB.

Root cause: `updateSqliteMigrationSteps` (`update-doctor-migration-attribution.ts`) keeps `PRAGMA locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE` on the source while it reads the post-migration generation. SQLite's lock bytes sit at offset 1 GiB: the pending byte, the reserved byte and the 510-byte shared range. On POSIX those locks are advisory. On Windows, `LockFileEx` locks are mandatory, so any other handle that reads `[0x40000000, 0x40000200)` gets `ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION`. Node reports that as `EBUSY ... read`, and the main-database hash in `fingerprintFile` (`sqlite-file-generation.ts`) fails there. Databases under 1 GiB have no lock-byte page, which is why this only hits large installs.

Small `-shm` reads are not the cause: Windows SQLite locks `-shm` at offset 120 and above, and the WAL-index header read covers only bytes 0–95. The earlier forced-lock experiment had to inject a lock there by hand.

## Fix

SQLite never stores content in the lock-byte page. The main-database digest now hashes those 512 bytes as zeros instead of reading them. SQLite never writes that page, and backups and VACUUM skip it, so it always reads back as zeros. The digest therefore matches a full read, and existing captures and receipts stay valid. The WAL and journal are still hashed in full because they have no lock bytes and a WAL can hold real frame data at that offset.

Accepted edge case: if another tool wrote nonzero bytes into the lock page, they now hash as zeros. That page is not database content, so this does not hide a database change.

## Evidence

- Regression test `hashes SQLite's lock bytes as the zeros SQLite leaves`. On base it fails with a different digest; with the fix it passes.
- Real Windows proof on Windows 11 ARM64 (Node 24.22.3), using a 1.15 GB WAL database. The real `readUpdateDatabaseGeneration` was bundled from base and from this branch. A second process held the same native exclusion the migration owner takes (`PRAGMA schema_version`, then `locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE; BEGIN EXCLUSIVE; ROLLBACK`):
  - base, unlocked: generation ok
  - base, under the exclusive owner: `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, read` (matches the field reports)
  - fix, unlocked: the same generation as base (`11003e4d…`), so digests are compatible
  - fix, under the exclusive owner: generation ok (`b33cfc60…`). That is exactly the unlocked read's empty-reader alternate, and the content digest is identical (`e96fafa8…`), so the existing admission accepts it.
- A raw mechanism check on the same VM: reads at offset 0 and right after the lock range succeed under EXCLUSIVE; the 512 lock bytes return EBUSY. A last-connection close checkpoint caused 41,320 EBUSY reads of those bytes in 592 ms.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on `update-database-generations`, `update-doctor-migration-wal-rebuild`, `update-database-backup-engine` and `sqlite-snapshot` tests: 139 passed, 2 skipped. `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint, format check and `git diff --check` all pass.
- Test cost: the new test hashes about 2 GiB of a sparse file and takes about 1.6 s of test time locally.

Not covered: a full managed Windows `openclaw update` with a database larger than 1 GiB. The proof above runs the production generation reader under the production lock sequence, not the whole updater. Private-copy paths (`copySourceFile`) still read the whole file, but the failing post-migration read uses the drained, copy-free path after `truncateSqliteWal`.

Refs #197083

prs.title: fix(doctor): stop false device credential warnings in full lint reports
prs.body:
﻿Fixes #204769

## What Problem This Solves

On a healthy, migrated SQLite profile, `openclaw doctor --lint --all` could report that local device credentials needed migration or repair. Gateway health could also report “Cannot load device identity.” Running either check alone did not produce that credential warning.

## User Impact

The full lint report uses the same local credentials as the selected checks. Genuine credential read failures and stale cached tokens still produce findings. No repair command or migration is needed for a healthy profile.

## Why This Change Was Made

The private inspection database is not the original shared database bound by the client credential migration receipt. Device Pairing now passes the source environment to its existing local identity and token readers, while continuing to inspect pairing records through the private view. Gateway Health uses Doctor’s existing source-state scope for the read-only status RPC. The revision removes the proposed credential copy entirely, so there is no inode mismatch, new snapshot preparation dependency, or new cleanup path.

## Evidence

- Ran `openclaw doctor --lint --all --json` and `openclaw doctor --lint --only <check-id> --json` separately for `core/doctor/device-pairing` and `core/doctor/gateway-health` on Linux with Node 26.12.1 and an isolated local Gateway. The shipped npm `2026.11.10` build (`6ea542f`, 77 checks) and a main build (`2cb81bb`, 78 checks) both reported `local-device-auth-unreadable` and `Cannot load device identity` under `--all`, but neither warning appeared under `--only`.
- The fixed CLI (`3f89701`, 78 checks) reported neither warning under `--all`; the one-check controls were unchanged. A historical Gateway crash record from initial fixture setup still appeared in both selections. The same profile was reused across the stable-to-candidate upgrade: the completed receipt still matched the original shared database’s device/inode, and the identity, token, and receipt rows were unchanged.
- The lint regression failed on main (`c7824fb`) at the all-versus-selected comparison with both false findings. It passed with the fix. The snapshot worker test also verified that a real stale local token is still reported when pairing records are inspected in private state, and the pairing suite still checks genuine identity and inventory read failures.
- Focused tests: 29 Doctor command, 15 device-pairing, and 133 related health-check tests passed. Targeted `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`, lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed. The final main merge did not change any of this PR’s four files. No macOS or Windows runtime was exercised.

prs.title: fix: keep the resident launcher when reinstalling Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #205617
Related: #204516, #204866

## What Problem This Solves

After an update has converted an installation to resident releases, `gateway install --force` can replace the launcher with the current package's `dist/index.js`. The Gateway can still answer health checks, but its pending trial loses the resident ready/rollback owner. Reusing a checked durable CLI can bypass the launcher for the same reason.

## User Impact

Ordinary Gateway installs and reinstalls keep the selected state directory's resident launcher, including a first pending trial whose previous version is still an unmodified npm package. Explicit retained-CLI recovery keeps precedence; separate node services, unowned npm installs, and supported legacy forwarding-package layouts keep their existing entries. No flag, schema, trial-format or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing release ownership predicate already knows that a published release **or v2 trial** owns the installation. Move that unchanged predicate into the existing release store and use it in the service selector; retain the existing legacy forwarding-package probe. Delete the competing inference that an ordinary install must identify its owner only from the currently serving package.

A checked same-version durable copy now uses the same service-specific planned entry as a new durable install, rather than masquerading as an explicit recovery override. The raw-string durable reuse return and its unused path calculation are removed; retained recovery strings and node entry rules are unchanged. The shared install-plan composition remains unchanged.

An unreadable/malformed trial is not silently ignored by reinstall: the existing store reader fails visibly instead of guessing a different service owner. Launcher-file existence alone does not establish ownership.

Scoped tokei production code (seven touched production files, tests excluded): **2,495 → 2,498 (+3)**. No line-cap exemption or guard compression. The updating contract is updated.

## Evidence

- Pinned base: `90297095602f362f3af2353a6a718c6867dad203`.
- **Red on base:** [AWS run_c1fd8b7dc8d3b4039c9990aa60d04f68](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c1fd8b7dc8d3b4039c9990aa60d04f68). The real `buildGatewayInstallPlan`/argument builder returned npm `dist/index.js` instead of the launcher for the pending plain-npm fallback; checked Gateway durable reuse returned its durable `dist/index.js` instead of the launcher. Both expected assertions failed. Settled release, legacy forwarding, orphan-launcher and node controls passed (2 failed / 4 passed selected cases); no assertion or expectation was narrowed.
- **Green:** [AWS run_ddbc17a2ba58265e394c69f8bd77071d](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ddbc17a2ba58265e394c69f8bd77071d): **55 tests passed in four suites**, production core types plus command/service test-project types passed, exact changed-file lint and test-line guard passed (+68 before formatting, allowance400). Two formatting-only repairs were captured from AWS oxfmt and applied exactly; no behavior/type rerun. Formatting passed in [AWS run_40c90a984fcc254b4765ae94d92f4302](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_40c90a984fcc254b4765ae94d92f4302).
- **Linux product gate PASSED:** [run_bac6c35b5f73cb91506fe10ff177aac8](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_bac6c35b5f73cb91506fe10ff177aac8). Published10→head; ordinary `gateway install --force` **without --wrapper** wrote actual `openclaw-launcher.mjs` (native MainPID50978). Same prepared trial `fc340ad2-4263-432e-8490-e478ba20e1f1` committed/succeeded (actual attempts2); authenticated serving connection reported2026.11.11-beta.1 and matching successor build, schema43 verified. Next public run `da46ec0a-1ec1-46a5-9fce-1a5c5c1092b2` was admitted, packed/installed/maintained, and finished `skipped/already-current` rather than stuck active; **no third release trial is claimed**. The corrected fixture allows legitimate phase progress during install-and-start while pinning immutable trial identity. Native stop/uninstall and npm-config cleanup passed; exact AWS leasecbx_f402bce8b884 released with `--wait`, exit0.
- Source qualification: product build/proof uses pre-format carrier **5a9b2d43e7533d0ff1af9ac7fbae29ade472b6fd**. Its exact diff to PR head90e1fa0147 is only two formatting hunks: a test statement wrap and a Promise type-union wrap erased at build. prs.title: fix(plugins): clarify dated SDK migration notices
prs.body:
Closes #190536

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin notices can say an API “keeps working until” a date that has already passed, even though the plugin is still loaded. A [November 17 report on 2026.11.5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/190536#issuecomment-6952934071) confirms the outdated notice appears on stable. A [2026.11.10 report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/190536#issuecomment-7161825635) shows the same wording for Codex (Oct 1) and Groq (Sep 30) in `doctor --lint --all` and the post-update Doctor summary, even with both plugins at their latest published versions.

## User Impact

Dated notices show the migration date and recommend checking for a plugin update. The date remains visible without implying that OpenClaw automatically disables the plugin or removes the API on that day. Workspace-status warnings are still counted; this change corrects their wording, not their severity or the availability of plugin updates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the same wording in the CLI and the Control UI. The date, details link, undated notices, and plugin behavior stay the same.

## Evidence

- On Linux with Node 24, `openclaw plugins inspect sdk-compat-proof --runtime` loaded the same local fixture importing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/cli-runtime` on both builds. The baseline said “retire on Oct 1, 2026. It keeps working until then”; the fix printed “Migration date: Oct 1, 2026. Check for a plugin update.”
- An independent `node --test` probe recorded SDK usage for the two reported dates and ran the production notice builder: **2 failed** on `2cb81bbb38a1` (both printed the old promise) and **2 passed** with the PR's byte-matched builder (both printed the migration date without the promise). This probes the shared formatter, not a full update.
- Source tracing on `v2026.11.10` and current main confirms that `core/doctor/workspace-status` uses the shared compatibility message for `doctor --lint --all`; the update Doctor records the same workspace-status finding text as a warning for the update summary. Neither consumer generates its own retirement wording.
- The Control UI browser test used the built app in Chromium with a fixture Gateway. It verified the text comes from the structured date, the Details link remains available, and no enable/disable request is sent. The two focused test files passed all 18 tests; the browser test and i18n verification also passed.

The screenshots use the same installed-plugin row on November 18, 2026, comparing `e93a426be32` with this change.

### Clean comparison

Before

![Before: enabled plugin notice says the APIs keep working until the elapsed migration date](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91882376-4719-446a-957c-41ab30543f9e)

After

![After: enabled plugin notice displays the migration date and update advice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b66e1409-c2ef-4111-91f0-0536bb710618)

### Annotated comparison

Before

![Before: past-date availability wording highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55ad5bd4-8de8-4a0f-bc13-a9e62a9d0aef)

After

![After: date and update advice highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/909b8eb1-12e6-4f60-bee6-39a560597dcd)

Core and Control UI typechecks, changed-file lint, and formatting passed.

prs.title: fix(tui): load long replies whole when reopening a session
prs.body:
Fixes #200408

## What Problem This Solves

After `openclaw tui` is closed and reopened on a session, an assistant reply longer than 8,000 characters ends in `...(truncated)...`. The stored reply is complete, and the TUI showed it in full before it was closed.

The TUI requested `chat.history` with `sessionKey`, `agentId` and `limit` only, so the Gateway applied its default 8,000-character display cap. The TUI renders history rows as-is and has no per-message expansion, so the capped text looked like the whole reply. `openclaw tui --local` applied the same default cap.

## User Impact

Reopened TUI sessions show each reply in full, up to 500,000 characters. Tool results keep the Gateway's default 8,000-character preview, so history payloads grow only by the long replies themselves.

## Why This Change Was Made

The issue names two documented routes: a per-request `maxChars` on `chat.history`, or `chat.message.get` per truncated entry (what the Control UI does). This PR takes the first.

- The TUI now sends `maxChars: 500000` (the schema maximum) and `toolResultMaxChars: 8000` on `chat.history`.
- `--local` passes the same two limits to `readChatHistoryPage`.
- Both limits live in `src/tui/tui-backend.ts` so the two backends cannot drift.

`maxChars` was chosen over `chat.message.get` because the TUI has no lazy-expansion surface: it would have to fetch every truncated row before rendering anyway, which adds a hydration step, concurrency bounds and a failure fallback for the same result. The Control UI's complete-history read already uses `maxChars: 500_000`. I am happy to switch routes if maintainers prefer `chat.message.get`; another contributor proposed that route on the issue.

Accepted limits:

- A reply over 500,000 characters is still capped.
- A newer TUI connected to a Gateway that predates `toolResultMaxChars` would have its history request rejected as an unknown parameter. I could not determine which release added the parameter; please say if a fallback is wanted.

## Evidence

Real Gateway over WebSocket (temporary test in `src/gateway/server.chat.gateway-server-chat-b.test.ts`, not committed): a stored 11,532-character assistant reply ending in `THE END`, read with the TUI's old and new `chat.history` parameters.

| Request | Text returned | Ends with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before: `limit` only | 8,018 characters, `truncated: true`, `reason: "display-cap"` | `...(truncated)...` |
| After: `maxChars: 500000`, `toolResultMaxChars: 8000` | 11,532 characters, identical to the stored reply | `THE END` |

The 8,018 matches the issue report (8,000 cap plus the 18-character marker).

Checks run on this head:

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/tui/gateway-chat.test.ts src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts`: 164 passed. The updated assertions cover the request parameters in Gateway mode and the page-reader parameters in `--local` mode.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `pnpm format:check` on the touched files: passed.

Not done: the reopened reply has not been viewed in a live `openclaw tui` with a real model. The development container had no systemd user session for the launcher's Gateway check and no configured model provider.

prs.title: fix: explain node restart steps after manual updates
prs.body:
Fixes #204266

## What Problem This Solves

A manual package replacement on a node-only host leaves its running node on the old runtime. Main's existing node-only routing (#204866) keeps the right package owner, but its result recommends reinstalling the node even when a simple restart will do, or when the observed node belongs to another installation.

## User Impact

After a successful in-place replacement with no local Gateway, the updater checks the effective service command and running state. If the node belongs to the replaced package, it reports the node (and PID when available), asks the operator to wait for idle, and prints the updated installation's `node restart` command. It makes no restart or ownership claim for foreign, stopped, absent, or uninspectable nodes. For a staged release, the CLI says the Gateway trial is pending and that a node restart alone cannot activate it.

The existing package and release owners stay in place. No node is restarted, no drain or idle policy changes, and no service definition is rewritten. The prepared-release message needs no extra native service probe. The legacy candidate path can report the advisory when a shipped updater delegates finalization; updaters that finish entirely in installed code need the separate stable backport (including 2026.11.10 where applicable).

## Evidence

- **Red on `2cb81bbb38a1`:** seven intended assertion failures. The same-package fixtures saw the old blanket `node install --force` advice instead of PID and restart-only advice (plain output and the JSON result); foreign, stopped, missing, and already-current controls incorrectly received advice. The staged-release CLI fixture did not explicitly identify the pending trial or say that a node restart cannot activate it.
- **Green on `bcc37e3d234b`:** 219 focused tests passed: 10 package advice, 38 release CLI, 36 release preparation, 95 post-update finalization, and 40 service maintenance. The proof uses `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with `--maxWorkers=1` and isolated state. The three Vitest shards reported 17.21 s, 288.67 s, and 6.49 s, respectively; 411.43 s end to end with test fixture compilation. Hosted CI timing is not yet available.
- In the deferred node-only case, the test starts a new `dist/index.js node run` process through the generated release forwarder. The child selects the old package and leaves the Gateway trial pending. This is a subprocess simulation, not a systemd or published-package upgrade test.
- Changed-file `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`, lint (six TypeScript files), formatting, docs inventory, and `git diff --check` passed. The merge preserves the prior PR commits and integrates main at `c734b2de9dd9`.
- Compared with the prior draft, there is no second advisory producer in release preparation or extra persisted warning key there. Against integrated main: +42 net production lines, +55 net test lines, +3 net documentation lines.

**Proof limits:** The reporter's [native Linux observations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/204266#issuecomment-7116719559) show an unchanged systemd PID on the published update, then reconnection after manual restart; they are not validation of this head. The isolated Linux environment has no user systemd bus, and no native macOS or Windows host was available. The published-updater-to-candidate hop, unchanged native PID, and recovery/reconnect on this head remain unproven. No live service or user installation was touched, and no full release qualification is claimed.

Thanks to @DonnieFi for the field report and reproduction details.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5d66242-4f71-4dd0-8a69-31ea7795a2a0)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c32c134a-c289-42c3-acbf-37194ea426a6)

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix: show the whole reply when you reopen a TUI session
prs.body:
Closes #200408 ## What Problem This Solves In `openclaw tui`, a reply longer than 8,000 characters is complete while it streams, but after you close and reopen the session it stops mid-sentence with `...(truncated)...`. The full reply is stored, yet the TUI gives no way to see the rest, so it looks as if the model stopped early or text was lost. ## User Impact User impact: reopening a TUI session (Gateway or `--local`) shows long replies in full again. If the full text cannot be shown, the preview stays and says why, instead of ending silently. ## Why This Change Was Made The Gateway caps text in `chat.history` to keep history pages small. The Control UI already loads capped rows in full through `chat.message.get` (#122207); the TUI took the capped text as it came. The TUI now does the same as the Control UI: after loading history, each assistant row marked `truncated: true` / `reason: "display-cap"` is replaced by the stored message, newest first, four reads at a time. History pages stay bounded, and there are no protocol or schema changes. When the full text cannot be shown, the preview is kept and its marker says why: - read failed, not found, or a Gateway without `chat.message.get`: `...(truncated; couldn't load the full reply. Reopen the session to try again)...` (same advice as the Control UI's "Couldn't load the full message. Try again.") - `chat.message.get` reports the stored reply as oversized (over its ~25 MB payload limit): `...(truncated; the full reply is too large to show here)...` Local mode (`openclaw tui --local`) had the same cap. Its history read moves from `embedded-backend.ts` into `src/tui/embedded-history-messages.ts`, unchanged, and full text is loaded after the existing budgets pick the rows (the 128 KiB per-message limit and the page limit), so loading full text never drops an older row from the page. The stored message is then read in-process with the same limits as the Gateway's `chat.message.get` handler, so both modes show the same reply. A reply over 128 KiB shows in full in both. As with Gateway clients, a page with loaded replies can end up over its byte budget. The first revision of this PR loaded local full text before those budgets. A reply over 128 KiB then became `[chat.history omitted: message too large]` instead of its preview, and expanded rows could push older rows off the page. This revision fixes both. Known limit, left as is: `chat.message.get` caps text at 1,000,000 characters, so in both modes a longer reply loads its first million characters, ending in the plain `...(truncated)...` marker. Command-line runs (`openclaw agent`) are not affected by any of this: they print the run result, not history. ## Evidence Live check, Windows 11, against a running 2026.11.5-beta.4 Gateway: the session from #200408 holds an 11,532-character reply that `chat.history` returns as 8,018 characters ending `...(truncated)...`. - Before (installed 2026.11.5-beta.4 TUI, session reopened): the reply stops mid-sentence at "forest ecology", followed by `...(truncated)...`. - After (this branch built from source, same session reopened): the whole reply is shown, ending with `THE END`. Before: After (Gateway): After (`--local`): live run of this branch, `openclaw tui --local --session agent:main:proof`, Windows 11. The run used throwaway `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, config and `OPENCLAW_WINDOWS_TASK_NAME`. The session holds two stored assistant replies, written with the repo's own transcript writer (`upsertSessionEntryCore` + `replaceTranscriptEvents`). An 8,000-character preview of either stops partway through paragraph 72. - 11,539 characters, ending `THE END`: after reopening, it shows in full (paragraphs 1–103 and `THE END`). - 150,078 characters, over the 128 KiB per-message limit: after reopening, it also shows in full (paragraphs 1–1,326 and its last line, `HUGE_REPLY_LAST_LINE`), as it does over the Gateway. The `src/tui/tui-pty-local.e2e.test.ts` harness times out on this Windows machine (its own existing cases too), so this was a manual run in a terminal. The retrieval-failure case can't be triggered live without corrupting storage; the unit tests below cover it.
Reopened TUI screen text (repeated middle paragraphs elided) ```text openclaw tui - local embedded - agent main - session proof session agent:main:proof Write the huge reply. Huge paragraph 1: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. Huge paragraph 2: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. [... paragraphs 3-1,324 elided ...] Huge paragraph 1325: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. Huge paragraph 1326: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. HUGE_REPLY_LAST_LINE Write the long reply. Long paragraph 1: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. Long paragraph 2: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. [... paragraphs 3-100 elided ...] Long paragraph 101: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. Long paragraph 102: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. Long paragraph 103: the tide pool keeps its water between waves, and every stone holds a small world of its own. THE END local ready | idle agent main | session proof | gpt-5.5 | deliver:off | tokens ?/200k ```
Focused tests: - `src/tui/gateway-chat.test.ts`: a capped row is replaced by the `chat.message.get` result; when the read reports unavailable, reports oversized, or is rejected, the preview is kept with the matching marker. - `src/tui/embedded-history-messages.test.ts` (new) runs the real history budgets with synthetic transcript rows: a capped reply shows its stored text; a 150,000-character stored reply shows in full; a reply the reader reports oversized, and a missing reply, keep their marked previews; loading a 30,000-character reply under a 40,000-byte page budget keeps the older 15,000-character row. The 150,000-character and page-budget cases fail when full text is loaded before the budgets (the order in the first revision) and pass here. - `gateway-chat.test.ts`, `embedded-backend.test.ts` and `embedded-history-messages.test.ts`: 172 passed. `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint, format, line-cap and mock-export ratchets pass. The dead-export scan reports three exports in untouched files that are already on `main` (`approval-shared.ts`, `spawn-broker/host.ts`, `system-agent/operation-types.ts`).

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With two configured agents and a designated system agent, running `openclaw skills` outside both workspaces asked for `--agent`. The same error prevented `skills list`, `skills info`, and `skills check` from showing the designated agent’s inventory. @yxshee reported this behavior in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195423.

## User Impact

These four commands now use the designated system agent from a neutral directory. An explicit `--agent` still takes precedence, followed by the agent whose workspace contains the current directory. A multi-agent roster without a designation still requires a choice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inventory caller opts into the same roster-validated system-agent selection used to identify the default in the agent list. Install, update, verify, and Workshop continue to use their existing workspace selection.

## Evidence

- Replayed the four registered CLI commands against synthetic profiles in isolated local state, with each of two agents designated in turn. All eight reads previously exited 1 before requesting inventory. After the change, all eight requested the selected agent’s inventory and displayed the expected workspace or skill description through the implicit-local fallback.
- Compared exit status, stdout, stderr, and Gateway requests for 13 controls. All matched, including nested cwd, explicit overrides and errors, sole and undesignated rosters, install/update/verify, and Workshop list/archive.
- The local fixture exercised an unavailable Gateway transport. A live Gateway and the repository Vitest suite were outside this local replay.

### Hosted verification

The CLI command suite passed 42/42 on the signed head and again on the protected test merge. The full dispatch’s dependency check reported 15 distinct path/symbol pairs in 11 files whose blobs match the parent. The parent workflow omitted that check. The private-profile runs exercise the registered CLI. A packaged CLI run and an upgrade from the latest stable release remain unverified. prs.title: fix: preserve Unicode spelling in Apple code highlights
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Apple chat code blocks and workspace file previews can receive two snippets that look identical but use different Unicode spellings. For example, after highlighting `é` as a single character, the highlighter can return that spelling when the next snippet uses `e` followed by a combining acute accent.

## User Impact

Completed chat code blocks and workspace previews now receive highlighted text with the same UTF-8 spelling as the snippet they requested. This concerns the text supplied to SwiftUI. The regression did not establish a difference in the visible glyphs or the saved file.

## Why This Change Was Made

The highlighter now compares the UTF-8 bytes of its language-and-source cache key. Swift string equality treats canonically equivalent spellings as equal. Byte comparison lets repeated requests reuse their highlights while keeping distinct source spellings in separate entries.

## Evidence

- Ran the exact highlighter test file with Swift Testing. The new composed-first and decomposed-first cases both failed against the parent. All 16 tests passed with the fix, including line endings, the line cap and eviction.
- Exercised the chat code block and independent file preview paths with four canonical pairs in both orders. Each consumer returned the earlier spelling eight times on the parent and zero times with the fix. Both recorded property-test seeds passed 500 generated cases each.
- Replayed 104 presentations covering LF, CRLF, CR, line and byte limits, and repeat rendering. SwiftLint passed on both changed files.
- Local coverage used the focused Swift package and the saved caller fixture. The full OpenClawKit package and a mounted app were outside the local run.

### Hosted verification

The exact-head macOS package run passed all 2,707 tests in 246 suites. Both Unicode-spelling cases passed, along with line-ending, line-limit, and cache-eviction controls. The package and caller fixtures cover cached output. A warm-cache capture from the installed app remains unverified. [macOS package log](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45733391151/job/139621237718)

prs.title: fix(update): settle plugin version warnings after convergence
prs.body:
Closes #205312

## What Problem This Solves

On the shipped in-place update path, post-install Doctor can see the older official npm plugins before the same update converges them. Its earlier version-drift findings then remain in the completed update's attention summary, asking users to perform an upgrade that already happened.

## User Impact

Users no longer receive stale plugin-version repair instructions for upgrades completed by the same run. Plugins that still need an update, unavailable targets, migration advisories, and unrelated Doctor findings remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate uses the existing shipped-parent plugin-convergence promise to describe pending npm cohort upgrades as provisional information during the package swap. The legacy finalization and resume paths also settle individual earlier version findings against the final confirmed version, including warning rows recorded before resume.

A later Doctor repair is credited only when the committed install record and the installed package version agree. Package-version settlement is independent of pending data migrations. Final mismatch advisories are a fallback when a more specific finding already exists. The owned-install release path already performs plugin maintenance before its advisory checks; this change addresses the compatibility bridge used by published in-place updaters.

## Evidence

- Red on base `8aace0e00`: two package-swap Doctor receipt regressions and the shipped-parent resume regression failed before the fix.
- Focused Vitest: 64 passed across version-drift, workspace status, post-core convergence, deferred warnings, post-plugin readiness and resume completion at `cb643dd4b`. The full resume suite (12 tests) also passed at the final head after removing the fixture-only assertion requested in review.
- Core/scoped TypeScript, lint, formatting, line-cap and assertion-safety checks passed at `cb643dd4b`; final-head scoped test TypeScript, lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. `pnpm build:runtime` and candidate tarball integrity checks passed at the final head.

### Real managed Gateway and persisted-state proof

Built and packed exact head [32636db2e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205491/commits/32636db2ef587cd1eb95ff03b659b1cb33200d38) (candidate version `2026.11.10`; SHA-256: `6c28d7d9a5d2fb59afeb73c630d128a56b5dd8e8bf743130f3ee1088f0709188`). All three runs used Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (arm64), Node 24.22.3, and an actual registered `openclaw-gateway.service` managed by `systemd --user`. The updater performed the service transition; no service shim or `--no-restart` was used. Before the first upgrade, an actual Gateway session, a synthetic chat-history marker, a workspace file, and the three official npm plugins were present. Control and patched runs started from the same consistent pre-upgrade snapshot.

| Real upgrade | Updater / persisted run | Gateway service state (PID before → after) | Matching actionable version warnings in post-swap Doctor | Completed stale warning rows | Stale warnings in saved report |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Published 2026.10.10 → published 2026.11.10 (control) | ok / succeeded | active (819) → active (5046) | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Published 2026.10.10 → candidate | ok / succeeded | active (10132) → active (14033) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Published 2026.11.10 → candidate (existing-state compatibility) | ok / succeeded | active (5046) → active (8574) | 0 | 0 | 0 |

In both older-release upgrades, `codex`, `groq` and `tokenjuice` were loaded at 2026.10.10 before the run, all converged to 2026.11.10, and all were loaded afterward. The published control recorded all three actionable version-drift messages in its post-swap Doctor warning receipt; the patched run recorded none, even though the same three plugins still required and completed convergence. The provisional-information classification is covered by the Doctor receipt regression tests. The patched completed run and saved report contained zero of the three obsolete repair instructions. Both older-release runs completed their post-plugin Doctor and readiness checks with exit 0. Subsequent standalone Doctor lint checks contained zero matching diagnostics; this counts only the reported version warnings.

**Stored-data compatibility:** The latest-stable run used the real state from the successful published control upgrade, including its persisted update history. The Gateway switched from the published build ID to the exact candidate build ID. Calls to `update.runs.get` before and after returned the same prior successful run (same status, before/after versions and step array), and the new completed run was readable. The original session ID and chat-history marker were still returned by `chat.history`. Gateway mode, bind, port, auth mode and auth credential, workspace setting and file content were preserved. The existing disabled automation remained disabled and retained its ID.

<details>
<summary>Redacted excerpts from the actual updater, Gateway status and saved report</summary>

Commands: the published control used `openclaw update --tag 2026.11.10 --yes --json --timeout 600`; both candidate runs used the same command with `--tag [candidate tarball]`. The excerpts below are selected JSON fields, original diagnostic sentences, and derived counts from the captured logs; local paths, endpoints, credentials and session identifiers are omitted.

**Control: published 2026.10.10 → 2026.11.10**

```text

Saved run (matching warning rows):

```

**Patched: published 2026.10.10 → candidate**

prs.title: fix(subagents): preserve explicit delegated auth profiles
prs.body:
Closes #120183

## What Problem This Solves

The original pre-persistence model-policy repair is already in main. The remaining change preserves an explicitly delegated native child's `model@auth-profile` selection, rather than silently running under another account when that configured profile becomes unavailable.

## User Impact

Explicitly delegated child and inherited fork requests retain their configured account or report why it cannot be used, rather than silently choosing another account. Ordinary automatic account selection stays unchanged. Unsupported exact-account CLI/worker handoffs are visible failures; the callback-bound subscription bridge refuses before inference instead of silently switching to metered API billing.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Carry one optional persisted requirement through child creation (hidden and visible), reset/rollover, thread admission, queued execution, post-hook routing, fallback, and inherited session forks. Preserve the missing selected ID so execution reports its unavailability instead of choosing another account.
- Use the existing auth planner and exact-profile completion contract at execution owners: primary turns, CLI/harness dispatch, initial/queued/after-turn/recovery/live-switch compaction, context-engine host completions, detached forks, and host-prepared BTW. Incompatible routes and unsupported CLI or worker-local credential handoffs fail closed. Gateway-owned worker inference retains its existing selected-profile owner. Config-only AWS SDK profiles remain valid.
- Preserve ordinary pins, automatic/configured children, and legacy rows without the marker. Same-ID reselection and explicit login reconnect retain strictness; a different-account replacement clears the old requirement. Model-only session changes retain the binding, even if execution must then refuse an incompatible route.
- Capture the active approved model for strict context-engine completions, rather than combining the selected account with the agent's unrelated default model. Clear superseded recovery selections and reject auth plans prepared for another account.
- Preserve the plugin fork API's explicitly authorized new-selection behavior. A model-only override admitted through `authorizeModelOverride` is a new selection, not automatic inheritance of the source account. An explicit same-ID profile reselection retains the source requirement. Merely naming the source model without a profile suffix needs no override authority and inherits the source account; it is not a new selection.
- Keep isolated-completion exact requirements distinct from ordinary host preferences in dispatch and read-only runtime status. Ordinary preferences remain provider-scoped; only delegated or explicitly authorized account selections are exact. Preserve worker runtime refusal before environment validation while refusing unsupported exact-profile worker-local inference before credentials, tunnel or dispatch.
- Resolved the original 13 conflicts against `ba6d94ec1771` using current extracted owners, without restoring removed giant runtime helpers. Integrated `d8fc8b7a5390` only after new generated-snapshot conflicts; regenerated those snapshots canonically.

## Evidence

- Reproduced removed-profile, routing/fallback, thread/visible-child, queue/live-switch, same-account reconnect/reselection, context completion, detached dispatch, stale recovery-plan, isolated harness, host BTW, and worker-placement failures before their fixes. Ordinary fallback remains covered alongside strict refusal.
- Prior unchanged-owner proof: **265 tests passed in 13 files**, including detached-fork dispatch, recovery/queued maintenance, host BTW and prompt-prefix stability. Prior owner correction run: **156 passed in 7 files**, covering isolated execution/status, plugin and utility completion, worker runtime rejection order and inference placement. Unchanged worker inference: **7 passed**, with 30 unrelated cases intentionally filtered out.
- Isolated real-Gateway/synthetic-provider fork account trace: **4 passed**, covering ordinary inherited selection, required same-ID explicit reselection, required own-model/no-suffix inheritance, and an older anchor after a model-only provider switch. Compatible fork requests retain the selected account; the incompatible required-account case refuses at owned inference with zero provider requests. This is not real-provider acceptance.
- Core and owning plugin, session, root-agent, worker, Gateway-server and Gateway-root test type graphs passed. Type-aware lint, line-cap ratchet, targeted docs MDX, format and diff checks passed.
- Test budget: **+839 net lines**, with a documented **439-line allocation** above the ordinary 400. These are distinct lifecycle, dispatch, compaction, credential-owner and real-Gateway account boundaries, not duplicate helper assertions. The allocation does not suppress coverage or a baseline failure.
- Simplification: credential authority remains with existing selection/auth owners; no new credential state, generation fences or runtime compatibility reader. Moved the coherent BTW account-policy test into its own suite and reused the shared compaction-failure owner. Against `d8fc8b7a5390`, production TypeScript is +454 net lines across 72 files; test delta is +839. Most production growth carries the optional selection fact across existing owners.
- Fresh complete-range local review on `b082a3f567c68` against `d8fc8b7a5390` found two actionable dispatch gaps: required CLI BTW backend compatibility and own-model forks from an older, different-provider anchor. Both now have valid red/green proof: the real CLI BTW owner refuses unsupported account forwarding, and the public real-Gateway model switch preserves the required old account through an older anchor, then refuses rather than substituting credentials. The 76-case affected sibling sweep and all four real-Gateway account cases pass. Current core/root-agent/Gateway-root types, scoped typed lint, format and test budget pass. A subsequent review found the one-shot embedded-to-CLI bridge could drop the required account for an opaque backend. The actual production dispatch boundary incorrectly invoked its stubbed CLI execution adapter before the guard; it now refuses unsupported forwarding before CLI admission and checks the canonical selector retained the exact profile. Its ordinary-control case still dispatches. The final correction uses the same required profile for eligibility and execution so API keys stay on the direct route. An eligible subscription dispatch carrying callback-bound credential lifetime checks is explicitly refused as unsupported before inference, with the existing terminal fallback-stop fact; it does not silently switch to metered embedded/API inference. The required-API routing regression and corrected ordinary-stored-subscription billing regression were red before their owning fixes. The unbound stored-subscription control still dispatches on the selected profile. A subsequent missing-metadata API-key-binding regression was red before its fix; explicit API-key bindings stay with the embedded credential owner even before the selected agent directory is resolved. The subscription refusal fixture now carries valid callbacks, not callbacks that would themselves reject. All 91 focused owning/sibling cases across six files pass (75.59 seconds wall time including compilation/setup; exact-head CI timing pending), with current core and owning nested-agent types, typed lint, formatting and the exact-base test budget. Fresh local review of the complete `53bbf101266a..ae9002af0998` correction range completed. Its P2 preflight-prediction concern is explicitly retained as a limitation: the public SDK helper reports route/backend/stored-mode eligibility, not callback-binding admission, and its maintained Active Memory consumer uses it only to budget timeouts and does not supply a callback binding. Final execution remains authoritative; expanding that public preflight contract is outside this repair. Published-head CI was green before these changes and is not current-head proof; exact-head [CI is running](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45734792421) on `ae9002af0998`; Security Review passed. No rerun was requested. This PR is not claimed merge-ready. The `7f2ae2807a84` CI worker CLI rejection-order failure was repaired and its existing owning test now passes; no rerun masked it. The prior `e40227172bc3b` CI run reported two PostgreSQL cron Gateway restart/finalization timeouts in conformance shard 5/6; this has **not** been qualified as inherited. No blind rerun or expected-failure exception was used.

## Remaining acceptance and boundaries

A profile ID is an operator-managed configured connection, not an immutable secret generation. Removal blocks the child while unavailable; the existing explicit reconnect flow may restore that same ID. No permanent revocation policy is introduced.

Codex-native BTW is a separate credential owner: it forks the active native thread and retains native login rather than preparing an OpenClaw profile. This marker does not redefine native account identity, and complete exact-account isolation across that boundary is **not claimed**. See [BTW's native contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/btw.md), personally inspected Codex [`ThreadForkParams` handling](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L4868-L4897), and [fork creation using the manager's auth owner](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d/codex-rs/core/src/thread_manager.rs#L2017-L2053).

The advisory SDK eligibility helper does not project callback-binding admission. The CLI bridge still cannot carry callback-bound credential lifetime checks; eligible subscription runs with those callbacks now stop explicitly instead of switching billing routes. The dispatch regressions stop at a stubbed execution adapter; they do not prove a third-party CLI login. Real-provider final-I/O proof after removal/reassignment and stable-to-head child upgrade acceptance remain unrun. Handler, persistence, mocked-transport and synthetic-provider Gateway proofs are not substitutes for those checks. This PR is not claimed merge-ready while exact-head CI/review or acceptance blockers remain.

No merges, closures, releases, or live Gateway state changes.
