## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the delayed-speech E2E failure when the latest player is ready after reload while an earlier attachment is still being authorized. Maintainer CI-fixer follow-up for [scheduled run 43676814527](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43676814527/job/132698861418).

## User Impact

All six bubbles stayed mounted and the latest audio decoded and played while the earlier player was pending. Both probes released that same unchanged packet at the first total-count sample: the original assertion failed with the exact one-versus-two signature, and the awaited assertion passed. Diagnostic gates are removed from the final test. The scheduled run lacks a per-artifact timeline, so its exact packet order remains unobserved.

prs.title: fix: clear the update warning after a retired model is repaired
prs.body:
Closes #204736

## What Problem This Solves

After Doctor finishes a deferred model repair, the update summary says the successful repair still needs attention. Saved update records from earlier versions also retain the completion as a warning.

## User Impact

Pending repairs retain their warning. Completed repairs retain their durable completion receipt and no longer add a warning to the update summary, including when an existing saved update record is loaded after upgrading.

## Why This Change Was Made

The producer settles its deferred warning without writing an additional success warning. The warning projection recognizes an older stored completion warning when the matching durable receipt is present. The saved record schema and bytes remain intact.

The completion signal is the normal durable `finalize:doctor:model-retirement` step, as requested in #204736. Only the redundant attention warning disappears. Partial or failed repairs and unrelated follow-ups remain visible. This fixes reporting for the legacy package-updater bridge on the 2026.11.10 line and the shared saved-report projection.

## Evidence

Real SQLite ledger, production `recordUpdateModelRetirement` and the production report renderer, on Linux with isolated state. The table shows attention counts from terminal output; the package-version strings were fixture inputs, not an installed upgrade.

| Scenario | Unchanged main (`2cb81bbb38a1`) | Fixed production code on PR head `413df37a1ee2` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| New run: deferred, then completed | 1 | 0 |
| Historical completion plus one real warning | 2 | 1 |
| Historical failed repair plus one real warning | 2 | 2 |
| Historical partial/skipped repair plus one real warning | 2 | 2 |

Both fresh runs displayed the deferred warning before convergence and retained a completed retirement step afterward. The fixed writer no longer creates the separate completion warning row. Historical fixtures were written and reloaded through the ledger; the saved steps remained unchanged. The sole warning in the fixed historical-completion case was the unrelated one.

- `src/infra/update-deferred-model-retirement.test.ts`: **base red** at the two intended attention-count assertions (2 failed, 2 negative controls passed; 23.12 s); **head green** (4 passed; 9.97 s). Ran with standalone Vitest and the repository's `unit-fast` config.
- Targeted `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`, lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed. The 70 unchanged report tests also passed with the fixed production code.
- This is ledger-to-report proof, not a shipped package swap. The isolated `update status` handler could not open its state readers under this checkout's secure-temp ancestor policy. No latest-stable package-upgrade trace or macOS reproduction is claimed.

### Original author’s validation

The saved-ledger regression exercised `createUpdateRun`, `recordUpdateRunStep`, `finishUpdateRun`, `getUpdateRun`, and `renderUpdateRunReport` through a temporary SQLite state directory (1 targeted test passed). All 71 report tests and eight post-activation inspection tests passed in that run, as did formatting and `git diff --check`. Six Doctor billing-route cases were blocked before assertions by SQLite worker Unix-socket `EPERM`; the full package-update trace was not verified.

prs.title: fix(agents): honor imageMaxDimensionPx at the provider and CLI image handoffs
prs.body:
Root cause: src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-stream-settle.ts:504 calls `materializeProviderContext` without the configured `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx`, and src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts:338 (`loadCliPromptImages`) hydrates CLI images without it, so both re-sanitize at the 1200 px default while the canonical hydration already uses the configured value.

Fixes #205642

Thanks @solarwinds95 for the detailed report, the config timeline and the bundle trace that pointed straight at both handoffs.

## What changed

- Provider handoff: passes `resolveImageSanitizationLimits(attempt.config).maxDimensionPx`, the same resolution `attempt-setup.ts`, `prompt-image-preparation.ts` and the worker/harness callers use. `materializeProviderContext` now accepts `maxDimensionPx` (it still omits `maxBytes`).
- CLI: `loadCliPromptImages` takes the run config and resolves the dimension itself, so the prehook loader, the initial payload and steered input all get it from one place.
- Nothing else: no change to compression policy, quality steps, the 5 MB provider / 6 MB CLI byte caps, or defaults. With `imageMaxDimensionPx` unset the resolver returns nothing and both paths keep 1200 px.

## What users see

With `imageMaxDimensionPx: 2400` on main, the provider path re-sanitized every image at 1200 px. Those bytes no longer matched the image hashes pinned by the canonical hydration (which used 2400), so the provider request dropped the images and sent "3 image attachments could not be loaded" instead. After the fix the provider gets the canonical images: images up to 2400 px are sent unchanged, larger ones are resized to 2400, and the follow-up turn replays the same bytes. The CLI path now honors the setting too.

Re-encode note: the reporter's two JPEGs (854x1280, 1000x1280) grew because they were re-encoded at 1200 px. With a configured limit at or above 1280 they are now sent byte-identical, so that case goes away for this configuration. The same re-encode at the default 1200 px (the "larger than source" sanitizer behavior) is unchanged and out of scope here.

## Evidence

Built Gateway in a secretless node:24.22.1 container, a local OpenAI-compatible stand-in that records the decoded size and hash of every image it receives, and a CLI-backend stand-in plugin that records the image files it is handed. One chat turn with JPEGs 854x1280, 1000x1280 and 3000x2000, then a text follow-up. Proof comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205663#issuecomment-7179545351

| run | config | provider/CLI receives (turn 1 and replay) | resize log on handoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| main x2 | 2400 | 0 images + "3 image attachments could not be loaded" | maxDimensionPx=1200 maxBytes=5242880 |
| fix x2 | 2400 | 854x1280 and 1000x1280 source bytes, 3000 px -> 2400x1600; replay identical | only 3000x2000 -> 2400 (canonical) |
| main / fix | unset | identical bytes on both (801x1200, 938x1200, 1200x800, same sha256) | 1200 |
| CLI main | 2400 | 801x1200, 938x1200, 1200x800 | maxDimensionPx=1200 maxBytes=6291456 |
| CLI fix | 2400 | 854x1280, 1000x1280 source bytes, 2400x1600 | 2400 |

There is no `imageMaxBytes` setting (`config validate` rejects `agents.defaults.imageMaxBytes`), so the byte caps stay the existing constants.

Tests: `attempt-stream-settle.image-limits.test.ts` (provider handoff, image dropped on main) and a case in `cli-runner.helpers.test.ts` (CLI file re-encoded at 1200 px on main). Both fail on main and pass here.

Deltas against main: production +10 / -1, tests +104 / -0.

prs.title: fix(google): preserve playback when Google Live splits audio into parts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Google Live can split one spoken response across several PCM parts. The bridge used to resample each part separately. In a phone call, three samples delivered together produced one playback byte, but the same samples delivered as one plus two produced no audio or playback mark. The bridge still reported the response as complete.

## User Impact

Playback now preserves the audio across part and message boundaries. Each emitted audio chunk gets a playback mark, and the final samples reach the caller before normal response completion.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Google bridge now uses the existing streaming resampler for contiguous output at the same sample rate. It drains the filter when the rate changes or generation ends, discards pending audio on interruption or a fresh session, and preserves it across a resumed connection.

## Evidence

- Compared 16 playback layouts through the actual Google provider callbacks with synthetic transport. All matched the one-shot codec byte for byte. Splitting 1,024 samples into two equal parts produced all 341 expected bytes. An equal-length ramp that previously differed at eight bytes matched exactly.
- Replayed the original failing input and passed 40 generated cases. Checked PCM passthrough, rate changes, cancellation, fresh and resumed connections, and extended-thinking completion.
- Isolated Vitest passed all four output regressions and six adjacent provider and input cases. The 240-sample telephony case emitted 75 bytes immediately and the final five before completion. All 24 adjacent telephony callback controls passed.
- The staged native line-cap check and formatting passed. Hosted Vitest passed four output-audio and 44 provider cases, including split audio, interruption, next generation and the 8 kHz transition. Project lint passed. [Google suites](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45621777215/job/139233091560) · [Protected CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45627734380) Live Google network and speaker playback remain unverified.

prs.title: feat(ui): render LaTeX in Control UI markdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI Markdown displayed supported LaTeX literally. This renders bounded math while preserving code, escaped input, currency, URLs and sanitized output.

## User Impact

Math is lazy-loaded; ordinary messages request no KaTeX engine, styles or fonts. Equations stay readable as source until ready, and failures keep that fallback. Wide equations scroll inside the message and now show a fade where content continues. Math stays findable in transcript search and readable in paste excerpts and web source previews.

Original contribution by @jjjhenriksen; repair work requested by @RomneyDa. Contributor authorship and coauthor credit are preserved; Allow edits from maintainers remains enabled.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @RomneyDa](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/clawtributor-review-pr-144324)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/41d889a9-23c8-4603-889b-a35ad86acfb6)

- [Rebase discussion and verification with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ac39fc44-8e46-4656-ba81-f57ba2533d4c)

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing parser, generation-fenced leaf, shared lazy runtime, MathML and separate sanitizer. One 200-expression allowance covers stable streamed additions and the mutable tail. KaTeX **0.18.2** addresses GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7 while retaining `trust: false`. Plain-text consumers of the shared parser (search, paste excerpts, source previews) read math tokens as their TeX source, so math stays searchable and readable outside the rendered view. Wide equations reuse the table fade convention rather than adding a new affordance.

This remains built-in math, not a plugin. Product decision (2026-11-08, @vyctorbrzezowski): use built-in math rendering with KaTeX and prepare this selected PR for merge; merging remains a separate decision. #175507 contains the earlier equivalent implementation, not this latest rebase. KaTeX is the one new dependency (MIT, pinned 0.18.2, loaded only when a message contains math); dense math retains real CPU cost, bounded by the 200-expression message budget.

## Evidence

- **Rebased November 22, 2026:** signed head `d9d99865410de426d0827e34e7e0f935b79b8b46` on main `f066f9cba3135d28a6ff7df1e1e1ba95684dda74`; tree `3b29185c5bcf51f74f56cf2a4104a62903c792ff`. The rebase applied without conflicts and preserves Jacqueline’s authorship and all coauthors. No merge or auto-merge was enabled.
- **Focused verification:** [secretless AWS Crabbox run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_734372330f2e48eab4804a6612826fc5), lease `cbx_f57c2839c2d0`, verified IAM endpoint 404. Frozen install, **147 tests in 9 files** (including table coverage), UI typecheck, formatting, lint and test-line ratchet passed. Boot-manifest generation succeeded; its generated upstream graph changes were retained verbatim after verifying that it was the only changed tracked file and comparing the imported bytes. The production build below ran with that generated manifest. The lease has been released.
- **Production build and base-relative performance:** `pnpm ui:check-performance:base f066f9cba3135d28a6ff7df1e1e1ba95684dda74` passed after manifest generation: chat boot **+1,774 B gzip**, New Session boot **−113 B**, startup **unchanged**, unchanged request counts. prs.title: feat(plugins): show deployment-specific supervisor guidance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Externally supervised installations correctly refuse native service management and self-update, but their recovery copy cannot identify the deployment's actual supervisor or command. Deployment packages need static guidance without a new operator setting or runtime registration callback. Closes #157668; static-plugin alternative to openclaw/rfcs#75.

## User Impact

People running OpenClaw under an external deployment manager see that package’s literal update or recovery command and can copy it from the dashboard. The package opts in through static plugin metadata; existing supervision refusals and manual control remain unchanged. No new operator setting or automatic command execution is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add bounded literal `supervisorGuidance` metadata to `openclaw.plugin.json`, with a parser and types on the existing `plugin-entry` SDK surface.
- Resolve metadata from exactly one enabled/allowed provider without activating plugin code. Missing actions, unavailable/malformed metadata, and ambiguous providers retain the built-in copy.
- Keep `OPENCLAW_SUPERVISOR_MODE=external` and every existing refusal/control decision authoritative. Commands are display-only: never executed, stored in update history, or stamped into prompts.
- Port to the current CLI/Doctor/setup owners and actual Gateway `update.run` pre-admission refusal, which has **no durable run**. Preserve the immutable release updater and retained legacy bridge.
- Require an explicit `includeSupervisorGuidance: true` request on both RPCs; default responses retain their existing shape for released closed validators.
- Repair the current result validator to recognize existing no-run refusals (`runId: null`, `ok: false`, skipped result); admitted runs still require a valid durable/OCM identity. This changes no emitted receipt or admission authority.
- Show transient literal guidance and a copy button through the current Solid dialog and extracted Settings attempt component. Unrelated failures never acquire supervisor commands; disconnects, denied access, failed reads and absent current guidance clear it.

## Current repair

Integrated main `1bc412fb747895bb7420bb8b02004103a2c607f8` for real conflicts. Removed obsolete setup recovery/type extraction and old UI restoration. Centralized repeated lookup in existing CLI/Doctor presentation owners; no new coordination, persistence or service authority. Generated Gateway predicates are mechanical output, separate from the authored port. Net test growth +698 includes independent parser, activation/discovery, current routed refusal and actual-bundle browser boundaries; allocation records the 298 lines above the default 400-line allowance.

The first local review identified unsolicited response extensions, observed config-read effects, a missing selected workspace, stale Retry copy, and an empty fallback row. All five were repaired together. New regressions reproduced four backend failures and the stale-command UI failure before the fixes; all now pass. Lookup uses isolated, unobserved config I/O, deferred shell fallback and the existing control-plane workspace selector. A fresh follow-up review found two additional issues: guidance now consumes the existing root-matched plugin quarantine decision before counting providers, and the unreachable legacy-handler guidance/test were removed. The real metadata-boundary quarantine regression was red before the fix and green afterward; a quarantined provider cannot suppress a healthy deployment package.

## Evidence

- Real static-manifest current `update.run` boundary: regression **red on unmodified main, green with the port**; current routed Gateway checks passed. No prepare/restart/broadcast or durable run is created by the current external refusal.
- Isolated real `pnpm openclaw gateway start --json`: structured refusal includes the package-owned command, with throwing plugin runtime unexecuted. On the port head `e1900bdf`, a separate foreground Gateway and shipped CLI exercised actual WebSocket `update.status` and `update.run`: defaults omit guidance; explicit requests receive the exact static command. The Gateway was stopped and its isolated port verified closed afterward.
- The actual compiled response validator from released tag `v2026.11.10` accepts the real default `update.status` receipt; the explicitly opted-in extension is rejected by that old closed validator as expected. The old release still rejects its inherited no-run `update.run` shape; the candidate validator is now corrected and separately proven below.
- Actual current `update.run` handler → generated result validator: the guidance refusal was red on the inherited string-only schema; all 13 owning handler cases pass after the correction, including accepted-ID and invalid-null-result guards. Current core and Gateway-method test types, type-aware lint, generated predicates, and native protocol contract/determinism checks pass.
- The result-contract union initially omitted the generated public Swift admitted-receipt model. Real Swift callers failed to compile when the model was absent and when optional initializer arguments moved ahead of the required arguments; the admitted caller now compiles against the full canonical generated protocol. The admitted struct retains its original initializer argument order and source API. Swift pre-admission refusals remain untyped, as before; a proposed permissive refusal model was removed rather than introducing a second, weaker contract. Both owning native artifact tests and all 13 update handler cases pass.
- Static parser/manifest/discovery suites: 36 passed. Current status-config/resolver/routed refusal suites after review repair: 47 passed.
- All 15 affected update UI suites: 160 passed, including no-run refusal and withholding commands for unrelated failures.
- Actual production Solid bundle, Chromium 1440×1100: 2 browser cases passed. Checked generic/custom refusal, literal HTML-looking command text, actual clipboard bytes, retained Settings guidance and no run/history/report requests.
- Port validation at `e1900bdf`: core/UI and Gateway/services/Doctor/commands/update test type graphs all passed. The subsequent result-contract correction passes its current core and Gateway-method graphs.
- Port full build at `e1900bdf`, targeted type-aware lint, format, generation and i18n verification: passed (including all 165 public SDK subpaths, shipped-API surface check and four touched MDX pages).
- Local ClawSweeper: the full port review at `e1900bdf` cleared its seven repaired findings; subsequent committed correction reviews found the inherited result-contract mismatch and two Swift compatibility issues. All were repaired. The final `8249f0c9..c3a519ee` review reports no correctness or security findings.

### Inherited / unrun

Three lifecycle stale-cleanup test cases fail identically on unmodified pinned main: the fixture expects raw `process.env`, while the unchanged restart owner passes its service environment projection (`OPENCLAW_PROFILE` is undefined, not inherited `default`). These are recorded failures, **not passing caller-suite evidence**. The port's async policy callback assertion was separately corrected; its native policy regression passes. Initial affected-caller sweep: 195 passed/4 failed; after that correction, remaining failures are exactly those three inherited cases.

Pinned main independently returns `runId: null` for pre-admission update refusals while its result schema requires a string. The actual released validator rejects both default and opted-in no-run receipts on this inherited field mismatch. The candidate now fixes this mismatch with separate admitted/no-run result states; the earlier released validator is unchanged, and its rejection is not counted as passing upgrade proof.

Browser data is synthetic and supplied through the Gateway fixture; the screenshots are the actual production UI, not a recreated screen. Separately, the port-head production Control UI was connected to a real isolated foreground Gateway with an installed synthetic deployment plugin: clicking Update Gateway → Update and restart showed the exact package command, and the real clipboard matched its bytes. No existing live deployment/model or stable-upgrade acceptance is claimed. The old body's prior-head CI/upgrade claims and unavailable media have been replaced rather than treated as current evidence. No merge, closure, release or live deployment mutation.

## Visual proof

Same synthetic no-run external refusal, en-US, Chromium 1440×1100. Before: current main `1bc412fb`; after: repaired head `e1900bdf54929a5e97a9bb1a5d6d33a21738dc94` (UI unchanged from the captured `8a0a58b` bundle). Clean frames first, measured annotated copies second; wide captures are stacked for readability.

### Clean before
![Before: generic external-supervisor refusal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d973ba1f-b687-49d3-a7a8-f5e6c392d9be)

### Clean after
![After: deployment name, run location and literal copyable update command](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/525a9edb-ebe5-4e31-9b1e-e1182a5a2fa0)

### Annotated before
![Before: generic recovery copy highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf661fb6-1400-4e71-a686-f8865324f2db)

### Annotated after
![After: static deployment guidance highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e59bd0b-3c53-47b6-b69f-3742319c6569)

### Retained Settings guidance
![After: the current Settings attempt component retains the same literal guidance](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bdba69e-2a6e-4abe-ad38-8367e1bb3173)

### Real isolated Gateway + production UI

Supplemental port-head capture (UI unchanged by later validator/native-generation-only corrections): actual production Control UI connected over WebSocket to a real isolated Gateway with an installed synthetic deployment plugin (not a Gateway browser fixture). Update refusal and copy action exercised end to end; no existing live deployment or model proof. Isolated Gateway stopped afterward.

![Final head: actual isolated Gateway supplies the installed plugin command to the production UI, with successful copy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b96c990-8695-443f-b8bd-66dcd98d02f6)

## Current CI

Published candidate `8b06d8692e2fd83291ecb4644e0691c61accdabf`; exact-head CI is pending. Earlier-head checks are not current-head proof.

The first current-head CI found an unchecked generated-artifact lookup in the new test. It now uses the existing named assertion helper; the actual owning `root.scripts` type graph and both native artifact cases pass. The earlier `root.tooling` graph did not cover this test and is not substituted for that proof. No production behavior changed in this correction.

CI follow-through: refreshed the exact UI request assertions for explicit supervisor-guidance opt-in without weakening session-key, authorization, refresh or timeout checks (four cases red before, all 66 cases across both files green after; 2.20 seconds locally). The status-schedule fixture now preserves real exports; its 22 owning cases, proper Gateway/UI test type graphs, typed lint and format pass. The mock-export ratchet was red and passes after removing two obsolete exact allowances (including the already-preserved daemon supervision mock). Five additional net test lines keep complete mock exports and exact wire assertions; allocation is 298 for net +698. No production or visual behavior changed.

Prior-head CI also timed out during plugin-SDK boundary artifact preparation after 420 seconds, after emitting the SDK and Discord declarations. No compiler diagnostic was reported at that boundary; this is not qualified as inherited or passing, and remains pending fresh-head CI.

prs.title: feat(media): support validated SQL query attachments
prs.body:
Related: #164212

## What Problem This Solves

Plain-text SQL query files currently fail the attachment type checks, and a generic `text/plain` response can rename a paired-node SQL file to `.txt`. This change recognizes SQL MIME metadata, preserves `.sql`, and carries the validated file through the existing managed document download path, including WebChat.

The file still goes through the existing filesystem authorization, size limits and complete-content text validation. Binary impersonation, other source/script formats and HTML publication/provenance keep their existing rules. The configurable type override proposed in #164212 remains a separate product/security decision.

The branch is a single commit on `main` at `79e42e0877d9e3641e365b17517b9f19e0c4320a`. On that `main`, `managed-image-attachments.test.ts` is above its line cap, so the SQL managed fetch/download test lives in the sibling `managed-image-attachments.sql-documents.test.ts`; no existing test helpers move.

## Evidence

Hosted CI for this head is waiting for maintainer workflow approval; the results below are local.

- Both SQL MIME spellings failed at the actual managed fetch/download caller before the classifier repair, then passed with identical file bytes and document metadata.
- At `4ecb64deb5689d27ff83b78ca1c5dfd2c01d2df5` (macOS, Node 26.5.0), the six affected test files pass 260/260 when each is run with `node scripts/test-projects.mts <file>`. With the four production files reverted to `main`, 254 pass and 6 fail; the 6 failures are the SQL acceptance cases this PR adds or extends, and the added negative case also passes on `main`.
- `check-test-lines-ratchet` (net +136, allowance 400) and `check-test-mock-exports` pass. `check-changed --base origin/main` passes 34 of 36 checks; the two failing checks (changelog attributions, dead-export scan) report only files this PR does not change.

The checks above use public source and synthetic fixtures. Real-model Gateway proof is in the section below. Full-suite and live channel acceptance are not claimed.

## Maintainer Decision Requested

Please decide whether validated SQL query files should be a built-in supported attachment format. This PR keeps arbitrary-file overrides separate. Real-model Gateway evidence for SQL send, inbound `.sql` retention and WebChat download is in the section below; a paired-node `file_fetch` transfer was not exercised. The maintainer format decision remains a merge requirement.

## Real-model Gateway proof at the current head — 2026-11-25 (UTC)

Built the exact PR head `4ecb64deb5689d27ff83b78ca1c5dfd2c01d2df5` with `pnpm build` (Node 26.5.0, macOS 15.5) and ran it as a loopback-only Gateway with token auth, no messaging channels, and a fresh isolated state directory and workspace for every run. The agent is the default `main` agent with its default tools. The model is real and unscripted: an open-weight Qwen-family model served by vLLM from a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint, configured as the bundled `vllm` provider (model `vllm/Qwen`). The model chose its own tools, and every model response carries the endpoint's response id and token usage. The control is the published **2026.11.10** package, which does not contain this PR, with the same config, workspace, fixtures, prompts and model.

**1. Assistant sends a workspace SQL file to WebChat** — `openclaw gateway call chat.send --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","message":"Please send me the SQL query file.","idempotencyKey":"…"}'`, then `agent.wait` and `chat.history`. The workspace file is `query.sql`, 53 bytes (`SELECT name, price / FROM widgets / ORDER BY price DESC;`).

PR head, last of three runs: the model listed the workspace with `exec`, read `query.sql` with `read`, then called `message` with `{"action":"send","media":"<workspace>/query.sql","filename":"query.sql",…}` (three model responses; 19,214 / 19,640 / 19,695 prompt tokens). The delivered assistant message carries:
```json
{"type":"attachment","attachment":{"artifactId":"artifact_managed_media_<id>","url":"/api/chat/media/outgoing/agent%3Amain%3Amain/<id>/full","kind":"document","label":"query.sql","mimeType":"text/x-sql","sizeBytes":53}}
```
Downloading that URL from the Gateway with the bearer token:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/x-sql
content-disposition: attachment; filename="query.sql"; filename*=UTF-8''query.sql
Content-Length: 53
```
The body is byte-identical to the workspace file (`cmp` exit 0; SHA-256 `c1650cc2c61507ab5d2476f42ba431564f2da0cf41224671ae6c94790753cb59` for both). The same URL without the token returns 401. The staged copies keep the extension (`media/outbound/query---<id>.sql`, `media/outgoing/originals/<id>.sql`).

2026.11.10, same prompt and model, two runs. In one, the delivered assistant message carries `{"type":"attachment_error","attachment":{"code":"unsupported-format","kind":"document","label":"query.sql"}}`. In the other, the model's `message` send with the same `media` path returned `Current-source media could not be staged. ⚠️ query.sql: Rejected by the local attachment allowlist. Send a supported file type.` In both, the model pasted the SQL inline instead.

**2. User uploads a SQL file whose MIME is reported as `text/plain`** — `chat.send` in a separate session with `attachments: [{"type":"file","fileName":"orders.sql","mimeType":"text/plain","origin":"file","content":"<base64 of a 4-line SELECT>"}]`: the PR head stores `media/inbound/orders---<id>.sql`, byte-identical to the 59-byte upload; 2026.11.10 stores the same upload as `media/inbound/orders---<id>.txt`.

**All attempts.** Five PR-head runs and two control runs, each with fresh state. In the first two PR-head runs, which used an earlier fixture containing a `WHERE` clause, the endpoint stopped answering once the model had read the file, so scenario 1 ended before the send step. A direct `curl` to the endpoint outside OpenClaw reproduces this with the file's text alone and succeeds without the `WHERE` clause, so the other three runs use the fixture above. All three delivered the `text/x-sql` attachment with a download byte-identical to the workspace file (in one, after two rejected `message` calls, the model sent a `/tmp` copy of the file). Every PR-head run stored its upload as `.sql`; both control runs failed to attach the file and stored `.txt`.

In all three successful PR-head runs the model chose the `message` tool, so the real model did not exercise the `MEDIA:` reply directive at the PR head. That path is covered by the earlier fixture-driven run on this head: a local fake OpenAI-compatible model replied `MEDIA:./query.sql` with the 43-byte file and produced a `text/x-sql` attachment and an identical download; its 2026.11.4 baseline, recorded on 2026-11-16, returned `unsupported-format` and stored `.txt`.

Not covered: a paired-node `file_fetch` transfer, any messaging channel, Control UI rendering (no screenshot), and other models or providers. This proof does not change the built-in format decision requested above.

prs.title: fix(cli): selected TTS providers appear configured without credentials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`infer tts providers --local` can report a selected speech provider as configured even when its required API key is missing.

## User Impact

Local provider inspection distinguishes selection from credential availability, matching Gateway inventory. It retains the inspected agent's saved API-key visibility and reports unavailable SecretRefs as nonfatal diagnostics. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Local inventory uses the speech provider's existing asynchronous configured check and read-only, agent-scoped credential helpers. Provider selection, inventory metadata, and speech conversion retain their existing owners.

The conflict resolution accepts main's removal of redundant image/video test permutations in #205574 and keeps the dedicated TTS provider regressions. It adds no production behavior, tests, dependency changes, or test-line allocation beyond the existing PR.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `da0ffb2d3e42765b06e7afd27391fb355c722c6c`, merging main `3fa253a2dc68555e405454dd3324a5c604742d69` into previously submitted `218c35364ad6efe40494547d596359dcf11c9521`. The four-file diff from this main has SHA256 `7284892c5e46d28ba8bb3855d3a3ed48110fe22c65f606951b6c8d7dd7178b76`.

For this exact candidate, whitespace checks, esbuild TypeScript transpilation, and oxfmt checks passed. The direct production owner, shared configuration reader, and dedicated TTS regression file are byte-identical to the prior hosted head. This does not establish an unchanged dependency graph or a current runtime pass. Code execution and commit creation used secretless, non-root, no-network containers with read-only source/dependencies and limits of 256 MiB, 0.5 CPU, 64 PIDs, and 32 MiB private temporary storage.

The prior one-worker inventory Vitest attempt exited with SIGKILL/137 after writable task-owned artifact/cache overlays were prepared; it established no test pass. It was not repeated for this test-deletion conflict repair. Full tests, type-aware lint/typecheck, a new built CLI/Gateway run, and heavy builds were not rerun locally. Current-head GitHub CI remains required; earlier CI results below cover only their recorded heads.

An independent coding-agent reviewer examined the complete four-file committed diff, related owners/callers, conflict resolution, and raw validation evidence for the exact base/head above. It found no supported P0/P1/P2 finding. This was a source/evidence review, not local autoreview or ClawSweeper execution; it does not close the CI/runtime gaps above.

Historical built CLI/Gateway observations demonstrate the original false-ready result and its correction, including no-key, agent-scoped saved-key, and unavailable-SecretRef controls. They remain historical evidence, not a runtime claim for this merge head. No external provider service, synthesis, model account, or audio device was exercised.

<details>
<summary>Historical behavior proof, earlier validation, and previous conflict integration</summary>


**Prior submitted head:** `7cadf77fc10f049a4761fe0fe4c749f00c490e72`. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41699218219) and [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41699218219/job/126142154613) passed for this exact head. The [current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176340#issuecomment-6254047517) reports sufficient proof and no findings or before-merge actions. Status checked November 11; runtime records below are retained, not new executions.

Prior candidate: `7cadf77fc10f049a4761fe0fe4c749f00c490e72`, integrated with the then-pinned main `372f91d3362ef9145af08d573f6f3e8ba85b16c8`. The prior five-file diff SHA256 is `2c2e078d7c01724bf493cdf04525e00b55e19bdf3f2f3344ed26341adf68f110`.

Current-source validation passed in secretless task containers with an independent frozen-lockfile install:

- 110 focused and complete capability CLI tests, including all seven provider-inventory regressions and current cancellation/output siblings.
- Formatting, normal type-aware lint with pinned Bun/oxlint parity, production core types, and all six source-selected canonical test-consumer typegraphs.
- File-line cap, test-line ratchet and whitespace checks. Test lines: 6,439,755 against a 6,440,430 effective ceiling, leaving 675 lines.
- Supported built-CLI entry point: `node scripts/run-node.mjs --help` completed in 306.7 seconds. Full declaration emission was skipped via the supported flag, so this is not full release-package/DTS proof.

The clean built HEAD and canonical build-input signature matched the exact current source. A foreground built Gateway and normal public CLI then produced the following observations with real native ElevenLabs plugin metadata and isolated synthetic state:

| Official command / condition | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| `infer tts providers --gateway --json`, selected ElevenLabs without a key | `configured: false`, `selected: true` |
| Gateway stopped and joined; `infer tts providers --local --agent main --json` | `configured: false`, `selected: true` |
| `models auth paste-api-key --provider elevenlabs --agent proof`, synthetic key only | proof agent `configured: true`; main remains `false` |
| Explicit unavailable ElevenLabs API-key SecretRef while the saved proof key exists | exit `0`, `configured: false`, native degraded read-only diagnostic |

Active provider, selection, availability, model list and voice list matched between the no-key Gateway and local results. Gateway shutdown exited 0 with its native clean receipt, no forced kill, no remaining process group and no task-owned descendants. The final run has no deferred-cleanup warning. Build/input, command, raw output and cleanup receipts were retained.

The unavailable-ref/no-saved-key-borrow control above is specifically ElevenLabs and the new injection fallback. It does not redefine another provider's existing native readiness policy, such as xAI's profile fallback. No speech synthesis, remote voice fetch, external provider/model account, audio hardware or Control UI was exercised. The container had no external network or real credentials; Control UI was disabled for this CLI/Gateway scenario.

Historical behavioral RED remains separately bound: the original official CLI/Gateway run on discovery main `14a53244238016c712d2313640c7d72e7e46181e` observed Gateway `false` versus local `true` with no key, and original fix `71c70f65e4066e671b06e93e0951648e61d63a4e` changed local to `false`. A recheck on main `5fb1a7515b3cec51dcb79e964962b9bbbc31d4b4` retained that defect. Those macOS observations are historical, not execution on this integrated Linux candidate. The earlier hosted 7/7 inventory and 105/105 CLI results likewise remain prior-head evidence.

Setup failures are preserved: initial lint stopped while offline pinned-Bun staging was unavailable; the canonical checksum/revision-verifying staging path prepared the required fork, and the affected lint/parity check then passed. An initial current-source runtime had correct inventory results but deferred startup cleanup because task-only directories inherited group-write permissions. Their permissions were repaired and only the runtime was repeated; the final private-directory run passed with those warnings absent. Already valid tests/build/checks were reused with exact source bindings.

An independent host-agent review covered the complete five-file committed diff at the base/head above, checked the source and raw verification/runtime evidence, and found no remaining supported P0/P1/P2 finding. This was an independent source/evidence review, not a local autoreview or ClawSweeper run.

The Gateway health sample was taken during startup (`ok: true`, `coreReady: false`); it subsequently reached ready and served the actual provider RPC. Container logs retain unsupported exec isolation, SQLite page-cache warm and offline catalog warnings. This proof establishes the inventory behavior above, not general deployment health.

Prior-head CI and review completed; links and source attribution are provided above. The PR remains Ready for review with maintainer edits enabled.


## Current conflict integration follow-up

The branch now includes current `origin/main` at `3256fe14aaee0e8865fb67f2bd1d236f40ea8139` and resolves the reported `src/cli/capability-cli/shared.ts` conflict while retaining the PR's `read_only_status` secret-resolution mode and main's `ExpectedCliError` handling. The merge commit is `c4c6bfa2af87204bb93ec415a3c0a257b2f031ee`; the follow-up test-coverage commit is `0dc92c081aabbe7ec5067bee155f8178d93fae21`.

For this exact candidate, the five-file diff from current main has SHA256 `bafe1b55539b6f3305aac5e2cfb50b5d3ac8b82302dce6ca73ea93fddab0d0fa`. Focused `git diff --check` and secretless Docker esbuild transpilation of `shared.ts`, `tts-runtime.ts`, `tts-runtime.providers.test.ts`, and `capability-cli.test.ts` passed under the bounded no-network, non-root 256 MiB / 0.5 CPU / 64-PID runner. Full repository tests and heavy builds were not rerun locally; hosted CI is the broad gate for this new head.

</details>

prs.title: fix: show named characters in exported session messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In a standalone HTML session export, a message containing `©` showed that spelling in the conversation card. The same thing happened inside emphasis. Both should display ©.

## User Impact

User and assistant messages now display named characters in ordinary Markdown. Inline code and typed URLs keep the original spelling. The embedded transcript retains the original message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The export viewer was escaping ordinary text a second time before the browser displayed it. It now delegates ordinary text and nested inline formatting to the bundled Marked renderer. The link renderer uses Marked’s autolink flag to display a typed address literally. Explicit link labels still support inline Markdown, and raw HTML and code retain their existing handling.

## Evidence

- Replayed the same synthetic `/export-session` transcript before and after the change. Across 22 cards per revision, paragraph and emphasized text displayed © on the fix, and inline code displayed `©`. Numeric references, literal HTML, HTTPS link markup and archived message content matched their controls.
- The minimized case and both exact property replays passed. A larger local property run ended before returning a result.
- Replayed 42 cards per revision through the standalone viewer. For `<https://example.test/©>`, the visible link text and destination both retained `©`. The embedded transcript was byte-identical on the frozen source, the previous draft head, and this repair.
- DOM regressions cover prose and inline code for both message roles, plus the visible label and destination of automatic and explicitly labeled links. Hosted Vitest passed the named-reference and autolink regressions on the signed head. [HTML export tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45628529082/job/139256429666) · [Protected CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45632603961)

prs.title: chore(ci): remove four unused exports flagged by dependency checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The dependency check reports four unused exports in the model catalog publisher, Control UI project access, and the Crabbox and Slack test helpers. They also appear in the scheduled main check. [Dependency check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45684969398/job/139456204604) · [Scheduled main check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45685091056/job/139456249630)

## User Impact

This removes four diagnostics for contributors running the unused-export check. The catalog still requires at least 200 models, and project access decisions and Crabbox fixture output retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model-count constant, project access reason type and Crabbox catalog helper each have a caller in their own file. They can stay local. The Slack platform-error fixture has no callers and can be removed.

## Evidence

- Knip 6.40.0 inspected the four affected modules and 45 tracked files that reference them. Both ordinary and entry-export scans reported all four names on the parent and cleared them on this patch. Both detected a deliberately unused export in a scratch copy.
- Reversing the three export modifiers and restoring the Slack fixture reproduced all four parent files byte for byte. The pinned formatter passed on all four files.
- The full-source dependency check on `699243b8` cleared all four diagnostics. The production scan passed, and the combined check reported no unused files. The job failed because the script and full-tree scans both reported `detectParallelsHostIp` and `listVmNames`. Scheduled main reported those same two Parallels exports alongside the four addressed here. [Exact-head job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45689685912/job/139472564691) · [Scheduled main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45685091056/job/139456249630) · [Parallels repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205481)

The Incognito chat browser case also timed out at 240 seconds. Scheduled main timed out on the same case and stack with the same shard counts. The second Gateway shard passed. The Parallels repair has since landed on main. The six-to-two comparison above describes the signed head alone. [Browser shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45689685912/job/139472561841) · [Scheduled main browser shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45685091056/job/139456245493) · [Parallels squash](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f46ec3498b4cbd02c5dbf4ab36e1b7fa1cf16774)

### Combined dependency proof

The signed integration commit `6eb5b035` combines the four reviewed file changes with main `04b854b2`, which includes the Parallels preflight correction from [#205481](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205481). The dependency job checked out that commit and ran `scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts --all`. The script, production and full-tree reports, including unused-file analysis, all passed. [Full-source job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45725545358/job/139595085390)

prs.title: fix: repair included config through directory symlinks
prs.body:
Related: #204892. Follow-up to #204979 and #204916.

## What Problem This Solves

I fixed startup/update config repair rejecting valid included configuration beneath a directory symlink with “Legacy config plan is missing include write identities.”

## User Impact

The existing repair owner can migrate the included file without flattening its directives or replacing the directory link. Missing identities, changed sources, unsafe paths and recovery refusals remain enforced. Config-file symlinks remain read-only under the existing config-write contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

I check the existing include provenance, which names the reads whose hashes and targets were captured. The watcher inventory also contains canonical aliases; those aliases are not additional inputs requiring separate write identities. Older snapshots retain the existing fallback.

The complete diff against `293eb5118dd4cdc6172852f44b985d5dab1e0772` is **+23/-3 in three files**: production **+7/-1**, tests **+16/-2**. I extended existing cases; no new harness, option or recovery owner. Launcher tests are unchanged from that base.

## Evidence

- I reproduced the linked-include failure on the exact base above, then passed the same real migration/restoration case with the fix. It preserves authored bytes and the directory link, and retains external-path refusal.
- Final prepared-plan/source-fence and in-place recovery selection: **6 passed**. Config symlink contracts: **16 passed**, two Windows-only skips.
- I ran the existing real Gateway E2E with a directory-linked root and the **2026.10.10 corpus**: migration and seeded agents/schedules/chat RPC checks passed. One case selected, six unselected; 10.82 s test time, 181.50 s wrapper wall including the 124.9 s runtime build. The temporary E2E adaptation was removed.
- Three typecheck graphs, focused lint/format and diff checks passed. I completed `pr-simplify`; fresh independent Auto Review was **P0-only, scoped-clean** on tree `a699b197674343a07065c8954c6f9699fde8e494`. Unchanged-input proof was reused after reconciliation.
- **Still unproven:** actual installed old-updater roundtrip, supported **9.x extended-stable and 10.x upgrade lanes**, and macOS/Windows service updates. The corpus test is not an installed-updater run. I did not retry or bypass the recorded package-age refusal.
- I marked this ready to request [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45733790326), not to claim landing readiness. Preflight passed; broad checks are running. That run skipped `published-driver-update`, so it does not fill the installed-updater proof gap. Task-owned processes and temporary fixtures were cleaned up.

prs.title: fix(cli): help find disabled automations after a lookup miss
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you look up an automation with an incorrect or outdated name or ID, the CLI suggests a list that hides disabled automations. An automation can still exist even when the suggested command shows no results.

## User Impact

The terminal error points to `openclaw cron list --all`, which includes disabled automations you can already see. Listing does not start, enable, or edit anything. The error still exits with status `1`, and scripts get the same JSON failure on stdout. No migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the CLI’s existing read-only list rather than changing what the default list shows. Both the `show` lookup and typed Gateway lookup failures use the same terminal guidance. The Gateway’s error text, older-Gateway fallback, and visibility checks stay unchanged.

| Surface and trigger | Before (exact stderr) | After (exact stderr) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI: an automation name or ID is not found (`cron show missing-job` or a typed Gateway miss) | ``Automation not found: missing-job. Run `openclaw cron list` to see recent automation ids.`` | ``OpenClaw couldn’t find the automation “missing-job”. Run `openclaw cron list --all` to see IDs for enabled and disabled automations.`` |

**Skill in practice:** The writing skill calls for one next step that works where the reader is. Testing the original suggestion showed why an existing command was not enough: it hid the disabled automation the person needed to find. The revised hint names the supported flag and what it shows, without asking the reader to change automation state.

## Evidence

- Real Linux CLI on an isolated Gateway, using the same synthetic, disabled `Backup summary` automation. On base `9ebbda2124b0`, the suggested `openclaw cron list` exited `0` and said `No automations.` On candidate `cfd47b60b28d`, the exact printed `openclaw cron list --all` exited `0` and showed the automation’s ID and `disabled` status. Its details and empty run history were byte-for-byte unchanged after the lookup. The default list still omitted it.
- `show`, `get`, and `edit` misses, with and without `--json`, kept exit `1` and byte-identical stdout. The terminal guidance changed on stderr only.
- Three regression cases failed on the old hint: typed failure rendering and missed `show` lookups against modern and legacy Gateway fixtures. On the candidate, 142 CLI tests and 9 Gateway visibility tests passed; the filtered real CLI subprocess test passed too. The legacy result is protocol-fixture evidence, not a run against a historical Gateway binary.
- Focused typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting, copy check, pre-commit hook, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review and hosted CI were not run in this local verification.

### Terminal comparison

Both captures use the same synthetic fixture on an isolated Gateway. The after capture shows an excerpt of the automation list.

**Before**

![Before: the suggested list omits the disabled automation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bece849d-2f99-4cd8-a5cf-6a3107220189)

**After**

![After: the suggested list shows the disabled automation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09f2b2dd-d737-4062-9682-b5c19c952cb2)

Contributed by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e346c5e4-f828-45b2-be8f-1aad6754fbad)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/a91e849c-9c9b-4d7d-bb43-9776d9c82604)

prs.title: improve: avoid reloading unchanged Usage reports
prs.body:
Related: [COG-GTM/openclaw#2](https://github.com/COG-GTM/openclaw/pull/2). Upstream already reuses day-key formatters via [#103097](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103097); this addresses separate work in the current Gateway.

## What Problem This Solves

On a UTC client, switching the Usage page from Local to UTC kept the same calendar and date range but rebuilt the report. A detailed Usage request also rebuilt the snapshot when the next request merely added sorting or pagination. On larger stores that means waiting for work the Gateway just completed.

## User Impact

These equivalent requests can now reuse a current report. Usage totals, date labels, sorting, paging, and access checks stay the same. Other IANA time zones still use their own calendars, including DST. No settings or migration required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route explicit named UTC through the existing UTC interpretation before choosing the date arithmetic or snapshot key, and retain four-digit historical date labels. Remove the presence of presentation options from the detail snapshot key: sorting and pagination happen after it loads. Distinct projections, full-context requirements, access, and revisions still distinguish snapshots. No new cache or invalidation rule.

## Evidence

Compiled Gateway, Linux and Node 26.12.1, real localhost WebSocket, 1,000 synthetic SQLite sessions over 180 days. Five serial baseline/candidate/baseline triples with restored fixtures. Times are median / nearest-rank p95 (with five samples per arm, p95 is the maximum).

| Workload | Baseline A | UTC patch | Baseline B |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| First warm Local → UTC switch | 94.85 / 99.11 ms | 23.96 / 24.70 ms | 94.59 / 100.90 ms |
| Switch process CPU | 159.87 / 192.51 ms | 41.82 / 100.28 ms | 162.22 / 220.83 ms |
| Cold first response | 536 / 595 ms | 441 / 525 ms | 490 / 527 ms |
| Cold complete report | 1,709 / 1,747 ms | 1,596 / 1,681 ms | 1,661 / 1,732 ms |

The 1,000-session run compared `d6b252e6992b` and `790575d130ba`: the warm switch eliminated a 1,000-row, 1,262,584-byte preparation on every candidate sample. All 15 complete reports matched aside from runtime timestamps. Cold startup still performs backfill, which can legitimately invalidate a snapshot, and its CPU was mixed (first-response median 1,632 / 1,660 / 1,321 ms). No general cold speedup or browser-rendering improvement is claimed.

A separate 200-session run on the final local candidate `2da73174c7d1` confirmed the exact switch dispatches after an untimed warm-up checked for a cache hit: both controls inventoried and read 200 sessions, prepared the 200 rows, and fetched the 50-row page. The candidate fetched only the page. The same reply equality assertion passed. The detail-request regression independently verifies one summary load instead of two while returning the right sorted page and full total; no RPC latency claim for that path.

Build clean source checkouts with `pnpm build sourcePerformance`. From the candidate, run `TZ=UTC NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-usage-gateway.ts --base <baseline> --head <candidate> --ui <frozen-control-ui> --out <new-output-directory> --sessions 1000 --cold-backend --cold-pairs 5 --cold-backend-utc-switch` (use `--sessions 200` and omit `--cold-pairs` for the smoke). Host one-minute load across the 1,000-session samples was 5.88–11.72.

Both cache regressions failed before their fixes. 68 focused Gateway tests and 34 infrastructure tests passed, covering the cache boundaries, invitation revocation, DST and historical date labels. Targeted lint/format, core/script typechecks, and the compiled build passed. Independent scoped reviews checked the calendar and snapshot behavior and led to strengthening the benchmark warm-up and read counters.

Thanks @steipete for flagging the original report and asking for the sibling audit.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/550dd3c6-b9d7-4dca-9edb-8e936c1b2fa2)

## Worked on by

- @steipete

prs.title: fix(gateway): stop fencing session recall on transcript-only refreshes
prs.body:
Closes #205386

## What Problem This Solves

On a busy Gateway, `sessions_search` called with a query but without `sessionKey` intermittently failed with:

> Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request

The failure was not one-shot: recall captures the disclosure revision before its SQLite worker read and re-validates it afterwards, twice. Any transcript activity happening anywhere on the Gateway reset that revision, so both read attempts were fenced and the call threw. Supplying `sessionKey` skips the recall path, which is why the same search worked when the key was passed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/gateway/session-row-projection.ts` called `revisions.invalidate()` inside `transcriptUpdates.refresh()` on every transcript refresh — both the certified fast path and the materialized slow path. `invalidate()` clears the memoized sharing token that `searchRecallSessionTranscripts` captures as `projection.sharingRevision` and compares after each worker read (`sessions-search-recall.ts:55,187,197`). A transcript write to any unrelated row therefore looked like a disclosure-scope change.

Transcript-only refreshes update presentation facts (activity summary, preview, transcript watermark); they do not change who may read a session. The fix removes that single invalidation and documents the invariant. Every genuine scope change still invalidates the token through its own path:

- `mark()` for structural and visibility publications;
- `revisions.materialized()` for board and membership changes;
- `revisions.replace()` / `remove()` for row replacement and lifecycle;
- the catalog owner refresh.

Fact consumers are unaffected: `publishFacts` still runs on both refresh paths, so summaries and previews keep updating. No change to the recall fence itself, no new dependencies, no guard weakening.

## User Impact

Session recall on a busy Gateway keeps working while other sessions are writing transcripts: `sessions_search` without a `sessionKey` no longer needs retries. Disclosure protection is unchanged — real visibility, sharing, membership, owner, or lifecycle changes during a read still fence the response and produce the same error.

## Evidence

Real runtime: the shipped `startGatewayServer` entry (`node --import tsx` against this worktree's source), a fresh `chmod 700` state dir, a real WebSocket protocol client, and 48 materialized busy sessions receiving continuous transcript writes while each search is in flight. Each scenario runs 4 recall searches without `sessionKeys` plus 2 searches with explicit `sessionKeys`.

Before the fix (bug present in the same harness):

```
[proof] round 3 recall without sessionKeys (1609ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] round 4 recall without sessionKeys (1972ms): {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Error: Session search scope changed while reading; retry the request"}}
[proof] round 1 search with explicit sessionKeys (1430ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] with explicit sessionKeys: 2/2 succeeded
[proof] RESULT: FAIL (recall reported a scope change)
```

After the fix:

```
[proof] round 1 recall without sessionKeys (8668ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] round 2 recall without sessionKeys (1580ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] round 3 recall without sessionKeys (1095ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] round 4 recall without sessionKeys (1097ms): {"ok":true,"hits":["agent:main:visible-target"]}
[proof] with explicit sessionKeys: 2/2 succeeded
[proof] RESULT: PASS (recall tolerated transcript-only activity)
```

Regression tests (new tests fail with the invalidation restored, pass with the fix):

```
node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/gateway/session-row-projection.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-row-projection.invalidation.test.ts \
  src/gateway/session-row-projection.transcript-regression.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-search-scope.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-search.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-search-invited-policy.test.ts
 Test Files  6 passed (6)
      Tests  64 passed (64)
```

- `session-row-projection.test.ts`: sharing revision stays stable across a transcript-only refresh, and still changes on membership edits.
- `sessions-search-scope.test.ts`: recall succeeds while unrelated rows emit transcript activity during the worker read, and still throws when the disclosure scope genuinely changes during both attempts.

`oxlint` on the three touched files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `tsgo` cannot run in this environment (system GLIBC is older than 2.32), so type checking is delegated to the exact-head CI run.

prs.title: fix(cli): clarify when the last explicit model alias is removed
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After `openclaw models aliases remove` removes the last alias saved in the config, it says “No aliases configured.” A fresh `models aliases list` can still show a built-in alias such as `gemini`.

## User Impact

The successful removal now says “No explicit model aliases remain in your config.” The message is accurate whether a built-in alias appears in the next list or the list is empty.

## Why This Change Was Made

The removal command counts aliases saved in the config. Listing also includes defaults for configured model targets. The change makes the existing count clear in the CLI output.

@ScientificProgrammer documented this sequence in [PR #81641](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/81641). That merged fix explains the rejection when someone subsequently tries to remove the built-in alias. This change corrects the message from the preceding successful removal.

## Evidence

- Ran the registered CLI commands in fresh processes against a private config file. After removing the last explicit alias, a cold JSON and plain-text list showed `gemini` for `google/gemini-4-argon`. Both lists were empty for a model without a built-in alias.
- The rejection for removing a built-in alias, an explicit opt-out, and a case-insensitive alias collision were also exercised. Each successful removal delivered one config-write notification. Rejected commands produced none.
- Both changed files passed the pinned formatter. The project Vitest suite was not run locally in the code-only author checkout.

### Captured CLI output

Each command below ran in a fresh process against the same isolated profile. These stdout excerpts omit config and backup paths and redact the model ID.

```console
$ openclaw models aliases remove a
No explicit model aliases remain in your config.
$ openclaw models aliases list --plain
gemini [redacted model ID]
```

On the parent, removal printed `No aliases configured.` before the same cold list returned `gemini`. In the profile with no effective aliases, the corrected removal printed the same confirmation and the cold plain list produced zero lines. The signed-head project suite passed all 10 cases. [Hosted alias tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45730271084/job/139610965204)

prs.title: fix: report the default deep research runtime accurately
prs.body:
Closes #205544

## What Problem This Solves

Deep Research's capabilities answer says `direct-provider`, although ordinary portable requests select `isolated-agent-runtime`. An agent checking capabilities before a default research job is therefore told to expect the wrong execution route.

## User Impact

Capabilities now report the default accurately. Explicit `requiredAuthMode: "oauth"` requests retain their direct-provider route and OAuth-only constraint. No execution, credential, billing, or configuration policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The routing change in #177228 left the older capability constant behind. Re-auditing the registered tool, job owner, portable adapter, and host completion contract on pinned main confirmed that the metadata owner—not the router—needs the fix.

Kept this small branch and reconciled current main in place; rebuilding it would not improve the fix. Applied `pr-simplify`: one production-line replacement, one field added to the existing registered-tool assertion, and documentation of the default/OAuth distinction without repeating the exception. Existing default, OAuth-only, and no-direct-fallback tests are reused. No new test cases, helpers, comments, limits, or runtime branches.

Diff against the pinned base: **production +1/−1; tests +1/−1; docs +12/−10** (3 files, net +2 lines).

## Evidence

Audit base: `df720d5644b8e6b3a82ebfef32b7349fcc92c240`. Published head: `10ab65a1542a8d3c1d50ec843d8334b71f5cb93b`.

**Actual built backend, no mock Gateway:** built both baseline and candidate with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime` (58.6s / 55.4s). Used the built CLI's baseline setup and foreground Gateway in separate temporary profiles, with token authentication and loopback ports. Both reached readiness. The same authenticated `POST /tools/invoke` request, `{"tool":"deep_research","args":{"action":"capabilities"},"sessionKey":"main"}`, returned HTTP 200:

```text
Baseline response.details.portable:
{"runtime":"direct-provider","nativeFunctionCallingRequired":false}

Candidate response.details.portable:
{"runtime":"isolated-agent-runtime","nativeFunctionCallingRequired":false}
```

Both Gateway processes exited 0; their listeners closed and disposable state was removed. This proves the capabilities endpoint, **not a model-backed research job**. The backend build profile is not a full release/declaration build.

**Regression and local checks:**
- On the pinned baseline implementation, the registered-tool/routing pair returned **1 failed, 7 passed**, failing specifically on the wrong runtime value. On the candidate, the full plugin command `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/test-extension.mts deep-research --maxWorkers=1` passed **105 tests in 10 files**, 59.18s Vitest duration. These tests use fixture runtime I/O.
- Changed registered-tool file: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/deep-research/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **2 passed**, 41.38s Vitest / 44.05s wrapper wall time; the changed capabilities case took 163ms, with cold worker compilation dominating. Hosted CI seconds are unavailable.
- Targeted lint, extension production/test typechecks, format, and whitespace checks passed.
- Bound Auto Review, local candidate against the pinned base, **P0–P3**: `scoped-clean`, zero findings.

**Aggregate check is not green:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged --base df720d5644b8e6b3a82ebfef32b7349fcc92c240 --timed` exited 1. Its max-lines/env guard could not resolve ancestry in the managed shallow checkout; the same guard passed separately with its supported `--no-merge-base` option against the exact prepared base. Remaining reported failures:
- Changelog attribution at `CHANGELOG/2026.11.10.md:8130`.
- Eight unused exports across the Crabbox/Slack test support, model-catalog publisher, operator-role policy, project access, and roles UI. Every reported owning file and both scanners were byte-identical to the pinned base; the patch changes no imports or exports. This is source attribution, not a separately executed baseline full-tree scan. Unrelated files and safeguards were left unchanged.

**Not checked:** no real default portable model job, OAuth-provider job, entitlement, or billing qualification was run. The sandbox has no authorized live-model binding; the configured remote runner failed preflight, and no lease was allocated. These unchanged model-execution paths are not claimed as observed proof.

**Hosted review and CI:** [ClawSweeper revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205647#issuecomment-7178895481) reviewed `10ab65a1542a8d3c1d50ec843d8334b71f5cb93b`: **Diamond (5/6)** overall, proof, and patch quality; **zero actionable findings; proof sufficient (terminal)**. It accepted the built-Gateway endpoint evidence for this metadata-only change and requested no additional model-job proof. Marked ready for review at the requester's instruction on 2026-11-26. [CI run 45732823075](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45732823075) completed successfully for this head; [the aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45732823075/job/139621136355) confirms every selected lane succeeded, with no inherited-failure exception. The projected `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review, and security-sensitive review statuses also passed. CI executed merge revision `02ea034118ee4f5c5d202954b4b49406d6e299c6` against base `293eb5118dd4cdc6172852f44b985d5dab1e0772`. `build-artifacts`, native-app, and UI E2E lanes were not selected for this patch; they are not claimed as executed. GitHub reports the open, non-draft PR mergeable with a clean merge state. Stopped at merge-readiness; no merge or auto-merge was requested.

prs.title: fix(exec): still say a command timed out when its cleanup also fails
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts:717` turned every rejected `wait()` into a generic runtime error, so when cleanup missed its hard deadline after OpenClaw's own timeout had stopped the command (`src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay-host.ts:201` rejects the pending result on purpose), the timeout was lost and finalization added the cleanup error a second time.

Fixes #205627

Thanks @stealthybear for the report, the repro and this fix.

## What Problem This Solves

When a command run through exec hits its timeout and its processes or output then take more than about 5 seconds to close, the result the agent receives says only "service child cleanup did not complete before its hard deadline". The agent can't tell that the command simply ran past its timeout, so it can't decide to retry with a longer one.

## User Impact

The result again says `Command timed out after N seconds.` (status failed, `timedOut: true`, failure kind `overall-timeout`), followed by the cleanup failure, which is still reported once. The same holds for the no-output timeout and the memory bound. Results of a command you cancel yourself, of normal exits and of timeouts whose cleanup finishes in time are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The supervisor already knows why it stopped the run (`forcedReason`), but when cleanup then expires, `wait()` rejects with the cleanup error and the reason is lost. Rejecting stays right, since an unconfirmed cleanup must not look clean to the other callers of `wait()`. Exec already hears that reason through the spawn's `onCancel` (the supervisor forwards every stop there) and keeps the first one; the supervisor and its run type stay unchanged. Exec uses it when `wait()` rejects after a stop it didn't ask for: it builds the stopped result from that reason and hands the cleanup error to finalization, which appends it after the timeout text and marks cleanup as uncertain, as it already does for other cleanup failures.

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** one repro script run unchanged on fresh profiles of the released 2026.11.10 and of this PR: a stub model makes the agent call exec once with `timeoutSeconds: 4`; the command hands its stdout to a helper process outside its tree, prints `started` and sleeps. The table shows the exec result the model received in the next request (recorded by the stub).

| Run | Released 2026.11.10 | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Output held open past the timeout | `started`, then only `Error: service child cleanup did not complete before its hard deadline; …` (twice) | `started`, `Command timed out after 4 seconds.`, the usual timeout advice, then the cleanup error once |
| Control: same command without the helper | `Command timed out after 4 seconds.` | identical |

![Exec result the model received: released 2026.11.10 vs this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stealthybear/openclaw/bee25005ab1853687d0ef20401fe2aee7eb88bd3/before-after.png)

Tested on `27f797bca07` (based on `1bc412fb747`).

- Review: autoreview (claude), `1bc412fb747..27f797bca07`, P0–P2: clean. A GPT and a Gemini review asked for a test where cleanup succeeds but the output stays open (added), and for reading the stop reason from the supervisor (done in 27f797b, then reverted by a maintainer commit so the supervisor stays unchanged; `onCancel` already carries the same reason).
- Tests: `bash-tools.exec-runtime.cleanup.test.ts` gets one table (cleanup join rejects, succeeds, absent) (the relay-host case for the supervisor field left with that field). All three fail on main and pass here. Wall time with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: cleanup test 3.9 s (25 tests), awaited-output test 40.0 s (9 tests, mostly transform). Lint and `tsgo` pass. CI has not run on this head yet.
- **No request proof:** the fix changes only the exec tool result, not how requests are built; the stub log above shows the result as sent.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Code at `1bc412fb747`:

- `src/process/supervisor/service-child-relay-host.ts:201` (`expireCleanup`) rejects the pending root result with the cleanup-expiry error when the stopped tree isn't confirmed gone within the deadline, so `ManagedRun.wait()` rejects instead of returning the `overall-timeout` exit the supervisor chose in `requestCancel` (`supervisor.ts:276`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts:707-720` turned that rejection into a generic runtime error, so `buildExecExitOutcome` never wrote the timeout text; finalization (`:464-482`) then appended the same error a second time.

Reported once: on the host path the extinction join either rejects with the same expiry (finalization's catch reports it) or succeeds because only the output stayed open (the saved error is reported through finalization's error list); without a join (sandbox) the saved error is reported the same way.

Left as on main: a run you cancel yourself (`manual-cancel`) whose cleanup then expires still reports the cleanup error instead of the cancel, because changing what a cancel reports is a separate question.

How the repro keeps the output open: `holder.py` receives the command's stdout and stderr over a Unix socket (`SCM_RIGHTS`) and holds them for 20 s, so the relay never sees EOF. First seen with `openclaw doctor --json` run through exec with a 420 s timeout.

</details>

## Maintainer proof on the final head

Re-run in secretless `node:24.22.1` Linux containers on a built Gateway, real agent turns through the real exec tool, reporter's holder scripts: main `da760885b959` twice, head `d6d015d4b77d` twice. Repro: main shows only the cleanup error (twice, first line `Error: service child cleanup …`); head shows `Command timed out after 4 seconds.` plus the usual advice, then the cleanup error once. Controls unchanged on both: timeout with fast cleanup (timeout text, no cleanup error), cleanup expiry without a timeout (background + `process kill`: cleanup error, no timeout text), normal command (`hello-205627`).

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: the exec result (text, `failureKind`, `timedOut`) only for commands OpenClaw stopped (timeout, memory bound) whose cleanup then fails.
