prs.title: fix: keep Git-installed plugins working after an OpenClaw update
prs.body:
Closes #204156
Related: #205569, #205573, #205567

## What Problem This Solves

After changing releases, a plugin installed from Git can retain its OpenClaw peer link to the previous release. The new Gateway then refuses to load the plugin, leaving its tools unavailable.

## User Impact

Pinned Git plugins remain usable when the managed installation switches to another release. `openclaw doctor --fix` can repair an existing stale link, and a retry can finish an interrupted repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair path now uses the same source and checkout identity as the Git installer. It checks the registered checkout and Git commit, then targets the serving release. An existing link is replaced only when it points to another release of that installation. A missing link can be recreated without overwriting a file or a package that appears in the meantime.

## Evidence

- On macOS arm64, installed a local Git plugin pinned to one commit in an isolated managed release layout. With the published **2026.11.7** package (`e31bbf0`), its real Gateway tool returned HTTP 200 from release A. After selecting a separate release directory B with the same published package, the persisted peer still pointed to A. The Gateway logged a peer-link audit refusal and the tool returned HTTP 404.
- Built the exact candidate `7b7cad3` with `pnpm build:runtime`. Two independently seeded profiles retained the same Git pin. Starting the candidate Gateway repaired the link and returned HTTP 200 with the candidate SDK path. Running `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` in the second profile repaired its stale link before startup, and the Gateway returned the same successful result.
- The focused peer-link suites passed **53 tests** on the final commit. They cover interruption after unlinking, retry, and preserving a regular package that appears during repair. Core typecheck, changed-file lint, formatting, and the repository commit checks passed.

The reproduction selected real package directories through a disposable release link. It did not run a system service installation, the full self-updater, or an external model. Linux and Windows runtime evidence remains for CI.

OpenAI Codex (GPT-6.2 Sol, xhigh) authored the patch, tests, and verification.


### Named profile replay on `3e8159a`

The real Git release launcher ran `--profile work` on macOS arm64. The launcher and its selected releases were under `home/.openclaw/git-install`. The Git checkout and state were under `home/.openclaw-work`. The checkout commit stayed pinned throughout. The tested profiles and plugin were disposable fixtures.

```text
Stock shared launcher --profile work: OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (e31bbf0)
work pin 642130defa9a HTTP 200 via A/dist/plugin-sdk/core.js
Original PR shared launcher --profile work: OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (7b7cad3)
work pin 642130defa9a after shared host B, peer still A, HTTP 404
Original doctor --profile work: peer still A, Git pin 642130defa9a

Reviewed shared launcher --profile work: OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (3e8159a)
work pin 642130defa9a HTTP 200 via fixed shared release/dist/plugin-sdk/core.js
Doctor updated named profile peer to shared release before startup; pin 642130defa9a
work pin 642130defa9a HTTP 200 via fixed shared release/dist/plugin-sdk/core.js
```

The original change reported this audit failure, with the temporary path replaced by `<fixture>`.

```text
peer link audit failed: <fixture>/home/.openclaw-work/git/git-e17adb066d1bd4e5/repo/node_modules/openclaw points to <fixture>/home/.openclaw/git-install/releases/stock-a/openclaw instead of <fixture>/home/.openclaw/git-install/releases/published-patch-b/openclaw
```

The review revision resolves the serving release from its verified active installation and uses the named profile for the Git checkout. On the preceding commit, the unit reproduction failed both when a named profile was actively serving and when the candidate host was inactive. Both controls pass on this revision. Six affected suites passed 123 tests, including the interrupted-repair retry. Core typecheck, targeted lint and formatting, and the complete runtime build passed.

prs.title: feat(macos): use the signed-in person's saved session pins
prs.body:
## What changes

The macOS app uses the signed-in person's saved session pins, as the web sidebar does since #204436. It advertises `personal-session-pins` and reads and reorders that profile's saved layout (`ui.railShortcuts`). Pinning a snoozed thread is refused until it wakes, matching the Gateway contract. Jason decided Mac pins and the Archive Undo marker ship together in this PR.

**Older Gateways: read-only fallback.** When the Gateway does not advertise `personal-session-pins`, legacy shared pins stay visible but Pin/Unpin are disabled. The row menu explains why: "Update the Gateway to change personal session pins." An updated Mac never writes shared pins it would present as personal. Archive and Restore keep working.

**Dropping an unpinned thread onto a saved pin** first pins it with `sessions.patch` (with `expectedSessionId`). The Gateway, as pin owner, then refuses a thread that was snoozed, archived or replaced on another device. Only after that does the Mac place the new pin beside the target with the same guarded `users.prefs.set` layout write it uses for reordering. No new RPC field is added. If placement fails after the pin committed, the pin stays last and the error is visible.

**iOS is unchanged.** iOS shares OpenClawKit but does not advertise the capability and has no sidebar data owner. Mac-only paths are gated with `#if os(macOS)` or on that owner. iOS adoption is #199685.

## Archive Undo marker contract

The Mac needs Undo to restore a shared pin that Archive cleared, without guessing from the personal list. Jason approved storing a private archive-occurrence marker on the existing session row.

- A connection advertising `session-archive-undo-v1` can be used for Undo. That requires a direct personal-pin operator with a durable profile on a SQLite agent store. It sends `archived: true, requestArchiveUndo: true` with `expectedSessionId`. Only a committed Archive returns an opaque `archiveUndoToken`, on the single response or on that target's successful batch outcome.
- Undo is a single `sessions.patch` with the same target, `archived: false` and the token. If that Archive cleared a shared pin, Undo creates a **fresh** shared pin. It never restores the old timestamp or edits anyone's personal order.
- The token belongs to the issuing live connection and expires after one hour. Any later shared pin or unpin (including an equal-value clear), Restore, replacement, re-Archive, SDK/Doctor rewrite of the archive facts, or another connection invalidates it. Ordinary Restore never re-pins. PostgreSQL and memory-only stores keep guarded Archive without receipts.
- On a personal-pin connection without receipts, a successful Archive retires any earlier Undo notice. It then says "Archived without Undo. Restore from Threads… → Archived."
- Agent schema **v45** adds the nullable `session_nodes.archive_undo_marker` column under stopped-writer maintenance. No existing node rows are rewritten. The divergent preview v44 and any pre-v45 non-null marker are refused. Migration witness, backup tables and PostgreSQL generated schema are updated.
- **Reader-floor contract:** v45 is another nullable-column step after v44.
  - A real SQLite v44→v45 migration keeps the v44 reader floor (`minReader` 44); the storage-migration test pins this.
  - The PostgreSQL step keeps the v44 floor too; PostgreSQL never issues the marker.
  - `floorRaisingDatabases` treats agents at v43–v44 as additive up to v45, so the update preflight does not demand a rollback image for them.
  - A stale v45 marker cannot be redeemed without the live issuing connection's token.

## Fit with main's architecture checks

- **Session identity:** the Gateway no longer compares session ids or lifecycle revisions for Undo. It asks the session store through `isArchiveUndoRequestShape`, `isArchivedOccurrenceRestore` and `isSameSessionOccurrence` in `src/config/sessions/session-archive-undo.ts`. The guards are the same as before.
- **Database worker:** the marker's clear, issue, read and consume statements are fixed-shape prepared queries in the existing entry-write query cache (`getSessionEntryWriteQueries`). They run in the same entry transaction, and the replacement read uses the same cached reader. The archive batch writer is back in `session-accessor.sqlite-entry-write.ts`, as on `main`. Main-thread SQLite T1 calls stay at 166 → 166.
- All baseline ratchets pass locally against `main`: session-identity, database-worker, max-lines, test-lines and others. The import-cycle and line-cap checks also pass.

## Verification

Tested commit `0ce92742f7aa11bf918acf55e6fe776f4d3f83aa`, tree `4a6752ea47a1c026c3116d13cc9e75327c4f3e9d`; the published head `5c5f1dd5a4e5` has the same tree. It merges `main` at `2cb6842eb7ec` (which includes #204436 as `63b81379`). The diff against that `main` is the macOS/shared Swift changes, the Undo marker and the v45 migration. All state is synthetic and disposable.

- **Named drop through the pin owner:** `a named drop pins through the Gateway before placing the new pin` drives the real `ChatSessionSidebar.dropInteraction` against a scripted Gateway connection.
  - If the Gateway refuses the pin, as it does for a thread snoozed elsewhere: exactly `sessions.patch` is sent and the saved layout is unchanged.
  - If the Gateway accepts: `sessions.patch` comes first, then the guarded layout write places the new pin before its target.
  - On the previous Swift sources (`9b8f2e52`), the test fails in both cases: the refused row was written straight into the layout.
- **Gateway Archive Undo over real sockets:** `server.sessions.archive-undo.integration.test.ts` starts a Gateway and connects a personal-pin Mac client and a legacy client over WebSocket. Results:
  - Hello advertises `session-archive-undo-v1` only to the personal-pin client.
  - Archive returns a token, and Undo restores a cleared shared pin with a fresh `pinned_at`.
  - Undo of a personal-only pin leaves `pinned_at` null and the personal order unchanged.
  - Superseded, spent, legacy-cleared and one-hour-expired tokens fail with `INVALID_REQUEST` and leave the row byte-identical.
  - A legacy client asking for a receipt gets `FORBIDDEN`.
- **Gateway, migration and upgrade suites on the merged tree:** 25 files passed in 5 Vitest shards. Besides Undo and archive lifecycle, these cover:
  - worktree lifecycle, connection state and remote ingress;
  - v44→v45 storage migration, member access and schema creation;
  - agent port and retained schema;
  - both personal-pin suites and the PostgreSQL generator;
  - `state-upgrade-databases`, `state-upgrade`, schema metadata, `ordinary-upgrade` and patch participation;
  - expected-identity patches, archive permissions and three historical migration fixtures.

  PostgreSQL conformance for the engine, port-descriptor, member-access and archive-lifecycle files was run locally against `pgvector:pg17`, set up as in CI, and passed. Six entry-write and replacement suites also passed after the marker SQL moved.
- **Swift:** `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter 'ChatSessionSidebar|ChatSessionSnooze|ChatGatewayEventSubscription|ChatViewModelAgentNavigation|ChatSessionGroupCatalog'` passed 354 tests in 27 suites. The macOS app product builds.
- **Static checks:**
  - Passed: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm protocol:check`, regenerated validators, PostgreSQL canonical verify, Kysely verify, SQLite transcript baseline, worker inventory, `native:i18n:verify` and `format:check`.
  - SwiftFormat is clean on touched Swift files, and SwiftLint `--strict` is clean for the iOS/shared scope.
- **Test lines:** within the allowance plus the 515 lines recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/macos-session-pins.txt`, checked by the baseline ratchets against `main`.

**No installed-app Mac run exists for this candidate.** Jason's live Mac app was not used and no VM was created. The Mac evidence above is package tests driving the real sidebar interaction, the macOS build and a signed Gateway WebSocket trace, not a physical drag → Archive → Undo in an installed app.

**Reproduce:**

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.archive-undo.integration.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-entry-patch.archive-undo.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db.storage-migration.test.ts src/state/state-upgrade-databases.test.ts
swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter 'ChatSessionSidebar(Batch|ArchiveUndo|ArchiveToken|Menu)Tests'
```

## Local review

An exact-head local ClawSweeper review (GPT-6.2 Sol) of `1d80561a` rated it **D** (proof D, patch C). One round of fixes followed:

- **[P2] Pin edits disabled after a lost refresh (fixed).** A reorder could be acknowledged and the follow-up preference read then time out. That read cleared the verified profile and disabled Pin, Unpin and drag. Now only a definitive reply changes the verified state. The existing acknowledged-move test asserts the profile stays verified when the refresh times out. It fails on `1d80561a` and passes now.
- **[P3] Read-only Pin explained (fixed).** On a Gateway without personal pins, the row menu shows "Update the Gateway to change personal session pins." under the disabled Pin item.
- **[P3] Docs (fixed).** `docs/platforms/mac/webchat.md` now separates older Gateways, which keep Undo, from personal-pin connections without receipts, which use Threads… → Archived.

Still open: there is no installed-app Mac run, so real-behavior proof stays at harness level. The review again asked whether pins and the Undo marker should ship together. Jason decided to ship them together in this PR.

prs.title: fix(update): a pnpm update no longer fails after activating when the installed release came from an update
prs.body:
Related: #205167 (what users see and how to recover), #204836, #203458, #201740

## Status on November 25: 2026.11.10 shipped without this, so it now targets `release/2026.11.11`

- npm `latest` is 2026.11.10, published from `6ea542fd97e`. That is the base this PR was measured against, so the published 2026.11.10 has the fault described below.
- This PR now targets `release/2026.11.11` (head `1be6d3ddc6b` when retargeted). The commit is unchanged. `git merge-tree --write-tree` against that head is clean. The 8 commits that line adds over `v2026.11.10` touch none of the five files here and nothing under `src/update/`, `src/infra/` or `src/state/`. Rechecked on November 25 at 16:20 UTC against `7038eed8f33`, now 30 commits over `v2026.11.10`: the merge is still clean, the schema is still state 40 and agent 42, and none of the five files here is touched. That head does change other files under `src/infra/` and `src/state/` (SQLite snapshots and read-only inspection). The R, G and B cells ran on the 2026.11.10 base. The C cells ran this commit on `1be6d3ddc6b`, the 2026.11.11 head at the time; nothing has been rerun on `7038eed8f33`.
- What this commit can and cannot do from here:
  - The update from the published 2026.11.10 to 2026.11.11 is run by the installed 2026.11.10. A pnpm install that reached 2026.11.10 through `openclaw update` gets the exit 1 once, whether or not 2026.11.11 contains this commit. The candidate does not change it (rows B1, B2 and B4 below).
  - With this commit in 2026.11.11, the update after that is run by a fixed updater and exits 0 once the failed run is repaired (row C1 u4). Without it, the same exit 1 repeats on every same-schema release (row C4 u3).
- The beta hop is now measured, and it fails. A pnpm install that got 2026.11.10-beta.3 through `openclaw update` and then updates to the final 2026.11.10 exits 1 with `update-recovery-pending`. A beta.3 from a plain `pnpm add -g` updates cleanly.

| Cell | Installed version, and how it got there | Target | Exit | Outage | Recorded run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | 2026.11.10-beta.3, by `openclaw update` | 2026.11.10, pack of the base | **1** | 67 s | `running` |
| B2 | 2026.11.10-beta.3, by `openclaw update` | 2026.11.10, pack of this PR | **1** | 75 s | `running` |
| B3 (control) | 2026.11.10-beta.3, by `pnpm add -g` | 2026.11.10, pack of the base | 0 | 69 s | succeeded |
| B4 u2 | 2026.11.10-beta.3, by `openclaw update` | published 2026.11.10 | **1** | 68 s | `running` |
| B4 repair | `openclaw update repair`, as the failed update prints | none | 0 | 52 s | succeeded |
| B4 u3 | published 2026.11.10, after that repair | 2026.11.11, pack of the base with a version bump | **1** | 72 s | `running` |

In every failing row the new version is installed, `openclaw --version` works and the Gateway serves the target. The schema is state 40 and agent 42 before and after each of these hops. Same setup as the cells in Evidence; one run each. The recorded facts of B1 to B4 are in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205078#issuecomment-7154279666).

Measured after that, with the published packages as the starting point (cells C1, C3 and C4). Each cell starts with `pnpm add -g openclaw@2026.11.9` from npm and one `openclaw update --yes` to the published 2026.11.10. That first hop exited 0 in all three, with 64 to 74 s of outage.

| Cell | Step | Updater, and how it was installed | Target | Exit | Outage | Recorded run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 u2 | `openclaw update --yes` | published 2026.11.10, by `openclaw update` | 2026.11.11 with this commit | **1** | 76 s | `running` |
| C1 watch | none, for 17 minutes | | | | none | `running` in all 41 status reads |
| C1 u3 | `openclaw update --yes` | 2026.11.11 with this commit, not repaired | 2026.11.12 with this commit | **1**, refused after 1.7 s | none | `running` |
| C1 repair | `openclaw update repair`, Gateway left running | 2026.11.11 with this commit | none | 0 after 69 s | 51 s | succeeded |
| **C1 u4** | `openclaw update --yes` | 2026.11.11 with this commit, repaired | 2026.11.12 with this commit | **0** | 69 s | succeeded |
| C3 u2 | `openclaw update --yes` | published 2026.11.10, by `openclaw update` | head of `release/2026.11.15`, schema 40/42 → 41/43 | 0 | 63 s | succeeded |
| C4 u2 | `openclaw update --yes` | published 2026.11.10, by `openclaw update` | 2026.11.11 without this commit | **1** | 69 s | `running` |
| C4 repair | `openclaw update repair` | 2026.11.11 without this commit | none | 0 after 71 s | 52 s | succeeded |
| **C4 u3** | `openclaw update --yes` | 2026.11.11 without this commit, repaired | 2026.11.12 without this commit | **1** | 72 s | `running` |

What these rows show:

- **This commit ends the repeat.** A 2026.11.11 with it updates to the next same-schema version with exit 0 (C1 u4). The same tree without it fails again (C4 u3).
- **One manual step remains for installs already on 2026.11.10.** Their update to 2026.11.11 exits 1 whatever 2026.11.11 contains (C1 u2, C4 u2). The run record does not settle by itself: it stayed `running` in phase `verifying` for 17 minutes, and the Gateway journal has no reconcile line in that time. The next `openclaw update` is refused in 1.7 s and names `openclaw update repair`. After that one repair, updates are clean.
- **A schema-changing target is not affected** (C3), with the same published 2026.11.10 as the updater.
- **Shortest recovery measured:** `openclaw update repair` with the Gateway left running (69 to 71 s, about 51 s of outage), then `openclaw update`.
- **Left behind after the repair and the clean update (C1):** `openclaw update status` still lists the failed run's recovery set as "unresolved after a failed update" and its next action is to inspect the capture's `manifest.json`. About 534 MiB of capture and about 534 MiB of database snapshot stay on disk for the 512 MiB store.

The same chain on macOS (cells MC1 and MC2: macOS 27.2 on arm64 in a local VM, the Gateway as a LaunchAgent, pnpm 12.23.0, the same packs, one run each). The first hop, published 2026.11.9 → published 2026.11.10, exited 0 in both with 75 and 81 s of outage.

| Cell | Step | Target | Exit | Outage | Recorded run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MC1 u2 | `openclaw update --yes` from the published 2026.11.10 | 2026.11.11 with this commit | **1** | 103 s | `running` |
| MC1 watch | none, for 5 minutes | | | none | `running` in all 31 status reads |
| MC1 u3 | `openclaw update --yes`, not repaired | 2026.11.12 with this commit | **1**, refused after 2.2 s | none | `running` |
| MC1 repair | `openclaw update repair`, Gateway left running | none | 0 after 59 s | 46 s | succeeded |
| **MC1 u4** | `openclaw update --yes` | 2026.11.12 with this commit | **0** | 88 s | succeeded |
| MC2 u2 | `openclaw update --yes` from the published 2026.11.10 | 2026.11.11 without this commit | **1** | 103 s | `running` |
| MC2 repair | `openclaw update repair` | none | 0 after 67 s | 54 s | succeeded |
| **MC2 u3** | `openclaw update --yes` | 2026.11.12 without this commit | **1** | 93 s | `running` |

macOS behaves like Linux here: the fault, the refusal, the repair and the effect of this commit are the same, and the messages match apart from IDs. Outages are longer (103 s against 69 to 76 s for the failing update). After MC1, `openclaw update cleanup --dry-run` lists the failed run's capture as protected (`unresolved-failed-update`, 560 MB) with 0 bytes to clean. The recorded facts are in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205078#issuecomment-7169357456).

Packs for these cells, none published: "2026.11.11 with this commit" is `release/2026.11.11` at `1be6d3ddc6b` plus this commit applied without committing, so its build reports `1be6d3d`. "2026.11.12" is the same tree with only a version bump. The packs without this commit are the unmodified `1be6d3ddc6b` and its version bump. The 2026.11.15 pack is `release/2026.11.15` at `ae07e2709f3`. The recorded facts of C1, C3 and C4 are in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205078#issuecomment-7155524515).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a pnpm global install, the second `openclaw update` after reaching 2026.11.10 fails with `update-recovery-pending` when the installed 2026.11.10 was itself put there by `openclaw update` and the target has the same database schema.

## User Impact

With this commit in a release (2026.11.11 is the next one), a pnpm user who updated to that release can run a plain `openclaw update` to the next same-schema release and get exit 0, a finished run record, and a working `openclaw` command and Gateway, with no manual step.

Without it (measured on the unmodified `release/2026.11.10` head), that update:

- exits 1 with `update-recovery-pending` and `First failure: plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global was lost … Cannot find module`,
- leaves the run recorded as `running`; `openclaw update status` shows "needs attention" and two different next steps ("Stop the Gateway first … then run openclaw update repair" and "Next action: openclaw update cleanup --dry-run"),
- needs a manual `openclaw update repair`; even after that, `openclaw update status` keeps reporting the recovery set as "unresolved after a failed update. Retained original state requires manual inspection".

The new version is installed, the Gateway serves it, and the `openclaw` command works in both cases. Nothing is lost; the failure is in the record and the next steps the user is told to take.

Update behavior: the fix runs in the updater, which is the installed version. It helps updates driven by a 2026.11.10 that contains it. The first update onto 2026.11.10 is unaffected either way (it migrates the schema and passed on the unmodified head, see the table).

## Why This Change Was Made

A pnpm updater that an earlier `openclaw update` installed runs from its group's project-local store (`<pnpm home>/global/v11/<group>/node_modules/openclaw`). Activating the next version moves that group into the transaction backup, so the running updater's own `dist` disappears. Work started inside the update already loads workers through the retained-runtime generation. Process-wide owners that start workers from detached or earlier async contexts (the state lease heartbeat carrier, the file-log worker pool) still resolved them from the installed package, so their spawns failed with `Cannot find module`, the plugin lifecycle lease was lost, and the update ended `update-recovery-pending` while the new Gateway was already serving.

This is a port of #203458 from main. While it is bound, the retained-runtime generation also registers a process-wide resolver, and `createCpuTrackedWorker` applies it. Async-context bindings keep precedence, a URL the generation already produced is final, and nothing changes outside an update that retained its runtime.

Root cause, checked against the alternatives:

- **Updater installed by an update, not same-schema updates in general.** The same packed 2026.11.10 → 2026.11.11 hop exits 0 when 2026.11.10 was installed with plain `pnpm add -g` (row R1, Gateway from the global virtual store `store/v11/links/...`). It fails when 2026.11.10 was installed by `openclaw update` (rows R2/R3, Gateway from `global/v11/<group>/node_modules/openclaw`). That store layout is exactly the condition #203458 fixes.
- **The worker spawn after activation.** The ported test, run on the base with only the new resolver module copied in, fails with the same error the cell shows: `Cannot find module '…/installed/dist/probe.worker.mjs'` (`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`).
- **Not #203406.** That PR names the Gateway recovery after a `service-revalidation-failed` refusal. Here the restart is not refused (`Gateway: restarted and verified`), the reason is `update-recovery-pending`, and the Gateway is serving. So #203406 is not needed for this failure and is not ported.
- **Fixed with this commit alone.** The same chain with only this commit added exits 0 on both hops (row G2).

## Cherry-pick for the release line

- Base: `release/2026.11.10` at `6ea542fd97e2876aa4c871ccc494ed5419a03c5c` (refetched right before opening this PR; unchanged).
- One commit: `8e3a9a19e4201da85cf324ccfef518855898897b`, 5 files, +121/−2. No schema, config key, protocol, dependency, lockfile, retention or stored-field change.
- Applies cleanly: `git cherry-pick --no-commit 8e3a9a19e42` on a detached checkout of `origin/release/2026.11.10` succeeded with no conflicts; `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/release/2026.11.10 8e3a9a19e42` is clean.
- The production hunks in `runtime-worker-generation.ts`, the new `runtime-worker-process-generation.ts` and the test file are byte-identical to main. Two differences from main:
  - main also moved two types into `worker-cpu-types.ts` to keep `worker-cpu.ts` under its line cap. This branch's `worker-cpu.ts` stays under the cap (oxlint clean), so only the 2-line change is ported.
  - `wrapper-components.txt` gets its entry at this branch's position.
- Replaces #201740, which conflicts with this branch and carried 17 commits, including merges.
- `release/2026.11.11` at `1be6d3ddc6b918c9f095c9c468958f0d989cb1da`: `git merge-tree --write-tree` with this commit is clean. That line is 8 commits ahead of `v2026.11.10` and none of them touches these files.

## Evidence

Packs built from the release branch with `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`: 2026.11.10 is the commit under test, and 2026.11.11 is the same commit with only a local version bump (never published, same schema).

Each cell:

- Linux Docker with a real systemd user Gateway, pnpm 12.23.0 global install.
- A 512 MiB agent database under light writes (256 KiB/s) and a 250 ms `/readyz` probe.
- Plain `openclaw update --yes`, with the pack served as the npm registry inside the container.
- Cells ran one at a time.

| Row | Tested SHA | Installed (how) | Update to | Exit | Wall | Gateway outage | Afterwards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R2 u1 (first update) | base `6ea542fd97e` | published 2026.11.9 (pnpm add) | 2026.11.10, schema 38/36 → 42/40 | 0 | 136 s | 69 s | CLI and Gateway on 2026.11.10, run succeeded |
| **R2 u2** | base `6ea542fd97e` | 2026.11.10 (by `openclaw update`) | 2026.11.11, same schema | **1** `update-recovery-pending` | 119 s | 74 s | CLI and Gateway on 2026.11.11; run stuck `running`; told to run `openclaw update repair` |
| R3 (repeat + next step) | base `6ea542fd97e` | 2026.11.10 (by `openclaw update`) | 2026.11.11, same schema | **1** `update-recovery-pending` | 124 s | 79 s | `openclaw update repair` exit 0 (72 s); status still lists an unresolved recovery set |
| R1 (control) | base `6ea542fd97e` | 2026.11.10 (pnpm add) | 2026.11.11, same schema | 0 | 124 s | 84 s | CLI and Gateway on 2026.11.11, run succeeded |
| G2 u1 (first update) | head `8e3a9a19e42` | published 2026.11.9 (pnpm add) | 2026.11.10, schema 38/36 → 42/40 | 0 | 128 s | 65 s | CLI and Gateway on 2026.11.10, run succeeded |
| **G2 u2** | head `8e3a9a19e42` | 2026.11.10 (by `openclaw update`) | 2026.11.11, same schema | **0** | 131 s | 69 s | CLI and Gateway on 2026.11.11, run succeeded, no recovery set or warning in `update status` |
| G1 (control) | head `8e3a9a19e42` | 2026.11.10 (pnpm add) | 2026.11.11, same schema | 0 | 109 s | 72 s | CLI and Gateway on 2026.11.11, run succeeded |

Red, unmodified `release/2026.11.10` (`6ea542fd97e`), 2026.11.9 → 2026.11.10 → 2026.11.11:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71fe0e10-a32d-4484-ac48-893f7a3f9e57

Green, this commit (`8e3a9a19e42`), same chain and fixture:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2002a27a-76b1-4233-bc4f-c820374fecc1

The recordings replay the recorded cell logs and facts; they are not live captures.

<details><summary>Decisive raw lines, red R2 u2 (base)</summary>

```
⚠️ OpenClaw update failed: update-recovery-pending.
Failed: update — Exit code: unknown; Update 14b6386b-f68f-4c2e-8dbd-0cdb9e27e79f has unfinished recovery; reconcile it before starting another update.
First failure: plugin lifecycle lease core:plugin-lifecycle/global was lost; retry the operation | OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_LOST | Cannot find module [redacted-path]
Run `openclaw update repair` to finish this recovery.
```

`openclaw update status` afterwards:

```
│ Update   │ needs attention · see run details below │
Abandoned update detected; the Gateway will reconcile its recorded outcome. Stop the Gateway first (openclaw gateway stop --force), then run openclaw update repair to reconcile it now.
Recorded verification: service running (2026.11.11); version verified; channels ready; HTTP ready; core ready.
Update recovery set 14b6386b-…: ambiguous
Next action: openclaw update cleanup --dry-run
```

R3, after `openclaw update repair` (exit 0) and another `openclaw update --yes` (already-current):

```
Update recovery set …/manifest.json: unresolved after a failed update. Retained original state requires manual inspection. …
```

Gateway processes in the two layouts (R1 passes, R2 fails):

```
R1: node … ~/um/pnpm-home/store/v11/links/@/openclaw/2026.11.10/<hash>/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway
R2: node … ~/um/pnpm-home/global/v11/<group>/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway
```

</details>

<details><summary>Decisive raw lines, green G2 u2 (head)</summary>

```
Update target: 2026.11.11
Update safety checks ran in the candidate updater (2026.11.11).
Phases: requested (14.21s) → staging (12ms) → validating (21.86s) → activating (60.06s) → restarting (3.35s) → verifying (27.96s)
Recorded verification: service running (2026.11.11); version verified; channels ready; HTTP ready; core ready.
Gateway downtime: 69.15s.
```

`openclaw --version` → `OpenClaw 2026.11.11 (8e3a9a1)`; last run `succeeded`, 2026.11.10 → 2026.11.11; no `Cannot find module` in the update output.

</details>

Reproduce:

1. Pack `release/2026.11.10` (`node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`). Then bump every `package.json` version to an unused version with the same schema, add its `CHANGELOG/<version>.md`, and pack again.

The first fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for the removed installed worker, the second with `expected '/installed/other.mjs' to be '/installed/other.mjs.retained.mjs'`.

Those nits: it checks the resolver rather than a spawn, and its call-count assertion duplicates the identity check.

prs.title: fix: keep Browser panel previews and addresses current
prs.body:
Closes #205601

## What Problem This Solves

The chat Browser panel reports a load failure for working Lightpanda sessions, can keep the old address after agent navigation, and can keep a low-resolution frame enlarged after Chromium viewport resizing.

## User Impact

Lightpanda explains that it has no visual preview, while its tab address and the agent's browsing remain usable. The address catches up when focus leaves the toolbar. A successful managed-browser viewport resize refreshes the live stream even if the page does not repaint on its own.

No settings, migrations, or engine changes are required. Existing-session, attached, and remote browsers keep their current no-auto-resize policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel now recognizes the existing structured unsupported-capability response rather than treating a deliberate engine limit as a failed browser. It reuses the current tab metadata when no screenshot exists, reconciles an address whose update was held while editing, and invalidates the stream through its existing debounced resize lifecycle after a successful viewport fit. Annotation and inspection still pin their captures.

Intent checked: Lightpanda's no-screenshot contract is deliberate (#154508), as is protecting address edits while focus moves to Go (#176564). Live streaming (#141031) and shared-window preservation (#172655) are retained; the fix addresses missed UI reconciliation, not those policies.

## Evidence

I ran the three new regressions with production files restored to main `2407c717932356ac345258ebc2da67889f80623c`, then restored the fix. The current published head is `feabaaf3c5bf4ef69da81e4c9f0be2f6b2a0e0e7`:

| Regression | Main | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `keeps a screenshot-free browser usable without reporting a load failure` | False load error instead of capability explanation | Pass; no repeated unsupported captures, address updates, visual profile still works |
| `catches up the address after agent navigation while the address field had focus` | Expected second URL, received first URL | Pass |
| `refreshes a switched tab's frame after viewport resize without an unsolicited repaint` | No fresh capture after successful viewport fit | Pass |

```text
Main + new tests: 3 failed, 52 skipped; 1.22 s
Fixed focused run: 7 files passed, 153 tests passed; 2.43 s
```

The new tests are in `browser-panel-route.test.ts` and `browser-panel-stream.test.ts`. Focused checks also cover the browser client, toolbar, native-browser flow, viewport policy, and controller recovery. UI production typecheck, UI-component test typecheck, formatting, localization verification, and the Control UI ownership checks pass. The [exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45723360564) succeeded: 31 jobs passed and 27 were skipped. Per-test CI timing was not collected.

Lint has one inherited failure: `browser-panel-owner.ts` exceeds the 700-line limit on main (710 counted lines) and on this head (706). I reproduced it once on main. The existing line-growth commit guard passes because the file shrank. No rule was weakened and no unrelated extraction was added.

Local autoreview was attempted for P0-P2 but could not start its required read-only sandbox. No independent-review verdict is claimed.

The pr-simplify pass kept the existing owners, shared structured-error decoding, removed duplicate address selection from the panel owner, and dropped a viewport probe that already passed on main. Net change: +54 production lines and +117 test lines, with no new modules.

### Runtime proof on the final head

[Redacted trace excerpt and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205605#issuecomment-7178216659) from two isolated test gateways compare **main `04b854b` with PR `feabaaf3c5bf4ef69da81e4c9f0be2f6b2a0e0e7`**.

- Lightpanda 1.0.2: trusted Enter kept `/tools/browser/setup/` visible throughout a 1,163 ms navigation with a 1,000 ms fixture response delay. Its 11 in-flight animation-frame samples and 18 toolbar timer samples showed only the typed destination.
- Trusted Reload requested the same destination and completed in 1,160 ms; 23 in-flight frame samples and 19 timer samples again showed only that path. Independent gateway tab reads confirmed the destination after Enter and Reload.
- The trace reports 131 post-Enter frame samples and no other observed address. Main also retained the typed address during loading, but had no toolbar Reload; its error-panel Refresh retried only the preview.
- The Lightpanda no-preview message, destination address after returning focus to chat, and full-resolution 633×1231 Chromium frame all passed. Main enlarged a 396×771 frame.
- Typed Go, annotation, and inspection passed on both builds in the supplied run. The report records that both test gateways were removed and their ports were closed.

The persistent 16:9 frame / black lower half **did not reproduce on main or the PR** with headless Chromium 156 or windowed Chrome 158. It is not an end-to-end reproduced or verified fix claim. The supplied screenshots were inspected and their public inline uploads checked against the originals; these runtime observations came from the supplied test run, not a new independent execution here.

### Typed-address regression proof

I reproduced ClawSweeper's stale-final-address P2 on `b502d49` and fixed its screenshot-free navigation reconciliation in `8e679fb`. The subsequent real runtime check on `8e679fb` confirmed the final address and Reload destination, plus the Lightpanda preview message, address after agent navigation, sharp Chromium resize, typed Go, and annotation/inspection pinning.

That run also found a loading-state regression: during a one-second Lightpanda navigation to `/tools/browser/setup/`, the prior `/profiles/` address flashed for about 1.3 seconds. Main kept the submitted address visible. This head leaves the submitted address alone while the existing navigation-loading state is active; ordinary focus-exit reconciliation still runs when idle.

The extended regression fails on `8e679fb` immediately after Enter: expected `https://example.test/typed`, received `https://example.test/article`. With the fix, it verifies the submitted address immediately after blur and throughout a blocked one-second response, then checks completion and Reload separately. All 153 focused tests, UI production/test typechecks, touched-file lint, formatting, and the UI ownership checks pass. The pr-simplify pass kept the fix to the existing loading state and strengthened the existing regression without adding another owner or test scaffold.

The published head has the same tree as tested commit `0cf8a7a7723c19278be4735b2f6b9c239f15a249`. The supplied final-head runtime trace and screenshots above now cover the loading interval, settled destination, and Reload on `feabaaf` against main `04b854b`.

## Contributor credit

Dan Riccio reported the failures and specified the verification scope.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-browser-side-panel-bugs-s1fb9f981)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: fix(signal): preserve trailing spaces in inline code
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal messages could lose the final space in an inline-code table cell when the cell ended a message or a chunk. For example, Markdown parses `` `  go  ` `` as four characters, including a space on each side of `go`. The outgoing Signal message contained only the first three. A cell containing only spaces could lose its entire monospace range.

## User Impact

Signal preserves the full inline-code text and its monospace range, including after a link expands to show its destination. Ordinary prose and fenced-code framing keep their existing trimming behavior.

When a long code cell consists entirely of spaces, Signal skips any standalone blank packet and delivers the following row. Each physical send gets its own receipt. The first eligible send consumes a single-use reply target.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal formatter knows which characters belong to inline code before it expands links. It uses that boundary to trim trailing formatting whitespace and then renders the text and UTF-16 style ranges together. This also covers a code cell at the end of one chunk when the next row goes in another.

## Evidence

- Replayed the failing case at seed `63203:4` and 10,000 distinct generated cases. All passed.
- Captured the normal outbound sender's synthetic Signal RPC requests. The terminal monospace range changed from three to four UTF-16 units. All 12 sender cases and 20 chunk-limit controls passed, including all-space cells, emoji, link expansion, and a following row.
- Checked prose, fences, and code-table and off-table modes. The repository formatter, staged diff checks, and the targeted `no-param-reassign` lint rule passed.
- Replayed eight mixed-message cases through the formatted sender and captured Signal RPC requests. At a 20-character limit, six blank slices were skipped, all four nonblank packets arrived in order, and the sender produced four matching receipts. Checked both first-only and repeated quotes.
- Four whole-input controls matched the frozen sender. An empty input sends nothing, ordinary spaces retain the text-or-media error, and wholly blank inline code falls back to one packet with its authored spelling.
- Hosted Bun/Vitest passed 34 Signal core cases and 24 format cases, including the following row, physical reply packet and whole-message fallback controls. [Signal suites](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45628406083/job/139255884879) · [Protected CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45628406083) The sender proof used an offline RPC capture. Live Signal delivery remains unverified.

prs.title: fix(protocol): carry provider-issued tool-call IDs longer than the identifier budget
prs.body:
Fixes #203099

## What Problem This Solves

Worker inference stream frames and transcript commits rejected provider-issued tool-call IDs longer than 256 characters because those IDs inherited the internal worker identifier budget. Compatible providers emit opaque IDs that can exceed it — a GitHub Copilot diagnostic run produced a 458-character ID, the frame check returned null, and the run silently fell back to a different model.

## Why This Change Was Made

Provider-issued tool-call IDs are opaque upstream strings, unlike internal session/run/turn identifiers: `toolcall_start` stream-frame ids, transcript `toolCall` ids, and their matching `toolResult` references now travel with the payload budget (the same shape that long provider response IDs required in #170461), while internal identifiers and `toolName` keep the identifier budget. A provider ID larger than the frame payload budget is still rejected, and the generated protocol predicates were regenerated to match.

## User Impact

Worker-backed sessions keep tool calls from providers that mint long opaque tool-call IDs (GitHub Copilot observed at 458 characters) instead of dropping the call and falling back to another model. Existing short IDs remain valid; no wire-format or migration change is required.

## Evidence

Rebased onto upstream `main` at `3ee8fc5376` (head `b3b0815eca`, Node 26.12.1, Linux). The only rebase conflict was the generated `protocol.generated/predicates.js`; it was regenerated from the schemas with `pnpm gateway:validators:gen` and `--check` reports no drift.

Red/green at the shipped validation boundary. The reporter's own frame sequence, run through the real `validateWorkerInferenceEventFrame` validator:

| Phase | Build | 256-char id | 257-char id | 458-char id |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RED | upstream main (unpatched) | true | **false** | **false** |
| GREEN | this branch | true | true | true |

Unit regression (`pnpm exec vitest run packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-admission.test.ts`, 21/21 pass at head `b3b0815eca`): "carries provider-issued tool-call IDs longer than the identifier budget" fails on the unpatched schemas (the 458-char stream frame, the transcript toolCall content part, and the matching toolResult reference are all rejected) and passes with the fix, including the payload-budget rejection and whitespace-pattern rejections. `test-lines` ratchet: net +120, allocation credit 120 via `config/test-lines-allocations/203099-worker-toolcall-id-length.txt`.

Gap: the end-to-end Copilot turn (real provider minting the long ID) was not reproduced here — no Copilot credentials on this host; the reporter's shipped-dist observation and the validator-level red/green above cover the changed boundary.

prs.title: fix(subagents): notify the parent agent when Stop cancels sub-agents
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a person presses Stop in the Control UI (or the macOS app that hosts it) while the agent itself is idle but its sub-agents are still working, the app sends a session-wide `sessions.abort`. That Stop also cancels every running sub-agent of the session, which is the documented behavior. But canceled children never deliver a completion, and nothing else tells the parent agent what happened, so the agent keeps waiting for results that will never come, or later sees only bare process-exit failures. An orchestrator running several long sub-agents loses hours of work with no trace of why.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stop keeps its current meaning; the defect is the silence. Every explicit Stop that cancels sub-agents now queues one system notice for the parent session. It names the canceled sub-agents, says the Stop was deliberate and what kind it was, and tells the agent not to restart the work unless the user asks:

> An explicit session Stop from a connected app canceled 2 running sub-agents: slow-a, slow-b. They won't report back. Check their sessions before relying on any partial work, and don't restart them unless the user asks.

For a single sub-agent the sentence is singular ("It won't report back. Check its session…"). Empty labels are skipped, and names beyond the first ten are counted ("slow-a and 2 more").

- New `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-stop-notice.ts` builds the notice and enqueues it through the existing system-event owner (`enqueueSystemEvent`). Zero kills queue nothing; labels are normalized, empty ones dropped, and at most 10 are named.
- The Gateway cancellation owner, `abortControlledSubagents`, calls it once per request after the cascade settles, when the caller passes an explicit `stopSource`: session-wide `sessions.abort` (`client-session`, "An explicit session Stop from a connected app"), exact-run `chat.abort` / `sessions.abort` (`client-run`, "An explicit Stop of your turn"). An exact-run `sessions.abort` either stops an embedded run directly or forwards to the `chat.abort` handler; both paths pass `client-run`. A session-wide `sessions.abort` that lands on an active embedded run takes the same turn-scoped path, so its notice reads as a Stop of that turn.
- Chat `/stop` (`stopSubagentsForRequester`) uses the same helper (`channel-user`, "A user /stop command"). It already replied "Stopped N sub-agents" to the person; now the agent learns it too.
- The notice is a queued system event: it doesn't start a turn and doesn't touch the stable prompt prefix; the parent's next turn reads it.
- Docs: `docs/tools/subagents/operations.md` ("Stopping").

No protocol, schema or config change. Which sub-agents a Stop selects is unchanged.

## User Impact

After an explicit Stop, the parent agent's next turn says which sub-agents were canceled and by what kind of Stop, so it stops waiting for them, can inspect their sessions, and does not restart work a person just stopped. Non-explicit cancellations (shutdown, timeouts) are unchanged.

Not in this PR: whether the Control UI should offer a session-wide Stop (or map Escape to it) when only sub-agents are running. That is a product decision and is left for a follow-up.

## Evidence

- Regression test: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.abort-cascade.test.ts` "tells the requester's next turn which children a session/exact run Stop canceled" — red on the base, green with the fix. `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-stop-notice.test.ts` covers the singular sentence, an empty label, one name with more remaining, and two names with more remaining.
- Consumer tests: all `chat.abort*`, `sessions.abort*`, `agent.abort*` suites in `src/gateway/server-methods` plus `subagent-control.test.ts` and the auto-reply abort tests pass (32 files on the final head). oxlint and oxfmt clean on touched files; `git diff --check` clean.
- End to end, isolated Gateway (own state and port), real agent on a real model (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol` through the Codex runtime): the parent spawns two sub-agents that run `sleep 900`, ends its turn, then the script sends exactly what the Control UI Stop sends when no local run id is known: `sessions.abort {key, clearQueued: true, userInitiated: true}`. Both runs: the sub-agents are killed and their processes are gone. Then the parent is asked whether its sub-agents are still running.
  - Base: "There is no system notice about their running status in this turn."
  - Fix: quoted the notice verbatim and answered that they were canceled.
  - This run used the earlier notice wording (it said "cancelled" and suggested spawning replacements). The wording was revised after review and was not rerun end to end; the unit and Gateway tests above cover the final text.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex) on the committed branch range against `origin/main`, P0 and P2 thresholds: no findings (the reviewer saw the diff only). I checked by hand that the two `sessions.abort` branches are exclusive, so one request queues one notice.

prs.title: fix: show which step and path failed when the Mac app cannot start its Gateway
prs.body:
Part of #203785
Part of #203737
Part of #198902

## What Problem This Solves

If the macOS app fails to start its local Gateway, a bare “Permission denied” message does not tell you which operation failed or which file or folder to check. This draft improves the diagnostic; it does not fix the underlying permission problem in #198902.

## User Impact

The app status and in-app log identify the failing startup stage. If Gateway log setup fails before Bun starts, they name the actual folder or log file. Compound failures identify the stage without guessing at a path. The full diagnostic is private in macOS unified logging.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup now distinguishes failure to prepare or open the log from failure to launch the process. An unwritable Gateway log file cannot carry the error; the in-app log and status can.

## Evidence

The supplied candidate compiled on the pinned base, before the pre-push review fixes. On the revised staged tree `4902df24d161`, whitespace checks, `pnpm native:i18n:verify` and strict source review passed; bound Auto Review was scoped-clean through P3. The manager regressions distinguish log-folder and log-file failures from a launch failure.

**Draft hold:** the exact-head native build, SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, `GatewayProcessManagerTests` and `GatewayChildSupervisorTests` have not run. On a disposable non-root macOS runner, deny a test log target and verify that app status and the in-app log show the actual stage and path. No real-app capture has been made.

Contributed by @TheAngryPit.

prs.title: fix: show the correct hour for Activity peaks across half-hour clock changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Last 24 hours Activity chart could label a session one hour early across a half-hour daylight-saving change. On Lord Howe Island, a spring peak at 3 AM appeared as 2 AM in both the bar tooltip and the accessible chart summary.

## User Impact

Hourly bar tooltips, axis labels, and the peak announced to screen readers use the start of the bucket that counted the sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway returns the first requested bucket boundary. On transition days it can fall at half past the hour in local time. The chart now starts there and advances by elapsed hours. Daily and monthly labels still follow the local calendar.

## Evidence

- On the parent, mounted Chromium showed 2 AM for the 3 AM spring peak and 1 AM for the 2 AM fall peak on Lord Howe. Both the hovered tooltip and the accessible summary reproduced the error.
- All eight Activity polish Chromium cases passed on the fix, including both Lord Howe transitions, both New York transitions, Kathmandu, UTC, and the existing desktop and narrow layouts. The tests used the compiled Activity page and a mock Gateway response.
- Formatting and scoped type-aware lint passed on both changed files.
- The [signed Chromium job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45727893024/job/139603277632) passed all eight cases. The [test type check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45727893024/job/139604527156) also passed. The hovered peak and accessible summary were checked in the compiled UI with a mock Gateway. Shipped-app before/after images were not captured.

Technical details The publish sync matches overlay entries by shared page paths; a nested match must also be unique. Each new entry therefore carries the full direct page list of its English group with the `zh-CN/` prefix, and is appended inside the existing parent entry's `pages` array. Existing labels are not displaced: matching is first-come-first-served, and the new entries only fill groups that had no label. This PR does not touch the eight top-level groups covered by #176304 (those are on other tabs) and does not modify any other tab, so the two changes do not overlap. This tab now uses `智能体` (`智能体协作`, `子智能体`, `ACP 智能体`), matching the published zh-CN pages. The rest of the sidebar still uses the legacy `代理` spelling; aligning every tab is a separate change. prs.title: fix: keep the Linux browser panel aligned at larger text sizes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Linux, increasing the system text scale can make the embedded browser shrink and spill over the chat beside it. For example, with GNOME text scaling at 125% and the monitor scale at 100%, a 360 × 220 CSS-pixel browser slot gives the child view a 288 × 176 CSS-pixel viewport.

## User Impact

The browser stays inside its panel when opened or resized at a larger text size. Users can keep their system text-size preference.

## Why This Change Was Made

WebKitGTK applies text scaling to the dashboard's CSS coordinates. GTK places the child webview in logical window coordinates. The Linux desktop bridge includes the dashboard's `window.devicePixelRatio` with each presentation so the native host can multiply the rectangle by `devicePixelRatio / window.scale_factor()` before passing it to the existing layout. The conversion cancels the monitor scale and retains WebKit's effective page scale.

## Evidence

Ubuntu 26.04.1 VM, GNOME Wayland and WebKitGTK 2.52.6. Both captures use the real Linux companion and native browser view with the same synthetic dashboard, viewport, and 125% text scale. Before is `b48d578d0237`. After is `854fc4348549`.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The native browser overlaps the upper-left edge and leaves part of its blue panel empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cab10090-3ca5-439b-9792-4ccb26d2a03a) | ![The native browser lines up with the blue panel and fills its width and height](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/562a2d4d-ff3e-413f-aa30-9a2a2cc82375) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The red outline marks the misplaced browser and the blue outline marks its intended slot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c84c5444-afb9-4d9c-85b6-a32ba7cd4baf) | ![The green outline shows the browser and its panel sharing the same bounds](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bfa944e-f72f-4d38-ab6c-f4b4b1092061) |

### Native red/green regression at 125%

I reran the same viewport assertion with both Linux binaries in the GNOME Wayland VM. The fixture opens a real native browser view using a synthetic Gateway, measures its viewport at two panel widths, and maximizes and restores the window between measurements. It asserts that the child viewport matches the slot at both widths.

| Binary | Child at a 360 × 220 CSS px slot | Child at a 408 × 220 CSS px slot | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base `b48d578d0237` | 288 × 176 | 326 × 176 | Failed the viewport assertion, exit 1 |
| Patched `854fc4348549` | 360 × 220 | 408 × 220 | Passed both size assertions, exit 0 |

### Other checks

- At 100%, the candidate matched both slot sizes. The regression test covers the conversion with monitor scales of 1× and 2×.
- The native build, Rust formatting check, six focused Rust browser tests, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The X11 smoke test reached the expected child viewport and timed out waiting for a pointer click on both builds in this VM.
- The sample text matched pixel for pixel after maximizing and restoring both builds. Hardware-specific text blur remains unverified. [Related report in Wry](https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/issues/1727)


- The official GitHub workflows for this head are awaiting approval from a maintainer. [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45725734580) · [Linux App run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45725734374)

prs.title: fix: keep WebChat approvals from interrupting waiting turns
prs.body:
Closes #205610
Related: #194034

## What Problem This Solves

Typing `/approve <id> allow-once` in WebChat can run the approved command but fail the waiting turn with `SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite`. The typed approval and its confirmation also enter the next model context because WebChat records a second, unmarked copy.

## User Impact

New fast approval exchanges remain visible in history without interrupting the waiting turn or entering the agent's conversational context. Approval authorization, command execution, and transcript conflict checks are unchanged. Existing history is not rewritten; there is no migration or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fast approval dispatch now carries the existing context-free command classification on both the delivered reply and the shared transcript mirror. WebChat's existing finalizer then applies that classification to its own user and assistant records. The shared mirror retains it for direct and routed delivery.

This fixes the producer rather than suppressing SQLite errors or retrying the approved command. The fast path was introduced by `2987571782893d3c9568852861ab579739a07fea` to release waiting turns. #169026 added shared transcript capture, #152512 established the context-free status contract, and #201271 explicitly left WebChat's separate recorder out of its shared-command fix. #194034 covers only the shared-mirror part of this defect.

## Evidence

The regression uses the real WebChat handler, shared dispatcher, SQLite transcript writers, visible-history reader, and SessionManager. That regression stubs the external approval-resolution RPC. The separate live WebSocket proof below exercises approval and a real command.

| Check | Main `ac9a0c6ab463c6f698203877ade316793c299601` | This change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Next model context after a typed approval | Includes approval and confirmation | Unchanged from before approval |
| Original assistant append after confirmation, while its operation is still running | Rejects with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` | Commits successfully |
| Approval confirmation and visible history | Present | Still present |

- The exact final regression fails both behavioral assertions with main production restored, and passes with the fix.
- 147 focused tests across 9 files passed, covering the regression, approval authorization, fast dispatch, command lifecycle/history, transcript ancestry, and tool-prefix stability. The final typed regression was rerun separately: 3.719 seconds test time, 47.26 seconds command wall time including worker preparation. After the valid review cleanup, the regression passed again in 5.892 seconds test time / 61.20 seconds command wall time; targeted lint, formatting, and diff checks also passed. Production source is unchanged from the live-tested head.
- Core and Gateway-methods test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local ClawSweeper was unavailable from a clean configured checkout. Autoreview was attempted on the complete candidate against main at P0-P2, but the installed Codex CLI failed its read-only sandbox preflight before review started. No independent local review result is claimed, and no sandbox permissions were broadened. [Hosted ClawSweeper review of `68ef3fa3`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205613#issuecomment-7177624925) found no production defect. Its valid test-cleanup suggestion was applied by deleting only the unrelated warning-silence assertion. A fresh review will assess the new evidence and head.
- `pr-simplify`: reused the existing recording owners and replaced raw test-history scanning with the existing typed visible-history reader. No new storage, retry, or error-suppression machinery. Delta against main: +9 net production lines, +112 regression-test lines, and a documentation clarification.

### Supplied live WebChat proof

[Redacted inline trace and analysis](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205613#issuecomment-7178168502), supplied from a separate machine: fresh local Gateways, authenticated WebChat WebSockets, a scripted local model, and a real shell command. These are supplied observations, not a live run performed by this agent.

| Observation | Main `b48d578d023765ac86fe44d38d65cfac991ad03c` | Live-tested PR `68ef3fa3dd5ed2db9ff8ee586f263f8b0fa5cee0` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Marker before / after approval | Absent / present | Absent / present; command exit 0 |
| Original turn | SQLite transcript conflict, error | `WEBCHAT_TURN_FINISHED`, `agent.wait=ok`, delivered |
| Approval in tool-result continuation POST | Not reached | Typed text / confirmation / ID: 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Approval in next user-turn POST | Typed text / confirmation / ID: 2 / 1 / 3 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Visible approval history | Present, unmarked | Present, both recorder pairs context-free |

The counts scan complete provider HTTP JSON bodies before redaction. Head `7c6cd3fefa06c37a3941862d985de8e7fcc8670e` changes only a test assertion and documentation relative to the live-tested head; production source is identical. The runner reported closed test listeners and removal of temporary builds, state, and raw logs. No VMs were used.

### Activity recap scope

The separate Activity recap request still contains the exchange on both builds: typed text / confirmation / ID counts are 1 / 1 / 2 before and 2 / 2 / 4 after. This PR does **not** claim that approval text never reaches any model.

Recaps are a separate history-to-utility-model feature. [#147441](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147441) introduced chronological transcript recaps; [#147901](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147901) deliberately selected user/assistant conversation text instead of tool noise. The [source reader](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/68ef3fa3dd5ed2db9ff8ee586f263f8b0fa5cee0/src/gateway/session-activity-summary-source.ts#L25-L49) and [utility-model documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/68ef3fa3dd5ed2db9ff8ee586f263f8b0fa5cee0/docs/gateway/config-agents/models.md#L69) use transcript excerpts, not the agent's filtered conversational context. Since approval exchanges intentionally stay in history, suppressing them from recap prompts would change that separate input policy. Recap selection is left unchanged and explicitly outside this fix; the docs now name conversational context precisely.

Not verified: browser UI, a real external model provider, or Signal. The current-head CI and requested re-review are separate from the supplied live proof.

Reported by Dan Riccio.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-webchat-approve-turn-failure-s447a6d66)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resetting a chat while a Markdown table is expanded removes the message, but the old table can stay open over the replacement conversation and keep keyboard focus.

## User Impact

Resetting the chat dismisses its old table. Appending a message keeps the table open. Escape and Close still return focus to the button that opened a table when that button is present.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript already tracks table removals. It now remembers which source table owns the expanded view and checks whether that table is still in the transcript after each batch of DOM changes. This preserves the dialog when the same table moves during an update. The existing pane cleanup continues to handle switching chats. [Earlier pane-lifecycle fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/136433)

## Evidence

- Reproduced in Chromium with the mounted Control UI and a synthetic Gateway. After a same-chat reset, the source row and button disappeared while the old modal kept focus. The bundled regression found one expanded dialog when it expected zero.
- With the fix, the old dialog closed, a replacement table opened, and Escape returned focus to the replacement button. Append and a remove-and-reinsert of the same row preserved the original dialog and its focus.
- The bundled chat copy suite passed all four cases. The two Markdown table suites passed all 17 cases. The final regression also passed after a lint-only fixture change. Scoped formatting and lint passed.

The signed revision also passed the same-chat reset regression in the [hosted Chromium bundle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45724945583/job/139593086807) and [protected PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45725048961). prs.title: fix(gateway): isolate a throwing artifact grant release during cleanup
prs.body:
Closes #204594

## What Problem This Solves

`removeDownload()` deletes a download ticket and then calls the owner's `release()` unprotected. A single throwing release aborted the entire cleanup sweep: the remaining artifact-download grants on the connection kept their `read`, `assertCurrent`, and `release` closures (leaked), the client's grant bucket survived in the `downloads` map, and the failure escaped connection-abort listeners, expiry sweeps, and Gateway teardown as an uncaught exception (crash risk).

## Fix

The ticket is deregistered before `release()` runs, so a failure at that boundary is not recoverable and leaves no caller able to retry it. `removeDownload()` now catches a throwing release: cleanup continues for the remaining tickets on the connection, the client's bucket is removed, and no exception escapes the sweep. The failure is also recorded through the Gateway warning channel (`gateway: artifact download grant release failed during cleanup: ...`) so shutdown callers can see that a connection's session resources were not fully disposed.

## Evidence

### Direct-module probe (pre-fix vs post-fix)

Driving the production grant module directly via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`, pre-fix (unmodified main) with two grants on one client and the first release throwing on connection abort:

- uncaught exception escaped: `release boom (first grant)`
- release calls observed: `["first"]` (second grant never released)
- client bucket: still present in the `downloads` map (`resolveArtifactDownloadGrant` still resolved both tickets)

Post-fix (same sequence):

- uncaught exceptions: none
- release calls observed: `["first", "second"]`
- client bucket: gone (`resolveArtifactDownloadGrant` resolves neither ticket)

### Gateway-path regression (committed)

`sessions-files.host-read.test.ts` now exercises the real Gateway request path: two session-file download grants are created through the actual RPC handler (`sessionsFilesHandlers` → `respondSessionFileDownload` → `createArtifactDownload`) with the real composite release owner (repository dispose + host-read release via the placement owner + retained session-read release). The first grant's placement owner throws during disconnect; the test asserts on the real HTTP download adapter that cleanup still retires **both** tickets (404 on both URLs), the sibling grant's release ran (`[1, 2]`), and exactly one Gateway warning was recorded naming the failed owner.

The vitest suite could not run to completion on this constrained environment (OOM, exit 137 on the compile subprocess), so CI remains the authoritative run for the committed regression; the direct-module probe above was executed locally at head `9be407288c` and the fix carries no behavioral change beyond isolation and recording.

## Notes for reviewers

- The ticket is deleted before `release()` (pre-existing order), so marking the failure retryable would leave a deregistered ticket with no sweeper; catching at the boundary is the smallest correct isolation.
- `grant.retired = true` is set before the release attempt, so a throwing release cannot leave a grant that both stays live and re-releases later through `retainArtifactDownloadStream().release()`.
- The main `CI` workflow on this head is in `action_required` (fork approval was invalidated when `main` landed a `ci.yml` change in #204635); it needs a maintainer approval to run, same as PR #201086.

prs.title: fix: recover saved replies when a session update finishes a chat run
prs.body:
Closes #205582

## What Problem This Solves

A chat can stop showing its working indicator while its saved assistant reply is still missing. When a terminal session update settles the exact local run before its final chat event, the page clears run state without reading the updated transcript. Later recovery then sees no active run and does nothing.

This path is reproduced on main `d290bbe6be8e2` in focused tests and main `2407c71` through the real Control UI in Safari with controlled delivery. The relay lets the terminal row reach Safari before held live reply events: main stays empty for 3,543 ms; the tested production code recovers READY at 116 ms. Ordinary delivery did not reproduce the original intermittent five-second report.

## User Impact

The page immediately requests the saved transcript when a session update settles its active run. Existing exact-run matching, queue release, stale-read rejection, and hidden-pane branch deferral remain in place. No settings, schema changes, migrations, new timers, or artificial delay of the run indicator.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep terminal settlement in the existing lifecycle owner, and pair it with the existing history loader at the page boundary shared by session publications and direct session events. Recovery is triggered only when a locally active run was actually settled, so repeated terminal publications do not add reads.

The original settlement behavior came from #126180 (`a77fbdef3306f`) to unblock queued follow-ups after a missed terminal event. This preserves that intended behavior and restores the omitted saved-reply recovery. Adjacent #203938 repairs returning to retained chats; it is already on main and does not repair this active-run settlement path.

The pr-simplify pass retained one shared recovery boundary and removed an unnecessary presentation callback. The review follow-up also removes one assertion on an incidental in-flight loader phase, preserving the conditional await and all saved-reply, run-clearing and request-budget checks. Against main: production +24/-8 lines, tests +70/-25 lines. No new recovery state or timer machinery.

## Evidence

- Baseline proof with the recovery regression tests: **2 expected failures, 2 passes**. Both shared-row publication and direct `sessions.changed` delivery clear the active run but issue **0** history reads instead of **1**.
- Production-fix validation at `f3381b8`: **113 focused tests passed** across pane recovery, terminal recovery, page state, and lazy live-event ordering. The new cases verify the saved reply appears, stream/run state clears, and repeated settlement adds no history request. Combined wall time: **6.54 seconds**.

prs.title: fix(doctor): pass synthetic agentSessionKey to include session-gated tools in schema inspection
prs.body:
Closes #205370

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor's **Runtime tool schemas** check falsely warns that `ask_user` is an unknown `tools.allow` entry, even when a Discord session correctly offers it (`questionInputMode: "buttons"` in `extensions/discord/src/channel.ts`).

**Reproduction:**
1. Configure a finite `tools.allow` that includes `"ask_user"` and a Discord channel.
2. Run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`.
3. Observe: `[tools] tools.allow allowlist contains unknown entries (ask_user). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.`

This happens on every doctor run (every Docker boot), which may cause operators to drop a working tool from their allowlist.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause:** `collectAgentRuntimeToolSchemaFindings` in `src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-projection.ts` calls `createOpenClawCodingTools` **without a `sessionKey`**. The session-gating predicate `shouldIncludePrimarySessionToolForOpenClawTools` in `src/agents/openclaw-tools.registration.ts:184` requires a non-empty `sessionKey` to include `ask_user`. Without it, `ask_user` is never added to the doctor's projected tool inventory, so the unknown-entry check fires.

**Fix:** Pass a synthetic `sessionKey` (`doctor-tool-schema-inspection-<agentId>`) when doctor builds the tool inventory. This makes the inspection session look like a real primary session, so session-gated tools are included in the projection and the false warning disappears.

**Why this is safe:**
- The synthetic key is only used for schema projection (read-only inventory), never for execution.
- `isPrimaryBootstrapRun` returns `true` for non-subagent/non-ACP keys, which is the intended classification for doctor's inspection context.
- No behavior change for real agent runs; this only affects doctor's diagnostic inventory.

**Note:** `assembleOpenClawCodingTools` reads `sessionKey`, not `agentSessionKey`. The first version of this fix used `agentSessionKey` and did not eliminate the warning; the correct parameter is `sessionKey`.

## User Impact

- **Before:** Every doctor run falsely warns that `ask_user` is unknown, eroding trust in the warning and tempting users to remove a valid tool from `tools.allow`.
- **After:** Doctor correctly recognizes `ask_user` as a valid entry when the channel supports it (e.g., Discord with `questionInputMode: "buttons"`).

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI Proof (BASE vs HEAD)

**Setup:** Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` with:
- `agents.entries.main.tools.allow: ["ask_user", "exec", "read"]`
- `channels.discord.enabled: true` (provides `questionInputMode: "buttons"`)
- Fixture model provider (`openai-completions` API)

**Command (both runs):**
```sh
openclaw doctor --lint --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --json
```

**BASE (524a56ed00d, before fix):**
```
[tools] agents.main.tools.allow allowlist contains unknown entries (ask_user). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.
```
→ **RED**: warning present (1 occurrence in stderr)

**HEAD (bcf44ed8e96, after fix):**
```
(no unknown entries warning)
```
→ **GREEN**: warning eliminated (0 occurrences in stderr)

Both runs produce identical JSON stdout (`"ok": true`, `"checksRun": 1`, `"findings": []`), confirming the warning is emitted to stderr only and does not affect the health-check verdict.

### Latest-Stable Upgrade Proof (v2026.11.10 → HEAD)

This is the exact upgrade scenario reported in #205370 (Docker / npm on official `2026.11.10`).

**Setup:** One shared `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (`/tmp/doctor-upgrade/stable/state` → copied to `head/state`) and one shared `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` with the same allowlist + Discord channel as above. The state dir is populated by the **stable** binary first, then reused unchanged by the candidate binary — settings and data are preserved across the upgrade.

**Step 1 — v2026.11.10 stable (tag `v2026.11.10` = commit `6ea542fd97e`, version `2026.11.10` in `package.json`):**

```sh
$ node dist/cli/run-main.js doctor --lint --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --json
# stderr:
[tools] agents.main.tools.allow allowlist contains unknown entries (ask_user). These entries are shipped core tools but unavailable in the current runtime/provider/model/config.
# stdout:
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":76,"findings":[],"recoveryCopies":{...}}
```
→ **RED**: warning present on the official stable release.

**Step 2 — upgrade to this PR's HEAD (dist built from `b1ff5558330`, same blob as `bcf44ed8e96` for the two touched files), same state dir, same config:**

```sh
$ node dist/cli/run-main.js doctor --lint --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --json
# stderr: (no `unknown entries` warning; only unrelated DEP_PLUGIN_SDK deprecation notices)
# stdout:
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":75,"findings":[],"recoveryCopies":{...}}
```
→ **GREEN**: warning eliminated, settings/data carried over, no config edits required.

**Delta `checksSkipped: 76 → 75`:** HEAD runs one additional internal sub-check now that the projected inventory matches the allowlist; the verdict (`ok`, `findings`) is unchanged.

### Code Path

1. `src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-projection.ts:126` — `createOpenClawCodingTools` called without `sessionKey` (before fix).
2. `src/agents/openclaw-tools.registration.ts:184-186` — `shouldIncludePrimarySessionToolForOpenClawTools` returns `false` when `sessionKey` is empty.
3. `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts:619-634` — `ask_user` is only created when the predicate passes.
4. `src/agents/agent-tools.assembly.ts:363` — `assembleOpenClawCodingTools` maps `agentSessionKey: e?.sessionKey` (reads `sessionKey`, not `agentSessionKey`).

### Unit Test

`src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-projection.test.ts` verifies that `collectAgentRuntimeToolSchemaFindings` passes the synthetic `sessionKey` and that `ask_user` is not flagged as unknown when present in `tools.allow`.

## Impact Surface

| File | Change | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-projection.ts` | +4 lines (add `sessionKey` param + comment) | Low: read-only diagnostic path |
| `src/flows/doctor-tool-schema-projection.test.ts` | +95 lines (new test) | None: test-only |

## Cleanup

No production state, credentials, or user data touched. The synthetic session key is ephemeral and never persisted. Test state directories (`/tmp/doctor-proof/{base,head}`) are isolated and removed after proof.

---

**Precedent:** N/A — first fix for this specific false-positive pattern in doctor tool schema inspection.
