prs.title: agents: let the sessions tool clear a thinking override
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent `sessions` tool could set a session thinking override with `action: "patch"` and `thinkingLevel`, but could not clear one. The reset words the rest of OpenClaw accepts (`default`, `inherit`, `inherited`, `clear`, `reset`, `unpin`) were forwarded to `sessions.patch` as level names and rejected as `invalid thinkingLevel`. `sessions.patch` only clears the override for `null`, and the tool parameter is a string, so a model had no way to send it. The same tool already clears a model override with `model: "default"`.

Closes #204998.

## Changes

- `src/agents/tools/sessions-tool-patch.ts`: `readSessionsToolPatch` maps `thinkingLevel` through `isSessionDefaultDirectiveValue` (the helper `/think` uses) and sends `null` for reset words. Explicit levels, including `off`, pass through unchanged, and unknown words are still rejected by the gateway. The single-session patch and the `targets` batch both build their patch through this function.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-tool.response.test.ts`: four cases (`default`, `inherit`, `clear`, `reset`) expecting `sessions.patch` to receive `thinkingLevel: null`, plus one case that `off` passes through unchanged.

## Evidence

Direct call of `readSessionsToolPatch` from source (`node --import tsx/esm`), same inputs on current `main` and on this branch:

| input `thinkingLevel` | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `high` | `"high"` | `"high"` |
| `off` | `"off"` | `"off"` |
| `default` | `"default"` | `null` |
| `inherit` | `"inherit"` | `null` |
| `reset` | `"reset"` | `null` |

On `main`, the string `"default"` is what reaches `sessions.patch`, which is what the issue shows being rejected.

Tests: `pnpm vitest run src/agents/tools/sessions-tool.response.test.ts` passes (9 tests, including the 5 new ones). With the one-line change reverted, the four reset-word cases fail and the `off` case passes. Repo formatter reports both touched files correctly formatted.

What was not tested: no live agent turn through the embedded runner (the issue's loopback-model run was not repeated), and `sessions.patch` itself was not exercised end to end; its `null` handling is read from the code and unchanged. `sessions-tool.test.ts` and `sessions-tool.batch.test.ts` were started but did not finish in my environment's time limit, so they were not confirmed. The full repo-wide `check:changed` was not run.

## Checklist

- [x] I understand what this code does: the tool passed the raw string to `sessions.patch`, which clears only on `null`; the change translates the shared reset words to `null` at the tool boundary, like the `model` line above it.
- [x] Local validation: the targeted vitest file passes and the formatter is clean; see the untested items above.
- [ ] Review-flow doc read; will follow up on Barnacle/ClawSweeper feedback

prs.title: models: reject --agent on fallbacks list and image-fallbacks list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`models fallbacks list` and `models image-fallbacks list` accepted the inherited `--agent` option and silently printed the global default chain, while their `add`/`remove`/`clear` siblings reject `--agent` as global-only. This routes both `list` leaves through the same global-only path.

Closes #204996.

## Changes

- `src/cli/models-cli.ts`: the fallback `list` leaf (both groups, registered in the shared loop) now runs through `withGlobalModelsRuntime(command, `${name} list`, ...)`, matching `add`/`remove`/`clear`.
- `src/cli/models-cli.runtime.ts`: `GlobalOnlyModelCommandName` fallback union extended with `"list"`.
- `src/cli/models-cli.test.ts`: two cases in the existing "rejects unsupported agent scope" table covering `fallbacks list` and `image-fallbacks list` with `--agent`, asserting rejection and that the command handler is not called.
- `docs/cli/models.md`: the global-only sentence now lists `add`, `remove`, `clear`, and `list`.

## Evidence

Isolated config: `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks = ["openai/gpt-5.4"]`, agent `ops` with its own `model.fallbacks` chain, run from source via `node --import tsx/esm src/entry.ts` with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Before (current main):
- `models --agent ops fallbacks list` → prints global `openai/gpt-5.4`, exit 0 (bug)
- `models --agent ops image-fallbacks list --json` → `{"fallbacks": []}`, exit 0 (bug)

After:
- `models --agent ops fallbacks list` → "openclaw models fallbacks list does not support --agent; it is global and never agent-scoped. ...", exit 1
- `models --agent ops image-fallbacks list --json` → `{"ok": false, "error": {"type": "cli_error", "message": "... does not support --agent ..."}}`, exit 1
- `models fallbacks list` (no flag) → still prints the global list, exit 0
- `models --agent ops fallbacks clear` → unchanged sibling rejection, exit 1

Tests: `pnpm vitest run src/cli/models-cli.test.ts src/commands/models/fallbacks-shared.test.ts` → 2 files, 48/48 passed, including the two new cases.

## Checklist

- [x] I understand what this code does: the `list` leaf previously used the plain runtime wrapper, so the inherited `--agent` was never validated; the command then read only `agents.defaults`. The change makes it take the same rejection path as its siblings.
- [x] Local validation: targeted vitest suites pass (48/48); repo formatter reports all touched files correctly formatted. The full repo-wide `check:changed` was not run (pre-commit ratchet needs git >= 2.41; this environment has 2.34)
- [ ] Review-flow doc read; will follow up on Barnacle/ClawSweeper feedback

prs.title: feat: let administrators manage roles in Settings → Team → Roles
prs.body:
Related: Participate work on `main` (#204783, #204914)

## What Problem This Solves

Administrators of a shared OpenClaw Gateway can only manage operator roles (`gateway.roles`) by editing raw config. They can't easily see what a role allows, who has it, or give one person different participant tools without hand-writing JSON. The Remote access page shows each member's role but has no way to see what it means.

## User Impact

User impact: administrators get **Settings → Team → Roles**. It lists every role with the people who have it, explains in plain language what each role allows in a person's own sessions and in sessions they're invited to, and lets them edit, create, duplicate and delete roles and assign people. Changing an existing person's role now happens only here: Remote access keeps role badges and the invite role picker, but its per-member Change role control is removed. Nothing changes for non-administrators.

## Why This Change Was Made

Roles are core Gateway config that the core Gateway enforces, so the editor is a core Settings page rather than a plugin. It uses only existing Gateway methods:
- **Reads:** `config.get` and `users.list`. The people counts come from `users.list`.
- **Saves:** one `config.patch` per change, sending the hash the page loaded. A role edit also checks that the role hasn't changed since the editor opened, so a concurrent change is reported instead of overwritten.
- **Assignments:** `users.setRole`.

Writing still requires `operator.admin`, as before. Deleting a role first moves its people (and repoints its GitHub mappings) to a role the admin picks. The default role can't be deleted. The participant tool list moves to `src/shared` so the page offers exactly the Gateway's list.

Design and placement were reviewed with Josh on a mockup before implementation. Targets `main`, which now has the Participate work (invited access, `invitedAlsoAllow`, default participant tools) this page edits.

### Lockout protection

Setting `gateway.roles.default` puts everyone without an assignment under roles, including the administrator who sets it. On a live Gateway that turned the admin into a viewer, and no role could manage roles to undo it from the UI. This branch now:
- **Adds a built-in `admin` role** (`operator.admin`, all agents), installed with the other OpenClaw ID presets (and by Doctor for existing installs) and offered under New role. It is assigned to nobody.
- **Asks who stays an administrator before roles turn on.** Choosing a default from "None" opens *Turn on roles for everyone*: the signed-in person is preselected and can't be unchecked, existing admins are kept, and others can be added. An admin role is created first if none grants `operator.admin`. Admins are assigned before the default is saved.
- **Lets `users.setRole` save an assignment before a default exists.** It grants nothing until a default turns roles on. The dialog needs this; it relaxes the refusal added in #197712.
- **Refuses role changes that would remove your own admin access.** A `config.set`/`config.patch`/`config.apply` or `users.setRole` that would leave the profile making it without `operator.admin` is rejected with a message naming the fix. Owner and shared-token connections are never under roles, so `openclaw config unset gateway.roles.default` on the Gateway host always recovers.
- **Reconnects people whose access widens.** A connection whose scopes were capped by its role reconnects when a role change would grant more, instead of keeping the narrower scopes until it reconnects on its own.
- **Explains recovery** on the "Only administrators can manage roles" screen.
- **Makes the built-in `guest` role invite-only, up to Send.** It now reads and works only in sessions people invite it to (`sessions.others: "invited"`, `maxInvitedAccess: "send"`), stays sandboxed, and keeps all agents. The New role dialog's Guest choice matches, and the separate Collaborator choice is gone because it became identical. Existing `guest` definitions are not rewritten.
- **Shows progress while saving.** Role dialogs and the role editor's Save show a spinner, and who has each role reloads after each save.

Accepted edge: an agent run acting for a person carries no profile on its connection, so the self-lockout check does not cover it; recovery from the Gateway host still works.

## Evidence

Remote access before/after for the removed controls is in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203453#issuecomment-7150190192); the Remote access rows below are from the first revision.

Mock Gateway fixtures in the real Control UI (dark, 1280×860). These screenshots predate the rebase onto `main`. Before = `origin/openclaw-2b7/participate` 5672d417181d, after = this branch c056c927e938. Same fixtures for both.

### Turning on a default role

Mock Gateway fixtures in the real Control UI (dark, 1280×860), choosing `viewer` as the default with no default set. Before = previous head db5d1fbcadc6, after = e9d1bb708a0c. Same fixtures for both.

**What was checked:**

prs.title: fix(models): clear transient cooldowns on auth refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an operator manually resolves a rate limit or capacity issue (such as replenishing provider quota or waiting out an upstream burst), the Gateway continues rejecting requests locally if an active `rate_limit` or `overloaded` cooldown window remains stored on the auth profile. The existing `models.authRefresh` control-plane write rebuilds the runtime snapshot from disk, but provides no mechanism to reset active transient cooldown windows without restarting the Gateway or waiting for the provider backoff window to expire.

## User Impact

Operators can trigger `models.authRefresh` with `clearTransientCooldowns: true` to immediately clear stored `rate_limit` and `overloaded` cooldowns and failure counters across authoritative store owners (both shared store and local agent store). Hard blocks such as `billing`, `auth_permanent`, and `subscription_limit` are strictly preserved to ensure account and credit safety. If store locking encounters contention or write unavailability, an actionable `UNAVAILABLE` error is returned rather than falsely acknowledging refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Added `clearTransientCooldowns` helper in `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage-state.ts` that clears only `cooldownFields` (`cooldownUntil`, `cooldownReason`, `cooldownClassification`, `cooldownModel`) for transient reasons (`rate_limit`, `overloaded`) and resets transient error counters while leaving `blockedFields` and `disabledFields` untouched.
- Extended `ModelsAuthRefreshParamsSchema` in `packages/gateway-protocol` with optional `clearTransientCooldowns: Type.Optional(Type.Boolean())` and regenerated protocol predicates.
- In `models.authRefresh` Gateway handler:
  1. Authoritative Health Ownership: routes the transient cooldown clearing to both the shared auth store (`sharedStoreWrite: true`) and the agent's local store (when distinct from shared main), ensuring inherited credentials recover properly.
  2. Unsuccessful Cooldown Writes: checks the result of `updateAuthProfileStoreWithLock`. If store update returns `null` (due to SQLite lock contention or unreadable/contended state), responds with an actionable `UNAVAILABLE` error shape instead of returning `{ refreshed: true }`.

## Evidence & Verification

- **Real Behavior Proof:** Integration test in `src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-refresh.integration.test.ts` sets up active transient cooldowns alongside active billing disables across both shared store and local agent store, verifies that a normal refresh preserves cooldowns, and verifies that `models.authRefresh` with `clearTransientCooldowns: true` atomically clears transient cooldowns in both stores on disk while strictly preserving billing blocks (`passed 1 Vitest shard in 74.08s`).
- **Data Compatibility Proof:** Legacy auth stores without `usageStats` or with partial `usageStats` safely no-op without mutation or failure. Non-transient records (`billing`, `auth_permanent`) remain completely intact.
- **Unit Tests:** `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage-state.test.ts` passes 34/34 tests (`agents-support` in 7.02s).
- **Protocol & Linters:**
  - `pnpm gateway:validators:check` (unchanged)
  - `PROTOCOL_SINCE_BASE_SHA=d274da0983c43eb784a335a80cf728fe9472414a pnpm protocol:check` (passed)
  - `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet --base upstream/main` (passed)
  - `pnpm check:test-mock-exports --base upstream/main` (passed)
  - `pnpm oxlint` and `pnpm oxfmt --check` (clean, 0 errors, 0 warnings)

prs.title: fix(plugins): stop source-receipt warnings during model refresh
prs.body:
Related: #177882 (source-receipt warning only; the separate memory-search failure is outside this fix).

## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing models can succeed while the Gateway logs “Plugin source receipt was not recorded: Shared-state admission requires the host broker” and fails to save the record of captured native companion files. This still reproduces on main after #200320.

## User Impact

Model refresh saves its captured native-file receipts without the host-broker warning. Receipt-write failures stay advisory, and the existing discovery deadline is preserved. No configuration, schema migration, or operator action is required for the fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog worker forwards publications over its existing task channel to the retained host-owned publisher, rather than trying to acquire shared-state authority itself. Retained artifacts use the current task channel, exchanges are serialized, and pending receipt writes settle before that channel closes.

The adaptation preserves #200320's broker-owned source roots and cleanup, as well as main's sleep-aware admission watchdog. The two receipt regressions move into a dedicated broker-backed test file instead of restoring the native suite retired on main. The task admission owner keeps its existing input-size validation; the duplicate caller check was removed.

Original fix and regression tests contributed by @MertBasar0. This continues the same PR and preserves its authorship.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/18472a57-03bf-47c3-90c6-29f26dfbd442)

## Evidence

**Fresh real-Gateway comparison on 2026-11-18:** both eager and retained/lazy model refreshes succeed in both variants. Host-broker warnings fall from **2 to 0**; persisted receipts rise from **0 to 1**, covering both captured artifacts with independently verified SHA-256 hashes after Gateway shutdown. The synthetic plugin is installed through the real CLI. No model inference or native binary execution was used; both isolated Gateways and their owned children were joined.

**Current validation:** three regression cases fail on the pinned base for the intended missing-receipt/deadline reasons; **66 focused tests across eight files pass** on the adaptation. After the final duplicate-validation simplification, **40 pool tests pass** (20 repeat earlier coverage), and the real-Gateway comparison passes again. Core, agent-test and package-test typechecks, targeted production/test lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass.

**Published head:** `bba64ec693034893bd25b2db9440ef44affdbb4c`; its complete tree matches the validated workspace. Independent source-snapshot review found no actionable defects across all nine changed files. A test comment was clarified afterward without changing executable behavior. The reviewer did not run tests or verify a checkout; the local Auto Review launcher was unavailable and is not claimed as completed. [One hosted re-review was requested](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198572#issuecomment-6989886602) after the branch and proof were updated; completion is pending. **Required CI is blocked on maintainer workflow approval:** [CI run 44385446283](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44385446283) targets this exact head, reports `action_required`, and has zero jobs started. Other fork workflows also await approval. A repository maintainer must review the fork workflow changes and use **Approve and run workflows** on the pending run(s). Earlier review/CI do not certify this head. The PR remains draft.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes false release-validation failures when CLI child agents discover the parent's controller barrier or the plugin watchdog observes unfinished read-only installation discovery.

## User Impact

No user-visible runtime change. Release validation retains its announcement-order, no-installation, and no-leaked-process checks without confusing fixture-owned control or startup discovery with a product failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scope the announcement barrier through the existing plugin tool factory to the parent probe session. Before the watchdog's unchanged checks, join installation discovery through `update.status`; retain the original ready-log offset so post-ready installation work still fails.

Forwardports the reviewed repairs already landed on `release/2026.10.1` at `756a515b0afda4e5c6760f32f1e41dd5ea41ae3c` (including CLI commit `d5c0db78deb`). No production behavior, budgets, snapshots, or expected-failure exceptions change.

## Evidence

- Main focused tests: 56 plugin probe cases and 17 CLI fixture/helper cases passed. The announcement regression loads the generated plugin and fails on the original release fixture.
- New test cost: `pnpm test src/gateway/gateway-cli-backend.live-cache.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed in 19.52 seconds including wrapper/compiler verification; test time 9 ms. CI seconds are not available yet.
- [Real Docker CLI subscription proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37769312084) passed with the release fixture repair: child completion preceded barrier release, and the canonical parent reply preceded completion delivery.
- Fresh independent P0/P1 review is scoped-clean.
- Focused core/script lint, Docker E2E lint, raw-HTTP2 guard, and `git diff --check` passed, including checks not reached after the aggregate scan stopped.
- Main changed-file gate passed its ratchets, formatting, boundary checks, and every core-test typegraph, then failed the dead-export scan on untouched baseline exports: `SessionPendingInputState` (production and full-tree scans) and `discardStreamSegmentIndexes` (production scan). Replaying the canonical scan on clean main `7a1ac513eec` reproduced those exact failures. They are inherited, not waived or repaired in this fixture PR; the aggregate gate is not claimed green.

The [exact packaged watchdog Docker shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37773003484/job/113308544892) passed on its first attempt against release candidate `756a515b0afda4e5c6760f32f1e41dd5ea41ae3c`; lane execution took 72 seconds. All process and post-ready installation guards remained enabled. No FRV pass or publication is claimed.


## Current UI CI qualification — November 25, 2026

The current failed UI jobs ran synthetic merge `850f1c1c3` of this unchanged head into main `6cbc8838b316861468ab3099714c63efc6a5342c`. A narrow production-bundle browser replay on that **unmodified main parent**, with byte-identical root/UI dependency manifests and lockfile, reproduced three exact failures without this PR:

- [Warm reload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45686879402/job/139462225110): stable-format history expected 16 entries, received 17; running inline command never renders “Outcome unknown” after Stop.
- [Warm history scope change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45686879402/job/139462225139): the expected history request never arrives.

Two hosted failures remain **environment-sensitive and unqualified**, not labelled inherited or waived: the [forced-colors segmented-control assertion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45686879402/job/139462225149) and [persistent composer recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45686879402/job/139462225151) passed in the narrow macOS replay. The nonpersistent composer sibling failed differently on unmodified main and does not qualify the hosted persistent-case failure. Hosted CI used Linux; no same-runner-class replay or blind rerun was requested.

The first local replay stopped during fixture bundle preparation because workspace member dependency links were absent; after linking the existing installation (without changing dependencies), the actual owner replay completed: 3 failed / 5 passed, then composer 1 failed / 1 passed. These are qualified failure-attribution results, **not green CI or a UI fix**. This PR changes only release probe fixtures; no UI code, snapshots, budgets, or failure exceptions were changed.

An overlong planning question or extraction query makes portable deep research stop with a generic evidence gap. The result does not tell the user which limit was exceeded.

The research prompts now state their length limits. If a model still exceeds one, the partial report names the stage, field, and limit without including the model’s text. The response remains subject to evidence validation; it is not truncated automatically.

The fix keeps the existing schema limits and exposes bounded validation details in the result. It avoids cutting search terms or exact evidence quotes.

prs.title: feat(android): add Talk status chimes
prs.body:
Related: #204311 · Web: #204355 · Apple: #204362

## What Problem This Solves

When using Android Talk hands-free, you have to look at the phone to know when it can hear you or whether you actually hung up.

## User Impact

Talk plays a short sound when the microphone first works and another when a call ends normally. In turn-based Talk, a third sound tells you when you can speak again after a spoken reply. Realtime Talk already keeps the microphone open, so it never plays that third sound. All three are on by default and can be turned off individually in **Settings → Voice → Status chimes**.

## Why This Change Was Made

The phone already knows when capture and playback are ready; the Gateway doesn’t need to send a cue. The microphone does not send the chime back as speech. On a realtime hang-up, recording stops immediately but the call’s output route stays active until the chime finishes. Both ends of the call therefore use **call volume**, even when media volume is much lower. The three bundled cues are loudness-matched. No changes to Wear OS, Web, Apple, Gateway configuration, or Android permissions.

## Evidence

- Based on `1bc412fb7478`. From `apps/android`: `./gradlew :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.SecurePrefsTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.AndroidAudioInputSessionTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest :app:assembleThirdPartyDebug`. **177 passed, none skipped; APK assembled.** The tests include a real GatewaySession talking to a test WebSocket: PCM read during or across a chime never reaches the relay. Native recognition covers reply completion vs. failed playback; the audio-input test checks that the recorder can stop before communication mode is released.
- All three packaged WAVs match the measured inputs: **−19.8 LUFS** each (FFmpeg EBU R128). On a physical Galaxy Fold8, a tester confirmed the start and hang-up sounds were balanced on an earlier build carrying this change; this upstream APK was tested separately on an emulator, not installed on that phone.
- On the emulator, upgraded the unchanged main APK in place, toggled **Call end** off, and relaunched: that choice persisted and the other two stayed on. Local AutoReview could not review the complete diff because it does not accept WAV assets; no independent review pass is claimed.

**Settings → Voice**, Android emulator, same built-in screenshot fixture and viewport. Left: unchanged main. Right: this PR, all three preferences at their defaults. The images show the controls, not the sound.

prs.title: fix(tui): clarify how to dismiss a BTW reply
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a BTW reply arrives in the terminal UI, its card says “Press Enter or Esc to dismiss.” With a draft in the editor, Enter sends the draft and leaves the card visible.

## User Impact

The card now says “Press Esc in the editor to dismiss.” Esc closes the card and preserves the draft and cursor position. Enter still sends a nonempty draft and dismisses the card when the editor is empty.

## Why This Change Was Made

The input handler already gives each key to the right control. The footer can give accurate instructions without tracking draft state or changing how a focused picker handles keys.

## Evidence

- Replayed ten keyboard cases on the parent and the staged tree through the real terminal input parser, editor, card renderer and selector, with an inert in-memory Gateway transport. All requests ended there. On the parent, Enter sent the one-letter draft `a` once while the old hint remained visible.
- On the repaired tree, Esc dismissed the card with the cursor still at column 7 of `Maple card`. Empty Enter dismissed the card, and the focused selector handled Enter and Esc while preserving the underlying card. The same key events had identical editing and submission effects on both trees.
- Both changed files passed the pinned formatter. The project Vitest suite was not run locally because the sparse author checkout had no qualified workspace install.

prs.title: fix: reload repaired plugins without restarting the Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #205569
Related: #204156, #204189, #205567

## What Problem This Solves

When an update repaired a plugin in its original directory, the running Gateway still rejected `plugins.reload` with the error it recorded at startup. The plugin stayed unavailable even though its host peer link was now correct.

## User Impact

Operators and post-update maintenance can reload a repaired plugin without restarting the Gateway. A plugin whose files are still invalid stays unavailable, and reloading one plugin does not release another from quarantine.

## Why This Change Was Made

Explicit reload checks the requested plugin’s selected directory against its install record and runs the existing payload verifier before preparing the replacement. Ordinary loads continue to honor quarantine without repeatedly inspecting the filesystem.

## Evidence

An isolated Linux Gateway with two synthetic managed Git plugins reproduced `missing-openclaw-peer-link` on main (`072481c1683c`) after in-place repair. With the fix, the same RPC rejected the still-broken target, then activated it after repair without a restart. The second plugin remained quarantined even after its files were repaired. All 44 focused tests passed, as did core and Gateway-root typechecks, lint, formatting, docs links and `git diff --check`. The full macOS update and Gemini OAuth request were not replayed.

Reported and diagnosed by @hannesrudolph.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep quiet Activity session timestamps current
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If you leave Activity open on a quiet session, its “2m ago” label can stay there for six more minutes. Opening Activity again, or looking at the same timestamp in Inbox, shows “8m ago.”

## User Impact

The age beside a visible session now advances while you read the page. You can leave Activity open on desktop or mobile without refreshing it to see how long a session has been quiet.

## Why This Change Was Made

The row now reads the shared minute clock when it displays an age. The clock pauses while the document is hidden and catches up when it becomes visible. Presence expiry and session refresh keep their existing schedules.

## Evidence

A local Chromium run opened the built Control UI against an isolated synthetic Gateway. The browser clock advanced six minutes while the same session row stayed mounted and visible. The final three observations refer to the same session timestamp.

| Chromium observation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Activity at the start | 2m ago | 2m ago |
| Same Activity row six minutes later | 2m ago | 8m ago |
| Inbox at the end | 8m ago | 8m ago |
| Fresh Activity view at the same instant | 8m ago | 8m ago |

The repaired row showed each minute from 2 through 8. All 12 scheduled Gateway ticks arrived, the quiet window triggered zero additional Activity feed reads, and the before/after request counts matched for every method. An explicit session refresh and Chromium’s back-forward cache restoration both showed the correct age.

The new mounted regression failed on the parent with `expected '2m ago' to be '8m ago'`. All 53 tests across the Activity view, Activity controller, Activity page presence, presence lifecycle, and shared visible-clock suites passed on the patch. This was local browser and Vitest proof with synthetic data. Hosted project CI is pending.

The signed change passed all three hosted Control UI unit shards and the production and test type checks. The local Chromium replay executed the compiled Activity bundle and verified the 2-to-8-minute change on the same row. The release artifact build was skipped in this workflow. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45720419457)

The dependency check failed on 13 distinct exports in six source files. Those files are byte-identical to the signed parent. All 13 production rows and all five full-tree rows also appeared on an earlier main run. [Dependency job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45720419457/job/139577980014) · [Main comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45561863237/job/139027509204)

prs.title: fix: show how to enter an automation recipient when suggestions fail
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Control UI Automations, the recipient-suggestion error asks you to check the Gateway connection and try again. There is no Retry button in this state, and the failure does not prevent you from entering a recipient.

## User Impact

The alert now points to **Advanced → Results** in the editor. Enter the chat ID, phone number, or user ID in **Recipient**, then select **Save changes**. If you see the alert on an automation’s details page, select **Edit** to reach that field. Suggestions, diagnostics, account selection, access, and scheduling are unchanged.

| Surface | Exact before | Exact after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Automation details and editor after recipient suggestions fail | Couldn’t load recipient suggestions. Check the Gateway connection and try again. Details: The Telegram directory is unavailable | Couldn’t load recipient suggestions. You can enter the recipient in the editor under Advanced → Results. Details: The Telegram directory is unavailable |

## Why This Change Was Made

The alert reuses the translated names of the existing **Advanced** and **Results** controls. The same wording works on the details page and in the editor, where **Advanced** starts closed.

**Skill in practice:** Use the labels people see on screen and give them a next step that works. A failed suggestion lookup doesn’t tell us the Gateway disconnected, but manual entry remains available.

## Evidence

- Exercised the bundled Control UI in Chromium at 1280 × 900 in light theme. A deterministic Gateway fixture rejected the Telegram recipient lookup without disconnecting. On both revisions, the browser opened the automation from the sidebar, found the alert on the details page and in the editor, entered a new **Recipient**, and sent it only on **Save changes**. Reopening the automation after a reload showed the value returned by the fixture. No live Gateway, scheduler, or Telegram delivery was exercised.

prs.title: fix: show who wrote each message when an agent reads Slack history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent reads Slack history with the message tool's `read` action, most messages identify their author only by a Slack user ID such as `U0BVA95R1C7`. Agents and tools built on `read`, such as the Knowledge "Learn from Slack" scribe, cannot tell who said what. In a live run the scribe produced a transcript that named authors only by ID.

## User Impact

`read` results now include each author's Slack profile names as `user_profile` (`display_name`, `real_name`, `name`), the same field Slack itself sometimes includes, so existing readers pick up names without changes. `user` stays the author's identity. Nothing to configure: the default manifest already grants `users:read`. If a lookup fails (missing scope, deactivated user, rate limit), that author's messages look exactly as they do today and the read still succeeds. Mentions inside `text` stay as `<@U…>`, so agents can still use them to address people.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readSlackMessages` takes a new opt-in `includeAuthorProfiles`. Only the message-tool `read` action opts in. The other internal callers (approval message updates and member-join room context) don't, so they make no extra Slack calls. Messages that already carry a Slack-supplied `user_profile` keep it unchanged. I left `<@U…>` mention rewriting out on purpose: replacing IDs in `text` would drop identity that agents rely on.

Names come from one shared, bounded profile cache. The Slack monitor's per-context `users.info` cache for inbound events moved into `extensions/slack/src/user-profiles.ts`, and reads now use it too:

- There is one cache per account, limited to 2048 entries (least recently used are dropped), the same limit as before. Entries are keyed by token, workspace (Enterprise Grid team) and user. Two tokens on one account, for example the bot token and a user token from a different workspace, never share entries.
- Monitor startup clears the account's cache, so restarting the monitor still re-reads names, as it did before.
- Failed lookups are not cached, as before. Uncached authors on a page are still looked up in parallel. The lookup client rejects 429s instead of sleeping through `Retry-After`.
- Monitor name derivation (used by name-based allowlist matching) is unchanged: display name, then profile real name, then handle.
- Inbound messages and bot-token reads use the same token, so they share entries. A user-token reader such as the scribe shares entries only with its own earlier reads.

**Expected `users.info` calls for a "Learn from Slack" run:** before the cache, each channel page and each thread read looked up every distinct author again, roughly 50–200 calls per run against Slack's Tier 4 limit (~100/min). With the cache, a run makes about one call per distinct author across all channels and threads it reads, typically a few dozen. Later runs make calls only for new authors, or for everyone again after the Slack monitor restarts.

Docs: added "Read author names" to `docs/channels/slack/access-control.md`.

## Evidence

- Focused tests (`actions.read.test.ts`): names are added with one lookup per distinct author; a failed lookup leaves that author's messages unchanged; an existing `user_profile` is kept; bot messages are untouched; nothing is looked up unless requested. `action-runtime.test.ts` asserts the read action opts in.
- Work-count test: two reads by one account and token reuse lookups; only the failed author is retried. A different account, a different team, or a different token each make fresh lookups.
- `pnpm test:extension slack` (164 files): all pass except the new cache test, which failed only because that test file mocked `./client.js` without the token-key helper. After fixing the mock, `actions.read.test.ts` passes. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint (`extensions/slack/src`), oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean.
- Live Slack check (read-only) against a real workspace channel, calling the changed `readSlackMessages` with a real user token (before the cache change). 15 messages from 11 authors: 1 of 15 had a profile without the option, 15 of 15 had display/real names with it, including Slack Connect users.
- Independent reviews (Astra subagents). The first pass found no P0–P2 issues and checked that `missing_scope`, `user_not_found` and HTTP 429 fall back without waiting. On the cache change, it flagged a cross-workspace cache key, now fixed by keying on the token, and the test mock gap above, also fixed. The final pass found no other P0–P2 issues.
- Not done: no isolated-Gateway QA Lab run that calls `read` through a model. Sharing between the monitor and reads was verified by code tracing, not a dedicated runtime test.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix(gateway): exclude browser UI pairings from silent-prune clustering
prs.body:
Related to #203145

## What Problem This Solves

Pairing a second Control UI browser profile silently deletes the first profile's device pairing. The silent-pairing prune worker clusters records by `clientId + clientMode + displayName`, but browser UI clients keep a durable per-profile device identity (a localStorage keypair), so two profiles are two distinct devices that merely share client metadata. Once the older pairing ages past the 60s grace window and its socket is closed, the next profile's silent pairing prunes it; the old profile then fails closed and its device-bound automations stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

`silentPairingClusterKey` in `src/infra/device-pairing-core.kernel.ts` assumed every silent pairing came from an ephemeral state dir that mints a fresh keypair per run. That holds for CLI/node clients, not for browser UI clients whose device ids are stable per profile. The fix excludes `openclaw-control-ui`, `webchat-ui`, and `openclaw-browser-copilot` (canonicalized with the existing `normalizeGatewayClientName`) from clustering as both anchor and victim, matching the pairing docs' "remembered until revoked or explicitly removed" contract for durable browser identities. CLI/node temp-dir dedup, manual/trusted-cidr exclusions, the recent-approval grace, and connected-device protection are unchanged.

Scope note: this issue also carries `needs-product-decision` / `needs-security-review` labels for the broader account-scoped pairing model. This PR deliberately does not redesign authorization or scope ownership; it only stops the cleanup worker from deleting distinct durable browser identities — the data-loss symptom reported here. Flagging for maintainer and security review accordingly.

## User Impact

Multiple browser profiles (or Control UI + WebChat) on one gateway keep their pairings and device-bound automations across reconnects. No config change. Existing CLI/node ephemeral-state cleanup behavior is preserved.

## Evidence

Real before/after against a live gateway run from this branch's TS source (isolated dev state dir, token auth, loopback). Two WS clients with distinct ed25519 device identities and identical `clientId=openclaw-control-ui` / `mode=ui` / displayName: A pairs (silent-approved), disconnects, 65s elapse (> 60s grace), then B pairs:

| Run | Code | A present after B pairs | prune log |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | origin/main | **false** (A deleted) | `device pairing pruned superseded silent pairing ... prunedCount=1` |
| after | this branch | **true** (A and B both kept) | none |

Commands (cwd = checkout):

```
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway --force
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs pair-prune-proof.mts --token <token> --port 19001 --label before
```

Before output: `after B pairing: A present=false B present=true`, and the gateway log shows `pruned deviceId=3a05371b... approvedVia=silent` at the second B connected. After output: `after B pairing: A present=true B present=true`, zero prune log lines.

Committed regressions in `src/infra/device-pairing-prune.test.ts`: distinct profiles sharing client metadata survive for all three browser client ids (parameterized), plus a case variant where the anchor carries the mixed-case id — the exclusion must normalize the stored clientId before its early return, so on base the anchor clusters with its canonical-id sibling and prunes it. Red/green on the same file, swapping only `device-pairing-core.kernel.ts`:

```
git checkout origin/main -- src/infra/device-pairing-core.kernel.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/device-pairing-prune.test.ts
# 4 failed | 11 passed — all 4 new browser-identity cases fail on base
git checkout HEAD -- src/infra/device-pairing-core.kernel.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/device-pairing-prune.test.ts
# 15 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/device-pairing-prune.test.ts
# 3 passed — existing gateway prune guards unchanged
node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/infra/device-pairing-core.kernel.ts src/infra/device-pairing-prune.test.ts
# 0 warnings, 0 errors; oxfmt --check clean
```


### Upgrade & data-model compatibility proof (stable v2026.11.10 → candidate)

The run above exercised isolated fresh state only. This run proves that a browser pairing + token created on released stable carries forward and keeps working on the candidate, and that the fix holds on upgraded state. Same isolated state dir across the stable→candidate boundary; distinct ports; throwaway proof token; loopback bind; production `~/.openclaw` untouched.

Binaries — both self-report version `2026.11.10`, distinguished by commit:
- **stable** (bug present): `OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f)`, installed via `npm install openclaw@2026.11.10`
- **candidate** (this branch, fix present): `OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (363ed24)`, built via `pnpm build cliStartup` → `node openclaw.mjs`

Driver: `contributions/pr-203145-evidence/upgrade-proof.mts` (not committed). Profile A's ed25519 keypair is persisted across the boundary to model a browser profile's durable localStorage identity; B gets a fresh keypair. Both share `clientId=openclaw-control-ui`, `mode=ui`, and displayName — the metadata cluster condition.

| Phase | Binary | State dir | Action | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stable baseline | stable `6ea542f` | fresh BASE | A pairs → disconnect → 65s → B pairs | **A pruned**: `aCountAfterB=0`; gateway log `device pairing pruned superseded silent pairing device=562bc690…` — bug reproduced on released stable |
| stable seed | stable `6ea542f` | fresh UPG | A pairs (keypair persisted) | A silent-approved, listed `count=1` — pre-upgrade state carried into the candidate |
| **upgrade** | **candidate `363ed24`** | **same UPG, not wiped** | load state → reconnect A → disconnect → 65s → B pairs → reconnect A | **A retained end-to-end** (see below) |

Upgrade-phase data points (`proof-upgrade.txt`, A deviceId `f1ed957d…`):
- `aCountAtCandidateStartup: 1` — the pairing written by stable loads on the candidate (data-model compatibility: existing stored data still loads)
- `aAuthenticatedAtStartup: true` — A's retained pairing + token authenticates immediately after the upgrade
- `aCountAfterB: 1`, `bCountAfterB: 1` — after the 60s grace window, pairing B does **not** prune A on upgraded state (the fix)
- `aAuthenticatedAfterB: true`, `aCountAfterBReconnect: 1` — the original profile still authenticates after the second profile paired

Contrast: stable prunes A (1 `pruned superseded silent pairing` log line, baseline `aPruned=true`); candidate retains A (0 prune log lines, `aSurvivedUpgradeAndSecondPairing=true`). Same store, same A identity across the boundary — only the binary changed.

prs.title: fix: restore only the failed update’s recorded files
prs.body:
Related: #205165, #204915

## What Problem This Solves

A failed update still reconstructs its rollback from build-global receipts and a directory scan, rather than the files that candidate recorded. Returning to the same build can consume an older receipt, and a legacy import's prospective removal list can delete a store normal runtime created later.

## User Impact

A new resident launcher restores exactly the selected release's recorded pre-images, removes its recorded additions first, and keeps later runtime-created stores. An invalid or incomplete manifest fails visibly with a triage next step instead of silently guessing or switching to the old release with unrestored state. No operator action, schema change, new flag or manifest field is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing state publisher owns the write set; the launcher only executes it. The v1 manifest remains `{v:1,runId,files:[{live,preimage}]}` in the target release directory. Rename replay is restart-safe. Before mutation the publisher still records the full prospective list; after successful import and native close, it durably republishes that same manifest with unused prospective file families removed. Families actually created during boot retain all sidecar removals. An interrupted import before completion conservatively retains the broad list (the explicitly accepted rare case); no persisted provenance field is added.

Manifest-backed rollback never interprets global `.upgraded-<build>` receipts or scans `.pre` paths. Targets without `.restore` retain the shipped compatibility interpreter, including the early Git launcher; the modern fallback scopes legacy receipt consumption to the trial's existing freshness window. Retire compatibility only when the supported update/rollback floor passes the last published target without `.restore`. A still-running older resident judges the first hop until a native service start loads format 4; this PR does not pretend an on-disk rewrite upgrades that process.

Simplification: modern recovery has one declared write-set owner; inference is isolated in the explicitly temporary compatibility module. Scoped tokei production code (six touched production files, excluding tests): **1,265 → 1,381 (+116)**. Test-line guard: **+198**, below the existing 400 allowance; no allocation/exemption.

## Evidence

- Pinned base: `627f23654573975faa0492e44562f5755b2d4101`; head: `7f07553a09ec2443dbdddfdcde4c0000ec812115`.
- AWS owner/consumer suites: 90 assertions across seven files pass across the initial wave and the single repaired generated-import consumer. Covers authoritative target-only restore, external paths, stale same-build/global receipts, malformed manifests, interrupted rename replay, legacy fallback, late SQLite/WAL preservation and immutable retry originals. The initial wave exposed a quoted old export in one existing test; both quoted uses were migrated, with assertions unchanged, and that consumer passed on the final head.
- Production/state-test types, changed-file lint/format and test-line guard passed. Full build and package integrity passed on the final head: [AWS run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1f93f346dea32b949bb9fcc1a1412188). Carrier `07484900409ed1cf2a1671cac06d98d53751afcd` binds identical source; candidate SHA256 `321b3d2674d23ed6d56cecfe1e10476fec4c006b173dfcb908a3ae8ccd6ca012`.
- **Linux product proof PASSED:** [AWS run_229630b615517bb14dcb3cc0d2550023](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_229630b615517bb14dcb3cc0d2550023), unchanged head. Installed published **2026.11.10 → head**, then prepared/activated a same-source schema43 fault successor through the real resident format4 launcher. The fault candidate disconnects its ready IPC after durable migration, allows normal HTTP/RPC startup, and crashes on the driver's private signal. No trial, slot, manifest, readiness or service result is fabricated.
- The literal restore record's SQLite image was renamed back with the same device/inode (**66305/3512406**); schema **42**, original two OAuth witness rows restored, and the fixture's new migration table absent. After manifest completion, real public `sessions.create` wrote `agent:pending:manifest-reader-witness`; public `sessions.list` proved that later store/session survived automatic rollback. Trial `79bb7303-7fbf-497c-9b4a-53427b1a7393` ended `rolled-back`; previous head served. Native service stop/uninstall and removal of the lane's npm config passed.
- This lane explicitly uses existing public `gateway install --wrapper <actual openclaw-launcher.mjs>` to pin the reader. Ordinary `gateway install --force` wrote the slot's `dist/index.js`; that real service-ownership bug is separately filed as #205617. Default reinstall coverage is not claimed. Corrected fault tarball SHA256: `dcd2f8aa0ed4797e0ce425a6a83aa38b581bbfe4773e41c11c6e8c026e92930a`. Private complete receipts: `direction-2026-11-24/UpdateOwner-reader-checks/product-complete.tgz`.
- **Exact-head CI GREEN.** Local review complete: patch correct, security cleared, no findings, confidence0.76 (`~/.cache/clawsweeper-local-review/7f07553a09ec.md`). Historical isolated-base comparison ran no assertions due missing workspace-extension dependencies; no base-red result is claimed, and it did not gate the product proof. No Windows/macOS product proof is claimed.

prs.title: feat: links to a setting open and highlight its row in Settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw tells someone to change a setting, for example after a reply fails because no fallback model is set up, it can only name the Settings page. The person lands at the top of the page and has to hunt for the row. Many rows, including browser-only preferences and rows that plugins draw, had no stable name a link could use, so nothing could point at them reliably.

## User Impact

- A link such as `/settings/infrastructure#gateway.publicOrigin` opens the page, unfolds the group that hides the row, scrolls it to the middle of the screen and marks it with an accent edge bar and a short wash. Focus moves to the row, never into its control, and nothing is changed. The bar stays until the person clicks or types; with reduced motion the page jumps and the mark stays still.
- Every row on every Settings page now has one stable setting ID: config rows use their config path (`gateway.publicOrigin`, `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`), one agent's rows use `agent.<path>`, browser-only preferences use `local.<key>`, native app settings `device.<key>`, profile rows `profile.<field>`, and other rows `<page>.<name>`. Rows that repeat per item use one pattern plus the item, such as `providers.openai`.
- Plugin Settings views declare the IDs they draw in `controlUi.settingsViews[].settings` (`plugin.<id>.*`, `channels.<owned channel>.*` or `plugins.entries.<id>.*`). The host refuses a row ID the view did not declare. A channel detail opens from `/settings/channels?channel=<id>`, so `/settings/channels?channel=whatsapp#plugin.whatsapp.linkedPhone` lands on the WhatsApp plugin's linked phone. Plugins published before this change keep loading; their views simply have no linkable rows until they declare IDs.
- The Channels page row that opens a channel is now `channelsPage.channel.<id>`; `channels.<id>` stays the channel's config path.

## Why This Change Was Made

One list owns the IDs: `src/shared/control-ui-settings/` maps each hand-built page to the settings it shows, with the disclosure that hides a row and the config section that holds it. Generic config rows need no entry; their config path is their ID. One arrival owner in the Settings shell resolves the link (including renamed IDs and the nearest enclosing setting), waits for rows that render after Gateway reads, and keeps the mark on a row the page redraws.

The arrival and the setting list load with Settings, and the mark is drawn inline on the row, so the chat and new-session boot bundles and the shared stylesheets stay at their current size.

`pnpm check:control-ui-setting-ids` keeps it deterministic in lint, `check:changed` and CI: every row on a Settings page must carry a listed ID or be marked as a status/action row, every listed ID must be drawn exactly once, bundled plugins may draw only the IDs their manifests declare, and `config/control-ui-setting-ids.txt` keeps published IDs: removing one needs an alias so old links still land.

Two nearby fixes came out of checking every row: a config setting with several object shapes (such as `channels.twitch` or a secret provider) was drawn in both the common and advanced groups of the Advanced page; it is now drawn once. Rows in a channel detail sit flush with the dialog edge, so their mark reaches past the text there.

Accepted edge cases: a row the page redraws within 10 seconds of arrival gets the mark again, unless the person has clicked or typed. Rows that only exist with live data (native app, push notifications, cloud workers) are checked statically, not opened in the browser suite.

## Evidence

- Captured with the real Control UI against a mocked Gateway in Chromium at 1280×800, dark theme. Before: `main` at 3f4e2bd3a4c6e. After: the pre-rebase implementation with the channel-detail spacing change (368b856b26386).
- All **10 Chromium Settings deep-link tests** passed on the final integrated source against the mocked Gateway. Coverage includes generated and hand-built pages, model and plugin rows, the theme importer, MCP server switches, per-agent tool access and command allowlists, and provider account priority.
- `pnpm ui:check-performance` against a local build of c635b051de14e: chat boot JS 1336655 → 1336663 B gzip with the same 21 requests, new boot JS 820731 → 820739 B, total CSS unchanged (346225 B gzip, 1783458 B raw).
- `pnpm check:control-ui-setting-ids` OK; `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck all, SAFETY, SQLite, plugin boundaries, Plugin SDK surface and the other gates pass. Lint fails only on `max-lines` in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-session.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts`, `src/wizard/setup.ts` and `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts`, and the dead-export scan only on `src/state/state-upgrade-tree.ts: skipEntry`; this PR does not touch those files and they fail the same way on `main`.
- Unit and node suites for touched owners pass (UI lib, components, config and search pages: 9901 passed; `memory-page.browser.test.ts` "keeps the header and every tab panel on one column" also fails on `main`, and `talk-device-navigation.test.tsx` timed out only in the full parallel run and passes alone).
- Test-line check passed against 6c1efeaf6b3ec: +1,049 net lines, 400 allowed and 649 allocated for the ID checker, browser flows (including delayed custom editors), arrival lifecycle and plugin manifest checks.
- Final local autoreview compared 6c1efeaf6b3ec to edd447bc9b9ad (the published tree at f0dd6da311552). No actionable P0 or P1 findings. This was static review; browser and typecheck results are separate.

### Generated config page: `/settings/infrastructure#gateway.publicOrigin`

Before (`main` 3f4e2bd3a4c6e): the page opens at the top. After: the row is centered, marked and focused.

Before: the Channels page opens with WhatsApp closed. After: the WhatsApp detail opens on the plugin's linked-phone row.

prs.title: fix(linux): let dashboard users grant microphone access
prs.body:
Closes #202024

## What Problem This Solves

Microphone input in the Linux companion's embedded Gateway dashboard fails with “Microphone access is blocked. Allow it in browser site settings to list inputs.” The embedded app has no browser site-settings permission control, leaving the user unable to grant access.

## User Impact

The registered Gateway dashboard can request microphone access through a native Allow/Deny dialog that identifies the Gateway origin. Deny is the default. Camera and screen capture are not granted, and ordinary embedded browsing tabs and widgets do not receive this handler.

**Runtime requirement:** this enables microphone consent and WebRTC for registered dashboards, but does not supply a WebRTC-capable engine. Full Talk was confirmed on Ubuntu 22.04.5 with a locally built WebKitGTK 2.55.0 development runtime using LibWebRTC. Stock installations are not guaranteed to support Talk; WebKitGTK 2.54 disables WebRTC during the backend transition. Use a regular browser when the system runtime lacks support. This PR does not bundle or upgrade WebKit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Linux shell did not handle WebKit's media permission requests. The change installs an audio-only consent handler before a registered dashboard starts navigation and uses the existing Gateway document owner to admit requests. A pending dialog is cancelled on navigation or closure; accepting a stale dialog cannot grant access to another dashboard.

The dashboard settings explicitly enable media streams and WebRTC; microphone access still requires the native consent decision. The change adds no dependencies, stored permissions, Gateway configuration, or browser-engine packaging. Experimental runtime builds, library patches, and launch scripts are excluded.

## Evidence

- Follow-up on 2026-11-22: the reporter confirmed a real Talk session with microphone input and Bluetooth response playback using the same permission-enabled desktop binary plus `set_enable_webrtc(true)` and an unpatched WebKit main build at `7f49613cb85904e9ab361c1d9c7f36d34b35fb3d` (GTK3 API 4.1, `ENABLE_WEB_RTC=ON`, `USE_LIBWEBRTC=1`). No legacy WebKit/GStreamer fixes were applied to that engine. This is development-runtime evidence, not a claim about stock Ubuntu packages.
- That runtime also passed an independent localhost peer test with synthetic capture: outgoing/incoming audio, data echo, and advancing HTML audio playback, including an answer without the MID RTP extension. An isolated actual OpenClaw launch reported `RTCPeerConnection: function; offer: offer; bundle: true`. Synthetic tests do not establish physical microphone or speaker quality; the reporter's live session provides that separate confirmation.
- The follow-up source delta is one settings call. Rust formatting passes; the previously built and tested experimental binary already contains this exact call. Existing consent/build proof below is retained from the original permission revision, rather than presented as newly rerun.

- Reproduced the failure through the actual Linux desktop binary on base `cd2ae19272a3ee7be456385fa7efc56d6e2109a6`, using an isolated local HTTP dashboard fixture: `getUserMedia({audio:true})` returned `NotAllowedError` without a prompt. The patched desktop binary displays the native consent dialog. The reporter also confirmed the prompt in their actual Gateway dashboard.
- The native GTK/WebKit regression passes with synthetic capture devices: Allow returns an audio track; Deny, combined audio/video, and an unadmitted origin all reject. It never records a physical microphone. The test is explicitly display-dependent and must be invoked with `--ignored --test-threads=1`.
- All 53 existing `gateway_windows::` tests pass.
- Locked Linux debug build, Rust formatting, targeted documentation formatting, and patch whitespace checks pass.
- Author simplification/code review completed. Local autoreview and ClawSweeper are not installed; no independent review is claimed. The prior hosted review found no code defects and requested desktop Allow/Deny and baseline evidence. The follow-up results below address those proof requests. A maintainer capability decision and review of the updated revision remain outstanding.

### Desktop permission results (2026-11-22)

Collected after the review, through the actual OpenClaw Linux executable and its registered dashboard path, using a localhost HTTP fixture and a separate temporary HOME/XDG profile for each decision. The reporter selected the native dialog buttons. The page calls `getUserMedia({audio:true})`, reports track kinds or the exception name to the fixture, and immediately stops all granted tracks. No audio is recorded or uploaded.

```text
Original pre-permission desktop: Baseline: NotAllowedError
Patched desktop, Allow:          Allow: allowed:audio
Patched desktop, Deny:           Deny: NotAllowedError
```

The baseline executable was freshly built from the pre-permission app sources at `cd2ae19272a3ee7be456385fa7efc56d6e2109a6`. Both the baseline comparison and patched desktop used the same local WebKitGTK 2.55.0 runtime described above. The patched executable contains the exact permission module now on PR head `8bdd795c367bac38acad4ff6836efc7cf564537e`. Each case used a fresh app process/profile; a first attempt to test Deny then Allow within one page retained denial and was not used as Allow evidence.

The committed native regression was rerun with system WebKit. A temporary negative control omitted the test fixture's call to install the permission handler, reproducing the pre-fix lack of a handler; this is explicitly a negative control, not an unchanged test run against a baseline that lacks the new module.

```text
Handler omitted:
  assertion left == right failed
  left:  Some("NotAllowedError")
  right: Some("allowed:audio")
  FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed

Handler restored:
  microphone_linux::tests::webkit_microphone_consent ... ok
  1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
```

The restored regression covers Allow, Deny, combined audio/video rejection, and an unadmitted origin. Temporary source changes were restored; the checkout is clean. Earlier fixture runs encountered temporary-directory cleanup errors involving the desktop portal mount after delivering their capture results; the final Deny and matched-runtime baseline runs both exited successfully. This evidence establishes the permission behavior, while the separate reporter-confirmed Talk session establishes real microphone/Bluetooth use. The maintainer capability decision remains outstanding.

The screenshots below show the real desktop app displaying a synthetic dashboard fixture, not a full authenticated Talk session. The “after” image is the native dialog; the “before” image is the dashboard's rejected capture result. Images contain only fixture content.

### Before

![Before: microphone capture fails without a consent prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/861b9824-6deb-4027-9ade-13e97b8f9128)

### After

![After: the Linux app offers Deny and Allow for microphone access](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08b2274d-8618-4337-a214-684ad1b5d1eb)

<details>
<summary>Focused verification commands</summary>

```sh
cd apps/linux/src-tauri
cargo +1.97.1 fmt --check
WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1 \
  cargo +1.97.1 test --locked --bin openclaw-desktop \
  microphone_linux::tests::webkit_microphone_consent -- --ignored --test-threads=1
cargo +1.97.1 test --locked --bin openclaw-desktop gateway_windows::
cargo +1.97.1 build --locked
```

The renderer environment settings work around this test host's graphics issue. EGL warnings also occurred during the passing capture tests.

</details>

prs.title: chore(qa): cover onboarding Gateway health outcomes
prs.body:
## Problem
Onboarding QA did not reliably distinguish successful reachability preflight from failure of the final health RPC, so an unhealthy fixture could exercise the wrong boundary.

## Solution
Preserve the current onboarding/state owners while porting the healthy and unhealthy Classic PTY scenarios. Wait for actual Gateway startup readiness, answer the current memory prompt, and clean up background PTY processes on failure. The fault proxy forwards startup/probe traffic and all token-auth CLI preflight retries; only a backend health RPC after successful preflight receives the synthetic final-health error. Added a real HTTP/WebSocket proxy regression covering that distinction.

## Validation
- Real isolated token-auth Gateway plus shipped `pnpm openclaw health`: prior proxy returned success (red); repaired proxy observes successful preflight, faults the final RPC, and returns the expected synthetic error (green). No live Gateway/state used.
- Proxy regression passed; shell/tooling fixtures (39 tests), QA coverage (3 tests), touched format/lint, shell syntax, canonical scripts typecheck, and diff checks passed.
- Independent local review of the full port and subsequent correction found no remaining actionable findings.
- Full packaged Docker Classic-wizard PTY flow remains unrun locally: Docker daemon is unavailable. The real Gateway/health CLI proof above does not substitute for that complete wizard flow. CI on this new head is still required; historical proof on earlier heads is not current-head proof.

### CI repair follow-up
The first new-head `check-lint` found two implicit `ws.RawData` stringifications. Decode all binary frame forms explicitly using the existing proxy decoder contract. The real proxy regression passed again, and the canonical type-aware lint wrapper passed for both the script and root test. The follow-up head requires its own hosted CI; the previous failed lint result is retained as prior-head evidence, not relabeled passing.

## Latest CI repair

The hosted root-script typecheck exposed a `ws.RawData` overload ambiguity in the real proxy fixture. Narrowed its ArrayBuffer and Buffer variants explicitly; the real child-proxy regression, exact root-script test type graph, canonical type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Current-head CI pending. Full Docker wizard acceptance remains unrun because no Docker daemon is available.


## Current review-gate blocker

At `d5e7523927450f84656543674e92f6e8d4351f48`, the [required review job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45705489441/job/139526463746) exhausted its bounded recovery because the PR comparison inventory was inconsistent: REST reported 67,030 files, while the capped PR-files endpoint returned 3,000. The current GraphQL file count was 0.

A pinned [live-main versus exact-head comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/da760885b959802ab9a725f030f8940ab40dd4cc...d5e7523927450f84656543674e92f6e8d4351f48) returns exactly the expected 10 files and merge-base `ba6d94ec17712094f485b85d6923f246b459844b`. Meanwhile, even an uncached PR metadata read still reports old base `f08559c33cb2c3214566cd3e61d3d495ba9fa4a1` rather than the live main ref above. The PR-files result also includes unrelated paths.

This is an unresolved PR-comparison projection inconsistency, not completed security review. No gate bypass, manufactured commit, base toggle, or blind rerun was used. Required review remains blocked until its complete comparison inventory is consistent. The Docker wizard acceptance gap above remains unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

The forced-colors browser check can inspect a radio control after the Settings page is ready but before its independent preferences/config load selects Dark or Beta. Main CI then fails before checking the intended styling.

## User Impact

This repairs the browser check; application behavior and appearance are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wait for the expected selected state with the existing assertion polling API. Keep the unselected, forced-colors decoration, and keyboard-focus assertions intact. The change replaces one test line and adds no production code, helpers, delays, or retries of the scenario.

## Evidence

- Main failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45713161228/job/139553265272.
- Isolated Linux Chromium reproduction: the original checked-state read was false; Dark became selected immediately afterward, while application readiness was already true. The original assertion still failed.

- Fixed source `d4654b8ff35f49f00e79f2c70b0cc4f707ab04d7`: isolated Linux Chromium test passed both existing scenarios (1 test, 7 unrelated cases skipped); the UI fixture build also passed.

Opening a Logbook activity on tablet or desktop placed its image and notes to one side of the title. Switching between 12-hour and 24-hour time changed both the size and the direction of the offset.

The image, notes, and distractions now start directly below the activity title in either clock format. On phones they still align with the colored stripe, and collapsed cards look the same.

prs.title: fix(ui): stop showing background processes as sidebar activity
prs.body:
## Problem

A session whose turn had ended but still had a background process running (a dev server, a watcher, a long build) kept a quieter spinning ring in the sidebar, stayed pinned past the quiet-row cap like an active run, and lit its catalog group's running dot. A leftover process is not the session working, so the sidebar read as busy when nothing was happening.

## Change

Background processes no longer count as sidebar activity:

- The leading ring on sidebar rows, rail shortcuts and catalog rows only shows for an active turn or running subagents. The quiet `--background` ring variant, its CSS and the `Background work running` label are removed.
- `rowDemandsVisibility` and `catalogSessionActivity` no longer treat `backgroundProcessCount` as activity, so background-only rows follow the normal quiet-row cap and no longer light running dots.
- The `unread` state description no longer depends on background processes.

Kept on purpose: a paused (yielded) subagent waiting on its own command still shows its parent as working (`childShowsParentWorking`), since that turn will resume. Processes stay visible where they belong: **Details → Processes** and the **Processes** panel. The Gateway's `backgroundProcessCount` row field is unchanged.

Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md` now describes the ring without the background variant.

## Evidence

Mocked Gateway Control UI E2E, dark theme, same fixture on both revisions: one running session, one session with `backgroundProcessCount: 1`, one idle session. Before = `af9c697714fb` (main), after = this branch.

Related: #202399

## What Problem This Solves

Opening an unknown Control UI URL directly shows the intended 404 page, but the sidebar agent menu only offers “Create new agent”. Existing agents are missing until the user leaves the page.

## User Impact

The agent menu offers existing agents immediately on missing pages. The requested URL, “Page not found” message, and “Go to chat” action stay unchanged. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

I removed the route-ID requirement from the existing shell-owned agent loading path. The roster belongs to the sidebar, not to a matched page. Connection checks, cached lists, and request deduplication remain in place. Discovery is skipped when the agents capability is absent, so other shell initialization continues safely.

The pr-simplify pass kept one browser regression in the existing sidebar suite and added no new state or helpers. Compared with main: production +2/-3 lines; tests +34 lines.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix: explain what to do when an automation changes during editing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If an automation’s settings change after you open **Edit**, OpenClaw won’t save your edits over the newer settings. The old message didn’t say your edits weren’t saved. When OpenClaw couldn’t load the latest settings, “Refresh” didn’t say what to refresh or warn that reloading would discard the edits still on screen.

## User Impact

When the automatic read fails, the editor still has your draft. Copy your edits before reloading the browser page. Once the Gateway can load the latest settings again, open **Edit**, review those settings, and reapply your edits. If the automatic read succeeds, the latest settings are already in the editor for review and the rejected edits need to be reapplied.

### Automatic read fails

**Before:** This automation changed on the Gateway, but the latest definition could not be loaded. Refresh before retrying.

**After:** This automation changed before your edits could be saved. Copy your edits before reloading the page, then review the latest settings in Edit before reapplying them.

### Automatic read succeeds

**Before:** This automation changed on the Gateway. The latest definition is loaded; review it before retrying.

**After:** This automation changed before your edits could be saved. Review the latest settings shown here, then reapply your edits.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing save recovery knows whether its read replaced the draft or left it on screen. The two English messages use that result. The Active switch, missing-revision feedback, structured errors, permissions, and storage behavior are unchanged. There is no new control or automatic retry.

### Skill in practice

The [OpenClaw writing skill’s error guidance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/.agents/skills/openclaw-writing/references/error-messages.md) asks writers to say what happened to the reader’s work and name an action that can work. Both conflicts reject the save, but only one leaves the draft on screen to copy. The copy names what the reader sees and the verified next action rather than saying “definition,” “Refresh,” or “retry” without context.

Contributor: [@vyctorbrzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e346c5e4-f828-45b2-be8f-1aad6754fbad)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/17fe790b-7293-4661-a51d-973e6e190f9d)

## Evidence

Chromium loaded the built Control UI at the garden-inventory detail route and connected to a synthetic Gateway. **Save changes** sent a stale revision and received `CRON_JOB_CHANGED`. In the failed-read case, the draft stayed on screen; copying it, reloading the same route, and reopening **Edit** loaded the current settings after the simulated read was available again. In the successful-read case, the current settings replaced the draft immediately. In both cases, reapplying the edit sent the current revision and preserved the other change in the outgoing patch. This verifies browser recovery and requests, not live storage persistence.

Both exact-copy assertions failed on the pinned base for the old wording. The patch passed 9 browser cases and 88 focused unit and renderer tests, plus the Control UI build, typecheck, scoped lint and format, and i18n checks.

[Before and after screenshots for both read outcomes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205622#issuecomment-7177767546) (Chromium, 1280 × 900, light theme, synthetic data).

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix(workboard): stop showing PR-loading warnings and apply agent filter before paging on Sessions boards
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening a Workboard Sessions board with many active sessions shows two stacked full-width notices above the columns: an orange warning that pull-request facts for dozens of sessions are not loaded yet or stale, and a second bar stating how many sessions loaded along with a caveat that the agent filter only applies to loaded sessions. The pull-request notice often never clears because unrelated runtime and run-registry events wipe prepared PR snapshots, sessions deferred by the per-batch PR load budget enter 60 s–15 min failure backoff instead of retrying on the next wave, and the Sessions board service never schedules a wake-up when `retryAt` becomes due. Meanwhile, the agent filter ran only client-side after the server sliced the first 100 sessions, forcing the extra disclaimer above the board.

## User Impact

- Background pull-request loading finishes in bounded waves and survives unrelated agent-run, subagent, catalog, profile, and transcript events instead of repeatedly resetting to stale or unloaded states.
- Routine background PR loading no longer shows an orange warning banner above the columns; warnings stay reserved for actual session-fact outages and GitHub rate limiting.
- Selecting an agent on a Sessions board filters all authorized sessions on the server before paging (without widening the board's saved `scope.agentIds`), removing the client-side filter caveat.
- When more than 100 matching sessions exist, a compact pagination footer (`Showing X of Y sessions` + **Load more sessions**) renders below the board viewport so columns start immediately under the toolbar.
- No migrations, config changes, or breaking RPC changes; `workboard.sessionsBoard.read` accepts an optional `view.agentId` filter.

## Why This Change Was Made

All three defects lived at existing owners:

1. **Prepared PR snapshot retention** (`src/gateway/control-ui-session-pr-prepared-read.ts`): narrowed `subscribeFacts` invalidation using `sessionChangeScopeAffectsStoredRows` (plus `config` and stored-row mutations) so unrelated run, catalog, profile, category, and transcript events stop clearing prepared PR snapshots.
2. **Deferred wave retries and board wake-up** (`src/gateway/session-facts-read.ts`, `extensions/workboard/src/sessions-board.ts`): separated budget-deferred PR loads from genuine failures so deferred sessions retry promptly (2 s wave delay without escalating failure backoff), and made the Sessions board respect `source.retryAt` both in projection expiry and via a bounded wake timer.
