prs.title: improve: remove the address bar from the link reader
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The link reader that opens pull requests, issues and commits beside the chat puts a browser address bar above every document: Back and Forward, the item's URL in an editable field, a new-tab button, Refresh, a link to the original, and a menu. It takes a full row of a narrow panel, and its main parts go unused. Links in chat already open in their own reader tab, so the URL field and the history buttons serve only a link followed inside a document, and the document header right under the bar already names the item.

Stacked on #203982, which this pull request targets. It can retarget `main` once that one lands.

## User Impact

The document starts one row higher, and the reader has one way to move between items: tabs.

- **Document header:** Refresh and the link to the original (for example **Open on GitHub**) are two icon buttons at the end of the header's first line.
- **Links inside a document:** a link to another supported item opens in its own tab, as a link in chat does. A link to the same item, such as a comment anchor, stays in its tab. Back and Forward are gone.
- **Refresh outcome:** a failed refresh, or a notice that the item changed, shows as text where the date was, in the same line. It used to sit behind a tooltip and a menu.
- **Empty tab:** the tab strip's **+** opens an empty tab with a URL field, as before. This is the only place where a URL is typed.
- **Removed:** the **Copy link** menu item. The link to the original still offers the browser's own copy action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vyctor's review of the redesigned reader: the bar at the top does not earn its place, since new links open new tabs; only the link to the original needs a new home.

Decisions worth a reviewer's attention:

- **One item per tab.** With no address bar there is no visible way back from a link followed inside a document, so that link opens a tab instead of replacing the document. The per-tab history, its 30-entry bound and the `newTab: false` routing exception are removed; a tab now holds one target.
- **Actions live at the top of the document, not in a fixed row.** Refresh and the external link scroll away with the header. Refresh still keeps the reading position; the browser tests dispatch the click for that reason and say so.
- **A notice outranks the reference.** In a phone-width panel the header's first line cannot fit both, so the reference truncates and the notice keeps its width. The row height never changes, so the title below does not move.
- **Two strings changed** to fit their new place: the "item changed" notice is shorter, and the screen-reader text for a refresh in flight reads as a sentence.

Known limits: opening the reader from the Chat side panel's **+** menu for the first time does not focus the URL field (unchanged). Typing the URL of an item that is already open in another tab loads it in the empty tab instead of selecting the existing one (unchanged; only links deduplicate).

Size against #203982: production TypeScript +80 −247, styles +37 −109, tests +85 −145, docs +18 −16.

## Evidence

Same reader panel and document in the preview bench (simulated Gateway, dark theme), at 820 px and 400 px. Before is #203982 at `f8e3071c4803`; After is this branch.

**Before**

![Before: an address bar with Back, Forward, a URL field, new tab, Refresh, a GitHub link and a menu sits above the document](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c93c578d-fe6e-4a1d-9592-7e3a12bd4f8f)

**After**

![After: the document starts under the tab strip, with Refresh and Open on GitHub as two icons at the end of the header's first line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5196781-ac6b-4b31-bdf6-8a91d02a06ff)

At 400 px:

**Before**

![Before, 400 px: the address bar takes a row and truncates the URL](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35d690e2-64c1-4b77-9be0-97b5cc0408d8)

**After**

![After, 400 px: the header's first line holds the state, the reference, the date and the two actions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4888188c-31af-4042-9b87-dbbb5b947da3)

Checked on the final commit: reader panel, content and routing tests; the GitHub panel, checks, loading, refresh and Activity browser tests. The refresh browser test now uses a realistic reference and asserts, at 1400, 820 and 390 px, that the failure notice is fully visible and that the title keeps its position. Lint for the touched files, the style lint, UI typecheck, format and the i18n check are clean. Local autoreview of the commit before the copy pass found no P0–P2 issues; the later changes were wording, two strings, the notice's width rule and its test.

Gap: layout shift was not re-measured against a real isolated Gateway for this change; the header row's height is unchanged, and the mocked-Gateway browser tests cover the title's position.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```
pnpm test ui/src/components/link-reader-panel.test.ts ui/src/components/link-reader-content.test.ts ui/src/app/link-reader-routing.test.ts
pnpm test ui/src/e2e/github-panel.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/link-reader-checks.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/link-reader-loading.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/link-reader-refresh.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/activity-session-git.e2e.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:ui && pnpm ui:i18n:verify && pnpm check:control-ui-controllers
pnpm exec stylelint --config config/stylelint.config.mjs "ui/src/components/link-reader-*.css"
```

</details>

prs.title: fix: recover automations from deleted accounts with configured keys
prs.body:
Closes #205579

## What Problem This Solves

After an automation's saved inference account is removed, editing it to a plain model reports success but leaves the deleted account bound. The next run fails even when a fresh job on that model works with the configured API key. The recovery message also recommends an account-listing command that refuses to run while the Gateway is online.

## User Impact

An explicit plain-model edit can recover a deleted-account job onto an environment or provider-config key without recreating the job. Available accounts remain bound, including personal accounts. Unrelated edits and clearing the model override do not release the binding.

Recovery refuses another stored account or a missing credential instead of silently switching accounts or accepting a broken edit. Choosing a stored account still requires `model@profile`, and same-provider recovery cannot change the recorded runtime. Both account-error messages now point to `openclaw gateway call models.authStatus`. The deleted-account error also shows `openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model <provider/model>` for recovery onto an environment or provider-config key.

## Why This Change Was Made

I kept the intentional account continuity introduced by #172590 and scoped recovery to an explicit edit after account removal. I reused the credential authorization owner, the existing route planner and the existing binding-clear operation. There is no new setting, schema, migration or automatic fallback.

Compatibility: `CronStoredJob.inferenceBinding` remains optional and its representation is unchanged. The existing `src/cron/store/job-mutations.ts` update path already deletes that field for an explicitly validated `null` binding, as used for native-login adoption. This change reuses that operation; it does not rewrite jobs on load or upgrade. The regression tests reopen the persisted job, and the separate Gateway run retained the existing job ID, schedule and history. I did not run an upgrade rehearsal.

I also updated the account-recovery documentation.

## Evidence

- The independent real-Gateway and scheduler reproduction on main `d8fc8b7a5390` is described in #205579. I used that supplied reproduction rather than starting another Gateway.
- I ran the regression assertions against unchanged main source at `aecbf92d24e54dd24f3c93299209404f53f72367`: all six failed for the expected behavior. The environment/config-key cases kept the deleted binding, the unsafe/no-credential edits incorrectly reported success, and both execution paths printed the offline-only hint.
- On the recovery implementation, **99 tests passed across four focused files**, including all six regression cases and existing personal-account, explicit-rebinding, runtime and credential-isolation coverage. Total wrapper wall time: **337.24 seconds**. The Gateway owner suite took 251.41 seconds; the three cron suites took 81.92 seconds. These existing suites use the real SQLite/auth owners and reopen persisted jobs; they are not a live provider or scheduler run. Final-head CI completed successfully in **19 minutes 41 seconds** ([run 45716574064](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45716574064)); that is workflow elapsed time, not per-test CPU time.
- Production typecheck, the Gateway-method and cron-test typechecks, changed-file lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- I ran the repository's `pr-simplify` author pass before final verification. The change reuses existing owners without a new recovery abstraction or test-only production seam. Delta against main: production **+51 lines**, tests **+69 lines**, docs **+10 lines**. The guidance change extends the existing error and its two execution-path regressions; the simplification pass required no extra helper or test scaffold.
- On the final code, I reran the three cron files: **50 tests passed**, including both removed-account paths checking the plain-model recovery command. Those two assertions fail without the message change. Test-wrapper wall time was **120.65 seconds** (118.35 seconds inside Vitest). Production and cron-test typechecks, changed-file lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed again.
- **Local independent review unavailable:** autoreview could not launch Codex in its required read-only sandbox. I preserved the sandbox restrictions; no clean independent-review result is claimed.

Focused test command:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/server-methods/cron.inference-binding.test.ts \
  src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-profile-propagation.test.ts \
  src/cron/inference-binding.test.ts \
  src/cron/inference-binding-executor.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

### External runtime verification

The separately supplied runtime check passed on `aec99054cb5f` across four isolated Gateways, using `OPENAI_API_KEY` in some and `models.providers.openai.apiKey` in others.

On main, removing the bound account and making a plain-model edit left both the manual run and the next scheduled run failing on the deleted account. With the PR, both runs succeeded on the static key. The job ID, schedule and history were preserved; a valid binding survived a plain edit; explicitly selecting another shared account worked; and adopting a personal account was refused.

I did not run those Gateways myself. The runtime logic is unchanged from that verified commit; the final delta adds only the plain-model recovery example and its assertions.

**Not verified:** rendered final-head error capture or real-provider billing. Final-head CI is green for `c5b972de41ca526f0ec5844096b6240b73975a05`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency review and security-sensitive review. [ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205592#issuecomment-7176811131): **ready for maintainer review**, no findings and no before-merge items. Its remaining proof note asks for inspectable sanitized output from the separately run Gateways and a shipped-entry-point capture of the final diagnostic; those artifacts are not attached.

Contributor credit: reported and requested by Dan Riccio.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-stuck-automation-account-fix-sa1bf3641)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search

Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson (closed for inactivity on 2026-11-18): their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.11.6 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. - Patterns are workspace-relative globs. A leading `./` or `/` and a trailing `/` are accepted (`memory/dreaming/` is the same as `memory/dreaming/**`), and per-agent lists add to the global list. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, using the same minimatch options as the `extraPaths` matcher beside it in the memory host SDK (so patterns behave the same on Node and Bun), is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). **Portable glob matching (ClawSweeper's 2026-11-09 review on `05585b7`):** the exclusion matcher called `path.posix.matchesGlob`, which Bun implements with `Bun.Glob`: extglobs never match and wildcards match dotfiles, so `["memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md"]` excluded a report on Node but not on Bun. Main's #194912 had just moved the `extraPaths` matcher to minimatch for the same reason. `1463f6e` moves those minimatch options into one shared constant and uses it for `excludePaths` too, with compiled matchers cached per configured list. Results on Node are unchanged; on Bun they now match Node. **Pattern spellings (`2b7dc7f`):** gitignore-style spellings such as `memory/dreaming/`, `./memory/dreaming/**` or `/memory/dreaming/**` excluded nothing. `resolveMemorySearchIndexConfig`, which every reader (scan, watcher, scope hash, remote file worker) gets its settings from, now normalizes each entry once: trim, drop empty entries, use `/` separators, strip one leading `./` or `/`, turn a trailing `/` into `/**`, and dedupe in order. The matcher is unchanged. The docs and help example drop `memory/.dreams/**`: that folder only holds `.txt` and `.json` dreaming state, which memory search never indexes. Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main `a2f7aa9`: production +102/-21 in 15 files (including moving main's glob options into the shared constant); tests +159/-3; docs +18/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2668 -> 2672 on main `a2f7aa9`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on `78d4f9f` (on main `431392a`), starting from the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.11.6` from npm (installed with `--ignore-scripts`; the CLI runs without the package's install scripts). The current head `fa31efc` adds only a merge of main `a2f7aa9`. Earlier runs from 2026.11.5 on `59298b8`, from 2026.11.4 on `ddb2348`, from 2026.11.3 on `c210875`, from 2026.11.2 on `1463f6e` and on `05585b7` (before the portable-matcher change), from 2026.11.1 on `6d9ace7` and from 2026.10.10 on `b607675` showed the same behavior. Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade from 2026.11.6 and existing data:** 2026.11.6 builds the index (10 files, 10 chunks). After this branch's `doctor --fix` (main's agent-database migrations since 2026.11.6, v38 -> v43), the existing index loads clean (`Dirty: no`) and returns the same results and scores as 2026.11.6, before any re-index. With `excludePaths` unset, `memory index` keeps the stored scope hash, the chunking version and every stored chunk row (same count and same fingerprint over `id`, `path`, `hash`). This PR adds no database schema or stored fields; the scope hash changes only when `excludePaths` is set. The branch build prints main's version string, 2026.11.5, because 2026.11.6 shipped from a release branch. **Opting in:** setting `excludePaths` marks the index dirty with a scope change and pauses vector search until a rebuild, both shown in `memory status`. `memory index` then drops the 7 reports and keeps the 3 curated files; the curated note ranks first, and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.11.6 OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.223 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.218 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.213 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.208 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.204 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.11.6): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (2026.11.6): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (78d4f9f) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.11.6 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v38 -> v43 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 10 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main # existing 2026.11.6 index, before any re-index 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.223 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.218 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.213 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.208 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.204 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (this branch, no excludePaths): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Pattern spelling on `2b7dc7f`:** the same synthetic workspace with a trailing-slash pattern, `["memory/dreaming/"]`, which matched nothing before `2b7dc7f`.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw --version OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (2b7dc7f) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.249 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.243 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.238 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.232 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.227 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw config get memory.search.excludePaths [ "memory/dreaming/" ] $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher: a local chat-completions stub calls `memory_search` once, through `dispatch_action`, because current main keeps `memory_search` behind Tool Search for this model. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within about 2 s and never indexes the report.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback ... # throwaway Gateway [gateway] ready $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "When does the nightly backup run?" # stub model calls memory_search once via dispatch_action Done. tool call: dispatch_action {"id":"memory_search","args":{"query":"nightly backup"}} # memory_search result paths (from the stub log): memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~2s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```
**Regressions fail without the fix:** - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` "rebaselines shared exclusions when a differently scoped agent joins and leaves" fails with `excludePaths` removed from `selectionKeys` ("expected setScopes to be called once, but got 0 times"). - `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` "drops generated Dream reports once excluded and keeps curated edits fresh" fails when the config resolver drops `excludePaths` (the report is still found). - `internal.test.ts` "keeps generated dreaming reports out of default and overlapping extra paths" also lists files with `memory/dreaming/**/!(*.keep).md`. With the old `path.posix.matchesGlob` matcher, `listMemoryFiles` under Bun still returns the report: on stock Bun 1.3.14 it lists `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md, memory/dreaming/light/report.md`, and with `1463f6e` only `memory/current.md, memory/dreaming/light/pinned.keep.md`. On Node both matchers agree, so the Node run passes either way; the CI shard that runs this test (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-6`) sets up the pinned Bun 1.4.4 test runtime. **Changed test files** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `685db0c`, same test code as `8eb4b7b`): | File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` | 29 passed | 48s | 41.65s | | `manager-reindex-state.test.ts` | 49 passed | 40s | 36.19s | | `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` | 11 passed | 71s | 64.91s | | `watch-policy.test.ts` | 6 passed | 47s | 41.51s | | `internal.test.ts` | 43 passed | 4s | 749ms | | `memory-search.test.ts` | 39 passed | 46s | 42.06s | Vitest time is mostly cold transform; the new manager case takes about 4 s and the other new cases take 1-24 ms. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` on `83eb31b` (main `200afde`, same code) passes typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports, plugin boundaries and the other changed-file guards. Three lanes fail outside this PR: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection`) and the public Plugin SDK surface budget (`agent-harness-runtime`) fail identically on clean main `200afde`, and the dead-export scan lists only auto-reply, gateway and UI exports this PR does not touch. The `pnpm check:docs` content checks pass. Test lines grow by a net +154, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/memory-search-exclude-paths-188294.txt`: default scope-hash compatibility, the shared-watcher rebaseline, discovery and portable (Node/Bun) glob matching, and the exclusion rebuild. **PR CI:** CI has not run on the current head `fa31efc` (merging main `a2f7aa9`) or on the seven heads before it: GitHub holds this fork PR's workflows until a maintainer clicks "Approve and run" (`action_required`), so `openclaw/ci-gate` shows failure until CI completes. The last completed run, on `fc2ef72`, passed 72 checks; its three failing memory-core tests are in files this PR does not touch, failed the same way on main without this PR, and main fixed them in #197543. Earlier red runs also came from main and were fixed there. Merges of main conflicted only on the generated config baseline, which was regenerated each time. The full CI history is in this description's edit history. **Local review:** autoreview, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode against `upstream/main`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, "patch is correct" (0.87). It ran on `685db0c`, before the rebases onto `200afde` and `f980e01`, which changed only the base and the generated baseline files. For `2b7dc7f`: autoreview with the Claude engine, local mode, P0–P2: scoped-clean, "patch is correct" (0.8). On `2b7dc7f`, `memory-search.test.ts` (39/39; the updated case fails on `e768746`), `schema.help.quality.test.ts`, `internal.test.ts` and `workspace-memory-client.test.ts` pass, as do `tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt, `check:docs`, `config:docs:check` and the test-line ratchet. On `fa31efc` (main `a2f7aa9`), `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `config:docs:check`, `prompt:snapshots:check`, oxfmt on this PR's files, `check:docs` and the test-line ratchet (net +154, covered by the allocation) pass, and so do the touched tests plus neighboring memory tests (18 files). Locally, one `cli.test.ts` test from main's #197543 (`fails index --force after full verification records orphaned provenance`) fails; it fails the same way on main `a2f7aa9` without this PR. Not covered: Windows paths (the matcher normalizes `path.sep`) and a live remote node workspace (the harness test checks that list and watch requests carry `excludePaths`).

prs.title: fix: explain how to recover from automation scratch errors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Gateway returns `UNAVAILABLE` in Automation scratch, the editor shows a technical error without telling you what to do next. Reloading replaces the draft with the saved version, so reloading without first copying your edits can lose your work.

## User Impact

The panel now names the next step for an unavailable load, reload, save, or removal. After a reload error, copy any edits you want to keep before reloading again. After an unconfirmed save or removal, copy your edits and reload to check what’s saved before making another write. The redacted diagnostic is still available under **Show details**. Other errors, including access and revision conflicts, keep their existing messages. Scratch actions and draft lifetimes are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor already knows which request it sent. Use that context to name **Load scratch** or **Reload scratch** without adding a new retry control. An unavailable response doesn’t confirm what was stored. Reloading checks the current state without issuing another write.

## Evidence

**Context:** Automations → Greenhouse stock check → Edit → Automation scratch. The production Control UI build ran in 1280 × 900 light-mode Chromium against a connected synthetic Gateway. The fixture explicitly returned `UNAVAILABLE` without changing its saved notes. This was not a lost-acknowledgement or live persistence test.

**Before (exact rendered fixture text for all four operations):**

> Synthetic scratch request unavailable

**After (exact rendered copy):**

| Operation | Copy |
| --- | --- |
| Load | Couldn’t load scratch. Use Load scratch to try again. |
| Reload | Couldn’t reload scratch. Copy any edits you want to keep before trying Reload scratch again. |
| Save | OpenClaw couldn’t confirm the save. Copy any edits you want to keep, then use Reload scratch to check what’s saved. |
| Remove | OpenClaw couldn’t confirm removal. Copy any edits you want to keep, then use Reload scratch to check what’s saved. |

**Skill in practice:** [OpenClaw writing: error messages](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/.agents/skills/openclaw-writing/references/error-messages.md) separates recovery guidance from diagnostics and keeps uncertain results uncertain. The new copy names the next control and leaves the write outcome unconfirmed. **Show details** preserves the diagnostic without making it the headline.

- Four browser scenarios passed on pinned main (`1bc412fb7478`) and the patch. The patched build showed the new copy and disclosed the diagnostic on request. Failed reload, save, and removal kept the edits visible until the reader chose to reload. Reload did not issue a second write. In the rejected-save fixture, a separately initiated save succeeded after reloading and restoring the edits.
- The scratch editor and its consuming Automations page passed 41 focused tests. The save and reload copy assertions failed on main for the intended reason. UI typecheck, targeted Solid/TypeScript and CSS lint, formatting, controller guard, i18n verification, and diff checks passed. Broad CI and live Gateway proof were not run.

### Clean comparison: Save scratch

Pinned main `1bc412fb7478` and draft head `aadbb8753e6b2` (the same tree as the locally tested `57faa005af0b`). The Gateway rejection is synthetic.

**Before**

![Before: Save scratch shows only a raw unavailable error beneath the retained edits](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7826b167-5fa0-40ee-b176-b0ed71e0763f)

**After**

![After: Save scratch asks the reader to copy edits and reload to check what was saved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3ab3561f-fec0-4fb0-bec4-240afad63402)

### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Before, annotated: the raw error does not offer a recovery step](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc2febe8-756a-4bcf-8cfa-b0633afc5813)

**After**

![After, annotated: the copy recommends checking what is saved before another write](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c591e31a-0864-4895-ac01-34b8375d3def)

[Supplementary screenshots: expanded diagnostic and load, reload, and remove states](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205618#issuecomment-7177433118).

Co-authored with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e346c5e4-f828-45b2-be8f-1aad6754fbad)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5b082270-7815-4fe2-9039-0d5a2cc0311e)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: test(qa-lab): replayed plugin media paths stay text in the next provider request
prs.body:
Closes #168610
Related: #101866

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: nothing fails when a media path from a plugin tool registered under a core tool name, replayed from Telegram history, reaches the next provider request as an image or file input or with its text rewritten.

## User Impact

User impact: no runtime change. QA Lab gains a Crabline Telegram regression on the final provider request for replayed media references, and a mock-provider directive that scripts exact tool calls. The Crabline dependency patch gains Telegram reply ingress, used only by QA, so that regression can send its second turn as a reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR used to expect replay to rewrite the plugin's path to `[unverified media reference removed]/generated/...`, the behavior #101866 proposed. That expectation was wrong. #101866 was closed unmerged on October 31, and the [closing comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101866#issuecomment-6541917131) found that on main replayed references stay literal text, produce no `input_image` or `input_file` payloads, and leave stored rows unchanged. It asks that a follow-up preserve stable conversation bytes and start from a final-provider-request regression. This PR is that regression.

`telegram-plugin-core-name-media-history` installs a run-owned, non-bundled plugin that registers `music_generate` and returns a PNG under the state media directory. No music provider is configured, so the plugin's tool is the one that runs. The state media directory is a local media root, so the prompt image loader would accept that file. Turn 1 calls the tool and replies with the path through the real Telegram plugin. The last provider request on turn 2 must have:

- no `input_image` or `input_file` part anywhere in `input`, and `imageInputCount` 0;
- the turn 1 reply, byte for byte, as the bot's own `(you):` line in the Telegram chat window of the current turn's runtime context, and separately in the earlier assistant message.

Turn 2 is a Telegram reply to the bot's turn 1 message. Since #183190, an existing plain Telegram DM carries its history in the session transcript and leaves the chat window out of the turn's runtime context; replies, topics, groups and fresh DMs keep it (`shouldSuppressPersistedDmChatWindowContext` in `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.session.ts`). Sent as a plain DM, turn 2's request has no window line for the reply. On the reply path the window is the plugin's own (`Conversation context (chronological, selected for current message)`), which names the bot's messages `<first_name> (you)` (`buildTelegramSelfSenderName` in `extensions/telegram/src/group-history-window.ts`), so the check matches `(you): ` followed by the exact reply. The reply quote, `[Replying to: "..."]`, carries the same text without that prefix.

`QA tool plan:` works as before: the mock calls each listed tool in order with the given arguments, then replies, and `{{media:N}}` becomes the first media path the Nth result carried. It now sits at the end of main's scripted automation chain, so `server.ts` is identical to main.

pr-simplify, against merge base `f5f27c3ef6e`:

- Removed: the placeholder expectation and its `path.sep` suffix; the unmanaged control path, which only made sense for selective redaction; the `server.ts` hunk, which after merging main grew it from 2251 to 2253 counted lines against the line-cap ratchet; and the `exec_command` ordering case with its cron argument checks, which test the cron planner rather than this change.
- Still protected: a plan never preempts a scripted cron turn, plan order and media substitution, undeclared tools, drive-rooted Windows paths, and Code Mode `wait`.
- Delta against main `5767fe7aae6`: no production code. qa-lab mock +119/-2; tests +155/-1 (`server.tool-plan.test.ts` +124, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/qa-tool-plan-directive-168610.txt`, and the Crabline reply case +31/-1); qa-lab reply mapping +43/-1 (`crabline-telegram-replies.ts` +33, `crabline-transport.ts` +10/-1); scenario +240; Crabline patch +125; `patches/README.md` +2; `pnpm-lock.yaml` 4 patch-hash lines.

Crabline patch: Crabline 0.2.0's Telegram server had no reply ingress. Admin inbound never set `reply_to_message`, the server kept no sent messages to quote, and its `sendMessage` events did not carry the assigned `message_id`, so the harness could not name the bot's message. For Telegram only, `patches/@openclaw__crabline@0.2.0.patch` now keeps accepted sends, `editMessageText` results and admin inbound messages by chat and `message_id`, records `messageId` on accepted send events, and turns an admin inbound `replyToMessageId` into a Bot API `reply_to_message` (without a nested reply), refusing an unknown target with `message to be replied not found`. The bridge forwards `OpenClawCrablineInboundInput.replyToId` as that field. The patch grows by 125 lines; its existing Feishu hunks are byte-identical, Crabline stays at 0.2.0, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` changes only its 4 patch-hash lines (`87093d75728e` -> `616107004291`). qa-lab maps a bot send's bus ID to the recorded `messageId` in `crabline-telegram-replies.ts`; inbound bus IDs already are Telegram message IDs. `patches/README.md` records the hunks and the test that retires them. Crabline main has the same gap; filed upstream as openclaw/crabline#377, offering the patch as a PR there so this one can go.

## Evidence

### Update 2026-11-25 (head `a5a54185d6b`)

Fixed the P2 in `a5a54185d6b`. `mock-openai-tool-plan.ts` now counts a step only when `isResponsesToolCallOutput(item)` holds, so standalone context without a call ID (the `notifications`/`slack` record from the finding) no longer completes a plan step.

New HTTP case in `server.tool-plan.test.ts`, "does not count standalone context as a completed QA tool plan step": a one-call `music_generate` plan with that context record after the plan message. On `3ee90ab042f` it fails with `Expected music_generate tool call`; a probe showed the planner skipping the tool and replying `plugin BUG-QA-TOOL-PLAN-NO-MEDIA-0`, as the review described. With the fix the tool call comes first and then `plugin /state/media/generated/b.mp3`, so the context record does not shift the `{{media:N}}` index either.

- `server.tool-plan`, `server.automation-context` and `server.progress`: 36 of 36, twice.
- `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` pass; each fails on an injected TS2322 as a control. oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Test cost: `pnpm test extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.tool-plan.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` is 13 s wall (9.4 s Vitest); the new case takes 3 to 12 ms. +172 net test lines, inside the 400 allowance.
- Merges cleanly with main `1bc412fb747`. Of the PR's 11 files, main has changed only `pnpm-lock.yaml` since the base `eee7a1bd526` (`19520dd133d`, the Codex 0.172.0 bump). On that merge `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes, and `server.tool-plan` 6/6, `server.automation-context` 9/9, `server.progress` 21/21 and `crabline-transport-message-id` 4/4 pass twice each.


### Merged with main `eee7a1bd526` (head `3ee90ab042f`, 2026-11-24)

The branch was 2,490 commits behind. `3ee90ab042f` merges main; the only conflict was `pnpm-lock.yaml` at the Crabline importer entry, where main added `@openclaw/fs-safe-captured-0.27.1` and this PR changes the patch hash. Both are kept. Main still pins `@openclaw/crabline` 0.2.0 and has not touched `patches/@openclaw__crabline@0.2.0.patch` since this branch's base, so the patch applies to the same package bytes. The lockfile differs from main's only in this PR's 4 patch-hash lines (`87093d75728e` -> `616107004291`), and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes. On an M4 Pro, Node 26.12.1:

- QA Lab `telegram-plugin-core-name-media-history` over the Crabline Telegram driver (mock-openai, `--fast`): passes 1/1. A non-bundled plugin serves `music_generate`, and the next provider request replays the saved path as text (`mediaParts: 0`, `imageInputCount: 0`).
- 32 qa-lab test files (every `crabline-*.test.ts`, the Feishu wire round trip included, and every mock-openai test): 286 passed, 0 failed.
- `deps:patches:check` (`no new pnpm patches; 17 approved patches allowlisted`) and `deps:npm-lock:check:changed` pass.
- Static checks on the merge, with `--base eee7a1bd526` where a check takes one: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `check:test-types` 0 errors; oxlint and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files; the line-cap, assertion-safety and mock-export ratchets, the conflict-marker check and the PR wrapper inventory test (`eager-import-closure.test.ts`) pass. `check-test-lines-ratchet`: net +154, the same as before the merge; the 124-line allocation covers `server.tool-plan.test.ts`.

Upstream Crabline fixed the gap in openclaw/crabline#378 (`057c00af631`, 2026-11-21), which closed openclaw/crabline#377. No release carries it yet: the latest is 0.2.2, published 2026-11-16. So the Telegram hunks stay until an upstream release passes the Telegram reply case in `crabline-transport-message-id.test.ts` without them, as `patches/README.md` says. The Feishu codec hunks in the same patch have their own removal condition.

### Merged with main `5767fe7aae6`, turn 2 as a reply (head `e3e14dbee94`)

Main `5767fe7aae6` merged in (`314bb6233df`), then `27a15890e05` for the reply and the Crabline patch, and `e3e14dbee94` for the window check. On an M4 Pro, same command as below:

- This head passes twice: 1/1, 19.6 s and 20.2 s for the scenario (76 s and 23 s for the command; the first includes the build). The checked line: `#3 … [reply target] Crabline (you): QA-CORE-NAMED-<id> plugin <state>/media/generated/qa-core-named-<id>.png`, with 0 media parts and `imageInputCount` 0.
- Turn 2 sent as a plain DM, without `replyToId`, fails the window check. Its request has 0 `(you): <reply>` lines, 0 reply quotes and no copy of the reply at all: the runtime context is the conversation info and no window (#183190).
- With the reply kept and only the window line's reply text replaced before the check, it fails too. That request still has `[Replying to: "<reply>"]` once, so the quote alone does not satisfy the check.
- With main's `mock-openai-automation-turns.ts`, turn 1 fails: `timed out after 90000ms; final bus-event kinds=[inbound-message,outbound-message]`. Turn 1 waits up to 90 s for a reply carrying the marker. Main's mock has no `QA tool plan:` directive, so it never calls `music_generate`; its one reply, sent 1 s after the inbound, is `Protocol note: acknowledged. Continue with the QA scenario plan and report worked, failed, and blocked items.` That run was on `27a15890e05`; `e3e14dbee94` only changes turn 2's check.
- The merge alone, before the reply, failed the old history check because main's #183190 dropped the window from the plain-DM turn 2. Removing that one `deliveryOnly` line locally made it pass.

Unit and gates on this head:

- 37 qa-lab test files pass: 14 mock-openai files, the 6 catalog and report files, every `crabline-*.test.ts` (the Feishu wire round trip included) and `proper-lockfile-runtime.test.ts`. Main's #198943 deleted `server.tool-routing.test.ts`, so the plan cases now live in `server.tool-plan.test.ts` (124 lines, 5 cases).
- With main's `mock-openai-automation-turns.ts`, 4 of the 5 plan cases fail (`Expected music_generate tool call`, and `expected 'Protocol note: acknowledged. Continue…' to be 'BUG-QA-TOOL-PLAN-UNDECLARED…'`). That is the same shape as the scenario's turn-1 timeout: main's mock answers a plan with its generic protocol note. The earlier evidence below removed the plan at this unit level only; it had no scenario run with main's mock.
- The new `crabline-transport-message-id.test.ts` case replies to the first of two bot sends and reads `reply_to_message` with that send's text back from `getUpdates`. With main's Crabline patch installed it fails: `Telegram QA reply target <uuid> has no Crabline message_id.`
- On `27a15890e05`: `tsgo` (7 lanes, 0 errors), oxlint, oxfmt, the test-lines (+154, allowance 400, credit 124), line-cap, max-lines and assertion-safety ratchets, `deps:patches:check`, `deps:npm-lock:check:changed` and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` pass, and the installed Crabline files match all 8 target blobs in the patch. On `e3e14dbee94`, which only changes the scenario: oxfmt on it, the two scenario catalog test files and the four ratchets pass.
- Cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, macOS arm64, two runs): `crabline-transport-message-id.test.ts` 37.6 s cold and 9.8 s warm wall, the new case about 300 ms. `server.tool-plan.test.ts` 32.8 s and 6.1 s.

### Earlier head `fa0ef91b76c`

Main `f5f27c3ef6e` merged in, on an M4 Pro, with `node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --channel-driver crabline --channel telegram --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario telegram-plugin-core-name-media-history --concurrency 1 --fast`:

- That head passed: 1/1, 22.4 s for the scenario, 105 s for the whole command including the build. The second request has 0 media parts, `imageInputCount` 0, and 2 replayed copies of the reply, both with the path unchanged.
- With a local patch that makes prompt image preparation also scan the replayed inbound history, it fails: `the replayed plugin path became provider media: {"mediaParts":["\"type\":\"input_image\""],"imageInputCount":1}`.
- With a local patch that rewrites the replayed channel-history text the way #101866 did, it fails: `second request did not replay the first reply with the plugin path unchanged`. The assistant-message copy kept the path; the channel-history copy read `[unverified media reference removed]/generated/qa-core-named-<id>.png`.
- With channel-history replay disabled locally (history limit 0), it fails: `the current turn's channel history did not replay the first reply unchanged`. The previous head `e57316ac0fa` passed that same run on the assistant-message copy alone, which is the gap ClawSweeper found.
- None of these patches is on the branch.

Unit and gates on that head:

- The `server.tool-routing.test.ts` and qa-lab catalog tests (scenario catalog and channels, coverage report, CI smoke plan, profile selection, tool coverage report) pass: 7 files, 102 tests. All 13 mock-openai test files pass: 200 tests.
- Removing the plan from the chain fails the four plan cases. Putting it first fails the ordering case (`Expected message tool call`).
- oxfmt, type-aware oxlint (a planted error is reported), `tsgo:all`, and the line-cap, assertion-safety, test-timeout-race and max-lines ratchets pass.
- The test-lines ratchet reports `over by: 10` with this change's +92 allocated. Those 10 lines are already over on main.

Cost: the scenario is crabline-only and its primary coverage ID, `plugins.plugin-tools`, is not in `smoke-ci`, so nothing per-PR runs it unless selected.

- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `server.tool-routing.test.ts` 32.8 s (cold worker cache, 24.3 s of it compiling) and 6.8 s wall, 525 ms and 403 ms of tests. CI run 42426840111, Bun: `server.tool-routing.test.ts` 999 ms of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-extensions-config`).

Not covered:
- A trusted core tool's managed path; I did not look for a synchronous core tool in QA that returns one.

prs.title: test: cover seeded reply-marker retention across private completion
prs.body:
Related: #173650

## What Problem This Solves

The existing tests did not check whether a requester's already-persisted final-delivery marker survives a transcript-only private subagent completion. This PR covers that constructed retention scenario.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. This does not fix the missed user update in #173650 or reproduce its obligation lifecycle from spawn through settlement.

## Why This Change Was Made

The test drives the announcement, requester-command and tool-policy owners, with an outstanding `pendingFinalDelivery` marker supplied by the fixture. It checks the private instruction, effective tool availability, marker retention and absence of a requester-visible delivery receipt.

My earlier claim that the issue review settled the historical cause as model follow-through was wrong. That distinction remains unresolved. Retaining a seeded marker does not establish whether the reported owed update ever acquired that marker or how its registry obligation was settled. The test header at `ae52c5a61701` already states this limit; the description now does too.

## Evidence

### Update 2026-11-25 (head `d0ac4439e28`)

For `d0ac4439e28`, described in my comment above: main `00a9cbf6d65` merged in, and the fixture binds the delegated handoff to its configured route, since #203271 removed `DEFAULT_MODEL`. It still merges cleanly with main `1bc412fb747`. Since `00a9cbf6d65`, main has changed one of the PR's 4 files, `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs` (5 commits). On that merge, each twice: `agent-command.private-completion-obligation.test.ts` 3/3 and `subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts` 76/76.


**Shipped Gateway run, October 26, at `ae52c5a61701a6fa959280f4600a05632eae0b60`.** This PR changes only 3 test files, so the Gateway that ran is the production code of base `3e0475a199e5877f1b5e0c086437ef1fedd3b693`. Built on macOS arm64 with Node `24.22.1`, pnpm `12.15.0`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm build qaRuntime`; `dist/index.js` SHA-256 `2338a25698b877d2e7321c901ffff4fcab827eb100809251a3ed17bd3314e47b`. Each run had its own throwaway HOME, state and config, and started `node dist/index.js gateway run --bind loopback`. The real Telegram plugin polled a loopback Bot API stub, and the model was a loopback scripted Responses provider. No session state was seeded. No credentials or external endpoints were used.

The script follows #173650. One Telegram DM asks for a background read. The requester calls `sessions_spawn` with `completionTarget: "parent"` and replies "I'll relay the result here the moment it lands." The child returns `PR175029-CHILD-RESULT-7f3a`. In the private completion turn the scripted model replies with text and calls no tool.

Run 1: every `sendMessage` answers HTTP 500. 18:25:03 to 18:29:31 UTC, 8 of 8 checks passed. Harness output, IDs shortened:

```text
18:28:26 provider: requester turn -> sessions_spawn {"task":"PR175029-CHILD-TASK Reply with exactly PR175029-CHILD-RESULT-7f3a.","label":"pr175029-bounded-read","runtime":"subagent","completionTarget":"parent","context":"isolated"}
18:28:32 provider: requester continuation -> final text "PR175029-PROMISE I'll relay the result here the moment it lands."
18:28:39 db: at requester sendMessage, markers=[{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","intentId":"18c42769-...","kind":"replayable","deliveries":[{"id":"83ee452c-...","state":"queued"}]}]
18:28:39 telegram: sendMessage #1 answered 500 text="PR175029-PROMISE I'll relay the result here the moment it lands."
18:28:47 db: before child release, markers=[{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","intentId":"18c42769-...","deliveries":[{"id":"83ee452c-...","state":"unknown"}]}]
18:29:02 provider: private completion turn; tools=49 message=true; replying transcript-only, no tool call
18:29:18 db: after completion agent:main:main pendingFinalDelivery={"kind":"replayable","text":"PR175029-PROMISE I'll relay the result here the moment it lands.","intentId":"18c42769-...","deliveries":[{"id":"83ee452c-...","state":"unknown"}],...}
18:29:18 db: subagent_runs 2c6a2378-... completionTarget=parent expectsCompletionMessage=true completion.required=true delivery={"status":"delivered","disposition":"delivered",...}
18:29:18 PASS: The same marker (intentId) is still outstanding after the private completion
18:29:18 PASS: Marker contents are unchanged by the private completion
18:29:18 PASS: No channel send carried the private completion's final text
18:29:19 db: message_tool_run_outcomes rows=0; session_input_completions rows=1
18:29:20 db: requester transcript seq=11 role=assistant text="PR175029-RELAY Recorded privately: the child returned PR175029-CHILD-RESULT-7f3a."
18:29:20 telegram: sendMessage calls total=2 texts=["PR175029-PROMISE I'll relay the result here the moment it lands.","I couldn't deliver my reply. Please ask again."]
18:29:31 harness: done in 268.4s; 8/8 checks passed
```

- Marker creation: the requester's own turn persisted the `replayable` marker for its promise. It read `queued` when the send reached Telegram and `unknown` after the 500.
- Tool availability: the private completion request offered 49 tools, `message` among them, and carried `SUBAGENT_PRIVATE_COMPLETION_INSTRUCTION` ("Your final reply stays internal ... send it through an available, permitted messaging tool") plus the ledger line `outcome=ok; delivery=pending; requester_continuation=none`.
- Retention: the marker read just before the child was released and the marker read after the completion settled are identical, intent `18c42769` with delivery `83ee452c` still `unknown`.
- Delivery facts: the registry recorded the completion `delivered` with `completion.required=true`. `session_input_completions` has one row for `announce:v1:agent:main:subagent:...` with `status=ok`, `stopReason=stop`. `message_tool_run_outcomes` has 0 rows. The completion's text is transcript row 11 and was never sent. The only channel sends were the failed promise and the Telegram fallback notice, which also got a 500.

Run 2, control: every `sendMessage` succeeds. 18:29:31 to 18:31:11 UTC, 7 of 7 checks passed. The marker was present (`queued`) when the promise reached Telegram and was gone at the first read 0.7 s later. The private completion created no marker. The registry, `session_input_completions`, `message_tool_run_outcomes` and transcript facts match run 1, with one channel send in total.

So the scenario the new test pins now comes from the shipped Gateway instead of a fixture: a marker the requester created is retained, and not settled, by a transcript-only private completion that had `message` available. This does not reproduce #173650. There the promise was delivered and nothing was outstanding when the completion arrived, and here the no-send is scripted, not a model decision. I have not rerun this on current main.

Harness `proof-175029.mts` (Telegram stub, scripted provider and the database reads), SHA-256 `5fd7bbd867dad06164b2a62949224730843c3c9f299c44c8483cb60b11d52b6a`. Raw harness logs: run 1 SHA-256 `b1affd848176a44d17aaaceaa270226975fe9c2d9274b1aed14c949d34249928`, run 2 `544ec768ee7b6375b286fb9e935d49183e1b72dc9935cb28148c275c474c6f19`. Both Gateways exited 0 on SIGTERM.

**What the test covers.** The test calls real `runSubagentAnnounceFlow`, `agentCommandFromGatewayIngress` and `runAgentAttempt`. The Gateway method is an in-process adapter, the embedded model result is scripted, and tool factories are shared fast stubs. It seeds both `pendingFinalDelivery` and child spawn lineage. The three cases check:

- A verified private-completion handoff derives its origin-sensitive private instruction from the announce owner, permits `message` through the real policy pipeline, retains the same prepared marker, and returns `delivered: true` without `requesterVisibleFinalDelivered`.
- An operator `tools.deny: ["message"]` excludes `message` while retaining other tools and the marker.
- An unconsumed delegated handoff disables tools while retaining the marker.

The related existing private-text fixture asserts `deliver: false`, `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "automatic"`, no `sendMessage` call and no visible-final receipt. The new test is registered on the forked database-worker route.

**Historical validation, not a rerun of the current head:** at `778eafe7da02`, the new file passed 3 tests in each of 3 runs; announcement delivery passed 145; marker tests passed 5. Database-worker registry passed 12 at `58aeae3de18f`. Mutation controls failed when the parent instruction mapping or retained-tools policy was removed, and the deny case failed when global policy was skipped. These controls show sensitivity to those boundaries, not reproduction of the historical incident.

**Prior-head CI (before this adaptation):** [CI run 39845293165](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39845293165) completed successfully on CI merge `bfe4f403a373a480e866faf2b4af7442e4c0bcbe` (`ae52c5a61701` merged into base `67408f3f5422043acbf3fa5fae641567119c8455`). [Changed-1 job 120057533859](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39845293165/job/120057533859) records 3/3 private-completion obligation tests and 124/124 announcement-delivery tests. The dependency-review, security-sensitive-review and ci-gate commit statuses also report success from [gate run 39846815916](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39846815916).

**Compatibility adaptation and focused validation (October 29).** #182124 replaced the exported constant with `buildSubagentPrivateCompletionInstruction(requesterOrigin)`. The fixture now asserts the expected instruction as an independent literal and exercises the origin-sensitive path. Production behavior is unchanged.

The qualified source is tree `c9d281d8e85c1a124e1b4e02ce50c901bb9a122a` on base `4a2a1962d9caaf965c0432c7c9a84e5a40290f7d`, with Node `24.22.1`, pnpm `12.15.0`, pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1` and the frozen lockfile. Focused checks cover 150 distinct passing cases: 3 private-completion cases, 135 related announcement cases and 12 database-worker registry cases. Scoped lint, formatting, whitespace checks and the agents-root/agents-sessions test typechecks passed.

Reintroducing the removed export fails only at the fixture with TS2724. Replacing the requester origin passed to the private-instruction builder with `undefined` produces exactly the intended retention-case failure, with the other 2 cases passing. After restoring the source, the full three-case command passed and exited 0 in 99.08 seconds, including wrapper verification and cleanup; the supervisor confirmed source restoration and no remaining owned processes. Repeated confirmation cases are not added to the 150 total. Origin-negative log SHA-256: `d287960b9214e78c579212e96022715b40d90bb560711e6e88c475cf8bf4bf00`; restored-command log: `6ed67a655c0ab884cfe893871f2af65a5b8d7c6c4ac3dda38772a8c0a459af6c`. Interrupted attempts remain recorded as incomplete; their printed passes are not used as completed wrapper proof.

Reproduce the focused runtime and type checks with the pinned runtimes and dependencies:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-command.private-completion-obligation.test.ts --run --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json --incremental
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-sessions.json --incremental
```

Correction, 2026-11-03: an earlier version said current production creates only transport-only markers. That was wrong. The reply-runner path creates a `replayable` marker whenever the final has text (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-result.ts:328` and `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-input-admission.ts:151` on main `19aff5bfd42`). Only the agent-command path is transport-only (`src/agents/pending-final-delivery-marker.ts:118`). So the replayable marker this fixture seeds is a production shape, and the October 26 run log above shows one (`"kind":"replayable"`). The October 26 Gateway proof above remains tied to its historical base; no current-base unseeded marker lifecycle or live Telegram proof is claimed. The historical model no-send decision remains unresolved.

Before publication, main `1dca2e5bcb91d3d42895112f78a7a2d325b95e84` still lacked the new fixture; the related announcement test was unchanged and the registry insertion merged cleanly. This scoped check does not establish runtime success on that newer base. Published head: `d9258a5eb295fd1e8b66ef6abac2e3a7adfdab05`. [Fresh CI run 40956446253](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40956446253) completed successfully: 35 jobs passed and 30 were skipped, with no failures. It tested merge `6debea727f3075db0d858485539288e01c8679e0`, combining this head with upstream `9fa6391b5dbf802f6a7566fa28f16f1a76e112cb`. [Changed-test job 123738414902](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40956446253/job/123738414902) records 3/3 private-completion cases and 110/110 announcement-delivery cases, both with exit 0. The PR's Checks tab remains the source for other workflow and review statuses.

**Adaptation to main `00a9cbf6d65` (November 24).** On the merge, 2 of the 3 cases failed because the delegated handoff was never consumed: the fixture bound it to `DEFAULT_MODEL`, which #203271 (`265577c4c15`) removed, so `consumeSubagentCompletionToolHandoff` returned nothing and the requester turn ran with `disableTools: true`. `d0ac4439e28` binds it to the fixture's configured primary, `openai/gpt-5.5`, asserts the embedded run carries that route, and drops the two `createAgentRunModelSelectionHandler` parameters #199529 removed (TS2353 in the agents-root typecheck). Production behavior is unchanged. #204178 and #204260 changed only undelivered completions, which now settle into requester history; this test's completion is delivered, and `src/agents/subagents/completion/` has no `pendingFinalDelivery` reference. On the merge (macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1, Vitest on Node, one worker): 3/3 private-completion cases in each of 2 runs, 76/76 announcement-delivery cases, and the agents-root and agents-sessions typechecks, oxlint, oxfmt and the line-cap, assertion-safety, mock-export and test-lines ratchets (`Net test lines: +380 ... allocation credit: 380`) pass. Replacing the requester origin passed to the private-instruction builder with `undefined` fails only the retention case.

**Incident evidence, 2026.10.3:** [the incident follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/173650#issuecomment-6323508739) records build `1ecf113bef64`, the actual private instruction and a permitted `message` tool, a promised user update, registry delivery recorded as delivered, and no corresponding send. The shipped run above shows the same registry and outcome-table facts on this head with a scripted no-send; it does not establish why the 2026.10.3 model did not send.

prs.title: fix(memory-lancedb): group chats recall and forget the owner's stored memories
prs.body:
Closes #200281

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a group or channel member gets the owner's stored memories in a reply, and can have the agent delete them, when memory-lancedb owns the memory slot.

## User Impact

User impact: by default only the owner's sessions recall or forget memory-lancedb memories. In groups, channels and direct chats with anyone else, `memory_recall` and `memory_forget` return a refusal with the reason and the next step, and automatic recall skips the turn before the prompt reaches the embedding provider. `ownerOnly: false` in the plugin config brings back today's behavior. `memory_store` and auto-capture are unchanged, and `openclaw ltm` still lists and searches for operators.

Owner sessions are the ones the Gateway gives an owner-private memory audience: direct chats with anyone in `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, Gateway clients with `operator.admin` (the Control UI, WebChat and the TUI connect with it), `openclaw agent` on its default session, and sessions and linked scheduled runs that inherit one of these. Sessions without that audience lose recall they have today: `openclaw agent --session-key` on a key that names no chat, Gateway clients without `operator.admin`, `tools.invoke`, and unlinked cron and hook runs. The docs list them.

Update behavior: existing configs stay valid and nothing is migrated. After updating, those sessions stop recalling until an operator sets `ownerOnly: false`. The key is read from live config on every call, so setting it applies on hot reload with no restart. Checked on an upgrade from 2026.11.4 below. Separately, main's memory-lancedb already needs a core newer than 11.4 (it imports `openclaw/plugin-sdk/node-crypto-runtime`), so a plugin-only update fails to load before and after this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin's provider already had the rule (`provider-runtime.ts`, `resolveReadDenial`), but the tools and the prompt hook never used it. This moves it into `memory-access.ts`, which the provider, both tools and automatic recall now share, and adds `ownerOnly` (default true) as the explicit way back. Automatic recall checks that the audience is still current once, right before it embeds the prompt; a recall that has started finishes, as root `AGENTS.md` asks. The provider's own answers stay owner-private whatever `ownerOnly` says, as on main.

Root `AGENTS.md` asks before new config options. If you'd rather ship this with no key, or with the default open, either is a few lines.

Not addressed here:

- `memory_store` and auto-capture still save group turns into the owner's store, as today, and `memory_store` still answers `Already stored` when the exact text is already there. Someone who can guess a memory's full text can confirm it that way.
- A session with `exec` or file tools on the Gateway host can read the LanceDB files directly, and no plugin check stops that. One of my live runs did exactly that, with the store under the workspace. The live scenario below denies those tools so it measures the plugin. Sandboxing non-owner sessions is the control for it.
- #196265 also edits `config.ts` and `index.ts`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Evidence

### Update 2026-11-25 (head `9519399f5e5`)

Upgrade proof from current stable, as the review asked. 2026.11.10 replaced 2026.11.9 as npm `latest` on 11-25 at 05:07 UTC, so the cell starts there. It installs published `openclaw@2026.11.10` and `@openclaw/memory-lancedb@2026.11.10`, stores facts as the owner, runs 11.10's own `openclaw update` to a build of this PR, installs the PR's plugin on the same HOME and LanceDB directory, and repeats the probes. It is the body's 2026.11.4 cell with only the version changed.

Stable 2026.11.10 (`6ea542f`), the bug:
- A non-owner chat (`chat.send` without `operator.admin`, its own session key) got both owner facts injected (`memory-lancedb: injecting 2 memories into context`), answered `4412`, and deleted the other fact: `Memory 376889ef-... forgotten.`
- tools.invoke `memory_recall` at a group key returned the owner's locker code.

Upgrade, same state:
- `openclaw update` rc 0, to `OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (9519399)`. Plugin install and `doctor --non-interactive` rc 0.
- The plugin config entry is identical before and after; the only config changes are doctor's own `agents.entries.main` and wizard stamp.
- Before the candidate starts, the table 11.10 wrote is unchanged: same schema, version 4, 1 row, 11 files, 39,021 bytes, read with `@lancedb/lancedb` 0.41.0 outside the gateway.

Candidate (this PR merged with main `40b23868a5d`):
- The owner's direct chat recalls the row 11.10 wrote (`injecting 1 memories`, `memory_recall` `Found 1 memories ... 4412`, reply `4412`), and so does the CLI default session.
- A non-owner chat is refused. `auto-recall skipped: this session has no owner-private memory audience`, no embedding request, no memory block in the prompt. `memory_recall` and `memory_forget` both return `Stored memories are not available in this session: ...`, and the row is still there (`Total memories: 1`).
- tools.invoke `memory_recall` at `agent:main:main` and at the group key, and `memory_forget` at the group key, are refused with the same text.
- `openclaw config set plugins.entries.memory-lancedb.config.ownerOnly false` hot-reloads on the same gateway pid (`config hot reload applied (plugins.entries.memory-lancedb.config.ownerOnly)`). A new non-owner chat gets recall and auto-recall back (`injecting 3 memories`, reply `4412`), and after a restart on the same state, forget by id at the group key works again (`Memory 83eecfde-... forgotten.`).
- The final table keeps its schema, with the 11.10 row and the candidate's row side by side.

Limits:
- The published 11.10 plugin bundles only the linux-x64 LanceDB binding, so on macOS arm64 it cannot store anything out of the box (#203211; fixed on main by #203539, not released). The stable phase used the issue's workaround, the darwin-arm64 binding from npm. The candidate's plugin got its binding normally.
- Chat model: a local OpenAI-compatible Qwen3.8 27B endpoint. Embeddings: `text-embedding-3`, 4096 dimensions. No paid provider.
- An owner's `openclaw agent` turn on a custom session key has no durable chat type, so it loses auto-recall after the upgrade; on 11.10 it had it. That follows from the default this PR proposes, and `ownerOnly: false` restores it, but owners who script the CLI will notice.
- Not run: a real channel group (group refusal here is tools.invoke at a group key plus a non-owner direct chat; the earlier QA Lab runs cover real groups), a real `commands.ownerAllowFrom` sender, scheduled jobs and hooks.

The branch now has main `40b23868a5d` merged in (`9519399f5e5`); only `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` conflicted, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`. No main commit has touched the PR's files since `40b23868a5d`, and the merge is clean with main `0f73e04b3f9`. The redacted step log is in the body, under Evidence.

prs.title: fix: exec refuses every command once lost launches fill the spawn broker
prs.body:
Related: #177656

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every exec fails with `Spawn broker child capacity exceeded (512); close running processes before retrying` until the Gateway restarts, once 512 commands have been lost between their launch grant and the broker's ownership receipt. On 2026.10.8 the same leak showed up as `Spawn broker request capacity exceeded` ([#177656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6629331547)): that release's `worker.ts` refused once `owned.size + starting.size + (resources?.size ?? 0)` reached 256. #166488 replaced that with the 512 owned-child cap and a separate 256 limit on pending spawns.

## User Impact

User impact: a command the Gateway loses after granting its launch no longer leaves a slot behind in the spawn broker, so a long-running Gateway keeps running exec instead of refusing every command after 512 such losses.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the service-child relay fails a command after the host has granted its launch, but before the broker's `owned` receipt arrives, the host retires the request at `owned`. The broker then transfers that command's pipes. The host's branch for requests it no longer tracks answered each transfer with `pipe-received` only. The broker forgets an owned command only once every transferred fd is drained (`forget()` in `worker.ts`). Until then the entry stays in the worker's `childAdmissions`, which `childCapacityError()` counts against `MAX_OWNED_CHILDREN = 512` (`protocol.ts`, since #166488). Nothing else drains a retired request's pipes before the broker shuts down, so the slot was gone for the life of the Gateway.

The untracked-pipe branch now also sends `output-drained` with an error for that fd. That is the same acknowledgement `BrokerChild.attachPipe` already sends for tracked requests. The helper is in `pipe.ts` because `host.ts` counts 690 lines against its 700-line `max-lines` cap (oxlint 1.89.0, blank lines and comments skipped), and the helper would take it over.

This is the leak in [KarolAdamiec's heap readings on #177656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6629331547): one `owned` entry with `openPipes=1` left per post-launch identity loss, until the broker hit its cap and exec was dead for about 9 h. The host-side `nativeInitiated` path from [an earlier comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6546377246) does not leak on main: the worker answers `launch allowed:false` with an `error` frame, which clears it (re-measured below).

## Evidence

### Update 2026-11-25 (head `dedff9e3f03`)

Merged main `9fb2059f340` as `dedff9e3f03`; clean, and the branch was 5,717 commits behind. The PR still changes only its 4 files (+65/-2), with no adaptation.

Main `9fb2059f340` has not fixed it, and no main commit has touched the PR's files since (checked through `0f73e04b3f9`). `host.ts` still answers a late pipe on a retired request with only `pipe-received`, and `worker.ts` `forget()` still waits for `entry.openPipes.size === 0`, which only `output-drained` clears. The closest main change, `9a38762e705` (#200567), releases retired request references, not pipes.

- `host-transport-retirement.test.ts` passes 20 of 20 (main added 2 since the body's 18). With main's `host.ts` and `pipe.ts`, "drains a pipe that arrives after a lost command retired its request" fails with the assertion the body quotes: `expected undefined to match object { type: 'output-drained', id: 1, ... }`.
- The rest of the spawn-broker files I ran pass twice each: `host` 16/16, `handoff` 10/10, `host-scope-settlement` 13/13, `proxy-retention` 2/2, `worker-admission-settlement` 2/2, `stdin-handoff` 1/1.
- `tsgo:core` and the 29 changed core-test graphs pass, each with a TS2322 control. oxlint, oxfmt, and the line-cap and max-lines ratchets pass.
- Test cost: `host-transport-retirement.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` 6.7 s warm (45 s cold, 98% transform); the new case takes 1 ms. +35 net test lines, inside the 400 allowance.

Not re-run on the merge: the real-broker harness from the body (the injected post-grant losses). Its limits stand: the loss is injected in the host, macOS only, broker under tsx.


Measured on head `eae91e923b9` and main `3855c896edd` (2026-11-09), macOS arm64. `src/process/spawn-broker/` is identical in this PR's merge base `d44c9ad927d` and in `3855c896edd`. Runtimes are stated per result. The real-broker runs are Node 26.12.1, as in a shipped Gateway. Vitest results are given under Node (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`) and under the pinned Bun 1.4.4 fork. Bun is the local default, and it is what this PR's CI node shards run (`OPENCLAW_CI_TEST_RUNTIME_POLICY: bun-all`).

**Real broker with an injected post-grant loss.** A standalone script drives the real `SpawnBrokerHost`. The worker is a real Node process (`node --import tsx src/process/spawn-broker/worker.ts`), with real V8 IPC, really transferred stdio sockets and real `/bin/sleep 300` commands. Both the script and the worker run on Node 26.12.1, recorded from inside each process (`process.versions.bun` unset). The loss is the only injected fault. The launch callback writes the grant and then fails the host's child on the same turn, so `owned` cannot have arrived yet:

```ts
child = host.spawn("/bin/sleep", ["300"], { stdio: "pipe" }, (launch) => {
  const written = launch(); // `launch allowed:true` is written to the worker here
  child.fail(new Error("injected relay loss after launch grant"));
  return written;
});
```

Read-only taps record both ends of the IPC: a pass-through wrapper on the host's `ChildProcess.send` plus message listeners, and a `NODE_OPTIONS=--import` preload in the worker that logs what it receives and what it spawns. No broker code is patched.

| | main `3855c896edd` | this PR `eae91e923b9` |
|---|---|---|
| losses injected | 512, then loss #513 refused | 1100, none refused |
| late pipes (host no longer tracked the request) | 1536, each answered `pipe-received` only | 3300, each answered `pipe-received` + `output-drained` |
| `output-drained` received by the worker | 0 of 1536 | 3300 of 3300 |
| native exit of the lost commands | 512 of 512 exited on `SIGTERM`, 0 alive | 1100 of 1100 exited on `SIGTERM`, 0 alive |
| `/bin/sh -c 'printf exec-ok'` after the losses, and 2 s later | `Spawn broker child capacity exceeded (512); close running processes before retrying`, both times | `exit=0 stdout="exec-ok"`, both times |
| free slots (admit `sleep 300` until refused) | 0 | 512, then #513 refused at the cap |
| broker restarted | no: same pid, host generation 1 | no: same pid, host generation 1 |

The taps record each command's exit signal, not who sent it. That the SIGTERM comes from the cleanup the host retains at `owned` (`terminateLostBrokerChild`) is from reading the code; nothing else in this flow signals those commands. On both trees the host's own `requests` and `childAdmissions` are empty at every checkpoint (loss #1 and every 128th loss), so the slot that leaks on main is the worker's. When main refuses, the worker has no live command children, only tsx's esbuild service. The same script on this PR merged locally into `3855c896edd` gives the same numbers as the `eae91e923b9` column.
