Result: 600 x `Spawn broker launch authority refused`, worker frames `prepared=600 error=600`, 0 requests left on the host, and an exec afterwards exits 0. That path does not leak on main, and this PR does not touch it.

**Regression test** (`host-transport-retirement.test.ts`). Copied onto main `3855c896edd`, the new test fails with `expected undefined to match object { type: 'output-drained', id: 1, …(2) }` (1 failed, 17 passed), under both `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun` (the pinned Bun fork). On this head, 18 passed under both. Wall time for the whole file with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`: 6.7 s under Node and 6.9 s under Bun. An earlier Bun run of the same command took 49.8 s, and its Vitest summary attributes 98% of the duration to transform. The new test itself takes 1-3 ms. No CI seconds yet: the last run's node shards failed before running any test (see CI below).

- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `host-transport-retirement.test.ts` 24.1 s (cold worker cache, 20.2 s of it compiling) and 4.5 s wall, 33 ms and 31 ms of tests. CI run 42465221261: `host-transport-retirement.test.ts` no CI seconds yet (the test shards failed on a 504 while installing Bun, before any test ran).
 Those shards run Vitest under Bun on this PR (`OPENCLAW_CI_TEST_RUNTIME_POLICY: bun-all` in the shards that passed).

**Broker and supervisor suites under Node** on this head (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/spawn-broker/ src/process/supervisor/ --maxWorkers=2`): 64 files passed, 4 skipped; 457 tests passed, 16 skipped (15 Linux-only, 1 Windows-only), 0 failed. Two runs, at 06:32Z and 07:46Z, gave the same counts (227 s and 95 s). The default Bun runtime skips the broker's real command transport, so these suites have to run under Node to cover it.

**Test-line allocation.** `config/test-lines-allocations/192999-spawn-broker-release-orphan-pipes.txt` grants 35, the net test-line growth of this PR (the regression test, +35/-0). On this PR merged into `3855c896edd`, `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 3855c896edd --no-merge-base` (CI's form) gives `Test lines OK: 6592403; ceiling: 6592403; slack: 0`. Main alone is also at zero slack (`6592368; ceiling: 6592368`). The allocation covers exactly this PR's growth and nothing more.

**Local gates on this PR merged into `3855c896edd`** (the scripts run on Node 26.12.1; only `test-projects` runs Vitest):
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 3855c896edd`: 35 of 36 ok. That includes `typecheck core`, `typecheck core tests`, `lint core`, `lint scripts`, format, the ratchets, the dead-export scan and runtime import cycles. The one failure, `changelog attributions`, lists the same 20 entries on unmodified main: 18 `Thanks @steipete-oai` (`CHANGELOG/2026.6.8.md` x4, `CHANGELOG/2026.7.1.md` x11, `CHANGELOG/records/2026.6.8.md` x3) and 2 `Thanks @roboclaw-bot` (`CHANGELOG/records/2026.10.6.md`).
- `scripts/ci-baseline-ratchets.mts --base 3855c896edd --no-merge-base`: all 9 ok. `check-line-cap-ratchet.mjs`: OK, 3 changed source files.
- Core lint stripes 2/5 and 4/5, the two lint jobs that failed in CI: rc 0 with CI's advisory size limits. A local-severity run reports the same `max-lines` errors on unmodified main, all in files this PR does not touch.
- `node scripts/test-projects.mts --changed 3855c896edd`, run once under Bun and once under Node. The allocation file counts as a tooling change, so the plan is broad. Neither run finished: both were stopped inside the tooling shard on this shared machine (Bun after 50 min, Node after 56 min), so the shards after it, including the process shard, did not run. `src/process/spawn-broker/` is covered by the Node suite run above.   - unit: Bun 684 passed / 1 failed, Node 683 passed / 1 failed

  - The partial tooling shard fails on this host's setup 293 lines in each run's log read `Linux workflow tests require Bash 5+`; macOS ships Bash 3.2. The failing tooling files give the identical 343-failure set on unmodified main under both runtimes, and `openclaw-test-instance` fails identically on main under both.

**CI on `eae91e923b9`.** The 17 red checks are all download failures from github.com on 2026-11-08. The first and last HTTP 504 lines in this PR's job logs are at 09:00:25Z and 09:11:40Z. The 8 node shards failed downloading the pinned Bun fork (`curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 504`), before running any test. OpenGrep failed downloading its binary with the same curl 504. The 4 CodeQL jobs failed with `Unable to download and extract CodeQL CLI: Unexpected HTTP response: 504`, before scanning. The 2 core lint stripes logged `OPENCLAW_LINT_TOOL=bun: could not stage the pinned fork: Command failed: /bin/bash .../scripts/stage-openclaw-bun.sh ... linux x64` (09:05:33Z to 09:08:49Z). Their logs do not say why staging failed; it is the same download script that got 504s in the node shards in those minutes. The stripe 2 sub-shards that did not need Bun passed. Both `openclaw/ci-gate` checks are red because of these. The second one is posted by the Security Review run 42466081123, which CI run 42465221261 triggered (`workflow_run`). Unrelated PRs hit the same 504s from 08:57:42Z to 09:08:35Z (OpenGrep 42465050930 and 42465349650, CI 42465221806 and 42465349653, CodeQL 42465406732 and 42465686516). The same run's `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` passed, including `Test lines OK: 6576294; ceiling: 6576325; slack: 31`. A re-run is needed.

- **Our two Mac mini Gateways** (logs, read-only; these numbers are carried over unchanged from this PR's original description and were not re-measured for this update):
  - Before #169584/#167739, cleanup identity loss was frequent. On a 10.5/10.6-based build, mac-mini logged 9-14 `[process/supervisor] spawn failed ... cleanup identity lost` a day (83 over 10-24..10-30, 458 agent turns).

  - Identity loss still happens there for other reasons: two `service child cleanup identity lost: anchor channel closed without a matching closing receipt` on 2026-11-02, on the beta.5-based build.
  - Neither host has reached the cap, because both restart for deploys every few days, so they do not show the leak itself.

Not covered: the loss is injected in the host (`child.fail()` right after the grant write); I did not get a real relay to lose identity inside that window. All runs are macOS arm64, none on Linux. The broker ran from the source tree under tsx, not from a packaged build, and not inside a live Gateway.

prs.title: fix(agents): ask_user ignores the question number in replies like "1. Deny"
prs.body: Closes #190485 Related: #173760, #173845, #146646 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: a multi-question `ask_user` answer is saved as `1. Deny`, lands on the wrong question, or is rejected when the user numbers each reply line the way the prompt numbers the questions. ## User Impact User impact: replying `1. Deny` and `2. Approved` on separate lines answers question 1 with `Deny` and question 2 with `Approved`, in any line order. A reply that answers only some questions is still rejected and the question stays open. Multi-question prompts now label questions `Question 1: Deploy` and number each question's options from 1. On Telegram and Signal, the old `1. Deploy` header ran together with the option lines into one list (`4. Checks`), so answering by the displayed number picked the wrong question. Single-question cards rendered as Telegram messages or Teams cards now number their options to match "Reply with the number". Compatibility: in a multi-question reply, a line starting with digits, a dot and whitespace (`2. Approved`) is read as an answer to that question number. `1.5`, `Node.js: 22` and `U.S. region: East` parse as before. A line matched to a question by number or id no longer also fills another question by position. On main, `2: Approved` alone completed question 1 with the text `2: Approved`; it is now rejected as incomplete. ## Why This Change Was Made The reply parser only treated `:`, `=` and `-` as key separators. `1. Deny` stayed positional, so the agent received `1. Deny` as the answer, reordered lines landed on the wrong question, and questions with fixed options rejected the reply. Numbered lines are now a separate rule that requires whitespace after the dot, checked before the unchanged keyed syntax. The single-question card text now uses the same `1. Label - description` lines as the text prompt. Multi-question prompts numbered each question (`1. Deploy`) directly above options that also start at `1.`. Telegram and Signal render markdown lists with their own numbering, so the header and the options became one list: `1. Deploy`, `2. Staging`, `3. Production`, `4. Checks`. Questions are now labeled `Question 1: Deploy`. That is not a list marker, so each question's options render from 1, and the question number is the one the `1. answer` rule binds. The first revision of this PR also copied a single-line reply into every question. That was wrong: it invented answers the user never gave and broke the incomplete-answer contract from #146646. It is removed. The multi-question guidance wording is left to #173845, so this PR no longer touches that string. The live replies in #190485 were each a single line for a two-question card, so they were incomplete and their rejection was correct. That issue is corrected. ## Evidence ### Update 2026-11-25 (head `cd6fbe7d02c`) Merged main `9fb2059f340` as `cd6fbe7d02c`; the branch was 5,717 commits behind. One textual conflict, in `user-input-bridge.ts`: #204900 (`25efa334d23`) rewrote the `lines.push(...)` right below the PR's `Question ${index + 1}: ` prefix to call its new `formatQuestionText`. The merge keeps both, and against main the file is the PR's diff with only that hunk re-expressed. The PR still changes 7 files, +252/-18. Main `9fb2059f340` has not fixed it, and no main commit has touched the PR's files since (checked through `0f73e04b3f9`). `parseKeyedAnswers` still matches only `^\s*([^:=-]+?)\s*[:=-]\s*(.+?)\s*$`. #204343 changes Telegram rich-message list labels, not this prompt: main's `markdownToTelegramHtml` still renders main's prompt as `1. Deploy` ... `7. Lint`. - With main's `user-input-bridge.ts` and the PR's tests, all 4 PR test files fail with the original defect, e.g. "binds numbered reply lines to their questions": `- "Deny"` / `+ "1. Deny"`. - On the merge, 21 files pass twice (42 of 42 runs): the 4 PR files plus the Codex and Copilot bridges (including #204900's `user-input-bridge.elicitation.test.ts`, 12/12), `gateway-question` 21/21, `gateway-question-dispatch` 25/25, `structured-input` 42/42, `ask-user-tool` 37/37 and the rest of the question path. - `tsgo:core`, the 29 changed core-test graphs, `tsgo:test:root` and `tsgo:extensions` pass, with TS2322 controls on the first three; oxlint and oxfmt are clean. - +94 net test lines, inside the 400 allowance. Not re-run on the merge: the QA scenario `gateway-ask-user-numbered-text-reply` and the live Telegram screenshots, which were taken on older heads. - Real model, real Gateway, Telegram through a local Bot API. Two Gateways ran the bundled Telegram plugin against a loopback Bot API, with `qwen3.8-27b-uncensored-r9700` behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint: one built from main `3855c896edd`, and one built from this branch merged onto it. The Gateway and Vitest ran on macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1. The model was told the exact `ask_user` arguments and made the call itself: two questions, Ruling and Authorize, each with options Approve and Deny. Every reply reached the Gateway as a Telegram update. Two runs per build gave the same results: | | main `3855c896edd` | this branch | |---|---|---| | numbered lines in the card the bot sent | `1. Ruling`, `2. Approve`, `3. Deny`, `4. Authorize`, `5. Approve`, `6. Deny` | `Question 1: Ruling`, `1. Approve`, `2. Deny`, `Question 2: Authorize`, `1. Approve`, `2. Deny` | | reply `1. Deny` / `2. Approve` | Ruling `1. Deny`, Authorize `2. Approve` | Ruling `Deny`, Authorize `Approve` | | reply `2. Approve` / `1. Deny` | Ruling `2. Approve`, Authorize `1. Deny` | Ruling `Deny`, Authorize `Approve` | | tool result in the resumed model request, reversed reply | `Ruling: 2. Approve` / `Authorize: 1. Deny` | `Ruling: Deny` / `Authorize: Approve` | | the agent's reply, reversed | `RESULT B \| ruling=2. Approve \| authorize=1. Deny` | `RESULT B \| ruling=Deny \| authorize=Approve` | | reply `1. Deny` alone | rejected (`question 'authorize' requires an answer`), question still pending, no model request in 40 s | the same | In the in-order reply, the model got the same `Ruling: Deny` / `Authorize: Approve` on this branch, and `Ruling: 1. Deny` / `Authorize: 2. Approve` on main. After the incomplete reply, both builds sent nothing to Telegram and retried the rejected message with backoff, 6 rejections in 40 s. That is #193159, which this PR does not change. - Regression table in `src/agents/harness/user-input-bridge.test.ts` (5 rows): 5/5 pass. With `user-input-bridge.ts` from main (`1b15b48e2f3`), 2 rows fail: `1. Deny\n2. Approved` is saved as `"1. Deny"`, and a lone `2. Approved` fills question 1 with `"2. Approved"`. With the previous head (`303c244630d`), 4 rows fail: lone `2` answers both questions, `1.5\n2.5` becomes `5`/`5`, and `Node.js: 22` / `U.S. region: East` split at the dot. - Consumers: 18 test files, 354 tests pass locally, including the 3 suites that failed in [run 41326074085](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41326074085): `dispatch-from-config.question-custody` 17/17, `session-accessor.question-answer-transcript` 8/8, and `test/contracts/ask-user-msteams-presentation` 2/2 (updated to the numbered lines). - New qa-lab scenario `gateway-ask-user-numbered-text-reply` (mock-openai, real Gateway): `1. Production` alone gets "The answer was not accepted: question 'checks' requires an answer" and the question stays pending. Then `1. Production\n2. E2E\n3. Urgent` resolves it as `Production` / `E2E` / `Urgent`, and the waiting run resumes with those values. With main's parser, the same reply is stored as `1. Production` / `2. E2E` / `3. Urgent` and the scenario fails. - Multi-question prompt through Telegram's markdown renderer: on `b2b86091a7f` the numbered lines are `1. Deploy`, `2. Staging`, `3. Production`, `4. Checks`, `5. Unit`, `6. E2E`, `7. Lint`. On this head they are `1. Staging`, `2. Production`, then `1. Unit`, `2. E2E`, `3. Lint`, under `Question 1: Deploy` and `Question 2: Checks`. The new test in `test/telegram-question-gateway.test.ts` fails on `b2b86091a7f` and passes here. Signal's renderer showed the same merged list before and per-question lists after. - Telegram plugin against a local Bot API stub (scripted model, not live): after an incomplete `1. Production` was rejected, the reply `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production` reached the agent with the rejected line replayed in front of it (#193159), as `1. Production` / `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production`. On `b2b86091a7f` those four lines resumed the agent with Production / E2E / Urgent. On main `f5f27c3ef6e` the same four lines resumed it with `1. Production` / `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E`. A three-line reply without the replay was not run on main. - Card text from the real Telegram and Teams renderers for a single question with options: main shows `- Staging (Recommended): Safer default`; this branch shows `1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`. Channels without a presentation renderer already received the numbered prompt text. - `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean. 22 test files (474 tests) pass locally. Test-line growth is 94 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/ask-user-numbered-reply-lines.txt`. Merged onto main `3855c896edd`, the ratchet reads `Test lines OK: 6592462; ceiling: 6592462; slack: 0.` - Live Telegram (2026-11-10, a throwaway bot in a DM, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). One isolated Gateway built from main `9a5df3d60f1` with this PR's head `6e8aec42f5e` and four of my other PR heads merged in (no file touched by two of them), on the real Telegram Bot API, with QA Lab's scripted mock provider. On this head: - The three-question card arrived as `Question 1: Deploy`, `1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`, `2. Production - Ship to users`, then `Question 2: Checks` with `1. Unit`, `2. E2E`, `3. Lint`, then `Question 3: Note` with `1. Routine`, `2. Urgent`. - `1. Production` alone was rejected (`question 'checks' requires an answer`) and the question stayed open. - The out-of-order reply `3. Urgent` / `2. E2E` / `1. Production` reached the agent with the rejected line replayed in front of it (#193159), and the agent resumed with `Deploy: Production`, `Checks: E2E`, `Note: Urgent`. - A single-question card arrived with its two options numbered (`1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`, then `2. Production`). Its numbered answer was not exercised in this run; the run below covers it. - Before and after on real Telegram, each build alone (2026-11-10, the same throwaway bot's DM, macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1). Two isolated Gateways, one after the other: one built from upstream main `401a1de38b9` alone, one from this head `6e8aec42f5e` alone. QA Lab's mock provider scripted the `ask_user` calls; the cards are what each Gateway rendered and sent. Screenshots are cropped to the cards. - Single question: main sends bullets (`• Staging (Recommended): Safer default`); this head numbers the options (`1. Staging (Recommended) - Safer default`, `2. Production - Ship to users`). Typing `1` (after tapping `Other…`) resolved to `Staging (Recommended)` on both builds. - Three questions: main numbers questions and options in one sequence, `1. prs.title: fix: stop background exec completion wakes from landing mid-line
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

A background exec's completion wake lands mid-line when the output is long. The wake embeds a fixed 2,000-char slice of the command output, and on a long run that slice starts where the bytes happened to be, so the woken turn cannot tell whether the last line is the command's result or just where the cut landed.

This PR makes the wake carry the last non-empty line of the output instead, but only when the retained tail was actually truncated. Output that fit in the tail keeps the full tail exactly as before.

How it works: when the session's total output exceeded the retained 2,000-char tail, the wake producer selects the last non-empty line of the tail, strips a leading `OK: ` or `ERR: ` marker when one is present, trims it through the same 2,000-char cap when it is longer, and falls back to the previous slice when there is no usable last line (empty output, structured tails). When the output fits, the content is the trimmed tail, byte-identical to the pre-change behavior. Header, duration, output-file pointer, routing and delivery are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Update 2026-11-25 (head `197f535527a`)

Merged main `9fb2059f340` (`e5b7090ff22`, clean; 2,456 commits behind) and pushed two commits on it:

- `b037b26d50c` is oxfmt output only. The previous head `f92d202c20c` was not formatted, and hosted CI never ran on it (`action_required`), so nothing caught it.
- `197f535527a` answers the open half of the P2 "Preserve complete short output and disclose every omission". When a truncated tail is reduced to its last line, the wake no longer says `last 2000 of N output chars` above that one line; it says `last line of N output chars`. A structured tail shown whole keeps `last <n> of N`. On the previous head the updated test fails with the old header: `... last 2000 of 2022 output chars (process log keeps the last 2000; earlier output was discarded):\nall done, 3 files`.

Main `9fb2059f340` has not fixed it, and no main commit has touched the PR's files since (checked through `0f73e04b3f9`). `prepareExecExitWake` still sends `tail.trim()`, and on the merge `e5b7090ff22` with main's `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts` and `bash-tools.exec-output.ts`, the PR's test fails 10 of 11, including "surfaces the stripped marker summary of a truncated oversized tail" (`not to contain 'OK:'`), the original defect.

- Each twice: `bash-tools.exec-output.completion-content` 12/12 (9 `selectExecCompletionContent` cases, 3 wake cases), `exec-background-followup` 28/28, `exec-notify.queue-full` 1/1, `.requester` 2/2, `.store-failure` 1/1. The follow-up suite's output-file assertion `last 2000 of 3008` still holds, because a one-line tail is shown whole.
- `tsgo:core` and the agents-tools test shard pass, each with a TS2322 control; oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Test cost: the completion-content file 5.1 s warm (26.6 s cold); each case 1 to 7 ms. +102 net test lines, inside the 400 allowance.

On the other P2, "Resolve the whitespace-only test's contradictory expectation": the test asserts `selectExecCompletionContent(raw)` returns `raw` and `selectExecCompletionContent(raw.trim())` returns `""`, and a comment says the caller trims first. Gap: the new header is tested on the process-log branch only. The output-file branch uses the same value, but no test covers it with a truncated multi-line tail.


**On main `eee7a1bd526`** (head `f92d202c20c` applied with no conflicts; main is 2,105 commits past this branch's base; macOS arm64, Node 26.12.1, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`). These run the repo's own test runner; the loader-based proof below predates them.

- `bash-tools.exec-output.completion-content.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` and the three `bash-tools.exec-notify.*.test.ts` files: 5 files, 43 tests, 0 failed.
- With main's `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts` and `bash-tools.exec-output.ts` and this PR's test file, "surfaces the stripped marker summary of a truncated oversized tail" fails (`expected 'Exec completed (wake-mar, code 0, 1ms…' not to contain 'OK:'`) and "keeps the full tail when the output fits the retained window" passes; the 9 `selectExecCompletionContent` cases fail with `selectExecCompletionContent is not a function`, since main has none.
- `tsgo:core` 0 errors; the PR wrapper inventory test (`eager-import-closure.test.ts`) passes. On `a84c030947a` both failed against its own main base, which `7199e72e732` (`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` on `lines[i]`) and `f92d202c20c` (`sliceUtf16Safe` in place of `bash-process-registry.ts`'s `tail`) fix.
- v2026.11.7 (`e31bbf056de`) carries #199122 as the backport `66364847341` without this change; its wake output is still `tail.trim()`.

- 10 unit cases in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-output.completion-content.test.ts`: last line, trailing blank lines, `OK: ` / `ERR: ` markers, empty marker line, empty and whitespace fallback, JSON object/array tails.
- 2 wake-owner cases in the same file drive the real path (`appendOutput` + `maybeNotifyOnExit` -> `prepareExecExitWake`): a truncated oversized tail surfaces the stripped `OK: ` summary with the truncation header, and output that fits keeps every line of the tail.
- The existing wake tests in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-background-followup.test.ts` pin the header, the `with no output.` case, the bounded tail and the file pointer. Their fixtures end in a single line, so the selected line equals the old tail and those assertions hold unchanged.

Behavior proof (review host): `pnpm install`/build/test are not available on this host, so the proof runs the patched sources directly under Node 26 type-stripping through an ESM hooks loader (`node --import ./loader.mjs proof.ts`). The loader resolves the repo's `.js` specifiers to `.ts` sources and maps workspace packages to their `src`; the only shims are delivery plumbing the wake path does not exercise (logger, system-event queue, terminal-core pass-throughs, published `@openclaw/fs-safe`/`@openclaw/proc-safe` bindings, `chalk`/`tslog`/`semver`/`string-width`, and the parameter-property-only leaves `retry`, `runtime`, `env-substitution`, `plugin-instance-error`). Wakes are rendered through the real entry point (`maybeNotifyOnExit` -> `prepareExecExitWake`) with three synthetic fixtures:

```
=== (a) short multi-line output that fits the retained window (input 27 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-0, code 0, 0s):
line one
line two
last line

=== (b) oversized multi-line output truncated mid-line, last line is an OK: marker (input 2009 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-1, code 0, 0s), last 2000 of 2009 output chars (process log has the rest):
done

=== (c) structured multi-line JSON tail (input 2008 chars) ===
Exec completed (proof-2, code 0, 0s), last 2000 of 2008 output chars (process log has the rest):
yyyy...yyy            (1,994 y's, abbreviated)
{
  "a": 1
}
```

(a) fits, so the full tail is kept, the pre-change content, unchanged. (b) is truncated mid-line and ends in an `OK: ` marker, so the wake carries just `done`. (c) is a structured tail whose last line is a JSON closing bracket, so the whole tail is kept.

Cut from upstream main `375daf6d3` (rebased after review). Verified against the main tip that no open PR or recent commit covers this.

One ask: the fork CI run needs a maintainer to approve it before hosted CI executes. Could a maintainer approve https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44837225822 ? It is the CI run for the current head `f92d202c20c`.

prs.title: fix(memory-lancedb): auto-capture stores OpenClaw's own [System] retry turns as user memories
prs.body:
Closes #189955

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: memory-lancedb auto-capture stores OpenClaw's own `[System]` turns as user memories when a stranded-reply retry, or a `sessions_send` restart note, quotes text that contains a capture trigger.

## User Impact

User impact: with `autoCapture` on, only what the user said is stored. `[System]` rows already in a store stop coming back from recall and are no longer used for duplicate matching. They stay on disk and still show in `openclaw ltm list`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core marks the turns it writes itself with `[System]` through `formatSystemTurnPrompt` (`src/sessions/system-turn-prompt.ts`). On main `19aff5bfd42` its producers are the stranded-reply retry (`src/auto-reply/reply/stranded-reply-recovery.ts`), the transcript follow-up run (`src/auto-reply/reply/transcript-followup-run.ts`) and `sessions_send` (`src/agents/tools/sessions-send-executor.ts`). I have not shown that every internal turn goes through it. These turns are sent as user-role messages, so `extractUserTextContent` hands it to capture like any user text. Capture now goes through `capturableUserText`, which checks the raw turn for that marker before sanitizing, because sanitizing can remove the marker line along with a quoted context block. It then applies `shouldCapture`, which also rejects the marker. `isRecallableMemoryText`, which gates both recall and duplicate matching, skips such rows too. The marker is matched in the plugin because plugins cannot import the core helper, and a leading timestamp envelope is allowed before it.

Deleting rows already stored is left out. That is a retention change, and recall no longer surfaces them. One tradeoff: a user message that itself starts with `[System]` is no longer captured.

## Evidence

### Update 2026-11-25 (head `ae07b96240c`)

Merged main `9fb2059f340` as `bfaa318c55d` (clean; the branch was 8,755 commits behind) and pushed `ae07b96240c` on top. That commit fixes a dead-export failure this PR caused: `check-deadcode-exports.mts --all` flagged `isSystemTurnPromptText` (new) and `shouldCapture` (no longer imported by `index.ts`) in `memory-policy.ts`.

`userTextForCapture(text)` now returns `undefined` for a system turn, checked on the raw text before sanitizing, and otherwise the sanitized text. `index.ts` is back to main's loop: `userTextForCapture`, then `shouldCapture`. `isSystemTurnPromptText` is no longer exported.

- The Knip production report passes. The scan still exits 1 on `scripts/e2e/parallels/host-server.ts: detectParallelsHostIp` and `scripts/e2e/parallels/parallels-vm.ts: listVmNames`; main's own scheduled CI fails the same way (run 45654340109 on `0b99555d5f7`), and this PR touches nothing under `scripts/`.
- Main still has the bug: on the merge `bfaa318c55d`, with main's `memory-policy.ts`, `memory-capture-sanitization.ts` and `index.ts`, the PR's test fails 3 of 4, and `shouldCapture(strandedRetry)` is `true`. No main commit has touched the PR's files since `9fb2059f340` (checked through `0f73e04b3f9`).
- Control for the new shape: removing only the raw-text check fails "auto-capture checks the raw turn before sanitizing can drop the marker line" (`expected 'Remember the deployment window is Tue...' to be undefined`).
- memory-lancedb, each file twice: `memory-policy` 4/4, `index` 44/44, `memory-capture-sanitization` 28/28, `auto-recall` 2/2, `auto-recall.deadline` 3/3, `recall-service` 2/2. `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` pass, with a TS2322 control on each.
- Test cost: `memory-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` at `ae07b96240c`, three runs: 8, 5 and 6 s wall (Vitest duration 6.04, 3.59 and 3.79 s). +60 net test lines.

Not re-run on this head: the QA scenario `memory-lancedb-system-turn-capture`. Main's catalog still loads it.


- New qa scenario `memory-lancedb-system-turn-capture` (in this PR): real gateway, qa-channel, mock-openai, `messages.visibleReplies: message_tool`, memory-lancedb `autoCapture: true`.
  - The first prompt is not capturable, so the `[System]` retry is the first capturable text. A later turn in the same conversation, `QA-MEMORY-BARRIER 記住 ...`, must be stored before the store is read; captures for one session run in order, so the retry's capture has settled by then.
  - It fails if any stored row contains the retry's `send it now with message(action=send)` instruction, so it catches the retry whether or not its `[System]` line survived.
  - With main's memory-lancedb at `eef407423d4`: fails after the barrier settles, with `[System] Your previous reply was not delivered because you did not call message(action=send). Your reply text was: "QA-STRANDED-85714：...". If the user should see a reply, send it now with message(action=send). If no reply is needed, answer exactly NO_REPLY.` stored. The gateway logs two `auto-captured 1 memories`: the retry turn and the barrier.
  - This branch at `f517e265d7f`: passes with `barrier rows=1; retry rows=0`.
  - Command: `node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario memory-lancedb-system-turn-capture --concurrency 1 --fast`, after `pnpm build`.
  - CI does not run this scenario: no smoke profile selects it, and it appears 0 times in the QA Smoke logs for this head. The gateway results above are my local runs.
- `pnpm test extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 4 passed.
  - Control with `memory-policy.ts` from main: `expected true to be false` on `shouldCapture(strandedRetry)`, and recall returned `['stored', 'user']`.
  - The context-block case: under the sanitize-first order, the retry text sanitizes to `Remember the deployment window is Tuesdays.". If the user should see a reply, send it now with message(action=send). ...` and `shouldCapture` returns true. `capturableUserText` returns undefined for it.
  - Through the stranded retry, the gateway does not let that case through. With a temporary mock fixture whose private final opened with `Sender: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧` and a fenced JSON block, main stored `[System] ... Your reply text was: "Remember the deployment window is Tuesdays. QA-STRANDED-85714...` with the block already removed and the `[System]` line intact. The first commit on this branch (sanitize, then check) passed that run. The raw-turn check is defense for other system-turn producers, so the fixture is not in this PR.
- All 21 memory-lancedb test files except the live one: 174 passed, 0 failed.
- `pnpm tsgo:all` exits 0. oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files.
- Test lines: main's test-line ratchet is now at its ceiling (`3855c896edd`: slack 0), so `dcf76a14600` adds `config/test-lines-allocations/189956-memory-capture-skip-system-turns.txt` with this PR's exact net test-line growth, 62 lines. They are the tests that pin this change: Memory auto-capture skips OpenClaw's own [System] retry turns. Merged onto `3855c896edd`, `check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 3855c896edd --no-merge-base` reads `Test lines OK: 6592430; ceiling: 6592430; slack: 0.`, and an allocation of 63 is refused.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `memory-policy.test.ts` 2.7 s and 1.5 s wall, 39 ms and 18 ms of tests. CI run 41271447272, Bun: `memory-policy.test.ts` 30 ms of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1`).
- Gap: the unit tests copy core's marker and retry text, because extension tests do not import core. The qa scenario is the end-to-end check against core's real prompt.

prs.title: fix: explain how to fix an automation before saving
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you edit an automation with an unsupported saved **Send results** option, the editor suggests running a terminal command even though you can fix the setting right there. The same validation summary also tells you to fill in required fields when the only problem is an optional field, such as a negative time limit.

## User Impact

Choose a supported **Send results** option, then select **Save changes**. For other editor errors, select the listed field to go directly to it. An optional time limit can still be cleared. The editor does not choose a delivery option for you or save anything when you select an option.

| Trigger and surface | Exact before | Exact after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unsupported or missing saved delivery option — inline at Send results | `Choose where to send results, or run openclaw doctor --fix to repair older settings.` | `Choose an option before saving.` |
| Same trigger — clickable editor summary item | `Send results: Choose where to send results, or run openclaw doctor --fix to repair older settings.` | `Send results: Choose an option before saving.` |
| Blocked editor, including an invalid optional time limit — help below **Can’t save yet** | `Fill in the required fields below to save.` | `Select a field below to fix it.` |

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor already leaves an unsupported saved choice unselected, focuses the existing picker from the summary, and sends the chosen option only on explicit save. The summary uses the same focus action for required and optional fields. This patch changes two English strings and updates their browser assertions; it does not change field validation, persistence, save-result handling, permissions, or the Gateway contract.

**Skill in practice:** The writing guide says to place recovery where the reader can act and name controls as they appear. The **Send results** label already names the control in both places, so its message gives the next action without repeating the label or sending the reader to a terminal. The summary tells the reader what the clickable list actually does instead of treating every invalid field as required.

Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e346c5e4-f828-45b2-be8f-1aad6754fbad)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5def37a2-ee34-4e22-9ba8-602f331fa2d1)

## Evidence

**Send results:** clean [before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efb6be56-54da-4246-8bec-15db0678c116) and [after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/105ec1dc-b124-49db-a2c7-98471e83f50c), then annotated [before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1fc7399-6f3e-4c75-b948-582c62f4c76a) and [after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5af46527-10d7-4ee3-abd3-cb25ca3b6894). Both pairs are shown below.

**Optional time limit:** [Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/54cf7b42-81d4-4162-aa79-e9f603959ed4) and [after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1920f73f-3f35-4b16-ad8e-520318f29229).

- Playwright Chromium, light theme, en-US, 1280 × 1000. Before: pinned main `1da4ec2b1537ac880439568c07ff8bf2742b3994`. After: `4e7db72f891370a051a1e2d74e6b55353c22875f` (tree `1820b9739f799ead855da5c237b5f283b37fcd4f`). Captures use the built Control UI against an isolated real Gateway and SQLite database. The paused garden automation is synthetic; its unsupported stored mode was seeded in the offline fixture to match the existing Gateway regression. No automation ran and no provider or destination was contacted.
- Clicked the delivery summary item to focus **Send results**, then chose **Don’t send**. The stored job stayed unchanged until **Save changes**. The browser sent one revision-checked update; an independent `cron.get` and a browser reload confirmed the choice. For the optional-field case, entering `-1` in **Time limit (seconds)** blocked saving. Selecting the field from the summary, clearing it, and saving left no timeout override.
- Three focused browser cases and the existing Gateway/SQLite unsupported-mode test passed. UI typecheck, targeted lint, format, copy and i18n verification, and whitespace checks passed. The i18n baseline regenerated byte-identically; stale translations fall back to English until the normal translation refresh.
- Simplification pass: no new controls, state, code paths, or durable fixture. Production +2/−3; tests +11/−5 in two existing cases. No hosted CI, independent review request, live inference/delivery, or translation refresh was attempted during the original local verification.
- Draft overlap: [#199330](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199330) changes recipient/thread controls and related strings; [#201277](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201277) removes reasoning and related options. After [#205583](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205583) merged, the English catalog conflict was resolved without changing either set of messages. Three focused Chromium cases, including the isolated Gateway save and reload flow, and 30 editor and webhook unit tests passed on the reconciled tree. The UI states shown above were unchanged, so the screenshots retain their original capture revisions.

prs.title: fix(ui): align model metadata checks with the stacked layout
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The model-defaults browser test rejects the account details stacked below a model name, even though that layout is intentional in [#203682](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203682). prs.title: fix(voice): answer phone, meeting and FaceTime consults on Claude CLI agents
prs.body:
Closes #202208

Related: #188440, #161885, #164229, #199379, #199378; supersedes closed #191683.

## What Problem This Solves

On an agent whose model runs on Claude CLI (or another CLI runtime), a phone call (Voice Call realtime), a meeting bot (Google Meet, Teams, Zoom, Slack huddles) or a FaceTime call cannot get an answer from the agent: every consult fails with `No API key found for provider "anthropic"` or a sign-in error, and the caller hears an error. Typed messages and Discord voice to the same agent work.

## User Impact

User impact: phone, meeting and FaceTime voice consults run on the agent's own runtime, including Claude CLI and its configured fallbacks, like a typed message. Embedded-runtime agents keep working. Tool policy is unchanged: callers and meeting participants are guests, FaceTime owners stay owners, and a phone consult's `voice_call` can still only end the current call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared helper `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` always ended in `runEmbeddedAgent` with an explicit provider/model, which calls the provider API directly and never selects the agent's runtime. Discord voice works because it runs a normal agent turn through `runCommandFromIngress`.

- `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` gains `runner: "agent-turn"`: after the helper prepares the consult session (fork from the requester, lineage, delivery fields, lifecycle admission), the consult runs as a turn of that session through `runCommandFromIngress` with `deliver: false`. Prompt building, timeout, cancellation, `onRunStarted`, speakable-text extraction and yield acknowledgements are unchanged. The default stays `embedded`, so Talk (which adapts embedded tool context and is being reworked in #164229 / #199379) and third-party SDK callers are untouched.
- Voice Call, meeting-bot and FaceTime opt in. Voice Call passes a model override only when `responseModel` is configured and a thinking override only when `realtime.consultThinkingLevel` is set; otherwise the session's own selection applies. Meeting consults no longer force thinking `high`; they use the session default. A level a bridge does pass (FaceTime always asks for `off`, Voice Call passes `realtime.consultThinkingLevel`) is a one-run choice: a model without that level runs at its closest one, as on the embedded runner (`8711c7b5a`, below).
- Plugin ingress (`runCommandFromIngress` wrapper): a plugin may omit `messageChannel` for a turn on its own surface. Owner authority still needs a bundled or trusted official plugin, and a named channel must still be the plugin's own. `toolBindings` are accepted only for tools the plugin declares in `contracts.tools`. **This widens the plugin ingress capability** (previously only channel plugins could admit turns); it stays narrower than `runEmbeddedAgent`, which any plugin can already call with an owner bit. Flagging for SDK/security owner review.
- The Claude CLI path carries `toolBindings` from the command attempt into the MCP loopback grant, as the embedded runner already does, so `voice_call` stays bound to the live call.
- Voice Call runs the consult in its service context so Gateway-dispatched tools such as `sessions_send` work from webhook handlers.

Not changed: the Voice Call classic (non-realtime) responder (#188440), Talk's Gateway consult path (#164229 / #199379), Discord voice.

## Review fixes (ClawSweeper review of `1fd6919`)

Rebased onto `main` `d7d546f29` (first commit now `1698a745c`, unchanged content). Second commit `503beb2ae`, one focused test per finding, each red on the first commit and green after:

- **[P1] Sender policy at the MCP boundary.** A Gateway-launched CLI run's loopback grant now resolves requester policy like its embedded twin (`senderPolicyMode: "always"`, owner WebChat still exempt), also when a capped tool list drops node exec, which is what switched it to `when-sender-id` before (`src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts`, `tool-resolution-authority.ts`; keyed on the grant's existing `nodeExecAllowed`, which only Gateway-launched CLI grants carry). HTTP `/tools/invoke` keeps `when-sender-id`. Voice Call also passes the remote party's number (`from` inbound, `to` outbound, the identity inbound admission checks) as the consult's `senderId`, so `toolsBySender` entries apply to the caller. Tests: `src/gateway/mcp-http.voice-consult-grant.test.ts` (real MCP loopback, grant built by `buildCliMcpGrantContext`: `tools/list` without `sessions_send`, `tools/call sessions_send` refused, control case with an identified caller), `tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts`, Voice Call `runtime.test.ts`.
- **[P2] Verbose not saved.** New `verboseOnce` command option (like `thinkingOnce`): it sets the run's verbose level and is never written to `SessionEntry.verboseLevel`. Consults use it instead of `verbose: "off"`. Test: `session-preparation.test.ts` (one-shot runs at off and the row keeps `full`; the persistent override still saves).
- **[P2] Workspace.** The agent turn gets the consult's already-resolved `workspaceDir` (restored `spawnedWorkspaceDir`).
- **[P2] Account and reply target.** The turn's run context carries the resolved account, destination (`currentChannelId`) and thread (`currentThreadTs`), with `deliver: false` unchanged. Tests for both: `agent-consult-runtime.test.ts`.
- **[P2] Voice policy surface.** The CLI MCP grant keeps a provider that carries a tool policy (`voice`, `discord-voice`, `node`) when it is not a delivery channel, so the voice filter still drops `tts`. The same surface also hides `ask_user` (no question input on a phone line), as on the embedded route. Other non-channel providers stay unset as before. Test: `mcp-grant-context.test.ts`.
- **Tests.** The mock-echo binding case in `attempt-execution.cli-mcp.test.ts` is removed; the loopback test above covers the grant at the MCP boundary.

## Follow-up fix found by the meeting/FaceTime e2e (`8711c7b5a`)

The first FaceTime e2e (a stand-in plugin with FaceTime's consult parameters, `evidence-e2e-surfaces-red-503beb2ae.log`) failed on `503beb2ae`: FaceTime passes `thinkLevel: "off"`, and on the agent-turn route the command's model selection rejects an explicit level the model lacks, so every FaceTime consult on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` failed with `Thinking level "off" is not supported for anthropic/claude-opus-5-5. Use one of: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra.` The embedded runner clamps such a level to the closest supported one, so this was a regression for any FaceTime agent on such a model, embedded or CLI. New command option `thinkingOnceClosest` lets a one-run level fall through to the attempt's existing clamp, as subagent spawns already do; consults set it. A persistent `/think` override and other callers still get the error. Test: a new row in `model-selection.configured.test.ts` ("prefers observed max support"), red with `503beb2ae`'s `model-selection.ts`, green after; the helper and Voice Call tests assert the flag. After the fix the FaceTime consult runs at `--effort low` and the Gateway logs `Thinking level clamped to low for anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (requested off; preference retained).`

## Follow-up fix found while tracing a Google Meet e2e failure (`7f72cb5c7`)

Plugin `runEmbeddedAgent` runs its turn as a detached work continuation ("plugin turns can outlive both the triggering request root and its async work scope"); plugin `runCommandFromIngress`, which this PR's agent-turn route uses, did not. A meeting's realtime bridge is opened inside the `googlemeet.join` request, so a consult that reaches the command queue after the request that started it has ended lost its admission with `Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.`, where the embedded route kept going. `runCommandFromIngress` now runs its turn as a detached continuation, the same way (`src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ts`, one wrap). Test: `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ingress-continuation.test.ts` (an ingress turn that starts after its parent root and async scope ended), red on `8711c7b5a` with `GatewayDrainingError` at `enqueueCommandInLane` ← `runtime-agent.ts`, green after (`evidence-unit-ingress-continuation-7f72cb5c7.md`); the PR's test-lines allocation goes from 13 to 69 for it. A consult whose tool call itself arrives after that request ended still fails one step earlier, at `beginSessionEffect`, on `main` too; see "Pre-existing" under Evidence.

## Evidence

### Proof status: meeting callback path is blocked by a known bug on `main`

On this PR alone, as on `main`, a meeting consult that arrives through the normal provider callback cannot complete, because of a known bug on `main` that this PR does not touch: a realtime voice consult issued from a callback runs under the already-released root of the request that opened the call (`googlemeet.join` / `googlemeet.create`), and `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` → `beginSessionEffect` refuses it with `GatewayDrainingError` ("Gateway is temporarily unavailable" / "Gateway is draining") before any runner is chosen. It fails the same way on the embedded route on `main`.

- Reported in #142610 (meeting, Google Meet) and #202915 (FaceTime).
- Fixed by #202979 (fresh root admission inside `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent`, covers every voice bridge) and, for meetings only, #142692. Both are open and waiting on maintainers.
- This PR only changes what happens after admission (which runner executes the consult), so it neither causes nor fixes that refusal. Once #202979 (or #142692) lands, the normal meeting callback reaches this PR's agent-turn route unchanged. This is shown below: with #202979 applied **temporarily** on top of `7f72cb5c7` (throwaway local branch, never pushed, not part of this PR), a meeting consult delivered through the normal provider callback after `googlemeet.join` returned was answered by the real Claude CLI; the same run on `7f72cb5c7` alone is refused at `beginSessionEffect` ("Meeting through the normal provider callback").

The proof below is sufficient for the change this PR makes: real Claude CLI answers on the phone route with sender-policy refusal; bundled Google Meet and FaceTime plugins running their own code into the agent-turn route with real Claude CLI answers; a **live FaceTime call on the exact head** by the FaceTime plugin author; and an upgrade from the latest stable release with existing sessions and saved preferences intact. The meeting callback entry is shown too, with the separate fix applied temporarily; without that fix it stays blocked by the bug above, not by this change.

### Real model (Claude CLI 2.1.325, operator's own login, `8711c7b5a`)

Same isolated QA Gateway as the stub runs (private state, own log file, `env -i`), with the real `claude` binary behind a small logging wrapper that gives only the CLI process the operator's `HOME` so its login works, and logs argv, the CLI's `system/init` tool list, `tool_use` names and the final result (no credentials). Twilio and the realtime peer stay simulated; the fixture's consult question is replaced. The `anthropic` provider base URL points at an unreachable local port, so any embedded fallback could not reach the API. Files: `evidence-e2e-real-answer-8711c7b5a.log`, `evidence-e2e-real-policy-8711c7b5a.log` (same runs on `503beb2ae`: `*-503beb2ae.log`).

`safe-read-only`, caller asks "what is 17 times 23?":

```text

[+25.8s] consult answered in 3606 ms
FINAL TOOL RESULT: {"text":"17 times 23 is 391."}
real claude system/init: {"claude_code_version":"2.1.325","model":"claude-opus-5-5","apiKeySource":"none",
  "tools":["ToolSearch","mcp__openclaw__memory_get","mcp__openclaw__memory_search","mcp__openclaw__read","mcp__openclaw__voice_call","mcp__openclaw__web_fetch"],
  "mcp_servers":[{"name":"openclaw","status":"connected","source":"dynamic"}]}

`owner` policy, `tools.toolsBySender["*"].deny: ["sessions_send"]`, `tts` allowed; the caller asks the agent to relay a message with `sessions_send`. The requester's own chat turn (first CLI process) has `sessions_send`, `tts` and `ask_user`; the phone consult (last CLI process) has none of them, the model says so, and a direct call on the consult's own loopback grant is refused:

FINAL TOOL RESULT: {"text":"No, the message wasn't sent, because a tools-by-sender policy blocks the sessions_send tool for this phone session."}

  tools/call gateway       -> "gateway needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner. Do not retry gateway."

```

(`session_status` inside the consult shows `Runtime: Claude CLI` and `Auth: api-key (qa-mock-anthropic ...)`: the QA harness seeds a placeholder Anthropic profile; the CLI itself reports `apiKeySource: "none"`, i.e. its own login.)

### Meeting and FaceTime through the bundled plugins (Claude CLI 2.1.325, operator's own login, `7f72cb5c7`)

Same isolated QA Gateway and Claude CLI wrapper as the phone run, on a dist built from `095c1ce7e` (the same tree as `7f72cb5c7`, whose commit message was reworded afterwards). Only the `claude` process gets the operator's `HOME`, and the `anthropic` API base URL is a dead local path (0 requests reached it). This time the **bundled** plugins run their own code; a test plugin (`.artifacts/vci-e2e/surface-real-plugin`) stands in only for what has no local equivalent. Three real consults in total (meeting ×2, FaceTime ×1; the meeting log is the second run, which also lists the consult's session row; the first gave the same answer). Files: `evidence-e2e-real-meeting-7f72cb5c7.log`, `evidence-e2e-real-facetime-7f72cb5c7.log`, commands in `commands-e2e-real-surfaces-7f72cb5c7.md`.

**Google Meet.** `googlemeet.join {transport: "chrome", mode: "bidi"}` on the bundled `google-meet` plugin: its Chrome transport, realtime engine and `createMeetingRealtimeEngineBindings(...).handleToolCall` → `consultMeetingAgent` → `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` (`runner: "agent-turn"`) → google-meet's own `api.runtime.agent.runCommandFromIngress` (no `messageChannel`, guest). Faked: `browser.request` (the Chrome tab, in call with mic on and audio routed), `pactl`/`parec`/`pacat` on `PATH` (the meeting audio device), and the realtime voice peer, which emits `openclaw_agent_consult` and records the tool results.

**FaceTime (owner).** The bundled `facetime` plugin is loaded and registered with `ownerHandles` and a realtime config. A test-side Gateway preload (`surface-real-preload.mjs`, a Node load hook, in memory, no file edited) records the plugin's own `register(api)` argument and exports its bundled, otherwise unexported `startFaceTimeTalkDriver`. The test plugin then starts that talk driver for the owner handle with facetime's own `api.runtime`, config and logger, from its service context (where the `facetime-runtime` service would create its helper RPC server). Everything after that is the plugin's code: talk driver → `createFaceTimeConsultController` → `handleToolCall` → `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent {senderIsOwner: true, runner: "agent-turn", thinkLevel: "off"}` → facetime's `runCommandFromIngress` (bundled-plugin owner admission). Faked: the native helper and carrier (no FaceTime.app, no injected helper, no call events), the capture helper (`facetime-audio-capture` printing its two readiness lines) and `sox` on `PATH`, and the realtime peer. The platform check is not faked: it only gates the `facetime-runtime` service (native helper supervisor), which stays off on Linux; the talk driver and controller do not read `process.platform`.

  gateway config.get -> "Action not available: config.get"   (passed the owner gate; config reads are off on this surface)
[agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=2073 outBytes=19
Thinking level clamped to low for anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (requested off; preference retained).

Owner admission: a non-owner turn gets `gateway needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner` before the tool runs (phone run above); the FaceTime consult's call reaches the tool. The earlier stand-in run (`evidence-e2e-surfaces-8711c7b5a.log`) showed the other side: the same owner consult from a non-bundled plugin is refused with `Plugin "vci-surface-consult" cannot admit authenticated owner authority for channel "unknown".`

**Pre-existing, not changed here.** When the peer delivers its tool call from a timer created in its `connect()` (the async context a provider WebSocket opened by `googlemeet.join` has) after `googlemeet.join` has returned, the consult fails before any runner is chosen: `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` → `beginSessionEffect` throws `GatewayDrainingError` because that request's root is already released. `beginSessionEffect` sits at the same place in the helper on `main` (`src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts:352` at `d7d546f29`), so this hits the embedded route the same way; the runs above deliver the peer's events from the test plugin's service context instead. File: `evidence-e2e-meeting-released-root-7f72cb5c7.log` (stub `claude`, no model turn):

```text
FINAL TOOL RESULT: {"error":"Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly."}
[vci-debug] GatewayDrainingError Error
    at new GatewayDrainingError (dist/gateway-work-admission-*.mjs)
    at beginSessionEffect (dist/session-controller.lifecycle-*.mjs)
    at consultRealtimeVoiceAgent (dist/realtime-session-harness-*.mjs)
    at async consultMeetingAgent (dist/plugin-sdk/meeting-runtime.js)
```

This is the known `main` bug described under "Proof status" above (#142610, #202915), with open fixes in #202979 and #142692; this PR leaves it to those.

### Meeting through the normal provider callback, with #202979 applied temporarily (Claude CLI, `7f72cb5c7` + #202979)

Same isolated Gateway as the runs above (`env -i`, private home, state dir, config and log file). Agent `main` is on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` with `agentRuntime: claude-cli`, and the `anthropic` API base URL is a dead local path, so an answer can only come from the CLI. In the real-model run only the `claude` process gets the operator's `HOME`, through a logging wrapper on the Gateway's `PATH`. The bundled `google-meet` plugin runs its own code: `googlemeet.join {transport: "chrome", mode: "bidi"}`, its Chrome transport and PipeWire-Pulse backend check, the realtime engine, then `handleToolCall` → `consultMeetingAgent` → `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` (`runner: "agent-turn"`) → `runCommandFromIngress`. Faked, because there is no local equivalent: `browser.request` (a test plugin loaded through `plugins.load.paths`, with the browser plugin disabled, acts as a Chrome tab that is in the call with the mic on and audio routed), `pactl`/`parec`/`pacat` stubs on `PATH`, and the realtime voice provider and peer. **What changed from the meeting run above:** the peer now sends `openclaw_agent_consult` through the normal provider callback. The call comes from a timer created in the bridge's `connect()`, which runs in the async context of the `googlemeet.join` request, and the timer fires only after the driver has recorded that `googlemeet.join` returned. It no longer comes from the test plugin's service context. A test-only Gateway preload (an in-memory Node load hook; no file is edited) logs where any `GatewayDrainingError` is constructed.

**#202979 is not part of this PR.** It was applied only for these runs: its single commit (`8fbc75de3`) was cherry-picked onto a throwaway local branch on top of `7f72cb5c7`, built with `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 pnpm build`, run, and then deleted. The branch was never pushed. This PR's head is still `7f72cb5c7` (local and fork). The cherry-pick had no textual conflicts. Its production change (`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` wrapped in `tryBeginGatewayRootWorkAdmission("realtime-voice-agent-consult")`) is byte-for-byte #202979. I made one test-only change: on this branch FaceTime consults run as an agent turn, so #202979's new FaceTime test also needs a `runCommandFromIngress` mock, and it asserts that mock instead of `runEmbeddedAgent`. Temporary patch versus `7f72cb5c7`:

```text
 .../facetime/tests/talk-driver.consult.test.ts     | 144 ++++++++++++++++++++-
 src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts             | 135 +++++++++++++++++--
 src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts                  |  39 +++++-
 3 files changed, 302 insertions(+), 16 deletions(-)
```

Tests on the temporary branch:
- #202979's own tests (`src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.test.ts`, `extensions/facetime/tests/talk-driver.consult.test.ts`): 39 passed.

Isolated Gateway (QA gateway child, private state, mock voice provider, mock realtime bridge that calls `openclaw_agent_consult`), stub `claude` on `PATH` speaking stream-json and calling the real MCP loopback. No real model or provider credential.

| `safe-read-only` tools on the CLI route | n/a | MCP tools exactly `memory_get, memory_search, read, voice_call, web_fetch`; `write` → "Tool not available"; `voice_call initiate_call` → "This realtime consult may only end_call." |
| `owner` tool policy, guest caller | n/a | `sessions_send` to another session accepted; owner-only `gateway` refused ("not started by the owner"); `voice_call` still end_call-only |

Latency (gap called out in the task): the consult now goes through typed-turn preparation (session, model and runtime selection, workspace bootstrap) instead of a direct embedded run. On quiet runs with an embedded (mock) agent, base answered in 2.0 / 2.4 s and this branch in 2.4 / 3.2 s from media start to the final tool result, so expect up to roughly half a second more. Runs on this shared host that hit I/O stalls ranged 5.8–15.9 s on base and 6.6–8.2 s on the branch, so treat the numbers as indicative. Queueing: the turn queues only behind other turns of the same consult session (per call, per meeting, per FaceTime call), not behind the requester's chat, because the consult session is its own key.

The branch merged `main` at `cc79ae6` in `15a238d`. Commit `a5e3371` reverses a temporary, synthetic-fixture-only CI probe; its source tree is identical to `15a238d`. - Beam adoption: [PR job 139002954370](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45554107749/job/139002954370) failed `src/gateway/server.beam-owned-view.test.ts` at line 591 with `UNAVAILABLE`. The Beam test, handler, state lifecycle, and test runner files are unchanged between scheduled `main` revision `e80be914` and the PR CI tested base `79e42e0`. This is a test module lifecycle failure exposed by file order; the production lifecycle guard remains in place.

The test passes alone on local `main`, so the failure is sensitive to its run context.

prs.title: fix: preserve memory trust after Claude CLI file edits
prs.body:
Refs: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180796
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165452, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/153426

## What Problem This Solves

Explicitly selected native Claude `Edit`/`Write` can change saved memory without updating its provenance, causing the next clean edit to quarantine it. CLI loopback and native network results could also lose turn taint, allowing untrusted memory to retain agent trust.

## User Impact

Local Claude CLI memory writes retain their hash continuity and turn origin: clean tracked files remain eligible for automatic memory, while tainted, non-owner, and already-quarantined files remain untrusted. Native tool permissions do not expand; Agent/Workflow-only selections still deny native Edit/Write.

This does not rehabilitate existing quarantine, change the schema or hash-continuity rule, or track shell writes, paired-node writes, or other harnesses' native tools. The session-rooted tool-builder repair is separate in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201509.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share one host-owned admitted-turn taint state across CLI events, transcript recording, native observations, and loopback write/edit/apply_patch. Capture the canonical preimage after an allowed native `PreToolUse` and observe the actual file after successful `PostToolUse` through the existing provenance owner. Native execution and rollback remain native-owned.

The P1 follow-up reuses the backend's existing `projectNativeToolAuthority` capability mapping to classify native network results, including Claude `WebFetch` and `WebSearch` when no projected MCP network-tool metadata exists. It does not guess from native tool spelling or accept client-supplied taint. MCP and display-only events do not acquire native capability metadata. Simplification retained the existing owners; no new capability API, store, schema, or recovery path was added.

## Evidence

### Current repair

- Native WebFetch and WebSearch regressions failed against prior PR head `44fd853a85b0ffeed0ca9ba01d6efeded374f458`: provenance remained `agent` after native mutation and a clean tracked follow-up, and the root files remained in bootstrap. They pass with this repair.
- The regressions use the production Claude backend's metadata, actual stdio transport and parser/event/tracking path, actual PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks, a synthetic native executable, and real filesystem/provenance/bootstrap. They seed `MEMORY.md`, `USER.md`, and `memory/nested/note.md`. Native-only cases intentionally have no projected MCP network metadata. Clean, non-owner, stale-hash/quarantine, failed-mutation, retired-callback, and Agent/Workflow-only controls remain covered; separate controls reject name-only, MCP, and display-only classification.
- Focused native, loopback, taint, transcript, permission, and protocol suites: **160 tests across 9 files passed**. The final native fixture also passed all **6 cases** after the small test-table simplification. Commands used `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks`.
- Core and affected agent-test type lanes, scoped lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. An initial lint preparation hit the host's OS-thread limit; the same supported lint path passed with `GOMAXPROCS=2`. No checks were disabled.

### Real Claude proof — prior combined build

[Holger's live proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201478#issuecomment-6995176499) reports 20 real Claude CLI turns on an isolated Gateway. Before: `da8fd166f5bca52a464470cf9172bdd7a58106cf`. After: this PR's **old head `44fd853a85b0` plus PR #201509 head `8cd5bf449788`, merged locally**. All live turns were owner turns via `chat.send` with `operator.admin`.

That proof covers clean and network-tainted **loopback** writes, native Edit/Write hash continuity and bootstrap eligibility, failed native edits, sticky quarantine after shell-induced hash drift, and Agent/Workflow-only denial. It supersedes the previous blanket statement that no real Claude proof had been performed, but **does not cover the native-network P1 flow or this new head**.

Coverage limits:
- The native Edit/Write live runs used **agent-level** `tools.exec.host: "node"` while Claude still ran locally. **Per-session** `execHost: "node"` instead selected paired-node placement and failed without a paired node (`missing execNode`). Paired-node writes remain out of scope.
- A missed PostToolUse and a retired callback/grant could not be forced live; those remain synthetic-boundary controls.
- **Required live rerun on head `5656d83c6340d84137ced409b63fafc0682193ff`:** native WebFetch/WebSearch → native Edit/Write → clean tracked edit → provenance and fresh-session bootstrap checks. This rerun remains reserved to Holger; prior-head combined-build proof is not current-head proof.

### Review status

[ClawSweeper's P1 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201478#issuecomment-6993425706) covers old head `44fd853a85b0` and identified the native-network defect addressed here. It is prior-head review evidence, not a fresh review of this repair. The earlier Auto Review helper was unavailable; no clean local review or new hosted re-review is claimed. **Remain draft: live rerun and current-head independent/security review are pending. No landing performed.**

Contributor: Holger Gruenhagen (@holgergruenhagen).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @holgergruenhagen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/692b31b0-d814-47d4-aa85-65f70a3d4c48)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/f5c7778d-2e4d-4562-9405-715610c495a5)

## Worked on by

- @holgergruenhagen

prs.title: fix(macos): launch alert shows the CLI's schema refusal instead of generic credential steps
prs.body:
Closes #201468

## What Problem This Solves

When the macOS app's bundled CLI refuses a forward schema migration because an older Gateway service still uses the same state, the launch alert hides the refusal. Instead it tells the user to run `openclaw doctor --fix` and restore backup credentials. Doctor meets the same refusal, so that advice cannot work, and the refusal's own remedy appears only in the unified log.

## User Impact

User impact: with an older, separately installed Gateway service (for example a global npm install), the alert now shows the CLI's refusal. The refusal names both versions, the service's install root, and `openclaw update`.

Every other credential startup failure still shows the existing Doctor/backup recovery, unchanged. That includes native credential admission errors, other CLI failures such as an invalid config, timeouts, and the background-only stderr path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ClientCredentialStartup.prepare` now throws a `PreparationError`. When the CLI exited with the refusal from `assertGatewayServiceSchemaMigrationAllowed` (`src/state/openclaw-state-service-installation.ts`), the error also carries that sentence. The launch handler shows that sentence only for that refusal.

Two cases deliberately keep the generic recovery:

- **Native admission failures**, such as `Local client credential schema does not match version 1`. They carry no next step. This addresses the earlier review finding.
- **The previous build's app-managed service**, the `StaleGatewayServiceReplacement` path. There the refusal names `openclaw update`, which reports `host-managed` on an app-owned install, so it would replace one wrong instruction with another. That variant has a different root cause: replacement stops the service, but the guard reads the installed service definition. It is described in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/201468#issuecomment-7020325845 and belongs in its own fix.

The alert title and the generic text are the existing strings, so the localization inventory does not change. The branch is rebased on main after #201505, so the handler uses `requestTermination()`.

## Evidence

### Proven on this revision

- **Regression test** (`ClientCredentialStartupTests`): drives the real `ClientCredentialStartup.prepare` boundary with a child CLI that exits 1 and prints the schema refusal on stderr. It asserts:
  - the recovery is exactly the CLI's refusal sentence for a separately managed older service;
  - generic recovery is kept for the app-managed stale-service replacement path;
  - generic recovery is kept for a native admission error (`Local client credential schema does not match version 1`);
  - generic recovery is kept for an unrelated CLI failure (the existing failed-preparation test).
- **Composition test:** the `ClientCredentialStartupCompositionTests` malformed-config launch keeps its expected `OpenClaw client credentials need recovery.` stderr.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes (`changed=false`); the alert title and the generic recovery strings are unchanged. `git diff --check` is clean.
- `git merge-tree` against current `main` (91dee12) is clean. #203382 conflicts only in `ClientCredentialStartup.swift`. The compatible resolution keeps #203382's exact-entrypoint replacement admission and applies this PR's refusal classification only on the non-replacement path, so either order of landing works.

### Still required before merge

- `ClientCredentialStartupTests` RED on base `64416d16a2` with the regression-only patch applied, then GREEN on head `8d899626d0`.
- Maintainer-approved `macos-swift` CI on the exact head.
- On a disposable Mac, captures of a locally built packaged app:
  1. the generic Doctor/backup alert before the fix;
  2. the CLI's schema-refusal sentence after the fix, against an older, separately managed Gateway;
  3. the generic Doctor/backup alert still shown for a native credential admission failure.

I have no Mac, so no macOS execution or packaged-app behavior is claimed. A step-by-step recipe for a volunteer is in the comment below.

prs.title: fix: let Macs and iPhones join claws that use custom member roles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signing in to a claw with OpenClaw ID from the Mac app (and the upcoming iOS app) fails right after another device approves it, with "Setup did not finish". It happens whenever the claw has a member with a role other than `operator` or `viewer`, for example a custom participant role. Member roles became opaque names in #197697, but the Swift client still rejected any other role and treated the claw's whole membership snapshot as malformed.

## User Impact

On claws with custom member roles, owners and members can approve a new Mac or iPhone again, and members can join them. Claws that only use `operator` and `viewer` are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Swift snapshot check now accepts any role name matching the protocol's `isMemberRole` rule (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`), so the client agrees with the Gateway and Discovery. The role still grants nothing on the client, and the rest of the strict snapshot validation is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on the iOS simulator (iOS 27.2) against a live staging claw that has a custom member role: after a web approval, the client logged `OpenClawIDNodeEnrollmentError.malformed` from snapshot validation. The macOS app built from main failed the same way.
- `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter 'OpenClawIDMemberJoinTests|OpenClawIDOwnerEnrollmentTests|OpenClawIDNode'`: 56 tests passed on macOS 27.2 / Xcode 27.2. The member-join test now approves a `participant` role.
- With this fix on the iOS simulator, the same web approval completed: the device was admitted as an owner device of the claw ("You're all set").
- Not yet shown: the updated test failing on the base.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix: open an agent turn for a subagent that finishes after the reply
prs.body:
## Problem

If a subagent finishes after the parent has already replied, its "<agent> finished" row floats under the finished turn. It has no avatar and isn't part of any turn. The parent's work on that result then starts a separate turn below it. If the same child finishes again in the meantime, the row shows up twice.

The cause is in the Gateway's display projection. A completion that wakes the parent becomes a receipt, and that receipt kept no run id. The wake input is saved with the send key of the run it starts (`<runId>:user`). `subagentCompletionMessage` read the run id only from `steerTargetRunId` and `runId`, so the receipt belonged to no run. The UI's turn grouping then left it outside every agent frame.

A turn that opens with a row instead of text, such as a "finished" row or a tool row like "Read a.ts", also sat at the top of the avatar instead of centered on it. Text lines are centered by the bubble's top padding, but rows had no matching offset.

## Change

- `subagentCompletionMessage` falls back to the wake's send key. The receipt now carries the run its wake started, so the Control UI puts it at the top of that agent turn, with the avatar, followed by the parent's work and reply. This also works while the parent hasn't written anything yet.
- History is projected when it's read, so existing transcripts are fixed too. No migration is needed.
- A second completion from the same child that steers into that run now has the same run id, so it joins the same row. Each agent in the row is named once and shows the outcome of its latest run.
- Completions that arrive while the parent waits on its children (a settle wake that resumes the turn) still stay in the answered block with their Resumed rule.
- When an assistant turn with a gutter avatar opens with an activity group or tool row, that row gets top padding of `(avatar − row line height) / 2`, so its line is centered on the avatar. Direct threads without an avatar, reply-attributed groups and turns that open with text keep their current spacing.

## Evidence

- Gateway projection test: a wake receipt carries the run it started. It fails on `main` and passes here.
- New transcript-chain test: a completion that arrives after the answer opens its own agent frame, both before and after the parent replies.
- Render test: two receipts in a row for the same agent show one "finished" row.
- Passing: `chat-display-projection.visibility`, `chat-message.tools`, `chat-background-run-lifecycle`, `chat-thread-incremental`, `chat-pending-input-display`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:core`, oxlint, oxfmt and stylelint.
- Reproduced from a real parent transcript: receipts at seq 3096, 3112 and 3068 rendered outside every agent frame. With the run id, each one joins the frame of its announce run.
- Alignment measured in the browser: with a 36px avatar and a 21px row, the row's top used to match the avatar's top (169px for both). With this change it is at 177px, which centers it on the avatar.

### Clean comparison: the parent replied to the completion

Control UI with a mock Gateway. The history was made by running `projectChatDisplayMessages` from each revision on the same synthetic raw transcript: a wake input saved with the announce run's send key, then the parent's reply. Before is `main` at aecbf92d24e5, after is this branch.

### Annotated comparison

### Before the parent writes anything
