prs.title: fix: explain how to correct an automation’s next check delay
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a running automation’s agent omits its next-check delay or supplies a value the tool rejects, the error doesn’t show a working value. The agent needs to know which argument to change and what to send in the follow-up call.

## User Impact

The agent’s error now names the `in` argument and gives a working example: `"5m"`. This is model-facing tool output, not a change to chat copy or the Automations page. No human action or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the two messages change. Missing or empty input still throws `ToolInputError` (400); unparseable or nonpositive durations still throw plain `Error`. The tool schema, parser, active-run authority, proposal receipt, and scheduling behavior are unchanged. The Gateway invoke transport still masks plain errors; making them visible there by changing their category is outside this patch.

## Evidence

The same isolated in-process agent loop ran on the exact base and candidate. A scripted provider fixture called the actual Automations tool and received the results below on its follow-up model requests. No provider was contacted and no Gateway call, persistent job, or scheduler timer was created.

| `next_check` input | Before (literal model output) | After (literal model output) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Omit `in` | `in required` | ``Set `in` to a non-empty duration string, for example `"5m"`.`` |
| `in: "later"` | `cron next_check in must be a positive duration` | ``Set `in` to a duration greater than zero, for example `"5m"`.`` |
| `in: "0m"` | `cron next_check in must be a positive duration` | ``Set `in` to a duration greater than zero, for example `"5m"`.`` |
| Corrected call, `in: "5m"` | `{"ok":true,"delayMs":300000}` | `{"ok":true,"delayMs":300000}` |

The three error cases were marked `isError: true` in both runs; the corrected call was not. The run registry recorded a 300,000 ms proposal. The committed regression failed on the old wording (3 failed, 9 passed) and passed after the change. The candidate’s focused test run passed all 69 tests (including the temporary evidence fixture; 53.4 s tool wall time). Targeted lint, the changed-file `services-cron` test typecheck, formatter, copy check, and diff checks passed. No screenshots: this evidence is the model boundary, not rendered UI or a live provider. No CI or independent review ran; bound autoreview was not available.

**Skill in practice:** Write for the first reader (the agent), name the exact argument, and give one recovery example that the tool accepts. Keep the product term “automation” in prose instead of carrying the internal “cron” name into the message. The simplification pass retained the existing validation owner and fixture; production +16/−4, tests +30/−0. No new runtime helper, exception class, or scheduling path.

Co-authored with @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e346c5e4-f828-45b2-be8f-1aad6754fbad)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5f8a660c-38f4-4112-ae75-221234b2005a)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: stop the terminal UI from re-showing old run errors after a reconnect
prs.body:
Root cause: src/tui/tui-session-run-coordinator.ts:306 re-appends every retained run-error notice after every queued history rebuild, and the retained list (filled at src/tui/tui-run-lifecycle.ts:424) is never retired by newer runs, so old failures land below newer messages, under the latest "gateway reconnected after transport loss" line.

Fixes #205527

Thanks @compoodment for the detailed report, screenshot and Gateway journal that showed no new provider errors.

## What Problem This Solves

After a Gateway restart or any TUI reconnect, the terminal UI showed old run errors (for example past automation rate-limit failures) again at the bottom, right under `gateway reconnected after transport loss`, with nothing marking them as old. Each reconnect followed by any new run repeated the same block, so operators chased failures that had not happened.

## User Impact

Old run errors stay where they were shown; once a newer run happens, a history rebuild no longer brings them back below newer messages. A new failure still shows as before. A freshly connected TUI renders the same history as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The TUI keeps rendered run errors in memory so a history rebuild that was delayed by another run (which clears and redraws the chat) does not erase them (#104864). That retention never ended: every later rebuild appended all retained errors at the end. Now the first observation of a newer run retires the retained errors in the coordinator that owns them. The delayed-rebuild case from #104864 still restores the error, because that rebuild follows a run that was already running when the error arrived. No Gateway change: the errors are client-side memory, not replayed events.

Deltas vs main: production +5 lines (one condition, two comment lines), tests +11 lines (one regression in the existing coordinator suite, red on main).

## Evidence

Built Gateway and TUI from this branch and from main (43f872f17162) inside a secretless node:24.22.1 container. A scripted chat-completions fixture returned HTTP 429 for one scheduled main-session automation (3 attempts, 3 run errors) and normal replies otherwise. TUI driven in a tmux pty; flow: `hello one`, failing automation, `hello two`, then twice: Gateway restart, TUI reconnect, one successful automation run.

| Run | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| errors, restart 1 + ok run | 3 old `run error` rows under the reconnect line | 0 |
| errors, restart 2 + ok run | 3 old `run error` rows under `... x2` | 0 |
| control: new failure after 2 reconnects | 4 rows (3 old + new) | 1 (the new one) |
| control: no errors, 2 restarts | 0, screens identical | 0, screens identical |
| control: fresh TUI connect | 0 rows, history identical | 0 rows, history identical |

Terminal captures: [evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205555#issuecomment-7174124749). Focused tests: `src/tui/tui-session-run-coordinator.test.ts` and `src/tui/tui-event-handlers.test.ts` pass (130); the new regression fails on main (`restoreTerminalError` called twice). The existing `restores a terminal error when another run delays a history reload` test passes unchanged.

Merge danger: two-way door. Client-only, in-memory TUI behavior; a revert fully restores the previous behavior. Blast radius: the TUI chat log after history rebuilds.

prs.title: fix: show an example for unreadable automation dates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you create or edit a one-time automation through the Gateway API and enter a date OpenClaw can’t read, the error repeats your input and names a timestamp standard without showing a usable value.

## User Impact

The response gives an example of a future date and time you can submit. OpenClaw no longer echoes the rejected value. A rejected create saves nothing, and a rejected edit leaves the existing automation unchanged. The accepted formats and the `INVALID_REQUEST` error code are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway’s shared validator already knows when it can’t parse the date. It now gives both callers the same correction without changing validation, access checks, or the handling of past and far-future dates.

**Skill in practice:** Say what happened, give one action the reader can take now, and keep raw input out of the reader-facing message. Show an accepted example without implying it is the only format.

## Evidence

| Trigger / surface | Exact Before | Exact After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway WebSocket `cron.add` or `cron.update` with a nonempty, unreadable one-time date | `Invalid schedule.at: expected ISO-8601 timestamp (got synthetic-unreadable-time)` | `OpenClaw couldn’t read the scheduled time. Enter a future date and time, such as 2026-11-26T22:30:00.000Z.` |

The after cell is the exact validator output for a fixed reference time of November 25, 2026, at 22:30 UTC. Real Gateway requests get a dynamic example one day ahead of the validation time.

On the pinned base, both authenticated WebSocket calls returned these fields (request ID omitted; the submitted value is synthetic):

```json
{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Invalid schedule.at: expected ISO-8601 timestamp (got synthetic-unreadable-time)"}}
```

On the fix, the isolated Gateway regression asserted `ok: false`, the same `INVALID_REQUEST` code, and the after sentence with its generated timestamp on both calls. It verified that the failed add created no record and the failed update left the existing job unchanged. It then used the timestamp from the live response to retry both calls and read back both saved schedules.

The Gateway regression and eight parser and timestamp tests passed on `56a6a2831d0886a9929facfc663b7d00a2357ae6` (48.64 seconds locally, including cold compilation). Targeted lint, typecheck, copy, format, and diff checks passed. The campaign reviewer checked the exact candidate and its merge tree; bound autoreview was unavailable. Hosted CI was not run. This is a WebSocket API response, not a changed Control UI or CLI screen.

Proposed by [@vyctorbrzezowski](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski).

prs.title: fix: sessions_history no longer reports truncation for stripped usage metadata
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts:151` set the sanitizer's truncation bit whenever it deleted top-level `details`, `usage` or `cost`. Lines 522-523 turn that bit into `contentTruncated`, and line 543 turns it into `truncated`. An intact reply like "hello" therefore reported truncation.

Fixes #205271. Thanks @samueltardieu for the precise report and @ericcurtin for the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_history` reports `contentTruncated: true` and `truncated: true` for a short reply like "hello" whose text is intact. This happens whenever the provider recorded usage, because the only thing removed is metadata. Callers such as conversation scribes can't tell intact text from clipped text, and reading one message at a time doesn't clear the flag.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stripping `usage`, `cost` and `details` no longer sets the truncation flag. These fields are still stripped exactly as before.

None of the three is visible text:
- `usage` and `cost` are accounting numbers.
- `details` is the Gateway's display projection of a tool result: exit code, cwd, diff, browser tab, approval state. The model never saw it in the original turn. The model-facing tool text stays in `content`, which is still clipped and flagged.

Stripping is unconditional, and no option returns these fields, so a flag for them can't lead a caller to do anything. It was also set on nearly every read from a real provider. Visible text clipping, the 80 KB cap and oversized-row replacement still set the flags as before. No new fields, and the tool description is unchanged.

## User Impact

`contentTruncated` and `truncated` are true only when visible text was shortened or messages were dropped or replaced.

## Evidence

- Regression test: a short message with `usage` reports no truncation. It fails on main (`contentTruncated: true`, `truncated: true`) and passes here.
- Touched and importing suites pass (11 files including `openclaw-tools.sessions`, `sessions-history-tool`, anchor budget, gateway chat history and prefix stability). oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Gateway proof (built dist, real agent turns, `POST /tools/invoke` and an in-turn `sessions_history` call, main vs this head, twice each, with controls for long text, the 80 KB cap and tool-result `details`): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205335#issuecomment-7176856836

## Merge danger

Two-way door. This only changes two booleans in a read-only tool result: no stored state, schema or config changes, and a revert fully undoes it. Blast radius: `sessions_history` callers that read `truncated` or `contentTruncated`.

## What Problem This Solves

When you click **Run now** on an automation whose saved settings OpenClaw can’t use, the error tells you to check the schedule and instructions. The Gateway response does not identify a field. For example, a saved command assigned to the main chat is rejected even if its schedule and command are both valid.

| Where | Exact before | Exact after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Automations** → an open automation → **Run now** | “Couldn’t start this automation. Check its schedule and instructions.” | “OpenClaw couldn’t start this automation with its saved settings.” |
| **Settings → Agents → Automations** → **Run now**, using the name Daily digest | “Daily digest: Couldn’t start this automation. Check its schedule and instructions.” | “Daily digest: OpenClaw couldn’t start this automation with its saved settings.” |
| Automations when the response is shown after you leave the originating automation, using the same name | “Daily digest: Couldn’t start this automation. Check its schedule and instructions.” | “Daily digest: OpenClaw couldn’t start this automation with its saved settings.” |

## Why This Change Was Made

Both surfaces already use the same English copy for the Gateway’s `invalid-spec` result. The result means the run did not start; it does not say which setting is wrong or guarantee a new history row. The change stays at that copy owner and keeps the receipt, history refresh, diagnostics, access rules, and error formatting intact.

**Skill in practice:** The writing guide calls for tracing the producer and both readers. The receipt is specific enough to name the saved-settings problem, but not specific enough to prescribe a field change, promise a history row, or recommend another run.

## Evidence

- In Chromium at 1280 × 900, clicked **Run now** against an isolated, built Gateway through both entry points before and after. The persisted synthetic legacy fixture used a valid command with a saved main-chat target that does not accept commands. No mock WebSocket, external delivery, or provider inference was used. Both entry points returned `invalid-spec` with `ran: false`. For this fixture, the **Skipped** history row retained its diagnostic, and **Edit** opened the automation settings. The post-navigation name prefix uses the existing attribution path, covered by the focused test.
- The focused regression failed on the old wording and passed on the new one. 38 focused tests passed across action feedback, lazy English registration, the Automations page, and the Agent Automations panel. Targeted lint, formatting, copy, locale, and Git whitespace checks passed. Both UI builds reported the same existing largest CSS and chat boot request budget notices. Full CI and foreign locales were not tested.

prs.title: fix: explain how to correct an automation webhook URL
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you create or edit an automation that sends results to a webhook, the editor gives the same error for a missing URL prefix, an address it can’t read, and an address with a username or password. The message doesn’t tell you which part to fix.

## User Impact

The **Webhook URL** field and its clickable validation summary now say what to correct. The same URLs are accepted or rejected, nothing saves until you choose **Create automation** or **Save changes**, and the editor doesn’t check whether the webhook can be reached.

| Trigger and surface | Exact before | Exact after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blank URL — inline | `Webhook URL is required.` | `Enter the URL where OpenClaw should send results.` |
| Blank URL — summary | `Webhook URL: Webhook URL is required.` | `Webhook URL: Enter the URL where OpenClaw should send results.` |
| Missing or unsupported URL prefix — inline | `Webhook URL must be a valid http(s):// URL without embedded credentials.` | `Start the URL with https:// or http://.` |
| Missing or unsupported URL prefix — summary | `Webhook URL: Webhook URL must be a valid http(s):// URL without embedded credentials.` | `Webhook URL: Start the URL with https:// or http://.` |
| URL can’t be parsed or its host is rejected — inline | `Webhook URL must be a valid http(s):// URL without embedded credentials.` | `OpenClaw can’t read this URL. Check it for typos.` |
| URL can’t be parsed or its host is rejected — summary | `Webhook URL: Webhook URL must be a valid http(s):// URL without embedded credentials.` | `Webhook URL: OpenClaw can’t read this URL. Check it for typos.` |
| Username or password in the URL — inline | `Webhook URL must be a valid http(s):// URL without embedded credentials.` | `Use a webhook URL with no username or password in the address.` |
| Username or password in the URL — summary | `Webhook URL: Webhook URL must be a valid http(s):// URL without embedded credentials.` | `Webhook URL: Use a webhook URL with no username or password in the address.` |

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor already checks the prefix, parses the URL, and rejects usernames or passwords in the address. Each existing check now selects the message that matches its result, in one place. The editor doesn’t suggest removing credentials from a URL that might need them; it asks for a webhook URL without a username or password in the address.

**Skill in practice:** The writing guide asks for the known cause and an action the reader can take where the error appears. Tracing the validator showed it can name a missing prefix or a username/password, but it can’t say which part of a malformed address is wrong or whether a remote endpoint works.

## Evidence

- Chromium 156 exercised the production-built Control UI at 1280 × 1050, light theme and English, with a synthetic Gateway. All four rejection states were captured before and after. In each, the inline and summary text matched, the create action stayed disabled, and activating the summary with Enter focused **Webhook URL**. A valid HTTPS URL cleared both messages and reached the mock as a create request. Editing a saved automation rejected shorthand; a corrected HTTP URL reached the mock as an update request. No run, real Gateway write, or network delivery was tested.
- The webhook validation regression failed for the four expected prefix or username/password fixtures on base. 95 focused Control UI tests passed on the change (41.46 s local wall time, including first-time transforms). Control UI typecheck, scoped boundary lint, catalog verification, copy check, changed-file formatting, and diff checks passed; regenerating the raw-copy baseline found no drift. Hosted CI was not run.
- Author source review and simplification confirmed the existing validator remains the only owner. Production diff: +9/−6 lines; tests: +11/−5. Independent autoreview could not start because its preflight requires temporary space outside the checkout. No independent review result is claimed.

Missing URL prefix during creation. Before: pinned main `cbb3bd640908`. After: tested commit `921a4a92991c`, which has the same tree as the published head. The URL and automation are synthetic.

``To check the result on the same Gateway, use `openclaw automations runs` with the automation ID and `--run-id {runId}`.`` | **Skill in practice:** Name what stopped (the CLI wait), don’t claim the run failed, and give the reader one lookup that won’t start the automation again. - Real CLI and isolated loopback Gateway on Linux: a disabled automation with a synthetic 12-second command exceeded a 500 ms wait. prs.title: improve(ui): highlight skill references in the composer
prs.body:
Related: #152599 (inline `$skill` references; standalone slash commands are unchanged). Builds on #192242.

## What Problem This Solves

Selected skills remain raw `$command_name` text in the composer, making them harder to distinguish from surrounding prose and person mentions.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session show known skill references as highlighted, atomic names with the existing skill icon and no visible `$`. Copying and sending preserve the canonical reference. No configuration or migration is required.

**Studio benchmark:** Chat matched the first person mention. New Session still falls short of p95 parity (77.28 vs 71.63 ms across 50 matched observations per variant). The current CI and existing asset budgets passed; the performance gap is open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the generic native-first editor and extension contract from the final merged #192242, rather than introduce another editor, overlay or dependency. Skills use the existing command catalog and share atomic boundary editing with people. Display labels no longer grant reference identity: only canonical commands and normalized command identifiers are recognized. Unknown references, shell variables, escaped dollars and code remain literal.

Ordinary edits map existing skill decorations instead of rescanning the draft. Token/Markdown-sensitive edits still use the canonical parser; image-bearing drafts deliberately retain full parsing. Atomic editing checks only affected chip boundaries and does not serialize large pastes for single-character separator checks. Literal dollars may load the small parser, but cannot fetch CodeMirror until a reference is admitted. Catalog replacement explicitly refreshes labels/removals and admits unchanged restored drafts; subscriptions end with their native/editor owners. Native undo snapshots, asynchronous handoff, IME boundaries and retired-frame guards are preserved. Skill integration still composes through the mention adapter, not a new feature framework.

## Performance acceptance for this landing

Use production builds and alternate samples on the same host. The known-good reference is `491c2944` (merged person mentions); keep an identical-reference control and the previous skill head `0283e5b6`. Collect at least 10 paired Chromium samples per route, cold and warm separately, and record renderer CPU median/p95, structural work counts and request/asset sizes.

Chat and New Session must stay native for a long unrelated draft containing `$HOME`, with zero whole-draft skill scans on subsequent unrelated typing. In rich mode one ordinary key after a 64 or 128 KiB word must not require work proportional to the word. Confirm exact `$command_name` output, late catalog changes, Markdown/escaped text, cursor, undo and chip selection.

Person-only typing, selection, undo, mixed typing and large paste must stay within the identical-reference sample spread, with no repeatable regression in median or p95. Time cold first skill from the first `$` through selection and an interactive editor; compare with the analogous first person mention and the old skill head. Validate the real Gateway flow as well as the repeatable benchmark. Enforce the startup asset gate without raising the limits.

## Evidence

### Studio qualification of the final product tree

Paired production Chromium, renderer CPU in ms, synthetic Gateway for timings, with identical baseline as a control. Kept the original tails. Repeated five scenarios whose original runs overlapped other validation.

| First use | Known-good person mention | Candidate skill |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Chat, 10 pairs | 84.50 / 88.26 | 84.25 / 86.96 |
| New Session, all 50 pairs | 68.95 / 71.63 | 67.63 / 77.28 |
| New Session, 20 pairs | 69.25 / 71.63 | 67.83 / 104.45 |
| New Session confirmation alone, 10 pairs | 69.62 / 72.99 | 68.53 / 72.21 |

Values are median / p95. New Session originally had two higher samples (104.45 and 117.36 ms); neither recurred in the ten untraced confirmation pairs or the separate trace. The cause is unconfirmed, so this does not claim full p95 parity. The following 30 untraced pairs retained the earlier observations and produced no candidate samples above 77.28 ms. The 50-pair identical person-mention control was 68.43 / 73.93 ms. A local matcher experiment removed 400 name normalizations on the first dollar with 200 skills, but the measured paired median improved only 0.91 ms, within control variation; that experiment is not part of this PR. For ordinary typing, undo and mixed paste, differences were within the matched run's variation.

- An unrelated 69,014-character draft stayed native. Skill scans over 12 unrelated keystrokes fell from 38 to zero in Chat and 27 to zero in New Session. The rich editor reads four old document positions after an ordinary key, down from 65,540 in the long-word case.
- An isolated real Gateway and production Chromium accepted exact skill references in both routes. Chat also demonstrated downstream expansion. The bundled Chat E2E checks handoff and the raw payload for two skills; the 390 px New Session E2E and 12 focused Chromium tests passed after consolidating duplicate coverage.
- The paired build against main passed the existing asset limits: Chat −10 B gzip, New Session +372 B gzip, no new startup requests. The test-only follow-up removed 97 counted lines and passes the exact CI ratchet with 34 lines to spare.


### Current candidate

- Signed head \`86339fea5f6d65f5b3eb4c5e61eeee3fee5fb027\` matches the production build verified in Chromium against an isolated real Gateway on Chat and New Session. Raw \`$HOME\` stays native; person avatar selection and undo still work; the installed skill was copied and accepted by the Gateway as the exact raw reference. The test model endpoint was local; explicit expansion was verified in Chat only.
- On the 69,014-character literal-dollar draft, twelve unrelated keys caused 38 → 0 full lexical scans in Chat and 27 → 0 in New Session. One rich edit after a 65,536-character word went from 65,540 → 4 document reads; the revised count stayed 4 at 32,768 and 131,072 characters.
- The current-main merge build passes all asset budgets without changing limits. JavaScript request counts stayed 21 for Chat and 17 for New Session. Gzip change: Chat −10 B, New Session +372 B, largest JavaScript asset +430 B. The older budget evidence below refers to its pinned historical base.
- Late catalog, token boundary and Markdown coverage passed in Chromium. A trusted browser case also proves the fast path invalidates correctly when a controlled writer changes earlier text to a known skill without changing the draft length. Typechecks, focused lint and independent P2 review passed.

### Current repair and review — November 16

Published head `0283e5b68266ebb706dab8a9d74623406693488e` has exactly the tested product tree of implementation `ec4b449ebd8e2e0e468f10da9fec32b8ec9b789b` (`37b3739503d08c1fbe431ff51ae1ba6af24bcb99`); the publisher's final commit is attribution-only.

- **218 browser tests passed in 13 files**, including person/skill editor consumers, native handoff, undo, paste/drop, composition simulation, ref disposal, catalog/command consumers, overflow, height and mobile fixtures. UI and script typechecks, scoped lint/format, controller guard and whitespace checks passed.
- **Both source-server real-UI Chat/New Session flows passed** with a synthetic Gateway. The new network assertion first failed on both routes: `$HOME`/`$unknown` fetched the rich editor. It now passes while actual skill selection and canonical submission still work.
- Both hosted P2 findings on `6d45233` were reproduced red and repaired: display-name aliases could look selected without resolving on submission; unchanged drafts did not react to catalog arrival/rename/removal. The catalog regression verifies stable editor identity, raw text and selection.
- Independent local **autoreview through P2 was scoped-clean** for the final staged repair against `6d45233`, subsequently committed as `ec4b449`. It included the generic editor, mention adapter, import lifecycle, catalog owner, Gateway reference-resolution contract and Markdown parser as context. Static review is not runtime proof. Earlier reviewer findings for indentation, adjacent backticks, native history and literal-dollar loading were repaired; the staged-only loading finding disappeared when the reviewed working-tree fix was committed.
- **900 valid repair timing observations** were collected across explicit source stages: 390 at `08ec3b39`, 270 at `452d63a5`, then **240 on the final product tree**. Completed interrupted work was retained rather than replayed; one restart interruption in the first stage is excluded from valid observations. Earlier-stage measurements are not relabeled as final-head proof.
- Final separate diagnostics found **zero full-draft skill scans for twelve unrelated keys** in both Chat and New Session, down from twelve on the original feature. Ten people/eight skill chips and exact raw text survived; one editor remained mounted and stylesheet rules did not grow during typing. A final bounded 21-round-trip session lifecycle replay also passed on baseline and candidate; this is not a universal no-leak claim.

### Acceptance rule — unchanged

Baseline `491c2944f56ad7d6d9a561a17dfffcd42cab49e3` already contains the final merged mention foundation. Compare same-toolchain production builds with at least ten serial rotating baseline/candidate/identical-baseline rounds. Report median, p95, ranges and host load; keep traced diagnostics separate. Require no correctness loss, unexpected RPCs, per-key remounts/owner-echo transactions or unbounded resource growth. Median regression must be at most 5% with no worse p95; unresolved tails need confirmation. A confirmed move above 20% blocks blanket performance acceptance. Existing asset limits remain unchanged. Mock-renderer, live-Gateway and native-device evidence remain separate.

### Final production-build timings

Chromium `156.0.8078.4`, Linux x64, real production UI with a synthetic Gateway. These are **renderer main-thread CPU milliseconds per action**, not per-key latency, INP, total process CPU or live-provider latency. Long typing is twelve trusted characters in a 64 KiB draft; mixed drafts contain ten people/eight skills. Paste is 256 KiB synthetic clipboard input. Catalog size is 200. Each row has ten observations per variant; each cell is **median / p95**. A/A is an identical baseline.

| Flow | Baseline | Final candidate | A/A control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat person-only long | 55.567 / 60.265 | 55.551 / 60.269 | 56.480 / 59.302 |
| Chat mixed long | 52.028 / 58.309 | 54.160 / 57.572 | 54.125 / 56.980 |
| Chat literal dollars | 38.862 / 43.498 | 39.343 / 42.133 | 38.111 / 45.286 |
| New Session person-only long | 52.058 / 54.542 | 53.371 / 58.238 | 53.519 / 57.152 |
| New Session mixed long | 45.783 / 50.206 | 46.555 / 55.102 | 46.154 / 49.780 |
| New Session mixed paste | 23.195 / 25.057 | 23.746 / 26.502 | 22.933 / 25.102 |
| Chat first skill, including first dollar | 47.118 / 52.273 | 87.230 / 91.677 | 48.570 / 52.067 |
| New Session first skill, including first dollar | 45.679 / 49.449 | 74.020 / 81.182 | 44.615 / 48.706 |

The original mixed-typing median regressions were +8.39% Chat and +8.97% New Session. Final mixed medians are +4.10% and +1.69% versus baseline, and +0.06% and +0.87% versus A/A. This supports removal of the measured hot-path waste, not universal parity: New Session person/mixed/paste p95 are still +6.78%, +9.75% and +5.77% versus baseline. The complete acceptance rule therefore remains unmet.

**First-use work is not hidden in preparation.** New `first-skill` workloads start from an untouched native draft and include the first dollar, catalog readiness, typing the query, selecting the skill and settling imports. Older `activate-skill` rows measured selection after typing the query; they are selection-only evidence, not cold first-use parity. Native-to-rich first-use cost remains approximately +40.1 ms in Chat and +28.3 ms in New Session. At the earlier `08ec3b39` stage, short skill-only typing was 20.170 → 36.529 ms and 200 occurrences were 64.712 → 127.286 ms. Those are native-versus-rich feature costs, not all attributable to parsing, and are not waived or claimed as final-head measurements.

Final CPU ranges: Chat mixed baseline 49.655–58.309 / candidate 51.451–57.572 ms; New Session mixed baseline 45.098–50.206 / candidate 44.695–55.102 ms; Chat first-skill baseline 46.277–52.273 / candidate 85.950–91.677 ms; New Session first-skill baseline 43.821–49.449 / candidate 70.785–81.182 ms. Final host load ranged 1.95–6.04 on 128 logical CPUs. Complete distributions and per-run manifests remain in the linked task under `catalog-final-summary.txt`, `catalog-final.log.summary.json`, and raw observations. No outliers were removed.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, prior evidence and scope</summary>

The committed workload extends `scripts/lib/control-ui-chat-composer-scenarios.ts`, using the existing engine runner. With matched baseline and candidate builds:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts \
  --bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --compare-bundle-dir dist/control-ui \
  --control-bundle-dir .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui \
  --source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --compare-source-root . \
  --control-source-root .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base \
  --engines chromium --viewport desktop --pairs 10 \
  --steps composer-qualification-chat-first-skill,composer-qualification-new-first-skill,composer-qualification-chat-literal-dollar,composer-qualification-chat-person-long,composer-qualification-chat-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-person-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-long,composer-qualification-new-mixed-paste \
  --output .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/rerun
```

Earlier qualification of `6d45233` retained 510 editing/activation and 62 startup observations, 157 browser cases, eight emulated narrow/dark observations, four scan diagnostics, profiles and bounded retention. Its boot CPU and heap results are historical evidence, not a fresh final-head certification. Earlier repairs retained their own exact-source summaries; only the final table above qualifies the current product tree.

The simplify pass preserves the existing foreign-DOM owner and CodeMirror extension contract. No dependency, editor, overlay, global cache, custom Markdown parser or permission change was added. Necessary growth covers the skill feature, selective invalidation, native history and catalog notification/disposal. Versus `491c2944`, production UI is +714/−263 lines, tests +488/−19, and benchmark code +359/−1. Net test growth is 469 lines; the documented per-change allocation is 69 beyond the standard 400 for reproduced handoff, Markdown, lazy-loading and catalog/identity failures. Startup/performance limits were not raised.

</details>

### Startup asset gate — still failed

Final normalized largest-JS gzip is **569,985 → 570,497 bytes (+512)**. The inherited-over-cap differential permits only 64 bytes: **448 bytes remain over the allowed increase**. Original feature growth was +676 bytes; this repair does not claim the remaining failure is harmless. Chat/New boot gzip grows 539/486 bytes; request counts remain 21/17. CSS bytes and request counts are unchanged. The boot manifest was regenerated without a source diff. No unrelated byte-offset changes or budget increases were used.

Reproduction: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --dist dist/control-ui --base-dist .openclaw/tmp/skill-perf/base/dist/control-ui --json`. The strict comparison exits 1. Inherited absolute CSS/request overages are distinguished from this new differential failure.

### Remaining limits

This is a verified repair update to a draft, not a shipping or zero-regression claim. Startup size, native-to-rich feature cost and remaining p95 regressions are unresolved. WebKit/Firefox could not load the app under the environment's proxy policy on either build; no bypass was attempted. Native OS IME, mobile Safari, real-device/network and live Gateway/provider performance remain unqualified. Composition browser tests simulate events, not a physical input method. No merge or deployment occurred.

The existing inspected visual evidence is retained; this repair changes computation and correctness, not the chip design. Captures use the real UI with a synthetic Gateway; mobile is an emulated 390px viewport.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A long machine-generated extension took four lines in the Review file heading. It pushed the directory and diff body down and left change counts beside the middle of the name.

## User Impact

The heading uses one line for the filename, gives the identifying stem priority over an unusually long extension, and leaves ordinary names like chat.ts and map.png intact. The full name stays in the title and the toggle’s accessible label.

## Why This Change Was Made

The file tree and diff heading now use the same filename split. The heading limits the width of an extension instead of letting it consume the stem. Diff content, change counts, and file selection behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

At 390 px the selected filename went from four lines (80 px) to one (20 px). A click and Enter toggled the original file in both mobile and desktop presentations. The mounted panel was checked at the four campaign viewports, and short extensions were verified in both presentations. The clean and annotated comparisons show a synthetic diff. prs.title: fix(agents): preserve accepted context-engine prompt budgets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Publishing an accepted context-engine turn as ready currently checks the transcript boundary but can replace its effective prompt budget. For example, the same accepted turn can change `runtimeContext.tokenBudget` from 180000 to 64000, or from a known budget to unknown, before `commitTurn` reconstructs typed runtime settings. Ordinary ready-state retries already reject conflicting payloads.

The accepted-to-ready transition now rejects a changed effective budget before updating the row. It compares finite budget values using the same normalization as runtime settings; equivalent unknown values remain compatible. This is a defensive integrity check at the existing durable transition, with no config or API change.

## User Impact

Conflicting publication cannot revise the budget recorded for an accepted turn. The original accepted payload remains available for recovery. Matching budgets, unknown budgets and the current reconstruction of typed settings remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Acceptance and publication are separate durable steps. The SQL transition already protects turn ownership and transcript identity; the accepted prompt budget must also remain stable. This keeps the fix at its persistence owner without adding full runtime-settings serialization or changing native/CLI budget selection, assembly caps, recovery, acknowledgements or operator-source preservation.

## Evidence

- The existing real SQL outbox suite gained an eight-case table. On the unchanged production baseline, the three changed-budget cases fail with the intended missing-collision rejection; five compatible cases pass. A rejected publication must leave the accepted payload unchanged.
- Complete focused owner suite passed 27/27: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/harness/context-engine-turn-outbox.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Wrapper wall time 153.12s; Vitest duration 138.27s, dominated by shared cold compilation (99.686s for 20,587 inputs). The eight new cases took 1.042s combined. Hosted CI time is unmeasured.
- `git diff --check`, formatting and normal pre-commit hooks pass.
- Owning agents/harness typecheck passed on the unchanged candidate: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-tools.json --noEmit --incremental`. A task-specific SSD build-info path and stricter 120-second timeout were used. The first attempt found a missing public shared-resource directory in the sparse checkout; hydrating it made the unchanged check pass. No source change or skipped checks.
- Exact-head local follow-up: normal owning core lint, source-SDK boundary/transport, canonical full source build and strict tarball integrity checks now pass; see below. The earlier extension-boundary preparation reached its unchanged 300,000 ms deadline; subsequent normal preparation passed without changing that guard. Four absolute packaged-UI budget failures, installed/live shipped-entry behavior, genuine upgrade preservation and mandatory CI/review remain outstanding.
- Package-function diagnostics independently reproduced the changed effective-budget transition on released v2026.11.10. Synthetic input, not live-provider or Gateway rollout evidence. This PR does not change release artifacts or operator state.

Tested candidate: `ed8b8ebca1f3e81e56ebc3857de39510e761acc2` (tree `d21e27fb9a502a96592f0b0306d9e09693f730d8`), based on `d3e0449b818308c4d23ecc9d0506bb1166025083`. Normal pre-commit hooks passed. This is separate from the Ollama embedding transport fix in #205356.


### Stored-row compatibility follow-up

A public synthetic file-backed SQLite proof writes rows through the **pristine released 2026.11.10 worker**, closes/reopens the file, then uses the **reviewed 2026.11.10 worker with the matching budget guard** and actual drain to recover and commit them. This is stored-row compatibility across the guarded package change; it is **not an exact contributed-head full build, a real version upgrade, or a shipped CLI/Gateway producer reproduction**.

All six stored cases passed: accepted and ready rows with known budgets (128000/64000), unknown budgets, and entirely absent runtime context. Typed commit reconstruction preserved the known values and kept unknown/absent values null. Changed-budget publication against the three pristine accepted rows failed closed and left their stored payloads unchanged; normal recovery then committed the original facts. One simulated lost acknowledgement survived another close/reopen and replayed identical commit input. Result: six unique commits, seven calls, zero pending rows, SQLite integrity `ok`. No schema or payload-format change was introduced.

The actual SQL serialization/transition/recovery and drain are exercised; only closed-transcript input and the idempotent engine are synthetic. The separate owning repository suite remains 27/27, with exact-head targeted typecheck passed. A conflicting budget arising from a shipped producer has **not** been demonstrated; this remains a defensive integrity check. The review's shipped-entry behavior request, four absolute packaged-UI budget failures, genuine upgrade preservation and maintainer acceptance remain open. Exact-head local declaration/full-source-package proof is recorded below. Keep draft.

### Focused core lint follow-up

The supported command passed on unchanged head `ed8b8ebca1f3e81e56ebc3857de39510e761acc2`:

```sh

```

Normal wrapper/schema preparation and type-aware policy remained enabled. The wrapper explicitly treats core configs as source-backed; no extension declaration skip override was supplied. No source changes, new commits, ready transition or merge.

### Exact-head local build/package follow-up

Unchanged tested head `ed8b8ebca1f3e81e56ebc3857de39510e761acc2` now passes normal owning worker/test core lint and extension-boundary canary lint, normal source-SDK declaration preparation, exact current-input receipt validation and SDK transport packing. The existing 300-second source-boundary deadline and local resource policy were unchanged.

The normal full source build also passed (332.3 seconds), including canonical unified tsdown declarations, runtime/bootstrap checks and Control UI generation. The public SDK export/size check passed at **5,347,852 / 5,385,536 bytes** (5,320,000-byte ratchet plus 65,536-byte output variance). The canonical source tarball passed `check-openclaw-package-tarball.mjs --require-bundled-workspace-deps`: preflight, extraction, npm inventory and dist-import graph. This is exact-head local source-package evidence; it is not an official release, an actual package-install/live CLI/Gateway test, or a genuine version upgrade.

Normal commands used:

```sh

```

**Strict UI budget check: exit 1, four unresolved violations.** Normal UI generation intentionally uses report-only measurement, so its success does not establish a strict budget pass. The separate strict command above reports:

prs.title: fix(ollama): stop silently truncating embedding input
prs.body:
Closes #205353

## What Problem This Solves

Ollama defaults `/api/embed` to truncating input beyond the embedding model's context window. OpenClaw omits that option, so an oversized request can succeed with a vector for only a prefix, silently losing trailing facts from retrieval.

## User Impact

Oversized embedding requests return Ollama's context-length error instead of accepting a truncated-prefix embedding. Inputs that fit the model window continue through the same transport. This does not add automatic splitting or guarantee a successful index rebuild after an oversized input is rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Send `truncate: false` through the existing provider transport. One regression uses the real guarded HTTP transport and a synthetic loopback endpoint implementing Ollama's documented default; existing string and batch request expectations include the option.

The [Ollama embed API](https://docs.ollama.com/api/embed) documents both behaviors. No configuration, permissions, SDK, or stored-data migration changes. The complete diff adds one production payload field and 21 net test lines.

prs.title: fix(android): honor Markdown table column alignment
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android chat renders Markdown table headers and body cells flush left even when the author marks a column as centered or right-aligned. A column of numbers, for example, loses its shared right edge.

## User Impact

Chat now honors column alignment in both headers and body rows. Existing messages pick up the alignment when displayed. Unmarked columns keep their default alignment.

## Why This Change Was Made

CommonMark already supplies the alignment on each table cell. The Android renderer now passes it to the same Compose `Text` that draws the cell’s styled content.

## Evidence

- The new Robolectric Compose test measures all eight header and body labels in one table with unmarked, left, center, and right columns. On the frozen renderer the centered header had 0 px of leading space where it needed 62.5 px. The patched renderer passed the test on SDK 36.
- A chat history replay through the real controller, Room, and Compose, paired with a direct Markdown render, measured 380 cells across 88 cases, including 40 horizontally scrolled cases. All 205 center/right failures were corrected and all 175 left/default cells still passed.
- The existing Markdown and list-layout suites passed all 42 tests. Both changed files passed ktlint 1.8.0. Full pinned Gradle and physical-device rendering remain unverified locally.

The captures show the same synthetic two-column table in Robolectric at mdpi, using frozen `b6e7fcfb` and patched tree `94afa2cd`. The first column requests center alignment and the second requests right alignment.

![Markdown table before and after, showing center and right alignment in both rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d15cabb-a656-44f2-a1d7-643bcc3255d3)

![Measured right-column edges. The largest offset falls from 137 pixels to zero.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/292a9305-6d18-4a16-ab64-8b541244b263)

prs.title: fix(agent-db): drop orphaned FTS5 shadows before recreating standing_intents_fts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent database whose `standing_intents_fts` virtual table is gone but whose FTS5 shadow tables remain cannot converge. SQLite refuses to recreate the virtual table:

```
fts5: error creating shadow table standing_intents_fts_data: table already exists
```

`CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` does **not** help here: the guard only covers the virtual table, not its shadows. The schema ensure path therefore fails, and the caller reports

```
SqliteWorkerError: SQLite worker stopped before its result was received
```

which surfaces as `memory-core: standing intent maintenance failed`.

Measured with the SQLite behaviour that produces it:

| state | `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS x USING fts5(text)` |
|---|---|
| virtual table present | `table x already exists` |
| virtual table gone, shadows present | `fts5: error creating shadow table x_data: table 'x_data' already exists` |

The second row is the one that breaks the ensure path. The guard is absent in the first row too, but that row is not reached here — the ensure path only runs when the virtual table is missing.

## Fix

Drop the orphaned shadow tables before the canonical agent schema is applied, so the ensure path can recreate the virtual table. When the virtual table is still present, the shadows are left untouched.

Two corrections that the first revision of this PR needed, both found by review and reproduced here:

1. **The index is rebuilt, not just recreated.** `standing_intents_fts` is an external-content FTS5 table (`content = 'standing_intents'`, `content_rowid = 'intent_key'`). A recreated external-content index starts empty, so dropping the shadows and recreating the virtual table would leave every pre-existing row unsearchable. The repair now issues `INSERT INTO standing_intents_fts(standing_intents_fts) VALUES('rebuild')` after the schema is applied — but only when shadows were actually dropped, so the normal ensure path does not reindex on every run.
2. **The orphan check reads the live catalog.** The first revision used the admitted schema snapshot (`getAdmittedSqliteSchemaFacts`) and fell back to a fresh capture. The orphaned-shadow state is exactly the state where a pinned snapshot can still claim the virtual table exists, in which case the cleanup silently does nothing and the ensure path still fails. The check now always uses `captureSqliteSchemaFacts(db)`.

## Why this place

`ensureOpenClawAgentStandingIntentsSchema` (`src/state/openclaw-agent-standing-intents-schema.ts`) is the owner that recreates `standing_intents_fts`. It already exports the shadow table list (`STANDING_INTENTS_FTS_SHADOW_TABLES`), so the cleanup needs no new table list.

## Evidence

**The failure is reproduced, not inferred.** The test fixture now builds the orphan state explicitly: `DROP TABLE` on an FTS5 virtual table removes its shadows as well, so the shadows are re-created as standalone tables. Against that state, the plain recreate fails with the issue's error:

```
fts5: error creating shadow table standing_intents_fts_data: table 'standing_intents_fts_data' already exists
```

**RED/GREEN, measured with the same SQLite semantics the fix runs against:**

| variant | virtual table after repair | pre-existing row findable via `MATCH` |
|---|---|---|
| cleanup without rebuild | present | **no match** — index empty |
| cleanup with rebuild | present | **1 match** |

The reproduction script for both rows is included in this PR description's source (the same sequence runs against `node:sqlite`, the same engine the agent database uses).

**Test coverage added** (`src/state/openclaw-agent-standing-intents-schema.fts-shadow.test.ts`):

- orphaned shadows are cleaned up and the virtual table is recreated;
- the fixture state actually breaks the plain recreate (so the first test cannot pass vacuously);
- the rebuilt index contains the pre-existing row (guards the rebuild);
- a live virtual table keeps its shadows (guards against over-eager cleanup).

## Notes

- No database data is dropped: only FTS5 shadow tables of an **absent** virtual table are removed, and the index is rebuilt from the owning content table.
- The same shadow-orphaning shape can occur for the other FTS5 tables (`session_transcript_fts`, `memory_index_*_fts`); this change fixes the standing-intents path that was observed failing. Happy to extend it if the maintainers prefer a shared helper.

## What Problem This Solves

iOS users need native chat and the embedded Dashboard to use the same Gateway-verified personal identity instead of grouping all paired apps under shared credentials.

## User Impact

Users can choose personal Tailscale sign-in when adding a secure Tailscale Serve Gateway, or change it through the visible control on an existing paired Gateway. Successful personal authentication is used for native chat and the existing embedded Dashboard/Profile; there is no second Profile screen.

Leaving the choice off preserves token/QR access. Personal sign-in does not grant administrator permissions, and a failed personal connection never silently falls back to Shared owner. Device/node admission stays separate from human operator identity. Personal mode still excludes persistent offline chat/outbox and Watch command delivery; existing saved history is not migrated or deleted.

The Gateway must serve the matching Control UI changes in this PR. Updating only the iOS app while retaining an older Dashboard parser is not sufficient.

## Why This Change Was Made

The app reuses existing Tailscale admission, signed-device challenges, connection settings and the Gateway registry. Pairing admits the node before starting the personal operator connection; route changes retire obsolete attempts. Trust/retry intent belongs to the matching connection attempt, not a recreated screen.

The Dashboard accepts credential-free Tailscale authorization only with a matching verified recovery scope. Its signing authority remains native and is retired on route changes.

Design help remains welcome: personal identity should follow the explicitly chosen and successfully verified authentication method. A Tailscale address alone is transport, not proof of a person. Broader Profile/account-linking UX, operator naming, local Mac Primary adoption and Cloudflare composition remain separate slices.

The umbrella covers broader clients; this PR is the bounded iOS Tailscale implementation. Existing macOS personal sessions should be reused, not described as absent everywhere.

**Vítor — September 30:**

> But you need to look at this against current main, do you understand?

Current-main inspection was required before deciding what was missing. This transcript records that instruction, not a claim that the candidate is integrated with every subsequent main revision.

### 4. Profile is where optional identities should eventually come together

**Vítor — October 2:**

> We need a way to link people's accounts […] I should be able to say, look, this is my account, and add it to Profile, do you see?

> For anything that interacts directly with OpenClaw, such as channels, this matters, because otherwise the memory itself gets confused.

He connected attribution to an agent harness's longer-term memory: treating one human as unrelated app/channel identities can fragment the user's experience and memory associations. He reported that concern while using a memory integration; this is product rationale, not a measured memory-corruption result.

**Vítor — October 2:**

> And Profile should be where you link or configure identities.

> In more complex cases with multiple identities, such as channels plus authentication, they should all be able to belong to the same profile.

Optional account linking and a unified Profile belong to the umbrella's follow-up work. They must not turn this first slice into automatic account merging, role changes, or inferred identity equivalence between Telegram and an auth provider.

### 5. Authentication should drive identity, without removing the Dashboard

**Vítor — October 2:**

> You're using Tailscale Serve, but you haven't chosen to use Tailscale authentication, for example. That's fine: you use Shared owner. If you decide to use Tailscale authentication, you use Tailscale and automatically stop using Shared owner, do you see?

> In other words, I think this needs to be tied to authentication, do you understand?

The distinction is intentional: using Tailscale Serve as transport is not the same as choosing and successfully verifying personal Tailscale authentication. The preferred UX should follow the validated authentication choice instead of adding an independent “who am I?” switch. This is the requested design direction; the candidate still has the temporary explicit selector.

**Vítor — October 2, after reporting the missing native Dashboard:**

> Not having the Dashboard is unacceptable. If we've fixed the Dashboard issue and then introduce a regression ourselves in another fix, that makes no sense. We need both.

The requirement was **personal native attribution and a usable embedded Dashboard together**, with existing Gateway permissions respected. A chat-only fix that regressed Dashboard access was not acceptable. His report prompted the Dashboard correction; it was not an instruction to grant administrator permissions to every authenticated person.

**Vítor — October 2:**

> But logically, shouldn't it use whatever authentication the person has? Why complicate it?

> At its core, authentication should determine which auth you use, and Shared owner or Owner should be for when you don't have that and only have a token.

### 6. Upgrade observations must retain differences between saved setups

**Vítor — October 2, before replacement testing:**

> Let's test whether it breaks existing setups.

**Vítor — October 2, correcting an over-broad upgrade interpretation:**

> No, that's not what happened. My personal Gateway's setup was preserved. The other one wasn't—the Hive one wasn't. […] But mine, the normal one, started directly. […] We're also comparing different experiences.

The operator reported that one existing personal setup reopened directly while the other required QR pairing. His explanation of why the installations differed was tentative. The transcript must preserve the observed distinction, not convert it into “all saved routes upgraded without intervention” or a proven root cause.

**Vítor — October 2:**

> And we have video. We have the moment when I used the QR code; we have all of that.

> I think it's working. It connected and authenticated directly with the QR code, opened Profile, and my profile appears here.

**Vítor — later that day:**

> Right, but now I've recorded video and everything. […] You've fixed it, the Dashboard appears now; the UX question is where we put shared versus non-shared.

These are operator reports from physical testing. The attached GIFs show only their captioned portions; they do not independently establish complete cold-relaunch migration, forbidden final effects, or final-head coverage of every earlier observation. The remaining proof requests stay explicit rather than erasing the useful human observations.

### 7. Reuse the existing Profile; reject duplicated screens and shortcuts

The assistant introduced a separate native Profile wrapper and entry points while trying to make the selector discoverable. Vítor rejected that direction.

**Vítor — October 2:**

> The problem is that a Profile screen already exists. Creating another one makes no sense. None at all.

> And then you put shortcuts to that screen in several places. What sense does that make? It's vanilla first.

The correction was to remove the duplicate UI layer and keep the existing embedded Profile, personal admission and Dashboard work. That rejected UI experiment is not part of the reviewed candidate. The temporary selector should not be disguised as the final discoverable UX.

Vítor also explicitly requested the upstream `test-audit` workflow, not merely a generic principles review, and later checked that it had actually been used. The test cleanup removed redundant assertions without changing production behavior; its verification is reported separately in the PR evidence.

### 8. Small PRs, separate naming follow-up, and lead-designer integration

**Vítor — October 2:**

> Shared owner doesn't make sense unless it's a multiplayer harness. Otherwise, what does Shared mean? Shared with whom? […] I think we should keep it, but we need to think about this.

> Yes, but Shared should only be for multiplayer.

> We should split this into small PRs under the umbrella. One of them should cover those two options for Shared owner.

Naming “Owner” versus “Shared owner” for single-user/multiplayer contexts is a proposed separate small contribution. It does not authorize silently renaming the current shared principal or removing its compatible behavior in this PR.

**Vítor — October 2, authorizing this PR's temporary UX and design request:**

> Make the PR like this and ask the lead designer to help us integrate it. But suggest synchronizing it with authentication: if it's Tailscale, activate it automatically, as I already told you.

**Resulting contribution boundary:** ship no duplicate Profile, preserve existing shared admission, carry verified personal identity into iOS human operations and the embedded Dashboard, and ask the lead designer to integrate selection/recovery with the existing auth/Profile flow. Automatic identity adoption, account linking, naming, broader native-client adoption and maintainer acceptance remain separate proposals or gates. The transcript explains the human decisions behind the candidate; it is not a replacement for security or runtime qualification.

prs.title: fix(android): keep your place in code when a chat reply finishes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Android chat, scroll to the end of a long code block while an assistant is replying. When the reply finishes and moves into history, the reader jumps back to the first line.

## User Impact

The code stays on the line you were reading when the reply finishes and when chat history refreshes. A different reply or another code block starts with its own reading position, even if the code is identical.

## Why This Change Was Made

The streaming reply and the history entry are separate Compose rows. Carry the reading position across that transition only when a unique new entry from the same run starts with the streamed text and the fenced block matches. Keeping the controller’s text and run identity together also preserves the reader when the server acknowledges a locally started run. If history arrives before the stream ends, each mounted fence keeps its own reading position once scrolled. A matching fence still at its start adopts the stream’s position once.

## Evidence

- In mounted Android chat with a 257-line block, **End of code** reached `FAR Ω` at offset 4484. The frozen build jumped to `FIRST` at 0 after the reply finished. The fix held 4484 through final delivery and a separate history refresh. Copy returned the full source.
- A same-run commentary message with identical fences opened at 0/0. The genuine final restored 160/420, and its newly appended third fence opened at 0. An independent mounted replay with offsets 128/364 also retained both through refresh.
- Two concurrent runs showing identical text kept independent offsets of 4484 and 280 across a server acknowledgment. Expanding a truncated history entry retained offset 9101.
- All six `ChatCodeBlockLayoutTest` cases passed on Robolectric SDK 36 with native graphics. The controller and Room replay used a mounted SDK 34 fixture and synthetic Gateway events. Physical-device behavior remains unverified.
- The fenced-reader regression passed in both hosted Android variants on `efb35c5c4821`. Both jobs failed the delivery geometry test at the `OpenClaw · Live` assertion. [Play result](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45703078554/job/139518729869) · [Third-party result](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45703078554/job/139518729928)
- The geometry fixture now uses a Gateway chat delta and a lifecycle end for the same pending run. In a focused SDK 34 replay, the original fixture passed on the parent and missed the Live label on the signed revision. The corrected events passed on both revisions. Both hosted variants passed the geometry and reader regressions on `b3261a980f6f`. [Play](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45706928842/job/139531862760) · [Third-party](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45706928842/job/139531862761)
- **Terminal first.** In the mounted controller replay, the terminal event cleared the stream before the history viewport took over. The reader held 4484 through settlement and a separate refresh. An identical sibling started at 0.
- **History first.** A synthetic `sessions.changed` event loaded the delivered entry while both rows were mounted. The signed parent lost 4484 at terminal. The repair held 4484 through terminal and refresh when the history fence was untouched. When the reader scrolled the history fence to 96 before terminal, it held 96 through both events.
- In the mounted two-fence test, live offsets were 160/420 and history offsets were 96/0. At terminal the history fences showed 96/420. After the reader scrolled the second fence to 500, refresh kept 96/500. All six SDK 36 reader tests passed locally on the tree signed as `2c6b3156f22a`.

**Installed-app proof remains open.** These are mounted Robolectric checks. No task-isolated device was connected, and the existing screenshot scenes do not exercise this event order. The screenshots below show the earlier mounted fixture.

Both screenshots show the settled reply after the same **End of code** action on frozen `b6e7fcfb` and signed `efb35c5c4821`, respectively. The fixture uses synthetic text.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Settled code block showing FIRST at the top](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2ab9ac1-18eb-454d-9220-e07923a3d09e) | ![Settled code block showing FAR Ω on the last line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19e7bae1-0630-4611-bad0-44907d00c532) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![FIRST marked where the reader reset after settlement](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef60fade-8f46-4e0c-95b1-c18818921e62) | ![FAR Ω marked where the reader stayed after settlement](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e291f7f3-40cf-48b7-92d9-2025a08f0885) |

The corrected head `2c6b3156` passed both Android flavors. In each JUnit report, all six code-reader tests passed, including settlement and refresh, and all 116 composer-layout tests passed, including the full-screen Live-to-final transition. [Play report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45711010150/job/139545793141) · [Third-party report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45711010150/job/139545793040)

prs.title: feat(litellm): declare managesOwnAvailability in plugin manifest
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LiteLLM is an upstream proxy and routing gateway that balances requests across multiple models, API keys, and backends, owning its own rate limit backoffs and transient retry handling. When LiteLLM returns a transient 429 (`rate_limit`) or 503 (`overloaded`), OpenClaw recorded and persisted a local auth-profile cooldown for that profile, locking out subsequent requests locally even though the proxy may have alternative healthy backends available.

## User Impact

Users utilizing LiteLLM as their model provider will no longer experience local auth-profile lockouts upon encountering transient 429 (`rate_limit`) or 503 (`overloaded`) responses. The local transient cooldown is bypassed, while authentication failures (401), billing limits (402), and subscription restrictions remain strictly enforced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Declaring `"managesOwnAvailability": true` in `extensions/litellm/openclaw.plugin.json` opts the LiteLLM provider plugin into OpenClaw's provider-managed transient capacity recovery mechanism (established in #141825 alongside OpenRouter and Kilo Gateway). The core availability policy reads this declaration from metadata before loading the provider runtime.

## Evidence

### 1. Behavior Proof: Production Transport & Failure Handling

Tested against an isolated mock upstream using OpenClaw's real OpenAI completions transport (`streamOpenAICompletions`) and failure recovery pipeline (`handleEmbeddedAssistantFailure` via `failoverRetryController`) with the plugin manifest loaded directly from `extensions/litellm/openclaw.plugin.json`.

```
================================================================
PROOF OF BEHAVIOR: LiteLLM managesOwnAvailability
Production transport: streamOpenAICompletions + handleEmbeddedAssistantFailure
Real plugin manifest loaded: extensions/litellm/openclaw.plugin.json
================================================================

SCENARIO 1: BEFORE PATCH (managesOwnAvailability = false)
- Upstream response: HTTP 429 Rate limit exceeded (retry-after: 60)
- Stream result: stopReason=error errorCode=429
- Persisted state on disk:
    cooldownUntil: 1795643742156
    cooldownReason: rate_limit
- Subsequent request check:
    isProfileInCooldown("litellm:manual", "proof-model"): true
    -> RESULT: Subsequent request WOULD BE SKIPPED locally (profile locked out)

SCENARIO 2: AFTER PATCH (managesOwnAvailability = true)
- Upstream response: HTTP 429 Rate limit exceeded (retry-after: 60)
- Stream result: stopReason=error errorCode=429
- Persisted state on disk:
    cooldownUntil: undefined (NOT PERSISTED)
    cooldownReason: undefined (NOT PERSISTED)
- Subsequent request check:
    isProfileInCooldown("litellm:manual", "proof-model"): false
    -> RESULT: Subsequent request CAN PROCEED (gateway manages recovery)

SCENARIO 3: AFTER PATCH - 503 Overloaded (transient failure)
- Upstream response: HTTP 503 Service overloaded
- Persisted state on disk: cooldownUntil: undefined, cooldownReason: undefined
- Subsequent request check: isProfileInCooldown: false (CAN PROCEED)

SCENARIO 4: AFTER PATCH - 401 Auth Failure (credential failure)
- Upstream response: HTTP 401 Invalid API key
- Persisted state on disk: cooldownUntil: <timestamp>, cooldownReason: auth
- Subsequent request check: isProfileInCooldown: true (ENFORCED & LOCKED OUT)

SCENARIO 5: AFTER PATCH - 402 Billing Failure (balance failure)
- Upstream response: HTTP 402 Insufficient balance
- Persisted state on disk: disabledReason: billing
- Subsequent request check: isProfileInCooldown: true (ENFORCED & LOCKED OUT)
```

### 2. Unit & Integration Tests

- `src/plugins/provider-availability-policy.test.ts`: Verifies bundled `litellm` manifest declares `managesOwnAvailability: true`.
- `src/agents/auth-profiles.markauthprofilefailure.test.ts`: Verifies end-to-end failure marking on disk/SQLite: 429/503 skips cooldown persistence for LiteLLM, while 401 (`auth`) and 402 (`billing`) remain strictly enforced.
- `extensions/litellm/index.test.ts`: All 13 existing LiteLLM extension tests pass.
- Verified test suite passes: 3 Vitest shards passed cleanly.
- Code hygiene: `run-format` and `oxlint` pass with zero errors.

prs.title: fix: check for a usable account before switching session models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A session could report a successful model switch even when the Gateway had no account for the requested provider. The failure showed up on the next message instead of when the choice was saved.

## User Impact

If the requested host route reports a missing or failed account, the switch is rejected and the previous selection stays in place. OpenClaw does not try another provider or restart the current turn. Someone who wants the same model through a different provider must select that provider explicitly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session patch reads the requested route’s published account facts before saving an inherited host runtime selection. This check does not start discovery, choose a runtime, or turn an inherited runtime into a pin. A cold catalog or a cooldown is not treated as a missing account. An active or required worker with local inference owns its ambient credentials; an explicitly pinned account is still honored. No provider fallback, tool-specific policy, or banner change is included.

## Evidence

A regression exercises the Gateway’s session patch handler with a synthetic session and credentials for the relay only. On the base, the unavailable direct route was accepted. On the rewritten patch, the direct request is rejected without changing the stored session, a separate explicit relay request succeeds without pinning a runtime, and required worker-local inference is not rejected for missing Gateway credentials. No live sessions or external inference were used.

All 174 tests in the six focused Gateway and agent suites passed, along with the core typecheck, targeted lint and formatting, and whitespace checks. Local diff review found no actionable P0/P1 issues.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): view_image and read cannot open a channel image by media://inbound ref
prs.body:
Closes #196287
Related: #129269

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `view_image` ("Sandbox media reference is not staged") and `read` ("File not found") failing in a sandboxed session when given the `media://inbound/<id>` ref of a channel image (Matrix here). The staged copy is in the workspace and the prompt names both forms.

## User Impact

The model can open a current-turn channel attachment by either name the prompt gives. No new permissions or configuration. Security-sensitive path (CONTRIBUTING guard); needs `/allow-security-sensitive-change`.

## Why This Change Was Made

#129269 mapped only `file_*` upload handles to staged paths and left `media://inbound/...` refs on the flat path, where the staged copy never is. The map now also carries each staged fact's canonical `media://inbound/<id>`; the resolver and `read` use it when no workspace file exists at the flat path. Workspace-boundary checks run on the staged path unchanged. PDF goes through the same resolver.

## Evidence

Four tests: the real `stageSandboxMedia` then resolving the ref (`IMG_9854---8705be7d-….jpg`); `read` through tool assembly on a staged ref; `read` keeping a real workspace file over the alias; two facts sharing one ref dropping the alias (both staged copies exist, so only the ambiguity rule rejects it).

Before (main):

```text
Caused by: Error: Sandbox media reference is not staged: media://inbound/IMG_9854---8705be7d-aa4d-4744-aa9e-607677e85cde.jpg
 ❯ resolveSandboxedBridgeMediaPath src/agents/sandbox-media-paths.ts:69:13
Error: File not found: media/inbound/a.txt.
```

After: touched test files pass on macOS with the default temp dir. Wall time (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`): `sandbox-media-paths.test.ts` 4.8 s, `agent-tools.read.staged-media.test.ts` 8.5 s, `stages-inbound-media-into-sandbox-workspace.test.ts` 6.4 s. Net test growth is +114 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/sandbox-inbound-media-ref.txt`: the four tests cover the staging-to-resolution handoff, sandboxed `read` assembly, workspace precedence and the ambiguity rule for media:// refs. The `realpath` in the staging fixture is needed because macOS tmp is a symlink and the media store must match the resolved source. `pnpm check:changed` fails only on the dead-export guard, in files this PR doesn't touch (`src/daemon/launchd.ts`, `src/plugins/provider-runtime.ts`, …).

Live check: v2026.11.2 (b556fdf) plus this PR's source changes (4c807210, 5e4173a2), as my gateway on macOS, podman sandbox backend, Matrix encrypted DM, photo sent with the message. Redacted tool calls:

```text
view_image {"path": "media://inbound/IMG_0099---69a0e34c-….jpg"}
→ success: "Loaded 1 image into private model context …" (image/jpeg, 169379 bytes), rewrittenFrom: "media://inbound/IMG_0099---69a0e34c-….jpg"
read {"path": "media://inbound/IMG_0099---69a0e34c-….jpg"}
→ success: kind "image", image/jpeg, 170913 bytes
```

Stock 2026.11.2 fails the same `view_image` call with "not staged".

Not covered: the Docker backend; a ref from an earlier turn (the map is per turn, so it still fails as before); spellings other than the canonical `media://inbound/<id>` (they fail closed as before); PDF has no specific test.
