prs.title: fix(codex): avoid repeated discovery for unavailable plugin apps
prs.body:
Related: #99071 (similar discovery symptoms; no historical disk-I/O attribution).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Codex discovery delays between messages when a configured plugin app remains missing or inaccessible.

## User Impact

User impact: unchanged conversations no longer force hosted connector discovery on every message for the same unavailable plugin apps. An unavailable app can take up to one minute to be reconsidered automatically; installation, explicit invalidation, and manual refresh remain immediate. No configuration changes or migration are required, and unavailable or policy-denied apps remain unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Readiness repair reuses a successful, covering forced refresh in the existing app-inventory cache for one minute, including a negative result, and joins an equivalent forced refresh already in flight. Account/thread isolation and target coverage still apply. Non-forced cold reads do not suppress the first forced repair; activation, current native policy checks, and explicit refresh retain their existing paths. There is no second cache manager, new configuration option, or permission-policy change.

Explicit runtime refresh also invalidates cached thread readiness in that account/runtime. A scoped thread refresh leaves siblings alone. Key construction and invalidation share the existing cache owner and unchanged thread-ID encoding.

## Evidence

Committed regressions use credential-free external I/O fixtures through the production config builder, manual command handler, and warm thread lifecycle/client owners. Acceptance: bound unchanged unavailable-app discovery without suppressing explicit refresh or relaxing admission.

| Scenario | Before | Current candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three unchanged config builds, missing/inaccessible app | 3 forced reads on base | 1 |
| Three unchanged warm lifecycle turns, inaccessible app | 3 forced reads on base | 1 |
| Three unchanged builds, ready app control | 0 forced reads | 0 |
| Successful runtime refresh within the negative thread cooldown | Next warm build still excluded the connected app | Both cached same-runtime threads reconsider and admit the available, policy-allowed app |
| Other account/runtime snapshots and current native denial | Must remain isolated/enforced | Remain isolated/enforced |

- Original discovery regressions are red on `cfa40212f9c6ce442a36e6ad6b8df07eec9b6ae5` and green with bounded reuse, including the warm-lifecycle entry point with synthetic native I/O.
- Follow-up regression is red on production source matching reviewed head `2ffb9d003a19049a2db1b3a2b762f55bd1b49bd8`: the actual `/codex plugins refresh` handler succeeds at the runtime key, but the next production thread-config build still returns an empty app policy. With the clock frozen inside 60 seconds, the fix recovers two thread keys, leaves other canonical account/runtime keys untouched, and still enforces a subsequent native denial without more inventory work.
- Red/green command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/command-plugins-readiness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "repairs warm thread readiness after runtime refresh" --reporter=dot`. A separate cache contract protects encoded sibling-thread scope during targeted invalidation.
- Current focused runs: **440 tests passed across 14 Codex files**, including the four requested modules, activation/manual refresh, migration, read-only/scheduled policy, lifecycle and run attempts. Prompt-prefix stability: **14 passed**. Total: **454 passing tests across 15 files**.
- Scoped repository typecheck covering all eight changed TypeScript files and imported consumers, oxlint on those eight files, nine-file formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Fresh independent Auto Review through **P0–P2**, using `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. It covered the complete nine-file local candidate against `cfa40212…` (diff SHA-256 `13d10df931e6920eb6f0564f3b59429603b1bba58efef414b1191ba58415595a`). This supersedes the earlier P0-only local assessment; the reviewer did not independently execute tests or verify live native integration.
- Author simplification: the existing invalidation operation owns runtime/thread invalidation; the existing encoded thread-key constructor moved to that same cache/key owner and all callers migrated. No second manager, new option, generation/fence, or test-only production seam. Whole-candidate delta against the base: production +77/-20, tests +261/-3, docs +11.

Native contract inspected at pinned Codex 0.164.0 revision [6aaac694](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/apps_processor/installed.rs): non-forced installed reads reuse the native snapshot, while forced reads refresh hosted runtime tools.

Limits: synthetic lifecycle/work-count proof, not an authenticated Gateway/model/connector run, macOS incident reproduction, or measured live latency/disk-I/O improvement. This does not establish a cause or fix for a separate WebSocket reset loop. Broad [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199120/checks) is running; local proof is not a CI pass.

Contributor credit: Jacqueline Henriksen.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/06c4f96a-597f-422a-9735-1351c122f5d1)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/131dc99c-4032-420a-871c-1820b0e131b5)

prs.title: fix: keep long file extensions from crowding the Chat Files list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An unusually long file extension could take all the space in a Chat Files row. The filename before the dot disappeared. Wrapping the extension instead made that row taller than neighboring files.

## User Impact

Files stay on one line. When space is tight, the long extension ends in an ellipsis so the filename and the arrow remain visible. Short extensions such as `.ts` stay readable. Selecting the row still opens the exact file.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mobile and desktop Files lists give both parts of the name room instead of letting the extension grow without limit. No file paths, text sizes, or Sessions sidebar styles change.

## Evidence

The clean and annotated pairs show the same synthetic file in the real Chat Files panel on an emulated 390 × 844 phone at default text size. On the base, the filename before the dot had zero visible width. It now has 95 px, and the row stays 48 px high, the same as README.md. The previous wrapped PR revision made the same row 80 px high. All 10 focused browser tests passed. At all four campaign widths, opening the exact file and returning preserved the chat draft and issued no file write. Base styles: `ab2da2bfe8c44`; revised head: `209fb096538a3`.

prs.title: fix(ui): show the author's avatar on pending suggestions, like queued messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In a shared chat, suggestions from other people sit in a tray above the composer until the owner sends, queues, edits or dismisses them. Each row showed only the author's name, while the pending-message queue right next to it shows the sender's avatar, so the two trays looked unrelated. Reported by Vyctor Brzezowski, whose screenshot also showed a long pasted suggestion taking over the footer. #204920 has since fixed that overflow with a one-line preview that expands on click.

## User Impact

Each suggestion row now starts with its author's avatar, followed by the name and a one-line preview, the same way queued messages show their sender. The tray uses the queue's border, corner, surface and light-theme outline, so the two trays look like one design. There is no queue icon on the left, because a suggestion is waiting for the owner's decision, not queued to send. Expanding a row, the three-row cap with "+N more", the close button for dismissed suggestions and the actions that appear on hover all work as before. Nothing needs migrating or configuring.

## Why This Change Was Made

The request was a preview of at most two lines plus the queue's avatar. #204920 had already made the collapsed row one line that opens to the full text, with a browser test that keeps the row compact. One line meets "no more than two lines", so this change keeps it and adds only what was still missing. The tray reuses the queue's own `.chat-queue` class, and each row uses the `ChatAuthorAvatar` component that queued messages use. Nothing is copied from the queue's styles, so the change removes more CSS than it adds. The avatar replaces the name chip that was shown only to guests, so every viewer sees the same row.

## Screenshots

Guest view (1180px) from `session-suggestions.e2e.test.ts` with `OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1`, and the owner tray (900px) from `chat-session-suggestions.browser.test.tsx`. Both use the tests' mocked Gateway fixtures. Before is `main` at `d8fc8b7`; after is this change at `a8cf50b`, whose diff is identical to the current rebased head `58fc28e`.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: guest suggestion row with a red name chip and no avatar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a13ba60-6645-494a-bb25-27eac0e3c840) | ![After: guest suggestion row with Alice's avatar and bold name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d008c5a6-a4a0-40b6-bf9a-ecc3dfb2ae8d) |
| ![Before: owner tray rows show only small author names](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09fab788-73fb-4d91-b170-849f7092857a) | ![After: owner tray rows start with author avatars, preview still one line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13bfdd9d-b506-4d4b-b611-e4d810885cdb) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Name chip without avatar highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb6db5cf-6c12-40b1-8774-3f657dc8b4eb) | ![Avatar and name highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89320828-45c4-4966-86f2-5b2ed59ace5d) |
| ![Name-only column highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28671b69-7845-491a-85de-a1a1360f33b4) | ![Avatar column highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e92f5f8a-bdaf-41dd-89e3-be4406654bd1) |

## Evidence

- Resolved the merge with #204920 by keeping its structure (expandable rows, three-row cap, close action) and adding the avatar and preview span on top.
- Rebased onto `main` as `58fc28e` to resolve a conflict with the new accepted-suggestion e2e test; both tests are kept and the PR's diff is otherwise unchanged.
- On `58fc28e`, all CI passes: lint, types, `checks-ui`, `control-ui-performance` and all 10 e2e shards, with `openclaw/ci-gate` green.
- An earlier head copied the queue's tray styles into `.session-suggestions`. `control-ui-performance` flagged that as a new failure, because the CSS budgets have no headroom. Reusing `.chat-queue` fixed it.
- Shard 6/10 timed out once on `a8cf50b` in `agent-identity-reconnect.e2e.test.ts`, a flow this PR doesn't touch; it passes on `58fc28e`.
- Removed an earlier unit test that pinned class names and child order (flagged by ClawSweeper). The two-line owner case was also removed, because #204920's browser test (`chat-session-suggestions.browser.test.tsx`, 390px and 900px) covers compact owner rows.
- Locally on `58fc28e`: `session-suggestions.e2e.test.ts` (11/11), `chat-session-suggestions.browser.test.tsx` (2/2) and `chat-session-suggestions.test.tsx` (5/5) pass.

Sending a WhatsApp group message with a member’s phone number mentioned in italics displayed the number but dropped the recipient metadata. The member could miss the mention.

Italic mentions now address the same group members as plain, bold and strikethrough mentions. Literal underscores inside words stay literal, including in non-Latin text.

prs.title: fix(agents): merge requester connect tools into a cached MCP catalog
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #158710.

In the Codex harness, when one requester-scoped per-requester OAuth MCP
server is already authenticated and contributes tools, the OAuth
`connect` tool for a second, unauthenticated MCP server is omitted from
the advertised catalog for that turn — so the agent can never start the
second server's sign-in flow while the first server's tools are live.

Root cause, in `materializeRequesterScopedMcpToolsForHarnessRunCore`
(`src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-harness.ts`):

```ts
if (liveCatalog.tools.length > 0 && scopedRuntimeHandle) {
  rememberAdvertisedScopedMcpCatalog(scopedRuntimeHandle, liveCatalog);
}

const advertisedCatalog =
  getAdvertisedScopedMcpCatalog(params.sessionId) ??
  (liveCatalog
    ? mergeMcpConnectCatalog(liveCatalog, scopedRuntime?.requesterConnect)
    : undefined);
```

The nonempty `liveCatalog` is remembered in the session cache *before*
`advertisedCatalog` is selected. Because `getAdvertisedScopedMcpCatalog`
now returns that just-remembered value, the `??` short-circuits and the
`mergeMcpConnectCatalog(...)` branch — the only place that adds the
second server's `connect` tool — never runs, even on the very first
call for that session.

## Fix

Select the base catalog (cached-or-live) first, then always merge the
requester's connect entries into it:

```ts
const baseAdvertisedCatalog = getAdvertisedScopedMcpCatalog(params.sessionId) ?? liveCatalog;
const advertisedCatalog = baseAdvertisedCatalog
  ? mergeMcpConnectCatalog(baseAdvertisedCatalog, scopedRuntime?.requesterConnect)
  : undefined;
```

`mergeMcpConnectCatalog` (`src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-requester-connect.ts`)
already only adds connect entries for servers *absent* from the base
catalog and returns the base catalog unchanged when none are missing,
so this is safe for every prior case (no requester-connect surface,
both servers authenticated, cache already merged, etc.) and only
changes the previously-broken mixed-authentication case.

## Evidence

Added a regression test,
`materializeRequesterScopedMcpToolsForHarnessRunCore > advertises an
unauthenticated server's connect tool alongside an already-authenticated
server's tools`, which configures a live catalog with an authenticated
`user-mail` server plus a `requesterConnect` surface covering both
`user-mail` and an unauthenticated `calendar` server, and asserts the
returned tool list contains both `calendar__connect` and
`user-mail__inbox`.

Confirmed the test fails on the pre-fix code and passes after the fix
by toggling only the source file:

```
$ git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-harness.ts   # pre-fix
$ pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-harness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 × materializeRequesterScopedMcpToolsForHarnessRunCore > advertises an unauthenticated server's
   connect tool alongside an already-authenticated server's tools 8ms
   AssertionError: expected [ 'user-mail__inbox' ] to deeply equal [ 'calendar__connect', 'user-mail__inbox' ]
 Tests  1 failed | 33 passed (34)

$ git checkout HEAD -- src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-harness.ts   # fix restored
$ pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-harness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
```

Also ran the sibling Codex consumer suite (unchanged, confirms no
regression in the harness's caller):

```
$ pnpm test extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  186 passed (186)
```

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` was also run; its only failing check
(`assertion SAFETY comment ratchet`, on `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`,
a file untouched by this PR) reproduces identically on unmodified
`upstream/main`, confirming it's pre-existing and unrelated to this change.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was prepared by an autonomous Claude Code agent, including root
cause analysis, the fix, the regression test, and this description.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## November 18 update

Updated the catalog merge against current main while preserving senderless sign-in behavior and requester boundaries. The regression covers one authenticated server plus a second server requiring sign-in. A real mixed-auth Codex/OAuth setup is still needed for live proof.

Earlier measurements above retain their original head and environment; the following link records validation of this updated head.

The November 18 refresh used Codex assistance and independent source review.

Validated revision: `ff18cbba678d78fee3d98c809a26f11ea0b796e8`.
Final changed-file compiler, lint and format checks: https://github.com/chelsealong/oss-pipeline/actions/runs/44301565948
Runtime validation: https://github.com/chelsealong/oss-pipeline/actions/runs/44300700034 (Foundry runtime suites also recorded in run 44299410378).

prs.title: fix(gateway): personal MCP access fails for authenticated HTTP callers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Personal MCP connections configured for per-requester authorization are unavailable when a verified person calls the Chat Completions or Responses HTTP APIs.

## User Impact

Authenticated callers can reach their own connection and consent flow. A shared token or password does not select a person's MCP identity, and requests without verified identity get no personal requester. Users still authorize their own connections; credentials are not copied or migrated.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared HTTP runner now carries the existing server-verified canonical profile ID into the agent run. A shared gateway credential identifies its holder, not a person, so token/password methods are explicitly excluded even if owner attribution contains a profile. There is no fallback to an owner, previous caller, email string, session identifier, or prompt content.

Existing channel/account context, admission, revocation, and cancellation checks remain intact. This uses the existing identity and authentication-method helpers, with no deployment-specific configuration or agent-layout assumption.

## Evidence

- The same missing sender is reproduced on **v2026.9.8** (`fc23bc864`), **v2026.10.9** (`8b18b5578`), and current **main** (`dbba4b262`). The PR targets main and uses its existing `gatewayProfile` fixture.
- Before the fix on this main base: **2 failed / 28 passed**, with failures at the missing canonical sender and A-to-B-to-A caller transition. These are product assertions, not setup failures.
- After the fix: **279 tests passed across 7 files**, covering the shared runner, both HTTP APIs, MCP requester/cache/connect contracts, and prompt-prefix stability.
- Core and owned-test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, line-cap/max-lines ratchets, and the staged test-line budget check passed.
- Local AutoReview covered the complete three-file candidate now committed as `ce8caa5c0` against `dbba4b262` through **P2**, with no actionable findings. Both authentication owners were supplied as context; the reviewer did not independently inspect HTTP/MCP consumers or rerun the tests.
- Production growth is **9 lines**. The **71 new regression lines** cover canonical identity, caller isolation, and missing/shared-secret identity using existing fixtures. A separate exact 71-line allocation records that growth; the shared budget scalar is unchanged.
- Timing: the standalone baseline regression took **75.83 s** including cold compilation. The patched runner's 30 cases total **2.382 s** in reported case durations; the final seven-file command took **288.54 s**. CI time is pending.

The MCP tests use local synthetic fixtures. Live user consent, protected third-party reads, and deployment acceptance are not claimed. Broader CI remains pending.

prs.title: fix(mcp): per-requester MCP ignores the signed-in Gateway profile in chat
prs.body:
Related: #138113

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: people who chat with an agent through the Gateway share one per-requester MCP sign-in when they come in through the same backend client, and signed-in Control UI users get no sign-in at all, even though the Gateway has verified who each person is.

## User Impact

User impact: each person with a verified Gateway profile (a signed-in Control UI user, or a person a backend client brings in through trusted-proxy auth) connects and uses their own account on an `oauth.identity: "per-requester"` MCP server from chat. It is the same account their MCP Apps already use. One person's sign-in no longer serves everyone behind a backend client, and their pending sign-ins no longer replace each other.

Unchanged: channel senders, shared token or password logins, system and internal turns, cron, subagents and heartbeats.

After updating, people who used a per-requester server through a backend client sign in once more. The row their client's shared identity already holds is kept and still serves connections without a verified profile; verified people neither use nor replace it.

## Why This Change Was Made

A Gateway chat turn's sender is the connection's client id (`gateway-client`, for example), or nothing for operator UI clients, and requester-scoped MCP keys sign-ins on that sender. The verified profile is already known at `chat.send` ingress, and MCP Apps already key a profile's sign-ins by it.

- `chat.send` ingress records the caller's verified profile on the run. It comes from the existing caller-identity authority, which is set only for a verified identity and never for the shared owner, and only the person's own input carries it, not system or internal turns.
- When an attempt is built, the profile is bound to the run's admitted operator authority, and that binding is checked right before every credential effect: in the session MCP manager before it selects requester credentials, and in every executor the materializer returns for a requester-scoped server (tool calls, sign-ins, resource and prompt listings and reads, and the app view read after a call). A sign-in such an executor starts also hands the authority and the call's abort signal to the OAuth owner as its login lifecycle, so the owner rechecks them before each discovery, registration and store write; that holds for a Codex harness tool remembered from another requester too, which starts this requester's sign-in when it has no live counterpart. A revoked, closed or reassigned authority throws there, before any request leaves, and never falls back to the shared transport sender. This sits under the existing cancellation a role change already triggers, so an executor the turn still holds cannot send a request once its authority ends.
- The manager keys the profile as MCP Apps do (internal channel, no account). Plugin connection resolvers therefore receive the person's profile for these turns, as they already do for MCP Apps, instead of the client id. The embedded runner and the Codex harness pass the binding through.
- Queued runs from different profiles never collect into one run.
- No schema, store format or key grammar changes (`mcp-oauth-identity.ts` is untouched). Rows a 2026.10.5 Gateway wrote load and work as before for the principals that own them (shown below with the published release).

This follows the precedence proposed in #138113 (verified Gateway profile, else channel sender, else fail closed), as its own run fact rather than a change to `SenderId`. The `agent` method and the OpenAI-compatible HTTP surface mentioned there are not covered and keep today's behavior.

Needs your decision on that identity contract: profile-first for direct Gateway chat turns, the profile tuple for resolver plugins, and the one-time sign-in for verified backend users.

## Evidence

### Through the CLI, upgrading from the latest stable release

A local harness (not part of this PR) runs `openclaw gateway run` from the published `openclaw@2026.10.5` (npm `latest`), then from this branch's build at `9c32a097d9`, on one state directory. Every change goes through the CLI: `doctor --fix`, `config patch`, `devices list` / `devices approve`, `users list`, and `gateway call users.setRole` / `agent.wait` as the local shared owner. The other pieces are a local standard MCP OAuth server whose one tool names the account behind the bearer token, and a scripted model. Alice and Bob connect through one backend device as `gateway-client`, named by a trusted-proxy header over TLS.

1. **Upgrade with existing credentials:** 2026.10.5 signs the shared-token backend client in through its real OAuth flow and writes the row. After `doctor --fix` migrates the state, this branch serves that client from the same row with no new sign-in.
2. **Two people, one backend client:** after the device is approved, Alice and Bob each get their own link. Alice finishes her sign-in after Bob started his (the step the e2e below fails on `main`), and each call reaches the server as that person's account.
3. **Revocation mid-turn:** Alice's turn is held after her tools and credentials are prepared, and the owner sets her role to one without scopes. The Gateway disconnects her and aborts the turn, and the account server records no further call.
4. **Unverified clients:** back on shared-token auth, the backend client, which has no verified identity, still uses the 2026.10.5 row.

```text
[01] openclaw 2026.10.5 (npm): openclaw gateway run, shared-token auth
     PASS backend client (gateway-client) is asked to connect: sign-in link returned
     PASS consent returns through http://127.0.0.1:<port>/oauth/mcp/callback: HTTP 200
     PASS released Gateway: "tool said: signed in as shared-account"
[02] stop 2026.10.5: exit 0
[03] this branch (9c32a097d9): openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive: exit 0
[04] this branch: openclaw gateway run, same state directory and config
     PASS upgraded Gateway, no new sign-in: "tool said: signed in as shared-account"
[05] stop: exit 0
[06] openclaw config patch (proxy): exit 0
[07] this branch: openclaw gateway run, trusted-proxy auth over TLS, roles (default member)
     PASS new backend device is held for pairing: "device pairing required (requestId: <id>)"
     PASS openclaw devices list --json: the backend device's request is pending
[08] openclaw devices approve <request>: one backend device for everyone behind the proxy
     PASS Alice and Bob (same device, client id gateway-client) each get their own sign-in link; the backend's row is not used
     PASS Alice consents after Bob's sign-in started; callback HTTP 200
     PASS Alice: "tool said: signed in as alice-account"
     PASS Bob is still asked to connect his own account
     PASS Bob: "tool said: signed in as bob-account"
     PASS openclaw users list --json: Alice's verified profile exists
[09] Alice's next turn is held after her tools are prepared
[10] openclaw gateway call users.setRole {role: "denied"}: role now "denied"
     PASS held turn ends "error" (aborted); account server calls stay 4
[11] stop: exit 0
[12] openclaw config patch (token): exit 0
[13] this branch: shared-token auth again
     PASS shared-token backend client keeps the 2026.10.5 sign-in: "tool said: signed in as shared-account"
[14] stop: exit 0
account server calls, in order: shared-account, shared-account, alice-account, bob-account, shared-account
```

<details>
<summary>Matching Doctor and Gateway log lines (redacted)</summary>

```text
- Upgraded agent database schema in <state>/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v25 -> v31.
[ws] closed before connect conn=<id> fwd=203.0.113.10 code=1005 reason=n/a phase=auth_validated cause=pairing-required handshake=failed
[gateway] device pairing approved device=<device> role=operator
[ws] authenticated user disconnected code=4001 reason=operator role changed conn=<id> user=alice@example.test
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="Your operator role changed; reconnect before continuing." errorName=Error taskKind=turn sessionKey=<session> runId=<id>
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback chain stopped: reason=caller_signal_aborted candidate=requester-proof/model errorName=Error
```

</details>

### In the repository

`src/gateway/chat-send-requester-mcp-oauth.e2e.test.ts` runs the same scenario in process against `startGatewayServer`, the server `gateway run` starts, with real WebSocket connect and device pairing, `chat.send`, OAuth discovery and PKCE, the Gateway's `/oauth/mcp/callback`, and the HTTP MCP transport. Its last step revokes a third person while their sign-in waits on the provider's authorization server discovery: once discovery answers, no client is registered and no pending sign-in is saved. A second case keeps a shared-token backend client on a row in the format 2026.10.5 writes.

```text

 ✓ src/gateway/chat-send-requester-mcp-oauth.e2e.test.ts > keeps a shared-token backend client on the sign-in its own identity holds 3990ms
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The same file on `main` fails while signing Alice in, because Bob's later sign-in start replaced the pending sign-in the two of them share:

```text
requester MCP proof failed while signing Alice in
 × src/gateway/chat-send-requester-mcp-oauth.e2e.test.ts > signs each verified person in separately through one backend client 17092ms
   → expected 404 to be 200 // Object.is equality
```

Unit tests:

- `agent-bundle-mcp-requester-profile.test.ts`: the bound profile passes while it is the run's live operator authority; another profile, a revoked source (which stays retired) and a closed admission throw.
- `agent-bundle-mcp-manager.requester-connect.test.ts`: two profiles on one backend sender get separate links and store keys, and an authorized profile gets the real tools while the other still gets `connect`. Once a profile loses its authority, acquisition throws without reading OAuth state. Executors the turn already holds then refuse before the runtime is reached, with no cancellation involved: the tool call, a new sign-in, and the resource and prompt listings and reads. A sign-in it starts hands the OAuth owner a login lifecycle with the call's abort signal, and a revocation mid-sign-in throws through it.
- `agent-bundle-mcp-harness.test.ts`: a session advertises `calendar__events` from a requester who connected, and an unconnected profile's turn holds that tool as its sign-in. Once the profile loses its authority, the tool refuses before OAuth starts; while the profile is current, it starts sign-in, and a revocation during that sign-in stops it.
- `agent-bundle-mcp-requester-connect.authority.test.ts`: a real sign-in, through the real OAuth owner and an isolated state database, against a local OAuth provider. A requester who keeps access registers a client and gets a link. - `get-reply-run.requester-authority.test-support.ts` (run by `get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts`): a verified caller's profile reaches the run; an unverified caller and a system turn get none. prs.title: fix: enable personal MCP sign-in from browser chat
prs.body:
Related: #138113

## What Problem This Solves

A user can sign in to Control UI but still be unable to connect a personal MCP account from chat. Browser turns have a verified Gateway profile, while personal MCP discovery expects a channel sender ID and therefore omits the connect tool.

## User Impact

User impact: authenticated browser chat can offer personal MCP sign-in, with credentials kept separate for each profile even when profiles share a chat session. Shared MCP tools retain their existing behavior. Background work and subagents do not inherit browser credentials, and a turn with ambiguous personal participants cannot start a personal tool call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The admitted human-turn owner supplies a private, session-bound browser identity to the native and harness MCP consumers. This preserves the meaning of `SenderId` for channel authorization and metadata. Personal tools check the admitted participant when execution starts and reject retained calls after disposal. Work already in flight follows the existing runtime contract.

This is an independently maintained, narrower alternative to #188164 by @apps3000 and #177356 by @Canvinus. Their work informed the separation of browser profiles from transport sender IDs and the authority/lifecycle cases to check. This branch does not depend on either PR or copy their commits. It reuses the existing personal-participant resolver and credential partitioning; it does not add a profile-first identity policy for other channels or repeated checks after every await.

Maintainer decision requested: should direct and visible Control UI turns use this private profile-to-MCP handoff while channel sender semantics remain unchanged?

## Evidence

Publication update (20 November): merged upstream `c72c65a94` in `a18e81e87`. The only conflict was between adjacent imports in `attempt-bundle-tools.ts`; both imports are retained. All contribution additions and deletions match the tested commit below, and the diff against the new base passes `git diff --check`. The 53 tests, type/lint checks, and runtime build below apply to `c50283d04`; they have not been rerun on the merged head. This remains a draft pending merged-head validation and live OAuth replay.

On the base revision, the direct and visible browser regressions fail because personal MCP preflight returns `false`; the five exclusion cases pass. With this patch, all 53 focused tests across five files pass, including separate sign-in identities for two profiles in one session, retained-call rejection, and shared-tool independence. Both targeted type graphs, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

The `qaRuntime` build passed, including runtime post-build checks (350 seconds). This draft requests review of the identity policy; the live OAuth replay below remains unfinished.

Live candidate limitation: this exact upstream implementation has not completed browser-to-provider OAuth consent or an authenticated MCP request. Our deployed workaround did complete real browser sign-in, but it populated `SenderId`; that observation is supporting defect evidence, not a live test of this implementation. See the [sanitized Pilot evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188164#issuecomment-6977193737).

Local autoreview checked the complete source change against the base at P0–P2 priority. Its final result had no actionable findings. The earlier shared-tool restriction was corrected, and the final review also covered connect-only servers. The reviewer inspected source; it did not run tests or a browser.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and check details</summary>

Base: `9903773c4da39eddddf8bc40ff954fad311e1feb`. Candidate: `c50283d04` (the tested file hashes match the committed source).

The final focused test command took 253 seconds including worker compilation. The baseline replay took 218 seconds and produced the two expected failures. The two type graphs took 99 seconds; lint plus SDK declaration preparation took 296 seconds.

Environment: isolated, secretless Linux x64 container with Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, frozen dependencies, repository-pinned Bun, one test worker, and a 2 CPU / 5 GiB test limit. The runtime build used 6 GiB after the normal capacity check refused 5 GiB; no memory-check override was used. No live Gateway state or personal credential stores were mounted.

The regression uses the actual admitted-turn, participant, MCP manager, and harness materialization paths. It replaces OAuth credential status and provider authorization at the external boundary. It tests profile separation, shared-only acquisition, direct/visible turns, retained tools, anonymous/mismatched profiles, other sessions, memory work, and subagents. A materialization regression checks that ambiguous personal authority blocks personal tools while shared tools remain callable.

```sh
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-webchat.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime-shared.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-harness.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-materialize.lifecycle.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-bundle-tools.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-agents-root","core-test-agents-other"]' --concurrency 1
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
```

The repository lint wrapper checked all seven changed TypeScript files. The formatter processed all eight changed files; `git diff --check` passed.

</details>

prs.title: fix: personal MCP sign-in fails in authenticated Webchat
prs.body:
## Summary

Authenticated Webchat has a verified profile but no transport `SenderId`. With a personal (`oauth.identity: "per-requester"`) MCP server, asking to connect an account therefore exposes no personal sign-in tool.

Capture the exact live single-participant Webchat authority at the admitted human-turn owner, before private admission state is projected away. Both native execution and the public harness bridge consume that host capture. The transport sender, existing requester credential tuple and OAuth callback owner are unchanged.

## Scope and authority

- Direct and admitted visible human Webchat turns only. The profile, connection, session, run, tool fingerprint and live participant must agree.
- Recheck authority after awaited preparation and at HTTP/OAuth effects. Releasing a view closes its executors without attaching a turn guard to a reusable cached runtime.
- Preserve verified transport senders. Do not infer personal access for queued follow-ups, ambiguous multi-person steers, scheduled/spawned work, memory flushes or control operations.
- No new config, storage schema, public SDK export or provider-specific integration. The JSON result projection is an unchanged move to its existing content owner to respect file size.

**Maintainer scope decision remains open:** this is the narrow direct-Webchat capability from #138113. #177356 covers broader authenticated ingress; its separate proof does not validate this patch. #187952 concerns memory attribution rather than MCP credential authority.

## Inspectable behavior proof

[Reproduction script, instructions and redacted observed results](https://gist.github.com/apps3000/b0405ddf7299f71b763256d2dddf3134).

The same standalone script was run against two independently built checkouts, with only synthetic accounts, local HTTP servers and a deterministic local model fixture:

| Source | Observed outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Original merge base `315380c4789590e3aff9be3cfc6fcfcb9e1f6eee` | Gateway and authenticated chat run; `personal_cloud__connect` is missing, dispatch reports unknown tool ID, no OAuth HTTP request occurs. |
| Current head `6e19a6441567c8bcc1a695a91b26aa5876c6344a` | Two verified profiles in one shared session obtain distinct personal links. Each native OAuth callback completes **after its chat reply**. Subsequent real MCP identity reads return Ada, Grace, Ada. |

The fixed runtime was rebuilt from this exact head (`build-info.json.commit` matches), then the proof was rerun: **5 chat.send turns, 15 model-fixture requests, 2 token exchanges**. This reaches the actual Gateway, native agent, MCP discovery/connect, HTTP transport, OAuth callback and SQLite credential owners. The script checks PKCE and rejects a reply containing the other account's identity.

This is protocol/frontdoor proof, not a browser-rendering test or a claim about a real Google/Composio provider.

## Review feedback addressed

- The OAuth mock export finding was already fixed in `63d0af3` by preserving real exports; the current mock-export ratchet passes without baseline changes.
- Removed the low-value native acquisition-argument echo test.
- Replaced the synthetic awaited-effect test with **four real OAuth-boundary cases**: native/harness × revoked/second-person-steered during the first discovery response. Authorization delegates to the real first-party implementation, MCP SDK, guarded HTTP and SQLite store. Each case checks the intended authority error, **exactly one HTTP request**, and **no stored token, verifier or authorization URL**.
- Routed that suite to the existing host-owned SQLite broker/fork lane because these cases now use actual persistent state.
- Kept the narrower identity and released-view tests. The change-local regression allocation is exactly **461 lines**, with no shared budget or mock baseline relaxation.

The negative cases deny subsequent network/persistence after authority changes during preparation. They do not claim coverage of revocation during an already-published post-reply callback; that existing callback lifecycle is unchanged.

## Validation

At current head:

- Focused native wrapper: **24 tests / 2 files pass**, **15.06 s** wall time; Vitest **8.76 s** (includes the four HTTP/SQLite cases and the affected native owner suite).
- Targeted test types (`agents-root`, `agents-other`), type-aware lint, format, test-line and mock-export ratchets, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Runtime build `qaRuntime` passes (**70 s**), followed by the exact-built-head Gateway proof above.
- Shared **autoreview**, Codex GPT-6.1 Sol / medium, reviewed the review-feedback delta and supplied unchanged authority/OAuth owners through **P0–P2**: `scoped-clean`, no actionable findings. It is source review, not maintainer approval; the reviewer did not execute tests. The only later source edit added lint-required braces without changing behavior.

Earlier broader evidence remains revision-specific: 93 focused tests and full build with 161 SDK subpaths at `b9c8ce0f`; [upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41024843137) passed at `63d0af3`. The new head changes tests/routing/allocation only. Those earlier CI results are not presented as new-head CI.

## Remaining gates and limits

- This external contribution still requires the upstream maintainer's security-sensitive-path approval and the scope decision above.
- New-head [CI 41107237106](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41107237106) completed with failures. The failure attribution and unchanged-main controls are documented below; no failed check is represented as passing.
- A full Codex app-server process, real Composio/Google sign-in and production rollout were not exercised. Harness coverage here reaches the public requester materialization boundary.
- Production remains on the official release; no candidate patch was deployed.


## New-head CI failure attribution

CI executed GitHub merge `da94d17e26fa60d6ccd192b51296c68c96de8f1f` against main `9e8a058de8afcdaf03f5774979e7d2e494b80a1c`, rather than the old source base used for the original reproduction. A separate unchanged-main checkout with fresh frozen dependencies reproduces the same failures. [Commands, exact scope and observed results](https://gist.github.com/apps3000/b0405ddf7299f71b763256d2dddf3134#file-ci-baseline-md).

| Failed CI owner | Unchanged-main evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Cron admission, large-18 | Native abort/owner-abort/permission/revocation cases and Gateway mutation revoke/abort expect `skipped`, receive `ok`. |
| Cron isolated fallback, large-22 | Explicit and stored fallback ladders are not reached. Both matching cases reproduced without this PR. |
| Gateway spawn fallback, small-11 | `configured agent ladder` returns `error` instead of `ok`; `hidden child control` omits the expected backup. Both reproduced without this PR. |
| Reply/session fallbacks, small-9 | Matching streaming-recovery and fallback-transcript failures reproduced on unchanged main. The scheduled-session variant is covered by the separate control in the linked evidence. |
| Test-line ratchet | Main itself has 6,307,252 lines against a 6,304,616 ceiling: **2,636 inherited excess lines**. The merge adds exactly our 461-line allocation to both values and retains the same excess. The guard accepts zero-delta debt but rejects a positive-delta tree still above its ceiling. |

All seven failed test files are byte-identical in main and the CI merge. No unrelated runtime repair, baseline raise, additional inherited-debt allocation, expected-failure marker or guard change was added to make these checks green. Maintainer resolution of the existing failures/debt and security/scope approval remain pending.

prs.body:
Closes #138113

Closes #188164 — supersedes the authenticated Webchat requester and OAuth lifecycle fix.

Closes #202434 — supersedes the alternative browser fix, including shared-tool independence when personal authority is denied.

Closes #177356 — supersedes the verified-profile fix for users behind the same Gateway backend and reuses their MCP Apps sign-in.

Closes #189257 — supersedes the verified requester fix for Chat Completions and Responses HTTP callers.

Closes #158852 — supersedes the cached-catalog fix for a missing connect tool when another personal server is already connected.

Contributor credit: @apps3000, @SeveHo, @Canvinus, @tguggenberger-lab, and @chelsealong for the authored commits and proof carried forward; @jacobtomlinson for reporting the HackMD reproduction and directing the combined repair. The original commit authors are preserved; integration is a separate commit.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b88083e9-c798-484b-8632-377bbc5d25b7)

## What Problem This Solves

People signed in to the Control UI can be unable to connect a personal MCP account. Gateway clients behind the same trusted proxy can share a sign-in, and verified OpenAI-compatible HTTP callers can lack a personal requester altogether. A separate catalog bug hides a second server's sign-in tool once another server is connected.

## User Impact

Verified users can use their own OAuth account from browser chat, trusted-proxy Gateway chat, and the Chat Completions and Responses HTTP routes. Their profile uses the same credential namespace as MCP Apps. People previously using a backend's shared requester identity will sign in once as themselves; the legacy credential is not deleted or copied. Shared MCP servers and channel sender attribution are unchanged. Scheduled and spawned work does not inherit a personal account. If another participant steers a turn while a personal MCP write is in flight, the write that already started still returns its result; later personal calls in that turn are refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Gateway-verified identity and admitted turn authority rather than rewriting transport sender IDs. A browser request must match the live participant; personal MCP calls reuse the attempt's Stop and ownership checks. HTTP owner status remains a decision of the admitted grant, separate from verified personal MCP identity. Select the cached/live catalog first, then add absent servers' connect entries. The single-use sign-in-link trust model is unchanged; use a private session or a mutually trusted audience. This does not add personal sign-in to Settings or `openclaw mcp login`, nor change standalone Claude Code or OpenClaw's separate `claude-cli` runner.

## Evidence

### Current head `3cdf776d`

[Isolated continuation verification](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_994d0e30d984b20fce5f395c8c92464c) passed formatting, lint, and the full Gateway in-process continuation test file on tree `ba383c1c19f67e55909a49642710ec594b65924c`. The only change from `a1dd2bd4` is the continuation assertion from @vincentkoc's #205526 (`3f45122816fd9`). It matches the current role denial and still asserts that no turn starts. No product code changed; hosted checks on this head are separate.

### Prior head `a1dd2bd4`

[Isolated fixture verification](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f8a81a0d7fc5ed97c50ce8be064d4fdb) matched published tree `e1eeff3f8d34b073e8882a0ce6ebe240a7276661`. Only the Webchat requester test changed since `bfa76bc1`: it now uses the existing admitted-operator grant fixture. The exact failing test-typecheck shard and the requester test file both passed. The same run reproduced the separate in-process continuation test's denial-message assertion on the previous head and its exact `main` base `ed458390`; the request was denied in both cases.

### Unchanged product tree from `bfa76bc1`

[Passing isolated AWS run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_546aabb911a32670082617058caed8e8) verified predecessor tree `f7402fd2a166670bd01b29fe8852bb6fcb22c80a`. The branch incorporates `main` at `ed458390`, including #204928 and #204894. The [previous head/base comparison](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5cbca5e42574e91740d067edd8781e31) reproduced both original assertions on `9516aecb` and its CI base `269f88452`. Both test files passed on the updated tree, along with core typecheck, lint, formatting, the targeted requester/harness/HTTP tests, and the Gateway OAuth suite. The HTTP conflict resolution retains both the upstream owner grant and the separate verified MCP requester.

### HTTP and cached-catalog proof requested in review

The [prior passing run on `9c19fcee`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_406d719d2579b9b85ef0c80cca2f07ab) and the integrated product run exercised the real Gateway HTTP handlers and production requester-scoped harness SDK:

- **`POST /v1/chat/completions`:** HTTP 200. Gateway-verified Alice got a sign-in link, completed consent and the real Gateway callback, then called the MCP account tool and got `alice-http`.
- **`POST /v1/responses`:** HTTP 200. Gateway-verified Bob independently completed the same flow and got `bob-http`. Both sign-in links were issued before either user completed consent.
- **Warm harness catalog:** the production `materializeRequesterScopedMcpToolsForHarnessRun` cached `accounts/whoami` for Alice's session with no `notes` tools or client registration. The next preparation advertised `notes__connect` alongside `accounts__whoami`. Executing that real connect tool and completing its Gateway callback made `notes__whoami` return `alice-notes`; `accounts__whoami` still returned `alice-http`. This verifies the harness SDK boundary, not a live Codex backend.

### Earlier verification

- [Integrated verification at `9516aecb`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a6b39c99c93191c41963554f30b9a68e): core typecheck, formatting, lint, eight targeted files, and four Gateway OAuth cases passed on the exact predecessor tree. The integration removed the obsolete operator lifetime recheck and tests Stop through the actual attempt signal.
- [Review-fix proof at `573fff87`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_501f15b164fb03e7ee27645043b8c312): the settlement regression fails against the prior settlement code (`21afee89`) and passes with the fix. An already admitted write returns its result after a steer; a later personal call is still refused. All 78 focused tests and three Gateway OAuth tests passed.
- [Changed test file at `9c19fcee`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_20164beccba6ce4c6df501b6a785a4bd): the changed requester test file passed after deduplicating test setup.
- [Shipped-CLI in-place upgrade at `9c19fcee`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_66d59b9207e89fa35181d9557755587b): a foreground `openclaw@2026.11.7` Gateway used a synthetic OAuth account, then the candidate's `doctor --fix --non-interactive` migrated the agent database v38 → v43. A fresh candidate Gateway reused the same shared-token backend account without another sign-in and with exactly one client registration. Per-profile sign-in is new; verified users sign in once as themselves after upgrade.
- [First baseline comparison](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_364986b683ffeb057cf7bd494b222f90) and [second baseline comparison](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_8300859ffaad1ede7d684539f00b0104): matching assertions from `9c19fcee` reproduced at its original base `36bc0460`, including prompt cache, scheduled compaction, UI command, pending-input maintenance, and Codex continuation. Those five targeted files later passed on `9516aecb`.

The isolated runs used synthetic OAuth/MCP servers and a scripted model. They do not test live HackMD, browser rendering, or a live Claude or Codex backend. The source PRs remain open while this replacement is reviewed.

prs.title: fix: explain how to correct a one-time automation schedule
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you save a one-time automation with a date that has passed or is more than 10 years away, OpenClaw reports the internal field name instead of telling you how to fix it. The future-date error can even say “10 years ahead” and “Maximum allowed: 10 years” in the same message.

## User Impact

The message now tells you to choose a later or earlier time. Rejected edits can still be corrected in the open form. Scheduling limits, error codes, and save behavior are unchanged.

| Surface / trigger | Exact before | Exact after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Automations → Once → Save changes, or the automation tool/API. The selected time is outside the past grace period. Example: Feb 23 at 11:00 UTC, with the Gateway clock at noon. | `schedule.at is in the past: 2026-02-23T11:00:00.000Z (60 minutes ago). Current time: 2026-02-23T12:00:00.000Z` | `That time is in the past (2026-02-23T11:00:00.000Z). Choose a time after 2026-02-23T12:00:00.000Z.` |
| Same surfaces, with the selected time beyond the 10-year limit. Example: Jan 1, 2037 against the same Gateway clock. | `schedule.at is too far in the future: 2037-01-01T00:00:00.000Z (10 years ahead). Maximum allowed: 10 years` | `The scheduled time (2037-01-01T00:00:00.000Z) is more than 10 years away. Choose an earlier date and time.` |

## Why This Change Was Made

Both requests use the same Gateway validator, so the wording changes there without adding UI-specific formatting or another recovery path. The exact timestamps remain available; only the redundant rounded offsets were removed.

**Skill in practice:** The writing guide pointed toward one correction the reader can make in the form rather than a retry or a settings link. Tracing the validator exposed something the guide alone couldn’t: flooring the year count could make a rejected date appear to meet the limit.

## Evidence

- Reproduced both old messages through isolated Gateway `cron.add` and `cron.update` RPCs. On the final patch, six focused tests passed across timestamp validation and automation-tool correction and retry. Targeted type diagnostics, lint, formatting, copy lint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- After-fix WebSocket proof on `ff52526249d8`: an isolated Gateway returned `INVALID_REQUEST` for both inputs through both `cron.add` and `cron.update` (four cases), with the following messages. The stored jobs list was identical before and after the four rejected requests.

  ```text
  cron.add     That time is in the past (2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z). Choose a time after 2026-11-25T22:08:40.585Z.
  cron.update  That time is in the past (2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z). Choose a time after 2026-11-25T22:08:40.591Z.
  cron.add     The scheduled time (2100-01-01T00:00:00.000Z) is more than 10 years away. Choose an earlier date and time.
  cron.update  The scheduled time (2100-01-01T00:00:00.000Z) is more than 10 years away. Choose an earlier date and time.
  ```

- Two focused Chromium cases passed in the actual Automations editor. Both errors rendered verbatim, the date remained editable, and **Save changes** was available. The browser received fixture replies with the observed baseline text and final validator output. The isolated Gateway RPC proof was separate; this was not a browser-to-Gateway run. Broad CI was not run locally.
- Local autoreview could not start because its isolation requires a temporary directory outside the repository. No independent autoreview verdict was produced.

### More than 10 years away

Actual Control UI at 1280 × 980 in UTC, with a synthetic automation. Before shows the message from `3ee8fc53769c`; after shows the message from `fff00ed3a203c`. The editor code is unchanged.

#### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: the rounded future date looks like it meets the limit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/610c8f2c-8ec6-4f09-8d2a-cd6d00392616)

**After**

![After: the future-date error gives the actual limit and next step](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dce74988-087d-439d-88d4-440db9283e99)

#### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Annotated before: rounded time looks allowed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b0dfbd1-25e7-4071-b450-2ed0ca7e8167)

**After**

![Annotated after: actual limit and next step](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d7a1467-bccc-4a81-a852-f1a5cdcdb39e)

[See the past-time error comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205519#issuecomment-7171724207).

Contributor: [Vyctor Brzezowski (@vyctorbrzezowski)](https://github.com/vyctorbrzezowski)

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e346c5e4-f828-45b2-be8f-1aad6754fbad)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5291412e-7f95-4f28-907d-16ba126d23c6)

prs.title: feat(android): use the signed-in person's saved session pins
prs.body: ## Problem #204436 moves session pins to the signed-in person's saved sidebar order on the Gateway. Android still read and wrote the old shared `pinned` flag, so its sidebar and Threads view could disagree with the person's own pins on other clients. ## What changes (Android only) - Android advertises `personal-session-pins` in `connect.caps`. It enables personal pin edits only when `hello-ok` confirms the capability for an operator with verified durable preferences. Otherwise pins are read-only ("Personal pins are read-only here.") or, on older Gateways, "Update the Gateway to change personal session pins." - Pin and unpin send a pin-only `sessions.patch`, separate from shared settings. Pinned order follows the Gateway's requester-scoped `sessions.list`. A retained off-page selection reconciles its pin state. After a pin edit the roster reloads once: the Gateway pushes `users.prefs.changed` before it acknowledges the patch, and the acknowledgement reuses the read that push started. It reads again only if that read failed or no push arrived. - Snooze uses the Gateway clock throughout. Roster rows and live `sessions.changed` updates on the same connection use the last accepted list's clock sample. A snooze time chosen from the menu is converted to Gateway time before it is sent, so the saved wake time and the "Wakes …" / "Wake session · …" labels match the chosen time on a skewed handset. Disconnecting drops the sample. When the deadline passes, the visible window refreshes once; retries are bounded and stop when the connection, agent or socket changes. To pin a snoozed thread, wake it first. - **Threads → Archived** has no local roster. It shows "Loading threads…" while the first read is pending, and "Threads unavailable" with a **Retry** button if no read has succeeded. "No archived threads" appears only after the Gateway returns an empty list. - Six new native i18n source entries for these messages; locale refresh comes from the usual bot PR. One line in `docs/platforms/android.md`. Not included: Swift/macOS, Archive Undo, the v45 migration, and every Gateway or protocol change. Android uses no `pinPlacement`, `archiveUndoToken` or `expectedArchivedAt`. ## Builds on #204436 The core, Gateway and web changes landed in `main` as `63b8137967c2bfebb8544da0905b2d5ccf4e3e1f` (#204436). This branch merged `origin/main` at `fd1c0692258`, taking `main`'s version of every core file, so the PR diff is now `apps/android/**` plus `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` (Android entries only) and `docs/platforms/android.md`. ## Evidence Current head: `58854b065eb90e6834dd4213aed4f51ff948b22d`, tree `8634968044b1e42df67a45e2b3e8ff2d430f71bd`. On this head the full PR CI is green, including `android-test-play` and `android-test-third-party`. Locally, the **full** `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` run (300 suites, 3,745 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped) and ktlint passed on `dd9d6f6da69`; the only later change is the test-only `SessionBrowserRefreshTest` commit. Full-suite CI on the merged head found three test-only problems in tests the targeted runs did not cover: - `RootScreenFoldTest.sidebarSessionLongPressDragRequestsPinOnRelease` assumed the old shared pin write. Drag-to-pin now needs a personal-pin connection, so the fixture grants personal pin access and checks the same exact pin patch through the capability lease. - `ChatComposerLayoutTest` called `NodeRuntime.replaceGatewayCapabilities(Set)` by reflection. The method also takes the pin grant now, and the test calls the new signature. - `SessionBrowserRefreshTest` asserted rendered archive states immediately after reads that finish off the UI thread. It failed once on the third-party flavor. Each assertion now waits up to 5 s for that exact state; the states and the read counts are unchanged. Test audit of the two files touched for the CI fixes: I read every test and helper in `RootScreenFoldTest` (21 tests). Each drives the real `RootScreen` and checks observable layout, focus, navigation or the pin request; no helpers are dead and nothing needed changing. In `ChatComposerLayoutTest` (116 tests, 6,622 lines), I read the setup and fixtures, the changed test, and a sample of reader and composer tests line by line. For the rest I checked mechanically: every test asserts directly or through an asserting helper; there are no unused private helpers, skips, sleeps or self-equal assertions; the one failure handler rethrows after printing diagnostics; and screenshot capture is env-gated with its own assertions. No test-only changes were needed. The emulator run below was done on `605dda5755bb9be17ffd02cfaf62590d1773bcfa` (tree `05e0f8bf26348dd7c1f8fcfec50ef5d9ffa8d0ff`). Since then, the Android production code changed only through the merge from `main`, which switched core to the landed #204436. The emulator run was not repeated. ### Installed app on an emulator (API 36) Setup: a fresh disposable Pixel 6 AVD (Android 16 / API 36, Google APIs arm64) installed Play Debug from the tested commit, built with `./gradlew -PopenclawBuildCommit=605dda5755bb… :app:assemblePlayDebug`. The APK's SHA-256 (`edacfe47a8f63942845a62d491dcd17731f7c0f82585428547039e9178d0f742`) matched the installed `base.apk`. The Gateways ran on host loopback, which the app reaches through the emulator bridge `10.0.2.2`, with isolated HOME/state and a synthetic shared token. Their threads were created with `sessions.create`, and the "peer" was the `openclaw gateway call` CLI using the same owner profile. The app connected through the repository's debug-only connect receiver, as in `apps/android/scripts/voice-e2e.sh`. Rows and menu states below are the installed app's UIAutomator accessibility tree. No model, live Gateway, real pins or personal device was used. 1. **Saved pin order is shown.** Candidate Gateway (the pre-merge core from #204436). The saved order was set to `[birch, amber]` via `users.prefs.set ui.railShortcuts` before the app connected. Sidebar → Pinned showed **Birch** (y=1167), then **Amber** (y=1307). 2. **A peer's pin change appears without refresh.** With the sidebar left open and no app input, the peer CLI set `[amber, cedar, birch]`. About 3 s later the app showed **Amber** (1167), **Cedar** (1307), **Birch** (1447). 3. **A pin edit from Android saves the personal order.** In Threads, long-press Cedar → **Unpin**. Android showed Pinned **Amber, Birch**, and Cedar moved under Ungrouped. The peer's `users.prefs.get` returned `["session:agent:main:amber","session:agent:main:birch"]`. 4. **Pins are read-only against an older Gateway.** Unmodified published `openclaw@2026.11.7` (its dist contains no `personal-session-pins`), with a shared pin on "Shared Cedar". Sidebar → Pinned showed "Update the Gateway to change personal session pins." above **Shared Cedar**. In the Threads long-press menu, that item's clickable container was `enabled=false`, while Snooze was `enabled=true`. Tapping it left the menu open. Afterwards `sessions.list` still returned Cedar `pinned:true` with the same `pinnedAt` (`1795563585111`) and Birch unpinned. The skewed-handset scenario was not run on the device; the unit tests below cover it. The disposable AVD, Gateway state, token, homes and logs are deleted. **Screenshots, captured on `605dda5` before the merge from `main`.** Unaltered installed-app screencaps, downscaled to 405×900, with synthetic data only. | 1. Saved order: Birch, Amber | 2. After peer change: Amber, Cedar, Birch | 3. After Android Unpin of Cedar | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | 4a. Older Gateway (2026.11.7): sidebar | 4b. Older Gateway: Threads menu | | --- | --- | | | | ### Unit tests and lint - `cd apps/android && ./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatController*' --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.Session*' --tests ai.openclaw.app.AppearancePreferenceRuntimeTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.gateway.GatewaySessionInvokeTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.ConnectionManagerTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.PersonalSessionPinOrderTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.SessionBrowserRefreshTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.ui.SessionsScreen*'` gave 35 suites, **725 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped**, and ktlint passed, on both `605dda5755b` and the merged head. - Red before the fixes, green after (same command with the production files reverted): - `liveSnoozeUsesIssuingGatewayTimeForExistingAndNewRows` covers a fast handset, a live snooze on existing and new rows, a disconnect, and a new connection generation. - `menuSnoozeSavesTheChosenHandsetTimeInGatewayTime` checks that on a handset five minutes fast the sent deadline is five minutes earlier and the returned row shows the chosen time. - `aPinAcknowledgementReusesItsPushReadAndReadsAgainOnlyWhenThatReadFails` checks 1 read when the push read succeeds, 2 when it fails, and 1 when no push arrives; the roster shows the saved pin each time. Before the fix it saw 1 read where 2 were expected. - `SessionsScreenSearchTest` did not compile without the Loading and Unavailable empty states. - `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes. The strict locale-parity check lists the new IDs as untranslated until the locale refresh. ## Local review status The exact-head local ClawSweeper review (ClawRouter `openai/gpt-6.2-sol`) of `605dda5755b`, base `c8d43c3b931`, gave proof tier C, patch tier D, overall D. Its four P2 findings are open and listed below for follow-up. ## Follow-up The four P2 findings from that review, verbatim. They stay open as follow-up work after this PR lands. 1. **Restore personal pin order when a peer wakes a thread** (`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/chat/ChatController.kt`) > Open Android while a saved pin is snoozed so the roster records it as unpinned, then wake it from another client. The live event clears snooze but does not carry the personal pin. The row upsert preserves `pinned=false` and its old position, so the thread returns outside Pinned and can offer Pin even though it is already saved. Refresh the requester-ranked roster when a live update changes whether a saved pin can appear. 2. **Use a valid Gateway clock sample for Snooze from search** (`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/chat/ChatController.kt`) > After reconnecting, let the roster read fail while Threads search succeeds. The search response has a Gateway timestamp and uses it to render the row, but it discards that sample for writes. Choosing In 1 hour on a handset five minutes fast then sends a deadline 65 minutes ahead of Gateway time. Share an accepted clock sample across reads on the same connection, or obtain one before writing rather than silently assuming the clocks agree. 3. **Keep successful search results when a background refresh fails** (`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/SessionsScreen.kt`) > Search for a thread beyond the loaded roster, then let an ordinary row update trigger a browser refresh while the search RPC times out. The active-search fallback returns the local roster's empty match list, and the UI replaces the successful remote result with No matching threads. Preserve the previous result on a failed background read; use local matches as a fallback only when no authoritative result is available. 4. **Do not restart thread searches for unrelated row activity** (`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/chat/ChatController.kt`) > The global revision advances for any changed presented row, including observer activity, and every advance cancels and restarts the query. With ongoing activity, a slow search can repeatedly lose its in-flight read; before the first result, it also repeatedly pays the debounce. Invalidate for changes that can affect the query's rows or membership, and do not cancel a usable read for an unrelated activity update.

prs.title: fix: keep session IDs clear of Running and Queued in Activity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Activity → Current work, a long session ID could extend underneath Running or Queued. Wrapping each title and ID instead made similar sessions take several lines each.

## User Impact

The session name is the primary line, the muted ID is the secondary line, and the status keeps its own space. Long names and IDs end in an ellipsis. Short ones stay intact. Selecting a row still opens the exact session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix stays in Current work. It uses weight and color for hierarchy, not larger type. It does not change font sizes, the Run Inspector, the person profile, or the Sessions sidebar.

## Evidence

The comparisons show the real Activity page with synthetic sessions on an emulated 390 × 844 phone at default text size. On the same fixture the revised first row was 64 px tall, as on the base, rather than the 105 px wrapped row in the previous PR revision. The title and ID remained 14 px and 12 px. Both longer IDs stayed out of the status column. The focused browser test selected the queued session and returned to the list. The same open-and-return interaction worked at 820, 1180, and 1440 px. Base Activity source: `50ff9d4633719`; corrected head: `c52320ebe9dea`.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before: the long ID extends into the Running and Queued column.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fbd33bac-a625-470f-8c78-79e63c652523) | ![After: names and IDs truncate on separate lines, with status still visible.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4da96fcc-f421-4f68-b293-d67f71a34fc2) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Outlined: the ID continues past its text column.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5b0ef2d-44d7-4c9c-9a31-9f4f579d5e09) | ![Outlined: the ID stops before the status.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edb37e99-8f71-4aba-a167-86c8ed4c665b) |

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep admitted pin requester and retry outside pin wakes
prs.body:
Follow-up to #204436 (requester personal session pins in Gateway tools and web, landed as 63b8137967c2). That PR accepted three edge cases for later. This PR fixes the two that reproduce on `main`. The third does not occur on `main`.

## Problem

1. **Sidebar wake retry.** When a saved pin outside the sidebar's list (for example, while the Archived filter is on) reaches its snooze end, the sidebar runs a one-time refresh. If that read stalls, the sidebar repeats it immediately without pacing. If the repeat also fails, no other read is scheduled, and the pin stays hidden until something else refreshes the list.
2. **Requester identity during a write.** `sessions.patch` / `sessions.patchMany` with `pinned` capture the requester at admission. Just before the preference write, they called `profiles.readCurrent()`, which checks the connection's *current* profile selection again. A selection change in between rejected the admitted write ("Gateway requester identity changed") instead of committing it for the original requester. This contradicts "Check authority one time, when work starts."
3. **Snooze vs Wake under clock skew in the Sessions table menu.** This does not reproduce on `main`. The Sessions table menu never offers Snooze or Wake. `pages/sessions/session-menu.tsx` never sets `snoozeAllowed` ("Snooze controls belong to the sidebar", since #168773), and the docs list Snooze/Wake as sidebar-only. The sidebar menu already uses the roster's Gateway time (`snoozeTime: view.gatewayTimeForSavedPin(...)`), and `app-sidebar.pin-clock.test.ts › uses the current sidebar read for the selected saved pin` covers it at ±60 s. With a signed, writable profile at ±60 s skew, the table menu for a snoozed saved pin listed `Unpin session, Rename…, Mark as unread, Copy link, Open in, Move to group, Archive session, Advanced`, with no Snooze or Wake. No code change for this item.

## Solution

- **Gateway (2):** after `profiles.admit()`, `patchPersonalSessionPins` no longer calls `profiles.readCurrent()`. The pre-write recheck still covers lifetime and Stop (`owner.assertCurrent()`), each target's visibility, snooze, archive and replacement checks, and the preference CAS. It writes to the admitted `owner.profileId`. Direct handler callers without the router's target witness still check the live connection through `prepareSessionSharingAccess`, so a profile switch still refuses there. Production mutations go through the router.
- **Web (1):** the list's event-refresh coordinator gets `wake()`. It queues the same window wake a snooze cutoff (`activityExpiresAt`) queues, so a retryable failure (timeout or retryable `UNAVAILABLE`) retries once with the roster's pacing and `retryAfterMs`. The sidebar's outside-pin timer calls `sessionData.wakeSidebarSessions()`. That goes to `sessions.wakeList(query)` in chip mode and to the all-agent roster binding in roster mode. Repeated wakes merge. If another agent's read has replaced the primary window, the wake reads the requested agent directly, as before, with one attempt. `reset()` also clears a pending wake that has no Gateway receipt.

Changed: 14 files (9 source, 4 tests, 1 test harness), +174 / −32.

## Evidence

Tested head `1bb2936143f155961be1f7d8472f0d0efa518f1d` (base `627f2365457`). Each regression test fails without its fix and passes with it.

**Requester identity**: `sessions-personal-pins.admission.test.ts`. The connection switches profile inside the preference write.
```
before:  × an admitted pin commits for its original requester after the connection switches profile
           → promise rejected "Error: Gateway requester identity changed…" instead of resolving
after:   ✓ (all 8 in the file, incl. Stop / snooze / replacement still preventing the write)
```
The test asserts the write targets the original viewer and the saved layout becomes `["route:usage", "session:agent:main:own"]`. I removed the old "requester change still prevents" case because it asserted the behavior this PR fixes.

**Sidebar wake retry**: `app-sidebar.pin-clock.test.ts`. With Archived selected, the saved pin's wake read hits a 1 s `sessions.list` timeout stall.
```
before:  × … outside the Archived query using its Gateway clock (wake read stalls: true)
           → expected 3 to be 2   (immediate unpaced repeat, then no recovery)
after:   ✓ one failed read, paced retry ~5 s later restores the pin, no further reads in 120 s
         Tests 8 passed (8)
```

**Local review follow-ups** (ClawSweeper findings on `7d5998f5`): `session-roster-wake-recovery.test.ts` and `event-refresh-coordinator.test.ts`.
```
before:  × wakes the sidebar's own primary agent and retries one failed wake read
           → expected [ 'other' ] to deeply equal [ 'main' ]
         × keeps a failed consumer wake owed until reset retires it (reset true)
           → expected "vi.fn()" to be called +0 times, but got 1 times
after:   Tests 33 passed (33)
```

Reproduce:
```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-personal-pins.admission.test.ts
cd ui && node ../scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run src/components/app-sidebar.pin-clock.test.ts src/lib/sessions/event-refresh-coordinator.test.ts src/lib/sessions/session-roster-wake-recovery.test.ts
```

Wider local checks on the tested head:
- UI `lib/sessions`, `lib/agents`, `components/app-sidebar*`, `components/session-data*` and `pages/sessions`: 178 files, 2,257 tests passed.
- Gateway personal-pin, pin-event publisher, user-preferences and session-tool batch suites passed.
- oxfmt and oxlint are clean on changed files.
- `tsc` reports no errors in changed files.

Proof gap: both fixes cover timing and failure paths: a profile switch between admission and the write, and a `sessions.list` stall exactly at wake time. A live isolated Gateway cannot trigger either one on demand. These tests drive the production router, handler and SQLite state, and the real sidebar, roster and coordinator owners with a scripted `sessions.list`. This is not a recorded browser run.

Test audit: I read all four touched test files and the sidebar harness in full. Nothing mirrors the implementation. No retries were added and no assertions were loosened.

## Local review (exact head)

ClawSweeper local review (ClawRouter GPT-6.2 Sol) of PR head `add17519a4dd` (tree identical to `1bb2936143f1`): **patch is correct**, confidence 0.92, **no review findings**. Patch tier C, proof tier F, overall F. The proof tier is F because the evidence is test-only: the Gateway test drives the production router and SQLite with a scripted profile switch, and the sidebar test scripts the list timeout in jsdom. As noted under Proof gap, a live isolated Gateway cannot produce a mid-write profile switch or a `sessions.list` stall exactly at wake time without fault injection. The earlier review of `7d5998f5` raised two findings; both are fixed above.

## Impact

- A pin write admitted for one profile is saved to that profile even if the connection switches profile mid-write. Visibility, archive, snooze and CAS checks still apply.
- A snoozed saved pin reappears after a brief Gateway stall at wake time, and the sidebar no longer sends an immediate unpaced repeat read during the stall.
- No protocol, config, schema or docs changes.

Credit: follows #204436 by @fuller-stack-dev.
