prs.title: fix: explain how to correct CLI automation schedules
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a positional automation schedule is rejected, the CLI can tell you that a flag you never typed is invalid. It also suggests a field count even when the expression already has that many fields.

## User Impact

The CLI explains what it couldn’t use and shows accepted input. Creation and editing still reject the same schedules before sending them to the Gateway. Exit status and the JSON error type are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Creation and editing already use the same schedule validator. Updating its three messages covers both positional and flag-based inputs without changing scheduling behavior.

| Surface / trigger | Exact before | Exact after |
|---|---|---|
| `automations create 'tomorrow'`, or rejected `--at` on create/edit | `Invalid --at. Use an ISO timestamp or a duration like 20m.` | `OpenClaw couldn’t use that run time. Use a date and time like 2030-01-15T09:00:00Z or a delay like 20m.` |
| `automations create 'every weekday'`, or rejected `--every` on create/edit | `Invalid --every. Use a duration like 10m, 1h, or 1d.` | `OpenClaw couldn’t use that repeat interval. Use --every 10m or, when creating an automation, "every 10m".` |
| Rejected cron expression, positional input `9am standup with the team today` | `Invalid cron expression "9am standup with the team today". Use 5 fields like "0 9 * * *" or 6 fields like "0 0 9 * * *".` | `OpenClaw couldn’t use the cron expression “9am standup with the team today”. For example, "0 7 * * *" means every day at 7:00 AM. Six-field expressions put seconds first.` |
| Same cron error with rejected `--cron '0 25 * * *'` on create/edit | `Invalid cron expression "0 25 * * *". Use 5 fields like "0 9 * * *" or 6 fields like "0 0 9 * * *".` | `OpenClaw couldn’t use the cron expression “0 25 * * *”. For example, "0 7 * * *" means every day at 7:00 AM. Six-field expressions put seconds first.` |

**Skill in practice:** A bare `10m` would change `every weekday` from a repeating schedule to a one-time run, so the recovery gives the full positional form (`"every 10m"`) as well as the flag. Review caught a limit of the first draft: `0 25 * * *` already has five fields, so the revised error explains a working example instead of diagnosing the field count. It describes the six-field form separately.

## Evidence

Ran the real CLI before and after with isolated local state: four rejected creates and one rejected edit, including a malformed positional expression and a five-field expression with an invalid hour. All five exited `1` on both revisions, with matching terminal and JSON messages and the same `cli_error` type. The parser confirms `0 7 * * *` runs at 7:00 AM in the schedule’s timezone and the six-field form takes seconds first. All 190 focused CLI tests passed; targeted lint, formatting, copy check, and `git diff --check` passed. Hosted CI is not part of this proof. Local autoreview stopped at its temporary-directory isolation preflight before launching a reviewer.

### Terminal screenshots

Actual Linux terminal output for the same five commands. JSON was captured separately.

**After**

prs.title: fix: explain how to correct a custom automation schedule
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a custom automation schedule can’t be saved, the blank-field error only says the expression is required. For a rejected expression such as `0 25 * * *`, the error talks about the number of fields even though the expression already has five.

## User Impact

The blank field now gives a valid example. When an expression can’t be parsed, the editor gives a valid example and explains the schedule it represents. The same guidance appears in the clickable validation summary. Nothing is saved automatically, and validation and scheduling behavior are unchanged.

| Surface / trigger | Exact before | Exact after |
|---|---|---|
| Custom schedule, blank expression, inline | `Cron expression is required.` | `Enter a cron expression, such as 0 7 * * *.` |
| Custom schedule, blank expression, validation summary | `Expression: Cron expression is required.` | `Expression: Enter a cron expression, such as 0 7 * * *.` |
| Custom schedule, nonblank expression the parser rejects (for example `0 25 * * *`), inline | `Enter 5 fields like 0 9 * * * or 6 fields like 0 0 9 * * *.` | `Check the cron expression. For example, 0 7 * * * means every day at 7:00 AM.` |
| Same rejected expression, validation summary | `Expression: Enter 5 fields like 0 9 * * * or 6 fields like 0 0 9 * * *.` | `Expression: Check the cron expression. For example, 0 7 * * * means every day at 7:00 AM.` |

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor already distinguishes a blank expression from one it can’t parse. Both presentations use the same English strings, so the fix stays there and uses the example already in the field placeholder. #201283 and #199315 concern nearby timing controls, not these two strings.

**Skill in practice:** The writing guide pushed the blank message from a requirement to an action the reader can take in place. Tracing the parser showed that it reports failure, not which field was wrong. That’s why the rejected-expression message explains a known-good example rather than guessing the cause or telling the reader to replace their schedule.

## Evidence

The production-built Control UI was exercised in Chromium at 1280 × 1000, in English, with synthetic Gateway data. Both states were captured before and after. The browser check verified the inline and summary copy, that the summary focuses the field, and that entering `0 7 * * *` clears the error and enables **Create automation**. prs.title: fix(state): skip table_xinfo on virtual tables in sqlite-copy-swap
prs.body:
Related: #200271

## What Problem This Solves

After an OpenClaw upgrade, Gateway startup can fail while migrating an active agent's SQLite store if that store has a sqlite-vec memory index (`memory_index_chunks_vec` using `vec0`). When the startup Doctor chain cannot finish the schema upgrade and falls back to the generic copy-and-swap rebuild, the fallback opens the database without loading sqlite-vec, inspects the virtual table, and crashes with `no such module: vec0`. The same store can be upgraded offline with `openclaw doctor --fix`, so the data itself is fine; Gateway just cannot start until that workaround is used. #200284 already stops completed retained-deletion agents from entering this path, but an active agent still hits the crash.

## User Impact

Gateway startup should complete the copy-and-swap fallback for active agent databases that contain a vec0 memory index, without requiring an offline doctor run first. The vector table is a derived index: the fallback drops it and memory-core rebuilds it on demand from `memory_index_chunks`. Previous files stay pinned as `.pre-*` backups. No operator action or data migration is required after this change lands; until then, `openclaw doctor --fix` remains the workaround.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback already never copies virtual tables or their shadow tables. Skipping `PRAGMA table_xinfo` on `type = 'virtual'` (as it already does for shadow tables) and excluding virtual source tables from the copy loop lets the rebuild finish without loading sqlite-vec. Loading sqlite-vec on the swap connection would be a larger change and is unnecessary because a missing vector table is treated as incomplete and rebuilt from the chunk rows.

## Evidence

Reproduced on OpenClaw 2026.11.10, Node 24, Linux/WSL2, upgrading an active agent store from schema 19 toward the then-current expected schema 42. Startup migration entered the copy-and-swap fallback and failed with sanitised log lines of the form:

```text
State upgrade chain failed at agent-schema ... is at schema 19 after the chain, expected 42
Reason: no such module: vec0
```

Offline `openclaw doctor --fix` upgraded the same store successfully, which is the current workaround.

Locally, a unit test that builds an agent database containing `memory_index_chunks_vec USING vec0(...)` through `buildAgentDatabaseByCopy` (without loading sqlite-vec on the swap connection) reproduced `Error: no such module: vec0` before this change. After the change:

- `pnpm test src/state/sqlite-copy-swap.test.ts src/state/state-upgrade.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 75 tests passed, including a new test that the fallback upgrades an active agent database with a vec0 index and keeps `.pre-*` backups.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` and `pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --type-check` on the changed files: passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src`: passed

The live Gateway start after this patch was not re-run in the original failing environment; validation is from the sanitised pre-fix logs and the focused tests above.

prs.title: fix(ui): preserve one-shot cron times across editor time zone changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Renaming a one-shot automation could reschedule it if the browser’s time zone changed while the editor was open. Cloning could also shift the scheduled instant or disable Save when the displayed minute fell in a daylight-saving gap in the new zone.

## User Impact

Renaming a one-shot keeps its original instant, including seconds and milliseconds. Cloning copies that same instant. Entering a different wall time schedules the job in the browser’s current time zone.

## Why This Change Was Made

The editor remembers the local minute it showed alongside the stored timestamp. Validation and save now use that timestamp while the field still matches the original display. Previously, save formatted the stored timestamp again in the new time zone to decide whether the field had changed.

## Evidence

- On the parent, the mounted Chromium rename test sent `2030-03-09T20:25:00.000Z` for a job scheduled at `2030-03-10T02:10:01.001Z`. The clone test disabled Save after switching to New York. The explicit reschedule control passed.
- All five tests in the Chromium cron descriptions suite passed on the fix. A separate mounted editor replay used the registered Gateway handlers and reopened SQLite after every save. All 13 cases matched the expected instant, including unchanged clones, repeated hours, reopened editors, and explicit edits.
- Formatting and type-aware lint passed for the original four files. The field-key type correction cleared all 14 renderer diagnostics in a scoped compiler comparison and produced identical JavaScript. The browser tests changed Chromium’s time zone on the same open page. Jobs stayed disabled throughout.

## Hosted verification

The five Chromium cron tests and all seven production and test type jobs passed on the corrected head. The browser tests used mock transport. The separate 13-case replay used the registered Gateway handlers and reopened SQLite after each save. [Chromium job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45696189858/job/139495079521)

The manual workflow finished red on the dependency scan and its aggregate. All 13 production and five full-tree diagnostics also occurred on the parent and in a trusted main run. [Dependency job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45696189858/job/139495079904) · [Main comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45561863237/job/139027509204)

prs.title: fix(discord): keep the selected servers and channels during setup
prs.body:
## Summary

The Discord setup wizard now saves new server and channel selections by numeric ID and shows which Discord server and channel each entry matched.

## What Problem This Solves

When more than one server matched a name, setup could pick the first server. A failed lookup could also discard other successful lookups, switch an existing access policy, or leave a new allowlist empty without telling the operator. Re-selecting a configured channel could also replace its settings.

## User Impact

Enter a server name, `Server/#channel`, or `#channel` during guided setup. If the server cannot be identified uniquely, enter `guild:<id>` to choose it. The wizard retains the requested channel while selecting the server. A bare number still identifies a channel. Each unsuccessful entry can be retried or explicitly skipped, and the summary counts actual additions. If an entry would override an existing name, wildcard, or inherited channel rule, setup explains how to keep or edit that rule. The empty-allowlist warning also applies when the operator skips access configuration. Declining to finish cancels fresh setup.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord setup hook in `extensions/discord/src/setup-guild-access.ts`, registered by `setup-core.ts`, owns the interactive decision and writes the policy and selected entries together. It keeps existing guild and channel records when adding entries. The wizard reuses the Discord allowlist input parser and REST operations, and treats a full server-list page as inconclusive for name matching. The wizard checks existing rules before writing a more specific ID. Repairing previously saved configurations belongs to the separate Doctor change in #205558.

## Evidence of Fix

| Wizard input or condition | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Duplicate server name, server/channel pair, or channel across servers | On the base revision, declining the edit changed a disabled policy to allowlist. The change preserves the policy and existing restrictions, or writes only the ID selected on retry. |
| Mixed existing, new and skipped entries | The base revision overwrote settings on the selected channel. The new flow retained its disabled flag and mention rule and counted only the new selection. |
| Full guild page, failed lookup, unavailable token reference | The wizard requests a server ID when uniqueness is uncertain, keeps successes from the same edit, and can retry with a lookup credential while preserving the configured reference. |
| Existing name, wildcard or thread-parent rule | Six regression cases failed on the first PR commit. The corrected wizard preserves the prior policy and rule and counts the selection as skipped. |
| Fresh empty allowlist | Two regression cases failed on the first PR commit. Skipping access configuration now shows the warning, and declining to finish cancels fresh setup. |
| Interactive CLI, isolated config and local Discord REST fixture | `pnpm openclaw channels add discord` reported two additions and one skip. The saved file contained the two selected numeric guild/channel pairs. A follow-up CLI run skipped an entry covered by a disabled, name-keyed channel rule and kept the original rule and its guild user restriction. |
| Upgrade from the npm release 2026.11.10 to head `9f17c4a3f4d` | The release wrote and validated the profile. The new CLI read the same file, added the two chosen numeric pairs, and preserved the existing guild sender restriction and disabled name-keyed channel exactly. The final file passed validation. |

[Redacted terminal captures and before/after configuration evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205554#issuecomment-7174672427). Discord responses in this run came from a local fixture.

## Testing

Ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/{setup-surface,resolve-channels,resolve-users,setup-adapter,setup-account-state}.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. All 49 tests passed. The eight new review cases failed on the previous PR commit and passed with the correction. The targeted TypeScript, lint and format checks and the CLI build passed. Independent review identified the rule-precedence and empty-setup cases above and verified their corrections. Discord responses in the regression tests came from fixtures. Live Discord validation was unavailable because the shared QA bot lease could not be acquired.

prs.title: fix: stop /reasoning on making Claude refuse every later turn until /new
prs.body:
Closes #205486 ## What Problem This Solves When someone turns reasoning visibility on with `/reasoning on` or `/reasoning stream`, the next Claude turn (for example `claude-opus-5-5` on the `claude-cli` runtime) fails with Anthropic's `[reasoning_extraction]` refusal. Every later turn in that session fails the same way until `/new`, and the error says nothing about the cause. ## User Impact `/reasoning on`, `stream` and `off` change only what OpenClaw shows, as the reasoning visibility docs describe ("whether thinking blocks are shown in replies"). Claude-backed sessions keep answering after the toggle. The command's reply and the saved level are unchanged, and `/elevated` still tells the model about its change. No action is needed after upgrading. Queued system events are held in memory only, so nothing stored carries the old line. ## Why This Change Was Made A reasoning level change queued a system event (`Reasoning ON - include .`, `Reasoning STREAM - emit live .`, `Reasoning OFF - hide .`), and the next turn carried it as a `System:` line, for every provider. Almost every provider plugin reports native reasoning output (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, MiniMax), and the prompt builder gives those models no `` tag hint. For them the event was the only instruction to write their reasoning out as visible text, which Anthropic refuses as reasoning extraction. Tagged-output models already get the `` rule in the system prompt on every turn, along with `Reasoning=`, so the event added nothing for them either. The fix removes the event where it is made, in the directive handler, rather than filtering it later. ## Evidence **Result in plain words.** On the current stable release, `/reasoning on` followed by a plain question puts the line into the next Claude Code prompt, and Anthropic refuses the turn. On this branch, the same steps on the same state and config give a normal answer for both `on` and `stream`. The prompt holds no reasoning line, and the Gateway logs no refusal. **Real Gateway runs.** Each run used a throwaway state directory with a stub Telegram Bot API (`channels.telegram.apiRoot`), with the turns sent as owner DMs through Telegram updates. The agent was `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` on `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"` with `reasoningDefault: "on"` and no fallbacks, on Node 24.22.3 with Claude Code 2.1.332. A logging wrapper recorded each Claude Code launch's stdin. Steps: `/new`, `/reasoning off`, one plain turn, `/reasoning `, then "a bus leaves at 9:50 and the trip takes 1 h 25 min. When does it arrive? Answer briefly."
Before: OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f) from npm, level on ```text level=on reasoning_line_in_prompt=1 reasoning_extraction_log_lines_added=3 replies_after_question=["⚠️ OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply. For details, open Settings → Logs in the OpenClaw app or run openclaw logs"] ``` The question's Claude Code stdin held: ```text System: [2026-11-25 18:52:10 UTC] Reasoning OFF - hide . System: [2026-11-25 18:52:39 UTC] Reasoning ON - include . ``` Gateway log: `lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:... error="API Error: Opus 5.5's safeguards flagged this ...` `Details: [reasoning_extraction]`
After: this branch (3edf959 on main 04cd806fe), built with pnpm build and started with node dist/index.js gateway run on a copy of the same state ```text level=on reasoning_line_in_prompt=0 reasoning_extraction_log_lines_added=0 replies_after_question=['11:15. 9:50 plus 1 h is 10:50, and 25 more minutes makes 11:15.'] level=stream reasoning_line_in_prompt=0 reasoning_extraction_log_lines_added=0 replies_after_question=['It gets in at 11:15. Adding 1 hour to 9:50 gives 10:50, and 25 more minutes makes it 11:15. ...'] ```
**Regression test.** A new case in `reply.directive.directive-behavior.shows-current-verbose-level-verbose-has-no.test.ts` changes the level to `on`, `stream` and `off`. It then drains the real system-event queue with `drainFormattedSystemEvents`, the function that builds the next turn's `System:` block, and checks that the block holds no reasoning or `` text. A second case checks that `/elevated on` still reaches that block. The two existing tests that expected the reasoning event now expect none.
Regression test on the base (main 04cd806fe without the fix): 3 failed ```text FAIL keeps /reasoning on out of the next turn's model context FAIL keeps /reasoning stream out of the next turn's model context FAIL keeps /reasoning off out of the next turn's model context AssertionError: expected 'System: [2026-11-25 18:59:11 UTC] Rea…' not to match /reasoning|/i + Received: "System: [2026-11-25 18:59:11 UTC] Reasoning OFF - hide ." Test Files 1 failed (1) Tests 3 failed | 13 passed (16) ```
**Checks on the head**, Node 24.22.3: - `pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on the directive-behavior file (16/16), `directive-handling.model.test.ts` and `directive-handling.mixed-inline.test.ts` (64/64), and `get-reply-directives-apply.test.ts` (14/14) all pass. - `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` pass. - `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files pass. - `pnpm build` passes. **Local review.** A manual review of `upstream/main..HEAD` (one commit) found no findings. Nothing else reads `formatReasoningEvent` or the `mode:reasoning` context key, and the system-event queue is not persisted, so an upgrade leaves no stale line behind. **Gaps.** - I ran no real Telegram client; the transport was the stub Bot API. - I did not run the `anthropic-api` runtime or non-Anthropic providers live. For those, the regression test is the proof, since the change is provider-independent. - I did not check here whether the "Thinking" message shows in the chat. This change does not touch display, but on `claude-cli` Opus 5.5 returns empty thinking unless Claude Code's thinking summaries are on, which is a separate issue.

prs.title: fix: keep compaction from blocking approved scheduled work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compaction can turn an already approved scheduled action into an invented verification or stop instruction in the summary, leaving unattended work held even though the user authorized it.

Fixes #205387

## Why This Change Was Made

The compaction summary contract already separates completed requests from unresolved asks. These rules apply that boundary to open TODOs and preserve settled approvals when earlier verification details are absent.

## User Impact

Summaries will be instructed to keep settled approvals as decisions and reserve open TODOs for work the user requested or an unresolved tool or execution failure.

## Evidence

- Production module boundary, same command and input: `pnpm exec tsx proof-live.ts` found both policies absent on validation base `6223e638c41ae08784ec2678124f98d80ff595fa`; on head `8491c2fd3965d0e1622b683c8f6dd42a2354a567`, both were present and the pending-request control remained present.
- Focused integration regression `pnpm test src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'sends distinct history and split-turn summary formats'`: base failed at the missing TODO-policy assertion; head passed (1 passed, 34 skipped).
- The reported model session was not exercised: the OpenClaw CLI refused under its runtime-artifact publication guard while Gateway state could not be verified. No live model output is claimed.

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-live.ts
base:
todo-policy: absent
approval-policy: absent
pending-ask-control: Make the exact request below the first item in ## Pending user asks.
head:
todo-policy: Treat ## Open TODOs as unresolved actions: include only unfinished work the user requested or an actual unresolved tool/execution failure. Do not invent an audit, fact-check, verification gate, or stop/hold instruction.
approval-policy: Record settled user approvals and approved execution plans under ## Decisions. Missing details about earlier verification do not revoke an approval or add a new gate to an already-approved request.
pending-ask-control: Make the exact request below the first item in ## Pending user asks.
```

<details>
<summary>proof-live.ts</summary>

```ts
import { buildCompactionStructureInstructions } from "./src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.ts";

const prompt = buildCompactionStructureInstructions(
  "Keep the deployment decision.",
  undefined,
  "Continue the already approved scheduled posts.",
);
const checks = [
  [
    "todo-policy",
    prompt.match(/Treat ## Open TODOs as unresolved actions:.*$/mu)?.[0],
  ],
  [
    "approval-policy",
    prompt.match(/Record settled user approvals.*$/mu)?.[0],
  ],
  [
    "pending-ask-control",
    prompt.match(/Make the exact request below the first item in ## Pending user asks\./u)?.[0],
  ],
];
for (const [name, value] of checks) {
  console.log(`${name}: ${value ?? "absent"}`);
}
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(android): keep the turn recap when returning to a conversation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Android, a completed turn’s duration and output-token count could disappear after opening another conversation and returning. The final message was still visible.

## User Impact

The recap stays with the same completed turn when the conversation reloads. A newer transcript entry clears it, even if the two replies have identical text. Leaving before a turn settles still discards the pending recap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway supplies a stable transcript entry ID. Android now uses it to identify both the completed turn and the newest displayed message for recap comparisons. An optimistic message or a history row without an entry ID uses its local message ID.

## Evidence

- The new controller regression failed on the original implementation when returning to the same entry. All 24 message-identity tests passed with the fix under Robolectric on Android API 34.
- A headless Compose and Room replay preserved the 10-second, 100-token recap across a conversation switch and live history reload. A newer entry cleared it, and a late history response preserved the selected conversation’s read position.
- Local checks used Kotlin 2.4.20 and ktlint 1.8.0.

On signed head `40878914`, the repository-pinned Android Gradle tests passed all 24 identity cases in each build variant. `completedRecapAnchorSurvivesReturningToTheSameEntry` passed in 0.044s on Play and 0.034s on third-party. The local Room and headless Compose journey exercised switching away and returning to the same entry. A mounted Android device capture is still unavailable. [Play job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45687585284/job/139464981634) · [Third-party job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45687585284/job/139464981649)

prs.title: fix(ios): keep shared link captions when the title is blank
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an iOS app shares a link with a caption, it can supply an empty or whitespace-only title alongside that caption. OpenClaw’s share draft then contains only the URL, so the sender has to re-enter the caption.

## User Impact

The draft includes the supplied caption and URL when the title is blank. A meaningful title still takes precedence, with its original spacing intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The share extension selects the first meaningful title as it reads the shared items. It checks whitespace for selection and keeps the original string for the draft. When no item supplies a meaningful title, the existing content and URL deduplication rules select the fallback.

## Evidence

A regression using a string-backed `public.url` item provider failed against the original extractor for empty and whitespace-only titles. The same test passed after the change, including its absent-title and meaningful-title controls. On macOS, 16 focused Swift tests passed. Across 1,184 synthetic provider requests, every draft matched the expected text and URL. A share containing an image also retained the original image provider.

The changed sources and tests compiled for the arm64 iOS Simulator target with SDK 27.2. The 16 focused tests executed with macOS Foundation. The hosted iOS app build passed. Its voice and lifecycle simulator groups were skipped for these paths, so this run produced no iOS execution of the extractor or composer tests and no Share Extension capture. [iOS build and test steps](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45686971827/job/139462844500)

The regression checks the extracted title as well as the finished draft. `SharedContentPayload` exposes title and text separately, and the deep-link builder labels them separately. Keeping the title assertion protects meaningful-title precedence even when two payloads would compose the same visible draft.

prs.title: fix: show the full file path when reading or editing a skill on phones
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a phone, selecting a supporting file with a long path could stretch the skill dialog beyond the screen. The end of the filename and the right edge of its text area disappeared, both when editing a personal skill and when reading a shared one.

## User Impact

You can read the full selected file path above its contents without scrolling the dialog sideways. The editor keeps the same margins as the other fields. Shared skills remain read-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selected-file field now fits the dialog and lets long paths wrap. File selection, contents, and save behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

In the 390 px phone viewport, the dialog had 366 px of available width, but the selected file expanded its contents to 582 px. After the fix, the contents fit in 366 px in both the personal editor and shared reader. Checks covered switching between text and binary files, owner search and no matches, and closing the dialog with the keyboard and returning focus. Across phone, both tablets, and desktop, 28 comparisons of the original library rows and wider filename labels were pixel-identical.

The screenshots show the same synthetic personal skill and selected file on an emulated 390 × 844 phone. No skill was saved, installed, attached, or removed. Stock main: `450441b904031`. Atlas repair: `844bc8d87bbd0`.

A PDF opened in the session pane can give much of its available width to the browser’s thumbnail sidebar. The document becomes harder to read, and users may have to widen the pane or adjust the viewer before they can see it comfortably.

## User Impact

Supported native PDF viewers open with the page fit to the pane’s width and thumbnails collapsed. The toolbar stays available for zoom and navigation. No setting change or migration is needed. The existing download action and preview size limit are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Set the native viewer’s initial fit and thumbnail options at the shared PDF preview. The viewer handles resizing directly; OpenClaw does not remount it or replace its controls.

## Evidence

- The new viewer-option regression assertion failed on the base and passed with the change. All 20 focused PDF preview and worker tests passed, along with formatting and targeted lint.
- In Chromium, the real Control UI used a synthetic PDF and a mock Gateway. The document filled the 755 px pane with thumbnails collapsed; narrowing the pane to 653 px refit the same document without reloading the frame. The existing session-file preview, Files-panel entry and original-byte download test passed.
- Native macOS, Safari, and Firefox rendering were not exercised. A local independent review could not start because Codex failed its read-only sandbox preflight; no independent local verdict is claimed.

prs.title: fix(android): render display math in chats with carriage returns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android chat showed display-math delimiters as ordinary text when an assistant message used bare carriage returns for line breaks. A multiline equation between two paragraphs reproduced the problem in loaded history and in the completed streaming response.

## Why This Change Was Made

The math segmenter now counts bare carriage returns as line breaks, matching CommonMark's paragraph positions. It preserves existing CRLF bytes when reconstructing the equation so the 5,000-byte rendering limit keeps its original behavior.

## User Impact

Dollar- and bracket-delimited equations reach the math renderer with their surrounding paragraphs intact. Fenced examples remain literal, and an unfinished equation stays ordinary Markdown while the response is streaming.

## Evidence

- The new regression failed on the parent commit and passed after the fix. All nine focused Markdown math tests passed, including the oversized CRLF payload.
- An Android API 34 Robolectric fixture exercised the chat controller, Room, and the Compose assistant-message renderer across 16 cases and 73 streaming updates. The repaired bare-CR frame matched the LF/CRLF control pixel for pixel.
- The images show the native text fallback for the synthetic equation in Android's light theme. WebView bitmap rendering and physical-device appearance remain unverified.

![Android chat before and after. The literal dollar delimiters disappear and the two equation lines occupy their own block.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0ba44c7-4c40-48f5-b850-4a8b7906e8cf)

![Annotated comparison highlighting the delimiter lines before the fix and the equation block afterward.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cc801f2-5da7-4805-af9c-6c55720f5b0f)

Both captures use the same viewport and message. Before is `b6e7fcfb`. After is this PR's reviewed tree `715abd19`.
Both Android variants passed all 41 Markdown tests, including the bare-CR regression and the oversized-equation fallback. [Play tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45695714651/job/139493216478) · [Third-party tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45695714651/job/139493216477)

The first screenshot job stopped at Home with an Android System UI alert. The targeted retry captured the standard store scenes and the workflow passed. Those scenes cover a different chat fixture. [Successful retry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45695714651/attempts/2)

prs.title: feat(queue): tell the sender whether a busy-time message steered the running turn
prs.body: Related: #25222, #83871, #124731, #159816 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: in a chat channel, a message sent while a run is active gets no visible response. The sender can't tell whether it steered the running turn or is waiting for its own, so people resend, or `/stop` a run that was already doing what they asked. ## User Impact User impact: with `messages.queue.steerReceipts: true`, each message that arrives during a run in steer mode gets its own reply quoting that message: - `🦞🛞 Current run steered with your new message.` once the runtime has taken the message into the running turn - `⏳ Couldn't steer the current run; your message is queued behind it.` when the message falls back to a followup turn and the queue keeps it - when the fallback runs into `messages.queue.cap`, the receipt follows the queue's actual disposition instead of promising an answer: `summarized` (including a summary line that was elided but is still retained), `dropped` (asks the sender to resend), or `at-cap` (a sibling steer is still parked, so the outcome isn't final yet) - fallback receipts say where the message is now and never promise an answer, because the queue can still change. With `drop: old`, if a later overflow evicts a message that was reported as queued, the sender gets one follow-up reply to that message: dropped, please resend. Summary-entry trimming has no disposition hook, so the summary receipt says older entries can be trimmed instead of sending a second notice It is off by default, so nothing changes unless an operator turns it on. **Scope, stated upfront:** #25222 describes a broader busy-reply contract: all queue modes, configurable text, `/stop` and `/new` guidance, and stable reason codes. This PR is a first, opt-in piece of that for steer mode only, where the outcome is known exactly. If you'd rather extend it here (for example make the text configurable, or cover `followup`/`collect`), or change the default wording, tell me and I'll adjust. ## Why This Change Was Made `runActiveReplySteer` already knows the outcome, and the receipt is sent at exactly those points: - **Steered** fires only after `finalizeReplyMessageInjectionAttempt` returns `accepted`, meaning the runtime took the input. For runtimes that steer at tool boundaries, that's when the current tool call ends, so the receipt is never premature. - **Fallback** fires on every path that hands the message back to the followup queue. `parkSteerCandidate().fallback()` returns where the message ended up (`queued` / `at-cap` / `summarized` / `dropped`), because releasing the park reapplies queue overflow. For `queued`/`at-cap` fallbacks, `armSteerReceiptEvictionNotice` wraps the run's existing `onQueueDisposition` (the observer still runs first) and sends the follow-up on `queue-cap-old`, ordered after the first receipt. - Cancelled or aborted steers send nothing, and ambient room events never get a receipt. The receipt goes out through `routeReply` as a standalone reply with `mirror: false`, so the model never sees its own receipts. It is deliberately not the message's terminal reply: a queued message still owes its real answer from the followup, and a second terminal reply for the same inbound would collide with it. Two channel details learned from real traffic: - **Telegram quotes only an explicit `replyToId`.** It has no `threading.resolveReplyTransport`, so the payload names the message. `FollowupRun.messageId` is often unset on the steer path, so the id falls back to `sessionCtx.MessageSid`, the same fallback `resolveAcceptedSteerRunId` already uses. - **`responsePrefixContext` comes from the active run**, so operators who template `messages.responsePrefix` see the model, not a literal `{modelFull}`. **Config surface:** one boolean. The core config budget goes from 2464 to 2465 (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`). It's opt-in because #83871 asked for this without default chat noise. If you'd prefer receipts on by default with no key, which fits "every action has a visible outcome", I can drop the key. `schema.labels.ts` was already over the line cap. The `messages.*` labels moved unchanged into `schema.labels.messages.ts`, and the file shrinks. ## Evidence **Live**, on a Telegram deployment running this PR plus #159816 (claude-cli, Claude Code 2.1.280), in DMs and a forum topic with `message_tool_only` group replies. Examples from the logs: - A message sent mid-turn got its receipt 1 to 50 s later, when the running tool call finished. For example: `outbound send ok … threadId=35 replyToMessageId=71` 4 s after message 71. - Each turn then ended with one reply covering both messages, and no followup turn replayed the steered message. - The operator testing it preferred per-message receipts with no debounce, so each message gets its own quoted confirmation. **Tests:** `src/auto-reply/reply/steer-receipt.test.ts` has 12 pure unit tests, with `routeReply` mocked and no timers, I/O or Gateway boot: - off unless the key is set - the steered and queued texts - replies to the steered message id in the right thread and account, with `mirror: false` - falls back to the source message id when the queued run has none - silent for room events and unroutable origins - never throws when delivery fails - no fallback text (`queued`, `at-cap`, `summarized`, `dropped`) promises an answer - the eviction follow-up fires once, after the fallback receipt, quoting the original message; it is not armed when receipts are off and ignores other dispositions `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/enqueue.steering.test.ts` asserts the fallback disposition for each drop policy (`summarize`, `old`, `new`), including a deferred overflow behind a parked sibling (`drop: old` reports `queue-cap-old` for the evicted earlier fallback), a run whose summary line was elided but is still retained, and the same run reported `dropped` once more overflow trims its elided copy. Single-worker wall time (`vitest run --maxWorkers=1 `, local): | File | Tests | Duration | |---|---:|---:| | `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/enqueue.steering.test.ts` | 10 | 12.3 s | | `src/auto-reply/reply/steer-receipt.test.ts` | 12 | 2.1 s | Also run: - The existing steer-adoption and `runReplyAgent` suites, and `src/config/schema*`: passing. The common-tier snapshot gains exactly `messages.queue.steerReceipts`. - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` against current main: the conflict-marker and line-cap ratchets pass. It then stops on the env-var budget (484 > 483), which comes from main because this diff adds no env vars. `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the final head. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix: show the full session name and kind when expanding a row on phones
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a phone, expanding a row in Sessions still left a long session name cut off. The same row could push the session kind past the edge of the details panel, so opening the details did not tell you which session you were looking at.

## User Impact

The full name wraps inside the expanded row, and the status and kind stay visible beside it. The collapsed list remains compact. The Sessions sidebar is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The expanded details header now reserves room for the status and kind instead of making them compete with the name. This affects only the Sessions page on phones and preserves the row alignment from #203265.

## Evidence

On a 390 px phone, the status and kind previously extended to x=400 at default text and x=422 at 140%; both now end at x=365. The full synthetic session name is visible at both sizes. Checks covered expanding a session and returning to the list, using filters and the agent picker, and selecting and clearing a row by touch and keyboard. Across 92 matched captures on phone, both tablet orientations, and desktop, 14 comparisons of short names or wider headers were pixel-identical.

The before and after screenshots show the same expanded row on an emulated 390 × 844 phone at 140% text. No live session was read or changed. Stock main: `450441b904031`. Atlas repair: `b3d56ab75f8b6`.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Expanding the session still clips its name and pushes the session kind offscreen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b1f14db-de8e-461a-bfd2-4cf33b9b86f2) | ![The full session name wraps, with Live and direct visible inside the expanded row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/922c4045-7551-4439-97c1-85b6ae8f3f6e) |

### Annotated comparison

The list row stays compact. The outline highlights the identity shown only after expanding the selected session, not the Sessions sidebar.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before: The selected identity is clipped. The kind extends beyond the detail.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b194082c-0adb-47ed-9658-a957b6f3483d) | ![After: The selected detail is complete. The compact row above is unchanged.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cb1c959e-33b6-47c5-9aaa-972528d73a19) |

Contributor: @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0bfa560b-6bf6-4ea6-aea6-4b52c7042325)

prs.title: fix: cron jobs treat node policy denials as failures
prs.body:
Related: #166763 (wrapped remote-node policy denial and persisted cron diagnostics).

## What Problem This Solves

Unattended cron runs could report success when a remote node rejected an exec command with `SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED`, including when the Gateway wrapped the native denial in an `UNAVAILABLE` error.

## User Impact

Cron jobs now preserve native node policy denials as fatal execution failures. The persisted run keeps the original denial text and a structured tool diagnostic; ordinary node transport failures retain the existing nonfatal policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

The node exec path retained structured failure metadata, but a Gateway wrapper could obscure the denial code and the cron projection discarded the tool name and code. This change:

- recognizes the native denial marker through the Gateway wrapper;
- carries the denial message and code through sanitized tool results;
- persists the original denial text without classifier decoration;
- retains `toolName` and `code` in normalized cron diagnostics.

## Evidence

The selected-test wrapper completed five shards in 292.13s. [Exact-head ClawSweeper review, revision 19](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160620#issuecomment-5876130261), completed with no introduced code or security findings. prs.title: fix(android): keep turn recap tokens readable on narrow screens
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a narrow Android phone at large system font sizes, the completed-turn recap can give the output-token count zero layout width. In a 328 dp transcript row, the count for a 90-second turn with 1,234 tokens painted in eleven lines and overlapped the separator. The text stayed inside the viewport.

## User Impact

The duration and token count can wrap onto separate lines. When they fit, both appear inline. Turns without token metadata show the duration alone.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the original repair offered by @saariuslystoned in [issue #196069](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/196069). It gives the text the space remaining beside the icon and keeps the separator with the token count when the group wraps.

## Evidence

- A trusted Robolectric native-graphics replay measured the original row at 328 dp on a 360 dp phone, with 2× system text and the Standard app setting. Seven painted pixels overlapped. The standard-size and wide controls remained inline.
- Both contributor tests passed in the protected Android Play job. Robolectric SDK 31 mounted the recap at 320 dp with 2.8× and 1× text and checked the missing-token case. The two tested files matched the contributor head byte for byte. At 328 dp and 2×, the pinned AndroidX line-break calculation moves the measured token group to the next line. A pixel capture of the repaired component at that exact size and a physical-device observation remain open. [Android Play job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45689157492/job/139470377803) · [JUnit artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45689157492/artifacts/15057714814)

The two font-scale assertions are retained. They check the scale reported by the mounted text layout before the tests assert wrapping, overflow, and standard-size alignment.

Fixes #196069

prs.title: fix: reconcile conflicting legacy approvals without replacing current policy
prs.body:
## Problem
Doctor deliberately retains a conflicting retired approvals file rather than silently replacing the current SQLite policy. Operators need a read-only comparison and an explicit way to retain the current policy and retire those legacy bytes.

## Solution
Add `openclaw approvals reconcile` for a redacted, read-only preview, and `--keep-current` for explicit retirement under the existing maintenance/migration owner. Preserve the exact canonical policy row, archive exact legacy bytes with platform-enforced private creation, then remove the legacy source. Never import legacy credentials on that path. Reuse the current owner’s interrupted source/claim handling and keep policy preview available when separate credential custody needs repair; socket comparison is then explicitly unavailable rather than falsely equal. No new persisted schema or automatic policy selection.

## Validation
- Actual shipped CLI in isolated state: preview preserved the exact current row and legacy bytes; `--keep-current` preserved the exact row, archived exact private bytes, removed the legacy source, and repeated without changes. Synthetic legacy credential was not printed.
- Focused migration, CLI, and passive-startup tests passed, including missing credential custody, an interrupted hard-link claim, contradictory retained names, missing/invalid current policy, exact archive bytes, absent/invalid-profile preview, and macOS native-helper refusal/restoration.
- Core and scoped CLI/infra typechecks, touched lint/format, and diff checks passed; review-fix core typecheck also passed.
- Independent local review identified archive privacy and read-only recovery gaps; these were repaired. Follow-up recovery reviews also caught absent/invalid-profile preview and native-helper diagnostic gaps; those are fixed and covered. The final small diagnostic/root-shape follow-up was locally inspected and tested, not sent through a fourth independent review.
- A fresh installed-stable-to-this-head upgrade/service campaign was not run. Historical evidence on earlier heads is not current-head upgrade proof. New-head CI remains required.

## Latest CI repair

CI follow-up: documented why the passive-startup fixture isolates config loading, plugins, terminal output, process exit and Gateway state probing. All 4 passive startup cases and the mock-export guard pass; no baseline exception or production behavior changed. New-head CI pending.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): store every reply in chat history, not just the final one
prs.body: Closes #195856 Related: #164293, #166511 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: with the `claude-cli` backend, replies sent before the final message vanish after a CLI session rotation, or after a run is killed or fails. ## User Impact User impact: completed user-addressed replies remain in the conversation after a session reset. Text from an interrupted run remains visible, marked "Interrupted". Yielded progress remains progress; scheduled execution prose retains its audit-only policy. ## Why This Change Was Made Previously, only the final reply was durable; earlier replies depended on the currently bound Claude log. This change buffers the latest revision per native UUID and persists it when the next assistant record arrives or the process ends. Writes retain normal preparation hooks and ownership checks. Final settlement deduplicates by native identity and awaits queued writes, including on failure. The change works with commentary streaming enabled or disabled. #164293 covers commentary-enabled persistence; #166511 covers a watchdog interruption slice. Settlement uses a closed assistant-metadata operation: content, identity, timestamps, topology and replay inputs cannot change. It preserves the transcript generation and returns the current anchor without relaxing generic rewrite invalidation or changing account admission. ## Evidence ### Scheduled Claude fixture diagnostics — [3d6297baf2c7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196092/commits/3d6297baf2c7ec6626af724840d9363b62ee5491) The [failed hosted case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45690617324/job/139476416345) had reached its intentional clock advance, but retained only the child’s exit code. This test-only change keeps the nonzero exit and failing cron status, and reports the synthetic child's failing operation and a bounded reason without dumping a scheduled job, input, or credentials. It does not relax the exactly-one-edit or cancellation assertions. - On the pre-change fixture, [an induced HTTP 415](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_57e08be98660d6ee59f9e5cbba021755) reached the parent as a generic exit 1. On the [instrumented fixture](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_dbbee2cc04e8189705a756ce006f3be2), the parent identified the HTTP failure at `tools/list` and separately identified malformed tool arguments. These controlled failures do **not** identify the historical exception. - The final reviewed test passed all nine scenarios against the clean CI base. Additional early-completion and native-creator error controls both failed as intended, surfaced the phase, and did not print the synthetic private marker. Independent review, pinned type-aware lint and formatting passed. Production code is unchanged. - A separate upstream-only stress control ran the original scenario sequence twelve times with failure-only diagnostics: 117/117 tests passed across the shard. No natural exception was captured. The authenticated Claude CLI Stop → native-session rotation → reload flow remains unverified. - [Hosted CI on this commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45703112336) ran [all nine scheduled-message scenarios successfully](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45703112336/job/139518864961), including the exact trusted channel-edit case. The original error did not recur. The sole failed test was [the previously reproduced baseline Goal role-loss assertion at line 522](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45703112336/job/139518864576); the overall CI gate remained red. ### November 25 CI correction — [b3ff347256fb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196092/commits/b3ff347256fbf106a6bbc7d906767c5d815ef14e) The [preceding CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45686751611) found two type-aware lint errors and two new session-ID comparisons. The correction reuses the native snapshot key for comparison and settlement, makes the stream callback independent of its receiver, and awaits outstanding event handlers at test teardown. No test expectations, lint rules or baseline allowances changed. Pinned Oxlint reproduced both diagnostics before the fix and reported none afterward; the identity ratchet, formatting and whitespace checks passed. Independent source review found no actionable issues. Two other Gateway failures are inherited: the Goal role-loss assertion at line 522 reproduced with the same expected/received error on the clean CI base `bb0fc6578574`, using a test-only home. The in-process continuation assertion at line 325 has the same failure on [scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45675425119/job/139422317092). Neither assertion was changed. [Hosted CI on the correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45690617324) passed the repaired lint and identity checks, but the overall gate failed. Three test jobs failed: - Goal role loss: the same line-522 baseline failure described above. - SQLite startup verification: the [checkpoint assertion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45690617324/job/139476415977) matches [known issue #205290](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/205290), including both frame counts (`16461 > 16461`). - [Scheduled Claude CLI channel edit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45690617324/job/139476416345): the synthetic Claude process exited with code 1. The same 10-file shard passed 90/90 twice on the clean CI base and 90/90 on the PR head in isolated AWS with diagnostic instrumentation. The process exception was not identified; these passes do not establish that the CI-merge failure is inherited. The synthetic fixture is not the requested real Claude CLI Stop → native-session rotation → reload test in Crabbox. Source review, syntax/format checks and `git diff --check` completed. Hosted [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45686751611) is separate. **The real Claude CLI Stop → native-session rotation → reload flow has not been verified on this commit.** Earlier live results below apply only to their named commits. ### Earlier focused proof - Focused CLI parser, transcript, account admission, Gateway history, import closure, and Control UI regressions: 363 tests passed, 3 skipped across the proof runs. The focused Stop-before-flush regression passed again after porting its fixture to the current transcript owner. Changed test-project typechecks passed for agents, Gateway, commands, and chat UI. ### Upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.5 to head `7b3e9d23b50` Both builds were made from clean checkouts (buildstamps `e13cf15ece9` = v2026.11.5, and `7b3e9d23b50`). SQLite `user_version` went from 38 to 42. `quick_check` returned `ok` before and after. A pre-migration backup was written, and its integrity check passes. - **Existing data:** the selected model and settings are the same. All 11 canonical transcript events match before and after the upgrade (field-by-field projection). The same session reopened **before** any new turn showed the old history: `DONE-A` once and the interrupted story once. - **First candidate turn (native replacement):** `REPLACEMENT-OK-196092` settled as a new message. The local session ID is unchanged, and the Claude CLI binding moved to a new native session. The imported reply matches the new binding. After reload, `DONE-A`, both interrupted stories and the new reply each appear exactly once, and two events are appended after the unchanged 11. - **Scope note:** v2026.11.5 never wrote non-final text to canonical storage; it showed it only from the bound Claude log. That covers the narration lines and the pre-tool text of completed runs. Once the first post-upgrade turn replaces the Claude session, that pre-upgrade text is no longer shown. This PR persists such text for runs from this version on; it cannot recover text the old version never stored. This upgrade's replacement came from `cli session reset … reason=mcp`. The resume-hash canonicalization in `bundle-mcp.ts`, which this PR does not change, now normalizes the openclaw server's `alwaysLoad`. As a result, bindings stored while tools were deferred do not match once after upgrading. v2026.11.5, story interrupted by Stop, after reload · after upgrading, same session before a new turn · after the replacement turn, after reload: ### November 18 conflict-repair update — `51bc1056a612` Updated against main `b609d22c129f2944c1abaec1d2895eb659493a36`, preserving the newer transcript-lease and stopped-first-session recovery behavior. - Held replies arriving without snapshot callbacks now use the same native-keyed settlement writer as streamed snapshots. Both paths retain each answer once, including transformed output and a final interim result. The separate recursive interim writer and its identity helper were removed. - Three held-history cases failed after a mechanical merge (one saved answer instead of two), then passed after reconciliation. The existing history matrix now also exercises streamed snapshot deduplication. - Independent review identified three P2 cases: saved commentary trimming an unrelated answer, an unterminated final revision losing to an earlier snapshot, and delivered-failure recovery skipping settlement. Seven regression cases failed before their repairs, including confirmed progress (`final: false`) delivery; matching mirrors are hidden without promoting progress into completed-answer evidence. - Repaired runner/parser/chat-consumer checks: **217 passed, 3 skipped** across 10 files (86.64 s). Final parser/framing/budget/reasoning/persistence checks: **229 passed, 3 skipped** across 8 files (54.67 s). The final progress/final delivery correction passed 90 tests (3 skipped) across history, transcript, and settlement suites (66.49 s). These selections overlap and are not additive totals. - Core and UI typechecks, targeted format/lint, `git diff --check`, and exact-base max-lines/test-lines ratchets passed. The test allocation is 860 lines beyond the ordinary 400-line allowance, covering native identity/settlement and the held-reply/commentary/terminal-revision/delivered-failure regressions. Whole-change net delta against this base: +831 production lines and +1,260 test lines. Stream framing and budget accounting now live together in the existing stream-limits owner, with unchanged limits, keeping the parser within its file-size cap. - **Independent review:** User-authorized, separate read-only source review covered the candidate against the stated base and the subsequent repair deltas. Three P2 findings were reproduced and corrected; the same reviewer confirmed all findings resolved. This was source inspection, not an independent test rerun. Native autoreview was unavailable: its bounded attempt timed out after 180 seconds without a report; no clean autoreview result is claimed. - **Proof limits:** the v2026.11.5 upgrade run above is a live run at head `7b3e9d23b50`. The other live Claude/Control UI evidence below is retained from the stated earlier revisions. Current-head hosted CI must be read separately; no prior-head result is represented as a current-head pass. ### Earlier implementation evidence - Native Claude CLI steering: three accepted steers (A/B/C), with one `DONE: STEER-A, STEER-B, STEER-C` live and after reload. Narration stays between the steers. - Stable upgrade from v2026.11.3: Doctor migrated schema 27 → 42. prs.title: fix(discord): repair name-keyed server rules in Doctor
prs.body:
## Summary

Discord Doctor can now move an existing server rule from a name to an operator-confirmed numeric ID. On a writable configuration, unattended Doctor records the IDs of servers that match an ambiguous rule and pauses their incoming activity until the operator resolves it. On a read-only deployment, Doctor reports the matching IDs so the operator can fix the deployment source. This covers existing configurations. [#205554](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205554) covers server selection during setup.

## What Problem This Solves

1. Doctor previously left name-keyed rules in place without identifying the rule or offering a way to move its attached restrictions. The Discord adapter now reports the authored path and repairs each rule in its original scope. See `extensions/discord/src/doctor.ts` and `extensions/discord/src/doctor-guilds.ts`.
2. An unattended run had no durable record of which servers were affected by an ambiguous name. Discord Gateway dispatch, queued-message delivery and voice admission now consult the account's recorded server IDs. See `extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.ts`, `extensions/discord/src/monitor/ingress.ts` and `extensions/discord/src/voice/access.ts`.

## Why this design

- Keep the account-specific pause on the unresolved rule. An interactive repair removes the bookkeeping. A manual rekey to a numeric ID also releases the pause.
- Move the entire rule so user, role, channel, and tool restrictions stay together. Retain both entries and report the conflict when the proposed ID already exists in the same scope.
- Keep the directory lookup inside the Discord plugin. Use the existing config writer for unattended persistence, and preserve regular delivery for other servers and DMs.

## Relation to the setup change

The two PRs are based independently on main. Both touch the server directory reader in `extensions/discord/src/guilds.ts`. When integrating the second PR, retain setup's single-page reader and Doctor's paginated lookup through the same owner. [Setup PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205554)

## Evidence of Fix

| Path and command | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline, `pnpm openclaw doctor --non-interactive` | Doctor completed without identifying the name-keyed rule. |
| `pnpm openclaw doctor --non-interactive`, `pnpm openclaw doctor </dev/null`, and `pnpm openclaw doctor --yes` | Each saved the two matching IDs. The third server's rule and the original restrictions survived. |
| Update child, `pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` | The candidate persisted the same pause with update mode enabled, including on a config saved by stable 2026.11.10 Doctor. |
| Interactive terminal, `pnpm openclaw doctor --fix` | Entering the intended ID moved the rule with its user and tool restrictions and cleared its pause. The adapter test also verifies that an occupied destination preserves both entries. |
| Three starts of `pnpm openclaw gateway run` against a local Discord simulator | Only the unaffected server reached the durable ingress queue on the first two starts. After manually rekeying the rule, messages from all three reached ingress on the third start. |
| Externally managed diagnosis, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_READONLY=1` and `OPENCLAW_NIX_MODE=1`, each with `pnpm openclaw doctor --non-interactive` | Before the follow-up, a read-only config stopped diagnosis at the write refusal. Both managed modes now finish, name the rule and matching IDs, and leave existing server policy in effect. Correct the key in the deployment source and redeploy. |
| Manual downgrade, 2026.11.10 `openclaw config validate` | The older schema rejected the unresolved pause field and accepted the interactively repaired config. |

The restart check inspected persisted message receipts. Live Discord validation stopped before login because the test bot lease was unavailable.

<details>
<summary>Terminal and persisted-state excerpts (synthetic IDs redacted)</summary>

Stable Doctor completed with the name-keyed rule in place. After switching the isolated install to the candidate, the update-mode Doctor saved the following server rules. The second line is the result from a separate interactive repair of that paused config.

```text
after update Doctor: {"ops": {"users": ["123"], "tools": {"deny": ["exec"]}, "doctorPausedGuildIds": {"default": ["server-A", "server-B"]}}, "server-C": {"requireMention": true}}
after interactive repair: {"server-C": {"requireMention": true}, "server-A": {"users": ["123"], "tools": {"deny": ["exec"]}}}
```

The Gateway fixture sent one message per server on each independent start. These are the actual ingress receipt rows, keyed by message ID. The first two starts used the persisted pause. The third followed a manual rekey.

```text
gateway cycle 0 received ['message-1C'] expected ['message-1C']
gateway cycle 1 received ['message-2C'] expected ['message-2C']
gateway cycle 2 received ['message-3A', 'message-3B', 'message-3C'] expected ['message-3A', 'message-3B', 'message-3C']
```

</details>

The review follow-up exercised an operator edit during the server-directory request on both revisions. These terminal lines come from checking the saved config after Doctor exited:

```text
before: exit 1 operator edit True pause field present False
after:  exit 0 operator edit True pause field present False
```

The local voice admission test rejected an otherwise-allowed speaker from the paused guild and admitted the same speaker from another guild. The durable-queue test admitted both messages before starting the monitor, then observed only the unaffected message at dispatch and a completed receipt for the paused message.

On the read-only fixture, Doctor printed the report below. Both read-only and Nix runs reached `Doctor complete`. Inspection of the read-only fixture showed the original restrictions and no newly saved pause.

```text
Discord account default: could not confirm a saved pause for servers
[server A], [server B] at channels.discord.guilds["ops"].
Check the current config and rerun Doctor, or resolve the name in the deployment source.
```

## SDK and caller upgrade contract

The generated channel config baseline gains six paths: the pause field, account key and ID array element under each of the root and account guild schemas. These represent one optional saved field. The channel Doctor hooks receive optional input for interactive text and a config revision for unattended writes. Existing callers of the guild directory reader keep their single-page behavior. For a manual downgrade, resolve paused rules in the current version first. When rekeying by hand, remove the `doctorPausedGuildIds` field from the rekeyed rule so the older version can load it.

## Boundary decisions for Discord and Doctor maintainers

1. Review the scope of the pause at incoming Gateway dispatch, queued delivery, and voice speaker admission. Scheduled or operator-initiated outbound work remains available.
2. Review the config write during unattended diagnosis. It uses the observed source revision and persists the IDs on the unresolved rule.

## Testing

- `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-prompter.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-flow.test.ts extensions/discord/src/doctor.test.ts extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/ingress.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.startup.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 97 tests on the original revision. On the follow-up, the voice access suite and `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/ingress.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all 9 and 12 cases respectively. The updated extensions typecheck and config documentation baseline check passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm config:channels:check`, scoped oxlint and oxfmt checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

prs.title: fix: keep notification agent choices compact and distinguish matching names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In Notifications settings, choosing one agent with a long ID made the phone button three lines tall. Inside the chooser, two agents with the same display name each took four lines. The checkboxes sat between the names and IDs, and the characters that distinguished the agents wrapped to another line.

## User Impact

The button now shows one agent name or a count for multiple selections. In the chooser, each checkbox lines up with its name. A secondary line keeps the end of a long ID visible, so you can distinguish similarly named agents. You can still search by the full name or ID. The complete selection remains available to assistive technology and on hover.

## Why This Change Was Made

The settings row summarizes the selection; the chooser is where the exact agents are identified. Separating those jobs keeps both layouts compact without changing permissions, inheritance, or which IDs are saved.

## Evidence

At 390 × 844, the saved button changed from 70 px to 38 px. With identical display names, both ID endings—`violet` and `amber`—remained visible. At 390 × 844, 820 × 1180, 1180 × 820 and 1440 × 900, selecting Amber sent only Amber’s full ID to the simulated save. Reopening the chooser and searching for Amber found it checked; the device inherited that same ID. Both focused Chromium regressions and all 16 notification settings tests passed. No live preferences changed and no notification was sent.

These phone frames compare the previous PR head `349fda349d1bb` with `5591e30b104a3`: the saved button first, then the chooser. The original [phone baseline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c564ff8-4229-403f-ad5e-b9f3b4e83a71), [previous phone repair](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b9a8842-9f7a-4dc0-886a-7d3206a65380), [desktop baseline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df4e5c24-4508-4123-8ce3-4a7826adcfd0), and [desktop count](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9714af5e-4524-4a49-8049-ec8b7b8d6760) are preserved.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The test-consolidation campaign retains repeated namespace smoke samples, copied SSE framing and assertions already covered by stronger retained suites. This batch removes 201 net test lines while keeping the behavioral, authority and persistence guards identified in the keeper map.

Refs #198737.

## User Impact

Internal test maintenance only; production behavior is unchanged. Production LOC: +0/-0. Tests: +9/-210, **201 net removed across 11 existing files**; zero new tracked files. Additions are 4.286% of deletions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the campaign's approved value bar: preserve meaningful failure detection and fold useful assertions into existing keepers. Deliberately dropped distinctions are the basic Slack sample labels/order permutation; three redundant fake-WebSocket namespace samples; the off-to-party avatar direction (fedora-to-off remains); a cosmetic AB-in-DIV positive; repeated mocked audit-payload fields; and an ineffective Workspaces ID-log assertion. These are deliberate tradeoffs, not claims of case-for-case equivalence.

| `extensions/slack/src/channel.test.ts` | 0 / 48 | 48 | Same-file real outbound adapter oversized interactive/presentation delivery; `extensions/slack/src/outbound-payload.test.ts` ordered blocks, controls, fallback, target and receipts. |
| `extensions/slack/src/shared-interactive.test.ts` | 2 / 0 | -2 | Existing “caps Slack static selects at the Block Kit option limit” retains the 100-option boundary and now asserts accessibility text contains Option 100. |

| `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.media.test.ts` | 1 / 1 | 0 | Same-file “preserves the mirror boundary for legacy identity” now requires content as well as mirror identity. |

prs.title: fix(ui): include the first day of Activity charts after spring forward
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After clocks move forward, the Activity page can list a session under Last 7 days or Last 30 days while leaving it out of the daily chart. In New York at 12:15 a.m. on March 9, a session from 11:40 p.m. on March 1 was still within the last seven days. The list and summary counted it, but the chart showed no recorded activity.

## User Impact

Each session in the selected rolling window now contributes to the bar for its local activity date. The first bar can be a partial day. The 24-hour and last-12-month charts keep their existing boundaries.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session list measures the selected window in elapsed minutes. The daily chart now finds the local date containing that same cutoff and steps through calendar days to the end of today. This accounts for both one-hour and half-hour clock changes.

## Evidence

- Both new time-zone tests failed on the parent for the 7-day and 30-day windows. All three focused Vitest cases passed after the fix.
- In a mounted Chromium Activity page backed by the registered Gateway handler and SQLite, the March 1 bar counted the session. Across 12 more cases, all four spring-forward charts in New York and Lord Howe counted all seven eligible sessions. The eight fall and ordinary cases retained their bar labels, counts, and accessible descriptions.
- Twelve comparisons preserved every 24-hour and monthly boundary. Formatting and scoped type-aware lint passed for both changed files. The hosted Activity test file passed all three cases. [Hosted UI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45684969398/job/139456204155)

### Activity page before and after

Both captures use **Last 7 days** at 12:15 a.m. on March 9, 2026 in New York. The only session, “Notebook witness,” was last active at 11:40 p.m. on March 1.

**Before** · The list and summary count the session. The chart starts on March 2 and says “No recorded activity in this period.”

![Before the fix, the March 1 session appears below an empty Activity chart.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad94f14a-fc8a-4629-b32d-b860d0f2a81e)

**After** · The same list row and summary remain visible. The chart now starts on March 1 with a bar labeled 1.

![After the fix, the first bar counts one session on March 1 and the matching session is visible below.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e605305-abe8-46f0-91ec-d856613ad7b0)

Chromium rendered the built `/activity` page at the same viewport and clock for both captures. The before capture used `bf3729e4`, whose Activity source matches the PR parent. The after capture used the reviewed tree in `7d005205`. An isolated test transport passed the page’s `sessions.list` request to the registered Gateway handler at `b6e7fcfb`, backed by real SQLite and synthetic session data.

On `7d005205`, all three Activity window tests passed, including spring forward in New York and Lord Howe. The run finished red. Its dependency check reported the same six path/symbol pairs as scheduled main, and its Incognito browser case reached the same 240-second timeout as scheduled main. Both real-Gateway jobs built the runtime and Control UI artifacts successfully. prs.title: fix: deep_research hides why a search or model call failed
prs.body:
Closes #205501

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a `deep_research` search or model call fails on the portable engine, the result's gaps say only `Search unavailable: <query>` or `The model did not produce a complete response.` A timeout, an authorization refusal and a missing runtime look identical, so operators and automation can't tell whether a retry would help.

## User Impact

User impact: the gap now names the failure, for example `The model did not produce a complete response (LLM_COMPLETION_TIMEOUT).` or `Search unavailable: <query> (TimeoutError)`. The rest of the wording is unchanged, and error messages stay out of the report.

## Why This Change Was Made

The search and model `catch` blocks dropped the error, while the fetch path already appended the error's name. One formatter now labels all three gap types with the error's code when it has a string code, or its name otherwise. The code matters for model calls: the LLM runtime throws `LlmCompleteError` for its failures and puts the reason in `code` (`LLM_COMPLETION_TIMEOUT`, `LLM_COMPLETION_NOT_AUTHORIZED`, `LLM_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE`, ...). Messages stay out because they can carry provider or page text into the report. A fetch error that has a code now shows the code instead of the name.

Not included: the issue's `diagnostics` array, a new result field that needs a maintainer decision. Failures that `portable-tool.ts` raises itself (a model `stopReason` of `error`, `aborted` or `length`, or a `tools.invoke` response that is not `ok`) are plain errors and still read `(Error)`.

## Evidence

- New test in `extensions/deep-research/src/portable.test.ts`: a search rejected with a `TimeoutError` leaves `Search unavailable: river length (TimeoutError)`, and a model call rejected with an `LlmCompleteError` coded `LLM_COMPLETION_TIMEOUT` leaves `The model did not produce a complete response (LLM_COMPLETION_TIMEOUT).`; neither gap copies the error message. On the base commit it fails at the search gap, which carries no error.
- `pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `portable.test.ts` (20/20) and `tool.test.ts` (6/6) passes, about 30 seconds wall time locally.
- oxlint and the format check pass on the two changed files.
- Not run: targeted typecheck (`tsgo` is not installed in this checkout) and a live `deep_research` run (needs a model and a search provider). Broad checks are left to PR CI.
