prs.title: feat(voice-call): ask whether the caller is still there before hanging up for silence
prs.body:
Closes #205512

## What Problem This Solves

`realtime.idleHangupMs` ends a phone call as soon as the line has been quiet for that long, without a word. Callers who pause, step away for a moment, or have their audio drop out are cut off, and the ones still listening hear the line go dead.

## User Impact

With `realtime.idleCheckIn: true`, the first silence gets "Hello? Are you still there?" from the realtime model, in the caller's language, instead of a hangup. Continued silence gets a short goodbye, and the call ends once it has played, after a pause of three seconds for a reply. A caller who answers the check-in, or speaks up over the goodbye, keeps the call. It is off by default; without the setting, idle hangups work as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model cannot act on silence by itself, because no turn starts when nobody speaks, so the call prompts it at the speech-idle timeout. The check-in and goodbye are given to the model word for word, since realtime models asked for "a goodbye" tend to narrate the request instead. Both are normal model turns, so a caller who speaks up is heard and answered through the usual turn handling. Only speech detected from the caller re-arms the check-in; any sound still keeps the call alive, as before. Check-ins are capped at three per call and kept goodbyes at two, which bounds loops from echo or line noise, and a goodbye that never finishes playing is abandoned after 10 seconds. The logic lives in `realtime-idle-check-in.ts`; the call handler only passes its realtime config to playback and tags caller speech, so it does not grow.

## Evidence

- Live, on a larger build: a local version of this check-in has run since Nov 22 on a production Telnyx line (OpenAI realtime), on a 2026.11.6 source build with other local voice patches. That version speaks the goodbye as host speech and detects talk-over from audio levels; this PR uses normal model turns and the provider's speech events instead, and has not itself been run on a live call. From that line's gateway log since Nov 22, one call went quiet: the assistant checked in, the caller spoke again, the next silence got a second check-in, and when that one went unanswered the assistant said goodbye and the call ended. No caller has spoken up over an idle goodbye there yet, so that path has unit and handler test coverage only.

  ```
  2026-11-23T18:05:13.589+00:00 [voice-call] Realtime speech idle check-in callId=686475c6... providerCallId=<redacted> timeoutMs=8000
  2026-11-23T18:05:46.440+00:00 [voice-call] Realtime speech idle check-in callId=686475c6... providerCallId=<redacted> timeoutMs=8000
  2026-11-23T18:05:55.742+00:00 [voice-call] Realtime speech idle timeout callId=686475c6... providerCallId=<redacted> timeoutMs=8000
  ```

- Focused tests: `realtime-idle-check-in.test.ts` (check-in first, then the goodbye and a pause before the hangup; re-arming after caller speech, three times per call; talk-over during the goodbye and the pause after it; at most two kept goodbyes; a goodbye that never plays or never ends; no bridge; a call that closes) and two call-level tests in `realtime-call-control.test.ts` (check-in, goodbye and hangup on a live handler; a caller speaking up over the goodbye keeps the call). Four deliberate breakages of the module (no pause, no talk-over, no re-arm, no cap) each fail these tests.
- `pnpm test` on `realtime-idle-check-in.test.ts`, `realtime-call-control.test.ts`, `realtime-call-session-control.test.ts` and `config.test.ts`: 99 passed. Typechecks, oxlint, oxfmt, `config:docs:check`, `check:line-cap-ratchet` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` pass.
- Not exercised: providers other than OpenAI realtime. Providers without speech start events rely on caller transcripts here, so a caller speaking up over the goodbye is noticed a little later.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(android): keep inline code in markdown plain-text extraction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android chat renders remote Markdown images as plain alt text (no image fetching on this path). `buildPlainText` in `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/chat/ChatMarkdown.kt` handled `Text` and line-break nodes but fell through to the generic `else` branch for the leaf `Code` node, which recurses into `firstChild` — always `null` for a commonmark `Code` node — so inline-code literals were silently dropped.

Concretely, an alt like `![Open **`setup.json`** now](https://example.com/diagram.png)` rendered as "Open  now", and a code-only alt produced an empty string, falling back to the generic `image` label.

@saariuslystoned reported the dropped code literals and supplied the original one-line fix in [the Android issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/196086).

Fixes #196086

## Solution

Append the `Code` node's `literal` directly in `buildPlainText`, matching how the rendering path (`appendInlineNode`'s `is Code` branch) already handles inline code. The `org.commonmark.node.Code` import was already present.

## Impact

Inline-code literals in remote-image alt text now appear in the rendered placeholder text, including code-only alts which previously degraded to the generic `image` fallback. No other plain-text consumers change behavior: every non-leaf node still recurses as before.

## Evidence

### Before / after (Android chat, production markdown pipeline)

Captured on a local Android 16 (API 36) emulator from the app's built-in screenshot fixture mode (`openclaw.screenshotScene chat`, no Gateway or credentials involved). The fixture chat was temporarily extended with the two labels from the linked issue on both builds; that local scaffolding is not part of this PR. Both screenshots show the same seeded message rendered through the real `ChatMarkdown` pipeline:

![Before (main): label reads "Open  now" and the code-only alt falls back to "image"](https://github.com/Heetisk/openclaw/raw/proof/196086-screenshots/proof-before.png)

![After (this PR): label reads "Open setup.json now" and the code-only alt shows "config.yml"](https://github.com/Heetisk/openclaw/raw/proof/196086-screenshots/proof-after.png)

- Before: mixed label reads "Open  now" (inline code dropped); code-only alt falls back to the generic "image".
- After: mixed label reads "Open setup.json now"; code-only alt shows "config.yml".
- Both builds otherwise identical (`origin/main` + the same local fixture vs. this branch + the same fixture).

### Tests and CI

- Two focused regressions in `ChatMarkdownTest` exercise the user-visible path from the issue (`buildChatInlineMarkdown` → `appendInlineNode` → `MarkdownImage` → `buildPlainText`):
  - `imageAltTextKeepsInlineCodeLiteral`: mixed bold + inline-code alt extracts `Open setup.json now`.
  - `imageAltTextKeepsCodeOnlyFallback`: code-only alt extracts `setup.json` instead of falling back to `image`.
- CI green on head `1e79292b4`: `android-test-play` (runs these regressions), `android-ktlint`, `android-test-third-party`, both `android-access-native` lanes, `native-i18n`, `security-fast`, and `PR context and evidence`.

prs.title: fix(ios): keep reminder due times aligned with alarms when clocks turn back
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a clock turns back, the same local time occurs twice. If a caller scheduled a reminder for the later occurrence with an explicit UTC offset, the iOS reminder and its returned `dueISO` could show the earlier instant. Its absolute alarm still pointed to the requested time.

## User Impact

A reminder scheduled for the second occurrence with a whole-second ISO timestamp keeps its local date and time, and its start, due time and alarm agree on the requested instant. This applies to both hour-long and half-hour clock changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The service reconstructs the date from its Gregorian components. If the named time zone selects a different UTC offset, the service records the offset at the requested instant on those components. Ordinary dates retain their time zone. This builds on the absolute-alarm support contributed by xialonglee. [Original reminder alarm PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106376)

## Evidence

- With the parent service, the native regression found the start, due and returned time one hour early in New York and 30 minutes early on Lord Howe Island. The absolute alarms were correct in both cases.
- All five Swift Testing tests passed against the updated service, including four repeated-time inputs and three fixed-offset or named-zone controls. A check that pinned every offset failed both spring zone-identity controls.
- With unsaved Apple EventKit objects on macOS, all 568 scheduled cases using whole-second ISO timestamps with an explicit offset preserved their wall fields, start and due instants, serialized due time and absolute alarm. Four unscheduled inputs stayed unscheduled, and malformed input was rejected.
- A separate unsaved EventKit replay matched all 10 scheduled cases across New York, Lord Howe, Dublin and Chatham, including inputs supplied at +05:45. An omitted due date stayed unscheduled.
- The service and tests typechecked for arm64 iOS 18 with the iOS 27.2 SDK. SwiftLint reported zero violations in the two changed files. Local SwiftFormat 0.63.1 was unavailable. Saving to a reminder store and notification delivery on a device were outside this proof.

## User Impact

Each option has a single-line title beside its icon and a single-line hint directly below the title. Long text truncates rather than expanding the row. The selection check stays on the title line. Browse folders is unchanged.

The project picker reserves one text column for both labels; it does not change font sizes, project discovery, or the Sessions sidebar. Full strings remain in the accessible option text.

prs.title: fix: show recovery guidance for interrupted conversation startup
prs.body:
## Problem

Interrupted conversation startup showed raw harness/worktree failures without telling the user how to recover. Restoring history could lose the curated notice or expose a nested operator diagnostic.

## Changes

- Integrate main `ba6d94ec17712`, retaining current Toast, feedback, host-update, desktop-summary and failure-provenance owners; do not restore the retired inline banner or obsolete failed-edit actions.
- Recognize the actual Codex missing-thread and managed-worktree lease-loss producer errors, including lease loss without optional details. Show concise recovery guidance with the existing expandable details and copy action.
- For a missing saved conversation, explain that a new conversation is needed; never offer a retry into the same missing conversation or reuse the unrelated machine-update action. Messaging-channel replies retain the explicit `/new` recovery command.
- Persist only a closed startup diagnostic category in chat history, not the formatted nested cause chain. Preserve existing notice metadata and idempotent projection. Raw errors remain in operator diagnostics.

## Validation

- Original startup cases, optional lease suffix, private nested cause, metadata/idempotence, lazy notice mount and wrong retry-action regressions reproduced before their corrections.
- Focused real SQLite history, producer-copy and rendered notice tests pass. 291 core/history and 101 UI consumer cases pass; 55 producer/channel cases pass after the final channel-copy correction.
- Seven actual bundled Control UI browser cases pass, including desktop/mobile layout, restored history and correct missing-conversation controls. Synthetic Gateway fixtures supply errors; this is not a live-provider claim.
- Qualified core/UI type-aware lint, UI typecheck, controller guard, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Personally inspected sibling Codex `092d3acd6bec`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs:2870-2916`, for the actual missing-thread errors. No protocol/dependency changes.

Current-head CI remains the broad gate. Fresh local review findings were addressed, including restoring the explicit channel recovery command (red before the correction, green afterward). A current live-provider/Gateway startup failure was not exercised; the bundled-browser proof uses synthetic error fixtures.

## Visual evidence

The real bundled Control UI uses the same synthetic error fixture, light theme and 1280×900 viewport. Before: main `ba6d94ec17712`; after: `3afe1b1415901`. Identical 1280×800 crops omit the unrelated model-selector footer. The clean comparison comes first; annotation copies explain the same frames.

prs.title: fix: idle Gateway burns CPU scanning folders a shallow memory extraPaths pattern can never match
prs.body:
Root cause: extensions/memory-core/src/memory/watch-policy.ts:127 gives every `extraPaths` tree scope watch depth 128. Under Bun, fs-safe always polls, so every pass stats the whole tree, even when the entry's pattern can only match a few levels down.

Related #205462. This fixes that issue's traversal and CPU part. Its other two asks have different causes and stay open there: the fallback log has no reason because fs-safe's Bun check reports none, and heap growth across passes was not reproduced on current main.

Thanks @brandonperfetti for the detailed report and measurements, and @Israel-Kli for the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway running under Bun, such as the macOS app's Gateway, keeps working while idle when `memory.search.extraPaths` points a shallow pattern like `*/MASTER-PRIORITY-DOCUMENT.md` at a folder with a deep tree. Every 30 s polling pass walks every descendant, although the pattern can only match files two levels down.

## Fix

The memory watch policy now derives the watch depth from the pattern's segment count. It applies the same conservative rule the pattern matcher already uses: patterns with `**`, braces, brackets, parentheses, or `.`/`..` segments keep the full depth. Polling therefore stops at the deepest level a pattern can match. Indexed files are unchanged. The memory config docs no longer say that patterns never narrow the watched tree.

## Evidence

Real Gateway under Bun 1.4.5 in Docker, with isolated state. The fixture has 24,440 directories and 60,041 files, with 40 matching files at depth 2. The Gateway sat idle for 120 s with runs in ABAB order. Full output: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205478#issuecomment-7172955528

| | base b22df8b94835 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway CPU, 2 runs each | 3.13%, 3.86% | 2.13%, 2.06% (idle floor) |
| Directories stat'ed per pass | 24,442 | 442 |
| Filesystem syscalls per pass | 108,931 | 530 |
| Gateway RSS | ~1.53-1.60 GB | ~1.34-1.41 GB |
| Indexed files | 40 | 40 (identical paths) |

Controls:
- `**/MASTER-PRIORITY-DOCUMENT.md` still walks all 24,442 directories on this PR and indexes the same 41 files as base.
- A new `projnew/MASTER-PRIORITY-DOCUMENT.md` created while the Gateway was idle was found by `memory.search` on both sides.

Tests: the watch-policy, file-watcher filter/lifecycle, manager watcher filesystem and local file-watcher integration suites pass 39/39. The new depth test fails on base (`expected 128 to be 2`).

## Merge danger

Two-way door. Only the polling depth of patterned extra paths changes; nothing is stored or migrated, and a revert restores the full walk. Blast radius: memory watching of `extraPaths` entries with simple patterns.

prs.title: fix(plugin-sdk): install the mirror write assertion on the resolved transcript target
prs.body:
## Repair sweep — 2026-11-25

Rebased the repair onto main `ba6d94ec17712`. The mirror assertion is installed after agent inference, before reserving a transcript writer. The original admitted locator and callback are captured synchronously, and the existing transcript owner verifies the resolved target against the original session key, ID, store and storage environment; inferring an omitted agent must not authorize another transcript.

Current proof:
- Nine SDK owner tests pass against real isolated SQLite: the allowed omitted-agent write persists, captured caller options remain stable, conflicting session/store targets are refused before entering the writer, and revoked or foreign ownership leaves no assistant row. Each newly found key/store/captured-options regression was reproduced before fixing it, including relative-path capture across a working-directory change and non-concrete `(multiple)` selectors.
- Ten actual native Codex settled-turn finalizer cases pass through the compiled worker boundary and persist authorized final answers; the original finalizer failure was reproduced on main.
- Touched files pass qualified type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks. Fresh whole-range local ClawSweeper review at `d1b45f26bf84e` has no findings.
- Personally inspected sibling Codex `092d3acd6bec3e3a14bdc7e7a2810ab628ab759d`, including `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs:530-610`; no Codex dependency or protocol change.

The SDK negative owner cases and native finalizer success cases are distinct proof; this does not claim a current live-provider/channel run. CI on the pushed head remains the broad gate.

---

## Original proposal and historical evidence

## What Problem This Solves

#169343 (43584d99) introduced a regression: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/settled-turn-finalizer.native.test.ts` fails 4/9 on `main` ("persists a host-authorized summary with the actual native selection …"). The settled-turn summary mirror is refused with `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError`, so stock Codex settled-turn summaries are not persisted.

## Why This Change Was Made

#169343 moved the codex mirror's composed write assertion from per-append preparation to a write-level owner assertion, which fixed the Linux steering-settlement deadlock. However, it installed that assertion through `withSessionTranscriptWriteAssertion` on the caller's **unresolved** transcript target. The locked write then compares the installed context against the **resolved** owner scope (`storageTarget` from `resolveSessionTranscriptRuntimeTarget`). When the two differ, `assertTranscriptWriteContext` refuses the commit as a rebound writer claim; here the fields that can differ are `agentId`, `sessionId` and the store binding.

Fix: install the assertion inside `withProjectedSessionTranscriptWriteLock`, after it resolves the storage target, on exactly the `boundScope` it locks. The ordering property from #169343 is preserved: the assertion is still prepared before the writer is reserved. `withCodexSessionTranscriptMirrorWrite` goes back to a plain pass-through, and `assertCurrent` is now an optional field of `InternalSessionTranscriptWriteLockParams`.

Production LOC: +20/-19.

## User Impact

Stock Codex settled-turn summaries persist again on current `main`. The Linux steering deadlock fix from #169343 remains in place.

## Evidence

- `settled-turn-finalizer.native.test.ts`:
  - 9/9 at 43584d99^ (before #169343);
  - 4 failed / 5 passed at 43584d99 and on current `main`;
  - 9/9 with this change.
- `pnpm test` on this branch passes for `settled-turn-finalizer.native`, `run-attempt.steering-settlement`, `transcript-mirror`, `transcript-mirror.user-idempotency`, `transcript-mirror.visibility` and `run-attempt.steering`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` is clean.
- Linux proof on decfedd3 (CI run 38190752080, job `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-2`, Ubuntu runner, real SQLite `extension-database-workers` project): `settled-turn-finalizer.native.test.ts` 9/9 and `run-attempt.steering-settlement.test.ts` pass, so the #169343 deadlock fix still holds on Linux. A Blacksmith Testbox rerun (`tbx_01m4ptfke8wabpy1sd4a7c66c6`) never got capacity and timed out after 15m in `queued`, so CI is the Linux proof.
- Authority boundary at final persistence: new `src/plugin-sdk/codex-session-transcript-runtime.write-assertion.test.ts` runs against a real SQLite session store. It uses a locator without `agentId`, which is the finalizer shape.
  - **Resolved target persists:** the row commits.
  - **Mid-await revocation:** `assertCurrent` starts throwing after an awaited `readMessageFacts`. The append rejects with the revocation error and no row persists.
  - **Foreign ambient owner:** the write runs inside an owned write context for a different session. It rejects with `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError` and no row persists.
  - Against the pre-fix code, the first two cases fail with `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError` (the regression) and the foreign-owner case still passes. Binding to the resolved target therefore keeps the foreign-owner refusal and the commit-time revocation check.
- `checks-node-changed` failure (`test/embedded-transcript-cursor.e2e.test.ts` › "resumes a public raw cursor across /new and the next Gateway turn", `generation_mismatch`) is inherited. It fails the same way locally on the untouched merge base `f92690e1` without this change. This PR does not touch cursor or `/new` code.

## Current State (2026-10-12)

- Head `65e1341735a`. ClawSweeper: gold shrimp, no findings, nothing under "Before merge".
- Blocked: `checks-node-changed` selects `test/embedded-transcript-cursor.e2e.test.ts`, which fails on current main, and CI fail-fast then cancels the rest of the run.
  - A local bisect points to #169237 (`56d559212a0`). Its per-turn `captureModelPromptProjection` rewrite rotates the transcript generation, so raw-delta cursors reset (`generation_mismatch`).
  - Owner question posted: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169237#issuecomment-6118099447
- Next step: once main's cursor regression is resolved, merge main, confirm CI is green, then land via `scripts/pr`. #168401 depends on this landing first.

## Latest CI repair

CI follow-up: corrected the mutable assertion fixture’s inferred `never` return to its intended `void` contract. All 9 mirror assertion cases, the exact Plugin SDK test type graph, formatting, and type-aware lint pass. New-head CI pending.

prs.title: fix(exec): handle unsupported shell control characters consistently
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On POSIX hosts, an operator’s exec allowlist could approve a different set of commands from the ones the shell would actually run. The shared parser now checks where each ambiguous control byte occurs. The exec guard enforces the result before dispatch, and ordinary POSIX commands can still pass verified quoted bytes as data. Related issue #168133 covers the POSIX parser discrepancy.

## What was wrong

1. The parser in `src/infra/command-explainer` could return a complete-looking command list for text that the destination shell interprets differently. The allowlist could consequently approve an incomplete set of commands.
2. The exec guard in `src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.ts` discarded recovered commands after an incomplete parse. Its fallback could miss a protected operation.
3. Node dispatch in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.ts` needs the destination platform to interpret line endings. Local inspection alone could reject normal Windows CRLF input.

## Why this design

- Require a complete simple POSIX command before treating raw carriage returns, vertical tabs, or form feeds as argument data. Check every byte against the original source spans of literal arguments, including the gaps the parser can omit. Apply the same check to decoded POSIX wrapper commands.
- Keep this exception specific to POSIX. Windows callers use the existing destination-specific CRLF handling.
- Inspect recovered commands for protected operations. Automatic allowlist authorization still requires a complete parse.
- Distinguish unsupported input, parser work limits, and startup errors so operators know whether to edit the command or repair the installation.
- Apply destination-specific CRLF handling to the inspection copy. Pass the original command to the executor.

## Related changes

| Change | Responsibility | How it fits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #164775 | Earlier proposal for POSIX shell input | Closed in favor of #168133. The shared parser verifies literal arguments at their original source locations. It only inspects nested text as a command when the wrapper analysis identifies it as such. |
| #199590 | Replaced script-content preflight refusals with approval facts | Included in the base. The tests use the current launch-preparation fixture and retain checks for the node handoff and native Windows line endings. |
| #202177 | Preserves foreground command output | Included in the base. The ordinary-command regression checks the exact working directory output, including its trailing newline. |

## Evidence

| Path | Revision and observed effect |
| --- | --- |
| POSIX Gateway allowlist, approvals off | On Linux an allowlisted executable created two files whose names contained a carriage return, vertical tab, and form feed. Exact filename lookups succeeded for single and double quotes, including Unicode before the controls. The integration test also checked for exactly one process launch. |
| Guard and node dispatch | The guard rejected unverified control bytes, including in decoded command text. The POSIX check accepted a decoded simple command with a verified literal argument. The Windows guard rejected raw controls in quotes. |
| Node handoff and native Windows | The Linux handoff test reached the selected node. The [earlier native Windows job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42857710718) covered CRLF execution on `8aebd33`. |
| Fresh installed Gateway, Linux | Built and packed `aebf9d60980`, installed the local tarball into an empty directory, and configured the allowlist with approvals off. A Gateway agent created both exact quoted filenames. A second turn rejected a trailing raw carriage return and created no file. |
| Replacement of published v2026.11.10, Linux | The published Gateway at `6ea542f` created the same quoted filenames. Replaced the package with the candidate in that installation and reused its populated state. The candidate preserved both quoted filenames, refused the adjacent ambiguous command, and retained the same approval settings after shutdown. |
| Earlier Gateway with a live model, and packaged installs | The [earlier verification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194350#issuecomment-6754368106) records ordinary commands executing, unsafe input stopping before a marker was created, and approval settings surviving package replacement. Package tests used a local mock model. |

The installed tests used the Gateway agent RPC and a loopback scripted model to request exact commands and capture the tool result. Each positive turn passed raw CR, VT and FF in single- and double-quoted filenames to the allowlisted `/usr/bin/touch`. The adjacent refusal used the same executable with a raw CR immediately after a closing quote. The harness checked the filenames on disk and read the saved policy through the CLI before and after each Gateway run.

Redacted output from the two candidate installations:

```text
Fresh       OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (aebf9d6)
            Both exact filenames present. Argument data UTF-8 hex c3a9f09fa69e610d620b630c64
            Tool returned unsupported-control error. No denied filename created.
            Saved policy after shutdown: allowlist, ask off, fallback deny, /usr/bin/touch
Replacement OpenClaw 2026.11.10 (6ea542f) -> 2026.11.10 (aebf9d6)
            Both exact filenames present. Argument data UTF-8 hex c3a9f09fa69e610d620b630c64
            Tool returned unsupported-control error. No denied filename created.
            Saved policy after shutdown: allowlist, ask off, fallback deny, /usr/bin/touch
```

The candidate tarball passed the package integrity check. Its SHA-256 was `a72c37558a4eb9345d1281c2a291708b2b2257709a9c5caba8d32edb1ae8a47a`. The replacement used a local package install over the published release.

## Caller upgrade contract

On POSIX, simple single- and double-quoted literal arguments can carry carriage returns, vertical tabs, and form feeds. Input containing those bytes in ambiguous syntax, expansions, or compound commands is refused before approval or launch, including in full mode. Convert CRLF scripts to LF or express those bytes as escapes. Windows accepts native CRLF line endings. Oversized input, excessive nesting, and inspection deadlines stop execution in every mode. Split large commands or put the content in a script. After a parser startup failure, the next call retries initialization.

## Decisions for maintainers

1. Exec owners should review the compatibility boundary for full-mode callers and scripts that contain raw control characters outside simple literal arguments.
2. Windows exec owners retain responsibility for PowerShell and CMD continuation grammar.

## Testing

On Linux at `aebf9d60980` all eight affected files passed, with 186 tests passed and two platform-specific skips. The pre-PR base passed the same allowlisted filename check. The previous PR head rejected a benign quoted argument before spawn. The revised head preserved the exact filenames through the Gateway allowlist with approvals off.

The test-line budget checks 419 net new lines. A 19-line allocation covers process-level proof through the real allowlist and the guard cases that distinguish quoted data, unverified POSIX text, and Windows input. Core TypeScript, targeted lint and format, docs MDX, [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45699921762) and the [required security check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45701870136) passed. Prior live-model and native Windows evidence is linked above with its revision.

prs.title: fix(sessions): unclear recovery after missing checkouts or runtime disconnects
prs.body:
## Problem

A session whose managed checkout disappeared failed later with unclear runtime errors. Recovery also needs to settle stale accepted publication receipts without attempting Git in a missing directory.

## Changes

- Integrate current main while retaining its worktree registry and shared publication owners.
- Refuse a new agent run before bootstrap when its checkout is missing, with recovery guidance; do not silently recreate it.
- Let accepted publication receipts settle stale session/workspace bindings using registry custody even when the checkout is gone.
- Keep a still-current publication pending until its checkout is restored, preserving its receipt and idempotency key. Review caught and corrected an unintended terminal-failure regression here.
- Keep exclusive creation leases separate from shared existing-worktree run leases.

## Validation

- Missing-checkout agent/bootstrap regressions and 23 worktree run-lease cases pass.
- Prior final publication consumer run: 59 cases passed. After the final review correction, 56 existing publication cases passed; the new current-binding missing-checkout regression failed red (receipt became failed), then passed with restoration/recovery. All four stale-binding variants pass alongside it.
- Canonical type-aware owner lint, formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Fresh local review findings addressed. Current-head CI remains the broad gate.

## Limits

The publication boundary uses real SQLite custody with synthetic Git/GitHub transport; it is not a credentialed live GitHub publication proof. No live Gateway or shared checkout was modified.

prs.title: fix: keep the chosen runtime visible beside the model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two choices for the same long model pushed their runtime onto another line. The closed fallback picker also grew taller after saving.

## User Impact

OpenClaw and Codex stay visible beside the model, with the account on its own line in the menu. Inspect the label to read the full model name.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model name gives up space before the runtime. Both the open option and the saved selection use the same label.

## Evidence

At 390 px the option title fell from 37 to 19 px. At four viewport sizes, the two runtime labels fit and selecting Codex saved the mock fallback and showed Codex on the closed picker. prs.title: fix(agents): continue a malformed tool call after a consumed tool failure
prs.body:
Root cause: src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn-recovery.ts:465 treats a retained tool error as consumed only when `executionStarted === false` (and :484 also requires a not_started receipt on every failure), so a tool that ran and returned an error keeps vetoing the single continuation for a later tool call rejected before dispatch, although the model already read that failure.

Fixes #199537

Thanks @jaxonparrott for the production report and source trace, and @akushonkamen for the original fix.

## What Problem This Solves

A tool runs and returns an error, the model reads it and makes its next tool call, and that call streams malformed JSON arguments. The call is rejected before it runs, and the turn ends with "couldn't finish this reply" instead of getting the one continuation every other rejected call gets. In the reported cron run this threw away 13.5 minutes and 4.7M tokens.

## User Impact

The turn continues once and the model can re-issue its call or answer. Completed tools are not repeated. Failures the model has not seen (no result yet, a result after the rejected response, a prior turn, or a different tool), unfinished or asynchronous work, and the one-continuation budget still block, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The continuation replays nothing: the rejected call never ran, and the earlier failure already sits in the transcript before the rejected response. Whether that failed tool had started does not change what the continuation does, so the started/not-started split only blocked recovery. The retained error now counts as consumed when its failed result is the latest failure in the current turn, precedes the rejected response, and names the retained tool.

This keeps @akushonkamen's commits and reconciles them with the transcript check main gained in #170615: the settled-batch exemption from the original commit is superseded by that check, and the executed-failure cases join the existing rejected-call test table. `docs/concepts/agent-loop.md` describes the new boundary. No new model-facing text. Production lines: +5/-14.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway from source (`ocx src`) on main vs this branch, local Anthropic Messages fixture: an `edit` call that runs and returns an error, then a `write` call with truncated JSON arguments.

- Chat turn: main ends "Your request couldn't be completed." with no continuation request; this branch sends one continuation and the model answers. The failed `edit` is not repeated.
- Scheduled run (with #201117, which removes the separate optional-reply suppression): main ends `status=error`; with both fixes the run ends `status=ok` after one continuation.
- A model that keeps sending malformed calls: one continuation ("retrying 1/1"), then the turn fails as before.
- Controls with a successful tool before the malformed call: unchanged.
- Regressions `continues after consumed tool failures (started | unknown | earlier started)` fail on main and pass here; the negative table (missing, unconsumed, prior-turn, different tool, active, async) still passes.

Proof log: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/170846#issuecomment-6978399870

Merge danger: two-way door; a revert restores the started-failure veto. No config, schema or state change. Blast radius: turns whose last model response was a tool call rejected before dispatch after an earlier tool error in the same turn.

prs.title: docs: show how to test roles locally with a same-host proxy
prs.body:
Closes #202751

## What Problem This Solves

Someone evaluating multiplayer roles on one machine has no documented way to give test accounts their own sign-in. Token and password auth sign everyone in as the shared owner, which cannot hold a role, and the trusted-proxy pages assume a real identity provider. Two details also trip up a same-host setup: the Gateway rejects a loopback client address from a proxy, and a role only caps scopes, so an account without an `identityScopes` grant connects with none.

## User Impact

Operators can try roles locally with a short, tested recipe, and the recipe states plainly that this setup lets any local process act as any allowed account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The new "Test roles locally" section in the multiplayer quick setup uses only existing settings: trusted-proxy auth with `allowLoopback`, `allowUsers`, `identityScopes`, `gateway.roles`, the local Gateway password for maintenance commands, and `users.setRole` by profile ID after each first sign-in. The proxy example is a Caddy basic-auth site that overwrites `X-Forwarded-User` and sends a fixed documentation address (`192.0.2.10`) as the client address. The warning repeats the `allowLoopback` risk from the trusted-proxy page in this context, and lists how to keep the test narrow.

## Evidence

The recipe was run on OpenClaw 2026.11.5 (d119c6b) on macOS with Caddy 2.11.9. Ports in the run were 18830 (Gateway) and 18831 (Caddy) instead of the 18789 and 8080 in the docs; nothing else differs.

- The Gateway config from the recipe passes `openclaw config validate` (`"valid":true,"warnings":[]`). The Caddyfile passes `caddy validate`.
- First sign-in creates each profile with the default role. `users.setRole` by profile ID then assigns `administrator` and `member`; by email it is refused.
- After reconnecting, Alice has `operator.admin`, Bob has `operator.read` and `operator.write`, and Bob is denied an administrator method.
- Through the proxy without credentials: HTTP 401. Bob sending his own `X-Forwarded-User: alice@example.test` through the proxy still connects as Bob.
- A local client that skips the proxy and sends forged headers straight to the Gateway port connects with `operator.admin`. This is the behavior the warning describes.
- `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` (the new JSON5 block is schema-checked) and `pnpm check:changed` pass. `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` finds no broken link in `docs/start/multiplayer.md`; it reports 7 broken links elsewhere that are already present on `main`.
- Local review: ClawSweeper `review --local-range` against `origin/main` at head 6262add, `review_status: complete`, checkout access verified. Overall B, patch B, proof not applicable (docs only). No findings; security cleared ("describes an existing opt-in loopback trust mode with an accurate impersonation warning").

<details>
<summary>Runtime output (2026.11.5, credentials not printed)</summary>

```text
=== 1. First sign-in through Caddy (creates each profile)
[alice] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.sessions.read"]
[bob] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.sessions.read"]
=== 2. Profiles after first sign-in
alice@example.test id=219e263c-... role=- effectiveRole=viewer roleSource=default
bob@example.test id=4f383f74-... role=- effectiveRole=viewer roleSource=default
=== 3. Assign roles by profile id
alice -> administrator: ok
bob -> member: ok
--- users.setRole with an email instead of a profile id:
invalid users.setRole params: must have required property 'profileId'; at root: unexpected property 'email'
=== 4. Reconnect
[alice] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.admin"]
[alice] exec.approvals.get -> OK
[bob] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.read","operator.write"]
[bob] exec.approvals.get -> DENIED {"code":"FORBIDDEN","message":"missing scope: operator.admin",...}
=== 5. Spoofing checks
[anon] HTTP 401
[bob-forging] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.read","operator.write"]
[direct-forged] connected method=trusted-proxy role=operator scopes=["operator.admin"]
[direct-forged] exec.approvals.get -> OK
```

</details>

Not checked: signing in from a real browser. The run used a CLI-mode client without a device identity. The recipe links to the existing Control UI pairing section for the browser device step instead of describing it.

prs.title: fix: stop doctor asking for skill_workshop in tools.allow when the plugin is disabled
prs.body:
Closes #205371

## What Problem This Solves

When `plugins.entries.skill-workshop.enabled` is `false` and `tools.allow` is a finite list without `skill_workshop`, `openclaw doctor` still lists a "Fix now" item telling the user to add `skill_workshop` to `tools.allow`. Following it would widen the tool allowlist for a plugin the user turned off on purpose.

## User Impact

Doctor no longer reports Skill Workshop tool-policy findings for a disabled plugin entry, and a minimal `{ enabled: false }` entry stays warning-free. No config change or migration is needed. Findings for an enabled plugin are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Skill Workshop doctor check only read `autonomous.mode`, which defaults to `auto`, so an absent setting counted as "Workshop on". The check now also treats an explicitly disabled plugin entry as off, using the same gate that already suppresses the other findings when `autonomous.mode` is `off`.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test with `plugins.entries["skill-workshop"].enabled: false` and `tools.allow: ["read"]`. On the base commit it failed with the `tools.allow does not include "skill_workshop"` finding; with the fix it passes.
- `pnpm test extensions/skill-workshop/doctor-health-api.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 6 passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed; `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the two changed files are clean.
- I ran `openclaw doctor` end to end from source; see "Shipped CLI proof" below. `pnpm check:changed` did not complete in my environment (the SQLite worker ratchet and the doctor guard tests were interrupted, unrelated to this change), so I am relying on PR CI for the broader checks.

### Shipped CLI proof

Ran the real CLI entry point (`scripts/run-node.mjs`, the source wrapper behind the `openclaw` binary) on Node 26.12.0, Linux, from a throwaway home so no real state was touched. Before = base commit `7d2b9c37c` (only `extensions/skill-workshop/doctor-health-api.ts` reverted to base), after = this PR head `3b4552d58`. Host paths are shortened to `~`.

Config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, with the `skillWorkshopPlugin` migration marker a post-upgrade config has, so Doctor does not treat the entry as pre-restoration policy):

```json
{
  "meta": { "migrations": { "skillWorkshopPlugin": true } },
  "plugins": { "entries": { "skill-workshop": { "enabled": false } } },
  "tools": { "allow": ["read"] }
}
```

Command (same for all three runs; `enabled` is the only value that changes):

```sh
export HOME=~/oc-home OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=~/oc-home/.openclaw \
  OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=~/oc-home/.openclaw/openclaw.json CI=1
node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --non-interactive
```

**Before (base, `enabled: false`)**: the finding is present.

```text
Fix now:
- gateway.mode is unset; gateway start will be blocked.
  ...
- tools.allow does not include "skill_workshop".
  Location: tools.allow
  Next step: Add "skill_workshop" to tools.allow.
  Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skill-workshop
- Gateway health check failed: ...
```

**After (PR head, `enabled: false`)**: no Skill Workshop finding (`grep -c skill_workshop` on the full output is 0). The `Doctor: Skill Workshop tool policy` check still runs.

```text
Doctor: Skill Workshop tool policy
...
Fix now:
- gateway.mode is unset; gateway start will be blocked.
  ...
- Gateway health check failed: ...
Doctor: maintenance release

└  Doctor complete.
```

**After (PR head, `enabled: true`, same `tools.allow`)**: the finding still appears for an enabled plugin.

```text
Fix now:
- gateway.mode is unset; gateway start will be blocked.
  ...
- tools.allow does not include "skill_workshop".
  Location: tools.allow
  Next step: Add "skill_workshop" to tools.allow.
  Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/skill-workshop
- Gateway health check failed: ...
```

The remaining `gateway.mode`, Node patch-level, and gateway-credential lines come from the empty throwaway profile and are unrelated to this change. I did not run a v2026.11.10 to head upgrade.

prs.title: feat(matrix): answer an attachment and the text typed with it as one turn
prs.body:
Related: #161505

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the agent replies to a bare attachment and then separately to the user's question when a Matrix client without caption support (for example Element Web) sends the file and the typed text as two messages.

## User Impact

Operators can set `channels.matrix.mediaHoldMs` (or `accounts.<id>.mediaHoldMs`) so a captionless attachment waits briefly for the sender's next text and both are answered in one turn. Default `0` keeps today's behavior. When enabled, an attachment sent on its own is answered only after the wait (maximum 60 s). A held attachment keeps its place in the durable inbound queue, so a Gateway restart delivers it again instead of dropping it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hold sits between Matrix durable ingress (#176491) and the room message handler. A captionless attachment is buffered in the plugin SDK keyed inbound debouncer (keyed by room and thread); its delivery returns `deferred`, so the attachment keeps its own ingress claim while the room lane stays free for the text. The sender's next plain text joins it and becomes the attachment's caption, the same shape caption-capable clients already send, so existing caption handling produces one turn. The merged turn runs under `fanInChannelIngressLifecycles` of both claims: adoption, deferral, failure and abandonment settle both together, and a turn the handler drops before adoption still consumes both claims. Nothing is re-claimed and nothing is replayed. Any other message in the conversation (another sender, a second attachment, a poll, a location, a reaction), a control command, or the deadline dispatches the held attachment alone first; the debouncer holds the keyed lane until that turn is admitted, so a following `/stop` cannot overtake it. Control commands are recognised with the handler's own normalisation (route, mention patterns, display name) through one shared helper the handler now also uses. Voice messages and captioned attachments are never held. When the monitor closes, held claims are handed back (`onCancelled`) instead of starting turns, and a claim the drain aborts is dropped silently. The setting is Matrix-only, following the triage note that a global queue setting would widen the immediate-media policy to channels that don't need it.

Rebased onto main after #176491. Findings from the first review: the keyed lane is now held through admission (debouncer flush lifecycle); no synthetic replay claim exists any more (each event keeps its durable claim); command normalisation is shared with the handler; polls and locations flush the hold; encrypted double emission and cold-start history no longer reach the hold (ingress deduplicates by event id and skips historical rows before dispatch); the account-level override is bounded like the top-level field.

Second review round (Codex on `92913c1b5a`): an event the server already bundles a replacement for now bypasses the hold like redactions and edits (never folded, never held), and media without `filename` whose body is a single-line file name with an extension (pre-MSC2530 clients, for example `vacation photo.jpg`) is held as captionless; the handler's own caption heuristic is unchanged. Tests added for both. Third round: a reaction's thread is only known after its target is fetched, so a reaction now releases every attachment held in its room before it is dispatched, instead of being keyed at room level; test added. Fourth round: a text joins a held attachment only if its server timestamp is within the hold window of the attachment's (a replay after downtime drains old events back to back); the hold's command check reads the runtime's live config snapshot like normal ingress and uses the canonical `isControlCommandMessage` predicate, so bare abort triggers such as `stop` release the attachment first; tests added. Fifth round: a reaction also waits for attachments already on their way to a turn (flushed but not yet admitted) before it is dispatched, and a claim that cannot be reopened on close is logged rather than left as an unobserved rejection; tests added. Sixth round: the hold is measured from the attachment's server timestamp, so a replay after a restart keeps the original deadline (and an attachment already past it is not held at all) instead of starting a new window; a reaction releases held attachments only when the reaction handler could act on it (it targets one of the bot's own messages), never for a reaction to the held attachment itself or to another user's message; tests added. Seventh round: an attachment replayed after an outage longer than the hold still waits for the companion text that is already queued behind it in the lane (`readLaneBacklog`), so recovery stays one turn; when the reaction target lookup fails, ordering is preserved (the hold is released) rather than skipped; key-verification traffic bypasses the hold like the handler ignores it; the encrypted scenario also asserts no second reply; tests added. Eighth round: the hold reads reaction targets with the handler's own `extractMatrixReactionAnnotation` (a reaction without an explicit `rel_type` is recognised), and the expired-replay companion check applies the same ignored-event predicate as the classifier (edits, bundled replacements, verification traffic, the bot's own events never count as companions); tests added. Ninth round: the hold now uses the reaction handler's own preflight (`resolveMatrixReactionMayStartWork`: approval target, notification mode, target ownership, lookup failure preserves order), and the command check routes by the same effective thread as normal ingress (`resolveMatrixThreadRouting`); tests added.

Tenth round (ClawSweeper on `025c5c3d961`; the ninth-round commit above already covered its reaction-preflight and thread-routing findings): the two recovery cases the earlier body listed as known limits are now handled. (1) Encrypted companions: an expired replayed attachment decrypts queued companion ciphertext through the same local SDK path ingress uses for each delivery (`hydrateEvents`) before it judges it. Ciphertext that cannot be decrypted yet (late room key) still counts when its envelope fits (same sender, within the hold by server time, same thread relation, which stays in clear): the attachment then waits one hold window, and the text is checked again by the normal join rules when the lane delivers it decrypted, so a wrong guess costs at most that bounded wait. (2) Partly admitted catch-up batches: Matrix sync admission now shows each sync batch to the hold (`onSyncBatch`) until every event in it is durable, so an expired attachment that the drain delivers before the rest of its batch is admitted still finds the text that follows it. Nothing in the durable-ingress contract changes: no stored payload, ordering or claim behaviour differs, and nothing runs when `mediaHoldMs` is 0. Also fixed: the previous head's CI failure (`index.test.ts` runtime mock lacked `getOptionalMatrixRuntime`, which the shared reaction preflight's approval-reaction state reads). Tests added for each case, plus two live scenarios (below).

Rebuilt on current main (`ac13a7e0c13`, 2026-10-24) as one commit: main moved the Matrix config UI hints into `config-schema.ts` (the `mediaHoldMs` hint moved with them), inlined the reaction handler's notification mode (now one helper the handler and the hold share), and slimmed the QA scenario contract (`{ details }` executions, no actor cursor bookkeeping); the scenarios follow it.

Eleventh round: rebased on current main (`1f7035c15f3`, 2026-11-07) as one commit, `f31c19123c5`. Main now includes #192585 (`c2cb56c665e`), the core fix for #192522, which is the error the previous evidence recorded for `matrix-media-hold-command-ordering` (`ReplaySafeTranscriptConflictError` when a `/status` arrives while a turn on the same session is still preparing). Nothing in the hold changed since the tenth round. Other changes: the index test runtime mock passes the real module through (`importOriginal`) and overrides only `getMatrixRuntime` / `setMatrixRuntime`, so the mock-exports ratchet accepts it and its baseline entry is pruned; the total test-lines ratchet gets an allocation for the 1049 test lines this change adds (`config/test-lines-allocations/matrix-media-hold.txt`: `media-hold.test.ts`, the ingress sync-batch case, the runtime mock); generated config metadata and docs baseline are regenerated on this base. The command-ordering result on this base is in Evidence: it now passes most runs but still fails intermittently in core, with a different error.

The bound the setting advertises, no attachment waits longer than `mediaHoldMs` past its own server timestamp (or one window after a recovery replay), holds in every case.

Config surface: `channel` count 4003 -> 4005 for the two bounded `mediaHoldMs` fields (top-level and per-account).

## Evidence

Exact head `f31c19123c5`, on main `1f7035c15f3` (2026-11-07), run on a throwaway Linux x86 box.

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-matrix.config.ts extensions/matrix`: 129 files, 1190 tests pass (includes `media-hold.test.ts`, 33 cases).
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/ingress.test.ts`: 5/5.
- `vitest.extension-qa.config.ts` over the scenario catalog, coverage report, scenario selection, live scenario timeouts and the Matrix live-transport units: 53 files, 422 tests pass.
- `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 1f7035c15f3`: all nine pass (max-lines, assertion-safety, database-dialect, timeout-race, mock-exports, test-lines, config-docs, plugin-inventory, database-worker). `pnpm config:channels:check` and `pnpm config:docs:check` clean; `pnpm build` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` clean; oxlint, oxfmt and `pnpm lint:docs` clean; the pre-commit hook ran and passed.
- Data model: nothing stored changes. No ingress payload, SQLite, session or migration change; the two `mediaHoldMs` keys are optional and additive; nothing new runs when `mediaHoldMs` is 0.
- **Live behaviour proof (QA Lab Matrix lane, real Tuwunel homeserver + real Gateway + the real Matrix plugin, `--provider-mode mock-openai`)**: `pnpm openclaw qa matrix --provider-mode mock-openai --concurrency 1 --scenario …`, **7 of 7 pass** on the exact head in one run (report below). The mock provider answers the image prompt with the image's colours only when the image reached that turn, so a colour reply proves one turn.
  - `matrix-media-hold-attachment-then-text`, `-standalone-timeout`, `-restart-recovery`, `matrix-e2ee-media-hold`, `matrix-media-hold-outage-catch-up`, `matrix-e2ee-media-hold-outage-catch-up`: PASS.
  - `matrix-media-hold-command-ordering` (DM, hold 8 s): PASS in that run, but **not reliably**. Because the 10-24 failure was 3/3, I ran it ten times per tree on the same box (for this head, the run above plus nine runs of this scenario alone; three on the rebuilt 10-24 code):

    | Tree | Runs | Pass | Fail | Core error in the failed runs |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | this head `f31c19123c5` (main `1f7035c15f3`, includes #192585) | 10 | 9 | 1 | `SessionWorkStartChangedError: Persisted user turn changed before replay admission. Retry the turn.` |
    | this head with only #192585's production change reverted (20 lines in three files; local only) | 10 | 10 | 0 | none |
    | this head with `mediaHoldMs: 0` in the scenario (hold off; local only) | 10 | 10 | 0 | none |
    | the 10-24 code rebuilt on its 10-24 base `ac13a7e0c13` (local only; the 10-24 head is no longer fetchable) | 3 | 2 | 1 | `ReplaySafeTranscriptConflictError: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite` |

    Both failed runs show the sequence recorded on 10-24: the `/status` reply arrives, then the attachment's turn, which the hold dispatched before the command, dies before its reply, and the room gets "OpenClaw couldn't finish this request". The gateway lines from the failed run on this head:

    ```text
    [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main durationMs=947 error="Persisted user turn changed before replay admission. Retry the turn." errorName=SessionWorkStartChangedError taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:qa:main
    [model-fallback/decision] model fallback chain stopped: reason=local_runtime_coordination candidate=mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna errorName=SessionWorkStartChangedError
    Embedded agent failed before reply: Persisted user turn changed before replay admission. Retry the turn.
    ```

    My reading: #192585 fixed the 10-24 error (#192522) for `/status`, but the delivered `/status` exchange is still mirrored into the transcript through the shared command mirror (`mirrorDeliveredReplyToTranscript` -> `recordDeliveredCommandExchange`), and when that write lands between the attachment turn's replay preparation and its admission, admission refuses the turn. That is the mechanism #194303 (open) reports for `/stop`; #194451 (open) covers other directives on the older error. So the race is in core and not specific to Matrix, but the hold makes it likelier, because it dispatches the released attachment and the command back to back. With these counts I cannot say whether #192585 changed the rate for this flow. I have not changed the hold for it: the plugin has no signal for "this turn has passed replay admission" beyond adoption, which it already waits for. If maintainers prefer, the hold could keep the releasing command back until the attachment's turn has replied; that makes the command's reply slower, and a `/stop` sent while an attachment is held would then not stop that attachment's turn.
- Not run: a hand-driven Element Web session (the lane drives the same Matrix client API Element Web uses); the upgrade-survivor lane was not re-run this round (no stored data or migration changed since its 2026-10-19 pass).

<details>

prs.title: fix(android): pause idle gateway discovery without blocking consumers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android keeps scanning for local Gateways without an active consumer. Pausing discovery must not break background recovery, connected discovery browsing, or secondary Gateway connections.

## User Impact

Android can pause idle local scans. If the first connection to a saved Gateway is interrupted before an address is accepted, returning to the app can retry when the Gateway reappears. Stop cancels that pending retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stop idle NSD scans and retire their callbacks. Resume for a visible Discovered list or onboarding, foreground enabled secondary Gateways, and the initial saved discovered-route recovery. Rebuild local results on resume; accepted sessions retain their own reconnect address. When no address has been accepted yet, the foreground path waits for the saved Gateway's fresh address and retries once without overriding a newer Gateway action.

This preserves #104226's cold sticky-service recovery with foreground-only capabilities disabled, and #111932's foreground-only secondary operator sessions with device capabilities owned only by the focused Gateway.

## Evidence

- On `e618cb5d`, all three `GatewayDiscoveryLifecycleTest` cases passed in an isolated Android Play JVM run. The foreground reconnect regression timed out waiting for a retry on parent `ccd5afac` and passed with the fix. The Stop case confirms rediscovery does not restart the connection after Stop. Kotlin lint on both changed files and `git diff --check` also passed.
- [Hosted CI on parent `ccd5afac`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42929089769) passed Play, third-party, and Wear unit suites, Kotlin/app lint, both Android Access jobs, and the required gate. This is prior-head evidence. Independent Auto Review P0–P2 passed for that earlier revision, not the follow-up.
- No physical-device run on the new head. The original device proof applies only to `dfcb5f99`.

☁️ @saariuslystoned

prs.title: fix: recover catalogs after non-native preparation timeouts
prs.body:
## CI retention repair — 2026-11-25

The actual CI heap failure was traced to the manifest model-row cache retaining a superseded hosted catalog solely as an identity key. The cache now retains that identity weakly, while keeping the existing snapshot/config identity checks and cached rows. No timeout, permission, dependency, or configuration contract changes.

The existing compiled-worker heap regression failed before this correction; all 11 existing worker heap cases and 26 model-catalog tests now pass. The earlier six custody/recovery cases remain valid unchanged-input proof. Final local ClawSweeper code/security review of `809a029ac296..436da4a0499d` completed with no actionable findings. Its note that this small correction adds no new regression is covered by the existing failing CI regression, not a test-count waiver. Scoped lint/format pass. Current-head CI is pending; the prior failed head is not claimed green.

Current head: `436da4a0499d2a36a2c7c64f2d8d6bbaac2ba22d`.

## Current repair and validation (2026-11-25)

Ported onto main `ba6d94ec1771` without restoring the retired native integration suite or deleted directory-verifier helper. The existing custody integration suite now covers both pre-verification and post-verification import stalls through the real compiled Gateway worker and replacement publication owners. Each regression failed on main; all six cases pass with the fix. Recovery is asserted on the new published snapshot, never the superseded failed snapshot. Existing terminal-stall and host-sleep cases remain intact.

Qualified touched-owner type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Historical Docker/Gateway evidence below is not a new-head live run; current worker integration proof is not full user-visible Gateway/channel end-to-end proof. Hosted CI and that remaining runtime qualification are still required before merge readiness.

Fresh local ClawSweeper finding disposition: its P2 asks to extend terminal handling to native namespace copying/hashing outside reference verification. The reported bug and existing progress channel concern reference verification only. The current recovery owner (`prepared-model-runtime.refresh-scope.ts`, `recoverCatalog`) publishes with `catalogMode: "static"`; it does not automatically replay the failed discovery. Retaining normal recovery for other preparation work is intentional, not an automatic hot retry loop. A persistent filesystem stall may recur on a later discovery demand; this accepted limitation is now documented. Expanding permanent terminal classification and lifecycle instrumentation to every native file operation is outside this repair. No authority, file-admission checks, timeout budgets, dependency versions or configuration were changed.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Gateway model catalog stops recovering when a plugin import times out before native verification starts or after verification has finished.

## User Impact

User impact: normal catalog preparation timeouts recover through the existing shared worker lifecycle, while stalled native verification remains terminal for that capture. No configuration, migration, or timeout-budget changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native verifier reports entry, verified-member progress, and exit through one lifecycle owner. The catalog worker forwards start/end immediately and only classifies a timeout as stalled native admission while verification is active. Existing idle deadline renewal still requires new completed members.

Related: #166687. This follow-up does not establish resolution of the separately reported Windows MSIX startup starvation (#167406); preserved Windows replay and caller attribution remain unverified.

## Evidence

- Actual Gateway catalog-worker boundary: eight tests passed, covering imports blocked both before and after verification, ongoing verification progress, terminal verification stalls, and existing catalog refresh siblings. Wrapper wall time: 123.35 seconds.
- Negative controls reproduced both original wrong terminal classifications before their fixes.
- Fresh full-context independent P1 review: scoped-clean; no actionable findings.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --staged` is running; core typecheck passed and test graph checks are in progress. Cost measurement: `pnpm test src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.native.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed all eight tests in 111.47 seconds wall; individual test durations totaled 65.15 seconds (86.99-second Vitest invocation including transformation/setup). This existing native-worker suite must exceed 30 seconds to prove the real compiled worker, import boundary, shared catalog recovery, and terminal native admission—not a helper substitute. Fake timers bound the existing preparation deadline and an explicit import barrier replaces real sleeps; no new per-test Gateway/process boot was added. Hosted CI seconds will be recorded once its selected run completes.

prs.title: fix: keep Add server within reach after an MCP name conflict
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If you tried to add an MCP server with a long name that was already in use, the error stretched the form past the edge of the dialog. On a phone, the Add server button slipped out of reach just when you needed it to retry.

## User Impact

You can read the full duplicate name, change it, and tap Add server without re-entering the URL. Cancel stays visible too.

## Why This Change Was Made

Let long names wrap in the error message shared by Settings and the Chat composer. The dialog shell, server list, and validation behavior stay unchanged.

## Evidence

On the 390 px phone, the form overflowed by 94 px at default text and 260 px at 140% text. With the fix, overflow was zero and the Add server button was reachable on the phone, both tablets, and desktop at both text sizes. The Settings and Chat composer browser regressions failed before and passed after, including a retry by tap with the URL preserved. Eight captures of the original server list were pixel-identical.

Mounted Control UI, 390 × 844 emulated phone with synthetic server entries. Comparison: stock main `da13d2a9c3023` versus local repair `2e46c273a1fa3`.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope image capability discovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- scope attachment image-capability fallback to the selected provider instead of rebuilding every provider catalog
- keep runtime-only models by using the existing request-scoped live catalog path
- retry the complete Gateway projection when its published runtime owner is replaced during scoped discovery

## Root cause and owner

Attachment admission first reads the lifecycle-published catalog. When a selected runtime-only model is absent or has provisional text-only metadata, current main falls back to `readOnly: false`, which rebuilds the full cross-provider catalog inside the request. The provider-scoped catalog machinery exists, but this Gateway caller did not use it.

The canonical owner is the Gateway catalog projection. The second read now carries the selected provider into the existing prepared request-scoped live catalog. The projection checks the published owner before and after the asynchronous scoped read and reacquires the full owner on replacement, so catalog, config, agent identity, and auth projection never mix generations.

## ClawSweeper findings

- Early owner replacement: fixed by retrying at the Gateway projection boundary; the regression replaces the owner during scoped discovery and proves only the replacement catalog returns.
- Final provider I/O fence: the old branch tried to turn generation liveness into a public provider-auth revocation contract, but that was incomplete and added a large cross-plugin surface. This port removes that contract. Published-generation liveness governs whether results may publish; it does not retroactively revoke already-started provider requests. Results from a retired generation are discarded and the owner is reacquired.
- Runtime-only models: retained. An independent P1 review caught and rejected an intermediate static-only rewrite; the final branch uses the existing scoped live mode.
- Test-cost evidence: recorded below for the new image-capability file and the combined focused Gateway set.

## Scope

Seven Gateway files changed against integrated main: 222 insertions and 60 deletions. Reuses the existing scoped catalog owner; no provider/plugin implementation changes, new configuration, or cache.

## Validation

- Integrated main: `1f01f4944d45eb265081f8bfbf8d3e8e54ff4266`; resolved conflicts while retaining current static-capability and projection owners.
- Three focused Gateway suites: 86 tests passed (image capability, catalog projection, session utilities).
- Core production typecheck and targeted lint passed; `git diff --check` clean.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the seven-file candidate diff. Surrounding loader implementations were not included in the isolated reviewer bundle; integration assurance also relies on focused tests and source inspection.
- Previous validation counts and hosted evidence were for the old head and are not current-head proof.
- No new real-channel/live-provider proof was run.
- CI follow-up: the new catalog mock now accepts the loader's optional argument. The affected Gateway-server test-type leaf passed; 16 catalog tests passed. Current head: `8a7567d2df5d`. Replacement exact-head CI is pending, not claimed green.

Agent transcript omitted.


## Repair sweep — 2026-11-25

Integrated main `ba6d94ec1771` to resolve the actual import conflict, preserving both scoped catalog load types and the current session runtime resolver. No new behavior was introduced by the conflict resolution.

Validation: 18 scoped catalog/image-capability tests and all 67 session-utils consumer tests passed. Canonical targeted type-aware lint, scoped formatting, and diff checks against the integrated base passed. Initial test/lint setup failures were resolved with a private frozen dependency install; no shared install changed. Current-head CI is pending, not claimed green.

Current repair head: `cdbb6adf4685c3f35cc45d52be905e417bd5fbd3`. No merge performed.

prs.title: fix: repair session titles left as internal wake markers
prs.body:
Related: #194768

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes saved session names such as `[OpenClaw session event]` surviving `openclaw doctor --fix` after upgrading. Preventing new internal-wake titles did not clean up names already persisted by older versions.

## User Impact

After updating, run `openclaw doctor --fix` to repair affected names. Human labels, unrelated titles, session identity, transcripts, and activity timestamps remain unchanged. This does not change how Home/main sessions are represented in the sidebar.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Doctor's existing bounded title-repair owner. A display name is eligible only when it exactly matches a known historical wake-generated title, the first bounded transcript input corroborates that same wake, and no other explicit naming field overrides it. Recorded external-user input is never treated as wake evidence. This includes the old flattened/truncated exec-completion title. Names without transcript evidence remain intact. No fuzzy matching, new schema, runtime rewrite, or model call.

## Historical evidence — prior heads

- Persisted-marker regression failed before the change; all 13 Doctor title-repair tests pass afterward. Covers dry-run preservation, persisted removal, idempotence, manual labels, unrelated names, and unchanged activity.
- Built-CLI upgrade proof: created the bad main-session title in an isolated 2026.11.1 instance, then ran the patched Doctor. Verified the title was removed and session ID/activity timestamps were preserved.
- Real isolated Gateway/browser proof: Orion's header opened Orion's main transcript; after seeding the legacy title, running the patched Doctor, and restarting, the transcript reopened intact. Synthetic data; no model inference or live installation changes.
- Runtime build, core typecheck, focused lint/format, and diff checks passed. Build still reports existing UI boot-budget warnings; no UI assets/source changed by this PR.
- Fresh independent source review: no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper completed a full committed-range review of `d122c1b06011..1006e6acca971` (high reasoning, read-only), with no actionable correctness or security findings. It inspected tests but did not run them; execution results above are separate.
- Test cost: new regression 1.73s; complete file 85.61s including compilation (95.45s wrapper). CI time pending. The 29-line allocation is for the persisted-data regression and preservation/idempotence assertions. Production growth is seven lines, using the existing repair path; diagnostic browser/upgrade fixtures are not added to PR CI.


## Repair sweep — 2026-11-25

Integrated main specifically to retire the observed `check-docs` formatting failure in unchanged release-tooling files, not merely to refresh the base. Removed the obsolete 29-line allocation; the test delta fits the current automatic allowance.

A fresh full-current-main local review found two real issues in the original proposal: an explicitly created marker-shaped name could be cleared without any transcript, and the actual pre-#179219 exec title was whitespace-normalized/truncated rather than the raw prompt. Those regressions fail before correction. A further real regression confirms that an explicitly named external-user quotation of the full exec wake must also remain intact; recorded human provenance now excludes it. The repair now requires a matching first transcript wake, preserves an explicitly created name with no transcript, and recognizes the concrete historical exec title without duplicating a new title formatter.

Validation: all 16 Doctor title-repair cases pass, including the three red-before-fix regressions, idempotence, preview, human labels, unrelated names and activity preservation. The dedicated Doctor test typecheck (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.commands-doctor.json`) and scoped type-aware lint/format pass. The integrated head's `pnpm format:docs:check` passes (1,445 docs); the follow-up docs wording passes scoped formatting. The final correction range has a complete local code/security review with no remaining actionable findings. The final normalize-once simplification also reran all four affected cases; unchanged-input proof for the other cases is reused. Native/Gateway/latest-stable upgrade acceptance was not rerun; prior evidence above is historical, not current-head proof.

Simplification: one existing Doctor owner and bounded transcript read; no new persistence, identity state, schema, broad matcher or test-only production export. Against pinned main, the complete delta is four files: 84 test lines added, production +50/-13, and one docs sentence. Accepted ambiguity: an operator who deliberately reuses the exact old generated name on a session whose first input is that same canonical wake without recorded human provenance is indistinguishable from the legacy case; no new tracking state is added for that rare case.

Current repair head: `459b8a004430d43850409695043a9b535dc13424`. Current-head hosted CI will run on publication. No merge is requested.
