prs.title: fix: show an accepted suggestion as the approver's own message
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a session owner accepts a suggestion from someone they invited, the message shows up as if a stranger called "SB" sent it. The sender name is saved as "Suggested by Jason", so the avatar initials become **S**uggested **B**y. The message is also credited to the suggestion's author, even though it ran with the approver's access and only after the approver read and accepted it.

## User Impact

- An accepted suggestion now appears on the approver's side of the chat, with the approver's name and avatar.
- A "Suggested by <author>" label under the message credits the person who wrote it.
- The agent sees the approver as the sender, the same as if they had typed the message.
- Accepted suggestions now behave exactly like messages the approver types. The restrictions on synthetic (system-generated) senders no longer apply, so @-mentions and skill authoring are available, and they go through the same repository and automation admission as ordinary chat.
- Queued suggestions now survive a Gateway restart, because the sender matches the operator whose access was recorded. Before, recovery rejected them as a sender mismatch.
- Messages already saved under the old format keep their stored attribution and still show "SB". They are not rewritten.

## Why This Change Was Made

Accepting a suggestion is the approver vouching for the text and running it under their own access. So the approver is the single sender everywhere: transcript, avatar, agent-visible sender and permission checks. The author is kept only as a display-only `suggestedBy { id, name }` field in the transcript metadata. That field drives the UI label and never reaches model input. Dispatch now goes through the same authenticated chat entry as a typed message (`handleDirectExternalChatSend`), so repository-dispatch and automation-management admission match ordinary chat. The multi-user docs previously said suggestion attribution identifies the author; that sentence is updated to the new behavior.

## Evidence

Before: the stored shape before this change, `senderName: "Suggested by Alice"` with Alice's identity, renders as a left-side peer message with "SB" initials.

![Before: accepted suggestion renders as a peer message with SB initials and the name "Suggested by Alice"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5755ea81-ab90-4840-8f5e-f34350051d54)

After: the new shape renders as the owner's own message, with the owner's avatar and a "Suggested by Alice" label underneath.

![After: accepted suggestion renders on the owner's side with the owner's avatar and a muted "Suggested by Alice" label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b708cc7-23af-4018-aa76-0d070abefafc)

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-suggestions.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-suggestions.custody.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-suggestions.visibility.test.ts src/sessions/user-turn-transcript.persistence.test.ts`: passed. The dispatch test now asserts the dispatched client carries `suggestedBy` and no `senderAttribution` or `syntheticClient`. The persistence case round-trips the approver as sender plus `suggestedBy`.
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.tsx`: passed, including a new case for the own-side rendering and label.
- `ui/src/e2e/session-suggestions.e2e.test.ts` (mocked Gateway, Playwright): 11/11 passed, including a new case for an accepted suggestion. The screenshots above come from this suite.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck (core, core tests, UI), lint, i18n catalog and boundary checks passed. Two failures come from files this PR does not touch: the changelog attribution check (`CHANGELOG/2026.11.10.md` thanks a bot) and the dead-export scan (unused exports in `scripts/e2e/parallels/*`, `scripts/publish-model-catalog.mts`, `ui/src/pages/projects/project-access.ts` and test-support files). A formatting issue in this PR was fixed.
- An independent review found one issue: dispatch bypassed ordinary chat entry admission. Fixed in the second commit.
- Not exercised: a live two-person flow against a real Gateway and model. The Gateway path is covered by the handler and custody tests; the UI path by the mocked-Gateway e2e.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix: keep long process names compact above mobile output
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A long process name took five lines above Recent output on a phone. Most of that space showed directories rather than the executable the reader was trying to identify.

## User Impact

The executable stays visible on one line above the output. You can scroll the name horizontally to inspect the entire path, without scrolling the output or leaving the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the name is shortened visually. The full string stays in the document and in the hover title. The reader’s first and last output lines, exit information, and Back control keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

On a 390 × 844 phone at 140% text, the name fell from 127 to 25 px. Horizontal scrolling revealed the beginning of the exact command and returned to its ending. The first and last lines of retained output were reachable, and Back returned focus to the original process row. The same mobile-sheet flow passed on the 820 × 1180 portrait tablet. These are bundled Chromium views with a mocked Gateway and synthetic process output; no process was run or stopped through the UI. The comparison uses the previous PR revision (948781972f4e) and the repair (75a3c2019a9f).

prs.title: fix: show why a chat’s desktop is unavailable next to Retry
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a chat’s assigned desktop was unavailable, the Desktop panel put **Retry** far from the explanation. If checking for that desktop failed, the panel said **Desktop disconnected** and showed connection controls even though it had not found a device.

## User Impact

The reason and **Retry** now appear together. Retry checks whether the assigned desktop is available before showing connection controls. You can cancel a pending check with **Disconnect**; a late reply won’t reconnect you without an explicit **Reconnect**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Checking for a desktop is different from connecting to one. The panel now shows the status and action for the step it is actually performing. The same button retains keyboard focus while the check runs or fails.

## Evidence

The existing phone screenshots show an unavailable desktop and a failed retry. Across the phone, both tablets, and desktop, the gap between the reason and Retry went from 132–416 px to 16 px. Touch targets were at least 44 px tall. All 40 focused Desktop tests passed on the isolated patch, including failure, cancellation, and explicit reconnection. The mounted checks used a synthetic assigned device and simulated view-only frames. No real desktop was accessed or controlled. Screenshot baseline: `450441b904031`. Atlas repair: `804324d4e90f1`.

### Clean comparison

|---|---|
| ![The unavailable desktop message and Retry button sit far apart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ff404bf-1ccd-430a-a786-cd9a877f9a9d) | ![The same message and Retry button appear together](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca1d536b-964d-4253-8ea9-05cb3d130f66) |

prs.title: fix: keep Browser address suggestions on one line
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A long address could wrap the Browser’s **Go to** button onto several lines on a phone. It also made the suggestion taller in a narrow Chat panel on a landscape tablet. The address field already holds the whole editable destination.

## User Impact

The suggestion stays the height of a short address. Its visible label starts with the host and shortens the path with an ellipsis. The full destination remains available in the field, as the button’s accessible name and on hover. Selecting the suggestion sends the complete address to the Gateway, not its shortened label.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the focused Browser and Chat’s Browser panel use the same address toolbar. Only the suggestion needs truncation; typing, search and navigation keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

On main, the long suggestion took four lines (78 px), and text painted past the edge of the screen. On the candidate, short and long suggestions were each 30 px high; the accessible name and title retained the complete URL. Tapping the shortened suggestion sent that exact URL to the Gateway. Its network policy rejected the local test hostname, so that tap did not load the page. A separate **Go** action on the same tab reached the test page with the complete path and query (HTTP 200).

The same long URL in the phone-sized Browser address bar. Before: main `c076c1754ae9`. After: `30df40f40d71`. Chromium at 390 × 844, using the same local test page and isolated Gateway.

At enlarged text sizes on a phone, Learn more can wrap to the left edge of the Labs page header. The header clipped the left side of the link’s keyboard focus outline.

## User Impact

Keyboard users can see the entire outline without moving the link or the settings beneath it. The same behavior is retained on This device and Permissions.

Handle the wrapped link in the Settings header shared by these pages, and remove the device-only exception introduced by [#203667](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203667). This PR is based on that repair so reviewers see only the shared-header change and its regression.

prs.title: fix(update): report unrestored Gateways as repair warnings and check stop intent at native start
prs.body:
## Problem

After an update, `openclaw update repair` / `update finalize` restarts the Gateway that the update left stopped. On `main`, three spots turn a soft outcome into a hard error or skip a needed check:

1. If the Gateway does not start or verify after repair maintenance has already finished, the whole repair fails ("Gateway recovery after update repair failed…").
2. Before starting the service, repair inspects it, then re-reads and re-inspects it again in a `beforeMutation` callback that only the Windows Scheduled Task path calls. On macOS and Linux the stop-still-pending check therefore runs only once, well before the start.
3. On macOS and Windows, the service layer silently ignores the `beforeEffect` callback that systemd already honors, so a check meant to run right before `launchctl` / `schtasks` never runs there.

Separately, the managed-update helper's `shouldRecoverInterruptedUpdater` lets an update-history read error throw past its existing failure handling.

## Solution

- Repair: inspect the service, then recheck the existing selected-service binding and recovery admission at `beforeMutation` and the synchronous stop-still-pending check in `beforeEffect`, right before the native start. A Gateway that does not come back after repair is a warning naming `openclaw gateway start` and `openclaw gateway status --deep`; named data risk and process-cleanup failures still fail.
- Pass `beforeEffect` through `launchctl enable`/`bootstrap`/`kickstart` (including retries), `schtasks /Run`, and the Windows fallback script, matching systemd.
- Helper: an unreadable history while deciding on interrupted recovery is logged and falls through to the existing failure handling.

The repair sweep below updates the original implementation and validation.

## Impact

Fewer hard repair failures and no new refusals: the only new stop is "this update's Gateway stop was already retired" (an operator or another start acted meanwhile), which repair reports as a warning. Accepted edge: on macOS, if `bootstrap` auto-starts the Gateway and it records itself running within milliseconds, before the follow-up `kickstart`, repair warns even though the Gateway is up; the next `openclaw update repair` verifies it without restarting.

Backport twin: these are the `main` versions of commits on #193884 (`release/2026.11.3`).

Not included: the release branch also has a fallback for the helper reading update history after the candidate's Doctor advances the state schema. It does not reproduce on `main`: with the same fixture and without the fallback, the helper reads history and reaches repair, likely because `main` checks the schema once per process. The original release-branch fixtures diverged on `main`; the repair sweep below adds registered-CLI reassigned-service coverage at the current boundary.

## Evidence

- `update-repair-service` 25/25 (expectations updated for warning instead of failure; late stop retirement through the repair CLI)
- `launchd-start-authority` 3/3 (new), `schtasks.start` 20/20
- `update-managed-service-handoff-interrupted` 16/16, `-lifecycle` 70/70, `-cleanup-repair` 40/40
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt clean; `check-test-mock-exports --base origin/main` OK


## Repair sweep — 2026-11-25

Integrated main while preserving its selected Scheduled Task command and preparation/effect callbacks. Fresh local review found and corrected binding reassignment, disabled-task enable ordering, late recovery admission, unreadable recovery state, and warning visibility. Existing selected-service binding and recovery admission run at the native mutation boundary; every admission failure remains a failure. Only eligible post-repair service start/readiness outcomes become warnings, with the retained recovery instructions also visible in ordinary terminal output. No new authority owner or speculative fencing was added.

Validation: five real registered-CLI regressions failed before their corresponding corrections (rebound service, interrupted restore, late unfinished recovery, unreadable recovery state, and missing terminal instructions). All 40 repair-service cases and all 23 Scheduled Task start cases pass. The unreadable-directory fixture now injects EACCES at the actual filesystem boundary instead of relying on platform-specific chmod behavior; that case passes after the portability correction. Earlier 60-case repair/finalization/native-callback proof remains applicable to unchanged paths. Scoped type-aware lint, the dedicated CLI-update test typecheck (`test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.cli-update.json`), formatting and diff checks pass. Final local committed-range review is complete: the source corrections have no remaining actionable findings, and the final portable-fixture range is clean.

This serves the existing `update repair` legacy bridge route, not the new owned-install updater. The old allocation request is obsolete under the current automatic allowance. Current-head native upgrade/platform end-to-end acceptance and listed-owner review remain unverified; no merge is requested by this sweep.

Current repair head: `61f79025d00ab5ee06b5ef50a8aea372192fdc2b`. Current-head hosted CI pending publication.

prs.title: fix: keep Save in place when filtering Workboard labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Workboard card’s label picker opened above the labels on a phone, typing a search could make the menu shrink away from the card. The **Save** and **Cancel** buttons moved as the results changed. With the full list, **Save** could fall outside the visible menu.

## User Impact

You can narrow the list, select a label and reach **Save** in the same place. When space is tight, the choices scroll between the search field and the buttons.

## Why This Change Was Made

A picker that opens above the label field now keeps its opening height while you filter. Closing it releases that space. Pickers that open below the field keep their existing layout.

## Evidence

The phone screenshots show the same synthetic Workboard card after filtering twelve choices to one. Before, the gap between the picker and the label field grew from 6 px to 85 px. After, it stayed at 6 px. The Chromium regression checked that the search field, first result and **Save** stayed in place when the query was entered and cleared, and that **Save** remained reachable.

The regression passed on the publication checkout. Across 28 matched states at four screen sizes, 23 unaffected menu or control crops were pixel-identical. No real card was updated. Screenshot baseline: `8621a7c6647f4`. Original repair: `386a57fd02162`.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Filtering to one label lifts Save and Cancel away from the card’s labels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47c7abcc-ce92-420c-9015-95d6aea87d33) | ![With the same search, the buttons stay just above the card’s labels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa4a25c2-d209-4085-bd4a-f0e755ac32b5) |

Same twelve-label card with one search result on an emulated phone. The outline marks the action row relative to the card’s labels.

prs.title: fix(macos): show progress when reloading an unavailable dashboard
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On macOS, clicking **Reload** on an unavailable Dashboard starts a Gateway connection attempt, but the failure page still looks idle. A slow connection can make a working button look like it did nothing.

## User Impact

The Reload button shows a spinner during the connection attempt, blocks duplicate retries, and returns to its normal state if the attempt times out. Connection Settings remains available. The spinner respects Reduce Motion and exposes a connecting status to assistive technology. No configuration changes or migration are needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native Dashboard window already owns the pending Gateway operation. The failure page reflects that state rather than starting a timer or guessing when the retry has finished. The button keeps its footprint, so nearby controls do not move.

## Evidence

- [Before/after WebKit fixture preview](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205545#issuecomment-7173686330). It checked the Reload bridge payload, spinner and accessible status while retrying, unchanged button positions, Connection Settings, reduced motion, and a second retry after failure. The fixture simulated the native retry; native app screenshots are still pending.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` and `git diff --check` passed locally. The native WebKit regression covers the Dashboard manager’s pending and timeout states; compilation and execution are pending in [exact-head draft CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45694865033).
- Self-review: the change uses the existing window-owned retry state; it does not add a timer or a second recovery state. An independent review has not run.

Reported and co-authored by @vyctorbrzezowski.

prs.title: fix(macos): app quits with a generic credential alert when a separately managed Gateway blocks migration after an update
prs.body:
Related: #187000

## What Problem This Solves

After an app update, required client-credential maintenance can be blocked by another process or an unverifiable lock owner. The generic recovery alert exits rather than allowing an in-place retry after the operator resolves the contention.

## User Impact

The bundled CLI now distinguishes maintenance-lock refusals from unrelated credential failures. The app offers **Retry** / **Quit OpenClaw** with neutral recovery guidance; it does not infer a process manager from a saved LaunchAgent, a recorded role, or `--attach-only`. It never stops or replaces a process to satisfy this prompt. Background-only launches print guidance and quit without opening a panel. Invalid config and unrelated preparation failures keep generic recovery.

## Solution

`prepareStartupClientCredentials` wraps lock/state-owner contention as `ClientCredentialMaintenanceBlockedError`; `doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive --json` reports `client_credentials_maintenance_blocked`. The app recognizes that code and re-enters the existing CLI admission only when the operator chooses Retry. Main's service replacement/version policy and both legacy-lock owners are unchanged. This deliberately replaces the earlier owner-specific proposal instead of adding identity-matching machinery.

The app's alert presenter is dismissed during termination, and shutdown waits for credential startup to settle. The external-Quit regression now requires completion before the earliest cleanup deadline, not merely a clean deadline-forced exit.

## Repair sweep — 2026-11-25

Integrated main, preserving runtime-pin preparation and generic failed-startup Quit/reopen coverage. Updated a stale test to change the recorded inode: main correctly allows a device-number-only remount without Doctor. Removed the obsolete allocation file (the counted TypeScript test delta is within the automatic budget).

Validation: all 27 startup-credential and 43 registered-CLI cases pass, including real state-owner/legacy-lock contention, non-Gateway holders, unrelated failures, cleanup and cancellation. The original stale fixture failed twice before adaptation, and the added legacy-lock regression failed before its diagnostic correction. Targeted commands and config/CLI typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. Changed Swift files parse; native i18n verification reports 4,963 entries unchanged. Fresh local correction review is recorded below once complete.

Current repair head: `83ce9b0ad7988bac309a4aa5e2e4ba80a464f632`. Current-head CI is running. The complete native app product and all native test targets compile and link successfully without executing the tests. Interactive/background runtime, latest-stable upgrade acceptance, and refreshed visual evidence were not rerun in this sweep. The evidence below documents earlier implementations/heads only; its older diagnostic code and manager-specific copy are not the current contract.

Fresh local review additionally restored the existing command-runner type alias and preserved complete bounded CLI guidance, including the lock path and the condition before removing a stale lock. The brief recovery instructions stay outside a fixed-height, selectable, scrollable details area to keep Retry/Quit reachable with long diagnostics; the refreshed rendered view still needs native visual acceptance. Local committed-range reviews are complete. All actionable findings were addressed; the final static-copy correction has no remaining findings and security review is cleared. The simplification pass removed a static-copy assertion while retaining the long-diagnosis regression for the observed truncation bug; real CLI-code classification and bundled-command tests remain. Native tests are not run on the operator desktop: a filter is not the required OS-level isolation boundary.

## Historical evidence — prior design and heads

**Real CLI against a real isolated Gateway.** Private `HOME`/state/config, named profile `mgre2e`, port 34781, never the operator's Gateway:
- With `pnpm openclaw gateway run` holding state (pid 19622, role `gateway`) and a required migration (receipt device mismatch, the remount case), `doctor --client-credentials --fix --non-interactive --json` exited 2 with `"code": "client_credentials_gateway_held"` and the contention message naming that holder.
- Same running Gateway, unrelated failure (invalid config): exit 2, **no** code (`Cannot prepare client credentials with invalid config …`).
- After stopping that Gateway, the same command exited 0 with `{"ok": true}`, and the receipt returned to `complete` with the original device. This is the CLI side of **Retry**.

**Original-head regression evidence** (`c7e792e3b2d3`), red on the base and green with the fix:
- `startup-client-credentials.test.ts`: "attributes a required migration refusal to the Gateway only when a gateway holds state" uses a real state-owner lock. The `gateway` case fails without the fix, and the `agent-embedded` case proves non-Gateway holders are not attributed. Suite: 22/22.
- `register.maintenance.test.ts`: the coded JSON failure envelope and exit 2. Suite: 39/39.
- Swift, private `HOME`/state/`TMPDIR`: `ClientCredentialStartupTests` (`--json` arguments, only the Gateway-held code yields `GatewayHeldError`, owner-specific recovery text) and `StaleGatewayServiceReplacementTests` (the #190162 hosting matrix plus owner exclusions): 11/11.

**Original-head gates** (`c7e792e3b2d3`):
- `swift build` for the app product and the test targets passed.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, oxfmt, oxlint and `pnpm tsgo:core` / `tsgo:core:test` all pass.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` reports only 2 existing file-length violations in untouched files (`DashboardManager.swift`, `GatewayConnection.swift`).

**Original-head review:** local autoreview (Codex), committed range `d894035c7829..c7e792e3b2d3`, `--max-priority P2` with the owning sources as context: `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings (0.88). An earlier P0-only pass was also clean.

**ClawSweeper finding follow-up** (`dddadc75e57f`):
- Removed the unsupported incompatibility diagnosis and unconditional version-change advice from the alert and docs. Receipt reconciliation after a remount can require exclusive maintenance without changing the credential layout.
- Removed the unused app-version argument and the wording-only helper test; error attribution, cancellation, and bundled-owner tests remain. No detection or service-lifecycle behavior changed.
- Current checks passed: `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` (app and test targets), targeted SwiftFormat, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, docs oxfmt, and `git diff --check`.
- Native tests were not rerun on the operator desktop; the macOS guide requires OS-level isolation or a disposable runner. The earlier 11-test result above is prior-head evidence and includes the now-removed wording test. Subsequent explicitly authorized isolated native proof is recorded below.

**Native app validation on a prior head (`dddadc75e57f`):**

Performed natively with explicit operator authorization, in a fresh OCM environment: separate HOME/CFFIXED_USER_HOME, state/config/profile, bundle identity, test LaunchAgent, and port 34781. No copied operator credentials or channels. A sandbox guard denied app access to the operator state and writes to operator preferences/LaunchAgents, and blocked connections to the live Gateway ports. App metadata pins the tested commit.

- Stable `2026.10.10` service: the actual app showed the owner-preserving maintenance alert with Retry / Quit. Retrying while the service held state returned to the alert without migration. After stopping only the test service, Retry completed migration; the native credential socket returned the original synthetic device ID, public/private keys, and creation time. Test config remained unchanged.
- Compatible runtime: the test service ran the PR app's bundled runtime. A synthetic receipt device mismatch represented remount maintenance (not a real filesystem remount). The real app showed the same corrected maintenance alert without asserting version incompatibility. Retry while held returned to the alert. After stopping only this test service, Retry repaired the receipt; native credential admission preserved the original identity/keys and config.
- Operator config and Gateway LaunchAgent hashes remained equal to their pre-test values. The live Gateway restarted independently during the interrupted agent run, so continuous PID preservation is not claimed; no test command stopped or modified that service.

**Merged head (`58359d17191c`):** merged current `main` and fixed the Quit hang.

- Conflict resolution: `doctor --client-credentials` keeps both `prepareRuntimePins: true` from `main` and this PR's coded failure. The docs text moved to the new **Credential recovery** section.
- Quit fix: both credential-startup alert paths now use `AppDelegate.requestTermination()` instead of calling `terminate` on the main dispatch task.
- Isolated OCM run, same guards, app metadata pinned to this commit: with the test Gateway holding state and a synthetic receipt device mismatch, process sampling shows the app in `retryAfterExcludedGatewayFailure` → `NSAlert.runModal`. The bundled CLI exits 2 with `client_credentials_gateway_held`.
- Passing: `startup-client-credentials.test.ts` and `register.maintenance.test.ts` (64/64), app packaging, oxfmt, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` reports 5 violations, all in files this PR does not touch.
- Native test targets do not compile on `main`: `GatewayEndpointStoreTests.swift` calls the now-throwing `_testLocalConfig` without `try`. This PR does not touch that file. With a temporary local `try!` patch, not committed, the test targets built.

- Real alert clicks, same isolated OCM run on `58359d17191c`, pressed through the Accessibility API with the alert's actual text and controls read back:
  - **Retry** while the test Gateway held state: the alert returned and no migration ran.
  - **Quit OpenClaw**: the app exited in about 2 seconds. This is the path that hung on `dddadc75e57f`.
  - **Retry** after stopping only the test Gateway: the receipt returned to `complete` with the real device, and the native credential socket returned the original device ID, public/private keys, and creation time. Test config unchanged.
- Operator config and Gateway LaunchAgent hashes matched before and after.

**Remaining gaps:**

- **Visual screenshots remain missing.** `AppActivation.presentAlert` sets `alert.window.sharingType = .none`, so captures of the real alert are blank. No mockup or blank image is offered as proof.
- The alert's **Details** line uses `detail.suffix(300)`, so it can start mid-word (observed: "e directory."). The actionable end of the message is intact.
- Successful Retry is proved at the real app credential socket, not full chat/model connectivity. The full native suite remains CI-owned.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Incognito real-Gateway test waits for the first `chat.startup` response, but the shared RPC observer stopped recording that method when background-work coverage moved to history subscriptions. The request succeeds while the test waits until its overall timeout.

## User Impact

Restore the Incognito test's ability to verify the initial reply and two continuation sends. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record both `chat.startup` and `sessions.messages.subscribe`. The background-work test still needs subscription receipts, and the other helper consumers retain their method-filtered assertions. Follow-up to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205503.

## Evidence

- [Full main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45685091056/job/139456245493): Incognito test times out waiting for a method discarded by the observer.
- Source audit confirms the test's startup wait and the missing observer allowlist entry; the underlying request succeeded in the captured diagnostics.
- At `6db6cc85d265daff110fe2144611b1ea3a9803d1`, the real-Gateway run passed 8 tests across 7 suites: Incognito startup and both continuation sends, background work, quiet automations, child handoff, yielded replies, long-turn Stop, and button/slash Stop of owned processes.
- The opt-in Send now task proof was selected but skipped because `OPENCLAW_STEER_NOW_PROOF` was unset; it is not claimed as executed.
- Local review of the exact committed range found no correctness or security findings. Formatting and normal commit hooks passed.
- Scoped lint and UI E2E typecheck passed in the same isolated ascii-box run; command and wrapper exited 0, and the lease stopped cleanly.

prs.title: feat(voice-call): let phone calls ignore background voices instead of answering them
prs.body:
Closes #205510

## What Problem This Solves

On realtime phone calls, the model hears every voice the line picks up, such as a TV or other people in the room, and a realtime reply nearly always speaks. Callers hear the assistant answer voices that were never talking to it ("Sorry, how can I help?"), sometimes again and again, and it talks over them.

## User Impact

With `realtime.staySilentTool: true`, and the tool mentioned in `realtime.instructions`, the model can pass over speech that was not meant for it: nothing is spoken and the call keeps listening. It is off by default, so nothing changes unless an operator turns it on. The risk is a model that overuses it and ignores the real caller until they speak again; how well it judges depends on the instructions.

## Why This Change Was Made

A reply starts on every turn the line hears, and the model has no way to answer one without speaking, so instructions alone could not keep it quiet. `openclaw_stay_silent` is that silent answer: the call submits a suppressed tool result, so no reply is generated. It is opt-in because it only helps with instructions that say when to use it. To make room for it, the existing end-call result handling moves unchanged from `realtime-handler.ts` into `realtime-call-tools.ts`, next to the new tool, so the handler, already past its line cap, gets shorter instead of longer. #137895 also changes that end-call code, so whichever of the two lands second needs a small rebase.

## Evidence

- Live, on a larger build: enabled since Nov 22 on a production Telnyx line (OpenAI realtime), on a 2026.11.6 source build that also carries other local voice patches; this branch itself has not been run on a live call. Traffic on that line is light so far: since Nov 22 the gateway has logged one passed-over background turn.

  ```
  2026-11-23T17:31:29.096+00:00 [voice-call] Realtime background passed over callId=4620fd12...
  ```

- Focused tests: the runtime offers the tool only when configured, ahead of configured tools, and a configured tool with the same name cannot replace it; the call answers it with `{ ok: true }` and `suppressResponse`, without speaking or hanging up. The existing end-call tests pass unchanged after the move.
- `pnpm test` on `runtime.test.ts`, `config.test.ts`, `realtime-call-control.test.ts`, `realtime-handler.test.ts` and `realtime-handler.lifecycle.test.ts`: 173 passed. Typechecks, oxlint, oxfmt, `config:docs:check`, `check:line-cap-ratchet` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` pass.
- Not exercised: providers other than OpenAI realtime. The Google Live bridge does not apply `suppressResponse` yet, so with Google the model may still speak after invoking the tool; the docs say so.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: feat: let Ask OpenClaw run supported read-only commands
prs.body:
Part of #203784
Part of #203737
Stacked on #205492.

## What Problem This Solves

People troubleshooting in Ask OpenClaw often know the CLI command they want, but have to translate it to the conversation’s named diagnostic action. For example, asking for `openclaw gateway status --deep` should reach the existing deep Gateway diagnostic without leaving chat.

## User Impact

Ask OpenClaw accepts supported diagnostics in CLI form, including status, health, config reads, Gateway status, logs, and selected plugin, skill, model, and channel checks. `gateway status --deep` and `channels status --probe` retain their existing behavior. JSON output, custom log limits, and unsupported commands or flags are refused. Run `openclaw doctor --lint` directly in a terminal for the full lint.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exact argument matches dispatch to existing typed reads rather than running a CLI subprocess. That keeps config redaction, hosted log scope, and the Gateway and skills protections on their existing paths. Diagnostic text is sanitized and capped at 8,000 characters. The rescue command does not accept this action.

prs.title: fix(claude-cli): replies are lost when the watchdog kills a turn waiting on background work
prs.body:
## Problem
Claude CLI can finish an answer while its own background work is still pending. Ordinary silence recovery killed that continuation and could discard the completed answer.

## Solution
- Let the Anthropic runtime own continuation state, including nested tasks, started steering, stopped work, and earlier-input replay.
- Hold ordinary quiet recovery only while that backend-owned wait is active. The CLI watchdog owns the active execution budget and credits host suspension; controller-first wakeups cannot expire a second stale wall-clock deadline.
- Preserve an already completed answer if a later timeout settles the turn.
- Keep the existing bounded live-session replacement/cleanup deadline until replacement finishes. Host suspension during that pre-runtime cleanup still has the preexisting wall-clock behavior; this patch does not make cleanup unbounded to hide it.

## Current repair validation
Forward-ported to main `ba6d94ec17712`, preserving current admission and iterator cleanup owners.
- Real Claude-adapter stdio fixture: 72 tests passed; task ownership suite: 5 passed, including earlier-input replay red without the fix and green with it.
- Real session-controller continuation/host-suspension cases plus plugin runner: 31 tests passed. The suspension case explicitly ticks the controller before the CLI timer.
- Earlier combined continuation/compaction suites: 9 passed.
- Core and canonical extension typechecks, touched lint/format, and whitespace checks passed.
- Fresh independent local reviews drove the hold transitions, controller ownership, and replay repairs. The last narrow review raised suspension during pre-runtime replacement; that existing current-main behavior is deliberately retained to preserve the hard cleanup bound, not treated as a newly passing scenario.

## Remaining qualification
- CI must finish on this new head; previous-head CI is not current-head evidence.
- The original PR recorded a native Claude Code reproduction; that historical run was not repeated on this repair head. Current proof uses the real adapter with a synthetic native subprocess and real controller with a simulated clock.
- Existing Webchat settlement/persistence timing is unchanged: interim text can remain live-streamed until the run settles.

prs.body:
## Repair sweep — 2026-11-25

Applied the base stack's reviewed checkout-fixture correction here as well: copy the trusted runner-routing module into the executable-preflight fixture and evaluate actual workflow runner-selector expressions before classifying harness export coverage. The missing-module failure was reproduced on this branch, then six selected cases passed (230 unrelated cases not selected). Qualified type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks pass. The exact two-file repair diff is byte-identical to the freshly locally reviewed correction on #173581; that bounded review is reused, not represented as a new review of this entire provisioning proposal.

**Remaining blockers:** the stack's main integration/current Boat-routing equivalence is unfinished in #173581. Existing live registration/access/cancellation proof is also incomplete: the historical attempt returned HTTP 403 on GitHub runner registration. Resolving that requires a runner-administration owner and an explicitly approved paid campaign. This sweep did not provision AWS resources, change repository variables/groups, or claim successful registration or a full campaign. The PR is non-draft at the user's request, not declared merge-ready.

---

## Original proposal and historical evidence

## What Problem This Solves

Full Release Validation shares busy hosted/Blacksmith queues. This PR adds campaign-specific Crabbox provisioning and runner selection on top of #173581, which separately extracts existing runner policy without changing placement.

## User Impact

`pnpm ci:full-release:crabbox --max-runners 10 -- --sha <candidate> --workflow-sha <tooling>` provisions campaign-specific, one-job AWS runners for eligible Linux validation jobs. Existing defaults, native platforms, credentialed publishing, parent dispatch-and-wait coordinators, coverage, and matrix concurrency limits retain their behavior. The anchor cleanup is merged; standalone/manual expansion remains excluded.

## Implementation

- A bounded controller uses existing Crabbox broker authentication and GitHub runner registration, preserves CPU/architecture capacity classes, supports retained-request recovery, and settles campaign jobs before lease cleanup.
- Linux workers select one unique campaign-and-capacity label already registered by the controller. Parent/child dispatch and evidence carry the campaign identity.
- Extends the routing planner from the base PR with campaign selectors; matrix lookups retain their capacity, task, and dynamic RunsOn identities.
- Security/gate fallbacks preserve campaign or runner-group placement if preflight fails before publishing its map.

## Validation

- Current stacked head: 10 focused Crabbox controller/routing and real-manifest retry cases passed (11.51-second wrapper). Fresh review of the retry correction found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- The combined tree preserves previously reviewed and tested #173581 head `6734aee8d15b744f85e0281e321456482f707010` with the base PR’s partial-rerun correction carried through. Existing Crabbox behavior and proof below are reused; current-attempt selector lookup is validated separately. The base extraction separately passed 56,640 retained-map routing comparisons, 20 focused tests and the partial-rerun regression. A further 33,984 comparisons verify the combined Crabbox selectors on initial and partial-rerun attempts.
- 18 FRV routing/controller/nightly cases passed (5.65-second wrapper). Seventeen targeted planner, trusted-harness, and failed-preflight regression cases passed (33.57-second wrapper). The broader preliminary run exposed fixture/source-assertion mismatches; those were corrected and the affected cases rerun. No complete final-head broad-suite claim.
- Independent old/new comparison passed 22,878 actual YAML runner selections across all 38 runner-bearing CI jobs, preserving reachable ordinary/release, retry, fork, qualification, matrix, and dynamic RunsOn routes. The previous four-label selector was normalized to its equivalent unique campaign-capacity label.
- Scripts typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, workflow validation, and whitespace checks passed. Trusted dependency export was exercised through the owning harness.
- Independent P0–P2 review found the missing-map reservation issue; its regression failed before the fix and passed afterward. Fresh review returned no actionable findings.
- New regression cost: one table test exercises 12 job/status/reservation combinations, 83 ms measured body time (2.88-second standalone wrapper); about 0.083 CI compute seconds plus existing suite overhead, with no new workflow jobs.
- Live registration/access/cancellation and complete campaign proof remain separate, as below.

## Capacity and Cost

A prior campaign reached 402 non-skipped jobs outside CI, including 391 x64 Linux jobs and about 30.8 x64 Linux runner-hours. The CI graph adds roughly 217 jobs: plan for about 620 total, varying with inputs, skips, and retries. The controller limits concurrent leases, not total jobs.

Planning scenario: 620 jobs averaging ten minutes is 103.3 runner-hours. Assumed compute rates of $0.75–$1.50/hour imply roughly $78–$155, plus boot/idle time, storage, network, hosted coordination, and native-platform costs. These are assumptions, not measured Crabbox billing or an AWS quote.

## Remaining Live Proof

The agent with repository runner-administration access must verify registration/execution, real access restrictions against unrelated jobs, cancellation during warmup, late-child settlement, and cleanup. The earlier controller attempt reached AWS SSH but runner registration returned HTTP 403; that lease was released. Local routing/controller proofs do not establish live runner authorization or complete campaign execution. Campaign labels are routing selectors, not an authorization boundary.

On iOS, choosing 125% in Settings → Appearance → Text size does not carry over to the native chat. Returning to Settings after opening a chat shows 100% again because the settings web view was recreated with empty storage.

## Repair sweep — 2026-11-25

Addressed the checkout-test review findings: the executable trusted-preflight fixture now includes the routing module, and harness export checks evaluate the actual job `runs-on` expression before classifying the platform. This prevents Linux-only false coverage for Windows/macOS jobs.

Validation: reproduced the missing-module failure before the repair; six focused checkout/preflight cases pass (230 unrelated cases explicitly not selected). Touched tests pass type-aware lint, formatting and diff checks. A fresh local ClawSweeper review of the repair delta reports no findings.

**Still not merge-ready:** the branch's original runner-policy extraction conflicts with current main's subsequently changed Boat routing. This narrow review repair does not claim the old runner policy is equivalent to current main, nor that its existing integration conflicts are resolved. No runner registration, paid infrastructure, repository variables, or runner groups were changed. The dependent stack remains #173658.

---

## Original proposal and historical evidence

## What Problem This Solves

CI runner policy is duplicated in long `runs-on` expressions, making the workflow difficult to inspect and change.

## User Impact

No runner placement or CI coverage change. This is the first PR in a two-PR stack; Crabbox provisioning and Full Release Validation wiring belong exclusively to [#173658](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173658).

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing trusted preflight manifest resolves runner policy into named JSON selectors. Jobs consume a named JSON selector, choosing the initial or retry map using the current `github.run_attempt`. Preflight publishes both maps so partial reruns preserve existing hosted fallback even when successful preflight outputs are reused. Matrix jobs retain their task, capacity and dynamic RunsOn identities. Security and final gate jobs retain main's original fallback when preflight cannot publish its runner map. The trusted Git owner exports the new planner dependency; no additional planning job is introduced.

## Evidence

- Independent actual-YAML comparison: 56,640 runner selections match main, retaining successful preflight outputs across attempts 2 and 3 and covering failed-preflight/partial-output cases. Non-routing job commands, timeouts, dependencies, strategies and permissions are unchanged.
- Twenty focused routing, planner, trusted-export and failed-preflight cases passed with `--maxWorkers=1` (53.98-second wrapper). After the partial-rerun correction, five affected planner/export/fallback cases passed; the real-manifest retry regression passed separately (275 ms body, 6.09-second wrapper). Scripts and root test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, workflow validation and whitespace checks passed.
- New reservation regression: eight combinations in one table test (117 ms body time; about 0.117 CI compute seconds plus existing suite overhead), no additional CI jobs or processes. The retry regression uses one existing manifest fixture process (about 0.275 CI compute seconds plus suite overhead).
- No Crabbox inputs, registration, controller or campaign selectors are introduced here.

Review caught stale routing on partial reruns. The real-manifest regression failed before the fix (hybrid build retry incorrectly selected Blacksmith instead of hosted Ubuntu); jobs now choose the retry map without rerunning preflight.

prs.title: fix: /reasoning on makes Claude refuse every later turn as reasoning extraction until /new
prs.body:
Closes #205486

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after an owner turns reasoning visibility on with `/reasoning on` or `/reasoning stream`, every later turn on a Claude model (for example `claude-opus-5-5` on the claude-cli runtime) fails with Anthropic's `[reasoning_extraction]` refusal until `/new`.

## User Impact

User impact: `/reasoning on`, `stream` and `off` change only what OpenClaw shows, as the reasoning visibility docs describe, and Claude-backed sessions keep answering after the toggle. The command's acknowledgment and the saved setting are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Changing the level queued a system event, "Reasoning ON - include <think>.", into the next turn. For models with native thinking it was the only instruction to write reasoning out as visible text, which Anthropic refuses for the rest of the session. Models that use the `<think>` tag already get that rule from the system prompt on every turn, so the event added nothing for them. The directive no longer queues it. Elevated-mode events are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.model.test.ts`: the test that expected the `/reasoning stream` event now checks that `/reasoning on`, `stream` and `off` save the level and queue no system event, while `/elevated on` still queues its own. On the base commit it fails with `Reasoning ON - include <think>.` queued, the line from the report.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.mixed-inline.test.ts` counted that event after `/reasoning on`; it now expects none.
- `pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `directive-handling.model.test.ts` (45/45), `directive-handling.mixed-inline.test.ts` (19/19), `get-reply-directives-apply.test.ts` (14/14) and `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` (16/16) passes. `directive-handling.model.test.ts` takes about 75 seconds wall time locally with a warm transform cache (about 3.5 minutes cold); CI seconds to follow.

prs.title: fix(tool-usage): retention prune must not recreate missing registered agent databases
prs.body:
`pruneRegisteredAgentToolUsage` runs from Gateway maintenance and iterates every row in the agent database registry. Its `write` helper captures the execution with `"inherit"` creation and calls `execution.prepare()`, which creates the SQLite file when it is missing. A registered row whose database was deleted (for example a stale agent directory removed by hand) is recreated as an empty database on the next prune. If a cached handle for one such path exists, the later stat fails with ENOENT and aborts the loop for every remaining row.

The prune now writes in an existing-only mode. It captures without creation, skips `prepare()`, and treats an `undefined` result from `runExisting` as "nothing to prune". Flush, reset and import keep their creating behavior.

Adds a regression test that registers a missing database and asserts the prune leaves it missing. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.

Not addressed here: doctor only warns "Skipped missing registered agent database" and never removes the registry row, so stale rows persist until removed through `unregisterOpenClawAgentDatabase`.

prs.title: fix: let plugins retry model calls after a dropped connection
prs.body:
Supersedes #201536, which was closed without merging.

## What Problem This Solves

When a plugin makes a one-shot model request and the connection drops before the provider replies, OpenClaw can put a healthy credential on cooldown. A plugin that retries immediately gets a “temporarily unavailable” error instead of another connection. For a conversation summarizer, this can mean falling back to truncation.

## User Impact

Plugins can retry with the same credential after a confirmed pre-response disconnect. If another profile is configured, OpenClaw can still try it. Rate limits, authentication failures, billing failures, and timeouts after a response starts retain their existing cooldown behavior. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The one-shot completion path always told the shared health policy that the provider had started. It now uses the transport diagnostic, response ID, and partial content to distinguish a failed connection from a started response. A WebSocket failure followed by an SSE fallback is not treated as proof that the whole request failed before a response. The separate decision to advance to the next profile is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Both changed files, including the regression tests, are byte-for-byte identical to #201536 at `7dc6e68507f0`. On this replacement, the core TypeScript check, lint, format, and `git diff --check` passed. Auto Review found no P0 issues in the complete two-file change against `b2cef179b197`.
- In [the original Gateway run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201536), the first connection closed before headers; an immediate retry using the same profile returned HTTP 200 and `RECOVERED`. A 429 control still blocked the retry. The [original CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44866879512/job/136735559971) passed. These are prior results; the Gateway scenario and focused runtime tests were not rerun on this replacement.

Original fix, regression tests, and Gateway reproduction: @Marvinthebored (#201536).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b95e8e2d-102d-44a7-8acb-148f141f6fb7)

## Worked on by

- @Marvinthebored

prs.title: fix(ios): keep child sessions with their parent when moved
prs.body: Closes #198377 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: iOS children appear outside their parent family when stored child pins or groups differ from the parent. ## User Impact Families stay in their root's section in both the sidebar and Sessions screen. Child placement actions are unavailable; stored child metadata remains unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made - **Decision needed:** Should iOS replace independent child group placement with parent-owned family placement and remove child placement actions? **Author’s design:** Yes. Keep the family together so moving the parent moves the whole family. This deliberately replaces the independent child placement retained in #190403; it is not a claim of web parity. Stored child placement is preserved. The iOS owner still decides whether to ship this policy. - Align child pin controls with the root-only policy shipped in #140748. Family grouping also follows the parent rather than splitting descendants across sections. - Resolve the shared roster hierarchy before section placement, without applying sidebar status filters a second time. - Preserve stored child fields and existing recent-activity preview behavior; this is not a Gateway data migration. ### Child placement eligibility during search (f72edc1efc7) > Review [P2]: *Preserve child placement eligibility during sidebar search* (`RootSidebar.swift:686`). - Sidebar text search could remove a parent before building the tree, making a matching child appear eligible for Pin/Unpin and Move to Group. - The sidebar now derives menu eligibility from the unfiltered browsing tree, preserving existing Home and status promotion rules. - Regression: `RootTabsPresentationTests.sidebar search keeps child placement actions unavailable` covers a search matching only the child. - On the iOS simulator, the regression failed with the pre-fix depth policy and all 62 tests passed with the fix; SwiftFormat 0.63.1 lint passed on both changed files. ### Same-state upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.10 (iOS simulator, head 0ed88daf24f) > Review: *latest-stable-to-PR native upgrade proof*. Setup: one scratch Gateway, one fresh iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 27.2), paired once. The categories, pins and parent links live on the Gateway. Seeded over RPC: categories **Research** and **Delivery**; parent "Website refresh" pinned in Research; child "Landing page audit" with `parentSessionKey` set to the parent. | 1. Stable v2026.11.10 | 2. PR build installed over it | 3. PR build, parent moved to Delivery | |---|---|---| | | | | | Categories and pin present; the child is listed separately | Installed in place, with no erase, uninstall or re-pairing. Pairing and all Gateway data kept. The child is now indented under its parent | After `sessions.patch` moved only the parent, the child follows it into Delivery | Accessibility excerpt after the move: ```text StaticText identifier: 'SessionGroup.Header.Delivery', label: 'DELIVERY' Button label: 'Website refresh, just now' Button {22.0, 662.0} label: 'Landing page audit, 1 min. ago' # indented 12 pt under the parent ``` The organizer readback before and after the move keeps the pin, both session IDs and the child's parent link. The child's own category stays null, as expected for inherited placement. The Gateway hostname in the sidebar footer has been replaced with `gateway.example:8492` in all three captures. Limits: this was tested in the simulator against a scratch Gateway, not a physical phone. The step 3 capture was taken after a relaunch, with the app reading the moved state at launch. The PR build reports bundle version 2026.11.3 and stable reports 2026.11.10; versions are Info.plist metadata, so the commit is what identifies the build. ## Evidence - Regression verified red on the old implementation: 11 tests ran; the new test failed exactly its two placement assertions. After the fix, all 17 grouping/status-filter tests passed. - Native simulator proof passed one XCTest with lint enabled. It checks both child menus (Rename present; Pin, Unpin and Move to Group absent) and placement in Research. - Synthetic retained server metadata is tested, not an actual latest-stable binary upgrade. The stored pin badge can remain visible without owning placement. - AI-assisted implementation and two independent reviews; [redacted work record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0a9ea46c5b4e7c2b0ad69d685f8e319e1a4df675/WORK-RECORD.md) (summary, not a full transcript). ![Native family placement and child menu proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0a9ea46c5b4e7c2b0ad69d685f8e319e1a4df675/3A71B087-3EF0-4413-9F5C-A5A10ECFF47A.jpg) ![Native family placement and child menu proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0a9ea46c5b4e7c2b0ad69d685f8e319e1a4df675/C7C66171-EAC9-44B3-9539-54987CA30E71.jpg) ![Native family placement and child menu proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0a9ea46c5b4e7c2b0ad69d685f8e319e1a4df675/E9D225FF-BF6D-4B76-A283-D9A761EC380E.jpg) ![Native family placement and child menu proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/0a9ea46c5b4e7c2b0ad69d685f8e319e1a4df675/FEDCBC25-7C60-47A5-AF89-3CB4F8235E42.jpg)

prs.title: fix: preserve profiles when Linux onboarding cannot install the Gateway service
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Linux without a working user-systemd session, `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --install-daemon` can write config and create a workspace before exiting with a service-install error. If `--reset` is also requested, the reset can run before the same error is reported.

## What Changes

Check user-systemd availability before dispatching reset or setup, only for local, non-interactive Linux onboarding that explicitly requests daemon installation. Keep the installer's check in case availability changes after preflight. The error tells users to rerun with `--skip-daemon` or retry from a working user-systemd session.

## Evidence

### Behavior proof: real Linux CLI

Ran the CLI from this patch in an isolated Linux container with Node 24 and no working user-systemd session. The run used a disposable home, explicit config and state paths, and a dedicated workspace. Common options were `--non-interactive --accept-risk --mode local --auth-choice skip --skip-channels --skip-skills --skip-health --workspace "$workspace" --json`.

Captured terminal output from the Linux run (outer test script exited 0):

```text
ISOLATED_DEPS_READY
REFUSAL_EXIT=1
Cannot install the Gateway service: systemd user services are unavailable. Rerun with --skip-daemon for setup without a background service, or retry from a working user-systemd session.
FRESH_NO_CONFIG_OR_WORKSPACE
SKIP_DAEMON_CONTROL_OK
REFUSAL_EXIT=1
Cannot install the Gateway service: systemd user services are unavailable. Rerun with --skip-daemon for setup without a background service, or retry from a working user-systemd session.
RESET_CONFIG_AND_WORKSPACE_UNCHANGED
```

The harness parsed the CLI's JSON and printed the actual `message` only after asserting `ok: false`, `phase: "options"`, and `--skip-daemon` guidance. It asserted CLI exit 1 in both refusals. The named markers came from the harness, not the CLI; each printed only after these shell assertions passed:

| Scenario | Assertions behind the output |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh profile, `--install-daemon` | `test ! -e "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"` and `test ! -e "$workspace"`. |
| Same environment, `--skip-daemon` | CLI exit 0, then `test -s "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"` and `test -d "$workspace"`. |
| Existing profile, `--install-daemon --reset --reset-scope full` | Copied the config and added a workspace sentinel before invoking reset. `cmp` confirmed the config was byte-for-byte unchanged, and the sentinel still contained `sentinel`. |

For comparison, an earlier isolated Linux CLI run on unpatched `v2026.11.10-beta.3` reproduced the fresh-install bug: onboarding reported unavailable user systemd, but both the config and workspace were created. The runtime checks above cover the specified paths, not every possible filesystem side effect.

### Regression checks and limits

- On unpatched `main` (`5754fac480d8`), the new focused suite had **3 failures and 4 passes**: the probe was never called in the two refusal cases or in the supported local Linux case. With the patch, **45 tests across four focused onboarding suites passed**.
- The tests assert that neither reset nor setup is called on refusal. They also verify normal setup dispatch with a mocked working probe and no preflight for remote mode, daemon opt-out, an omitted daemon flag, or the covered macOS case.
- Core TypeScript, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Successful installation under a real user-systemd session was not exercised; the working-probe path was covered with mocks. The live Gateway was not touched.

Prepared with OpenClaw assistance.

## User Impact

Recognize the stored channel-delivery mirror on reload and use the completed, run-owned reply when choosing the answer to keep above Worked. The notice remains visible and tool activity keeps its existing collapsed treatment.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on `a1435125` in Chromium using the built Control UI and synthetic history supplied through a loopback Gateway fixture. Before the fix, the answer was hidden until Worked expanded. Afterward exactly one copy of the completed answer and the later notice were visible with Worked still collapsed.
- The production browser replay also covered marked and legacy Learned deliveries. All three scenarios passed. An independent Node rerun passed all 157 tests across the three focused suites. The regression checks a tool-activity control too.
- UI build, UI typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting and docs links passed. The stock and patched builds emitted the same report-only request and CSS budget warnings.

prs.title: fix(gateway): handle skipped start dates in trailing usage reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A trailing usage report could fail when its computed first date never occurred in the requested time zone. In Pacific/Apia, December 29, 2011 was followed by December 31. A two-day report on December 31 returned `INVALID_REQUEST` even though that day had usage.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the computed start of a trailing range is a skipped date, use the next civil day as the start. Callers that explicitly name a nonexistent date still receive the existing validation error.

## User Impact

Gateway-local and named-time-zone reports include usage from the days that occurred inside the requested window. This also covers presets such as a seven-day range whose first date was skipped.

## Evidence

- Replayed 620 trailing requests in four zones. The original code rejected 153 valid requests. All 620 passed with the fix.
- Exercised the registered `usage.cost` handler with synthetic report rows. The two-day Apia request returned the same three rows as December 31 alone. The one- and three-day controls, explicit skipped-date errors, UTC requests and repeated-midnight membership kept their original results.
- The focused Vitest regression failed in both time-zone modes on the parent. All five focused cases passed on the patched tree. Scoped formatting and lint passed.
- Hosted CI passed all 28 cases in the Gateway usage suite, including the skipped-day regression. The runtime and Control UI build passed. The local replay used synthetic report rows. [Gateway suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45615626331/job/139211230269) · [Protected CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45618564509)

prs.title: fix(ui): let Talk replies play after a stalled unlock clip
prs.body:
Closes #204390

## What Problem This Solves

Browser split Talk can stay silent after the Gateway returns a reply. A stalled silent unlock clip prevents the reply from playing and keeps the microphone from resuming.

## User Impact

A stalled unlock clip no longer blocks a reply indefinitely. Normal playback still uses the same gesture-primed audio element.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give the unlock clip one second to settle. On timeout, stop it and reset the element before loading the reply. Ignore a late primer completion so it cannot pause the reply.

## Evidence

Unit level: both regression cases failed on upstream main (no reply playback started after advancing the clock). With the fix, all 26 focused speech playback and split Talk tests passed, including the never-settling and late-settling cases. Scoped lint passed. Two independent code reviews found no blockers.

Real browser, native audio (added after review): the built Control UI at this head (`pnpm ui:build`) ships the fix in `control-ui-boot-shared-*.js` (the primer `new Audio(...)`, a `setTimeout` that pauses, removes `src` and reloads, and the `then` that clears the timer). I ran the playback owner, stock (parent of the first commit of this PR) and patched, in real Chromium 156 (headless, `--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required`) with a real `HTMLAudioElement` playing a real 0.8 s WAV reply through `GatewaySpeechPlayback.prepare()` then `speak()`, the same calls split Talk makes. Only the first `audio.play()` (the silent unlock clip) is replaced by a promise that never settles, to model the stall seen in headless Chromium in #204390; the reply `play()` is untouched. Wall time is measured from `prepare()`.

| build | primer | result |
|---|---|---|
| stock | normal | reply plays, `speak()` resolves after about 1.0 s |
| stock | stalled | `speak()` still pending after 8 s, reply never plays |
| patched | normal | reply plays, `speak()` resolves after about 0.95 s (no regression) |
| patched | stalled | reply starts at 1.04 s, ends 1.96 s, `speak()` resolves |

<details><summary>Raw output</summary>

```
browser: Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (headless, real HTMLAudioElement playback)

=== stock build, primer normal (wall 1053 ms) ===
1ms audio.play() #1 (primer) src=data:audio/wav;base6
2ms prepare() called (user gesture)
3ms talk.speak request
116ms reply element 'playing'
116ms play #1 resolved
119ms audio.play() #2 (reply) src=blob:null/7913f51f-3
139ms reply element 'playing'
139ms play #2 resolved
1042ms reply element 'ended'
1043ms speak() resolved (reply played to the end)

=== stock build, primer STALLED (wall 8016 ms) ===
0ms audio.play() #1 (primer) src=data:audio/wav;base6
0ms primer play() promise left pending (stalled)
0ms prepare() called (user gesture)
0ms talk.speak request
8005ms speak() STILL PENDING after 8 s

=== patched build, primer normal (wall 955 ms) ===
0ms audio.play() #1 (primer) src=data:audio/wav;base6
0ms prepare() called (user gesture)
1ms talk.speak request
5ms reply element 'playing'
5ms play #1 resolved
6ms audio.play() #2 (reply) src=blob:null/6cd25bde-e
11ms reply element 'playing'
11ms play #2 resolved
946ms reply element 'ended'
946ms speak() resolved (reply played to the end)

=== patched build, primer STALLED (wall 1971 ms) ===
0ms audio.play() #1 (primer) src=data:audio/wav;base6
0ms primer play() promise left pending (stalled)
0ms prepare() called (user gesture)
0ms talk.speak request
1011ms audio.play() #2 (reply) src=blob:null/3b70ace7-d
1040ms reply element 'playing'
1040ms play #2 resolved
1963ms reply element 'ended'
1963ms speak() resolved (reply played to the end)
```

</details>

Full split Talk turn (built Control UI, isolated Gateway, real microphone path): I created two throwaway Gateways on the same build, one serving this head's built Control UI (`pnpm ui:build`, via `gateway.controlUi.root`) and one serving the stock Control UI shipped in an earlier main build (its primer has no timeout). Both use a normal local setup: `parakeet-mlx` for speech-to-text and the `speech speak` local CLI for text-to-speech (`talk.realtime.mode: stt-tts`), and the default agent model. Headless Chromium 156 clicks "Start voice input" with its fake capture device playing a recorded spoken question ("What is the capital of France? Please answer in one short sentence."), so the real `getUserMedia` capture, `chat.send`, `talk.speak`, `HTMLAudioElement` playback and capture restart all run. The only injected fault is that the first `audio.play()` call (the silent unlock clip) returns a promise that never settles. Timestamps are ms since page load; only the first turn is relied on.

Stock UI, stalled unlock clip: the reply was synthesized but never played and the microphone was never restarted (log kept running 75 s):

```
6464ms UI served: stock; clicking 'Start voice input' (Talk, STT/TTS)
  6513ms audio.play() #1 (silent unlock clip)
  6513ms unlock clip play() promise left pending (injected stall)
  6650ms getUserMedia #1 (microphone capture started)
 15558ms gateway -> chat.send
 21661ms gateway <- chat final
 21671ms gateway -> talk.speak
 27422ms gateway <- talk.speak result (audio 326 KiB audio/wav)
```

This head, stalled unlock clip: the reply plays to the end and capture resumes:

```
6289ms UI served: patched; clicking 'Start voice input' (Talk, STT/TTS)
  6316ms audio.play() #1 (silent unlock clip)
  6317ms unlock clip play() promise left pending (injected stall)
  6430ms getUserMedia #1 (microphone capture started)
 17405ms gateway -> chat.send
 25358ms gateway <- chat final
 25373ms gateway -> talk.speak
 31837ms gateway <- talk.speak result (audio 529 KiB audio/wav)
 31837ms audio.play() #2 (reply)
 31840ms audio element 'playing' src=blob:http://
 43200ms audio element 'ended' src=blob:http://
 43251ms getUserMedia #2 (microphone capture RESUMED)
```

This head, no injected stall (no regression): the same loop completes.

```
6305ms UI served: patched; clicking 'Start voice input' (Talk, STT/TTS)
  6329ms audio.play() #1 (silent unlock clip)
  6429ms audio element 'playing' src=data:audio/w
  6494ms getUserMedia #1 (microphone capture started)
 18574ms gateway -> chat.send
 22634ms gateway <- chat final
 22664ms gateway -> talk.speak
 27787ms gateway <- talk.speak result (audio 264 KiB audio/wav)
 27787ms audio.play() #2 (reply)
 27789ms audio element 'playing' src=blob:http://
 33513ms audio element 'ended' src=blob:http://
 33607ms getUserMedia #2 (microphone capture RESUMED)
```

Limits: the stall is injected, not produced by the browser itself; the headless fake device stands in for a real microphone and speakers (it does not prove audible output); one run per variant, so no timing claim beyond "plays versus never plays".
