prs.title: fix: send the desktop and GitHub tools only after a chat first uses them
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

With Tool Search or Code Mode on (the default for OpenClaw's own runtime and for most frontier models), two heavy tools were still sent on **every** model request whether or not the chat ever used them: `computer` (desktop control) and `github_publish`. Together they were about 13k characters of tool definitions per request, and most of `github_publish`'s size was a long procedural manual in its description.

This PR makes both tools **load when the model looks them up, then stay direct**: they start in the Tool Search / Code Mode catalog with a short entry. When the model describes one (or tries to reach it through `dispatch_action`), the next request in the same turn carries its definition, so the model calls it as a normal direct tool, and the session keeps it for the rest of the conversation (across Gateway restarts). It also cuts `github_publish`'s description from about 6.1k to under 800 characters and moves each procedure into the result of the action where the model needs it.

User impact: a default unsandboxed session with Tool Search sends about 13k fewer characters (roughly 3.3k tokens) of tool definitions on every request until it actually uses one of these tools. Screenshots, the PR-preparation turn handoff and all Gateway checks behave as before.

### Root Cause

- `shouldCatalogTool` in `src/agents/tool-search-catalog.ts` keeps any `catalogMode: "direct-only"` tool out of the catalog, so it is sent on every request in every catalog mode.
- `computer` (`src/agents/tools/computer-tool.ts`) is direct-only because catalog bridges serialize nested results as JSON and drop the screenshot image block. It is built whenever the model has vision and a computer transport exists, whether or not anything is paired.
- `github_publish` (`src/agents/tools/github-publish-tool.ts`) is direct-only on unsandboxed sessions and sandboxed sessions that adopt a managed workspace, because `prepare_pr` / `publish` with `workspacePath` yield the turn and a Code Mode `exec` cannot carry that handoff. That marking was added by #178756 ("feat: prepare existing PRs from ordinary chats"); this PR keeps its handoff requirement and only changes when the definition is sent. Publication availability is set on essentially every non-detached Gateway turn (`attempt-gateway-tools.ts`), so every unsandboxed agent paid for it.
- `describeGitHubPublishTool` was a full manual (per-action workflows, requestId recovery, guest and maintainer eligibility, automations continuation, the re-review comment, landing policy): 6,129 of the tool's 7,161 definition characters.

Both reasons for direct-only are about how a call **runs** (result shape, turn handoff), not about whether the definition must be sent before the tool is ever used.

### What Changed

1. **New `catalogMode: "on-demand"`** (generic; only `computer` and the yielding `github_publish` listing use it in this PR):
   - The tool is cataloged with an `onDemand` descriptor fact; search, describe and directory entries carry `call: "loads as a top-level tool once looked up; call it by name, not through dispatch_action or exec"`, and directory rows are marked `[loads on lookup]`.
   - `dispatch_action` and Code Mode guest calls never run it: they load it and refuse with a message saying it is now a top-level tool to call by name (`ToolSearchRuntime.callEntry`), so screenshot results and turn handoffs only ever run through a direct call.
   - **Load on lookup.** `tool_describe` (and a refused `dispatch_action`) call the runner's `catalogRef.loadOnDemandTool`, which hydrates the entry, adds it to the run's context through a new agent-core `loadTool` hook on the tool execution context, so the next provider request in the same run sends it, and pins it for the session. A live test of the first version showed why this is needed: models do not call a tool that is missing from their tool list, so loading only on a call by name never fired.
   - The embedded runner's existing deferred-tool resolver (already used by `directory` mode) also hydrates an on-demand entry when the model calls it by name in `tools`, `directory` and Code Mode. The call is a normal direct tool call.
   - **The session's next-turn step keeps run-loaded tools.** `createSessionPrepareNextTurnWithContext` reset the tool list to the session's tools on a run's first continuation, which dropped a tool loaded during the first tool batch. It now keeps tools the run loaded for itself (marked by `appendRunContextTool`). This also keeps a resolved deferred tool for the rest of the run instead of re-resolving it on every call.
2. **Promotion lives in the existing session tool pin.** On hydration the definition is appended after the pinned tools (`promoteSessionTool`) and checkpointed with the existing `openclaw.system-prompt` transcript entry. On the next attempt the restored pin's names mark those on-demand tools direct before compaction (`promotedToolNames`), folded into the existing `installToolListingPin` catalog rebuild. No new state store.
   - Survives turns and Gateway restarts (transcript checkpoint).
   - `/new`, `/reset`, compaction and a model change start a new prompt series, so the tool is deferred again until its next use. Compaction was chosen as a reset point because it already rebuilds the provider cache and is where context is reclaimed.
   - Sessions pinned before this change already list both tools in their pin, so they stay direct for the rest of that series: no cache break on upgrade.
3. **Opt-in per runner.** Only the embedded attempt sets `loadsOnDemandTools`. Copilot, Codex app-server, cloud workers and headless catalogs cannot load a tool on its first direct call, so they keep on-demand tools direct exactly as today (Codex and Copilot catalogs treat `on-demand` like `direct-only`; the worker wire format maps it to `direct-only`). The flag is not part of the public plugin SDK parameters.
4. **Transport:** on-demand catalog names are passed as deferred tool names, so Chat Completions keeps history calls to them native inside the promoting turn.
5. **`github_publish` description:** a short summary plus one line per offered action (793 chars unsandboxed, 572 without publication, 252 observation-only). The moved guidance now arrives in a `next` field of each action's result (`github-publish-guidance.ts`), in both the text and `details`, because Code Mode guests receive only `details`; the Gateway payload's own fields are unchanged:
   - publish: accepted is not finished, retain requestId, never resubmit, continuation via automations;
   - readiness: never resubmit an accepted requestId;
   - edit read: send `headCommit` as `expectedHeadCommit` with the observed title/body, keep attribution and footer; edit write: read again after an uncertain response;
   - request_review: only `@clawsweeper re-review` was posted, read comments before retrying;
   - inspect: land only on an explicit request from a person with full operator write access, after review and required checks;
   - prepare_pr / refresh_base / upload_evidence / merge / close: their conflict, review-base and retry rules.
   Eligibility, write access and the busy refusals stay enforced and explained by the Gateway's existing checks and messages; nothing the Gateway enforces changed.

### Scope Boundary

- `openclaw` (security), `sessions_yield`, `view_image`, `structured_output`, `session_project` and the delegate tool stay `direct-only`.
- With Tool Search and Code Mode off, every tool is direct as before. The CLI/MCP and other harness paths are unchanged.
- The `message` tool schema work is a separate change and is not touched here.
- No Gateway, protocol schema, config or migration changes.

### Before / After

Real core tool construction (`createOpenClawCodingTools` with GitHub publication available, vision model) plus the real embedded surface runtime (`createAgentHarnessToolSurfaceRuntimeCore(...).compactTools`), default unsandboxed session, no plugins, isolated temp state dir. Sizes are JSON characters of `{ name, description, parameters }` of the provider-visible tools; tokens are chars / 4. Same script and environment on both revisions; sizes were identical across 5 samples per arm.

| | origin/main `328a438` | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Tool Search `tools` mode, always-sent tool chars | 27,411 (~6,853 tok) | 14,236 (~3,559 tok) |
| Code Mode, always-sent tool chars | 20,084 (~5,021 tok) | 6,909 (~1,727 tok) |
| `github_publish` definition chars | 7,161 | 1,821 |
| `github_publish` description, unsandboxed / no publication / observation-only | 6,129 / 2,775 / 500 | 793 / 572 / 252 |
| `computer` definition chars | 6,014 (always sent) | 6,014 (sent only after first use) |
| Catalog compaction per call, both modes (3 alternating rounds × 500 iterations, 20 warmup) | 0.175–0.207 ms | 0.231–0.262 ms |

The compaction step costs about 0.05 ms more per attempt because the catalog now holds two more large schemas. It runs once per attempt preparation; it is not whole-turn latency.

**Prompt cache:** the provider tool list changes once, on the request right after the lookup (same turn), by appending the definition after the existing tools; the session pin carries the same order into later turns, so the list then stays byte-identical for the rest of the series. Anthropic `defer_loading` tool references were not used: OpenClaw's Anthropic transport has no support for them, and adding it is a provider-transport feature beyond this change.

<details><summary>Measurement commands and environment</summary>

Linux x64, Node v24.22.1, one host, no Gateway, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` forced to a fresh temp directory by the script.

```bash
# baseline: a detached worktree of origin/main with dependencies installed
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/on-demand-tool-surface-measure.ts --root /path/to/base-checkout --samples 5 --iterations 500
# this PR
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/on-demand-tool-surface-measure.ts --root . --samples 5 --iterations 500
```

</details>

## Verification

Regression tests (each fails on origin/main behavior; checked by reverting both tools to `direct-only` and by disabling the restore step):

- `src/agents/tool-search.on-demand.test.ts`: in `tools`, `directory` and Code Mode, a default run's direct surface excludes `computer` and `github_publish` and the catalog holds both; a promoted tool is direct and out of the catalog; a runner without the opt-in and a headless catalog keep them direct; `tool_search` shows the call hint; `dispatch_action` and Code Mode guest calls refuse; the `tools` and `directory` prompt directories mark on-demand rows `[call directly]` and exempt them from the `dispatch_action` rule, and the Code Mode index marks them `[top-level call only; not from exec]`.
- `attempt-deferred-tool-resolver.test.ts`: through the real agent loop, in Tool Search `tools` mode and Code Mode, a direct call by name loads the deferred tool, the screenshot image block survives in the tool result, and promotion is recorded.
- `attempt-session-runtime-prepare.on-demand.test.ts` (shares its SQLite session fixture with the existing history-boundary test through `attempt-session-runtime-prepare.test-support.ts`): real SQLite-backed session manager plus real tool construction, catalog and attempt preparation, both Tool Search and Code Mode. Turn 1 does not send `github_publish`; after its first direct call it is sent on the next turn and after another restart, and compaction (Tool Search case) or `/reset` (Code Mode case) defers it again. The transport receives its name as a deferred tool, and 11 consecutive calls to it before its definition is sent pass the stream's unknown-tool guard (threshold 10) instead of being rewritten into a refusal on the 11th.
- `github-publish-tool.handoff.test.ts`: the `prepare_pr` / `workspacePath` turn handoff runs through the promoted direct tool in Code Mode.
- `github-publish-tool.test.ts`: description length bounds, and the old description's key guidance (requestId retention and no resubmission, read before edit, re-review wording, landing rules) arrives in the matching action results, with text and `details` carrying the same `next` and the Gateway payload's fields intact.
- `code-mode.github-publish.test.ts`: the real `github_publish` tool (managed-worktree sandbox) called from Code Mode guest code returns the receipt with its `requestId` and the publish `next` guidance in the guest value.
- `src/gateway/github-pr-workspace-preparation.test-support.ts`: the `prepare_pr` result still matches the Gateway result schema once `next` is set aside.

- `tool-search.on-demand.test.ts` (load on lookup): `tool_describe` and a refused `dispatch_action` call the runner's loader and the refusal names the direct call; `tool_search` alone does not load.
- `agent-session-loop-next-turn.test.ts`: through a real session, a tool loaded during the first tool batch is sent with the next request. It fails on the old next-turn step and on an agent loop without the `loadTool` hook.

Test-line budget: +449 net test lines against the 400 allowance, with a 49-line record in `config/test-lines-allocations/204805-on-demand-tool-loading.txt`. Before the allocation the suite was consolidated: table-driven Tool Search / directory / Code Mode / no-opt-in cases, one SQLite session fixture shared with the existing history-boundary test, one table of `github_publish` result guidance, reset coverage folded into the SQLite restart test instead of a separate prompt-state case, and a dropped `session-tool-listing` case that duplicated it. The remaining 27 lines are the three review regressions (11-call stream guard, real-tool Code Mode guidance, prompt-directory marker); cutting them would remove coverage for those fixes. `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passes.

Broader runs: 168 affected test files (Tool Search, Code Mode, prompt state, attempt preparation and streaming, system prompt, computer, github_publish and PR workspace preparation, registration, Copilot tool bridge, Codex dynamic tools, worker computer surfaces): 167 files passed. The one failing file, `src/agents/system-prompt-params.test.ts`, fails three repository-discovery cases only because this host's test temp directory sits inside an unrelated git checkout, so "no repository" discovery finds that checkout; this PR does not touch that code. `pnpm check:changed` passed with the dead-export scan skipped; that scan fails identically on origin/main on unused exports in `extensions/beam`, which this PR does not touch.

Review: `$autoreview` (Codex, branch mode against origin/main, P0–P1): scoped-clean, no findings, on the first version. The load-on-lookup follow-up (`fix: load on-demand tools when the model looks them up`) was self-reviewed; `pnpm check:changed` passed on it (dead-export scan skipped for the same unrelated `extensions/beam` failure), and the 48 affected test files (808 tests) pass.

### Real behavior proof

**Live run on a real Gateway (this PR applied to current main, Tool Search `tools` mode, Opus 5.5 on the direct Anthropic API route, fresh session):** asked to inspect this PR read-only with the GitHub tool, the model called `tool_describe` for `github_publish`, received the short description with `call: "loads as a top-level tool once looked up; ..."`, then called `github_publish` directly in the next request of the same run (`{action: "inspect_pr", pullRequestUrl: ...}`). The Gateway returned the PR's state, author, base and head (head commit matched this branch) plus `next: "This read binds nothing and grants no later authority."`, and the model answered correctly. Nothing was written to GitHub.

Two earlier live runs found the two gaps this PR now closes: the first version loaded the tool only on a call by name, which models do not make for an undeclared tool (the model ran `tool_describe`, tried `dispatch_action`, was refused, and gave up); the second loaded it on lookup, but the embedded runner's continuation resent the session's tool list and dropped it until the next turn. `fix: load on-demand tools when the model looks them up` and `fix: keep a looked-up tool for the rest of the run` fix those, each with a regression test that fails on the previous code.

**Upgrade:** the same Gateway was updated in place from v2026.11.9 (and from earlier revisions of this PR) to current main with this PR. Existing sessions kept working after the restart; sessions pinned before the change keep both tools direct until their next reset, so their provider tool list does not change on upgrade.

The closest feasible path without a live Gateway or model: the real attempt preparation with a real SQLite session transcript (`attempt-session-runtime-prepare.on-demand.test.ts`), and the real agent loop with the real deferred-tool resolver (`attempt-deferred-tool-resolver.test.ts`), shown above. Sizes come from the real tool factories and the real surface runtime.

## What was not tested

- Live, first version: with Opus 5.5 on the API route in Tool Search `tools` mode, the model ran `tool_describe` for `github_publish`, would not call the undeclared tool by name, tried `dispatch_action`, was refused, and gave up. That is the gap the load-on-lookup follow-up closes. A live retest of the final version passed (see Real behavior proof).
- No measured provider cache hit/miss; the one-change claim comes from the asserted pinned tool order across turns and restarts, not from provider usage numbers.
- No isolated Gateway end-to-end run through a chat channel.
- Promotion recorded during a turn that crashes before its checkpoint is written is lost; the model loads the tool again on its next use (accepted, visible and recoverable).

prs.title: fix(doctor): source-checkout Gateway advice no longer demands replacement
prs.body:
Closes #205413

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` detected a Gateway service running from a source checkout, but the same panel unconditionally told every operator to replace the service definition. A source-checkout service is a supported setup, so that advice pushed intentional installs toward an unnecessary repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The source-checkout warning now keeps the resolved path visible and makes the replacement command conditional:

- No action is needed when the checkout is intentional.
- The force-install command is only suggested for operators who expected the service to use a different installation.

Entrypoint mismatch detection, audit findings, and repair behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators running a deliberate source checkout see an informational explanation instead of a repair instruction. Operators who actually need to switch installations still get the exact command and destination guidance.

## Evidence

- Updated the Gateway service config regression in `src/commands/doctor-gateway-services.test.ts`. It asserts the conditional wording and that the old unconditional replacement sentence is gone.
- Focused Vitest after rebasing on `main`:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-gateway-services.test.ts` — 48 passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental` passed.
- `oxfmt --check`, `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, and `git diff --check` pass on the changed files.
- The fixture supplies the source-checkout layout directly; no live systemd service was created for this wording-only change.

prs.title: fix: keep the realtime provider's own error in the Gateway log
prs.body:
Closes #204633

## What Problem This Solves

When a gateway-relay Talk session's realtime provider fails after its socket opens, the client receives only the bounded text "Realtime provider error." and the Gateway writes nothing about the provider's own reason. Neither the client nor the operator can tell a key without realtime access from a provider outage or a rejected session setting, and the failure leaves no line to grep for.

## User Impact

User impact: a Talk session that fails at the provider now leaves one Gateway warning line naming the provider error, its code and its message, so an operator can see why the session could not start. Clients keep the same bounded issue text; key-like tokens are redacted from the logged line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The relay's `onError` path projected the provider error through the bounded client issue and dropped the detail. It now logs one line with the provider error name, code and message through the existing sensitive-text redaction, then emits the unchanged bounded issue to the client. The regression test lives in its own sibling file because `index.test.ts` is at its line cap.

## Evidence

**Behavior checked:** with a scripted gateway-relay provider whose `onError` carries `invalid_request_error: upstream rejected the realtime session`, the Gateway logs `Realtime relay provider error during connect: Error invalid_request_error: upstream rejected the realtime session`, the client projection still never contains the provider text, and a message quoting an `sk-` key is logged with the key removed.

Base-red, `328a43818a1` (`upstream/main` source, new test kept), `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/talk/relay/session-create.provider-error-log.test.ts`:

```text
 x ... keeps the provider's own error in the Gateway log while the client gets the bounded issue
 x ... redacts key-like tokens from the logged provider error
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed (2)
```

The relay error path emitted the bounded client issue and wrote nothing to the Gateway log.

Fix head, same command:

```text
 v ... keeps the provider's own error in the Gateway log while the client gets the bounded issue 1749ms
 v ... redacts key-like tokens from the logged provider error 59ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

Existing relay suite on the fix head, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/talk/relay/index.test.ts`:

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  113 passed (113)
```

`pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on the three changed files reports `All matched files use the correct format.`; `git diff --check` is clean.

**Not run / gaps:**

- No live OpenAI realtime key was used: the proof drives the relay's provider `onError` callback through the existing scripted transport, not a real provider rejection.
- Fork PR CI needs a maintainer to approve the run, so it has not run.

prs.title: fix: reconcile subagent completion after successful settlement
prs.body:
Related: #201339

## What Problem This Solves

After a requester yield batch successfully hands off a child result, the stored child run can still report a permanent delivery failure. The settle wake is then cleared even though the result reached the requester.

## User Impact

Successful requester handoffs are recorded as delivered, so monitoring and the Subagents list no longer retain a stale permanent-failure result for that run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The requester-batch mutation now reconciles a suspended permanent failure only when the settlement outcome confirms delivery and the row still owns the requester yield batch. Other unsuccessful or ambiguous outcomes keep their existing handling.

## Evidence

Result: on head `b4d0cc993f6612ea0752648da60209c2c24d883f` (rebased onto `main` `feea72c1863`), a permanently suspended completion that still owns its requester yield batch settles as delivered, and the unfixed base keeps `permanent_failure`.

Focused regression:

- Base `feea72c1863` with the fix reverted: `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-requester-delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` reports `Tests 1 failed | 10 passed (11)`. The new case fails with the stored delivery still at `"disposition": "permanent_failure"`.
- Head `b4d0cc993f66`: the same command reports `Tests 11 passed (11)` in one file, including `marks a permanently suspended completion delivered after its owned yield batch succeeds`.

Existing-data check: a `subagent_runs` row persisted by the unfixed build at `feea72c1863` is reopened by the fixed build and settled through the production requester-batch mutation. Observed output:

```json
{"readBeforeSettle":{"delivery":{"status":"suspended","suspendedReason":"permanent_failure"},"hasWake":true},"mutationStats":{"settled":1},"readAfterSettle":{"delivery":{"status":"delivered","disposition":"delivered","deliveredAt":300},"hasWake":false}}
```

The patch changes no schema or migration, and the pre-fix row loads and resolves with the fixed build.

Gateway handoff regression: `pnpm test extensions/qa-lab/src/plugin-subagent-current-requester.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 2/2 on this head. That suite runs a real Gateway child with the qa-channel transport and the scripted `mock-openai` provider, covering `sessions_spawn` followed by `sessions_yield` requester delivery to the originating conversation. It is regression coverage for this owner, not the suspended-permanent-failure reconciliation itself.

Checks: targeted `run-format.mts --check` passes on both touched files, and `git -c core.whitespace=cr-at-eol diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes.

Boundary: this proves the production SQLite mutation, persisted-row readback, and the real Gateway spawn/yield handoff path, not a live-model run that reaches the suspended-permanent-failure settlement. No model provider is configured in this environment, so that specific handoff and the Subagents-list rendering remain unproven here, and fork CI still needs maintainer approval to execute.

prs.title: fix(process): bare session IDs no longer report a false Gateway restart
prs.body:
Closes #205410

## What Problem This Solves

`process` only matched the full `slug:boot` session ID. Agents naturally pass the readable slug from the exec receipt, so a session that was still tracked looked lost. The error then blamed a Gateway restart that never happened and suggested rerunning the work.

A missing handle from the current boot had the same restart claim even when it had simply been removed or expired.

## Why This Change Was Made

`missingProcessMessage` now separates the three cases:

- A bare slug is not a lookup key. The message points at `process list` to recover the tracked ID.
- A handle with a different boot suffix keeps the existing restart-and-rerun guidance.
- A missing handle from the current boot reports removal or scope without claiming a restart.

Exact-match lookup is unchanged. There is still no automatic prefix resolution, so the boot suffix keeps protecting against stale-handle reuse.

## User Impact

Agents and operators who pass the readable part of a session ID get an actionable message instead of a phantom restart. Stale handles from an older boot keep the existing recovery guidance.

## Evidence

- Added `src/agents/bash-process-id.test.ts` covering a bare slug, an older boot suffix, and a current-boot ID.
- Updated the process-tool regression expectations in `src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts`.
- Focused Vitest after rebasing on `main`:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-process-id.test.ts` — 3 passed.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.process.poll-timeout.test.ts` — 22 passed.
  - `src/agents/bash-tools.process.scope.test.ts` — 3 passed before rebase; it covers the unchanged older-boot branch.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental` passed.

prs.title: improve: reduce Gateway presence broadcast allocations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Roster updates can allocate and serialize a full reset for every audience even when all recipients can apply a small delta. The Team heap profile attributed 1.51 MB of sampled allocation over 30 seconds to presence delivery preparation.

## User Impact

Gateway presence broadcasts allocate less. Matching recipients get the same payload bytes, and the projection still checks each recipient's current session visibility. Heartbeats, thaw refreshes, reconnect resets, and the fixed 200 ms publication window keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The publisher supplies one frozen wrapper. The delivery owner shares the legacy payload fragment and delta/reset bytes by the existing audience and baseline. A small delta can be proven shorter than any reset without serializing the reset. The exact-size fallback preserves the same reset selection at the boundary. The general broadcaster keeps its existing per-send behavior for custom fields and getters.

## Evidence

Five synthetic baseline/candidate/baseline triplets, with 80 recipients and 3,000 timed flushes each. A baseline is cleared every 50 flushes. Aggregate wire bytes and digests matched in all runs.

| Per flush | Baseline | Candidate | A/A control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Collection-inclusive sampled allocation | 308,696 B | 220,782 B | 309,791 B |
| Median CPU | 104.28 µs | 59.30 µs | 102.92 µs |
| Wall median / p95 | 104.27 / 111.24 µs | 59.32 / 61.64 µs | 102.92 / 106.50 µs |

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/presence-delivery-measure.ts --recipients 80 --reset-interval 50`. Add `--allocations` for the separate sampling pass. Results isolate preparation from socket I/O, and the existing transport fixtures exercise wire delivery.

The focused Gateway suites passed 53 tests. A real isolated Gateway sent the expected frames to all 80 sockets on initial connection and five reconnect waves. The affected Control UI browser test and both presence E2E tests passed. The delta regression fails on the base and passes with the change. The transport regression also exercises live per-recipient visibility with shared payload fragments. The publisher test confirms that idle intervals do not schedule another flush.

Production +36 LOC and tests +2 LOC. The added production logic keeps the exact delta/reset cutoff and preserves existing broadcaster behavior for caller-supplied fields, getters, and serialization hooks.

prs.title: fix(config): record the calling client on config.write audit records
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The config audit journal records the *writer process* for every `config.write` event. For Gateway-mediated writes that process is always the Gateway itself, so `pid`, `argv` and `cwd` identify the daemon but never the caller. A measured example from a live deployment:

```
ts 2026-11-05T23:50:59.242Z, pid 1464, ppid 339,
argv "node …/dist/index.js gateway --port 18789", cwd /home/wayne,
origin "config-rpc", changedPathCount 29, result "rename"
```

Twenty-nine config paths changed and the record cannot say who asked for it. That makes the journal useless for the question an audit trail exists to answer: which client changed this file.

Upstream already computes the answer — `resolveControlPlaneActor(client)` produces `{actor, deviceId, clientIp, connId}` in `src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts` — but that value reaches a log line and never the durable record. This PR carries it into the journal.

## The change

- **`src/config/io.types.ts`** — new `ConfigWriteAuditActor` and `ConfigWriteOptions.auditActor`.
- **`src/config/io.audit.ts`** — `createConfigWriteAuditRecordBase()` takes a single `attribution` object holding origin and optional actor, and emits each key only when present. A write with no client keeps the record byte-shape identical. One object rather than two separate parameters also keeps `io.write.ts` inside its 700-line cap without adding a line.
- **`src/config/io.write.ts`** — passes `attribution` through from the write options.
- **`src/gateway/server-methods/config-write-flow.ts`** — `commitGatewayConfigWrite` takes an optional `actor` and sets `auditActor` on the `config-rpc` write options.
- **`src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts`** — `config.set` and the apply/patch restart path pass the actor they already resolve.

## Evidence

**Tests — 151 passed / 3 files, exit 0** across `src/config/io.write-config.test.ts`, `src/config/io.audit.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts`.

**Falsifiers.** Each was applied, run, and reverted; each reddens exactly one test:

| mutation | reddens |
|---|---|
| drop `actor: options.auditActor` in `io.write.ts` | "persists the audit actor on the config.write journal record" |
| drop the call-site actor in `config.ts` | "config.set passes the calling client to the write as an audit actor" |
| drop the `auditActor` spread in `config-write-flow.ts` | the round-trip arm |

The no-client arm stays green under all three, which is the point: a write with no client must leave the record unchanged.

**Lint and types.** `oxlint` on every touched file: 0 errors. `format:check` clean. `tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit`: zero errors in any file this PR touches.

**Line budgets.** `io.write.ts` and `config.ts` are both inside the `max-lines` ratchet, which forbids growth on grandfathered files. `io.write.ts` is line-neutral (the single `attribution` object exists for this reason). The two required `actor:` call-site lines are offset by extracting `stripBundledProviderRuntimeDefaults` into `src/gateway/server-methods/config-provider-defaults.ts`, taking `config.ts` from 984 counted lines to 935 — a reduction, not a baseline bump.

**Unrelated failure, disclosed.** `src/commands/doctor-model-metadata-corruption.persistence.test.ts` fails on the machine this was developed on with "No safe OpenClaw temp root is available" caused by a group-writable jiti cache under a permissive umask. It fails identically with this patch stashed. The fix belongs to the temp-root guard, not to this PR.

prs.title: fix(workboard): preserve oversized stored proof notes on lifecycle updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A stored Workboard **proof note** longer than 2000 characters makes the card it belongs to permanently immutable.

`normalizeProof()` reads stored proof records through `normalizeProofInput()`, which bounds `note` at 2000 characters with `normalizeBoundedString()` and **throws**. Every card mutation re-normalizes the whole card before saving, so a single legacy over-cap note makes `update`, `addComment`, `addProof`, `move`, `reassign` and `complete` fail with:

```
proof note must be 2000 characters or fewer (got N)
```

where **N is the length of the stored note**, not of the payload being sent. The value cannot be corrected through the API, because the failing check happens on the read path before any write.

This is the same defect #154958 fixed for comments (issue #163552): lifecycle updates must preserve stored text, and only new or edited values need validation. That fix special-cased `normalizeComment()` against the stored comment list; the proof path kept the unconditional bound, so the proof half of the bug is still live on `main`.

### Change

- `normalizeProof()` now receives the stored proof list and passes the matching stored proof to `normalizeProofInput()`.
- `normalizeProofInput()` keeps an unchanged note verbatim and only bounds notes that are new or edited. The write path (`addProof`, `addProofWithArtifact`) passes no stored proof, so new and edited notes keep the existing 2000-character validation exactly as before.
- The proof normalizers move to `store-proof-normalizers.ts` and the shared primitives to `store-normalizer-primitives.ts`, because `store-normalizers.ts` is over the `max-lines` cap and the ratchet rejects any growth.

## Evidence

Reproduced on a gateway running `2026.10.10-beta.3`, where this fix is carried as a local patch:

1. Seed a card with a stored proof whose `note` is 2001 characters.
2. `store.update(cardId, { title: "..." })` → `Error: proof note must be 2000 characters or fewer (got 2001).`
3. With the patch applied, the same update succeeds, the stored note is preserved byte-for-byte, and a **new** over-cap note is still rejected with the same message.

The regression test seeds the legacy row through the persistence owner (`stores.cards.register`), below new-input validation, mirrors the existing `store.dispatch-comment-limit.test.ts` for the comment half, and asserts all three behaviours: preserved on update, preserved when a new proof is added, rejected when the note is new or edited.

Run locally:

```
pnpm vitest run extensions/workboard/src/store.oversized-stored-proof.test.ts
```

This clone is a sparse checkout without `node_modules`, so the test could not be executed here — CI is the gate for this change. `oxfmt` was applied at the repo-pinned version.

prs.title: fix(meeting): give the pulse capture source its own name
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Linux with **PulseAudio**, `openclaw teamsmeetings setup` always fails exactly one check:

```json
{ "id": "chrome-local-audio-device", "ok": false,
  "message": "OpenClaw PipeWire-Pulse sink or monitor source was not created." }
```

even though both modules load successfully.

Root cause: PulseAudio keeps **one name registry shared by sinks and sources**. `module-remap-source source_name=openclaw_meeting_audio` cannot take the sink's name, so PulseAudio creates the source as `openclaw_meeting_audio.2`; `ensureMeetingAudioBackend()` then lists sources and requires the **exact** name, never finds it, and throws. PipeWire's pulse server tolerates the sink/source name collision, which is why this only bites PulseAudio (WSLg, plain pulseaudio on Linux desktops).

Fix: the capture source gets its own name, `openclaw_meeting_audio_in`. The sink name, the human-facing device label (`device.description` = "OpenClaw Meeting Audio") and the `parec`/`pacat` command shape are unchanged; the capture device derives from the same constant, so there is still one place to change.

## Evidence

Reproduced on WSL2 (PulseAudio via WSLg) with a controlled pair:

- `module-null-sink sink_name=zz_ns_test` + `module-remap-source source_name=zz_ns_test` (same name) → `pactl list short sources` shows `zz_ns_test.2`; the exact name never appears.
- The host had left `openclaw_meeting_audio.2`, `.3` and `.4` behind from three earlier setup attempts — the same signature.

After the change:

- the source is created as exactly `openclaw_meeting_audio_in`;
- `parec --device=openclaw_meeting_audio_in --raw --format=s16le --rate=24000 --channels=1` captured 43 KB in 3 s;
- `pacat --playback --device=openclaw_meeting_audio` played cleanly (both exits were only the 3 s test timeout).

Tests: the new `uses distinct pulse device names for capture and playback` fails on the old constant (both commands pointed at `--device=openclaw_meeting_audio`) and passes with the fix; the `configured-node-host.test.ts` fixtures are updated for the new source name. `oxfmt@0.72.0` applied.

Not run locally: `vitest` — this working copy is a sparse `blob:none` clone with no `node_modules`, so CI is the gate.


## Real behaviour proof (shipped entry point, 2026-10-17)

Box: WSL2 (`6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`), PulseAudio via WSLg — the same machine that hit the failure.

### 1. After the change: `teamsmeetings setup` is green and the capture device is distinct

```
$ openclaw teamsmeetings setup --mode agent
{ "ok": true, "checks": [
    { "id": "chrome-profile",              "ok": true, "message": "Local Chrome uses the configured OpenClaw browser profile" },
    { "id": "guest-join",                  "ok": true, "message": "Guest name, auto-join, and tab reuse are configured" },
    { "id": "captions",                    "ok": true, "message": "Caption scraping is not used by talk-back modes" },
    { "id": "audio-bridge",                "ok": true, "message": "Command-pair audio bridge configured (pcm16-24khz)" },
    { "id": "chrome-local-audio-device",   "ok": true, "message": "Virtual meeting audio backend is ready" },
    { "id": "chrome-local-audio-commands", "ok": true, "message": "Configured Chrome audio commands are available" } ] }

$ pactl list short sources | grep openclaw
3  openclaw_meeting_audio.monitor  module-null-sink.c     s16le 2ch 48000Hz  SUSPENDED
5  openclaw_meeting_audio_in       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  IDLE
$ pactl list short sinks | grep openclaw
2  openclaw_meeting_audio          module-null-sink.c     s16le 2ch 48000Hz  IDLE
```

Before this change the same check reported `✗ Virtual meeting audio backend not ready` on this host, with `openclaw_meeting_audio.2/.3/.4` left behind by earlier attempts.

### 2. The collision, reproduced with the exact `pactl` call the pre-fix backend makes

Same box, sink already holding the name:

```
$ pactl load-module module-remap-source master=openclaw_meeting_audio.monitor \
      source_name=openclaw_meeting_audio rate=48000 channels=2 remix=no
25
$ pactl list short sources | grep openclaw
3  openclaw_meeting_audio.monitor  module-null-sink.c     s16le 2ch 48000Hz  RUNNING
5  openclaw_meeting_audio_in       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  SUSPENDED
6  openclaw_meeting_audio.2       module-remap-source.c  s16le 2ch 48000Hz  IDLE

exact-name matches for "openclaw_meeting_audio" among sources: 0
what PulseAudio actually created:                            openclaw_meeting_audio.2
```

That is precisely the predicate `pulseListContains(PIPEWIRE_SOURCE_NAME)` evaluates after module loading — so it fails, and the module was in fact created successfully. (Module 25 unloaded immediately afterwards.)

### 3. Re-running over an existing install keeps devices and settings (the upgrade case)

```
before: 1 remap source, guestName="Juno (OpenClaw notes)"
$ openclaw teamsmeetings setup --mode agent      # devices + settings already present
  ... 6 checks, "ok": true, "ok": true (overall)
after:  1 remap source                            # no duplicate module, nothing orphaned
```

### Scope of this proof

The `teamsmeetings setup` checks execute inside the running OpenClaw service, so the transcript in §1 comes from a build with exactly this one-line change applied to the installed bundle — I cannot show a pre-fix CLI transcript without restarting that service onto an unpatched build, so §2 gives the pre-fix side as the raw `pactl` reproduction plus the exact-name predicate instead of a fabricated failure transcript.

### On the added test

The existing raw-command-pair test asserts each command against the same two constants, so it would still pass if both constants were collapsed back into one shared name — the failure mode this PR fixes. The added test asserts the invariant directly (capture name ≠ playback name) and is the only guard on it.

### 4. Upgrade from a pre-fix install with legacy devices present

A 2026.10.4 install leaves the colliding remap sources behind (`openclaw_meeting_audio.2`, `.3`). Reproduced exactly, on the same host, with the same `pactl` call the pre-fix backend makes; then the fixed setup was run on top:

prs.title: fix: keep warmed cloud worker reserves through transient capacity-check failures
prs.body:
Closes #204616

## What Problem This Solves

With standing image capacity configured under `cloudWorkers.preparedPool`, the prepared-pool maintenance pass reads demand through `presence.current()`. That read swallows every error from the standing-image admission check and returns the same value it returns when there is genuinely no demand. The pass therefore treats a ready reserve with an unbounded deadline as superseded, writes a durable destroy intent, and the lifecycle tears the warm worker down. A transient failure — image profile or provider resolution, the live image-policy assertion, or an admitted intent that is momentarily not current — destroys warmed capacity and forces cold re-provisioning, which contradicts the comment next to the read that unavailable policy never expires inventory.

## User Impact

User impact: a momentarily unavailable capacity check no longer destroys warmed cloud-worker reserves. The pass reports one line, keeps the inventory, and retries the observation on its next maintenance run. Reserves whose finite deadline has passed are still retired, and no new capacity is granted from an unreadable observation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The presence read now returns an observation that separates a known demand from an unreadable one instead of flattening both into `undefined`. `current()` keeps its previous shape for consumers that only need the best known demand, and `runPreparedPoolPass` consumes `observe()`.

An unreadable observation proves neither presence nor absence, so it only holds back the two decisions that depend on it: demand-based supersession of a presence-owned reserve, and refill planning. Expiry, requested cleanup, disabled-capacity and surplus limits still run in the same early cleanup stage they ran in before, including for a reserve whose finite deadline passed during the outage. Unknown demand still refuses new capacity; it can no longer revoke inventory it cannot evaluate.

## Evidence

**Behavior checked:** with one ready standing image reserve (`purpose: "reserve"`, `expiresAtMs: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`), a second reserve whose finite deadline has passed, and a demand validator that starts throwing: the standing reserve stays `ready` with no destroy request, the expired reserve is still retired and destroyed, and the pass warns once.

Regression test: `src/gateway/worker-environments/prepared-pool-empty-workspace.test.ts` → `retains standing image reserves while demand validation is unavailable`, run with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/worker-environments/prepared-pool-empty-workspace.test.ts -t "retains standing image reserves"`.

base, `15b7df38086` (`upstream/main`, whole fix reverted, regression test kept):

```text
 → expected { ...(26) } to match object { state: 'ready', ...(1) }
 FAIL  src/gateway/worker-environments/prepared-pool-empty-workspace.test.ts > empty workspace prepared worker reserves > retains standing image reserves while demand validation is unavailable
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 6 skipped (7)
```

previous head, `6e4bf1a482f` (review finding: demand-unavailable pass skipped independent expiry cleanup):

```text
 × ... retains standing image reserves while demand validation is unavailable
 AssertionError: expected { ...(26) } to match object { state: 'destroyed', ...(1) }
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 6 skipped (7)
```

current head, `84fbaa85aaa`, same command:

```text
 ✓ ... retains standing image reserves while demand validation is unavailable
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 6 skipped (7)
```

neighboring owner suites on the current head (`prepared-pool-empty-workspace`, `prepared-pool-presence`, `prepared-pool-maintenance`, `prepared-pool`, `prepared-pool-standing-effects`):

```text
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  51 passed (51)
 Duration  253.95s
```

`pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on the three changed files reports `All matched files use the correct format.`; `git diff --check` is clean. `pnpm tsgo:core` passes on this head.

**Not run / gaps:**

- **Gateway/provider-lineage output is missing, and I cannot produce it here.** The scenario needs a worker provider that (a) supports prepared image reserves, and (b) can be made to fail its standing-intent assertion while a real Gateway runs the pool. I checked the in-tree options: the qa-lab `static-ssh` provider is `remote-exec` only (no prepared intents, no `preparedCapacity`); the paired-node-worker wire fixture configures `cloudWorkers.profiles.native` with `provider: "device"` for node placement, not standing image reserves; no bundled or test-double worker provider exposes the prepared-capacity path. Reproducing it therefore needs either cloud-worker credentials or a purpose-built provider test double (a plugin plus a controllable failure endpoint), which is outside this PR's scope.
- If a maintainer can run the scenario in a provider-backed environment, the exact steps are: one ready `purpose: "reserve"` record with `expiresAtMs: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, one reserve whose `expiresAtMs` has passed, then make `assertIntentCurrent` throw during a prepared-pool pass. Expected: the standing reserve stays `ready` with no destroy request, the expired reserve is retired, and the Gateway logs `Prepared capacity demand is unavailable`.
- Fork PR CI needs a maintainer to approve the run, so it has not run.

prs.title: fix: let an agent on a dedicated worker wait for its subagents
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/agents/tools/subagents-tool.ts:296` (main) builds the `subagents` tool without the Gateway-call timeout that its own 0 to 60 second `wait` needs, so a dedicated worker sends the call with `WorkerConnection`'s 30 second default (`src/worker/worker-connection.ts:65`, applied at `:198`), and any wait of about 30 seconds or longer loses that race and drops the worker's Gateway connection.

## What Problem This Solves

I'm porting [RFE Creator](https://github.com/fullsend-ai/rfe-creator) to OpenClaw, running on a dedicated worker. Upstream, its coordinator launches reviewer agents and waits for them with a bounded blocking call that it re-runs until they finish. `wait-for-wave` blocks for up to 90 seconds, sized to fit Claude Code's default two minute Bash timeout ([check_review_progress.py](https://github.com/fullsend-ai/rfe-creator/blob/29b362013fb7614fa3830d893828899a965a0654/scripts/check_review_progress.py#L139-L141)), and the agent runs it again on exit 3 ([RFE Creator's CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/fullsend-ai/rfe-creator/blob/29b362013fb7614fa3830d893828899a965a0654/CLAUDE.md#L116-L119)).

On OpenClaw the same pattern is `subagents` with `action: "wait"`, capped at the tool's 60 second limit and repeated. On a dedicated worker it breaks: any wait that runs 30 seconds or more fails at 30 seconds with `worker gateway-tool response timed out`, and the worker drops its connection to the Gateway. That includes the default wait, because the worker starts its 30 second clock before the Gateway starts its own.

The tool itself works. A child that needs about 40 seconds, with the agent waiting up to 55, gives a different result depending on where the agent runs, and this PR closes the gap:

```text
main,    agent on the Gateway:           completed after 37.8 s
main,    agent on a dedicated worker:    failed after 31.3 s: worker gateway-tool response timed out
                                         (the child finished 9 s later, at 40.2 s)
this PR, agent on a dedicated worker:    completed after 40.0 s
```

## User Impact

An agent on a dedicated worker can wait for its subagents as long as it asks, up to the tool's 60 second limit, and gets back a result or a normal timeout. For RFE review, the coordinator can wait 60 seconds, get back `timeout` or a finished reviewer, and wait again, the same loop upstream runs with its 90 second wait.

## Why This Change Was Made

On a worker, `subagents` runs on the Gateway, and the worker gives that call 30 seconds unless the tool declares it needs longer. `sessions_send` already declares this, and `subagents` was missing it. I added the same declaration, the requested wait plus 60 seconds, where the tool is built. Nothing else changes.

The missing completion announcement for worker children is a separate fix. So is the worker dropping its whole connection when one call times out, which I'd like to discuss on its own.

## Evidence

- Thanks @ederign for finding this in a real RFE Creator port and for the fix.
- Built Gateway plus a real paired node host running the shipped worker bundle, session dispatched to a device worker profile, scripted local model; the parent spawns a child that needs 50 seconds and waits with `subagents` `action: "wait"`. Full table: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205476#issuecomment-7171914650
  - main, worker, `timeoutSeconds: 60`, twice: after 30.07 s the tool result is `The node disconnected before the turn finished. Tool effects may be unknown; verify state before retrying.` (`WorkerNodeLostError`), and the child is interrupted.
  - this PR, worker, `timeoutSeconds: 60`, twice: `reason: "completed"` after 52.0 s and 52.2 s, when the child finished.
  - default wait on the worker: main fails the same way at 30.08 s; this PR returns the normal `reason: "timeout"` at 30.16 s.
  - Controls, unchanged: agent kept on the Gateway completes on both (50.6 s); a 10 second wait on the worker returns `reason: "timeout"` at 10.1 s on both.
- The regression test in `subagents-tool.test.ts` fails on main and passes here.
- Author's own run (local Gateway plus `openclaw connect --session-host` worker, gpt-4.1, child `sleep 35`, wait 55): main failed at 31.3 s with `worker gateway-tool response timed out`; this PR completed at 40.0 s. On OpenClaw Enterprise (runtime 35d714e) the failure reproduced 6 times at 31.2 to 32.2 s; the fix was not run there.

prs.title: fix(chat): restore your reading position after an empty search
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a transcript search finds no messages, clearing the query or closing search jumps to the beginning of the chat. This also loses the reader’s place if they scrolled through matching results before narrowing the search.

## User Impact

Close or clear an empty search to return to the message you last read at the same screen position. If you were following the latest messages, you return to the end. Searching still takes you to the first match, and opening a result still takes you to the selected message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The empty search view removes all virtualized messages. The transcript now records which visible message to restore before the rows disappear and issues the first-result scroll only after a result viewport has mounted.

The message-anchor approach builds on the original work by @vyctorbrzezowski in the closed, unmerged [PR #152095](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/152095).

## Evidence

Three focused Chromium regressions failed on the parent and passed on this change. The parent lost both marked messages and left the end follower 7,713 px from the bottom. Across 18 mounted cases covering desktop and portrait, the largest measured message displacement was 0.5625 px. The draft, editor, and loaded message array survived, and the end-follow controls finished at a zero-pixel gap.

## Hosted validation

All three Chromium regressions passed: Close returned to the earlier reading position, Clear returned to the deliberately read result, and Close from Latest restored the end follower. Both real-Gateway shards built the runtime and Control UI. [Chromium results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45675052598/job/139421272949)

The background-work test timed out at 120 seconds while observing the child’s in-flight startup response. The same test, stage and timeout occurred on main. Knip’s script and full-tree reports flagged two known Parallels preflight exports. Its production report passed. The aggregate retained these failures. [Gateway job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45675052598/job/139421273113) · [Main comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45645122717/job/139314901133) · [Dependency job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45675052598/job/139421273523)

In a mounted Chromium run with the [reply-reveal fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/205493), the original message returned at the identical viewport position after a no-match search closed. Latest then returned to the physical end.

Fixes #151970

prs.title: fix: let plugin counters show a label set at 0 before its first event
prs.body:
<!-- Template: .github/pull_request_template.md at ed8f4e680cbfc32182fee0b9286ef40c112bb1c3 -->

Closes #202816

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin that publishes counters through `api.metrics` cannot show a known label set at 0 before its first event. `counter(name).inc(labels, 0)` is dropped, so the series appears only after the first non-zero increment. Dashboards and `absent()` alerts then cannot tell an idle label set from one that is missing.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors can call `inc(labels, 0)` to export a label set at 0 on the Prometheus scrape, the usual way to pre-initialize counters. Core metrics and existing plugin series are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exporter's store skips counter increments of 0 before creating the series. Core counters rely on that: the model cost counter receives `costUsd ?? 0`, and skipping 0 keeps an unknown cost from showing as a measured $0. So the change applies only to plugin counter samples: a value of 0 uses the store's existing `max` mode instead of `add`. A new label set is created at 0 under the usual per-family and total limits. An existing series keeps its value and its cached output. Negative and non-finite values are still refused. The plugin families section of the Prometheus docs now says what `inc(labels, 0)` does.

## Evidence

- A scrape from a real Gateway with a path-loaded plugin shows the new `{outcome="error"} 0` series on this branch and not on main (Runtime output below).
- New store test, red on main for the missing `{outcome="error"} 0` line, green with the fix, red again with the fix reverted. It also checks that negative, NaN and Infinity values create no series, that core `counter(..., 0)` still creates none, and that a later 0 on an existing series does not re-render it.
- `pnpm test:extension diagnostics-prometheus` (77 passed) and `src/plugins/plugin-metrics.test.ts` (11 passed).
- `pnpm check:changed`: all checks pass except the dead export scan, which fails the same way on main ed8f4e680cb (`ui/src/pages/skills/skill-page-route.ts`: `createSkillPageReads`, `createSkillPageRoute`). `git diff --check` clean.

### Runtime output

Setup: isolated Gateway built from the checkout, own state folder, token auth with a throwaway token, loopback port 19455, `diagnostics-prometheus` enabled, and a path-loaded plugin `zero-proof` with `allowMetrics: true`. Five seconds after its service starts, the plugin logs and calls `inc({ outcome: "error" }, 0)`, then `inc({ outcome: "ok" }, 1)`. No model, channel or provider. prs.title: fix(codex): continue unchanged protected turns without a relay
prs.body:
## Problem

`368809d32848` added `assertCodexProtectedContextCarrier`, which fails a Codex turn before dispatch when all of these are true:

- the turn carries producer-annotated conversation context
- the thread is protected by active native work
- the connection has no parent-local inference relay

It fires even when the context hasn't changed and no compaction has happened. The error, "requires a current parent-local inference relay; the native thread is claimed by active work", gives the user no next step. The guard shipped in `v2026.10.10`, `v2026.11.1` and `v2026.11.2`, but `main` never had it, so release-line behavior differs from `main`.

## Solution

Back out `368809d32848` on `release/2026.11.3`, removing all three call sites and `protected-context-carrier.ts`. This matches `main`, where the helper doesn't exist.

`git revert` conflicted in the tests, so this isn't a pure revert:

- The relay-after-compaction assertions in `run-attempt-continuity.test.ts` stay. They cover the relay itself, not the refusal.
- The no-relay test now asserts that an unchanged continuation reaches `turn/start`, with no `thread/start`, `turn/interrupt` or `thread/unsubscribe`.
- The relay-loss-at-dispatch test is removed along with the guard. The `client-runtime` mock keeps its `importOriginal` spread and `config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` is unchanged; the first revision restored a closed mock and failed the mock-exports ratchet, which `1114170451fc` fixes.

## Impact

- Unchanged-context turns on protected no-relay threads now run instead of failing.
- Changed context on a protected thread is still refused, now with the actionable "still has background work after waiting for cleanup; stop its running work and retry." The old test matched `/claimed by active work/` only because the guard's own message contained those words.
- Accepted gap, same as `main`: without a relay, native compaction can drop conversation context, so a continuation can run without it. Codex rebuilds compacted history from user messages, the summary and canonical initial context (`codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs`). `dynamic-tools.md` keeps the existing limitation text; the paragraph describing the refusal is removed.
- Relay-backed connections are unaffected.

This branch keeps its existing doc wording rather than `main`'s "full handoff" text: `main`'s docs describe a handoff, but `thread-policy.ts` is identical on both branches and this PR changes no handoff code.

## Evidence

Rerun on the 11.3 rebase: `run-attempt-continuity.test.ts`, `run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts` and `thread-lifecycle.test.ts`, 92 passed. Original runs on the 11.2 branch:

- `run-attempt-continuity.test.ts` and `run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts`: 18 passed
- `thread-lifecycle.test.ts`, `thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts` and `run-attempt.test.ts`: 297 passed
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `check:test-mock-exports --base origin/release/2026.11.3`: pass
- `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`: fail, with no errors in `extensions/codex` or other files this PR touches. Errors are in `feishu`, `browser`, `discord` and `telegram`; I didn't rerun these on the base commit.

Not proven: a live Codex app-server run, and how often real connections have no relay.

## Release note

This targets `release/2026.11.3`. It was first opened against `release/2026.11.2`, but that line shipped with the guard on 2026-11-08 before this landed, so the PR was rebased onto the 11.3 tip `40223c5cc262` (clean cherry-pick). Merging it changes product code on the 11.3 candidate. It's an operator-requested addition, not a confirmed release blocker.

prs.title: fix: preserve Doctor failures during container shutdown
prs.body:
Closes #205095

## What Problem This Solves

When Doctor refuses to repair a configuration, it prints the reason and exits 1. If SIGTERM arrives while it finishes writing that output, both the standalone command and the image entrypoint can instead exit 143. That hides the configuration failure from the service supervisor.

## User Impact

A diagnosed repair failure now exits 1 even when shutdown overlaps it. A SIGTERM that interrupts activation before Doctor diagnoses the configuration still exits 143.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor records its refusal in the one-shot exit handler, which owns signal cleanup as well as output draining. The activation entrypoint preserves an independent failure from its Doctor child and still translates a forwarded signal back to the original signal status when appropriate.

## Evidence

I ran the built CLI and the shipped image entrypoint as separate processes in isolated Linux PID and network namespaces with a read-only configuration containing the retired `agents.list` key. These runs exercised the entrypoint script directly, without a Docker daemon.

| Invocation and signal timing | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`, SIGTERM after the final validation diagnostic | 143 | 1 |
| Entrypoint starting the gateway, same diagnostic and signal | 143 | 1 |
| Entrypoint starting the gateway, no signal | 1 | 1 |

The fixed entrypoint also exited 143 when interrupted during archive preparation, before final validation. The new regressions failed on the original implementation. The entrypoint and CLI tests cover a failure reported on either side of signal cleanup, plus ordinary interruption and forwarded signals.

All 87 focused tests passed, along with the runtime build, core and test type checks, formatting, scoped lint, and local review.

prs.title: fix(codex): collect late command results before settling silent turns
prs.body:
Related: #196061 and #196062 (confirmed running commands; this PR covers late terminal results).

## What Problem This Solves

A silent Codex turn can be marked failed when native command exits arrive just after the turn's completion. OpenClaw can finalize the transcript before receiving the actual command results.

## User Impact

Silent runs stay silent when the late results are received. Failed commands are still recorded as failed, and genuinely missing results still follow the existing error path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Give outstanding, unretained native commands a bounded 150 ms grace period before the final checkpoint, then drain queued notifications. Confirmed retained commands keep their existing handling.

## Evidence

**Real runtime, changed settlement window.** On `cd47ec3ffa66` in an isolated Docker Gateway with native Codex CLI `0.172.0`, 2 of 8 probes had a command pending after inventory returned no retained terminal. Diagnostic logging only; no synthetic or delayed app-server notifications. Each result matched the pending command ID (redacted below). Times are relative to inventory:

```text
                    Trial 3                   Trial 4
Inventory           +0 ms pending, unretained +0 ms pending, unretained
Native completion  +29 ms failed, exit 19    +92 ms failed, exit 19
Checkpoint        +153 ms no pending items +152 ms no pending items
Gateway agent RPC  OK (stop)                  OK (stop)
```

**Follow-up limits.** A second sweep (8 probes per arm) compared the same Gateway bundle with and without the new grace block. Neither arm hit the pending-but-unretained window in that sweep: the results were already available or the commands were still retained. A read-only check of the patched Gateway's SQLite transcript confirmed `NO_REPLY` and real `isError: true` tool results for four completed probes with early results. That is a persistence check, not a transcript check of the two late trials above. No live failing-control comparison or production rollout is claimed.

**Deterministic regression.** The synthetic app-server integration test reproduced `missingToolResultCount=2` on the base. All 12 tests in `run-attempt.native-background-outcome.test.ts` passed on the patch, including the regression verifying both late command failures survive in the snapshot. Formatting and whitespace checks passed.

releases.name: openclaw 2026.10.34
releases.body:
This is a gateway-only `extended-stable` release, which is our current equivalent to LTS. This release is OpenClaw from the end of October 2026, plus critical security updates, reliability and performance fixes, and features like new model support. The latest version of OpenClaw at the time of this release is [2026.11.10](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases#release-v2026.11.10)

## 2026.10.34

This extended-stable patch updates the Gateway and official npm plugins from 2026.10.33. It includes the core npm package and Gateway Docker images, but no native-app releases.

### Highlights

- OpenAI and ClawRouter: select GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, with system-prompt caching on the OpenAI API-key and Sign in with ChatGPT Responses routes. (#200766, #201094) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @fuller-stack-dev, and @obviyus.
- Tlon: group DMs use their own approval policy, and approved clubs remain authorized across Gateway restarts. (#202775) Thanks @joshavant.
- Update recovery: avoid leaving the Gateway offline when an update runs alongside database readers or replaces a running checkout, and recover the service after a failed Windows update rolls back. (#201330, #202541, #203241, #203264) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa.
- Conversation continuity: deliver ready child results without waiting for other helpers to finish, and accept follow-up chat messages after the preceding run completes. (#203176, #203102, #201790) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @obviyus, @RomneyDa, and @vincentkoc.
- Channel delivery: recover Telegram polling when update IDs reset, keep an undownloadable attachment from blocking replies, and reconnect all Discord accounts after a network outage. (#201167, #200682, #201415, #162189) Thanks @RomneyDa, @obviyus, and @mattreyes0824.

### Changes

- MiniMax: stop offering retired M2 models, including during live discovery, and use MiniMax-M3 for PDF text extraction. If your configuration explicitly selects an M2 model, switch it to a supported model. (#203998) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Fixes

- Access controls: apply the session permission mode consistently on Gateway tool calls, recheck bound Discord DMs against current policy, and keep Signal view-once attachments out of assistant context. (#202941, #196848, #196841) Thanks @obviyus and @drobison00.
- Channel setup: save new tokens through the channel secret store rather than writing them to config as plaintext. (#201428, #175333) Thanks @anmol0b, @sallyom, and @masatohoshino.
- Discord and Slack: queue independent Discord requests instead of replacing an active task, show when the target session is busy, and leave Slack question buttons available when a click comes from someone who cannot answer. (#201518, #201363, #201371, #201348) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc, @obviyus, and @shannon0430.
- Conversation delivery: return complete queued ACP replies, preserve Claude CLI final answers after progress messages, and avoid repeating tool work on a fallback model during long Claude CLI turns. (#202658, #200470, #200801, #200744) Thanks @obviyus, @chaeyn, @fede-kamel, and @jzmudzinski.
- Conversation recovery: resume saved requests when transcript metadata advances, and keep pending child results when the requesting run ends or a follow-up takes over. (#201477, #195275) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa and @jalehman.
- OpenAI and Codex: preserve session affinity for Sign in with ChatGPT and let Codex subagents start from agent folders with capital letters. (#197588, #197532, #201520, #201423) Thanks @sukhdeepjohar, @aatreya, @obviyus, and @thejeys19.
- Provider reliability: compact before predicted context overflow instead of trimming tool results already cached by the provider, stop retrying Anthropic requests that require credits, and preserve user-configured model rows on provider sign-in. (#199530, #201997, #201742, #201558) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @obviyus, @LinzeShi, @MertBasar0, and @Caitoz.
- Install and update: avoid hanging at NodeSource on Ubuntu 26.04, preserve pnpm-linked checkouts when switching to the npm release, and complete updates with read-only, unchanged config or old plugin leases. (#203538, #201701, #201331, #201314) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- Storage and backups: let large PostgreSQL maintenance operations finish, recover after silent database connection loss, port upgraded stores to PostgreSQL, and reclaim space when backup staging databases are deleted. (#201869, #201856, #201299, #201250, #199666) Thanks @VACInc, @chelsealong, @evemorgen, and @etzelm.
- Doctor: reuse the existing state database for offline update checks after backup, avoiding extra copies of large databases. (#202985) Authored by @steipete.
- Browser and Control UI: capture background tabs in headed or headless Chrome, keep final answers out of the collapsed Worked fold, and preserve pending dictation transcripts while showing progress. (#202878, #165312, #201626, #197429, #200235) Thanks @obviyus, @titan550, @Marvinthebored, @vyctorbrzezowski, @Peetiegonzalez, and @daniel-lxs.
- Automation and Feishu: deliver automation failure notices back to the chat that created the job and finish long replies in the same streaming card. (#203056, #161777, #139443) Thanks @obviyus, @ArthurNie, and @Simon2256928.

### Complete contribution record

This audited record covers the complete v2026.10.33..3656180a44de203e4b3be5fb02d768fcdb306767 history: 129 in-range PRs + 0 retained seed-only PRs = 129 unique PRs. The generation manifest also supplies direct commits as editorial input; the grouped notes above prioritize user impact.

issues.title: Vision: large inbound images fail silently — provider 502 → silent retry without images; add configurable max image size / stronger downscaling

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Send a typical iPhone photo (~4032×3024, ~4 MB JPEG) as a WebUI attachment.
2. Ask the model what the image shows.

#### Actual behavior

- The attachment upload itself succeeds; the file is stored under `~/.nanobot/media/websocket/` and the user message carries the correct `media` path.
- The provider returns `HTTP 502 {"error":{"message":"inference service temporarily unavailable","type":"bad_gateway_error"}}` for the large image payload.
- nanobot then retries the request **without images**, replacing them with text placeholders (`[image: <path>]` / "(Image file: ...)").
- The model replies "I couldn't view that image — it didn't come through", and even an explicit `read_file` on the stored JPEG returns only text placeholders. From the user's perspective, image support is simply broken, with no hint of the real cause.

#### Expected behavior

Either the image is delivered, or the failure is visible and actionable.

### Proposed Solution

1. **Configurable max image size for inbound/provider-bound images**, e.g. `agents.defaults.maxImagePixels` / `maxImageBytes` (or per-provider), so users on stricter endpoints can force aggressive downscaling (e.g. cap at 1568 px long side, ~0.5–1 MB) instead of relying on the current gentle policy.
2. **Stronger default downscaling**: the current preparation "re-encodes at the original dimensions, then reduces each dimension by at most 25% if needed" toward a 1 MB data-URL budget. For 12 MP phone photos this can still leave multi-MB payloads; consider iterating further (vision models rarely benefit beyond ~1568 px long side anyway).
3. **Surface the fallback**: when the retry-without-images path kicks in, tell the user in the chat (e.g. "image omitted: provider rejected it (HTTP 502), resized copy suggested") instead of a silent placeholder that reads like a transport failure. Ideally also retry once with a harder-downscaled image before falling back to text-only.

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Related Component

LLM Provider

### Additional Context

#### Environment

- nanobot 0.4.1 (pip install)
- Channel: bundled WebUI (WebSocket), accessed from iOS Safari (iPhone)
- Provider: custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`apiBase` + Chat Completions)
- Model: `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` (vision-capable — verified directly against the provider)

#### Diagnosis (verified experimentally)

Direct `curl`-level tests against the same provider/model:

| Payload | Result |
|---|---|
| 1×1 px PNG (tiny) | 200 OK, correct answer |
| Original 4032×3024 / 4.1 MB JPEG | HTTP 502, reproducible 3× |
| Same photo resized to 2048 px / 0.87 MB | 200 OK, image read correctly |
| Same photo resized to 1568 px / 0.58 MB | 200 OK, image read correctly |

So the model and provider handle vision fine — the payload size is the trigger, and the provider surfaces it as a misleading 502.
