issues.title: A2A: reply timeout permanently reports failure despite eventual successful execution

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Bug
An A2A reply-wait timeout is recorded as terminal execution failure even when the accepted profile task continues and later completes successfully. Subsequent GetTask returns the failed adapter record instead of the eventual owner result.

## Environment and evidence
Observed on a deployment based on v0.22.5, with unrelated deployment patches. The relevant timeout-to-failure mapping also remains in current upstream main inspected on 2026-10-31. This is not a claim of a full clean-install reproduction.

For a read-only forwarded-profile request, the final assistant response arrived approximately 327 seconds after admission, exceeding the then-default 300-second reply window. The owner's durable admission subsequently showed terminal/completed, failed=false, and a stored final response. A2A instead returned `TASK_STATE_FAILED` with `[profile reply unverified; accepted work was not cancelled]`; later GetTask retained that failure. No private request data is needed to reproduce this.

## Reproduction
In an isolated test, submit a harmless forwarded-profile task whose handler completes after the configured reply window. Capture its task ID. After the handler finishes successfully, retrieve that same task with GetTask without resending the instruction.

Actual: timeout is finalized as failed; eventual successful owner completion is not reconciled into the A2A task.
Expected: a caller's waiting deadline must not establish execution failure. Preserve accepted-task identity, report a nonterminal/accurately uncertain execution status, and allow retrieval of the eventual result without re-execution. Genuine execution failure should still be terminal failed.

## Source-level confirmation
A local harness invoked the actual forwarding method with the owner transport stubbed to raise TimeoutError. It returned the exact message above and STATE_FAILED. The outer adapter records that as the task's terminal outcome; GetTask reads the adapter record rather than refreshing from the owner admission.

The local-profile wait path similarly finalizes reply timeout as failed and removes the pending waiter. Please consider both paths and client disconnects when correcting the lifecycle.

## Mitigation and scope
Increasing A2A_REPLY_TIMEOUT covers longer turns but only postpones the same failure mode. It does not correct the status semantics or result reconciliation. A timeout must not trigger blind retries of potentially effectful work.

This report concerns recovery within the running gateway. Cross-restart task persistence is a separate concern, not required by this report.

## Acceptance
- A deliberately slow synthetic task can outlive the caller wait window without being falsely declared execution-failed.
- Its final result becomes retrievable using the existing task identity, without resubmission.
- Genuine failure/cancellation remains distinguishable from reply retrieval failure.
- Tracking cleans up correctly without orphaning live work or leaking background waiters.

## Blocked by
None. Independent of startup queue acknowledgement reporting.

issues.title: A2A: a task that outlives `A2A_REPLY_TIMEOUT` is marked failed and its late reply is discarded (also via SendStreamingMessage)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

issues.body:
**What happens**

If an inbound A2A task runs longer than `A2A_REPLY_TIMEOUT` (default 300 s), it is finalized as `failed` with
`[agent did not reply in time]`, but the agent session keeps running. When the session finishes, `send()` finds no
pending waiter and drops the reply. No A2A route can return the answer after that. The blocking `SendMessage`
caller has already received the failure. `SendStreamingMessage` waits on the same deadline. `GetTask`,
`SubscribeToTask` and push notifications all see the terminal `failed` state. The work is done and paid for, and
the caller sees a failure.

**Seen on** v0.22.2+2886 (`e8a8a9b`); `main` at `e5ea5fd` has the same code.

- 09:08:33: a peer's `SendMessage` (a multi-source research ask) creates task `task-fce8a3b2630f4cc2`.
- 09:13:33, exactly 300 s later: the caller receives `failed: [agent did not reply in time]`.
- The session kept working and finished at 09:33:43 (1510.5 s, 116 model calls, a 43,634-character answer). The
  gateway called `send()` at 09:33:44 (`[A2A] Sending response (43634 chars)`), but the A2A audit log has no outbound
  line for it and the task stays `failed`: the answer exists only in the session store.

**Code**

- [`adapter.py#L697-L699`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e5ea5fd9ccdf2913c0b21b24eb3d22b321d2e2a6/plugins/platforms/a2a/adapter.py#L697-L699):
  `_await_reply()` returns `(STATE_FAILED, "[agent did not reply in time]")` at `started + _reply_timeout()`.
- [`adapter.py#L665-L677`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e5ea5fd9ccdf2913c0b21b24eb3d22b321d2e2a6/plugins/platforms/a2a/adapter.py#L665-L677):
  `_finalize_task()` records that outcome as terminal, fires the push notification and pops the waiter.
- [`adapter.py#L735-L749`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e5ea5fd9ccdf2913c0b21b24eb3d22b321d2e2a6/plugins/platforms/a2a/adapter.py#L735-L749):
  `_rpc_message_stream()` waits on the same deadline. Between `working` and the end it writes only keepalive comments.
- [`adapter.py#L866-L873`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e5ea5fd9ccdf2913c0b21b24eb3d22b321d2e2a6/plugins/platforms/a2a/adapter.py#L866-L873):
  `send()` drops a reply that has no waiter (logged at debug level only) and ignores every non-final send, so the
  stream cannot carry progress either.
- `SendMessageConfiguration.returnImmediately` (spec §3.2, <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/>) is never
  read, so a client has no non-blocking path to fall back on.
- Client side, [`tools.py#L21`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e5ea5fd9ccdf2913c0b21b24eb3d22b321d2e2a6/plugins/platforms/a2a/tools.py#L21)
  and [`#L108`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e5ea5fd9ccdf2913c0b21b24eb3d22b321d2e2a6/plugins/platforms/a2a/tools.py#L108):
  `a2a_call` sends only a blocking `SendMessage`, with a 120 s default timeout, and never polls `GetTask`.

**Repro**

1. Set `A2A_REPLY_TIMEOUT=10` and restart the gateway.
2. Send `SendMessage`: "Run `sleep 30` in the terminal, then reply with exactly DONE."
3. At about 10 s the caller receives `failed: [agent did not reply in time]`.
4. At about 35 s the gateway logs `response ready` for the A2A session. `GetTask` on the same task id still returns
   the timeout failure, and "DONE" is never reachable.

**Expected**

The spec is "async first": long tasks are meant to be collected through `GetTask`, a subscription or a push
notification.

1. Reaching the wait deadline ends the wait, not the task. The task stays `working`, its waiter stays registered,
   and the late reply is recorded on it (task store, audit, push notification), so `GetTask`, `SubscribeToTask` and
   push deliver it.
2. Honour `returnImmediately: true` by returning the `working` task at once.
3. The orphan sweeper (`_fail_orphans_once`, bounded by `_MAX_ORPHAN_TIMEOUT`) stays the thing that eventually
   fails a task whose session really died.
4. Nice to have: send the agent's progress as `TaskStatusUpdateEvent`s on the stream, and let `a2a_call` poll
   `GetTask` when the result is not terminal.

**Workaround today:** raise `A2A_REPLY_TIMEOUT` and the caller's HTTP timeout together. That holds a connection
open for every long task and still loses anything that runs past the new window.

## Regression

1. What stops working: nothing for clients that wait for a terminal state. A blocking caller whose task passes the
   window now gets a non-terminal `working` task where it used to get `failed`, so a client that treated that
   `failed` as final has to poll `GetTask` or subscribe.
2. Behaviours changed / separable: (a) late-reply capture, with no `failed` at the wait deadline; (b)
   `returnImmediately`; (c) progress events on the stream; (d) polling in `a2a_call`. Each can ship on its own; (a)
   is the fix.
3. Override / kill switch / FDE agreement: an env flag such as `A2A_FAIL_ON_REPLY_TIMEOUT=1` keeps today's
   behaviour. There is no FDE party; this is an upstream open-source change.
4. Detection within a day / rollback: `/metrics` `tasks_failed` drops and a new late-reply counter rises; roll back
   by setting the flag.

**Related:** #78007, #91687, #109089 (same area, different bugs).

issues.title: Desktop layout presets: allow route tiles (e.g. the Kanban page) to keep their slot

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

labels.name: comp/desktop
labels.description: Electron desktop app (apps/desktop/*)

issues.body:
### What I want

A saved layout preset that restores a working arrangement in one click, including pages that open as route tiles:

```
| route tile /agentboom (plugin page) | route tile /kanban | chat (workspace) |
```

Both side columns are routes: the Kanban page, and a plugin page that is reached from a sidebar nav item (`SIDEBAR_NAV_AREA`) and opened beside the chat as a route tile. The plugin deliberately registers no layout pane, because closing a plugin's only pane switches the whole plugin off (`closeTreePane`).

### What happens now

`saveLayoutPresetTree` strips every `route-tile:*`, `session-tile:*` and `preview-tile:*` pane before it writes `hermes.desktop.layoutPresets.v2` (`apps/desktop/src/components/pane-shell/tree/preset-tree.ts:26`, `PRESET_EXCLUDED_PANE_PREFIXES`). On apply, open route tiles are adopted into the geometry wherever adoption puts them. So a preset of this arrangement keeps only the chat; both columns have to be dragged back by hand every time.

For session and preview tiles that makes sense (they are snapshots of what is open now, see #94260). A route tile is different: it is a page, not a conversation, so it can be layout.

### Proposal

- Keep `session-tile:` and `preview-tile:` excluded.
- Let a preset keep `route-tile:<route>` as a slot. On apply: if that route is open, it moves into its slot; if not, the slot stays empty (or rests collapsed) until the route is opened, and then the tile docks there instead of in the default spot.
- Optionally an opt-in per route, so only routes that make sense as layout (Kanban, Analytics, Control Center) do this.

### Why

With one project board per project (`hermes project bind-board`), Kanban and an orchestration plugin page become permanent columns next to the chat for people who run agent teams. Today a layout reset (see #89548; it also happened here on the first start of the app after updating to v0.23.4) means rebuilding both columns by hand. A preset with route slots would make that one click.

Environment: Hermes v0.23.4 (2026.9.24), desktop on macOS (arm64).

issues.body:
Summary

In the Hermes Desktop app, the transcript uses stick-to-bottom (use-stick-to-bottom is the single scroll owner in apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/thread/list.tsx, configured around line 545): whenever the reader is at the bottom, the view follows content growth to the live edge.

Consequence: when a reply longer than the viewport is produced, its beginning is pushed above the top edge of the visible window by the time the reply completes. The reader sees only the tail and must manually scroll up to read from the start — every single turn, for every long reply.

Requested behavior

A display setting, e.g. display.chat.reply_scroll (Settings → Chat), with at least two modes:

bottom (current default) — stick to the bottom while streaming.
reply-start — when a new assistant reply begins, scroll so the top of that reply is visible (the first lines land at or near the top of the viewport), and do not re-pin the view to the live edge while that reply streams. The reader follows the growing reply manually with normal scrolling; the "Scroll to bottom" jump pill already exists for returning to the live edge.
Optional refinement: an alternative follow-clamped mode that follows growth only until the reply's top reaches the viewport top, then holds position instead of pushing it off-screen.

Why

Long agent replies (reports, code, multi-section answers) are routinely longer than one viewport; reading from the top is the natural reading order.
Today the reader must fight the auto-follow on every turn; the jump pill only helps going DOWN, not UP to the reply's start.
Related but distinct issues: #135583 (reply lands below viewport), #147425 (reading position jumps when a reply finishes while scrolled up). Those are about where the view lands; this request is about a persistent preference for how new replies are revealed.
Implementation sketch (for maintainers)

The scroll ownership is centralized in ThreadMessageList (list.tsx) via useStickToBottom({ initial, resize, targetScrollTop }). Suggested approach:

Detect a new assistant message (turn boundary) via the existing structuralSignature / groups pipeline.
When reply_scroll === 'reply-start', on turn start resolve the top offset of the newest assistant row (message DOM node offsetTop relative to the scroll container) and issue one scrollTo there, then release the stick-to-bottom lock (e.g. via scrollLock) until the reader explicitly returns to the bottom (existing jump pill / re-lock path).
Keep bottom-stick as the default; gate the new behavior behind the setting so existing users are unaffected. Respect the existing selection-pin (scrollToBottomUnlessSelecting) and reading-position persistence (thread-scroll.ts) invariants.
Environment

Hermes Desktop (Electron), latest release
Repro: any session, request a reply longer than the viewport, observe the first lines scroll off the top edge while the view stays pinned to the live edge.
Заголовок (Title) — тот же, что присылал выше:

[Feature] Desktop: option to keep the beginning of a new reply in view (scroll to reply start instead of stick-to-bottom)

prs.title: fix(sessions): a saved route for a late-registering plugin platform is held, not deleted
prs.body:
If a chat came in over a plugin platform (Yuanbao today, any catalog platform) and that plugin is not loaded when the gateway starts, the gateway quietly deleted that chat's saved route the next time it saved, so the conversation's state was lost. Now the route is kept untouched until the plugin shows up, and then it rejoins the live chats so `/stop`, crash-resume and profile delete/rename treat it like any other.

**Existing user:** a Yuanbao (or other plugin-platform) chat whose plugin loads late — a multiplexed secondary profile's plugin, a plugin installed after boot, or one temporarily uninstalled — keeps its session route across restarts instead of losing it on the first save. **New user:** nothing changes.

This is the generic gateway half of the QQ Bot move (#159640) and the Feishu move (#159651), extracted so it lands on its own first. The first four commits' `gateway/session*.py` hunks are byte-identical to both branches; the last commit (review fixes below) goes on top, and the two move PRs take it too at rebase. It is already broken on main for every plugin platform; the Weixin / DingTalk / WeCom moves do not carry it.

## Before / after

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Saved route for a platform whose plugin is not registered at store load | skipped, then **deleted** from state.db on the next full save | **held**, written back on every save (a live entry under the same key wins) |
| Older `sessions.json` mirror copy of that key | could re-import over it | skipped: state.db stays primary |
| Row broken some other way (corrupt `updated_at`) | skipped; mirror copy recovers it | unchanged: only an unregistered platform makes a row held |
| Plugin registers later in the same process | route recovered from the sessions table without its own state (`/stop` suspension, `resume_pending` lost) | held row **joins the live index** with its own state |
| Boot crash-turn recovery / clean-startup marker discard | (route already dropped) | applied to held rows right away and saved, so it survives an exit before the plugin loads |
| Single-row write fails → full-rewrite fallback; state.db unreadable at boot, recovers later | (route already dropped) | both keep held rows (state.db copy wins over an older mirror copy) |
| Profile delete / rename | (route already dropped, row 1) | held rows purged / re-keyed with the profile, so a save cannot write them back or leave them under the old name |

## Live probe (real `gateway run --force`, fake HOME/HERMES_HOME/XDG/lock dir, no mocks)

state.db seeded with a `yuanbao` DM route and a `telegram` DM route, both with a crash-left turn marker, as a previous run that had the Yuanbao Labs plugin would leave them. Each gateway start is its own PID, killed (SIGKILL, unclean) after 40 s; the telegram marker makes boot recovery run a whole-index save.

| Leg | main (6e447b2c2f01) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Start 1, Yuanbao plugin not installed | `agent:main:yuanbao:dm:YB1` **gone** from state.db | row **kept**; boot crash recovery marks it `resume_pending=True` on disk |
| Start 2, real Yuanbao Labs plugin installed + enabled | no yuanbao row (lost in start 1) | row loads live, crash-turn → `resume_pending=True` |
| One process: boot recovery runs, then plugin installed + discovered, then the chat's next message | `resume_pending=False` (crash-turn verdict lost) | `resume_pending=True`, same session_id, written back to state.db |

Real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` md5 equal before/after.

## Tests

`tests/gateway/test_held_route_late_platform.py` (12 tests, Yuanbao as the late plugin platform; 9 red on main; the 3 others pin that a broken row is not held, that profile delete drops a held row, and that a DB row recovered after the plugin registers wins; the 5 review-fix tests are also red on the head before each fix). Full `tests/gateway/` locally: all pass except `test_run_progress_topics.py::test_base_processing_stops_typing_before_hung_post_delivery_callback`, which fails the same way on main locally. `scripts/check --only health`, ruff, boundary lint, tmp-literal check clean.

The QQ Bot and Feishu moves add the same tests under `tests/gateway/test_unparsed_route_survives_save.py` with their own platform; this file has its own name so their merges stay clean.

## NOT_COVERED

- No live multiplexed secondary-profile gateway leg; the late registration is exercised by the in-process plugin-install leg and the unit tests.

Related: #159640 (QQ Bot move), #159651 (Feishu move).

## Infographic

![held-routes-late-platforms](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab3f420/BMYlbI5jbLjtnSytUou1y_DArfvfKF.png)

prs.title: fix(desktop): support Unicode slash queries
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Typing `/두레이` or `/搜索` in the Desktop composer closes the slash menu because its trigger only accepts ASCII letters. The gateway already searches localized skill descriptions when it receives the query.

Both composer triggers now accept Unicode letters and combining marks. A slash inside the command token still keeps file paths out of completion.

## Related Issue

Fixes #160324.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix

## Changes Made

- Updated the leading and inline slash trigger patterns in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/text-utils.ts`.
- Added regression coverage for Korean and Chinese queries, an inline Devanagari query, and a path with Chinese directory names in `text-utils.test.ts`.

## How to Test

1. In Desktop, type `/두레이` or `look up /두레이` with a skill description that includes `두레이`. The palette should show the skill in both cases.
2. Run `pnpm --dir apps/desktop run test:ui src/app/chat/composer/text-utils.test.ts`. Both new tests fail on the base revision and pass with this change.
3. Run `pnpm --dir apps/desktop run test:ui` and `pnpm --dir apps/desktop run typecheck`. All 14,558 UI tests and the type check passed on macOS 27.3.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide.

prs.title: fix(auth): serialize OAuth refreshes for shared profile logins
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Hermes profiles can borrow a login stored in the root profile instead of keeping their own grant. Providers such as Codex, xAI, and Anthropic rotate refresh tokens on use. A profile-local lock does not coordinate two profiles borrowing the same grant. If both refresh before either writes back, they can lose the shared sign-in.

Related: #146683 (Anthropic), #133560 (Codex), and #81383 (xAI).

## Changes made

- Hold the owning store's lock from the pre-refresh read through write-back. After waiting for the lock, profiles re-read the grant and adopt a peer's rotation rather than refreshing the old token. The xAI resolver does this for both forced and proactive refresh, even if the replacement is still inside the proactive refresh window.
- For stored OAuth grants without a row ID, the default profile and a named profile borrowing its grant derive the same ID. The first pool refresh verifies the matching row and saves that ID under the owning-store lock. A cached legacy grant that no longer resolves there is not refreshed.
- Keep deferred provider I/O outside the credential-pool mutex and publish to the same entry even if round-robin selection changes the ordering. Resolve xAI writes to the exact stored record and preserve the separate Claude Code credential lock.
- Test both refresh orders for the default and named profiles, removal of a cached legacy grant, and xAI adoption while a replacement is still inside the proactive refresh window. Cover Codex and xAI pools, the xAI singleton resolver, and Anthropic pool grants backed by either a pool row or the legacy singleton. Isolate the Claude Code fixture from user configuration.

## How to test

Run the changed suites with the upstream test runner:

```sh
scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 --file-retries 0 \
  tests/agent/test_credential_pool_root_refresh.py \
  tests/agent/test_credential_pool_deferred_refresh.py \
  tests/agent/test_credential_pool_lease_refresh_reselect.py \
  tests/agent/test_credential_pool_refresh_sweep_spacing.py \
  tests/agent/test_credential_pool_anthropic_refresh_race.py \
  tests/agent/test_oauth_root_refresh_race.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_xai_oauth_writethrough.py
```

The shared-login tests use temporary profiles and a loopback token endpoint, not live provider accounts. They verify one rotation, adoption of the rotated grant by both profiles, and no duplicate auth store in either profile.

- Windows, Python 3.14.10: all 49 tests in the seven changed suites passed without retries. That includes all six two-process cases and the five cases for legacy identity and proactive refresh.
- Ruff passed on the changed Python files. The upstream code-health check passed against v0.23.4.

prs.title: fix(telegram): widen the long-text batch window so a jittered burst stays one turn
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A client-side split of a long Telegram message can arrive with a server-side gap of about 1.177 seconds between adapter updates. At `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:459` and `:461` on the base head, the 0.3-second long-text batch window and 1.0-second split window let the first half enter the model as a prompt before the second half arrives as a steer. This change widens those defaults while preserving the existing adaptive fast paths for shorter text.

Trade-off: text over 1,024 characters now waits up to 1.5 s (was 0.3 s) before it is flushed, and a split long message waits 2.0 s (was 1.0 s) between chunks; shorter text is unaffected, and both windows stay operator-overridable through the existing environment variables.

prs.title: Fix(desktop): add reduced effects preference
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a device-local **Settings → Appearance → General → Motion and Effects** preference with **Full** and **Reduced** modes.

Reduced mode preserves visible working-state indicators while replacing continuous shimmer and moving-gradient effects with static equivalents. It also prevents the shared status pulse from scheduling Web Animations and renders the shared SVG loader once instead of maintaining a `requestAnimationFrame` loop.

**Full remains the default**, so existing visuals are unchanged unless the user explicitly enables Reduced mode.

Continuous CSS animations, Web Animations, and frame-driven SVG loaders can keep Chromium's compositor active even when the surrounding UI is unchanged. Merely slowing the animations does not materially reduce that cost because frames are still composited at the display refresh rate. This preference provides an explicit, reversible control without forcing Electron into software rendering or changing the operating system's global reduced-motion setting.

## Related Issue

Mitigates 
[#73082](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/73082)
[#53902 ](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/53902)

This PR addresses persistent decorative and status-animation work. It does not claim to eliminate every feature-specific animation loop in Desktop.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- Added a persisted, device-local reduced-effects preference in `apps/desktop/src/store/reduced-effects.ts`.
- Added Full/Reduced controls to Desktop Appearance settings.
- Disabled continuous CSS animations and transitions in Reduced mode.
- Rendered shimmer text and the active-session arc as static indicators in Reduced mode.
- Stopped the shared `StatusPulse` Web Animation timer in Reduced mode.
- Changed the shared SVG `Loader` to render one static frame instead of scheduling continuous frames in Reduced mode.
- Stopped the pending-image canvas shimmer loop in Reduced mode, preserving static output through resize/theme changes and retaining Full mode's existing animation cap.
- Added translated settings copy for all nine bundled Desktop locales.
- Added regression tests for persistence, startup restoration, live mode switching, status pulses, loader and canvas frame scheduling, static-canvas repainting, and settings-search routing.

## How to Test

1. Launch Hermes Desktop and open **Settings → Appearance → General → Motion and Effects**.
2. Leave the setting on **Full** and confirm shimmer, the moving active-session arc, status pulses, and loaders retain their current behavior.
3. Select **Reduced** and confirm the change applies immediately without restarting Desktop.
4. Start a chat or compaction and confirm status text and the active-session indicator remain visible but static.
5. Quit and reopen Desktop and confirm the Reduced preference persists.
6. Compare Hermes Helper (GPU), Hermes Helper (Renderer), and WindowServer activity before and after enabling Reduced mode.

Manual testing on macOS arm64 showed a dramatic reduction in GPU activity after selecting Reduced while preserving working-state visibility.

prs.title: fix(config): stop ruamel's YAML 1.1 float lint from flooding stderr
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops ruamel's YAML 1.1 float lint from writing ~28 lines of stderr per affected scalar, per load, in every process that reads config.

Hermes asks ruamel for YAML 1.1 so bare `y`/`n`/`off` keep parsing as booleans. 1.1's float type *additionally* requires a dot in the mantissa, so a scalar like `5e-1` emits one `MantissaNoDotYAML1_1Warning` — even though ruamel parses it correctly as `0.5`. The values were never wrong; only the volume was:

```
$ printf 'compression:\n  threshold: 5e-1\n' > /tmp/h/config.yaml
$ HERMES_HOME=/tmp/h hermes status 2>err.txt >out.txt
$ grep -c 'Correct your float' err.txt
6          # six 21-line warning blocks for one float, around 14 lines of real output
```

A `config.yaml` with eight such scalars produced **32 warning blocks (~900 lines)** around a 14-line `hermes status`. That buries CLI output and breaks anything that parses stderr.

`scripts/ci/check_docs_drift.py` already works around this locally with a blanket `simplefilter("ignore")`. This PR answers it once, for that one category, in the shared policy module.

## Related Issue

No issue filed for this — the reproduction is small enough to live in this PR. Say the word and I'll open one if you'd rather track it there.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_yaml.py` — import `MantissaNoDotYAML1_1Warning`, register a module-level `warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=...)` with a comment recording why the 1.1 policy makes that lint noise rather than signal.
- `tests/test_hermes_yaml.py` — two tests: stderr silence across **both** load paths (`safe_load` and `roundtrip_yaml()`, which resolves 1.1 via `_Yaml11Resolver` rather than `yaml.version` and lints too), and a narrowness guard proving unrelated warnings still reach callers.

The filter is registered at import rather than inside `_load()` on purpose: a `catch_warnings()` context mutates process-global warning state, and on Python < 3.14 that is not thread-safe while config loads do run on tool threads. One idempotent registration at import has neither problem and covers both loaders.

## How to Test

1. Reproduce the noise on `main`:
   ```bash
   printf 'compression:\n  threshold: 5e-1\n' > /tmp/h/config.yaml
   HERMES_HOME=/tmp/h hermes status 2>err.txt
   grep -c 'Correct your float' err.txt   # 6 on main, 0 with this branch
   ```
2. Confirm the values are untouched (they always were) — from the repo root:
   ```bash
   python3 - <<'PY'
   import hermes_yaml
   print(hermes_yaml.safe_load("threshold: 5e-1"))
   PY
   # {'threshold': 0.5}
   ```
3. Tests (macOS 26.6.2, Python 3.14.9, pinned `ruamel.yaml==0.18.16` — the version CI uses):
   ```bash
   scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_hermes_yaml.py    # 12 passed
   ```
   The new stderr test fails against `main` and passes here — verified by running it with the source change reverted.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(config): …`)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — no hits for `MantissaNoDot` or the warning text
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] `just check` passes locally
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.6.2, Python 3.13 (test venv) and 3.14.9 (runtime)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — N/A, docstring behaviour unchanged
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — pure stdlib `warnings` filtering, nothing platform-specific; the C/pure parser retry path is exercised by the existing tests
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Before (one offending float in an otherwise empty config):

```
.../ruamel/yaml/constructor.py:508: MantissaNoDotYAML1_1Warning:
In YAML 1.1 floating point values should have a dot ('.') in their mantissa.
...
Correct your float: "5e-1" on line: 2, column: 13
```

After — measured with the patched module in the running tree, not just at library level:

```
$ HERMES_HOME=/tmp/h hermes status 2>err.txt >out.txt
$ grep -c 'Correct your float' err.txt
0                        # stderr is completely empty; stdout unchanged (14 lines both ways)
```

`MantissaNoDotYAML1_1Warning` is exported by `ruamel.yaml.error` in the pinned 0.18.16, so the import carries no version risk.

prs.title: fix(gateway): wait for a webapp.host address an interface is given after boot
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A gateway whose `webapp.host` is one specific address (a LAN, Tailscale/Headscale or WireGuard address, or a DHCP lease) can start before that address is assigned to its interface. The first bind then fails with `EADDRNOTAVAIL`, and `start_gateway_runtime_api` reports `Webapp unavailable: could not listen on HOST:PORT (the address is not assigned to any network interface on this machine)` and falls back to main's private loopback listener for the rest of the process's life. Nothing crashed, so no `Restart=` policy fires: the address stays dark until a human restarts the gateway.

That fallback is right for an address that is genuinely misconfigured. It is wrong for one that appears a second later, which is the normal case for a tailnet address at boot: the gateway unit has no ordering to `tailscaled`, and even `After=tailscaled.service` would not help, since the daemon reporting started is not the address being assigned.

This PR waits, bounded, for the address to appear and binds again. Unit ordering can only cover the daemons Hermes knows about, and not even reliably — a DHCP lease, a `wg-quick` interface or an address added by hand have the same shape. A bounded retry covers all of them with no unit-file knowledge, and costs nothing when the address is already there (the first attempt succeeds).

## Related Issue

Fixes #159606 

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/run_runtime.py`: new `_start_gateway_api_waiting_for_address()` wraps the single `start_gateway_api` call. On `EADDRNOTAVAIL` it sleeps 0.5s and retries until `WEBAPP_ADDRESS_WAIT_SECONDS` (20s) runs out, then raises as before, so the existing `Webapp unavailable` report and loopback fallback are unchanged. `HERMES_WEBAPP_ADDRESS_WAIT` overrides the wait in seconds; `0` restores the single attempt.
- `gateway/run_runtime.py`: only `EADDRNOTAVAIL` is retried. A busy port (`EADDRINUSE`), a refused bind and the loopback companion's own failure (`run_api.ListenerAddressError`) still report at once — waiting cannot fix any of them.
- `gateway/run_runtime.py`: the retry warning is logged once per attempt batch, not once per 0.5s poll, so the journal stays readable.
- `tests/gateway/test_webapp_address_wait.py` (new, 8 tests): the retry that succeeds, the no-Webapp call shape (`start_gateway_api(runner)` with no address), the bounded give-up raising the last error, `0` disabling the wait, `EADDRINUSE` not waited, `ListenerAddressError` not waited, and the override parsing (default, garbage value, unset).

Retrying is safe: `start_gateway_api`'s `except BaseException` already closes the listener, the companion socket and the mount, and clears `_ACTIVE_RUNNER`, before re-raising.

## How to Test

1. `python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_webapp_address_wait.py -q` → 8 passed.

2. The neighbouring listener tests are unchanged, including the one that pins the no-wait behaviour for an address that never appears: `tests/gateway/test_webapp_specific_address.py::test_an_address_no_interface_holds_leaves_the_webapp_unavailable_and_native_clients_a_listener`. With `HERMES_WEBAPP_ADDRESS_WAIT` unset the wait expires and the same receipt comes back, so that test still passes with the same intent.

3. Real-world check: with `HERMES_WEBAPP_ADDRESS_WAIT=2` and `webapp.host: 192.0.2.77` (TEST-NET-1, never assigned), the fixture peer still ends `state: unavailable` with the same reason — the wait expires and reports, it does not hang.

4. Original reproduction, now fixed: set `webapp.host` to a tailnet address, stop `tailscaled`, restart the gateway, then start `tailscaled`. Before: the Webapp stays down until a manual `systemctl restart hermes-gateway`. After: the journal shows the retry warning and the Webapp starts serving once the address appears, with no restart.

prs.title: fix(gateway): verify a backend migration after the restart lands, not on the request
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the ordering bug that makes `hermes gateway migrate --backends --apply` fail on any host that takes longer than a few seconds to restart its gateway, and stops a parked adapter from blocking the move entirely.

The verify step was racing the restart it had just asked for:

- `start_gateway` calls `host.gateway_verb("restart")` and **returns immediately**. A supervised restart only *requests* the restart — the gateway drains in-band and keeps its API up, answering `503 {"code": "gateway_draining"}` (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`) until it exits. Verification therefore spent its entire budget probing the very process it was replacing. Held open by a caller's own in-flight turn, that was 376 s of consecutive 503s, and `verify` failed with `no HTTP 200 on <addr>/api/status` even though the address was up the whole time.
- `VERIFY_SECONDS = 90` was the floor for the *whole* boot. On a busy multi-profile home the gateway prints its startup banner 56–92 s before `Starting Hermes Gateway`, so 90 s can never pass on such a host.
- `gateway_serving()` required `gateway_state == "running"`. One adapter that parks at startup (e.g. `sms` refusing without `SMS_WEBHOOK_URL`) pins the state to `degraded` permanently, and the migration could never verify at all — though it only needs the Webapp to serve.

Measured on the reporting host (macOS, launchd, ~20 profiles): the first two attempts rolled back; after this change the same command completes with all eight steps done.

## Related Issue

Fixes #

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_migrate_backends_apply.py`
  - `start_gateway` now records the pre-restart PID and waits for a **replacement** PID (`_await_replacement`, bounded by the new `RESTART_HANDOFF_SECONDS`) before the verify step's clock starts. Advisory only: verify stays the arbiter, and a hand-off that never lands prints a warning and falls through to it.
  - `VERIFY_SECONDS` 90 → 300, with the comment updated to say why the budget is generous.
  - `gateway_serving()` accepts `gateway_state` `degraded` as well as `running` — a platform being down does not mean the Webapp is not serving.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_migrate_backends_apply.py` — the shared fixture zeroes the new `RESTART_HANDOFF_SECONDS` alongside the other clock constants.
- `tests/hermes_cli/gateway_migrate_backends_apply/test_engine.py` — four tests over a host whose restart only answers 503 until it exits: verification never probes status before the hand-off; a hand-off that never lands still verifies and says so; `degraded` passes; a genuinely down state still rolls back.

## How to Test

1. On a host with a slow gateway boot, run `hermes gateway migrate --backends --apply --keep-webapp-address --yes --detach` from a shell outside the gateway.
2. Follow with `hermes gateway migrate --backends --status`. Before this change verify failed with `no HTTP 200 …` and rolled back; now the run reaches `verify` only after the replacement PID is up and completes with `done`.
3. Narrower: `python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/gateway_migrate_backends_apply/`.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass
- [x] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 26.6.2 (launchd, `gui/501`)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — docstrings on the new helper and the constants
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — N/A, no config keys
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — systemd (Linux) also drains in-band on SIGUSR1 and gets the same benefit; the wait is host-agnostic and only reads `gateway_pid()`
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Screenshots / Logs

Before (both attempts), from `~/.hermes/logs/backend-migration.log`:

```
  ✓ old backend stopped and disabled (unit file kept)
  ✗ verify failed: verification failed after 90s: no HTTP 200 on 127.0.0.1:9122/api/status
  ↩ Rolling back...
```

The gateway log over the same window — the restart only being *requested*, and the boot really taking that long:

```
13:32:43 INFO gateway.run: Restart requested; waiting for idle while serving normally (warn after 1800s)
13:39:00 INFO gateway.run: Restart wait complete after 377.0s: gateway idle; restarting
13:57:03 │           ☤ Hermes Gateway Starting...
13:58:03 INFO gateway.run: Starting Hermes Gateway...
```

`/api/status` while draining, and the state that used to fail the check:

```
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9122/api/status
{"error": "Gateway is draining existing work; retry shortly.", "code": "gateway_draining"}   # 503
{"gateway_state": "degraded", ...}                                                          # once idle, before the sms adapter was parked
```

After, the status tail:

```
Backend migration: done (step verify)
  message: migrated: the gateway serves 127.0.0.1:9122
```

prs.title: fix(gateway): find a user-unit dashboard from a shell without the user bus
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes gateway migrate --backends` finds who supervises a running dashboard by asking `systemctl --user` for a unit's `MainPID`. From a shell without `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` (SSH, `env -u`, some headless setups) that query fails. The dashboard of a user unit was then classified as a manual backend and listed a second time as its installed unit. The same PID showed up twice and blocked the migration as a competing backend.

`collect_backends()` now calls `_ensure_user_systemd_env()` first on Linux, as the gateway's other `systemctl --user` callers do (`update_cmd_fleet`, `update_cmd_posix_pause`), so discovery sees the unit as the dashboard's one owner. Ownership that still can't be proven keeps the existing fail-closed classification.

## Related Issue

Fixes #160028

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/gateway_migrate_backends.py`: `collect_backends()` sets up the user systemd environment before discovery (Linux only; the helper runs no subprocess).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_migrate_backends.py`: a user-unit dashboard, with a fake `systemctl --user` that fails like a shell without the user bus until `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is set, is reported once, as `systemd` with its unit and `user` scope.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_gateway_migrate_backends.py`: 26 passed, 3 skipped.
2. Without the fix, the new test fails: on `main` the dashboard comes back as a manual backend plus its unit. Checked by reverting only `gateway_migrate_backends.py`: the test fails without it and passes with it.

prs.title: fix(cli): parse relaunched inline-bootstrap dashboard and serve arguments
prs.body:
Fixes #158686

## Problem
When a `hermes dashboard` or `hermes serve` backend is relaunched by `venv_sync` (or runs via an inline Python bootstrap), the command line in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` or `ps` is structured like:
```bash
python3 -I -c "import sys, runpy; sys.path.insert(0, '...'); sys.argv = ['main.py', 'serve', '--host', '100.x.y.z', '--port', '9119']; sys._hermes_relaunched = True; runpy.run_module('hermes_cli.main', ...)"
```
In `hermes_cli/main_dashboard.py`, `_parse_dashboard_runtime()` previously ran `re.search(r"(?:^|\s)--host...")` directly against the command-line string. Because `--host` and `--port` were enclosed within single quotes inside the Python code string (e.g. `', '--host', '100.x.y.z'`), the regex failed to match (the character immediately preceding `--host` was `'`, not whitespace or start of line). This caused `_parse_dashboard_runtime()` to fall back to the default `127.0.0.1:9119`.

As reported in #158686, this broke `hermes gateway migrate --backends`: the planner read the old backend as `127.0.0.1:9119` rather than its actual listening address, leading to incorrect migration planning, mismatching address blockers, or verification rollbacks due to auth discrepancies.

## Solution
1. In `_parse_dashboard_runtime()`, tokenize the command and unwrap inline bootstrap source via `gateway.status_inline_source.inline_bootstrap_argv()`.
2. Extract `--host` and `--port` directly from the unwrapped tokens (supporting both `--flag <val>` and `--flag=<val>`), retaining the regex search as fallback.
3. Added a unit test in `tests/hermes_cli/test_process_identity_canonical_matchers.py` verifying that an inline-bootstrap command line extracts `("serve", "0.0.0.0", 9119)`.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add pure-language plugin
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/pure-language.yaml`, listing [joowon-jang/pure-language](https://github.com/joowon-jang/pure-language) pinned to `7b45059ab100f64acb50e667c1f2d738aa714b11` (0.1.0). The PR comes from the repository's owner (rule 5).

**What the plugin does:** keeps each answer in a single language. The target language is chosen per turn from an explicit command in the user's message (`answer in English`, `영어로 답해줘`, `日本語で答えて`, …; sticky for the session), otherwise from the language the user wrote in (54 languages across 22 scripts), otherwise a configurable default. `pre_llm_call` injects a one-line guard in that language (the longer rule only on the turn after a leak, to keep per-turn tokens low). `transform_llm_output` checks the final answer for leaks from other languages (foreign scripts, Simplified-only Han characters in Japanese, stray English words) and returns a cleaned copy. Korean answers get local fixes first (word tables with particle correction, Hanja → Hangul readings from bundled Unihan data). Only lines the local rules cannot fix are rewritten, in one bounded `ctx.llm.complete_structured` call; a rewrite that breaks the line's markdown structure is discarded, and on failure a deterministic fallback is used, so the answer is never lost. Code, URLs, paths, acronyms, proper nouns and anything the user typed are never changed; pasted terminal/log/stack-trace lines are not treated as a language, and verbatim quotes (3+ words) of this turn's tool output are kept. A message that is only pasted command output keeps the conversation's language, and an answer written wholly in the wrong language is rewritten as a whole in the same bounded call (left untouched if the call fails). Background turns that share the session (review forks) fire no `pre_llm_call` and are left alone.

The same repository also ships Claude Code and Codex hooks that reuse the engine; Hermes does not load them.

**Hermes surfaces used:** `register_hook("pre_llm_call")`, `register_hook("post_tool_call")` (observe-only: keeps this turn's tool output in memory so the answer may quote it verbatim; returns nothing), `register_hook("transform_llm_output")` (opt-in `hold_stream=True` via a user setting), `register_auxiliary_task("pure_language_rewrite")`, `ctx.llm.complete_structured(task=...)`. No tools, middleware, core patching or Python dependencies. `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes at the pinned commit.

**Disclosures** (also in the entry description and the README):

- **Model calls:** when an answer has leaks the local rules cannot fix, one extra call to the user's model through `ctx.llm` on the plugin's own auxiliary slot (default: main model; hard deadline 15 s in a worker thread, configurable 5–20 s, so Hermes' 30 s hook limit is never reached; after a failure or timeout model rewrites pause for 10 minutes and only local fixes apply). Clean answers make no call. Only the leaking sentences are sent, with a short instruction and an output budget sized to the input.
- **Network:** none of its own.
- **Credentials:** none; no `.env`, `auth.json` or other credential reads.
- **Local files:** reads optional `$HERMES_HOME/pure-language.json`; optional log of leak snippets (about 20 characters around each hit, never whole answers) at `$HERMES_HOME/logs/pure-language.log`, **off by default**, rotated at 1 MB. Bundled data files are derived from the Unicode Unihan database (Unicode License v3, see `NOTICE`).
- **No** shell commands, background processes, telemetry or self-updating code.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) — new catalog entry only

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/pure-language.yaml` (new file, no other changes)

## How to Test

1. `git clone https://github.com/joowon-jang/pure-language && git -C pure-language checkout 7b45059ab100f64acb50e667c1f2d738aa714b11`
2. `hermes plugins validate pure-language --install-deps` (passes locally on Hermes 0.23.4, Windows 11)
3. `python -m unittest discover -s tests` from the plugin root (16 tests, no model calls)
4. `hermes plugins install pure-language --enable`, then ask a question in one language and check the reply stays in it

prs.title: fix(approval): hardline blocklist bypassable via escaped quote in command text
prs.body:
## Summary

The hardline blocklist — documented as unbypassable, "not even with `--yolo`, `/yolo`, `approvals.mode=off`" — can be bypassed by placing one escaped double quote in front of any hardline command:

```python
>>> check_dangerous_command('cat "f\\"n.txt"; rm -rf --no-preserve-root /', "local")
{'approved': True, ...}
```

Reproduced on current `main` (`6c40300f9`). The same root cause also produces a false positive that blocks ordinary read-only commands, which is how I found it:

```
grep -n "^from\|^__all__\|^    \"" tools/environments/__init__.py
BLOCKED (hardline): command parser limit or malformed executable payload
```

Three commits, one root cause: shell quote state is evaluated against text that normalization has already rewritten.

## Root cause

`_normalize_command_for_detection` strips backslash escapes (`\"` → `"`) so that `r\m` cannot hide `rm`. That is correct for pattern matching, but two consumers need *faithful* quote state and currently receive the normalized string:

**1. Grep operand parsing (false positive).** `detect_hardline_command` passes normalized text to `_grep_safe_detection_variant`. After escape stripping, a valid pattern like `"^from\|^    \""` has an odd number of quotes, the parse is reported malformed, and the call fails closed. Legitimate `grep` invocations get hardline-blocked with a message about "malformed executable payload".

**2. Command-start marking (bypass).** `_CMDPOS`-anchored hardline patterns do not match `; reboot` on their own — they fire only after `_mark_command_starts` splices a separator at each quote-aware command start. With an escaped quote present, normalization leaves the quote open:

```
raw         echo "a\"b"; reboot
normalized  echo "a"b"; reboot          <- quote never closes
segments    ['echo "a"b"; reboot']      <- one unterminated segment
```

No start is marked, so the floor never fires. Any hardline command after such a prefix executes.

**3. `${IFS}` interaction (second bypass).** `_iter_shell_command_starts` treats `{` as a command-start opener, so it marks a start *inside* `${IFS}`, producing `${ \nIFS}`. That token no longer matches the IFS-collapse regex in normalization, so the expansion is never applied:

```
echo "a\"b"; rm${IFS}-rf${IFS}--no-preserve-root${IFS}/
```

Confirmed executable with a safe analogue (`echo${IFS}BYPASS_EXECUTED`, rc=0, second statement ran).

## Fix

Each commit is additive — variant generation is any-match, so adding a variant can only tighten the floor, never loosen it.

1. **`parse raw grep quote state before hardline checks`** — validate grep syntax against `_mask_quoted_newlines(command)` rather than normalized text. Quoted newlines are still masked (they are data), but escapes are left intact so quote counting is correct.

2. **`mark command starts from faithful quote state`** — emit an *additional* detection variant whose command starts are marked before normalization runs. The marker is `" \n"` rather than `"\n"`: a preceding backslash would otherwise absorb the inserted newline as a line continuation during normalization, silently undoing the marking. `_mark_command_starts` gains an optional `marker` parameter defaulting to `"\n"`, so existing callers are unchanged.

3. **`don't mark command starts inside parameter expansions`** — add `_scan_parameter_expansion_end` and skip the whole `${...}` span in `_iter_shell_command_starts` before the `(`/`{` opener check. Depth-tracked, quote-aware, escape-aware; an unterminated expansion is handled like the existing `$(`/backtick `None` cases.

## Verification

- **RED/GREEN per commit**: 14 → 0, 12 → 0, 4 → 0 failing tests.
- **Suite**: `222 passed, 1 skipped` across `test_execution_flag_detection.py`, `test_approval.py`, `test_blocked_command_guidance.py`.
- **Mutation-tested**: reverting each of the three source changes while keeping the tests fails 14, 12, and 4 tests respectively — no change is unprotected.
- **30 hand-checked cases** with `HERMES_YOLO_MODE=1`, asserting both `detect_hardline_command` and `check_dangerous_command(...)["approved"]`:
  - 10 bypass variants (escaped quote before `rm -rf /`, `reboot`, `shutdown`, `systemctl reboot`, `${IFS}`, `${IFS:0:1}`, `&&` and `;` separators) — all blocked.
  - 8 valid commands (the original `grep` false positive, `egrep` with escaped quote, PCRE data containing hardline text, quoted separators, quoted `${IFS}`) — all pass.
  - 11 non-regression cases (`reboot`, `rm -rf /`, `(reboot)`, `{ shutdown -h now; }`, `$(reboot)`, backticks, `bash -c "reboot"`, line continuation, bare `${IFS}` expansion) — identical results before and after.
  - Fail-closed preserved: `grep -n "unterminated file` still reports malformed.

## Notes

- A single-quote analogue (`echo 'a\'b'; reboot`) was investigated and is **not** a bypass — bash rejects it with rc=2 (unterminated quote), so it cannot execute.
- No existing detection was weakened and no existing test was modified; all changes to `tools/approval.py` are new code paths or a strict narrowing of a false-positive path.

prs.title: fix(auxiliary): classify provider rate limits signalled as 5xx
prs.body:
## Symptom

A gateway session repeatedly surfaces this to the user, several times per hour:

```
⚠️ Context compression timed out after 30.0s with no output from the summary model.
No messages were dropped — continuing without compression. Run /compress to retry,
/reset for a clean session, or check your auxiliary.compression model configuration.
```

Measured across ~24h of production gateway logs on one host: **69 timeout events across 24 distinct sessions**, one session hitting it 12 times. Every single event logs `total wait 30.1s` — meaning `CompressionCommitFence.touch_progress` was never called even once, so the host saw pure silence rather than a slow-but-generating model.

The auxiliary log line immediately preceding each event:

```
Auxiliary compression: transient transport error (attempt 1/2); retrying same provider
after 1.0s before fallback: Error code: 503 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type':
'api_error', 'message': 'Rate limit exceeded. Try again in 4h 23m ...'}}
```

## Root cause

The provider (an Anthropic-compatible load balancer) signals **rate limiting with HTTP 503**, not 429, carrying the reason in the payload.

1. `_is_rate_limit_error` only recognises HTTP 429 (plus an SDK class named `RateLimitError`), so it returns `False` for this 503.
2. `_is_transient_transport_error` returns `True` for any `500 <= status < 600`, so the rate limit is classified as a one-off transport blip.
3. The except-chain therefore retries the **same saturated provider** with `time.sleep(backoff)` instead of falling through to the provider/model fallback chain that `_is_rate_limit_error` exists to trigger. The provider says "try again in 4h 23m"; we retry in 1s, twice.
4. All of that happens *before* the first streamed token. The forward-progress hook only ticks on dispatch and on stream events — for an `AnthropicAuxiliaryClient`, `_client_streams_internally` is `True`, so ticks come from `create_anthropic_message(..., on_stream_event=...)`, which never fires because the request never succeeds. Gateway session hygiene sees no progress and kills the attempt at its idle budget.
5. An existing fast-fail for exactly this shape is gated on `_is_timeout_error` only, so a rate-limit 503 does not match and compression eats the full retry ladder on the critical preflight path.

Net effect: compression can never succeed while the provider is saturated, the message count never drops, the next turn re-triggers hygiene compression, and the user gets the warning again — a loop, with the fallback chain that would have rescued it never consulted.

## Changes

**1. Classify provider-signalled rate limits regardless of HTTP status** (`agent/auxiliary_client.py`)

`_is_rate_limit_error` now also recognises a 5xx whose payload explicitly indicates rate limiting or quota exhaustion (`rate limit`, `rate-limited`, `quota exceeded`, `quota-exhausted`, `try again in`). Bare 5xx with no such wording is untouched and still transient. 429 and `RateLimitError` detection are byte-identical to before.

`_is_payment_error` gets the mirrored treatment for 5xx-wrapped billing failures and keeps precedence, so unambiguous credit exhaustion stays in the payment bucket even though such payloads often also suggest retrying later.

`_is_transient_transport_error` now returns `False` for anything already classified as a rate-limit or payment error. Its docstring already claimed to be "deliberately narrow … distinct from `_is_payment_error` / `_is_auth_error` / `_is_rate_limit_error`"; the code now matches. Connection errors and genuine 5xx/408 retry exactly as before.

The predicate is fixed in one place, so the sync path, the async path, and `_create_with_progress`'s raise-through gate all inherit it.

**2. Fast-fail compression on rate limits, not just timeouts**

The compression critical-path guard now also skips the same-provider retry for a provider-signalled rate limit, in both the sync and async call paths, and names the reason in the log line. Cheap blips still retry.

**3. Truthful timeout messages** (`gateway/run.py`, `run_agent.py`)

The old text pointed users at `auxiliary.compression`, which is not the knob governing either wait. Each message now names the setting that actually applies to its own code path — `compression.hygiene_timeout_seconds` for gateway session hygiene, `compression.context_timeout_seconds` for the in-agent compress path — alongside the auxiliary provider.

When the compressor recorded a known cause, the message now says so ("because the summary provider reported a rate limit …") instead of asserting "no output from the summary model", which was actively misleading here. `compression_failure_cause()` (`agent/conversation_compression.py`) maps recorded failure state to one of a few **fixed** strings and never interpolates provider payloads, so account ids, request ids, and other secret-adjacent material cannot leak into a user-facing warning.

**4. Stop swallowing the underlying error** (`gateway/run.py`)

`Session hygiene auto-compress failed: ` was logging an empty reason in production. It now falls back to the exception type when `str(exc)` is empty, and normalises whitespace so the record stays one line.

## Non-goals

No changes to `hygiene_hard_message_limit`, compression thresholds, `target_ratio`, `protect_last_n`, the hygiene threshold, or the `_hyg_timeout_seconds` / `_hyg_total_ceiling_seconds` defaults. No new env vars.

Notably, the progress hook is **not** ticked during retry backoff sleeps. That would mask the stall and let a provider that is rate-limited for hours hold the turn open to the 600s ceiling. Correct classification is the fix; hiding the silence is not.

## Tests

New `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_rate_limit_5xx.py` plus assertions added to `test_compress_context_progress_timeout.py` and `tests/gateway/test_session_hygiene.py`, written as behaviour contracts:

- a 503 carrying rate-limit wording is a rate limit and **not** a transient transport error
- a 503 with generic server-error wording is **still** transient and still retries (no regression)
- billing/credit exhaustion is still a payment error, not a rate limit
- `task == "compression"` with a rate-limit error makes exactly one same-provider attempt before falling back
- non-compression tasks are unaffected by the compression fast-fail
- user-facing warnings name the correct config key, state the known cause, and contain no account identifier

### Verification

```
$ uv run pytest tests/agent/test_auxiliary_rate_limit_5xx.py \
    tests/agent/test_auxiliary_transient_retry.py \
    tests/agent/test_aux_progress_streaming.py \
    tests/agent/test_auxiliary_compression_timeout_floor.py \
    tests/agent/test_compress_context_progress_timeout.py \
    tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py \
    tests/gateway/test_session_hygiene.py -q
239 passed in 37.53s
```

Broader selection `pytest tests/agent -q -k "auxiliary or compress"` gives `2 failed, 775 passed`. Both failures are `test_auxiliary_main_first.py::TestResolveVisionCustomProvider` and are **pre-existing**: the same two fail identically on unmodified `origin/main` (`2 failed, 770 passed`) in a separate worktree, and both pass in an isolated process — order-dependent runtime-state leakage unrelated to these paths.

Mutation check, to confirm the new tests actually bite: removing the `_is_transient_transport_error` guard makes `test_rate_limit_503_is_not_transient_transport_error` and `test_billing_503_remains_payment_not_rate_limit` fail, and restoring it makes them pass.

`git diff --check` clean.

prs.title: fix(transport): strip internal scaffolding keys + classify 5xx validation errors as non-retryable
prs.body:
## Summary

Two related fixes for a deterministic-error retry flood observed when running against strict OpenAI-compatible gateways. The empty-response recovery path leaks an internal bookkeeping key onto the wire; the error classifier then mistakes the gateway's deterministic rejection for a transient server error and retries it into a flood.

## The bug

The empty-response recovery path in `run_agent.py` appends synthetic messages tagged with `_empty_recovery_synthetic`:

```python
_nudge_msg["_empty_recovery_synthetic"] = True
messages.append(_nudge_msg)
messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "...", "_empty_recovery_synthetic": True})
```

These are internal markers (so `_drop_trailing_empty_response_scaffolding` can later identify and strip them from the persisted transcript). They are **not** meant to reach the API.

`chat_completions`' `convert_messages` sanitizes Codex Responses leak fields (`codex_reasoning_items`, `call_id`, …) but **not** these `_`-prefixed markers. Real OpenAI and Anthropic silently ignore unknown message keys, so the bug stayed hidden there. Strict OpenAI-compatible gateways reject them:

```
502: [ObjectParam] [input[617]._empty_recovery_synthetic]
     [unknown_parameter] Unknown parameter: '_empty_recovery_synthetic'
```

Because the synthetic messages persist in the session, **every** subsequent request in that session carries the poisoned key and fails identically. The error classifier maps `502` → `server_error` → `retryable=True`, so the retry loop burns all 3 attempts, the transport-recovery path resets the counter and burns 3 more — a request flood against a request that can never succeed.

## Fix 1 — `chat_completions` transport (`agent/transports/chat_completions.py`)

`convert_messages` now drops any top-level message key starting with `_` (covers `_empty_recovery_synthetic`, `_empty_terminal_sentinel`, `_thinking_prefill`, and any future internal markers). OpenAI's message schema has no `_`-prefixed fields, so this is safe and future-proof. Deepcopy-on-demand semantics preserved — a clean message list is still returned by identity.

## Fix 2 — error classifier (`agent/error_classifier.py`)

Standard OpenAI returns request-validation failures as `4xx`. Some OpenAI-compatible gateways return them as `5xx` instead. When a `500`/`502` body carries an unambiguous request-validation signal — `unknown parameter` / `unsupported parameter` / `invalid_request_error` in the message text, or `invalid_request_error` / `unknown_parameter` / `unsupported_parameter` as the structured error code — it's now classified as a non-retryable `format_error` so the loop fails fast and falls back instead of flooding. Genuine `502 Bad Gateway` with no such signal stays retryable as before.

Fix 1 is the root cause; Fix 2 is defense-in-depth so any other deterministic `5xx`-as-validation-error can't produce the same flood.

## Tests

- `tests/agent/transports/test_chat_completions.py` — new: internal `_`-prefixed markers stripped; visible content preserved; original list untouched; clean list returned by identity.
- `tests/agent/test_error_classifier.py` — new: `502` + `unknown parameter` → non-retryable `format_error`; `502` + `unsupported parameter`; `500` + `invalid_request_error` error-code; plain `502 Bad Gateway` stays retryable.

All 448 tests in `tests/agent/transports/` + `tests/agent/test_error_classifier.py` + `tests/providers/test_transport_parity.py` pass. (`tests/run_agent/test_provider_parity.py` has 3 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change — they hit the live Nous API and fail on a context-window check; verified failing on pristine `main`.)

prs.title: perf(state): read-path split — per-thread read-only connections for recall reads
prs.body:
## Problem

The gateway shares one \`SessionDB\` across every agent, and every read — \`session_search\` discover/scroll/browse, memory prefetch, title resolution — goes through the same \`self._lock\` + single connection as every writer flush. That is one Python lock in front of a WAL database whose whole design point is concurrent readers alongside a single writer.

Under concurrent load this convoys hard. Production measurements (turn-waterfall traces, 2,605 turns): with 6-8 concurrent turns flushing tool results, a \`session_search\` FTS query that takes **0.23s standalone stretched to 112s** in-gateway, and one browse call's post-tool flush waited **137s** behind the same lock. \`session_search\` averaged 12.4s in-gateway vs 0.26s standalone on identical queries.

## Fix

Under WAL, the read-only recall methods (\`get_session\`, \`resolve_session_by_title\`, \`list_sessions_rich\`, \`get_messages\`, \`get_messages_around\`, \`get_anchored_view\`, \`search_messages\`) run on a per-thread \`mode=ro\` connection via a new \`_read_ctx()\` context manager — no lock at all. WAL readers see a consistent snapshot and never block on the writer; fresh read transactions begin per statement, so read-your-committed-writes holds for the flush-then-search patterns inside a turn.

Degradation is conservative:
- non-WAL journal mode (the NFS \`DELETE\` fallback) keeps the legacy locked single-connection path — rollback-journal readers can hit \`SQLITE_BUSY\` storms during writes;
- a failed read-only open falls back to the locked path and is remembered per thread (no per-query retry);
- \`close()\` closes the calling thread's read connection; other threads' connections hold no locks and are reclaimed by GC.

No user-facing knobs, no config changes — pure internal concurrency fix.

## Tests

\`tests/test_session_db_read_path_split.py\`: reads complete while another thread holds \`self._lock\` (the convoy repro), per-thread connection identity, read-your-writes visibility, non-WAL fallback, open-failure memoization, anchored-view/window reads off the lock.

## Production results (fork, 3 gateways, 2026-07-16)

Combined with an FTS-side fix, in-gateway \`session_search\` on the same workload dropped from 45-112s worst cases to double-digit milliseconds; the read-path split removes the ×10-20 contention multiplier for every DB read the gateway makes.

prs.title: refactor(agent): remove the inter-tool delay
prs.body:
## Problem

`tool_delay` sleeps 1.0s between sequential tool calls (`agent/tool_executor.py`). It has been present verbatim since the initial commit with no documented rationale, and on inspection it protects nothing:

- The sleep runs between **local tool executions**. The next LLM request only goes out after the whole batch completes, so it rate-limits no API.
- The parallel read-only tool path already runs with **no delay** — the two paths are inconsistent for no stated reason.
- The cost is real: every multi-tool turn pays (N−1) seconds of dead wall-clock. Per-turn tracing on a production deployment showed 0.06s tool executions spaced 1.08s apart; a 30-tool sequential turn spends 29 seconds asleep.

We have been running with the delay at 0 in production for several days across three gateways with no observed provider-side throttling or behavioral issues.

## Change

Remove the sleep, the `tool_delay` constructor parameter (`AIAgent.__init__` / `initialize_agent`), and the now-dead `agent.tool_delay = 0` assignments scattered across tests.

Note this removes a public constructor kwarg. In-repo, `run_agent.py` was the only pass-through caller and no config surface (config.yaml / CLI flag / env) exposed it. If maintainers prefer a deprecation cycle, I'm happy to keep an accepted-but-ignored kwarg for one release instead.

## Tests

- `tests/run_agent/test_run_agent.py`: 422 passed on this branch.
- Sequential-tool-loop suites (tool_call, guardrail, overflow, 413, malformed, partial-stream, completion-explainer): all pass.
- Removed only dead `agent.tool_delay = 0` lines from tests; no assertions changed.

## Measured impact

(N−1) seconds saved per sequential multi-tool turn; typical agentic turns in our tracing ran 5–30 tool calls.

prs.title: fix(memory): forward checkpoint requirement to v2 providers
prs.body:
## Symptom

With `compression.checkpoint_required: true` and a memory provider advertising `pre_compress_checkpoint_api_version = 2`, a failing durable write does **not** block compression. The provider swallows the failure, the host treats the checkpoint as succeeded, and lossy compression proceeds — silently defeating the guarantee the option exists to provide.

## Root cause

`MemoryManager.on_pre_compress()` detects v2 providers, selects the normalized `evidence_messages` for them, and re-raises their failures under `require_checkpoint` — but the actual call never forwards the flag:

```python
result = provider.on_pre_compress(provider_messages)
```

A v2 provider therefore runs in its default best-effort mode (`require_checkpoint=False`), so the exception path the host is prepared to re-raise is never taken.

## Reproduction

Probe provider registering what it receives:

```python
class ProbeProvider:
    pre_compress_checkpoint_api_version = 2
    def on_pre_compress(self, messages, **kwargs):
        observed.update(kwargs)   # -> {} : require_checkpoint never arrives
        return ""
```

A v2 provider whose durable write always fails passes `require_checkpoint=True` through `MemoryManager.on_pre_compress` without raising — compression proceeds, original messages are lost.

## Fix

Forward `require_checkpoint` only to providers advertising the requested checkpoint API version. Legacy providers keep the strict one-argument `on_pre_compress(self, messages)` contract, so bundled v1 providers (honcho, mem0, supermemory, …) are unaffected — passing the kwarg unconditionally would `TypeError` on every one of them.

## Tests

`tests/agent/test_pre_compress_checkpoint_contract.py` (+54 lines on the existing file): required and best-effort signaling, legacy signature compatibility, and required-mode failure propagation. 20 passed on current `main` (`7aebf300a7`).
