prs.title: perf(gateway): byte-stable system prompts — pin the session-context render, deliver per-turn notes on the user message
prs.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Stacked on #64293 (api_content sidecar) — the one-shot note relocation rides that PR's replay mechanism. The first commit here is #64293's; review the top commit.

## Problem

The composed gateway system prompt changes bytes between consecutive turns — byte-diffing a production capture localized the churn to the tail (~char 36,864 of 39,618). Two consequences, both per message:

1. **Provider prompt cache re-key.** The system prompt is the head of every request, so a one-byte change re-prefills the entire context. Production first-call prompt-cache hit rate measured 0.1%.
2. **Full AIAgent rebuild.** The ephemeral prompt participates in the gateway agent-cache signature (`_agent_config_signature`), so any byte change also discards the cached agent — tool schemas, LLM clients, frozen system prompt — and rebuilds it.

The volatile bytes all come from the `## Current Session Context` block, re-rendered from live platform state on every message:

- **Discord auto-thread rename** moves the `**Source:**` line and the origin-delivery line on turn 2 (placeholder title → generated title), and any later rename does it again.
- **Voice-channel state** (members/speaking) serializes differently essentially every turn the bot sits in a voice channel.
- **One-shot notes** — the auto-reset notice and the first-contact intro / profile-build directive — are present on turn 1 and absent on turn 2, a guaranteed diff.
- **`get_connected_platforms()`** returns platforms in dict insertion order, so a gateway restart or mid-process platform registration can reorder the `**Connected Platforms:**` line with zero semantic change.

## Change

Stacks on the api_content sidecar PR ("feat(cache): persist the exact bytes sent to the API in an api_content sidecar") and should merge after it.

1. **Per-session pin for the session-context render** (`gateway/run.py`). `_pinned_session_context_prompt` keys the rendered bytes by `_ephemeral_change_key` — a sha256 over exactly the fields `build_session_context_prompt` renders (platform, chat/thread ids, chat name/type/topic, user identity, shared-multi-user flag, Discord ids + tools gate + message-id *presence*, connected platforms, home channels, redact_pii, hermes-home display). Key hit → the pinned bytes are returned verbatim; key miss → one re-render and re-pin. The only re-renders left are real state changes: thread rename (including the one-shot auto-thread rename at turn 2), topic edit, `/sethome`, `redact_pii` flip, toolset flip. The pin (and the voice-channel last-value below) is dropped in `_evict_cached_agent`, so a rebuilt agent always re-renders once.

2. **Per-turn one-shot facts move onto the current user message** (`gateway/run.py`, `agent/turn_context.py`). The auto-reset notice, first-contact intro / profile-build directive, and voice-channel state no longer append to the ephemeral system prompt. They are staged per session (`_set_pending_turn_sidecar_notes`), consumed exactly once at the turn boundary in `run_sync`, and delivered by the prologue through the same user-message injection channel as plugin context — so the api_content sidecar persists the exact sent bytes and history replays them stably. Multimodal (list) content cannot take the string sidecar; the notes are appended as a durable text part instead of being dropped. Staged-but-never-consumed notes are cleared on session finalization (session keys are source-derived and reused by the next conversation) and staging happens after the message-text early-out, so an aborted turn cannot leak notes forward.

3. **Voice-channel note only-when-changed** (`gateway/run.py`). `_voice_channel_sidecar_note` compares the live Discord voice-channel context against the last value delivered for the session and emits `[Voice channel now: ...]` only on change (leaving the channel emits a "not connected" note once). The Discord section of the session-context prompt carries a static pointer line telling the model where the state appears (`gateway/session.py`).

4. **Sorted `get_connected_platforms()`** (`gateway/config.py`) so the rendered platform list and derived home-channel blocks are byte-stable across restarts and registration order.

## Correctness notes

- **Staleness is bounded by the key invariant**: any renderer input whose change alters the rendered bytes must appear in `_ephemeral_change_key`. The parity test mutates every rendered field and asserts render-change ⇒ key-change; omitting a field would mean serving stale (cosmetic) context, while an extra field only costs a spurious re-render. Message-id is keyed by presence only — its value is delivered per-turn in the user message and does not render.
- **Notes cannot be lost or double-delivered.** Staging is one-shot (popped in `run_sync`), the prologue consume clears the agent attribute, and `run_sync` assigns the attribute unconditionally so a reused cached agent never replays a stale note. The multimodal fallback appends the note as message content (persisted and replayed as-is).
- **No behavior change for non-gateway paths.** CLI/run_agent never set `_gateway_turn_context_notes`; the prologue consume is a no-op without it.
- **Intended one-time byte changes**: the static voice-channel pointer line in the Discord session context, and the connected-platforms sort (both stabilize immediately after deployment).

## Tests

- `tests/gateway/test_prompt_tail_freeze.py` (new, 37 tests): key↔render parity across every rendered input (incl. redact_pii and the Discord tools gate; message-id value change is a no-bust), pin verbatim-reuse identity, auto-thread rename busts exactly once then sha256-equal composed prompts, codex `_content_cache_key` constancy across turns, voice-channel only-when-changed matrix, one-shot staging semantics, connected-platforms order.
- `tests/agent/test_gateway_turn_sidecar.py` (new, 8 tests): consume is one-shot; string content delivers via the api_content sidecar with clean stored content; notes order after plugin context; multimodal list-append fallback.
- `tests/gateway`, `tests/agent`, `tests/run_agent` run against a clean checkout of the base: no failures unique to this change.

## Measured impact

Production gateway (Discord, median ~156k-token contexts): before, the composed system prompt changed at the tail nearly every turn and first-call prompt-cache hit rate was 0.1%, with a full AIAgent rebuild per message. With this change plus the api_content sidecar PR it stacks on, first-call prompt-cache hit rate went to 98.7% — all 220 messages in the measurement window replayed the head prefix intact, reusing the cached agent instead of rebuilding it.

prs.title: feat(cache): persist the exact bytes sent to the API in an api_content sidecar
prs.body:
## Problem

The first LLM call of every gateway turn gets ~0% provider prompt-cache hit rate while in-turn calls get 97-99%. The cause is that the bytes sent to the API are not the bytes replayed from the persisted transcript on the next turn:

1. Memory-prefetch and `pre_llm_call` plugin context are injected into the API copy of the current turn's user message only — the stored content stays clean, so next turn the message replays *without* the injection.
2. The gateway's persist override (#48677) writes cleaned content to the user row, not what was sent.
3. `get_messages_as_conversation` runs user/assistant content through `sanitize_context(...).strip()` on load, so content that sanitize rewrites (e.g. an echoed `<memory-context>` fence) replays different bytes after a reload.

Any of these diverges the request prefix at that message and re-prefills everything after it. At a median ~156k-token context this re-prefills the whole prefix on the first call of every turn — measured 27.9s for the first call vs 2.4-5.8s for cached in-turn calls on the same session.

## Change

Persist what you send: a nullable `messages.api_content` column stores the exact content string sent to the API for a message when it differs from the clean stored content, and replay substitutes it verbatim (no sanitize, no strip).

- **Schema** (`hermes_state.py`): nullable `api_content` column on `messages`; the declarative column reconciliation adds it on existing databases. `append_message` / `_insert_message_rows` accept it; `get_messages_as_conversation` returns it verbatim. New `set_latest_user_api_content` backfills the newest active user row (content-matched), needed by in-place preflight compaction below.
- **Composition** (`agent/turn_context.py`): the prefetch/plugin injection composition now lives in one helper, `compose_user_api_content`. The turn prologue stamps its output onto the live user message as `api_content`, and the `api_messages` build in `conversation_loop` sends the stamped bytes — one source, so the persisted sidecar and the wire cannot drift.
- **Persist ordering** (`agent/turn_context.py`): the crash-resilience user-turn persist moves after prefetch/`pre_llm_call`, so the user row is written once with its final sidecar. `_ensure_db_session()` stays before preflight compression — session rotation inserts a child row whose `parent_session_id` needs the parent row under `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`.
- **Replay** (`agent/conversation_loop.py`): every outgoing copy pops `api_content` (it is bookkeeping, never a provider field). The current turn's user message sends the stamped bytes (or composes live for callers that bypass the prologue); historical user/assistant messages replay the sidecar verbatim.
- **Gateway** (`gateway/run.py`, `gateway/session.py`): `_build_replay_entry` forwards the sidecar for user/assistant entries — without this the fix is inert on gateway platforms — but only when the replay pipeline did not rewrite the content (timestamp injection, auto-continue strip, mirror prefix): a rewrite means different bytes must replay, so the stale sidecar is dropped. `append_to_transcript` persists it on the gateway-side fallback path.
- **Flush** (`run_agent.py`): when the #48677 persist override replaces the row content, the sent bytes are kept in the sidecar; and content that load-time sanitize would rewrite is captured into the sidecar at flush time (compared in wire form — both sides stripped — so plain whitespace padding doesn't grow redundant sidecars).
- **Content rewrites drop the sidecar**: historical image strip and merge-summary-into-tail (`agent/context_compressor.py`), consecutive-user repair merge (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`), stale-confirmation redaction (`agent/replay_cleanup.py`) — replaying pre-rewrite bytes would resend exactly what the rewrite removed.
- **Other paths**: the max-iterations forced-summary request substitutes the sidecar like the main loop (`agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`); `/branch` session copies carry it (`gateway/slash_commands.py`, `hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py`); the chat-completions transport strips it defensively (`agent/transports/chat_completions.py`).

## Correctness notes

- **The sidecar is only stamped when it will match the wire.** The stamp shares the exact guard the `api_messages` build uses. Two callers are excluded because their wire bytes differ from the composition: `codex_app_server` turns bypass the `api_messages` build entirely, and MoA turns append per-call aggregated context to the API copy after composition (both keep their current cache behavior).
- **Index re-anchoring.** Compaction rebuilds `messages` with fresh copies, so `current_turn_user_idx` (which the stamp, the injection site, and the persist-override row all target) is re-anchored via `reanchor_current_turn_user_idx` after preflight compression and after in-loop compression restarts. Exact-content match wins over "last user message" so a todo-snapshot user message appended by compaction can't steal the anchor; it falls back to the last user message when merge-summary-into-tail rewrote the content.
- **In-place compaction ordering.** With in-place compaction, `archive_and_compact` inserts the current turn's user row before the prologue can compose the sidecar, and the subsequent crash persist skips already-persisted dicts — so the stamp is backfilled onto the freshly inserted row via `set_latest_user_api_content` (content-matched, newest active user row; a mismatch writes nothing). Rotation mode needs nothing: its fresh copies flush to the child session after the stamp.
- **The persist override never clobbers a compaction summary.** When the current-turn user row was merged with a compaction summary (`COMPRESSED_SUMMARY_METADATA_KEY`), the #48677 content override is skipped — overwriting would silently drop the summary from the durable transcript. The wire is already consistent there (the merge dropped the sidecar and sends the merged content).
- **The field never reaches a provider.** The `api_messages` build pops it from every copy; the max-iterations path and the chat-completions transport strip it independently.
- **Failure containment.** The column is nullable; rows without it behave exactly as before. The backfill and gateway forwards are guarded, and a missing/dropped sidecar degrades to today's behavior (one cache-boundary miss), never to wrong content.

## Tests

- `tests/agent/test_api_content_sidecar.py` (new, 31 tests): composition helper; SessionDB round-trip is verbatim (no sanitize/strip) and the column auto-migrates on a pre-sidecar database; prologue stamping order (the early persist sees the stamp, written in one insert); codex_app_server/MoA exclusions; re-anchoring; in-place backfill; persist-override and sanitize-divergence capture at flush; max-iterations substitution; stale-confirmation redaction drops the sidecar; and an end-to-end wire invariant against an in-process mock provider — the serialized user message replayed in turn N+1 (history reloaded from the store by a fresh agent) equals the bytes turn N sent, and the field never appears in any request payload.
- `tests/gateway/test_replay_entry_fields.py` (extended, 7 tests): `_build_replay_entry` forwards the sidecar for user/assistant when content is unchanged, drops it on any pipeline rewrite (timestamp/mirror), never forwards for tool roles; end-to-end `_build_gateway_agent_history` keeps/drops it accordingly.
- Full `tests/agent`, `tests/gateway`, `tests/run_agent`, and `tests/hermes_state` suites (~16.8k tests via `scripts/run_tests_parallel.py`): no regressions — the 49 failures observed (LSP env probes, workspace/coding-context detection, bedrock region, verification nudges, path completion, feishu UA, a startup-race timeout) reproduce identically, same tests and counts, on a clean checkout of the base commit; none are in files this PR touches.

## Measured impact

Production gateway sessions (median ~156k-token context): first-call latency 27.9s (cold prefill) vs 2.4-5.8s (cached) on the same session. With this change plus a follow-up that stabilizes the system-prompt prefix, first-call prompt-cache hit rate went from 0.1% to 98.7%; this change closes the message-replay divergence, which is the dominant component.

prs.title: fix(aux): translate response_format to output_config.format for anthropic transport
prs.body:
## Summary

The `anthropic_messages` transport forwards an OpenAI Chat Completions `response_format` payload verbatim to Anthropic-compatible endpoints. Strict gateways reject it:

```
HTTP 400 invalid_request_error:
response_format: OpenAI Chat Completions structured-output shape is not supported.
Use output_config.format = {"type": "json_schema", "schema": {...}}.
```

The shape is produced by core code, not the caller's choice: `agent/plugin_llm.py::PluginLlm._json_response_format` builds `{"response_format": {"type": "json_schema", ...}}` into `extra_body` for every `complete_structured(json_schema=...)` call. On a `chat_completions` provider this works; the moment the main provider is an `anthropic_messages` gateway, every plugin structured completion 400s.

Observed live: a Discord thread auto-title plugin using `ctx.llm.complete_structured` failed on 100% of calls for 2+ days (1,600+ logged errors) after the main provider switched to an Anthropic-compatible load balancer.

## Fix

`_translate_anthropic_response_format` in `agent/auxiliary_client.py`, applied in `_AnthropicCompletionsAdapter.create` where caller `extra_body` is merged:

- `{"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"schema": S, ...}}` → top-level `output_config["format"] = {"type": "json_schema", "schema": S}`
- `{"type": "json_object"}` → `{"type": "json_schema", "schema": {"type": "object"}}` — the installed Anthropic SDK (0.87.0) only exposes `JSONOutputFormatParam` with required `type: "json_schema"`; there is no schema-less JSON mode
- Merges into any existing `output_config` (e.g. adaptive-thinking `effort` for Claude 4.6+) instead of overwriting it
- `response_format` is excluded from the raw `extra_body` passthrough, same treatment and comment style as the existing `reasoning` exclusion (which is translated into native `thinking`)

The async path (`_AsyncAnthropicCompletionsAdapter`) delegates to the sync adapter via `asyncio.to_thread`, so it inherits the translation; a test pins that. Non-Anthropic transports (`chat_completions`, `codex_responses`) are untouched — `response_format` keeps flowing as-is there.

## Tests

`tests/agent/test_anthropic_structured_output.py` (5 tests, mock-captured kwargs on the adapter):

- json_schema → `output_config.format` carries the schema; no `response_format` leaks into extra_body
- json_object → permissive object schema mapping
- merge: `format` coexists with a pre-existing `output_config.effort`
- passthrough hygiene: unrelated extra_body keys still forward
- async adapter produces the same translation

```
tests/agent/test_anthropic_structured_output.py \
tests/agent/test_plugin_llm.py \
tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client_anthropic_custom.py \
tests/agent/test_auxiliary_relay.py
→ 41 passed
```

Also verified end-to-end against a live Anthropic-compatible gateway: the previously failing structured call now returns schema-conforming JSON.

prs.title: fix(agent): strip reasoning replay fields for strict chat-completions providers
prs.body:
## Problem

Assistant messages in agent history can carry two non-standard reasoning replay fields: `reasoning` (trajectory reasoning text) and `reasoning_details` (OpenRouter's unified structured-reasoning format, e.g. signed Anthropic thinking blocks). `reasoning_details` is deliberately kept on API-bound messages so OpenRouter can maintain multi-turn reasoning continuity — but it is not part of the OpenAI Chat Completions message schema, and it currently reaches **every** chat-completions endpoint.

Strict OpenAI-compatible providers (Fireworks, Mistral, and many self-hosted/proxy gateways) reject any request whose replayed assistant messages contain these fields with HTTP 400 `Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[N].reasoning_details'`. Once a session contains such a turn, every subsequent request fails. The common trigger is a mixed-provider session: turns produced via OpenRouter (or an Anthropic reasoning model) persist `reasoning_details`, and a model switch or fallback to a strict direct provider makes the whole history unreplayable. The existing reactive recovery only fires on Anthropic-flavored `thinking_signature` error text, so these generic 400s classify as non-retryable format errors — and even when recovery applies, it costs a failed round trip per session.

## Change

- `ChatCompletionsTransport.convert_messages()` now strips `reasoning` / `reasoning_details` from the wire copy of messages, gated on the target endpoint via a new `_base_url_consumes_reasoning_details()` helper: the fields are kept for endpoints that consume the replay (`openrouter.ai`, `nousresearch.com`) and stripped for everything else, including when no `base_url` is supplied (safe default for strict providers). This mirrors the existing keep/strip pattern used for the Gemini `extra_content` thought_signature.
- `build_kwargs()` passes `base_url` through to `convert_messages()` (it is already provided by both the profile and legacy call paths).
- The max-iterations summary path in `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` hand-builds messages and bypasses the transport; it already mirrored the other schema-foreign strips (`tool_name`, `codex_*`, `timestamp`) but leaked `reasoning_details`. The same gated strip is mirrored there.

## Correctness notes

- OpenRouter/Nous behavior is unchanged: `reasoning_details` is still replayed for reasoning continuity (signed Anthropic thinking blocks on tool-call turns require it). A new test pins this.
- Only the wire copy is sanitized — `convert_messages()` uses the existing copy-on-write scheme, so persisted history keeps the fields and future turns on routes that consume them can still replay reasoning state. A test asserts the source list is untouched.
- `reasoning` was already popped on the main-loop `api_messages` build for all providers ("trajectory storage only"); stripping it in the transport extends the same guarantee to direct `_build_api_kwargs()` entry points without changing main-loop behavior.
- `reasoning_content` is intentionally not touched: it is a provider-schema echo-back field (DeepSeek/Kimi thinking mode) reconciled per-provider by `reapply_reasoning_echo_for_provider()`.

## Tests

New:
- `tests/agent/transports/test_chat_completions.py`: strips `reasoning`/`reasoning_details` for a strict base_url and when base_url is unknown; keeps them for `openrouter.ai` / `inference-api.nousresearch.com`; source messages never mutated.
- `tests/run_agent/test_strict_api_validation.py`: end-to-end through `_build_api_kwargs()` — stripped for a Fireworks agent (history retained, `reasoning_content` untouched), kept for an OpenRouter agent.

Runs (all green):
- `tests/agent/transports/`, `tests/run_agent/test_strict_api_validation.py`
- `tests/run_agent/test_provider_parity.py`, `test_deepseek_reasoning_content_echo.py`, `test_thinking_only_sanitizer.py`, `test_thinking_sig_recovery_persistence.py`, `test_deepseek_v4_thinking_live.py`, `tests/agent/test_compressed_summary_metadata.py`, `tests/plugins/model_providers/`
- Full `tests/agent/` + `tests/run_agent/` (one pre-existing environment-dependent failure in `tests/agent/lsp/test_broken_set.py` reproduces identically on a clean checkout of `main`).

prs.title: perf(state): CJK bigram FTS index — replace trigram+LIKE routing for session search
prs.body:
Stacked on #65541 (read-path split) — review the last three commits.

## Problem

`search_messages` routes queries three ways: unicode61 FTS5, the trigram table, or a LIKE fallback. unicode61 indexes a CJK run as ONE token, so a 2-char Korean term (일본, 구글, 우리, …) can never match it; the trigram tokenizer needs ≥3 chars per term. Result: **any query containing a 1-2 char CJK token full-scans messages with LIKE across three columns** — measured 3-6.4s CPU per query on a 6.8GB production DB, and the dominant base cost behind a 12.4s in-gateway `session_search` average (Korean/Japanese/Chinese conversation workloads hit this constantly — 2-char words are everywhere in Korean).

The v1 layout also triple-stores text (standalone FTS content copies in both tables; the trigram index alone was larger than the messages data) and its unconditional `AFTER UPDATE` triggers re-tokenize whole messages on flag-only updates.

## Design

1. **`cjk_unicode61` tokenizer** (`native/fts5_cjk/fts5_cjk.c`, ~250 lines, no deps): wraps unicode61; CJK runs inside its tokens are re-emitted as overlapping character bigrams (Lucene CJKAnalyzer semantics), everything else passes through. FTS5 turns consecutive tokens from one query term into a phrase, so a bare term like 캘린더 gets exact substring semantics down to 2 chars at index speed. Built with `native/fts5_cjk/build.sh` → `~/.hermes/lib/libfts5_cjk.so` (override: `HERMES_FTS5_CJK_SO`).
2. **`messages_fts_v2`**: one standalone 3-column FTS5 table whose single MATCH path replaces the 3-way routing. Triggers are scoped `AFTER UPDATE OF content, tool_name, tool_calls`. Lone 1-char CJK terms keep the LIKE path (a bigram index only holds unigrams for isolated chars).
3. **Zero-regression fallback**: no .so → nothing changes (legacy tables and routing untouched). A DB that carries v2 triggers but can't load the tokenizer self-heals by dropping the triggers (writes never fail; index goes stale until re-migrated).
4. **Online migration** (`scripts/fts_v2_migrate.py`): create table+triggers → idempotent DELETE+INSERT batched backfill (resume state in `state_meta`) → integrity-check → sets a `fts_v2_ready` marker. Reads are gated on that marker so a partially-backfilled index is never served. Production run: 385k messages in 91s with live writers.
5. **Config surface** (per the env-var-for-config policy): `agent.fts_v2_read` (default on once the index is ready) and `agent.search_slow_ms` are config.yaml-authoritative, bridged to env at both the startup export block and the per-turn reload path. A slow-search log line names the routing path (fts_v2/fts5/trigram/like_scan) so future routing regressions are a journalctl grep.
6. **v1 retirement** (`scripts/fts_v1_drop.py`, operator-run): preflight (tokenizer loadable, v2 objects present, ready marker, integrity-check, rowcount parity) then drops the six v1 triggers + two tables. Freed ~5.9GB on our production DB. Fresh DBs with a loadable tokenizer are v2-native and never create the v1 tables.

## Production results (fork, 2026-07-16)

| query | before (in-gateway) | after |
|---|---|---|
| `나쵸 minpeter` | 58.1s | **50ms** |
| `"shared default" AND "웅기"` | 72.5s | **86ms** |
| `구글 캘린더 일정 없음 브리핑 …` | 45.4s | **27ms** |

Recall parity held on a replayed real-query benchmark (10/13 confirmed-relevant targets found, identical to legacy), and v2's FTS5 semantics fix a latent bug: the LIKE fallback matched multi-token queries as OR instead of AND.

## Tests

`tests/test_fts_v2_cjk.py` (tokenizer built on the fly; skips without a C toolchain), `tests/test_search_slow_query_log.py`, `tests/gateway/test_fts_v2_config_bridge.py` — bigram matching incl. no-false-positive-across-words, trigger mirroring, flag-only-update scoping, self-heal, partial-backfill refusal, fresh-DB v2-native, config bridges.

prs.title: perf(gateway): single-row routing UPSERT fast path for metadata-only saves
prs.body:
## Problem

On a production deployment with ~1,100 gateway routing keys, per-turn gateway persistence (session resolve + post-turn save) measured ~175ms p50. Profiling attributed ~50ms of that to the routing-index save: every `SessionEntry` re-serialized, a full `DELETE`+`INSERT` of every `gateway_routing` row in state.db, and a multi-MB `sessions.json` dump+fsync — and the steady-state turn pays it **twice** (once in `get_or_create_session`'s healthy-path `updated_at` bump, once in `update_session`), even though both writes only change `updated_at`/`last_prompt_tokens` on a single entry.

## Change

Add `SessionStore._save_entry(session_key)`: persist one routing entry via the existing `HermesDB.save_gateway_routing_entry` UPSERT instead of rewriting the whole index. Only the two metadata-only call sites use it:

- `get_or_create_session`'s healthy path (existing entry, no reset/recover/heal — just the `updated_at` bump)
- `update_session` (`updated_at` / `last_prompt_tokens`)

Structural transitions — create, recover, reset, session switch, prune, and compression-tip heals (anything that changes the key → session_id mapping) — keep the full-rewrite path, which also refreshes the legacy `sessions.json` mirror. Between structural saves the mirror can lag in metadata only; state.db is the primary durable store for routing, so restart rebinding is unaffected.

`update_session` also now runs its SQLite write and peer-record update outside `_lock`, so the commit never blocks concurrent routing lookups.

## Correctness notes

- **Generation guard vs concurrent full rewrites**: the entry is serialized under `_lock` together with the current routing generation. Under `_save_lock`, the UPSERT is skipped when a full snapshot taken *after* our serialize point has already persisted — that snapshot necessarily contains a same-or-newer copy of the key, so writing ours would regress it. A full snapshot *older* than our serialize point that lands after us can only regress that key's metadata by one racing turn (the next turn rewrites it), never the session_id: session_id changes always carry a newer generation and win via the existing guard in `_persist_routing_data`.
- **Torn peer rows**: `update_session` snapshots `session_id`/`origin`/`display_name` while still holding `_lock`, so a concurrent reset that rewrites the entry between lock release and the peer record cannot record a mix of old and new fields.
- **Heals force the full path**: `_heal_compression_tip_locked`'s return value now gates the fast path — a heal rewrites `entry.session_id` and must reach the `sessions.json` mirror too.
- **Fallbacks**: no DB, or a failed UPSERT, falls back to the full rewrite, so DB-less installs keep `sessions.json` — their primary store — durable every turn.

## Tests

New `tests/gateway/test_routing_save_fast_path.py` (13 tests): changed values always land in state.db; restart rebinding works when the `sessions.json` mirror lagged fast-path writes (or was deleted); compression heals and `force_new` transitions still rewrite the mirror; no-DB and failed-UPSERT fallbacks; peer fields snapshotted under `_lock`; generation-guard skip/proceed ordering, including restart rebinding after a skipped idempotent write.

`python -m pytest tests/gateway`: 9,124 tests, no regressions vs a clean checkout of `main` in the same environment (the same set of environment-dependent failures — Telegram/PTB and Feishu SDK version drift, path-completion fixtures — fails identically before and after this change).

## Measured impact

Production deployment of this change at ~1,100 routing keys: metadata-only routing saves dropped from ~50ms (full index rewrite + `sessions.json` dump+fsync, twice per turn) to <1ms per single-row UPSERT. Structural transitions are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(photon): unblock main — restore U+FFFC deferral, mock deps check in runtime-record tests
prs.body:
## Problem

Fixes #73783 — `main`'s `Python tests / Run tests slice 2/8` and `7/8` are red (which also fails every open PR's required checks). Two independent causes in the photon platform, both bisected in the issue.

## Change

**1. Restore the U+FFFC deferral** (`plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py`)

The early return added by the #54514 salvage drops placeholder-only text at the platform boundary, *before* the `_pending_fffc` deferral (from `afab7ed46`) can register it. The deferral already achieves the salvage's goal — a placeholder is never dispatched as a standalone text turn — while additionally keeping the timeout fallback for voice notes whose media event never arrives, and cancel-on-attachment. Removing the early return lets the deferral own the placeholder again; a NOTE comment marks the boundary so the next salvage doesn't reintroduce the drop.

**2. Mock the deps seam in the runtime-record tests** (`tests/plugins/platforms/photon/test_runtime_record.py`)

`_patch_spawn` stubs `_SIDECAR_DIR` with an *empty* `node_modules/`, which the unified `sidecar_deps_installed()` check (spectrum-ts probe) rejects — so `_start_sidecar()` raises before the record write on any runner without real sidecar deps (all CI slices). One `monkeypatch.setattr(photon_adapter, "sidecar_deps_installed", lambda: True)` in the shared helper; these tests exercise the runtime record, not dependency installation.

## Tests

Full photon suite: `tests/plugins/platforms/photon/` — **164 passed** (was 6 failing on main tip). The four fffc tests pin the restored deferral contract; both runtime-record tests reach the record write.

Note: `tests/conformance/test_vector_generator.py::test_committed_vectors_match_regeneration` also shows red on the same slices but passes locally for me — likely a separate CI-env drift, not addressed here.

prs.title: fix(tools): support CPython 3.14 ThreadPoolExecutor internals in DaemonThreadPoolExecutor
prs.body:
## Problem

`DaemonThreadPoolExecutor._adjust_thread_count` mirrors CPython 3.8–3.13 `ThreadPoolExecutor` internals (`self._initializer` / `self._initargs` and the 5-arg `_worker` signature). CPython 3.14 moved per-worker state into a `WorkerContext` built by the new `prepare_context()` classmethod and changed `_worker` to `(executor_ref, ctx, work_queue)`.

Under Python 3.14 every `submit()` dies on first dispatch:

```
AttributeError: 'DaemonThreadPoolExecutor' object has no attribute '_initializer'
```

This breaks all concurrent tool batches and background memory sync. Reproduces on pure `main`: `tests/tools/test_daemon_pool.py`, `tests/agent/test_memory_async_sync.py`, and the `TestSegmentedDispatchIntegration` cluster all fail under a 3.14 interpreter.

## Fix

Branch on `hasattr(ThreadPoolExecutor, "prepare_context")` and pass the matching worker args on each interpreter family, keeping `daemon=True` and the deliberately-skipped `_threads_queues` registration on both.

## Testing

- Python 3.14.6: `tests/tools/test_daemon_pool.py`, `tests/agent/test_memory_async_sync.py`, `tests/run_agent/test_tool_batch_segmentation.py` — 38 passed, 1 skipped (all failed before on 3.14).
- The 3.8–3.13 path is untouched (same attributes/signature as before, now behind the feature check).

prs.title: fix(secrets): fall back to os.environ on scope miss when multiplexing is off
prs.body:
## Problem

Since fdab380a1 (`fix(cron): run jobs under the profile secret scope`), the cron scheduler wraps **every** job in `set_secret_scope(build_profile_secret_scope(home))` — unconditionally, in both multiplexed and single-profile deployments. `build_profile_secret_scope()` parses `<home>/.env` only, and `get_secret()` treats any installed scope as authoritative: a scope miss returns `default` without consulting `os.environ`.

Single-profile deployments that provide provider credentials via the **process environment** rather than `<home>/.env` — systemd `Environment=`/drop-ins, secret-manager wrappers (`pass-cli run`, `op run`), plain shell exports — get this failure mode:

- interactive turns resolve keys fine (no per-turn scope is installed when multiplexing is off, so `get_secret` falls through to `os.environ`),
- **every scheduled cron job** resolves the same key to empty inside the scope wrap, the runtime falls back to the `no-key-required` placeholder, and the job 401s at its first LLM call.

The regression is silent and confusing to diagnose: the key is valid, `os.environ` holds it the whole time, and only cron-context reads go blind. (Observed in production as a daily briefing job 401-ing every midnight for two weeks while the same model worked in chat.)

## Change

`get_secret()` scope-miss behavior now depends on the deployment mode:

- **multiplex ON** — unchanged: the scope stays authoritative, absent means absent, never fall through to `os.environ` (which may hold another profile's value). The fail-closed `UnscopedSecretError` path is also unchanged.
- **multiplex OFF** — a scope miss falls through to `os.environ`. With a single profile there is no other profile to leak from; the scope (installed unconditionally around cron jobs) acts as a `.env` overlay instead of a blindfold, restoring the legacy `os.getenv` contract every call site had before Workstream A.

Scope **hits** are unaffected in both modes (`.env` values still win over the environment).

## Correctness notes

- No change to any multiplexed semantics: both existing fail-closed tests and the scope-authoritative tests pass untouched.
- `_is_global_env` handling is unchanged and still short-circuits before scope logic.
- The cron scheduler keeps installing the scope unconditionally — after this change that is harmless in single-profile mode and still load-bearing under multiplexing, so no scheduler change is needed.

## Tests

`tests/agent/test_secret_scope.py` gains `TestScopedSingleProfile` (4 cases):

- scope hit wins over `os.environ` (overlay precedence)
- scope miss falls back to `os.environ` — **fails before the fix** (this is the cron 401 regression)
- scope miss with nothing in the environment returns `default`
- the same miss with multiplexing ON stays scope-authoritative (guards against weakening isolation)

prs.title: perf(agent): reuse the per-request OpenAI wire client across sequential LLM calls
prs.body:
## Problem

Every LLM call builds a fresh `openai.OpenAI` wire client in `_create_request_openai_client` and closes it when the request finishes. Constructing the client allocates a new httpx connection pool, so every call pays a fresh TCP + TLS handshake to the provider.

Measured in a production deployment (instrumented client construction):

- client build: **19.2ms p50 / 35.5ms p95** per LLM call
- **~5.1 LLM calls per agent turn** (tool loops make several sequential calls)
- warm reuse of an already-built client: **0.008–0.039ms**
- net effect: **~75–80ms saved per typical tool-loop turn**

The per-request client exists for good reasons (SDK `max_retries=0`, per-request vision headers, the #29507 cross-thread close discipline), so the fix keeps the per-request lifecycle semantics and only skips the redundant rebuild when nothing about the request's client configuration changed.

## Change

Cache ONE reusable wire client on the agent, keyed by the effective client kwargs:

- `_create_request_openai_client` hands back the cached client when the effective kwargs are identical to the cached ones; any kwargs change (credential rotation, provider failover, vision headers) evicts the stale client and rebuilds.
- `_close_request_openai_client` keeps the client for the next call only when the close reason is one of `_REQUEST_CLIENT_REUSE_REASONS` (`request_complete` / `stream_request_complete`) — the reasons the request workers' own `finally` reports for a request that actually produced a response. Every other reason (error cleanups, stale/interrupt kills, retry cleanups) does a real close.
- The cache is a single checked-out slot (`in_use`): a second concurrent call gets a fresh untracked client with the old build-per-request lifecycle, so two calls never share one pool's close/abort lifecycle.
- `release_clients()` / `close()` really close the cached client via a new `_close_cached_request_openai_client` teardown hook.
- The MoA facade and Mock passthrough branches never enter the cache.

The callers in `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` now report a reuse-eligible close reason only when the request produced a response; error unwinds report `request_error_cleanup` / `stream_error_cleanup` so a retry after a request error always builds a fresh pool.

## Correctness notes

- **`max_retries=0` preserved.** The cached client is built through the same `request_kwargs` path, and a kwargs mismatch (including `max_retries`) evicts. The agent's outer retry loop remains the only retry loop.
- **Cross-thread abort discipline (#29507).** `client.close()` must only run on the thread that owns the pool's FDs. A stranger-thread abort (`_abort_request_openai_client`, used by the interrupt-check loop and the stale-call detector) only `shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)`s the sockets — and now also *poisons* the cache slot, so a pool whose sockets were shut down from another thread is never reused: the owner thread's close discards it and the next create rebuilds. Poisoning wins over a reuse-reason close.
- **Atomic stranger abort.** The holder read and the abort now happen under the request-client holder lock. Previously the abort fired after releasing the lock; in that window the worker's `finally` could pop + cache the client and the *next* call check it out, so the late abort would poison the slot and shut down an innocent in-flight request's sockets. The abort itself never blocks (socket shutdown + slot poison), so holding the lock across it only delays the racing pop, never the data path. The same discipline is applied to cron's inline `direct_api_call` abort.
- **Interrupt-break stream leak.** Breaking out of a half-read SSE stream on interrupt used to abandon the response with its connection still checked out of the httpx pool, while the partial response made the worker's `finally` report a reuse-reason close — caching the client together with the leaked connection (one more per interrupt until the pool exhausted and every request hit `PoolTimeout`). The stream is now closed on the break (owner thread); if that close fails, the slot is poisoned so the `finally` really closes the pool. The codex streaming runtime gets the same poison-on-close-failure treatment.
- **Vision headers keyed separately.** The copilot vision `default_headers` variant produces different effective kwargs, so a vision call after a text call (or vice versa) rebuilds rather than reusing the wrong headers. Nested kwargs dicts are snapshotted at cache time so an aliased inner dict mutated in place can't spuriously compare equal.
- **Credential/base_url rotation busts the key.** Rotation sites mutate `_client_kwargs`; the kwargs comparison fails and the stale client is evicted (closed from the creating thread, which is safe because `in_use` was false — no worker owns the pool's FDs).
- **Error paths always rebuild.** Only a clean response reports a reuse reason; API errors, cancel-swallows, stale kills, and interrupts all really close, so a retry never inherits a possibly-wedged pool (pinned by `test_retry_after_api_connection_error_recreates_request_client`).
- **Teardown while checked out.** If teardown runs while a worker has the client checked out (workers can outlive turns), the hook aborts the sockets instead of closing: the slot is already detached, so the worker's own `finally` sees an untracked client and does the real close on its thread.

## Tests

New:

- `tests/agent/test_request_client_reuse.py` — reuse on identical kwargs, eviction on kwargs change, vision-header variant keying, poison-on-abort, non-reuse close reasons, teardown (idle and checked-out), single-slot concurrency, MoA/Mock passthrough.
- `tests/run_agent/test_request_client_reuse_abort_races.py` — atomic holder-abort races (streaming, non-streaming, and cron inline paths), interrupt-break stream close and poison-on-close-failure, codex stream close-failure poisoning.

Updated:

- `tests/run_agent/test_openai_client_lifecycle.py` — successful requests now keep the wire client cached (closed at teardown instead of request end); the retry-after-connection-error test still pins that error paths rebuild.

Ran `tests/run_agent`, `tests/agent`, `tests/cron/test_cron_direct_api_call_62151.py`, `tests/hermes_cli/test_codex_runtime_switch.py`, and `tests/acp/test_session.py` locally (Linux).

## Measured impact

From a production deployment of this change: client construction cost dropped from 19.2ms p50 / 35.5ms p95 per LLM call to 0.008–0.039ms on reuse. At ~5.1 calls per turn this saves ~75–80ms of pure connection-setup latency per typical tool-loop turn, plus the provider-side benefit of a persistent connection across sequential calls.

prs.title: perf: take per-API-call token accounting off the turn thread
prs.body:
## Problem

Every API call inside the tool loop persists its token/cost delta by calling `SessionDB.update_token_counts()` synchronously on the turn thread — the hot site in `agent/conversation_loop.py` plus both codex app-server sites in `agent/codex_runtime.py`. Each call is a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` sessions `UPDATE` plus a `session_model_usage` upsert.

In a production deployment we measured this write at **3.3 ms p50 / 70.4 ms p95 per API call, with spikes up to 299 ms** against a cold multi-GB `state.db`. The tool loop stalls for that long between calls; a multi-tool turn with N API calls pays it N times. None of it needs to block the turn: the in-memory per-turn counters (`agent.session_estimated_cost_usd` etc.) that live displays read are updated separately and stay synchronous.

## Change

`SessionDB` gains a single-writer background queue for token deltas:

- **`queue_token_counts(session_id, **kwargs)`** — same signature and semantics as `update_token_counts`, but the critical path is a deque append + condvar notify. A dedicated daemon thread (`session-db-token-writer`, started lazily on first enqueue) applies deltas in enqueue order through the existing `update_token_counts` → `_execute_write` path, so SQLite access keeps the established `self._lock` / `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / jitter-retry discipline unchanged.
- **Coalescing** — when a backlog forms, *adjacent* deltas for the same `(session, model, cost_status, cost_source, pricing_version, billing_provider/base_url/mode)` route merge into one `UPDATE`: token/api-call fields sum, cost fields sum None-preservingly (an all-None run stays None so `COALESCE` keeps the stored value). `absolute=True` deltas (cumulative overwrites) never merge and act as ordering barriers.
- **`flush_token_counts(timeout=5)`** — blocks until the queue is drained; a plain attribute check when nothing is queued. Readers that surface token/cost totals call it first: `get_session`, `list_sessions_rich`, `_get_session_rich_row`, `list_gateway_sessions`, and `InsightsEngine.generate`.
- **Call sites** — the `conversation_loop.py` per-call site and both `codex_runtime.py` sites now enqueue instead of writing inline. Their existing row-existence retry and try/except guards are unchanged.

## Correctness notes

- **Ordering** — one writer thread applies deltas strictly in enqueue order; only adjacent same-route incremental deltas merge, so ordering across sessions and across a mid-session `/model` switch is preserved exactly. Route equality is required for a merge precisely because those fields feed the `COALESCE` backfill, the last-non-None-wins status fields, and the per-model usage attribution key — a merged apply is equivalent to sequential applies (covered by a row-equivalence test comparing full `sessions` + `session_model_usage` rows).
- **Flush barriers before route switches** — `update_session_model`, `update_session_billing_route`, and `update_session_meta` write the sessions row synchronously, bypassing the queue. A first-of-session delta still queued at switch time carries the pre-switch route; applying it *after* the switch `UPDATE` would trip the first-accounted-route branch in `update_token_counts` (row sees `api_call_count == 0` plus a route mismatch) and resurrect the old model/provider. All three flush the queue first, restoring the pre-queue happens-before.
- **Lock-free fast path vs in-flight batches** — the writer sets its busy flag *before* popping the queue, so `flush_token_counts`'s unlocked queue-then-busy check can never observe "empty and idle" while a popped batch is still unapplied.
- **Flush vs a stop-flagged writer** — a live writer is authoritative even when stop-flagged (close in progress): its loop drains the queue before exiting. Flush only drains on the caller's thread when the writer is dead or never started, claiming the same busy flag so concurrent flushes wait instead of racing.
- **Durability** — `AIAgent._persist_session` (turn finalize and every error-exit persist point) flushes; `close()` stops and drains the writer before the WAL checkpoint; an atexit hook (registered on first enqueue, unregistered on `close()` so closed instances aren't pinned until interpreter exit) drains at shutdown. Worst-case crash loss is the in-flight call's delta — the same window as the old inline write.
- **Enqueue after close** — once the writer is permanently stopped, `queue_token_counts` applies the delta inline instead of parking it on a queue nothing will drain; a closed-connection failure then raises at the call site, which already guards for it, exactly like the old synchronous path.
- **Failure isolation** — writer apply errors are logged (`logger.warning`) and never raise into a turn; the writer thread survives and keeps applying subsequent deltas.

## Tests

- New: `tests/agent/test_async_token_accounting.py` (19 tests) — strict enqueue-order across sessions, absolute-as-barrier semantics, backlog coalescing with exact sums including `session_model_usage`, coalesced-vs-sequential row equivalence, unit merge rules, None-cost preservation, `get_session` read-your-writes under a slow writer, empty-flush fast path, flush waiting out a stop-flagged live writer and a concurrent caller-drain, inline apply after writer stop, enqueue-after-close raising at the call site, `close()` drain surviving reopen, atexit idempotence and unregistration (weakref + gc), `_persist_session` drain via a real `AIAgent`, and writer failure logging + survival.
- Updated: `tests/run_agent/test_token_persistence_non_cli.py` to the `queue_token_counts` contract.
- Suites for every touched file pass: `tests/test_hermes_state.py`, `tests/hermes_state/`, `tests/test_sql_injection.py`, `tests/agent/test_insights.py`, `tests/agent/test_codex_app_server_persist.py`, and the full `tests/run_agent` tree (1974 passed, 3 skipped). The full `tests/agent` tree was run before and after the change on the same machine: the failure set is byte-for-byte identical (144 environment-dependent tests — LSP tooling, model-metadata network cache, codex transport, and similar — that fail the same way on a clean checkout of `main`; the after run passes the same 5468 tests plus the 19 new ones).

How to test:

```bash
pytest tests/agent/test_async_token_accounting.py tests/test_hermes_state.py tests/run_agent -q
```

Tested on Linux (Ubuntu, Python 3.12); the change touches no platform-specific I/O — it is pure `threading` + the existing SQLite write path.

## Measured impact

From a production deployment of this change:

- Enqueue critical path: **p50 0.0015 ms / p95 0.0036 ms**, vs 2.6 ms / 7.7 ms for the synchronous `UPDATE` on a *warm, small* DB — and vs 3.3 ms p50 / 70.4 ms p95 (up to 299 ms cold) observed in production before the change.
- Removes that entire cost from the turn thread after every API call; multi-tool turns with N calls save N× it.
- Total DB work is unchanged or lower: the same deltas are applied off-thread, and backlogs coalesce into fewer transactions.

## What does this PR do?

Cron preflight blocks a job with an explicit `local:<chat_id>` delivery target, even though the scheduler can deliver the result through the local chat's session owner. The job stops with `blocked_config` before it can run.

## Related Issue

Fixes #160320

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- `cron/scheduler_preflight.py` accepts explicit `local:<chat_id>` targets without loading gateway credentials for them. Empty addresses and addresses with leading whitespace still fail preflight. Other targets in the same job still go through platform and credential checks.
- `tests/cron/test_preflight_config.py` covers explicit local targets in `deliver` and `failure_deliver` and covers malformed local addresses.

## How to Test

From a Desktop chat, create a scheduled job and edit its delivery target to `local:<chat_id>` for an existing chat on the same profile. Run it with the profile's gateway active. The result should appear as a note in the addressed chat.

The two explicit-target regression cases reproduced `blocked_config` on the base. On Windows with Python 3.14.9, 88 tests passed across cron preflight, mixed and failure delivery, and local-session admission. A separate 20-case probe exercised both delivery lanes through the scheduler and gateway owner's queue and verified the notes in SQLite. It also verified malformed addresses and credential checks in mixed target lists. Desktop GUI verification is pending.

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh -j 3 tests/cron/test_preflight_config.py tests/cron/test_cron_failure_deliver.py tests/cron/test_cron_multiplex_profile_route_preflight.py tests/cron/test_preflight_managed_routes.py tests/cron/test_cron_room_delivery.py tests/cron/test_cron_bot_chat_delivery.py tests/gateway/test_local_chat_delivery.py tests/gateway/test_session_cron.py

```

- [x] Ran the blocking lint and code-health checks. All 22 checks passed.

prs.title: fix(projects): keep messaging sessions that carry a workspace
prs.body:
Messaging sessions that carry a workspace (`cwd`) or a `git_repo_root` are missing from the Projects view: `_PROJECT_TREE_EXCLUDED_SOURCES` drops every messaging-source row in SQL, before `build_tree()` ever sees it, so such a row can never be placed in the project that owns its folder.

The documented intent is narrower: only a messaging row with **no** workspace duplicates the desktop's Messaging section. A row that does carry a workspace is an ordinary workspace session and belongs in the tree.

This keeps that narrower rule and enforces it in the store, before `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`:

- adds `cwdless_excluded_sources` to `SessionQuery` and `SessionCountQuery`;
- adds the SQL predicate to `_session_filter_where` — `source NOT IN (...) OR nonblank cwd OR nonblank git_repo_root` — so a dropped row never consumes a slot of the result window;
- wires the field through the SQLite list/count paths, the pinned backfill, and both public facades (`hermes_state`, `gateway_session_store`);
- drops the previous post-query Python filter in `tui_gateway/methods_projects.py`.

`TRIM` is applied so an empty or whitespace-only `cwd` counts as no workspace, matching `build_tree`. `git_repo_root` is honoured as well, because `project_tree` places a cwd-less row in the project that owns its repo root.

Rows from messaging sources with neither anchor stay out of Projects, so no duplicate appears next to the Messaging section.

## Tests

- `tests/persistence_sqlite/conversation/test_listing_page_first.py` — new store-level case: cwd-less messaging rows are ordered ahead of kept rows with `limit=3`, so a post-`LIMIT` filter would return the wrong page. Covers `None`, empty and whitespace `cwd`, a real `cwd`, and a repo-root-only row.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_project_tree.py` — a messaging row with a workspace `cwd` still reaches `_project_tree_inputs()` and is placed in its declared project.

## Verification

```
tests/persistence_sqlite/conversation/test_listing_page_first.py
tests/tui_gateway/test_project_tree.py
tests/tui_gateway/test_projects_rpc.py          72 passed

tests/contracts                                  4829 passed, 57 skipped

git diff --check                                 clean
```

## What does this PR do?

Adds one catalog entry, `plugin-catalog/ttoken-provider.yaml`, for the **TTOken** model-provider plugin. The plugin is published by TTOken itself at https://github.com/naufalmaulana0577-ui/hermes-ttoken and pinned at `ead54b90328b2b123e22bcb324e04e961adc910f`.

[TTOken](https://ttoken.dev) is an Indonesian pay-per-token AI gateway billed in Rupiah. It serves DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen and more over one OpenAI-compatible API at `https://api.ttoken.dev/v1`. Many of its users run coding agents, and today they have to set TTOken up as a custom endpoint by hand. With this entry they can install it from the Marketplace, in the CLI or in Desktop, pick **TTOken** in `hermes model`, and paste a key.

This follows `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("Third-Party Product Integrations: Ship as a Standalone Plugin"): the provider lives in its own repository and this PR only adds the catalog file. The layout mirrors the existing `cloudgpu-provider` entry.

## Related Issue

None. This is a new catalog entry.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/ttoken-provider.yaml` (new):
  - `subdir: model-providers/ttoken`, `category: models`, `tier: community`
  - `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.0"`, also declared in the plugin's `plugin.yaml`
  - `requires_env: [TTOKEN_API_KEY]`

**Hermes surfaces used:** a single `ProviderProfile` registered with `register_provider()`:
- `api_key` auth, base URL `https://api.ttoken.dev/v1`
- live model list from `/v1/models`, with a static `fallback_models` list
- `model_capabilities` for context windows
- `catalog_aliases`

No tools, hooks, middleware, config schema, OAuth, Python dependencies, or Desktop code.

**Why `>=0.23.0`:** `catalog_aliases` first appears in `providers/base.py` at v0.23.0; `model_capabilities` is already in v0.22.0. Older releases would reject the unknown dataclass field at import.

## Disclosures (rule 13)

- **Network:** this is a model provider. Prompts, tool schemas, and `TTOKEN_API_KEY` go to `api.ttoken.dev`, or to `TTOKEN_BASE_URL` if the user sets it. TTOken forwards requests to the upstream model vendors behind each model.
- **Billing:** requests are charged to the user's TTOken wallet in Rupiah.
- **The plugin code:** no shell commands, background processes, file reads, telemetry, or stored credentials. The key is read through Hermes's provider route.

## How to Test

1. Validate the pinned commit:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/naufalmaulana0577-ui/hermes-ttoken
   cd hermes-ttoken && git checkout ead54b90328b2b123e22bcb324e04e961adc910f
   hermes plugins validate model-providers/ttoken
   ```
   All checks pass, the security scan reports `safe`, and the capability probe sees `ttoken` registered.
2. Run `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/`. It reports `OK`, with no warnings for this entry.
3. With a TTOken Gateway key:
   - `hermes plugins install ttoken-provider`, then `hermes model`, pick TTOken, and paste the key
   - or `hermes chat --provider ttoken -m deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`

   We can send maintainers a test key with credit on request.

**Earlier, in-tree testing:** before moving to the standalone plugin, the same provider profile was tested inside a `hermes-agent` checkout:
- its own tests: 6/6
- the provider wire snapshot: 63/63
- provider-related test files: no new failures; the remaining failures were Windows long-path issues that also occur on `main`

The gateway itself was checked against production on 2026-11-26 with a real key, including tool calls and prompts of about 208k tokens.

**Not run locally:**

prs.title: fix(desktop): an unfocused large paste becomes an attachment, not inline text
prs.body:
## What and why

Paste a large block of plain text onto the transcript — a copied whole reply, a log, a stack trace —
while no composer is focused, and the raw payload was inserted **inline as composer text**. A focused
paste obeys `large-paste.ts` and turns into a `.txt` attachment chip; the unfocused path bypassed
those thresholds entirely, so the same paste behaved differently depending on where focus happened to
be.

## What this changes

`focus.ts` gains `requestComposerAttachPastedText()`: the unfocused paste now asks a mounted composer
to attach the text through its own `onAttachPastedText`, i.e. the same threshold path a focused paste
uses. It mirrors the existing `requestComposerAttachImages` request/ack shape:

- resolves `true` when a mounted surface claimed and attached it;
- resolves `false` on no bridge, a messaging chat, a write failure, or a 5s reply timeout — and the
  caller then **falls back to an inline insert**, so the paste can never vanish;
- `index.tsx` subscribes, checks the target scope, and acks. A non-matching target acks `false`
  immediately rather than holding the caller for the timeout.

## Tests

```
apps/desktop: vitest --project ui src/app/chat/composer/paste-to-focus.test.ts   -> 15 passed
tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit                                                     -> exit 0, 0 errors
```

`paste-to-focus.test.ts` covers the routing policy end to end: a paste past the threshold becomes an
attachment instead of composer text, one at or under the threshold stays inline, and an unclaimed
attach falls back to an inline insert so the payload cannot vanish. It also pins the incident payload
(1,779 chars stays *under* the threshold, so it still lands inline) and confirms the policy never
applies to images.

It also pins `requestComposerAttachPastedText`'s own ack/timeout contract: a composer that never
answers settles the request `false` on the 5s reply timeout, and an ack arriving after that timeout
does not settle the promise a second time. Verified red by deleting the timeout's settle branch from
`focus.ts` — the test then hangs to the vitest limit, which is the stranding it exists to prevent.

Platform: Linux.


### Review note

The added ack/timeout test was verified red by deleting the timeout's settle branch from `focus.ts`:
the test then hangs to the vitest limit, which is the stranding it exists to prevent. Reverting the
deletion restores 15/15.

prs.title: fix(desktop): a media payload ends the live turn instead of queueing
prs.body:
## What and why

Policy: **messages are never queued.** A media payload (an image, a file) currently breaks that
policy on every surface, because it cannot ride a steer — the gateway carries no image into a tool
result — so it falls through to `queue`, and the user's message waits for the whole turn to finish.
On a long turn that is indistinguishable from being ignored, and on desktop it shows as "1 Queued"
with nothing happening.

A media payload cannot ride a steer or a redirect, so it must be **admitted as the next turn**. Under
`interrupt` mode the live turn should also be ended, so the admitted payload runs as soon as the turn
settles instead of waiting behind it. The interrupt is **soft** (`agent.interrupt()` defaults to
`hard_cancel=False`), so an already-accepted steer in `AIAgent._pending_steer` survives and is handed
off by the turn finalizer — a burst of messages is not destroyed by a later one (the #86134 loss).

## What this changes

**Desktop** (`busy-submit-state.ts`) — the busy action for a non-steerable payload was:

```ts
: compacting || hasComposerPayload ? 'queue' : 'stop'
```

i.e. any payload queued. Now it is `interrupt` for a payload, `queue` only while compacting (the
gateway holds a correction until compaction finishes), `stop` when there is nothing to send.

**Desktop** (`use-composer-submit.ts`) — a file payload always leaves the outbox via
`submitAsNextTurn`, which takes the same draft retry and sends it under the same `submission_id`. A
stale retry must not park the message a second time: that is how a media follow-up ended up as
"1 Queued" in the client while never reaching the gateway — no inbound event, no busy interrupt, the
turn ran to completion behind it. Text keeps its own routing (a plain message still steers), and a
blocking card still queues, because a steer cannot reach the model behind it.

**TUI** (`tui_gateway/session_auto_continue.py`) — `if mode == "interrupt" and not image_paths` kept
the live turn alive for attachments. Now `interrupt` ends the live turn for a payload too, with the
soft-interrupt reasoning documented at the call site.

## Tests

```
apps/desktop: vitest --project ui src/app/chat/composer src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions
  139 files, 1245 tests passed
```

Including the updated `use-composer-submit.test.tsx` (79 tests) and
`test_busy_submit_claims_attached_image_for_queued_turn`, which asserted the old behaviour:

```diff
-    assert not interrupted.wait(0.1)
+    # Policy: messages are never queued. A media payload cannot ride a steer or a
+    # redirect, so under `interrupt` the live turn is ended too and the admitted
+    # payload runs as soon as the turn settles.
+    assert interrupted.wait(0.1)
```

`tsc -p apps/desktop --noEmit` → exit 0, 0 errors.

### Also in this branch (not part of the media fix)

`use-prompt-actions` gains a `bypassBusyGate` submit option, so a `/goal` kickoff or a skill
dispatch runs as the next turn instead of being silently refused by the busy gate, and
`hermes-bots/group-round-prompt.ts` adds `/?INTERNAL NOTIFICATION` to the member control-frame
relabeling regex.

### One corner still drops a pending steer

The soft interrupt preserves an already-accepted steer, with one exception: an interrupt that lands
while the agent is inside API-error retry/backoff goes through `abort_turn_on_interrupt`, which
clears with `hard_cancel=True` even for a soft request (`agent/turn_recovery.py`). That is
pre-existing and not introduced here, but it means "a burst is never destroyed" is not absolute.

Platform: Linux.

## Note

The `use-composer-submit.ts` hunk in this branch adds `submitAsNextTurn` next to upstream's
`staysInComposer` / `sendOrHold` / `holdForRestart`. Those merged cleanly here (both blocks kept, each
closing its own brace); if `main` moves again in that function, the resolution is the same — the two
mechanisms are independent and neither calls the other's internals.

prs.title: fix(gateway): a stopped turn must not drive the /goal judge
prs.body:
## What and why

Stop does not stop a `/goal`. Interrupt a turn, and the post-turn hook still runs the goal judge on
the interruption text — the partial output of the turn the user just cancelled. The judge reads that
as progress and re-admits the continuation, so the loop is:

```
user hits Stop -> "[Continuing toward your standing goal]" -> model starts -> user hits Stop -> ...
```

There is no escape from the composer. The gateway already has `_turn_failed()` to keep a failed turn
from driving the judge, with the reasoning that a failed turn's text is not an answer. An
**interrupted** turn is the same case and was not covered.

## What this changes

`gateway/run_goals.py` gains `_turn_interrupted()`, mirroring `_turn_failed()`: it reads
`interrupted` off the owner's captured result, which `run_turn_runner` sets for every stop path
(`{interrupted: True, completed: False}`). `_run_post_turn_hooks` folds it into a single
`no_evidence = failed or interrupted`, which then gates both the goal judge and the text handed to
the hooks:

```python
no_evidence = failed or interrupted
if final_text.strip() and not no_evidence:
    hooks.insert(0, ("goal continuation", self._post_turn_goal_continuation))
...
final_response="" if no_evidence else final_text,
```

The loop tick is still **released** (so `/loop` does not wedge with a tick stuck in flight); only the
judge is skipped, and it is skipped with no text, exactly like the failed case. The loop keeps
running.

### The related kickoff bug, same PR

`hermes_cli/goals.py`: a goal whose text starts with `/` was handed to the next surface as-is, and
every surface parses a leading `/` as a command — so the kickoff turn never started and the goal sat
active at 0 turns forever. The kickoff is now framed, which also fixes the goal being indistinguishable
from a fresh aside:

```python
GOAL_KICK_TEMPLATE = (
    "[Standing goal]\n"
    "Goal: {goal}\n\n"
    "Start working toward this goal now. Take the first concrete step. "
    "If you believe the goal is complete, state so explicitly and stop. "
    "If you are blocked and need input from the user, say so clearly and stop."
)
```

Both are the same user-visible complaint — "a `/goal` loop that I cannot control" — which is why they
are together rather than split.

## Tests

```
tests/gateway/test_loop_command.py               -> 12 passed
tests/hermes_cli/test_cli_goal_kick_prompt.py    -> 5 passed
                                     17 passed in 9.02s
```

- `test_interrupted_turn_never_drives_goal_judge` — an interrupted turn's partial text
  (`"Operation interrupted: waiting for model response (79.5s elapsed)."`) must not drive the judge;
  asserts the judge is not awaited, the in-flight tick is released, and the loop stays `active`.
  Red without `_turn_interrupted`.
- `test_cli_goal_kick_prompt.py` — a goal beginning with `/` produces a framed kickoff that does not
  begin with a slash, and the already-seen dedup still works.

Both files also pass unchanged on `main` @ `fe9a4b58ec`, so this is additive.

Platform: Linux. Python 3.14.9.

prs.title: feat(gateway): carry background process notices into the running turn on their own marker row
prs.body:
## What and why

A background process that finishes while a turn is running cannot reach that turn. The notice is
queued, and on desktop/CLI it waits for the *next user message* — so a long agentic turn (or a turn
the model is sitting in) never learns that the command it started has exited. Same story for a
`watch_match`.

This adds a mid-turn seam for **process-registry notices** (`completion`, `watch_match`), so the
notice lands at the running turn's next tool boundary:

```
process exits mid-turn -> gateway offers the notice to the running agent
                       -> agent queues it (notify_between_tool_calls)
                       -> next tool batch appends a role:"user" row with its own marker
                       -> model sees it before its next API call
```

If the turn ends without another tool batch, the finalizer drains the queue into
`result["pending_notifications"]` and the gateway runs the first leftover as its own turn — the
existing "completion arrives on an idle session" behaviour — with the rest queued behind pending
work. Nothing is dropped in either direction.

### The queue is closed atomically at finalize

The finalizer's drain **closes** the queue under the same lock `notify_between_tool_calls` writes
with, and `notify_between_tool_calls` returns `False` once closed. Without that, a notice accepted
between the drain and the turn's teardown would sit on an agent nothing is scheduled to drain again —
silently lost, because a background completion has no user left to retry it. The `False` sends the
notice down the admit-as-its-own-turn path instead. The queue re-opens at the next turn's start,
keeping anything a turn that never reached its finalizer left behind.

### A steer on the same batch wins the slot

If a `/steer` row was appended on the same batch, the notice is **requeued** rather than appended
beside it. Two adjacent `role:"user"` rows are exactly what `repair_message_sequence` refuses to weld
(a persisted steer row is never merged), and on the wire the notice's frame would then ride inside a
row that *opens* with the user-authority steer marker — machine output speaking as the user.

### Scope, and how this differs from #136708

#136708 carries results by **appending to the next tool result** (`agent/background_results.py`,
`attach_to_tool_tail`, persisted as part of that tool row). This gives the notice **its own
`role:"user"` row** and never mutates the tool row. They occupy the same role-alternation-safe
boundary but do not conflict:

| | #136708 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| event types | `async_delegation` (durable claim) | `completion`, `watch_match` (no claim) |
| carrier | next tool result row | own `role:"user"` row |
| marker | `[BACKGROUND RESULT …]` | `[INTERNAL NOTIFICATION …]` |
| ack/settle | claim acked when the flush persists | nothing to ack |

`_deliver_notice_mid_turn` returns `False` for `async_delegation`, so if both land a delegation result
still travels #136708's path. **Note for maintainers:** #136708's current head also covers
`completion` behind `display.background_process_busy_result_mode` (default `queue`). Under the default
there is no overlap — #136708 declines, this PR delivers — but under `steer` #136708 takes the
`completion` and this path is bypassed (still live for `watch_match`, which #136708 never touches).
One gate should be chosen for the `completion` case; the two-line config read to gate this PR is
below. I raised this in #136708.

The marker is deliberately **not** the steer marker. `STEER_MARKER_OPEN` grants the text user
authority ("a direct message from the user"); a process notice is machine output, and reusing it
would let a process's stdout speak as the user. It is registered in `CONTROL_FRAME_OPENERS` so the
existing republish guards treat it like the other control frames.

## Layout

`gateway/run_notifications_midturn.py` (`GatewayMidturnNotificationMixin`) and
`agent/midturn_notifications.py` hold the feature; both origin modules are over their `FILE_LINES`
caps, so this follows the repo's existing split-topic-module pattern rather than growing them.

## Config

None — this is unconditional. A `background_process_busy_result_mode: queue` default would leave the
bug in place for everyone who does not know the key exists, which is the whole population the fix is
for. `delegation.*` is untouched. If maintainers want it gated before merge, reading a
`display.background_process_busy_result_mode` in `_deliver_notice_mid_turn` is a two-line change.

## Tests

```
tests/agent/test_midturn_notifications.py                -> 14 passed
tests/gateway/test_midturn_notification_delivery.py      ->  5 passed
tests/gateway/test_busy_leftover_notifications.py        ->  6 passed
                                        25 passed
```

- `test_midturn_notifications.py` — unit tests of the boundary: notices are queued via
  `agent.notify_between_tool_calls` and appended by `apply_pending_notifications_to_tool_results`
  called directly; a queued notice appears as its own row after the newest tool result, carries the
  notification marker and **not** the steer marker. These tests do **not** exercise the `tool_executor`
  hook (they are green with `_finalize_tool_batch`'s hook call reverted); the hook itself has no
  direct test.
- `test_midturn_notification_delivery.py` — the gateway seam: a `completion` for a busy session is
  offered to the running agent and no turn is admitted; `async_delegation` is refused and keeps its
  own path; an idle session keeps the admit-as-a-turn path.
- `test_busy_leftover_notifications.py` — the finalizer/gateway handoff: a notice with no boundary
  left becomes the next turn when nothing is pending, and queues behind pending work otherwise.

Also run, unchanged, to prove no regression in the seams this touches:

```
tests/gateway/test_completion_delivery.py                -> 42 passed
tests/gateway/test_loop_command.py
tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_queue_on_busy.py      -> 85 passed (group)
```

Gates: `scripts/check` health ratchet → **0 blocking** (ruff 0.15.22 on the pinned config);
`ruff check` on every changed file → clean.

Platform: Linux. Python 3.14.9.

## Note on the ack-before-persist race raised in #136708

That race does not apply here, by construction: a process notice has no durable claim, so nothing is
acknowledged when the row is staged. If the flush fails the row simply was not written, and the
finalizer still has the text. There is no `delivered` flag to be set prematurely.

prs.title: fix(desktop): refresh the session list and other windows after a rename
prs.body:
Closes #136157

## Problem

Renaming a session from the desktop session tab saves to the DB but the visible name often doesn't update until an unrelated refresh (turn end, poll, reconnect, profile switch). Repro and trace in the issue.

## Root cause

The rename dialog's save is optimistic-only. It patches the loaded sidebar slices (`$sessions`/`$cronSessions`/`$messagingSessions`/`$projectTree`), but when the renamed session's row is not in any loaded slice (a restored tile aged out of the paginated recents page, a session reached from an older project lane), both patches are reference-stable silent no-ops — and unlike the `/title` slash path, no `refreshSessions()` is ever scheduled. The backend write is correct and transactional; the bug is purely client-side staleness. Secondary windows are also never told (`broadcastSessionsChanged()` is not called).

## Fix

- `store/session-sync.ts`: add `$sessionsListRefresh` + `requestSessionsListRefresh()` — the poster-side half the session-sync bus can't provide (a BroadcastChannel never echoes to its own poster).
- `use-session-list-actions.ts`: the list controller listens for the nudge and re-pulls (its existing profile-scope/generation guards make this safe).
- `session-actions-menu.tsx`: `RenameSessionDialog.submit` nudges + broadcasts after a successful rename — the same pattern the turn-complete refresh uses (`use-message-stream/index.ts`).
- New invariant test in `session-actions-menu.test.tsx`.

## Verification

- New test proven red on `main` (stashed the fix: 1 failed | 10 passed), green after.
- Full desktop UI suite: 1214 files / 10730 tests pass (the 2 failures in `voice-prefs.test.ts` are pre-existing on `main`, confirmed by stashing).
- `python scripts/check`: 11 checks, ok.

prs.title: fix(agent): include provider/model/endpoint in terminal API failure messages
prs.body:
Fixes #66351

## Problem

When an API call exhausts its retries during a chat session, the user sees e.g.:

```
API call failed after 3 retries: Client error: HTTP 400
```

with no indication of which provider/model/endpoint failed. The retry loop already prints this context on every attempt, but only via `_buffer_vprint` (verbose log output) — chat sessions never see it. The internal `logger.error` also carries `provider=... model=...`, but the user-facing `final_response` dropped it. (The `Client error: ...` text itself is httpx's `HTTPStatusError` string bubbling through `_summarize_api_error()`.)

## Change

**`agent/conversation_loop.py`** — append provider/model/endpoint to `final_response` on both terminal error paths:

- **Retry-exhausted** — the "API call failed after N retries: ..." message now ends with `(provider: ..., model: ..., endpoint: ...)`
- **Non-retryable abort** — immediate hard-4xx failures get the same context suffix

```
API call failed after 3 retries: Client error: HTTP 400
(provider: openrouter, model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, endpoint: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1)
```

**`gateway/run.py`** — raise `_looks_like_gateway_provider_error`'s length heuristic from 400 to 520 chars. Worst-case envelopes (~343 chars: 300-char summary truncation + prefix) previously fit under 400 and were rewritten to the safe generic reply on chat surfaces; the appended context line could push them past the old guard, which would have leaked raw provider errors (including the endpoint) into group chats. 520 keeps every previously-sanitized envelope sanitized. Boundary test added in `test_telegram_noise_filter.py`.

## Compatibility

- The structured `error` field keeps the bare summary — cron notifications and CLI error output are unchanged.
- The desktop app's completion-error matcher anchors only on `^API call failed after \d+ retries:`, so the appended suffix is safe.
- On sanitized chat surfaces (Telegram, Discord, …) provider errors are still rewritten to the generic reply as before; the added context primarily benefits raw-text surfaces (TUI, desktop, API, local CLI).

## Testing

- `tests/gateway/test_telegram_noise_filter.py` (incl. new 400–520 boundary test) — 211 passed
- `tests/run_agent/test_nonretryable_error_html_summary.py`, `tests/run_agent/test_24996_fallback_exhaustion_cooldown.py` — 6 passed
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_tui_resume_flow.py`, `tests/gateway/test_7100_transient_failure_transcript.py`, `tests/agent/test_reasoning_stale_timeout_floor.py`, `tests/run_agent/test_18028_content_policy_blocked.py` — 120 passed
