prs.title: fix(plugins): keep llama-server from outliving a crashed backend
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Note on location: #8830 points at `qwenpaw/local_models/llamacpp.py`, which #8499 replaced with `plugins/provider/local-llamacpp/` before `v2.3.1-beta.1`. The defect is the same in the new copy, and that is what this PR patches.

`llama-server.exe` survives QwenPaw dying (#8830). The plugin launches it with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and nothing else — no new process group, no job — so when the backend crashes or is force-killed, nothing tells the server to stop. The reporter's table shows four successive starts each leaving a healthy server behind on its own random port; the fifth start then finds no RAM commit left, the child dies inside `load_model`, and all the user sees is `llama.cpp server exited before becoming ready`.

`stop_server` covers the orderly path (SIGTERM, then kill, bounded). It never runs on a crash, and the reporter notes the `atexit` path does not run either. The same hole exists on POSIX: `start_new_session` puts the server in its own group, but the group signal is also sent by `stop_server`, which a `SIGKILL` of the provider skips.

**Fix: bind the server's lifetime to the provider, at the kernel level, on both platforms.**

- **Windows** — a job with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`. When the provider's last job handle goes away, on any exit path including `TerminateProcess`, the kernel terminates every member.
- **Linux** — `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` set in a `preexec_fn` that runs between fork and exec. `SIGKILL` of the parent makes the kernel deliver `SIGKILL` to the child.

No exit handler has to run in either case, which is the point: crash-path coverage by construction, not by cleanup code a crash skips.

macOS has no equivalent knob, so it keeps the existing behaviour (`start_new_session` + group signal on an orderly stop).

## Evidence

**Windows** — same `process_options()` arguments the plugin uses, then `taskkill /F /PID <parent>` without `/T`, exactly as a crash leaves it:

```
parent pid=10460 child pid=1448
child alive after parent was killed: True      <- orphan reproduced
```

with a kill-on-close job:

```
parent pid=10308 child pid=12188
child alive after parent was killed: False     <- fix verified
```

**Linux** — real kernel, Ubuntu 24.04 / kernel 6.8.0-138 / Python 3.12.3, run against the patched `io_helpers.py` (not a stand-in):

```
process_options keys: ['preexec_fn', 'start_new_session']
--- control (no hook) ---           child_alive_after_parent_sigkill=True
--- patched process_options() ---   child_alive_after_parent_sigkill=False
VERDICT: FIX HOLDS
```

**On the documented `preexec_fn` risk.** The Python docs warn that it is not safe with threads, because the child can deadlock before exec. That is a probability, not a certainty, so it was measured rather than assumed:

| shape | worst case | stalls |
|---|---|---|
| 8 / 32 / 96 hog threads, 400–800 forks each | 0.016s / 0.061s / 0.126s | 0 |
| 16 / 48 / 96 threads forking simultaneously, 30–40 rounds | ≤ 0.029s | 0 frozen |
| bare `os.fork()` without exec, 32 / 128 / 256 threads | ≤ 0.014s | 0 stuck |
| 64 threads, 180s soak | 0.015s over 38,244 forks | 0 |

About 150,000 fork/exec cycles in total: **the deadlock never reproduced**. It is not eliminated on principle — the window the docs describe is "another thread held a C-level lock at fork time", and only libraries that fail to register an `atfork` handler keep that window open. This hook calls `libc.so.6` and nothing else, which is why it held up.

The measurement also changed the implementation: with the lookup `LIBC.prctl(...)` inside the child, the 96-thread worst case was **0.126s** — 15× the control — against **0.016s** once the function pointer is taken in the parent. The code resolves `_PRCTL` at import and the child does exactly one call.

## Scope

Type: B (process lifecycle / failure handling)

- **This stops new orphans; it does not reclaim existing ones.** Servers left over from earlier crashes keep running — they need a restart or a manual kill. Reclaiming them means deciding which `llama-server.exe` on the machine is ours; separate change.
- **Adopting an already-running server** instead of spawning a fresh one is the other half of what the report describes. It needs a persisted port/pid contract and a handshake; out of scope.
- macOS: no `PDEATHSIG`, so nothing changes there.

## Self-review

1. **Job creation fails / prctl unavailable** — logged, server still starts, only the protection is missing. No start path throws.
2. **Repeated launches** — one job per backend, later servers join it; `assign` on the same process is idempotent.
3. **Two launches at once** — `assign` runs synchronously after the `to_thread(Popen)` await, on the event-loop thread, so two coroutines cannot both see an empty handle; `_server_transitioning` already serialises server switches.
4. **Test doubles without `_handle`** — skipped with a debug log instead of raising, so the existing fake-`Popen` tests keep working.
5. **Parent already dead before `prctl` runs** — the child checks `getppid() == 1` and leaves immediately, since `PDEATHSIG` would never fire.

## Test scope

- Target: `tests/plugins/local_model/unit/test_llamacpp_backend.py` — 100 passed, 2 skipped (the two Linux-only cases skip on Windows)
- Neighbour: `tests/plugins/local_model/unit` — 263 passed
- Wider: `tests/plugins` — 303 passed, 1 failed, 25 errors
  - The single failure (`test_provider.py::test_existing_provider_settings_and_path_survive_unload`) fails identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout, so it predates this change.
  - The 25 errors are `integration/` refusing to run without `pip install -r plugins/provider/local-llamacpp/requirements.txt`; environment, not code.
- Linux cases were additionally run on a real Ubuntu 24.04 host against the patched module (transcript above), not only through CI.
- Falsify: replacing `self._server_job.assign(process)` with `pass` → `test_setup_server_binds_the_process_to_its_job` fails
- `pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files: mypy, black, flake8, pylint all pass

prs.title: feat(telegram): isolate agent sessions by forum topic
prs.body:
## Description

Telegram forum topics were invisible to session routing: every topic in a forum resolved to `telegram:<chat_id>`, so all topics shared one agent session, one memory and one Console conversation. Topic identity existed only as a reply-routing field, which meant outbound replies could land in the right topic while the conversation history was mixed.

This PR makes the session id carry the topic, and teaches outbound target parsing the resulting format.

```diff
 _message_meta(update)
+  is_topic_message = message.is_topic_message
+  thread_id = message.message_thread_id
+  if supergroup and thread_id == 1 and (is_topic_message or chat.is_forum)
+    thread_id = None            # General topic is chat scope
+
+_session_id(meta)
-  return telegram:<chat_id>
+  if supergroup and is_topic_message and thread and thread > 1
+    return telegram:<chat_id>:<thread>
+  return telegram:<chat_id>
```

Session mapping:

| Chat | `message_thread_id` | `is_topic_message` | Session |
|---|---|---|---|
| private | — / 77 | — | `telegram:42` |
| non-forum supergroup | — | — | `telegram:-100` |
| non-forum group, reply thread | 77 | false | `telegram:-100` |
| forum, General topic | 1 | true | `telegram:-100` |
| forum topic | 77 | true | `telegram:-100:77` |

Outbound target parsing (`TelegramDriver._target`) was a prefix branch plus a `split(":", 1)[1]`; it now does `session.removeprefix("telegram:").partition(":")` — one path for both `telegram:<chat>` and `telegram:<chat>:<thread>`. Parsed thread ids are normalized before use: leading zeros stripped, `1` collapsed to "no thread" (General), and anything non-ASCII/non-decimal raises `OUTBOUND_TARGET_UNKNOWN` (the existing empty-topic rejection also stays). `meta["message_thread_id"]` still wins when present; the parsed value is the fallback for replies opened from a session id alone. Non-`telegram:` session ids keep the old behavior of addressing the captured user id as the chat.

**Related Issue:** Fixes [#8827](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8827)

**Security Considerations:** Routing-only change, no auth or secret handling touched. The new parsing path is stricter than before: a malformed or empty thread segment in an outbound session id raises `OUTBOUND_TARGET_UNKNOWN` instead of being passed through, and thread ids are restricted to ASCII decimal digits before they become `send_message(message_thread_id=...)` kwargs.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

- [x] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes
- [x] Official channel changes are covered in `tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py` (startup, shutdown and message delivery)
- [ ] Shared host/process changes are covered in `test_channel_host.py` / `tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_process.py`
- [ ] Console changes retain the built-in contract checks in `tests/contract/channels/`

## Testing

Telegram channel unit tests, then the channel contract gate:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py -q
PYTHON_BIN=.venv/bin/python ./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed
```

New coverage in `tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py`:

- `test_native_update_keeps_chat_and_topic_reply_target` — parametrized matrix over private / supergroup / forum, General vs real topic, checking `conversation.thread_id`, `metadata.session_id` and the `message_thread_id` kwarg actually handed to `send_message`.
- `test_forum_topics_use_independent_sessions` — topics 201 and 202 get distinct sessions.
- `test_open_reply_target_routes_to_chat_and_topic` — parsing `telegram:-100`, `telegram:-100:1`, `telegram:-100:77`, and non-`telegram:` ids (`123`, `reminders`, empty).
- `test_open_reply_target_rejects_empty_topic_id` — malformed segment raises `OUTBOUND_TARGET_UNKNOWN`.
- `test_attachment_reads_local_file_and_uses_same_topic` — media sent in a topic keeps the topic thread.

Manual check with a real bot: forum with the default General topic plus one extra topic; send a message in each, confirm Console shows separate conversations, confirm replies and approval cards stay in the originating topic, and confirm General still shares the chat-level conversation.

## Evidence

Branch `moltlau3/feature-isolate-agent-sessions-by-telegram-forum`, single commit `0879356ef` plus the `thread_id` ordering fix.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py -q
...................                                                      [100%]
19 passed in 0.67s
```

```bash
PYTHON_BIN=.venv/bin/python ./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed
tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py::test_native_update_keeps_chat_and_topic_reply_target[supergroup-1-True-True-telegram:-100-None] PASSED [ 15%]
tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py::test_forum_topics_use_independent_sessions PASSED [ 42%]
tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py::test_open_reply_target_routes_to_chat_and_topic[telegram:-100:1--100-None] PASSED [ 52%]
tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py::test_open_reply_target_rejects_empty_topic_id PASSED [ 78%]
tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py::test_attachment_reads_local_file_and_uses_same_topic PASSED [ 84%]
============================== 19 passed in 0.68s ==============================
All channel checks passed.
```

Before the ordering fix, the same suite failed 7 of 19 with `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'thread_id'` at `platform.py:324` on every supergroup case.

Also, tested by replacing the telegram plugin running QwenPaw. All message routed correctly as mentioned in description.

## Additional Notes

- One-time history split: existing forum-topic conversations move from `telegram:<chat_id>` to `telegram:<chat_id>:<thread_id>`, so a topic's first message after upgrade starts with empty history for that topic. General-topic and non-forum traffic keeps its existing session id, so there is no data migration and no session store change.
- `pre-commit` is not installed in this environment (`No module named pre_commit`), so the two pre-commit boxes are unchecked — run it before marking Ready for review. `scripts/check-channels.sh` defaults to `python3`, which lacks `pytest`/`pip` here; `PYTHON_BIN` points it at `.venv`.

prs.title: feat(desktop): add Linux deb and AppImage packaging to the Tauri build
prs.body:
## Description

Linux currently has no desktop artifact. `desktop-build.yml` builds only Windows and macOS, `tauri.conf.json` declares `"targets": ["app", "nsis"]` with `.icns`/`.ico` icons only, and `RELEASING.md` documents the desktop apps as "Windows + macOS" — so Linux users must run the Docker image or build from source.

Related issues: **#8442** — the Linux parity umbrella; this PR lands its packaging half (deb + AppImage), while Computer Use and Chrome Native Messaging follow in separate PRs. **#5668** — the x86_64 AppImage request; the AppImage build is added here, and release publishing plus the updater follow in the next PR.

The packaging chain was already platform-neutral, which is why this is a packaging shell rather than a port:

| Piece | Already handled |
|---|---|
| Resource lookup | `backend/command.rs` resolves `python/bin/python3`, `node-runtime/bin/node`, `qwenpaw-backend` (no `.exe`) for every non-Windows target |
| Python runtime | `stage_python_runtime.py` maps Linux to `{arch}-unknown-linux-gnu` |
| Node runtime | `stage_node_runtime.py` maps Linux to `linux-{arch}` |
| Backend build | `build_pyinstaller.sh` is a generic unix script; macOS signing lives in its own wrapper |
| PyInstaller spec | platform branches exist only for darwin codesign and win32 executable names |
| Icons | generated from `scripts/pack/assets/icon.svg` |

### What this PR does

**Bundle configuration** (`console/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`)

- add `deb` and `appimage` to `bundle.targets`, keeping `app` and `nsis` untouched
- list the existing 512×512 `icons/icon.png` so Linux bundlers have a PNG
- add `bundle.publisher` and `bundle.copyright` (the deb `Maintainer` field is mandatory)
- declare `bundle.linux.deb.depends` explicitly: `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0`, `libgtk-3-0t64 | libgtk-3-0`, `libayatana-appindicator3-1`

**Build entry point** (`scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh`)

Mirrors the macOS orchestration without signing: `npm ci` → version sync → console build → `build_pyinstaller.sh` (PyInstaller backend plus bundled Python/Node runtimes) → `tauri build --bundles deb,appimage` → collect both artifacts into `dist/`. `QWENPAW_SKIP_BACKEND_BUILD=1` retries packaging without rebuilding the backend.

**Five build-host defects this exposed, each fixed in place**

1. **Python series came from the bootstrap interpreter.** On a 3.14 host the staged runtime left the `requires-python` range and dependency installation failed. `stage_python_runtime.py` now uses the host series only when it is supported (3.11–3.13) and otherwise falls back to 3.13 with a printed notice.
2. **The bundle carried the CUDA stack.** `whisper` pulls torch, and the default Linux wheel declares the CUDA runtime through `DT_NEEDED` on `libtorch_cpu.so` itself (`libcudart.so.13`), so `nvidia-*` plus `triton` added ~4 GB and could not be stripped after the fact. Linux builds now install torch from the CPU index first, so the requirement is already satisfied and the CUDA payload never enters the bundle.
3. **The product name broke `linuxdeploy`.** A space in `productName` puts a space in the AppDir and resource paths (`usr/lib/<productName>/`), which splits the `ldd` invocation linuxdeploy performs for every ELF; `ldd` exits 1 and bundling aborts with the unhelpful `failed to run linuxdeploy`. Linux now uses the space-free `QwenPawDesktop` (the window title still comes from `app.windows[0].title`; data remains under `~/.qwenpaw`).
4. **A failed run poisoned the next one.** Tauri merges into an existing AppDir, so leftovers under the previous product name survived; the bundle directories are now removed before bundling.
5. **linuxdeploy cannot infer dependencies for a bundled runtime.** It walks every ELF in the AppDir — thousands of files inside the Python runtime — and aborts on the first unresolved name, which is pure overhead for a tree that ships its own dependencies. When bundling fails, the script now deduplicates the resource tree that Tauri emits under two names (one real copy plus a symlink), points `.DirIcon` at the icon named by the desktop entry, and packs the AppDir with `appimagetool`.

**Packaging hygiene** — a single build left ~20 GB of intermediates behind (`target/release/binaries` 9.7 GB, `target/release/bundle/appimage_deb` 9.7 GB). They are now removed after the artifacts are collected (`QWENPAW_DESKTOP_KEEP_STAGING=1` keeps them).

**CI** (`desktop-build.yml`, new `build-tauri-linux` job on `ubuntu-24.04`)

Installs the Linux packaging dependencies, builds both formats, verifies the launched app with Playwright through a new `.github/actions/verify-tauri-linux` action (plus `scripts/verify/launch_tauri_linux.sh`, which runs the AppImage under Xvfb, waits for `~/.qwenpaw/desktop_port`, and exports `BASE_URL`), records checksums, and uploads the deb, the AppImage and the verify logs. `desktop_verify.py` gains the `tauri-linux` UI mode (Playwright WebKit).

**Docs** — a Linux section in `website/public/docs/desktop.{en,zh}.md` (requirements, deb vs AppImage install, first-run data paths, updates, uninstall) and the release support matrix.

### Evidence

Environment: Ubuntu 26.04 (GNOME 50, Wayland-only), rustc 1.99.1, webkit2gtk-4.1 2.52.6, node v24.21.0, host Python 3.14.

```text
$ bash scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh
== Checking prerequisites ==
  [INFO] python3 3.14 is outside 3.11-3.13; the bundled runtime will be staged as 3.13
== Step 2: PyInstaller backend + bundled runtimes ==
== Installing CPU-only torch ==
...
== Step 3b: tauri bundling failed; packing the AppDir with appimagetool ==
    deduplicating usr/lib/QwenPaw Desktop -> symlink to QwenPawDesktop
-rwxr-xr-x 976M  dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.AppImage
-rw-r--r--  1.3G dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb
```

```text
$ dpkg-deb -I dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb
 Package: qwen-paw-desktop
 Version: 2.3.0-beta.1
 Architecture: amd64
 Installed-Size: 3489035
 Maintainer: QwenPaw Contributors
 Depends: libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0, libgtk-3-0t64 | libgtk-3-0, libayatana-appindicator3-1, ...
```

```text
$ dpkg-deb -c dist/...deb | grep -oE "usr/lib/[^/]+" | sort -u
usr/lib/QwenPawDesktop            # single resource tree

$ apt-get install --dry-run ./dist/...deb | tail -3
The following NEW packages will be installed:
  qwen-paw-desktop
0 upgraded, 1 newly installed
```

Installed and launched on the target machine:

```text
$ sudo apt install ./dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb && qwenpaw-desktop
[backend] packaged command: /usr/lib/QwenPaw Desktop/binaries/qwenpaw-backend/qwenpaw-backend
[backend] bundled python runtime: .../python-runtime/python/bin/python3
[backend] bundled node runtime: .../node-runtime
[backend] shared runtime 2.3.0-beta.1 connected after 9534ms (launched=true)
```

The window renders, the sidecar connects, and `~/.qwenpaw` is created on first launch.

### Open items (separate changes)

- Release plumbing (`desktop-publish.yml` / `desktop-promote.yml`, OSS paths, `linux-x86_64` in the updater manifest) and the AppImage updater client branch — PR2.
- Arm64 (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`) — follow-up once x86_64 is green.
- The AppImage has been built, structurally verified (valid AppImage, correct desktop entry, deduplicated payload) and **launched successfully on the target machine**; CI covers the launch on every build.

### 描述

Linux 目前没有桌面产物：`desktop-build.yml` 只构建 Windows 与 macOS，`tauri.conf.json` 的 `targets` 只有 `["app","nsis"]`，图标只有 `.icns`/`.ico`，`RELEASING.md` 也写着「Windows + macOS」——Linux 用户只能跑 Docker 或从源码构建。

相关 issue：**#8442** —— Linux 对齐的总 issue，本 PR 落地其中的打包部分（deb + AppImage），Computer Use 与 Chrome Native Messaging 由后续 PR 完成；**#5668** —— x86_64 AppImage 提案，本 PR 补上 AppImage 构建，发布与自动更新由下一个 PR 完成。

打包链本来就是平台中立的，所以这是补一个打包壳，而不是移植：

| 部分 | 已就绪 |
|---|---|
| 资源查找 | `backend/command.rs` 对所有非 Windows 目标已按 `python/bin/python3`、`node-runtime/bin/node`、无 `.exe` 的 `qwenpaw-backend` 查找 |
| Python runtime | `stage_python_runtime.py` 已映射 Linux 到 `{arch}-unknown-linux-gnu` |
| Node runtime | `stage_node_runtime.py` 已映射 Linux 到 `linux-{arch}` |
| 后端构建 | `build_pyinstaller.sh` 是通用 unix 脚本，macOS 签名单独封装 |
| PyInstaller spec | 平台分支只有 darwin 签名与 win32 可执行名 |
| 图标 | 由 `scripts/pack/assets/icon.svg` 生成 |

### 本 PR 做了什么

**打包配置**（`console/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`）

- `bundle.targets` 追加 `deb` 与 `appimage`，保留原有 `app`、`nsis`
- 列入已有的 512×512 `icons/icon.png`，供 Linux 打包器使用
- 补 `bundle.publisher` 与 `bundle.copyright`（deb 的 `Maintainer` 是必填项）
- 显式声明 `bundle.linux.deb.depends`：`libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0`、`libgtk-3-0t64 | libgtk-3-0`、`libayatana-appindicator3-1`

**构建入口**（`scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh`）

照抄 macOS 编排、去掉签名：`npm ci` → 版本同步 → console 构建 → `build_pyinstaller.sh`（PyInstaller 后端 + 内嵌 Python/Node runtime）→ `tauri build --bundles deb,appimage` → 两个产物归集到 `dist/`。`QWENPAW_SKIP_BACKEND_BUILD=1` 可在不重建后端的情况下重试打包。

**这次暴露并修复的五个构建机缺陷**

1. **Python 版本跟随引导解释器**：3.14 宿主会让内嵌运行时越出 `requires-python` 范围、装依赖失败。现在宿主 3.11–3.13 直接用宿主版本，否则回退 3.13 并打印提示。
2. **包里带上 CUDA 栈**：`whisper` 引入 torch，而 Linux 默认 wheel 通过 `libtorch_cpu.so` 的 `DT_NEEDED`（`libcudart.so.13`）硬依赖 CUDA runtime，`nvidia-*` 与 `triton` 合计约 4GB 且**事后删不掉**。改为 Linux 先装 CPU 版 torch，依赖需求即被满足，CUDA 载荷根本不进包。
3. **产品名里的空格打断 `linuxdeploy`**：AppDir 与资源路径（`usr/lib/<productName>/`）都带空格，linuxdeploy 对每个 ELF 调用的 `ldd` 会被拆参，`ldd` 退出码 1，整体报 `failed to run linuxdeploy` 且无细节。Linux 改用无空格的 `QwenPawDesktop`（窗口标题仍来自 `app.windows[0].title`，数据仍在 `~/.qwenpaw`）。
4. **一次失败会污染下一次**：Tauri 合并而非重建 AppDir，旧产品名的残留会留下；现在打包前先清空 bundle 目录。
5. **linuxdeploy 对内嵌 runtime 做依赖推导没有意义**：它会遍历 AppDir 里每个 ELF（内嵌 Python runtime 有数千个），任一解析失败即整体中止；而我们的树自带全部依赖。现在失败时自动去重 Tauri 的双份资源（一份真身 + 一个软链）、修正 `.DirIcon`、改用 `appimagetool` 直接压 AppDir。

**打包卫生**：一次构建会残留约 20GB 中间产物（`target/release/binaries` 9.7GB、`target/release/bundle/appimage_deb` 9.7GB），现在归集产物后自动清理（`QWENPAW_DESKTOP_KEEP_STAGING=1` 可保留）。

**CI**（`desktop-build.yml` 新增 `build-tauri-linux`，`ubuntu-24.04`）

安装 Linux 打包依赖、构建两种格式、用新增的 `.github/actions/verify-tauri-linux` 通过 Playwright 验证启动后的应用（配套 `scripts/verify/launch_tauri_linux.sh` 在 Xvfb 下运行 AppImage、等 `~/.qwenpaw/desktop_port`、导出 `BASE_URL`），记录校验和并上传 deb/AppImage/验证日志。`desktop_verify.py` 增加 `tauri-linux` 模式（Playwright WebKit）。

**文档**：`website/public/docs/desktop.{en,zh}.md` 增加 Linux 章节（系统要求、deb/AppImage 安装、首启数据目录、更新与卸载），并更新发布支持矩阵。

### 证据

环境：Ubuntu 26.04（GNOME 50，仅 Wayland），rustc 1.99.1，webkit2gtk-4.1 2.52.6，node v24.21.0，宿主 Python 3.14。

```text
$ bash scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh
  [INFO] python3 3.14 is outside 3.11-3.13; the bundled runtime will be staged as 3.13
== Installing CPU-only torch ==
== Step 3b: tauri bundling failed; packing the AppDir with appimagetool ==
    deduplicating usr/lib/QwenPaw Desktop -> symlink to QwenPawDesktop
976M  dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.AppImage
1.3G  dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb
```

```text
$ dpkg-deb -I dist/...deb
 Package: qwen-paw-desktop | Version: 2.3.0-beta.1 | Architecture: amd64
 Installed-Size: 3489035 | Maintainer: QwenPaw Contributors
```

prs.title: fix(code-mode): let run_tool_batch reach catalog tools inside code mode
prs.body:
## Description

In code mode, `run_tool_batch` could not call any other tool: every inner call failed with `ToolNotFoundError`.

`CodeModeTool.execute_tool` runs each script tool call in a one-tool invocation toolkit (`_execution_toolkit`), and `CodeModeToolkit.call_tool` forwarded every call to it. `run_tool_batch` dispatches its inner calls through `get_current_toolkit()`, which is the outer `CodeModeToolkit`. Those calls were therefore forwarded into the invocation toolkit that holds only `run_tool_batch`, as the issue traces.

Now, when the invocation toolkit doesn't hold the requested tool, `CodeModeToolkit.call_tool` sends the call to `self.catalog`, through the catalog's own `call_tool` pipeline. A call to the invoked tool itself still runs in its invocation, and calls outside an invocation are unchanged. The inner calls don't take `execution_slot`, so they can't wait on the slot the outer `run_tool_batch` holds.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8903

**Security Considerations:** Inner calls now go through the catalog's `Toolkit.call_tool`, the same pipeline `run_tool_batch`'s `_call_tool` documents for a normal agent turn (permission checks, group activation, state injection). Previously they failed before reaching any tool. Open #7926 changes governance inside `run_tool_batch` itself and doesn't touch `code_mode.py`.

prs.title: fix(agents): retry generic media bad requests without media
prs.body:
Historical tool results from `view_video` can reintroduce video into later
model requests. When the provider returns a generic `400 Invalid request
parameters`, the existing fallback does not recognize it, so follow-up
messages in the same session keep failing.

Retry once without media only if the failed request actually sent media and
the response does not identify a specific invalid parameter. The retry does
not modify stored history, affect file delivery, or cache a model capability
change. If the retry also fails, propagate the error.

Fixes #8887.

prs.title: test(contract): sort handler parametrization for stable xdist collection
prs.body:
## Description

`pytest -n` aborts during collection whenever more than one xdist worker collects `tests/contract/runner/test_control_command_contract.py`: the two handler-contract parametrizations derive their cases from a `set` of class objects, class objects hash by identity, and each worker's interpreter therefore produces a different case order (`Different tests were collected between gw0 and gw1`, reproduced 3/3). The suite cannot be run in parallel at all while this file is included.

**Fix:** sort the concrete handlers by `(module, qualname)` in `_concrete_handlers()`. The file already sorts its string parametrization (`sorted(_EXPECTED_DEFAULTS)`); this applies the same determinism to the class-based ones. No assertions change.

prs.title: feat(harness): add Antigravity CLI (ACP) harness plugin
prs.body:
## Description

Adds the optional `qwenpaw-harness-agy` third-party agent harness plugin under `plugins/harness/agy/`, allowing QwenPaw agents to run on the Antigravity CLI via its Agent Client Protocol server (`agy acp`).

This PR covers **only the third-party agent harness backend plugin** (not a model provider) and uses strictly the public QwenPaw Plugin SDK (`1.1.0`, `qwenpaw.plugins.harnesses`).

### Highlights
- **ACP server & session management (`plugins/harness/agy/adapter.py`)**:
  - One `agy acp` process per working directory, or isolated per conversation when MCP servers are attached (with configurable LRU cap and idle TTL eviction via `QWENPAW_AGY_MAX_IDLE_ISOLATED_SERVERS` / `QWENPAW_AGY_IDLE_SERVER_TTL_SECONDS`).
  - Session mappings scoped by `[user_id, channel, session_id]` in `plugin-data/qwenpaw-harness-agy/agy_sessions.json` with one-time legacy copy from `harnesses/agy_sessions.json`.
  - Strips inherited parent `ANTIGRAVITY_*` IPC variables (preserving `ANTIGRAVITY_APP_DATA_DIR`) so child `agy acp` processes boot cleanly even when launched from an Antigravity IDE terminal.
- **Models, thinking levels & approvals**:
  - Per-turn `model`, `thought_level` (including compound IDs such as `<model>-<effort>`), and `mode` applied via ACP `set_config_option`.
  - Five approval presets (`ask`, `accept-edits`, `plan`, `auto`, `full-access`). Interactive approvals route through `HarnessCallContext.request_approval(...)`; refusals select the CLI's reject option so the turn continues cleanly; `full-access` runs on a server started with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.
- **Auth fingerprinting (`plugins/harness/agy/auth_fingerprint.py`)**:
  - Hashes stable non-secret account identity fields (macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service, or SSH token file; fail-open when unavailable) so switching accounts via `agy acp --login` automatically recycles idle servers and invalidates cached status/models.
- **Prompting, MCP projection, attachments & commands**:
  - Appends host background-work rules, workspace identity/memory files (`SOUL.md`, `PROFILE.md`, `MEMORY.md`), and any truncated remainder of `AGENTS.md` (>24 KB) via ACP session `_meta`.
  - Reminds the session to wait when non-daemon tool calls are still `in_progress` at `end_turn` (capped per turn), and supports `/swarm`.
  - Projects QwenPaw MCP servers (`stdio` with optional `cwd` wrapper, plus `http`/`sse` when advertised by the ACP server) and supports image (local path, `file://`, inline `data:` URL with magic-byte MIME sniffing) and file attachments.
- **Plugin frontend & packaging**:
  - Self-contained plugin frontend under `plugins/harness/agy/frontend/` wrapping `plugins/harness/_shared/ui/Settings.tsx` (which also displays `account.plan` when present) with all seven locales (`en`, `zh`, `ja`, `ru`, `pt-BR`, `vi`, `id`).
  - Wired into `sync_harness_helpers.py`, `build_harness_frontends.sh`, `generate_plugin_metadata.py`, `.github/workflows/harness-plugin-tests.yml`, `test_generate_plugin_metadata.py`, and `thirdPartyAgentLocales.test.ts`.

**Security Considerations:**
- Credentials are never stored or logged; `auth_fingerprint.py` hashes only stable identity metadata with SHA-256 and fails open if keyring access is locked or unavailable.
- Parent `ANTIGRAVITY_*` IPC environment variables are stripped when spawning `agy acp`.
- Interactive permission requests are bound strictly to the live `HarnessCallContext` and cancelled if a callback arrives outside an active turn.
- Verified against `python -m qwenpaw.plugins.check --run` (zero private host imports).

prs.title: feat(memory): add reranker model center with service test, multi-query precision history and auto-verify
prs.body:
## Description

**What this PR does:** Adds a reranker model center to the reranker settings (Runtime Config → Memory & Retrieval), mirroring the existing Embedding model center, and upgrades the ranking-precision verification from a single binary smoke test into a multi-query, persisted, and optionally scheduled metric.

**Why:** A misconfigured reranker is currently invisible until retrieval quality degrades. The new center surfaces configuration status, current model, service verification (connectivity + latency) and a meaningful ranking-precision figure (`correct/total`, 10-run rolling average, sparkline) so a bad model is visible at a glance and its trend can be tracked across restarts.

The overview shows four slots: configuration status, current model, service verification and ranking precision.

### Changes

- **Reranker model center**: `RerankerModelCenter` overview on the same 4-column grid and status styles as the embedding card; session-scoped `rerankerVerificationStore` keyed by agent + service fingerprint, invalidated when the service config changes or the agent switches.
- **Service verification**: `POST /workspace/reranker/test` sends a real rerank request with sample documents (one clearly relevant plus two distractors) and returns latency, relevance scores mapped back to request order, and whether the expected most-relevant document ranked first. The outbound call runs under a hard `asyncio.wait_for` deadline, upstream HTML error pages are stripped to plain text, and the API key is masked in returned messages.

prs.title: chore(deps): bump reme-ai to 0.4.2.3
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QwenPaw pins `reme-ai==0.4.2.0`. On Windows the memory tag index never rebuilds, so `/memory/tags` and `/memory/tag-files` answer 503 (#8580). The root cause was fixed in ReMe by canonicalizing legacy Windows paths instead of failing the rebuild — ReMe #717.

**That fix first ships in 0.4.2.3, not in 0.4.2.2.**

```
v0.4.2.1  has #717 = False
v0.4.2.2  has #717 = False
v0.4.2.3  has #717 = True
          "* fix(tag-index): canonicalize legacy Windows paths instead of failing rebuild
             by @BeiMu-new in https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe/pull/717"
```

So bumping to 0.4.2.2 would install cleanly and still leave #8580 broken. This PR goes to 0.4.2.3, the first release that actually carries the fix.

0.4.2.3 requires `mcp<3,>=1.28.1`. QwenPaw pins `mcp 1.28.1`, which sits inside that range, so the new build resolves without touching any other constraint.

## Scope

Type: A (single-point fix)

Four places spell the version out and they move together:

- `pyproject.toml` — `reme-ai==0.4.2.0` → `reme-ai==0.4.2.3`
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/reme_light_memory_manager.py` — `_REQUIRED_REME_VERSION = "0.4.2.3"`
- `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_reme_start.py` — the monkeypatched `reme.__version__` must equal the constant, otherwise the version check fires before the assertion under test
- `tests/integration/test_reme_watch_contract.py` — the install line in the module docstring

## Self-review

1. **Only the target semantics move** — `git diff --stat` is 4 files, `+4 −4`. Every changed line is a version literal.
2. **Callers of `_REQUIRED_REME_VERSION`** — three uses, all inside `reme_light_memory_manager.py`: the startup comparison, the mismatch message and the reinstall hint. None of them branch on a specific version, so the value change is safe.
3. **`0.4.2.0` left in place where it is a historical statement** — the comment in `reme_tags.py:59` describes what 0.4.2.0 did (why the long-tag fallback exists) and `website/public/release-notes/v2.3.0.*` records what that release shipped. Rewriting either would make the record wrong; neither is the current pin.
4. **Local environment untouched** — the regression run below used a separate venv with 0.4.2.3 installed, so the running instance keeps 0.4.2.0 until this lands.

## Test scope

Run with `PYTHONPATH=src` against a venv where `reme-ai==0.4.2.3` is installed:

- `tests/integration/test_reme_consistency_contract.py` + `test_reme_embedding_contract.py` + `test_reme_tags_contract.py` — **6 passed**
- `tests/integration/test_reme_watch_contract.py` — **1 passed**
- `tests/unit/agents/memory` — **303 passed** (1 pre-existing asyncio warning)
- `pre-commit run --files <the four files>` — all hooks passed

The tag-index contract above is the one that exercises the #717 path on a real ReMe application; it passes on 0.4.2.3.

## Evidence

```
$ python -c "import reme; print(reme.__version__)"
0.4.2.3                      # venv used for the regression run

$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/integration/test_reme_*_contract.py -q
6 passed                     # consistency + embedding + tags
1 passed                     # watch

$ PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/unit/agents/memory -q
303 passed
```

Refs #8580, ReMe #717

prs.title: feat(memory): allow a separate model for ReMeLight memory writing
prs.body:
## Description

`ReMeLightMemoryManager` currently injects the agent's main model into ReMe's `as_llm` component before every memory-writing job (`auto_memory` / `auto_dream` / `daily_paper` / `auto_fin`), so memory writing always consumes the same (often expensive) model used for chatting.

This PR adds an optional `memory_model` slot to `reme_light_memory_config`, so memory writing can run on an independent, lighter model:

- Uses `{"provider_id": "...", "model": "..."}` as the canonical format; a string is treated as a bare model name that inherits the main model's provider, including version-tagged names such as `qwen2.5:7b`.
- When unset, behavior is unchanged (main model is used).
- If dedicated-model construction fails (including non-`ProviderError` SDK exceptions), the manager logs a warning and injects the usable main model. Runtime failures before output can also fall back to that model. Main-model failures still propagate. Image jobs exclude the main-model fallback unless it has confirmed image support.
- The injected model is refreshed before every LLM job, so config changes take effect without a restart.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7664

**Security Considerations:** `memory_model` stores only a provider/model reference; no credentials are written to `agent.json` (API keys stay in the provider store).

prs.title: feat(memory): explain an unhealthy tag index and offer a rebuild
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`GET /memory/tags` and `GET /memory/tag-files` answer a flat
`503 "Memory tag index is unavailable"` whenever the tag index is unhealthy, and
the Console pane collapses every failure into "Load failed — retry".

That leaves a Windows user in #8863 with no way forward: the pane is empty, the
retry button never helps, and nothing says the tag index is an optional derived
index that can be rebuilt. The reporter found the workaround by hand
(`POST /memory/reindex?scope=embedding`); the UI should offer it.

## Change

**Backend**

- `reme_tags.py` raises a dedicated `TagIndexUnavailableError` instead of a bare
  `RuntimeError`, so the router can tell "the tag index is unhealthy" apart from
  every other runtime failure.
- `_run_memory_tag_action` maps that error to a structured 503:
  `{"code": "tag_index_unavailable", "message": ..., "rebuild": {"endpoint": ...,
  "scopes": ["all", "embedding"]}}`.
  Every other `RuntimeError` keeps the previous flat string detail.

**Console**

- `MemoryTagsNavigator` reads the structured code through `parseErrorDetail` and
  renders a dedicated state: why the pane is empty, plus a "Rebuild index"
  action.
- That action calls the existing `agentsApi.rebuildMemoryIndex(agentId, "all")`.
  No new endpoint, no new backend capability — the pane gets an entry point for
  something that is already there.

## Evidence

Before: any tag-index failure produced `503` with a plain string, and the pane
said only "Load failed".

After:

```
GET /api/agents/bot/memory/tags
503 {"detail": {"code": "tag_index_unavailable",
                "message": "Memory tag index is unavailable",
                "rebuild": {"endpoint": "/agents/bot/memory/reindex",
                            "scopes": ["all", "embedding"]}}}
```

Tests in `tests/unit/app/routers/test_agents_router.py`:

| test | covers |
|---|---|
| `test_tag_browser_explains_an_unhealthy_index` (tags, tag-files) | structured 503 plus the rebuild hint |
| `test_tag_browser_keeps_the_flat_message_for_other_runtime_errors` | the flat path is unchanged |
| `test_tag_browser_returns_unavailable_instead_of_empty` | still 503, never an empty success |

## Not in this PR

Making the reindex itself survive a failing tag rebuild belongs to ReMe, not
here: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe/pull/780. This PR only makes the
failure explainable and actionable in the UI.

Once that ReMe change ships, a rebuild triggered from this pane stops failing on
the tag step, so the same button covers both the reporting gap and the recovery
path.

prs.body:
## Description

This change makes TelegramChannel handle polling failures more explicitly instead of relying on PTB internals alone. It now:

  - detects polling network error vs conflict
  - tracks consecutive retries separately for each case
  - requests a clean outer reconnect by stopping the updater and rebuilding the application
  - applies reason-specific retry delays:

      - conflicts: fixed delay

This fixes the case where Telegram stops receiving messages after a brief disconnect and only recovers after manually restarting QwenPaw or toggling the channel.

issues.title: [Feature]: Embed memory recall queries with a configurable prefix for instruction-tuned embedding models

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: memory
labels.description: Auto scope: src/memory/** changed.

labels.name: status:in-progress
labels.description: Open PR actively targets this issue; recheck when PR closes.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let memory recall embed the search query with a configurable prefix, so instruction-tuned embedding models can be used for memory as they were trained.

### Problem statement

Memory uses one embedding call for everything: `EmbeddingProvider::embed` / `embed_one` (`crates/zeroclaw-memory/src/embeddings.rs`) embeds a stored memory and a recall query in exactly the same way. That is right for OpenAI or Gemini embeddings, which treat both sides alike. It is wrong for the instruction-tuned models that are now the strongest open options for local or self-hosted embedding, such as Qwen3-Embedding, E5 and BGE: they are trained to embed a passage as-is and a query with an instruction in front (`Instruct: <task>\nQuery:<text>` for Qwen3-Embedding, `query: ` for E5), and without it they rank noticeably worse.

Numbers from one deployment, replaying its own recall path (hybrid search, its rerank settings, memories created before each conversation began) over its real messages, with every injected memory judged for usefulness:

| embedder | useful share of injected memories | useful earlier-conversation memories per message |
|---|---|---|
| Gemini `gemini-embedding-001` (current) | 51% | 0.68 |
| keyword only (`bm25`) | 50% | 0.55 |
| Qwen3-Embedding-4B, query sent as-is | 45% | 0.53 |
| Qwen3-Embedding-4B, query with its instruction | 49% | 0.72 |

The same local model goes from worse than keyword search to level with the hosted model once the query carries its instruction. The second column is the case that matters most in practice for that user: a new conversation picking up facts from an earlier one. Today ZeroClaw cannot send that instruction, so anyone who wants local embeddings for memory gets the worse row.

### Proposed solution

1. A `[memory] embedding_query_prefix` option, unset by default. When set, it is prepended to the recall query, and only the query, before embedding.
2. Applied at the query sites of the backends that embed queries: SQLite recall, and both Qdrant recall paths. Store and re-index paths are untouched, so stored vectors do not change and no re-embedding is needed when the prefix is set or changed.
3. The SQLite embedding cache keys on the text actually embedded, so a prefixed query gets its own cache entry instead of reusing the vector of the same text stored as a memory.

A verbatim prefix rather than a model-specific template keeps it to one string that covers Qwen3-Embedding, E5, BGE and similar models.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Provider-native query modes (Gemini's `task_type`, Cohere's `input_type`); a later `embed_query` on the trait could carry those, this change does not need it.
- A per-route prefix on `[[embedding_routes]]`.
- Any default change: unset behaves exactly as today.

### Alternatives considered

- **Prefix the query in the runtime before it reaches memory:** it would also prefix the keyword search text, which must stay unchanged.
- **Put the prefix in every stored memory's text too:** wrong for these models, which expect passages without the instruction, and it would change stored vectors.
- **A wrapper embedder:** the embedder is hot-swapped on configuration changes through `refresh_embedder`, which would drop a wrapper; the backends already hold the per-query settings.

### Acceptance criteria

- With the option unset, recall embeds the same text as today and shares the cache with identical stored text.
- With it set, recall embeds `prefix + query`; stored content and re-indexing embed the unprefixed text.
- A repeated prefixed query is served from the cache.
- Both Qdrant recall paths apply the prefix.

### Architecture impact

`zeroclaw-config` (one optional `MemoryConfig` field) and `zeroclaw-memory` (the SQLite and Qdrant query sites, a small helper in `embeddings.rs`, wiring in the backend factory). No trait changes.

### Risk and rollback

Low: opt-in, query side only. Rollback is unsetting the option; no stored data changes either way.

### Expected routing

Ordinary feature triage.

### Next decision surface

Ordinary triage. A PR implementing this follows.

### Breaking change?

No.

### Data hygiene checks

- [x] I removed personal/sensitive data from examples, payloads, and logs.
- [x] I used neutral, project-focused wording and placeholders.

issues.title: test(tunnel): start_forwarder_rechecks_the_process_after_the_probe fails on macOS runners (200 ms timing window)
issues.body:
## Summary

`tunnel::tailscale::tests::start_forwarder_rechecks_the_process_after_the_probe` fails on the macOS platform-test runner. It has a 200 ms timing window that macOS runners don't reliably meet. Master fails it, so it isn't caused by any open PR. It only surfaced now because macOS started running the test suite after #12706 fixed the nextest install.

## Evidence

| Run | Commit | Result | Test time |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Scheduled Platform Tests, macOS](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45748664396/job/139671045783) | master `caada4005a` | **FAIL**, also on retry; 20946 of 20947 tests passed | 0.334 s |
| [PR #12678, macOS](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45743571808/job/139654327274) | `d1396c3bd8` | **FAIL**, also on retry | 0.265 s |
| [#12706, macOS](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45703895981) | #12706 head | pass | 0.216 s |

The panic in every failing run is the same: `a process that exited during the probe is not published: Child { … }` at `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tunnel/tailscale.rs:1606`. `start_forwarder` returned `Ok(child)` because the process was still alive when it was checked again after the probe.

## Cause

The test spawns `sh -c "sleep 0.05; printf … >&2; exit 1"` through `exit_with_stderr_after("0.05", "rejected")`. Its second status probe sleeps a fixed **200 ms** and then reports the forward as applied. The test only works if the shell has started, slept and exited within those 200 ms of spawn. Then the `try_wait()` after the probe sees the exit and `start_forwarder` returns `Exited`. On a loaded macOS runner, starting `sh` and `sleep` can take longer than that, so the process is still running when it is re-checked and gets published.

Linux CI and the earlier macOS run fit inside the window. The two failures came in at 0.265 s and 0.334 s, just past it.

## Possible fixes (test-only; `start_forwarder` behaves correctly)

- Have the probe wait until the stand-in has actually exited before it reports the forward, instead of waiting a fixed time. For example, the spawn closure can record the child's PID, and the probe can poll until that process is a zombie (`ps -o stat= -p <pid>` shows `Z`) without reaping it, so `start_forwarder`'s own `try_wait()` still sees the exit.
- Or, as a stopgap, widen the margin, e.g. a 2 s probe delay against the 50 ms exit. That costs about 2 s of test time and makes failure much less likely without ruling it out.

Other tests in this module that pair a `sleep` stand-in with a fixed probe delay may have the same weakness on macOS. They currently pass.

issues.body:
### Affected component

config/onboarding

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

A runtime profile can report `max_cost_per_day_cents = 4294967295` (effectively unbounded), while agent turns are still rejected after the process-wide cost ledger exceeds `$10.00` for the day. This happens when `[cost].daily_limit_usd` is omitted because its default is `10.0`.

The rejection does not identify the setting that supplied the limit. Switching to another agent or provider does not help because the cost tracker is process-global.

On current `master`, `max_cost_per_day_cents` is copied into `SecurityPolicy` and used for parent/child escalation checks, but the provider-call budget check consults `CostConfig.daily_limit_usd`. The Config UI therefore presents two apparently overlapping daily-cost controls without showing their precedence or the effective limit.

### Expected behavior

ZeroClaw should define and expose one clear contract for global and per-agent daily cost limits.

If both limits are intended to apply, request-time enforcement should use the effective limit and the Config UI and rejection message should identify its value and source. If `max_cost_per_day_cents` is only a delegation-policy ceiling rather than a per-agent spending limit, its name, description, and UI placement should make that distinction explicit.

An agent using the built-in unbounded runtime profile should not appear unbounded while an undisclosed default global limit is actively blocking it.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# In config.toml, bind two agents to an effectively unbounded runtime profile.
[runtime_profiles.unbounded]
max_cost_per_day_cents = 4294967295

[agents.first]
runtime_profile = "unbounded"

[agents.second]
runtime_profile = "unbounded"

# Do not add a [cost] section, so daily_limit_usd defaults to 10.0.
# Configure pricing for a model and run priced turns until aggregate daily
# recorded cost exceeds $10, then submit another turn through either agent.
```

The next provider call is rejected even though the selected runtime profile displays an effectively unlimited daily cost value.

### Impact

Affected users: operators using runtime profiles and cost tracking through the Config UI.

Frequency: deterministic once the shared daily ledger crosses the default `$10.00` limit.

Consequence: all priced agent turns are blocked until the daily window resets or the separate global setting is discovered and changed. The visible runtime profile suggests that changing agents or providers should avoid the cap, but it cannot.

### Logs / stack traces

```text
Budget exceeded: $10.6189 of $10.00 Day limit. Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets.
```

### ZeroClaw version

v0.8.4; the same configuration and enforcement split is present on `master` at `cb2b20a9fe59004b7ef03e123942d31f29236d15`.

### Rust version

rustc 1.97.0 (2d8144b78 2026-07-07)

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2 (Apple silicon)

### Regression?

Unknown

issues.body:
### Affected component

provider

### Severity

S2 - degraded behavior

### Current behavior

Channels that save inbound images and render `[IMAGE:<path>]` markers (Signal, Telegram, Discord) keep those markers in session history: `collapse_inline_image_payloads` strips inline `data:` payloads from older turns but deliberately preserves file-path markers "so a later turn can re-inflate from disk". Multimodal preparation then loads image markers from every user message in history (`should_normalize_message_images`), so each preserved path marker is read from disk and sent to the provider again on every later turn.

Only two settings bound this. `[multimodal] max_images` (default `4`) caps the total, evicting the oldest first. `[multimodal] max_image_turns` defaults to `0`, which its schema doc describes as disabling age-based trimming entirely. With defaults, the most recent four images are re-sent on every turn for the life of the session.

The re-sent image carries nothing that marks it as previously sent. When a later text-only message refers to "this one" or "the attached photo", the model treats the re-sent image as a new attachment and describes a "new" photo that was never sent, inventing details that differ from the real one.

Observed on Signal DMs with a fresh session. Only Signal was tested; the Telegram and Discord behaviour, and the unaffected `data:` URI channels, follow from the code paths above.

1. User sends a photo with a question; the reply describes it correctly.
2. User sends "and this one?" with no attachment; the reply describes "another photo of the same subject" with lighting and details that are not in any sent image.
3. User sends "what about this one?" with no attachment; another invented description.
4. User asks how many photos were sent; the reply says 3. One was sent.

### Expected behavior

A text-only follow-up does not receive descriptions of images that were not sent with it. Either earlier images stop being re-sent after the turn they arrive in, or the model can tell re-sent history images apart from attachments on the current message.

Possible directions: a non-zero default for `max_image_turns`, or labelling re-sent history images as previously sent so they are not presented like current attachments. Related: #8151, #11166, #9887.

Any fix needs to keep #8151 working: that bug was fixed by preserving these path markers so a deferred image stays available on a later turn. Dropping earlier images (including the `max_image_turns = 1` workaround) gives that up, which favours labelling re-sent images over removing them.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a vision-capable model and the default `[multimodal]` settings (`max_image_turns = 0`).
2. Start a fresh session on Signal, Telegram, or Discord and send one image with a question.
3. Send text-only follow-ups such as "and this one?" and "what about this one?".
4. Ask how many photos you have sent.

With `[multimodal] max_image_turns = 1`, the age trim is applied on follow-up turns (the `multimodal: age-trimmed old images from conversation history` log line appears) and the phantom descriptions did not reproduce in several follow-up attempts (a small sample).

### Impact

Users get confident descriptions of images that do not exist, and the invented exchanges stay in session history and reinforce later answers. It affects every channel that renders file-path image markers (currently Signal, Telegram, and Discord). Channels whose images reach the model as inline `data:` URIs through the media pipeline have those payloads collapsed in history and are not affected. Re-sending earlier images also re-uploads and re-encodes them on each turn, which the `max_image_turns` doc names as the cost it exists to prevent.

### Logs / stack traces

None captured; the behaviour is in the model's replies. Code references: `trim_images_by_age` and the `max_image_turns > 0` gate in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/multimodal.rs`; the `max_image_turns` field in `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/schema.rs`.

### ZeroClaw version

0.8.5 (`v0.8.5-432-g32f90e9ba`, current `master` plus the #7891 Signal attachment branch)

### Rust version

1.98.0

### Operating system

Linux

### Regression?

Unknown

issues.body: ## Affected component Config metadata and RPC (`zerocode/tui` and web dashboard surfaces) ## Severity S2 - degraded behavior ## Current behavior Selecting a non-English locale translates ZeroCode's shell, pane titles, and Config actions, but the Config group headings, section labels, section help, field labels, and field descriptions remain English. This is not missing catalogue coverage. The shared Config metadata contract currently emits display-ready English: - `SectionGroup::label()` returns English strings. - `humanize_section_key()` derives English labels. - `Section::help()` returns English prose. - `ConfigSectionEntry` carries `label`, `help`, and `group` as display strings. - `ConfigFieldEntry` carries an English `description` without a stable localization key. ZeroCode and the web dashboard render those strings directly. Every non-English locale therefore falls back to English for the core settings taxonomy even when the surrounding UI is translated. ## Expected behavior Config surfaces should receive stable semantic identifiers and localize display copy at the client boundary, with explicit English fallback. Section ordering and config paths must continue using stable keys, not translated labels. At minimum: - Groups localize from a stable group identifier. - Sections localize from the existing section key. - Section help and field descriptions expose stable localization identifiers. - ZeroCode and web resolve those identifiers through their supported localization source. - Search, ordering, RPC routing, and config paths remain locale-independent. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure ZeroCode to use a non-English locale such as `zh-CN`. 2. Restart ZeroCode and open the Config pane. 3. Observe that pane titles and Config action hints are translated. 4. Observe that Config group headings, section labels, help, field labels, and field descriptions remain English. 5. Open the web Config surface with a non-English locale and observe that section labels and help still come from the server as English display strings. ## Impact This affects all non-English users of the ZeroCode and web Config surfaces on every visit. Core provider, runtime, security, and tool settings appear in a mixed-language interface, making initial setup and ongoing configuration harder to understand. ## ZeroClaw version Observed in v0.8.3. The same metadata contract is present on current `master` at filing time. ## Operating system Observed on macOS. The source-level behavior is cross-platform. ## Regression? Unknown ## Architecture impact The shared Config schema is the source of truth, but it should expose semantic identity rather than require clients to translate English wire strings. An additive migration can retain the current English strings as compatibility fallbacks while adding stable group, section-help, and field-description identifiers for clients. Likely ownership points: - `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/sections.rs` - `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/traits.rs` - `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/types.rs` - `apps/zerocode/src/config_manager.rs` - `apps/zerocode/locales/*/zerocode.ftl` - `web/src/pages/Config.tsx` ## Risk and rollback Risk is medium because the metadata crosses config, runtime/gateway RPC, ZeroCode, and web boundaries. Prefer additive fields and client-side fallback to the existing English strings during migration. That preserves compatibility and provides a straightforward rollback path. ## Related work - #8584 covers migrating the web dashboard's own translation source to Fluent; it does not define localized shared Config metadata. - #7117 completed broad Config UX parity and explicitly left translation completeness as separate follow-up work. - #6698 addressed stale or missing Fluent catalogue coverage; this defect occurs before catalogue fallback because the shared metadata has no localization identifiers. ## Acceptance criteria - Shared Config RPC/schema metadata exposes stable localization identifiers instead of requiring clients to translate English display strings. - ZeroCode localizes group headings, section labels, section help, field labels, and field descriptions for supported locales. - Web Config consumes the same stable identifiers through its chosen Fluent/generated localization path. - Missing translations have an explicit English fallback. - Group ordering, filtering, section routing, and config field paths do not depend on translated text. - Tests cover at least one non-English locale end to end for group/section metadata and at least one field/help string. - RPC compatibility and migration behavior are documented or covered by tests. ## Pre-flight checks - [x] Reproduced in the latest release and confirmed in current `master` source. - [x] Searched open and closed issues for the same Config metadata localization defect. - [x] This report contains no secrets or personal data.

issues.body:
### Tracker kind

implementation tracker

### Purpose

This tracker coordinates the implementation of daemon-held OIDC refresh grants for device-bound Zerocode sessions. The design is the ADR-017 amendment merged in #12496 (section "Keep device sessions alive through IdP refresh, held by the daemon"). The holding-crate exception is the `zeroclaw-runtime` ADR-016 row merged in #12609.

Today a device session cannot outlive one access token:

- the gateway's device-grant relay never forwards the IdP's refresh token;
- the dashboard callback wipes any refresh token it receives;
- `Enrollment` has no `grant_type=refresh_token` request;
- Zerocode presents its login-time access token on every reconnect.

So a laptop that sleeps past `exp` resumes to `-32010` and the user has to sign in again, even though the IdP session is still valid.

Parent: #8289 (stage 5 token lifecycle).

### Decisions

These were recorded on 2026-11-24 by @tidux.

- **Every refusal deletes the grant.** This covers any OAuth error answer to a refresh, `invalid_client` and `unauthorized_client` included, not only `invalid_grant`. A client misconfiguration therefore signs device sessions out, and recovery is one interactive sign-in after the fix. This follows ADR-017's "every refusal fails closed".
- **A grant records its client authentication.** Each grant stores the `token_endpoint_auth_method` its refresh token was issued under: `client_secret_basic` for the device grant, `client_secret_post` for the Authorization Code exchange. Refresh and revocation reuse that method. This keeps grants from browser sign-in usable on providers that accept only a client's registered method.
- **Clients.** Zerocode is the reference client. The refresh RPC (slice 5) is specified as a client-agnostic `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` contract that any device-bound RPC client holding a ledger certificate can use. [zerodroid](https://github.com/SyscallBrain/zerodroid), which enrolls through the same gateway-relayed device grant and certificate route, is a design consideration only and not an officially supported client. Where supporting both is impossible, Zerocode wins.

### Scope and non-goals

The slices follow the #12609 row and the ADR's crate split. Each one is a separately reviewable and reversible PR.

| # | Slice | Owner crate(s) | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `Enrollment` refresh and revocation requests. A `grant_type=refresh_token` request that omits `scope` and uses the client authentication enrollment already uses. RFC 7009 revocation where discovery advertises `revocation_endpoint`. Failures are classified as never sent or outcome unknown. | `zeroclaw-runtime` (`enrollment.rs`) | In review: #12716 (includes client-authentication recording) |
| 2a | `refresh_grant.rs` storage side. The in-memory pending grant, keyed by a hash of its paired access token and bounded by that token's lifetime (capped at the device-code lifetime and one hour). Claims are bound to provider and principal. Sealing through `SecretStore` refuses plaintext, so with secrets encryption off no grant is kept. | `zeroclaw-runtime` | In review: #12717 (with slice 3) |
| 2b | Refresh state machine. Version compare-and-set so deletion wins, single-flight refresh, a durable in-flight marker, and the uncertain state with exactly one retry. Rotated tokens are stored durably before release, and every refusal deletes the grant. | `zeroclaw-runtime` (`refresh_grant.rs`, `cert_ledger.rs`) | Next |
| 3 | Certificate-ledger grant table. Claim the pending grant in the same transaction that records the certificate, keep the grant across renewal, and delete it on revocation or unrenewed lapse. | `zeroclaw-runtime` (`cert_ledger.rs`) | In review: #12717 (ledger schema v3) |
| 4 | Gateway hand-off. The device-grant poll and browser callback store the refresh token as a pending grant instead of discarding it. The certificate route claims it. The dashboard keeps no refresh capability. | `zeroclaw-gateway` | Not started |
| 5 | RPC refresh method. A pre-auth method admitted like `cert/renew`, only over mTLS from an active, unrevoked certificate whose `device_id` owns the grant. It verifies the refreshed token through the same `oidc.<alias>` provider and the same issuer + `sub`, and returns only the access token. Sign-out deletes the grant and revokes the token. Grants whose provider is removed or repointed are deleted on a new authorization generation. | `zeroclaw-runtime` (`rpc/`), `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` | Not started |
| 6 | Zerocode client. Read the token from one shared refreshable source. Refresh ahead of `exp`, then re-`initialize`. After sleep, refresh before reconnect, then resume by `tui_id`/`tui_sig`. A mid-session `-32010` gets at most one refresh-and-reinitialize attempt. | `apps/zerocode` | Not started |
| 7 | Per-provider opt-in config, and docs. Rewrite the identity-providers Keycloak guidance for refresh: short access tokens, with SSO session idle and max lengths setting the session; `offline_access` semantics; refresh-token rotation. Also update `authentication.md`. | `zeroclaw-config`, docs | Not started |
| 8 | Live evidence. Run against Keycloak with refresh-token rotation on and off. Cover refresh across expiry and sleep/resume, a disabled user being refused, and sign-out revocation. | n/a | Not started |

Non-goals:

- Any refresh capability for the dashboard, or any client-held refresh token. ADR-017 keeps the dashboard expiring to sign-in.
- Refresh for tokens printed by `zeroclaw oidc login` / `zeroclaw oidc token`.
- Adding `offline_access` or any scope implicitly.
- Keeping dashboard sessions alive through an IdP outage. That is #12096 and #12245.
- Okta/Entra real-tenant refresh evidence. It is an ADR-017 acceptance gate, tracked under #12496. Keycloak is the first target here.

### Linked work

- [x] #12496: ADR-017 amendment (daemon-held refresh, Okta/Entra)
- [x] #12609: ADR-016 `zeroclaw-runtime` exception row for refresh grants. It was approved by @JordanTheJet [on the PR](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12609), but the row's "Approved by" cell on master still reads "Pending Core Team approval". #12708 recorded the approval in that cell, and has merged.
- [x] #12497: per-provider `scopes` / `service_scopes`
- [ ] #8289: parent OIDC tracker (stage 5 token lifecycle)
- Related: #12096, #12245, #12091

### Routing evidence and next decision

- Reason to stay open: this is the sequencing surface for a multi-PR, cross-crate security change.
- Next decision: land slice 1 (runtime request primitives, no behavior change for existing flows), then slices 2–3 (storage and binding) before any refresh token is retained.
- Revisit boundary: per the #12609 row, re-review before a refresh grant reaches the dashboard or another client, can be presented as a bearer, retains more than one refresh token per provider alias and device, or is refreshed by any other flow.

### Close criteria

The ADR-017 refresh acceptance gate is met. Tests cover:

- rotation, single-flight refresh, and durable rotation before release;
- principal mismatch, `invalid_grant`, certificate revocation, provider repointing, and sign-out deletion;
- first binding: two devices signing in as the same person concurrently each end up with only their own grant, and an unclaimed pending grant expires without attaching to any certificate;
- a refresh racing a deletion stores and releases nothing;
- an unknown outcome leads to exactly one retry and no loop;
- the dashboard still holds no refresh capability.

In addition:

- Keycloak live evidence (slice 8) is linked here.
- The docs describe opt-in, session length and revocation truthfully.

### Stale-exemption requested?

No, not at this time.

prs.title: test(providers): hold the runtime proxy guard in the tool-round wire fixture
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` fails intermittently in full `zeroclaw-providers` runs. The cause is shared state, not timing. `responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config` and `codex_responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_after_construction` point the process-wide runtime proxy at a throwaway server for `model_provider.openai`. They serialise on `RuntimeProxyTestGuard`; the tool-round fixture (`wire_body`) did not take that guard. When it overlapped one of them, its OpenAI clients were built through the proxy, and its request went to the proxy fixture instead of its own server.
  - That gives three failure modes, all of which I've seen locally:
    - a decode error, when the proxy answers with its own JSON
    - "Connection refused", once the proxy test has stopped its server
    - the fixture's 5 s timeout, when a stream never sees its final event
  - `wire_body` now holds the guard for its lifetime.
- **Scope boundary:** test-only. No production code changes. I didn't audit other fixtures for the same pattern.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-providers` tests only. The tool-round test now waits for a running proxy test instead of overlapping it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11467 (added the test)

### What this does, simply

Two tests temporarily switch on a global HTTP proxy for the OpenAI provider, and they take a shared lock so nothing else is affected while they do. One newer test didn't take that lock. When it happened to run at the same moment, its requests went through the other test's fake proxy, and it failed for reasons that had nothing to do with what it checks. It now takes the lock too.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The loop below reproduces it deterministically.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `cargo test` on `zeroclaw-providers`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:** the providers test binary run 40 times with only the three tests involved (`native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config codex_responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_after_construction`):

```text
master ee2f5f58f7:  40 of 40 runs failed
  panicked at crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/openai.rs:1951:26:
  called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: error decoding response body
this branch:        0 of 40 runs failed

cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-providers -- --check                          ok
cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --lib  (twice)
  test result: ok. 1979 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings  ok
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Before the fix, the same test had failed in full-suite runs with "Connection refused" (openai.rs:1940) and with its 5 s timeout (openai.rs:1951).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk, test-only: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: feat(matrix): host Goal controls at foreground turn boundaries [Goal V1 proposal 6/12]
prs.body:
## Summary

> Draft proposal slice 06/12; keep this PR Draft and unmerged. It depends on #11882 and the earlier Goal stack. This is a cumulative proposal, not work authored entirely by this slice. The receiving update integrates the published parent, preserves native Matrix ingress and delivery, and adapts the peer-tool test fixture to the fallible constructor.

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Connect Matrix's normal foreground turn/session path to Goal controls and lifecycle, including addressed commands without discarding the remaining message payload.
  - Preserve one task/session authority and usage writer, ordinary spend limits alongside Goal budgets, and ownership of committed-but-unlaunched work through cancellation and failed cleanup. Incomplete accounting is not disguised as a safe resumable pause.
  - Preserve ordinary visible thinking, tool/progress, narration, text and core-error paths, applying the current configured leak policy at display boundaries without rewriting provider input, raw events, private history or receipts.
  - Compose Goal execution with ordinary executed-tool provenance and result-aware recovery: validate complete result slots before filtering, preserve opaque results/receipts/history and later requests, and keep native Goal fatal causes authoritative.
  - Reconcile the updated provider accounting and runtime boundaries: retain known rejected usage without accepting the rejected response, preserve native failure and fallback paths, and verify that a started foreground child settles before returning its timeout.
- **Scope boundary:** This is the first Matrix host, not standalone stack enablement or Web Goal admission. The IPC/WSS host and its required 17 unit/2 integration tests belong to PR #11884 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11884), revocation to PR #11885 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11885), and canonical durable pairing to PR #11886 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11886). No automatic resume, new repetition/stagnation policy, repetition-based message suppression, general runtime extraction, or broader resumability is introduced. The deadline repair is fixture-only. The Matrix host does not add a provider route, a new wire or config field, or another database migration.
- **Blast radius:** Goal admission/lifecycle and spend/accounting; Matrix foreground control/delivery and visible-output guards; ordinary runtime `run` future storage; child/delegate/SOP/tool-pipeline participation and tool recovery; Goal configuration/localization and existing ordinary consumers. Authorization, ordinary limits, raw/private data, native errors and non-Goal tool lifecycle remain protected.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on PR #11882 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11882). Related tracker #10341 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341). Related RFC #8303 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303). No issue is closed by this proposal.

Core review is requested for the bounded residual runtime Goal host/composition, task/session storage, usage and foreground-child settlement/drain, and turn/tool/SOP pairing seams. A recorded reviewed runtime exception or authoritative ownership change is still required **before merge**; this feature PR grants neither. The comparable footprint assessment remains required **before enabled rollout**. Treat this as a high-risk lifecycle/accounting proposal, not a deployment-ready feature.

### What this does, simply

Goal work uses the same Matrix conversation and output path as ordinary work. Controls wait for safe turn boundaries where required. A clarification follows the ordinary output path before Goal Mode announces that it is paused. When work has already started, the runtime keeps responsibility for settling it and cleaning up after a failure or timeout. The later stack slices remain necessary.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)
