prs.title: refactor(providers): share native capability protocols and HTTP transport
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (stacked layer; depends on #12454).
- **What changed and why:** Add shared OpenAI-compatible embedding, transcription, speech, and native Decisions protocol adapters, plus one transport builder that applies resolved headers, credentials, TLS, timeout, and live proxy policy.
- **Scope boundary:** This layer owns provider-side wire protocols and transport reuse. Registry activation, migration, active consumer switching, agent/session selection, CLI, Web, and ZeroCode remain in later stacked layers.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-api` embedding contract and `zeroclaw-providers` capability adapters/transport. Existing legacy embedding construction remains available and lenient; registry construction can opt into strict declared dimensions when a later consumer supplies them.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12454. Supersedes #9809 as part of the stacked replacement series.

### What this does, simply

Provider vendors can share the same wire protocol. This layer keeps those wire implementations in one provider-owned protocol namespace and gives all capability adapters one transport construction path. Error responses are bounded and sanitized, redirects are disabled for capability calls, empty bearer keys are omitted, and cached clients are invalidated when the live proxy policy changes.

## Testing (required)


### Latest master refresh — November 25, 2026

- Merged validated parent #12454 containing master badcc3da4d; tested revision 0ecca1963871993fc7ed348002ea94725d5a8da7.
- [Current-head Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45531018581): all 51 non-Docker checks passed, including CI Required Gate. Docker builds are tracked separately.
- Greptile reviewed this exact head at 5/5 with no new actionable findings; no unresolved review threads at capture.
- Self-review confirmed the layer boundary remains protocol/transport-only, legacy embedding dimensions remain lenient, and the shared bounded/sanitized upstream error helper, client reuse and decision protocol reference remain present.
- Local refresh checks: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check HEAD^1 HEAD`, passed. No local compile/tests. Earlier evidence below retains its original revision.


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; mock HTTP boundary tests cover protocol parsing, bounded errors, legacy embedding construction, resolved dimension validation, and transport-cache reuse.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** GitHub CI runs the workspace tests, lint, feature/platform matrix, security, and source-image checks for the exact head; the current Quality Gate is [44921289445](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44921289445). Full provider execution remains delegated to CI per the stacked workflow.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No paid/live-provider request is claimed; no registry consumer or user-facing surface is activated here. The report-only risk workflow and source-image checks are evaluated by the same current-head CI run; no non-required baseline failure is carried into this head.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — exit 0; `git diff --check` — exit 0.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Rebuilt the layer on top of #12454's current head `8ae63adb4e` and retained only the native protocol/transport commits. The legacy `OpenAiEmbedding::new` path remains dimension-lenient; the resolved `EmbeddingProviderConfig` path validates an explicitly supplied width. Shared error and transport-cache tests remain in the provider/config boundaries.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no CLI, web, TUI, or channel surface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `59df8164e3`; exact-head validation is provided by the GitHub checks on this PR.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Native capability calls now share protocol serialization/parsing and transport policy without activating registry consumers.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests/builds are delegated to GitHub CI because this layer's matrix is expensive locally.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No new caller is activated; existing capability calls use the shared transport.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Shared transport supplies selected credentials and headers, omits empty bearer keys, disables redirects, and propagates client construction errors. Upstream error bodies are capped before sanitization.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Redirects are disabled so credentials cannot follow an unexpected endpoint; proxy/client cache entries are invalidated by the existing live proxy authority.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for the three deliberate transport behaviors listed below. Existing constructors and legacy embedding width behavior remain available in this preparatory layer.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No root-format or CLI change in this layer.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Capability requests use a 60-second embedding deadline, reject redirects, and omit empty bearer headers. Existing legacy embedding construction continues accepting server-reported widths; only resolved construction validates a declared width. Later registry activation owns migration behavior.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert dependent consumer layers first, then revert this protocol/transport layer.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Protocol parsing, timeout, redirect, client construction, or vector-width checks fail at the provider boundary.

Stack integration: this PR is based on #12454 and contains only native protocol/transport changes. Refresh later layers after this PR's head is accepted. Original #9809 is closed and replaced by this stack.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #9809 by @NiuBlibing (replaced collectively by this stacked series).
- Scope materially carried forward: This PR carries the native protocol and transport slice; registry activation and UI slices remain in later PRs.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No.
- If `No`, why: The original PR and this stack have the same author; there is no additional contributor to attribute with a co-author trailer.

prs.title: test(tunnel): make the tailscale forwarder tests independent of process start time
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `start_forwarder_rechecks_the_process_after_the_probe` fails on macOS CI on master. It assumed a `sh` stand-in would start, sleep 50 ms and exit within a fixed 200 ms probe delay. macOS runners can take longer than that just to start the process. The stand-in is still alive when it is checked again, gets published, and `expect_err` panics.
  - The test now controls the order instead of timing it. The stand-in exits only when the probe closes its stdin, so the first poll always sees it alive. The probe reports the forward only after the stand-in has exited, and it waits for that exit **without reaping**: `waitid(P_PID, pid, WEXITED | WNOWAIT)` on unix, `WaitForSingleObject` on a second handle on Windows. So `start_forwarder`'s own `try_wait()` still observes the exit.
  - The other forwarder tests whose stand-ins exit (`…waits_out_a_port_that_is_being_released`, `…reports_a_port_that_stays_held`, `…retries_a_serve_config_conflict`, `…does_not_retry_other_failures`, `…gives_up_after_bounded_conflicts`, `…does_not_take_an_existing_forward_as_its_own`) shared `quick_startup()`'s 300 ms apply deadline. A slow process start turns that into `NotApplied` instead of `Exited`. `quick_startup()` now allows 10 s, which only caps waits that end sooner. The one test of the deadline, `start_forwarder_kills_a_process_that_never_applies`, sets 300 ms explicitly.
  - Removes `exit_with_stderr_after`, whose only caller was the rewritten test.
- **Scope boundary:** Test code only, in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tunnel/tailscale.rs`. `start_forwarder` and every production path are unchanged. No CI workflow or runner change.
- **Blast radius:** The `tunnel::tailscale` unit tests only.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12719

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw publishes a port through Tailscale, it starts a `tailscale serve` process. It treats the port as published only if that process is still running after Tailscale reports the forward. These tests check that logic with a small shell script standing in for `tailscale`.

One test relied on the script finishing within a fifth of a second. That holds on Linux but not on GitHub's macOS machines, where starting a process can take longer, so the test has failed there since macOS CI started running the suite. The test now tells the script exactly when to finish and waits until it has, so it no longer depends on how fast the machine is. Several sibling tests had a similar hidden 0.3 s limit, which now only applies to the test that is actually about that limit.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Slow process start can be recreated on Linux, which shows the before/after directly.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** N/A (unit tests; no user-facing surface)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A `sh` shim that delays every process start by 300 ms:
  ```sh
  mkdir -p /tmp/slowsh && printf '#!/bin/sh\nsleep 0.3\nexec /bin/sh "$@"\n' > /tmp/slowsh/sh && chmod +x /tmp/slowsh/sh
  ```
- **Steps to run:** `PATH=/tmp/slowsh:$PATH cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tunnel::tailscale`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `45 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `start_forwarder_rechecks_the_process_after_the_probe` panics at `tailscale.rs:1606` with `a process that exited during the probe is not published`, the same panic as macOS CI. Other forwarder tests fail intermittently with `NotApplied`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` (Linux build, clippy, tests) runs the module on Linux.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `Platform Test` (macOS/Windows) does **not** run on this PR: its `pull_request` path filter only matches `platform-tests.yml` and `coding_cli.rs`. The macOS and Windows helpers are compile-checked locally in isolation (see below). Their first real run is the scheduled nightly `Platform Test` after merge, unless the workflow is dispatched on this branch beforehand.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Rust 1.98.0, as pinned in CI):
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tunnel::`: `126 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`.
  - With the 300 ms shim, old vs. new test binary, 10 runs each of the target test: **master 10/10 failed** (panic at `tailscale.rs:1606`, identical to CI); **branch 0/10 failed**.
  - With shims adding 300 ms, 1 s and 2 s to every process start, 5 runs each of the whole `tunnel::tailscale` module on this branch: `45 passed; 0 failed` every time. Before the `quick_startup()` change, the 1 s shim failed 5 tests per run.
  - Without the shim the module still takes 0.32 s.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Platform helpers compiled in isolation with clippy `-D warnings`. The full crate can't be cross-checked here because `ring` and `libsqlite3-sys` need a macOS SDK. The unix `waitid` helper was compiled verbatim against `libc = "=0.2.189"` (the locked version) for `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. The Windows helper was compiled verbatim against `windows = "=0.61.3"` (locked) for `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`. It mirrors the existing `OpenProcess`/`WaitForSingleObject` use in `control_plane/authority.rs`.
  - 240 runs under 96 busy-loops plus 24 concurrent copies on a 32-core Linux host: master and branch both 0 failures. CPU load alone doesn't recreate the macOS failure; slow process start does, which is why the shim is the A/B above.

prs.title: feat(config): introduce independent provider registry domain types
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (stacked review; merge after #12448)
- **What changed and why:** Introduce the typed provider registry domain for connections, capabilities, model references, presets, overrides, and fallback validation. Add the model/API resolution primitives that later layers consume.
- **Scope boundary:** This layer owns registry domain types and validation/resolution only. Runtime activation, registry editing RPCs, provider construction, CLI, ZeroCode, and Web consumers remain in later stacked PRs.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-api` capability contracts and `zeroclaw-config` provider-registry types/resolution. No active user-facing consumer is switched in this layer.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12448. Related to #12450. This stacked series supersedes #9809 (closed).

### What this does, simply

A connection describes how to reach a provider, while a model entry describes a concrete model and capability exposed through that connection. This layer gives those concepts typed representations and a single resolver for inherited API options, explicit `null` clearing, model-level wire API selection, capability validation, and provider fallback graph validation. Later layers can build consumers on this canonical boundary without duplicating TOML parsing or provider/model lookup.

## Testing (required)


### Latest master refresh — November 25, 2026

- Merged validated parent #12448 containing master badcc3da4d; tested revision 56dd5cdd0670b97771cf9dd6d5d1e65d9742da6f.
- Added the registry-domain types for master's Antigravity CLI and Grok CLI typed credentials. Antigravity process options share chat preset inheritance, retain bounded deadlines, and reject HTTP-only model settings. Active provider construction/migration remain in their later layers.
- [Current-head Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45527859826): all 51 non-Docker checks passed, including CI Required Gate. Docker builds are tracked separately.
- [Workspace Test output](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45527859826/job/138915550526): 20,917/20,917 passed; hardware 189/189 and golden replay 7/7 passed. All three new secret-lifecycle/process-option regressions passed.
- Greptile reviewed this exact head at 5/5 with no new actionable findings; all review threads resolved at capture. Local validation: `cargo fmt --all` and `git diff --check`, passed. No local build/test run. Earlier evidence below retains its original revision.


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; this is a non-user-facing domain layer and the focused resolver/configuration tests exercise the changed boundary.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** GitHub CI runs the workspace format, lint, test, feature, platform, schema, and compatibility matrix for this head; the current Quality Gate is [44919895321](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44919895321). Full builds and tests remain delegated to CI per the stacked-review workflow.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No runtime/network consumer is activated in this layer. Security and source-image checks are evaluated by the current master workflow and are not changed here.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — exit 0.
  - `git diff --check` — exit 0.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Rebuilt the branch from the current #12448 head and retained only the domain-registry commit plus the ASR timeout/endpoint resolution fixes; the exact tested head is `8ae63adb4ee4ed5a66fbb63d4b2b0876820dce84`. The incremental diff is limited to the provider registry domain and its API/config resolution surface.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no CLI, web, TUI, or channel surface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `8ae63adb4e`; full behavior validation is provided by the GitHub CI checks on this exact head.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Registry construction now has one typed source for connection/model/capability resolution, including ASR timeout inheritance, explicit timeout clearing, complete endpoint overrides, and per-kind wire API validation without requiring a connection defaults table. Resolver regressions also cover fallback duplicate/cycle rejection. Secret masking/restoration failures are returned to export, gateway, and RPC callers instead of being silently discarded.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests and builds are intentionally delegated to GitHub CI because this is a domain-only preparatory layer.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Secret masking and restoration helpers now return and propagate serialization/deserialization errors; credential values and masking behavior are otherwise unchanged.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes; this layer defines the canonical domain and leaves existing loading and consumers unchanged until later stacked layers.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No active surface is switched on by this layer.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert dependent registry-consumer layers first, then revert this layer.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Registry-domain compilation or focused resolution tests fail; later layers cannot resolve canonical model/capability references.

Stack integration: this PR targets upstream `master` and is reviewed incrementally after #12448. Merge the parent first and refresh children. The original #9809 is closed; this is the domain-types layer of the replacement stack.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #9809 by @NiuBlibing (replaced collectively by this stacked series).

prs.title: feat(memory): embed recall queries with a configurable prefix
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Instruction-tuned embedding models (Qwen3-Embedding, E5, BGE) are trained to embed a stored passage as-is and a query with an instruction in front, and rank worse than keyword search without it. Memory embedded both sides the same way, so these models could not be used as trained. The issue has measurements from one deployment's own recall path.
  - New `[memory] embedding_query_prefix`, unset by default. When set it is prepended to the recall query, and only the query, at the SQLite recall site and both Qdrant recall paths (`recall`, `recall_for_agents`), through one helper, `embeddings::query_embedding_text`.
  - Store and re-index paths are untouched, so stored vectors do not change and setting or changing the prefix needs no re-embedding.
  - The SQLite embedding cache keys on the text actually embedded, so a prefixed query gets its own cache entry instead of reusing the vector of identical stored text. With no prefix (or an empty one) the embedded text and the cache sharing are exactly as before.
- **Scope boundary:** no trait change, no provider-native query modes (Gemini `task_type`, Cohere `input_type`), no per-route prefix on `[[embedding_routes]]`, no default change. The keyword (BM25) side of hybrid search is unaffected: the prefix only reaches the embedder.
- **Blast radius:** memory recall on the SQLite and Qdrant backends when the option is set; nothing when it is unset. Lucid recalls through its local SQLite store and inherits the behaviour. The prefix is read when the backend is built; a live `refresh_embedder` swap keeps it, and changing the prefix itself takes effect at the next start.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11892.

### What this does, simply

Some of the best free embedding models want to be told "this is a search question" when they embed a question, and not when they embed the notes being searched. ZeroClaw could not tell them that, so those models found the wrong memories. This adds one setting for that sentence. Nothing changes for anyone who does not set it.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** memory recall (`cli`, `web`, channels alike); no surface-specific behaviour.
- **Setup / preconditions:** an OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint serving an instruction-tuned model, e.g. `llama-server --embedding -np 1` with Qwen3-Embedding, configured as `embedding_provider = "custom:http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1"`.
- **Steps to run:** set `embedding_query_prefix = "Instruct: Given a user message, retrieve memories that help answer it\nQuery:"`, store a few memories, then recall; watch the embedding server's request log.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** stored memories arrive at the server as written; each recall query arrives with the instruction in front.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the query arrives as-is and there is no way to add the instruction.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** At `eccc9bbc33df84798f24aa571f4988a194ab7e77`, [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39399998268/job/118552230449), Lint and CI Required Gate passed. The memory and config crates' tests cover query-only formatting and cache behavior; the workspace check covers factory wiring. The local command results below remain evidence for their recorded earlier revision.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (head `a8b6e8de35`, base `24938afc6d` = current `master`)

```sh

cargo test -p zeroclaw-memory --lib                                           # 559 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib                                           # 1816 passed; 0 failed
```

prs.title: feat(colony): add agent workspace
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add Colony to the Agent panel: a blueprint canvas for reusable Queen-led teams, agent selection, recurring prompts, rooms and explicit channel connections.
  - Connect reviewed goals to real Queen and specialist turns, grouped clarification, one-time tool approvals, pause/resume/cancel and Continue/Fresh.
  - Enforce exclusive membership, separate communication directions, live policy, selected context, durable recovery and existing usage limits.
  - Keep membership and policy in config, lifecycle in the existing task control plane and consumption in the existing cost ledger. A dedicated `zeroclaw-colony` crate owns orchestration.
  - Initialize the root component fixture and regenerate the inherited Calm palettes from the canonical theme registry so the complete stack passes workspace and installer checks.
- **Scope boundary:** One installation and one active goal per colony; assignments settle sequentially. Remote/shared agents, nested colonies and collaborative canvas editing are outside this release. The underlying workspace navigation and SOP rework belong to the parent PR.
- **Blast radius:** Agent admission, delegation, peer messaging, scoped channel dispatch/reload, config publication, control-plane persistence, approval routing, API schemas and the Agent workspace.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #11414.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `agent`, `channel`, `config`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `tests`, `channel:core`, `tool:delegate`, `web`, `stacked`, `zerocode`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `channel:acp`, `do-not-merge`.

### What this does, simply

Agents currently work through separate conversations. Colony lets a user select specialists, give them one goal and review a Queen's questions and settings together. The Queen then uses the saved team for that goal and later goals. A canvas wire grants one direction of communication; the Queen's plan determines the work. Adding a proposed team is one explicit review, rather than a series of approval prompts.

The box is enforced in the backend. Outside agents cannot be contacted through ambient delegation, rooms have independent read/post grants, and external channels require an exact configured conversation plus explicit inbound/outbound grants. Existing tool access and approvals still apply. See the [feature and testing guide](https://github.com/IftekharUddin/zeroclaw/blob/7ea2f43f97066e9d8ad6055e5e5932018d209b44/docs/book/src/architecture/colony.md), [controller](https://github.com/IftekharUddin/zeroclaw/blob/7ea2f43f97066e9d8ad6055e5e5932018d209b44/crates/zeroclaw-colony/src/lib.rs) and [gateway boundary](https://github.com/IftekharUddin/zeroclaw/blob/7ea2f43f97066e9d8ad6055e5e5932018d209b44/crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_colony.rs).

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. This is a draft for feature testing; keep it unmerged while #11414 is open.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`; configured messaging channels when testing external nodes.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Check out this PR; use Node 24 LTS, a testing config with native gateway pairing and at least two configured agents/providers. Real external delivery additionally requires an existing configured channel and allowlisted recipient.
- **Steps to run:**

  ```sh
  cargo web install
  cargo web build
  cargo run -- daemon
  ```

  1. Open the printed dashboard URL and pair. In Agent, switch the left panel to Colony.
  2. Drag a rectangle around independent agents, create a colony and enter a goal. Answer the grouped questions, select prior context/access and review before Start.
  3. Start, inspect specialist progress and approve an exact tool request if prompted. Pause/Resume, Cancel, then reuse the team with Continue and Start fresh.
  4. Draw one communication direction, test that a reply requires its reverse, add a room/channel and inspect independent grants. Edit recurring text during work and choose Now or Next admitted run.
  5. Switch back to Conversations and verify the draft/stream is retained. Disable a member and verify its next turn is blocked. Try deleting/renaming a member or connected channel before removing its Colony reference.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Saved teams run real owned work; permission changes apply live, disabled agents receive no new turn, queued messages respect Pause, and deleting a paused owner or dangling a referenced alias is refused.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same Agent entry has no Colony mode, graph, Queen setup, reusable goal controls or Colony communication API.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Local checks are the primary evidence. The initial feature head also passed GitHub Format, Security, Repository Structure, Docs Style, no-default-features, 32-bit and Web Permission Tests. CI is rerunning on the fixture/theme follow-up; a passing complete matrix is not yet claimed.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Full Docker CI and the cross-platform/all-feature matrix remain for CI. Live provider credentials and real external-channel delivery were not used.
- **Commands run and tail output:** macOS arm64, Rust 1.97.1, Node 24.19.0. Cargo commands used an existing shared target directory.

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  # exit 0

  cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-colony -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api --all-targets --features zeroclaw-gateway/schema-export -- -D warnings
  Finished dev profile in 33.04s

  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib --features schema-export -- --test-threads=4
  test result: ok. 653 passed; 0 failed

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-colony --lib
  test result: ok. 31 passed; 0 failed

  cargo test -p zeroclaw-config colony --lib
  # 4 passed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime colony --lib
  # 7 passed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime policy_change --lib
  # 3 passed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime scoped_exhausted_budget --lib
  # 1 passed
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels colony_channel --lib
  # 1 passed

  cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib --features schema-export colony_alias_http -- --test-threads=2
  test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 650 filtered out

  cargo web gen-api
  # generated API, descriptions and enums
  cd web
  npm run build
  # TypeScript + Vite build passed
  npm test
  npm run test:permissions
  npm run test:contexts
  # passed
  WEB_SMOKE_DIST=1 npm run test:colony
  # compiled renderer smoke passed

  scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  Summary: 0 error(s)

  Collected 14 added links; checked 7 local targets; 0 errors
  ```

  `cargo build --locked --release -p zeroclaw` passed without warnings on feature commit `7ea2f43f97` in 6m 56s (the prior build also passed in 12m 44s). The final CI follow-up changes only the component-test initializer and generated ZeroCode themes; the complete workspace/default/all-targets check passes with both changes.

  ```text
  cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets
  Finished dev profile in 5m 26s; final theme-consumer recheck passed in 5.02s

  # all 21 surfaces passed
  cargo generate sop-syntax --check
  # passed
  ```

  Initial CI compile failures shared one missing `AppState.colony_runtime` field in `tests/component/config_patch_cli.rs`, now fixed and verified by the exact workspace command. Installer Drift found the parent stack's missing generated Calm Dark/Light palettes; the canonical generator restored parity. The scoped PR title check is also corrected.

  Native debug test binaries emitted the macOS linker warning that `__eh_frame` exceeds the 16 MiB compact-unwind encoding limit. Tests executed successfully; this is a debug-test binary size/performance limitation, not a claimed clean master comparison. The optimized build emitted no such warning.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The actual compiled dashboard was exercised in Chrome with synthetic HTTP/model/channel responses. Native Rust tests independently exercise the ordinary Queen/worker runner against a loopback provider, exact one-time AlwaysAsk approval, a real file effect, goal-attributed usage, recovery, concurrent admission, live room revocation, disabled members and config-publication races. No enlarged Tokio stack or live external credentials were used.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Feature commit `7ea2f43f97` plus final CI follow-up `f5001f5da2` (workspace and generator checks), web renderer at 1440×980 and narrow 320/390-pixel layouts. Captures record the dirty base revision plus seven source fingerprints; every renderer fingerprint matches this commit. Evidence is under `docs/book/src/assets/colony/`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Desktop graph](https://github.com/IftekharUddin/zeroclaw/blob/7ea2f43f97066e9d8ad6055e5e5932018d209b44/docs/book/src/assets/colony/desktop-graph.png), [grouped review](https://github.com/IftekharUddin/zeroclaw/blob/7ea2f43f97066e9d8ad6055e5e5932018d209b44/docs/book/src/assets/colony/desktop-review.png), [320-pixel setup](https://github.com/IftekharUddin/zeroclaw/blob/7ea2f43f97066e9d8ad6055e5e5932018d209b44/docs/book/src/assets/colony/mobile-320.png), [reproduction and run metadata](https://github.com/IftekharUddin/zeroclaw/blob/7ea2f43f97066e9d8ad6055e5e5932018d209b44/docs/book/src/assets/colony/README.md).
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Selection opened grouped setup; reviewed batches added specialists and their future-role connections together; one-way wiring stayed one-way; Now/Next prompt choices, room/channel grants, tool approval, pause/resume/cancel and Continue/Fresh were exercised; mode switching retained chat drafts.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `./dev/ci.sh all` was attempted but stopped before tests when Docker could not resolve `docker.io/docker/dockerfile:1.7` due to a registry context deadline. HTTP link probing was excluded by the repository's offline link gate; local target checks passed. No claim of full Docker or cross-platform CI success.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Directed agent/room/channel capabilities and a scoped room tool are new. They default closed; the existing profile filter, sandbox and exact tool approval gate remain authoritative.
- New external network calls? **Yes.** Queen and specialist turns can use existing provider/channel adapters. No new external service is introduced; configured credentials, allowlists, live directional grants and existing network policies apply.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.** Colony accepts paired native operators and rejects provider-identity headers; it reuses existing credential handling.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Captures, models, domains, agents and context are synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Goal, prompt, room and selected-context text reach agents. They are data rather than permission grants; trusted actor identity and live config authorize each operation. Automatic recall/history/persona injection is suppressed for Colony runs.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Model output cannot enlarge access or cross the box. Supervised agent proposals require one explicit batch approval; autonomous proposals use existing team templates and existing bounds. Missing usage/pricing blocks limited goals, cancellation prevents new owned work, and uncertain effects require recovery review.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** for installations without colonies. Joining a colony intentionally changes that agent's communication/context boundaries and may require idle chats to reconnect.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Additive `colonies` config, agent `core_command`, Colony API/schema and Fluent keys; no new environment variable or CLI command.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** Workspace Rust floor remains 1.96.0.
- Exact upgrade steps: Build the dashboard and binary, use native pairing, create a team through setup and review imported context/access. Existing config defaults to no colonies. Selected agents must settle active work before joining. Goal caps cover admitted goal turns; initial setup clarification retains existing agent/profile limits. Direct conversations outside a goal retain noninteractive tool-approval denial.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Cancel owned goals, wait for their turns to settle, remove saved colonies through `DELETE /api/colonies/{id}`, then return to the parent binary/branch. For a source rollback, revert both the CI follow-up and feature commit together. Back up config and the task database first. Reverting code alone does not remove saved team definitions or selected references.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No separate flag; empty `colonies` config leaves agents on the existing paths. The Agent-panel toggle changes the view.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A paused goal with an approval, permission, budget or uncertain-turn blocker; `colony_goal_failed`, `colony_budget_unavailable` or `colony_budget_exhausted`; rejected alias mutations; missing external replies after a revoked outbound grant. Additive history tables can remain; older binaries do not execute Colony continuations.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. This stacks on #11414 and does not supersede another PR.

prs.title: fix(memory): compare SQLite recall time bounds as instants
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - SQLite writes `created_at` with `Local::now().to_rfc3339()`, so each row carries the offset of the host that wrote it, but every `since`/`until` filter compared it with the caller's bound as text. On a host that is not on UTC, a `...Z` window (the format the `memory_recall` tool documents) is shifted by the host offset; on any host, a fractional-second row at a bound compares wrong because `.` sorts before `+`/`Z`.
  - The SQL predicates in recent/time-only recall, the keyword LIKE fallback, `recall_for_principal`, `export` and `export_for_principal` now compare `julianday()` values, falling back to the old text comparison when SQLite cannot parse a value. The FTS/vector stage's local check uses the RFC3339 helper #12026 added for Qdrant.
  - That helper moves from `QdrantMemory` to a crate-level `timestamp_in_range`, so Qdrant, SQLite and `AgentScopedMemory::export` (which had the same string comparison) share it.
- **Scope boundary:** Stored values are not rewritten; timestamps that do not parse keep the lexical comparison. PostgreSQL already casts to `TIMESTAMPTZ` and is unchanged. Qdrant behavior is unchanged (same helper, new location).
- **Blast radius:** Time-bounded `recall`, `recall_for_principal`, `export` and `export_for_principal` on the SQLite backend (the default `memory.backend`), and `AgentScopedMemory::export` over any backend.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12026 (same fix for Qdrant), #10921.

### What this does, simply

`memory_recall` validates `since`/`until` as RFC3339 and checks `since < until` as instants, but the SQLite backend then compared those strings character by character against timestamps written in the host's local offset. With the host on UTC+8, a memory stored at `2026-09-26T12:30:00+08:00` (04:30 UTC) sorts after `2026-09-26T05:00:00Z` and was dropped from a 04:00–05:00 UTC window, while one stored at `2026-09-26T04:30:00+08:00` (20:30 UTC the previous day) was returned. The bounds are now compared as points in time.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; run the two new tests on `master` and on this branch.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Memory backend API (`SqliteMemory`, `AgentScopedMemory`); no surface or channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Rust toolchain; no services or credentials.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-memory --lib rfc3339`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `sqlite::tests::time_bounded_recall_compares_rfc3339_instants` and `agent_scoped::tests::export_compares_rfc3339_bounds_as_instants` pass; all five SQLite paths return `["a", "b", "c"]`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** both fail: `recent path left: ["b", "d", "e"] right: ["a", "b", "c"]` and `left: ["previous_day"] right: ["inside"]`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Lint (fmt/clippy) and the Rust test jobs build and test `zeroclaw-memory`; not yet run on this head, so the local runs below are the evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for this crate; the PostgreSQL backend is untouched.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-memory --lib` -> `569 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib memory_` -> `50 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-memory --all-targets -- -D warnings` -> exit 0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` -> exit 0. Cargo 1.97.1.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The SQLite test writes five rows covering both bounds spelled with other offsets, a 9-digit fraction inside the window, a row that sorts inside but is the previous day in UTC, and one 1 ms past `until`, then checks `recall("*")`, keyword `recall`, `export`, `recall_for_principal` and `export_for_principal`. Only the tests were applied to `master` for the red run. Not verified: the PostgreSQL feature build, and a running daemon.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no user-visible interface change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `4251509de`, memory backend API, the two unit tests above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** see the before/after assertion output above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Time-bounded recall/export over rows with mixed offsets returns the rows inside the window.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace-wide tests: only `zeroclaw-memory` changed; the `zeroclaw-tools` memory tests were run as the caller.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes; unparseable timestamps keep the previous comparison.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert <sha>`.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; this is the V4 → V5 configuration boundary and must land after #12446 and alongside the structural registry layer.
- **What changed and why:** Freeze the released V4 generation and make V5 the current persisted schema.
- Add an isolated V4 → V5 migration step, preserving comments, values, and encrypted fields while retaining versioned backups.
- Re-stamp shipped examples and install artifacts to V5, and add generation/migration regression coverage.
- **Scope boundary:** V3 → V4 remains frozen. This PR does not add the provider registry shape; that structural conversion belongs to #12450. The unrelated master `.dockerignore`/`xtask` source-image issue is tracked by #12571 and is not included here.
- **Blast radius:** Config loading, migration, generation, offline config edits, install examples, and any later registry layer that consumes V5.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12446. Depends on #12571 for source-image CI recovery. Related to #12450 and #9809 (closed; this stacked series is the replacement implementation).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw 0.9.0 released schema V4. That layout must remain reproducible for downgrade and historical generation, while new provider/model configuration work needs a new boundary. This PR makes V5 current and keeps the old V3 → V4 chain unchanged. A V4 file is migrated to V5 by changing only its version stamp in the document-preserving path; comments, quoting, values, and encrypted text remain intact. Structural provider conversion is intentionally deferred to #12450, so this layer is safe to land immediately before that conversion layer rather than becoming a standalone release shape.

Reviewed V4 → V5 document-preserving migration and idempotence, including encrypted values and versioned backups. ## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Google replaced Gemini CLI with Antigravity CLI, and Gemini CLI stopped serving Google AI free, Pro, and Ultra accounts on June 18, 2026. This PR removes the `gemini_cli` coding-CLI tool outright: its implementation, registration, inventory row, attribution, coding-CLI adapter and budget test cases, and orchestrator tool lists.

prs.title: feat(mcp): expose local configuration controls with deferred writes
prs.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in stdio MCP bridge for scoped configuration changes. A directly authorized agent can discover settings and request a write through the existing gateway. The gateway authenticates an OIDC principal and enforces that principal's grants and writable paths. The bridge does not write the configuration file or expose an operator reload tool.

### What this does, simply

An operator can allow a particular agent to change a particular setting, such as one runtime profile's context limit. If runtime work is active, the bridge returns a job ID and waits for an idle observation. Idle is not an admission lock or operator approval. RPC execution now holds an active-turn lease during the actual turn; an idle open session does not count as work.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

Follow the scoped OIDC example in the MCP guide, grant one writable leaf and enable delegate-inheritance denial for the server. Verify an allowed change, rejection outside that path, and that a delegated agent cannot access the withheld server. Exercise a queued write during an active RPC turn.

### How I tested

All 25 Python bridge tests passed on the changed implementation. The branch includes Rust coverage for OIDC activity access and delegated MCP isolation. Consult the checks on the current head for hosted Rust validation.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

The bridge requires an explicit loopback gateway and OIDC provider selection. It reads the service token from an owner-only file and disables HTTP redirects and proxy inheritance. Native pairing tokens are no longer the setup path. The gateway remains responsible for authorization: configure a non-admin principal with only the necessary grants and exact writable paths. A broad profile would still grant broad authority. Use the documented delegate-inheritance denial for this server. Queued mutations are not blindly replayed on uncertain delivery. No live credentials or production data are required for tests.

## Compatibility (required)

This is opt-in. The bridge requires a daemon supporting the authenticated configuration activity probe, an OIDC service credential, and an explicit server and bundle grant. Earlier draft configurations using operator pairing must be replaced. Existing MCP servers retain their prior inheritance policy unless the new option is enabled.

## Rollback

Remove the bundle grant and revoke the service credential. Stop outstanding bridge workers before removing their private job records. Revert any already-applied configuration changes through the normal configuration interface.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A.

prs.body:
## Summary

> **Draft proposal 7/12.** This is an incomplete stack prefix, not a
> request to merge or enable Goal Mode. Tested revision:
> `f1ddcee969a545b35013ce38333a4129a16a4e4e`. Focused local validation
> and independent product and standards checks passed. Exact-head hosted
> CI has not run on this revision yet.

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Carries Goal command and lifecycle types through the canonical
    `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` contract. Native IPC and WSS share the same
    session-bound dispatch and existing `sessions:execute` grant;
    the in-process Web adapter does not admit or advertise Goal commands.
  - Applies live authority and current session identity at the boundaries
    where new Goal operations are admitted. Ordinary disconnect is not a
    lifecycle command; losing an observer after launch does not prevent a
    successful parent result from being saved. Explicit session disposal
    fences the exact Goal, and optional sibling cleanup skips busy and
    Goal-bound sessions.
  - Routes exact `/goal` in ZeroCode. Completion follows daemon discovery.
    Goal controls leave paused ordinary prompts and draft attachments alone.
    Goal output and errors render without settling another prompt.
  - Registers one supervisor per native session and counts only genuinely
    unwinding connection work. Explicit disposal retires an idle supervisor;
    orphan cleanup can release an exact settled terminal worker without
    changing its durable Goal or accounting. Pending operations and
    undelivered failure notices still prevent release. A durably recorded
    unknown provider outcome does not by itself keep a live slot occupied.
- **Scope boundary:** Native Goal RPC and ZeroCode integration over slice 6.
  No Web Goal admission, later policy cutover, later tool pairing changes,
  configuration migration, or enabled rollout.
- **Blast radius:** RPC discovery, authorization, session admission and
  cleanup; foreground Goal/native Agent execution; shared queue and usage
  policy; ZeroCode input, wire and transcript consumers; OpenRPC.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #11883 —
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11883.
  Related #10341 — https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341.
  Related RFC #8303 — https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303.
  No issue is claimed closed.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode users can control budgeted Goals on their native sessions. Goal
work uses the same session lifecycle and accounting as regular work. A
regular prompt submitted while Goal work owns the session keeps its queue
and attachments until its own turn ends. A disconnect does not prevent a
successful Goal response from being saved. A remote client can reconnect
while its owned session is still live; after orphan retirement the saved
transcript can be resumed locally, not over WSS.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — automated native IPC/WSS, composer,
  and final transcript fixtures cover this Draft's local checks. An earlier
  draft was exercised separately; no current-tip live test is claimed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** No current-head
  hosted result is claimed before publication. Required CI covers Linux
  and Windows, parallel runtime and channels, native transports, lint,
  security, and the OpenRPC generator alias. On the preceding head
  `528bef4c`, the [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44382594373)
  was not green. Its two test jobs exposed incomplete setup in the stale
  session-delete fixture; the repair wires the fixture to one canonical
  temporary Goal registry without changing production or assertions.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current hosted checks are pending.
  Native macOS does not prove Linux or Windows behavior. Full local
  ZeroCode and parallel-runtime results below are not green. Actual
  disconnect and worker-count assertions ran on local IPC; WSS coverage
  is the existing shared-behavior suite, not a separate disconnect run.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  | Check | Observed result |
  | --- | --- |
  | `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | exit 0 |
  | `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-goal --all-targets -- -D warnings` | dev profile finished; exit 0 on the current fixture repair |
  | `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto --features schema-export` | `28 passed; 0 failed` |

prs.title: feat(runtime): let the operator override an exceeded cost limit
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `cost.allow_override` was documented but read by nothing, so an exceeded shared limit always failed the turn and the only way on was a daemon restart. With it on, the main tool loop now pauses before a provider call that would exceed the shared daily or monthly limit and asks through the turn's approval channel (`tool_name = cost_limit_override`, exported as `COST_LIMIT_OVERRIDE_APPROVAL`). Deny, no answer within 10 minutes, or a channel that cannot ask stops the turn exactly as before. ZeroCode and Telegram wait the full 10 minutes; ACP waits the shorter of 10 minutes and `acp.session_timeout_secs`, because the ACP channel uses the trait's default timeout; other chat channels keep their own `approval_timeout_secs` (300 s by default), so there the shorter wait applies.
  - Approval calls `CostTracker::grant_override`, which records the override for the current UTC day or month on state shared by every derived tracker, so one answer covers every session and delegation of the daemon. `check_budget` skips that limit (and its warning) while the stored period matches, so it expires on its own at rollover. Per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, and `grant_override` refuses when `allow_override` is off.
  - The grant is kept in memory only. It ends at the next UTC day or month rollover, or when the daemon restarts, and a restart restores enforcement. Nothing is written to `state/cost-overrides.json`; a file left by an earlier build is ignored.
  - A turn waiting on its own prompt also watches for a grant from another session (a `watch` channel on the tracker). When one arrives it drops its request and continues. `RpcApprovalChannel` sends a new `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn` (`request_id`), for any approval that ends without an answer from its client, and ZeroCode takes that prompt down. Before this, approving in one session left the same prompt up in the other, and that turn stopped at the 10-minute timeout although the limit was already lifted.
  - `RpcApprovalChannel` and `AskUserApprovalBridge` now implement `request_approval_attributed_with_timeout`. The trait default wrapped `request_approval_attributed`, whose own 120 s deadline fired first, so the 10-minute wait would have been cut short.
  - ZeroCode renders a `cost_limit_override` approval as a centred, bold red notice with Override and Stop buttons instead of the tool card. Only Override or Stop (key or click) closes it. If the daemon refuses the answer (for example `FORBIDDEN`), the notice comes back with the error so the user can answer again; a timeout shows the error without bringing the notice back, because the daemon may already have the answer.
- **Scope boundary:** no warning at `warn_at_percent` (#10950) and no notice for a turn that stops with no override possible; both need a daemon-to-client budget event this PR does not add. `cost.enforcement.mode` stays unread. Applying `config/set` limit changes to the live tracker is #11587.
- **Holding-crate exception:** the #11589 row in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` covers `src/agent/{approval_bridge,cost}.rs`, `src/agent/turn/{approval_gate,mod,provider_call}.rs`, `src/rpc/approval_channel.rs` and `locales/en/cli.ftl`. It doesn't yet cover the RPC enforcement adapter in `src/rpc/{context,dispatch,local}.rs`, or the attribution-only edits in `src/agent/agent.rs`, `src/daemon/mod.rs` and `src/integrations/registry.rs`. The ancestry, admission and binding rules themselves live in `zeroclaw-config` (`cost::override_grant`). A row amendment that covers these files and states the memory-only grant is drafted on fork branch `docs/runtime-exception-11589` (`e7868ca2a`, on `master` `1c1cd118a`). Like #11697, it needs its own Core Team-approved PR; this PR can't grant it.
- **Blast radius:** turns that hit a shared limit with `allow_override = true` now wait for an answer instead of failing, on any channel that answers approvals (ZeroCode, ACP, Telegram inline buttons). The approval bridge's timeout plumbing is used only by callers that pass a budget; tool approvals are unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11585
- Must merge after #12500: under the current default, `warn` still blocks until #12500 lands.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw can stop the agent when spending passes a daily or monthly limit. There was a setting meant to let you go past the limit, but nothing used it: once the limit tripped, every message failed, and the only way to continue was to raise the limit and restart, which closes every open session.

Now, with that setting on, the agent pauses when it reaches the limit and ZeroCode shows a red box asking whether to keep going. Say yes and the same task carries on, and the limit stays lifted until the day (or month) ends or the daemon restarts. If several sessions were waiting at the limit, one yes lets all of them continue. Say no, or leave it for ten minutes, and the task stops as it does today. Chat apps that cannot ask still stop at an enforced limit on their own, but they benefit from a grant made elsewhere—the lift is daemon-wide for every session, delegation, and unattended scheduled or cron job using that shared tracker. Other shared limits and per-agent or per-hop ceilings still apply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` `tui` (ZeroCode Code tab over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[cost] enabled = true`, `allow_override = true`, `daily_limit_usd` just above today's recorded spend.
- **Steps to run:** in ZeroCode, run a prompt that makes a few model calls until spend passes the limit. When the red notice appears, click Override. Then open a second session and send a prompt. Separately: get two sessions waiting on the notice at once and Override in one; and restart the daemon after an Override and send a prompt.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first turn pauses on the red notice and continues after Override; the second session is not asked again; with two waiting, the other notice closes and its turn continues; after a daemon restart the limit is enforced again and the next turn asks again. With Stop instead, the turn ends with the budget error.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the turn fails with `Budget exceeded: ... Cannot make further API calls until the budget resets.`, there is no prompt, and every later turn fails until a restart.

### How I tested

- **Authority recheck after the peer lookup (head `5d2ca670b747`):** `session/approve` for a cost-override prompt now rechecks the admitted session, the caller's current `SessionApprove` grants and ownership, and the pending request's session binding after the peer-process lookup. It holds the authority lease through delivery, so no await sits between the last check and `resolve_from_operator`. A caller who lost `sessions:update` during the lookup gets `FORBIDDEN`, the prompt stays pending and no override is granted. New tests: `rpc::dispatch::tests::cost_override_approve_rechecks_authority_after_peer_lookup` pauses the lookup, revokes the grant and checks for no approval and no grant. `cost_override_approve_accepts_unchanged_authority_after_peer_lookup` is the control: the approval is acknowledged and the real budget gate grants the override. With only the test commit applied to `ab919d606c`, the revocation test fails (the old handler answers `acknowledged: true`) and the control passes. On this head, through the local cargo wrapper: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` → `5902 passed; 2 failed`, the two being the `relay::local_dial_tests` loopback-stall tests that also fail on the base; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --test '*'` → all 15 integration binaries pass.
```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check   # rustfmt --edition 2024 on the changed files
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib cost::tracker
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib budget_override
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib approval_
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- budget_override_tests rpc::approval_channel
cargo test -p zerocode --bins -- approval parse_approval cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode cost_limit
cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode approval
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust test and clippy jobs for the four crates; Docs Style for `docs/book/src/ops/cost-tracking.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no automated end-to-end test drives a real provider turn into the gate. The gate tests use a scoped tracker with a scripted channel. The live run above covers that path by hand at the current head.
- **Commands run and tail output:** historical focused run on `2830dc912` (superseded by current head `fb2af71c36ed`) (`d01ad8eb1ad9` plus two ZeroCode-only fixes. Greptile 4429329518: a refused cost-limit answer brings the notice back and shows the error. Greptile 4429693704: a restored notice is cleared when its turn ends, so a refusal that also stopped the turn doesn't leave it up), Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, in its own target dir (the log shows zerocode compiled from this tree):
  - `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4` → lib `52 passed`, bin `1566 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored`, including `refused_cost_limit_answer_restores_the_notice_and_shows_the_error` (the daemon answers `FORBIDDEN`; the notice and request id come back, and the error text is shown; a following `TurnComplete` then clears the notice).
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo fmt -p zerocode -- --check` → clean.
  - The runtime, config and api crates are unchanged since `d01ad8eb1ad9`, so the results below still apply to them.
- Previous head `d01ad8eb1ad9` (`d0297b2c4` narrow-pane fix plus a clean merge of `master` `1c1cd118a`), Linux x86_64:
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api --lib` → runtime `5905 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored`, config `1834 passed; 0 failed`, api `322 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zerocode` → lib `52 passed`, bin `1564 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, which also fails on `master` on this host. `cost_limit_notice_keeps_full_scope_timeout_and_buttons_visible` passes at widths 30, 40, 76 and 100.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo fmt --check` → clean.
  - Historical note only: that paragraph described an older head. On 138d775c4c290598399c4ba54f020461b1e4a4c7, CI Required Gate passes. This PR does not change Cargo.lock or deny.toml.
  - The earlier head `5d2ca670b7` had a green CI Required Gate.
- **Greptile round 3 (on the master merge `e7c4aa6b3f68`):** the typing wrapper now resumes typing when another session's grant releases a waiting prompt, and keeps it off for a cancelled turn (`abandoned_approval_resumes_typing_unless_the_turn_was_cancelled`, which fails with the guard disarmed). Clippy `-D warnings` clean on `zeroclaw-channels` and `zeroclaw-runtime`; channels `approval_typing abandoned_approval approval_wait_resumes unsupported_approval_resumes` 5 passed; rustfmt and the comment hygiene gate pass.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Coverage: tracker override (day lifts, rollover expiry, derived trackers share it, per-hop and per-agent ceilings still bind, day does not lift month, refused when not allowed); gate (approve continues and does not ask twice, deny and runtime timeout stop, no prompt without `allow_override` or a channel); RPC channel honours a 600 s budget through `dyn Channel`; ZeroCode notice render and button clicks; a restart restoring enforcement (grants are memory-only), cross-session release, `approval_withdrawn` sent only for unanswered prompts and cleared only for the matching id. I ran the override live in the experiment build; the two follow-up bugs above came from that run.
- **Visual interface evidence:** historical live run on `d01ad8eb1ad9` (not exact-head for `fb2af71c36ed`) (real X11 window captures, daemon and ZeroCode from the same debug build, priced local stub provider). [Manifest](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/MANIFEST.txt):
  - [Cost-limit prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L01-cost-limit-prompt-150x42.png); [Stop ends only that turn, no further provider call](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L02-stop-ends-turn-150x42.png).
  - **Child-client IPC:** the daemon's `shell` tool opens a ZeroCode client (pid 3991336, a descendant of the daemon; see [ancestry](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/child-ancestry.txt)). Ctrl+O there [is refused and the turn stops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L05-child-client-ctrl-o-refused.png). The trace records `RPC cost override refused: independent operator process required` (`cost_override_untrusted_process`, `peer_pid` 3991336).
  - **Cross-session release:** with the child and a second, independent client both waiting, [Ctrl+O in the second client releases both turns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L07-grant-in-second-releases-child-desktop.png). It emits one `Approve` event, and [the main turn continues under the same grant](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L08-main-turn-continues-under-grant-150x42.png).
  - **Narrow pane:** in a pane about 42 columns wide, [Stop and Override stack on separate rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L09-narrow-pane-stacked-buttons-42col.png), and [clicking the stacked Override continues the turn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11589/live-d01ad8eb1/11589-L10-narrow-pane-override-click-continues-42col.png).
  - Earlier macOS screenshots of `ab919d606c`: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11589#issuecomment-6514704152. Earlier build: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11589#issuecomment-6160109618.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Current head `138d775c4c290598399c4ba54f020461b1e4a4c7` (includes this morning's master merge). Historical ZeroCode tests were on `2cd669c27`; historical runtime tests and the live X11 run linked above were on `d01ad8eb1ad9` / `2830dc912` (ZeroCode Chat pane over local RPC, `zeroclaw daemon`)—those captures remain labelled historical, not exact-head proof of this SHA. Older local runs on `225c52bb636f` (master `f12da7462a0f`, remote macOS arm64 builder). Earlier live run: experiment build https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261013T015950Z-b89c9e407c42.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the captures, trace lines (`trace-child-refusal.jsonl`, `trace-grant.jsonl`), stub request log and config excerpt are all in the manifest folder linked above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full crate suites not run locally; CI runs them.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (grants are memory-only; no new file is written)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The override is off by default and only an operator answer grants it; a runtime timeout or unreachable client does not.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. With `allow_override = false` (the default) behaviour is unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: one new key, `channels.telegram.<alias>.cost_override_operators` (numeric Telegram user IDs allowed to override in group chats; defaults to empty, which denies group overrides; no wildcards or usernames). Also one new RPC `session/update` type, `approval_withdrawn`, which older clients ignore; `allow_override` now does what its docs say, and the docs are corrected.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After squash merge, `git revert <squash-commit>`. Before merge, do not revert master merges. Current head is `138d775c4c290598399c4ba54f020461b1e4a4c7`.
