prs.title: feat(gateway): serve config writes, Quickstart and reload via the core
prs.body:
> Stacked on #11351, with #11390, #11388, #11368 and #11391 integrated. Review only this PR's own commits; prerequisite commits are carried because the parent branches are hosted on a fork.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - The separate gateway currently refuses settings writes, Quickstart and daemon reload. Serve those routes through the core, preserving the existing HTTP response types, validation, drift protection and write-only secret responses.
  - Share the existing JSON Patch staging between HTTP and RPC. Extend `config/set-many` with optional operations, drift guarding, operation results and warnings; keep the existing string-based `sets`, `config/set` and `config/delete` behavior.
  - Resolve every operation's path authority before staging and again after preparation. Comparisons also need Config read. Hold the authority lease through synchronous transaction enqueue; the retained job owns the config writer and agent reservations through publication. Skill-bundle directory creation uses the same admission boundary.
  - Pass remote HTTP origin context in the reload request. The core checks its live remote-admin policy, actual pairing guard and current grants through reload enqueue, avoiding a policy snapshot between two RPC calls.
  - Construct the large config-write futures directly in their boxes. The default-stack real-RPC oracles now exercise provider alias refusals without overflowing the dispatcher frame. Unary property errors omit the batch operation index while batch errors retain it.
- **Scope boundary:** The in-process gateway keeps its publication/reload-banner path and calls the shared patch stager. `DELETE /api/config/map-key` remains unavailable pending the owned-state/live-ACP cascade in #11172. Config read routes and frontend presentation are outside this change.
- **Blast radius:** RPC config mutation, live-session preparation/publication, the separate gateway's config and Quickstart adapters, and reload admission. Every new RPC field is optional. Narrow principals can encounter the stricter checks listed below.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #11002. Depends on #11351, #11390, #11388, #11368 and #11391.
- **Labels:** None set by this PR submission.

### Served routes

| HTTP route | Core method |
|---|---|
| `PATCH /api/config` | `config/set-many` with operations and drift guarding unless overridden |
| `PUT` / `DELETE /api/config/prop` | `config/set-many` with one replace/remove operation |
| `POST /api/config/map-key` | `config/map-key-create`, including skill-directory scaffolding |
| `POST /api/config/rename-map-key` | `config/map-key-rename` |
| Five `/api/quickstart/*` routes | `quickstart/state`, `fields`, `validate`, `apply`, `dismiss`; dismiss answers 204 |
| `POST /admin/reload` | `config/reload` with origin context derived by the HTTP edge |

### Contract additions

- `config/set-many` params: `sets` defaults to empty; optional `ops` contains `{op, path, value?, comment?}`. Absent operations retain the existing sets behavior; present-empty operations are a no-op patch that returns warnings. Nonempty sets together with operations are refused. Optional `drift_guard` defaults to false and is refused without operations.
- Operation semantics follow the existing HTTP add/replace/remove/test/comment behavior. A failed batch names its first `op_index` and commits nothing. Every operation obeys config write-path selectors; a comparison additionally requires Config read. Writes require the create/update/delete verb implied by their effect under the method's existing Config update grant.
- `config/set-many` results add optional `results` and `warnings`, defaulting to empty. Each result has `op`, dotted `path`, and optional `value`, `populated`, `comment`. Plaintext remove preserves explicit `value: null`; secret operations expose populated only. Warnings contain `code`, `message`, `path`.
- `config/map-key-create` under `skill_bundles` scaffolds the canonical resolved directory before persistence, matching the existing HTTP effect. A scaffold failure remains a logged best-effort outcome.
- `config/reload` adds optional `remote_admin`, default false. Null/absent params preserve older local callers. The edge creates the origin fact from `ConnectInfo`; the core resolves existing policy from live Config and the active pairing guard. No config key or cached policy is added.
- `initialize.features` advertises `config.patch_ops`, `config.skill_bundle_dir`, and `config.remote_admin_reload`.

The OpenRPC document is regenerated from the protocol types and method table.

### Compatibility limits and permission differences

- A principal with Delete but no Update can clear a property in-process but cannot use the core's existing Update-gated set-many method. Comparisons now also need Read, and test/comment paths obey selectors; the older in-process patch path has a separate authorization gap to address.
- Quickstart apply uses the core contract's `quickstart:execute`; the in-process route uses whole-config Create and Update. Quickstart telemetry remains `tui` until #11176 supplies the surface parameter.
- The separate gateway authenticates loopback reload callers, so missing credentials yield 401 where the in-process local route admits them. Remote reload remains closed without live opt-in and active pairing.
- Generic authentication/grant refusals use the gateway's `{error, code}` body rather than the in-process `{error}` body. Save failures retain their 500 status but may have a generic core-backed error body.

### Integration notes

- The refusal-mapping merge preserves structured reasons in refreshed session/config mutation paths. Its updated tests seed the identity key their in-process connection requires; this does not change production key provisioning.
- URL masking's unresolved-placeholder case uses the canonical `ConfigApiError::for_prop` mapping so both mutation surfaces refuse it consistently.
- The version/limits merges preserve both router shutdown/timeout arguments and core version-skew arguments. The refreshed session-list test follows the parent's current interface.
- The latest approved preview fixes and the landed macOS test-import fix are integrated by merge. Prerequisite branches are preserved.

### What this does, simply

The settings editor, first-run setup and reload button can use the gateway running in its own process. It asks the core to validate and save settings, preserves secrets, refuses conflicting on-disk edits, and creates the directory for a new skill bundle. A save already admitted by the core finishes safely if the browser disconnects. Deleting an entire alias still waits for the complete owned-state cascade.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the complete two-process dashboard workflow.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web` through the separate gateway; HTTP/RPC automated oracles.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build the daemon and `zeroclaw-gw` from this branch, use a built dashboard and paired token, and point the gateway at the daemon socket.
- **Steps to run:** Change and clear a setting; add/rename an alias; create a skill bundle; edit the same setting in `config.toml` outside the dashboard and save; run Quickstart; request daemon reload.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Supported writes and setup work through the core; drift yields 409 until explicitly overridden; the skill directory exists; reload obeys live remote-admin policy.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Master has no complete separate-gateway flow. On prerequisite preview #11351, the same requests return `capability_missing`; the built-in gateway supplies the existing behavior oracle.

### How I tested

All local Cargo checks used `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0`, one command at a time, with at least 80 GiB free before each build. The final Rust implementation is `b0c1f5ea29`; `69db01bc08` adds only its regenerated OpenRPC output.

- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- config_ops:: config_patch config_set_many initialize config_map_key config_set_ config_delete config_reload tui_list
  test result: ok. 107 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw-gateway --features gw-bin --lib --test gw_preview
  lib: 734 passed; 0 failed
  gw_preview: 6 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto
  34 passed; 0 failed
cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- openrpc
cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- openrpc --check
  wrote the tracked document; check exit 0
cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw --features zeroclaw-gateway/gw-bin --all-targets
  Finished dev profile; exit 0
cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto --features zeroclaw-gateway/gw-bin --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets
  both exit 0; no production warnings
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-deps
  exit 0
cargo fmt --all -- --check
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  both exit 0; Comment hygiene gate passed
```

The unchanged `tests/architecture/cli_fluent_coverage.rs` was compiled in an isolated test-only harness with only its scan root replaced: 9 passed, 0 failed. Its detector and mutant fixtures ran as well. The all-targets check includes the root crate's integration-test callers.

The real in-process RPC oracles compare status, content type, JSON/body, live values and normalized parsed TOML. Array order remains significant and comment assertions are explicit. They cover valid/refused writes, drift override, secret projection, directory creation, generic versus cascade alias misses, Quickstart and reload. Authority tests cover write/read revocation after waits and cancellation after admission. The standalone process suite verifies restart/reconnect, version refusal, TLS and production limits.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Fresh required CI will cover the final pushed head; pending CI is not counted as passing evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local execution covers macOS. Windows named-pipe execution and independent review are outside this local run.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source/caller review, canonical policy ownership, and exact failure causes with a default-stack RPC regression. No manual browser workflow is claimed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; API/RPC transport and authorization changes, with no presentation change. Response bodies, content types, statuses, live config and saved TOML values are compared by automated oracles; comment assertions remain explicit.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 69db01bc086f2d7ae0b7a66174b4b20320996e21 (same Rust tree as the validated implementation); commands and output above cover the same final implementation.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Automated HTTP response assertions and the standalone-process suite; no screenshot claim.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Successful edits produce equal state on both paths; refused batches save nothing; queued revocation refuses the write/read; caller cancellation preserves publication; stale remote-admin opt-in cannot admit reload.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** A full workspace runtime run was not repeated; focused config/authority tests, full gateway/protocol suites and all-targets caller checks cover this change. Any inherited required CI regression remains a failure requiring its owner's fix.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: existing authenticated HTTP capabilities are now reachable through the separate gateway, and the core performs the existing skill-directory effect. Existing Config verbs/selectors apply; no broader directory selection is introduced.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes: the added RPC operation results preserve write-only populated projection, and comparisons refuse secrets. Masked/empty secret writes remain refused. Existing credential forwarding is retained.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; synthetic credentials and temporary directories only.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Fresh authority leases bind admission; retained ownership protects publication; type/scoped validation, drift guard, version refusal and production limits stay in force. Permission-model differences are explicit above and require review.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for existing RPC callers; optional parameters/results retain legacy behavior. Narrow-principal behavior on newly served routes is qualified above.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No new keys or flags.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A. Use matching daemon/gateway builds as required by the preview.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's squash commit through a follow-up PR once landed. While stacked, revert its own commits in reverse order and preserve prerequisite merges.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added. Existing drift override and remote-admin opt-in retain their meanings.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A core-backed config response differs from the built-in route, a refused batch changes saved state, an admitted save fails to publish after caller cancellation, or remote reload is accepted after policy opt-out.

prs.title: feat(android): add native tools and standalone app
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add five typed, Android-only tools for screenshots, accessibility-tree reads, UI actions,
    app launch, and read-only device facts. The implementation is compiled only for Android and
    remains disabled until `[android].enabled = true`.
  - Add `apps/android/`, a standalone arm64 zerodroid APK that bundles ZeroClaw, the dashboard,
    an app-private Unix-socket bridge, AccessibilityService, native Android APIs, a generic Android
    skill, and the CellClaw-derived floating overlay.
  - Preserve the runtime security boundary: device actions stay approval-visible, generated app
    profiles separate read-only inspection from autonomous control, gateway pairing remains on,
    and fresh installs leave phone tools, LAN, SSH, boot start, and the overlay off.
  - Include the gateway/session and Android key-publication fixes required for long mobile turns,
    then add full/lite CI, fail-closed packaging, signing/provenance checks, provider-default
    validation, release notes, and an on-device verification checklist.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not add a ZeroRelay/OIDC remote-device node, publish APKs or a Play
  listing, add a notification-listener channel, or bundle user-specific app automations. Those
  remain follow-up work. The app retains the `zerodroid` package identity and independent v0.3
  signing lineage for upgrade compatibility.
- **Blast radius:** High but default-closed. The config schema gains an additive `[android]`
  section; production Linux, macOS, and Windows binaries do not compile the Android tool family.
  Gateway webhook timeout/session behavior changes on every platform. Android builds add a new
  permission, signing, and packaging surface. This is intentionally an XL draft: the Rust client,
  Kotlin server, wire contract, app policy, and package gate form one vertical slice, and merging
  only one half would leave a nonfunctional distribution.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related zeroclaw-labs/zerodroid#1 tracks the later network-capability-node /
  ZeroRelay direction; this PR does not close it.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `ci`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `agent`, `config`, `gateway`, `runtime`,
  `tool`, `security:secrets`, `tool:browser`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web` for the bundled dashboard. The model-facing operations
  use the existing Tool attribution surface. The Android app and overlay are a package/UI boundary
  that does not yet have a `surface` enum value.
- **Setup / preconditions:** An arm64 Android 11+ device; Android SDK 36/build-tools 36.1.0; NDK
  28.2.13676358; JDK 17; Node from `.nvmrc`; Rust 1.96.1; `cargo-ndk`. A provider credential is
  needed only for a live agent turn.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Run `cargo web build`.
  2. Run
     `ANDROID_NDK_HOME="$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/28.2.13676358" cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a build --release --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw`.
  3. Run `apps/android/scripts/stage-jnilibs.sh`.
  4. From `apps/android`, run the full/lite debug unit, lint, and assemble tasks documented in
     `apps/android/README.md`.
  5. Install one APK, open zerodroid, select/configure a provider, enable Phone tools, and grant
     Accessibility manually. Leave Autonomous control off for inspection-only testing.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Both APK flavors contain the exact arm64 ZeroClaw binary,
  dashboard, and only the generic Android skill. The app starts the on-device gateway; the tool
  registry exposes `android_screenshot`, `android_ui_read`, `android_action`, `android_launch`,
  `android_device`, and the guarded generic `screenshot`. The bubble reflects live state and its X
  collapses the panel without stopping the circle/service.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** There is no `apps/android` project, no Android tool
  family/config, and no in-APK accessibility/native bridge to build or run.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** At exact head
  b8075e8d2bdc407c05b174fbb1cb67ec4147bb4d, all 33 applicable hosted checks passed and four
  correctly skipped. The dedicated `Android app` workflow rebuilt the dashboard and arm64 binary,
  staged every required payload, validated provider defaults and the Gradle wrapper, and ran the
  full/lite unit, lint, and debug-assemble matrix. The required repository gate covered formatting,
  Clippy, warnings-denied rustdoc, tests, security, architecture, and cross-platform builds.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No API 30 physical/emulator instrumentation run. The physical
  smoke used Android 16/full. Only the configured Gemini provider received a live agent turn;
  provider defaults were validated credential-free for 19 hosted providers and four local
  providers. An exact-head screenshot-to-model call against Settings was intentionally not run
  because that would transmit potentially sensitive screen content without separate approval.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0

  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  Finished `dev` profile ... in 1m 58s

  cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools \
    -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib
  zeroclaw-config: 1387 passed
  zeroclaw-tools: 1679 passed
  zeroclaw-runtime: 3822 passed; 3 ignored
  exit 0

  ANDROID_NDK_HOME="$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/28.2.13676358" \
    cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a build --release --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw
  Finished `release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 9m 13s

  ./gradlew --no-daemon \
    :app:testLiteDebugUnitTest :app:testFullDebugUnitTest \
    :app:testLiteReleaseUnitTest :app:testFullReleaseUnitTest \
    :app:lintLiteDebug :app:lintFullDebug \
    :app:lintLiteRelease :app:lintFullRelease \
    :app:assembleLiteDebug :app:assembleFullDebug --console=plain
  BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 44s
  167 actionable tasks: 89 executed, 78 up-to-date

  apps/android/scripts/check-model-defaults.py
  Validated 19 hosted defaults; skipped 4 local providers.

  python3 -m unittest discover -s apps/android/scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'
  Ran 3 tests ... OK
  ```

  The cross-build warnings were three Android-target dead-code warnings in unmodified
  `browser_open.rs`; host `--all-targets` Clippy is clean. Gradle also reports deprecations in the
  imported Security Crypto, Google Sign-In, and legacy `SmsManager` paths; lint passes, and those
  migrations remain follow-up work before promoting the app beyond experimental.

  Additional passing gates: `actionlint`, `shellcheck`, `bash -n`, `xmllint`, staged `gitleaks`,
  `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`, `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh`, app Markdown lint, Gradle
  wrapper checksum/distribution startup, APK signature/hash/zipalign checks, and 16 KiB ELF
  alignment checks for all six arm64 native libraries in both flavors. A negative-control
  `assembleLiteDebug` without staged payload failed at `verifyBundledPayload`, naming the missing
  binary, dashboard, and skill.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A v0.3 release-signed full APK from final commit
  b4e2081b5317225b14d5f5c0e41be6a9685f00cf installed over the existing app. The app process,
  bundled `libzeroclaw.so`, private `/data/user/0/.../ui.sock`, AccessibilityService, bridge
  service, and overlay service all ran. On the tree-identical pre-squash head, an authenticated
  `GET /api/tools?agent=phone` returned the five `android_*` tools plus guarded `screenshot`; a
  bubble prompt produced sanitized trace entries for `android_launch` and `android_ui_read`, opened
  Settings, and returned `com.android.settings`. The final squashed APK was then rebuilt with its
  exact commit stamp, installed, and rechecked for process/socket/service startup. The bubble was
  green while idle, used the CellClaw panel/accent palette, and X collapsed only the panel.
  Removing the temporary adb forward did not stop the on-device agent. I did not send messages,
  submit forms, purchase, call, or act on another account.
- **Visual interface changed?** Yes
- **Tested revision, interface, and terminal or viewport dimensions:**
  b8075e8d2bdc407c05b174fbb1cb67ec4147bb4d for hosted full/lite builds;
  b4e2081b5317225b14d5f5c0e41be6a9685f00cf for the zerodroid app and floating-overlay physical
  smoke; 1272x2772 display.
- **Screenshot evidence:** Local screenshots were inspected for the idle circle, expanded/result
  panel, and X-collapse transition. They are not attached because the device
  surroundings contain private UI data and publication was not separately approved. Keep this PR
  in draft until a maintainer-approved privacy-safe capture is attached.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Start launched the bundled process; enabling the
  overlay produced a green idle circle; submitting the harmless Settings/read prompt opened
  Settings and rendered `com.android.settings`; pressing X removed the panel while the circle and
  OverlayService remained.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** API 30 instrumentation was unavailable. The
  exact-head screenshot-to-model call was skipped for screen-content privacy. Public release/tag,
  Play publishing, and signed artifact upload were intentionally not run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** The APK can request
  Accessibility, overlay, location/BLE/Wi-Fi scans, telephony/SMS/contacts, foreground service,
  boot, and battery-exemption access. Capabilities default off, Android grants remain manual, and
  unused prospective permissions were removed.
- New external network calls? **Yes.** The app runs the existing provider/gateway paths and exposes
  opt-in paired LAN access; native bridge traffic stays token-authenticated on loopback, while UI
  control uses an app-private Unix socket. No telemetry call was added.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Android key publication uses atomic
  `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` because SELinux forbids hard links. Provider prefs are
  Keystore-backed where available; gateway path, webhook secret, bridge token, and pairing token
  remain separate. Release signing stays local and is absent from GitHub Actions.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **Yes.**
  `apps/android/NOTICE` preserves required public upstream authorship/copyright attribution. No
  device data, account content, credentials, private screenshots, or user-specific automation is
  committed; the staged secret scan is clean.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Accessibility trees
  and screenshots can carry hostile third-party app text into model context. Read output is capped;
  consequential calls support `expect_package`; mutating actions remain autonomy/approval gated;
  the tool docs explicitly classify screen content as untrusted.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The principal new risk is agent access to the
  owner's authenticated phone UI. The family is additive, Android-only, disabled by default, UID-
  isolated, bounded, and separately gated for read-only inspection versus autonomous action. LAN,
  SSH, boot start, sensitive permissions, and overlay each require explicit opt-in.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.** Existing configs deserialize with Android disabled, and desktop
  production builds do not compile or register the Android implementation.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Adds `[android]` config and Android release-signing
  environment variables; no existing CLI command is removed or renamed.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** CI uses the repository's Rust 1.96.1 and Node 24 pins.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Existing ZeroClaw
  users need no action. Android users opt in with `[android] enabled = true` or the app's Phone tools
  switch. Old debug-signed v0.2 zerodroid installs must be uninstalled before the v0.3 signing
  lineage; that clean reinstall deletes app-private config and requires re-granting Android access.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR (feature commit
  b4e2081b5317225b14d5f5c0e41be6a9685f00cf plus its two CI follow-ups). On a device, switch Phone
  tools and Autonomous control off, revoke Accessibility/overlay grants, stop the app, or uninstall
  `org.zerodroid.bridge`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[android].enabled = false` is the default. The app has
  separate Phone tools, Autonomous control, LAN, SSH, boot, and overlay switches.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `android: skipped registration`, `android_action: skipped
  registration`, `service_unavailable`, `screenshot_failed`, `gateway error`, missing `ui.sock`,
  absent `libzeroclaw.so`, failed `verifyBundledPayload`, or a foreground-service notification that
  repeatedly enters restarting/failed state.

prs.title: feat(gateway): add OpenAI chat completions endpoint
prs.body:
Closes #8550
Related #8603
Related #6850

## Motivation

ZeroClaw's gateway exposes a WebSocket chat interface, but many LLM client libraries, IDE extensions, and orchestrators (LangChain, OpenAI SDK, Continue.dev, Aider) speak the OpenAI Chat Completions protocol natively. Without an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint, these tools cannot talk to ZeroClaw without custom adapters.

This PR adds `POST /v1/chat/completions` — an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that enables direct integration with any OpenAI SDK or tool by pointing the base_url at ZeroClaw, routes to agents through the `model` field (`zeroclaw/<alias>`), and is off by default (`gateway.chat_completions_enabled = false`).

---

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **Current head:** `84d276a9`
- **Commits:** 4 — (1) the endpoint + shared runner + all prior-round fixes, squashed; (2) honest-request-semantics and fail-closed-ownership changes; (3) cross-transport guard, claim atomicity, queue slot, and wire-contract hardening; (4) Unicode case-folding in session-key guard normalization. Author/committer use a GitHub noreply identity per the privacy merge gate.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `config`, `agent`, `docs`, `tests`, `tool:delegate`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`
- **What changed and why:**

  **New endpoint & shared runner:**
  - Add `POST /v1/chat/completions` with streaming (SSE) and blocking (JSON) modes. `model` routes to agents (`zeroclaw/<alias>`); `x-session-key` provides session continuity; `tools` and `tool_choice` restrict available tools per request.
  - Extract `turn_runner.rs` — a transport-neutral turn lifecycle spine shared by WS and HTTP paths. Cooperative timeout via `TurnStatus::TimedOut`; callers pass a transport-specific forward closure.
  - Blocking responses return `finish_reason: "stop"` with final text. SSE suppresses thinking/tool events and emits error envelopes on failure/cancel. OpenAPI schemas auto-derived from Rust types.

  **Session ownership (cross-transport, fail-closed):**
  - `SessionBackend::claim_session_agent_alias` provides atomic compare-and-set ownership claims before every history load across HTTP, WebSocket, and RPC. Built-in JSONL backend serializes claims across independent processes via per-session advisory file locks; SQLite backend verifies the UPSERT affected-row count. Default trait returns `Err(Unsupported)` so third-party backends must explicitly opt in. WebSocket rejects `Unsupported` claims unconditionally (connection-scoped transport requires deterministic ownership); HTTP and RPC accept empty sessions as graceful degradation.
  - `migrate session-ownership` CLI command uses the same atomic claim. `Conflict` is skipped (never overwritten); `Unsupported` backends fall back to best-effort. Supports `--list`, `--claim`, and interactive bulk mode across JSONL and SQLite.
  - WebSocket cross-transport guard: HTTP requests targeting an active WS session return 409; DELETE similarly refuses while a WS holds the lease. Guard keys are normalized (`guard_key`) across all in-memory boundaries to prevent case-collision bypasses on case-insensitive filesystems (zero storage migration).

  **DELETE linearization:**
  - DELETE handler acquires the session queue before checking the WS lease or canceling the turn token, serialising with concurrent WebSocket admission through a single linearized boundary. Session queue admission atomically registers pending counts under the slots-map lock, preventing idle eviction from creating duplicate permits for the same session.

  **Tool contract & request scoping:**
  - Client `tools` list is a name whitelist only; descriptions and parameters resolve to server-authoritative `Tool::spec()`. Request tool scope propagates into background and parallel delegate spawns.

  **Wire contract & message semantics:**
  - Consolidation uses the routed agent's own provider/model/temperature, bounded by semaphore. `x-request-id` and `x-session-key` on all handler-processed responses. Rate-limit headers report real sliding-window state. SSE error wire format documented with `event: error` name and timeout/internal_error types. Request message roles restricted to the 6 documented values (`system|developer|user|assistant|tool|function`); `tool_calls`, `name`, and `tool_call_id` in request messages return 400 as unsupported under transparent execution.

  **Config & docs:**
  - Two new `[gateway]` keys: `chat_completions_enabled` (default `false`), `chat_rate_limit_per_minute` (default `60`, `0` disables rate limiting).

  **This round (honest request semantics + ownership hardening) — on top of the above:**
  - **Model routing (RFC #8603 boundary):** `model` accepts only `zeroclaw/<alias>` (and `zeroclaw` / `zeroclaw/default` / empty for the default agent). Any other label (e.g. `gpt-4`) is now rejected with 400 rather than silently routed to the default agent and echoed back.
  - **Generation settings config-owned:** `temperature` is rejected per-request; omission preserves the routed agent's configured value. Behavior-changing controls (`parallel_tool_calls`, `service_tier`, `reasoning_effort`, `functions`, `function_call`, `modalities`, `audio`, `prediction`, `web_search_options`) are modeled and rejected with 400 instead of being silently dropped. Benign annotation fields (`metadata`, `store`) stay tolerated.
  - **Ownership fail-closed on inconsistent backends:** all three transports reject non-empty sessions when the atomic claim is `Unsupported` **regardless of what the legacy ownership getter returns** — closing a path where a backend that reported an owner but could not claim atomically could expose a transcript to another agent.
  - **HTTP session-key narrowing:** the HTTP entry restricts client-supplied `x-session-key` to ASCII `[a-z0-9_-]`, keeping the storage id injective on every filesystem. Uppercase and non-ASCII letters are rejected with 400. WebSocket and RPC keep the broader `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` check for their pre-existing sessions (see Known gaps).
  - **Test wiring:** the chat-completions router is built through one shared constructor used by both production and tests, with a disabled-route (404) regression; stale review-history comments rewritten as invariants.

  **Unicode session-key guard normalization (this round — on top of the above):**
  - **guard_key Unicode folding:** `guard_key()` now uses `str::to_lowercase()` (full Unicode case folding) instead of `to_ascii_lowercase()`, so that Cyrillic and Greek case variants that collide on case-insensitive filesystems (macOS APFS/HFS+, Windows NTFS) share the same guard identity — queue slot, WS lease, cancel token. Characters without a lowercase mapping (CJK ideographs, digits) are unchanged.
  - **Centralized normalization:** `SessionActorQueue` no longer duplicates normalization; all guard boundaries (WS connection guard, HTTP cross-transport 409, DELETE lease check, cancel-token lifecycle, session-queue acquire and queue_depth) call the single canonical `guard_key()`.
  - **Regression tests:** `guard_key_folds_unicode_case` verifies Cyrillic (`gw_Алиса` ≡ `gw_алиса`) and Greek (`gw_Αλφα` ≡ `gw_αλφα`) case-variant collision; `guard_key_idempotent` extended to Unicode.
  - Storage identifiers (filenames, SQLite TEXT columns) are unchanged — no migration required for existing sessions.

- **Scope boundary:** Cross-transport session access is guarded by normalized guard keys (now Unicode-aware), per-session queue serialization, and atomic ownership claims — HTTP and WS can safely access the same session with proper serialization. Does not add `/v1/models`, `/v1/embeddings`, multi-modal content, or end-to-end `tool_choice` enforcement at the provider boundary. No changes to Webhook / A2A / ACP paths.

---

## Testing

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — enable the endpoint and verify with the curl smoke command below.
- **A/B setup / preconditions:** enable `gateway.chat_completions_enabled = true`; configure at least one agent (`[agents.default]`) with a provider model. For cross-agent ownership tests, configure a second agent (e.g. `[agents.coding]`) and drive both a `zeroclaw/default` and a `zeroclaw/coding` request against the same `x-session-key` to observe the ownership rejection.
- **Steps to run:** `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:42617/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"zeroclaw/default","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'`
- **Expected:** `200` with `finish_reason: "stop"`, `content` non-null, `tool_calls: null`, `x-session-key` in response headers.

### How I tested

```
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
All clean

$ cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
0 warnings

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway
test result: ok. 511 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored   (lib)
test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored      (integration)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test result: ok. 3420 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra --lib
test result: ok. 124 passed; 0 failed

$ cargo test --test component
test result: ok. 220 passed (incl. 14 migrate CLI tests for sqlite+jsonl)
```

### CI status (exact-head `84d276a9`)

All 28 checks pass; 3 expected skips; 0 failures. The Parallel Runtime Test flake observed in prior CI runs (`run_brackets_successful_turn_with_agent_start_and_agent_end` — pre-existing on master, introduced by PR #9490) did not reproduce on the current head.

### Live smoke: 37 scenarios / 94 checkpoints — all pass on head `84d276a9`

The smoke suite was updated this round to cover the tightened compatibility boundary (model-label rejection, temperature, behavior controls, uppercase session keys). All new-behavior assertions passed.

| Group | Scenarios | Checkpoints | Coverage |
|-------|-----------|-------------|----------|
| A: Request validation | 5 | 35 | Health, 23 request-level unsupported params→400 + 4 message-level rejections (role allow-list, tool_calls, name, tool_call_id) + metadata/store tolerated |
| B: Response modes & streaming | 5 | 12 | Blocking, SSE streaming, include_usage, abort |
| C: Session lifecycle | 7 | 12 | Single-message recall, x-session-key, uppercase & dot key→400, full history, persistence, concurrent serialisation, DELETE+no-resurrection |
| D: Session security & ownership | 4 | 7 | Cross-agent rejection (HTTP 400 + WS SESSION_AGENT_MISMATCH), meta-only delete + reuse (cross-agent + same-agent) |
| E: Tool control | 7 | 13 | tool_choice=none/required/{function}→400, 6 malformed shapes, unknown tools, empty tools, mixed known+unknown |
| F: Auth & rate-limit | 2 | 2 | X-Request-ID, rate-limit headers |
| G: Model routing | 3 | 6 | Empty→default, unknown agent→400, gpt-4/gpt-4o/claude-3-opus→400 |
| H: WebSocket transport | 4 | 9 | Cross-transport 409 (H1+H2, 5), multi-turn history (H3, 2), guard key normalization B1 (H4, 2) |
| **Total** | **37** | **94** | |

---

## Security & Privacy Impact

- **New permissions?** Yes — new HTTP endpoint (default-off, existing auth) and CLI `migrate session-ownership` subcommand.
- **Cross-agent access?** Built-in JSONL/SQLite backends enforce atomic fail-closed ownership on every backend-keyed entry point (HTTP, WS, RPC), and caller-controlled session ids cannot reassign a built-in backend's transcript. Isolation for a **custom** `SessionBackend` is contingent on that backend correctly implementing `claim_session_agent_alias`: the default trait returns `Unsupported`, which now causes all transports to reject non-empty sessions, but a mis-implemented custom backend can still bypass isolation. This is enforced, not categorically impossible.
- **Prompt injection?** No new injection surface — request content is treated as conversation input to the routed agent, same as the WS path; tool schemas are server-authoritative.
- **Secrets / tokens changed?** No — no new secret storage, logging, or token handling; API keys remain provider-config-owned.
- **Persistence integrity?** Session keys are injective at the HTTP entry (ASCII `[a-z0-9_-]`); noncanonical client-supplied keys are rejected before backend keying. Cross-transport guard identities use Unicode-aware case folding (`guard_key`) so that Cyrillic and Greek case variants share the same guard (queue slot, lease, cancel token) — preventing concurrent access to the same transcript on case-insensitive filesystems. Migration paths use the same atomic `claim_session_agent_alias`, preventing TOCTOU overwrites by concurrent transports.

---

## Compatibility

- **Backward compatible?** Endpoint default-off; session key resolution backward compatible for existing keys; new config fields have defaults. `model` labels that are not a ZeroClaw agent target now return 400 (previously silently routed to the default agent), and per-request `temperature`/behavior-changing fields now return 400 — deliberate compatibility-boundary tightenings for honest request semantics. Pre-existing sessions without ownership metadata require migration via `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership`.
- **MSRV / toolchain:** unchanged; no new toolchain or edition requirement.
- **Upgrade steps (breaking trait change):** `SessionBackend::claim_session_agent_alias` default returns `Err(Unsupported)`, and all transports reject non-empty sessions on that result. Custom backends that previously relied on the non-atomic `get`+`set` fallback must implement atomic claim to keep serving non-empty sessions, or accept that non-empty sessions will be rejected on all transports; built-in JSONL/SQLite already implement it. No data migration is required for built-in backends.
- **Config / CLI surface changed?** Yes — two new `[gateway]` keys (`chat_completions_enabled`, `chat_rate_limit_per_minute`); new `zeroclaw migrate session-ownership` CLI subcommand.
- **Wire contract:** `408` timeout uses `"type": "timeout"`; rate-limit headers report real sliding-window values (not hardcoded constants); noncanonical session ids rejected on all RPC methods; `x-request-id` is a response header (not an inbound parameter); 413 responses omit `X-Request-ID`/`x-session-key` (body-size middleware fires before handler); unsupported/behavior-changing request fields return 400 with `error.type: "unsupported_parameter"`.

---

## Known gaps / follow-ups

- **Session-key case collision on channel/webhook paths:** `sanitize_session_key` preserves case on channel-derived keys (e.g. `slack_U01ABC`). On case-insensitive filesystems, two channels whose keys differ only in case could collide at the storage layer. This pre-dates the PR (present on `master` via `sender_session_id`) and requires a storage migration to fully resolve for channel paths. Gateway cross-transport case collision is resolved by guard key normalization at all in-memory boundaries (ASCII `to_ascii_lowercase` in commit 3, upgraded to Unicode-aware `to_lowercase` covering Cyrillic and Greek in commit 4).
- **`messages[].content: null`** (assistant tool-call messages with null content) is currently coerced to an empty string; honoring null content is a separate follow-up.
- **WebSocket/RPC session-key alphabet** still accepts Unicode alphanumerics via `is_canonical_session_key()` (e.g. `user_Алиса` is a valid WS session key). This is safe under the Unicode-aware guard normalization (commit 4 ensures case variants share guards), but means two Unicode case variants that DON'T collide on case-sensitive filesystems (Linux ext4) will serialize under a shared guard despite having distinct storage files. This is the conservative safe side (over-serialization, never data corruption). Further narrowing WS/RPC to match HTTP's `[a-z0-9_-]` is a potential follow-up that would require a migration plan for any pre-existing Unicode WS session keys.

---

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback:** Set `chat_completions_enabled = false` + `POST /admin/reload` (daemon-supervised). Standalone: restart gateway.
- **Full revert:** `git revert <merge-commit-sha>` — no database migration needed. Sidecar `.meta.json` files are ignored by the old code path.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** unexpected 400s on `/v1/chat/completions` for previously-accepted `model` labels or `temperature`/behavior fields (expected under the new boundary); 400 on mixed-case or non-ASCII `x-session-key` (expected); 409 on HTTP requests to a session held by an active WebSocket.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep agent turns alive after viewer disconnect
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Treat the dashboard WebSocket as a viewer/controller rather than the owner of an active agent turn, detaching the viewer on close or failed Pong delivery without cancelling turn execution.
  - Enforce injective collision-free gateway session identity across WebSocket, REST, memory, and persistence layers. Malformed ids are rejected before any storage lookup, so a punctuation alias such as `gw_a.b` can no longer address the `gw_a_b` transcript under a second lifecycle key, and the legacy non-gateway escape hatch now takes an exact non-sanitizing lookup instead of the lossy existence probe.
  - Make `SessionLifecycle` the sole in-process authority for session incarnation, deletion, finalization, and persistence disposition, bounding unmutated authority cells (`MAX_AUTHORITIES = 10_000`) without weakening tombstones or poison markers.
  - Reconnect the dashboard through session-state authority: keep the composer locked while running, owe one authoritative history fetch per connection (discharged only by a fetch that lands, so retries and already-idle reconnects cannot unlock over a stale transcript), scope that obligation and the socket recycle to the conversation the connection is on, and enable follow-up continuity, Stop, and Retry.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not alter `SessionBackend` storage trait contracts, does not re-add an alternate deleter in runtime RPC, and does not alter non-gateway tool targets. Without session persistence, a turn survives detach but missed stream output is not replayable. Does not add bounded or TTL reclamation for retained deletion tombstones, poisoned cells, or the per-session turn-version map; see the open item below.
- **Blast radius:** Gateway WebSocket connection handshake, REST session routes, detached turn lifecycle, and web dashboard chat UI.
- **Linked issue(s):** Resolves #8559. Related #9641, #10538.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `docs`, `dependencies`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `tool`, `tests`, `distinguished contributor`, `needs-author-action`, `web`, `risk:high`, `size:XL` (live snapshot from `gh pr view 9002 --json labels`).

## Current exact-head validation

- **Head:** `177325b1b12e256d14d1de487dd6657c3c33aa65`
- **Base integrated:** `origin/master` at `46479bdca74bedb5c71e30afab657ccaac77dab4` (merge commit `13dd825`). One conflict, in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs`: both sides appended new `#[tokio::test]` functions to the same block of the persistence-routing test module. Resolved by keeping both sets of tests, this branch's two RPC session-delete ownership regressions and master's session-state/ACP-incarnation tests, with no test dropped or edited on either side.
- **What this head adds over `cdad3339`:** the master merge above, the no-persistence session-id validation fix described next, and the six browser-boundary captures under `.pr-evidence/` that the actual-interface section below reports.
- **New in this head, from the 2026-09-08 automated re-review:** `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` returned its empty no-persistence body before resolving the id, so with `session_persistence = false` a malformed gateway id such as `gw_a.b` answered `200` while the WebSocket upgrade and the persisted REST routes answered `400` for the same id. The path id is now validated before the early return (`crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api.rs:1877`), matching the no-backend session-state route at `:2337`, with a regression at `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api.rs:2792`.
- **Open item carried forward:** retained tombstones, poisoned cells, and the per-session turn-version map still have no bounded reclamation policy.

## Actual-interface evidence

Environment used for this run: an isolated local daemon on `127.0.0.1:42743`, built at the `ci` profile from `753b912f1166ce92566e73bc05fad0d6bce058be`, which is the code at the current head `177325b1b12e256d14d1de487dd6657c3c33aa65` (that commit adds only the six images below). It serves the production dashboard bundle from `web/dist` through `[gateway] web_dist_dir`, with `[gateway] session_persistence = true` on the SQLite backend, and it talks to a controlled loopback OpenAI-compatible provider on `127.0.0.1:42744` that holds every completion for 25 seconds before answering. No external network call and no real credential are involved.

**Server half, verified through the production routes:**

```text
$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'status=%{http_code} type=%{content_type} size=%{size_download}\n' http://127.0.0.1:42743/
status=200 type=text/html; charset=utf-8 size=2234        # production web/dist bundle, not a dev server

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'status=%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:42743/agent/dev
status=200

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'http://127.0.0.1:42743/api/sessions/gw_a.b/messages'
400                                                       # identity boundary, live, persistence ON

$ curl -sS 'http://127.0.0.1:42743/api/sessions/gw_a_b/messages'
{"messages":[],"session_id":"gw_a_b","session_persistence":true}

# one full turn over the same /ws/chat route the dashboard opens
[probe] handshake: HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
[probe] t=  0.0s {"message_count": 0, "resumed": false, "session_id": "evidence-probe-one", "type": "session_start"}
[probe] t= 25.9s {"content": "MOCK-ANSWER for [...evidence probe one...] :: token-count=15", "type": "chunk"}

# the detach claim itself: viewer socket closed 3 s into a 25 s turn, no Stop, no delete
t= 3.0s VIEWER SOCKET CLOSED
t= 7.0s state=running persistence=True
t=11.0s state=running persistence=True
t=15.0s state=running persistence=True
t=19.0s state=running persistence=True
t=23.0s state=running persistence=True
t=27.0s state=idle persistence=True
t=27.0s transcript has 2 messages (user prompt + completed assistant answer)
```

The turn kept running for twenty seconds with no viewer attached and persisted its answer. The pre-change behavior, where socket close cancels the turn, is what the branch's server-side regressions pin; I did not stand up a second daemon on `master` for a side-by-side live run.

**Client half, captured through the production dashboard route:**

Browser: headless Google Chrome 152.0.7977.83 on macOS 26.5.1 (aarch64), driven over the DevTools protocol against `http://127.0.0.1:42743/agent/dev`, which serves the built `web/dist` bundle. Viewport 1280x800 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1. Conversation `3e9c508c-dca6-4735-b2be-0a765cfa0f57`, session persistence on, provider delay 25 s.

| # | Action | Observed result | Capture |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Open `/agent/dev` | Composer enabled, placeholder `Type a message...`, status dot `Connected`. | `.pr-evidence/pr-9002-01-idle-composer.png` |
| 2 | Send `detach probe: name the capital of France and nothing else` | Composer disabled within 0.6 s, placeholder `Running…`, Send replaced by the red Stop control. | `.pr-evidence/pr-9002-02-locked-running.png` |
| 3 | Click the sidebar `Dashboard` link 2.6 s into the 25 s turn, so the chat unmounts and this viewer's socket closes | The chat page is gone and no composer exists in the DOM. From a second client, `GET /api/sessions/{id}/state` answered `running` with the same `turn_id` at +2.5 s, +5.0 s, +7.5 s, +10.0 s and +12.5 s after leaving. | `.pr-evidence/pr-9002-03-left-the-chat.png` |
| 4 | Return to the chat with the browser Back button, 13.8 s after sending | Composer still disabled with the placeholder still `Running…` and Stop still shown; input was never accepted. The transcript is still empty here because the gateway commits the message pair when the turn finishes, so this capture shows the lock holding with nothing yet hydrated. | `.pr-evidence/pr-9002-04-returned-still-locked.png` |
| 5 | Wait for the provider to answer | The completed answer (`MOCK-ANSWER for [...] :: token-count=17`) was already rendered when the composer unlocked, 25.8 s after sending; the placeholder then returned to `Type a message...`. | `.pr-evidence/pr-9002-05-hydrated-answer-unlocked.png` |
| 6 | Send the dependent follow-up `repeat the token-count number you just printed, digits only` | It sent cleanly and was answered in the same conversation: two answers in the transcript, then `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` held four messages and the session reported `idle`. | `.pr-evidence/pr-9002-06-dependent-follow-up.png` |

The run asserts, not just photographs, the central claim: the script fails if the composer is enabled on return at step 4, and it records whether the answer was on screen at the moment of unlock (it was). The captures carry no tokens and no personal data: one local agent alias `dev`, the mock model name `openai.mock`, and the mock's deterministic answers.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, `channel=wss`
- **Setup / preconditions:** Run the gateway with the web dashboard, an authenticated browser session, and session persistence enabled. A provider that takes a few seconds to answer makes the detached window easy to hit by hand.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Send a prompt, navigate away while it runs, then return before completion.
  2. Confirm input stays read-only with a "Running…" placeholder and Stop button visible until completion.
  3. Confirm persisted history appears once idle without duplicate messages, and a dependent follow-up prompt sends cleanly.
  4. Return *after* the turn has already finished (so the first session-state answer is `idle`) and confirm the completed answer is on screen before the composer unlocks.
  5. Repeat with explicit Stop during a detached turn; verify the in-flight abort unlocks the composer.
  6. Test the failed recovery state (for example a 401, or a 503 on the history fetch); verify the fail-closed lockout, and that Retry unlocks only once the history fetch succeeds.
  7. Identity: with a session `gw_a_b` present, call `GET`, `POST`, and `DELETE /api/sessions/gw_a.b`. Each must answer 400 and leave `gw_a_b` untouched.
  8. Identity with persistence off: set `[gateway] session_persistence = false` and call `GET /api/sessions/gw_a.b/messages`. It must answer 400, not the empty 200 body.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Viewer loss does not cancel the turn; reconnect remains fail-closed until authoritative history is loaded; Stop and delete retain cancellation authority; stale or poisoned writers cannot proceed; invalid session ids are rejected with HTTP 400 before any storage lookup, in both persistence modes.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** WebSocket loss or failed Pong delivery cancelled the active turn, punctuation collisions (`a.b` vs `a_b`) split lifecycle authority over one JSONL file, and recovery failures could strand the composer permanently locked without a recovery affordance. - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `No`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`
- **Upgrade steps for existing users:** Client-selected gateway session ids are now validated at the WebSocket upgrade and the REST session routes before any storage lookup, in both persistence modes. An id is accepted when it is at most 128 bytes, carries at most one `gw_` prefix, and uses only ASCII alphanumerics, `-`, and `_`. Ids with punctuation (`a.b`), a doubled prefix (`gw_gw_x`), or over 128 bytes now receive HTTP 400 instead of being sanitized into a shared session file. With `session_persistence = false`, `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` now returns 400 for such an id instead of an empty 200 body. Clients that minted such ids should switch to the accepted alphabet; existing transcripts remain readable under the sanitized key they were actually stored as (for example `a_b`). On the JSONL backend, where the stored key is the sanitized file name, a punctuated legacy channel key such as `discord.room` is no longer accepted through the gateway session routes; the default SQLite backend stores keys verbatim and keeps serving those ids. This restriction is intentional: it is what makes one session id map to exactly one transcript and one lifecycle authority.

- **Observable failure symptoms:** HTTP 400 on session create or connect for previously accepted ids, a dashboard composer that stays locked after a turn completes, or stalled detached-turn completion in gateway logs.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose the composition-seam row for bounded-delegation ceiling carriage (#9872, #10391)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #10391 (the #9872 fix) carries a bounded delegate's tool-name ceiling into the scheduler tools, `sop_execute`, `sop_advance`, `sop_workshop`, `spawn_subagent` and `send_message_to_peer`. To do that through the native registry factory it adds a crate-private `caller_ceiling` input on `NativeRecipeInputs`, forwards it in `src/composition/config_backed.rs` (two added lines), adds one `None` in the owned SOP step assembly call in `src/composition/supplied_only_traps.rs`, adds 15 `bounded-ceiling-*` refusal messages in `locales/en/cli.ftl`, and adds tests.
  - Review on #10391 pointed out that the ceiling-carriage row (#11652) does not list `src/composition/config_backed.rs`, and that threading the ceiling through that factory needs its own Core-approved row before #10391 merges.
  - This adds one row, directly under the #11652 row, for that extension. The approval cell records Audacity88's November 14 Core placement decision ([review](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12403#pullrequestreview-5905465683)); the scope, destination and review conditions are unchanged from the version approved at `6162c006ab`.
  - The #11652 row and every other row are unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** The table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` only. No code. The row does not add a construction, a public API, a capability kind or a tool grant, and does not change approval, admission or budget authority. It does not build a ceiling for sessions narrowed by an RPC principal's tool selector (`src/agent/agent.rs` still passes `None` there; #12232 withholds the tools that need an unrestricted principal from such sessions, see #12394), and it does not cover a recipe or factory that builds those tools itself.
- **Blast radius:** Merge eligibility of #10391's runtime changes under ADR-016.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9872, Related #10391, Related #11652, Related #12394

### What this does, simply

The runtime crate is a holding crate: new work there needs a recorded Core decision. The row from #11652 records the decision for carrying the bounded-delegation ceiling through the tools, the loop and SOP code. #10391 also needs a new input on the composition seam, a forwarding line in the config-backed registry source, new refusal messages and tests, which that row does not list. This row lists them, so Core can approve or narrow them explicitly. It also records what stays outside: recipes that only forward their inputs carry the ceiling without reading it, and a recipe or factory that builds those tools itself needs its own row.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for scope only.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** None. This changes a governance table, not a `surface` or `channel`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A checkout of this branch and of #10391's head.
- **Steps to run:** Compare the row's path list with `git diff --name-only master...<#10391 head> -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime`, and check that every runtime path in that diff is listed either in the #11652 row or in the new one.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** One added row with four cells; every existing table line unchanged; every runtime path of #10391 named by one of the two rows.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `src/composition.rs`, `src/composition/config_backed.rs`, `src/composition/supplied_only_traps.rs`, `locales/en/cli.ftl`, `src/sop/test_support.rs` and the new test files are not named by the #11652 row.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The docs checks on the changed file (Docs Style runs on `.md` changes).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` only selects `docs/book/src/*.md`, so on this diff it is expected to skip; I ran it with the file forced.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `git diff --numstat origin/master HEAD`: `1	0	crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`.
  - `DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`:

    ```text
    No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.
    markdownlint-cli2 v0.20.0 (markdownlint v0.40.0)
    Linting: 1 file(s)
    Summary: 0 error(s)
    ```

  - `python3 scripts/ci/collect_changed_links.py --base <merge-base> --docs-files crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md --check-local-targets`: `Collected 0 added link(s) from 1 docs file(s).`
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Each path and symbol the row names, against #10391 at `02e647d3a` and against `master` at `2c0a8c263`: the field and `#[non_exhaustive]` (`src/composition.rs`), the two forwarding lines (`src/composition/config_backed.rs`), the `caller_allowed` parameter (`src/agent/turn/mod.rs`) and its one `None` (`src/composition/supplied_only_traps.rs`), the 15 locale keys, the added test files, and which SOP tools receive the ceiling (`src/tools/mod.rs`). Also which build paths pass `None` (independent delegation in `src/tools/delegate.rs`, the RPC-principal session path in `src/agent/agent.rs`). Not verified: I did not run the docs gates through CI, and I did not read the #11652 head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A for interface. The row was checked against #10391 at `02e647d3a` and against `master` at `2c0a8c263` (results above, as of those revisions). On 2026-11-19 the branch was merged with `master` at `dfc70a2b4` without conflicts (merge commit `69ebd67e55`); the diff against that `master` is still the one added row in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`. I did not re-run the docs gates or re-check the row's paths against the current #10391 head `9365b1638d`. CI Required Gate on `69ebd67e55`: passed, [run 44648483271](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44648483271).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No build or tests: no code changes.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes, if Core approves: the row permits the named additions in the holding crate. It grants no runtime authority, and it keeps the existing ceiling (no new tool grants, no change to approval, admission or budget authority).
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The only `Yes` is conditional on approval. The risk is that approving the row is read as approving more than the code does; the row names each file and states what it does not cover.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Revert the commit. If #10391 has merged by then, the code it covers stays; reverting withdraws the permission for further additions under this row.

### Question for Core, not changed here

The #11652 row lists "the matching call in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`". Searching `assemble_owned_execution`, `all_tools_with_runtime` and `caller_allowed` in that file, on `master` at `2c0a8c263` and on #10391 at `02e647d3a`, finds no match, and #10391 does not change the file. I did not read the #11652 head to see whether the call existed then. This PR leaves that mention as it is.

prs.title: fix(shell): reap the process group a returned command left running
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Every `shell` command runs in its own session, so its process group is its own. `ChildGroupGuard` already tears that whole group down on timeout or cancellation, but a command that returned normally disarmed the guard. A child the command had backgrounded (`sleep 300 &`, `yes > /dev/null &`) then kept running with nothing to bound it: the tool timeout no longer applies once the command has answered, and the process is reparented to init, so it outlives the turn, the job and a daemon restart. On one busy host a single agent run left 368 `yes` processes behind at load 376.
  - After a normal return the tool now terminates whatever is still alive in that group: `SIGTERM` to `-pgid`, a bounded grace, then `SIGKILL` for what has not exited, and it logs how many processes it swept. Only `-pgid` is signalled; a group id that is not positive or that names the daemon's own group is refused.
  - The sweep runs before the post-exit pipe drain, not after. A background child normally holds the tool's stdout/stderr open, so draining first spent the whole drain budget waiting on a process that was about to be killed. A command with a background sleeper now returns in about 30 ms instead of about 280 ms. Output the command itself produced is untouched.
  - Two new `[shell_tool]` keys: `reap_background_on_return` (default `true`) and `reap_grace_secs` (default `2`).
- **Scope boundary:** the shell tool and its config section only. Timeout and cancellation cleanup are unchanged. A descendant that calls `setsid()` or `setpgid()` itself still escapes, exactly as on the timeout and cancellation paths today.
- **Blast radius:** commands that deliberately start a detached daemon through the shell tool. They are now stopped when the command returns unless the operator sets `reap_background_on_return = false`.
- **Linked issue(s):** none.

### What this does, simply

If an agent runs `some-command &` through the shell tool, the command finishes, the tool reports its result, and the background process keeps going forever. Nothing watches it any more. This change kills those leftovers when the command returns, the same way the tool already does when a command times out.

Operators who really do start long-lived background services from the tool can turn the new behaviour off with one config line.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` - covered by the unit tests below.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** none directly; this is the `shell` tool.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zeroclaw-config` tests and clippy cover both crates touched.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** the tests are Unix process-group tests; the Windows path is unchanged.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux, head `4701cc999`, rebased on master `4f3ca7c38`):

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output)

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::shell
test result: ok. 81 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib shell_tool
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile
```

- **Tests added or changed:** the shell tool reaps a backgrounded child on return; a command with nothing to sweep returns well inside the grace; a background child holding the tool's pipe does not cost the drain budget; the config defaults and a partial `[shell_tool]` section keep the remaining defaults.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `4701cc999`; no interface capture.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace test run was not repeated for this change.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- Process signalling changed? Yes: the tool now sends `SIGTERM`/`SIGKILL` to the command's own process group after a normal return. Mitigation: only a positive `-pgid` is ever signalled, the daemon's own group is refused, and the group is the one the tool created for that command.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Mostly: the default changes behaviour for commands that background work and expect it to survive the command. They need `[shell_tool].reap_background_on_return = false`. Documented in `docs/book/src/security/sandboxing.md`.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: two new optional keys in `[shell_tool]` with defaults.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: the keys are additive and default to the safe behaviour; no migration is needed.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Rollback strategy:** set `[shell_tool].reap_background_on_return = false`, or revert the two commits.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a background service started through the shell tool disappears when the command returns.

Fixed

Changed

  • AIX: Restore 'c_ulong' as the type of 'statvfs.f_fsid'. (#5616)
  • Android: Make prop_info an extern type (#5561)
  • Apple: Mach API is now available on non-MacOS targets again. This should resolve some issues building ecosystem crates. (#5612), (#5636)
  • FreeBSD: Add back NOTE_PCTRLMASK with a deprecation warning (#5600)

0.2.190

There is now a single config for enabling 64-bit time_t: libc_unstable_time64. This can be set unconditionally; it opts in to 64-bit time_t on the following platforms that use 32-bit by default:

  • 32-bit Linux-GNU
  • 32-bit Linux-uClibc
  • 32-bit Linux-musl. Note that setting this flag also enables some other changes that happend in musl v1.2.
  • 32-bit Windows-GNU
  • ESP-IDF (all targets with this environment are 32-bit)

Most other 32-bit platforms are either already using 64-bit time_t, or are considered legacy and will not be gaining support from their upstream maintainers.

You can enable this using RUSTFLAGS:

RUSTFLAGS='--cfg=libc_unstable_time64' cargo ...

Note that there may still be some changes to features gated by this config option, hence "unstable"
