prs.title: fix(providers): tell the model when a text-only follow-up has no new image
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Earlier user images keep their `[IMAGE:<path>]` markers in history so a deferred image stays available, and multimodal preparation re-sends them on every later turn looking exactly like fresh attachments. With the default `max_image_turns = 0`, a text-only follow-up such as "and this one?" then gets a confident description of a photo that was never sent (#11554).
  - A text-only user message that follows an earlier user image now carries a short model-facing note: "Note: no new image is attached to this message; any images above were sent earlier." The note is never added to image-bearing messages, earlier images are still sent (deferred access from #8151 keeps working), and conversations without images take the existing fast path untouched.
  - The note is added in one small pass after normalization (`note_text_only_followups`). Whether a message gets it depends only on that message and the ones before it, read from the request's input as it was before the age trim and the image cap, so the note never changes an earlier message from one request to the next and does not itself rewrite the provider prompt-cache prefix (the constraint from Audacity88's triage of #11554).
  - Some providers (the OpenAI-compatible and OpenAI Codex ones) prepare messages the runtime has already prepared, so a second pass must not change them: a message that already holds the note is left alone, and so is one an earlier pass reduced to the removed-image placeholder, the rejected-marker note, or the could-not-load note (each matched in the form its pass writes it: the placeholder and the could-not-load note only at the end of the message, the rejected-marker note anywhere, since it replaces the marker in place; so a user quoting the placeholder or could-not-load wording mid-sentence still gets the note). Image markers are counted with the same helper that selects the no-image fast path, so prose that uses marker syntax without a loadable reference (for example `[IMAGE:<path>]`) does not count as an earlier image. Tool-result carriers neither get the note nor count as earlier user images.
  - When provider-image quarantine or recovery (`omit_provider_image_ids`) removes every image from a captioned message, the provider view now keeps the caption followed by `[image removed from history]`, as it already did for image-only messages. Without this, a provider's second pass would add the new note to the very message the user sent an image with.
- **Scope boundary:** This fixes the behaviour #11554 reports (text-only follow-ups). Image-bearing messages are not labelled, so nothing marks a new image sent while earlier ones are still in history as new; that is outside the reported repro and is not addressed here. In the live check below, one local model still described a second photo sent straight after the first on its own, with no note anywhere in that request; this is one model and a short session, not evidence that the label is unneeded in general. A channel that stores a photo and its caption as separate consecutive user messages would see the note on the caption. The channel crate's own image placeholders (for example the one written when an inline image payload is collapsed from history, or "could not be read") are not recognised, so such a message after an earlier path-marker image also gets the note; the note then sits beside the channel's own placeholder, and for "could not be read" the two may read as contradictory. No change to `max_image_turns`, `max_images`, eviction, tool-result carriers, or stored history.
- **Blast radius:** The provider-visible text of text-only user messages that follow a user image, for every provider (shared multimodal preparation in `crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/multimodal.rs`), and the provider-only quarantine and recovery views of captioned messages whose images are all omitted. Each noted message gains about 20 tokens while the earlier image message stays in history, including after its image is evicted or age-trimmed; that keeps the note stable for the prompt cache. Text-only fallback requests strip media markers first and get no note. The runtime measures the prepared messages, so the note is counted in the context budget. Stored session history is unchanged.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11554. Related #8151, #11582.

### What this does, simply

When you send a photo in a chat and then keep talking, ZeroClaw keeps showing that photo to the model on every later message, so the model can still refer back to it. The model had no way to tell that the photo was old, so a follow-up like "and this one?" made it describe a brand-new photo that you never sent. Now, when your message has no image of its own and there was an image earlier, ZeroClaw adds a one-line note telling the model that nothing new is attached and the images above were sent earlier. The earlier photo is still there for the model to use.

### Possible follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The string checks for messages an earlier pass already prepared exist because some providers prepare the runtime's prepared messages a second time. Skipping that second preparation would make them unnecessary, but it is a cross-crate change.
- The image cap and the age trim leave a bare caption when they remove a captioned message's images; leaving the same placeholder there as quarantine now does would make the three paths consistent. It is not needed for this fix, because those trims always remove the oldest images first.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `signal` (with #11556); Telegram and Discord take the same path-marker route on master
- **Setup / preconditions:** a vision-capable model, default `[multimodal]` settings (`max_image_turns = 0`), a fresh session on Telegram or Discord. Signal image attachments need my open #11556, which is not on master yet.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Send one photo with a question.
  2. Send "and this one?" with no attachment.
  3. Send "what about this one?" with no attachment.
  4. Ask how many photos you have sent.
  5. Ask a question about the first photo.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** steps 2 and 3 are answered without describing a new photo; step 4 counts one; step 5 is answered from the first photo.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** as reported in #11554 (observed on Signal with master at 0.8.5 plus a Signal attachment branch for #7891): step 2 described "another photo of the same subject" with invented details, step 3 gave another invented description, and step 4 answered three. Step 5 was not part of the report.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` (format, clippy, and the workspace test run, which includes the `zeroclaw-providers` and `zeroclaw-runtime` tests that cover the new behaviour and the root `component` CLI test this PR updates).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not exercise model behaviour; the live check below covers that for one model.
- **Commands run and tail output:** in a throwaway container on this branch:
  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  exit 0
  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
  exit 0
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --locked --lib -- multimodal::
  test result: ok. 216 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1779 filtered out
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --locked --lib
  test result: FAILED. 1990 passed; 1 failed; 4 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers --locked --test hailo_ollama
  test result: ok. 60 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw --locked --test component
  test result: FAILED. 262 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw --locked --test integration
  test result: ok. 142 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
  ```
  On the previous revision of this branch, which differed only by the `earlier_images_note_survives_the_age_trim_of_the_earlier_image` test and one doc comment in `multimodal.rs`:
  ```text
  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
  exit 0
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --lib
  test result: ok. 5798 passed; 0 failed; 8 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --locked --lib
  test result: FAILED. 2004 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  ```
  New tests:
  - `text_only_followup_after_an_image_is_told_no_new_image_is_attached` (the note is appended and the text, including leading indentation, is kept verbatim)
  - `text_before_the_first_image_gets_no_note`
  - `earlier_images_note_is_stable_across_requests` (later requests leave earlier messages byte-identical)
  - `earlier_images_note_survives_eviction_of_the_earlier_image` and `earlier_images_note_survives_the_age_trim_of_the_earlier_image` (the note is decided from the input, so it stays after the cap or the age limit removes the earlier image)
  - `preparing_prepared_messages_again_changes_nothing`, `a_failed_image_after_an_earlier_one_is_not_noted_on_a_second_pass`, `a_refused_marker_after_an_earlier_image_is_not_noted_on_a_second_pass`, and `a_message_whose_images_were_omitted_is_not_noted_on_a_second_pass` (prepare, then prepare the result again; the last one omits images in between)
  - `tool_result_carriers_neither_get_nor_trigger_the_note`
  - `quoting_the_could_not_load_wording_does_not_suppress_the_note`
  - `prose_that_only_contains_the_marker_prefix_is_not_an_earlier_image`

  The existing `image_cap_eviction_is_bounded_and_prefix_stable` still passes. I also removed each guard in turn (the existing-note check, each of the three already-prepared checks, the carrier skip, the input-based decision, and the caption placeholder on omit); each removal makes at least one of these tests fail. In `zeroclaw-runtime`, `enforce_retrims_against_the_prepared_population_for_retained_images` compared prepared and raw token estimates for a history with two text-only follow-ups after an image; it now compares against the prepared messages with only the image turn left raw, so it still isolates per-image pricing. In the root `component` suite, `interactive_agent_renders_image_recovery_and_next_text_turn` checked that the next turn's newest user message ends with "next text-only turn"; that message now also carries the note, so it checks that the message contains the text.

  The three failures are unrelated to this change. `openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` fails in full-suite runs in my environment and passes when run alone; its fixture has no images, and this change does not touch `openai.rs`. `tts::tests::edge_tts_removes_temp_output_when_read_fails` relies on `chmod 000` making a file unreadable, which does not hold in my container, which runs as root. `daemon_startup_feedback::daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions` fails at the same line when run alone on this branch and on unmodified master `e8d2e5fc8` in the same container.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** On Signal, with a local model served by llama.cpp through the OpenAI-compatible provider (which runs the second preparation pass), I ran the five steps above in a fresh session against a daemon built from v0.8.6 plus this branch's code change and my other PR branches (#11556 and #11660, open; #11637 and #11595, since merged to master). Steps 2 and 3 did not describe a new photo, step 4 counted one, and step 5 was answered from the first photo. An earlier revision of this change gave the same results. In a second session on the same build and setup, after `/clear` and with photos not used in any earlier test, I sent photo A with a question, then a different photo B with "and what is this one?", asked how many photos I had sent, asked about the first and then the second photo, and then sent a third photo C with "what about this one?". B was described on its own, without repeating or blending A, and C was described as the newest photo; the count was two; and the questions about the first and second photo were answered from A and B. Not verified: the "before" behaviour was not re-run on current master or v0.8.6; Telegram, Discord, and other models were not tested.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no rendered interface changes; the change is model-facing text in the provider request.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** unit and integration tests on this branch's head, except the `zeroclaw-runtime` clippy and library runs and the `zeroclaw-channels` library run, which are from the previous revision (see above); live check on Signal against v0.8.6 plus this branch's code change, as described above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A: the observable result is the model's reply in a private chat; the unit tests assert the exact note text and placement.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** text-only follow-ups after a photo: no invented photo; photo count: one; question about the first photo: answered from it; in a second session, a new photo after an earlier one was described on its own and the photo count was two.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full workspace test suite was not run. The `zeroclaw-providers`, `zeroclaw-runtime`, and `zeroclaw-channels` library suites, the `zeroclaw-providers` `hailo_ollama` test, and the root `component` and `integration` suites were run; other workspace crates and integration suites were left to CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: the note and the removed-image placeholder are fixed constants; no user, channel, or file content is interpolated into them. User text can only suppress the note on its own message (for example by quoting the note), and cannot make the note appear without a real image marker in an earlier user message.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a text-only follow-up answered as if no earlier image existed would indicate the note is misleading the model; earlier images missing from the request would indicate a regression in deferred access (covered by the tests above).

prs.title: refactor(parser): share incremental response parsing outside runtime
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge only after the dependencies below.
- **What changed and why:** Move streaming protocol detection, reasoning-tag stripping and terminal-marker state machines into the shared parser; retain runtime tool admission, event delivery and parser regression tests.
- **Scope boundary:** No schema changes or new per-model configuration. Authorization, tool execution, cancellation and whole-turn replay stay in runtime.
- **Blast radius:** Parser and runtime streaming output, protocol suppression and diagnostic offsets.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Stack part 2; reference implementation `921b8ee993a0b2439a0c2c41cb84337270942a06`. Depends on #12444.

### What this does, simply

Streaming responses can contain reasoning or tool-call text that needs incremental parsing. This change moves the parsing state machines into the shared parser crate. Runtime still owns event delivery, admission and cancellation, while the parser only transforms input into parsed output.

## Testing (required)


### Latest master refresh — November 25, 2026

- Merged the validated parent containing master badcc3da4d; tested revision 530f45223fbfd14a5cf1d50731a638e7d2249ba9.

prs.body:
## Summary

**Draft proposal 5/12.** This dependent slice is not independently enableable or merge-ready. Failed local validation, full-stack proof, and Core approval remain open. GitHub owns the current mergeability and hosted-check state.

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds parent-turn checkpoints and execution-epoch supervision so ordinary Goal controls can settle at a turn boundary while immediate controls fence the owning worker.
  - Persists each accepted parent candidate exactly once before verification, after accounting validation; preserves original errors when recording a failure.
  - Bounds and validates verifier responses instead of deriving lifecycle authority from ordinary agent prose.
  - Connects process-local Goal coordination to the existing control-plane and daemon reload boundaries without introducing another durable lifecycle owner.
- **Scope boundary:** Slice 05 depends on #11881. Its owned diff is `f8359c4f5ed2c8760f437ae6e1f83727e97a2904..7d02d8aa7394e028c2fb5040763e0018be5a4472` (18 paths). The PR-to-`master` diff also contains its predecessors. This slice does not provide the later Matrix or ZeroCode host integrations; no production Goal host is wired end to end here.
- **Blast radius:** Goal control/execution contracts, session drivers, durable task/session integration, and daemon reload coordination. The delegate-file change only adapts a test fixture.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #11881. Related RFC #8303 and tracker #10341; this slice does not close either issue.

https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11881
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341

### What this does, simply

A Goal can outlive one agent turn. Pause, cancellation, reload, and the next turn must agree about which worker owns execution and which response is already saved. This slice supplies that coordination and its host-contract tests. It is infrastructure for the later surface adapters, not an independently usable Goal Mode release.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — this slice does not wire a production Goal host; the automated host-contract tests exercise the implemented boundary.

### How I tested

#### Current Draft head `ece8c8a9c769ae06149efaef6524403d06d84453`

- **Hosted checks relied on:** the [exact-head Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45757025078) passed. The PR check rollup had 50 successes and seven conditional skips with no failures or pending checks. This includes the main test suite, parallel runtime test, Security, and CLI-only build.
- **Local commands and results:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and both comment-hygiene scripts exited 0 (`61 passed, 0 failed`; `Comment hygiene gate passed.`). `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-goal` passed all 105 tests, and `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-runtime --test goal_execution_host_contract` reported `110 passed; 0 failed`. `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-goal -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` exited 0.
- **Change exercised:** a failed restart-pause write blocks successors while admitted work settles and the original error is returned. A worker still waiting for its lease is fenced, not terminally failed. The held-lease regression first reproduced `Failed` instead of `Running`, then passed after the repair. The verifier prompt agrees with the parser's existing JSON-object rule.
- **Review and limits:** independent review passed with advisories. One drain error can skip later workers on that host; an audit error can follow an already durable pause or budget change. Neither limitation was introduced by the repair. No live service, provider, Matrix or ZeroCode session was exercised. This slice does not wire the later production adapters.

#### Earlier local integration evidence (`abcc27cd`)

These were not rerun as full local gates on the current head. The unfiltered workspace Nextest run exited 100: `21475 tests run: 21457 passed (6 slow, 2 leaky), 18 failed, 45 skipped`. The failures were one macOS PATH fixture, two relay backlog fixtures reproduced on upstream, eleven gateway cases, three provider deadlines, and one RPC-client flood deadline. The fifteen gateway/provider/RPC selectors passed on both parent and candidate when run serially; that does not explain the original failures, including the missing WebSocket close code.

The local parallel script exited 101 after `6465 passed; 2 failed; 10 ignored` in its first runtime repetition. The five separate supplemental runs filled the missing coverage; they did not turn the script green. The two remaining runtime repetitions reproduced the relay failures, and one also hit an unresolved delegate timeout that passed in isolated parent and candidate runs. All three channel repetitions reported `2109 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored`. Workspace MSRV Clippy exited 101 on an upstream-reproduced lint in unchanged `zeroclaw-infra`; the affected crates passed Clippy on the hosted CI toolchain. Local advisory checks exited 0 on the recorded snapshot with ten inherited allowed warnings, not a substitute for hosted Security CI.

#### Earlier local results (`7d02d8aa7394e028c2fb5040763e0018be5a4472`)

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None for this candidate yet. Fresh hosted checks are required after the update.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** This slice does not provide the later Matrix or ZeroCode production hosts, so their end-to-end delivery and parity are not established here. The local failures and skipped tests below remain open.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0, no output.
  - `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0; ``Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 0.71s``.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-goal`: exit 0; three test targets reported 49, 52, and 2 passed.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test goal_execution_host_contract`: exit 0; `110 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --test session_goal_control_plane_contract`: exit 0; `27 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib goal_accounting::`: exit 0; `64 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config goal`: exit 0; `26 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh`: exit 0; `58 passed, 0 failed`. `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: exit 0; `Comment hygiene gate passed.`
  - `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast`: **FAIL, exit 100**:

    ```text
    Summary [168.101s] 21039 tests run: 21035 passed (1 slow, 2 leaky), 4 failed, 44 skipped
    ```

    Failures were the Telegram approval timeout fixture, the case-variant filesystem fixture tracked in #11959, and two relay listener-backlog fixtures. The relay failures were reproduced on the pinned upstream base. The Telegram test's precise cause remains unproven; unchanged source and three later channel-library passes do not establish that cause.
  - `bash scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh`: **FAIL, exit 101**; the first runtime repetition reported `6335 passed; 2 failed; 10 ignored` for the same relay fixtures. The script stopped there; its other five repetitions did not run.
  - Separate supplemental executions used the script's exact `cargo test --locked --quiet -p <crate> --lib -- --test-threads=16` arguments: the two additional runtime runs each reported `6335 passed; 2 failed; 10 ignored`; three channel runs each reported `2059 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored`. These are separate observations, not a pass for the failed script.
  - `cargo deny check advisories` with cargo-deny 0.19.9: **FAIL, exit 1**; `advisories FAILED` for RUSTSEC-2026-0543, RUSTSEC-2026-0555, and RUSTSEC-2026-0548. Dependency repair remains outside this slice.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed the lifecycle, accounting and authority paths and their tests. No live provider, service, Matrix room, or ZeroCode session was exercised.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A for the slice-owned changes: they add no rendered interface. The inherited dashboard evidence and its pending screenshot attachments are tracked in #11881.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `7d02d8aa7394e028c2fb5040763e0018be5a4472`; Rust library and host-contract tests, not a supported-interface transcript.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A for the slice-owned changes; command output is summarized above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Automated cases cover deferred controls, lifecycle fencing, persistence, accounting, and restart coordination at host-contract boundaries.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No live-host test was run because this slice does not wire a production host. The failed scripted gate's later repetitions were not run by that script; separate equivalent-command observations are reported above.

The local monitoring was polling-limited for some runs: no competing build was confirmed, but transient unobserved processes cannot be ruled out. The earlier interrupted runs and the slow/leaky test observations are not reclassified as passes.

https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11959
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11881

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes, internal Goal execution/control APIs; no new external grants or filesystem access scope.**
- New external network calls? **No new endpoint or transport.** Goal model operations use the existing configured provider boundary.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Parent/verifier content remains untrusted model-visible text.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Bind execution and control to the exact task/session/epoch. Validate bounded verifier output into typed decisions; ordinary prose does not authorize lifecycle transitions. The later production hosts must preserve ordinary authorization and event-egress protections.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No — Rust API consumers must migrate.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No new keys or command grammar in this slice.** Start paths inherit the predecessor's explicit-budget requirement when defaults are absent.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users:
  - Relative to the owned base, update `GoalSessionDriver::acquire_execution` implementations for the checkpoint argument and pending-admission closure; do not interrupt a lease already returned. Direct `GoalExecutionHost::acquire_execution` and `GoalRuntime::acquire_execution` callers also supply the checkpoint. Update `GoalExecutionEngine::run` callers for `GoalHostSettingsSource` and `GoalParentTurnCheckpoint`; exhaustive `GoalExecutionOutcome` matches must handle `Fenced`.
  - Relative to the owned base, this slice adds a crate-private field to `ControlPlaneHandle`, so external struct literals using its formerly public fields no longer compile. Use `ControlPlaneHandle::open(data_dir)` when its store semantics fit. This slice supplies no public custom-store constructor; consumers needing one require an owning API decision, not an assumed setter.
  - Relative to the previously published `d97dd116`, candidate-persistence failure now records `candidate_persistence_failed` and preserves the original error. Accounting is validated before the empty-candidate check and persistence. Verifier raw-response allowance changes from 512 KiB to 1 MiB; each blocker's serialized payload remains limited to 4,096 bytes. Typed verifier accounting errors record `accounting_missing_or_invalid` and are returned unchanged even if recording the transition fails. Candidate append is persistence-only, and start paths honor `BudgetRequired`.
  - Rebuild downstream consumers against the accepted stack. No database, serde, wire-format, or configuration-key migration is introduced by this slice.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** This prefix must not be enabled independently. After an eventual merge, revert dependent slices in reverse order, then `git revert <slice-05-squash-commit>` (or `git revert -m 1 <slice-05-merge-commit>` if a merge commit was used). Preserve durable task/session records. For a future enabled host, stop admission and settle/fence active workers before rollback; this PR does not supply an operator-facing rollout procedure.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added here; do not enable the incomplete prefix.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Checkpoint work that does not settle, missing/duplicated parent responses, a worker remaining active during restart drain, or task/epoch ownership disagreement.

## Remaining proposal gates

- The restart-pause write failure paths are repaired and covered above. Retain the remaining host-integration verification for immediate-control ordering when `pause_before_launch` drains a predecessor and the invariant-documentation advisory for the ticket counter.
- **Scoped Core placement request, not approval:** #12407 added a row marked pending that describes #11878–#11881. It does not grant authority for #11882's daemon restart wiring. The residual adapters in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/control_plane/boot.rs` and `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/daemon/mod.rs` are intended for the existing kernel/task-lifecycle owner. Goal policy and execution remain in `zeroclaw-goal`. A concrete receiving caller and a separately reviewed, applicable exception row or authoritative ownership change are required before merge.
- Core/CODEOWNERS approval, full-stack proof, rollout and footprint prerequisites remain open. Hosted CI passed on the current head; historical local failures above remain failures. Keep #11882 Draft: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11882.

prs.title: fix(cli): localize config set value prompts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch** `master`
- **What changed and why**
  - The masked value reader and the plain plugin-setting reader now ask for input using the same Fluent key, `cli-config-value-prompt`, with the resolved config path as its argument.
  - All five built-in CLI catalogs define the message. The test formats it directly from each catalog so the English fallback cannot conceal a missing translation.
- **Scope boundary** The change covers the label displayed when either value reader opens. Each reader still handles and stores its input through its existing path.
- **Blast radius** Interactive `zeroclaw config set` and its runtime CLI catalogs.
- **Linked issue** Closes #11950

### What this does, simply

With French selected, the CLI now asks “Saisissez une valeur pour …” when you enter a configuration value. Previously this line stayed in English while nearby messages followed the selected language. The prompt identifies the field being edited, and secret input remains masked.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, if reviewing the terminal interaction.
- **Interface exercised** `cli`
- **Setup / preconditions** Use an isolated config with `locale = "fr"` and a plugin instance that declares a plain string setting and an `x-secret` string setting.
- **Steps to run** For each setting run `zeroclaw --config-dir "$fixture" config set "plugins.entries.$instance.config.$field"` without a value argument. Enter a dummy value and press Enter. Repeat with `locale = "en"`.
- **Expected on this branch** The French prompt includes the complete setting path. The secret field masks the typed value and the plain field displays it. In English both retain “Enter value for …”.
- **Prior behavior** Both paths use the English prompt even with French selected. The two pre-change call sites contain that literal on `cda933e6b9`. I also observed that behavior in the released 0.9.0 CLI at `6c78ba5`.

### How I tested

- **Checks relied on** The focused runtime unit test exercises the Fluent parser and path substitution in English, Spanish, French, Japanese and Simplified Chinese. The CLI build enables WASM plugin metadata so the plain setting enters the same branch a real installed plugin uses.
- **CI coverage gap** The locale unit test does not open a terminal. I checked both input readers in a PTY in English and French.
- **Commands run and tail output**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` exited 0.
  - `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib config_set_value_prompt` reported `1 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo build --locked --offline -p zeroclaw --no-default-features --features agent-runtime,plugins-wasm --bin zeroclaw` finished successfully. The binary identified itself as `zeroclaw 0.9.0 (v0.9.0-15-g49ef74e33f)`.
- **Beyond CI** I gave the fixture plugin a plain `region` field and an `x-secret` `password` field and submitted dummy values to each with English and French selected. All four commands exited 0. The secret reader masked keystrokes in both languages and the plain reader displayed the value.
- **Visual interface evidence** Exact final-interface output.
- **Tested revision and interface** Signed head `49ef74e33f` (tree `ec521fd5f0`), interactive CLI, 160-column PTY, isolated config for each case. The rebuilt binary reported this revision. Its SHA-256 before and after all four PTY runs was `c7ee0ccc580f1b032f3bea9bd32f51ec821761fd80b1cbdb72ab99c0f3cb565a`. Apple’s linker emitted a compact-unwind-size warning for the debug link; all four processes exited 0.
- **Exact-output evidence and observed result** The first visible lines in French, with terminal styling removed, were:

```text
Saisissez une valeur pour plugins.entries.zpi1_WyJleGFtcGxlIiwidG9vbCIsImV4YW1wbGUiXQ.config.password
Saisissez une valeur pour plugins.entries.zpi1_WyJleGFtcGxlIiwidG9vbCIsImV4YW1wbGUiXQ.config.region: fixture-value
```

- **Checks skipped** Full workspace testing is left to CI. The local checks cover all translations and both changed terminal paths.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. The two human-readable prompts follow the selected locale. Existing commands, arguments and stored values keep their meanings.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps for existing users? None.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback** Revert the localization commit, `b75bead14d`, on a review branch.
- **Feature flags or config toggles** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms** A value prompt shows a Fluent key or omits the path.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. The predecessor #11812 merged. This PR implements its localization follow-up.

prs.title: feat(plugins): add host-mediated agent wake dispatch (dispatch.wake)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds `@unstable(feature = plugins-wit-v0-dispatch)` interface `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` (`wake(target-agent, prompt) -> result<_, dispatch-error>`) and gated `import dispatch;` on `world tool-plugin` (`wit/v0/tool.wit`), gated by `PluginPermission::AgentDispatch` (`agent_dispatch`).
  - Adds `AgentWakeBackend` / `AgentWakeService` on `PluginHostServices` (`zeroclaw-plugins`), `OptionalImports::dispatch` linker gating + coherence checks, `PluginState::wake_agent` (enforcing `ToolExecute` call-frame phase, host-call budget, grant, and target/prompt grammar), and host-owned `WasmTool::caller_alias`.
  - Adds operator grant fields `PluginEntryConfig::{dispatch_agents, dispatch_rate_per_min}` in `zeroclaw-config` (default-closed `[]` and `30`/min, strict alias/padding/bounds validation), `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool` in `zeroclaw-api`, and `manifest_owns_instance_state` row seeding so `agent_dispatch`-only manifests receive a `[[plugins.entries]]` row on install.
  - Implements `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/plugin_wake.rs` and wires `plugin_host_services_with_wake` / `register_plugin_tools` in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/mod.rs` under the ADR-016 exception approved in #12417: live-config target authorization, `MAX_PLUGIN_WAKE_DEPTH = 2`, per-instance continuous token bucket, per-`(instance, target)` wake coalescing, `AgentExecutionCapability` admission, `TaskKind::PeerInbox` durable `TaskRecord` registration/settlement, and `CostTracker` scoping.
  - **CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`):** Increments the hardcoded `wit/v0/` input-inventory assertion in `Check (plugins cranelift runtime)` (`Run runtime plugin admission regressions`, line 1241) from `17` to `18` to account for the new `wit/v0/dispatch.wit`, matching the `expected_inputs` update in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/r5_namespace_tests.rs`. Appends `--test dispatch_plugin_e2e` to the existing `Run plugin component tests` step and adds a `Run runtime plugin wake dispatch tests` step to the cranelift runtime leg (`cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib tools::plugin_wake`). No workflow triggers, runner labels, permissions, pinned actions, or secrets changed.
  - Adds `tool-dispatch-fixture` WASM guest + `dispatch_plugin_e2e`, unit tests across all touched crates, and documentation (`plugin-protocol.md`, `plugin-manifest-fields.md`, `writing-a-tool-plugin.md`, `CHANGELOG-next.md`).
- **Scope boundary:** `tool-plugin` world only; `channel-plugin` and `memory-plugin` do not import `dispatch`. No synchronous plugin-to-agent RPC, no ambient target grants, no edits to `send_message_to_peer.rs`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` changes only the `len(inputs) != 18` inventory count and the two test selections above. A dispatch-granted `WasmTool` reports `requires_unrestricted_principal`, so restricted (non-admin) principals never receive it. `wit/v0` remains experimental (no `.frozen` marker); `@unstable(feature = plugins-wit-v0-dispatch)` keeps existing `wit/v0` plugins linking unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Additive WIT import, optional `PluginEntryConfig` fields, `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool`, runtime adapter wiring, and the `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` inventory entry in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` / `r5_namespace_tests.rs`. Default-closed (`dispatch_agents = []`) until an operator explicitly grants target aliases for an `agent_dispatch` plugin.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12416, Related #12417

### What this does, simply

Tool plugins run in a fresh store per call with no network listener or access to the agent loop. This adds a gated `dispatch.wake(target-agent, prompt)` host import so an operator-authorized tool plugin can nudge a target agent into an asynchronous turn—coalescing burst wakes onto at most one queued follow-up turn, capping recursion at 2 hops, and enforcing live per-instance rate limits and target allowlists. It also updates the runtime plugin admission step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (and its matching `r5_namespace_tests.rs` list) to expect 18 WIT input files instead of 17 now that `wit/v0/dispatch.wit` exists.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; automated WASM component E2E (`dispatch_plugin_e2e`) and runtime mock-provider coalescing/panic/cost tests (`plugin_wake`) exercise the full boundary directly.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Required CI runs workspace format, clippy (with CI's pinned toolchain), `zeroclaw-api`, `zeroclaw-config`, `zeroclaw-plugins`, `zeroclaw-runtime` (including the `r5_namespace_tests` fixture-receipt proof), architecture runner-label checks, and docs/links checks.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None after this head. Earlier revisions had one: required CI selected neither `dispatch_plugin_e2e` nor the runtime `tools::plugin_wake` tests, because the default-feature Test job does not enable `plugins-wasm-cranelift` and the cranelift runtime leg selects modules explicitly. This head adds both selections to the plugin backend job.
- **Commands run and tail output (on head `f72f78a8ff` / prior `8ac25c5f9b` before the 2-line inventory update):**

  ```text
  $ cargo fmt --all -- --check
  (exit 0)

  $ python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))"
  (exit 0)

  $ cargo test --test architecture ci_runner_labels
  test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 80 filtered out; finished in 0.01s

  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --features plugins-wasm-cranelift r5_namespace_tests -- --list
  29 tests, 0 benchmarks

  $ bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh upstream/master
  Summary: 0 error(s)

  $ bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh upstream/master
  🚫 Errors...........0

  $ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --all-targets -- -D warnings
  Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 28.42s

  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-api --lib
  test result: ok. 323 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.01s

  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib plugin_entry_
  test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1984 filtered out; finished in 0.01s

  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --lib -- --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 478 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 11.42s

  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-plugins --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --test dispatch_plugin_e2e
  test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 16.89s

  $ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --features plugins-wasm-cranelift plugin_wake
  test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 6311 filtered out; finished in 8.04s

  $ cargo test --bin zeroclaw --features plugins-wasm channel_instance
  test result: ok. 17 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 732 filtered out; finished in 0.01s
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Verified compiled `tool-dispatch-fixture` (`wasm32-wasip2`) end-to-end through both `WasmTool` (`dispatch_plugin_e2e`) and `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend` (`wasm_tool_dispatch_reaches_the_runtime_backend_end_to_end`).
  - Verified under local `rustc 1.99.0` that `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --features plugins-wasm-cranelift --all-targets -- -D warnings` surfaces only pre-existing lints in untouched files (`crates/zeroclaw-providers/src/lib.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/{upload,dispatch}.rs`, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/stream_guard.rs`) and zero warnings in `plugin_wake.rs` or `tools/mod.rs`.
  - Note: in default parallel execution on an earlier run, pre-existing `component_logging::tests::plugin_log_queue_enforces_byte_bounds` flaked once on shared queue bytes; under `--test-threads=1` all 478 `zeroclaw-plugins` lib tests pass.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no UI or terminal presentation changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Head `f20b7dd83b` (lease fix on top of `e51b8e968c`, which merges upstream master `9111460994`). Locally on this head: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-plugins -p zeroclaw-runtime --features zeroclaw-runtime/plugins-wasm-cranelift,zeroclaw-plugins/plugins-wasm-cranelift --all-targets -- -D warnings` (clean); `zeroclaw-plugins` lib with `plugins-wasm-cranelift` (485 passed, 1 ignored); `dispatch_plugin_e2e` (5 passed); `zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::plugin_wake` (22 passed, stable across 3 repeated runs on `f20b7dd83b`, including the HTTP-mock cases, the principal regression, the accepted-wake-loss and SOP step-scope regressions, the revoked-grant-while-waiting regression, the two follow-up registration-retry regressions, and the lifecycle-lease regression on the real coordinator); `zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::plugin_live_config` (3 passed, including the bounded-delegate attribution guard); docs quality and links gates. The principal regression was confirmed to fail with the override removed; the two accepted-wake-loss regressions and the step-scope regression were written first and failed on `5229d4395a`; `accepted_wake_survives_a_transient_followup_registration_failure` fails with the requeue disabled, and `registration_backoff_releases_the_finished_turns_lifecycle_lease` fails (`active_turns` = 1) without the lease release. Earlier command tails above are from `f72f78a8ff`. Interface: WIT `zeroclaw:plugin/dispatch` + `PluginEntryConfig` + `RuntimeAgentWakeBackend`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Granted `dispatch.wake` schedules a coalesced `PeerInbox` turn attributed to `InternalPrincipal::PluginTool` with target cost scoping; ungranted/padded/oversized/rate-limited/deep wakes fail closed with the closed `dispatch-error` variants.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `zeroclaw-runtime` / full workspace test suite deferred to CI after verifying all targeted suites above locally.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: adds `PluginPermission::AgentDispatch` (`agent_dispatch`) gating the `tool-plugin` world's `dispatch` import. Mitigated by default-closed `PluginEntryConfig::dispatch_agents = []`, live config evaluation on every call, `MAX_PLUGIN_WAKE_DEPTH = 2`, per-instance token-bucket rate limiting (`dispatch_rate_per_min`), host-owned `caller_alias` attribution, `ToolExecute`-only frame gating, and withholding dispatch-granted tools from restricted principals (`requires_unrestricted_principal`), since a wake does not carry the caller's live agent/tool selectors into the target turn. A wake issued from a headless SOP step carries that step's tool scope into the woken turn (per wake, coalesced follow-ups included), and a wake is accepted onto a slot only once a worker owns it, so a failed setup never drops a wake that already returned success; a follow-up whose durable registration fails transiently is requeued and retried with capped backoff, re-checking the live grant and target before each attempt; the finished turn's lifecycle lease is released before draining, so an idle target stays deletable during that wait.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. A granted tool plugin supplies a prompt the target agent sees. Operator target grants, the 1024-byte bound, and the target agent's risk profile limit its reach; the prompt remains untrusted input.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (`wit/v0` is experimental and `@unstable(feature = plugins-wit-v0-dispatch)` leaves existing `wit/v0` components unaffected; new `PluginEntryConfig` fields default to empty/`None`).
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes (`[[plugins.entries]].dispatch_agents` and `[[plugins.entries]].dispatch_rate_per_min`, both optional with fail-closed defaults).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: No action required for existing installs; operators enabling an `agent_dispatch` plugin explicitly configure `plugins.entries.<key>.dispatch_agents` (and optionally `dispatch_rate_per_min`) to allow target wakes.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set `dispatch_agents = []` on the affected `[[plugins.entries]]` rows in live config; new plugin wakes are denied without a rebuild. For a code rollback after merge, revert the merged PR commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `plugins.entries[].dispatch_agents = []` (default) disables all wake targets; WIT surface is gated behind `plugins-wit-v0-dispatch`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Wakes return `dispatch-error::access-denied` (`dispatch_agents` empty/missing) or `rate-limited` / `unavailable`, logged via `zeroclaw_runtime::tools::plugin_wake` with `action = Reject` or `Dispatch`.

prs.title: feat(channels): route external peers to an explicit destination
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Stacked on #12116: the first commit is #12116's head (patch-identical), and the remaining commits implement peer routing and preserve it with reply pacing enabled. Review the increment over #12116.
- **Reshaped after @JordanTheJet's review of 2026-11-20:** the route is generic, the channel declares whether routes apply, and the channel renders the mention. No shared crate names a channel type: the Discord branches in `send_message_to_peer` (including #12116's `channel_ref_is_discord`), `send_via` and route validation are gone. This is the split from the review: the generic route plus Discord as the first channel that supports it; other channels can declare support later.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Some channels identify an external peer by user rather than by a place to post. On Discord an `external_peers` entry is a user ID, but messages are posted to channels and threads, and bots cannot DM other bots. `send_message_to_peer` and `send_via` used that user ID (for `send_via`, the group's *first* entry) as the destination, so sends failed with Discord's 404 `Unknown Channel`, and which peer `send_via` picked depended on list order.
  - This adds an operator-chosen per-peer route, `[peer_groups.<name>.routes."<peer>"]`, with `destination` (where to post, in the channel's own format) and an optional `mention`, following the decisions in #10926 (comment of 2026-11-06).
  - `Channel::supports_peer_routes()` (default `false`, Discord `true`) is the declaration, next to `supports_native_polls` and `supports_outbound_send`. A delivery is checked against it before anything is sent, through `PeerAddressing` (`Direct`, `Peer`, `Routed`): an unrouted peer on a channel that needs routes is refused with guidance, and a route on a channel that doesn't support them is refused instead of ignored.
  - `SendMessage` carries the routed peer (`routed_peer`) next to `allowed_mentions`. `with_routed_peer` sets the ping rule: nobody, or with `mention = true` only the routed peer. The channel renders the mention and owns the rule: Discord derives it from the routed peer itself rather than trusting the caller, sends the peer ID in Discord's form (a route key may be written with a leading `@`), applies it to every chunk and attachment payload, prefixes `<@id>`, and refuses a routed message aimed at an interaction reply.
- **The route rules are unchanged, with their tests:** admission stays in `external_peers`, a wildcard can't be routed, an ignored peer isn't routable, a route only applies through groups the sending agent is in, conflicting routes across two groups fail and name both, and a routed message can only ping the routed peer, and only with `mention = true`.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Discord is the only channel that declares peer routes. Other channels keep delivering to the external peer itself; Matrix and Signal are left to separate slices.
  - No peer selector and no group default for `send_via`: a group or channel target posts only when exactly one eligible routed peer exists. Explicit per-peer sends stay with `send_message_to_peer`.
  - The route is not checked against the Discord channel's `channel_ids`, which keeps its meaning as the listening filter. No `thread` field: `destination` is the ID the sender posts to.
  - Unrouted sends and sends on other channels keep their payloads; `allowed_mentions` is omitted unless a route sets it.
- **Blast radius:**
  - `zeroclaw-api`: `SendMessage` gains `allowed_mentions` and `routed_peer` (both `None` by default, set by both constructors), so struct-literal sites get two more fields. New `RoutedPeer`, `PeerAddressing`, `PeerRouteError`, and the defaulted `Channel::supports_peer_routes`.
  - The cron/announcement `DeliveryFn` gains a final `PeerAddressing` argument. `deliver_announcement` keeps its signature and passes `Direct`; the new `deliver_announcement_addressed` carries the rest.
  - The Discord sender builds every chunk through one helper, `chunk_payload`. For plain chunks it produces the same request body as the previous `DiscordOutgoing::text` path (tested).
  - Config validation no longer checks Discord ID formats or rejects routes on other channel types: config can't see a channel's declaration, so that check moved to send time. On such a channel `send_via` refuses a route for the recipient in any of the agent's groups covering it, and names the group that sets it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10926. Depends on #12116.

### What this does, simply

A peer group lists who an agent may talk to on a channel. On Discord, an outside participant (another bot or a person) is listed by user ID, but a bot can't post to a user ID: it posts into a channel or thread, and bots can't DM other bots. So asking an agent to message such a peer failed with a confusing "Unknown Channel" error.

With this change, the operator says where messages for that peer should go:

```toml
[peer_groups.discord_peers]
channel = "discord.main"
agents = ["assistant"]
external_peers = ["111111111111111111"]

[peer_groups.discord_peers.routes."111111111111111111"]
destination = "333333333333333333"   # channel or thread ID to post in
mention = true                       # optional: start with a ping of the peer
```

`send_message_to_peer` to that peer, or `send_via` to that group, then posts in the configured channel or thread. The result names the destination, so the agent knows it posted in a shared place rather than a private message. The route never lets anyone new in, can't be used for an ignored peer, and only applies through groups the sending agent is in. If two of the agent's groups route the same peer to different places, the send fails and names both groups. A routed message can only ping the routed peer, and only when `mention = true`.

The Discord channel says it needs routes; no code outside it mentions Discord. Another channel with the same problem only has to declare support and render its own mention.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional; unit coverage is focused, and a live Discord check shows the end-to-end effect.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `discord` (agent tool calls `send_message_to_peer` and `send_via`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Discord bot in a server with a test channel or thread. An agent on `discord.<alias>`, and a peer group containing that agent with another bot or user ID in `external_peers`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Without a route, ask the agent to `send_message_to_peer` the external peer on the Discord channel ref.
  2. Add the `routes."<peer ID>"` block above with your channel or thread ID, reload, and repeat.
  3. Optionally set `mention = true`, and include `@everyone` or another user's mention in the message text.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Step 1 fails with an error explaining how to add a route. Step 2 posts in the destination, and the tool result names it. In step 3 the message starts with the peer's mention, and only the peer is pinged.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Step 1 fails with Discord's `404 Unknown Channel`, because the user ID is used as a channel ID (#12116 replaces this with an actionable error). There is no way to route.

### How I tested

- **Reply-pacing regression at `1ee29284e`:** With a real Discord channel wrapped using a nonzero `reply_min_interval_secs`, the configured peer route failed with `RoutesUnsupported` on the preceding code. After forwarding the inner channel's capability, the same test accepts the routed peer and rejects an unrouted external peer with `RouteRequired`. On this revision, 216 Discord module tests and all 19 pacing-wrapper tests passed (`--locked --no-default-features --features channel-discord`); channel-crate formatting passed. No live Discord delivery was made.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust lint and test jobs cover the API, config, tools, channels, runtime and gateway changes; Docs Style and the links gate cover the two Markdown files.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live Discord API call in CI; the payload shape is covered by unit tests.
- **Commands run and tail output** (aarch64 Linux, rustc 1.97.1, on `425b93579` over master `665904f6d`; suites on a 20-core build host, fmt and docs gates also on the author's host. The earlier revision `936a112ed` differed only by one doc-comment link (CI's `cargo doc` rejected a redundant explicit link target); on it, `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`, `cargo fmt --check` and clippy on `zeroclaw-channels` are clean):

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  -> clean
cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets -> clean
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-channels \
  -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-plugins --all-targets -- -D warnings -> clean
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api --lib
  test result: ok. 324 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- route peer_group multi_agent
  test result: ok. 84 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- send_via i18n
  test result: ok. 39 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib -- discord orchestrator::tests::routed announcement_delivery deliver_announcement whatsapp
  test result: ok. 351 passed; 0 failed
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- send_message_to_peer cron i18n locale fluent
  test result: ok. 436 passed; 0 failed   (route tests also run in isolated child processes, each required to report "1 passed")
scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh    -> Summary: 0 error(s)
scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh      -> Checked 1 local docs link target(s)
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh -> passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `send_message_to_peer`'s route tests run in an isolated child process with a delivery stand-in that checks `PeerAddressing` the way the orchestrator does; the orchestrator test checks the real `deliver_announcement_addressed` against a recording channel that declares or doesn't declare routes.
  - Routed replies queued by `send_via` always leave through `send_final` with the routed peer attached, never through draft finalization (a peer route is only recorded together with a resolved target channel). This was checked in the code; there is no end-to-end turn test for it.
  - Not verified: a live Discord post from this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (tool results and Discord message payloads only; no UI change).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `425b93579` and `936a112ed` (doc-comment change only), the commands above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the tests above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `zeroclaw-desktop` is excluded locally because its GTK system libraries are not on this host (CI excludes it too). The full workspace `cargo test` was not run; the workspace builds with all targets, and the focused suites above cover the changed modules.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** A configured route can post outside the Discord channel's `channel_ids` listening filter. It is operator-configured only. It applies only to a peer the sending agent's own groups already admit and do not ignore, and conflicting routes fail closed. The docs state that everyone with access to the destination can read routed messages.
- New external network calls? No. Same Discord message endpoint, to a different operator-chosen channel.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. IDs are synthetic, e.g. `111111111111111111`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No new untrusted input. Routed message text comes from the agent as before, and the explicit `allowed_mentions` policy stops it from pinging anyone except the routed peer.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes, with one Discord behavior change.** `send_via` to a Discord peer group, or to a Discord channel one group covers, that has external peers but no single routed peer now fails with guidance instead of posting to the first external peer's user ID. That post already failed with `404 Unknown Channel`. Groups with no external peers keep their existing rejection, and other channels are unchanged.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New optional `[peer_groups.<name>.routes."<peer>"]` with `destination` and `mention`. Existing configs load unchanged; a route outside `external_peers`, a wildcard or duplicate key, or an empty destination is a load-time error, and a route on a channel that doesn't support routes fails at send time.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: none needed. To deliver to a Discord external peer, add a route as shown above.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert` of this PR's commit. Routes are opt-in config; without them, the only change is the clearer `send_via` rejection described above.

prs.title: feat(webchat): wire ACP startup cutover and switch dashboard transport to /acp
prs.body:
## Summary

This final layer lets operators switch the dashboard from `/ws/chat` to ACP at gateway startup. With `[gateway].acp_webchat_cutover = true`, the gateway imports readable legacy `gw_*` conversations, advertises ACP in the served HTML, and returns HTTP 410 from `/ws/chat`. With the flag off, the dashboard uses `/ws/chat`.

- **Base branch** `master`, stacked on `feat/acp-gateway-auth-and-reconnect`
- **What changed and why**
  - The conversation picker and session API keep the existing WebChat `gw_` key format. History and rename accept both the full key and bare session ID.
  - The ACP adapter resumes a saved chat and reattaches to an active turn after reload. Replayed completions refresh the saved transcript while keeping displayed tool cards and thinking. The saved answer appears once. Scoped Clear waits for ACP to close the active conversation before enabling a new one. Switching conversations keeps the composer disabled until the new socket is ready. A refused resume closes the socket and stops automatic reconnects.
  - Operator WebChat reads and writes use ACP during cutover. Other conversations retain their legacy REST access and agent lifecycle handling.
  - Delete cancels the running turn, removes the old operator WebChat copy, and clears the ACP transcript. Tool-only assistant steps with no text are omitted from REST history.
  - An unreadable legacy transcript reserves its session ID in the import ledger. Resume refuses the session while the import is pending. Repairing the file and restarting the gateway restores its history under the original ID. Readable transcripts still import at startup.
- **Scope boundary** The startup switch defaults to `false`. Removing `/ws/chat` and the voice route split are follow-up work.
- **Blast radius** `zeroclaw-config`, gateway startup, ACP relay and dashboard session routes, the infra session store, the channels ACP back-channel, and the web dashboard. ACP `session/request_permission` carries `_meta.zeroclaw.expiresAtUnixMs` for IDE clients as well.
- **Linked issue** Depends on #12653

### What this does, simply

Operators can bring their existing dashboard conversations over to ACP, reopen them from the picker, and continue a reply across a browser reload. The gateway switch lets operators choose when to move.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface exercised** `surface: web`.
- **Setup** Enable cutover and start a gateway with an agent and an existing `gw_*` session.
- **Steps** Open the dashboard, select the imported conversation, verify its history, send a prompt, and reload before the reply completes.
- **Expected on this branch** The replacement socket reattaches and the browser displays the completed reply once.
- **Prior behavior on `master`** WebChat connected to `/ws/chat` and kept its own transcript and transport.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on** `CI Required Gate` covers workspace lint, build and tests. Focused checks below exercise the specific cutover changes.
- **Commands run and results**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` exited 0.
  - `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-infra --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` finished successfully.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib acp_ws_cutover_restores_legacy_dashboard_session` (1 passed) checks the live HTTP and WebSocket routes, picker response fields, both REST key forms, continued channel access, and removal of the legacy transcript after Delete.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib legacy_gateway_import` (6 passed) verifies import, retry and preserved deletion. `operator_webchat_routes_ignore_other_sessions_and_empty_assistant_steps` also passed.
  - `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib acp_channel::tests --features channel-acp-server` (33 passed) checks the approval deadline using the clock independently of the production helper.
  - `npm run build`, `npm run test:acp` (6 passed) and the session lifecycle test (65 passed).
- **Import recovery at `7eb780d41`** The JSONL regression imported a readable chat alongside a corrupt transcript, reopened the ACP store, verified the pending ID could neither resume nor be claimed by a new session, and recovered its history under the same ID after repair. Six import tests and six ACP web tests passed. Scoped infra Clippy passed with warnings denied.
- **Scoped Clear and replay follow-up at `aff5fcaa9`** The ACP server tests passed for cancellation of a parked turn before close returns and for reporting a committed transcript on successful completion. The dashboard build, 103 session lifecycle tests and six ACP socket tests passed. The reload regression covers history arriving with and without the completed answer, including identical answers in separate turns.
- **Replay display follow-up at `98ce3968f`** Both reload tests keep the earlier thinking, the replayed thinking, and the completed tool card when the first history fetch includes or misses the current reply. Identical replies in separate turns each appear once. The dashboard build, 103 lifecycle tests, and six ACP tests passed.
- **Beyond CI** With cutover enabled, Chromium opened an imported JSONL conversation through the picker and rendered its saved answer. It streamed a new reply. During another streamed turn, it reloaded the page, opened a new `/acp` socket, received an active-turn reattach acknowledgment, and rendered the completed reply once. A corrupt JSONL transcript alongside the readable ones was logged and the gateway still started.
- **Known coverage gap** The browser run used a loopback gateway with a scripted streaming provider and pairing disabled. The pairing and OIDC browser matrix remains for staging.
- **Visual interface evidence** Exact final-interface output from Chromium at `b41555c40`.
- **Action and observed output** Selected “Imported conversation smoke” and saw “Imported smoke answer.” Reloaded during the second streamed turn and saw one additional “Streamed reply complete,” with an active-turn reattach acknowledgment on the new socket.
- **Commands intentionally skipped** Full workspace tests are covered by CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or filesystem access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets, tokens, or credential handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in the diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced or changed? No.

The session routes retain operator authentication and enforce owner and surface checks on ACP-backed operations.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes, with cutover opt-in.
- Config, environment, or CLI surface changed? Yes, `[gateway].acp_webchat_cutover`.
- Rust or toolchain floor changed? No.
- To upgrade, stop the old gateway, enable `[gateway].acp_webchat_cutover`, and restart. The ACP database is `sessions/acp-sessions.db`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback** Set `[gateway].acp_webchat_cutover = false` and restart to return to `/ws/chat`.
- **Feature flag** `[gateway].acp_webchat_cutover`, default `false`.
- Each transport writes to its own store. Re-enabling cutover skips previously imported keys, so turns written during rollback stay in the legacy store. Back up both stores if those turns must be retained.
- **Observable symptoms** The disabled legacy socket returns HTTP 410 during cutover. The gateway logs unreadable legacy transcripts and fails startup if the configured legacy store is unavailable.

prs.title: fix(tools): reject send_message_to_peer to Discord external peers with an actionable error
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `send_message_to_peer` hands any known non-agent target (an entry from a
    peer group's `external_peers`) to announcement delivery. On Discord that
    delivery posts to `/channels/{recipient}/messages`, but Discord external
    peers are user IDs, so the send fails with Discord's opaque
    `404 Unknown Channel (10003)` and the agent cannot tell what to do instead.
  - The tool now rejects that case before delivery, using configuration only:
    the target has already been validated as a configured external peer (not an
    agent alias), and the channel ref's type is `discord` (same case-insensitive
    `<type>.<alias>` split that delivery uses). No ID-syntax guessing and no
    network calls; Discord user and channel IDs are both snowflakes.
  - The error explains why (user ID vs channel/thread ID, bots cannot DM bots,
    peer groups carry no channel mapping) and what to do: post in a channel or
    thread shared with the peer and mention the peer there.
- **Scope boundary:** No new config keys, no peer → channel/thread routing, no
  DM path. Peer-agent targets (in-process delivery) and external peers on other
  channel types are unchanged. `send_via` is not changed: it resolves its
  recipient from the first `external_peers` entry through `Channel::send` in
  `zeroclaw-tools`, a separate path whose recipient semantics belong to the
  routing design discussion in #10926.
- **Blast radius:** `send_message_to_peer` calls whose target is an external
  peer on a Discord channel. Those sends could not be delivered before; they
  now fail earlier with a clearer message.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10926 (identity vs. delivery-destination
  design; the Discord evidence for this failure is in
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10926#issuecomment-6511170110).
  This PR does not resolve it.

### What this does, simply

Agents can message configured peers with `send_message_to_peer`. For a human
or bot that is not a ZeroClaw agent, the tool sends through the channel's
normal delivery, which on Discord needs a channel or thread ID. Peer lists on
Discord hold user IDs, so the message went to a "channel" that does not exist
and Discord answered with a bare 404. This PR stops that send up front and
tells the agent to talk to the peer in a shared channel or thread instead. How
peers should be routed on Discord is left to the separate design discussion.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the change is a pre-delivery rejection
  covered by a unit test that exercises `SendMessageToPeerTool::execute`;
  reproducing the live 404 needs a Discord bot pair.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the runtime crate's
  lib tests, clippy and fmt cover the changed file.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no live Discord round-trip in CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - RED on master 5a51398dd with only the new execute tests applied:
    `discord_external_peer_is_rejected_before_channel_delivery ... FAILED`
    (`a Discord user target must not report delivery`: master hands the user
    ID to announcement delivery; in the unit test no live Discord handler is
    registered, so it reports success where production gets the 404).
    `non_discord_external_peer_still_reaches_delivery ... ok`.
  - GREEN, `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- --skip tunnel::tailscale`
    on default features and again with every `tool-*`/`tools-external`
    feature: all three new tests pass and every other `send_message_to_peer`
    test passes. 5846 and 5861 passed respectively, 0 failed, 8 ignored
    (run with `umask 077`; under a group-writable umask, three `rpc::local`
    endpoint-lock tests reject the temp dir, which is unrelated to this change).
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`,
    `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh <changed file>`: clean.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The original failure was seen
  on one deployment: a `send_message_to_peer` call targeting a second bot's
  Discord user ID returned `404 Unknown Channel (10003)`. The new error path
  was not exercised against live Discord.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** `tunnel::tailscale` lib
  tests were skipped locally because they reconfigure the host's Tailscale
  Serve state.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
  (test IDs are synthetic)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No (the
  error echoes the target the model itself passed, already Debug-quoted)

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (the rejected sends could not succeed before)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.
