prs.title: feat(gateway): add OIDC auth, principal scoping, and turn reconnect replay to /acp
prs.body:
## Summary

Dashboard WebChat and editor ACP sessions are moving onto a shared turn and session lifecycle. This layer adds dashboard identity and reconnect support to the ACP gateway.

- **Base branch:** `master` (stacked on `feat/acp-session-management-and-import`)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Dashboard sign-ins can connect to `/acp` when pairing is required. A scoped sign-in must select a granted agent. It can open one live session per socket, with an 8 MiB frame and message cap and the same per-sign-in and account conversation budgets as `/ws/chat`. The two transports share those budgets. To reconnect, a replacement socket sends `resumeSession` and can reuse its own detached conversation’s slot even when all four slots are occupied.
  - Scoped sessions use principal-owned storage and memory and the principal's tool grants. Steering, MCP initialization, and external channel seeding are restricted to operator access. A changed grant set closes the scoped socket and cancels its turns.
  - The gateway keeps a detached turn running and lets its owner restore and reattach. Replay metadata lives in ACP `params._meta` and `result._meta`, permission request IDs retain the `zc-out-` prefix, and concurrent prompts return `SESSION_BUSY` immediately. A prompt for an unopened session returns `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`.
- **Scope boundary:** The dashboard frontend opts into this transport in #12654. Signed-in callers can reach `/acp` as soon as this PR lands.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-gateway` ACP, dashboard session authorization and conversation admission, `zeroclaw-channels` ACP session construction, the shared infra session queue, and the runtime helpers used to apply principal tool posture.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12652

### What this does, simply

A signed-in dashboard user can reconnect to a running ACP turn under the same permissions. Existing ACP clients retain standard prompt errors and can ignore the new replay metadata.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- Sign in as a scoped user, connect to `/acp?agent=<allowed-agent>`, and open a session. Verify a different account cannot restore it and a grant change closes the original socket with `4403`.
- Start a slow turn, disconnect, then reconnect with the same sign-in and `resumeSession=<id>` in the URL. Call `session/resume` and `_zeroclaw/session/reattach` to receive the remaining events and completion.
- With a paired ACP client, submit two prompts on the same active session. The second receives `SESSION_BUSY` while the first finishes.

### How I tested

- `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib scoped_acp` passed all 4 signed-in gateway tests. These cover owner isolation, filtered tools, grant narrowing, shared conversation limits, ACP errors, steering, frame size, and completing a replayed approval at full capacity.
- `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib acp::tests` passed all 8 gateway ACP tests, including replay order, cursor scoping, owner checks, and shutdown.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- On `c6a95ef0c`, the unmodified acp-tui 0.1.1 client received a `file_read` permission request with a `zc-out-` ID. The client's Allow once handler sent the selected response, the tool read a fixture file, and the client displayed the file marker and `stopReason: end_turn`.
- The six-client text and restore results in the conversation were captured on earlier revisions. Dashboard replay and the production web build were verified on #12654 with the updated wire format.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Interactive browser and external-client runs are separate from CI.
- **Visual interface evidence:** The frontend ships with #12654.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `Yes`
- New external network calls? `No`
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `Yes`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No`
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `No`
- **Risk and mitigation:** Dashboard session cookies can authenticate at `/acp`. Origin checks, live grant checks, principal-owned storage, and shared conversation budgets apply. A supplied pairing credential takes precedence over a cookie.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes for ACPv1 prompt, permission, and session handling.` Replay adds optional payload metadata and `_zeroclaw/` extension methods. The gateway still accepts pairing credentials as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No new settings or commands.` The existing gateway `?agent=` selector is required for scoped sign-ins.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the upstream merge of this PR. If #12654 has landed, roll back that dependent layer first.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** #12654 controls the dashboard transport. The cookie-authenticated ACP route takes effect when this PR lands.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Scoped sign-ins receive unexpected upgrade errors, prompt admission fails on an idle session, or a reattached socket loses updates.

prs.body:
## Summary

> **Draft:** Local validation has unresolved failures, and the local review
> remains **FAIL**. Exact-head hosted Security and the CI Required Gate have
> failed. Screenshot attachments are pending. This proposal is not ready for
> review or merge.

- **Base branch:** `master`. This staged slice depends on #11880 and on the
  Anthropic per-attempt accounting prerequisite #12478.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add the staged Goal execution and accounting foundation so a Goal can
    retain known usage, fence its session and epoch, and stop before another
    model call when accounting is uncertain.
  - Preserve ordinary spending limits and the existing usage ledger while
    accounting for actual provider/model attempts, including fallback.
  - Preserve usage and errors across interruption and settlement, and
    serialize immediate fencing with initial Goal dispatch.
  - Make shared configuration editing retain unrelated existing validation
    warnings without permitting a related invalid edit; show those warnings
    at the changed dashboard save and toggle boundaries.
  - Authorize the complete configuration write set before returning
    cross-field validation details; PATCH `test` requires Config read access.
- **Scope boundary:** This slice does not provide complete production Goal
  admission, Matrix/ZeroCode parity, automatic restart execution, a second
  ledger, a new provider router, deployment, or live-room validation. Later
  receiving hosts must preserve resumable handling of a safely accounted
  ordinary spend-limit refusal. The existing `/goal` channel catalog entry is
  not advertised or parsed as a built-in command in this prefix; a later
  receiving slice must wire the command before it becomes available again.
- **Blast radius:** Goal and accounting Rust APIs, agent-turn settlement,
  provider attempt attribution, SQLite task/intent persistence, shared
  configuration validation, gateway authorization, and dashboard saves.
  The control-plane SQLite connection uses WAL with `synchronous=FULL` and
  requests `fullfsync` where supported; this can increase write latency for
  non-Goal tasks using the same store.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8303 and #10341. Depends on #11880 and #12478.
  Runtime-placement proposal #12407 has an approving review but is unmerged;
  its proposed row does not cover every runtime behavior in this candidate.
  The separately reviewed policy record and an accepted receiving use case
  remain prerequisites to merge.

### What this does, simply

A long-running Goal needs to know what it spent and whether it is safe to
continue, even if a request fails or is interrupted. This slice adds those
foundations while retaining the normal spending limits. It also makes
pre-existing configuration warnings visible when unrelated settings are saved.
The remaining stack supplies the production Goal entry points and surfaces.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the dashboard warning behavior.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, configuration editor.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Node.js 24+, npm, a browser, two shells and clean
  checkouts of base `cda933e6...` and candidate `f8359c4f...`. The recorded
  before/after comparison used the earlier candidate `c2663143...`; the after
  side was also repeated on `f8359c4f...`. Ports 59153 and 59154 must be free. The
  fixture below binds loopback and keeps synthetic settings in memory; it is not
  a gateway and does not exercise authentication or disk persistence.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Start the fixture below in the first shell. In the `web/` directory of one
     checkout, run `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`, then
     `ZEROCLAW_GATEWAY_HOST=127.0.0.1 ZEROCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=59153 npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 59154 --strictPort`.
  2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:59154/config` in a new browser tab. Select
     Scheduler, change Max Tasks from 64 to 65 and press that section's Save.
  3. Change Max Tasks to 66, select Gateway, change Websocket Ping Interval
     Secs from 30 to 45, then press Save all.
  4. Visit `http://127.0.0.1:59153/fixture-state` to inspect the two mock
     PATCHes. Stop the two processes, restart the fixture to reset its values,
     and repeat with the other checkout in a new browser tab.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Both actions save the specified values
  to the fixture and display the returned Goal-cost warning. Save all clears
  the global unsaved banner; the Gateway section may still display a stale
  unsaved-change footer.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** At `cda933e6...`, the same fixture
  recorded the same two PATCHes, but neither save action displayed the returned
  warning. The stale Gateway footer also appeared.

<summary>Runnable loopback-only mock for the steps above</summary>

```sh
node --input-type=commonjs <<'NODE'
// Disposable, in-memory presentation fixture; it does not access a gateway.
const http = require('node:http');

const values = {
  'scheduler.max_tasks': 64,
  'scheduler.max_concurrent': 4,
  'gateway.websocket_ping_interval_secs': 30,
};
const writes = [];
const sections = ['scheduler', 'gateway'].map(key => ({
  key, label: key === 'scheduler' ? 'Scheduler' : 'Gateway', help: '',
  has_picker: false, completed: true, ready: true, group: 'Agent',
  is_quickstart: false, shape: 'direct_form', cost_category: '',
}));
const warnings = [{
  code: 'pre_existing_validation_error',
  path: 'goal.default_cost_limit_usd',
  message: 'goal.default_cost_limit_usd must be finite and non-negative',
}];

function entries(prefix) {
  return Object.entries(values)
    .filter(([path]) => !prefix || path === prefix || path.startsWith(`${prefix}.`))
    .map(([path, value]) => ({
      path, category: path.split('.')[0], section: path.split('.')[0],
      kind: 'integer', type_hint: 'u64', value: String(value),
      populated: true, is_secret: false,
    }));
}

const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
  const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://127.0.0.1');
  const send = (status, body) => {
    res.writeHead(status, { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'cache-control': 'no-store' });
    res.end(JSON.stringify(body));
  };
  if (req.method === 'GET' && url.pathname === '/health')
    return send(200, { require_pairing: false, paired: false, fixture: 'pr11881-real-fields' });
  if (req.method === 'GET' && url.pathname === '/api/auth/methods')
    return send(200, { pairing_required: false, oidc: [] });
  if (req.method === 'GET' && url.pathname === '/api/config/sections')
    return send(200, { sections });
  if (req.method === 'GET' && url.pathname === '/api/config/list')
    return send(200, { entries: entries(url.searchParams.get('prefix')) });
  if (req.method === 'GET' && url.pathname === '/api/config/drift')
    return send(200, { drifted: [] });
  if (req.method === 'GET' && url.pathname === '/api/config/reload-status')
    return send(200, { pending_reload: false });
  if (req.method === 'OPTIONS' && url.pathname === '/api/config')
    return send(200, {});
  if (req.method === 'GET' && url.pathname === '/fixture-state')
    return send(200, { values, writes });
  if (req.method === 'PATCH' && url.pathname === '/api/config') {
    let body = '';
    req.on('data', chunk => { body += chunk; });
    req.on('end', () => {
      try {
        const ops = JSON.parse(body);
        if (!Array.isArray(ops) || ops.some(op => op.op !== 'replace' || !(op.path in values)))
          return send(400, { error: 'unsupported fixture operation' });
        for (const op of ops) values[op.path] = op.value;
        writes.push(ops);
        return send(200, { saved: true, results: ops, warnings });
      } catch { return send(400, { error: 'invalid fixture request' }); }
    });
    return;
  }
  return send(404, { error: 'fixture endpoint not implemented' });
});

server.listen(59153, '127.0.0.1', () => {
  process.stdout.write(`fixture listening on ${server.address().port}\n`);
});
NODE
```

  rendering.** Diagnostics are restricted or scrubbed at their existing
  authorization boundaries. The local review remains FAIL for the disclosed
  validation gaps.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?
  **No known introduction.** The dashboard fixture uses synthetic values.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed?
  **Yes.** Goal content remains untrusted; typed control and verifier results
  govern transitions.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Session/epoch fences and
  accounting checks protect continuation; ordinary owners retain provider and
  authorization policy. Core runtime placement and receiving-host coverage
  remain separate pre-merge obligations.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No, not fully Rust source-compatible.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** HTTP config edit validation
  and warning behavior change; Goal defaults distinguish unset from explicit
  zero. The previous `/goal` channel catalog entry is removed in this prefix;
  complete Goal ingress remains in later slices.
- Config editor callers may see writes rejected where the previous editor
  accepted them: an error that cannot be safely retained fails closed, fixing
  an earlier error can reveal another that requires a batch repair, and a
  list removal or reorder can change a diagnostic's index. A caller without
  Config read access receives a generic validation failure or a single
  hidden-details warning; PATCH `test` requires that read access. Secret
  write responses still omit retained warnings; those warnings are logged.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No declared change.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`:
  Existing Rust `TaskRecord` literals must supply `session_id` and
  `execution_epoch`; non-Goal records can use `None` and `0`, while Goal
  producers must use a valid session and guarded epoch. `GoalTaskRecord`
  literals must also supply the pending-call pair and accounting state, and
  `CostRecord` literals must supply `provider_ref` (`None` when unknown).
  Existing runtime task-type paths are re-exported, and the new fields have
  deserialization defaults. Custom `GoalTaskRegistry` implementations and
  callers must migrate from the removed unguarded create/objective/pause/resume
  methods to the session-bound guarded API; Goal objectives are immutable.
  The control-plane database migrates from the base schema v10 to v14. Running
  or paused legacy Goals without a usable session or objective are failed
  during convergence. Take a consistent backup of
  `<data_dir>/control_plane.db` and `<workspace_dir>/state/costs.jsonl` before
  upgrading; compatibility with an older binary after migration is not proved.
  This compatibility list remains subject to review.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Keep Goal admission disabled; if later
  enabled, stop/drain Goal work, stop the daemon and preserve a consistent
  copy of the control-plane database and usage ledger. Revert landed dependent
  slices in reverse order through the normal revert process. Do not assume an
  older binary can safely use the v14 database merely because it logs a newer
  version warning. If a restore is required, retain the post-upgrade state for
  recovery: restoring a pre-upgrade backup discards subsequent changes.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Goal admission is staged and disabled.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unexpected config validation failures,
  task/epoch or ledger divergence, or a Goal unable to settle accounting.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge the declared dependencies first.
- **What changed and why:** Zerocode edits the canonical connection/model registry and consumes exact model references in configuration, Quickstart and chat. Masked editor baselines preserve credentials; text navigation, save help and the independent Fluent catalogs match the JSON workflow. Chat switch feedback and the title use the same resolved registry model ID.
- **Scope boundary:** The parent supplies the V5 registry and backend protocol. This layer covers the TUI and follow-up integration fixes, including the Web cost-rate navigation correction; the broader Web registry UI is a separate child.
- **Blast radius:** TUI onboarding, configuration save/reload, model selection, validation feedback and cost-rate navigation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Depends on #12450. Current head: `3fc94511a9`.

### What this does, simply

The terminal setup screens now edit the same reusable connections and named models that the backend resolves. A name such as `chat.demo.gateway` stays one complete model reference. Users can save the registry, pick that model in Quickstart and switch to it in chat. The editor shows its revision and distinguishes Enter (new line) from Ctrl+S (save). The revision-labeled screenshots below document all three workflows with the matching daemon; the latest master integration and follow-up help-text changes are covered separately below.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; the interactive workflow supplements automated CI.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui`, English locale, actual xterm at 160 columns × 50 rows, matching local daemon.

prs.title: feat(providers): support Qwen MP4 video-file input
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Send explicitly supplied Qwen MP4 video files as `video_url` parts containing `data:video/mp4;base64,...`, across streaming, non-streaming, history, and native-tool Chat Completions requests.
  - Scope local file reads to the current Agent turn's filesystem policy, with no-follow directory/file opens, regular-file checks, and a request-wide raw-video budget below 7,000,000 bytes.
  - Preserve mixed image/video requests and separate system text. Unavailable, unsupported and over-budget user videos retain their literal markers; history cannot stop later chat. Successful loads consume the shared budget newest message first. Tool-result bodies and system/assistant video examples remain literal.
  - Add factory-to-HTTP, Agent-turn, filesystem-boundary, and opt-in live Qwen tests.
- **Scope boundary:** Chat Completions MP4 files and inline MP4 Data URLs. MCP attachment promotion is tracked in the dependent draft #12579. Responses, remote video fetching, frame extraction, audio-track interpretation, and codec validation are outside this change.
- **Blast radius:** Qwen/Qwen Code compatible-provider request shaping, the shared compatible message-part enum, current-turn filesystem-policy propagation, and provider documentation. Other providers retain their request behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12671 for the separately reviewed, Core Team-approved runtime exception record required before this feature merges. Related #11383 for the earlier video-input discussion and tool-body marker trust-boundary concerns. This is Qwen-specific and carries no code from that MiniMax PR.

### What this does, simply

A Qwen user can supply `[VIDEO:/absolute/path/clip.mp4]` or an inline MP4 Data URL and have the actual file reach the model. Previously the video reference reached Qwen as text. Files are read only when the current Agent policy permits them; low-level provider callers without a policy scope can use inline bytes but cannot open local paths. The service samples the video using its default settings.

The supported model families and dated snapshots are enumerated in `qwen_video::supports_model`. Only Qwen3.8-Flash was exercised against a real service; the other documented IDs have transport validation coverage.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; deterministic factory/HTTP and Agent-turn tests cover the changed boundary. The ignored provider live test documents optional paid reproduction; no paid run was made for this revision.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate on `28a00b928`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45314198597) completed successfully, including CI Required Gate, Security, Lint, Test, parallel runtime tests, platform checks and the declared MSRV. It covers the current code and docs; the local HTTP/policy and negative-control tests below supply focused behavior evidence. The branch merges upstream `74c8af5cf`, including #12694. Passing CI does not replace Core Team review or the #12671 merge dependency.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local platform is macOS/aarch64 with rustc 1.97.1. The linked CI supplies its cross-platform and MSRV checks. Live inference is explicit opt-in and was not rerun for this revision.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers -- --test-threads=1
lib: 2030 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored
integration: 1 passed; 60 passed; 3 ignored

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib qwen
16 passed; 0 failed

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent_turn_applies_its_filesystem_policy_to_qwen_video --config 'profile.test.package.zeroclaw-runtime.opt-level=2'
1 passed; 0 failed; macOS ld compact-unwind size warning remains

cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished dev profile; no warnings

cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check
BASE_SHA=github/master DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/providers/catalog.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
BASE_SHA=github/master DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/providers/catalog.md scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
0 Markdown errors; 8 link-check tests passed
```

The initial parallel provider run had two OpenAI failures: a runtime proxy-config test received an extra request, and a streaming fixture decoded that proxy's JSON instead of a Chat response. The complete serial run above passes without filtering. The Agent policy test passed at opt-level=1 and opt-level=2, but both emitted macOS ld's compact-unwind table size warning. It is recorded as a platform limitation, not a zero-warning run; Clippy remains warning-free. Diagnostics are not disabled. An initial docs-lint attempt lacked npm network/cache access; the successful rerun uses the existing temporary npm cache. Optional HTTP link checking is unavailable because lychee is not installed.

The directory-replacement negative control changes only `open_dir_nofollow(name)` to `open_dir(name)`: `video_open_rejects_intermediate_directory_replacement` must fail with the relative `private` symlink. The original source is restored in `finally`; the same test and all Qwen tests then pass. The normal and private targets contain different bytes.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Factory-to-actual-HTTP regression exercises all eight Chat entry points with MP4, oversized MP4, WebM, missing files, unsupported `qwen-plus`/`qwen3-coder-plus`, Discord CDN URL, invalid Base64, absent read scope, policy denial and mixed valid/invalid references. Every unavailable-video case sends a subsequent ordinary chat retaining the history. Deleted history falls back; two 4 MB clips in different turns send the newer clip and retain the older marker as text. Valid inline MP4 makes tool-body non-promotion tests sensitive to a removed carrier guard.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no presentation or rendered interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `28a00b928`. Automated assertions live in `compatible_qwen_video_tests.rs`, `qwen_video.rs::tests`, and `agent/qwen_video_tests.rs`. No runtime/config/channel public types change in this follow-up.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** HTTP assertions check the dispatched request, decoded video bytes, mixed image/video, preserved literal markers, unchanged assistant role coalescing, and streamed/non-streamed parity.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Valid video is delivered; failed promotion preserves original user text and continues dispatch. Preparation explicitly carries text and loaded video parts to serialization, so fallback text is not rescanned. Existing task-local policy, resolved-path validation, per-component no-follow, nonblocking regular-file checks and bounded reads are retained.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Paid Qwen validation remains opt-in. Historical smoke on `016e14f67` used Qwen3.8-Flash and a public OpenCV sample (3559 input/151 output tokens, 4.21s); it is not evidence for the new fallback behavior. No full workspace or local Linux/Windows/MSRV claim.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes:** an additive video-input capability can read and transmit user-selected MP4 files. It uses the current turn's existing read policy and does not enlarge allowed roots.
- New external network calls? **Yes:** the existing authenticated Qwen Chat request can now carry video bytes. No separate fetch/upload endpoint is added.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No:** runtime authentication is unchanged. The ignored live test reads explicitly supplied test-only environment variables.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No:** committed fixtures are synthetic; live media is external and uncommitted.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes:** explicit genuine-user video references become model-visible media; tool bodies, system, and assistant text are excluded from promotion.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: File disclosure is constrained by lexical and resolved read-policy checks, per-component no-follow opens, nonblocking regular-file checks, and bounded reads. Only successfully validated video bytes become media; failed references remain literal text and do not abort dispatch. Container-header checks do not guarantee valid codecs; the service owns decoding.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes:** additive Qwen video-file support; existing image and text requests retain their behavior.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes:** additive handling of the existing VIDEO marker syntax for supported Qwen models and `ZEROCLAW_TEST_QWEN_*` opt-in test variables. No runtime configuration field or CLI flag is added.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Existing deployments need no migration. To opt in, use a supported Qwen model and an allowed MP4 reference. Direct provider consumers reading paths must use `with_video_read_policy`; the Agent turn supplies this automatically. The live test documents its explicit credential, endpoint, model, and fixture variables.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual merge commit. The follow-up fix is `28a00b928`; the branch also includes the original feature commit and an upstream merge. Revert the dependent MCP PR first if both have landed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added; image/text requests remain available.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Service rejection of video content, missing expected video parts, or a response indicating that the file is unavailable. The factory HTTP regression exposes missing/malformed video parts.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. Related #11383 is contextual reference; this PR does not supersede it or incorporate its code.

prs.title: fix(web): retain Config field help when schema lookup misses
prs.body:
## Summary

Related #9363. Base branch `master`.

- The dashboard reads field help from the Config JSON Schema. Its path lookup can follow properties and maps. It loses the description when a list entry uses a natural key, such as `model_routes.reasoning.deep.model`.
- The gateway now includes the field's existing English description in `GET /api/config/list` when one is available. Both field rows and secret-map headers use it if the schema lookup misses. The response can grow by one string per documented field.
- The model-route hint, provider and model descriptions now contain operator guidance. The Rust construction notes stay beside the fields as ordinary comments. The Config derive also uses this text for ZeroCode.

This addresses the English fallback criterion. Shared translation IDs, catalogue entries and the dashboard Fluent work in #8584 remain open.

### What this does, simply

When an operator opens a named model route, the dashboard can now explain what to enter in the Model field. It gets the explanation with the field it already received. A dot in the route name does not require another request or any special parsing.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

Open a configured model route in dashboard Config and inspect its Model row. For example, with a route whose hint is `reasoning.deep`, the row for `model_routes.reasoning.deep.model` should display “Model identifier used by this route's provider profile.” The Save button should stay disabled until you edit a value.

### How I tested

- I added a regression to the existing FieldForm renderer suite. With the old renderer, both cases failed on the missing help text. With the fix, both passed, including the concurrent-save case. Command from `web/`: `node node_modules/jiti/lib/jiti-cli.mjs src/components/sections/FieldForm.enableToggle.test.ts`.
- I checked five cases in Chromium using the production FieldForm and styles, a fixture gateway and English locale. The named route showed the list description. Existing schema text took precedence. An older gateway could omit the new field. An undocumented field had no help text. A secret-map header displayed its static description.
- Tested source: `804189dfd8ccc2c1827750c56d77d4ab0d7c768e`. The screenshot shows the named route at 1024 × 470. The fixture supplies synthetic values and the model description from this revision. [Browser screenshot](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/blob/ae5d019954f8b9f7409ce7efabb20e0f5dd8ac0d/config-field-help.png)
- I added a Rust handler test for a dotted route and checked the empty-description and secret-value serialization assertions. Rust formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Local disk space was insufficient for a clean gateway build. The Rust test run and a live-daemon dashboard check are still pending.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

New permissions or filesystem access: No. New external calls: No. Secret or credential handling changed: No. Personal data in the fixtures: No. Model-visible input changed: No. The response copies a static schema description. Secret values still use the existing masking path.

## Compatibility (required)

Backward compatible: Yes. Config, environment or CLI migration: None. Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed: No. Empty descriptions are omitted. Older gateways continue to use the schema lookup.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Revert the squash commit. There are no flags or migrations. If named-route help disappears, check the `description` on the matching list entry and the help rendered below the field path.

prs.title: chore(channels)!: move IRC and Twitch out of the binary into registry plugins
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Remove the compiled-in IRC and Twitch channels. Both now ship as the `irc` and `twitch` WASM plugins, which a stock host installs without a rebuild. Twitch was a thin adapter over the IRC channel, so the two leave together. This takes the raw-TCP IRC channel out of the "retain built-in" list in #8850, now that a compatible, validated package exists.
  - `[channels.irc.*]` and `[channels.twitch.*]` become **retired config keys**, the same mechanism WATI used. Each load drops the section and prints a notice that names the plugin and its install and bind commands. The next save (or `zeroclaw config migrate`) removes it from `config.toml`, secrets included. `config migrate` first copies the original file to `config.toml.backup`, which keeps the old credentials until a later migration replaces it; the channel overview now tells operators to treat that copy (and any older `config.toml.v<version>.backup` or manual copy) as secret material and delete it once the plugin binding works and a rollback is no longer needed.
  - `ChannelKind::Irc` and `ChannelKind::Twitch` stay in the attribution enum so historical records deserialize. They are marked not inbound-capable, so they leave the SOP trigger registry, as WATI did.
  - Keep `OutboundContentFormat::PlainText` for migrated `plugin.<alias>` bindings whose `[channels.plugin.<alias>].package` is `irc` or `twitch` (and fall back to `PlainText` for bare `"plugin"` or unresolved plugin aliases whenever an enabled plain-text plugin binding exists), so Markdown link destinations are still scanned by the outbound leak redactor across drafts, multi-message narration flushes, final replies (including `send_via` redirects), and announcements.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - No other channel changes, and no plugin-runtime changes.
  - No automatic conversion of an old section into a plugin binding. The plugin must be installed first, and the encrypted credentials belong to a different config row.
  - The schema version is not bumped (see the reviewer question below).
- **Blast radius:**
  - Release archives never included IRC or Twitch: neither is in the dist feature set. They shipped only in `channels-full` source builds and the `all-features` image. That image and `--preset full` also build the plugin runtime, so every install that had these channels can install the plugins.
  - A plain `cargo build --features channels-full` without `plugins-wasm` loses them, and needs `plugins-wasm` added.
  - Generated installer surfaces (`Containerfile`, `setup.bat`, `dev/ci/docker-tags.toml`) were checked against `cargo generate installers`: no drift.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8850. Depends on zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins#174 (merged and published), which publishes the `irc` and `twitch` 0.2.0 packages this PR points operators to.

### Reviewer decision: `retired_in: 4`, no schema bump

The `RETIRED_KEYS` policy comment asks for a version bump when no pending version covers a retirement. V4 shipped in v0.9.0. I used `retired_in: 4` without a V5 bump because:
- Every load already applies every retired key, whatever version the file declares, so operators see the same thing either way.
- A V5 bump would make every config saved by this binary unreadable by v0.9.0 ("newer than this binary supports"). That's a large side effect for a channel removal, and it would be the first V5 change.

If maintainers prefer the bump, it's a mechanical follow-up: a `MIGRATION_STEPS` entry, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 5`, and a regenerated fixture.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw used to carry IRC and Twitch support inside its binary, but most installs (every release download) didn't include them, and getting them meant rebuilding ZeroClaw. They are now plugins you install with one command. This PR removes the old built-in copies. If an existing config still has an IRC or Twitch section, ZeroClaw says exactly what to do instead of silently ignoring it, and the rest of the config keeps working.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the upgrade path.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (`zeroclaw config`, `zeroclaw plugin`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** a build with `--features plugins-wasm-cranelift,channels-full`, and a config dir whose `config.toml` holds `schema_version = 4`, a provider, `[agents.assistant] channels = ["irc.libera"]`, a `[channels.irc.libera]` section with a `sasl_password`, a peer group on `irc.libera`, and `[plugins] enabled = true`. Both `irc` and `twitch` 0.2.0 are published in the plugin registry (zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw-plugins#174).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. `zeroclaw --config-dir D config get agents.assistant.channels`
  2. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin install irc`
  3. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin bind irc --channel-alias libera`
  4. Set `server`, `nickname`, and `channels` on the printed `plugins.entries.<key>.config.*` paths, and the server on `.egress_hosts`, with `config set --no-interactive`.
  5. `config set --no-interactive agents.assistant.channels '["plugin.libera"]'`
  6. `zeroclaw --config-dir D plugin info irc`
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - Step 1 exits 0. It prints the retired-key warning naming the `irc` plugin and its install and bind commands, then a `config migrate` hint, on stderr, with no secret value shown. The complete output is in **Migration receipt** below.
  - Steps 2 to 5 succeed even though the agent still references `irc.libera`.
  - After the first save, `config.toml` no longer holds `[channels.irc]` or its secret.
  - Step 6 reports `plugin.libera configuration validates against the package schema.`, `The activation plan admits plugin.libera`, and `Loads: yes`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the built-in IRC channel loads from `[channels.irc.libera]`.

prs.title: fix(mcp): replay a tool call rejected for a stale HTTP session
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A Streamable HTTP MCP server that has terminated a session (idle eviction, restart) must answer every request carrying that `Mcp-Session-Id` with HTTP 404, and the client must start a new session ([spec, Session Management](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/transports#session-management)). The HTTP transport already maps this to `McpTransportError::StaleSession`, but the request stays marked outcome-unknown, so `dispatch_rpc` recovers the session in the background and fails the call with `outcome unknown and request was not replayed`.
  - The 404 is a definitive answer: the server rejected the request at session lookup and never executed it. This PR marks such a request as rejected-unexecuted (back to the pre-write phase, same epoch) before returning `StaleSession`, so the existing bounded pre-write path resets the transport, re-runs the handshake and replays the call on the new session.
  - In practice every first tool call after the server dropped the session failed. With a server that evicts idle sessions after 30 minutes, that is the first call of almost every conversation with a low-traffic agent.
  - This restores, for Streamable HTTP only, the replay that #7351 added (`call_tool_reconnects_on_stale_session`) and #9418 removed together with the other post-write replays. The test #9418 rewrote into no-replay is rewritten back.
- **Scope boundary:** Only the Streamable HTTP transport's 404/410-with-session branch. Timeouts, dropped streams and other post-write failures keep the no-replay rule from #9418. The legacy SSE transport is unchanged: its 404 stays outcome-unknown (`sse_post_404_is_not_replayed_to_derived_endpoint` untouched). A sessionless 404 is still a plain error (`call_tool_does_not_retry_sessionless_404` untouched).
- **Blast radius:** HTTP MCP servers only: a call that got a stale-session 404/410 is now replayed after the reconnect instead of failing. `MAX_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS` (2) bounds it: a server that keeps answering 404 after fresh handshakes gets three attempts in total, then the error surfaces (new test `call_tool_stale_session_replays_are_bounded`).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9418, Related #7351

### What this does, simply

When an MCP server forgets a session, for example after the session sat idle for half an hour, it answers the next request with "404, no such session". ZeroClaw already understood that answer and reconnected, but it threw away the request that got the 404, so the user's tool call failed even though the server had done nothing with it. Now ZeroClaw reconnects and sends that same call again; if the server keeps rejecting it, ZeroClaw gives up after two retries. Calls whose fate really is unknown (a timeout, a connection that dropped mid-request) are still never repeated.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: the wiremock tests reproduce the server's 404 deterministically; a manual run needs an MCP server with a short idle-session TTL.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `zeroclaw-tools` unit tests cover the transport phase change and the client replay path.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ rustc --version
rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01)
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output)
$ cargo test -q -p zeroclaw-tools --locked --lib mcp_
test result: ok. 245 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1120 filtered out; finished in 1.20s
$ cargo clippy -q -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
```

prs.title: feat(oidc): hold, seal and store refresh grants in the certificate ledger (#12707 slices 2–3)
prs.body:
> **Stacked:** Depends on #12716. Until #12716 merges, this PR also shows its two commits (`3bc71705d1`, `519d558a04`); review `dd79f6a34a` onward.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - This is part of slices 2–3 of #12707, the daemon-held OIDC refresh grants from the ADR-017 amendment in #12496: where a refresh token waits after sign-in, how it is bound to a device's certificate, how it is sealed and stored, and when it ends. The refresh itself (single-flight, version compare-and-set, in-flight marker, uncertain state) is the next PR. Nothing calls this code yet; the gateway hand-off is slice 4.
  - **`refresh_grant.rs`** (new, in the auth-provider subsystem):
    - `PendingGrants` holds a refresh token in memory, keyed by a SHA-256 of the access token from the same token response. That access token is what the certificate request then presents as its bearer, so two devices signing in as one person claim different grants.
    - A pending grant expires with its access token, capped at the sign-in flow's lifetime and at one hour, the same ceiling Zerocode puts on device codes. At most 1,024 are held. An access token offered twice holds neither grant.
    - `claim` removes the grant and returns it only for the provider alias, issuer, client and canonical principal it was issued for. A mismatched or expired claim gets nothing, and the grant is spent either way.
    - `seal` encrypts the refresh token through `SecretStore`. It refuses to produce a grant when the store returned plaintext, which happens when `[secrets] encrypt = false`: a refresh token is never stored in the clear, and that device simply gets no refresh grant. `unseal` refuses a stored value that is not `enc2:` ciphertext.
  - **`cert_ledger.rs`** (schema v3):
    - A new `refresh_grants` table holds one sealed refresh token per provider alias and `device_id`. It records the issuer, client, canonical principal and client authentication the token was issued under.
    - `record_issued_with_refresh_grant` stores the grant in the same `IMMEDIATE` transaction that publishes the certificate (`promote_staged`), so they land together or not at all. A grant never attaches to a certificate it wasn't issued with. Renewal keeps the grant, because `device_id` survives renewal.
    - **Revocation:** revoking any of a device's certificates, revoking the device, and the undelivered sweep each delete its grants inside the revocation transaction. `revoke_device` now also deletes grants, and commits, when the device had no active certificate left.
    - **Lapse:** a grant whose device has no active, unexpired certificate has lapsed. `refresh_grant()` deletes it in the same transaction as that check, and opening the ledger sweeps any others.
    - **Deletion primitives for slice 5:** `delete_refresh_grant` for sign-out, and `delete_refresh_grants_not_issued_by` for a provider entry that was removed or repointed.
    - **Migration:** a v2 ledger gains the table through its own path. Sending it through the v0/v1 rebuild would backfill `delivered_at` and mark its undelivered certificates delivered. A v0 or v1 ledger gets the table inside its rebuild transaction.
  - **Docs:** `secure-transport.md` describes the v3 upgrade and the exact downgrade back to schema v2.
- **Scope boundary:** Within the approved ADR-016 row from #12609 (approval recorded in #12708):
  - `refresh_grant.rs` holds the pending grant and the durable grant sealed through `SecretStore`.
  - `cert_ledger.rs` gets a refresh-grant table in the existing ledger database, a pending grant is claimed in the same transaction that records its certificate, and grants are deleted on revocation or unrenewed lapse.
  - `mod.rs` only declares `refresh_grant` and re-exports its types.
  - Not in this PR: the refresh state machine (next PR), the gateway hand-off (slice 4), the RPC method, sign-out and provider-change wiring (slice 5), Zerocode (slice 6), and the per-provider opt-in (slice 7).
- **Blast radius:**
  - **Ledger schema:** every daemon that opens `tls/ledger.db` migrates it to v3. The v2 → v3 step adds an empty table and index.
  - **Revocation paths:** `mark_revoked`, `revoke_device` and the undelivered sweep each run one more `DELETE` in their existing transaction.
  - **Open:** opening the ledger runs one sweep statement.
  - **Behavior:** no certificate behavior changes.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12707, Related #12496, Related #12609, Related #8289. Depends on #12716.

### What this does, simply

When a device signs in, the identity provider hands back a refresh token alongside the access token. This PR adds the two places that refresh token lives:
- briefly in memory until the device asks for its certificate;
- then encrypted in the certificate ledger, tied to that one device.

It disappears whenever the device's certificate is revoked or runs out. It is never written unencrypted, and it can't end up attached to a different device or person. Nothing uses it yet; the next PRs add the refresh itself and connect it to sign-in.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Nothing calls this yet; the behavior is covered by unit tests against real SQLite ledgers and a real `SecretStore`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` runs the new `security::auth_provider::refresh_grant` and `security::cert_ledger` tests, and `Lint` runs clippy. Docs Style covers `secure-transport.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:**
  - Concurrency is covered for pending claims, with 8 threads racing for one grant.
  - Ledger ordering against a concurrent revocation relies on the existing `IMMEDIATE`-transaction serialization that `promote_staged` and the revocation paths already share. The failure side is pinned with the existing `after_stage` hook.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux, at `4a120b6cf2`):

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
(clean)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- security::
test result: ok. 453 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- cert enroll rpc::dispatch::tests::cert
test result: ok. 160 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -- api_oidc_enroll api_pairing cert
test result: ok. 24 passed; 0 failed
$ scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
$ DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/zerocode/secure-transport.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - **New tests:** 11 for `refresh_grant` and 15 for the ledger. The existing 45 ledger tests pass unchanged on v3.
  - **Negative controls:** 13, each a temporary change that must fail at least one test. Each one did, and the restored source is byte-identical:
    - no grant delete on a single-certificate revocation;
    - no grant delete on device revocation;
    - the grant inserted outside the publish transaction;
    - no liveness check on read;
    - no lapse sweep at open;
    - the v2 ledger falling through to the rebuild;
    - the provider sweep comparing the alias only;
    - `claim` ignoring the binding;
    - a mismatched claim keeping the grant;
    - a repeated access token overwriting;
    - `seal` accepting plaintext;
    - `claim` ignoring expiry;
    - `unseal` accepting plaintext.
  - **Downgrade:** a test runs the documented SQL on a v3 ledger that holds a grant. The result matches a fresh v2 ledger's table and indexes, keeps every certificate, and re-upgrades cleanly.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `4a120b6cf2`; Rust library API and unit tests in `refresh_grant.rs` and `cert_ledger.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `cargo test --workspace`. The change is limited to `zeroclaw-runtime`'s security module; the ledger's other users (RPC certificate renewal, gateway enrollment and pairing) were run above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The grant table lives in the existing `tls/ledger.db`.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. This adds storage for IdP refresh tokens.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. The tests use synthetic values.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - **Encryption at rest:** refresh tokens are stored only as `SecretStore` ciphertext. With encryption disabled, no grant is produced at all.
  - **In memory:** pending grants are held under a hash of the access token, never the token itself, and refresh tokens are zeroized on drop. `Debug` output never includes token material; tests pin this.
  - **Binding:** a grant binds only to the certificate published in the same transaction, for the provider and principal the bearer verified as. It is deleted inside every revocation transaction and on lapse.
  - **Residual risk:** a compromised daemon secret store yields refresh tokens until the provider refuses them. ADR-017 records this, with certificate revocation and provider-side revocation as the bounds.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for upgrades. A v0, v1 or v2 ledger is migrated in one transaction with every certificate kept.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: None. A downgrade to a build expecting schema v2 needs the step under Rollback.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback:** revert the squash commit. Daemons that already opened their ledger with this build have it at schema v3, and an older build refuses a newer ledger (the existing fail-closed rule). Before starting the older build, run the SQL from `secure-transport.md` on `<data_dir>/tls/ledger.db`:

```bash
sqlite3 <data_dir>/tls/ledger.db "DROP TABLE refresh_grants; PRAGMA user_version = 2;"
```

  Nothing writes grants until slice 4, so the dropped table is empty and nothing else is lost.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** None. The table stays empty until a later slice writes to it.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - A failed migration stops the daemon with an error naming `tls/ledger.db` and leaves the ledger unchanged.
  - A regression in the revocation paths would show as a revocation or renewal error. Those paths each gained one `DELETE` in their existing transaction.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A

prs.title: feat(zerocode): confirm config deletion and reset
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Require target confirmation before deleting a Config alias or Costs resource, or resetting a configured field.
  - Keep deletion refusals, cleanup warnings and refresh failures in a scrollable result panel until dismissed. A completed or uncertain mutation cannot be retried by dismissing its result.
  - Name the actions Delete and Reset in Help and rebinding while preserving existing stored binding identifiers.
  - Show the resolved Delete shortcut in the footer for an existing alias or Costs entry, so deletion is discoverable without opening Help.
- **Scope boundary:** ZeroCode only. No new cascade rules, daemon mutation semantics, undo storage or secret-value display.
- **Blast radius:** Config input routing, client response handling and Config action labels. Skills archival and local keybinding override clearing retain their behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11487. Related #11172 for the optional daemon deletion preview.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's Config editor can remove aliases and restore fields to their default behavior. Previously, pressing the deletion or reset key sent the change immediately. The daemon could reject an unsafe deletion, but it could not tell whether a valid deletion was accidental.

This PR shows the selected target first. You can confirm or cancel; moving the underlying selection cannot change the captured target. After confirmation, the result stays readable, including warnings when cleanup was incomplete or the list could not be refreshed.

When the daemon supports `config/delete-plan`, the confirmation shows its blockers and references that would be removed. Older daemons show an explicit unavailable-preview notice. The daemon still makes the final authorization and deletion decision.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

Delete and Reset share one Config dialog: either a confirmation with a captured target, or a result that cannot send a mutation. The outer input loop gives it priority over pane navigation and paste. Typed client responses preserve the daemon's applied flag and optional warnings; no second cascade planner is introduced. The larger diff includes request-recording regressions for destructive input and failure paths, plus existing action consumers that follow the renamed Rust variants.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the running TUI's presentation.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a disposable Config alias or Costs entry, or a non-secret field whose reset is safe. Use a ZeroCode binary built from this PR with an existing daemon connection.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config and focus an existing alias or Costs entry. Check that the footer shows the resolved Delete binding (`x` by default), then press it. Check the displayed target and cancel with Esc. Reopen confirmation and confirm only a disposable target. For a field, use the resolved Reset binding (`d` by default). The Delete hint should disappear on the Add row or when Delete is unbound.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Opening and cancellation do not change configuration. Confirmation applies one change to the displayed target. The result remains visible until dismissed; long text can be scrolled.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same Delete or Reset key sends the mutation immediately, without a target-confirmation step.

### How I tested

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
passed

cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
passed

cargo test --no-fail-fast -p zerocode
1646 passed; 2 failed
```

- **Validation revision and environment:** I ran the checks above on the Mac mini at `0ab51b9854b6e6e8e91d05053e06c06116ed6a67` through `zc-cargo-narrow`, with two Cargo jobs and two test threads for the package run. These are local results; CI results for this head are not included.
- **Known test failures:** `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` also fails on clean master `f2b432db` on this Mini. `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` is a known timing flake. The package run therefore has two failures.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source and response-contract comparison. Recorded outbound requests exercise the real Config handlers and client: open/cancel/mouse/paste/repeat, captured alias and Costs targets, reset tab/cursor preservation, blocked and unavailable previews, preview failure and committed refresh failure. The footer regression covers custom and unbound Delete shortcuts, independent alias/Costs selection, and Add/filter/pane suppression. Master integration preserves SecretMap container refusal and Config RPC-timeout handling; their focused tests passed alongside confirmation. Existing Config editing tests also passed. No live configuration was deleted for this verification.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots of the current code: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11510#issuecomment-6514492960 (macOS Terminal.app captures built from `7564c57fe8`; the current head `0b48c4d220` only deletes `#[cfg(test)]` evidence-frame code). They show a required field with no reset offered and the explanation when `d` is pressed, the reset confirmation and result panel on an optional field (the key removed from config.toml), and the Spanish notice. Earlier experiment-build screenshots: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11510#issuecomment-6233163044.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Automated confirmation sent one mutation for the captured target; cancellation sent none. Refresh failure retained the committed result and warning without retrying.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full-workspace validation was not run locally. The package checks and their two known failures are recorded above.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots of the current code: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11510#issuecomment-6514492960 (macOS Terminal.app captures, built from `7564c57fe8`; the head since then only removes test code). Earlier screenshots from my experiment build: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11510#issuecomment-6233163044.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; the optional read-only preview uses the existing daemon RPC connection.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Confirmation displays paths and aliases, not field values or the planner's raw reference values.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No; fixtures use neutral names.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for stored configuration and daemon mutation contracts. Delete and Reset now require confirmation.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. Help and rebinding labels change; stored `config_tab.toggle_secret` and `config_tab.delete_row` identifiers remain valid.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: No configuration migration. Costs deletion uses Delete (`x` by default); the old redundant Reset (`d`) deletion shortcut is removed. Existing custom Delete bindings still resolve through the preserved identifier. Only `METHOD_NOT_FOUND` permits the unavailable-preview path; other preview failures are shown instead of enabling confirmation.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's commit and use the prior ZeroCode binary. This restores immediate Delete/Reset behavior; it does not undo changes already confirmed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Existing keybinding overrides continue to apply.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Confirmation does not open, displays a wrong target, disappears instead of preserving an error, or a confirmed mutation reports a refresh failure. The daemon's authorization and deletion safeguards remain unchanged.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): reopen open sessions when zerocode restarts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - zerocode's sidebar list of open sessions lived only in memory. The daemon keeps every transcript, but quitting zerocode lost which sessions were open, so each launch started from an empty sidebar.
  - The list (session ids, agent aliases, order, focus, and the last Chat/Code pane on screen) is now saved whenever it changes, as an owner-only JSON file per connection target under `<config-dir>/open-sessions/`.
  - At launch the saved list goes to the existing reconnect resume path (`set_resume_sessions`), so restored sessions reattach by id exactly as they do after a daemon reconnect: focused first, the rest in the background.
  - On by default (`[sidebar] restore_sessions = true`). `zerocode --fresh` starts one launch with an empty sidebar and still saves its own list.
  - Each zerocode window on a daemon keeps its own list in a numbered slot, held by an OS file lock. A window takes the lowest free slot, so closing a second window and opening it again while the first runs reopens the second window's sessions. At restore, sessions another running window has in its list are skipped with a notice. Without that, two windows would reattach the same live session, and either window could cancel the other's turn. That stale-session and multi-tab hazard is why #8911 (silent auto-resume, for #8653) was closed in favour of the #8922 picker. The lock is released when the owning window exits, including on a crash.
  - Each window publishes the list it is about to reopen before its panes start (an empty list on `--fresh`), so other windows never judge by the previous occupant's stale list.
  - Saved Code sessions the daemon no longer lists, and saved Chat sessions with no stored history (for example deleted), are dropped with one notice.
  - When the daemon refuses to reattach a restored session because this terminal's environment differs from the one the session started in (FORBIDDEN `-32012`, "Session environment differs" or "Session retains a local operator environment"), the entry stays where it was, with the same order and focus. Its pane shows a translated notice that the saved session can't be reattached from this terminal environment and that the daemon still keeps the old conversation, plus an explicit "start a new conversation" action (the existing new-session key, Ctrl+N by default). Only that action opens a fresh session in the same slot, with the same agent and mode, and the saved list then tracks the new id. If creating it fails, the refused entry and its notice stay. Switching from the notice to another session moves the refused entry to the background, and closing it while a live session is focused closes only that row, so the live session stays on screen. Nothing is replaced automatically, other errors behave as before, and the daemon's environment check is unchanged.
  - Fully resuming the old conversation in that case is left to upstream #11921 (history persistence so tasks can resume after restart).
  - Local daemon connections only. Over WSS the daemon admits a resume only from the client identity that owns the session (`capture_session_access`), and a relaunched window connects with a new one, so a saved remote list could only produce failed rows. Reclaiming a remote identity per window slot is a follow-up.
- **Scope boundary:** Local connections only; remote (`--connect`) windows are unchanged. Client only (`apps/zerocode`); no daemon, RPC or runtime change. Queued messages, unsent drafts and attachments are not saved. A turn that was running when zerocode quit is not resumed or rerun.
- **Blast radius:** zerocode startup (one extra `session/list-acp` call and/or one `session/messages` probe per saved Chat session on a local connection when a saved list exists) and the per-frame sidebar derivation (a cheap comparison; the file is written only when the list changes, and never while disconnected).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8653, #8911, #8922.

### What this does, simply

When you quit zerocode and start it again, the sessions you had open in the sidebar come back: same order, same one focused, on the pane you were using. The conversations themselves were always kept by the daemon. What was lost was the list of which ones you had open. If a saved session has since been deleted, it is skipped with a short notice. If a saved session can't be reattached from the terminal you relaunched in, it stays in its place with a notice and an option to start a new conversation there. Each zerocode window keeps its own list: close a second window and open it again, and it gets its own sessions back. A session already open in another window is not opened twice. Use `zerocode --fresh` to start one launch with an empty sidebar, or set `restore_sessions = false` under `[sidebar]` to turn the feature off.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (zerocode Chat and Code panes)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A local daemon with at least two agents.
- **Steps to run:** Open two Code sessions and one Chat session from the sidebar, focus the second Code session, quit zerocode, start it again. Then quit and start once more with `zerocode --fresh`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** With one `zerocode` open, open a second window, add a session there, close it and reopen it: it comes back with that session, and the first window is unchanged. The second launch opens on the Code pane with the same three sidebar rows in the same order and the second Code session focused, transcripts loaded. The `--fresh` launch starts with an empty sidebar.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Every launch starts with an empty sidebar (or the recent-session picker); the previous launch's open sessions must be reopened one by one.

### How I tested

- **Current head:** `214a73cc5` (`8628b342c` plus the fix for Greptile 4429702542: if switching from a refused restore notice to another retained session fails, the refused entry stays focused, so its notice and "start a new conversation" still work). Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, in its own target dir (the log shows zerocode compiled from this tree): `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4` → library 52 passed; binary 1,599 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored, including the new `chat::tests::a_failed_switch_from_a_refused_notice_keeps_the_refused_entry_focused` (Chat and Code panes). `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean.
- **Previous head:** `8628b342c` (the fix for Greptile 4429144032: closing a refused restore row after switching to a live session no longer replaces that session; test `closing_a_refused_entry_after_switching_away_keeps_the_working_session`).
- **Previous head:** `b8f816f436`, a merge of master `1c1cd118a` into `d05cdf055c`. The merge conflicted only in `apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs`: master added `cleanup_notice` to `ResumeEntry` and this branch added `environment_refused`, so the struct and its constructors keep both fields. On a Linux x86_64 build host (rustc 1.99.1): `cargo test --locked -p zerocode -- --test-threads=4` → library 52 passed; binary 1,596 passed, 1 failed (the known `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`); `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed.
- **Previous tested revision:** `d05cdf055cb2a9a61f343643619abe730dc78b4c` on the Mac mini, with the results below.
- **Formatting:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- **Package suite:** `cargo test -p zerocode`, through `zc-cargo-narrow` with `-j2` for compilation and two test threads: library 54 passed; binary 1,600 passed, 1 failed (the known failure below). The TestBackend evidence-frame tests were removed in this revision; the behaviour tests stay.
- **Deleted-Chat regressions (new or updated, all pass):** `open_sessions::tests::deleted_chat_session_is_skipped_at_restore`, `open_sessions::tests::chat_sessions_survive_startup_without_a_complete_daemon_listing`, `open_sessions::tests::chat_restore_drops_only_the_specific_missing_session_refusal`, `open_sessions::tests::mixed_restore_prunes_code_by_list_and_chat_by_history_in_order`. Each saved Chat entry is probed with `session/messages` (limit 1): no stored history, or the daemon's "Session not found or not owned by this principal" refusal, drops it with the existing notice; any other error keeps it for the normal resume path. I ran the first test against `409b7725ef` and it fails there (`dropped` is 0, expected 1), because that head kept every saved Chat ID.
- **Environment-refusal regressions (all pass):** `chat::tests::focused_restored_environment_refusal_keeps_slot_focus_and_notice`, `chat::tests::background_restored_environment_refusal_keeps_slot_and_opens_notice_on_focus`, `chat::tests::restored_environment_refusal_new_conversation_replaces_only_the_selected_slot`, `chat::tests::failed_refused_session_replacement_keeps_saved_id_and_notice`, `chat::tests::unrelated_forbidden_restore_keeps_existing_error_behaviour`, `chat::tests::session_picker_environment_refusal_keeps_selected_entry_and_notice`, `chat::tests::chat_entry_retry_adopts_restored_environment_refusal_action`, `chat::tests::restored_environment_refusal_requires_typed_code_and_specific_message`. On `c4f45eb508` the focused-refusal case promotes the background session over the refused one and shows no notice, so the first test's focus and notice assertions fail there.
- **Known failures:** `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` also fails on clean master `f2b432db` on this Mini (it passes when run alone). `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` is a known timing flake (it passed in this run).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That both guards are load-bearing: with the local-only gate removed, `remote_connections_neither_save_nor_restore` fails; with the early publish removed, both `*_publishes_*` tests fail; with the live-window check removed, `sessions_open_in_another_running_window_are_not_restored` fails. Real launches against a live daemon are captured in https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11727#issuecomment-6536921024 (on `8628b342cb`) and https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11727#issuecomment-6546062078 (on `214a73cc5143`); see Screenshots below.
- **Intentionally skipped:** Full workspace tests; this change is confined to `apps/zerocode` and its docs page.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11727#issuecomment-6536921024 (relaunch and `--fresh`, on `8628b342cb`) and https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11727#issuecomment-6546062078 (dragged cross-pane order after restart, per-window lists, and the environment-refusal notice followed by an explicit new conversation, on `214a73cc5143`). Those are the evidence revisions. The current head `f91c108057acef4e287283d446955a41dcf6e95e` is a later master merge; CI Required Gate passed there. The screenshots were not recaptured on it.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: zerocode writes one new file plus an empty lock file per window slot and connection target under its own config directory. It is written owner-only (`0600`) and atomically, through the same `secure_file::write_private_atomic` funnel as `zerocode-config.toml`.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The file holds session ids, agent aliases and the connection label (socket path or WSS URL). The label is already shown on the dashboard. Credentials are not stored.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: see the first item.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. A config file without `restore_sessions` restores (default on); a missing, damaged or newer-format list file is ignored.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: `[sidebar] restore_sessions` (env `ZEROCODE_sidebar__restore_sessions`) and the `--fresh` flag. Documented in `docs/book/src/zerocode/config.md`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: nothing to do on upgrade. To keep the old behavior, set `restore_sessions = false` under `[sidebar]`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the squash commit. Without a revert, set `[sidebar] restore_sessions = false` or launch with `--fresh`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[sidebar] restore_sessions`, `--fresh`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a launch that reopens sessions the user closed, or the toast "Could not save the open-session list".
