prs.title: feat(sessions): add persistent session prompt attachments
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds an opt-in SQLite collection of four bounded prompts owned by one durable Chat session. Restart preserves them; whole-session reset, deletion and TTL cleanup remove them transactionally with their owner. Schema initialization, legacy prompt binding and ownership reconciliation migrate in one immediate transaction, including rollback on failure.
  - Adds current-session `session_prompt_list`, `session_prompt_set` and `session_prompt_delete`. Mutations require exact one-time approval by default. Global/per-risk-profile `session_prompt_approval = "disabled"` is an explicit operator choice. The tools are direct-only, not skill aliases, pipeline children or inherited auxiliary capabilities. Memory-free RPC Chat retains these tools independently of long-term memory exclusion; ACP remains unsupported.
  - Injects a deterministic next-primary-turn section after immutable host context. Provider context, explicit list and dedicated approval previews retain content; ordinary events, progress and retained/export history mask it without rewriting provider working history. Modifying LLM hooks are skipped for private requests rather than receiving a masked mutable copy. Independent child transcripts do not inherit attachment-bearing parent prompt scope; same-agent SOP continuation retains its existing primary transcript without prompt-tool capability. Its scoped tool-protocol rebuilds preserve complete approved context and refuse overflow before dispatch. Unsupported prompt-tool calls are rejected before approval, and their arguments/results are excluded from SOP step audit capture.
  - Binds primary work to the admitted durable incarnation. Chat deletion now coordinates RPC and gateway work: cancel the captured generation, serialize deletion, refuse ambiguous candidate keys, commit an unambiguous durable deletion in SQLite, and invalidate the gateway generation only after commit. A non-creating admission binds the selected key, owner and SQLite incarnation (or JSONL in-process lifecycle observation) before signalling; the backend rechecks it under its storage lock or transaction before an effect. Full stored keys are mapped to the actual owning queue, and unprovable identities are refused. Streaming HTTP turns register cancellation against the current queue generation and retain that generation until the turn and stream cleanup finish. HTTP deletion treats the full storage key from the Dashboard list as literal, including when the row disappeared before confirmation. HTTP deletion uses the same identity-bound admission, with storage work on blocking workers and queue ownership retained through settlement. RPC reserves both relevant ACP identities when a full RPC storage key resolves to a display ID. Successful JSONL deletion and reset invalidate pending append observations for that transcript. If either configured durable store fails to open, unqualified reaped-session deletion refuses to proceed. Specify the mode to select an available store. Committed RPC/HTTP cleanup survives a dropped request. SQLite rollback preserves the durable owner and leaves an idle WebSocket usable; already-cancelled work cannot be restored. Each overlapping delete retains its own generation-bound cancellation claim until it finishes, so an early failure cannot clear another waiter’s signal. This also protects late or replacement token registration without cancelling a successor generation. JSONL also refuses multiple distinct candidate files before cleanup; an I/O error can still interrupt its non-transactional file cleanup. Gateway cancellation binds the exact admitted queue key and generation, preventing deletion of an underscore session from cancelling a distinct dotted WebSocket session.
  - Merges official `master` through `b503bc5758fa`. The merge preserves per-turn timestamps and recorded cancellation results alongside required session-prompt budgeting and hook cleanup for participating calls. The earlier sync through `fa48765b3e3c` remains part of the branch. Tool advertisement retains both normalized exclusions and the session-prompt admission gate; a channel regression covers elicitation alongside private session prompts. An earlier sync through `6877da56d2a0` preserved the relay-dashboard and session-coordination wiring. The new scoped dashboard RPC route forwards strict approval policy and the retry status; a rejected action is redisplayed only when the owner-bound request was still pending. The prior `a66cc98a47d7` sync changed the early undispatchable-call path to omit session-prompt arguments from observer and stream events, and to abandon a hook only when it entered the hook pipeline. Orphan retirement compares the same redacted history projection used by RPC persistence, while refusing retirement when the stored history is incomplete.
    An earlier sync through `65f8eb3c9284` keeps the tool assembly’s upstream owned-session memory routing and the feature’s direct-only prompt-tool boundary. One existing SOP test fixture supplies the new optional owner field with `None`, preserving the unowned case.
    The prior `c54e002a836e` sync retains upstream dashboard sign-in lifetimes and delegated principal-memory ownership. Initial Chat construction uses the same sign-out-aware session-permit helper as later turns, preserving the deletion fence while closing a waiting signed-out viewer. Current authority is resolved again after session/storage waits and held through cancellation or durable mutation; the admitted attachment owner survives execution-time preparation. Guarded JSONL deletion refuses targets whose complete physical identity and filesystem semantics cannot be proved; SQLite remains atomic. Preserves supplied-only registries, native recipes, memory provenance and child capability/principal wiring while retaining Chat-only prompt admission. Prompt-tool exclusion now runs after registry sealing so it cannot misclassify a supplied tool as a deferred built-in. Request-only tool-context retention preserves the full required prompt section and working transcript. Executed-result privacy now survives typed history and native/text request replay even when a hook rewrites an ordinary call into a prompt tool. Earlier literal strict Signal-preview and independent-child isolation fixes remain intact.
- **Scope boundary:** Channel and gateway-RPC Chat sessions, including Web and ZeroCode Chat. No ACP prompt support, JSONL prompt support, cron/SOP/delegate/subagent/one-shot/auxiliary capability, arbitrary-session management, REST collection management or new slash commands. Ordinary ACP lifecycle handling remains isolated from Chat candidates. Ambiguous multiple Chat rows or JSONL files are refused until their identity can be established. No deployment, WIT/WASM ABI change, new lockfile package or workflow-permission expansion. `zeroclaw-infra` adds direct dependencies on already-locked `tokio-util` and Linux-only `rustix` (`fs` and `std` features), and Windows-only `same-file` for transcript identity checks.
- **Blast radius:** Against official `1b1873d852a27659991649adcda49ebcab07efea` at `990af85a1f6a3f618d3257d23c9bf17b83043ad4`: storage/lifecycle, daemon coordination, approvals/redaction, channels/RPC, configuration/localization, Web/ZeroCode and prompt budgeting; CI also adds a WhatsApp gateway feature-test lane. Private-request hook exclusion affects programmatic hook transforms, cancellation and model selection.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9998, the accepted contract; Related #10405, the Chat/ACP tracker. ACP remains a separate follow-up. Related #10412 is parallel session-contract work, not a dependency or supersession.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9998
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10405
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10412

### What this does, simply

A chat can keep a small reminder attached to itself rather than relying on remaining conversation history. A later primary turn receives it after restart, but another session and auxiliary workers do not. Successful whole-session reset starts without the attachments. The feature is off by default.

Operators normally approve the exact proposed mutation once. Unsupported confirmation surfaces refuse it; ordinary approvals still work. Prompt text grants no permissions and cannot override immutable safety/host instructions. If the complete collection and required tool-protocol framing cannot fit, provider dispatch fails instead of silently dropping content.

There are at most four attachments, each at most 2 KiB and 8 KiB collectively. Symbolic IDs follow `[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`. Changes take effect on the next top-level turn, not during the already-running turn.

When RPC deletion has admitted the matching gateway durable session, it fences that gateway lifecycle so an open WebSocket cannot recreate the deleted session. A same-ID successor is a new owner, not permission for the old connection or queued work to continue. Deleting `team_alpha` does not cancel an unrelated active `team.alpha` WebSocket queue; HTTP/SSE still uses its actual normalized queue and raw abort ID.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, on disposable sessions.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web` and `surface: tui` (ZeroCode Chat/Dashboard); messaging channels `matrix`, `slack`, `telegram`, `signal`, plus CLI confirmation. Other adapters have negative strict-capability coverage, not enabled-feature claims.
- **Setup / preconditions:** SQLite Chat persistence, `[channels].session_prompts_enabled = true`, global `session_prompt_approval = "required"`, matching clients. Default full tool selection includes the tools; a minimal configuration must name `session_prompt_list`, `session_prompt_set` and `session_prompt_delete` in `[tools].optional`, then reload. Selection grants no execution permission and does not gate injection of stored attachments into an enabled primary Chat turn. Operator WebSocket Chat additionally requires `[gateway].session_persistence = true`; scoped signed-in dashboard Chat instead uses the daemon RPC session backend and starts a new core session per chat. Restart after enabling the operator prerequisite. Matrix-only configurations need not enable gateway persistence.
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to set `{"id":"task","content":"Keep this chat focused on the synthetic inventory task."}`; inspect the literal preview and approve once. List the collection, send another turn, restart and ask again. Check another session, then reset the original and list again. Inspect and reject a 2 KiB synthetic proposal after scrolling to its end. Separately keep a WebSocket open, delete its Chat session through RPC and try another prompt through that old connection; reconnect to create or use the intended successor.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Next-turn injection and restart persistence are current-session-only; successful reset clears the collection. Strict approval has one-time allow/reject, no Always, and rejection changes nothing. After committed deletion the old WebSocket reports `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`; it cannot recreate or adopt the successor. Durable deletion failure is reported without claiming success and preserves the durable state.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The prompt collection/configuration/tools do not exist. The independent RPC/gateway deletion paths can leave an open gateway connection able to recreate deleted durable Chat state.

### How I tested

**Master sync at `990af85a1f6a3f618d3257d23c9bf17b83043ad4`.** Merged upstream `1b1873d852`. The RPC rehydration test helper retains queue admission and the existing-session check and passes the upstream method argument. The stale-refresh test uses the helper to acquire admission. An upstream ZeroCode refresh fixture now supplies the approval fields required by this branch. Local validation passed 26 RPC rehydration tests, two configure-binding tests, the ZeroCode session-refresh test, formatting, and comment hygiene. Hosted CI finished with 54 passes, five expected skips, and no failures. Security, CI Required Gate, and Greptile passed. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45738971111

**Master sync at `0d1828e967c9cb7e458cce56a02b3970e336c971`.** Merged upstream `330282cc91`. The gateway preserves opt-in SSE detach behavior and uses the generation-aware registry for cancellation and cleanup. Local checks passed for 14 webhook SSE tests, 3 cancellation registry tests, and 11 session deletion tests. All targets of gateway, runtime, and channels compiled in the local check. Formatting, staged whitespace, comment hygiene, Markdown quality, and local docs links passed. Hosted CI finished with 54 passed and five expected skips. Security, CI Required Gate, and Greptile passed. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45419972939

**Master sync at `d388b7c1b9870decadf39fb6bdb55a440172e17a`.** Rust 1.98.1 focused tests reported 22 tool-preparation, 61 prompt, 77 session-prompt and 2 cancellation-during-approval passes, with zero failures in each filter. The filters overlap. The parser suite reported 209 passes and one ignored test. The broader runtime stream filter reported 126 passes. Workspace formatting, staged whitespace and the runtime agent comment-hygiene gate passed. Security failed at cargo audit on both the PR head and its master parent. Both runs reported RUSTSEC-2026-0594 for cookie 0.16.2 and 0.18.1 and RUSTSEC-2026-0319 for anymap2 0.13.0. Those lockfile entries are unchanged against master, so dependency remediation belongs upstream. PR job https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45200317222/job/137781761359 and master job https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45149764803/job/137608134100. CI Required Gate also failed because it aggregates Security. The other 52 checks passed and five conditional checks were skipped. Passing checks include Test, Parallel Runtime Test, CLI-only build, Lint, and Greptile checks. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45200317222

**Dashboard Sessions screenshot.** The current production Web build was rendered in Chrome at 1280×800 using a loopback API fixture with synthetic SQLite-shaped gateway and channel rows. The gateway row shows an enabled Delete control. The channel row shows the disabled control and the owning-interface caption. [Dashboard Sessions screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb87c85a-1d7c-4132-8db7-cb85daa14797).

**Test-only follow-up `2676acb6c072b2c8caf69890a57f3e7ac969a2e0`:** The first hosted run failed Test, Test (opt-in tools) and Parallel Runtime Test on fixtures that expected the previous deletion rules. The follow-up uses an unambiguous SQLite target for the WebSocket cases and restores the test-only synchronization point for the RPC absence case. Focused reruns returned `7 passed; 0 failed`, with production code unchanged from `1247ea4e897a82b95f9014b3eb346b70f9287b7e`. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44982364682

**Production change at `1247ea4e897a82b95f9014b3eb346b70f9287b7e`:** The SSE suite returned `9 passed; 0 failed`. RPC deletion `26 passed; 0 failed`, storage admission `12 passed; 0 failed`, and queue lease `1 passed; 0 failed`. Gateway deletion `11 passed; 0 failed`. Rust 1.98.1 strict Clippy passed on infra, runtime, gateway and tools at the same executable code revision. Comment hygiene passed (58 fixture cases plus the gate). Earlier candidate checks: infra, runtime, and gateway passed all-targets compilation; ACP deletion `5 passed; 0 failed`; live deletion lock contention `1 passed; 0 failed`; existing-transcript append admission `2 passed; 0 failed`; Dashboard message POST `9 passed; 0 failed`; sessions_send `10 passed; 0 failed`; session-store `136 passed; 0 failed`; SQLite `103 passed; 0 failed`; session-prompt `77 passed; 0 failed`; RPC protocol `28 passed; 0 failed`. Affected-package Rust 1.98.1 Clippy passed with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`; `openrpc --check` reported `zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync`; comment-hygiene fixtures reported `58 passed, 0 failed` and the worktree gate passed. Web typecheck, 40 voice tests and shared context tests passed at merge head `e81c023`; subsequent edits affected Rust storage/deletion and documentation. Hosted CI for `2676acb6c072b2c8caf69890a57f3e7ac969a2e0`: 54 checks passed and five expected conditional checks were skipped. CI Required Gate, Test, Test (opt-in tools), Parallel Runtime Test, and Greptile passed. Greptile added no comments. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44983062759. The compiler emitted deprecated atomic-method warnings and the macOS linker emitted an unwind-section warning.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Previous head `2676acb6c072b2c8caf69890a57f3e7ac969a2e0`: 54 checks passed and five expected conditional checks were skipped. CI Required Gate, Test, Test (opt-in tools), Parallel Runtime Test, and Greptile passed. Greptile added no comments. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44983062759. Historical run on `571f2a3a05911ff9dffd7f0c276cdd8625aa2367`, all 54 executed checks passed, including Test, Parallel Runtime Test, Lint, Security, Web Permission Tests and CI Required Gate; five conditional jobs were skipped and no required job was skipped. These cover workspace tests, concurrency, static checks and the Web boundary. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/42889840830
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Exact-head hosted CI status is reported above. The earlier dashboard end-to-end fixture exercises strict approval, retry and stale refusal, but is not exact-head or deployed smoke evidence. The positive Linux ext JSONL deletion path was cross-compiled but has not been exercised on a proven Linux ext filesystem. The exact access-revoked-during-retryable-response intersection was checked in source, not exercised dynamically.
- **Commands run and tail output:** On `571f2a3a0591`, `cargo +1.98.1 test --locked -p xtask --lib` reported `250 passed; 0 failed`; the six OpenRPC tests passed, including the descriptor regression. The following implementation checks ran at `8b073afb448d`; `571f2a3a0591` changes only the OpenRPC test. Rust 1.98.1 (CI uses 1.98.0): RPC protocol `28 passed`; runtime approval `261 passed`; runtime session-prompt `75 passed`; gateway approval `20 passed`; exact stale-dashboard regression `1 passed`; `cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-rpc-proto --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed; `cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin generate -- openrpc --check` reported `openrpc: docs/book/src/architecture/zeroclaw-rpc.openrpc.json is in sync`. The macOS linker emitted an `__eh_frame` size warning also recorded on a clean older upstream ancestor; the old run was not a passing-test claim. Web `npm run typecheck` passed; session lifecycle `64 passed`; turn-stream `13 passed`; approval-preview `1 passed`. Docs quality reported `0 error(s)`, docs links `6 tests OK`, and comment-hygiene fixtures `58 passed, 0 failed` plus `Comment hygiene gate passed`. npm reported an existing unknown `python` user-config warning; React reported `react-test-renderer` deprecation.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The dashboard fixture exercises the real signed-in WebSocket-to-RPC path with synthetic identities/model responses: strict Always is refused without consuming the one-time request and the same preview is redisplayed; a request answered elsewhere is not redisplayed. The initial test-fixture priority and missing mock failures were corrected; a mistyped short `--exact` filter selected zero tests and is not evidence. A prior dashboard parallel run had two timing/flood failures; both and the full suite passed serially on an earlier integration tree. No deployed or live-channel smoke was run for this update.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot. [Web screenshot at preceding head `8b073afb448d` (the subsequent commit changes only an OpenRPC test)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac1c585b-4fa4-4361-a75e-5143b8736541): the local fixture intentionally synthesizes a refusal and preview replay after Deny solely to demonstrate the visual state; real backend tests separately exercise rejected Always and expired requests. Previous screenshots below are historical and are not current-head proof.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Current-code visual smoke was not rerun; the following visual evidence is historical at `571f2a3a05911ff9dffd7f0c276cdd8625aa2367`; gateway integration fixture and Web context tests ran on `8b073afb448d`, whose only subsequent change is the OpenRPC test. The production Web UI at preceding head `8b073afb448d` (the subsequent commit changes only an OpenRPC test) was exercised in a local browser with a synthetic fixture; [the screenshot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac1c585b-4fa4-4361-a75e-5143b8736541) shows its refusal notice and retained strict preview.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The screenshot is linked above; command results are recorded in the testing entry.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** In the screenshot, the synthetic fixture returns a refusal after Deny; the localized notice appears and the strict preview remains. Separate gateway tests exercise refused Always and ensure stale/unconfirmed requests do not reappear. The Web error notice uses the web localization catalogue, with English fallback for untranslated locales.

<details>
<summary>Historical interface evidence; not current-head or deployment proof</summary>

Screenshot; historical captures remain revision-labeled. Historical strict-preview captures cover non-trimming wrapping at 60×32 and 100×32, scrolling to the final detail with a fixed footer, and visible Unicode escapes at 60×32. These use the production ZeroCode UI with a synthetic Unix-RPC producer, not a real-daemon smoke test. [Narrow strict preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e65f37ed-a726-4aff-acba-79cfa159c137), [wide strict preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad356901-cd02-42d5-85b0-dc53918b78e2), [scrolled final detail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68ffe734-dcfe-41fe-8cff-a50bf1aebc41), [visible Unicode escapes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75d8533c-28cb-4e59-a98c-b9c3ff9aeaa6).

Historical strict-preview and Unicode captures use the production ZeroCode UI built from `0ed42836b5` (UI sources unchanged at `c4b1bc939725`) with a synthetic Unix-RPC producer. The runtime Unicode repair is tested separately at `c4b1bc939725`; the reused UI binary does not contain that runtime repair. Historical Web at `451354716983c21cc0511490c08e06b1999ca363`, production SPA with synthetic HTTP/WebSocket producer. Historical ZeroCode at `cc46a7088726a4bf1b250e05a9a7a038410ccf32` plus three infrastructure corrections, locked production binary at 100×32 with synthetic Unix-RPC producer. Historical Dashboard Kill at `71c8e45c514f8f1730e5ab01690108c553181b72`, English 100×32 synthetic Unix-RPC scenario. None is current deployed runtime execution. The master merge changes other ZeroCode code; current whole-UI/build-input equivalence is not claimed. The strict-approval renderer is unchanged by this integration, and the captures remain evidence only for their recorded revisions.

[Web strict initial](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/497e0855-8c3d-47e8-b4c5-dfaf727a4955), [Web strict end](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab0605a0-b473-4495-807a-bc4f9759bfbe), [Web ordinary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51e47b9e-54f0-4152-8613-4fa7f1676afd); [ZeroCode strict top](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b906d4e1-b25f-4be8-8460-f83d59fa55e7), [strict end](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f19cdbd2-ca72-48c3-a1bb-35f6b75a99d3), [ordinary compact control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c328bbf-c4ba-49b7-b641-54d055c50c25); [Kill pending](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f1cf5b5-7f30-42f7-8b7e-05cece05838f), [ended](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f78128ca-1db5-4055-88ab-8b5ffcb15cee), [replaced](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8c5e9a1-ed9a-4338-b74c-b47f1179482c), [RPC failure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3be481bd-5bed-4c53-94c5-6390b213321d).

In the historical captured scenarios, a literal 2 KiB proposal scrolls to its end while strict one-time allow/reject stays visible and Always is absent; ordinary approval retains Always. Kill shows pending, then clears only the matching ended session; changed selection is preserved and RPC failure retains detail with an error. The historical strict-preview captures show residual indentation surviving wraps, the final detail reachable by scrolling, visible `\u{E0041}`, `\u{200B}`, `\u{FE0F}` and `\u{00AD}`, and `allow_once` arriving at the synthetic RPC fixture. The Unicode capture reuses the production UI binary whose UI sources are unchanged by the display-escaper correction; it does not claim that the older binary contains the runtime repair. Runtime regression tests independently verify the encoded summary and unchanged original content. No production runtime-to-RPC integration, complete Web build-input equivalence or deployed smoke is claimed by these captures. Normal word-wrap separator consumption remains; byte-perfect whitespace visibility is not promised.

</details>

**Placement:** #11439 covers its recorded runtime scope; #12341 separately proposes the additional paths and remains pending approval before this feature merges. Publication for review does not itself grant that exception.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11439
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12341

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Opt-in durable metadata and current-session tools. Admission/transactional ownership checks prevent stale or cross-session mutations.
- New external network calls? **No.** Session-prompt approval previews use existing transports without marker expansion/upload. Matrix clients may independently fetch URL previews; disable those in the reviewing client when appropriate. A relay-terminated dashboard exposes previews and list results to that configured relay.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Opaque bounded text intentionally enters the system prompt, beneath immutable host/safety authority.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Exact default-required single-use approval, current-session incarnation ownership, direct-only dispatch, complete prompt-budget checks and output masking contain the risk. `disabled` relaxes additional content-bound confirmation, not ordinary authorization, and can permit auto-approved writes without operator preview. Hooks cannot read sensitive bodies/results. Content hashes can permit low-entropy guessing; masking is not secrecy. Sensitive text-mode exchanges omit unrepresentable media declarations; ordinary rounds/native carriers retain upstream behavior. Previously stored opaque transcripts are not retroactively scrubbed.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **No for Rust source APIs; additive/defaulted wire and configuration fields.** Feature-off users retain ordinary session operations but are affected by the explicit lifecycle, retention, reserved-name and native-prompt changes below.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** `[channels].session_prompts_enabled` defaults to `false`; global/per-risk-profile `session_prompt_approval` accepts `required`/`disabled`, global default `required`, profile default inheritance. SQLite only; enabled JSONL is rejected. When session prompts are enabled, operator WebSocket Chat needs gateway persistence or fails with `SESSION_PROMPT_LOAD_FAILED` before dispatch; scoped signed-in dashboard Chat uses the daemon RPC session backend.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- **If backward compatibility is No or either surface/floor question is Yes: exact upgrade steps for existing users:** Back up SQLite, rebuild out-of-tree Rust consumers, match Web/ZeroCode clients to the daemon and restart after enabling persistence. Existing WebSockets need reconnect after policy changes; channels need restart. RPC resolves current policy at primary-turn entry and again at protected session/storage effects after waits; the durable attachment owner remains bound to the admitted turn. Add `Config.session_prompt_approval = Required`, `ChannelsConfig.session_prompts_enabled = false`, and `RiskProfileConfig.session_prompt_approval = None` to struct literals to preserve defaults.

For all scoped dashboard approvals, an unacknowledged answer now emits an error, and an RPC delivery failure closes the socket and refuses outstanding approvals. A `retryable: true` RPC response only confirms a bound strict request was pending at response time; it may expire before the next answer. Missing status is treated as unconfirmed. Replaying a retryable preview restarts the Web countdown with its original duration, so the displayed countdown can overstate remaining time; the core deadline still controls the decision.

**Rust integration migrations:**

- In `zeroclaw-rpc-proto`, initialize `SessionApproveResult.retryable` (normally `None`) and `SessionUpdateEvent::ApprovalRequest.allow_always` (normally `None`) in struct literals or exhaustive patterns. Both are optional on the wire. `SessionDeleteParams.chat_mode` is optional for `session/delete`; unrelated methods retain `SessionIdParams`.

- Add `ChannelApprovalRequest.strict_session_prompt_approval`, approval `allow_always`, and `SessionDeleteParams.chat_mode` (defaulted/optional on wire). Old Always responses fail closed without consuming strict requests. The default `Channel::request_approval_attributed` refuses strict requests before delegating to a legacy approval implementation. Custom adapters must override it with the literal-preview and operator-confirmation contract to support these mutations. Unsupported/WASM adapters decline strict requests; ordinary approval remains available and WIT/WASM ABI is unchanged.
- ZeroCode Rust consumers constructing `SessionUpdate::ApprovalRequest` must supply `allow_always`; missing wire fields default to `true` for older ordinary producers. `RpcClient::session_kill` changes from `Result<()>` to `Result<SessionKillResult>` (with `session_id` and `killed`); callers must inspect `killed` before reporting an ended session. The channel prompt-building compatibility helpers are now test-only, but were already crate-private on master and create no external Rust migration.
- Add `TurnAttribution.session_id: Option<String>` for caller-visible identity separately from durable `session_key`. Both `rpc::turn::execute_turn` and `execute_turn_prepared` take `session_prompts: Option<SessionPromptAdmission>` after `cost_context`; capture `{ backend, owner }` at primary Chat admission, never resolve a fresh owner after asynchronous preparation. Excluded execution uses `None`.
- Migrate queue `generation` use to `transcript_generation` or the separate async lifecycle-generation/lease APIs. `GatewayStarter` and gateway supervision constructors receive the shared coordination capability; `RpcContext` requires `gateway_sessions`. Share it across restart within a daemon generation, create a fresh coordination scope on reload, and do not share Chat coordination with ACP.
- `AppState.cancel_tokens` changes from upstream `Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<CancellationToken>>>>` to `Arc<Mutex<GatewayCancellationRegistry>>`. Direct constructors use the registry instead of a plain map; entries are `GatewayCancellationEntry { session_key, generation, token }`. Registration and deletion helpers carry the actual admitted queue key and lifecycle generation, not a queue reconstructed from a normalized abort ID. Wire/configuration/SQLite formats are unchanged by this correction. Do not invent generations outside the lifecycle.
- `SessionStore::insert_admitted` is removed. Use `insert_admitted_if_absent` with the matching session permit held through restoration; handle an existing successor without replacement. `insert` acquires admission itself and must not be called while holding that permit. `insert_for_prompt` requires matching cancellation registration. `SessionStore::register_cancel_token` is test-only/crate-private; external code must use RPC lifecycle rather than directly maintaining that registry. The separate public infra gateway registration helper remains the admission path for gateway tokens; do not bypass its latch/replacement checks with raw map insertion.
- Gateway `PendingApprovals` maps IDs to public `PendingApproval` entries with crate-private fields. Construct it with `new_pending_approvals()` and pass it to `WsApprovalChannel::new`; external manual insertion/resolution must be retired or replaced by a separately designed adapter API. `ApprovalPendingMap::register` now requires `strict_session_prompt_approval: bool`; its old `insert` helper is test-only. Use `insert_with_policy(..., false)` for ordinary approvals and explicit strict metadata for prompt mutations.
- The new `GatewayCancellationRegistry::pending_deletions()` diagnostic accessor returns `&HashMap<String, HashMap<u64, usize>>`, with outstanding guard counts per queue generation. Consumers of earlier PR builds that inspected `HashSet` generation values must use the count map and `contains_key`; the registry's active-token map compatibility remains separate. This accessor and pending-state representation are new relative to master, not a pre-existing wire protocol.
- Implement `admit_session_deletion` and its identity-bound handle for guarded RPC and operator HTTP Chat deletion, including when prompt injection is disabled. The handle must compare the complete candidate set and exact lifetime under storage serialization before a signal and at commit, recheck authority, and report whether the owning queue identity is exact. Its `SessionDeletionAuthorization` callback receives all present `SessionDeletionCandidate` values at once (an empty slice means absent, while a candidate with no principal is a present legacy-unowned row) and returns one effect guard held through classification and the effect. Custom implementations and forwarding decorators must adopt this callback contract. Dashboard message POST, RPC append and sessions_send also require the new admit_existing_append capability. Its default returns Unsupported, and forwarding backends must preserve the selected transcript identity and conditional append behavior. Defaults reject unsupported operations and unknown queue identity; forwarding decorators must forward the admission and handle intact. `admit_session_prompt_owner_authorized` remains required for prompt storage. JSONL has process-local lifecycle observations and non-atomic file cleanup; SQLite performs the durable commit atomically.

**Observable changes, including with attachments disabled:**

- `sessions_reset` invokes whole-session reset, clearing attachments and rotating incarnation atomically in SQLite. Its "already empty" wording still counts removed messages, not attachment removal. Message-only clear preserves attachments.
- Durable `/new` deletion failure keeps existing history and reports `channel-runtime-new-session-failed` instead of claiming success. Legacy JSONL can treat a transcript it cannot inspect as absent. Without an attached backend and with prompt injection disabled, ordinary ephemeral behavior remains.
- Chat RPC deletion considers the raw, `rpc_` and `gw_` keys but refuses distinct candidate sessions rather than deleting all aliases. A scoped owner may delete an authorized live-only RPC session when the backend is unavailable; no gateway turn is cancelled without a proven shared durable identity. Guarded JSONL RPC and gateway deletion require an exact, single-link file with an unambiguous complete filename on positively identified Linux ext storage with casefold disabled. Names containing underscores, including ordinary `rpc_` and `gw_` keys, are refused on every platform; persistent JSONL deletion through these paths is refused on macOS and other unproved filesystems. This conservative restriction applies even with session prompts disabled. Use SQLite for supported guarded persistent-session deletion; JSONL file cleanup is non-transactional and external writers are not coordinated. The operator Dashboard directs operators to the owning interface for RPC or channel sessions. On JSONL, the Delete button can still appear enabled for a gateway row. The backend returns a conflict and preserves the transcript. Custom backends that cannot provide identity-bound admission fail closed. ACP remains separate. Queue admission can report `SESSION_BUSY`; a deleted gateway connection must reconnect. A cancellation delivered before a subsequent failure cannot be undone.
- Current-session views, strict previews, turn spans and delegate forensic principal identity use the canonical storage key. Public RPC/cost/OpenCode/shell identity remains separate; `ZEROCLAW_SESSION_ID` prefers caller-visible identity. ACP identity is unchanged.
- The three session-prompt tool names are reserved for plugins/skills even when disabled, including prepared-skill registration. Rename conflicts. They also follow master's built-in selection: default full includes eligible prompt tools; minimal requires their explicit names in `[tools].optional` and a reload. This selection changes availability, not authorization or injection of already-stored prompts into an enabled primary Chat turn. Deferred MCP tools must use full `server__tool` names rather than conflicting bare suffixes. Indirect `unfiltered_tool_arcs` excludes prompt tools; use canonical direct calls.
- Native tool framing changes from 42 to 36 characters ("Use tools when this request needs it") for exact budget substitution, including feature-off turns. Native prompt fingerprints consequently change. Complete native/XML prompt framing is paired; nonempty attachment overflow fails closed without truncating host context.
- Strict mutation previews visibly encode Unicode 17 format/default-ignorable characters, including legitimate joiners and variation selectors. This can change how joined text and emoji look in the preview; stored text, content hashes and provider context keep the original bytes. This is display encoding, not a new restriction on valid prompt text.
- Channel retention preserves upstream selection after the last user-role row, including synthetic text-tool results. Text-protocol call/result exchanges are omitted from retained history; native-tool retention remains unchanged. Privacy projection scans the complete exchange before selection so host-marked results can identify sensitive calls. Provider working history is unchanged.
- Export recovery separately recognizes malformed JSON/XML/MiniMax prompt-tool material before ordinary diagnostic output; shared streamed detection retains master's name-based behavior. Recovery is best-effort, not approval or execution. Unrepresentable text media carriers are omitted only for marked sensitive rounds; ordinary media behavior remains upstream.
- Programmatic `HookHandler::before_llm_call` is skipped when the request or active scope carries private session-prompt content, including max-iteration summaries. Its transforms, cancellation and model selection do not apply to these requests; ordinary requests retain them. Ordinary unmarked invocation examples retain hook processing when the feature is disabled; host-marked sensitive results remain protected. Observational input masking remains separate, and provider working history is never replaced with a masked hook projection.
- With single-tool rounds enabled, the host instruction is inserted before the private Session Prompts suffix. Diagnostic exports retain that instruction, and host protocol replacement leaves opaque attachment bytes unchanged. Trim reconstruction preserves the canonical host prompt before reapplying the transient instruction. Ordinary no-attachment and no-system behavior is preserved. The guide documents a reserved-heading limitation: host text (workspace files, skill/tool descriptions) with a standalone `## Session Prompts` after a blank line can be mistaken for the private suffix, leaving later tool-format/framing instructions unchanged and masking later host text in diagnostic/export views. Dispatch still rejects disallowed multi-tool calls; a failed turn may need a client retry. Use another heading in host text. This sync documents the limitation without changing runtime behavior.
- Independent child transcripts withhold attachment-bearing parent protocol scope, while same-agent inline SOP continues the primary transcript without attachment tools. Ordinary non-attachment child protocol inheritance is pre-existing and intentionally unchanged by this repair; this is not general child-context isolation.

The additive incarnation migration adopts valid unbound legacy attachments and removes mismatches/orphans. Historical legacy ownership cannot be proved retroactively; reset questionable old sessions. Feature-off does not delete stored attachments or scrub old histories. Downgrading and clearing history with an older binary can leave attachments that reappear after re-upgrade; reset affected sessions before downgrade and retain the backup.

`ToolResultMessage` adds the public `session_prompt_tool_result: bool` field.
Out-of-tree Rust struct literals must initialize it: use `false` for ordinary
results and preserve the host-derived value when replaying existing results.
Exhaustive patterns must bind the new field or use `..`; forwarding code must
preserve the flag.
The reserved key is exported as
`zeroclaw_api::model_provider::SESSION_PROMPT_HISTORY_RESULT_KEY`. Absent
serialized fields default to `false`; ordinary serialized results omit the
field. Marked results retain the existing native host key or text privacy
marker through Chat replay, including when a tool hook changed the original
call name. This is privacy provenance, not a capability or ACP prompt support.

The legacy public `SessionBackend::delete_session_owned` SQLite implementation retains master's two-autocommit deletion behavior. Runtime Chat now uses the identity-bound `admit_session_deletion` handle; external Rust consumers must select an operation matching their authorization and lifecycle requirements. Retiring or transactionally repairing the legacy method is deferred to a separate follow-up.

The runtime loop facade additionally exposes `scope_required_session_prompt_section` for channel orchestration. This is an additive Rust API; it grants no tool capability or wire access.

A stalled, non-reading dashboard client can delay sign-out close processing while the server sends the rejection of a forbidden Always approval. The existing SOP-frame reply path has the same timing limitation. Later input is still checked against current authority; this integration leaves that broader transport hardening for follow-up.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Reset/delete affected sessions with this version first when stored attachments must be removed; back up SQLite and restore the previous known-good binary/client pair. Reverting this feature restores previous source behavior but does not retroactively clean stored data. Keep the backup for migration recovery.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Set `[channels].session_prompts_enabled = false` and restart. This stops injection/tools, not attachment persistence, redaction of previously marked history or the feature-off lifecycle/retention changes described above. Reset/delete is required to remove attachments.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `SESSION_PROMPT_LOAD_FAILED`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `SESSION_BUSY`, `FORBIDDEN`, `channel-runtime-new-session-failed`, strict-preview refusal or prompt-budget errors before provider dispatch. Modifying-hook callbacks not firing for classified private requests is intentional; deployments relying on hook transforms/cancellation/model selection must account for this exclusion and host-marked sensitive results retained across feature disablement. Inspect lifecycle/approval metadata without dumping prompt bodies. An idle old WebSocket refusing after committed deletion is expected behavior, not a reason to bypass the owner fence.

prs.title: feat(goal): extract transport-neutral Goal policy contracts [Goal V1 proposal 3/12]
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Extract the transport-neutral Goal controller and task contracts into the
    experimental `zeroclaw-goal` crate while keeping durable task and SQLite
    ownership in the existing control plane; record the runtime dependency in
    the existing inventory and the crate's Experimental stability tier.
  - Share the Goal budget value type through `zeroclaw-api`, retaining separate
    rules for configured defaults and explicit finite command limits.
  - Fence Matrix Goal ownership by the authenticated raw principal and return
    a non-revealing session-unavailable result for a different principal.
  - Reject invalid Goal-related configuration edits at the shared gateway
    validation boundary, and preserve unset optional numbers in the dashboard.
- **Scope boundary:** This slice does not wire a production Goal executor,
  Matrix/ZeroCode transport, or automatic restart execution. It does not grant
  a runtime-placement exception or change production TLS policy. The included
  webhook-audit change is limited to plain-HTTP loopback test fixtures.
  `[goal].enabled` can be saved and validated, but cannot enable execution by
  itself in this prefix.
- **Blast radius:** Rust consumers of task and Goal APIs, the control-plane
  SQLite store and recovery path, configuration saves and dashboard optional
  numeric fields. The control-plane durability setting also affects ordinary
  delegate, subagent and peer-task writes. `synchronous=FULL` and
  `fullfsync=ON` increase durability but may increase write latency; that
  performance cost has not been measured here.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10341 and RFC #8303. Depends on #11879 and,
  transitively, #11878. The separate runtime-exception proposal is #12407.

### What this does, simply

This prepares the shared rules and durable records that later Goal Mode
adapters will use. It keeps those rules in one place and protects a session's
Goal from being controlled or replaced by a different Matrix principal. A
session-key collision can still make a session unavailable; the response does
not disclose the other principal or Goal details. This slice alone does not
make `/goal` operational.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the inherited dashboard behavior.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`; no messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a disposable local dashboard and gateway or
  an in-memory mock with Goal token and cost defaults of 500 and 2.5. Do not
  use a live operator configuration.
- **Steps to run:** In Config → Goal, clear Default Token Limit and click Save.
  Then clear Default Cost Limit Usd, enter `0` for Default Token Limit and
  click Save all. Inspect the config PATCH requests.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The first clear sends `null`; the
  second sends cost `null` and token `0`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** A cleared optional number is parsed
  as numeric `0` instead of `null`.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Hosted CI for head
  `7fecad13…` completed with 50 successful checks, eight conditional skips,
  and two failures. The successful checks include `Test`, `Security`, Web
  Permission Tests, Windows task-owner recovery, Format and Lint. CI tested
  synthetic merge `ffd1ec38…` with upstream `2c0a8c26…`, including the newer
  Web dependencies. `Parallel Runtime Test` and `CI Required Gate` failed;
  this is not an all-green result.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/43375134334
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The parallel job passed two runtime
  repetitions and failed its third on the Anthropic fallback test. Its channel
  repetitions did not run. The same test and error were observed in an earlier
  master CI run (#12351); the related cached-client issue #12236 describes a
  matching failure mechanism, but this run's interleaving is unproven. A retry
  was refused because the account lacks Actions administration permission.
  Full-stack Matrix/ZeroCode parity and the production executor belong to
  later slices. The separate Core runtime-placement decision is still pending.
  The later executor must supply the actual daemon process and boot identity
  for restart recovery to recognize a dead owner. The extracted controller
  still needs a real production receiving caller; boot reconciliation is the
  current production use of the Goal contracts.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/43375134334/job/131719823435
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/42693729496/job/129423248897
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12351
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12236
- **Commands run and tail output:** On `7fecad13cc8c580c5837dbf6996de637d629617c`,
  the runtime-composition consumer was compiled with `cargo test --locked
  --offline -p runtime-composition-consumer --no-run`; its compiled
  `dependency::dependency_boundary` test was then run directly. Before the
  inventory entry it failed with `unapproved runtime normal dependency
  zeroclaw-goal`; after the entry it reported:

  ```text
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 9 filtered out
  ```

  `cargo test --locked --offline --test architecture --no-run` built the
  architecture test, which was run directly with `--test-threads=1`:

  ```text
  test result: ok. 90 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
  ```

  The two comment-hygiene gates reported:

  ```text
  58 passed, 0 failed
  Comment hygiene gate passed.
  ```

  The first architecture build was interrupted when another Cargo job began;
  no test ran in that attempt. The successful retry emitted the known macOS
  `__eh_frame` linker warning. Rust 1.98.1 was used. The local dashboard run
  also emitted npm's unknown `python` user-config warning and Vite's future
  native-config-loader `__dirname` warning.

  On the immediately preceding `b7f2f497…` tree, which differs only in the
  dependency-inventory entry, the focused Goal host and SQLite contract tests
  reported 48 and 27 passed, respectively; the unchanged parallel gate reported
  6,196 runtime tests and 2,059 channel tests passed in each of three runs
  (10 and 2 ignored, respectively). Focused all-target Clippy with
  `-D warnings` and formatting passed. The Web permissions suite reported 42
  passed. These results are prior-head evidence,
  not current-head hosted CI.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** At `7fecad13…`, the actual Web
  dashboard was exercised against a loopback in-memory mock. Section Save sent
  token `null`; Save all sent cost `null` and explicit token `0`. This did not
  exercise gateway authentication or disk persistence. The candidate is a
  descendant of the published branch and previews a clean merge with the
  observed upstream head. No live room, provider, deployment or database
  migration was exercised.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot of the actual Web renderer with
  the in-memory mock, captured after clearing and saving the token field:

  ![Cleared optional token limit after Save](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a5e3f13-b53e-4457-b728-c1fe731fb186)

- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `7fecad13…`, `surface=web`,
  English, 1280×720, Vite and a disposable loopback mock; the Rust dependency
  and architecture test binaries also ran at this revision. The screenshot's
  bytes match the existing predecessor attachment. Focused runtime, channel
  and Web checks above ran at preceding `b7f2f497…`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The screenshot above is the
  exact-head capture. The mock observed PATCH values `null`, then `null` and
  `0` for the actions described above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The Web form displayed
  “Saved 1 field(s)” after the token clear; the mock observed the values above.
  The runtime dependency ratchet rejected the missing Goal entry before the
  correction and accepted the actual owner and reason afterward.

prs.body:
## Summary

Goal V1 proposal 2/12: configuration and command grammar only; this slice does
not execute Goals.

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Define the Goal command grammar, including multiline resume responses and
    immediate-pause syntax, without advertising an unwired command.
  - Add default-disabled Goal configuration and verifier-alias validation.
    Preserve absent budget defaults separately from explicit zero through
    full, incremental and gateway saves.
  - Reject invalid edits to Goal inputs with field-specific errors while
    allowing unrelated edits with a pre-existing warning.
  - Fix the shared dashboard numeric parser so clearing an optional number
    sends `null` through both Save and Save all; an explicit zero remains zero.
- **Scope boundary:** This builds on the durable task/control-plane foundation
  in #11878. It activates no Goal executor, provider call, transport admission,
  scheduler or Goal usage-ledger integration. The general first-error policy
  for unrelated non-Goal settings is not repaired here.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust task, config and command APIs; schema
  introspection, alias references, configuration persistence and gateway
  validation; and the shared Web configuration form.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10341 and #8303; Depends on #11878. The broader
  editor repair is in #11881. The separate runtime-policy proposal is #12407.
  This slice closes neither the tracker nor the RFC.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11878
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11881
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12407

### What this does, simply

This describes and validates Goal commands and settings, but does not run them.
Omitted budget defaults stay unconfigured; positive defaults provide a finite
limit, and both explicitly zero defaults select unlimited. Later admission must
still check opt-in, verifier validity, authorization and the effective budget.

In the dashboard, clearing an optional numeric field now unsets it rather than
silently saving zero. Invalid edits to Goal inputs are rejected rather than
being saved as an unrelated warning.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the dashboard save paths.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, ordinary dashboard over a paired
  gateway. No messaging channel or Goal execution is required.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a disposable config and loopback-only gateway
  with pairing enabled. No paid provider, installed daemon, operator config
  or live room is needed. Do not invoke Reload daemon or a Goal command.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config → Goal. Set Default Token Limit to `500` and
  use section Save; clear it and Save again. Inspect the request and disposable
  TOML, then open a fresh document. Save explicit `0`. Set the cost to `2.5`,
  clear it, navigate away and back, and use Save all. Finally save token `750`
  through Save all.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Clearing sends JSON `null` and removes
  the corresponding key. The fresh document shows an empty optional field.
  Explicit zero and the untouched sibling survive, and later edits remain
  possible.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Frozen base `535f0844` has no Goal
  section. With a disposable config, clearing an existing optional numeric
  field exercises the same shared parser, which sends zero rather than `null`.
  The earlier pre-repair proposal head `6e74d5a8` reproduced the bad zero write
  for the optional Goal schema. These are distinct comparisons.

### How I tested

- New external network calls? No; verifier aliases are checked without calling

prs.title: feat(oidc): add refresh and revocation requests to enrollment (#12707 slice 1)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - This is slice 1 of #12707, the daemon-held OIDC refresh grants from the ADR-017 amendment in #12496. It adds the two identity-provider requests a refresh grant needs to `Enrollment`. It stores nothing, and nothing calls it yet.
  - **`Enrollment::refresh(refresh_token, auth)`** sends `grant_type=refresh_token` (RFC 6749 §6) without `scope`, so a refresh never asks for more than the original grant, even if `scopes` was widened since sign-in. Its outcomes are classified for the grant layer:
    - `Ok(Granted)` returns the new token. Its `refresh_token` is `None` when the provider kept the current one.
    - `Ok(Refused)` means the provider answered with an OAuth error. The grant layer will delete the grant for any refusal, `invalid_client` included, as recorded in #12707.
    - `Err(NotSent)` means the refresh token provably never left the process: the token was blank, discovery failed, or the connection was never established (DNS, TCP or TLS, including a connect timeout).
    - `Err(Unknown)` means the request may have reached the provider, which may already have rotated the token. This covers a connection lost after it was established, a redirect, a non-OAuth error status, and a 200 that can't be presented. ADR-017 retries this case exactly once.
    - No error message includes the response body or any token.
  - **`Enrollment::revoke_refresh_token(refresh_token, auth)`** sends an RFC 7009 revocation, but only when discovery advertises a `revocation_endpoint`. That endpoint is held to the same URL policy as the other discovered endpoints, checked only when a revocation is about to be sent, so a provider advertising a bad one changes nothing for the existing flows.
  - **`ClientAuthentication`** (`client_secret_basic` / `client_secret_post`) serializes as the OAuth `token_endpoint_auth_method` names, so a grant can record the method its refresh token was issued under and reuse it. A provider may accept only a client's registered method; Authelia's default, for example, refuses HTTP Basic. `DEVICE_GRANT` (Basic) and `AUTHORIZATION_CODE` (Post) name what each flow sends, and the flows now read those constants. To make that possible, the code exchange now goes through the shared client-authentication helper. Every existing flow sends the same request as before.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - This is within the `enrollment.rs` part of the approved ADR-016 row from #12609 (approval recorded in #12708): a refresh request that omits `scope`, RFC 7009 revocation, and classifying a failed refresh as never sent or outcome unknown.
  - Not yet in this PR: retaining refresh tokens (the gateway still discards them), `refresh_grant.rs`, the certificate-ledger table, the RPC method and Zerocode. Those are slices 2–6 of #12707.
  - `auth_provider/mod.rs` is unchanged. Callers name these types through the public `enrollment` module.
- **Blast radius:**
  - The new methods have no callers.
  - The one changed path is the Authorization Code exchange (dashboard sign-in, `zeroclaw oidc login --browser`, gateway browser enrollment). It now builds its form through `with_client_auth` with the same fields: `client_id`, plus `client_secret` for a confidential client. A new test pins this.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12707, Related #12496, Related #12609, Related #12708, Related #8289

### What this does, simply

To keep a device signed in after its access token expires, the daemon will have to swap a refresh token for a new access token, and revoke it on sign-out. This PR teaches the OIDC client how to send those two requests, and how to tell "the provider never saw this", "the provider said no" and "we can't tell what happened" apart. That distinction matters because a provider may have already replaced the refresh token. Nothing uses these requests yet; later PRs in #12707 do.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The behavior is covered against a mock identity provider, and nothing calls it yet. Live Keycloak evidence is slice 8 of #12707.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Test` runs the new `auth_provider::enrollment` tests, and `Lint` runs clippy. Both are required.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:**
  - CI has no real identity provider; the tests use wiremock.
  - A timeout while waiting for the answer is classified as `Unknown` by the same rule as a lost connection, but no test exercises it, because that would take the 15 s client timeout.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux, at `519d558a04`, rebased on `master` after #12706):

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
(clean)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib auth_provider
test result: ok. 160 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway oidc
test result: ok. 50 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo check --locked -p zerocode
(clean)
$ scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I ran negative controls: each change below was made temporarily, and the restored source passes.
  - sending `scope` on refresh;
  - reporting every send error as `NotSent`;
  - echoing the response body in an `Unknown` error;
  - reporting an OAuth refusal as `Unknown`;
  - dropping `client_secret` from the `client_secret_post` form;
  - refreshing with a fixed method instead of `auth`;
  - pointing `DEVICE_GRANT` or `AUTHORIZATION_CODE` at the wrong method.

  Each makes at least one test fail. The two constant controls first passed: the test compared against the constants the flows read. Each flow is now pinned to its documented method by literal value.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `519d558a04`; Rust library API and wiremock tests in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/security/auth_provider/enrollment.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** See above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `cargo test --workspace`: only `enrollment.rs` changed. Its dependents (`zeroclaw-gateway` OIDC tests, `zerocode`) were run or checked above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? Yes, once a later slice calls them. These are the token-endpoint refresh request and the RFC 7009 revocation request, both to the configured issuer's discovered endpoints.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. The new requests carry a refresh token and the client's credentials.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. The tests use synthetic values.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - **Where credentials go:** they are sent only to endpoints from a discovery document whose issuer exactly matches the configured one, and held to the HTTPS/exact-loopback URL policy. Redirects are never followed.
  - **No leaks:** outcomes and errors never include the response body or token material, and `Debug` stays redacted. Tests pin both.
  - **Rotated tokens:** a possibly-delivered request is reported as `Unknown` rather than "never sent", so the grant layer won't replay a refresh token the provider may have rotated, which could trip reuse detection.
  - **Client authentication:** `client_secret_post` sends the secret only in the form body to the token or revocation endpoint, as the code exchange already did.

## Compatibility (required)

- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

prs.title: ci(workflows): retry tool downloads instead of failing the job
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - CI downloads `cargo-nextest`, `cargo-deny` and `cargo-audit` with a single `curl` piped into `tar`, so one 5xx or dropped connection fails the job before any code runs. On 2026-11-09, merge-queue run 42569447258 (the entry for #12100) failed seven test jobs at `Install cargo-nextest`, and the next queue run, 42571610051, lost `Test (channel Matrix)` at the same step 23 minutes later.
  - Each of the nine downloads now goes to a file with `curl --retry 5 --retry-delay 3 --retry-all-errors` and is extracted afterwards. Extracting from a file is what makes the retry safe: a retried transfer restarts the file, whereas a pipe would have fed `tar` half an archive.
  - Covered: the six Linux `cargo-nextest` installs and the `cargo-deny` and `cargo-audit` installs in `ci.yml`; `cargo-audit` in `daily-audit.yml`; the macOS and Windows `cargo-nextest` installs in `platform-tests.yml`. Git Bash's `tar` reads `D:\...` as a remote host, so the Windows leg converts the path with `cygpath`, as `windows-tests.yml` already does.
  - The macOS image ships Rust without `~/.cargo/bin`, so on master the macOS platform leg fails at `Install cargo-nextest` itself (`tar: could not chdir to '/Users/runner/.cargo/bin'`). None of the last 60 scheduled runs, back to 09-24, passed. The install now creates that directory and adds it to `PATH` when it isn't already there.
- **Scope boundary:** No version changes. `cargo-nextest` still comes from `get.nexte.st/latest`, and `cargo-deny` and `cargo-audit` keep their pinned releases. The advisory Windows job's pinned, checksummed download is untouched.
- **Trade-off:** a download that is really broken, such as a moved URL, now takes about 15 seconds longer to fail.
- **Blast radius:** The install steps of the required test jobs and `Security`, the scheduled platform tests, and the daily advisory scan.
- **Linked issue(s):** None

### What this does, simply

Several CI jobs download a testing or auditing tool at the start. When the download site had a bad moment, the job failed straight away, which turned the required gate red or ejected a pull request from the merge queue for no reason connected to its change. The download is now retried a few times before the job gives up.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: this PR's own CI runs the changed Linux installs, and `platform-tests.yml` runs on this PR because the file changed.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Quality Gate run on this PR (all six Linux installs, plus `Security`), and the `Scheduled Platform Tests` run this PR triggers (macOS and Windows installs). On master the macOS leg fails at the install step and the Windows leg at `Run tests`, so read the `Install cargo-nextest` step on both, not the job result. Windows `Run tests` still fails for reasons unrelated to installs.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `daily-audit.yml` runs on a schedule or manual dispatch only; it can be dispatched on this branch. The macOS leg hasn't reached `Run tests` since at least 09-24, so whether those tests pass is not known yet.
- **Commands run and tail output:** run on `dfe8ab35bd` with this patch applied:

```text
$ actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/platform-tests.yml
(no output)
$ actionlint .github/workflows/daily-audit.yml
(two SC2016 info notes on the scan step; the same two appear on master)
$ curl -LsSf --retry 5 --retry-delay 3 --retry-all-errors -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/cargo-nextest.tar.gz" https://get.nexte.st/latest/mac
$ tar zxf "$RUNNER_TEMP/cargo-nextest.tar.gz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin" && "$RUNNER_TEMP/bin/cargo-nextest" nextest --version
cargo-nextest 0.9.152 (26ebeda79 2026-11-13)
```

```text
no ~/.cargo/bin:        exit 0; adds ~/.cargo/bin to GITHUB_PATH; cargo-nextest 0.9.152
~/.cargo/bin on PATH:   exit 0; GITHUB_PATH unchanged; cargo-nextest 0.9.152
master's step, no dir:  tar: could not chdir to '.../.cargo/bin' (the CI error)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That no test or doc quotes the old install commands. The maintainer doc's paragraph on tool installs is updated to match.

prs.title: fix(rpc): rehydrate reaped ACP sessions on provider switch
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A failed ZeroCode Code-pane turn drops the live ACP incarnation so the next prompt can rebuild provider-safe history from the durable row.
  - `/model-provider` is `session/configure`. That handler only looked at the live map, so a switch after a provider rate-limit returned `-32000` `Session not found` for a session that still existed in the ACP store.
  - `session/configure` now restores that reaped row, under the configure method's leases, before applying the provider override.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change prompt admission, checkpoint recovery rules, or when a failed turn drops the live incarnation. Does not change provider failover itself.
- **Blast radius:** `session/configure` on a reaped ACP session now rebuilds the agent before writing overrides. Live sessions and chat-mode sessions take the existing path. Rehydration leases are parameterized by the calling method instead of being hard-wired to `session/prompt`. configure's pending-binding wait now runs after the optional restore instead of before it, so it also covers a session another request restored.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

A Code pane keeps its conversation in the ACP store. When the model provider fails the turn, for example an OpenAI Codex rate limit, ZeroClaw removes the in-memory session on purpose. The next prompt knows how to put that session back. Changing the provider with `/model-provider` did not. It looked only at the in-memory map, decided the session was gone, and refused the switch with `-32000`.

This PR makes the provider-switch call restore the saved Code-pane session first, then apply the new provider. A session that was never saved, or that was killed, still gets `Session not found`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. The reliable reproduction is the new unit test; a manual A/B needs a failed Code-pane turn.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` Code pane (`channel` `rpc`, chat mode ACP) via `/model-provider` (`session/configure`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Code pane session whose provider can fail a turn (the reported case was an OpenAI alias with Codex auth, then `/model-provider` to an xAI alias). The automated test uses the persistence dispatcher and does not need live credentials.
- **Steps to run:** On a Code pane, send a prompt that ends in a failed turn, then run `/model-provider <other-provider>`. Automated: `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib session_configure_` (covers the restore path and both concurrent-restore interleavings).
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The switch succeeds and later prompts use the selected provider. The unit test asserts the reaped session is live again and its route resolver names `openai.provider-b`. The two interleaving regressions assert that when another request restores the session with a pending binding, configure waits for reconciliation, and the reported selection, stored override and live route all name `openai.provider-b` afterwards.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `/model-provider` returns `-32000` `Session not found` even though the ACP row is still in the store.

### How I tested

Focused runtime tests cover the new restore path, both concurrent-restore interleavings from review, and the existing rehydration and configure paths that share the edited function. The full `zeroclaw-runtime` lib suite and crate clippy on CI's pinned toolchain were run locally on `c98b20fc4`. Workspace-wide clippy and `cargo test` were not; required CI on this head covers them.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None yet for `c98b20fc4`. Do not treat pending checks as evidence.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local evidence does not include workspace clippy or the workspace test suite. CI lint and test jobs cover that gap once they run on this head.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0, no output

cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 00s

# Before the fix (new tests + test hook on ee958454a handler):
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib session_configure_waits_for_binding_restored -- --test-threads=1
# ..._restored_before_live_lookup ... FAILED
#   reconciliation must not revert the provider configure reported as selected
#   left: "openai.test-provider"  right: "openai.provider-b"
# ..._restored_during_admission_wait ... FAILED
#   configure must wait for the binding another request restored

# After the fix (c98b20fc4):
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib session_configure_ -- --test-threads=1
# test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 6185 filtered out

# Stress: the two interleaving regressions, default parallel harness, 25 runs
# pass=25 fail=0

cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
# test result: ok. 6185 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The failing path was identified from a Code-pane rate-limit turn (`openai` + Codex auth) followed by `/model-provider` to xAI, which returned `-32000`. I did not re-run that live provider switch after the patch. The unit tests reproduce the dropped live incarnation, the configure call, and both concurrent-restore interleavings.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A`. No presentation-sensitive interface state changed. The user-visible change is whether the slash command succeeds.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `c98b20fc4`. Automated evidence is the `zeroclaw-runtime` lib tests above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Test tails above.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** `session/configure` on a reaped ACP session restores the agent and installs the requested provider override. When another request restored it with a pending binding, configure waits for reconciliation first, so the override is not reverted.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and workspace `cargo test` were skipped locally because this change is one RPC handler plus regression tests in one crate. Crate clippy was run on CI's pinned 1.98.0; local stable 1.99.0 reports new lints in untouched code (`zeroclaw-providers`, `fetch_update` deprecations), unrelated to this PR. CI on this head is the intended coverage for the rest.

- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? (`No`)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

Low-risk. `git revert c98b20fc4 2aec36aa4` restores the previous `session/configure` lookup. After revert, `/model-provider` on a Code pane whose last turn failed again returns `-32000` until the session is reopened.
